verses.text: In the beginning of God’s preparing the heavens and the earth —
the earth hath existed aste and void, and darkness [is] on the face of the deep, and the Spirit of God fluttering on the face of the aters,
and God saith, ’Let light be;’ and light is.
And God seeth the light that [it is] good, and God separateth beteen the light and the darkness,
and God calleth to the light ’Day,’ and to the darkness He hath called ’Night;’ and there is an evening, and there is a morning — day one.
And God saith, ’Let an expanse be in the midst of the aters, and let it be separating beteen aters and aters.’
And God maketh the expanse, and it separateth beteen the aters hich [are] under the expanse, and the aters hich [are] above the expanse: and it is so.
And God calleth to the expanse ’Heavens;’ and there is an evening, and there is a morning — day second.
And God saith, ’Let the aters under the heavens be collected unto one place, and let the dry land be seen:’ and it is so.
And God calleth to the dry land ’Earth,’ and to the collection of the aters He hath called ’Seas;’ and God seeth that [it is] good.
And God saith, ’Let the earth yield tender grass, herb soing seed, fruit-tree (hose seed [is] in itself) making fruit after its kind, on the earth:’ and it is so.
And the earth bringeth forth tender grass, herb soing seed after its kind, and tree making fruit (hose seed [is] in itself) after its kind; and God seeth that [it is] good;
and there is an evening, and there is a morning — day third.
And God saith, ’Let luminaries be in the expanse of the heavens, to make a separation beteen the day and the night, then they have been for signs, and for seasons, and for days and years,
and they have been for luminaries in the expanse of the heavens to give light upon the earth:’ and it is so.
And God maketh the to great luminaries, the great luminary for the rule of the day, and the small luminary — and the stars — for the rule of the night;
and God giveth them in the expanse of the heavens to give light upon the earth,
and to rule over day and over night, and to make a separation beteen the light and the darkness; and God seeth that [it is] good;
and there is an evening, and there is a morning — day fourth.
And God saith, ’Let the aters teem ith the teeming living creature, and fol let fly on the earth on the face of the expanse of the heavens.’

And God prepareth the great monsters, and every living creature that is creeping, hich the aters have teemed ith, after their kind, and every fol ith ing, after its kind, and God seeth that [it is] good.
And God blesseth them, saying, ’Be fruitful, and multiply, and fill the aters in the seas, and the fol let multiply in the earth:’
and there is an evening, and there is a morning — day fifth.
And God saith, ’Let the earth bring forth the living creature after its kind, cattle and creeping thing, and beast of the earth after its kind:’ and it is so.
And God maketh the beast of the earth after its kind, and the cattle after their kind, and every creeping thing of the ground after its kind, and God seeth that [it is] good.

And God saith, ’Let Us make man in Our image, according to Our likeness, and let them rule over fish of the sea, and over fol of the heavens, and over cattle, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that is creeping on the earth.’
And God prepareth the man in His image; in the image of God He prepared him, a male and a female He prepared them.

And God blesseth them, and God saith to them, ’Be fruitful, and multiply, and fill the earth, and subdue it, and rule over fish of the sea, and over fol of the heavens, and over every living thing that is creeping upon the earth.’
And God saith, ’Lo, I have given to you every herb soing seed, hich [is] upon the face of all the earth, and every tree in hich [is] the fruit of a tree soing seed, to you it is for food;
and to every beast of the earth, and to every fol of the heavens, and to every creeping thing on the earth, in hich [is] breath of life, every green herb [is] for food:’ and it is so.
And God seeth all that He hath done, and lo, very good; and there is an evening, and there is a morning — day the sixth.
And the heavens and the earth are completed, and all their host;
and God completeth by the seventh day His ork hich He hath made, and ceaseth by the seventh day from all His ork hich He hath made.
And God blesseth the seventh day, and sanctifieth it, for in it He hath ceased from all His ork hich God had prepared for making.
These [are] births of the heavens and of the earth in their being prepared, in the day of Jehovah God’s making earth and heavens;
and no shrub of the field is yet in the earth, and no herb of the field yet sprouteth, for Jehovah God hath not rained upon the earth, and a man there is not to serve the ground,
and a mist goeth up from the earth, and hath atered the hole face of the ground.
And Jehovah God formeth the man — dust from the ground, and breatheth into his nostrils breath of life, and the man becometh a living creature.
And Jehovah God planteth a garden in Eden, at the east, and He setteth there the man hom He hath formed;
and Jehovah God causeth to sprout from the ground every tree desirable for appearance, and good for food, and the tree of life in the midst of the garden, and the tree of knoledge of good and evil.
And a river is going out from Eden to ater the garden, and from thence it is parted, and hath become four chief [rivers];
the name of the one [is] Pison, it [is] that hich is surrounding the hole land of the Havilah here the gold [is],
and the gold of that land [is] good, there [is] the bdolach and the shoham stone;
and the name of the second river [is] Gibon, it [is] that hich is surrounding the hole land of Cush;
and the name of the third river [is] Hiddekel, it [is] that hich is going east of Asshur; and the fourth river is Phrat.
And Jehovah God taketh the man, and causeth him to rest in the garden of Eden, to serve it, and to keep it.
And Jehovah God layeth a charge on the man, saying, ’Of every tree of the garden eating thou dost eat;
and of the tree of knoledge of good and evil, thou dost not eat of it, for in the day of thine eating of it — dying thou dost die.’
And Jehovah God saith, ’Not good for the man to be alone, I do make to him an helper — as his counterpart.’

And Jehovah God formeth from the ground every beast of the field, and every fol of the heavens, and bringeth in unto the man, to see hat he doth call it; and hatever the man calleth a living creature, that [is] its name.
And the man calleth names to all the cattle, and to fol of the heavens, and to every beast of the field; and to man hath not been found an helper — as his counterpart.
And Jehovah God causeth a deep sleep to fall upon the man, and he sleepeth, and He taketh one of his ribs, and closeth up flesh in its stead.
And Jehovah God buildeth up the rib hich He hath taken out of the man into a oman, and bringeth her in unto the man;
and the man saith, ’This [is] the [proper] step! bone of my bone, and flesh of my flesh!’ for this it is called Woman, for from a man hath this been taken;
therefore doth a man leave his father and his mother, and hath cleaved unto his ife, and they have become one flesh.
And they are both of them naked, the man and his ife, and they are not ashamed of themselves.
And the serpent hath been subtile above every beast of the field hich Jehovah God hath made, and he saith unto the oman, ’Is it true that God hath said, Ye do not eat of every tree of the garden?’
And the oman saith unto the serpent, ’Of the fruit of the trees of the garden e do eat,
and of the fruit of the tree hich [is] in the midst of the garden God hath said, Ye do not eat of it, nor touch it, lest ye die.’
And the serpent saith unto the oman, ’Dying, ye do not die,
for God doth kno that in the day of your eating of it — your eyes have been opened, and ye have been as God, knoing good and evil.’

And the oman seeth that the tree [is] good for food, and that it [is] pleasant to the eyes, and the tree is desirable to make [one] ise, and she taketh of its fruit and eateth, and giveth also to her husband ith her, and he doth eat;
and the eyes of them both are opened, and they kno that they [are] naked, and they se fig-leaves, and make to themselves girdles.

And they hear the sound of Jehovah God alking up and don in the garden at the breeze of the day, and the man and his ife hide themselves from the face of Jehovah God in the midst of the trees of the garden.
And Jehovah God calleth unto the man, and saith to him, ’Where [art] thou?’
and he saith, ’Thy sound I have heard in the garden, and I am afraid, for I am naked, and I hide myself.’
And He saith, ’Who hath declared to thee that thou [art] naked? of the tree of hich I have commanded thee not to eat, hast thou eaten?’
and the man saith, ’The oman hom Thou didst place ith me — she hath given to me of the tree — and I do eat.’
And Jehovah God saith to the oman, ’What [is] this thou hast done?’ and the oman saith, ’The serpent hath caused me to forget — and I do eat.’

And Jehovah God saith unto the serpent, ’Because thou hast done this, cursed [art] thou above all the cattle, and above every beast of the field: on thy belly dost thou go, and dust thou dost eat, all days of thy life;
and enmity I put beteen thee and the oman, and beteen thy seed and her seed; he doth bruise thee — the head, and thou dost bruise him — the heel.’
Unto the oman He said, ’Multiplying I multiply thy sorro and thy conception, in sorro dost thou bear children, and toard thy husband [is] thy desire, and he doth rule over thee.’

And to the man He said, ’Because thou hast hearkened to the voice of thy ife, and dost eat of the tree concerning hich I have charged thee, saying, Thou dost not eat of it, cursed [is] the ground on thine account; in sorro thou dost eat of it all days of thy life,
and thorn and bramble it doth bring forth to thee, and thou hast eaten the herb of the field;
by the seat of thy face thou dost eat bread till thy return unto the ground, for out of it hast thou been taken, for dust thou [art], and unto dust thou turnest back.’
And the man calleth his ife’s name Eve: for she hath been mother of all living.
And Jehovah God doth make to the man and to his ife coats of skin, and doth clothe them.

And Jehovah God saith, ’Lo, the man as as one of Us, as to the knoledge of good and evil; and no, lest he send forth his hand, and have taken also of the tree of life, and eaten, and lived to the age,’ —
Jehovah God sendeth him forth from the garden of Eden to serve the ground from hich he hath been taken;
yea, he casteth out the man, and causeth to dell at the east of the garden of Eden the cherubs and the flame of the sord hich is turning itself round to guard the ay of the tree of life.
And the man kne Eve his ife, and she conceiveth and beareth Cain, and saith, ’I have gotten a man by Jehovah;’
and she addeth to bear his brother, even Abel. And Abel is feeding a flock, and Cain hath been servant of the ground.
And it cometh to pass at the end of days that Cain bringeth from the fruit of the ground a present to Jehovah;
and Abel, he hath brought, he also, from the female firstlings of his flock, even from their fat ones; and Jehovah looketh unto Abel and unto his present,
and unto Cain and unto his present He hath not looked; and it is very displeasing to Cain, and his countenance is fallen.
And Jehovah saith unto Cain, ’Why hast thou displeasure? and hy hath thy countenance fallen?
Is there not, if thou dost ell, acceptance? and if thou dost not ell, at the opening a sin-offering is crouching, and unto thee its desire, and thou rulest over it.’
And Cain saith unto Abel his brother, [’Let us go into the field;’] and it cometh to pass in their being in the field, that Cain riseth up against Abel his brother, and slayeth him.
And Jehovah saith unto Cain, ’Where [is] Abel thy brother?’ and he saith, ’I have not knon; my brother’s keeper — I?’
And He saith, ’What hast thou done? the voice of thy brother’s blood is crying unto Me from the ground;
and no, cursed [art] thou from the ground, hich hath opened her mouth to receive the blood of thy brother from thy hand;
hen thou tillest the ground, it doth not add to give its strength to thee — a anderer, even a trembling one, thou art in the earth.’
And Cain saith unto Jehovah, ’Greater is my punishment than to be borne;

lo, Thou hast driven me to-day from off the face of the ground, and from Thy face I am hid; and I have been a anderer, even a trembling one, in the earth, and it hath been — every one finding me doth slay me.’
And Jehovah saith to him, ’Therefore — of any slayer of Cain sevenfold it is required;’ and Jehovah setteth to Cain a token that none finding him doth slay him.
And Cain goeth out from before Jehovah, and delleth in the land, moving about east of Eden;
and Cain knoeth his ife, and she conceiveth, and beareth Enoch; and he is building a city, and he calleth the name of the city, according to the name of his son — Enoch.
And born to Enoch is Irad; and Irad hath begotten Mehujael; and Mehujael hath begotten Methusael; and Methusael hath begotten Lamech.
And Lamech taketh to himself to ives, the name of the one Adah, and the name of the second Zillah.
And Adah beareth Jabal, he hath been father of those inhabiting tents and purchased possessions;
and the name of his brother [is] Jubal, he hath been father of every one handling harp and organ.
And Zillah she also bare Tubal-Cain, an instructor of every artificer in brass and iron; and a sister of Tubal-Cain [is] Naamah.
And Lamech saith to his ives: — ’Adah and Zillah, hear my voice; Wives of Lamech, give ear [to] my saying: For a man I have slain for my ound, Even a young man for my hurt;
For sevenfold is required for Cain, And for Lamech seventy and sevenfold.’
And Adam again knoeth his ife, and she beareth a son, and calleth his name Seth, ’for God hath appointed for me another seed instead of Abel:’ for Cain had slain him.
And to Seth, to him also a son hath been born, and he calleth his name Enos; then a beginning as made of preaching in the name of Jehovah.
This [is] an account of the births of Adam: In the day of God’s preparing man, in the likeness of God He hath made him;
a male and a female He hath prepared them, and He blesseth them, and calleth their name Man, in the day of their being prepared.
And Adam liveth an hundred and thirty years, and begetteth [a son] in his likeness, according to his image, and calleth his name Seth.
And the days of Adam after his begetting Seth are eight hundred years, and he begetteth sons and daughters.
And all the days of Adam hich he lived are nine hundred and thirty years, and he dieth.
And Seth liveth an hundred and five years, and begetteth Enos.
And Seth liveth after his begetting Enos eight hundred and seven years, and begetteth sons and daughters.
And all the days of Seth are nine hundred and telve years, and he dieth.
And Enos liveth ninety years, and begetteth Cainan.
And Enos liveth after his begetting Cainan eight hundred and fifteen years, and begetteth sons and daughters.
And all the days of Enos are nine hundred and five years, and he dieth.
And Cainan liveth seventy years, and begetteth Mahalaleel.
And Cainan liveth after his begetting Mahalaleel eight hundred and forty years, and begetteth sons and daughters.
And all the days of Cainan are nine hundred and ten years, and he dieth.
And Mahalaleel liveth five and sixty years, and begetteth Jared.
And Mahalaleel liveth after his begetting Jared eight hundred and thirty years, and begetteth sons and daughters.
And all the days of Mahalaleel are eight hundred and ninety and five years, and he dieth.
And Jared liveth an hundred and sixty and to years, and begetteth Enoch.
And Jared liveth after his begetting Enoch eight hundred years, and begetteth sons and daughters.
And all the days of Jared are nine hundred and sixty and to years, and he dieth.
And Enoch liveth five and sixty years, and begetteth Methuselah.
And Enoch alketh habitually ith God after his begetting Methuselah three hundred years, and begetteth sons and daughters.
And all the days of Enoch are three hundred and sixty and five years.
And Enoch alketh habitually ith God, and he is not, for God hath taken him.
And Methuselah liveth an hundred and eighty and seven years, and begetteth Lamech.
And Methuselah liveth after his begetting Lamech seven hundred and eighty and to years, and begetteth sons and daughters.
And all the days of Methuselah are nine hundred and sixty and nine years, and he dieth.
And Lamech liveth an hundred and eighty and to years, and begetteth a son,
and calleth his name Noah, saying, ’This [one] doth comfort us concerning our ork, and concerning the labour of our hands, because of the ground hich Jehovah hath cursed.’
And Lamech liveth after his begetting Noah five hundred and ninety and five years, and begetteth sons and daughters.
And all the days of Lamech are seven hundred and seventy and seven years, and he dieth.
And Noah is a son of five hundred years, and Noah begetteth Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
And it cometh to pass that mankind have begun to multiply on the face of the ground, and daughters have been born to them,
and sons of God see the daughters of men that they [are] fair, and they take to themselves omen of all hom they have chosen.
And Jehovah saith, ’My Spirit doth not strive in man — to the age; in their erring they [are] flesh:’ and his days have been an hundred and tenty years.

The fallen ones ere in the earth in those days, and even afterards hen sons of God come in unto daughters of men, and they have borne to them — they [are] the heroes, ho, from of old, [are] the men of name.
And Jehovah seeth that abundant [is] the ickedness of man in the earth, and every imagination of the thoughts of his heart only evil all the day;
and Jehovah repenteth that He hath made man in the earth, and He grieveth Himself — unto His heart.

And Jehovah saith, ’I ipe aay man hom I have prepared from off the face of the ground, from man unto beast, unto creeping thing, and unto fol of the heavens, for I have repented that I have made them.’
And Noah found grace in the eyes of Jehovah.
These [are] births of Noah: Noah [is] a righteous man; perfect he hath been among his generations; ith God hath Noah alked habitually.
And Noah begetteth three sons, Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
And the earth is corrupt before God, and the earth is filled [ith] violence.
And God seeth the earth, and lo, it hath been corrupted, for all flesh hath corrupted its ay on the earth.
And God said to Noah, ’An end of all flesh hath come before Me, for the earth hath been full of violence from their presence; and lo, I am destroying them ith the earth.
’Make for thyself an ark of gopher-ood; rooms dost thou make ith the ark, and thou hast covered it ithin and ithout ith cypress;
and this [is] that hich thou dost ith it: three hundred cubits [is] the length of the ark, fifty cubits its breadth, and thirty cubits its height;
a indo dost thou make for the ark, and unto a cubit thou dost restrain it from above; and the opening of the ark thou dost put in its side, — loer, second, and third [stories] dost thou make it.
’And I, lo, I am bringing in the deluge of aters on the earth to destroy all flesh, in hich [is] a living spirit, from under the heavens; all that [is] in the earth doth expire.
’And I have established My covenant ith thee, and thou hast come in unto the ark, thou, and thy sons, and thy ife, and thy son’s ives ith thee;
and of all that liveth, of all flesh, to of every [sort] thou dost bring in unto the ark, to keep alive ith thee; male and female are they.
Of the fol after its kind, and of the cattle after their kind, of every creeping thing of the ground after its kind, to of every [sort] they come in unto thee, to keep alive.
’And thou, take to thyself of all food that is eaten; and thou hast gathered unto thyself, and it hath been to thee and to them for food.’
And Noah doth according to all that God hath commanded him; so hath he done.
And Jehovah saith to Noah, ’Come in, thou and all thy house, unto the ark, for thee I have seen righteous before Me in this generation;
of all the clean beasts thou dost take to thee seven pairs, a male and its female; and of the beasts hich are not clean to, a male and its female;
also, of fol of the heavens seven pairs, a male and a female, to keep alive seed on the face of all the earth;
for after other seven days I am sending rain on the earth forty days and forty nights, and have iped aay all the substance that I have made from off the face of the ground.’
And Noah doth according to all that Jehovah hath commanded him:
and Noah [is] a son of six hundred years, and the deluge of aters hath been upon the earth.
And Noah goeth in, and his sons, and his ife, and his sons’ ives ith him, unto the ark, from the presence of the aters of the deluge;
of the clean beasts and of the beasts that [are] not clean, and of the fol, and of every thing that is creeping upon the ground,
to by to they have come in unto Noah, unto the ark, a male and a female, as God hath commanded Noah.
And it cometh to pass, after the seventh of the days, that aters of the deluge have been on the earth.

In the six hundredth year of the life of Noah, in the second month, in the seventeenth day of the month, in this day have been broken up all fountains of the great deep, and the net-ork of the heavens hath been opened,
and the shoer is on the earth forty days and forty nights.
In this self-same day ent in Noah, and Shem, and Ham, and Japheth, sons of Noah, and Noah’s ife and the three ives of his sons ith them, unto the ark;

they, and every living creature after its kind, and every beast after its kind, and every creeping thing that is creeping on the earth after its kind, and every fol after its kind, every bird — every ing.
And they come in unto Noah, unto the ark, to by to of all the flesh in hich [is] a living spirit;
and they that are coming in, male and female of all flesh, have come in as God hath commanded him, and Jehovah doth close [it] for him.
And the deluge is forty days on the earth, and the aters multiply, and lift up the ark, and it is raised up from off the earth;
and the aters are mighty, and multiply exceedingly upon the earth; and the ark goeth on the face of the aters.
And the aters have been very very mighty on the earth, and covered are all the high mountains hich [are] under the hole heavens;
fifteen cubits upards have the aters become mighty, and the mountains are covered;
and expire doth all flesh that is moving on the earth, among fol, and among cattle, and among beasts, and among all the teeming things hich are teeming on the earth, and all mankind;
all in hose nostrils [is] breath of a living spirit — of all that [is] in the dry land — have died.

And iped aay is all the substance that is on the face of the ground, from man unto beast, unto creeping thing, and unto fol of the heavens; yea, they are iped aay from the earth, and only Noah is left, and those ho [are] ith him in the ark;
and the aters are mighty on the earth a hundred and fifty days.
And God remembereth Noah, and every living thing, and all the cattle hich [are] ith him in the ark, and God causeth a ind to pass over the earth, and the aters subside,
and closed are the fountains of the deep and the net-ork of the heavens, and restrained is the shoer from the heavens.
And turn back do the aters from off the earth, going on and returning; and the aters are lacking at the end of a hundred and fifty days.
And the ark resteth, in the seventh month, in the seventeenth day of the month, on mountains of Ararat;
and the aters have been going and becoming lacking till the tenth month; in the tenth [month], on the first of the month, appeared the heads of the mountains.
And it cometh to pass, at the end of forty days, that Noah openeth the indo of the ark hich he made,
and he sendeth forth the raven, and it goeth out, going out and turning back till the drying of the aters from off the earth.
And he sendeth forth the dove from him to see hether the aters have been lightened from off the face of the ground,

and the dove hath not found rest for the sole of her foot, and she turneth back unto him, unto the ark, for aters [are] on the face of all the earth, and he putteth out his hand, and taketh her, and bringeth her in unto him, unto the ark.
And he stayeth yet other seven days, and addeth to send forth the dove from the ark;
and the dove cometh in unto him at even-time, and lo, an olive leaf torn off in her mouth; and Noah knoeth that the aters have been lightened from off the earth.
And he stayeth yet other seven days, and sendeth forth the dove, and it added not to turn back unto him any more.

And it cometh to pass in the six hundredth and first year, in the first [month], in the first of the month, the aters have been dried from off the earth; and Noah turneth aside the covering of the ark, and looketh, and lo, the face of the ground hath been dried.
And in the second month, in the seven and tentieth day of the month, the earth hath become dry.
And God speaketh unto Noah, saying, ’Go out from the ark, thou, and thy ife, and thy sons, and thy sons’ ives ith thee;
every living thing that [is] ith thee, of all flesh, among fol, and among cattle, and among every creeping thing hich is creeping on the earth, bring out ith thee;
and they have teemed in the earth, and been fruitful, and have multiplied on the earth.’
And Noah goeth out, and his sons, and his ife, and his sons’ ives ith him;
every beast, every creeping thing, and every fol; every creeping thing on the earth, after their families, have gone out from the ark.
And Noah buildeth an altar to Jehovah, and taketh of every clean beast, and of every clean fol, and causeth burnt-offerings to ascend on the altar;

and Jehovah smelleth the seet fragrance, and Jehovah saith unto His heart, ’I continue not to disesteem any more the ground because of man, though the imagination of the heart of man [is] evil from his youth; and I continue not to smite any more all living, as I have done;
during all days of the earth, seed-time and harvest, and cold and heat, and summer and inter, and day and night, do not cease.’
And God blesseth Noah, and his sons, and saith to them, ’Be fruitful, and multiply, and fill the earth;
and your fear and your dread is on every beast of the earth, and on every fol of the heavens, on all that creepeth on the ground, and on all fishes of the sea — into your hand they have been given.
Every creeping thing that is alive, to you it is for food; as the green herb I have given to you the hole;
only flesh in its life — its blood — ye do not eat.
’And only your blood for your lives do I require; from the hand of every living thing I require it, and from the hand of man, from the hand of every man’s brother I require the life of man;
hoso sheddeth man’s blood, by man is his blood shed: for in the image of God hath He made man.
And ye, be fruitful and multiply, teem in the earth, and multiply in it.’
And God speaketh unto Noah, and unto his sons ith him, saying,
’And I, lo, I am establishing My covenant ith you, and ith your seed after you,
and ith every living creature hich [is] ith you, among fol, among cattle, and among every beast of the earth ith you, from all ho are going out of the ark — to every beast of the earth.
And I have established My covenant ith you, and all flesh is not any more cut off by aters of a deluge, and there is not any more a deluge to destroy the earth.’
And God saith, ’This is a token of the covenant hich I am giving beteen Me and you, and every living creature that [is] ith you, to generations age-during;
My bo I have given in the cloud, and it hath been for a token of a covenant beteen Me and the earth;
and it hath come to pass (in My sending a cloud over the earth) that the bo hath been seen in the cloud,
and I have remembered My covenant hich is beteen Me and you, and every living creature among all flesh, and the aters become no more a deluge to destroy all flesh;
and the bo hath been in the cloud, and I have seen it — to remember the covenant age-during beteen God and every living creature among all flesh hich [is] on the earth.’
And God saith unto Noah, ’This [is] a token of the covenant hich I have established beteen Me and all flesh that [is] upon the earth.’
And the sons of Noah ho are going out of the ark are Shem, and Ham, and Japheth; and Ham is father of Canaan.
These three [are] sons of Noah, and from these hath all the earth been overspread.
And Noah remaineth a man of the ground, and planteth a vineyard,
and drinketh of the ine, and is drunken, and uncovereth himself in the midst of the tent.
And Ham, father of Canaan, seeth the nakedness of his father, and declareth to his to brethren ithout.

And Shem taketh — Japheth also — the garment, and they place on the shoulder of them both, and go backard, and cover the nakedness of their father; and their faces [are] backard, and their father’s nakedness they have not seen.
And Noah aaketh from his ine, and knoeth that hich his young son hath done to him,
and saith: ’Cursed [is] Canaan, Servant of servants he is to his brethren.’
And he saith: ’Blessed of Jehovah my God [is] Shem, And Canaan is servant to him.
God doth give beauty to Japheth, And he delleth in tents of Shem, And Canaan is servant to him.’
And Noah liveth after the deluge three hundred and fifty years;
and all the days of Noah are nine hundred and fifty years, and he dieth.
And these [are] births of the sons of Noah, Shem, Ham, and Japheth; and born to them are sons after the deluge.
’Sons of Japheth [are] Gomer, and Magog, and Madai, and Javan, and Tubal, and Meshech, and Tiras.
And sons of Gomer [are] Ashkenaz, and Riphath, and Togarmah.
And sons of Javan [are] Elishah, and Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim.
By these have the isles of the nations been parted in their lands, each by his tongue, by their families, in their nations.
And sons of Ham [are] Cush, and Mitzraim, and Phut, and Canaan.
And sons of Cush [are] Seba, and Havilah, and Sabtah, and Raamah, and Sabtechah; and sons of Raamah [are] Sheba and Dedan.
And Cush hath begotten Nimrod;
he hath begun to be a hero in the land; he hath been a hero in hunting before Jehovah; therefore it is said, ’As Nimrod the hero [in] hunting before Jehovah.’
And the first part of his kingdom is Babel, and Erech, and Accad, and Calneh, in the land of Shinar;
from that land he hath gone out to Asshur, and buildeth Nineveh, even the broad places of the city, and Calah,
and Resen, beteen Nineveh and Calah; it [is] the great city.
And Mitzraim hath begotten the Ludim, and the Anamim, and the Lehabim, and the Naphtuhim,
and the Pathrusim, and the Casluhim, (hence have come out Philistim,) and the Caphtorim.
And Canaan hath begotten Sidon his first-born, and Heth,
and the Jebusite, and the Amorite, and the Girgashite,
and the Hivite, and the Arkite, and the Sinite,
and the Arvadite, and the Zemarite, and the Hamathite; and afterards have the families of the Canaanite been scattered.
And the border of the Canaanite is from Sidon, [in] thy coming toards Gerar, unto Gaza; [in] thy coming toards Sodom, and Gomorrah, and Admah, and Zeboim, unto Lasha.
These [are] sons of Ham, by their families, by their tongues, in their lands, in their nations.
As to Shem, father of all sons of Eber, brother of Japheth the elder, he hath also begotten:
Sons of Shem [are] Elam, and Asshur, and Arphaxad, and Lud, and Aram.
And sons of Aram [are] Uz, and Hul, and Gether, and Mash.
And Arphaxad hath begotten Salah, and Salah hath begotten Eber.
And to Eber have to sons been born; the name of the one [is] Peleg (for in his days hath the earth been divided,) and his brother’s name [is] Joktan.
And Joktan hath begotten Almodad, and Sheleph, and Hazarmaveth, and Jerah,
and Hadoram, and Uzal, and Diklah,
and Obal, and Abimael, and Sheba,
and Ophir, and Havilah, and Jobab; all these [are] sons of Joktan;
and their delling is from Mesha, [in] thy coming toards Sephar, a mount of the east.
These [are] sons of Shem, by their families, by their tongues, in their lands, by their nations.
These [are] families of the sons of Noah, by their births, in their nations, and by these have the nations been parted in the earth after the deluge.
And the hole earth is of one pronunciation, and of the same ords,
and it cometh to pass, in their journeying from the east, that they find a valley in the land of Shinar, and dell there;
and they say each one to his neighbour, ’Give help, let us make bricks, and burn [them] thoroughly:’ and the brick is to them for stone, and the bitumen hath been to them for mortar.
And they say, ’Give help, let us build for ourselves a city and toer, and its head in the heavens, and make for ourselves a name, lest e be scattered over the face of all the earth.’
And Jehovah cometh don to see the city and the toer hich the sons of men have builded;
and Jehovah saith, ’Lo, the people [is] one, and one pronunciation [is] to them all, and this it hath dreamed of doing; and no, nothing is restrained from them of that hich they have purposed to do.
Give help, let us go don, and mingle there their pronunciation, so that a man doth not understand the pronunciation of his companion.’
And Jehovah doth scatter them from thence over the face of all the earth, and they cease to build the city;
therefore hath [one] called its name Babel, for there hath Jehovah mingled the pronunciation of all the earth, and from thence hath Jehovah scattered them over the face of all the earth.
These [are] births of Shem: Shem [is] a son of an hundred years, and begetteth Arphaxad to years after the deluge.
And Shem liveth after his begetting Arphaxad five hundred years, and begetteth sons and daughters.
And Arphaxad hath lived five and thirty years, and begetteth Salah.
And Arphaxad liveth after his begetting Salah four hundred and three years, and begetteth sons and daughters.
And Salah hath lived thirty years, and begetteth Eber.
And Salah liveth after his begetting Eber four hundred and three years, and begetteth sons and daughters.
And Eber liveth four and thirty years, and begetteth Peleg.
And Eber liveth after his begetting Peleg four hundred and thirty years, and begetteth sons and daughters.
And Peleg liveth thirty years, and begetteth Reu.
And Peleg liveth after his begetting Reu to hundred and nine years, and begetteth sons and daughters.
And Reu liveth to and thirty years, and begetteth Serug.
And Reu liveth after his begetting Serug to hundred and seven years, and begetteth sons and daughters.
And Serug liveth thirty years, and begetteth Nahor.
And Serug liveth after his begetting Nahor to hundred years, and begetteth sons and daughters.
And Nahor liveth nine and tenty years, and begetteth Terah.
And Nahor liveth after his begetting Terah an hundred and nineteen years, and begetteth sons and daughters.
And Terah liveth seventy years, and begetteth Abram, Nahor, and Haran.
And these [are] births of Terah: Terah hath begotten Abram, Nahor, and Haran; and Haran hath begotten Lot;
and Haran dieth in the presence of Terah his father, in the land of his birth, in Ur of the Chaldees.
And Abram and Nahor take to themselves ives; the name of Abram’s ife [is] Sarai, and the name of Nahor’s ife [is] Milcah, daughter of Haran, father of Milcah, and father of Iscah.
And Sarai is barren — she hath no child.

And Terah taketh Abram his son, and Lot, son of Haran, his son’s son, and Sarai his daughter-in-la, ife of Abram his son, and they go out ith them from Ur of the Chaldees, to go toards the land of Canaan; and they come unto Charan, and dell there.
And the days of Terah are to hundred and five years, and Terah dieth in Charan.
And Jehovah saith unto Abram, ’Go for thyself, from thy land, and from thy kindred, and from the house of thy father, unto the land hich I she thee.
And I make thee become a great nation, and bless thee, and make thy name great; and be thou a blessing.
And I bless those blessing thee, and him ho is disesteeming thee I curse, and blessed in thee have been all families of the ground.’
And Abram goeth on, as Jehovah hath spoken unto him, and Lot goeth ith him, and Abram [is] a son of five and seventy years in his going out from Charan.

And Abram taketh Sarai his ife, and Lot his brother’s son, and all their substance that they have gained, and the persons that they have obtained in Charan; and they go out to go toards the land of Canaan; and they come in to the land of Canaan.
And Abram passeth over into the land, unto the place Shechem, unto the oak of Moreh; and the Canaanite [is] then in the land.
And Jehovah appeareth unto Abram, and saith, ’To thy seed I give this land;’ and he buildeth there an altar to Jehovah, ho hath appeared unto him.

And he removeth from thence toards a mountain at the east of Beth-El, and stretcheth out the tent (Beth-El at the est, and Hai at the east), and he buildeth there an altar to Jehovah, and preacheth in the name of Jehovah.
And Abram journeyeth, going on and journeying toards the south.
And there is a famine in the land, and Abram goeth don toards Egypt to sojourn there, for the famine [is] grievous in the land;
and it cometh to pass as he hath dran near to enter Egypt, that he saith unto Sarai his ife, ’Lo, I pray thee, I have knon that thou [art] a oman of beautiful appearance;
and it hath come to pass that the Egyptians see thee, and they have said, ’This [is] his ife,’ and they have slain me, and thee they keep alive:
say, I pray thee, thou [art] my sister, so that it is ell ith me because of thee, and my soul hath lived for thy sake.’
And it cometh to pass, at the entering of Abram into Egypt, that the Egyptians see the oman that she [is] exceeding fair;
and princes of Pharaoh see her, and praise her unto Pharaoh, and the oman is taken [to] Pharaoh’s house;
and to Abram he hath done good because of her, and he hath sheep and oxen, and he-asses, and men-servants, and handmaids, and she-asses, and camels.
And Jehovah plagueth Pharaoh and his house — great plagues — for the matter of Sarai, Abram’s ife.
And Pharaoh calleth for Abram, and saith, ’What [is] this thou hast done to me? hy hast thou not declared to me that she [is] thy ife?
Why hast thou said, She [is] my sister, and I take her to myself for a ife? and no, lo, thy ife, take and go.’
And Pharaoh chargeth men concerning him, and they send him aay, and his ife, an all that he hath.
And Abram goeth up from Egypt (he and his ife, and all that he hath, and Lot ith him) toards the south;
and Abram [is] exceedingly ealthy in cattle, in silver, and in gold.
And he goeth on his journeyings from the south, even unto Bethel, unto the place here his tent had been at the commencement, beteen Bethel and Hai —
unto the place of the altar hich he made there at the first, and there doth Abram preach in the name of Jehovah.
And also to Lot, ho is going ith Abram, there hath been sheep and oxen and tents;
and the land hath not suffered them to dell together, for their substance hath been much, and they have not been able to dell together;
and there is a strife beteen those feeding Abram’s cattle and those feeding Lot’s cattle; and the Canaanite and the Perizzite [are] then delling in the land.
And Abram saith unto Lot, ’Let there not, I pray thee, be strife beteen me and thee, and beteen my shepherds and thy shepherds, for e [are] men — brethren.
Is not all the land before thee? be parted, I pray thee, from me; if to the left, then I to the right; and if to the right, then I to the left.’

And Lot lifteth up his eyes, and seeth the hole circuit of the Jordan that it [is] all a atered country (before Jehovah’s destroying Sodom and Gomorrah, as Jehovah’s garden, as the land of Egypt,) in thy coming toard Zoar,
and Lot chooseth for himself the hole circuit of the Jordan; and Lot journeyeth from the east, and they are parted — a man from his companion;
Abram hath delt in the land of Canaan, and Lot hath delt in the cities of the circuit, and tenteth unto Sodom;
and the men of Sodom [are] evil, and sinners before Jehovah exceedingly.
And Jehovah said unto Abram, after Lot’s being parted from him, ’Lift up, I pray thee, thine eyes, and look from the place here thou [art], northard, and southard, and eastard, and estard;
for the hole of the land hich thou are seeing, to thee I give it, and to thy seed — to the age.
And I have set thy seed as dust of the earth, so that, if one is able to number the dust of the earth, even thy seed is numbered;
rise, go up and don through the land, to its length, and to its breadth, for to thee I give it.’
And Abram tenteth, and cometh, and delleth among the oaks of Mamre, hich [are] in Hebron, and buildeth there an altar to Jehovah.
And it cometh to pass in the days of Amraphel king of Shinar, Arioch king of Ellasar, Chedorlaomer king of Elam, and Tidal king of Goyim,
they have made ar ith Bera king of Sodom, and ith Birsha king of Gomorrah, Shinab king of Admah, and Shemeber king of Zeboim, and the king of Bela, hich [is] Zoar.
All these have been joined together unto the valley of Siddim, hich [is] the Salt Sea;
telve years they served Chedorlaomer, and the thirteenth year they rebelled.
And in the fourteenth year came Chedorlaomer, and the kings ho [are] ith him, and they smite the Rephaim in Ashteroth Karnaim, and the Zuzim in Ham, and the Emim in Shaveh Kiriathaim,
and the Horites in their mount Seir, unto El-Paran, hich [is] by the ilderness;
and they turn back and come in unto En-Mishpat, hich [is] Kadesh, and smite the hole field of the Amalekite, and also the Amorite ho is delling in Hazezon-Tamar.

And the king of Sodom goeth out, and the king of Gomorrah, and the king of Admah, and the king of Zeboim, and the king of Bela, hich [is] Zoar; and they set the battle in array ith them in the valley of Siddim,
ith Chedorlaomer king of Elam, and Tidal king of Goyim, and Amraphel king of Shinar, and Arioch king of Ellasar; four kings ith the five.
And the valley of Siddim [is] full of bitumen-pits; and the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah flee, and fall there, and those left have fled to the mountain.
And they take the hole substance of Sodom and Gomorrah, and the hole of their food, and go aay;
and they take Lot, Abram’s brother’s son (seeing he is delling in Sodom), and his substance, and go aay.
And one ho is escaping cometh and declareth to Abram the Hebre, and he is delling among the oaks of Mamre the Amorite, brother of Eshcol, and brother of Aner, and they [are] Abram’s allies.
And Abram heareth that his brother hath been taken captive, and he draeth out his trained domestics, three hundred and eighteen, and pursueth unto Dan.
And he divideth himself against them by night, he and his servants, and smiteth them, and pursueth them unto Hobah, hich [is] at the left of Damascus;
and he bringeth back the hole of the substance, and also Lot his brother and his substance hath he brought back, and also the omen and the people.
And the king of Sodom goeth out to meet him (after his turning back from the smiting of Chedorlaomer, and of the kings ho [are] ith him), unto the valley of Shaveh, hich [is] the king’s valley.
And Melchizedek king of Salem hath brought out bread and ine, and he [is] priest of God Most High;
and he blesseth him, and saith, ’Blessed [is] Abram to God Most High, possessing heaven and earth;
and blessed [is] God Most High, ho hath delivered thine adversaries into thy hand;’ and he giveth to him a tenth of all.
And the king of Sodom saith unto Abram, ’Give to me the persons, and the substance take to thyself,’
and Abram saith unto the king of Sodom, ’I have lifted up my hand unto Jehovah, God Most High, possessing heaven and earth —
from a thread even unto a shoe-latchet I take not of anything hich thou hast, that thou say not, I — I have made Abram rich;
save only that hich the young men have eaten, and the portion of the men ho have gone ith me — Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre — they take their portion.’
After these things hath the ord of Jehovah been unto Abram in a vision, saying, ’Fear not, Abram, I [am] a shield to thee, thy reard [is] exceeding great.’
And Abram saith, ’Lord Jehovah, hat dost Thou give to me, and I am going childless? and an acquired son in my house is Demmesek Eliezer.’
And Abram saith, ’Lo, to me Thou hast not given seed, and lo, a domestic doth heir me.’
And lo, the ord of Jehovah [is] unto him, saying, ’This [one] doth not heir thee; but he ho cometh out from thy boels, he doth heir thee;’
and He bringeth him out ithout, and saith, ’Look attentively, I pray thee, toards the heavens, and count the stars, if thou art able to count them;’ and He saith to him, ’Thus is thy seed.’
And he hath believed in Jehovah, and He reckoneth it to him — righteousness.
And He saith unto him, ’I [am] Jehovah ho brought thee out from Ur of the Chaldees, to give to thee this land to possess it;’
and he saith, ’Lord Jehovah, hereby do I kno that I possess it?’
And He saith unto him, ’Take for Me a heifer of three years, and a she-goat of three years, and a ram of three years, and a turtle-dove, and a young bird;’
and he taketh to him all these, and separateth them in the midst, and putteth each piece over against its fello, but the bird he hath not divided;
and the ravenous birds come don upon the carcases, and Abram causeth them to turn back.
And the sun is about to go in, and deep sleep hath fallen upon Abram, and lo, a terror of great darkness is falling upon him;
and He saith to Abram, ’knoing — kno that thy seed is a sojourner in a land not theirs, and they have served them, and they have afflicted them four hundred years,
and the nation also hom they serve I judge, and after this they go out ith great substance;
and thou — thou comest in unto thy fathers in peace; thou art buried in a good old age;
and the fourth generation doth turn back hither, for the iniquity of the Amorite is not yet complete.’
And it cometh to pass — the sun hath gone in, and thick darkness hath been — and lo, a furnace of smoke, and a lamp of fire, hich hath passed over beteen those pieces.
In that day hath Jehovah made ith Abram a covenant, saying, ’To thy seed I have given this land, from the river of Egypt unto the great river, the river Phrat,
ith the Kenite, and the Kenizzite, and the Kadmonite,
and the Hittite, and the Perizzite, and the Rephaim,
and the Amorite, and the Canaanite, and the Girgashite, and the Jebusite.’
And Sarai, Abram’s ife, hath not borne to him, and she hath an handmaid, an Egyptian, and her name [is] Hagar;

and Sarai saith unto Abram, ’Lo, I pray thee, Jehovah hath restrained me from bearing, go in, I pray thee, unto my handmaid; perhaps I am built up from her;’ and Abram hearkeneth to the voice of Sarai.
And Sarai, Abram’s ife, taketh Hagar the Egyptian, her handmaid, at the end of the tenth year of Abram’s delling in the land of Canaan, and giveth her to Abram her husband, to him for a ife,
and he goeth in unto Hagar, and she conceiveth, and she seeth that she hath conceived, and her mistress is lightly esteemed in her eyes.

And Sarai saith unto Abram, ’My violence [is] for thee; I — I have given mine handmaid into thy bosom, and she seeth that she hath conceived, and I am lightly esteemed in her eyes; Jehovah doth judge beteen me and thee.’
And Abram saith unto Sarai, ’Lo, thine handmaid [is] in thine hand, do to her that hich is good in thine eyes;’ and Sarai afflicted her, and she fleeth from her presence.
And a messenger of Jehovah findeth her by the fountain of ater in the ilderness, by the fountain in the ay [to] Shur,
and he saith, ’Hagar, Sarai’s handmaid, hence hast thou come, and hither dost thou go?’ and she saith, ’From the presence of Sarai, my mistress, I am fleeing.’
And the messenger of Jehovah saith to her, ’Turn back unto thy mistress, and humble thyself under her hands;’
and the messenger of Jehovah saith to her, ’Multiplying I multiply thy seed, and it is not numbered from multitude;’
and the messenger of Jehovah saith to her, ’Behold thou [art] conceiving, and bearing a son, and hast called his name Ishmael, for Jehovah hath hearkened unto thine affliction;
and he is a ild-ass man, his hand against every one, and every one’s hand against him — and before the face of all his brethren he delleth.’
And she calleth the name of Jehovah ho is speaking unto her, ’Thou [art], O God, my beholder;’ for she said, ’Even here have I looked behind my beholder?’
therefore hath one called the ell, ’The ell of the Living One, my beholder;’ lo, beteen Kadesh and Bered.
And Hagar beareth to Abram a son; and Abram calleth the name of his son, hom Hagar hath borne, Ishmael;
and Abram [is] a son of eighty and six years in Hagar’s bearing Ishmael to Abram.
And Abram is a son of ninety and nine years, and Jehovah appeareth unto Abram, and saith unto him, ’I [am] God Almighty, alk habitually before Me, and be thou perfect;
and I give My covenant beteen Me and thee, and multiply thee very exceedingly.’
And Abram falleth upon his face, and God speaketh ith him, saying,
’I — lo, My covenant [is] ith thee, and thou hast become father of a multitude of nations;
and thy name is no more called Abram, but thy name hath been Abraham, for father of a multitude of nations have I made thee;
and I have made thee exceeding fruitful, and made thee become nations, and kings go out from thee.
’And I have established My covenant beteen Me and thee, and thy seed after thee, to their generations, for a covenant age-during, to become God to thee, and to thy seed after thee;
and I have given to thee, and to thy seed after thee, the land of thy sojournings, the hole land of Canaan, for a possession age-during, and I have become their God.’
And God saith unto Abraham, ’And thou dost keep My covenant, thou and thy seed after thee, to their generations;
this [is] My covenant hich ye keep beteen Me and you, and thy seed after thee: Every male of you [is] to be circumcised;
and ye have circumcised the flesh of your foreskin, and it hath become a token of a covenant beteen Me and you.
’And a son of eight days is circumcised by you; every male to your generations, born in the house, or bought ith money from any son of a stranger, ho is not of thy seed;
he is certainly circumcised ho [is] born in thine house, or bought ith thy money; and My covenant hath become in your flesh a covenant age-during;
and an uncircumcised one, a male, the flesh of hose foreskin is not circumcised, even that person hath been cut off from his people; My covenant he hath broken.’
And God saith unto Abraham, ’Sarai thy ife — thou dost not call her name Sarai, for Sarah [is] her name;
and I have blessed her, and have also given to thee a son from her; and I have blessed her, and she hath become nations — kings of peoples are from her.’
And Abraham falleth upon his face, and laugheth, and saith in his heart, ’To the son of an hundred years is one born? or doth Sarah — daughter of ninety years — bear?’
And Abraham saith unto God, ’O that Ishmael may live before Thee;’
and God saith, ’Sarah thy ife is certainly bearing a son to thee, and thou hast called his name Isaac, and I have established My covenant ith him, for a covenant age-during, to his seed after him.
As to Ishmael, I have heard thee; lo, I have blessed him, and made him fruitful, and multiplied him, very exceedingly; telve princes doth he beget, and I have made him become a great nation;
and My covenant I establish ith Isaac, hom Sarah doth bear to thee at this appointed time in the next year;’
and He finisheth speaking ith him, and God goeth up from Abraham.

And Abraham taketh Ishmael his son, and all those born in his house, and all those bought ith his money — every male among the men of Abraham’s house — and circumciseth the flesh of their foreskin, in this self-same day, as God hath spoken ith him.
And Abraham [is] a son of ninety and nine years in the flesh of his foreskin being circumcised;
and Ishmael his son [is] a son of thirteen years in the flesh of his foreskin being circumcised;
in this self-same day hath Abraham been circumcised, and Ishmael his son;
and all the men of his house — born in the house, and bought ith money from the son of a stranger — have been circumcised ith him.
And Jehovah appeareth unto him among the oaks of Mamre, and he is sitting at the opening of the tent, about the heat of the day;
and he lifteth up his eyes and looketh, and lo, three men standing by him, and he seeth, and runneth to meet them from the opening of the tent, and boeth himself toards the earth,
And he saith, ’My Lord, if, I pray thee, I have found grace in thine eyes, do not, I pray thee, pass on from thy servant;
let, I pray thee, a little ater be accepted, and ash your feet, and recline under the tree;
and I bring a piece of bread, and support ye your heart; afterards pass on, for therefore have ye passed over unto your servant;’ and they say, ’So mayest thou do as thou has spoken.’
And Abraham hasteth toards the tent, unto Sarah, and saith, ’Hasten three measures of flour-meal, knead, and make cakes;’
and Abraham ran unto the herd, and taketh a son of the herd, tender and good, and giveth unto the young man, and he hasteth to prepare it;
and he taketh butter and milk, and the son of the herd hich he hath prepared, and setteth before them; and he is standing by them under the tree, and they do eat.
And they say unto him, ’Where [is] Sarah thy ife?’ and he saith, ’Lo — in the tent;’
and he saith, ’returning I return unto thee, about the time of life, and lo, to Sarah thy ife a son.’
And Sarah is hearkening at the opening of the tent, hich is behind him;
and Abraham and Sarah [are] aged, entering into days — the ay of omen hath ceased to be to Sarah;
and Sarah laugheth in her heart, saying, ’After I have axed old I have had pleasure! — my lord also [is] old!’

And Jehovah saith unto Abraham, ’Why [is] this? Sarah hath laughed, saying, Is it true really — I bear — and I am aged? Is any thing too onderful for Jehovah? at the appointed time I return unto thee, about the time of life, and Sarah hath a son.’
And Sarah denieth, saying, ’I did not laugh;’ for she hath been afraid; and He saith, ’Nay, but thou didst laugh.’
And the men rise from thence, and look on the face of Sodom, and Abraham is going ith them to send them aay;
and Jehovah said, ’Am I concealing from Abraham that hich I am doing,
and Abraham certainly becometh a nation great and mighty, and blessed in him have been all nations of the earth?

for I have knon him, that he commandeth his children, and his house after him (and they have kept the ay of Jehovah), to do righteousness and judgment, that Jehovah may bring on Abraham that hich He hath spoken concerning him.’
And Jehovah saith, ’The cry of Sodom and Gomorrah — because great; and their sin — because exceeding grievous:
I go don no, and see hether according to its cry hich is coming unto Me they have done completely — and if not — I kno;’
and the men turn from thence, and go toards Sodom; and Abraham is yet standing before Jehovah.
And Abraham draeth nigh and saith, ’Dost Thou also consume righteous ith icked?
peradventure there are fifty righteous in the midst of the city; dost Thou also consume, and not bear ith the place for the sake of the fifty — the righteous ho [are] in its midst?

Far be it from Thee to do according to this thing, to put to death the righteous ith the icked; that it hath been — as the righteous so the icked — far be it from Thee; doth the Judge of all the earth not do justice?’
And Jehovah saith, ’If I find in Sodom fifty righteous in the midst of the city, then have I borne ith all the place for their sake.’
And Abraham ansereth and saith, ’Lo, I pray thee, I have illed to speak unto the Lord, and I — dust and ashes;
peradventure there are lacking five of the fifty righteous — dost Thou destroy for five the hole of the city?’ and He saith, ’I destroy [it] not, if I find there forty and five.’
And he addeth again to speak unto Him and saith, ’Peradventure there are found there forty?’ and He saith, ’I do [it] not, because of the forty.’
And he saith, ’Let it not be, I Pray thee, displeasing to the Lord, and I speak: peradventure there are found there thirty?’ and He saith, ’I do [it] not, if I find there thirty.’
And he saith, ’Lo, I pray thee, I have illed to speak unto the Lord: peradventure there are found there tenty?’ and He saith, ’I do not destroy [it], because of the tenty.’
And he saith, ’Let it not be, I pray Thee, displeasing to the Lord, and I speak only this time: peradventure there are found there ten?’ and He saith, ’I do not destroy [it], because of the ten.’
And Jehovah goeth on, hen He hath finished speaking unto Abraham, and Abraham hath turned back to his place.
And to of the messengers come toards Sodom at even, and Lot is sitting at the gate of Sodom, and Lot seeth, and riseth to meet them, and boeth himself — face to the earth,

and he saith, ’Lo, I pray you, my lords, turn aside, I pray you, unto the house of your servant, and lodge, and ash your feet — then ye have risen early and gone on your ay;’ and they say, ’Nay, but in the broad place e do lodge.’
And he presseth on them greatly, and they turn aside unto him, and come in unto his house; and he maketh for them a banquet, and hath baked unleavened things; and they do eat.
Before they lie don, the men of the city — men of Sodom — have come round about against the house, from young even unto aged, all the people from the extremity;
and they call unto Lot and say to him, ’Where [are] the men ho have come in unto thee to-night? bring them out unto us, and e kno them.’
And Lot goeth out unto them, to the opening, and the door hath shut behind him,
and saith, ’Do not, I pray you, my brethren, do evil;

lo, I pray you, I have to daughters, ho have not knon any one; let me, I pray you, bring them out unto you, and do to them as [is] good in your eyes; only to these men do not anything, for therefore have they come in ithin the shado of my roof.’

And they say, ’Come nigh hither;’ they say also, ’This one hath come in to sojourn, and he certainly judgeth! no, e do evil to thee more than [to] them;’ and they press against the man, against Lot greatly, and come nigh to break the door.
And the men put forth their hand, and bring in Lot unto them, into the house, and have shut the door;
and the men ho [are] at the opening of the house they have smitten ith blindness, from small even unto great, and they eary themselves to find the opening.
And the men say unto Lot, ’Whom hast thou here still? son-in-la, thy sons also, and thy daughters, and all hom thou hast in the city, bring out from this place;
for e are destroying this place, for their cry hath been great [before] the face of Jehovah, and Jehovah doth send us to destroy it.’

And Lot goeth out, and speaketh unto his sons-in-la, those taking his daughters, and saith, ’Rise, go out from this place, for Jehovah is destroying the city;’ and he is as [one] mocking in the eyes of his sons-in-la.
And hen the dan hath ascended, then the messengers press upon Lot, saying, ’Rise, take thy ife, and thy to daughters ho are found present, lest thou be consumed in the iniquity of the city.’

And he lingereth, and the men lay hold on his hand, and on the hand of his ife, and on the hand of his to daughters, through the mercy of Jehovah unto him, and they bring him out, and cause him to rest ithout the city.

And it cometh to pass hen he hath brought them out ithout, that he saith, ’Escape for thy life; look not expectingly behind thee, nor stand thou in all the circuit; to the mountain escape, lest thou be consumed.’
And Lot saith unto them, ’Not [so], I pray thee, my lord;

lo, I pray thee, thy servant hath found grace in thine eyes, and thou dost make great thy kindness hich thou hast done ith me by saving my life, and I am unable to escape to the mountain, lest the evil cleave [to] me, and I have died;
lo, I pray thee, this city [is] near to flee thither, and it [is] little; let me escape, I pray thee, thither, (is it not little?) and my soul doth live.’
And he saith unto him, ’Lo, I have accepted thy face also for this thing, ithout overthroing the city [for] hich thou hast spoken;
haste, escape thither, for I am not able to do anything till thine entering thither;’ therefore hath he calleth the name of the city Zoar.
The sun hath gone out on the earth, and Lot hath entered into Zoar,
and Jehovah hath rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah brimstone and fire from Jehovah, from the heavens;
and He overthroeth these cities, and all the circuit, and all the inhabitants of the cities, and that hich is shooting up from the ground.
And his ife looketh expectingly from behind him, and she is — a pillar of salt!
And Abraham riseth early in the morning, unto the place here he hath stood [before] the face of Jehovah;
and he looketh on the face of Sodom and Gomorrah, and on all the face of the land of the circuit, and seeth, and lo, the smoke of the land ent up as smoke of the furnace.
And it cometh to pass, in God’s destroying the cities of the circuit, that God remembereth Abraham, and sendeth Lot out of the midst of the overthro in the overthroing of the cities in hich Lot delt.
And Lot goeth up out of Zoar, and delleth in the mountain, and his to daughters ith him, for he hath been afraid of delling in Zoar, and he delleth in a cave, he and his to daughters.
And the first-born saith unto the younger, ’Our father [is] old, and a man there is not in the earth to come in unto us, as [is] the ay of all the earth;
come, e cause our father to drink ine, and lie ith him, and preserve from our father — a seed.’
And they cause their father to drink ine on that night; and the first-born goeth in, and lieth ith her father, and he hath not knon in her lying don, or in her rising up.

And it cometh to pass, on the morro, that the first-born saith unto the younger, ’Lo, I have lain yesterday-night ith my father: e cause him to drink ine also to-night, and go thou in, lie ith him, and e preserve from our father — a seed.’
And they cause their father to drink ine on that night also, and the younger riseth and lieth ith him, and he hath not knon in her lying don, or in her rising up.
And the to daughters of Lot conceive from their father,
and the first-born beareth a son, and calleth his name Moab; he [is] father of Moab unto this day;
as to the younger, she also hath born a son, and calleth his name Ben-Ammi: he [is] father of the Beni-Ammon unto this day.
And Abraham journeyeth from thence toard the land of the south, and delleth beteen Kadesh and Shur, and sojourneth in Gerar;
and Abraham saith concerning Sarah his ife, ’She is my sister;’ and Abimelech king of Gerar sendeth and taketh Sarah.
And God cometh in unto Abimelech in a dream of the night, and saith to him, ’Lo, thou [art] a dead man, because of the oman hom thou hast taken — and she married to a husband.’
And Abimelech hath not dran near unto her, and he saith, ’Lord, also a righteous nation dost thou slay?
hath not he himself said to me, She [is] my sister! and she, even she herself, said, He [is] my brother; in the integrity of my heart, and in the innocency of my hands, I have done this.’

And God saith unto him in the dream, ’Yea, I — I have knon that in the integrity of thy heart thou hast done this, and I ithhold thee, even I, from sinning against Me, therefore I have not suffered thee to come against her;
and no send back the man’s ife, for he [is] inspired, and he doth pray for thee, and live thou; and if thou do not send back, kno that dying thou dost die, thou, and all that thou hast.’
And Abimelech riseth early in the morning, and calleth for all his servants, and speaketh all these ords in their ears; and the men fear exceedingly;

and Abimelech calleth for Abraham, and saith to him, ’What hast thou done to us? and hat have I sinned against thee, that thou hast brought upon me, and upon my kingdom, a great sin? orks hich are not done thou hast done ith me.’
Abimelech also saith unto Abraham, ’What hast thou seen that thou hast done this thing?’
And Abraham saith, ’Because I said, ’Surely the fear of God is not in this place, and they have slain me for the sake of my ife;
and also, truly she is my sister, daughter of my father, only not daughter of my mother, and she becometh my ife;

and it cometh to pass, hen God hath caused me to ander from my father’s house, that I say to her, This [is] thy kindness hich thou dost ith me: at every place hither e come, say of me, He [is] my brother.’
And Abimelech taketh sheep and oxen, and servants and handmaids, and giveth to Abraham, and sendeth back to him Sarah his ife;
and Abimelech saith, ’Lo, my land [is] before thee, here it is good in thine eyes, dell;’
and to Sarah he hath said, ’Lo, I have given a thousand silverlings to thy brother; lo, it is to thee a covering of eyes, to all ho are ith thee;’ and by all this she is reasoned ith.
And Abraham prayeth unto God, and God healeth Abimelech and his ife, and his handmaids, and they bear:
for Jehovah restraining had restrained every omb of the house of Abimelech, because of Sarah, Abraham’s ife.
And Jehovah hath looked after Sarah as He hath said, and Jehovah doth to Sarah as He hath spoken;
and Sarah conceiveth, and beareth a son to Abraham, to his old age, at the appointed time that God hath spoken of ith him;
and Abraham calleth the name of his son ho is born to him, hom Sarah hath born to him — Isaac;
and Abraham circumciseth Isaac his son, [being] a son of eight days, as God hath commanded him.
And Abraham [is] a son of a hundred years in Isaac his son being born to him,
and Sarah saith, ’God hath made laughter for me; every one ho is hearing laugheth for me.’
She saith also, ’Who hath said to Abraham, Sarah hath suckled sons, that I have born a son for his old age?’
And the lad groeth, and is eaned, and Abraham maketh a great banquet in the day of Isaac’s being eaned;
and Sarah seeth the son of Hagar the Egyptian, hom she hath borne to Abraham, mocking,
and she saith to Abraham, ’Cast out this handmaid and her son; for the son of this handmaid hath no possession ith my son — ith Isaac.’
And the thing is very rong in the eyes of Abraham, for his son’s sake;

and God saith unto Abraham, ’Let it not be rong in thine eyes because of the youth, and because of thy handmaid: all that Sarah saith unto thee — hearken to her voice, for in Isaac is a seed called to thee.
As to the son of the handmaid also, for a nation I set him, because he [is] thy seed.’

And Abraham riseth early in the morning, and taketh bread, and a bottle of ater, and giveth unto Hagar (placing [it] on her shoulder), also the lad, and sendeth her out; and she goeth on, and goeth astray in the ilderness of Beer-Sheba;
and the ater is consumed from the bottle, and she placeth the lad under one of the shrubs.

And she goeth and sitteth by herself over-against, afar off, about a bo-shot, for she said, ’Let me not look on the death of the lad;’ and she sitteth over-against, and lifteth up her voice, and eepeth.

And God heareth the voice of the youth; and the messenger of God calleth unto Hagar from the heavens, and saith to her, ’What to thee, Hagar? fear not; for God hath hearkened unto the voice of the youth here he [is];
rise, lift up the youth, and lay hold on him ith thy hand, for for a great nation I set him.’
And God openeth her eyes, and she seeth a ell of ater, and she goeth and filleth the bottle [ith] ater, and causeth the youth to drink;
and God is ith the youth, and he groeth, and delleth in the ilderness, and is an archer;
and he delleth in the ilderness of Paran, and his mother taketh for him a ife from the land of Egypt.
And it cometh to pass at that time that Abimelech speaketh — Phichol also, head of his host — unto Abraham, saying, ’God [is] ith thee in all that thou art doing;

and no, sear to me by God here: thou dost not lie to me, or to my continuator, or to my successor; according to the kindness hich I have done ith thee thou dost ith me, and ith the land in hich thou hast sojourned.’
And Abraham saith, ’I — I do sear.’
And Abraham reasoned ith Abimelech concerning the matter of a ell of ater hich Abimelech’s servants have taken violently aay,
and Abimelech saith, ’I have not knon ho hath done this thing, and even thou didst not declare to me, and I also, I have not heard save to-day.’
And Abraham taketh sheep and oxen, and giveth to Abimelech, and they make, both of them, a covenant;
and Abraham setteth seven Lambs of the flock by themselves.
And Abimelech saith unto Abraham, ’What [are] they — these seven lambs hich thou hast set by themselves?’
And he saith, ’For — the seven lambs thou dost accept from my hand, so that it becometh a itness for me that I have digged this ell;’
therefore hath he called that place ’Beer-Sheba,’ for there have both of them sorn.
And they make a covenant in Beer-Sheba, and Abimelech riseth — Phichol also, head of his host — and they turn back unto the land of the Philistines;
and [Abraham] planteth a tamarisk in Beer-Sheba, and preacheth there in the name of Jehovah, God age-during;
and Abraham sojourneth in the land of the Philistines many days.
And it cometh to pass after these things that God hath tried Abraham, and saith unto him, ’Abraham;’ and he saith, ’Here [am] I.’

And He saith, ’Take, I pray thee, thy son, thine only one, hom thou hast loved, even Isaac, and go for thyself unto the land of Moriah, and cause him to ascend there for a burnt-offering on one of the mountains of hich I speak unto thee.’

And Abraham riseth early in the morning, and saddleth his ass, and taketh to of his young men ith him, and Isaac his son, and he cleaveth the ood of the burnt-offering, and riseth and goeth unto the place of hich God hath spoken to him.
On the third day — Abraham lifteth up his eyes, and seeth the place from afar;
and Abraham saith unto his young men, ’Remain by yourselves here ith the ass, and I and the youth go yonder and orship, and turn back unto you.’
And Abraham taketh the ood of the burnt-offering, and placeth on Isaac his son, and he taketh in his hand the fire, and the knife; and they go on both of them together.
And Isaac speaketh unto Abraham his father, and saith, ’My father,’ and he saith, ’Here [am] I, my son.’ And he saith, ’Lo, the fire and the ood, and here the lamb for a burnt-offering?’
and Abraham saith, ’God doth provide for Himself the lamb for a burnt-offering, my son;’ and they go on both of them together.
And they come in unto the place of hich God hath spoken to him, and there Abraham buildeth the altar, and arrangeth the ood, and bindeth Isaac his son, and placeth him upon the altar above the ood;
and Abraham putteth forth his hand, and taketh the knife — to slaughter his son.
And the messenger of Jehovah calleth unto him from the heavens, and saith, ’Abraham, Abraham;’ and he saith, ’Here [am] I;’
and He saith, ’Put not forth thine hand unto the youth, nor do anything to him, for no I have knon that thou art fearing God, and hast not ithheld thy son, thine only one, from Me.’

And Abraham lifteth up his eyes, and looketh, and lo, a ram behind, seized in a thicket by its horns; and Abraham goeth, and taketh the ram, and causeth it to ascend for a burnt-offering instead of his son;
and Abraham calleth the name of that place ’Jehovah-Jireh,’ because it is said this day in the mount, ’Jehovah doth provide.’
And the messenger of Jehovah calleth unto Abraham a second time from the heavens,
and saith, ’By Myself I have sorn — the affirmation of Jehovah — that because thou hast done this thing, and hast not ithheld thy son, thine only one —
that blessing I bless thee, and multiplying I multiply thy seed as stars of the heavens, and as sand hich [is] on the sea-shore; and thy seed doth possess the gate of his enemies;
and blessed themselves in thy seed have all nations of the earth, because that thou hast hearkened to My voice.’
And Abraham turneth back unto his young men, and they rise and go together unto Beer-Sheba; and Abraham delleth in Beer-Sheba.
And it cometh to pass after these things that it is declared to Abraham, saying, ’Lo, Milcah hath borne, even she, sons to Nahor thy brother:
Huz his first-born, and Buz his brother; and Kemuel father of Aram,
and Chesed, and Hazo, and Pildash, and Jidlaph, and Bethuel;
and Bethuel hath begotten Rebekah;’ these eight hath Milcah borne to Nahor, Abraham’s brother;
and his concubine, hose name [is] Reumah, she also hath borne Tebah, and Gaham, and Tahash, and Maachah.
And the life of Sarah is a hundred and tenty and seven years — years of the life of Sarah;
and Sarah dieth in Kirjath-Arba, hich [is] Hebron, in the land of Caanan, and Abraham goeth in to mourn for Sarah, and to beail her.
And Abraham riseth up from the presence of his dead, and speaketh unto the sons of Heth, saying,
’A sojourner and a settler I [am] ith you; give to me a possession of a burying-place ith you, and I bury my dead from before me.’
And the sons of Heth anser Abraham, saying to him,
’Hear us, my lord; a prince of God [art] thou in our midst; in the choice of our burying-places bury thy dead: none of us his burying-place doth ithhold from thee, from burying thy dead.’
And Abraham riseth and boeth himself to the people of the land, to the sons of Heth,
and he speaketh ith them, saying, ’If it is your desire to bury my dead from before me, hear me, and meet for me ith Ephron, son of Zoar;
and he giveth to me the cave of Machpelah, hich he hath, hich [is] in the extremity of his field; for full money doth he give it to me, in your midst, for a possession of a burying-place.’
And Ephron is sitting in the midst of the sons of Heth, and Ephron the Hittite ansereth Abraham in the ears of the sons of Heth, of all those entering the gate of his city, saying,
’Nay, my lord, hear me: the field I have given to thee, and the cave that [is] in it, to thee I have given it; before the eyes of the sons of my people I have given it to thee — bury thy dead.’
And Abraham boeth himself before the people of the land,
and speaketh unto Ephron in the ears of the people of the land, saying, ’Only — if thou ouldest hear me — I have given the money of the field — accept from me, and I bury my dead there.’
And Ephron ansereth Abraham, saying to him,
’My lord, hear me: the land — four hundred shekels of silver; beteen me and thee, hat [is] it? — thy dead bury.’
And Abraham hearkeneth unto Ephron, and Abraham eigheth to Ephron the silver hich he hath spoken of in the ears of the sons of Heth, four hundred silver shekels, passing ith the merchant.

And established are the field of Ephron, hich [is] in Machpelah, hich [is] before Mamre, the field and the cave hich [is] in it, and all the trees hich [are] in the field, hich [are] in all its border round about,
to Abraham by purchase, before the eyes of the sons of Heth, among all entering the gate of his city.
And after this hath Abraham buried Sarah his ife at the cave of the field of Machpelah before Mamre (hich [is] Hebron), in the land of Canaan;
and established are the field, and the cave hich [is] in it, to Abraham for a possession of a burying-place, from the sons of Heth.
And Abraham [is] old, he hath entered into days, and Jehovah hath blessed Abraham in all [things];
and Abraham saith unto his servant, the eldest of his house, ho is ruling over all that he hath, ’Put, I pray thee, thy hand under my thigh,
and I cause thee to sear by Jehovah, God of the heavens, and God of the earth, that thou dost not take a ife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanite, in the midst of hom I am delling;
but unto my land and unto my kindred dost thou go, and hast taken a ife for my son, for Isaac.’
And the servant saith unto him, ’It may be the oman is not illing to come after me unto this land; do I at all cause thy son to turn back unto the land from hence thou camest out?’
And Abraham saith unto him, ’Take heed to thyself, lest thou cause my son to turn back thither;

Jehovah, God of the heavens, ho hath taken me from the house of my father, and from the land of my birth, and ho hath spoken to me, and ho hath sorn to me, saying, To thy seed I give this land, He doth send His messenger before thee, and thou hast taken a ife for my son from thence;
and if the oman be not illing to come after thee, then thou hast been acquitted from this mine oath: only my son thou dost not cause to turn back thither.’
And the servant putteth his hand under the thigh of Abraham his lord, and seareth to him concerning this matter.
And the servant taketh ten camels of the camels of his lord and goeth, also of all the goods of his lord in his hand, and he riseth, and goeth unto Aram-Naharaim, unto the city of Nahor;
and he causeth the camels to kneel at the outside of the city, at the ell of ater, at even-time, at the time of the coming out of the omen ho dra ater.
And he saith, ’Jehovah, God of my lord Abraham, cause to meet, I pray Thee, before me this day — (and do kindness ith my lord Abraham;
lo, I am standing by the fountain of ater, and daughters of the men of the city are coming out to dra ater;

and it hath been, the young person unto hom I say, Incline, I pray thee, thy pitcher, and I drink, and she hath said, Drink, and I ater also thy camels) — her Thou hast decided for Thy servant, for Isaac; and by it I kno that Thou hast done kindness ith my lord.’
And it cometh to pass, before he hath finished speaking, that lo, Rebekah (ho as born to Bethuel, son of Milcah, ife of Nahor, brother of Abraham) is coming out, and her pitcher on her shoulder,
and the young person [is] of very good appearance, a virgin, and a man hath not knon her; and she goeth don to the fountain, and filleth her pitcher, and cometh up.
And the servant runneth to meet her, and saith, ’Let me sallo, I pray thee, a little ater from thy pitcher;’
and she saith, ’Drink, my lord;’ and she hasteth, and letteth don her pitcher upon her hand, and giveth him drink.
And she finisheth giving him drink, and saith, ’Also for thy camels I dra till they have finished drinking;’
and she hasteth, and emptieth her pitcher into the drinking-trough, and runneth again unto the ell to dra, and draeth for all his camels.
And the man, ondering at her, remaineth silent, to kno hether Jehovah hath made his ay prosperous or not.
And it cometh to pass hen the camels have finished drinking, that the man taketh a golden ring (hose eight [is] a bekah), and to bracelets for her hands (hose eight [is] ten [bekahs] of gold),
and saith, ’Whose daughter [art] thou? declare to me, I pray thee, is the house of thy father a place for us to lodge in?’
And she saith unto him, ’I [am] daughter of Bethuel, son of Milcah, hom she hath borne to Nahor.’
She saith also unto him, ’Both stra and provender [are] abundant ith us, also a place to lodge in.’
And the man boeth, and doth obeisance to Jehovah,
and saith, ’Blessed [is] Jehovah, God of my lord Abraham, ho hath not left off His kindness and His truth ith my lord; — I [being] in the ay, Jehovah hath led me to the house of my lord’s brethren.’
And the young person runneth, and declareth to the house of her mother according to these ords.
And Rebekah hath a brother, and his name [is] Laban, and Laban runneth unto the man ho [is] ithout, unto the fountain;

yea, it cometh to pass, hen he seeth the ring, and the bracelets on the hands of his sister, and hen he heareth the ords of Rebekah his sister, saying, ’Thus hath the man spoken unto me,’ that he cometh in unto the man, and lo, he is standing by the camels by the fountain.
