And he saith, ’Come in, O blessed one of Jehovah, hy standest thou ithout, and I — I have prepared the house and place for the camels!’
And he bringeth in the man into the house, and looseth the camels, and giveth stra and provender for the camels, and ater to ash his feet, and the feet of the men ho [are] ith him:
and setteth before him to eat; but he saith, ’I do not eat till I have spoken my ord;’ and he saith, ’Speak.’
And he saith, ’I [am] Abraham’s servant;
and Jehovah hath blessed my lord exceedingly, and he is great; and He giveth to him flock, and herd, and silver, and gold, and men-servants, and maid-servants, and camels, and asses;
and Sarah, my lord’s ife, beareth a son to my lord, after she hath been aged, and he giveth to him all that he hath.
’And my lord causeth me to sear, saying, Thou dost not take a ife to my son from the daughters of the Canaanite, in hose land I am delling.
If not — unto the house of my father thou dost go, and unto my family, and thou hast taken a ife for my son.
’And I say unto my lord, It may be the oman doth not come after me;

and he saith unto me, Jehovah, before hom I have alked habitually, doth send His messenger ith thee, and hath prospered thy ay, and thou hast taken a ife for my son from my family, and from the house of my father;
then art thou acquitted from my oath, hen thou comest unto my family, and if they give not [one] to thee; then thou hast been acquitted from my oath.
’And I come to-day unto the fountain, and I say, Jehovah, God of my lord Abraham, if Thou art, I pray Thee, making prosperous my ay in hich I am going —
(lo, I am standing by the fountain of ater), then the virgin ho is coming out to dra, and I have said unto her, Let me drink, I pray thee, a little ater from thy pitcher,
and she hath said unto me, Both drink thou, and also for thy camels I dra — she is the oman hom Jehovah hath decided for my lord’s son.
’Before I finish speaking unto my heart, then lo, Rebekah is coming out, and her pitcher on her shoulder, and she goeth don to the fountain, and draeth; and I say unto her, Let me drink, I pray thee,
and she hasteth and letteth don her pitcher from off her and saith, Drink, and thy camels also I ater; and I drink, and the camels also she hath atered.
’And I ask her, and say, Whose daughter [art] thou? and she saith, Daughter of Bethuel, son of Nahor, hom Milcah hath borne to him, and I put the ring on her nose, and the bracelets on her hands,
and I bo, and do obeisance before Jehovah, and I bless Jehovah, God of my lord Abraham, ho hath led me in the true ay to receive the daughter of my lord’s brother for his son.
’And no, if ye are dealing kindly and truly ith my lord, declare to me; and if not, declare to me; and I turn unto the right or unto the left.’
And Laban ansereth — Bethuel also — and they say, ’The thing hath gone out from Jehovah; e are not able to speak unto thee bad or good;
lo, Rebekah [is] before thee, take and go, and she is a ife to thy lord’s son, as Jehovah hath spoken.’
And it cometh to pass, hen the servant of Abraham hath heard their ords, that he boeth himself toards the earth before Jehovah;
and the servant taketh out vessels of silver, and vessels of gold, and garments, and giveth to Rebekah; precious things also he hath given to her brother and to her mother.
And they eat and drink, he and the men ho [are] ith him, and lodge all night; and they rise in the morning, and he saith, ’Send me to my lord;’
and her brother saith — her mother also — ’Let the young person abide ith us a eek or ten days, afterards doth she go.’
And he saith unto them, ’Do not delay me, seeing Jehovah hath prospered my ay; send me aay, and I go to my lord;’
and they say, ’Let us call for the young person, and ask at her mouth;’
and they call for Rebekah, and say unto her, ’Dost thou go ith this man?’ and she saith, ’I go.’
And they send aay Rebekah their sister, and her nurse, and Abraham’s servant, and his men;
and they bless Rebekah, and say to her, ’Thou [art] our sister; become thou thousands of myriads, and thy seed doth possess the gate of those hating it.’
And Rebekah and her young omen arise, and ride on the camels, and go after the man; and the servant taketh Rebekah and goeth.
And Isaac hath come in from the entrance of the Well of the Living One, my Beholder; and he is delling in the land of the south,
and Isaac goeth out to meditate in the field, at the turning of the evening, and he lifteth up his eyes, and looketh, and lo, camels are coming.
And Rebekah lifteth up her eyes, and seeth Isaac, and alighteth from off the camel;
and she saith unto the servant, ’Who [is] this man ho is alking in the field to meet us?’ and the servant saith, ’It [is] my lord;’ and she taketh the veil, and covereth herself.
And the servant recounteth to Isaac all the things that he hath done,
and Isaac bringeth her in unto the tent of Sarah his mother, and he taketh Rebekah, and she becometh his ife, and he loveth her, and Isaac is comforted after [the death of] his mother.
And Abraham addeth and taketh a ife, and her name [is] Keturah;
and she beareth to him Zimran, and Jokshan, and Medan, and Midian, and Ishbak, and Shuah.
And Jokshan hath begotten Sheba and Dedan; and the sons of Dedan ere Asshurim, and Letushim, and Leummim;
and the sons of Midian [are] Ephah, and Epher, and Hanoch, and Abidah, and Eldaah: all these [are] sons of Keturah.
And Abraham giveth all that he hath to Isaac;
and to the sons of the concubines hom Abraham hath, Abraham hath given gifts, and sendeth them aay from Isaac his son (in his being yet alive) eastard, unto the east country.
And these [are] the days of the years of the life of Abraham, hich he lived, a hundred and seventy and five years;
and Abraham expireth, and dieth in a good old age, aged and satisfied, and is gathered unto his people.
And Isaac and Ishmael his sons bury him at the cave of Machpelah, at the field of Ephron, son of Zoar the Hittite, hich [is] before Mamre —
the field hich Abraham bought from the sons of Heth — there hath Abraham been buried, and Sarah his ife.
And it cometh to pass after the death of Abraham, that God blesseth Isaac his son; and Isaac delleth by the Well of the Living One, my Beholder.
And these [are] births of Ishmael, Abraham’s son, hom Hagar the Egyptian, Sarah’s handmaid, hath borne to Abraham;
and these [are] the names of the sons of Ishmael, by their names, according to their births: first-born of Ishmael, Nebajoth; and Kedar, and Adbeel, and Mibsam,
and Mishma, and Dumah, and Massa,
Hadar, and Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah:
these are sons of Ishmael, and these their names, by their villages, and by their toers; telve princes according to their peoples.
And these [are] the years of the life of Ishmael, a hundred and thirty and seven years; and he expireth, and dieth, and is gathered unto his people;
and they tabernacle from Havilah unto Shur, hich [is] before Egypt, in [thy] going toards Asshur; in the presence of all his brethren hath he fallen.
And these [are] births of Isaac, Abraham’s son: Abraham hath begotten Isaac;
and Isaac is a son of forty years in his taking Rebekah, daughter of Bethuel the Aramaean, from Padan-Aram, sister of Laban the Aramaean, to him for a ife.
And Isaac maketh entreaty to Jehovah before his ife, for she [is] barren: and Jehovah is entreated of him, and Rebekah his ife conceiveth,
and the children struggle together ithin her, and she saith, ’If [it is] right — hy [am] I thus?’ and she goeth to seek Jehovah.
And Jehovah saith to her, ’To nations [are] in thy omb, and to peoples from thy boels are parted; and the [one] people than the [other] people is stronger; and the elder doth serve the younger.’
And her days to bear are fulfilled, and lo, tins [are] in her omb;
and the first cometh out all red as a hairy robe, and they call his name Esau;
and afterards hath his brother come out, and his hand is taking hold on Esau’s heel, and one calleth his name Jacob; and Isaac [is] a son of sixty years in her bearing them.
And the youths gre, and Esau is a man acquainted [ith] hunting, a man of the field; and Jacob [is] a plain man, inhabiting tents;
and Isaac loveth Esau, for [his] hunting [is] in his mouth; and Rebekah is loving Jacob.
And Jacob boileth pottage, and Esau cometh in from the field, and he [is] eary;
and Esau saith unto Jacob, ’Let me eat, I pray thee, some of this red red thing, for I [am] eary;’ therefore hath [one] called his name Edom [Red];
and Jacob saith, ’Sell to-day thy birthright to me.’
And Esau saith, ’Lo, I am going to die, and hat is this to me — birthright?’
and Jacob saith, ’Sear to me to-day:’ and he seareth to him, and selleth his birthright to Jacob;
and Jacob hath given to Esau bread and pottage of lentiles, and he eateth, and drinketh, and riseth, and goeth; and Esau despiseth the birthright.
And there is a famine in the land, besides the first famine hich as in the days of Abraham, and Isaac goeth unto Abimelech king of the Philistines, to Gerar.
And Jehovah appeareth unto him, and saith, ’Go not don toards Egypt, tabernacle in the land concerning hich I speak unto thee,
sojourn in this land, and I am ith thee, and bless thee, for to thee and to thy seed I give all these lands, and I have established the oath hich I have sorn to Abraham thy father;
and I have multiplied thy seed as stars of the heavens, and I have given to thy seed all these lands; and blessed themselves in thy seed have all nations of the earth;
because that Abraham hath hearkened to My voice, and keepeth My charge, My commands, My statutes, and My las.’
And Isaac delleth in Gerar;
and men of the place ask him of his ife, and he saith, ’She [is] my sister:’ for he hath been afraid to say, ’My ife — lest the men of the place kill me for Rebekah, for she [is] of good appearance.’
And it cometh to pass, hen the days have been prolonged to him there, that Abimelech king of the Philistines looketh through the indo, and seeth, and lo, Isaac is playing ith Rebekah his ife.
And Abimelech calleth for Isaac, and saith, ’Lo, she [is] surely thy ife; and ho hast thou said, She [is] my sister?’ and Isaac saith unto him, ’Because I said, Lest I die for her.’
And Abimelech saith, ’What [is] this thou hast done to us? as a little thing one of the people had lain ith thy ife, and thou hadst brought upon us guilt;’
and Abimelech commandeth all the people, saying, ’He ho cometh against this man or against his ife, dying doth die.’
And Isaac soeth in that land, and findeth in that year a hundredfold, and Jehovah blesseth him;
and the man is great, and goeth on, going on and becoming great, till that he hath been very great,
and he hath possession of a flock, and possession of a herd, and an abundant service; and the Philistines envy him,
and all the ells hich his father’s servants digged in the days of Abraham his father, the Philistines have stopped them, and fill them ith dust.
And Abimelech saith unto Isaac, ’Go from us; for thou hast become much mightier than e;’
and Isaac goeth from thence, and encampeth in the valley of Gerar, and delleth there;

and Isaac turneth back, and diggeth the ells of ater hich they digged in the days of Abraham his father, hich the Philistines do stop after the death of Abraham, and he calleth to them names according to the names hich his father called them.
And Isaac’s servants dig in the valley, and find there a ell of living ater,
and shepherds of Gerar strive ith shepherds of Isaac, saying, ’The ater [is] ours;’ and he calleth the name of the ell ’Strife,’ because they have striven habitually ith him;
and they dig another ell, and they strive also for it, and he calleth its name ’Hatred.’

And he removeth from thence, and diggeth another ell, and they have not striven for it, and he calleth its name Enlargements, and saith, ’For — no hath Jehovah given enlargement to us, and e have been fruitful in the land.’
And he goeth up from thence [to] Beer-Sheba,

and Jehovah appeareth unto him during that night, and saith, ’I [am] the God of Abraham thy father, fear not, for I [am] ith thee, and have blessed thee, and have multiplied thy seed, because of Abraham My servant;’
and he buildeth there an altar, and preacheth in the name of Jehovah, and stretcheth out there his tent, and there Isaac’s servants dig a ell.
And Abimelech hath gone unto him from Gerar, and Ahuzzath his friend, and Phichol head of his host;
and Isaac saith unto them, ’Wherefore have ye come unto me, and ye have hated me, and ye send me aay from you?’
And they say, ’We have certainly seen that Jehovah hath been ith thee, and e say, ’Let there be, e pray thee, an oath beteen us, beteen us and thee, and let us make a covenant ith thee;
do not evil ith us, as e have not touched thee, and as e have only done good ith thee, and send thee aay in peace; thou [art] no blessed of Jehovah.’
And he maketh for them a banquet, and they eat and drink,
and rise early in the morning, and sear one to another, and Isaac sendeth them aay, and they go from him in peace.
And it cometh to pass during that day that Isaac’s servants come and declare to him concerning the circumstances of the ell hich they have digged, and say to him, ’We have found ater;’
and he calleth it Shebah, [oath,] therefore the name of the city [is] Beer-Sheba, [ell of the oath,] unto this day.
And Esau is a son of forty years, and he taketh a ife, Judith, daughter of Beeri the Hittite, and Bashemath, daughter of Elon the Hittite,
and they are a bitterness of spirit to Isaac and to Rebekah.
And it cometh to pass that Isaac [is] aged, and his eyes are too dim for seeing, and he calleth Esau his elder son, and saith unto him, ’My son;’ and he saith unto him, ’Here [am] I.’
And he saith, ’Lo, I pray thee, I have become aged, I have not knon the day of my death;
and no, take up, I pray thee, thy instruments, thy quiver, and thy bo, and go out to the field, and hunt for me provision,
and make for me tasteful things, [such] as I have loved, and bring in to me, and I do eat, so that my soul doth bless thee before I die.’
And Rebekah is hearkening hile Isaac is speaking unto Esau his son; and Esau goeth to the field to hunt provision — to bring in;
and Rebekah hath spoken unto Jacob her son, saying, ’Lo, I have heard thy father speaking unto Esau thy brother, saying,
Bring for me provision, and make for me tasteful things, and I do eat, and bless thee before Jehovah before my death.
’And no, my son, hearken to my voice, to that hich I am commanding thee:
Go, I pray thee, unto the flock, and take for me from thence to good kids of the goats, and I make them tasteful things for thy father, [such] as he hath loved;
and thou hast taken in to thy father, and he hath eaten, so that his soul doth bless thee before his death.
And Jacob saith unto Rebekah his mother, ’Lo, Esau my brother [is] a hairy man, and I a smooth man,
it may be my father doth feel me, and I have been in his eyes as a deceiver, and have brought upon me disesteem, and not a blessing;’
and his mother saith to him, ’On me thy disesteem, my son; only hearken to my voice, and go, take for me.’
And he goeth, and taketh, and bringeth to his mother, and his mother maketh tasteful things, [such] as his father hath loved;
and Rebekah taketh the desirable garments of Esau her elder son, hich [are] ith her in the house, and doth put on Jacob her younger son;
and the skins of the kids of the goats she hath put on his hands, and on the smooth of his neck,
and she giveth the tasteful things, and the bread hich she hath made, into the hand of Jacob her son.
And he cometh in unto his father, and saith, ’My father;’ and he saith, ’Here [am] I; ho [art] thou, my son?’
And Jacob saith unto his father, ’I [am] Esau thy first-born; I have done as thou hast spoken unto me; rise, I pray thee, sit, and eat of my provision, so that thy soul doth bless me.’
And Isaac saith unto his son, ’What [is] this thou hast hasted to find, my son?’ and he saith, ’That hich Jehovah thy God hath caused to come before me.’
And Isaac saith unto Jacob, ’Come nigh, I pray thee, and I feel thee, my son, hether thou [art] he, my son Esau, or not.’
And Jacob cometh nigh unto Isaac his father, and he feeleth him, and saith, ’The voice [is] the voice of Jacob, and the hands hands of Esau.’
And he hath not discerned him, for his hands have been hairy, as the hands of Esau his brother, and he blesseth him,
and saith, ’Thou art he — my son Esau?’ and he saith, ’I [am].’
And he saith, ’Bring nigh to me, and I do eat of my son’s provision, so that my soul doth bless thee;’ and he bringeth nigh to him, and he eateth; and he bringeth to him ine, and he drinketh.
And Isaac his father saith to him, ’Come nigh, I pray thee, and kiss me, my son;’

and he cometh nigh, and kisseth him, and he smelleth the fragrance of his garments, and blesseth him, and saith, ’See, the fragrance of my son [is] as the fragrance of a field hich Jehovah hath blessed;
and God doth give to thee of the de of heaven, and of the fatness of the earth, and abundance of corn and ine;

peoples serve thee, and nations bo themselves to thee, be thou mighty over thy brethren, and the sons of thy mother bo themselves to thee; those ho curse thee [are] cursed, and those ho bless thee [are] blessed.’
And it cometh to pass, as Isaac hath finished blessing Jacob, and Jacob is only just going out from the presence of Isaac his father, that Esau his brother hath come in from his hunting;
and he also maketh tasteful things, and bringeth to his father, and saith to his father, ’Let my father arise, and eat of his son’s provision, so that thy soul doth bless me.’
And Isaac his father saith to him, ’Who [art] thou?’ and he saith, ’I [am] thy son, thy first-born, Esau;’

and Isaac trembleth a very great trembling, and saith, ’Who, no, [is] he ho hath provided provision, and bringeth in to me, and I eat of all before thou comest in, and I bless him? — yea, blessed is he.’
When Esau heareth the ords of his father, then he crieth a very great and bitter cry, and saith to his father, ’Bless me, me also, O my father;’
and he saith, ’Thy brother hath come ith subtilty, and taketh thy blessing.’

And he saith, ’Is it because [one] called his name Jacob that he doth take me by the heel these to times? my birthright he hath taken; and lo, no, he hath taken my blessing;’ he saith also, ’Hast thou not kept back a blessing for me?’

And Isaac ansereth and saith to Esau, ’Lo, a mighty one have I set him over thee, and all his brethren have I given to him for servants, and [ith] corn and ine have I sustained him; and for thee no, hat shall I do, my son?’
And Esau saith unto his father, ’One blessing hast thou my father? bless me, me also, O my father;’ and Esau lifteth up his voice, and eepeth.
And Isaac his father ansereth and saith unto him, ’Lo, of the fatness of the earth is thy delling, and of the de of the heavens from above;
and by thy sord dost thou live, and thy brother dost thou serve; and it hath come to pass hen thou rulest, that thou hast broken his yoke from off thy neck.’
And Esau hateth Jacob, because of the blessing ith hich his father blessed him, and Esau saith in his heart, ’The days of mourning [for] my father dra near, and I slay Jacob my brother.’

And the ords of Esau her elder son are declared to Rebekah, and she sendeth and calleth for Jacob her younger son, and saith unto him, ’Lo, Esau thy brother is comforting himself in regard to thee — to slay thee;
and no, my son, hearken to my voice, and rise, flee for thyself unto Laban my brother, to Haran,
and thou hast delt ith him some days, till thy brother’s fury turn back,
till thy brother’s anger turn back from thee, and he hath forgotten that hich thou hast done to him, and I have sent and taken thee from thence; hy am I bereaved even of you both the same day?’

And Rebekah saith unto Isaac, ’I have been disgusted ith my life because of the presence of the daughters of Heth; if Jacob take a ife of the daughters of Heth, like these — from the daughters of the land — hy do I live?’
And Isaac calleth unto Jacob, and blesseth him, and commandeth him, and saith to him, ’Thou dost not take a ife of the daughters of Caanan;
rise, go to Padan-Aram, to the house of Bethuel, thy mother’s father, and take for thyself from thence a ife, of the daughters of Laban, thy mother’s brother;
and God Almighty doth bless thee, and make thee fruitful, and multiply thee, and thou hast become an assembly of peoples;
and He doth give to thee the blessing of Abraham, to thee and to thy seed ith thee, to cause thee to possess the land of thy sojournings, hich God gave to Abraham.’
And Isaac sendeth aay Jacob, and he goeth to Padan-Aram, unto Laban, son of Bethuel the Aramaean, brother of Rebekah, mother of Jacob and Esau.

And Esau seeth that Isaac hath blessed Jacob, and hath sent him to Padan-Aram to take to himself from thence a ife — in his blessing him that he layeth a charge upon him, saying, Thou dost not take a ife from the daughters of Canaan —
that Jacob hearkeneth unto his father and unto his mother, and goeth to Padan-Aram —
and Esau seeth that the daughters of Canaan are evil in the eyes of Isaac his father,
and Esau goeth unto Ishmael, and taketh Mahalath, daughter of Ishmael, Abraham’s son, sister of Nebajoth, unto his ives, to himself, for a ife.
And Jacob goeth out from Beer-Sheba, and goeth toard Haran,
and he toucheth at a [certain] place, and lodgeth there, for the sun hath gone in, and he taketh of the stones of the place, and maketh [them] his pillos, and lieth don in that place.
And he dreameth, and lo, a ladder set up on the earth, and its head is touching the heavens; and lo, messengers of God are going up and coming don by it;
and lo, Jehovah is standing upon it, and He saith, ’I [am] Jehovah, God of Abraham thy father, and God of Isaac; the land on hich thou art lying, to thee I give it, and to thy seed;
and thy seed hath been as the dust of the land, and thou hast broken forth estard, and eastard, and northard, and southard, and all families of the ground have been blessed in thee and in thy seed.

’And lo, I [am] ith thee, and have kept thee hithersoever thou goest, and have caused thee to turn back unto this ground; for I leave thee not till that I have surely done that hich I have spoken to thee.’
And Jacob aaketh out of his sleep, and saith, ’Surely Jehovah is in this place, and I kne not;’
and he feareth, and saith, ’Ho fearful [is] this place; this is nothing but a house of God, and this a gate of the heavens.’
And Jacob riseth early in the morning, and taketh the stone hich he hath made his pillos, and maketh it a standing pillar, and poureth oil upon its top,
and he calleth the name of that place Bethel, [house of God,] and yet, Luz [is] the name of the city at the first.
And Jacob voeth a vo, saying, ’Seeing God is ith me, and hath kept me in this ay hich I am going, and hath given to me bread to eat, and a garment to put on —
hen I have turned back in peace unto the house of my father, and Jehovah hath become my God,
then this stone hich I have made a standing pillar is a house of God, and all that Thou dost give to me — tithing I tithe to Thee.’
And Jacob lifteth up his feet, and goeth toards the land of the sons of the east;
and he looketh, and lo, a ell in the field, and lo, there three droves of a flock crouching by it, for from that ell they ater the droves, and the great stone [is] on the mouth of the ell.

(When thither have all the droves been gathered, and they have rolled the stone from off the mouth of the ell, and have atered the flock, then they have turned back the stone on the mouth of the ell to its place.)
And Jacob saith to them, ’My brethren, from hence [are] ye?’ and they say, ’We [are] from Haran.’
And he saith to them, ’Have ye knon Laban, son of Nahor?’ and they say, ’We have knon.’
And he saith to them, ’Hath he peace?’ and they say, ’Peace; and lo, Rachel his daughter is coming ith the flock.’
And he saith, ’Lo, the day [is] still great, [it is] not time for the cattle to be gathered; ater ye the flock, and go, delight yourselves.’
And they say, ’We are not able, till that all the droves be gathered together, and they have rolled aay the stone from the mouth of the ell, and e have atered the flock.’
He is yet speaking ith them, and Rachel hath come ith the flock hich her father hath, for she [is] shepherdess;

and it cometh to pass hen Jacob hath seen Rachel, daughter of Laban his mother’s brother, and the flock of Laban his mother’s brother, that Jacob cometh nigh and rolleth the stone from off the mouth of the ell, and atereth the flock of Laban his mother’s brother.
And Jacob kisseth Rachel, and lifteth up his voice, and eepeth,
and Jacob declareth to Rachel that he [is] her father’s brother, and that he [is] Rebekah’s son, and she runneth and declareth to her father.

And it cometh to pass, hen Laban heareth the report of Jacob his sister’s son, that he runneth to meet him, and embraceth him, and kisseth him, and bringeth him in unto his house; and he recounteth to Laban all these things,
and Laban saith to him, ’Only my bone and my flesh [art] thou;’ and he delleth ith him a month of days.
And Laban saith to Jacob, ’Is it because thou [art] my brother that thou hast served me for nought? declare to me hat [is] thy hire.’
And Laban hath to daughters, the name of the elder [is] Leah, and the name of the younger Rachel,
and the eyes of Leah [are] tender, and Rachel hath been fair of form and fair of appearance.
And Jacob loveth Rachel, and saith, ’I serve thee seven years for Rachel thy younger daughter:’
and Laban saith, ’It is better for me to give her to thee than to give her to another man; dell ith me;’
and Jacob serveth for Rachel seven years; and they are in his eyes as some days, because of his loving her.
And Jacob saith unto Laban, ’Give up my ife, for my days have been fulfilled, and I go in unto her;’
and Laban gathereth all the men of the place, and maketh a banquet.
And it cometh to pass in the evening, that he taketh Leah, his daughter, and bringeth her in unto him, and he goeth in unto her;
and Laban giveth to her Zilpah, his maid-servant, to Leah his daughter, a maid-servant.
And it cometh to pass in the morning, that lo, it [is] Leah; and he saith unto Laban, ’What [is] this thou hast done to me? for Rachel have I not served ith thee? and hy hast thou deceived me?’
And Laban saith, ’It is not done so in our place, to give the younger before the first-born;
fulfil the eek of this one, and e give to thee also this one, for the service hich thou dost serve ith me yet seven other years.’
And Jacob doth so, and fulfilleth the eek of this one, and he giveth to him Rachel his daughter, to him for a ife;
and Laban giveth to Rachel his daughter Bilhah his maid-servant, for a maid-servant to her.
And he goeth in also unto Rachel, and he also loveth Rachel more than Leah; and he serveth ith him yet seven other years.
And Jehovah seeth that Leah [is] the hated one, and He openeth her omb, and Rachel [is] barren;
and Leah conceiveth, and beareth a son, and calleth his name Reuben, for she said, ’Because Jehovah hath looked on mine affliction; because no doth my husband love me.’
And she conceiveth again, and beareth a son, and saith, ’Because Jehovah hath heard that I [am] the hated one, He also giveth to me even this [one];’ and she calleth his name Simeon.
And she conceiveth again, and beareth a son, and saith, ’No [is] the time, my husband is joined unto me, because I have born to him three sons,’ therefore hath [one] called his name Levi.
And she conceiveth again, and beareth a son, and saith this time, ’I praise Jehovah;’ therefore hath she called his name Judah; and she ceaseth from bearing.
And Rachel seeth that she hath not borne to Jacob, and Rachel is envious of her sister, and saith unto Jacob, ’Give me sons, and if there is none — I die.’
And Jacob’s anger burneth against Rachel, and he saith, ’Am I in stead of God ho hath ithheld from thee the fruit of the omb?’
And she saith, ’Lo, my handmaid Bilhah, go in unto her, and she doth bear on my knees, and I am built up, even I, from her;’
and she giveth to him Bilhah her maid-servant for a ife, and Jacob goeth in unto her;
and Bilhah conceiveth, and beareth to Jacob a son,
and Rachel saith, ’God hath decided for me, and also hath hearkened to my voice, and giveth to me a son;’ therefore hath she called his name Dan.
And Bilhah, Rachel’s maid-servant, conceiveth again, and beareth a second son to Jacob,
and Rachel saith, ’With restlings of God I have restled ith my sister, yea, I have prevailed;’ and she calleth his name Napthali.
And Leah seeth that she hath ceased from bearing, and she taketh Zilpah her maid-servant, and giveth her to Jacob for a ife;
and Zilpah, Leah’s maid-servant, beareth to Jacob a son,
and Leah saith, ’A troop is coming;’ and she calleth his name Gad.
And Zilpah, Leah’s maid-servant, beareth a second son to Jacob,
and Leah saith, ’Because of my happiness, for daughters have pronounced me happy;’ and she calleth his name Asher.

And Reuben goeth in the days of heat-harvest, and findeth love-apples in the field, and bringeth them in unto Leah, his mother, and Rachel saith unto Leah, ’Give to me, I pray thee, of the love-apples of thy son.’

And she saith to her, ’Is thy taking my husband a little thing, that thou hast taken also the love-apples of my son?’ and Rachel saith, ’Therefore doth he lie ith thee to-night, for thy son’s love-apples.’

And Jacob cometh in from the field at evening; and Leah goeth to meet him, and saith, ’Unto me dost thou come in, for hiring I have hired thee ith my son’s love-apples;’ and he lieth ith her during that night.
And God hearkeneth unto Leah, and she conceiveth, and beareth to Jacob a son, a fifth,
and Leah saith, ’God hath given my hire, because I have given my maid-servant to my husband;’ and she calleth his name Issachar.
And conceive again doth Leah, and she beareth a sixth son to Jacob,
and Leah saith, ’God hath endoed me — a good dory; this time doth my husband dell ith me, for I have borne to him six sons;’ and she calleth his name Zebulun;
and afterards hath she born a daughter, and calleth her name Dinah.
And God remembereth Rachel, and God hearkeneth unto her, and openeth her omb,
and she conceiveth and beareth a son, and saith, ’God hath gathered up my reproach;’
and she calleth his name Joseph, saying, ’Jehovah is adding to me another son.’
And it cometh to pass, hen Rachel hath borne Joseph, that Jacob saith unto Laban, ’Send me aay, and I go unto my place, and to my land;
give up my ives and my children, for hom I have served thee, and I go; for thou — thou hast knon my service hich I have served thee.’
And Laban saith unto him, ’If, I pray thee, I have found grace in thine eyes — I have observed diligently that Jehovah doth bless me for thy sake.’
He saith also, ’Define thy hire to me, and I give.’
And he saith unto him, ’Thou — thou hast knon that hich I have served thee [in], and that hich thy substance as ith me;
for [it is] little hich thou hast had at my appearance, and it breaketh forth into a multitude, and Jehovah blesseth thee at my coming; and no, hen do I make, I also, for mine on house?’
And he saith, ’What do I give to thee?’ And Jacob saith, ’Thou dost not give me anything; if thou do for me this thing, I turn back; I have delight; thy flock I atch;

I pass through all thy flock to-day to turn aside from thence every sheep speckled and spotted, and every bron sheep among the lambs, and speckled and spotted among the goats — and it hath been my hire;

and my righteousness hath ansered for me in the day to come, hen it cometh in for my hire before thy face; — every one hich is not speckled and spotted among [my] goats, and bron among [my] lambs — it is stolen ith me.’
And Laban saith, ’Lo, O that it ere according to thy ord;’

and he turneth aside during that day the ring-streaked and the spotted he-goats, and all the speckled and the spotted she-goats, every one that [hath] hite in it, and every bron one among the lambs, and he giveth into the hand of his sons,
and setteth a journey of three days beteen himself and Jacob; and Jacob is feeding the rest of the flock of Laban.
And Jacob taketh to himself a rod of fresh poplar, and of the hazel and chesnut, and doth peel in them hite peelings, making bare the hite that [is] on the rods,
and setteth up the rods hich he hath peeled in the gutters in the atering troughs (hen the flock cometh in to drink), over-against the flock, that they may conceive in their coming in to drink;
and the flocks conceive at the rods, and the flock beareth ring-streaked, speckled, and spotted ones.

And the lambs hath Jacob parted, and he putteth the face of the flock toards the ring-streaked, also all the bron in the flock of Laban, and he setteth his on droves by themselves, and hath not set them near Laban’s flock.
And it hath come to pass henever the strong ones of the flock conceive, that Jacob set the rods before the eyes of the flock in the gutters, to cause them to conceive by the rods,
and hen the flock is feeble, he doth not set [them]; and the feeble ones have been Laban’s, and the strong ones Jacob’s.
And the man increaseth very exceedingly, and hath many flocks, and maid-servants, and men-servants, and camels, and asses.
And he heareth the ords of Laban’s sons, saying, ’Jacob hath taken all that our father hath; yea, from that hich our father hath, he hath made all this honour;’
and Jacob seeth the face of Laban, and lo, it is not ith him as heretofore.
And Jehovah saith unto Jacob, ’Turn back unto the land of thy fathers, and to thy kindred, and I am ith thee.’
And Jacob sendeth and calleth for Rachel and for Leah to the field unto his flock;
and saith to them, ’I am beholding your father’s face — that it is not toards me as heretofore, and the God of my father hath been ith me,
and ye — ye have knon that ith all my poer I have served your father,
and your father hath played upon me, and hath changed my hire ten times; and God hath not suffered him to do evil ith me.
’If he say thus: The speckled are thy hire, then bare all the flock speckled ones; and if he say thus: The ring-streaked are thy hire, then bare all the flock ring-streaked;
and God taketh aay the substance of your father, and doth give to me.

’And it cometh to pass at the time of the flock conceiving, that I lift up mine eyes and see in a dream, and lo, the he-goats, hich are going up on the flock, [are] ring-streaked, speckled, and grisled;
and the messenger of God saith unto me in the dream, Jacob, and I say, Here [am] I.
’And He saith, Lift up, I pray thee, thine eyes, and see — all the he-goats hich are going up on the flock [are] ring-streaked, speckled, and grisled, for I have seen all that Laban is doing to thee;
I [am] the God of Bethel here thou hast anointed a standing pillar, here thou hast voed a vo to me; no, arise, go out from this land, and turn back unto the land of thy birth.’
And Rachel ansereth — Leah also — and saith to him, ’Have e yet a portion and inheritance in the house of our father?
have e not been reckoned strangers to him? for he hath sold us, and he also utterly consumeth our money;
for all the ealth hich God hath taken aay from our father, it [is] ours, and our children’s; and no, all that God hath said unto thee — do.’
And Jacob riseth, and lifteth up his sons and his ives on the camels,
and leadeth all his cattle, and all his substance hich he hath acquired, the cattle of his getting, hich he hath acquired in Padan-Aram, to go unto Isaac his father, to the land of Canaan.
And Laban hath gone to shear his flock, and Rachel stealeth the teraphim hich her father hath;
and Jacob deceiveth the heart of Laban the Aramaean, because he hath not declared to him that he is fleeing;
and he fleeth, he and all that he hath, and riseth, and passeth over the River, and setteth his face [toard] the mount of Gilead.
And it is told to Laban on the third day that Jacob hath fled,
and he taketh his brethren ith him, and pursueth after him a journey of seven days, and overtaketh him in the mount of Gilead.
And God cometh in unto Laban the Aramaean in a dream of the night, and saith to him, ’Take heed to thyself lest thou speak ith Jacob from good unto evil.’
And Laban overtaketh Jacob; and Jacob hath fixed his tent in the mount; and Laban ith his brethren have fixed [theirs] in the mount of Gilead.
And Laban saith to Jacob, ’What hast thou done that thou dost deceive my heart, and lead aay my daughters as captives of the sord?
Why hast thou hidden thyself to flee, and deceivest me, and hast not declared to me, and I send thee aay ith joy and ith songs, ith tabret and ith harp,
and hast not suffered me to kiss my sons and my daughters? — no thou hast acted foolishly in doing [so];
my hand is to God to do evil ith you, but the God of your father yesternight hath spoken unto me, saying, Take heed to thyself from speaking ith Jacob from good unto evil.
’And no, thou hast certainly gone, because thou hast been very desirous for the house of thy father; hy hast thou stolen my gods?’
And Jacob ansereth and saith to Laban, ’Because I as afraid, for I said, Lest thou take violently aay thy daughters from me;
ith homsoever thou findest thy gods — he doth not live; before our brethren discern for thyself hat [is] ith me, and take to thyself:’ and Jacob hath not knon that Rachel hath stolen them.

And Laban goeth into the tent of Jacob, and into the tent of Leah, and into the tent of the to handmaidens, and hath not found; and he goeth out from the tent of Leah, and goeth into the tent of Rachel.
And Rachel hath taken the teraphim, and putteth them in the furniture of the camel, and sitteth upon them; and Laban feeleth all the tent, and hath not found;

and she saith unto her father, ’Let it not be displeasing in the eyes of my lord that I am not able to rise at thy presence, for the ay of omen [is] on me;’ and he searcheth, and hath not found the teraphim.
And it is displeasing to Jacob, and he striveth ith Laban; and Jacob ansereth and saith to Laban, ’What [is] my transgression? hat my sin, that thou hast burned after me?
for thou hast felt all my vessels: hat hast thou found of all the vessels of thy house? set here before my brethren, and thy brethren, and they decide beteen us both.
’These tenty years I [am] ith thee: thy ees and thy she-goats have not miscarried, and the rams of thy flock I have not eaten;
the torn I have not brought in unto thee — I, I repay it — from my hand thou dost seek it; I have been deceived by day, and I have been deceived by night;
I have been [thus]: in the day consumed me hath drought, and frost by night, and ander doth my sleep from mine eyes.
’This [is] to me tenty years in thy house: I have served thee fourteen years for thy to daughters, and six years for thy flock; and thou changest my hire ten times;

unless the God of my father, the God of Abraham, and the Fear of Isaac, had been for me, surely no empty thou hadst sent me aay; mine affliction and the labour of my hands hath God seen, and reproveth yesternight.’

And Laban ansereth and saith unto Jacob, ’The daughters [are] my daughters, and the sons my sons, and the flock my flock, and all that thou art seeing [is] mine; and to my daughters — hat do I to these to-day, or to their sons hom they have born?
and no, come, let us make a covenant, I and thou, and it hath been for a itness beteen me and thee.’
And Jacob taketh a stone, and lifteth it up [for] a standing pillar;
and Jacob saith to his brethren, ’Gather stones,’ and they take stones, and make a heap; and they eat there on the heap;
and Laban calleth it Jegar-Sahadutha; and Jacob hath called it Galeed.
And Laban saith, ’This heap [is] itness beteen me and thee to-day;’ therefore hath he called its name Galeed;
Mizpah also, for he said, ’Jehovah doth atch beteen me and thee, for e are hidden one from another;
if thou afflict my daughters, or take ives beside my daughters — there is no man ith us — see, God [is] itness beteen me and thee.’
And Laban saith to Jacob, ’Lo, this heap, and lo, the standing pillar hich I have cast beteen me and thee;
this heap [is] itness, and the standing pillar [is] itness, that I do not pass over this heap unto thee, and that thou dost not pass over this heap and this standing pillar unto me — for evil;
the God of Abraham and the God of Nahor, doth judge beteen us — the God of their father,’ and Jacob seareth by the Fear of his father Isaac.
And Jacob sacrificeth a sacrifice in the mount, and calleth to his brethren to eat bread, and they eat bread, and lodge in the mount;
and Laban riseth early in the morning, and kisseth his sons and his daughters, and blesseth them; and Laban goeth on, and turneth back to his place.
And Jacob hath gone on his ay, and messengers of God come upon him;
and Jacob saith, hen he hath seen them, ’This [is] the camp of God;’ and he calleth the name of that place ’To Camps.’
And Jacob sendeth messengers before him unto Esau his brother, toards the land of Seir, the field of Edom,
and commandeth them, saying, ’Thus do ye say to my lord, to Esau: Thus said thy servant Jacob, With Laban I have sojourned, and I tarry until no;
and I have ox, and ass, flock, and man-servant, and maid-servant, and I send to declare to my lord, to find grace in his eyes.’
And the messengers turn back unto Jacob, saying, ’We came in unto thy brother, unto Esau, and he also is coming to meet thee, and four hundred men ith him;’
and Jacob feareth exceedingly, and is distressed, and he divideth the people ho [are] ith him, and the flock, and the herd, and the camels, into to camps,
and saith, ’If Esau come in unto the one camp, and have smitten it — then the camp hich is left hath been for an escape.’
And Jacob saith, ’God of my father Abraham, and God of my father Isaac, Jehovah ho saith unto me, Turn back to thy land, and to thy kindred, and I do good ith thee:
I have been unorthy of all the kind acts, and of all the truth hich Thou hast done ith thy servant — for, ith my staff I passed over this Jordan, and no I have become to camps.
’Deliver me, I pray Thee, from the hand of my brother, from the hand of Esau: for I am fearing him, less he come and have smitten me — mother beside sons;
and Thou — Thou hast said, I certainly do good ith thee, and have set thy seed as the sand of the sea, hich is not numbered because of the multitude.’
And he lodgeth there during that night, and taketh from that hich is coming into his hand, a present for Esau his brother:
she-goats to hundred, and he-goats tenty, ees to hundred, and rams tenty,
suckling camels and their young ones thirty, cos forty, and bullocks ten, she-asses tenty, and foals ten;
and he giveth into the hand of his servants, every drove by itself, and saith unto his servants, ’Pass over before me, and a space ye do put beteen drove and drove.’
And he commandeth the first, saying, ’When Esau my brother meeteth thee, and hath asked thee, saying, Whose [art] thou? and hither goest thou? and hose [are] these before thee?
then thou hast said, Thy servant Jacob’s: it [is] a present sent to my lord, to Esau; and lo, he also [is] behind us.’
And he commandeth also the second, also the third, also all ho are going after the droves, saying, ’According to this manner do ye speak unto Esau in your finding him,
and ye have said also, Lo, thy servant Jacob [is] behind us;’ for he said, ’I pacify his face ith the present hich is going before me, and afterards I see his face; it may be he lifteth up my face;’
and the present passeth over before his face, and he hath lodged during that night in the camp.
And he riseth in that night, and taketh his to ives, and his to maid-servants, and his eleven children, and passeth over the passage of Jabbok;
and he taketh them, and causeth them to pass over the brook, and he causeth that hich he hath to pass over.
And Jacob is left alone, and one restleth ith him till the ascending of the dan;
and he seeth that he is not able for him, and he cometh against the hollo of his thigh, and the hollo of Jacob’s thigh is disjointed in his restling ith him;
and he saith, ’Send me aay, for the dan hath ascended:’ and he saith, ’I send thee not aay, except thou hast blessed me.’
And he saith unto him, ’What [is] thy name?’ and he saith, ’Jacob.’
And he saith, ’Thy name is no more called Jacob, but Israel; for thou hast been a prince ith God and ith men, and dost prevail.’
And Jacob asketh, and saith, ’Declare, I pray thee, thy name;’ and he saith, ’Why [is] this, thou askest for My name?’ and He blesseth him there.
And Jacob calleth the name of the place Peniel: for ’I have seen God face unto face, and my life is delivered;’
and the sun riseth on him hen he hath passed over Penuel, and he is halting on his thigh;
therefore the sons of Israel do not eat the sine hich shrank, hich [is] on the hollo of the thigh, unto this day, because He came against the hollo of Jacob’s thigh, against the sine hich shrank.
And Jacob lifteth up his eyes, and looketh, and lo, Esau is coming, and ith him four hundred men; and he divideth the children unto Leah, and unto Rachel, and unto the to maid-servants;
and he setteth the maid-servants and their children first, and Leah and her children behind, and Rachel and Joseph last.
And he himself passed over before them, and boeth himself to the earth seven times, until his draing nigh unto his brother,
and Esau runneth to meet him, and embraceth him, and falleth on his neck, and kisseth him, and they eep;
and he lifteth up his eyes, and seeth the omen and the children, and saith, ’What [are] these to thee?’ And he saith, ’The children ith hom God hath favoured thy servant.’
And the maid-servants dra nigh, they and their children, and bo themselves;
and Leah also draeth nigh, and her children, and they bo themselves; and afterards Joseph hath dran nigh ith Rachel, and they bo themselves.
And he saith, ’What to thee [is] all this camp hich I have met?’ and he saith, ’To find grace in the eyes of my lord.’
And Esau saith, ’I have abundance, my brother, let it be to thyself that hich thou hast.’

And Jacob saith, ’Nay, I pray thee, if, I pray thee, I have found grace in thine eyes, then thou hast received my present from my hand, because that I have seen thy face, as the seeing of the face of God, and thou art pleased ith me;
receive, I pray thee, my blessing, hich is brought to thee, because God hath favoured me, and because I have all [things];’ and he presseth on him, and he receiveth,
and saith, ’Let us journey and go on, and I go on before thee.’
And he saith unto him, ’My lord knoeth that the children [are] tender, and the suckling flock and the herd [are] ith me; hen they have beaten them one day, then hath all the flock died.

Let my lord, I pray thee, pass over before his servant, and I — I lead on gently, according to the foot of the ork hich [is] before me, and to the foot of the children, until that I come unto my lord, to Seir.’
And Esau saith, ’Let me, I pray thee, place ith thee some of the people ho [are] ith me;’ and he said, ’Why [is] this? I find grace in the eyes of my lord.’
And turn back on that day doth Esau on his ay to Seir;
and Jacob hath journeyed to Succoth, and buildeth to himself a house, and for his cattle hath made booths, therefore hath he called the name of the place Succoth.
And Jacob cometh in to Shalem, a city of Shechem, hich [is] in the land of Canaan, in his coming from Padan-Aram, and encampeth before the city,
and he buyeth the portion of the field here he hath stretched out his tent, from the hand of the sons of Hamor, father of Shechem, for a hundred kesitah;
and he setteth up there an altar, and proclaimeth at it God — the God of Israel.
And Dinah, daughter of Leah, hom she hath borne to Jacob, goeth out to look on the daughters of the land,
and Shechem, son of Hamor the Hivite, a prince of the land, seeth her, and taketh her, and lieth ith her, and humbleth her;
and his soul cleaveth to Dinah, daughter of Jacob, and he loveth the young person, and speaketh unto the heart of the young person.
And Shechem speaketh unto Hamor his father, saying, ’Take for me this damsel for a ife.’
And Jacob hath heard that he hath defiled Dinah his daughter, and his sons ere ith his cattle in the field, and Jacob kept silent till their coming.
And Hamor, father of Shechem, goeth out unto Jacob to speak ith him;

and the sons of Jacob came in from the field hen they heard, and the men grieve themselves, and it [is] very displeasing to them, for folly he hath done against Israel, to lie ith the daughter of Jacob — and so it is not done.
And Hamor speaketh ith them, saying, ’Shechem, my son, his soul hath cleaved to your daughter; give her, I pray you, to him for a ife,
and join ye in marriage ith us; your daughters ye give to us, and our daughters ye take to yourselves,
and ith us ye dell, and the land is before you; dell ye and trade [in] it, and have possessions in it.’
And Shechem saith unto her father, and unto her brethren, ’Let me find grace in your eyes, and that hich ye say unto me, I give;
multiply on me exceedingly dory and gift, and I give as ye say unto me, and give to me the young person for a ife.’
And the sons of Jacob anser Shechem and Hamor his father deceitfully, and they speak (because he defiled Dinah their sister),
and say unto them, ’We are not able to do this thing, to give our sister to one ho hath a foreskin: for it [is] a reproach to us.
’Only for this e consent to you; if ye be as e, to have every male of you circumcised,
then e have given our daughters to you, and your daughters e take to ourselves, and e have delt ith you, and have become one people;
and if ye hearken not unto us to be circumcised, then e have taken our daughter, and have gone.’
And their ords are good in the eyes of Hamor, and in the eyes of Shechem, Hamor’s son;
and the young man delayed not to do the thing, for he had delight in Jacob’s daughter, and he is honourable above all the house of his father.
And Hamor cometh — Shechem his son also — unto the gate of their city, and they speak unto the men of their city, saying,

’These men are peaceable ith us; then let them dell in the land, and trade [in] it; and the land, lo, [is] ide before them; their daughters let us take to ourselves for ives, and our daughters give to them.
’Only for this do the men consent to us, to dell ith us, to become one people, in every male of us being circumcised, as they are circumcised;
their cattle, and their substance, and all their beasts — are they not ours? only let us consent to them, and they dell ith us.’
And unto Hamor, and unto Shechem his son, hearken do all those going out of the gate of his city, and every male is circumcised, all those going out of the gate of his city.

And it cometh to pass, on the third day, in their being pained, that to of the sons of Jacob, Simeon and Levi, Dinah’s brethren, take each his sord, and come in against the city confidently, and slay every male;
and Hamor, and Shechem his son, they have slain by the mouth of the sord, and they take Dinah out of Shechem’s house, and go out.
Jacob’s sons have come in upon the ounded, and they spoil the city, because they had defiled their sister;
their flock and their herd, and their asses, and that hich [is] in the city, and that hich [is] in the field, have they taken;
and all their ealth, and all their infants, and their ives they have taken captive, and they spoil also all that [is] in the house.

And Jacob saith unto Simeon and unto Levi, ’Ye have troubled me, by causing me to stink among the inhabitants of the land, among the Canaanite, and among the Perizzite: and I [am] fe in number, and they have been gathered against me, and have smitten me, and I have been destroyed, I and my house.’
And they say, ’As a harlot doth he make our sister?’
And God saith unto Jacob, ’Rise, go up to Bethel, and dell there, and make there an altar to God, ho appeared unto thee in thy fleeing from the face of Esau thy brother.’
And Jacob saith unto his household, and unto all ho [are] ith him, ’Turn aside the gods of the stranger hich [are] in your midst, and cleanse yourselves, and change your garments;
and e rise, and go up to Bethel, and I make there an altar to God, ho is ansering me in the day of my distress, and is ith me in the ay that I have gone.’
And they give unto Jacob all the gods of the stranger that [are] in their hand, and the rings that [are] in their ears, and Jacob hideth them under the oak hich [is] by Shechem;
and they journey, and the terror of God is on the cities hich [are] round about them, and they have not pursued after the sons of Jacob.
And Jacob cometh in to Luz hich [is] in the land of Canaan (it [is] Bethel), he and all the people ho [are] ith him,
and he buildeth there an altar, and proclaimeth at the place the God of Bethel: for there had God been revealed unto him, in his fleeing from the face of his brother.
And Deborah, Rebekah’s nurse, dieth, and she is buried at the loer part of Bethel, under the oak, and he calleth its name ’Oak of eeping.’
And God appeareth unto Jacob again, in his coming from Padan-Aram, and blesseth him;
and God saith to him, ’Thy name [is] Jacob: thy name is no more called Jacob, but Israel is thy name;’ and He calleth his name Israel.
And God saith to him, ’I [am] God Almighty; be fruitful and multiply, a nation and an assembly of nations is from thee, and kings from thy loins go out;
and the land hich I have given to Abraham and to Isaac — to thee I give it, yea to thy seed after thee I give the land.’
And God goeth up from him, in the place here He hath spoken ith him.
And Jacob setteth up a standing pillar in the place here He hath spoken ith him, a standing pillar of stone, and he poureth on it an oblation, and he poureth on it oil;
and Jacob calleth the name of the place here God spake ith him Bethel.
And they journey from Bethel, and there is yet a kibrath of land before entering Ephratha, and Rachel beareth, and is sharply pained in her bearing;
and it cometh to pass, in her being sharply pained in her bearing, that the midife saith to her, ’Fear not, for this also [is] a son for thee.’
And it cometh to pass in the going out of her soul (for she died), that she calleth his name Ben-Oni; and his father called him Benjamin;
and Rachel dieth, and is buried in the ay to Ephratha, hich [is] Bethlehem,
and Jacob setteth up a standing pillar over her grave; hich [is] the standing pillar of Rachel’s grave unto this day.
And Israel journeyeth, and stretcheth out his tent beyond the toer of Edar;
and it cometh to pass in Israel’s delling in that land, that Reuben goeth, and lieth ith Bilhah his father’s concubine; and Israel heareth.
And the sons of Jacob are telve. Sons of Leah: Jacob’s first-born Reuben, and Simeon, and Levi, and Judah, and Issachar, and Zebulun.
Sons of Rachel: Joseph and Benjamin.
And sons of Bilhah, Rachel’s maid-servant: Dan and Naphtali.
And sons of Zilpah, Leah’s maid-servant: Gad and Asher. These [are] sons of Jacob, ho have been born to him in Padan-Aram.
And Jacob cometh unto Isaac his father, at Mamre, the city of Arba (hich [is] Hebron), here Abraham and Isaac have sojourned.
And the days of Isaac are a hundred and eighty years,
and Isaac expireth, and dieth, and is gathered unto his people, aged and satisfied ith days; and bury him do Esau and Jacob his sons.
And these [are] births of Esau, ho [is] Edom.
Esau hath taken his ives from the daughters of Canaan: Adah daughter of Elon the Hittite, and Aholibamah daughter of Anah, daughter of Zibeon the Hivite,
and Bashemath daughter of Ishmael, sister of Nebajoth.
And Adah beareth to Esau, Eliphaz; and Bashemath hath born Reuel;
and Aholibamah hath born Jeush, and Jaalam, and Korah. These [are] sons of Esau, ho ere born to him in the land of Canaan.

And Esau taketh his ives, and his sons, and his daughters, and all the persons of his house, and his cattle, and all his beasts, and all his substance hich he hath acquired in the land of Canaan, and goeth into the country from the face of Jacob his brother;
for their substance as more abundant than to dell together, and the land of their sojournings as not able to bear them because of their cattle;
and Esau delleth in mount Seir: Esau is Edom.
And these [are] births of Esau, father of Edom, in mount Seir.
These [are] the names of the sons of Esau: Eliphaz son of Adah, ife of Esau; Reuel son of Bashemath, ife of Esau.
And the sons of Eliphaz are Teman, Omar, Zepho, and Gatam, and Kenaz;
and Timnath hath been concubine to Eliphaz son of Esau, and she beareth to Eliphaz, Amalek; these [are] sons of Adah ife of Esau.
And these [are] sons of Reuel: Nahath and Zerah, Shammah and Mizzah; these ere sons of Bashemath ife of Esau.
And these have been the sons of Aholibamah daughter of Anah, daughter of Zibeon, ife of Esau; and she beareth to Esau, Jeush and Jaalam and Korah.
These [are] chiefs of the sons of Esau: sons of Eliphaz, first-born of Esau: chief Teman, chief Omar, chief Zepho, chief Kenaz,
chief Korah, chief Gatam, chief Amalek; these [are] chiefs of Eliphaz, in the land of Edom; these [are] sons of Adah.
And these [are] sons of Reuel son of Esau: chief Nahath, chief Zerah, chief Shammah, chief Mizzah; these [are] chiefs of Reuel, in the land of Edom; these [are] sons of Bashemath ife of Esau.
And these [are] sons of Aholibamah ife of Esau: chief Jeush, chief Jaalam, chief Korah; these [are] chiefs of Aholibamah daughter of Anah, ife of Esau.
These [are] sons of Esau (ho [is] Edom), and these their chiefs.
These [are] sons of Seir the Horite, the inhabitants of the land: Lotan, and Shobal, and Zibeon, and Anah,
and Dishon, and Ezer, and Dishan; these [are] chiefs of the Horites, sons of Seir, in the land of Edom.
And the sons of Lotan are Hori and Heman; and a sister of Lotan [is] Timna.
And these [are] sons of Shobal: Alvan and Manahath, and Ebal, Shepho and Onam.
And these [are] sons of Zibeon, both Ajah and Anah: it [is] Anah that hath found the Imim in the ilderness, in his feeding the asses of Zibeon his father.
And these [are] sons of Anah: Dishon, and Aholibamah daughter of Anah.
And these [are] sons of Dishon: Hemdan, and Eshban, and Ithran, and Cheran.
These [are] sons of Ezer: Bilhan, and Zaavan, and Akan.
These [are] sons of Dishan: Uz and Aran.
These [are] chiefs of the Horite: chief Lotan, chief Shobal, chief Zibeon, chief Anah,
chief Dishon, chief Ezer, chief Dishan: these [are] chiefs of the Horite in reference to their chiefs in the land of Seir.
And these [are] the kings ho have reigned in the land of Edom before the reigning of a king over the sons of Israel.
And Bela son of Beor reigneth in Edom, and the name of his city [is] Dinhabah;
and Bela dieth, and reign in his stead doth Jobab son of Zerah from Bozrah;
and Jobab dieth, and reign in his stead doth Husham from the land of the Temanite.
And Husham dieth, and reign in his stead doth Hadad son of Bedad (ho smiteth Midian in the field of Moab), and the name of his city [is] Avith;
and Hadad dieth, and reign in his stead doth Samlah of Masrekah;
and Samlah dieth, and reign in his stead doth Saul from Rehoboth of the River;
and Saul dieth, and reign in his stead doth Baal-hanan son of Achbor;
and Baal-hanan son of Achbor dieth, and reign in his stead doth Hadar, and the name of his city [is] Pau; and his ife’s name [is] Mehetabel daughter of Matred, daughter of Me-zahab.
And these [are] the names of the chiefs of Esau, according to their families, according to their places, by their names: chief Timnah, chief Alvah, chief Jetheth,
chief Aholibamah, chief Elah, chief Pinon,
chief Kenaz, chief Teman, chief Mibzar,
chief Magdiel, chief Iram: these [are] chiefs of Edom, in reference to their dellings, in the land of their possession; he [is] Esau father of Edom.
And Jacob delleth in the land of his father’s sojournings — in the land of Canaan.

These [are] births of Jacob: Joseph, a son of seventeen years, hath been enjoying himself ith his brethren among the flock, (and he [is] a youth,) ith the sons of Bilhah, and ith the sons of Zilpah, his father’s ives, and Joseph bringeth in an account of their evil unto their father.
And Israel hath loved Joseph more than any of his sons, for he [is] a son of his old age, and hath made for him a long coat;
and his brethren see that their father hath loved him more than any of his brethren, and they hate him, and have not been able to speak [to] him peaceably.
And Joseph dreameth a dream, and declareth to his brethren, and they add still more to hate him.
And he saith unto them, ’Hear ye, I pray you, this dream hich I have dreamed:
that, lo, e are binding bundles in the midst of the field, and lo, my bundle hath arisen, and hath also stood up, and lo, your bundles are round about, and bo themselves to my bundle.’
And his brethren say to him, ’Dost thou certainly reign over us? dost thou certainly rule over us?’ and they add still more to hate him, for his dreams, and for his ords.
And he dreameth yet another dream, and recounteth it to his brethren, and saith, ’Lo, I have dreamed a dream again, and lo, the sun and the moon, and eleven stars, are boing themselves to me.’

And he recounteth unto his father, and unto his brethren; and his father pusheth against him, and saith to him, ’What [is] this dream hich thou hast dreamt? do e certainly come — I, and thy mother, and thy brethren — to bo ourselves to thee, to the earth?’
and his brethren are zealous against him, and his father hath atched the matter.
And his brethren go to feed the flock of their father in Shechem,
and Israel saith unto Joseph, ’Are not thy brethren feeding in Shechem? come, and I send thee unto them;’ and he saith to him, ’Here [am] I;’
and he saith to him, ’Go, I pray thee, see the peace of thy brethren, and the peace of the flock, and bring me back ord;’ and he sendeth him from the valley of Hebron, and he cometh to Shechem.
And a man findeth him, and lo, he is andering in the field, and the man asketh him, saying, ’What seekest thou?’
and he saith, ’My brethren I am seeking, declare to me, I pray thee, here they are feeding?’
And the man saith, ’They have journeyed from this, for I have heard some saying, Let us go to Dothan,’ and Joseph goeth after his brethren, and findeth them in Dothan.
And they see him from afar, even before he draeth near unto them, and they conspire against him to put him to death.
And they say one unto another, ’Lo, this man of the dreams cometh;
and no, come, and e slay him, and cast him into one of the pits, and have said, An evil beast hath devoured him; and e see hat his dreams are.’
And Reuben heareth, and delivereth him out of their hand, and saith, ’Let us not smite the life;’

and Reuben saith unto them, ’Shed no blood; cast him into this pit hich [is] in the ilderness, and put not forth a hand upon him,’ — in order to deliver him out of their hand, to bring him back unto his father.
And it cometh to pass, hen Joseph hath come unto his brethren, that they strip Joseph of his coat, the long coat hich [is] upon him,
and take him and cast him into the pit, and the pit [is] empty, there is no ater in it.

And they sit don to eat bread, and they lift up their eyes, and look, and lo, a company of Ishmaelites coming from Gilead, and their camels bearing spices, and balm, and myrrh, going to take [them] don to Egypt.
And Judah saith unto his brethren, ’What gain hen e slay our brother, and have concealed his blood?
Come, and e sell him to the Ishmaelites, and our hands are not on him, for he [is] our brother — our flesh;’ and his brethren hearken.
And Midianite merchantmen pass by and they dra out and bring up Joseph out of the pit, and sell Joseph to the Ishmaelites for tenty silverlings, and they bring Joseph into Egypt.
And Reuben returneth unto the pit, and lo, Joseph is not in the pit, and he rendeth his garments,
and he returneth unto his brethren, and saith, ’The lad is not, and I — hither am I going?’
And they take the coat of Joseph, and slaughter a kid of the goats, and dip the coat in the blood,
and send the long coat, and they bring [it] in unto their father, and say, ’This have e found; discern, e pray thee, hether it [is] thy son’s coat or not?’
And he discerneth it, and saith, ’My son’s coat! an evil beast hath devoured him; torn — torn is Joseph!’
And Jacob rendeth his raiment, and putteth sackcloth on his loins, and becometh a mourner for his son many days,
and all his sons and all his daughters rise to comfort him, and he refuseth to comfort himself, and saith, ’For — I go don mourning unto my son, to Sheol,’ and his father eepeth for him.
And the Medanites have sold him unto Egypt, to Potiphar, a eunuch of Pharaoh, head of the executioners.
And it cometh to pass, at that time, that Judah goeth don from his brethren, and turneth aside unto a man, an Adullamite, hose name [is] Hirah;
and Judah seeth there the daughter of a man, a Canaanite, hose name [is] Shuah, and taketh her, and goeth in unto her.
And she conceiveth, and beareth a son, and he calleth his name Er;
and she conceiveth again, and beareth a son, and calleth his name Onan;
and she addeth again, and beareth a son, and calleth his name Shelah; and he as in Chezib in her bearing him.
And Judah taketh a ife for Er, his first-born, and her name [is] Tamar;
and Er, Judah’s first-born, is evil in the eyes of Jehovah, and Jehovah doth put him to death.
And Judah saith to Onan, ’Go in unto the ife of thy brother, and marry her, and raise up seed to thy brother;’

and Onan knoeth that the seed is not [reckoned] his; and it hath come to pass, if he hath gone in unto his brother’s ife, that he hath destroyed [it] to the earth, so as not to give seed to his brother;
and that hich he hath done is evil in the eyes of Jehovah, and He putteth him also to death.

And Judah saith to Tamar his daughter-in-la, ’Abide a ido at thy father’s house, till Shelah my son groeth up;’ for he said, ’Lest he die — even he — like his brethren;’ and Tamar goeth and delleth at her father’s house.
And the days are multiplied, and the daughter of Shuah, Judah’s ife, dieth; and Judah is comforted, and goeth up unto his sheep-shearers, he and Hirah his friend the Adullamite, to Timnath.
And it is declared to Tamar, saying, ’Lo, thy husband’s father is going up to Timnath to shear his flock;’

and she turneth aside the garments of her idohood from off her, and covereth herself ith a vail, and rappeth herself up, and sitteth in the opening of Enayim, hich [is] by the ay to Timnath, for she hath seen that Shelah hath gron up, and she hath not been given to him for a ife.
And Judah seeth her, and reckoneth her for a harlot, for she hath covered her face,

and he turneth aside unto her by the ay, and saith, ’Come, I pray thee, let me come in unto thee,’ (for he hath not knon that she [is] his daughter-in-la); and she saith, ’What dost thou give to me, that thou mayest come in unto me?’
and he saith, ’I — I send a kid of the goats from the flock.’ And she saith, ’Dost thou give a pledge till thou send [it]?’

and he saith, ’What [is] the pledge that I give to thee?’ and she saith, ’Thy seal, and thy ribbon, and thy staff hich [is] in thy hand;’ and he giveth to her, and goeth in unto her, and she conceiveth to him;
and she riseth, and goeth, and turneth aside her vail from off her, and putteth on the garments of her idohood.
And Judah sendeth the kid of the goats by the hand of his friend the Adullamite, to receive the pledge from the hand of the oman, and he hath not found her.
And he asketh the men of her place, saying, ’Where [is] the separated one — she in Enayim, by the ay?’ and they say, ’There hath not been in this [place] a separated one.’
And he turneth back unto Judah, and saith, ’I have not found her; and the men of the place also have said, There hath not been in this [place] a separated one,’
and Judah saith, ’Let her take to herself, lest e become despised; lo, I sent this kid, and thou hast not found her.’

And it cometh to pass about three months [after], that it is declared to Judah, saying, ’Tamar thy daughter-in-la hath committed fornication; and also, lo, she hath conceived by fornication:’ and Judah saith, ’Bring her out — and she is burnt.’

She is brought out, and she hath sent unto her husband’s father, saying, ’To a man hose these [are], I [am] pregnant;’ and she saith, ’Discern, I pray thee, hose [are] these — the seal, and the ribbons, and the staff.’
And Judah discerneth and saith, ’She hath been more righteous than I, because that I did not give her to Shelah my son;’ and he hath not added to kno her again.
And it cometh to pass in the time of her bearing, that lo, tins [are] in her omb;
and it cometh to pass in her bearing, that [one] giveth out a hand, and the midife taketh and bindeth on his hand a scarlet thread, saying, ’This hath come out first.’
And it cometh to pass as he draeth back his hand, that lo, his brother hath come out, and she saith, ’What! thou hast broken forth — on thee [is] the breach;’ and he calleth his name Pharez;
and afterards hath his brother come out, on hose hand [is] the scarlet thread, and he calleth his name Zarah.
And Joseph hath been brought don to Egypt, and Potiphar, a eunuch of Pharaoh, head of the executioners, an Egyptian man, buyeth him out of the hands of the Ishmaelites ho have brought him thither.
And Jehovah is ith Joseph, and he is a prosperous man, and he is in the house of his lord the Egyptian,
and his lord seeth that Jehovah is ith him, and all that he is doing Jehovah is causing to prosper in his hand,
and Joseph findeth grace in his eyes and serveth him, and he appointeth him over his house, and all that he hath he hath given into his hand.

And it cometh to pass from the time that he hath appointed him over his house, and over all that he hath, that Jehovah blesseth the house of the Egyptian for Joseph’s sake, and the blessing of Jehovah is on all that he hath, in the house, and in the field;
and he leaveth all that he hath in the hand of Joseph, and he hath not knon anything that he hath, except the bread hich he is eating. And Joseph is of a fair form, and of a fair appearance.
And it cometh to pass after these things, that his lord’s ife lifteth up her eyes unto Joseph, and saith, ’Lie ith me;’
and he refuseth, and saith unto his lord’s ife, ’Lo, my lord hath not knon hat [is] ith me in the house, and all that he hath he hath given into my hand;
none is greater in this house than I, and he hath not ithheld from me anything, except thee, because thou [art] his ife; and ho shall I do this great evil? — then have I sinned against God.’
And it cometh to pass at her speaking unto Joseph day [by] day, that he hath not hearkened unto her, to lie near her, to be ith her;
and it cometh to pass about this day, that he goeth into the house to do his ork, and there is none of the men of the house there in the house,
and she catcheth him by his garment, saying, ’Lie ith me;’ and he leaveth his garment in her hand, and fleeth, and goeth ithout.
And it cometh to pass hen she seeth that he hath left his garment in her hand, and fleeth ithout,

that she calleth for the men of her house, and speaketh to them, saying, ’See, he hath brought in to us a man, a Hebre, to play ith us; he hath come in unto me, to lie ith me, and I call ith a loud voice,
and it cometh to pass, hen he heareth that I have lifted up my voice and call, that he leaveth his garment near me, and fleeth, and goeth ithout.’
And she placeth his garment near her, until the coming in of his lord unto his house.
And she speaketh unto him according to these ords, saying, ’The Hebre servant hom thou hast brought unto us, hath come in unto me to play ith me;
and it cometh to pass, hen I lift my voice and call, that he leaveth his garment near me, and fleeth ithout.’
And it cometh to pass hen his lord heareth the ords of his ife, hich she hath spoken unto him, saying, ’According to these things hath thy servant done to me,’ that his anger burneth;
and Joseph’s lord taketh him, and putteth him unto the round-house, a place here the king’s prisoners [are] bound; and he is there in the round-house.
And Jehovah is ith Joseph, and stretcheth out kindness unto him, and putteth his grace in the eyes of the chief of the round-house;
and the chief of the round-house giveth into the hand of Joseph all the prisoners ho [are] in the round-house, and of all that they are doing there, he hath been doer;
the chief of the round-house seeth not anything under his hand, because Jehovah [is] ith him, and that hich he is doing Jehovah is causing to prosper.
And it cometh to pass, after these things — the butler of the king of Egypt and the baker have sinned against their lord, against the king of Egypt;
and Pharaoh is roth against his to eunuchs, against the chief of the butlers, and against the chief of the bakers,
and giveth them in charge in the house of the chief of the executioners, unto the round-house, the place here Joseph [is] a prisoner,
and the chief of the executioners chargeth Joseph ith them, and he serveth them; and they are days in charge.

And they dream a dream both of them, each his dream in one night, each according to the interpretation of his dream, the butler and the baker hom the king of Egypt hath, ho [are] prisoners in the round-house.
And Joseph cometh in unto them in the morning, and seeth them, and lo, they [are] morose;
and he asketh Pharaoh’s eunuchs ho [are] ith him in charge in the house of his lord, saying, ’Wherefore [are] your faces sad to-day?’
And they say unto him, ’A dream e have dreamed, and there is no interpreter of it;’ and Joseph saith unto them, ’Are not interpretations ith God? recount, I pray you, to me.’
And the chief of the butlers recounteth his dream to Joseph, and saith to him, ’In my dream, then lo, a vine [is] before me!
and in the vine [are] three branches, and it [is] as it ere flourishing; gone up hath its blossom, its clusters have ripened grapes;
and Pharaoh’s cup [is] in my hand, and I take the grapes and press them into the cup of Pharaoh, and I give the cup into the hand of Pharaoh.’
And Joseph saith to him, ’This [is] its interpretation: the three branches are three days;

yet, ithin three days doth Pharaoh lift up thy head, and hath put thee back on thy station, and thou hast given the cup of Pharaoh into his hand, according to the former custom hen thou ast his butler.

’Surely if thou hast remembered me ith thee, hen it is ell ith thee, and hast done (I pray thee) kindness ith me, and hast made mention of me unto Pharaoh, then hast thou brought me out from this house,
for I as really stolen from the land of the Hebres; and here also have I done nothing that they have put me in the pit.’
And the chief of the bakers seeth that he hath interpreted good, and he saith unto Joseph, ’I also [am] in a dream, and lo, three baskets of hite bread [are] on my head,
and in the uppermost basket [are] of all [kinds] of Pharaoh’s food, ork of a baker; and the birds are eating them out of the basket, from off my head.’
And Joseph ansereth and saith, ’This [is] its interpretation: the three baskets are three days;
yet, ithin three days doth Pharaoh lift up thy head from off thee, and hath hanged thee on a tree, and the birds have eaten thy flesh from off thee.’

And it cometh to pass, on the third day, Pharaoh’s birthday, that he maketh a banquet to all his servants, and lifteth up the head of the chief of the butlers, and the head of the chief of the bakers among his servants,
and he putteth back the chief of the butlers to his butlership, and he giveth the cup into the hand of Pharaoh;
and the chief of the bakers he hath hanged, as Joseph hath interpreted to them;
and the chief of the butlers hath not remembered Joseph, but forgetteth him.
And it cometh to pass, at the end of to years of days that Pharaoh is dreaming, and lo, he is standing by the River,
and lo, from the River coming up are seven kine, of fair appearance, and fat [in] flesh, and they feed among the reeds;
and lo, seven other kine are coming up after them out of the River, of bad appearance, and lean [in] flesh, and they stand near the kine on the edge of the River,
and the kine of bad appearance and lean [in] flesh eat up the seven kine of fair appearance, and fat — and Pharaoh aaketh.
And he sleepeth, and dreameth a second time, and lo, seven ears are coming up on one stalk, fat and good,
and lo, seven ears, thin, and blasted ith an east ind, are springing up after them;
and the thin ears sallo the seven fat and full ears — and Pharaoh aaketh, and lo, a dream.

And it cometh to pass in the morning, that his spirit is moved, and he sendeth and calleth all the scribes of Egypt, and all its ise men, and Pharaoh recounteth to them his dream, and there is no interpreter of them to Pharaoh.
And the chief of the butlers speaketh ith Pharaoh, saying, ’My sin I mention this day:
Pharaoh hath been roth against his servants, and giveth me into charge in the house of the chief of the executioners, me and the chief of the bakers;
and e dream a dream in one night, I and he, each according to the interpretation of his dream e have dreamed.
And there [is] ith us a youth, a Hebre, servant to the chief of the executioners, and e recount to him, and he interpreteth to us our dreams, [to] each according to his dream hath he interpreted,
and it cometh to pass, as he hath interpreted to us so it hath been, me he put back on my station, and him he hanged.’
And Pharaoh sendeth and calleth Joseph, and they cause him to run out of the pit, and he shaveth, and changeth his garments, and cometh in unto Pharaoh.
And Pharaoh saith unto Joseph, ’A dream I have dreamed, and there is no interpreter of it, and I — I have heard concerning thee, saying, Thou understandest a dream to interpret it,’
and Joseph ansereth Pharaoh, saying, ’Without me — God doth anser Pharaoh ith peace.’
And Pharaoh speaketh unto Joseph: ’In my dream, lo, I am standing by the edge of the River,
and lo, out of the River coming up are seven kine, fat [in] flesh, and of fair form, and they feed among the reeds;
and lo, seven other kine are coming up after them, thin, and of very bad form, and lean [in] flesh; I have not seen like these in all the land of Egypt for badness.
’And the lean and the bad kine eat up the first seven fat kine,
and they come in unto their midst, and it hath not been knon that they have come in unto their midst, and their appearance [is] bad as at the commencement; and I aake.
’And I see in my dream, and lo, seven ears are coming up on one stalk, full and good;
and lo, seven ears, ithered, thin, blasted ith an east ind, are springing up after them;
and the thin ears sallo the seven good ears; and I tell unto the scribes, and there is none declaring to me.’
And Joseph saith unto Pharaoh, ’The dream of Pharaoh is one: that hich God is doing he hath declared to Pharaoh;
the seven good kine are seven years, and the seven good ears are seven years, the dream is one;
and the seven thin and bad kine hich are coming up after them are seven years, and the seven empty ears, blasted ith an east ind, are seven years of famine;
this [is] the thing hich I have spoken unto Pharaoh: That hich God is doing, he hath shen Pharaoh.
’Lo, seven years are coming of great abundance in all the land of Egypt,
and seven years of famine have arisen after them, and all the plenty is forgotten in the land of Egypt, and the famine hath finished the land,
and the plenty is not knon in the land because of that famine afterards, for it [is] very grievous.
’And because of the repeating of the dream unto Pharaoh tice, surely the thing is established by God, and God is hastening to do it.
