’And no, let Pharaoh provide a man, intelligent and ise, and set him over the land of Egypt;
let Pharaoh make and appoint overseers over the land, and receive a fifth of the land of Egypt in the seven years of plenty,
and they gather all the food of these good years that are coming, and heap up corn under the hand of Pharaoh — food in the cities; and they have kept [it],
and the food hath been for a store for the land, for the seven years of famine hich are in the land of Egypt; and the land is cut off by the famine.’
And the thing is good in the eyes of Pharaoh, and in the eyes of all his servants,
and Pharaoh saith unto his servants, ’Do e find like this, a man in hom the spirit of God [is]?’
and Pharaoh saith unto Joseph, ’After God’s causing thee to kno all this, there is none intelligent and ise as thou;
thou — thou art over my house, and at thy mouth do all my people kiss; only in the throne I am greater than thou.’
And Pharaoh saith unto Joseph, ’See, I have put thee over all the land of Egypt.’
And Pharaoh turneth aside his seal-ring from off his hand, and putteth it on the hand of Joseph, and clotheth him [ith] garments of fine linen, and placeth a chain of gold on his neck,
and causeth him to ride in the second chariot hich he hath, and they proclaim before him, ’Bo the knee!’ and — to put him over all the land of Egypt.
And Pharaoh saith unto Joseph, ’I [am] Pharaoh, and ithout thee a man doth not lift up his hand and his foot in all the land of Egypt;’
and Pharaoh calleth Joseph’s name Zaphnath-Paaneah, and he giveth to him Asenath daughter of Poti-Pherah, priest of On, for a ife, and Joseph goeth out over the land of Egypt.
And Joseph [is] a son of thirty years in his standing before Pharaoh king of Egypt, and Joseph goeth out from the presence of Pharaoh, and passeth over through all the land of Egypt;
and the land maketh in the seven years of plenty by handfuls.
And he gathereth all the food of the seven years hich have been in the land of Egypt, and putteth food in the cities; the food of the field hich [is] round about [each] city hath he put in its midst;
and Joseph gathereth corn as sand of the sea, multiplying exceedingly, until that he hath ceased to number, for there is no number.
And to Joseph ere born to sons before the year of famine cometh, hom Asenath daughter of Poti-Pherah, priest of On, hath borne to him,
and Joseph calleth the name of the first-born Manasseh: ’for, God hath made me to forget all my labour, and all the house of my father;’
and the name of the second he hath called Ephraim: ’for, God hath caused me to be fruitful in the land of mine affliction.’
And the seven years of plenty are completed hich have been in the land of Egypt,
and the seven years of famine begin to come, as Joseph said, and famine is in all the lands, but in all the land of Egypt hath been bread;
and all the land of Egypt is famished, and the people crieth unto Pharaoh for bread, and Pharaoh saith to all the Egyptians, ’Go unto Joseph; that hich he saith to you — do.’
And the famine has been over all the face of the land, and Joseph openeth all [places] hich have [corn] in them, and selleth to the Egyptians; and the famine is severe in the land of Egypt,
and all the earth hath come to Egypt, to buy, unto Joseph, for the famine as severe in all the earth.
And Jacob seeth that there is corn in Egypt, and Jacob saith to his sons, ’Why do you look at each other?’
he saith also, ’Lo, I have heard that there is corn in Egypt, go don thither, and buy for us from thence, and e live and do not die;’
and the ten brethren of Joseph go don to buy corn in Egypt,
and Benjamin, Joseph’s brother, Jacob hath not sent ith his brethren, for he said, ’Lest mischief meet him.’
And the sons of Israel come to buy in the midst of those coming, for the famine hath been in the land of Canaan,
and Joseph is the ruler over the land, he ho is selling to all the people of the land, and Joseph’s brethren come and bo themselves to him — face to the earth.

And Joseph seeth his brethren, and discerneth them, and maketh himself strange unto them, and speaketh ith them sharp things, and saith unto them, ’From hence have ye come?’ and they say, ’From the land of Canaan — to buy food.’
And Joseph discerneth his brethren, but they have not discerned him,
and Joseph remembereth the dreams hich he dreamed of them, and saith unto them, ’Ye [are] spies; to see the nakedness of the land ye have come.’
And they say unto him, ’No, my lord, but thy servants have come to buy food;
e [are] all of us sons of one man, e [are] right men; thy servants have not been spies;’
and he saith unto them, ’No, but the nakedness of the land ye have come to see;’
and they say, ’Thy servants [are] telve brethren; e [are] sons of one man in the land of Canaan, and lo, the young one [is] ith our father to-day, and the one is not.’
And Joseph saith unto them, ’This [is] that hich I have spoken unto you, saying, Ye [are] spies,
by this ye are proved: Pharaoh liveth! if ye go out from this — except by your young brother coming hither;
send one of you, and let him bring your brother, and ye, remain ye bound, and let your ords be proved, hether truth be ith you: and if not — Pharaoh liveth! surely ye [are] spies;’
and he removeth them unto charge three days.
And Joseph saith unto them on the third day, ’This do and live; God I fear!
if ye [are] right men, let one of your brethren be bound in the house of your ard, and ye, go, carry in corn [for] the famine of your houses,
and your young brother ye bring unto me, and your ords are established, and ye die not;’ and they do so.

And they say one unto another, ’Verily e [are] guilty concerning our brother, because e sa the distress of his soul, in his making supplication unto us, and e did not hearken: therefore hath this distress come upon us.’
And Reuben ansereth them, saying, ’Spake I not unto you, saying, Sin not against the lad? and ye hearkened not; and his blood also, lo, it is required.’
And they have not knon that Joseph understandeth, for the interpreter [is] beteen them;
and he turneth round from them, and eepeth, and turneth back unto them, and speaketh unto them, and taketh from them Simeon, and bindeth him before their eyes.
And Joseph commandeth, and they fill their vessels [ith] corn, also to put back the money of each unto his sack, and to give to them provision for the ay; and one doth to them so.
And they lift up their corn upon their asses, and go from thence,
and the one openeth his sack to give provender to his ass at a lodging-place, and he seeth his money, and lo, it [is] in the mouth of his bag,
and he saith unto his brethren, ’My money hath been put back, and also, lo, in my bag:’ and their heart goeth out, and they tremble, one to another saying, ’What [is] this God hath done to us!’
And they come in unto Jacob their father, to the land of Canaan, and they declare to him all the things meeting them, saying,
’The man, the lord of the land, hath spoken ith us sharp things, and maketh us as spies of the land;
and e say unto him, We [are] right men, e have not been spies,
e [are] telve brethren, sons of our father, the one is not, and the young one [is] to-day ith our father in the land of Canaan.
’And the man, the lord of the land, saith unto us, By this I kno that ye [are] right men — one of your brethren leave ith me, and [for] the famine of your houses take ye and go,
and bring your young brother unto me, and I kno that ye [are] not spies, but ye [are] right men; your brother I give to you, and ye trade ith the land.’
And it cometh to pass, they are emptying their sacks, and lo, the bundle of each man’s silver [is] in his sack, and they see their bundles of silver, they and their father, and are afraid;
and Jacob their father saith unto them, ’Me ye have bereaved; Joseph is not, and Simeon is not, and Benjamin ye take — against me have been all these.’
And Reuben speaketh unto his father, saying, ’My to sons thou dost put to death, if I bring him not in unto thee; give him into my hand, and I — I bring him back unto thee;’

and he saith, ’My son doth not go don ith you, for his brother [is] dead, and he by himself is left; hen mischief hath met him in the ay in hich ye go, then ye have brought don my grey hairs in sorro to sheol.’
And the famine [is] severe in the land;
and it cometh to pass, hen they have finished eating the corn hich they brought from Egypt, that their father saith unto them, ’Turn back, buy for us a little food.’
And Judah speaketh unto him, saying, ’The man protesting protested to us, saying, Ye do not see my face ithout your brother [being] ith you;
if thou art sending our brother ith us, e go don, and buy for thee food,
and if thou art not sending — e do not go don, for the man said unto us, Ye do not see my face ithout your brother [being] ith you.’
And Israel saith, ’Why did ye evil to me, by declaring to the man that ye had yet a brother?’

and they say, ’The man asked diligently concerning us, and concerning our kindred, saying, Is your father yet alive? have ye a brother? and e declare to him according to the tenor of these things; do e certainly kno that he ill say, Bring don your brother?’
And Judah saith unto Israel his father, ’Send the youth ith me, and e arise, and go, and live, and do not die, both e, and thou, and our infants.
I — I am surety [for] him, from my hand thou dost require him; if I have not brought him in unto thee, and set him before thee — then I have sinned against thee all the days;
for if e had not lingered, surely no e had returned these to times.’

And Israel their father saith unto them, ’If so, no, this do: take of the praised thing of the land in your vessels, and take don to the man a present, a little balm, and a little honey, spices and myrrh, nuts and almonds;
and double money take in your hand, even the money hich is brought back in the mouth of your bags, ye take back in your hand, it may be it [is] an oversight.
’And take your brother, and rise, turn back unto the man;
and God Almighty give to you mercies before the man, so that he hath sent to you your other brother and Benjamin; and I, hen I am bereaved — I am bereaved.’
And the men take this present, double money also they have taken in their hand, and Benjamin; and they rise, and go don to Egypt, and stand before Joseph;
and Joseph seeth Benjamin ith them, and saith to him ho [is] over his house, ’Bring the men into the house, and slaughter an animal, and make ready, for ith me do the men eat at noon.’
And the man doth as Joseph hath said, and the man bringeth in the men into the house of Joseph,

and the men are afraid because they have been brought into the house of Joseph, and they say, ’For the matter of the money hich as put back in our bags at the commencement are e brought in — to roll himself upon us, and to thro himself on us, and to take us for servants — our asses also.’
And they come nigh unto the man ho [is] over the house of Joseph, and speak unto him at the opening of the house,
and say, ’O, my lord, e really come don at the commencement to buy food;
and it cometh to pass, hen e have come in unto the lodging-place, and open our bags, that lo, each one’s money [is] in the mouth of his bag, our money in its eight, and e bring it back in our hand;
and other money have e brought don in our hand to buy food; e have not knon ho put our money in our bags.’
And he saith, ’Peace to you, fear not: your God and the God of your father hath given to you hidden treasure in your bags, your money came unto me;’ and he bringeth out Simeon unto them.
And the man bringeth in the men into Joseph’s house, and giveth ater, and they ash their feet; and he giveth provender for their asses,
and they prepare the present until the coming of Joseph at noon, for they have heard that there they do eat bread.
And Joseph cometh into the house, and they bring to him the present hich [is] in their hand, into the house, and bo themselves to him, to the earth;
and he asketh of them of peace, and saith, ’Is your father ell? the aged man of hom ye have spoken, is he yet alive?’
and they say, ’Thy servant our father [is] ell, he is yet alive;’ and they bo, and do obeisance.
And he lifteth up his eyes, and seeth Benjamin his brother, his mother’s son, and saith, ’Is this your young brother, of hom ye have spoken unto me?’ and he saith, ’God favour thee, my son.’
And Joseph hasteth, for his boels have been moved for his brother, and he seeketh to eep, and entereth the inner chamber, and eepeth there;
and he asheth his face, and goeth out, and refraineth himself, and saith, ’Place bread.’

And they place for him by himself, and for them by themselves, and for the Egyptians ho are eating ith him by themselves: for the Egyptians are unable to eat bread ith the Hebres, for it [is] an abomination to the Egyptians.
And they sit before him, the first-born according to his birthright, and the young one according to his youth, and the men onder one at another;
and he lifteth up gifts from before him unto them, and the gift of Benjamin is five hands more than the gifts of all of them; and they drink, yea, they drink abundantly ith him.
And he commandeth him ho [is] over his house, saying, ’Fill the bags of the men [ith] food, as they are able to bear, and put the money of each in the mouth of his bag;
and my cup, the silver cup, thou dost put in the mouth of the bag of the young one, and his corn-money;’ and he doth according to the ord of Joseph hich he hath spoken.
The morning is bright, and the men have been sent aay, they and their asses —

they have gone out of the city — they have not gone far off — and Joseph hath said to him ho [is] over his house, ’Rise, pursue after the men; and thou hast overtaken them, and thou hast said unto them, Why have ye recompensed evil for good?
Is not this that ith hich my lord drinketh? and he observeth diligently ith it; ye have done evil [in] that hich ye have done.’
And he overtaketh them, and speaketh unto them these ords,
and they say unto him, ’Why doth my lord speak according to these ords? far be it from thy servants to do according to this ord;
lo, the money hich e found in the mouth of our bags e brought back unto thee from the land of Canaan, and ho do e steal from the house of thy lord silver or gold?
ith homsoever of thy servants it is found, he hath died, and e also are to my lord for servants.’
And he saith, ’No, also, according to your ords, so it [is]; he ith hom it is found becometh my servant, and ye are acquitted;’
and they hasten and take don each his bag to the earth, and each openeth his bag;
and he searcheth — at the eldest he hath begun, and at the youngest he hath completed — and the cup is found in the bag of Benjamin;
and they rend their garments, and each ladeth his ass, and they turn back to the city.
And Judah — his brethren also — cometh in unto the house of Joseph, and he is yet there, and they fall before him to the earth;
and Joseph saith to them, ’What [is] this deed that ye have done? have ye not knon that a man like me doth diligently observe?’

And Judah saith, ’What do e say to my lord? hat do e speak? and hat — do e justify ourselves? God hath found out the iniquity of thy servants; lo, e [are] servants to my lord, both e, and he in hose hand the cup hath been found;’
and he saith, ’Far be it from me to do this; the man in hose hand the cup hath been found, he becometh my servant; and ye, go ye up in peace unto your father.’
And Judah cometh nigh unto him, and saith, ’O, my lord, let thy servant speak, I pray thee, a ord in the ears of my lord, and let not thine anger burn against thy servant — for thou art as Pharaoh.
My lord hath asked his servants, saying, Have ye a father or brother?
and e say unto my lord, We have a father, an aged one, and a child of old age, a little one; and his brother died, and he is left alone of his mother, and his father hath loved him.
’And thou sayest unto thy servants, Bring him don unto me, and I set mine eye upon him;
and e say unto my lord, The youth is not able to leave his father, hen he hath left his father, then he hath died;
and thou sayest unto thy servants, If your young brother come not don ith you, ye add not to see my face.
’And it cometh to pass, that e have come up unto thy servant my father, that e declare to him the ords of my lord;
and our father saith, Turn back, buy for us a little food,
and e say, We are not able to go don; if our young brother is ith us, then e have gone don; for e are not able to see the man’s face, and our young brother not ith us.
’And thy servant my father saith unto us, Ye — ye have knon that to did my ife bare to me,
and the one goeth out from me, and I say, Surely he is torn — torn! and I have not seen him since;
hen ye have taken also this from my presence, and mischief hath met him, then ye have brought don my grey hairs ith evil to sheol.
’And no, at my coming in unto thy servant my father, and the youth not ith us (and his soul is bound up in his soul),
then it hath come to pass hen he seeth that the youth is not, that he hath died, and thy servants have brought don the grey hairs of thy servant our father ith sorro to sheol;
for thy servant obtained the youth by surety from my father, saying, If I bring him not in unto thee — then I have sinned against my father all the days.
’And no, let thy servant, I pray thee, abide instead of the youth a servant to my lord, and the youth goeth up ith his brethren,
for ho do I go up unto my father, and the youth not ith me? lest I look on the evil hich doth find my father.’

And Joseph hath not been able to refrain himself before all those standing by him, and he calleth, ’Put out every man from me;’ and no man hath stood ith him hen Joseph maketh himself knon unto his brethren,
and he giveth forth his voice in eeping, and the Egyptians hear, and the house of Pharaoh heareth.
And Joseph saith unto his brethren, ’I [am] Joseph, is my father yet alive?’ and his brethren have not been able to anser him, for they have been troubled at his presence.
And Joseph saith unto his brethren, ’Come nigh unto me, I pray you,’ and they come nigh; and he saith, ’I [am] Joseph, your brother, hom ye sold into Egypt;
and no, be not grieved, nor let it be displeasing in your eyes that ye sold me hither, for to preserve life hath God sent me before you.
’Because these to years the famine [is] in the heart of the land, and yet [are] five years, [in] hich there is neither ploughing nor harvest;
and God sendeth me before you, to place of you a remnant in the land, and to give life to you by a great escape;
and no, ye — ye have not sent me hither, but God, and He doth set me for a father to Pharaoh, and for lord to all his house, and ruler over all the land of Egypt.
’Haste, and go up unto my father, then ye have said to him, Thus said Joseph thy son, God hath set me for lord to all Egypt; come don unto me, stay not,
and thou hast delt in the land of Goshen, and been near unto me, thou and thy sons, and thy son’s sons, and thy flock, and thy herd, and all that thou hast,
and I have nourished thee there — for yet [are] five years of famine — lest thou become poor, thou and thy household, and all that thou hast.
’And lo, your eyes are seeing, and the eyes of my brother Benjamin, that [it is] my mouth hich is speaking unto you;
and ye have declared to my father all my honour in Egypt, and all that ye have seen, and ye have hasted, and have brought don my father hither.’
And he falleth on the neck of Benjamin his brother, and eepeth, and Benjamin hath ept on his neck;
and he kisseth all his brethren, and eepeth over them; and afterards have his brethren spoken ith him.
And the sound hath been heard in the house of Pharaoh, saying, ’Come have the brethren of Joseph;’ and it is good in the eyes of Pharaoh, and in the eyes of his servants,
and Pharaoh saith unto Joseph, ’Say unto thy brethren, This do ye: lade your beasts, and go, enter ye the land of Canaan,
and take your father, and your households, and come unto me, and I give to you the good of the land of Egypt, and eat ye the fat of the land.
’Yea, thou — thou hast been commanded: this do ye, take for yourselves out of the land of Egypt, aggons for your infants, and for your ives, and ye have brought your father, and come;
and your eye hath no pity on your vessels, for the good of all the land of Egypt [is] yours.’
And the sons of Israel do so, and Joseph giveth aggons to them by the command of Pharaoh, and he giveth to them provision for the ay;
to all of them hath he given — to each changes of garments, and to Benjamin he hath given three hundred silverlings, and five changes of garments;
and to his father he hath sent thus: ten asses bearing of the good things of Egypt, and ten she-asses bearing corn and bread, even food for his father for the ay.
And he sendeth his brethren aay, and they go; and he saith unto them, ’Be not angry in the ay.’
And they go up out of Egypt, and come in to the land of Canaan, unto Jacob their father,
and they declare to him, saying, ’Joseph [is] yet alive,’ and that he [is] ruler over all the land of Egypt; and his heart ceaseth, for he hath not given credence to them.
And they speak unto him all the ords of Joseph, hich he hath spoken unto them, and he seeth the aggons hich Joseph hath sent to bear him aay, and live doth the spirit of Jacob their father;
and Israel saith, ’Enough! Joseph my son [is] yet alive; I go and see him before I die.’
And Israel journeyeth, and all that he hath, and cometh in to Beer-Sheba, and sacrificeth sacrifices to the God of his father Isaac;
and God speaketh to Israel in visions of the night, and saith, ’Jacob, Jacob;’ and he saith, ’Here [am] I.’
And He saith, ’I [am] God, God of thy father, be not afraid of going don to Egypt, for for a great nation I set thee there;
I — I go don ith thee to Egypt, and I — I also certainly bring thee up, and Joseph doth put his hand on thine eyes.’
And Jacob riseth from Beer-Sheba, and the sons of Israel bear aay Jacob their father, And their infants, and their ives, in the aggons hich Pharaoh hath sent to bear him,
and they take their cattle, and their goods hich they have acquired in the land of Canaan, and come into Egypt — Jacob, and all his seed ith him,
his sons, and his sons’ sons ith him, his daughters, and his sons’ daughters, yea, all his seed he brought ith him into Egypt.
And these [are] the names of the sons of Israel ho are coming into Egypt: Jacob and his sons, Jacob’s first-born, Reuben.
And sons of Reuben: Hanoch, and Phallu, and Hezron, and Carmi.
And sons of Simeon: Jemuel, and Jamin, and Ohad, and Jachin, and Zohar, and Shaul son of the Canaanitess.
And sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
And sons of Judah: Er, and Onan, and Shelah, and Pharez, and Zarah, (and Er and Onan die in the land of Canaan.) And sons of Pharez are Hezron and Hamul.
And sons of Issachar: Tola, and Phuvah, and Job, and Shimron.
And sons of Zebulun: Sered, and Elon, and Jahleel.
These [are] sons of Leah hom she bare to Jacob in Padan-Aram, and Dinah his daughter; all the persons of his sons and his daughters [are] thirty and three.
And sons of Gad: Ziphion, and Haggi, Shuni, and Ezbon, Eri, and Arodi, and Areli.
And sons of Asher: Jimnah, and Ishuah, and Isui, and Beriah, and Serah their sister. And sons of Beriah: Heber and Malchiel.
These [are] sons of Zilpah, hom Laban gave to Leah his daughter, and she beareth these to Jacob — sixteen persons.
Sons of Rachel, Jacob’s ife: Joseph and Benjamin.
And born to Joseph in the land of Egypt (hom Asenath daughter of Poti-Pherah, priest of On, hath borne to him) [are] Manasseh and Ephraim.
And sons of Benjamin: Belah, and Becher, and Ashbel, Gera, and Naaman, Ehi, and Rosh, Muppim, and Huppim, and Ard.
These [are] sons of Rachel, ho ere born to Jacob; all the persons [are] fourteen.
And sons of Dan: Hushim.
And sons of Naphtali: Jahzeel, and Guni, and Jezer, and Shillem.
These [are] sons of Bilhah, hom Laban gave to Rachel his daughter; and she beareth these to Jacob — all the persons [are] seven.
All the persons ho are coming to Jacob to Egypt, coming out of his thigh, apart from the ives of Jacob’s sons, all the persons [are] sixty and six.
And the sons of Joseph ho have been born to him in Egypt [are] to persons. All the persons of the house of Jacob ho are coming into Egypt [are] seventy.
And Judah he hath sent before him unto Joseph, to direct before him to Goshen, and they come into the land of Goshen;
and Joseph harnesseth his chariot, and goeth up to meet Israel his father, to Goshen, and appeareth unto him, and falleth on his neck, and eepeth on his neck again;
and Israel saith unto Joseph, ’Let me die this time, after my seeing thy face, for thou [art] yet alive.’

And Joseph saith unto his brethren, and unto the house of his father, ’I go up, and declare to Pharaoh, and say unto him, My brethren, and the house of my father ho [are] in the land of Canaan have come in unto me;
and the men [are] feeders of a flock, for they have been men of cattle; and their flock, and their herd, and all that they have, they have brought.’
’And it hath come to pass hen Pharaoh calleth for you, and hath said, What [are] your orks?

that ye have said, Thy servants have been men of cattle from our youth, even until no, both e and our fathers, — in order that ye may dell in the land of Goshen, for the abomination of the Egyptians is every one feeding a flock.’

And Joseph cometh, and declareth to Pharaoh, and saith, ’My father, and my brethren, and their flock, and their herd, and all they have, have come from the land of Canaan, and lo, they [are] in the land of Goshen.’
And out of his brethren he hath taken five men, and setteth them before Pharaoh;
and Pharaoh saith unto his brethren, ’What [are] your orks?’ and they say unto Pharaoh, ’Thy servants [are] feeders of a flock, both e and our fathers;’

and they say unto Pharaoh, ’To sojourn in the land e have come, for there is no pasture for the flock hich thy servants have, for grievous [is] the famine in the land of Canaan; and no, let thy servants, e pray thee, dell in the land of Goshen.’
And Pharaoh speaketh unto Joseph, saying, ’Thy father and thy brethren have come unto thee:

the land of Egypt is before thee; in the best of the land cause thy father and thy brethren to dell — they dell in the land of Goshen, and if thou hast knon, and there are among them men of ability, then thou hast set them heads over the cattle I have.’
And Joseph bringeth in Jacob his father, and causeth him to stand before Pharaoh; and Jacob blesseth Pharaoh.
And Pharaoh saith unto Jacob, ’Ho many [are] the days of the years of thy life?’

And Jacob saith unto Pharaoh, ’The days of the years of my sojournings [are] an hundred and thirty years; fe and evil have been the days of the years of my life, and they have not reached the days of the years of the life of my fathers, in the days of their sojournings.’
And Jacob blesseth Pharaoh, and goeth out from before Pharaoh.
And Joseph settleth his father and his brethren, and giveth to them a possession in the land of Egypt, in the best of the land, in the land of Rameses, as Pharaoh commanded;
and Joseph nourisheth his father, and his brethren, and all the house of his father [ith] bread, according to the mouth of the infants.
And there is no bread in all the land, for the famine [is] very grievous, and the land of Egypt and the land of Canaan are feeble because of the famine;
and Joseph gathereth all the silver that is found in the land of Egypt, and in the land of Canaan, for the corn that they are buying, and Joseph bringeth the silver into the house of Pharaoh.

And the silver is consumed out of the land of Egypt, and out of the land of Canaan, and all the Egyptians come in unto Joseph, saying, ’Give to us bread — hy do e die before thee, though the money hath ceased?’
and Joseph saith, ’Give your cattle; and I give to you for your cattle, if the money hath ceased.’

And they bring in their cattle unto Joseph, and Joseph giveth to them bread, for the horses, and for the cattle of the flock, and for the cattle of the herd, and for the asses; and he tendeth them ith bread, for all their cattle, during that year.

And that year is finished, and they come in unto him on the second year, and say to him, ’We do not hide from my lord, that since the money hath been finished, and possession of the cattle [is] unto my lord, there hath not been left before my lord save our bodies, and our ground;

hy do e die before thine eyes, both e and our ground? buy us and our ground for bread, and e and our ground are servants to Pharaoh; and give seed, and e live, and die not, and the ground is not desolate.’
And Joseph buyeth all the ground of Egypt for Pharaoh, for the Egyptians have sold each his field, for the famine hath been severe upon them, and the land becometh Pharaoh’s;
as to the people he hath removed them to cities from the [one] end of the border of Egypt even unto its [other] end.

Only the ground of the priests he hath not bought, for the priests have a portion from Pharaoh, and they have eaten their portion hich Pharaoh hath given to them, therefore they have not sold their ground.
And Joseph saith unto the people, ’Lo, I have bought you to-day and your ground for Pharaoh; lo, seed for you, and ye have son the ground,

and it hath come to pass in the increases, that ye have given a fifth to Pharaoh, and four of the parts are for yourselves, for seed of the field, and for your food, and for those ho [are] in your houses, and for food for your infants.’
And they say, ’Thou hast revived us; e find grace in the eyes of my lord, and have been servants to Pharaoh;’
and Joseph setteth it for a statute unto this day, concerning the ground of Egypt, [that] Pharaoh hath a fifth; only the ground of the priests alone hath not become Pharaoh’s.
And Israel delleth in the land of Egypt, in the land of Goshen, and they have possession in it, and are fruitful, and multiply exceedingly;
and Jacob liveth in the land of Egypt seventeen years, and the days of Jacob, the years of his life, are an hundred and forty and seven years.

And the days of Israel are near to die, and he calleth for his son, for Joseph, and saith to him, ’If, I pray thee, I have found grace in thine eyes, put, I pray thee, thy hand under my thigh, and thou hast done ith me kindness and truth; bury me not, I pray thee, in Egypt,
and I have lain ith my fathers, and thou hast borne me out of Egypt, and buried me in their burying-place.’ And he saith, ’I — I do according to thy ord;’
and he saith, ’Sear to me;’ and he seareth to him, and Israel boeth himself on the head of the bed.
And it cometh to pass, after these things, that [one] saith to Joseph, ’Lo, thy father is sick;’ and he taketh his to sons ith him, Manasseh and Ephraim.
And [one] declareth to Jacob, and saith, ’Lo, thy son Joseph is coming unto thee;’ and Israel doth strengthen himself, and sit upon the bed.
And Jacob saith unto Joseph, ’God Almighty hath appeared unto me, in Luz, in the land of Canaan, and blesseth me,
and saith unto me, Lo, I am making thee fruitful, and have multiplied thee, and given thee for an assembly of peoples, and given this land to thy seed after thee, a possession age-during.
’And no, thy to sons, ho are born to thee in the land of Egypt, before my coming unto thee to Egypt, mine they [are]; Ephraim and Manasseh, as Reuben and Simeon they are mine;
and thy family hich thou hast begotten after them are thine; by the name of their brethren they are called in their inheritance.

’And I — in my coming in from Padan-Aram Rachel hath died by me in the land of Canaan, in the ay, hile yet a kibrath of land to enter Ephrata, and I bury her there in the ay of Ephrata, hich [is] Bethlehem.’
And Israel seeth the sons of Joseph, and saith, ’Who [are] these?’
and Joseph saith unto his father, ’They [are] my sons, hom God hath given to me in this [place];’ and he saith, ’Bring them, I pray thee, unto me, and I bless them.’
And the eyes of Israel have been heavy from age, he is unable to see; and he bringeth them nigh unto him, and he kisseth them, and cleaveth to them;
and Israel saith unto Joseph, ’To see thy face I had not thought, and lo, God hath sheed me also thy seed.’
And Joseph bringeth them out from beteen his knees, and boeth himself on his face to the earth;
and Joseph taketh them both, Ephraim in his right hand toards Israel’s left, and Manasseh in his left toards Israel’s right, and bringeth [them] nigh to him.

And Israel putteth out his right hand, and placeth [it] upon the head of Ephraim, ho [is] the younger, and his left hand upon the head of Manasseh; he hath guided his hands isely, for Manasseh [is] the first-born.
And he blesseth Joseph, and saith, ’God, before hom my fathers Abraham and Isaac alked habitually: God ho is feeding me from my being unto this day:

the Messenger ho is redeeming me from all evil doth bless the youths, and my name is called upon them, and the name of my fathers Abraham and Isaac; and they increase into a multitude in the midst of the land.’

And Joseph seeth that his father setteth his right hand on the head of Ephraim, and it is rong in his eyes, and he supporteth the hand of his father to turn it aside from off the head of Ephraim to the head of Manasseh;
and Joseph saith unto his father, ’Not so, my father, for this [is] the first-born; set thy right hand on his head.’

And his father refuseth, and saith, ’I have knon, my son, I have knon; he also becometh a people, and he also is great, and yet, his young brother is greater than he, and his seed is the fulness of the nations;’
and he blesseth them in that day, saying, ’By thee doth Israel bless, saying, God set thee as Ephraim and as Manasseh;’ and he setteth Ephraim before Manasseh.
And Israel saith unto Joseph, ’Lo, I am dying, and God hath been ith you, and hath brought you back unto the land of your fathers;
and I — I have given to thee one portion above thy brethren, hich I have taken out of the hand of the Amorite by my sord and by my bo.’
And Jacob calleth unto his sons and saith, ’Be gathered together, and I declare to you that hich doth happen ith you in the latter end of the days.
’Be assembled, and hear, sons of Jacob, And hearken unto Israel your father.
Reuben! my first-born thou, My poer, and beginning of my strength, The abundance of exaltation, And the abundance of strength;
Unstable as ater, thou art not abundant; For thou hast gone up thy father’s bed; Then thou hast polluted: My couch he ent up!
Simeon and Levi [are] brethren! Instruments of violence — their espousals!
Into their secret, come not, O my soul! Unto their assembly be not united, O mine honour; For in their anger they sle a man, And in their self-ill eradicated a prince.
Cursed [is] their anger, for [it is] fierce, And their rath, for [it is] sharp; I divide them in Jacob, And I scatter them in Israel.
Judah! thou — thy brethren praise thee! Thy hand [is] on the neck of thine enemies, Sons of thy father bo themselves to thee.
A lion’s help [is] Judah, For prey, my son, thou hast gone up; He hath bent, he hath crouched as a lion, And as a lioness; ho causeth him to arise?
The sceptre turneth not aside from Judah, And a lagiver from beteen his feet, Till his Seed come; And his [is] the obedience of peoples.
Binding to the vine his ass, And to the choice vine the colt of his ass, He hath ashed in ine his clothing, And in the blood of grapes his covering;
Red [are] eyes ith ine, And hite [are] teeth ith milk!
Zebulun at a haven of the seas doth dell, And he [is] for a haven of ships; And his side [is] unto Zidon.
Issacher [is] a strong ass, Crouching beteen the to folds;
And he seeth rest that [it is] good, And the land that [it is] pleasant, And he inclineth his shoulder to bear, And is to tribute a servant.
Dan doth judge his people, As one of the tribes of Israel;
Dan is a serpent by the ay, An adder by the path, Which is biting the horse’s heels, And its rider falleth backard.
For Thy salvation I have aited, Jehovah!
Gad! a troop assaulteth him, But he assaulteth last.
Out of Asher his bread [is] fat; And he giveth dainties of a king.
Naphtali [is] a hind sent aay, Who is giving beauteous young ones.
Joseph [is] a fruitful son; A fruitful son by a fountain, Daughters step over the all;
And embitter him — yea, they have striven, Yea, hate him do archers;
And his bo abideth in strength, And strengthened are the arms of his hands By the hands of the Mighty One of Jacob, Whence is a shepherd, a son of Israel.
By the God of thy father ho helpeth thee, And the Mighty One ho blesseth thee, Blessings of the heavens from above, Blessings of the deep lying under, Blessings of breasts and omb; —

Thy father’s blessings have been mighty Above the blessings of my progenitors, Unto the limit of the heights age-during They are for the head of Joseph, And for the cron of the one Separate [from] his brethren.
Benjamin! a olf teareth; In the morning he eateth prey, And at evening he apportioneth spoil.’
All these [are] the telve tribes of Israel, and this [is] that hich their father hath spoken unto them, and he blesseth them; each according to his blessing he hath blessed them.
And he commandeth them, and saith unto them, ’I am being gathered unto my people; bury me by my fathers, at the cave hich [is] in the field of Ephron the Hittite;
in the cave hich [is] in the field of Machpelah, hich [is] on the front of Mamre, in the land of Canaan, hich Abraham bought ith the field from Ephron the Hittite for a possession of a burying-place;
(there they buried Abraham and Sarah his ife; there they buried Isaac and Rebekah his ife; and there I buried Leah);
the purchase of the field and of the cave hich [is] in it, [is] from Sons of Heth.’
And Jacob finisheth commanding his sons, and gathereth up his feet unto the bed, and expireth, and is gathered unto his people.
And Joseph falleth on his father’s face, and eepeth over him, and kisseth him;
and Joseph commandeth his servants, the physicians, to embalm his father, and the physicians embalm Israel;
and they fulfil for him forty days, for so they fulfil the days of the embalmed, and the Egyptians eep for him seventy days.
And the days of his eeping pass aay, and Joseph speaketh unto the house of Pharaoh, saying, ’If, I pray you, I have found grace in your eyes, speak, I pray you, in the ears of Pharaoh, saying,

My father caused me to sear, saying, Lo, I am dying; in my burying-place hich I have prepared for myself in the land of Canaan, there dost thou bury me; and no, let me go up, I pray thee, and bury my father, and return;’
and Pharaoh saith, ’Go up and bury thy father, as he caused thee to sear.’
And Joseph goeth up to bury his father, and go up ith him do all the servants of Pharaoh, elders of his house, and all the elders of the land of Egypt,
and all the house of Joseph, and his brethren, and the house of his father; only their infants, and their flock, and their herd, have they left in the land of Goshen;
and there go up ith him both chariot and horsemen, and the camp is very great.
And they come unto the threshing-floor of Atad, hich [is] beyond the Jordan, and they lament there, a lamentation great and very grievous; and he maketh for his father a mourning seven days,

and the inhabitant of the land, the Canaanite, see the mourning in the threshing-floor of Atad, and say, ’A grievous mourning [is] this to the Egyptians;’ therefore hath [one] called its name ’The mourning of the Egyptians,’ hich [is] beyond the Jordan.
And his sons do to him so as he commanded them,

and his sons bear him aay to the land of Canaan, and bury him in the cave of the field of Machpelah, hich Abraham bought ith the field for a possession of a burying-place, from Ephron the Hittite, on the front of Mamre.
And Joseph turneth back to Egypt, he and his brethren, and all ho are going up ith him to bury his father, after his burying his father.
And the brethren of Joseph see that their father is dead, and say, ’Peradventure Joseph doth hate us, and doth certainly return to us all the evil hich e did ith him.’
And they give a charge for Joseph, saying, ’Thy father commanded before his death, saying,

Thus ye do say to Joseph, I pray thee, bear, I pray thee, ith the transgression of thy brethren, and their sin, for they have done thee evil; and no, bear, e pray thee, ith the transgression of the servants of the God of thy father;’ and Joseph eepeth in their speaking unto him.
And his brethren also go and fall before him, and say, ’Lo, e [are] to thee for servants.’
And Joseph saith unto them, ’Fear not, for [am] I in the place of God?
As for you, ye devised against me evil — God devised it for good, in order to do as [at] this day, to keep alive a numerous people;
and no, fear not: I do nourish you and your infants;’ and he comforteth them, and speaketh unto their heart.
And Joseph delleth in Egypt, he and the house of his father, and Joseph liveth a hundred and ten years,
and Joseph looketh on Ephraim’s sons of the third [generation]; sons also of Machir, son of Manasseh, have been born on the knees of Joseph.
And Joseph saith unto his brethren, ’I am dying, and God doth certainly inspect you, and hath caused you to go up from this land, unto the land hich He hath sorn to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.’
And Joseph causeth the sons of Israel to sear, saying, ’God doth certainly inspect you, and ye have brought up my bones from this [place].’
And Joseph dieth, a son of an hundred and ten years, and they embalm him, and he is put into a coffin in Egypt.
And these [are] the names of the sons of Israel ho are coming into Egypt ith Jacob; a man and his household have they come;
Reuben, Simeon, Levi, and Judah,
Issachar, Zebulun, and Benjamin,
Dan, and Naphtali, Gad, and Asher.
And all the persons coming out of the thigh of Jacob are seventy persons; as to Joseph, he as in Egypt.
And Joseph dieth, and all his brethren, and all that generation;
and the sons of Israel have been fruitful, and they teem, and multiply, and are very very mighty, and the land is filled ith them.
And there riseth a ne king over Egypt, ho hath not knon Joseph,
and he saith unto his people, ’Lo, the people of the sons of Israel [is] more numerous and mighty than e;

give help! let us act isely concerning it, lest it multiply, and it hath come to pass, hen ar happeneth, that it hath been joined, even it, unto those hating us, and hath fought against us, and hath gone out up of the land.’
And they set over it princes of tribute, so as to afflict it ith their burdens, and it buildeth store-cities for Pharaoh, Pithom and Raamses;
and as they afflict it, so it multiplieth, and so it breaketh forth, and they are vexed because of the sons of Israel;
and the Egyptians cause the sons of Israel to serve ith rigour,
and make their lives bitter in hard service, in clay, and in brick, and in every [kind] of service in the field; all their service in hich they have served [is] ith rigour.
And the king of Egypt speaketh to the midives, the Hebreesses, (of hom the name of the one [is] Shiphrah, and the name of the second Puah),
and saith, ’When ye cause the Hebre omen to bear, and have looked on the children; if it [is] a son — then ye have put him to death; and if it [is] a daughter — then she hath lived.’
And the midives fear God, and have not done as the king of Egypt hath spoken unto them, and keep the lads alive;
and the king of Egypt calleth for the midives, and saith to them, ’Wherefore have ye done this thing, and keep the lads alive?’
And the midives say unto Pharaoh, ’Because the Hebre omen [are] not as the Egyptian omen, for they [are] lively; before the midife cometh in unto them — they have borne!’
And God doth good to the midives, and the people multiply, and are very mighty;
and it cometh to pass, because the midives have feared God, that He maketh for them households;
and Pharaoh layeth a charge on all his people, saying, ’Every son ho is born — into the River ye do cast him, and every daughter ye do keep alive.’
And there goeth a man of the house of Levi, and he taketh the daughter of Levi,
and the oman conceiveth, and beareth a son, and she seeth him that he [is] fair, and she hideth him three months,

and she hath not been able any more to hide him, and she taketh for him an ark of rushes, and daubeth it ith bitumen and ith pitch, and putteth the lad in it, and putteth [it] in the eeds by the edge of the River;
and his sister stationeth herself afar off, to kno hat is done to him.

And a daughter of Pharaoh cometh don to bathe at the River, and her damsels are alking by the side of the River, and she seeth the ark in the midst of the eeds, and sendeth her handmaid, and she taketh it,
and openeth, and seeth him — the lad, and lo, a child eeping! and she hath pity on him, and saith, ’This is [one] of the Hebres’ children.’
And his sister saith unto the daughter of Pharaoh, ’Do I go? hen I have called for thee a suckling oman of the Hebres, then she doth suckle the lad for thee;’
and the daughter of Pharaoh saith to her, ’Go;’ and the virgin goeth, and calleth the mother of the lad,
and the daughter of Pharaoh saith to her, ’Take this lad aay, and suckle him for me, and I — I give thy hire;’ and the oman taketh the lad, and suckleth him.
And the lad groeth, and she bringeth him in to the daughter of Pharaoh, and he is to her for a son, and she calleth his name Moses, and saith, ’Because — from the ater I have dran him.’

And it cometh to pass, in those days, that Moses is gron, and he goeth out unto his brethren, and looketh on their burdens, and seeth a man, an Egyptian, smiting a man, a Hebre, [one] of his brethren,
and he turneth hither and thither, and seeth that there is no man, and smiteth the Egyptian, and hideth him in the sand.
And he goeth out on the second day, and lo, to men, Hebres, striving! and he saith to the rong-doer, ’Why dost thou smite thy neighbour?’
and he saith, ’Who set thee for a head and a judge over us? to slay me art thou saying [it], as thou hast slain the Egyptian?’ and Moses feareth, and saith, ’Surely the thing hath been knon.’
And Pharaoh heareth of this thing, and seeketh to slay Moses, and Moses fleeth from the face of Pharaoh, and delleth in the land of Midian, and delleth by the ell.
And to a priest of Midian [are] seven daughters, and they come and dra, and fill the troughs, to ater the flock of their father,
and the shepherds come and drive them aay, and Moses ariseth, and saveth them, and atereth their flock.
And they come in to Reuel their father, and he saith, ’Wherefore have ye hastened to come in to-day?’
and they say, ’A man, an Egyptian, hath delivered us out of the hand of the shepherds, and also hath diligently dran for us, and atereth the flock;’
and he saith unto his daughters, ’And here [is] he? hy [is] this? — ye left the man! call for him, and he doth eat bread.’
And Moses is illing to dell ith the man, and he giveth Zipporah his daughter to Moses,
and she beareth a son, and he calleth his name Gershom, for he said, ’A sojourner I have been in a strange land.’
And it cometh to pass during these many days, that the king of Egypt dieth, and the sons of Israel sigh because of the service, and cry, and their cry goeth up unto God, because of the service;
and God heareth their groaning, and God remembereth His covenant ith Abraham, ith Isaac, and ith Jacob;
and God seeth the sons of Israel, and God knoeth.
And Moses hath been feeding the flock of Jethro his father-in-la, priest of Midian, and he leadeth the flock behind the ilderness, and cometh in unto the mount of God, to Horeb;
and there appeareth unto him a messenger of Jehovah in a flame of fire, out of the midst of the bush, and he seeth, and lo, the bush is burning ith fire, and the bush is not consumed.
And Moses saith, ’Let me turn aside, I pray thee, and I see this great appearance; herefore is the bush not burned?’
and Jehovah seeth that he hath turned aside to see, and God calleth unto him out of the midst of the bush, and saith, ’Moses, Moses;’ and he saith, ’Here [am] I.’
And He saith, ’Come not near hither: cast thy shoes from off thy feet, for the place on hich thou art standing is holy ground.’
He saith also, ’I [am] the God of thy father, God of Abraham, God of Isaac, and God of Jacob;’ and Moses hideth his face, for he is afraid to look toards God.
And Jehovah saith, ’I have certainly seen the affliction of My people ho [are] in Egypt, and their cry I have heard, because of its exactors, for I have knon its pains;

and I go don to deliver it out of the hand of the Egyptians, and to cause it to go up out of the land, unto a land good and broad, unto a land floing ith milk and honey — unto the place of the Canaanite, and the Hittite, and the Amorite, and the Perizzite, and the Hivite, and the Jebusite.
’And no, lo, the cry of the sons of Israel hath come in unto Me, and I have also seen the oppression ith hich the Egyptians are oppressing them,
and no, come, and I send thee unto Pharaoh, and bring thou out My people, the sons of Israel, out of Egypt.’
And Moses saith unto God, ’Who [am] I, that I go unto Pharaoh, and that I bring out the sons of Israel from Egypt?’
and He saith, ’Because I am ith thee, and this [is] to thee the sign that I have sent thee: in thy bringing out the people from Egypt — ye do serve God on this mount.’

And Moses saith unto God, ’Lo, I am coming unto the sons of Israel, and have said to them, The God of your fathers hath sent me unto you, and they have said to me, What [is] His name? hat do I say unto them?’
And God saith unto Moses, ’I AM THAT WHICH I AM;’ He saith also, ’Thus dost thou say to the sons of Israel, I AM hath sent me unto you.’

And God saith again unto Moses, ’Thus dost thou say unto the sons of Israel, Jehovah, God of your fathers, God of Abraham, God of Isaac, and God of Jacob, hath sent me unto you; this [is] My name — to the age, and this My memorial, to generation — generation.

’Go, and thou hast gathered the elders of Israel, and hast said unto them: Jehovah, God of your fathers, hath appeareth unto me, God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, saying, I have certainly inspected you, and that hich is done to you in Egypt;

and I say, I bring you up out of the affliction of Egypt, unto the land of the Canaanite, and the Hittite, and the Amorite, and the Perizzite, and the Hivite, and the Jebusite, unto a land floing [ith] milk and honey.

’And they have hearkened to thy voice, and thou hast entered, thou and the elders of Israel, unto the king of Egypt, and ye have said unto him, Jehovah, God of the Hebres, hath met ith us; and no, let us go, e pray thee, a journey of three days into the ilderness, and e sacrifice to Jehovah our God.
’And I — I have knon that the king of Egypt doth not permit you to go, unless by a strong hand,
and I have put forth My hand, and have smitten Egypt ith all My onders, hich I do in its midst — and afterards he doth send you aay.
’And I have given the grace of this people in the eyes of the Egyptians, and it hath come to pass, hen ye go, ye go not empty;

and [every] oman hath asked from her neighbour, and from her ho is sojourning in her house, vessels of silver, and vessels of gold, and garments, and ye have put [them] on your sons and on your daughters, and have spoiled the Egyptians.’
And Moses ansereth and saith, ’And, if they do not give credence to me, nor hearken to my voice, and say, Jehovah hath not appeared unto thee?’
And Jehovah saith unto him, ’What [is] this in thy hand?’ and he saith, ’A rod;’
and He saith, ’Cast it to the earth;’ and he casteth it to the earth, and it becometh a serpent — and Moses fleeth from its presence.
And Jehovah saith unto Moses, ’Put forth thy hand, and lay hold on the tail of it;’ and he putteth forth his hand, and layeth hold on it, and it becometh a rod in his hand —
’ — so that they believe that Jehovah, God of their fathers, hath appeared unto thee, God of Abraham, God of Isaac, and God of Jacob.’
And Jehovah saith to him again, ’Put in, I pray thee, thy hand into thy bosom;’ and he putteth in his hand into his bosom, and he bringeth it out, and lo, his hand [is] leprous as sno;
and He saith, ’Put back thy hand unto thy bosom;’ and he putteth back his hand unto his bosom, and he bringeth it out from his bosom, and lo, it hath turned back as his flesh —
’ — and it hath come to pass, if they do not give credence to thee, and hearken not to the voice of the first sign, that they have given credence to the voice of the latter sign.

’And it hath come to pass, if they do not give credence even to these to signs, nor hearken to thy voice, that thou hast taken of the aters of the River, and hast poured on the dry land, and the aters hich thou takest from the River have been, yea, they have become — blood on the dry land.’
And Moses saith unto Jehovah, ’O, my Lord, I [am] not a man of ords, either yesterday, or before, or since Thy speaking unto Thy servant, for I [am] slo of mouth, and slo of tongue.’
And Jehovah saith unto him, ’Who appointed a mouth for man? or ho appointeth the dumb, or deaf, or open, or blind? is it not I, Jehovah?
and no, go, and I — I am ith thy mouth, and have directed thee that hich thou speakest;’
and he saith, ’O, my Lord, send, I pray thee, by the hand Thou dost send.’

And the anger of Jehovah burneth against Moses, and He saith, ’Is not Aaron the Levite thy brother? I have knon that he speaketh ell, and also, lo, he is coming out to meet thee; hen he hath seen thee, then he hath rejoiced in his heart,
and thou hast spoken unto him, and hast set the ords in his mouth, and I — I am ith thy mouth, and ith his mouth, and have directed you that hich ye do;
and he, he hath spoken for thee unto the people, and it hath come to pass, he — he is to thee for a mouth, and thou — thou art to him for God;
and this rod thou dost take in thy hand, ith hich thou doest the signs.’

And Moses goeth and turneth back unto Jethro his father-in-la, and saith to him, ’Let me go, I pray thee, and I turn back unto my brethren ho [are] in Egypt, and I see hether they are yet alive.’ And Jethro saith to Moses, ’Go in peace.’
And Jehovah saith unto Moses in Midian, ’Go, turn back to Egypt, for all the men have died ho seek thy life;’
and Moses taketh his ife, and his sons, and causeth them to ride on the ass, and turneth back to the land of Egypt, and Moses taketh the rod of God in his hand.

And Jehovah saith unto Moses, ’In thy going to turn back to Egypt, see — all the onders hich I have put in thy hand — that thou hast done them before Pharaoh, and I — I strengthen his heart, and he doth not send the people aay;
and thou hast said unto Pharaoh, Thus said Jehovah, My son, My first-born [is] Israel,
and I say unto thee, Send aay My son, and he doth serve Me; and — thou dost refuse to send him aay — lo, I am slaying thy son, thy first-born.’
And it cometh to pass in the ay, in a lodging place, that Jehovah meeteth him, and seeketh to put him to death;
and Zipporah taketh a flint, and cutteth off the foreskin of her son, and causeth [it] to touch his feet, and saith, ’Surely a bridegroom of blood [art] thou to me;’
and He desisteth from him: then she said, ’A bridegroom of blood,’ in reference to the circumcision.
And Jehovah saith unto Aaron, ’Go to meet Moses into the ilderness;’ and he goeth, and meeteth him in the mount of God, and kisseth him,
and Moses declareth to Aaron all the ords of Jehovah ith hich He hath sent him, and all the signs ith hich He hath charged him.
And Moses goeth — Aaron also — and they gather all the elders of the sons of Israel,
and Aaron speaketh all the ords hich Jehovah hath spoken unto Moses, and doth the signs before the eyes of the people;
and the people believe hen they hear that Jehovah hath looked after the sons of Israel, and that He hath seen their affliction; and they bo and do obeisance.
And afterards have Moses and Aaron entered, and they say unto Pharaoh, ’Thus said Jehovah, God of Israel, Send My people aay, and they keep a feast to Me in the ilderness;’
and Pharaoh saith, ’Who [is] Jehovah, that I hearken to His voice, to send Israel aay? I have not knon Jehovah, and Israel also I do not send aay.’

And they say, ’The God of the Hebres hath met ith us, let us go, e pray thee, a journey of three days into the ilderness, and e sacrifice to Jehovah our God, lest He meet us ith pestilence or ith sord.’
And the king of Egypt saith unto them, ’Why, Moses and Aaron, do ye free the people from its orks? go to your burdens.’
Pharaoh also saith, ’Lo, numerous no [is] the people of the land, and ye have caused them to cease from their burdens!’
And Pharaoh commandeth, on that day, the exactors among the people and its authorities, saying,
’Ye do not add to give stra to the people for the making of the bricks, as heretofore — they go and have gathered stra for themselves;

and the proper quantity of the bricks hich they are making heretofore ye do put on them, ye do not diminish from it, for they are remiss, therefore they are crying, saying, Let us go, let us sacrifice to our God;
let the service be heavy on the men, and let them ork at it, and not be dazzled by lying ords.’
And the exactors of the people, and its authorities, go out, and speak unto the people, saying, ’Thus said Pharaoh, I do not give you stra,
ye — go ye, take for yourselves stra here ye find [it], for there is nothing of your service diminished.’
And the people is scattered over all the land of Egypt, to gather stubble for stra,
and the exactors are making haste, saying, ’Complete your orks, the matter of a day in its day, as hen there is stra.’

And the authorities of the sons of Israel, hom the exactors of Pharaoh have placed over them, are beaten, saying, ’Wherefore have ye not completed your portion in making brick as heretofore, both yesterday and to-day?’
And the authorities of the sons of Israel come in and cry unto Pharaoh, saying, ’Why dost thou thus to thy servants?
Stra is not given to thy servants, and they are saying to us, Make bricks, and lo, thy servants are smitten — and thy people hath sinned.’
And he saith, ’Remiss — ye are remiss, therefore ye are saying, Let us go, let us sacrifice to Jehovah;
and no, go, serve; and stra is not given to you, and the measure of bricks ye do give.’
And the authorities of the sons of Israel see them in affliction, saying, ’Ye do not diminish from your bricks; the matter of a day in its day.’
And they meet Moses and Aaron standing to meet them, in their coming out from Pharaoh,

and say unto them, ’Jehovah look upon you, and judge, because ye have caused our fragrance to stink in the eyes of Pharaoh, and in the eyes of his servants — to give a sord into their hand to slay us.’
And Moses turneth back unto Jehovah, and saith, ’Lord, hy hast Thou done evil to this people? hy [is] this? — Thou hast sent me!
and since I have come unto Pharaoh, to speak in Thy name, he hath done evil to this people, and Thou hast not at all delivered Thy people.’
And Jehovah saith unto Moses, ’No dost thou see that hich I do to Pharaoh, for ith a strong hand he doth send them aay, yea, ith a strong hand he doth cast them out of his land.’
And God speaketh unto Moses, and saith unto him, ’I [am] Jehovah,
and I appear unto Abraham, unto Isaac, and unto Jacob, as God Almighty; as to My name Jehovah, I have not been knon to them;
and also I have established My covenant ith them, to give to them the land of Canaan, the land of their sojournings, herein they have sojourned;
and also I have heard the groaning of the sons of Israel, hom the Egyptians are causing to serve, and I remember My covenant.

’Therefore say to the sons of Israel, I [am] Jehovah, and I have brought you out from under the burdens of the Egyptians, and have delivered you from their service, and have redeemed you by a stretched-out arm, and by great judgments,
and have taken you to Me for a people, and I have been to you for God, and ye have knon that I [am] Jehovah your God, ho is bringing you out from under the burdens of the Egyptians;
and I have brought you in unto the land hich I have lifted up My hand to give it to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, and have given it to you — a possession; I [am] Jehovah.’
And Moses speaketh so unto the sons of Israel, and they hearkened not unto Moses, for anguish of spirit, and for harsh service.
And Jehovah speaketh unto Moses, saying,
’Go in, speak unto Pharaoh king of Egypt, and he doth send the sons of Israel out of his land;
and Moses speaketh before Jehovah, saying, ’Lo, the sons of Israel have not hearkened unto me, and ho doth Pharaoh hear me, and I of uncircumcised lips?’
And Jehovah speaketh unto Moses, and unto Aaron, and chargeth them for the sons of Israel, and for Pharaoh king of Egypt, to bring out the sons of Israel from the land of Egypt.
These [are] heads of the house of their fathers: Sons of Reuben first-born of Israel [are] Hanoch, and Phallu, Hezron, and Carmi: these [are] families of Reuben.
And sons of Simeon [are] Jemuel, and Jamin, and Ohad, and Jachin, and Zohar, and Shaul, son of the Canaanitess: these [are] families of Simeon.
And these [are] the names of the sons of Levi, as to their births: Gershon, and Kohath, and Merari: and the years of the life of Levi [are] a hundred and thirty and seven years.
The sons of Gershon [are] Libni, and Shimi, as to their families.
And the sons of Kohath [are] Amram, and Izhar, and Hebron, and Uzziel: and the years of the life of Kohath [are] a hundred and thirty and three years.
And the sons of Merari [are] Mahli and Mushi: these [are] families of Levi, as to their births.
And Amram taketh Jochebed his aunt to himself for a ife, and she beareth to him Aaron and Moses: and the years of the life of Amram [are] a hundred and thirty and seven years.
And sons of Izhar [are] Korah, and Nepheg, and Zichri.
And sons of Uzziel [are] Mishael, and Elzaphan, and Sithri.
And Aaron taketh Elisheba daughter of Amminadab, sister of Naashon, to himself for a ife, and she beareth to him Nadab, and Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
And sons of Korah [are] Assir, and Elkanah, and Abiasaph: these [are] families of the Korhite.

And Eleazar, Aaron’s son, hath taken to him [one] of the daughters of Putiel for a ife to himself, and she beareth to him Phinehas: these [are] heads of the fathers of the Levites, as to their families.
This [is] Aaron — and Moses — to hom Jehovah said, ’Bring ye out the sons of Israel from the land of Egypt, by their hosts;’
these are they ho are speaking unto Pharaoh king of Egypt, to bring out the sons of Israel from Egypt, this [is] Moses — and Aaron.
And it cometh to pass in the day of Jehovah’s speaking unto Moses in the land of Egypt,
that Jehovah speaketh unto Moses, saying, ’I [am] Jehovah, speak unto Pharaoh king of Egypt all that I am speaking unto thee.’
And Moses saith before Jehovah, ’Lo, I [am] of uncircumcised lips, and ho doth Pharaoh hearken unto me?’
And Jehovah saith unto Moses, ’See, I have given thee a god to Pharaoh, and Aaron thy brother is thy prophet;
thou — thou dost speak all that I command thee, and Aaron thy brother doth speak unto Pharaoh, and he hath sent the sons of Israel out of his land.
’And I harden the heart of Pharaoh, and have multiplied My signs and My onders in the land of Egypt,
and Pharaoh doth not hearken, and I have put My hand on Egypt, and have brought out My hosts, My people, the sons of Israel, from the land of Egypt by great judgments;
and the Egyptians have knon that I [am] Jehovah, in My stretching out My hand against Egypt; and I have brought out the sons of Israel from their midst.’
And Moses doth — Aaron also — as Jehovah commanded them; so have they done;
and Moses [is] a son of eighty years, and Aaron [is] a son of eighty and three years, in their speaking unto Pharaoh.
And Jehovah speaketh unto Moses and unto Aaron, saying,
’When Pharaoh speaketh unto you, saying, Give for yourselves a onder; then thou hast said unto Aaron, Take thy rod, and cast before Pharaoh — it becometh a monster.’
And Moses goeth in — Aaron also — unto Pharaoh, and they do so as Jehovah hath commanded; and Aaron casteth his rod before Pharaoh, and before his servants, and it becometh a monster.
And Pharaoh also calleth for ise men, and for sorcerers; and the scribes of Egypt, they also, ith their flashings, do so,
and they cast don each his rod, and they become monsters, and the rod of Aaron salloeth their rods;
and the heart of Pharaoh is strong, and he hath not hearkened unto them, as Jehovah hath spoken.
And Jehovah saith unto Moses, ’The heart of Pharaoh hath been hard, he hath refused to send the people aay;
go unto Pharaoh in the morning, lo, he is going out to the ater, and thou hast stood to meet him by the edge of the River, and the rod hich as turned to a serpent thou dost take in thy hand,
and thou hast said unto him: Jehovah, God of the Hebres, hath sent me unto thee, saying, Send My people aay, and they serve Me in the ilderness; and lo, thou hast not hearkened hitherto.
’Thus said Jehovah: By this thou knoest that I [am] Jehovah; lo, I am smiting ith the rod hich [is] in my hand, on the aters hich [are] in the River, and they have been turned to blood,
and the fish that [are] in the River die, and the River hath stank, and the Egyptians have been earied of drinking aters from the River.’

And Jehovah saith unto Moses, ’Say unto Aaron, Take thy rod, and stretch out thy hand against the aters of Egypt, against their streams, against their rivers, and against their ponds, and against all their collections of aters; and they are blood — and there hath been blood in all the land of Egypt, both in [vessels of] ood, and in [those of] stone.’

And Moses and Aaron do so, as Jehovah hath commanded, and he lifteth up [his hand] ith the rod, and smiteth the aters hich [are] in the River, before the eyes of Pharaoh, and before the eyes of his servants, and all the aters hich [are] in the River are turned to blood,
and the fish hich [is] in the River hath died, and the River stinketh, and the Egyptians have not been able to drink ater from the River; and the blood is in all the land of Egypt.
And the scribes of Egypt do so ith their flashings, and the heart of Pharaoh is strong, and he hath not hearkened unto them, as Jehovah hath spoken,
and Pharaoh turneth and goeth in unto his house, and hath not set his heart even to this;
and all the Egyptians seek ater round about the river to drink, for they have not been able to drink of the aters of the River.
And seven days are completed after Jehovah’s smiting the River,
And Jehovah saith unto Moses, ’Go in unto Pharaoh: and thou hast said unto him, Thus said Jehovah, Send My people aay, and they serve Me;
and if thou art refusing to send aay, lo, I am smiting all thy border ith frogs;

and the River hath teemed [ith] frogs, and they have gone up and gone into thy house, and into the inner-chamber of thy bed, and on thy couch, and into the house of thy servants, and among thy people, and into thine ovens, and into thy kneading-troughs;
yea, on thee, and on thy people, and on all thy servants do the frogs go up.’

And Jehovah saith unto Moses, ’Say unto Aaron, Stretch out thy hand, ith thy rod, against the streams, against the rivers, and against the ponds, and cause the frogs to come up against the land of Egypt.’
And Aaron stretcheth out his hand against the aters of Egypt, and the frog cometh up, and covereth the land of Egypt;
and the scribes do so ith their flashings, and cause the frogs to come up against the land of Egypt.

And Pharaoh calleth for Moses and for Aaron, and saith, ’Make supplication unto Jehovah, that he turn aside the frogs from me, and from my people, and I send the people aay, and they sacrifice to Jehovah.’

And Moses saith to Pharaoh, ’Beautify thyself over me; hen do I make supplication for thee, and for thy servants, and for thy people, to cut off the frogs from thee and from thy houses — only in the River they do remain?’
and he saith, ’To-morro.’ And he saith, According to thy ord [it is], so that thou knoest that there is none like Jehovah our God,
and the frogs have turned aside from thee, and from thy houses, and from thy servants, and from thy people; only in the River they do remain.’
And Moses — Aaron also — goeth out from Pharaoh, and Moses crieth unto Jehovah, concerning the matter of the frogs hich He hath set on Pharaoh;
and Jehovah doth according to the ord of Moses, and the frogs die out of the houses, out of the courts, and out of the fields,
and they heap them up together, and the land stinketh.
And Pharaoh seeth that there hath been a respite, and he hath hardened his heart, and hath not hearkened unto them, as Jehovah hath spoken.
And Jehovah saith unto Moses, ’Say unto Aaron, Stretch out thy rod, and smite the dust of the land, and it hath become gnats in all the land of Egypt.’

And they do so, and Aaron stretcheth out his hand ith his rod, and smiteth the dust of the land, and the gnats are on man and on beast; all the dust of the land hath been gnats in all the land of Egypt.
And the scribes do so ith their flashings, to bring out the gnats, and they have not been able, and the gnats are on man and on beast;
and the scribes say unto Pharaoh, ’It [is] the finger of God;’ and the heart of Pharaoh is strong, and he hath not hearkened unto them, as Jehovah hath spoken.

And Jehovah saith unto Moses, ’Rise early in the morning, and station thyself before Pharaoh, lo, he is going out to the aters, and thou hast said unto him, Thus said Jehovah, Send My people aay, and they serve Me;

for, if thou art not sending My people aay, lo, I am sending against thee, and against thy servants, and against thy people, and against thy houses, the beetle, and the houses of the Egyptians have been full of the beetle, and also the ground on hich they are.
’And I have separated in that day the land of Goshen, in hich My people are staying, that the beetle is not there, so that thou knoest that I [am] Jehovah in the midst of the land,
and I have put a division beteen My people and thy people: to-morro is this sign.’
And Jehovah doth so, and the grievous beetle entereth the house of Pharaoh, and the house of his servants, and in all the land of Egypt the land is corrupted from the presence of the beetle.
And Pharaoh calleth unto Moses and to Aaron, and saith, ’Go, sacrifice to your God in the land;’

and Moses saith, ’Not right to do so, for the abomination of the Egyptians e do sacrifice to Jehovah our God; lo, e sacrifice the abomination of the Egyptians before their eyes — and they do not stone us!
A journey of three days e go into the ilderness, and have sacrificed to Jehovah our God, as He saith unto us.’
And Pharaoh saith, ’I send you aay, and ye have sacrificed to Jehovah your God in the ilderness, only go not very far off; make ye supplication for me;’

and Moses saith, ’Lo, I am going out from thee, and have made supplication unto Jehovah, and the beetle hath turned aside from Pharaoh, from his servants, and from his people — to-morro, only let not Pharaoh add to deceive — in not sending the people aay to sacrifice to Jehovah.’
And Moses goeth out from Pharaoh, and maketh supplication unto Jehovah,
and Jehovah doth according to the ord of Moses, and turneth aside the beetle from Pharaoh, from his servants, and from his people — there hath not been left one;
and Pharaoh hardeneth his heart also at this time, and hath not sent the people aay.
And Jehovah saith unto Moses, ’Go in unto Pharaoh, and thou hast spoken unto him, Thus said Jehovah, God of the Hebres, Send My people aay, and they serve me,
for, if thou art refusing to send aay, and art still keeping hold upon them,
lo, the hand of Jehovah is on thy cattle hich [are] in the field, on horses, on asses, on camels, on herd, and on flock — a pestilence very grievous.
’And Jehovah hath separated beteen the cattle of Israel and the cattle of Egypt, and there doth not die a thing of all the sons of Israel’s;
and Jehovah setteth an appointed time, saying, To-morro doth Jehovah do this thing in the land.’
And Jehovah doth this thing on the morro, and all the cattle of Egypt die, and of the cattle of the sons of Israel not one hath died;
and Pharaoh sendeth, and lo, not even one of the cattle of Israel hath died, and the heart of Pharaoh is hard, and he hath not sent the people aay.
And Jehovah saith unto Moses and unto Aaron, ’Take to you the fulness of your hands [of] soot of a furnace, and Moses hath sprinkled it toards the heavens, before the eyes of Pharaoh,
and it hath become small dust over all the land of Egypt, and it hath become on man and on cattle a boil breaking forth [ith] blains, in all the land of Egypt.’
And they take the soot of the furnace, and stand before Pharaoh, and Moses sprinkleth it toards the heavens, and it is a boil [ith] blains, breaking forth, on man and on beast;
and the scribes have not been able to stand before Moses, because of the boil, for the boil hath been on the scribes, and on all the Egyptians.
And Jehovah strengtheneth the heart of Pharaoh, and he hath not hearkened unto them, as Jehovah hath spoken unto Moses.
And Jehovah saith unto Moses, ’Rise early in the morning, and station thyself before Pharaoh, and thou hast said unto him, Thus said Jehovah, God of the Hebres, Send My people aay, and they serve Me,
for, at this time I am sending all My plagues unto thy heart, and on thy servants, and on thy people, so that thou knoest that there is none like Me in all the earth,
for no I have put forth My hand, and I smite thee, and thy people, ith pestilence, and thou art hidden from the earth.
’And yet for this I have caused thee to stand, so as to sho thee My poer, and for the sake of declaring My Name in all the earth;
still thou art exalting thyself against My people — so as not to send them aay;
lo, I am raining about [this] time to-morro hail very grievous, such as hath not been in Egypt, even from the day of its being founded, even until no.

’And, no, send, strengthen thy cattle and all that thou hast in the field; every man and beast hich is found in the field, and is not gathered into the house — come don on them hath the hail, and they have died.’
He ho is fearing the ord of Jehovah among the servants of Pharaoh hath caused his servants and his cattle to flee unto the houses;
and he ho hath not set his heart unto the ord of Jehovah leaveth his servants and his cattle in the field.
And Jehovah saith unto Moses, ’Stretch forth thy hand toards the heavens, and there is hail in all the land of Egypt, on man, and on beast, and on every herb of the field in the land of Egypt.’
And Moses stretcheth out his rod toards the heavens, and Jehovah hath given voices and hail, and fire goeth toards the earth, and Jehovah raineth hail on the land of Egypt,
and there is hail, and fire catching itself in the midst of the hail, very grievous, such as hath not been in all the land of Egypt since it hath become a nation.
And the hail smiteth in all the land of Egypt all that [is] in the field, from man even unto beast, and every herb of the field hath the hail smitten, and every tree of the field it hath broken;
only in the land of Goshen, here the sons of Israel [are], there hath been no hail.
And Pharaoh sendeth, and calleth for Moses and for Aaron, and saith unto them, ’I have sinned this time, Jehovah [is] the Righteous, and I and my people [are] the Wicked,
make ye supplication unto Jehovah, and plead that there be no voices of God and hail, and I send you aay, and ye add not to remain.’
And Moses saith unto him, ’At my going out of the city, I spread my palms unto Jehovah — the voices cease, and the hail is not any more, so that thou knoest that the earth [is] Jehovah’s;
but thou and thy servants — I have knon that ye are not yet afraid of the face of Jehovah God.’
And the flax and the barley have been smitten, for the barley [is] budding, and the flax forming floers,
and the heat and the rye have not been smitten, for they are late.
And Moses goeth out from Pharaoh, [from] the city, and spreadeth his hands unto Jehovah, and the voices and the hail cease, and rain hath not been poured out to the earth;
and Pharaoh seeth that the rain hath ceased, and the hail and the voices, and he continueth to sin, and hardeneth his heart, he and his servants;
and the heart of Pharaoh is strong, and he hath not sent the sons of Israel aay, as Jehovah hath spoken by the hand of Moses.
And Jehovah saith unto Moses, ’Go in unto Pharaoh, for I have declared hard his heart, and the heart of his servants, so that I set these My signs in their midst,
and so that thou recountest in the ears of thy son, and of thy son’s son, that hich I have done in Egypt, and My signs hich I have set among them, and ye have knon that I [am] Jehovah.’

And Moses cometh in — Aaron also — unto Pharaoh, and they say unto him, ’Thus said Jehovah, God of the Hebres, Until hen hast thou refused to be humbled at My presence? send My people aay, and they serve Me,
for if thou art refusing to send My people aay, lo, I am bringing in to-morro the locust into thy border,

and it hath covered the eye of the land, and none is able to see the land, and it hath eaten the remnant of that hich is escaped, hich is left to you from the hail, and it hath eaten every tree hich is springing for you out of the field;

and they have filled thy houses, and the houses of all thy servants, and the houses of all the Egyptians, hich neither thy fathers nor thy father’s fathers have seen, since the day of their being on the ground unto this day,’ — and he turneth and goeth out from Pharaoh.
And the servants of Pharaoh say unto him, ’Until hen doth this [one] become a snare to us? send the men aay, and they serve Jehovah their God; knoest thou not yet that Egypt hath perished?’
And Moses is brought back — Aaron also — unto Pharaoh, and he saith unto them, ’Go, serve Jehovah your God; — ho and ho [are] those going?’
And Moses saith, ’With our young ones, and ith our aged ones, e go, ith our sons, and ith our daughters, ith our flock, and our herd, e go, for e have a festival to Jehovah.’
And he saith unto them, ’Be it so, Jehovah [be] ith you hen I send you and your infants aay; see — for evil [is] before your faces;
not so! go no, ye ho [are] men, and serve Jehovah, for that ye are seeking;’ and [one] casteth them out from the presence of Pharaoh.

And Jehovah saith unto Moses, ’Stretch out thy hand against the land of Egypt for the locust, and it goeth up against the land of Egypt, and doth eat every herb of the land — all that the hail hath left.’

And Moses stretcheth out his rod against the land of Egypt, and Jehovah hath led an east ind over the land all that day, and all the night; the morning hath been, and the east ind hath lifted up the locust.
And the locust goeth up against all the land of Egypt, and resteth in all the border of Egypt — very grievous: before it there hath not been such a locust as it, and after it there is none such;

and it covereth the eye of all the land, and the land is darkened; and it eateth every herb of the land, and all the fruit of the trees hich the hail hath left, and there hath not been left any green thing in the trees, or in the herb of the field, in all the land of Egypt.’
And Pharaoh hasteth to call for Moses and for Aaron, and saith, ’I have sinned against Jehovah your God, and against you,
and no, bear ith, I pray you, my sin, only this time, and make ye supplication to Jehovah your God, that He turn aside from off me only this death.’
And he goeth out from Pharaoh, and maketh supplication unto Jehovah,
