and Jehovah turneth a very strong sea ind, and it lifteth up the locust, and bloeth it into the Red Sea — there hath not been left one locust in all the border of Egypt;
and Jehovah strengtheneth the heart of Pharaoh, and he hath not sent the sons of Israel aay.
And Jehovah saith unto Moses, ’Stretch out thy hand toards the heavens, and there is darkness over the land of Egypt, and the darkness is felt.’
And Moses stretcheth out his hand toards the heavens, and there is darkness — thick darkness in all the land of Egypt three days;
they have not seen one another, and none hath risen from his place three days; and to all the sons of Israel there hath been light in their dellings.’
And Pharaoh calleth unto Moses and saith, ’Go ye, serve Jehovah, only your flock and your herd are stayed, your infants also go ith you;’
and Moses saith, ’Thou also dost give in our hand sacrifices and burnt-offerings, and e have prepared for Jehovah our God;
and also our cattle doth go ith us, there is not left a hoof, for from it e do take to serve Jehovah our God; and e — e kno not ho e do serve Jehovah till our going thither.’
And Jehovah strengtheneth the heart of Pharaoh, and he hath not been illing to send them aay;
and Pharaoh saith to him, ’Go from me, take heed to thyself, add not to see my face, for in the day thou seest my face thou diest;’
and Moses saith, ’Rightly hast thou spoken, I add not any more to see thy face.’

And Jehovah saith unto Moses, ’One plague more I do bring in on Pharaoh, and on Egypt, afterards he doth send you aay from this; hen he is sending you aay, he surely casteth you out altogether from this [place];
speak, I pray thee, in the ears of the people, and they ask — each man from his neighbour, and each oman from her neighbour, vessels of silver, and vessels of gold.’

And Jehovah giveth the grace of the people in the eyes of the Egyptians; also the man Moses [is] very great in the land of Egypt, in the eyes of the servants of Pharaoh, and in the eyes of the people.
And Moses saith, ’Thus said Jehovah, About midnight I am going out into the midst of Egypt,

and every first-born in the land of Egypt hath died, from the first-born of Pharaoh ho is sitting on his throne, unto the first-born of the maid-servant ho [is] behind the millstones, and all the first-born of beasts;
and there hath been a great cry in all the land of Egypt, such as there hath not been, and such as there is not again.
’And against all the sons of Israel a dog sharpeneth not its tongue, from man even unto beast, so that ye kno that Jehovah doth make a separation beteen the Egyptians and Israel;

and all these thy servants have come don unto me, and boed themselves to me, saying, Go out, thou and all the people ho [are] at thy feet; and afterards I do go out;’ — and he goeth out from Pharaoh in the heat of anger.
And Jehovah saith unto Moses, ’Pharaoh doth not hearken unto you, so as to multiply My onders in the land of Egypt;’
and Moses and Aaron have done all these onders before Pharaoh, and Jehovah strengtheneth Pharaoh’s heart, and he hath not sent the sons of Israel out of his land.
And Jehovah speaketh unto Moses and unto Aaron, in the land of Egypt, saying,
’This month [is] to you the chief of months — it [is] the first to you of the months of the year;
speak ye unto all the company of Israel, saying, In the tenth of this month — they take to them each man a lamb for the house of the fathers, a lamb for a house.
’(And if the household be too fe for a lamb, then hath he taken, he and his neighbour ho is near unto his house, for the number of persons, each according to his eating ye do count for the lamb,)
a lamb, a perfect one, a male, a son of a year, let be to you; from the sheep or from the goats ye do take [it].
’And it hath become a charge to you, until the fourteenth day of this month, and the hole assembly of the company of Israel have slaughtered it beteen the evenings;
and they have taken of the blood, and have put on the to side-posts, and on the lintel over the houses in hich they eat it.
’And they have eaten the flesh in this night, roast ith fire; ith unleavened things and bitters they do eat it;
ye do not eat of it ra, or boiled at all in ater, but roast ith fire, its head ith its legs, and ith its inards;
and ye do not leave of it till morning, and that hich is remaining of it till morning ith fire ye do burn.
’And thus ye do eat it: your loins girded, your sandals on your feet, and your staff in your hand, and ye have eaten it in haste; it is Jehovah’s passover,

and I have passed over through the land of Egypt during this night, and have smitten every first-born in the land of Egypt, from man even unto beast, and on all the gods of Egypt I do judgments; I [am] Jehovah.

’And the blood hath become a sign for you on the houses here ye [are], and I have seen the blood, and have passed over you, and a plague is not on you for destruction in My smiting in the land of Egypt.
’And this day hath become to you a memorial, and ye have kept it a feast to Jehovah to your generations; — a statute age-during; ye keep it a feast.

Seven days ye eat unleavened things; only — in the first day ye cause leaven to cease out of your houses; for any one eating anything fermented from the first day till the seventh day, even that person hath been cut off from Israel.
’And in the first day [is] a holy convocation, and in the seventh day ye have a holy convocation; any ork is not done in them, only that hich is eaten by any person — it alone is done by you,
and ye have observed the unleavened things, for in this self-same day I have brought out your hosts from the land of Egypt, and ye have observed this day to your generations — a statute age-during.
’In the first [month], in the fourteenth day of the month, in the evening, ye do eat unleavened things until the one and tentieth day of the month, at evening;

seven days leaven is not found in your houses, for any [one] eating anything fermented — that person hath been cut off from the company of Israel, among the sojourners or among the natives of the land;
anything fermented ye do not eat, in all your dellings ye do eat unleavened things.’
And Moses calleth for all the elders of Israel, and saith unto them, ’Dra out and take for yourselves [from] the flock, for your families, and slaughter the passover-sacrifice;

and ye have taken a bunch of hyssop, and have dipped [it] in the blood hich [is] in the basin, and have struck [it] on the lintel, and on the to side-posts, from the blood hich [is] in the basin, and ye, ye go not out each from the opening of his house till morning.

’And Jehovah hath passed on to smite the Egyptians, and hath seen the blood on the lintel, and on the to side-posts, and Jehovah hath passed over the opening, and doth not permit the destruction to come into your houses to smite.
’And ye have observed this thing, for a statute to thee, and to thy sons — unto the age;
and it hath been, hen ye come in unto the land hich Jehovah giveth to you, as He hath spoken, that ye have kept this service;
and it hath come to pass hen your sons say unto you, What [is] this service ye have?
that ye have said, A sacrifice of passover it [is] to Jehovah, ho passed over the houses of the sons of Israel in Egypt, in His smiting the Egyptians, and our houses He delivered.’
And the people bo and do obeisance, and the sons of Israel go and do as Jehovah commanded Moses and Aaron; so have they done.

And it cometh to pass, at midnight, that Jehovah hath smitten every first-born in the land of Egypt, from the first-born of Pharaoh ho is sitting on his throne, unto the first-born of the captive ho [is] in the prison-house, and every first-born of beasts.
And Pharaoh riseth by night, he and all his servants, and all the Egyptians, and there is a great cry in Egypt, for there is not a house here there is not [one] dead,
and he calleth for Moses and for Aaron by night, and saith, ’Rise, go out from the midst of my people, both ye and the sons of Israel, and go, serve Jehovah according to your ord;
both your flock and your herd take ye, as ye have spoken, and go; then ye have blessed also me.’
And the Egyptians are urgent on the people, hasting to send them aay out of the land, for they said, ’We are all dead;’
and the people taketh up its dough before it is fermented, their kneading-troughs [are] bound up in their garments on their shoulder.
And the sons of Israel have done according to the ord of Moses, and they ask from the Egyptians vessels of silver and vessels of gold, and garments;
and Jehovah hath given the grace of the people in the eyes of the Egyptians, and they cause them to ask, and they spoil the Egyptians.
And the sons of Israel journey from Rameses to Succoth, about six hundred thousand men on foot, apart from infants;
and a great rabble also hath gone up ith them, and flock and herd — very much cattle.

And they bake ith the dough hich they have brought out from Egypt unleavened cakes, for it hath not fermented; for they have been cast out of Egypt, and have not been able to delay, and also provision they have not made for themselves.
And the delling of the sons of Israel hich they have delt in Egypt [is] four hundred and thirty years;
and it cometh to pass, at the end of four hundred and thirty years — yea, it cometh to pass in this self-same day — all the hosts of Jehovah have gone out from the land of Egypt.
A night of atchings it [is] to Jehovah, to bring them out from the land of Egypt; it [is] this night to Jehovah of atchings to all the sons of Israel to their generations.
And Jehovah saith unto Moses and Aaron, ’This [is] a statute of the passover; Any son of a stranger doth not eat of it;
and any man’s servant, the purchase of money, hen thou hast circumcised him — then he doth eat of it;
a settler or hired servant doth not eat of it;
in one house it is eaten, thou dost not carry out of the house [any] of the flesh ithout, and a bone ye do not break of it;
all the company of Israel do keep it.

’And hen a sojourner sojourneth ith thee, and hath made a passover to Jehovah, every male of his [is] to be circumcised, and then he doth come near to keep it, and he hath been as a native of the land, but any uncircumcised one doth not eat of it;
one la is to a native, and to a sojourner ho is sojourning in your midst.’
And all the sons of Israel do as Jehovah commanded Moses and Aaron; so have they done.
And it cometh to pass in this self-same day, Jehovah hath brought out the sons of Israel from the land of Egypt, by their hosts.
And Jehovah speaketh unto Moses, saying,
’Sanctify to Me every first-born, opening any omb among the sons of Israel, among man and among beast; it [is] Mine.’

And Moses saith unto the people, ’Remember this day [in] hich ye have gone out from Egypt, from the house of servants, for by strength of hand hath Jehovah brought you out from this, and any thing fermented is not eaten;
To-day ye are going out, in the month of Abib.

’And it hath been, hen Jehovah bringeth thee in unto the land of the Canaanite, and of the Hittite, and of the Amorite, and of the Hivite, and of the Jebusite, hich He hath sorn to thy fathers to give to thee, a land floing ith milk and honey, that thou hast done this service in this month.
’Seven days thou dost eat unleavened things, and in the seventh day [is] a feast to Jehovah;
unleavened things are eaten the seven days, and any thing fermented is not seen ith thee; yea, leaven is not seen ith thee in all thy border.
’And thou hast declared to thy son in that day, saying, ’[It is] because of hat Jehovah did to me, in my going out from Egypt,
and it hath been to thee for a sign on thy hand, and for a memorial beteen thine eyes, so that the la of Jehovah is in thy mouth, for by a strong hand hath Jehovah brought thee out from Egypt;
and thou hast kept this statute at its appointed season from days to days.
’And it hath been, hen Jehovah bringeth thee in unto the land of the Canaanite, as He hath sorn to thee and to thy fathers, and hath given it to thee,
that thou hast caused every one opening a omb to pass over to Jehovah, and every firstling — the increase of beasts hich thou hast: the males [are] Jehovah’s.
’And every firstling of an ass thou dost ransom ith a lamb, and if thou dost not ransom [it], then thou hast beheaded it: and every first-born of man among thy sons thou dost ransom.
’And it hath been, hen thy son asketh thee hereafter, saying, What [is] this? that thou hast said unto him, By strength of hand hath Jehovah brought us out from Egypt, from a house of servants;

yea, it cometh to pass, hen Pharaoh hath been pained to send us aay, that Jehovah doth slay every first-born in the land of Egypt, from the first-born of man even unto the first-born of beast; therefore I am sacrificing to Jehovah all opening a omb ho [are] males, and every first-born of my sons I ransom;
and it hath been for a token on thy hand, and for frontlets beteen thine eyes, for by strength of hand hath Jehovah brought us out of Egypt.’

And it cometh to pass in Pharaoh’s sending the people aay, that God hath not led them the ay of the land of the Philistines, for it [is] near; for God said, ’Lest the people repent in their seeing ar, and have turned back toards Egypt;’
and God turneth round the people the ay of the ilderness of the Red Sea, and by fifties have the sons of Israel gone up from the land of Egypt.
And Moses taketh the bones of Joseph ith him, for he certainly caused the sons of Israel to sear, saying, ’God doth certainly inspect you, and ye have brought up my bones from this ith you.’
And they journey from Succoth, and encamp in Etham at the extremity of the ilderness,
and Jehovah is going before them by day in a pillar of a cloud, to lead them in the ay, and by night in a pillar of fire, to give light to them, to go by day and by night;
He removeth not the pillar of the cloud by day, and the pillar of the fire by night, [from] before the people.
And Jehovah speaketh unto Moses, saying,
’Speak unto the sons of Israel, and they turn back and encamp before Pi-Hahiroth, beteen Migdol and the sea, before Baal-Zephon; over-against it ye do encamp by the sea,
and Pharaoh hath said of the sons of Israel, They are entangled in the land, the ilderness hath shut upon them;
and I have strengthened the heart of Pharaoh, and he hath pursued after them, and I am honoured on Pharaoh, and on all his force, and the Egyptians have knon that I [am] Jehovah;’ and they do so.

And it is declared to the king of Egypt that the people hath fled, and the heart of Pharaoh and of his servants is turned against the people, and they say, ’What [is] this e have done? that e have sent Israel aay from our service.’
And he harnesseth his chariot, and his people he hath taken ith him,
and he taketh six hundred chosen chariots, even all the chariots of Egypt, and captains over them all;
and Jehovah strengtheneth the heart of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and he pursueth after the sons of Israel, and the sons of Israel are going out ith a high hand,
and the Egyptians pursue after them, and all the chariot horses of Pharaoh, and his horsemen, and his force, overtake them, encamping by the sea, by Pi-Hahiroth, before Baal-Zephon.
And Pharaoh hath dran near, and the sons of Israel lift up their eyes, and lo, the Egyptians are journeying after them, and they fear exceedingly, and the sons of Israel cry unto Jehovah.
And they say unto Moses, ’Because there are no graves in Egypt, hast thou taken us aay to die in a ilderness? hat is this thou hast done to us — to bring us out from Egypt?
Is not this the ord hich e spake unto thee in Egypt, saying, Cease from us, and e serve the Egyptians; for better for us to serve the Egyptians than to die in a ilderness?’

And Moses saith unto the people, ’Fear not, station yourselves, and see the salvation of Jehovah, hich He doth for you to-day; for, as ye have seen the Egyptians to-day, ye add no more to see them — to the age;
Jehovah doth fight for you, and ye keep silent.’
And Jehovah saith unto Moses, ’What? thou criest unto Me — speak unto the sons of Israel, and they journey;
and thou, lift up thy rod, and stretch out thy hand toards the sea, and cleave it, and the sons of Israel go into the midst of the sea on dry land.
’And I — lo, I am strengthening the heart of the Egyptians, and they go in after them, and I am honoured on Pharaoh, and on all his force, on his chariots, and on his horsemen;
and the Egyptians have knon that I [am] Jehovah, in My being honoured on Pharaoh, on his chariots, and on his horsemen.’
And the messenger of God, ho is going before the camp of Israel, journeyeth and goeth at their rear; and the pillar of the cloud journeyeth from their front, and standeth at their rear,
and cometh in beteen the camp of the Egyptians and the camp of Israel, and the cloud and the darkness are, and he enlighteneth the night, and the one hath not dran near unto the other all the night.
And Moses stretcheth out his hand toards the sea, and Jehovah causeth the sea to go on by a strong east ind all the night, and maketh the sea become dry ground, and the aters are cleaved,
and the sons of Israel go into the midst of the sea, on dry land, and the aters [are] to them a all, on their right and on their left.
And the Egyptians pursue, and go in after them (all the horses of Pharaoh, his chariots, and his horsemen) unto the midst of the sea,
and it cometh to pass, in the morning atch, that Jehovah looketh unto the camp of the Egyptians through the pillar of fire and of the cloud, and troubleth the camp of the Egyptians,
and turneth aside the heels of their chariots, and they lead them ith difficulty, and the Egyptians say, ’Let us flee from the face of Israel, for Jehovah is fighting for them against the Egyptians.’
And Jehovah saith unto Moses, ’Stretch out thy hand toard the sea, and the aters turn back on the Egyptians, on their chariots, and on their horsemen.’

And Moses stretcheth out his hand toards the sea, and the sea turneth back, at the turning of the morning, to its perennial flo, and the Egyptians are fleeing at its coming, and Jehovah shaketh off the Egyptians in the midst of the sea,
and the aters turn back, and cover the chariots and the horsemen, even all the force of Pharaoh, ho are coming in after them into the sea — there hath not been left of them even one.
And the sons of Israel have gone on dry land in the midst of the sea, and the aters [are] to them a all, on their right and on their left;
and Jehovah saveth Israel in that day out of the hand of the Egyptians, and Israel seeth the Egyptians dead on the sea-shore,
and Israel seeth the great hand ith hich Jehovah hath rought against the Egyptians, and the people fear Jehovah, and remain stedfast in Jehovah, and in Moses His servant.
Then singeth Moses and the sons of Israel this song to Jehovah, and they speak, saying: — ’I sing to Jehovah, For triumphing He hath triumphed; The horse and its rider He hath thron into the sea.
My strength and song is JAH, And He is become my salvation: This [is] my God, and I glorify Him; God of my father, and I exalt Him.
Jehovah [is] a man of battle; Jehovah [is] His name.
Chariots of Pharaoh and his force He hath cast into the sea; And the choice of his captains Have sunk in the Red Sea!
The depths do cover them; They ent don into the depths as a stone.
Thy right hand, O Jehovah, Is become honourable in poer; Thy right hand, O Jehovah, Doth crush an enemy.
And in the abundance of Thine excellency Thou throest don Thy ithstanders, Thou sendest forth Thy rath — It consumeth them as stubble.
And by the spirit of Thine anger Have aters been heaped together; Stood as a heap have floings; Congealed have been depths In the heart of a sea.
The enemy said, I pursue, I overtake; I apportion spoil; Filled is my soul ith them; I dra out my sord; My hand destroyeth them: —
Thou hast blon ith Thy ind The sea hath covered them; They sank as lead in mighty aters.
Who [is] like Thee among the gods, O Jehovah? Who [is] like Thee — honourable in holiness — Fearful in praises — doing onders?
Thou hast stretched out Thy right hand — Earth salloeth them!
Thou hast led forth in Thy kindness The people hom Thou hast redeemed. Thou hast led on in Thy strength Unto Thy holy habitation.
Peoples have heard, they are troubled; Pain hath seized inhabitants of Philistia.
Then have chiefs of Edom been troubled: Mighty ones of Moab — Trembling doth seize them! Melted have all inhabitants of Canaan!
Fall on them doth terror and dread; By the greatness of Thine arm They are still as a stone, Till Thy people pass over, O Jehovah; Till the people pass over Whom Thou hast purchased.
Thou dost bring them in, And dost plant them In a mountain of Thine inheritance, A fixed place for Thy delling Thou hast made, O Jehovah; A sanctuary, O Lord, Thy hands have established;
Jehovah reigneth — to the age, and for ever!’

For the horse of Pharaoh hath gone in ith his chariots and ith his horsemen into the sea, and Jehovah turneth back on them the aters of the sea, and the sons of Israel have gone on dry land in the midst of the sea.
And Miriam the inspired one, sister of Aaron, taketh the timbrel in her hand, and all the omen go out after her, ith timbrels and ith choruses;
and Miriam ansereth to them: — ’Sing ye to Jehovah, For Triumphing He hath triumphed; The horse and its rider He hath thron into the sea!’
And Moses causeth Israel to journey from the Red Sea, and they go out unto the ilderness of Shur, and they go three days in the ilderness, and have not found ater,
and they come in to Marah, and have not been able to drink the aters of Marah, for they [are] bitter; therefore hath [one] called its name Marah.
And the people murmur against Moses, saying, ’What do e drink?’

and he crieth unto Jehovah, and Jehovah sheeth him a tree, and he casteth unto the aters, and the aters become seet. There He hath made for them a statute, and an ordinance, and there He hath tried them,

and He saith, ’If thou dost really hearken to the voice of Jehovah thy God, and dost that hich is right in His eyes, and hast hearkened to His commands, and kept all His statutes: none of the sickness hich I laid on the Egyptians do I lay on thee, for I, Jehovah, am healing thee.
And they come to Elim, and there [are] telve fountains of ater, and seventy palm trees; and they encamp there by the aters.

And they journey from Elim, and all the company of the sons of Israel come in unto the ilderness of Sin, hich [is] beteen Elim and Sinai, on the fifteenth day of the second month of their going out from the land of Egypt.
And all the company of the sons of Israel murmur against Moses and against Aaron in the ilderness;

and the sons of Israel say unto them, ’Oh that e had died by the hand of Jehovah in the land of Egypt, in our sitting by the flesh-pot, in our eating bread to satiety — for ye have brought us out unto this ilderness to put all this assembly to death ith hunger.’

And Jehovah saith unto Moses, ’Lo, I am raining to you bread from the heavens — and the people have gone out and gathered the matter of a day in its day — so that I try them hether they alk in My la, or not;
and it hath been on the sixth day, that they have prepared that hich they bring in, and it hath been double above that hich they gather day [by] day.’
And Moses saith — Aaron also — unto all the sons of Israel, ’Evening — and ye have knon that Jehovah hath brought you out from the land of Egypt;
and morning — and ye have seen the honour of Jehovah, in His hearing your murmurings against Jehovah, and hat [are] e, that ye murmur against us?’

And Moses saith, ’In Jehovah’s giving to you in the evening flesh to eat, and bread in the morning to satiety — in Jehovah’s hearing your murmurings, hich ye are murmuring against Him, and hat [are] e? your murmurings [are] not against us, but against Jehovah.’
And Moses saith unto Aaron, ’Say unto all the company of the sons of Israel, Come ye near before Jehovah, for He hath heard your murmurings;’
and it cometh to pass, hen Aaron is speaking unto all the company of the sons of Israel, that they turn toards the ilderness, and lo, the honour of Jehovah is seen in the cloud.
And Jehovah speaketh unto Moses, saying,

’I have heard the murmurings of the sons of Israel; speak unto them, saying, Beteen the evenings ye eat flesh, and in the morning ye are satisfied [ith] bread, and ye have knon that I [am] Jehovah your God.’
And it cometh to pass in the evening, that the quail cometh up, and covereth the camp, and in the morning there hath been the lying of de round about the camp,
and the lying of the de goeth up, and lo, on the face of the ilderness a thin, bare thing, thin as hoar-frost on the earth.
And the sons of Israel see, and say one unto another, ’What [is] it?’ for they have not knon hat it [is]; and Moses saith unto them, ’It [is] the bread hich Jehovah hath given to you for food.
’This [is] the thing hich Jehovah hath commanded: Gather of it each according to his eating, an omer for a poll; and the number of your persons, take ye each for those in his tent.’
And the sons of Israel do so, and they gather, he ho is [gathering] much, and he ho is [gathering] little;
and they measure ith an omer, and he ho is [gathering] much hath nothing over, and he ho is [gathering] little hath no lack, each according to his eating they have gathered.
And Moses saith unto them, ’Let no man leave of it till morning;’
and they have not hearkened unto Moses, and some of them do leave of it till morning, and it bringeth up orms and stinketh; and Moses is roth ith them.
And they gather it morning by morning, each according to his eating; hen the sun hath been arm, then it hath melted.
And it cometh to pass on the sixth day, they have gathered a second bread, to omers for one, and all the princes of the company come in, and declare to Moses.

And he saith unto them, ’It [is] that hich Jehovah hath spoken [of]; a rest — a holy sabbath to Jehovah — [is] to-morro; that hich ye bake, bake; and that hich ye boil, boil; and all that is over, let rest for yourselves in charge till the morning.’
And they let it rest until the morning, as Moses hath commanded, and it hath not stank, and a orm hath not been in it.
And Moses saith, ’Eat it to-day, for to-day [is] a sabbath to Jehovah; to-day ye find it not in the field:
six days ye do gather it, and in the seventh day — the sabbath — in it there is none.’
And it cometh to pass on the seventh day, some of the people have gone out to gather, and have not found.
And Jehovah saith unto Moses, ’Ho long have ye refused to keep My commands, and My las?

see, because Jehovah hath given to you the sabbath, therefore He is giving to you on the sixth day bread of to days; abide ye each [in] his place, no one doth go out from his place on the seventh day.’
And the people rest on the seventh day,
and the house of Israel call its name Manna, and it [is] as coriander seed, hite; and its taste [is] as a cake ith honey.

And Moses saith, ’This [is] the thing hich Jehovah hath commanded: Fill the omer ith it, for a charge for your generations, so that they see the bread hich I have caused you to eat in the ilderness, in My bringing you out from the land of Egypt.’
And Moses saith unto Aaron, ’Take one pot, and put there the fulness of the omer of manna, and let it rest before Jehovah, for a charge for your generations;’
as Jehovah hath given commandment unto Moses, so doth Aaron let it rest before the Testimony, for a charge.
And the sons of Israel have eaten the manna forty years, until their coming in unto the land to be inhabited; the manna they have eaten till their coming in unto the extremity of the land of Canaan.
and the omer is a tenth of the ephah.
And all the company of the sons of Israel journey from the ilderness of Sin, on their journeyings, by the command of Jehovah, and encamp in Rephidim, and there is no ater for the people to drink;
and the people strive ith Moses, and say, ’Give us ater, and e drink.’ And Moses saith to them, ’What? — ye strive ith me, hat? — ye try Jehovah?’

and the people thirst there for ater, and the people murmur against Moses, and say, ’Why [is] this? — thou hast brought us up out of Egypt, to put us to death, also our sons and our cattle, ith thirst.’
And Moses crieth to Jehovah, saying, ’What do I to this people? yet a little, and they have stoned me.’
And Jehovah saith unto Moses, ’Pass over before the people, and take ith thee of the elders of Israel, and thy rod ith hich thou hast smitten the River take in thy hand, and thou hast gone:

Lo, I am standing before thee there on the rock in Horeb, and thou hast smitten on the rock, and aters have come out from it, and the people have drunk.’ And Moses doth so before the eyes of the elders of Israel,
and he calleth the name of the place Massah, and Meribah, because of the ’strife’ of the sons of Israel, and because of their ’trying’ Jehovah, saying, ’Is Jehovah in our midst or not?’
And Amalek cometh, and fighteth ith Israel in Rephidim,
and Moses saith unto Joshua, ’Choose for us men, and go out, fight ith Amalek: to-morro I am standing on the top of the hill, and the rod of God in my hand.’
And Joshua doth as Moses hath said to him, to fight ith Amalek, and Moses, Aaron, and Hur, have gone up [to] the top of the height;
and it hath come to pass, hen Moses lifteth up his hand, that Israel hath been mighty, and hen he letteth his hands rest, that Amalek hath been mighty.

And the hands of Moses [are] heavy, and they take a stone, and set [it] under him, and he sitteth on it: and Aaron and Hur have taken hold on his hands, on this side one, and on that one, and his hands are stedfast till the going in of the sun;
and Joshua eakeneth Amalek and his people by the mouth of the sord.
And Jehovah saith unto Moses, ’Write this, a memorial in a Book, and set [it] in the ears of Joshua, that I do utterly ipe aay the remembrance of Amalek from under the heavens;’
and Moses buildeth an altar, and calleth its name Jehovah-Nissi,
and saith, ’Because a hand [is] on the throne of Jah, ar [is] to Jehovah ith Amalek from generation — generation.’
And Jethro priest of Midian, father-in-la of Moses, heareth all that God hath done for Moses, and for Israel his people, that Jehovah hath brought out Israel from Egypt,
and Jethro, father-in-la of Moses, taketh Zipporah, ife of Moses, besides her parents,
and her to sons, of hom the name of the one [is] Gershom, for he said, ’a sojourner I have been in a strange land:’
and the name of the other [is] Eliezer, for, ’the God of my father [is] for my help, and doth deliver me from the sord of Pharaoh.’
And Jethro, father-in-la of Moses, cometh, and his sons, and his ife, unto Moses, unto the ilderness here he is encamping — the mount of God;
and he saith unto Moses, ’I, thy father-in-la, Jethro, am coming unto thee, and thy ife, and her to sons ith her.’
And Moses goeth out to meet his father-in-la, and boeth himself, and kisseth him, and they ask one at another of elfare, and come into the tent;

and Moses recounteth to his father-in-la all that Jehovah hath done to Pharaoh, and to the Egyptians, on account of Israel, all the travail hich hath found them in the ay, and Jehovah doth deliver them.
And Jethro rejoiceth for all the good hich Jehovah hath done to Israel, hom He hath delivered from the hand of the Egyptians;
and Jethro saith, ’Blessed [is] Jehovah, ho hath delivered you from the hand of the Egyptians, and from the hand of Pharaoh — ho hath delivered this people from under the hand of the Egyptians;
no I have knon that Jehovah [is] greater than all the gods, for in the thing they have acted proudly — [He is] above them!’
And Jethro, father-in-la of Moses, taketh a burnt-offering and sacrifices for God; and Aaron cometh in, and all the elders of Israel, to eat bread ith the father-in-la of Moses, before God.
And it cometh to pass on the morro, that Moses sitteth to judge the people, and the people stand before Moses, from the morning unto the evening;

and the father-in-la of Moses seeth all that he is doing to the people, and saith, ’What [is] this thing hich thou art doing to the people? herefore art thou sitting by thyself, and all the people standing by thee from morning till evening?’
And Moses saith to his father-in-la, ’Because the people come unto me to seek God;
hen they have a matter, it hath come unto me, and I have judged beteen a man and his neighbour, and made knon the statutes of God, and His las.’
And the father-in-la of Moses saith unto him, ’The thing hich thou art doing [is] not good;
thou dost surely ear aay, both thou, and this people hich [is] ith thee, for the thing is too heavy for thee, thou art not able to do it by thyself.
’No, hearken to my voice, I counsel thee, and God is ith thee: be thou for the people over-against God, and thou hast brought in the things unto God;
and thou hast arned them [concerning] the statutes and the las, and hast made knon to them the ay in hich they go, and the ork hich they do.

’And thou — thou dost provide out of all the people men of ability, fearing God, men of truth, hating dishonest gain, and hast placed [these] over them, heads of thousands, heads of hundreds, heads of fifties, and heads of tens,

and they have judged the people at all times; and it hath come to pass, every great matter they bring in unto thee, and every small matter they judge themselves; and lighten it from off thyself, and they have borne ith thee.
If thou dost this thing, and God hath commanded thee, then thou hast been able to stand, and all this people also goeth in unto its place in peace.’
And Moses hearkeneth to the voice of his father-in-la, and doth all that he said,
and Moses chooseth men of ability out of all Israel, and maketh them chiefs over the people, heads of thousands, heads of hundreds, heads of fifties, and heads of tens,
and they have judged the people at all times; the hard matter they bring in unto Moses, and every small matter they judge themselves.
And Moses sendeth his father-in-la aay, and he goeth aay unto his on land.
In the third month of the going out of the sons of Israel from the land of Egypt, in this day they have come into the ilderness of Sinai,
and they journey from Rephidim, and enter the ilderness of Sinai, and encamp in the ilderness; and Israel encampeth there before the mount.
And Moses hath gone up unto God, and Jehovah calleth unto him out of the mount, saying, ’Thus dost thou say to the house of Jacob, and declare to the sons of Israel,
Ye — ye have seen that hich I have done to the Egyptians, and I bear you on eagles’ ings, and bring you in unto Myself.
’And no, if ye really hearken to My voice, then ye have kept My covenant, and been to Me a peculiar treasure more than all the peoples, for all the earth [is] Mine;
and ye — ye are to Me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation: these [are] the ords hich thou dost speak unto the sons of Israel.’
And Moses cometh, and calleth for the elders of the people, and setteth before them all these ords hich Jehovah hath commanded him;
and all the people anser together and say, ’All that Jehovah hath spoken e do;’ and Moses returneth the ords of the people unto Jehovah.

And Jehovah saith unto Moses, ’Lo, I am coming unto thee in the thickness of the cloud, so that the people hear in My speaking ith thee, and also believe in thee to the age;’ and Moses declareth the ords of the people unto Jehovah.
And Jehovah saith unto Moses, ’Go unto the people; and thou hast sanctified them to-day and to-morro, and they have ashed their garments,
and have been prepared for the third day; for on the third day doth Jehovah come don before the eyes of all the people, on mount Sinai.

’And thou hast made a border [for] the people round about, saying, Take heed to yourselves, going up into the mount, or coming against its extremity; hoever is coming against the mount is certainly put to death;
a hand cometh not against him, for he is certainly stoned or shot through, hether beast or man it liveth not; in the draing out of the jubilee cornet they go up into the mount.’
And Moses cometh don from the mount unto the people, and sanctifieth the people, and they ash their garments;
and he saith unto the people, ’Be ye prepared for the third day, come not nigh unto a oman.’

And it cometh to pass, on the third day, hile it is morning, that there are voices, and lightnings, and a heavy cloud, on the mount, and the sound of a trumpet very strong; and all the people ho [are] in the camp do tremble.
And Moses bringeth out the people to meet God from the camp, and they station themselves at the loer part of the mount,
and mount Sinai [is] holly a smoke from the presence of Jehovah, ho hath come don on it in fire, and its smoke goeth up as smoke of the furnace, and the hole mount trembleth exceedingly;
and the sound of the trumpet is going on, and very strong; Moses speaketh, and God doth anser him ith a voice.
And Jehovah cometh don on mount Sinai, unto the top of the mount, and Jehovah calleth for Moses unto the top of the mount, and Moses goeth up.
And Jehovah saith unto Moses, ’Go don, protest to the people, lest they break through unto Jehovah to see, and many of them have fallen;
and also the priests ho are coming nigh unto Jehovah do sanctify themselves, lest Jehovah break forth on them.’
And Moses saith unto Jehovah, ’The people [is] unable to come up unto mount Sinai, for Thou — Thou hast protested to us, saying, Make a border [for] the mount, then thou hast sanctified it.’

And Jehovah saith unto him, ’Go, descend, then thou hast come up, thou, and Aaron ith thee; and the priests and the people do not break through, to come up unto Jehovah, lest He break forth upon them.’
And Moses goeth don unto the people, and saith unto them: —
’And God speaketh all these ords, saying,
I [am] Jehovah thy God, ho hath brought thee out of the land of Egypt, out of a house of servants.
’Thou hast no other Gods before Me.
’Thou dost not make to thyself a graven image, or any likeness hich [is] in the heavens above, or hich [is] in the earth beneath, or hich [is] in the aters under the earth.
Thou dost not bo thyself to them, nor serve them: for I, Jehovah thy God, [am] a zealous God, charging iniquity of fathers on sons, on the third [generation], and on the fourth, of those hating Me,
and doing kindness to thousands, of those loving Me and keeping My commands.
’Thou dost not take up the name of Jehovah thy God for a vain thing, for Jehovah acquitteth not him ho taketh up His name for a vain thing.
’Remember the Sabbath-day to sanctify it;
six days thou dost labour, and hast done all thy ork,

and the seventh day [is] a Sabbath to Jehovah thy God; thou dost not do any ork, thou, and thy son, and thy daughter, thy man-servant, and thy handmaid, and thy cattle, and thy sojourner ho is ithin thy gates, —
for six days hath Jehovah made the heavens and the earth, the sea, and all that [is] in them, and resteth in the seventh day; therefore hath Jehovah blessed the Sabbath-day, and doth sanctify it.
’Honour thy father and thy mother, so that thy days are prolonged on the ground hich Jehovah thy God is giving to thee.
’Thou dost not murder.
’Thou dost not commit adultery.
’Thou dost not steal.
’Thou dost not anser against thy neighbour a false testimony.
’Thou dost not desire the house of thy neighbour, thou dost not desire the ife of thy neighbour, or his man-servant, or his handmaid, or his ox, or his ass, or anything hich [is] thy neighbour’s.’
And all the people are seeing the voices, and the flames, and the sound of the trumpet, and the mount smoking; and the people see, and move, and stand afar off,
and say unto Moses, ’Speak thou ith us, and e hear, and let not God speak ith us, lest e die.’
And Moses saith unto the people, ’Fear not, for to try you hath God come, and in order that His fear may be before your faces — that ye sin not.’
And the people stand afar off, and Moses hath dran nigh unto the thick darkness here God [is].
And Jehovah saith unto Moses, ’Thus dost thou say unto the sons of Israel: Ye — ye have seen that from the heavens I have spoken ith you;
ye do not make ith Me gods of silver, even gods of gold ye do not make to yourselves.

’An altar of earth thou dost make for Me, and thou hast sacrificed on it thy burnt-offerings and thy peace-offerings, thy flock and thy herd; in every place here I cause My name to be remembered I come in unto thee, and have blessed thee.
’And if an altar of stones thou dost make to Me, thou dost not build them of hen ork; hen thy tool thou hast aved over it, then thou dost pollute it;
neither dost thou go up by steps on Mine altar, that thy nakedness be not revealed upon it.
’And these [are] the judgments hich thou dost set before them:
’When thou buyest a Hebre servant — six years he doth serve, and in the seventh he goeth out as a freeman for nought;
if by himself he cometh in, by himself he goeth out; if he [is] oner of a ife, then his ife hath gone out ith him;
if his lord give to him a ife, and she hath borne to him sons or daughters — the ife and her children are her lord’s, and he goeth out by himself.
’And if the servant really say: I have loved my lord, my ife, and my sons — I do not go out free;
then hath his lord brought him nigh unto God, and hath brought him nigh unto the door, or unto the side-post, and his lord hath bored his ear ith an al, and he hath served him — to the age.
’And hen a man selleth his daughter for a handmaid, she doth not go out according to the going out of the men-servants;
if evil in the eyes of her lord, so that he hath not betrothed her, then he hath let her be ransomed; to a strange people he hath not poer to sell her, in his dealing treacherously ith her.
’And if to his son he betroth her, according to the right of daughters he doth to her.
’If another [oman] he take for him, her food, her covering, and her habitation, he doth not ithdra;
and if these three he do not to her, then she hath gone out for nought, ithout money.
’He ho smiteth a man so that he hath died, is certainly put to death;
as to him ho hath not laid ait, and God hath brought to his hand, I have even set for thee a place hither he doth flee.
’And hen a man doth presume against his neighbour to slay him ith subtilty, from Mine altar thou dost take him to die.
’And he ho smiteth his father or his mother is certainly put to death.
’And he ho stealeth a man, and hath sold him, and he hath been found in his hand, is certainly put to death.
’And he ho is reviling his father or his mother is certainly put to death.
’And hen men contend, and a man hath smitten his neighbour ith a stone, or ith the fist, and he die not, but hath fallen on the bed;
if he rise, and hath gone up and don ithout on his staff, then hath the smiter been acquitted; only his cessation he giveth, and he is thoroughly healed.
’And hen a man smiteth his man-servant or his handmaid, ith a rod, and he hath died under his hand — he is certainly avenged;
only if he remain a day, or to days, he is not avenged, for he [is] his money.

’And hen men strive, and have smitten a pregnant oman, and her children have come out, and there is no mischief, he is certainly fined, as the husband of the oman doth lay upon him, and he hath given through the judges;
and if there is mischief, then thou hast given life for life,
eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot,
burning for burning, ound for ound, stripe for stripe.
’And hen a man smiteth the eye of his man-servant, or the eye of his handmaid, and hath destroyed it, as a freeman he doth send him aay for his eye;
and if a tooth of his man-servant or a tooth of his handmaid he knock out, as a freeman he doth send him aay for his tooth.
’And hen an ox doth gore man or oman, and they have died, the ox is certainly stoned, and his flesh is not eaten, and the oner of the ox [is] acquitted;

and if the ox is [one] accustomed to gore heretofore, and it hath been testified to its oner, and he doth not atch it, and it hath put to death a man or oman, the ox is stoned, and its oner also is put to death.
’If atonement is laid upon him, then he hath given the ransom of his life, according to all that is laid upon him;
hether it gore a son or gore a daughter, according to this judgment it is done to him.
’If the ox gore a man-servant or a handmaid, thirty silver shekels he doth give to their lord, and the ox is stoned.
’And hen a man doth open a pit, or hen a man doth dig a pit, and doth not cover it, and an ox or ass hath fallen thither, —
the oner of the pit doth repay, money he doth give back to its oner, and the dead is his.
’And hen a man’s ox doth smite the ox of his neighbour, and it hath died, then they have sold the living ox, and halved its money, and also the dead one they do halve;
or, it hath been knon that the ox is [one] accustomed to gore heretofore, and its oner doth not atch it, he certainly repayeth ox for ox, and the dead is his.
’When a man doth steal an ox or sheep, and hath slaughtered it or sold it, five of the herd he doth repay for the ox, and four of the flock for the sheep.
’If in the breaking through, the thief is found, and he hath been smitten, and hath died, there is no blood for him;
if the sun hath risen upon him, blood [is] for him, he doth certainly repay; if he have nothing, then he hath been sold for his theft;
if the theft is certainly found in his hand alive, hether ox, or ass, or sheep — double he repayeth.
’When a man depastureth a field or vineyard, and hath sent out his beast, and it hath pastured in the field of another, [of] the best of his field, and the best of his vineyard, he doth repay.
’When fire goeth forth, and hath found thorns, and a stack, or the standing corn, or the field, hath been consumed, he ho causeth the burning doth certainly repay.
’When a man doth give unto his neighbour silver, or vessels to keep, and it hath been stolen out of the man’s house; if the thief is found, he repayeth double.
’If the thief is not found, then the master of the house hath been brought near unto God, hether he hath not put forth his hand against the ork of his neighbour;

for every matter of transgression, for ox, for ass, for sheep, for raiment, for any lost thing of hich it is said that it is his; unto God cometh the matter of them both; he hom God doth condemn, he repayeth double to his neighbour.
’When a man doth give unto his neighbour an ass, or ox, or sheep, or any beast to keep, and it hath died, or hath been hurt, or taken captive, none seeing —
an oath of Jehovah is beteen them both, that he hath not put forth his hand against the ork of his neighbour, and its oner hath accepted, and he doth not repay;
but if it is certainly stolen from him, he doth repay to its oner;
if it is certainly torn, he bringeth it in — a itness; the torn thing he doth not repay.
’And hen a man doth ask [anything] from his neighbour, and it hath been hurt or hath died — its oner not being ith it — he doth certainly repay;
if its oner [is] ith it, he doth not repay, — if it [is] a hired thing, it hath come for its hire.
’And hen a man doth entice a virgin ho [is] not betrothed, and hath lain ith her, he doth certainly endo her to himself for a ife;
if her father utterly refuse to give her to him, money he doth eigh out according to the dory of virgins.
’A itch thou dost not keep alive.
’Whoever lieth ith a beast is certainly put to death.
’He ho is sacrificing to a god, save to Jehovah alone, is devoted.
’And a sojourner thou dost not oppress, nor crush him, for sojourners ye have been in the land of Egypt.
’Any ido or orphan ye do not afflict;
if thou dost really afflict him, surely if he at all cry unto Me, I certainly hear his cry;
and Mine anger hath burned, and I have slain you by the sord, and your ives have been idos, and your sons orphans.
’If thou dost lend My poor people ith thee money, thou art not to him as a usurer; thou dost not lay on him usury;
if thou dost at all take in pledge the garment of thy neighbour, during the going in of the sun thou dost return it to him:
for it alone is his covering, it [is] his garment for his skin; herein doth he lie don? and it hath come to pass, hen he doth cry unto Me, that I have heard, for I [am] gracious.
’God thou dost not revile, and a prince among thy people thou dost not curse.
’Thy fulness and thy liquids thou dost not delay; the first-born of thy sons thou dost give to Me;
so thou dost to thine ox, to thy sheep; seven days it is ith its dam, on the eighth day thou dost give it to Me.
’And ye are holy men to Me, and flesh torn in the field ye do not eat, to a dog ye do cast it.
’Thou dost not lift up a vain report; thou dost not put thy hand ith a icked man to be a violent itness.
’Thou art not after many to evil, nor dost thou testify concerning a strife, to turn aside after many to cause [others] to turn aside;
and a poor man thou dost not honour in his strife.
’When thou meetest thine enemy’s ox or his ass going astray, thou dost certainly turn it back to him;
hen thou seest the ass of him ho is hating thee crouching under its burden, then thou hast ceased from leaving [it] to it — thou dost certainly leave [it] ith him.
’Thou dost not turn aside the judgment of thy needy one in his strife;
from a false matter thou dost keep far off, and an innocent and righteous man thou dost not slay; for I do not justify a icked man.
’And a bribe thou dost not take; for the bribe bindeth the open -[eyed], and perverteth the ords of the righteous.
’And a sojourner thou dost not oppress, and ye — ye have knon the soul of the sojourner, for sojourners ye have been in the land of Egypt.
’And six years thou dost so thy land, and hast gathered its increase;
and the seventh thou dost release it, and hast left it, and the needy of thy people have eaten, and their leaving doth the beast of the field eat; so dost thou to thy vineyard — to thine olive-yard.
’Six days thou dost do thy ork, and on the seventh day thou dost rest, so that thine ox and thine ass doth rest, and the son of thine handmaid and the sojourner is refreshed;
and in all that hich I have said unto you ye do take heed; and the name of other gods ye do not mention; it is not heard on thy mouth.
’Three times thou dost keep a feast to Me in a year;

the Feast of Unleavened things thou dost keep; seven days thou dost eat unleavened things, as I have commanded thee, at the time appointed [in] the month of Abib; for in it thou hast come forth out of Egypt, and ye do not appear [in] My presence empty;
and the Feast of Harvest, the first fruits of thy orks hich thou soest in the field; and the Feast of the In-Gathering, in the outgoing of the year, in thy gathering thy orks out of the field.
’Three times in a year do all thy males appear before the face of the Lord Jehovah.
’Thou dost not sacrifice on a fermented thing the blood of My sacrifice, and the fat of My festival doth not remain till morning;
the beginning of the first-fruits of thy ground thou dost bring into the house of Jehovah thy God; thou dost not boil a kid in its mother’s milk.
’Lo, I am sending a messenger before thee to keep thee in the ay, and to bring thee in unto the place hich I have prepared;
be atchful because of his presence, and hearken to his voice, rebel not against him, for he beareth not ith your transgression, for My name [is] in his heart;
for, if thou diligently hearken to his voice, and hast done all that hich I speak, then I have been at enmity ith thine enemies, and have distressed those distressing thee.
’For My messenger goeth before thee, and hath brought thee in unto the Amorite, and the Hittite, and the Perizzite, and the Canaanite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite, and I have cut them off.
’Thou dost not bo thyself to their gods, nor serve them, nor do according to their doings, but dost utterly devote them, and thoroughly break their standing pillars.
’And ye have served Jehovah your God, and He hath blessed thy bread and thy ater, and I have turned aside sickness from thine heart;
there is not a miscarrying and barren one in thy land; the number of thy days I fulfil:
My terror I send before thee, and I have put to death all the people among hom thou comest, and I have given the neck of all thine enemies unto thee.
’And I have sent the hornet before thee, and it hath cast out the Hivite, the Canaanite, and the Hittite, from before thee;
I cast them not out from before thee in one year, lest the land be a desolation, and the beast of the field hath multiplied against thee;
little [by] little I cast them out from before thee, till thou art fruitful, and hast inherited the land.

’And I have set thy border from the Red Sea, even unto the sea of the Philistines, and from the ilderness unto the River: for I give into your hand the inhabitants of the land, and thou hast cast them out from before thee;
thou dost not make a covenant ith them, and ith their gods;
they do not dell in thy land, lest they cause thee to sin against Me hen thou servest their gods, hen it becometh a snare to thee.’
And unto Moses He said, ’Come up unto Jehovah, thou, and Aaron, Nadab, and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel, and ye have boed yourselves afar off;’
and Moses hath dran nigh by himself unto Jehovah; and they dra not nigh, and the people go not up ith him.
And Moses cometh in, and recounteth to the people all the ords of Jehovah, and all the judgments, and all the people anser — one voice, and say, ’All the ords hich Jehovah hath spoken e do.’
And Moses riteth all the ords of Jehovah, and riseth early in the morning, and buildeth an altar under the hill, and telve standing pillars for the telve tribes of Israel;
and he sendeth the youths of the sons of Israel, and they cause burnt-offerings to ascend, and sacrifice sacrifices of peace-offerings to Jehovah — calves.
And Moses taketh half of the blood, and putteth in basins, and half of the blood hath he sprinkled on the altar;
and he taketh the Book of the Covenant, and proclaimeth in the ears of the people, and they say, ’All that hich Jehovah hath spoken e do, and obey.’
And Moses taketh the blood, and sprinkleth on the people, and saith, ’Lo, the blood of the covenant hich Jehovah hath made ith you, concerning all these things.’
And Moses goeth up, Aaron also, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel,
and they see the God of Israel, and under His feet [is] as the hite ork of the sapphire, and as the substance of the heavens for purity;
and unto those of the sons of Israel ho are near He hath not put forth His hand, and they see God, and eat and drink.
And Jehovah saith unto Moses, ’Come up unto Me to the mount, and be there, and I give to thee the tables of stone, and the la, and the command, hich I have ritten to direct them.’
And Moses riseth — Joshua his minister also — and Moses goeth up unto the mount of God;
and unto the elders he hath said, ’Abide ye for us in this [place], until that e turn back unto you, and lo, Aaron and Hur [are] ith you — he ho hath matters doth come nigh unto them.’
And Moses goeth up unto the mount, and the cloud covereth the mount;
and the honour of Jehovah doth tabernacle on mount Sinai, and the cloud covereth it six days, and He calleth unto Moses on the seventh day from the midst of the cloud.
And the appearance of the honour of Jehovah [is] as a consuming fire on the top of the mount, before the eyes of the sons of Israel;
and Moses goeth into the midst of the cloud, and goeth up unto the mount, and Moses is on the mount forty days and forty nights.
And Jehovah speaketh unto Moses, saying,
’Speak unto the sons of Israel, and they take for Me a heave-offering; from every man hose heart impelleth him ye do take My heave-offering.
’And this [is] the heave-offering hich ye take from them; gold, and silver, and brass,
and blue, and purple, and scarlet, and linen, and goats’ [hair],
and rams’ skins made red, and badgers’ skins, and shittim ood,
oil for the light, spices for the anointing oil, and for the perfume of the spices,
shoham stones, and stones for setting for an ephod, and for a breastplate.
’And they have made for Me a sanctuary, and I have tabernacled in their midst;
according to all that hich I am sheing thee, the pattern of the tabernacle, and the pattern of all its vessels, even so ye do make [it].
’And they have made an ark of shittim ood; to cubits and a half its length, and a cubit and a half its breadth, and a cubit and a half its height;
and thou hast overlaid it [ith] pure gold, ithin and ithout thou dost overlay it, and thou hast made on it a ring of gold round about.
’And thou hast cast for it four rings of gold, and hast put [them] on its four feet, even to rings on its one side, and to rings on its second side;
and thou hast made staves of shittim ood, and hast overlaid them [ith] gold,
and hast brought the staves into the rings on the sides of the ark, to bear the ark by them,
in the rings of the ark are the staves, they are not turned aside from it;
and thou hast put unto the ark the testimony hich I give unto thee.
’And thou hast made a mercy-seat of pure gold, to cubits and a half its length, and a cubit and a half its breadth;
and thou hast made to cherubs of gold, beaten ork dost thou make them, at the to ends of the mercy-seat;
and make thou one cherub at the end on this side, and one cherub at the end on that; at the mercy-seat ye do make the cherubs on its to ends.
’And the cherubs have been spreading out ings on high, covering the mercy-seat over ith their ings, and their faces [are] one toards another — toards the mercy-seat are the faces of the cherubs.
’And thou hast put the mercy-seat on the ark above, and unto the ark thou dost put the testimony hich I give unto thee;

and I have met ith thee there, and have spoken ith thee from off the mercy-seat (from beteen the to cherubs, hich [are] on the ark of the testimony) all that hich I command thee concerning the sons of Israel.
’And thou hast made a table of shittim ood, to cubits its length, and a cubit its breadth, and a cubit and a half its height,
and hast overlaid it [ith] pure gold, and hast made for it a cron of gold round about,
and hast made for it a border of a handbreadth round about, and hast made a cron of gold to its border round about.
’And thou hast made to it four rings of gold, and hast put the rings on the four corners, hich [are] to its four feet;
over-against the border are the rings for places for staves to bear the table;
and thou hast made the staves of shittim ood, and hast overlaid them ith gold, and the table hath been borne ith them;
and thou hast made its dishes, and its bols, and its covers, and its cups, ith hich they pour out; of pure gold thou dost make them;
and thou hast put on the table bread of the presence before Me continually.
’And thou hast made a candlestick of pure gold, of beaten ork is the candlestick made; its base, and its branch, its calyxes, its knops, and its floers are of the same;
and six branches are coming out of its sides, three branches of the candlestick out of the one side, and three branches of the candlestick out of the second side;

three calyxes made like almonds in the one branch, a knop and a floer, and three calyxes made like almonds in one branch, a knop and a floer; so for the six branches hich are coming out from the candlestick.
’And in the candlestick [are] four calyxes made like almonds, its knops and its floers;
and a knop under to branches of the same, and a knop under to branches of the same, and a knop under to branches of the same, [are] to the six branches hich are coming out of the candlestick;
their knops and their branches are of the same, all of it one beaten ork of pure gold;
and thou hast made its seven lamps, and [one] hath caused its lights to go up, and it hath given light over-against its front.
’And its snuffers and its snuff dishes [are] of pure gold;
of a talent of pure gold he doth make it, ith all these vessels.
And see thou and do [them] by their pattern hich thou art shen in the mount.
’And thou dost make the tabernacle: ten curtains of tined linen, and blue, and purple, and scarlet; [ith] cherubs, ork of a designer, thou dost make them;
the length of the one curtain [is] eight and tenty by the cubit, and the breadth of the one curtain four by the cubit, one measure [is] to all the curtains;
five of the curtains are joining one unto another, and five curtains are joining one to another.
’And thou hast made loops of blue upon the edge of the one curtain, at the end in the joining; and so thou makest in the edge of the outermost curtain, in the joining of the second.
fifty loops thou dost make in the one curtain, and fifty loops thou dost make in the edge of the curtain hich [is] in the joining of the second, causing the loops to take hold one unto another;
and thou hast made fifty hooks of gold, and hast joined the curtains one to another by the hooks, and the tabernacle hath been one.
’And thou hast made curtains of goats’ [hair], for a tent over the tabernacle; thou dost make eleven curtains:
the length of the one curtain [is] thirty by the cubit, and the breadth of the one curtain four by the cubit; one measure [is] to the eleven curtains;
and thou hast joined the five curtains apart, and the six curtains apart, and hast doubled the six curtains over-against the front of the tent.
’And thou hast made fifty loops on the edge of the one curtain, the outermost in the joining, and fifty loops on the edge of the curtain hich is joining the second;
and thou hast made fifty hooks of brass, and hast brought in the hooks into the loops, and hast joined the tent, and it hath been one.
’And the superfluity in the curtains of the tent — the half of the curtain hich is superfluous — hath spread over the hinder part of the tabernacle;
and the cubit on this side, and the cubit on that, in the superfluity in the length of the curtains of the tent, is spread out over the sides of the tabernacle, on this and on that, to cover it;
and thou hast made a covering for the tent, of rams’ skins made red, and a covering of badgers’ skins above.
’And thou hast made the boards for the tabernacle, of shittim ood, standing up;
ten cubits [is] the length of the board, and a cubit and a half the breadth of the one board;
to handles [are] to the one board, joined one unto another; so thou dost make for all the boards of the tabernacle;
and thou hast made the boards of the tabernacle: tenty boards for the south side southard;
and forty sockets of silver thou dost make under the tenty boards, to sockets under the one board for its to handles, and to sockets under the other board for its to handles.
’And for the second side of the tabernacle, for the north side, [are] tenty boards,
and their forty sockets of silver, to sockets under the one board, and to sockets under another board.
And for the sides of the tabernacle estard, thou dost make six boards.
And to boards thou dost make for the corners of the tabernacle in the to sides.
And they are pairs beneath, and together they are pairs above its head unto the one ring; so is it for them both, they are for the to corners.
And they have been eight boards, and their sockets of silver [are] sixteen sockets, to sockets under the one board, and to sockets under another board.
’And thou hast made bars of shittim ood: five for the boards of the one side of the tabernacle,
and five bars for the boards of the second side of the tabernacle, and five bars for the boards of the side of the tabernacle at the to sides, estard;
and one hath caused the middle bar in the midst of the boards to reach from end unto end;
and the boards thou dost overlay [ith] gold, and their rings thou dost make of gold places for bars, and hast overlaid their bars ith gold;
and thou hast raised up the tabernacle according to its fashion hich thou hast been shen in the mount.
’And thou hast made a vail of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and tined linen, ork of a designer; he maketh it [ith] cherubs;
and thou hast put it on four pillars of shittim ood, overlaid [ith] gold, their pegs [are] of gold, on four sockets of silver.
’And thou hast put the vail under the hooks, and hast brought in thither ithin the vail the ark of the testimony; and the vail hath made a separation for you beteen the holy and the holy of holies.
’And thou hast put the mercy-seat on the ark of the testimony, in the holy of holies.
’And thou hast set the table at the outside of the vail, and the candlestick over-against the table on the side of the tabernacle southard, and the table thou dost put on the north side.
’And thou hast made a covering for the opening of the tent, blue, and purple, and scarlet, and tined linen, ork of an embroiderer;
and thou hast made for the covering five pillars of shittim [ood], and hast overlaid them [ith] gold, their pegs [are] of gold, and thou hast cast for them five sockets of brass.
’And thou hast made the altar of shittim ood, five cubits the length, and five cubits the breadth — the altar is square — and three cubits its height.
And thou hast made its horns on its four corners, its horns are of the same, and thou hast overlaid it [ith] brass.
And thou hast made its pots to remove its ashes, and its shovels, and its bols, and its forks, and its fire-pans, even all its vessels thou dost make of brass.
’And thou hast made for it a grate of net-ork of brass, and hast made on the net four rings of brass on its four extremities,
and hast put it under the compass of the altar beneath, and the net hath been unto the middle of the altar.
’And thou hast made staves for the altar, staves of shittim ood, and hast overlaid them [ith] brass.
And the staves have been brought into the rings, and the staves have been on the to sides of the altar in bearing it.
Hollo ith boards thou dost make it, as it hath been sheed thee in the mount, so do they make [it].
’And thou hast made the court of the tabernacle: for the south side southard, hangings for the court of tined linen, a hundred by the cubit [is] the length for the one side,
and its tenty pillars and their tenty sockets [are] of brass, the pegs of the pillars and their fillets [are] of silver;
and so for the north side in length, hangings of a hundred [cubits] in length, and its tenty pillars and their tenty sockets [are] of brass, the pegs of the pillars and their fillets [are] of silver.
’And [for] the breadth of the court at the est side [are] hangings of fifty cubits, their pillars ten, and their sockets ten.
And [for] the breadth of the court at the east side, eastard, [are] fifty cubits.
And the hangings at the side [are] fifteen cubits, their pillars three, and their sockets three.
And at the second side [are] hangings fifteen [cubits], their pillars three, and their sockets three.
’And for the gate of the court a covering of tenty cubits, blue, and purple, and scarlet, and tined linen, ork of an embroiderer; their pillars four, their sockets four.
All the pillars of the court round about [are] filleted [ith] silver, their pegs [are] silver, and their sockets brass.
’The length of the court [is] a hundred by the cubit, and the breadth fifty by fifty, and the height five cubits, of tined linen, and their sockets [are] brass,
even all the vessels of the tabernacle, in all its service, and all its pins, and all the pins of the court, [are] brass.
’And thou — thou dost command the sons of Israel, and they bring unto thee pure beaten olive oil for the light, to cause the lamp to go up continually;

in the tent of meeting, at the outside of the vail, hich [is] over the testimony, doth Aaron — his sons also — arrange it from evening till morning before Jehovah — a statute age-during to their generations, from the sons of Israel.

’And thou, bring thou near unto thee Aaron thy brother, and his sons ith him, from the midst of the sons of Israel, for his being priest to Me, [even] Aaron, Nadab, and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar, sons of Aaron;
and thou hast made holy garments for Aaron thy brother, for honour and for beauty;
and thou — thou dost speak unto all the ise of heart, hom I have filled [ith] a spirit of isdom, and they have made the garments of Aaron to sanctify him for his being priest to Me.

’And these [are] the garments hich they make: a breastplate, and an ephod, and an upper robe, and an embroidered coat, a mitre, and a girdle; yea, they have made holy garments for Aaron thy brother, and for his sons, for his being priest to Me.
’And they take the gold, and the blue, and the purple, and the scarlet, and the linen,
and have made the ephod of gold, blue, and purple, and scarlet, and tined linen, ork of a designer;
it hath to shoulders joining at its to ends, and it is joined.
’And the girdle of his ephod hich [is] on him, according to its ork, is of the same, of gold, blue, and purple, and scarlet, and tined linen.
’And thou hast taken the to shoham stones, and hast opened on them the names of the sons of Israel;
six of their names on the one stone, and the names of the remaining six on the second stone, according to their births;
the ork of an engraver in stone, openings of a signet, thou dost open the to stones by the names of the sons of Israel; turned round, embroidered [ith] gold, thou dost make them.
’And thou hast set the to stones on the shoulders of the ephod — stones of memorial to the sons of Israel — and Aaron hath borne their names before Jehovah, on his to shoulders, for a memorial.
’And thou hast made embroidered things of gold,
and to chains of pure gold, reathed ork thou dost make them, ork of thick bands, and thou hast put the thick chains on the embroidered things.
’And thou hast made a breastplate of judgment, ork of a designer; according to the ork of the ephod thou dost make it; of gold, blue, and purple, and scarlet, and tined linen thou dost make it;
it is square, doubled, a span its length, and a span its breadth.
’And thou hast set in it settings of stone, four ros of stone; a ro of sardius, topaz, and carbuncle [is] the first ro;
and the second ro [is] emerald, sapphire, and diamond;
and the third ro [is] opal, agate, and amethyst;
and the fourth ro [is] beryl, and onyx, and jasper; embroidered ith gold are they in their settings,
and the stones are according to the names of the sons of Israel, telve, according to their names, openings of a signet, each by his name are they for the telve tribes.
’And thou hast made on the breastplate reathed chains, ork of thick bands, of pure gold;
and thou hast made on the breastplate to rings of gold, and hast put the to rings on the to ends of the breastplate;
and thou hast put the to thick bands of gold on the to rings at the ends of the breastplate;
and the to ends of the to thick bands thou dost put on the to embroidered things, and thou hast put [them] on the shoulders of the ephod over-against its face.
’And thou hast made to rings of gold, and hast set them on the to ends of the breastplate, on its border, hich [is] over-against the ephod ithin;
and thou hast made to rings of gold, and hast put them on the to shoulders of the ephod, beneath, over-against its front, over-against its joining, above the girdle of the ephod,
and they bind the breastplate by its rings unto the rings of the ephod ith a ribbon of blue, to be above the girdle of the ephod, and the breastplate is not loosed from the ephod.
’And Aaron hath borne the names of the sons of Israel in the breastplate of judgment, on his heart, in his going in unto the sanctuary, for a memorial before Jehovah continually.

’And thou hast put unto the breastplate of judgment the Lights and the Perfections, and they have been on the heart of Aaron, in his going in before Jehovah, and Aaron hath borne the judgment of the sons of Israel on his heart before Jehovah continually.
’And thou hast made the upper robe of the ephod completely of blue,
and the opening for its head hath been in its midst, a border is to its opening round about, ork of a eaver, as the opening of a habergeon there is to it; it is not rent.
’And thou hast made on its hem pomegranates of blue, and purple, and scarlet, on its hem round about, and bells of gold in their midst round about;
a bell of gold and a pomegranate, a bell of gold and a pomegranate [are] on the hems of the upper robe round about.
’And it hath been on Aaron to minister in, and its sound hath been heard in his coming in unto the sanctuary before Jehovah, and in his going out, and he doth not die.
’And thou hast made a floer of pure gold, and hast opened on it — openings of a signet — ’Holy to Jehovah;’
and thou hast put it on a blue ribbon, and it hath been on the mitre — over-against the front of the mitre it is;

and it hath been on the forehead of Aaron, and Aaron hath borne the iniquity of the holy things hich the sons of Israel do hallo, even all their holy gifts; and it hath been on his forehead continually for a pleasing thing for them before Jehovah.
’And thou hast embroidered the coat of linen, and hast made a mitre of linen, and a girdle thou dost make — ork of an embroiderer.
’And for the sons of Aaron thou dost make coats, and thou hast made for them girdles, yea, bonnets thou dost make for them, for honour and for beauty;
and thou hast clothed Aaron thy brother ith them, and his sons ith him, and hast anointed them, and hast consecrated their hand, and hast sanctified them, and they have been priests to Me.
’And make thou for them linen trousers to cover the naked flesh: they are from the loins even unto the thighs;

and they have been on Aaron and on his sons, in their going in unto the tent of meeting, or in their draing nigh unto the altar to minister in the sanctuary, and they do not bear iniquity nor have they died; a statute age-during to him, and to his seed after him.
’And this [is] the thing hich thou dost to them, to hallo them, for being priests to Me: Take one bullock, a son of the herd, and to rams, perfect ones,
and bread unleavened, and cakes unleavened anointed ith oil, of fine heaten flour thou dost make them,
and thou hast put them on one basket, and hast brought them near in the basket, also the bullock and the to rams.
’And Aaron and his sons thou dost bring near unto the opening of the tent of meeting, and hast bathed them ith ater;
and thou hast taken the garments, and hast clothed Aaron ith the coat, and the upper robe of the ephod, and the ephod, and the breastplate, and hast girded him ith the girdle of the ephod,
and hast set the mitre on his head, and hast put the holy cron on the mitre,
and hast taken the anointing oil, and hast poured [it] on his head, and hast anointed him.
’And his sons thou dost bring near, and hast clothed them [ith] coats,

and hast girded them [ith] a girdle (Aaron and his sons), and hast bound on them bonnets; and the priesthood hath been theirs by a statute age-during, and thou hast consecrated the hand of Aaron, and the hand of his sons,
and hast brought near the bullock before the tent of meeting, and Aaron hath laid — his sons also — their hands on the head of the bullock.
’And thou hast slaughtered the bullock before Jehovah, at the opening of the tent of meeting,
and hast taken of the blood of the bullock, and hast put [it] on the horns of the altar ith thy finger, and all the blood thou dost pour out at the foundation of the altar;
and thou hast taken all the fat hich is covering the inards, and the redundance on the liver, and the to kidneys, and the fat hich [is] on them, and hast made perfume on the altar;
and the flesh of the bullock, and his skin, and his dung, thou dost burn ith fire at the outside of the camp; it [is] a sin-offering.
’And the one ram thou dost take, and Aaron and his sons have laid their hands on the head of the ram,
and thou hast slaughtered the ram, and hast taken its blood, and hast sprinkled [it] on the altar round about,
and the ram thou dost cut into its pieces, and hast ashed its inards, and its legs, and hast put [them] on its pieces, and on its head;
and thou hast made perfume ith the hole ram on the altar. It [is] a burnt-offering to Jehovah, a seet fragrance; a fire-offering it [is] to Jehovah.
’And thou hast taken the second ram, and Aaron hath laid — his sons also — their hands on the head of the ram,

and thou hast slaughtered the ram, and hast taken of its blood, and hast put on the tip of the right ear of Aaron, and on the tip of the right ear of his sons, and on the thumb of their right hand, and on the great toe of their right foot, and hast sprinkled the blood on the altar round about;

and thou hast taken of the blood hich [is] on the altar, and of the anointing oil, and hast sprinkled on Aaron, and on his garments, and on his sons, and on the garments of his sons ith him, and he hath been halloed, he, and his garments, and his sons, and the garments of his sons ith him.

’And thou hast taken from the ram the fat, and the fat tail, and the fat hich is covering the inards, and the redundance on the liver, and the to kidneys, and the fat hich [is] on them, and the right leg, for it [is] a ram of consecration,
and one round cake of bread, and one cake of oiled bread, and one thin cake out of the basket of the unleavened things hich [is] before Jehovah.
’And thou hast set the hole on the hands of Aaron, and on the hands of his sons, and hast aved them — a ave-offering before Jehovah;
and thou hast taken them out of their hand, and hast made perfume on the altar beside the burnt-offering, for seet fragrance before Jehovah; a fire-offering it [is] to Jehovah.
’And thou hast taken the breast from the ram of the consecration hich [is] for Aaron, and hast aved it — a ave-offering before Jehovah, and it hath become thy portion;

and thou hast sanctified the breast of the ave-offering, and the leg of the heave-offering, hich hath been aved, and hich hath been lifted up from the ram of the consecration, of that hich [is] for Aaron, and of that hich [is] for his sons;

and it hath been for Aaron and for his sons, by a statute age-during from the sons of Israel, for it [is] a heave-offering; and it is a heave offering from the sons of Israel, from the sacrifices of their peace-offerings — their heave-offering to Jehovah.
’And the holy garments hich are Aaron’s, are for his sons after him, to be anointed in them, and to consecrate in them their hand;
seven days doth the priest in his stead (of his sons) put them on, hen he goeth in unto the tent of meeting, to minister in the sanctuary.
’And the ram of the consecration thou dost take, and hast boiled its flesh in the holy place;
and Aaron hath eaten — his sons also — the flesh of the ram, and the bread hich [is] in the basket, at the opening of the tent of meeting;
and they have eaten those things by hich there is atonement to consecrate their hand, to sanctify them; and a stranger doth not eat — for they [are] holy;
and if there be left of the flesh of the consecration or of the bread till the morning, then thou hast burned that hich is left ith fire; it is not eaten, for it [is] holy.
’And thou hast done thus to Aaron and to his sons, according to all that I have commanded thee; seven days thou dost consecrate their hand;
and a bullock, a sin-offering, thou dost prepare daily for the atonements, and thou hast atoned for the altar, in thy making atonement on it, and hast anointed it to sanctify it;
seven days thou dost make atonement for the altar, and hast sanctified it, and the altar hath been most holy; all that is coming against the altar is holy.
’And this [is] that hich thou dost prepare on the altar; to lambs, sons of a year, daily continually;
the one lamb thou dost prepare in the morning, and the second lamb thou dost prepare beteen the evenings;
