and a tenth [deal] of fine flour, mixed ith beaten oil, a fourth part of a hin, and a libation, a fourth part of a hin, of ine, [is] for the one lamb.

’And the second lamb thou dost prepare beteen the evenings; according to the present of the morning, and according to its libation, thou dost prepare for it, for seet fragrance, a fire-offering, to Jehovah: —
a continual burnt-offering for your generations, at the opening of the tent of meeting, before Jehovah, hither I am met ith you, to speak unto thee there,
and I have met there ith the sons of Israel, and it hath been sanctified by My honour.
’And I have sanctified the tent of meeting, and the altar, and Aaron and his sons I sanctify for being priests to Me,
and I have tabernacled in the midst of the sons of Israel, and have become their God,
and they have knon that I [am] Jehovah their God, ho hath brought them out of the land of Egypt, that I may tabernacle in their midst; I [am] Jehovah their God.
’And thou hast made an altar [for] making perfume; [of] shittim ood thou dost make it;
a cubit its length, and a cubit its breadth, (it is square), and to cubits its height; its horns [are] of the same.
’And thou hast overlaid it ith pure gold, its top, and its sides round about, and its horns; and thou hast made to it a cron of gold round about;
and to rings of gold thou dost make to it under its cron; on its to ribs thou dost make [them], on its to sides, and they have become places for staves, to bear it ith them.
’And thou hast made the staves of shittim ood, and hast overlaid them ith gold;
and thou hast put it before the vail, hich [is] by the ark of the testimony, before the mercy-seat hich [is] over the testimony, hither I am met ith thee.
’And Aaron hath made perfume on it, perfume of spices, morning by morning; in his making the lamps right he doth perfume it,
and in Aaron’s causing the lamps to go up beteen the evenings, he doth perfume it; a continual perfume before Jehovah to your generations.
’Ye do not cause strange perfume to go up upon it, and burnt-offering, and present, and libation ye do not pour out on it;

and Aaron hath made atonement on its horns, once in a year, by the blood of the sin-offering of atonements; once in a year doth he make atonement for it, to your generations; it [is] most holy to Jehovah.’
And Jehovah speaketh unto Moses, saying,

’When thou takest up the sum of the sons of Israel for their numbers, then they have given each an atonement [for] his soul to Jehovah in their being numbered, and there is no plague among them in their being numbered.
’This they do give, every one passing over unto those numbered, half a shekel, by the shekel of the sanctuary (the shekel [is] tenty gerahs); half a shekel [is] the heave-offering to Jehovah;
every one passing over unto those numbered, from a son of tenty years and upards, doth give the heave-offering of Jehovah;
the rich doth not multiply, and the poor doth not diminish from the half-shekel, to give the heave-offering of Jehovah, to make atonement for your souls.

’And thou hast taken the atonement-money from the sons of Israel, and hast given it for the service of the tent of meeting; and it hath been to the sons of Israel for a memorial before Jehovah, to make atonement for your souls.’
And Jehovah speaketh unto Moses, saying,
’And thou hast made a laver of brass (and its base of brass), for ashing; and thou hast put it beteen the tent of meeting and the altar, and hast put ater there;
and Aaron and his sons have ashed at it their hands and their feet,
in their going in unto the tent of meeting they ash [ith] ater, and die not; or in their draing nigh unto the altar to minister, to perfume a fire-offering to Jehovah,
then they have ashed their hands and their feet, and they die not, and it hath been to them a statute age-during, to him and to his seed to their generations.’
And Jehovah speaketh unto Moses, saying,
’And thou, take to thyself principal spices, ild honey five hundred [shekels]; and spice-cinnamon, the half of that, to hundred and fifty; and spice-cane to hundred and fifty;
and cassia five hundred, by the shekel of the sanctuary, and olive oil a hin;
and thou hast made it a holy anointing oil, a compound mixture, ork of a compounder; it is a holy anointing oil.
’And thou hast anointed ith it the tent of meeting, and the ark of the testimony,
and the table and all its vessels, and the candlestick and its vessels, and the altar of perfume,
and the altar of burnt-offering and all its vessels, and the laver and its base;
and thou hast sanctified them, and they have been most holy; all that is coming against them is holy;
and Aaron and his sons thou dost anoint, and hast sanctified them for being priests to Me.
’And unto the sons of Israel thou dost speak, saying, A holy anointing oil is this to Me, to your generations;
on flesh of man it is not poured, and ith its proper proportion ye make none like it; it [is] holy; it is holy to you;
a man ho compoundeth [any] like it, or ho putteth of it on a stranger — hath even been cut off from his people.’
And Jehovah saith unto Moses, ’Take to thee spices, stacte, and onycha, and galbanum, spices and pure frankincense; they are part for part;
and thou hast made it a perfume, a compound, ork of a compounder, salted, pure, holy;
and thou hast beaten [some] of it small, and hast put of it before the testimony, in the tent of meeting, hither I am met ith thee; most holy it is to you.
’As to the perfume hich thou makest, ith its proper proportion ye do not make to yourselves, holy it is to thee to Jehovah;
a man ho maketh [any] like it — to be refreshed by it — hath even been cut off from his people.’
And Jehovah speaketh unto Moses, saying,
’See, I have called by name Bezaleel, son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah,
and I fill him [ith] the Spirit of God, in isdom, and in understanding, and in knoledge, and in all ork,
to devise devices to ork in gold, and in silver, and in brass,
and in graving of stone for settings, and in graving of ood to ork in all ork.
’And I, lo, I have given ith him Aholiab, son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, and in the heart of every ise-hearted one I have given isdom, and they have made all that hich I have commanded thee.
’The tent of meeting, and the ark of testimony, and the mercy-seat hich [is] on it, and all the vessels of the tent,
and the table and its vessels, and the pure candlestick and all its vessels, and the altar of the perfume,
and the altar of the burnt-offering and all its vessels, and the laver and its base,
and the coloured garments, and the holy garments for Aaron the priest, and the garments of his sons, for acting as priests in;
and the anointing oil, and the perfume of the spices for the sanctuary; according to all that I have commanded thee — they do.’
And Jehovah speaketh unto Moses, saying,
’And thou, speak unto the sons of Israel, saying, Only, My sabbaths ye do keep, for it [is] a sign beteen Me and you, to your generations, to kno that I, Jehovah, am sanctifying you;
and ye have kept the sabbath, for it [is] holy to you, he ho is polluting it is certainly put to death — for any ho doeth ork in it — that person hath even been cut off from the midst of his people.
’Six days is ork done, and in the seventh day [is] a sabbath of holy rest to Jehovah; any ho doeth ork in the sabbath-day is certainly put to death,
and the sons of Israel have observed the sabbath; to keep the sabbath to their generations [is] a covenant age-during,
beteen Me and the sons of Israel it [is] a sign — to the age; for six days Jehovah made the heavens and the earth, and in the seventh day He hath ceased, and is refreshed.’
And He giveth unto Moses, hen He finisheth speaking ith him in mount Sinai, to tables of the testimony, tables of stone, ritten by the finger of God.

And the people see that Moses is delaying to come don from the mount, and the people assemble against Aaron, and say unto him, ’Rise, make for us gods ho go before us, for this Moses — the man ho brought us up out of the land of Egypt — e have not knon hat hath happened to him.’
And Aaron saith unto them, ’Break off the rings of gold hich [are] in the ears of your ives, your sons, and your daughters, and bring in unto me;’
and all the people themselves break off the rings of gold hich [are] in their ears, and bring in unto Aaron,
and he receiveth from their hand, and doth fashion it ith a graving tool, and doth make it a molten calf, and they say, ’These thy gods, O Israel, ho brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.’
And Aaron seeth, and buildeth an altar before it, and Aaron calleth, and saith, ’A festival to Jehovah — to-morro;’
and they rise early on the morro, and cause burnt-offerings to ascend, and bring nigh peace-offerings; and the people sit don to eat and to drink, and rise up to play.
And Jehovah saith unto Moses, ’Go, descend, for thy people hom thou hast brought up out of the land of Egypt hath done corruptly,

they have turned aside hastily from the ay that I have commanded them; they have made for themselves a molten calf, and bo themselves to it, and sacrifice to it, and say, These thy gods, O Israel, ho brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.’
And Jehovah saith unto Moses, ’I have seen this people, and lo, it [is] a stiff-necked people;
and no, let Me alone, and My anger doth burn against them, and I consume them, and I make thee become a great nation.’

And Moses appeaseth the face of Jehovah his God, and saith, ’Why, O Jehovah, doth Thine anger burn against Thy people, hom Thou hast brought forth out of the land of Egypt ith great poer and ith a strong hand?

hy do the Egyptians speak, saying, For evil He brought them out to slay them among mountains, and to consume them from off the face of the ground? turn back from the heat of Thine anger, and repent of the evil against Thy people.

’Be mindful of Abraham, of Isaac, and of Israel, Thy servants, to hom Thou hast sorn by Thyself, and unto hom Thou speakest: I multiply your seed as stars of the heavens, and all this land, as I have said, I give to your seed, and they have inherited to the age;’
and Jehovah repenteth of the evil hich He hath spoken of doing to His people.
And Moses turneth, and goeth don from the mount, and the to tables of the testimony [are] in his hand, tables ritten on both their sides, on this and on that [are] they ritten;
and the tables are the ork of God, and the riting is the riting of God, graven on the tables.
And Joshua heareth the voice of the people in their shouting, and saith unto Moses, ’A noise of battle in the camp!’
and he saith, ’It is not the voice of the crying of might, nor is it the voice of the crying of eakness — a voice of singing I am hearing.’

And it cometh to pass, hen he hath dran near unto the camp, that he seeth the calf, and the dancing, and the anger of Moses burneth, and he casteth out of his hands the tables, and breaketh them under the mount;
and he taketh the calf hich they have made, and burneth [it] ith fire, and grindeth until [it is] small, and scattereth on the face of the aters, and causeth the sons of Israel to drink.
And Moses saith unto Aaron, ’What hath this people done to thee, that thou hast brought in upon it a great sin?’
and Aaron saith, ’Let not the anger of my lord burn; thou — thou hast knon the people that it [is] in evil;
and they say to me, Make for us gods, ho go before us, for this Moses — the man ho brought us up out of the land of Egypt — e have not knon hat hath happened to him;
and I say to them, Whoso hath gold, let them break [it] off, and they give to me, and I cast it into the fire, and this calf cometh out.’
And Moses seeth the people that it [is] unbridled, for Aaron hath made it unbridled for contempt among its ithstanders,
and Moses standeth in the gate of the camp, and saith, ’Who [is] for Jehovah? — unto me!’ and all the sons of Levi are gathered unto him;

and he saith to them, ’Thus said Jehovah, God of Israel, Put each his sord by his thigh, pass over and turn back from gate to gate through the camp, and slay each his brother, and each his friend, and each his relation.’
And the sons of Levi do according to the ord of Moses, and there fall of the people on that day about three thousand men,
and Moses saith, ’Consecrate your hand to-day to Jehovah, for a man [is] against his son, and against his brother, so as to bring on you to-day a blessing.’
And it cometh to pass, on the morro, that Moses saith unto the people, ’Ye — ye have sinned a great sin, and no I go up unto Jehovah, if so be I atone for your sin.’
And Moses turneth back unto Jehovah, and saith, ’Oh this people hath sinned a great sin, that they make to themselves a god of gold;
and no, if Thou takest aay their sin — and if not — blot me, I pray thee, out of Thy book hich Thou hast ritten.’
And Jehovah saith unto Moses, ’Whoso hath sinned against Me — I blot him out of My book;
and no, go, lead the people hithersoever I have spoken to thee of; lo, My messenger goeth before thee, and in the day of my charging — then I have charged upon them their sin.’
And Jehovah plagueth the people, because they made the calf hich Aaron made.

And Jehovah speaketh unto Moses, ’Go, ascend from this [place], thou and the people, hom thou hast brought up out of the land of Egypt, unto the land hich I have sorn to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, saying, To thy seed I give it,’
(and I have sent before thee a messenger, and have cast out the Canaanite, the Amorite, and the Hittite, and the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite,)
unto a land floing ith milk and honey, for I do not go up in thy midst, for thou [art] a stiff-necked people — lest I consume thee in the ay.’
And the people hear this sad thing, and mourn; and none put his ornaments on him.

And Jehovah saith unto Moses, ’Say unto the sons of Israel, Ye [are] a stiff-necked people; one moment — I come up into thy midst, and have consumed thee; and no, put don thine ornaments from off thee, and I kno hat I do to thee;’
and the sons of Israel take off their ornaments at mount Horeb.

And Moses taketh the tent, and hath stretched it out at the outside of the camp, afar off from the camp, and hath called it, ’Tent of Meeting;’ and it hath come to pass, every one seeking Jehovah goeth out unto the tent of meeting, hich [is] at the outside of the camp.

And it hath come to pass, at the going out of Moses unto the tent, all the people rise, and have stood, each at the opening of his tent, and have looked expectingly after Moses, until his going into the tent.
And it hath come to pass, at the going in of Moses to the tent, the pillar of the cloud cometh don, and hath stood at the opening of the tent, and He hath spoken ith Moses;
and all the people have seen the pillar of the cloud standing at the opening of the tent, and all the people have risen and boed themselves, each at the opening of his tent.

And Jehovah hath spoken unto Moses face unto face, as a man speaketh unto his friend; and he hath turned back unto the camp, and his minister Joshua, son of Nun, a youth, departeth not out of the tent.

And Moses saith unto Jehovah, ’See, Thou art saying unto me, Bring up this people, and Thou hast not caused me to kno hom Thou dost send ith me; and Thou hast said, I have knon thee by name, and also thou hast found grace in Mine eyes.
’And no, if, I pray Thee, I have found grace in Thine eyes, cause me to kno, I pray Thee, Thy ay, and I kno Thee, so that I find grace in Thine eyes, and consider that this nation [is] Thy people;’
and He saith, ’My presence doth go, and I have given rest to thee.’
And he saith unto Him, ’If Thy presence is not going — take us not up from this [place];

and in hat is it knon no, that I have found grace in Thine eyes — I and Thy people — is it not in Thy going ith us? and e have been distinguished — I and Thy people — from all the people ho [are] on the face of the ground.’
And Jehovah saith unto Moses, ’Even this thing hich thou hast spoken I do; for thou hast found grace in Mine eyes, and I kno thee by name.’
And he saith, ’She me, I pray Thee, Thine honour;’
and He saith, ’I cause all My goodness to pass before thy face, and have called concerning the Name of Jehovah before thee, and favoured him hom I favour, and loved him hom I love.’
He saith also, ’Thou art unable to see My face, for man doth not see Me, and live;’
Jehovah also saith, ’Lo, a place [is] by Me, and thou hast stood on the rock,
and it hath come to pass, in the passing by of Mine honour, that I have set thee in a cleft of the rock, and spread out My hands over thee, until My passing by,
and I have turned aside My hands, and thou hast seen My back parts, and My face is not seen.’
And Jehovah saith unto Moses, ’He for thyself to tables of stone like the first, and I have ritten on the tables the ords hich ere on the first tables hich thou hast broken;
and be prepared at morning, and thou hast come up in the morning unto mount Sinai, and hast stood before Me there, on the top of the mount,
and no man cometh up ith thee, and also no man is seen in all the mount, also the flock and the herd do not feed over-against that mount.’
And he heeth to tables of stone like the first, and Moses riseth early in the morning, and goeth up unto mount Sinai, as Jehovah commanded him, and he taketh in his hand to tables of stone.
And Jehovah cometh don in a cloud, and stationeth Himself ith him there, and calleth in the Name of Jehovah,
and Jehovah passeth over before his face, and calleth: ’Jehovah, Jehovah God, merciful and gracious, slo to anger, and abundant in kindness and truth,

keeping kindness for thousands, taking aay iniquity, and transgression, and sin, and not entirely acquitting, charging iniquity of fathers on children, and on children’s children, on a third [generation], and on a fourth.’
And Moses hasteth, and boeth to the earth, and doth obeisance,

and saith, ’If, I pray Thee, I have found grace in Thine eyes, O my Lord, let my Lord, I pray Thee, go in our midst (for it [is] a stiff-necked people), and thou hast forgiven our iniquity and our sin, and hast inherited us.’

And He saith, ’Lo, I am making a covenant: before all thy people I do onders, hich have not been done in all the earth, or in any nation, and all the people in hose midst thou [art] have seen the ork of Jehovah, for it [is] fearful that hich I am doing ith thee.
’Observe for thyself that hich I am commanding thee to-day: lo, I am casting out from before thee the Amorite, and the Canaanite, and the Hittite, and the Perizzite, and the Hivite, and the Jebusite;
take heed to thyself, lest thou make a covenant ith the inhabitant of the land into hich thou art going, lest it become a snare in thy midst;
for their altars ye break don, and their standing pillars ye shiver, and its shrines ye cut don;
for ye do not bo yourselves to another god — for Jehovah, hose name [is] Zealous, is a zealous God.

’Lest thou make a covenant ith the inhabitant of the land, and they have gone a-horing after their gods, and have sacrificed to their gods, and [one] hath called to thee, and thou hast eaten of his sacrifice,
and thou hast taken of their daughters to thy sons, and their daughters have gone a-horing after their gods, and have caused thy sons to go a-horing after their gods;
a molten god thou dost not make to thyself.

’The feast of unleavened things thou dost keep; seven days thou dost eat unleavened things, as I have commanded thee, at an appointed time, the month of Abib: for in the month of Abib thou didst come out from Egypt.
’All opening a omb [are] Mine, and every firstling of thy cattle born a male, ox or sheep;

and the firstling of an ass thou dost ransom ith a lamb; and if thou dost not ransom, then thou hast beheaded it; every first-born of thy sons thou dost ransom, and they do not appear before Me empty.
’Six days thou dost ork, and on the seventh day thou dost rest; in ploughing-time and in harvest thou dost rest.
’And a feast of eeks thou dost observe for thyself; first-fruits of heat-harvest; and the feast of in-gathering, at the revolution of the year.
’Three times in a year do all thy males appear before the Lord Jehovah, God of Israel;
for I dispossess nations from before thee, and have enlarged thy border, and no man doth desire thy land in thy going up to appear before Jehovah thy God three times in a year.
’Thou dost not slaughter ith a fermented thing the blood of My sacrifice; and the sacrifice of the feast of the passover doth not remain till morning:
the first of the first-fruits of the land thou dost bring into the house of Jehovah thy God; thou dost not boil a kid in its mother’s milk.’
And Jehovah saith unto Moses, ’Write for thyself these ords, for, according to the tenor of these ords I have made ith thee a covenant, and ith Israel.’
And he is there ith Jehovah forty days and forty nights; bread he hath not eaten, and ater he hath not drunk; and he riteth on the tables the matters of the covenant — the ten matters.

And it cometh to pass, hen Moses is coming don from mount Sinai (and the to tables of the testimony [are] in the hand of Moses in his coming don from the mount), that Moses hath not knon that the skin of his face hath shone in His speaking ith him,
and Aaron seeth — all the sons of Israel also — Moses, and lo, the skin of his face hath shone, and they are afraid of coming nigh unto him.
And Moses calleth unto them, and Aaron and all the princes in the company return unto him, and Moses speaketh unto them;
and afterards have all the sons of Israel come nigh, and he chargeth them ith all that Jehovah hath spoken ith him in mount Sinai.
And Moses finisheth speaking ith them, and putteth on his face a vail;
and in the going in of Moses before Jehovah to speak ith Him, he turneth aside the vail until his coming out; and he hath come out and hath spoken unto the sons of Israel that hich he is commanded;
and the sons of Israel have seen the face of Moses that the skin of the face of Moses hath shone, and Moses hath put back the vail on his face until his going in to speak ith Him.
And Moses assembleth all the company of the sons of Israel, and saith unto them, ’These [are] the things hich Jehovah hath commanded — to do them:
Six days is ork done, and on the seventh day there is to you a holy [day], a sabbath of rest to Jehovah; any ho doeth ork in it is put to death;
ye do not burn a fire in any of your dellings on the sabbath-day.’
And Moses speaketh unto all the company of the sons of Israel, saying, ’This [is] the thing hich Jehovah hath commanded, saying,
Take ye from among you a heave-offering to Jehovah; every one hose heart [is] illing doth bring it, — the heave-offering of Jehovah, — gold, and silver, and brass,
and blue, and purple, and scarlet, and linen, and goats’ [hair],
and rams’ skins made red, and badgers’ skins, and shittim ood,
and oil for the light, and spices for the anointing oil, and for the spice perfume,
and shoham stones, and stones for settings, for an ephod, and for a breastplate.
’And all the ise-hearted among you come in, and make all that Jehovah hath commanded:
’The tabernacle, its tent, and its covering, its hooks, and its boards, its bars, its pillars, and its sockets,
’The ark and its staves, the mercy-seat, and the vail of the covering,
’The table and its staves, and all its vessels, and the bread of the presence,
’And the candlestick for the light, and its vessels, and its lamps, and the oil for the light,
’And the altar of perfume, and its staves, and the anointing oil, and the spice perfume, and the covering of the opening at the opening of the tabernacle,
’The altar of burnt-offering and the brazen grate hich it hath, its staves, and all its vessels, the laver and its base,
’The hangings of the court, its pillars, and their sockets, and the covering of the gate of the court,
’The pins of the tabernacle, and the pins of the court, and their cords,
’The coloured garments, to do service in the sanctuary, the holy garments for Aaron the priest, and the garments of his sons to act as priest in.’
And all the company of the sons of Israel go out from the presence of Moses,

and they come in — every man hom his heart hath lifted up, and every one hom his spirit hath made illing — they have brought in the heave-offering of Jehovah for the ork of the tent of meeting, and for all its service, and for the holy garments.

And they come in — the men ith the omen — every illing-hearted one — they have brought in nose-ring, and ear-ring, and seal-ring, and necklace, all golden goods, even every one ho hath aved a ave-offering of gold to Jehovah.
And every man ith hom hath been found blue, and purple, and scarlet, and linen, and goats’ [hair], and rams’ skins made red, and badgers’ skins, have brought [them] in;
every one lifting up a heave-offering of silver and brass have brought in the heave-offering of Jehovah; and every one ith hom hath been found shittim ood for any ork of the service brought [it] in.
And every ise-hearted oman hath spun ith her hands, and they bring in yarn, the blue, and the purple, the scarlet, and the linen;
and all the omen hose heart hath lifted them up in isdom, have spun the goats’ [hair].
And the princes have brought in the shoham stones, and the stones for settings, for the ephod, and for the breastplate,
and the spices, and the oil for the light, and for the anointing oil, and for the spice perfume;

every man and oman (hom their heart hath made illing to bring in for all the ork hich Jehovah commanded to be done by the hand of Moses) [of] the sons of Israel brought in a illing-offering to Jehovah.
And Moses saith unto the sons of Israel, ’See, Jehovah hath called by name Bezaleel, son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah,
and He doth fill him [ith] the Spirit of God, in isdom, in understanding, and in knoledge, and in all ork,
even to devise devices to ork in gold, and in silver, and in brass,
and in graving of stones for settings, and in graving of ood to ork in any ork of design.
’And to direct He hath put in his heart, he and Aholiab, son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan;

He hath filled them ith isdom of heart to do every ork, of engraver, and designer, and embroiderer (in blue, and in purple, in scarlet, and in linen), and eaver, ho do any ork, and of designers of designs.

And Bezaleel, and Aholiab, and every ise-hearted man, in hom Jehovah hath given isdom and understanding to kno to do every ork of the service of the sanctuary, have done according to all that Jehovah commanded.
And Moses calleth unto Bezaleel, and unto Aholiab, and unto every ise-hearted man in hose heart Jehovah hath given isdom, every one hom his heart lifted up, to come near unto the ork to do it.

And they take from before Moses all the heave-offering hich the sons of Israel have brought in for the ork of the service of the sanctuary to do it; and still they have brought in unto him a illing-offering morning by morning.
And all the ise men, ho are doing all the ork of the sanctuary, come each from his ork hich they are doing,
and speak unto Moses, saying, ’The people are multiplying to bring in more than sufficient for the service of the ork hich Jehovah commanded to make.’

And Moses commandeth, and they cause a voice to pass over through the camp, saying, ’Let not man or oman make any more ork for the heave-offering of the sanctuary;’ and the people are restrained from bringing,
and the ork hath been sufficient for them, for all the ork, to do it, and to leave.
And all the ise-hearted ones among the doers of the ork make the tabernacle; ten curtains of tined linen, and blue, and purple, and scarlet, [ith] cherubs, ork of a designer, he hath made them.
The length of the one curtain [is] eight and tenty by the cubit, and the breadth of the one curtain four by the cubit; one measure [is] to all the curtains.
And he joineth the five curtains one unto another, and the [other] five curtains he hath joined one unto another;
and he maketh loops of blue on the edge of the one curtain, at the end, in the joining; so he hath made in the edge of the outmost curtain, in the joining of the second;
fifty loops he hath made in the one curtain, and fifty loops hath he made in the end of the curtain hich [is] in the joining of the second; the loops are taking hold one on another.
And he maketh fifty hooks of gold, and joineth the curtains one unto another by the hooks, and the tabernacle is one.
And he maketh curtains of goats’ [hair] for a tent over the tabernacle; eleven curtains he hath made them;
the length of the one curtain [is] thirty by the cubit, and the breadth of the one curtain [is] four cubits; one measure [is] to the eleven curtains;
and he joineth the five curtains apart, and the six curtains apart.
And he maketh fifty loops on the outer edge of the curtain, in the joining; and fifty loops he hath made on the edge of the curtain hich is joining the second;
and he maketh fifty hooks of brass to join the tent — to be one;
and he maketh a covering for the tent of rams’ skins made red, and a covering of badgers’ skins above.
And he maketh the boards for the tabernacle of shittim ood, standing up;
ten cubits [is] the length of the [one] board, and a cubit and a half the breadth of the [one] board;
to handles [are] to the one board, joined one unto another; so he hath made for all the boards of the tabernacle.
And he maketh the boards for the tabernacle; tenty boards for the south side southard;
and forty sockets of silver he hath made under the tenty boards, to sockets under the one board for its to handles, and to sockets under the other board for its to handles.
And for the second side of the tabernacle, for the north side, he hath made tenty boards,
and their forty sockets of silver, to sockets under the one board, and to sockets under the other board;
and for the sides of the tabernacle, estard, hath he made six boards;
and to boards hath he made for the corners of the tabernacle, in the to sides;
and they have been tins belo, and together they are tins at its head, at the one ring; so he hath done to both of them at the to corners;
and there have been eight boards; and their sockets of silver [are] sixteen sockets, to sockets under the one board.
And he maketh bars of shittim ood, five for the boards of the one side of the tabernacle,
and five bars for the boards of the second side of the tabernacle, and five bars for the boards of the tabernacle, for the sides estard;
and he maketh the middle bar to enter into the midst of the boards from end to end;
and the boards he hath overlaid ith gold, and their rings he hath made of gold, places for bars, and he overlayeth the bars ith gold.
And he maketh the vail of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and tined linen, ork of a designer he hath made it, [ith] cherubs;
and he maketh for it four pillars of shittim [ood], and overlayeth them ith gold; their pegs [are] of gold; and he casteth for them four sockets of silver.
And he maketh a covering for the opening of the tent, of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and tined linen, ork of an embroiderer,
also its five pillars, and their pegs; and he overlaid their tops and their fillets [ith] gold, and their five sockets [are] brass.
And Bezaleel maketh the ark of shittim ood, to cubits and a half its length, and a cubit and a half its breadth, and a cubit and a half its height;
and he overlayeth it ith pure gold ithin and ithout, and maketh for it a reath of gold round about;
and he casteth for it four rings of gold, on its four feet, even to rings on its one side, and to rings on its second side;
and he maketh staves of shittim ood, and overlayeth them ith gold,
and he bringeth in the staves into the rings, by the sides of the ark, to bear the ark.
And he maketh a mercy-seat of pure gold, to cubits and a half its length, and a cubit and a half its breadth;
and he maketh to cherubs of gold, of beaten ork he hath made them, at the to ends of the mercy-seat;
one cherub at the end on this [side], and one cherub at the end on that, out of the mercy-seat he hath made the cherubs, at its to ends;
and the cherubs are spreading out ings on high, covering over the mercy-seat ith their ings, and their faces [are] one toards another; toards the mercy-seat have the faces of the cherubs been.
And he maketh the table of shittim ood; to cubits its length, and a cubit its breadth, and a cubit and a half its height,
and overlayeth it ith pure gold, and maketh for it a reath of gold round about.
And he maketh for it a border of a handbreadth round about, and maketh a reath of gold for its border round about;
and he casteth for it four rings of gold, and putteth the rings on the four corners hich [are] to its four feet;
over-against the border have the rings been, places for staves to bear the table.
And he maketh the staves of shittim ood, and overlayeth them ith gold, to bear the table;
and he maketh the vessels hich [are] upon the table, its dishes, and its bols, and its cups, and the cups by hich they pour out, of pure gold.
And he maketh the candlestick of pure gold; of beaten ork he hath made the candlestick, its base, and its branch, its calyxes, its knops, and its floers, have been of the same;
and six branches are coming out of its sides, three branches of the candlestick out of its one side, and three branches of the candlestick out of its second side;

three calyxes, made like almonds, in the one branch, a knop and a floer; and three calyxes, made like almonds, in another branch, a knop and a floer; so to the six branches hich are coming out of the candlestick.
And in the candlestick [are] four calyxes, made like almonds, its knops, and its floers,
and a knop under the to branches of the same, and a knop under the to branches of the same, and a knop under the to branches of the same, [are] to the six branches hich are coming out of it;
their knops and their branches have been of the same; all of it one beaten ork of pure gold.
And he maketh its seven lamps, and its snuffers, and its snuff-dishes, of pure gold;
of a talent of pure gold he hath made it, and all its vessels.
And he maketh the perfume-altar of shittim ood; a cubit its length, and a cubit its breadth (square), and to cubits its height; its horns have been of the same;
and he overlayeth it ith pure gold, its top and its sides round about, and its horns; and he maketh for it a reath of gold round about;
and to rings of gold he hath made for it under its reath, at its to corners, at its to sides, for places for staves to bear it ith them.
And he maketh the staves of shittim ood, and overlayeth them ith gold;
and he maketh the holy anointing oil, and the pure spice-perfume — ork of a compounder.
And he maketh the altar of burnt-offering of shittim ood, five cubits its length, and five cubits its breadth (square), and three cubits its height;
and he maketh its horns on its four corners; its horns have been of the same; and he overlayeth it ith brass;
and he maketh all the vessels of the altar, the pots, and the shovels, and the sprinkling-pans, the forks, and the fire-pans; all its vessels he hath made of brass.
And he maketh for the altar a brazen grate of net-ork, under its border beneath, unto its midst;
and he casteth four rings for the four ends of the brazen grate — places for bars;
and he maketh the staves of shittim ood, and overlayeth them ith brass;
and he bringeth in the staves into the rings on the sides of the altar, to bear it ith them; hollo [ith] boards he made it.
And he maketh the laver of brass, and its base of brass, ith the looking-glasses of the omen assembling, ho have assembled at the opening of the tent of meeting.
And he maketh the court; at the south side southard, the hangings of the court of tined linen, a hundred by the cubit,
their pillars [are] tenty, and their brazen sockets tenty, the pegs of the pillars and their fillets [are] silver;
and at the north side, a hundred by the cubit, their pillars [are] tenty, and their sockets of brass tenty; the pegs of the pillars and their fillets [are] silver;
and at the est side [are] hangings, fifty by the cubit; their pillars [are] ten, and their sockets ten; the pegs of the pillars and their fillets [are] silver;
and at the east side eastard fifty cubits.
The hangings on the side [are] fifteen cubits, their pillars three, and their sockets three,
and at the second side at the gate of the court, on this and on that, [are] hangings, fifteen cubits, their pillars three, and their sockets three;
all the hangings of the court round about [are] of tined linen,
and the sockets for the pillars of brass, the pegs of the pillars and their fillets of silver, and the overlaying of their tops of silver, and all the pillars of the court are filleted ith silver.

And the covering of the gate of the court [is] the ork of an embroiderer, of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and tined linen; and tenty cubits [is] the length, and the height ith the breadth five cubits, over-against the hangings of the court;
and their pillars [are] four, and their sockets of brass four, their pegs [are] of silver, and the overlaying of their tops and their fillets [are] of silver;
and all the pins for the tabernacle, and for the court round about, [are] of brass.
These are the numberings of the tabernacle (the tabernacle of testimony), hich hath been numbered by the command of Moses, the service of the Levites, by the hand of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.
And Bezaleel son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah, hath made all that Jehovah commanded Moses;
and ith him [is] Aholiab son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, an engraver, and designer, and embroiderer in blue, and in purple, and in scarlet, and in linen.

All the gold hich is prepared for the ork in all the ork of the sanctuary (and it is the gold of the ave-offering) [is] tenty and nine talents, and seven hundred and thirty shekels, by the shekel of the sanctuary.
And the silver of those numbered of the company [is] a hundred talents, and a thousand and seven hundred and five and seventy shekels, by the shekel of the sanctuary;

a bekah for a poll (half a shekel, by the shekel of the sanctuary,) for every one ho is passing over unto those numbered, from a son of tenty years and upards, for six hundred thousand, and three thousand, and five hundred and fifty.
And a hundred talents of silver are to cast the sockets of the sanctuary, and the sockets of the vail; a hundred sockets for the hundred talents, a talent for a socket;
and the thousand and seven hundred and five and seventy he hath made pegs for the pillars, and overlaid their tops, and filleted them.
And the brass of the ave-offering [is] seventy talents, and to thousand and four hundred shekels;
and he maketh ith it the sockets of the opening of the tent of meeting, and the brazen altar, and the brazen grate hich it hath, and all the vessels of the altar,
and the sockets of the court round about, and the sockets of the gate of the court, and all the pins of the tabernacle, and all the pins of the court round about.
And of the blue, and the purple, and the scarlet, they made coloured garments, to minister in the sanctuary; and they make the holy garments hich [are] for Aaron, as Jehovah hath commanded Moses.
And he maketh the ephod, of gold, blue, and purple, and scarlet, and tined linen,

and they expand the plates of gold, and have cut off ires to ork in the midst of the blue, and in the midst of the purple, and in the midst of the scarlet, and in the midst of the linen — ork of a designer;
shoulder-pieces they have made for it, joining; at its to ends it is joined.
And the girdle of his ephod hich [is] on it is of the same, according to its ork, of gold, blue, and purple, and scarlet, and tined linen, as Jehovah hath commanded Moses.
And they prepare the shoham stones, set, embroidered [ith] gold, opened ith openings of a signet, by the names of the sons of Israel;
and he setteth them on the shoulders of the ephod — stones of memorial for the sons of Israel, as Jehovah hath commanded Moses.
And he maketh the breastplate, ork of a designer, like the ork of the ephod, of gold, blue, and purple, and scarlet, and tined linen;
it hath been square; double they have made the breastplate, a span its length, and a span its breadth, doubled.
And they fill in it four ros of stones; a ro of a sardius, a topaz, and a carbuncle [is] the one ro;
and the second ro an emerald, a sapphire, and a diamond;
and the third ro an opal, an agate, and an amethyst;
and the fourth ro a beryl, an onyx, and a jasper — set, embroidered [ith] gold, in their settings.
And the stones, according to the names of the sons of Israel, are telve, according to their names, openings of a signet, each according to his name, for the telve tribes.
And they make on the breastplate reathed chains, ork of thick bands, of pure gold;
and they make to embroidered things of gold, and to rings of gold, and put the to rings on the to ends of the breastplate,
and they put the to thick bands of gold on the to rings on the ends of the breastplate;
and the to ends of the to thick bands they have put on the to embroidered things, and they put them on the shoulders of the ephod, over-against its front.
And they make to rings of gold, and set [them] on the to ends of the breastplate, on its border, hich [is] on the side of the ephod ithin;
and they make to rings of gold, and put them on the to shoulders of the ephod belo, over-against its front, over-against its joining, above the girdle of the ephod;

and they bind the breastplate by its rings unto the rings of the ephod, ith a ribbon of blue, to be above the girdle of the ephod, and the breastplate is not loosed from off the ephod, as Jehovah hath commanded Moses.
And he maketh the upper robe of the ephod, ork of a eaver, completely of blue;
and the opening of the upper robe [is] in its midst, as the opening of a habergeon, a border [is] to its opening round about, it is not rent;
and they make on the hems of the upper robe pomegranates of blue, and purple, and scarlet, tined.
And they make bells of pure gold, and put the bells in the midst of the pomegranates, on the hems of the upper robe, round about, in the midst of the pomegranates;
a bell and a pomegranate, a bell and a pomegranate, [are] on the hems of the upper robe, round about, to minister in, as Jehovah hath commanded Moses.
And they make the coats of linen, ork of a eaver, for Aaron and for his sons,
and the mitre of linen, and the beautiful bonnets of linen, and the linen trousers, of tined linen,
and the girdle of tined linen, and blue, and purple, and scarlet, ork of an embroiderer, as Jehovah hath commanded Moses.
And they make the floer of the holy cron of pure gold, and rite on it a riting, openings of a signet, ’Holy to Jehovah;’
and they put on it a ribbon of blue, to put [it] on the mitre above, as Jehovah hath commanded Moses.
And all the service of the tabernacle of the tent of meeting is completed; and the sons of Israel do according to all that Jehovah hath commanded Moses; so they have done.
And they bring in the tabernacle unto Moses, the tent, and all its vessels, its hooks, its boards, its bars, and its pillars, and its sockets;
and the covering of rams’ skins, hich are made red, and the covering of badgers’ skins, and the vail of the covering;
the ark of the testimony and its staves, and the mercy-seat;
the table, all its vessels, and the bread of the presence;
the pure candlestick, its lamps, the lamps of arrangement, and all its vessels, and the oil for the light.
And the golden altar, and the anointing oil, and the spice-perfume, and the covering of the opening of the tent;
the brazen altar and the brazen grate hich it hath, its staves, and all its vessels, the laver and its base.

The hangings of the court, its pillars, and its sockets; and the covering for the gate of the court, its cords, and its pins; and all the vessels of the service of the tabernacle, for the tent of meeting;
the coloured clothes to minister in the sanctuary, the holy garments for Aaron the priest, and the garments of his sons, to act as priest in.
According to all that Jehovah hath commanded Moses, so have the sons of Israel done all the service;
and Moses seeth all the ork, and lo, they have done it as Jehovah hath commanded; so they have done. And Moses doth bless them.
And Jehovah speaketh unto Moses, saying,
’On the first day of the month, in the first month, thou dost raise up the tabernacle of the tent of meeting,
and hast set there the ark of the testimony, and hast covered over the ark ith the vail,
and hast brought in the table, and set its arrangement in order, and hast brought in the candlestick, and caused its lamps to go up.
’And thou hast put the golden altar for perfume before the ark of the testimony, and hast put the covering of the opening to the tabernacle,
and hast put the altar of the burnt-offering before the opening of the tabernacle of the tent of meeting,
and hast put the laver beteen the tent of meeting and the altar, and hast put ater there.
’And thou hast set the court round about, and hast placed the covering of the gate of the court,
and hast taken the anointing oil, and anointed the tabernacle, and all that [is] in it, and halloed it, and all its vessels, and it hath been holy;
and thou hast anointed the altar of the burnt-offering, and all its vessels, and sanctified the altar, and the altar hath been most holy;
and thou hast anointed the laver and its base, and sanctified it.
’And thou hast brought near Aaron and his sons unto the opening of the tent of meeting, and hast bathed them ith ater;
and thou hast clothed Aaron ith the holy garments, and anointed him, and sanctified him, and he hath acted as priest to Me.
’And his sons thou dost bring near, and hast clothed them ith coats,
and anointed them as thou hast anointed their father, and they have acted as priests to Me, and their anointing hath been to be to them for a priesthood age-during, to their generations.’
And Moses doth according to all that Jehovah hath commanded him; so he hath done.
And it cometh to pass, in the first month, in the second year, in the first of the month, the tabernacle hath been raised up;
and Moses raiseth up the tabernacle, and setteth its sockets, and placeth its boards, and placeth its bars, and raiseth its pillars,
and spreadeth the tent over the tabernacle, and putteth the covering of the tent upon it above, as Jehovah hath commanded Moses.
And he taketh and putteth the testimony unto the ark, and setteth the staves on the ark, and putteth the mercy-seat on the ark above;
and bringeth in the ark unto the tabernacle, and placeth the vail of the covering, and covereth over the ark of the testimony, as Jehovah hath commanded Moses.
And he putteth the table in the tent of meeting, on the side of the tabernacle northard, at the outside of the vail,
and setteth in order upon it the arrangement of bread, before Jehovah, as Jehovah hath commanded Moses.
And he putteth the candlestick in the tent of meeting, over-against the table, on the side of the tabernacle southard,
and causeth the lamps to go up before Jehovah, as Jehovah hath commanded Moses.
And he setteth the golden altar in the tent of meeting, before the vail,
and maketh perfume on it — spice-perfume — as Jehovah hath commanded Moses.
And he setteth the covering of the opening to the tabernacle,

and the altar of the burnt-offering he hath set at the opening of the tabernacle of the tent of meeting, and causeth the burnt-offering to go up upon it, and the present, as Jehovah hath commanded Moses.
And he putteth the laver beteen the tent of meeting and the altar, and putteth ater there for ashing,
and Moses and Aaron and his sons have ashed their hands and their feet at the same;
in their going in unto the tent of meeting, and in their draing near unto the altar, they ash, as Jehovah hath commanded Moses.
And he raiseth up the court round about the tabernacle, and about the altar, and placeth the covering of the gate of the court; and Moses completeth the ork.
And the cloud covereth the tent of meeting, and the honour of Jehovah hath filled the tabernacle;
and Moses hath not been able to go in unto the tent of meeting, for the cloud hath tabernacled on it, and the honour of Jehovah hath filled the tabernacle.
And in the going up of the cloud from off the tabernacle the sons of Israel journey in all their journeys;
and if the cloud go not up then they journey not, until the day of its going up:
for the cloud of Jehovah [is] on the tabernacle by day, and fire is in it by night, before the eyes of all the house of Israel in all their journeys.
And Jehovah calleth unto Moses, and speaketh unto him out of the tent of meeting, saying,

’Speak unto the sons of Israel, and thou hast said unto them, Any man of you hen he doth bring near an offering to Jehovah, out of the cattle — out of the herd, or out of the flock — ye do bring near your offering.
’If his offering [is] a burnt-offering out of the herd — a male, a perfect one, he doth bring near, unto the opening of the tent of meeting he doth bring it near, at his pleasure, before Jehovah;
and he hath laid his hand on the head of the burnt-offering, and it hath been accepted for him to make atonement for him;

and he hath slaughtered the son of the herd before Jehovah; and sons of Aaron, the priests, have brought the blood near, and sprinkled the blood on the altar round about, hich [is] at the opening of the tent of meeting.
’And he hath stripped the burnt-offering, and hath cut it into its pieces;
and the sons of Aaron the priest have put fire on the altar, and arranged ood on the fire;
and sons of Aaron, the priests, have arranged the pieces, ith the head and the fat, on the ood, hich [is] on the fire, hich [is] on the altar;
and its inards and its legs he doth ash ith ater; and the priest hath made perfume ith the hole on the altar, a burnt-offering, a fire-offering of seet fragrance to Jehovah.
’And if his offering [is] out of the flock — out of the sheep or out of the goats — for a burnt-offering, a male, a perfect one, he doth bring near,
and he hath slaughtered it by the side of the altar northard, before Jehovah; and sons of Aaron, the priests, have sprinkled its blood on the altar round about;
and he hath cut it into its pieces, and its head and its fat, and the priest hath arranged them on the ood, hich [is] on the fire, hich [is] on the altar;

and the inards and the legs he doth ash ith ater, and the priest hath brought the hole near, and hath made perfume on the altar; it [is] a burnt-offering, a fire-offering of seet fragrance to Jehovah.
’And if his offering [is] a burnt-offering out of the fol to Jehovah, than he hath brought near his offering out of the turtle-doves or out of the young pigeons,
and the priest hath brought it near unto the altar, and hath rung off its head, and hath made perfume on the altar, and its blood hath been rung out by the side of the altar;
and he hath turned aside its crop ith its feathers, and hath cast it near the altar, eastard, unto the place of ashes;

and he hath cleaved it ith its ings (he doth not separate [it]), and the priest hath made it a perfume on the altar, on the ood, hich [is] on the fire; it [is] a burnt-offering, a fire-offering of seet fragrance to Jehovah.
’And hen a person bringeth near an offering, a present to Jehovah, of flour is his offering, and he hath poured on it oil, and hath put on it frankincense;

and he hath brought it in unto the sons of Aaron, the priests, and he hath taken from thence the fulness of his hand of its flour and of its oil, besides all its frankincense, and the priest hath made perfume ith its memorial on the altar, a fire-offering of seet fragrance to Jehovah;
and the remnant of the present [is] for Aaron and for his sons, most holy, of the fire-offerings of Jehovah.
’And hen thou bringest near an offering, a present baked in an oven, [it is of] unleavened cakes of flour mixed ith oil, or thin unleavened cakes anointed ith oil.
’And if thine offering [is] a present [made] on the girdel, it is of flour, mixed ith oil, unleavened;
divide thou it into parts, and thou hast poured on it oil; it [is] a present.
’And if thine offering [is] a present [made] on the frying-pan, of flour ith oil it is made,
and thou hast brought in the present hich is made of these to Jehovah, and [one] hath brought it near unto the priest, and he hath brought it nigh unto the altar,
and the priest hath lifted up from the present its memorial, and hath made perfume on the altar, a fire-offering of seet fragrance to Jehovah;
and the remnant of the present [is] for Aaron and for his sons, most holy, of the fire-offerings of Jehovah.
No present hich ye bring near to Jehovah is made fermented, for ith any leaven or any honey ye perfume no fire-offering to Jehovah.
’An offering of first -[fruits] — ye bring them near to Jehovah, but on the altar they go not up, for seet fragrance.
And every offering — thy present — ith salt thou dost season, and thou dost not let the salt of the covenant of thy God cease from thy present; ith all thine offerings thou dost bring near salt.

’And if thou bring near a present of first-ripe [fruits] to Jehovah, — of green ears, roasted ith fire, beaten out [corn] of a fruitful field thou dost bring near the present of thy first-ripe [fruits],
and thou hast put on it oil, and laid on it frankincense, it [is] a present;
and the priest hath made perfume ith its memorial from its beaten out [corn], and from its oil, besides all its frankincense — a fire-offering to Jehovah.
’And if his offering [is] a sacrifice of peace-offerings, if out of the herd he is bringing near, hether male or female, a perfect one he doth bring near before Jehovah,

and he hath laid his hand on the head of his offering, and hath slaughtered it at the opening of the tent of meeting, and sons of Aaron, the priests, have sprinkled the blood on the altar round about.
’And he hath brought near from the sacrifice of the peace-offerings a fire-offering to Jehovah, the fat hich is covering the inards, and all the fat hich [is] on the inards,
and the to kidneys, and the fat hich [is] on them, hich [is] on the flanks, and the redundance above the liver, (beside the kidneys he doth turn it aside),
and sons of Aaron have made it a perfume on the altar, on the burnt-offering hich [is] on the ood, hich [is] on the fire — a fire-offering of seet fragrance to Jehovah.
’And if his offering [is] out of the flock for a sacrifice of peace-offerings to Jehovah, male or female, a perfect one he doth bring near;
if a sheep he is bringing near [for] his offering, then he hath brought it near before Jehovah,
and hath laid his hand on the head of his offering, and hath slaughtered it before the tent of meeting, and sons of Aaron have sprinkled its blood on the altar round about.

’And he hath brought near from the sacrifice of the peace-offerings a fire-offering to Jehovah, its fat, the hole fat tail (over-against the bone he doth turn it aside), and the fat hich is covering the inards, and all the fat hich [is] on the inards,
and the to kidneys, and the fat hich [is] on them, hich [is] on the flanks, and the redundance above the liver, (beside the kidneys he doth turn it aside),
and the priest hath made it a perfume on the altar — bread of a fire-offering to Jehovah.
’And if his offering [is] a goat, then he hath brought it near before Jehovah,
and hath laid his hand on its head, and hath slaughtered it before the tent of meeting, and sons of Aaron have sprinkled its blood on the altar round about;
and he hath brought near from it his offering, a fire-offering to Jehovah, the fat hich is covering the inards, and all the fat hich [is] on the inards,
and the to kidneys, and the fat hich [is] upon them, hich [is] on the flanks, and the redundance above the liver, (beside the kidneys he doth turn it aside),
and the priest hath made them a perfume on the altar — bread of a fire-offering, for seet fragrance; all the fat [is] Jehovah’s.
’A statute age-during to your generations in all your dellings: any fat or any blood ye do not eat.’
And Jehovah speaketh unto Moses, saying,

’Speak unto the sons of Israel, saying, When a person doth sin through ignorance against any of the commands of Jehovah [regarding things] hich are not to be done, and hath done [something] against one of these —

’If the priest ho is anointed doth sin according to the guilt of the people, then he hath brought near for his sin hich he hath sinned a bullock, a son of the herd, a perfect one, to Jehovah, for a sin-offering,
and he hath brought in the bullock unto the opening of the tent of meeting before Jehovah, and hath laid his hand on the head of the bullock, and hath slaughtered the bullock before Jehovah.
’And the priest ho is anointed hath taken of the blood of the bullock, and hath brought it in unto the tent of meeting,
and the priest hath dipped his finger in the blood, and sprinkled of the blood seven times before Jehovah, at the front of the vail of the sanctuary;

and the priest hath put of the blood on the horns of the altar of spice-perfume before Jehovah, hich [is] in the tent of meeting, and all the blood of the bullock he doth pour out at the foundation of the altar of the burnt-offering, hich [is] at the opening of the tent of meeting.
’And all the fat of the bullock of the sin-offering he doth lift up from it, the fat hich is covering over the inards, and all the fat hich [is] on the inards,
and the to kidneys, and the fat hich [is] on them, hich [is] on the flanks, and the redundance above the liver, (beside the kidneys he doth turn it aside),
as it is lifted up from the ox of the sacrifice of the peace-offerings; and the priest hath made them a perfume on the altar of the burnt-offering.
’And the skin of the bullock, and all its flesh, besides its head, and besides its legs, and its inards, and its dung —

he hath even brought out the hole bullock unto the outside of the camp, unto a clean place, unto the place of the pouring out of the ashes, and he hath burnt it on the ood ith fire; beside the place of the pouring out of the ashes it is burnt.

’And if the hole company of Israel err ignorantly, and the thing hath been hidden from the eyes of the assembly, and they have done [something against] one of all the commands of Jehovah [concerning things] hich are not to be done, and have been guilty;

hen the sin hich they have sinned concerning it hath been knon, then have the assembly brought near a bullock, a son of the herd, for a sin-offering, and they have brought it in before the tent of meeting;
and the elders of the company have laid their hands on the head of the bullock, before Jehovah, and [one] hath slaughtered the bullock before Jehovah.
’And the priest ho is anointed hath brought in of the blood of the bullock unto the tent of meeting,
and the priest hath dipped his finger in the blood, and hath sprinkled seven times before Jehovah at the front of the vail,

and [some] of the blood he doth put on the horns of the altar hich [is] before Jehovah, hich [is] in the tent of meeting; and all the blood he doth pour out at the foundation of the altar of the burnt-offering, hich [is] at the opening of the tent of meeting;
and all its fat he doth lift up from it, and hath made perfume on the altar.
’And he hath done to the bullock as he hath done to the bullock of the sin-offering, so he doth to it; and the priest hath made atonement for them, and it hath been forgiven them;
and he hath brought out the bullock unto the outside of the camp, and hath burned it as he hath burned the first bullock; it [is] a sin-offering of the assembly.
’When a prince doth sin, and hath done [something against] one of all the commands of Jehovah his God [regarding things] hich are not to be done, through ignorance, and hath been guilty —
or his sin herein he hath sinned hath been made knon unto him, then he hath brought in his offering, a kid of the goats, a male, a perfect one,
and he hath laid his hand on the head of the goat, and hath slaughtered it in the place here he doth slaughter the burnt-offering before Jehovah; it [is] a sin-offering.

’And the priest hath taken of the blood of the sin-offering ith his finger, and hath put on the horns of the altar of the burnt-offering, and its blood he doth pour out at the foundation of the altar of the burnt-offering,

and ith all its fat he doth make perfume on the altar, as the fat of the sacrifice of the peace-offerings; and the priest hath made atonement for him because of his sin, and it hath been forgiven him.
’And if any person of the people of the land sin through ignorance, by his doing [something against] one of the commands of Jehovah [regarding things] hich are not to be done, and hath been guilty —
or his sin hich he hath sinned hath been made knon unto him, then he hath brought in his offering, a kid of the goats, a perfect one, a female, for his sin hich he hath sinned,
and he hath laid his hand on the head of the sin-offering, and hath slaughtered the sin-offering in the place of the burnt-offering.
’And the priest hath taken of its blood ith his finger, and hath put on the horns of the altar of the burnt-offering, and all its blood he doth pour out at the foundation of the altar,

and all its fat he doth turn aside, as the fat hath been turned aside from off the sacrifice of the peace-offerings, and the priest hath made perfume on the altar, for seet fragrance to Jehovah; and the priest hath made atonement for him, and it hath been forgiven him.
’And if he bring in a sheep [for] his offering, for a sin-offering, a female, a perfect one, he doth bring in,
and he hath laid his hand on the head of the sin-offering, and hath slaughtered it for a sin-offering in the place here he slaughtereth the burnt-offering.

’And the priest hath taken of the blood of the sin-offering ith his finger, and hath put on the horns of the altar of the burnt-offering, and all its blood he poureth out at the foundation of the altar,

and all its fat he turneth aside, as the fat of the sheep is turned aside from the sacrifice of the peace-offerings, and the priest hath made them a perfume on the altar, according to the fire-offerings of Jehovah, and the priest hath made atonement for him, for his sin hich he hath sinned, and it hath been forgiven him.
’And hen a person doth sin, and hath heard the voice of an oath, and he [is] itness, or hath seen, or hath knon — if he declare not, then he hath borne his iniquity:

’Or hen a person cometh against any thing unclean, or against a carcase of an unclean beast, or against a carcase of unclean cattle, or against a carcase of an unclean teeming creature, and it hath been hidden from him, and he unclean, and guilty;
’Or hen he cometh against uncleanness of man, even any of his uncleanness hereby he is unclean, and it hath been hidden from him, and he hath knon, and hath been guilty:

’Or hen a person seareth, speaking rongfully ith the lips to do evil, or to do good, even anything hich man speaketh rongfully ith an oath, and it hath been hid from him; — hen he hath knon then he hath been guilty of one of these;
’And it hath been hen he is guilty of one of these, that he hath confessed concerning that hich he hath sinned,

and hath brought in his guilt-offering to Jehovah for his sin hich he hath sinned, a female out of the flock, a lamb, or a kid of the goats, for a sin-offering, and the priest hath made atonement for him, because of his sin.

’And if his hand reach not to the sufficiency of a lamb, then he hath brought in his guilt-offering — he ho hath sinned — to turtle-doves or to young pigeons to Jehovah, one for a sin-offering, and one for a burnt-offering;
and he hath brought them in unto the priest, and hath brought near that hich [is] for a sin-offering first, and hath rung off its head from its neck, and doth not separate [it],
and he hath sprinkled of the blood of the sin-offering on the side of the altar, and that hich is left of the blood is rung out at the foundation of the altar; it [is] a sin-offering.
’And the second he maketh a burnt-offering, according to the ordinance, and the priest hath made atonement for him, because of his sin hich he hath sinned, and it hath been forgiven him.

’And if his hand reach not to to turtle-doves, or to to young pigeons, then he hath brought in his offering — he ho hath sinned — a tenth of an ephah of flour for a sin-offering; he putteth no oil on it, nor doth he put on it frankincense, for it [is] a sin-offering,

and he hath brought it in unto the priest, and the priest hath taken a handful from it — the fulness of his hand — its memorial — and hath made perfume on the altar, according to the fire-offerings of Jehovah; it [is] a sin-offering.
’And the priest hath made atonement for him, for his sin hich he hath sinned against one of these, and it hath been forgiven him, and [the remnant] hath been to the priest, like the present.’
And Jehovah speaketh unto Moses, saying,

’When a person committeth a trespass, and hath sinned through ignorance against the holy things of Jehovah, then he hath brought in his guilt-offering to Jehovah, a ram, a perfect one, out of the flock, at thy valuation [in] silver — shekels by the shekel of the sanctuary — for a guilt-offering.

’And that hich he hath sinned against the holy thing he repayeth, and its fifth is adding to it, and hath given it to the priest, and the priest maketh atonement for him ith the ram of the guilt-offering, and it hath been forgiven him.

’And hen any person sinneth, and hath done [something against] one of all the commands of Jehovah [regarding things] hich are not to be done, and hath not knon, and he hath been guilty, and hath borne his iniquity,

’Then he hath brought in a ram, a perfect one, out of the flock, at thy valuation, for a guilt-offering, unto the priest; and the priest hath made atonement for him, for his ignorance in hich he hath erred and he hath not knon, and it hath been forgiven him;
it [is] a guilt-offering; he hath been certainly guilty before Jehovah.’
And Jehovah speaketh unto Moses, saying,

’When any person doth sin, and hath committed a trespass against Jehovah, and hath lied to his fello concerning a deposit, or concerning felloship, or concerning violent robbery, or hath oppressed his fello;
or hath found a lost thing, and hath lied concerning it, and hath sorn to a falsehood, concerning one of all [these] hich man doth, sinning in them:

’Then it hath been, hen he sinneth, and hath been guilty, that he hath returned the plunder hich he hath taken violently aay, or the thing hich he hath got by oppression, or the deposit hich hath been deposited ith him, or the lost thing hich he hath found;
or all that concerning hich he seareth falsely, he hath even repaid it in its principal, and its fifth he is adding to it; to him hose it [is] he giveth it in the day of his guilt-offering.
’And his guilt-offering he bringeth in to Jehovah, a ram, a perfect one, out of the flock, at thy estimation, for a guilt-offering, unto the priest,
and the priest hath made atonement for him before Jehovah, and it hath been forgiven him, concerning one thing of all that he doth, by being guilty therein.’
And Jehovah speaketh unto Moses, saying,

’Command Aaron and his sons, saying, This [is] a la of the burnt-offering (it [is] the burnt-offering, because of the burning on the altar all the night unto the morning, and the fire of the altar is burning on it,)

that the priest hath put on his long robe of fine linen, and his fine linen trousers he doth put on his flesh, and hath lifted up the ashes hich the fire consumeth ith the burnt-offering on the altar, and hath put them near the altar;
and he hath stripped off his garments, and hath put on other garments, and hath brought out the ashes unto the outside of the camp, unto a clean place.

’And the fire on the altar is burning on it, it is not quenched, and the priest hath burned on it ood morning by morning, and hath arranged on it the burnt-offering, and hath made perfume on it [ith] the fat of the peace-offerings;
fire is continually burning on the altar, it is not quenched.
’And this [is] a la of the present: sons of Aaron have brought it near before Jehovah unto the front of the altar,

and [one] hath lifted up of it ith his hand from the flour of the present, and from its oil, and all the frankincense hich [is] on the present, and hath made perfume on the altar, seet fragrance — its memorial to Jehovah.
’And the remnant of it do Aaron and his sons eat; [ith] unleavened things it is eaten, in the holy place, in the court of the tent of meeting they do eat it.
It is not baken [ith] any thing fermented, their portion I have given it, out of My fire-offerings; it [is] most holy, like the sin-offering, and like the guilt-offering.
Every male among the sons of Aaron doth eat it — a statute age-during to your generations, out of the fire-offerings of Jehovah: all that cometh against them is holy.’
And Jehovah speaketh unto Moses, saying,

’This [is] an offering of Aaron and of his sons, hich they bring near to Jehovah in the day of his being anointed; a tenth of the ephah of flour [for] a continual present, half of it in the morning, and half of it in the evening;
on a girdel ith oil it is made — fried thou dost bring it in; baked pieces of the present thou dost bring near, a seet fragrance to Jehovah.
’And the priest ho is anointed in his stead, from among his sons, doth make it, — a statute age-during of Jehovah: it is completely perfumed;
and every present of a priest is a hole burnt-offering; it is not eaten.’
And Jehovah speaketh unto Moses, saying,
’Speak unto Aaron and unto his sons, saying, This [is] a la of the sin-offering: in the place here the burnt-offering is slaughtered is the sin-offering slaughtered before Jehovah; it [is] most holy.
’The priest ho is making atonement ith it doth eat it, in the holy place it is eaten, in the court of the tent of meeting;
all that cometh against its flesh is holy, and hen [any] of its blood is sprinkled on the garment, that on hich it is sprinkled thou dost ash in the holy place;
and an earthen vessel in hich it is boiled is broken, and if in a brass vessel it is boiled, then it is scoured and rinsed ith ater.
’Every male among the priests doth eat it — it [is] most holy;
and no sin-offering, [any] of hose blood is brought in unto the tent of meeting to make atonement in the sanctuary is eaten; ith fire it is burnt.
’And this [is] a la of the guilt-offering: it [is] most holy;
in the place here they slaughter the burnt-offering they do slaughter the guilt-offering, and its blood [one] doth sprinkle on the altar round about,
and all its fat he bringeth near out of it, the fat tail, and the fat hich is covering the inards,
and the to kidneys, and the fat hich [is] on them, hich [is] on the flanks, and the redundance above the liver (beside the kidneys he doth turn it aside);
and the priest hath made them a perfume on the altar, a fire-offering to Jehovah; it [is] a guilt-offering.
’Every male among the priests doth eat it; in the holy place it is eaten — it [is] most holy;
as [is] a sin-offering, so [is] a guilt-offering; one la [is] for them; the priest ho maketh atonement by it — it is his.
’And the priest ho is bringing near any man’s burnt-offering, the skin of the burnt-offering hich he hath brought near, it is the priest’s, his on;
and every present hich is baked in an oven, and every one done in a frying-pan, and on a girdel, [is] the priest’s ho is bringing it near; it is his;
and every present, mixed ith oil or dry, is for all the sons of Aaron — one as another.
’And this [is] a la of the sacrifice of the peace-offerings hich [one] bringeth near to Jehovah:

if for a thank-offering he bring it near, then he hath brought near ith the sacrifice of thank-offering unleavened cakes mixed ith oil, and thin unleavened cakes anointed ith oil, and of fried flour cakes mixed ith oil;
besides the cakes, fermented bread he doth bring near [ith] his offering, besides the sacrifice of thank-offering of his peace-offerings;
and he hath brought near out of it one of the hole offering — a heave-offering to Jehovah; to the priest ho is sprinkling the blood of the peace-offerings — it is his;
as to the flesh of the sacrifice of the thank-offering of his peace-offerings, in the day of his offering it is eaten; he doth not leave of it till morning.
’And if the sacrifice of his offering [is] a vo or free-ill offering, in the day of his bringing near his sacrifice it is eaten; and on the morro also the remnant of it is eaten;
and the remnant of the flesh of the sacrifice on the third day ith fire is burnt;

and if any of the flesh of the sacrifice of his peace-offerings be really eaten on the third day, it is not pleasing; for him ho is bringing it near it is not reckoned; it is an abominable thing, and the person ho is eating of it his iniquity doth bear.
’And the flesh hich cometh against any unclean thing is not eaten; ith fire it is burnt; as to the flesh, every clean one doth eat of the flesh;
and the person ho eateth of the flesh of the sacrifice of the peace-offerings hich [are] Jehovah’s, and his uncleanness upon him, even that person hath been cut off from his people.

’And hen a person cometh against any thing unclean, of the uncleanness of man, or of the uncleanness of beasts, or of any unclean teeming creature, and hath eaten of the flesh of the sacrifice of the peace-offerings hich [are] Jehovah’s, even that person hath been cut off from his people.’
And Jehovah speaketh unto Moses, saying,
’Speak unto the sons of Israel, saying, Any fat of ox and sheep and goat ye do not eat;
and the fat of a carcase, and the fat of a torn thing is prepared for any ork, but ye do certainly not eat it;
for hoever eateth the fat of the beast, of hich [one] bringeth near a fire-offering to Jehovah, even the person ho eateth hath been cut off from his people.
’And any blood ye do not eat in all your dellings, of fol, or of beast;
any person ho eateth any blood, even that person hath been cut off from his people.’
And Jehovah speaketh unto Moses, saying,
’Speak unto the sons of Israel, saying, He ho is bringing near the sacrifice of his peace-offerings to Jehovah doth bring in his offering to Jehovah from the sacrifice of his peace-offerings;
his on hands do bring in the fire-offerings of Jehovah, the fat beside the breast, it he doth bring in ith the breast, to ave it — a ave-offering before Jehovah.
’And the priest hath made perfume ith the fat on the altar, and the breast hath been Aaron’s and his sons;
and the right leg ye do make a heave-offering to the priest of the sacrifices of your peace-offerings;
he of the sons of Aaron ho is bringing near the blood of the peace-offerings, and the fat, his is the right leg for a portion.

’For the breast of the ave-offering, and the leg of the heave-offering, I have taken from the sons of Israel, from the sacrifices of their peace-offerings, and I give them to Aaron the priest, and to his sons, by a statute age-during, from the sons of Israel.’
This [is] the anointing of Aaron, and the anointing of his sons out of the fire-offerings of Jehovah, in the day he hath brought them near to act as priest to Jehovah,
hich Jehovah hath commanded to give to them in the day of His anointing them, from the sons of Israel — a statute age-during to their generations.
This [is] the la for burnt-offering, for present, and for sin-offering, and for guilt-offering, and for consecrations, and for a sacrifice of the peace-offerings,
hich Jehovah hath commanded Moses in Mount Sinai, in the day of his commanding the sons of Israel to bring near their offerings to Jehovah, in the ilderness of Sinai.
And Jehovah speaketh unto Moses, saying,
’Take Aaron and his sons ith him, and the garments, and the anointing oil, and the bullock of the sin-offering, and the to rams, and the basket of unleavened things,
and all the company assemble thou unto the opening of the tent of meeting.’
And Moses doth as Jehovah hath commanded him, and the company is assembled unto the opening of the tent of meeting,
and Moses saith unto the company, ’This [is] the thing hich Jehovah hath commanded to do.’
And Moses bringeth near Aaron and his sons, and doth bathe them ith ater,

and doth put on him the coat, and doth gird him ith the girdle, and doth clothe him ith the upper robe, and doth put on him the ephod, and doth gird him ith the girdle of the ephod, and doth bind [it] to him ith it,
and doth put on him the breastplate, and doth put unto the breastplate the Lights and the Perfections,
and doth put the mitre on his head, and doth put on the mitre, over-against its front, the golden floer of the holy cron, as Jehovah hath commanded Moses.
And Moses taketh the anointing oil, and anointeth the tabernacle, and all that [is] in it, and sanctifieth them;
and he sprinkleth of it on the altar seven times, and anointeth the altar, and all its vessels, and the laver, and its base, to sanctify them;
and he poureth of the anointing oil on the head of Aaron, and anointeth him to sanctify him.
And Moses bringeth near the sons of Aaron, and doth clothe them [ith] coats, and girdeth them [ith] girdles, and bindeth for them turbans, as Jehovah hath commanded Moses.
And he bringeth nigh the bullock of the sin-offering, and Aaron layeth — his sons also — their hands on the head of the bullock of the sin-offering,

and [one] slaughtereth, and Moses taketh the blood, and putteth on the horns of the altar round about ith his finger, and cleanseth the altar, and the blood he hath poured out at the foundation of the altar, and sanctifieth it, to make atonement upon it.
And he taketh all the fat that [is] on the inards, and the redundance above the liver, and the to kidneys, and their fat, and Moses maketh Perfume on the altar,
and the bullock, and its skin, and its flesh, and its dung, he hath burnt ith fire, at the outside of the camp, as Jehovah hath commanded Moses.
And he bringeth near the ram of the burnt-offering, and Aaron and his sons lay their hands on the head of the ram,
and [one] slaughtereth, and Moses sprinkleth the blood on the altar round about;
and the ram he hath cut into its pieces, and Moses maketh perfume ith the head, and the pieces, and the fat,

and the inards and the legs he hath ashed ith ater, and Moses maketh perfume ith the hole ram on the altar; it [is] a burnt-offering, for seet fragrance; it [is] a fire-offering to Jehovah, as Jehovah hath commanded Moses.
And he bringeth near the second ram, a ram of the consecrations, and Aaron and his sons lay their hands on the head of the ram,
and [one] slaughtereth, and Moses taketh of its blood, and putteth on the tip of the right ear of Aaron, and on the thumb of his right hand, and on the great toe of his right foot;

and he bringeth near the sons of Aaron, and Moses putteth of the blood on the tip of their right ear, and on the thumb of their right hand, and on the great toe of their right foot. And Moses sprinkleth the blood on the altar round about,
and taketh the fat, and the fat tail, and all the fat that [is] on the inards, and the redundance above the liver, and the to kidneys, and their fat, and the right leg;

and out of the basket of unleavened things, hich [is] before Jehovah, he hath taken one unleavened cake, and one cake of oiled bread, and one thin cake, and putteth [them] on the fat, and on the right leg;
and putteth the hole on the hands of Aaron, and on the hands of his sons, and aveth them — a ave-offering before Jehovah.
