And Moses taketh them from off their hands, and maketh perfume on the altar, on the burnt-offering, they [are] consecrations for seet fragrance; it [is] a fire-offering to Jehovah;
and Moses taketh the breast, and aveth it — a ave-offering before Jehovah; of the ram of the consecrations it hath been to Moses for a portion, as Jehovah hath commanded Moses.

And Moses taketh of the anointing oil, and of the blood hich [is] on the altar, and sprinkleth on Aaron, on his garments, and on his sons, and on the garments of his sons ith him, and he sanctifieth Aaron, his garments, and his sons, and the garments of his sons ith him.

And Moses saith unto Aaron, and unto his sons, ’Boil ye the flesh at the opening of the tent of meeting, and there ye do eat it and the bread hich [is] in the basket of the consecrations, as I have commanded, saying, Aaron and his sons do eat it.
’And the remnant of the flesh and of the bread ith fire ye burn;
and from the opening of the tent of meeting ye go not out seven days, till the day of the fulness, the days of your consecration — for seven days he doth consecrate your hand;
as he hath done on this day, Jehovah hath commanded to do, to make atonement for you;
and at the opening of the tent of meeting ye abide, by day and by night seven days, and ye have kept the charge of Jehovah, and die not, for so I have been commanded.’
And Aaron doth — his sons also — all the things hich Jehovah hath commanded by the hand of Moses.
And it cometh to pass on the eighth day, Moses hath called for Aaron and for his sons, and for the elders of Israel,
and he saith unto Aaron, ’Take to thyself a calf, a son of the herd, for a sin-offering, and a ram for a burnt-offering, perfect ones, and bring near before Jehovah.
’And unto the sons of Israel thou dost speak, saying, Take ye a kid of the goats for a sin-offering, and a calf, and a lamb, sons of a year, perfect ones, for a burnt-offering,
and a bullock and a ram for peace-offerings, to sacrifice before Jehovah, and a present mixed ith oil; for to-day Jehovah hath appeared unto you.’
And they take that hich Moses hath commanded unto the front of the tent of meeting, and all the company dra near and stand before Jehovah;
and Moses saith, ’This [is] the thing hich Jehovah hath commanded; do [it], and the honour of Jehovah doth appear unto you.’

And Moses saith unto Aaron, ’Dra near unto the altar, and make thy sin-offering, and thy burnt-offering, and make atonement for thyself, and for the people, and make the offering of the people, and make atonement for them, as Jehovah hath commanded.’
And Aaron draeth near unto the altar, and slaughtereth the calf of the sin-offering, hich [is] for himself;

and the sons of Aaron bring the blood near unto him, and he dippeth his finger in the blood, and putteth [it] on the horns of the altar, and the blood he hath poured out at the foundation of the altar;
and the fat, and the kidneys, and the redundance of the liver, of the sin-offering, he hath made a perfume on the altar, as Jehovah hath commanded Moses;
and the flesh and the skin he hath burnt ith fire, at the outside of the camp.
And he slaughtereth the burnt-offering, and the sons of Aaron have presented unto him the blood, and he sprinkleth it on the altar round about;
and the burnt-offering they have presented unto him, by its pieces, and the head, and he maketh perfume on the altar;
and he asheth the inards and the legs, and maketh perfume for the burnt-offering on the altar.
And he bringeth near the offering of the people, and taketh the goat of the sin-offering hich [is] for the people, and slaughtered it, and maketh it a sin-offering, like the first;
and he bringeth near the burnt-offering, and maketh it, according to the ordinance;
and he bringeth near the present, and filleth his palm ith it, and maketh perfume on the altar, apart from the burnt-offering of the morning.

And he slaughtereth the bullock and the ram, a sacrifice of the peace-offerings, hich [are] for the people, and sons of Aaron present the blood unto him (and he sprinkleth it on the altar round about),
and the fat of the bullock, and of the ram, the fat tail, and the covering [of the inards], and the kidneys, and the redundance above the liver,
and they set the fat on the breasts, and he maketh perfume ith the fat on the altar;
and the breasts, and the right leg hath Aaron aved — a ave-offering before Jehovah, as He hath commanded Moses.
And Aaron lifteth up his hand toards the people, and blesseth them, and cometh don from making the sin-offering, and the burnt-offering, and the peace-offerings.
And Moses goeth in — Aaron also — unto the tent of meeting, and they come out, and bless the people, and the honour of Jehovah appeareth unto all the people;
and fire cometh out from before Jehovah, and consumeth on the altar the burnt-offering, and the fat; and all the people see, and cry aloud, and fall on their faces.
And the sons of Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, take each his censer, and put in them fire, and put on it perfume, and bring near before Jehovah strange fire, hich He hath not commanded them;
and fire goeth out from before Jehovah, and consumeth them, and they die before Jehovah.
And Moses saith unto Aaron, ’It [is] that hich Jehovah hath spoken, saying, By those draing near to Me I am sanctified, and in the face of all the people I am honoured;’ and Aaron is silent.
And Moses calleth unto Mishael and unto Elzaphan, sons of Uzziel, uncle of Aaron, and saith unto them, ’Come near, bear your brethren from the front of the sanctuary unto the outside of the camp;’
and they come near, and bear them in their coats unto the outside of the camp, as Moses hath spoken.

And Moses saith unto Aaron, and to Eleazar, and to Ithamar his sons, ’Your heads ye do not uncover, and your garments ye do not rend, that ye die not, and on all the company He be roth; as to your brethren, the hole house of Israel, they beail the burning hich Jehovah hath kindled;
and from the opening of the tent of meeting ye do not go out, lest ye die, for the anointing oil of Jehovah [is] upon you;’ and they do according to the ord of Moses.
And Jehovah speaketh unto Aaron, saying,
’Wine and strong drink thou dost not drink, thou, and thy sons ith thee, in your going in unto the tent of meeting, and ye die not — a statute age-during to your generations;
so as to make a separation beteen the holy and the common, and beteen the unclean and the pure;
and to teach the sons of Israel all the statutes hich Jehovah hath spoken unto them by the hand of Moses.’

And Moses speaketh unto Aaron, and unto Eleazar, and unto Ithamar his sons, ho are left, ’Take ye the present that is left from the fire-offerings of Jehovah, and eat it unleavened near the altar, for it [is] most holy,
and ye have eaten it in the holy place, for it [is] thy portion, and the portion of thy sons, from the fire-offerings of Jehovah; for so I have been commanded.

’And the breast of the ave-offering, and the leg of the heave-offering, ye do eat in a clean place, thou, and thy sons, and thy daughters ith thee; for thy portion and the portion of thy sons they have been given, out of the sacrifices of peace-offerings of the sons of Israel;

the leg of the heave-offering, and breast of the ave-offering, besides fire-offerings of the fat, they do bring in to ave a ave-offering before Jehovah, and it hath been to thee, and to thy sons ith thee, by a statute age-during, as Jehovah hath commanded.’
And the goat of the sin-offering hath Moses diligently sought, and lo, it is burnt, and he is roth against Eleazar, and against Ithamar, sons of Aaron, ho are left, saying,

’Wherefore have ye not eaten the sin-offering in the holy place, for it [is] most holy — and it He hath given to you to take aay the iniquity of the company, to make atonement for them before Jehovah?
lo, its blood hath not been brought in unto the holy place ithin; eating ye do eat it in the holy place, as I have commanded.’

And Aaron speaketh unto Moses, ’Lo, to-day they have brought near their sin-offering and their burnt-offering before Jehovah; and [things] like these meet me, yet I have eaten a sin-offering to-day; is it good in the eyes of Jehovah?’
And Moses hearkeneth, and it is good in his eyes.
And Jehovah speaketh unto Moses and unto Aaron, saying unto them,
’Speak unto the sons of Israel, saying, This [is] the beast hich ye do eat out of all the beasts hich [are] on the earth:
any dividing a hoof, and cleaving the cleft of the hoofs, bringing up the cud, among the beasts, it ye do eat.
’Only, this ye do not eat — of those bringing up the cud, and of those dividing the hoof — the camel, though it is bringing up the cud, yet the hoof not dividing — it [is] unclean to you;
and the rabbit, though it is bringing up the cud, yet the hoof it divideth not — unclean it [is] to you;
and the hare, though it is bringing up the cud, yet the hoof hath not divided — unclean it [is] to you;
and the so, though it is dividing the hoof, and cleaving the cleft of the hoof, yet the cud it bringeth not up — unclean it [is] to you.
’Of their flesh ye do not eat, and against their carcase ye do not come — unclean they [are] to you.
’This ye do eat of all hich [are] in the aters; any one that hath fins and scales in the aters, in the seas, and in the brooks, them ye do eat;

and any one that hath not fins and scales in the seas, and in the brooks, of any teeming creature of the aters, and of any creature hich liveth, hich [is] in the aters — an abomination they [are] to you;
yea, an abomination they are to you; of their flesh ye do not eat, and their carcase ye abominate.
’Any one that hath not fins and scales in the aters — an abomination it [is] to you.
’And these ye do abominate of the fol; they are not eaten, an abomination they [are]: the eagle, and the ossifrage, and the ospray,
and the vulture, and the kite after its kind,
every raven after its kind,
and the ol, and the night-hak, and the cuckoo, and the hak after its kind,
and the little ol, and the cormorant, and the great ol,
and the san, and the pelican, and the gier eagle,
and the stork, the heron after its kind, and the laping, and the bat.
’Every teeming creature hich is flying, hich is going on four — an abomination it [is] to you.
’Only — this ye do eat of any teeming thing hich is flying, hich is going on four, hich hath legs above its feet, to move ith them on the earth;
these of them ye do eat: the locust after its kind, and the bald locust after its kind, and the beetle after its kind, and the grasshopper after its kind;
and every teeming thing hich is flying, hich hath four feet — an abomination it [is] to you.
’And by these ye are made unclean, any one ho is coming against their carcase is unclean till the evening;
and anyone ho is lifting up [aught] of their carcase doth ash his garments, and hath been unclean till the evening: —
even every beast hich is dividing the hoof, and is not cloven-footed, and the cud is not bringing up — unclean they [are] to you; any one ho is coming against them is unclean.
’And any one going on its pas, among all the beasts hich are going on four — unclean they [are] to you; any one ho is coming against their carcase is unclean until the evening;
and he ho is lifting up their carcase doth ash his garments, and hath been unclean until the evening — unclean they [are] to you.
’And this [is] to you the unclean among the teeming things hich are teeming on the earth: the easel, and the mouse, and the tortoise after its kind,
and the ferret, and the chameleon, and the lizard, and the snail, and the mole;
these [are] the unclean to you among all hich are teeming; any one ho is coming against them in their death is unclean till the evening.

’And anything on hich any one of them falleth, in their death, is unclean, of any vessel of ood or garment or skin or sack, any vessel in hich ork is done is brought into ater, and hath been unclean till the evening, then it hath been clean;
and any earthen vessel, into the midst of hich [any] one of them falleth, all that [is] in its midst is unclean, and it ye do break.
’Of all the food hich is eaten, that on hich cometh [such] ater, is unclean, and all drink hich is drunk in any [such] vessel is unclean;
and anything on hich [any] of their carcase falleth is unclean (oven or double pots), it is broken don, unclean they [are], yea, unclean they are to you.
’Only — a fountain or pit, a collection of ater, is clean, but that hich is coming against their carcase is unclean;
and hen [any] of their carcase falleth on any son seed hich is son — it [is] clean;
and hen ater is put on the seed, and [any] of its carcase hath fallen on it — unclean it [is] to you.
’And hen any of the beasts hich are to you for food dieth, he ho is coming against its carcase is unclean till the evening;
and he ho is eating of its carcase doth ash his garments, and hath been unclean till the evening; and he ho is lifting up its carcase doth ash his garments, and hath been unclean till the evening.
’And every teeming thing hich is teeming on the earth is an abomination, it is not eaten;
any thing going on the belly, and any going on four, unto every multiplier of feet, to every teeming thing hich is teeming on the earth — ye do not eat them, for they [are] an abomination;
ye do not make yourselves abominable ith any teeming thing hich is teeming, nor do ye make yourselves unclean ith them, so that ye have been unclean thereby.
’For I [am] Jehovah your God, and ye have sanctified yourselves, and ye have been holy, for I [am] holy; and ye do not defile your persons ith any teeming thing hich is creeping on the earth;
for I [am] Jehovah ho am bringing you up out of the land of Egypt to become your God; and ye have been holy, for I [am] holy.
’This [is] a la of the beasts, and of the fol, and of every living creature hich is moving in the aters, and of every creature hich is teeming on the earth,
to make separation beteen the unclean and the pure, and beteen the beast that is eaten, and the beast that is not eaten.’
And Jehovah speaketh unto Moses, saying,
’Speak unto the sons of Israel, saying, A oman hen she giveth seed, and hath born a male, then she hath been unclean seven days, according to the days of separation for her sickness she is unclean;
and in the eighth day is the flesh of his foreskin circumcised;

and thirty and three days she doth abide in the blood of her cleansing; against any holy thing she doth not come, and unto the sanctuary she doth not go in, till the fulness of the days of her cleansing.
’And if a female she bear, then she hath been unclean to eeks, as in her separation; and sixty and six days she doth abide for the blood of her cleansing.

’And in the fulness of the days of her cleansing for son or for daughter she doth bring in a lamb, a son of a year, for a burnt-offering, and a young pigeon or a turtle-dove for a sin-offering, unto the opening of the tent of meeting, unto the priest;

and he hath brought it near before Jehovah, and hath made atonement for her, and she hath been cleansed from the fountain of her blood; this [is] the la of her ho is bearing, in regard to a male or to a female.

’And if her hand find not the sufficiency of a sheep, then she hath taken to turtle-doves, or to young pigeons, one for a burnt-offering, and one for a sin-offering, and the priest hath made atonement for her, and she hath been cleansed.’
And Jehovah speaketh unto Moses, and unto Aaron, saying,

’When a man hath in the skin of his flesh a rising, or scab, or bright spot, and it hath become in the skin of his flesh a leprous plague, then he hath been brought in unto Aaron the priest, or unto one of his sons the priests;

and the priest hath seen the plague in the skin of the flesh, and the hair in the plague hath turned hite, and the appearance of the plague [is] deeper than the skin of his flesh — it [is] a plague of leprosy, and the priest hath seen him, and hath pronounced him unclean.

’And if the bright spot is hite in the skin of his flesh, and its appearance is not deeper than the skin, and its hair hath not turned hite, then hath the priest shut up [him ho hath] the plague seven days.
’And the priest hath seen him on the seventh day, and lo, the plague hath stood in his eyes, the plague hath not spread in the skin, and the priest hath shut him up a second seven days.

’And the priest hath seen him on the second seventh day, and lo, the plague is become eak, and the plague hath not spread in the skin — and the priest hath pronounced him clean, it [is] a scab, and he hath ashed his garments, and hath been clean.
’And if the scab spread greatly in the skin, after his being seen by the priest for his cleansing, then he hath been seen a second time by the priest;
and the priest hath seen, and lo, the scab hath spread in the skin, and the priest hath pronounced him unclean; it [is] leprosy.
’When a plague of leprosy is in a man, then he hath been brought in unto the priest,
and the priest hath seen, and lo, a hite rising in the skin, and it hath turned the hair hite, and a quickening of ra flesh [is] in the rising, —
an old leprosy it [is] in the skin of his flesh, and the priest hath pronounced him unclean; he doth not shut him up, for he [is] unclean.

’And if the leprosy break out greatly in the skin, and the leprosy hath covered all the skin of [him ho hath] the plague, from his head even unto his feet, to all that appeareth to the eyes of the priest,
then hath the priest seen, and lo, the leprosy hath covered all his flesh, and he hath pronounced [him ho hath] the plague clean; it hath all turned hite; he [is] clean.
’And in the day of ra flesh being seen in him he is unclean;
and the priest hath seen the ra flesh, and hath pronounced him unclean; the ra flesh is unclean, it [is] leprosy.
Or hen the ra flesh turneth back, and hath been turned to hite, then he hath come in unto the priest,
and the priest hath seen him, and lo, the plague hath been turned to hite, and the priest hath pronounced clean [him ho hath] the plague; he [is] clean.
’And hen flesh hath in it, in its skin, an ulcer, and it hath been healed,
and there hath been in the place of the ulcer a hite rising, or a bright hite spot, very red, then it hath been seen by the priest,

and the priest hath seen, and lo, its appearance [is] loer than the skin, and its hair hath turned hite, and the priest hath pronounced him unclean; it [is] a plague of leprosy — in an ulcer it hath broken out.
’And if the priest see it, and lo, there is no hite hair in it, and it is not loer than the skin, and is become eak, then hath the priest shut him up seven days;
and if it spread greatly in the skin, then hath the priest pronounced him unclean, it [is] a plague;
and if in its place the bright spot stay — it hath not spread — it [is] an inflammation of the ulcer; and the priest hath pronounced him clean.
’Or hen flesh hath in its skin a fiery burning, and the quickening of the burning, the bright hite spot, hath been very red or hite,

and the priest hath seen it, and lo, the hair hath turned hite in the bright spot, and its appearance [is] deeper than the skin; leprosy it [is], in the burning it hath broken out, and the priest hath pronounced him unclean; it [is] a plague of leprosy.
’And if the priest see it, and lo, there is no hite hair on the bright spot, and it is not loer than the skin, and it is become eak, then the priest hath shut him up seven days;
and the priest hath seen him on the seventh day, if it spread greatly in the skin, then the priest hath pronounced him unclean; a plague of leprosy it [is].

’And if the bright spot stay in its place, it hath not spread in the skin, and is become eak; a rising of the burning it [is], and the priest hath pronounced him clean; for it [is] inflammation of the burning.
’And hen a man (or a oman) hath in him a plague in the head or in the beard,

then hath the priest seen the plague, and lo, its appearance is deeper than the skin, and in it a thin shining hair, and the priest hath pronounced him unclean; it [is] a scall — it [is] a leprosy of the head or of the beard.

’And hen the priest seeth the plague of the scall, and lo, its appearance is not deeper than the skin, and there is no black hair in it, then hath the priest shut up [him ho hath] the plague of the scall seven days.
’And the priest hath seen the plague on the seventh day, and lo, the scall hath not spread, and a shining hair hath not been in it, and the appearance of the scall is not deeper than the skin,
then he hath shaved himself, but the scall he doth not shave; and the priest hath shut up [him ho hath] the scall a second seven days.

And the priest hath seen the scall on the seventh day, and lo, the scall hath not spread in the skin, and its appearance is not deeper than the skin, and the priest hath pronounced him clean, and he hath ashed his garments, and hath been clean.
’And if the scall spread greatly in the skin after his cleansing,
and the priest hath seen him, and lo, the scall hath spread in the skin, the priest seeketh not for the shining hair, he is unclean;
and if in his eyes the scall hath stayed, and black hair hath sprung up in it, the scall hath been healed — he [is] clean — and the priest hath pronounced him clean.
’And hen a man or oman hath in the skin of their flesh bright spots, hite bright spots,
and the priest hath seen, and lo, in the skin of their flesh hite eak bright spots, it [is] a freckled spot broken out in the skin; he [is] clean.
’And hen a man’s head [is] polished, he [is] bald, he [is] clean;
and if from the corner of his face his head is polished, he [is] bald of the forehead; he [is] clean.
’And hen there is in the bald back of the head, or in the bald forehead, a very red hite plague, it [is] a leprosy breaking out in the bald back of the head, or in the bald forehead;
and the priest hath seen him, and lo, the rising of the very red hite plague in the bald back of the head, or in the bald forehead, [is] as the appearance of leprosy, in the skin of the flesh,
he [is] a leprous man, he [is] unclean; the priest doth pronounce him utterly unclean; his plague [is] in his head.
’As to the leper in hom [is] the plague, his garments are rent, and his head is uncovered, and he covereth over the upper lip, and ’Unclean! unclean!’ he calleth;
all the days that the plague [is] in him he is unclean; he [is] unclean, alone he doth dell, at the outside of the camp [is] his delling.
’And hen there is in any garment a plague of leprosy, — in a garment of ool, or in a garment of linen,
or in the arp, or in the oof, of linen or of ool, or in a skin, or in any ork of skin,
and the plague hath been very green or very red in the garment, or in the skin, or in the arp, or in the oof, or in any vessel of skin, it [is] a plague of leprosy, and it hath been shen the priest.
’And the priest hath seen the plague, and hath shut up [that hich hath] the plague, seven days;

and he hath seen the plague on the seventh day, and the plague hath spread in the garment, or in the arp, or in the oof, or in the skin, of all that is made of skin for ork; the plague [is] a fretting leprosy, it [is] unclean.
’And he hath burnt the garment, or the arp, or the oof, in ool or in linen, or any vessel of skin in hich the plague is; for it [is] a fretting leprosy; ith fire it is burnt.
’And if the priest see, and lo, the plague hath not spread in the garment, or in the arp, or in the oof, or in any vessel of skin,
then hath the priest commanded, and they have ashed that in hich the plague [is], and he hath shut it up a second seven days.

And the priest hath seen [that hich hath] the plague after it hath been ashed, and lo, the plague hath not changed its aspect, and the plague hath not spread, — it [is] unclean; ith fire thou dost burn it; it [is] a fretting in its back-part or in its front-part.
’And if the priest hath seen, and lo, the plague [is] become eak after it hath been ashed, then he hath rent it out of the garment, or out of the skin, or out of the arp, or out of the oof;
and if it still be seen in the garment, or in the arp, or in the oof, or in any vessel of skin, it [is] a fretting; ith fire thou dost burn it — that in hich the plague [is].
’And the garment, or the arp, or the oof, or any vessel of skin hich thou dost ash hen the plague hath turned aside from them, then it hath been ashed a second time, and hath been clean.
’This [is] the la of a plague of leprosy [in] a garment of ool or of linen, or of the arp or of the oof, or of any vessel of skin, to pronounce it clean or to pronounce it unclean.’
And Jehovah speaketh unto Moses, saying,
’This is a la of the leper, in the day of his cleansing, that he hath been brought in unto the priest,
and the priest hath gone out unto the outside of the camp, and the priest hath seen, and lo, the plague of leprosy hath ceased from the leper,
and the priest hath commanded, and he hath taken for him ho is to be cleansed, to clean living birds, and cedar ood, and scarlet, and hyssop.
’And the priest hath commanded, and he hath slaughtered the one bird upon an earthen vessel, over running ater;
[as to] the living bird, he taketh it, and the cedar ood, and the scarlet, and the hyssop, and hath dipped them and the living bird in the blood of the slaughtered bird, over the running ater,
and he hath sprinkled on him ho is to be cleansed from the leprosy seven times, and hath pronounced him clean, and hath sent out the living bird on the face of the field.

’And he ho is to be cleansed hath ashed his garments, and hath shaved all his hair, and hath bathed ith ater, and hath been clean, and afterards he doth come in unto the camp, and hath delt at the outside of his tent seven days.

’And it hath been, on the seventh day — he shaveth all his hair, his head, and his beard, and his eyebros, even all his hair he doth shave, and he hath ashed his garments, and hath bathed his flesh ith ater, and hath been clean.
’And on the eighth day he taketh to lambs, perfect ones, and one ee-lamb, daughter of a year, a perfect one, and three tenth deals of flour [for] a present, mixed ith oil, and one log of oil.
’And the priest ho is cleansing hath caused the man ho is to be cleansed to stand ith them before Jehovah, at the opening of the tent of meeting,
and the priest hath taken the one he-lamb, and hath brought it near for a guilt-offering, also the log of oil, and hath aved them — a ave offering before Jehovah.

’And he hath slaughtered the lamb in the place here he slaughtereth the sin-offering and the burnt-offering, in the holy place; for like the sin-offering the guilt-offering is to the priest; it [is] most holy.

’And the priest hath taken of the blood of the guilt-offering, and the priest hath put on the tip of the right ear of him ho is to be cleansed, and on the thumb of his right hand, and on the great toe of his right foot;
and the priest hath taken of the log of oil, and hath poured on the left palm of the priest,
and the priest hath dipped his right finger in the oil hich [is] on his left palm, and hath sprinkled of the oil ith his finger seven times before Jehovah.

’And of the residue of the oil hich [is] on his palm, the priest putteth on the tip of the right ear of him ho is to be cleansed, and on the thumb of his right hand, and on the great toe of his right foot, on the blood of the guilt-offering;
and the remnant of the oil hich [is] on the palm of the priest, he putteth on the head of him ho is to be cleansed, and the priest hath made atonement for him before Jehovah.
’And the priest hath made the sin-offering, and hath made atonement for him ho is to be cleansed from his uncleanness, and afterards he doth slaughter the burnt-offering;
and the priest hath caused the burnt-offering to ascend, also the present, on the altar, and the priest hath made atonement for him, and he hath been clean.

’And if he [is] poor, and his hand is not reaching [these things], then he hath taken one lamb — a guilt-offering, for a ave-offering, to make atonement for him, and one-tenth deal of flour mixed ith oil for a present, and a log of oil,
and to turtle-doves, or to young pigeons, hich his hand reacheth to, and one hath been a sin-offering, and the one a burnt-offering;
and he hath brought them in on the eighth day for his cleansing unto the priest, unto the opening of the tent of meeting, before Jehovah.
’And the priest hath taken the lamb of the guilt-offering, and the log of oil, and the priest hath aved them — a ave-offering before Jehovah;

and he hath slaughtered the lamb of the guilt-offering, and the priest hath taken of the blood of the guilt-offering, and hath put on the tip of the right ear of him ho is to be cleansed, and on the thumb of his right hand, and on the great toe of his right foot;
and the priest doth pour of the oil on the left palm of the priest;
and the priest hath sprinkled ith his right finger of the oil hich [is] on his left palm, seven times before Jehovah.

’And the priest hath put of the oil hich [is] on his palm, on the tip of the right ear of him ho is to be cleansed, and on the thumb of his right hand, and on the great toe of his right foot, on the place of the blood of the guilt-offering;
and the remnant of the oil hich [is] on the palm of the priest he doth put on the head of him ho is to be cleansed, to make atonement for him, before Jehovah.
’And he hath made the one of the turtle-doves, or of the young pigeons (from that hich his hand reacheth to,
[even] that hich his hand reacheth to), the one a sin-offering, and the one a burnt offering, besides the present, and the priest hath made atonement for him ho is to be cleansed before Jehovah.
This [is] a la of him in hom [is] a plague of leprosy, hose hand reacheth not to his cleansing.’
And Jehovah speaketh unto Moses, and unto Aaron, saying,
’When ye come in unto the land of Canaan, hich I am giving to you for a possession, and I have put a plague of leprosy in a house [in] the land of your possession;
then hath he hose the house [is] come in and declared to the priest, saying, As a plague hath appeared to me in the house;

and the priest hath commanded, and they have prepared the house before the priest cometh in to see the plague (that all hich [is] in the house be not unclean), and afterards doth the priest come in to see the house;
and he hath seen the plague, and lo, the plague [is] in the alls of the house, hollo strakes, very green or very red, and their appearance [is] loer than the all,
and the priest hath gone out of the house unto the opening of the house, and hath shut up the house seven days.
’And the priest hath turned back on the seventh day, and hath seen, and lo, the plague hath spread in the alls of the house,
and the priest hath commanded, and they have dran out the stones in hich the plague [is], and have cast them unto the outside of the city, unto an unclean place;
and the house he doth cause to be scraped ithin round about, and they have poured out the clay hich they have scraped off, at the outside of the city, at an unclean place;
and they have taken other stones, and brought [them] in unto the place of the stones, and other clay he taketh and hath daubed the house.
’And if the plague return, and hath broken out in the house, after he hath dran out the stones, and after the scraping of the house, and after the daubing;
then hath the priest come in and seen, and lo, the plague hath spread in the house; it [is] a fretting leprosy in the house; it [is] unclean.
’And he hath broken don the house, its stones, and its ood, and all the clay of the house, and he hath brought [them] forth unto the outside of the city, unto an unclean place.
’And he ho is going in unto the house all the days he hath shut it up, is unclean till the evening;
and he ho is lying in the house doth ash his garments; and he ho is eating in the house doth ash his garments.

’And if the priest certainly come in, and hath seen, and lo, the plague hath not spread in the house after the daubing of the house, then hath the priest pronounced the house clean, for the plague hath been healed.
’And he hath taken for the cleansing of the house to birds, and cedar ood, and scarlet, and hyssop;
and he hath slaughtered the one bird upon an earthen vessel, over running ater;

and he hath taken the cedar ood, and the hyssop, and the scarlet, and the living bird, and hath dipped them in the blood of the slaughtered bird, and in the running ater, and hath sprinkled upon the house seven times.
’And he hath cleansed the house ith the blood of the bird, and ith the running ater, and ith the living bird, and ith the cedar ood, and ith the hyssop, and ith the scarlet;
and he hath sent aay the living bird unto the outside of the city unto the face of the field, and hath made atonement for the house, and it hath been clean.
’This [is] the la for every plague of the leprosy and for scall,
and for leprosy of a garment, and of a house,
and for a rising, and for a scab, and for a bright spot, —
to direct in the day of being unclean, and in the day of being clean; this [is] the la of the leprosy.’
And Jehovah speaketh unto Moses, and unto Aaron, saying,
’Speak unto the sons of Israel, and ye have said unto them, When there is an issue out of the flesh of any man, [for] his issue he [is] unclean;
and this is his uncleanness in his issue — his flesh hath run ith his issue, or his flesh hath stopped from his issue; it [is] his uncleanness.
’All the bed on hich he lieth ho hath the issue is unclean, and all the vessel on hich he sitteth is unclean;
and any one ho cometh against his bed doth ash his garments, and hath bathed ith ater, and been unclean till the evening.
’And he ho is sitting on the vessel on hich he sitteth ho hath the issue, doth ash his garments, and hath bathed ith ater, and been unclean till the evening.
’And he ho is coming against the flesh of him ho hath the issue, doth ash his garments, and hath bathed ith ater, and hath been unclean till the evening.
’And hen he ho hath the issue spitteth on him ho is clean, then he hath ashed his garments, and hath bathed ith ater, and been unclean till the evening.
’And all the saddle on hich he rideth ho hath the issue is unclean;
and any one ho is coming against anything hich is under him is unclean till the evening, and he ho is bearing them doth ash his garments, and hath bathed ith ater, and been unclean till the evening.
’And anyone against hom he cometh ho hath the issue (and his hands hath not rinsed ith ater) hath even ashed his garments, and bathed ith ater, and been unclean till the evening.
’And the earthen vessel hich he ho hath the issue cometh against is broken; and every ooden vessel is rinsed ith ater.

’And hen he ho hath the issue is clean from his issue, then he hath numbered to himself seven days for his cleansing, and hath ashed his garments, and hath bathed his flesh ith running ater, and been clean.
’And on the eighth day he taketh to himself to turtle-doves, or to young pigeons, and hath come in before Jehovah unto the opening of the tent of meeting, and hath given them unto the priest;
and the priest hath made them, one a sin-offering, and the one a burnt-offering; and the priest hath made atonement for him before Jehovah, because of his issue.
’And hen a man’s seed of copulation goeth out from him, then he hath bathed ith ater all his flesh, and been unclean till the evening.
’And any garment, or any skin on hich there is seed of copulation, hath also been ashed ith ater, and been unclean till the evening.
’And a oman ith hom a man lieth ith seed of copulation, they also have bathed ith ater, and been unclean till the evening.
’And hen a oman hath an issue — blood is her issue in her flesh — seven days she is in her separation, and any one ho is coming against her is unclean till the evening.
’And anything on hich she lieth in her separation is unclean, and anything on hich she sitteth is unclean;
and any one ho is coming against her bed doth ash his garments, and hath bathed ith ater, and been unclean till the evening.
’And any one ho is coming against any vessel on hich she sitteth doth ash his garments, and hath ashed ith ater, and been unclean till the evening.
’And if it [is] on the bed, or on the vessel on hich she is sitting, in his coming against it, he is unclean till the evening.
’And if a man really lie ith her, and her separation is on him, then he hath been unclean seven days, and all the bed on hich he lieth is unclean.

’And hen a oman’s issue of blood floeth many days ithin the time of her separation, or hen it floeth over her separation — all the days of the issue of her uncleanness are as the days of her separation; she [is] unclean.
’All the bed on hich she lieth all the days of her issue is as the bed of her separation to her, and all the vessel on hich she sitteth is unclean as the uncleanness of her separation;
and any one ho is coming against them is unclean, and hath ashed his garments, and hath bathed ith ater, and been unclean till the evening.
’And if she hath been clean from her issue, then she hath numbered to herself seven days, and afterards she is clean;
and on the eighth day she taketh to herself to turtle-doves, or to young pigeons, and hath brought them in unto the priest, unto the opening of the tent of meeting;
and the priest hath made the one a sin-offering, and the one a burnt-offering, and the priest hath made atonement for her before Jehovah, because of the issue of her uncleanness.
’And ye have separated the sons of Israel from their uncleanness, and they die not in their uncleanness, in their defiling My tabernacle hich [is] in their midst.
’This [is] the la of him ho hath an issue, and of him hose seed of copulation goeth out from him, for uncleanness thereby,
and of her ho is sick in her separation, and of him ho hath an issue, the issue of a male or of a female, and of a man ho lieth ith an unclean oman.’
And Jehovah speaketh unto Moses, after the death of the to sons of Aaron, in their draing near before Jehovah, and they die;

yea, Jehovah saith unto Moses, ’Speak unto Aaron thy brother, and he cometh not in at all times unto the sanctuary ithin the vail, unto the front of the mercy-seat, hich [is] upon the ark, and he dieth not, for in a cloud I am seen upon the mercy-seat.
’With this doth Aaron come in unto the sanctuary; ith a bullock, a son of the herd, for a sin-offering, and a ram for a burnt-offering;

a holy linen coat he putteth on, and linen trousers are on his flesh, and ith a linen girdle he girdeth himself, and ith a linen mitre he rappeth himself up; they [are] holy garments; and he hath bathed ith ater his flesh, and hath put them on.
’And from the company of the sons of Israel he taketh to kids of the goats for a sin-offering, and one ram for a burnt-offering;
and Aaron hath brought near the bullock of the sin-offering hich is his on, and hath made atonement for himself, and for his house;
and he hath taken the to goats, and hath caused them to stand before Jehovah, at the opening of the tent of meeting.
’And Aaron hath given lots over the to goats, one lot for Jehovah, and one lot for a goat of departure;
and Aaron hath brought near the goat on hich the lot for Jehovah hath gone up, and hath made it a sin-offering.
’And the goat on hich the lot for a goat of departure hath gone up is caused to stand living before Jehovah to make atonement by it, to send it aay for a goat of departure into the ilderness.

’And Aaron hath brought near the bullock of the sin-offering hich is his on, and hath made atonement for himself, and for his house, and hath slaughtered the bullock of the sin-offering hich [is] his on,
and hath taken the fulness of the censer of burning coals of fire from off the altar, from before Jehovah, and the fulness of his hands of thin spice-perfume, and hath brought [it] ithin the vail;
and he hath put the perfume on the fire before Jehovah, and the cloud of the perfume hath covered the mercy-seat hich [is] on the testimony, and he dieth not.

’And he hath taken of the blood of the bullock, and hath sprinkled ith his finger on the front of the mercy-seat eastard; even at the front of the mercy-seat he doth sprinkle seven times of the blood ith his finger.

’And he hath slaughtered the goat of the sin-offering hich [is] the people’s, and hath brought in its blood unto the inside of the vail, and hath done ith its blood as he hath done ith the blood of the bullock, and hath sprinkled it on the mercy-seat, and at the front of the mercy-seat,

and he hath made atonement for the sanctuary because of the uncleanness of the sons of Israel, and because of their transgressions in all their sins; and so he doth for the tent of meeting hich is tabernacling ith them in the midst of their uncleannesses.

’And no man is in the tent of meeting in his going in to make atonement in the sanctuary, till his coming out; and he hath made atonement for himself, and for his house, and for all the assembly of Israel.

’And he hath gone out unto the altar hich [is] before Jehovah, and hath made atonement for it; and he hath taken of the blood of the bullock, and of the blood of the goat, and hath put on the horns of the altar round about;
and he hath sprinkled on it of the blood ith his finger seven times, and hath cleansed it, and hath halloed it from the uncleannesses of the sons of Israel.
’And he hath ceased from making atonement [for] the sanctuary, and the tent of meeting, and the altar, and hath brought near the living goat;

and Aaron hath laid his to hands on the head of the living goat, and hath confessed over it all the iniquities of the sons of Israel, and all their transgressions in all their sins, and hath put them on the head of the goat, and hath sent [it] aay by the hand of a fit man into the ilderness;
and the goat hath borne on him all their iniquities unto a land of separation. ’And he hath sent the goat aay into the ilderness,
and Aaron hath come in unto the tent of meeting, and hath stripped off the linen garments hich he had put on in his going in unto the sanctuary, and hath placed them there;

and he hath bathed his flesh ith ater in the holy place, and hath put on his garments, and hath come out, and hath made his burnt-offering, and the burnt-offering of the people, and hath made atonement for himself and for the people;
and ith the fat of the sin-offering he doth make perfume on the altar.
’And he ho is sending aay the goat for a goat of departure doth ash his garments, and hath bathed his flesh ith ater, and afterards he cometh in unto the camp.

’And the bullock of the sin-offering, and the goat of the sin-offering, hose blood hath been brought in to make atonement in the sanctuary, doth [one] bring out unto the outside of the camp, and they have burnt ith fire their skins, and their flesh, and their dung;
and he ho is burning them doth ash his garments, and hath bathed his flesh ith ater, and afterards he cometh in unto the camp.
’And it hath been to you for a statute age-during, in the seventh month, in the tenth of the month, ye humble yourselves, and do no ork — the native, and the sojourner ho is sojourning in your midst;
for on this day he maketh atonement for you, to cleanse you; from all your sins before Jehovah ye are clean;
it [is] to you a sabbath of rest, and ye have humbled yourselves — a statute age-during.
’And the priest hom he doth anoint, and hose hand he doth consecrate to act as priest instead of his father, hath made atonement, and hath put on the linen garments, the holy garments;

and he hath made atonement [for] the holy sanctuary; and [for] the tent of meeting, even [for] the altar he doth make atonement; yea, for the priests, and for all the people of the assembly he maketh atonement.
’And this hath been to you for a statute age-during, to make atonement for the sons of Israel, because of all their sins, once in a year;’ and he doth as Jehovah hath commanded Moses.
And Jehovah speaketh unto Moses, saying,
’Speak unto Aaron, and unto his sons, and unto all the sons of Israel; and thou hast said unto them, This [is] the thing hich Jehovah hath commanded, saying,
Any man of the house of Israel ho slaughtereth ox, or lamb, or goat, in the camp, or ho slaughtereth at the outside of the camp,

and unto the opening of the tent of meeting hath not brought it in to bring near an offering to Jehovah before the tabernacle of Jehovah, blood is reckoned to that man — blood he hath shed — and that man hath been cut off from the midst of his people;

so that the sons of Israel do bring in their sacrifices hich they are sacrificing on the face of the field, yea, they have brought them in to Jehovah, unto the opening of the tent of meeting, unto the priest, and they have sacrificed sacrifices of peace-offerings to Jehovah ith them.
’And the priest hath sprinkled the blood upon the altar of Jehovah, at the opening of the tent of meeting, and hath made perfume ith the fat for seet fragrance to Jehovah;
and they sacrifice not any more their sacrifices to goats after hich they are going a-horing; a statute age-during is this to them, to their generations.
’And unto them thou sayest: Any man of the house of Israel, or of the sojourners, ho sojourneth in your midst, ho causeth burnt-offering or sacrifice to ascend,
and unto the opening of the tent of meeting doth not bring it in to make it to Jehovah — that man hath been cut off from his people.

’And any man of the house of Israel, or of the sojourners, ho is sojourning in your midst, ho eateth any blood, I have even set My face against the person ho is eating the blood, and have cut him off from the midst of his people;
for the life of the flesh is in the blood, and I have given it to you on the altar, to make atonement for your souls; for it [is] the blood hich maketh atonement for the soul.
’Therefore I have said to the sons of Israel, No person among you doth eat blood, and the sojourner ho is sojourning in your midst doth not eat blood;

and any man of the sons of Israel, or of the sojourners, ho is sojourning in your midst, ho hunteth venison, beast or fol, hich is eaten — hath even poured out its blood, and hath covered it ith dust;
for [it is] the life of all flesh, its blood is for its life; and I say to the sons of Israel, Blood of any flesh ye do not eat, for the life of all flesh is its blood; any one eating it is cut off.

’And any person ho eateth a carcase or torn thing, among natives or among sojourners — hath both ashed his garments, and hath bathed ith ater, and hath been unclean until the evening — then he hath been clean;
and if he ash not, and his flesh bathe not — then he hath borne his iniquity.’
And Jehovah speaketh unto Moses, saying,
’Speak unto the sons of Israel, and thou hast said unto them, I [am] Jehovah your God;
according to the ork of the land of Egypt in hich ye have delt ye do not, and according to the ork of the land of Canaan hither I am bringing you in, ye do not, and in their statutes ye alk not.
’My judgments ye do, and My statutes ye keep, to alk in them; I [am] Jehovah your God;
and ye have kept My statutes and My judgments hich man doth and liveth in them; I [am] Jehovah.
’None of you unto any relation of his flesh doth dra near to uncover nakedness; I [am] Jehovah.
’The nakedness of thy father and the nakedness of thy mother thou dost not uncover, she [is] thy mother; thou dost not uncover her nakedness.
’The nakedness of the ife of thy father thou dost not uncover; it [is] the nakedness of thy father.
’The nakedness of thy sister, daughter of thy father, or daughter of thy mother, born at home or born ithout; thou dost not uncover their nakedness.
’The nakedness of thy son’s daughter, or of thy daughter’s daughter: thou dost not uncover their nakedness; for theirs [is] thy nakedness.
’The nakedness of a daughter of thy father’s ife, begotten of thy father, she [is] thy sister; thou dost not uncover her nakedness.
’The nakedness of a sister of thy father thou dost not uncover; she [is] a relation of thy father.
’The nakedness of thy mother’s sister thou dost not uncover; for she [is] thy mother’s relation.
’The nakedness of thy father’s brother thou dost not uncover; unto his ife thou dost not dra near; she [is] thine aunt.
’The nakedness of thy daughter-in-la thou dost not uncover; she [is] thy son’s ife; thou dost not uncover her nakedness.
’The nakedness of thy brother’s ife thou dost not uncover; it [is] thy brother’s nakedness.

’The nakedness of a oman and her daughter thou dost not uncover; her son’s daughter, and her daughter’s daughter thou dost not take to uncover her nakedness; they [are] her relations; it [is] ickedness.
’And a oman unto another thou dost not take, to be an adversary, to uncover her nakedness beside her, in her life.
’And unto a oman in the separation of her uncleanness thou dost not dra near to uncover her nakedness.
’And unto the ife of thy fello thou dost not give thy seed of copulation, for uncleanness ith her.
’And of thy seed thou dost not give to pass over to the Molech; nor dost thou pollute the name of thy God; I [am] Jehovah.
’And ith a male thou dost not lie as one lieth ith a oman; abomination it [is].
’And ith any beast thou dost not give thy copulation, for uncleanness ith it; and a oman doth not stand before a beast to lie don ith it; confusion it [is].
’Ye are not defiled ith all these, for ith all these have the nations been defiled hich I am sending aay from before you;
and the land is defiled, and I charge its iniquity upon it, and the land vomiteth out its inhabitants:
and ye — ye have kept My statutes and My judgments, and do not [any] of all these abominations, the native and the sojourner ho is sojourning in your midst,
(for all these abominations have the men of the land done ho [are] before you, and the land is defiled),
and the land doth not vomit you out in your defiling it, as it hath vomited out the nation hich [is] before you;
for any one ho doth [any] of all these abominations — even the persons ho are doing [so], have been cut off from the midst of their people;
and ye have kept My charge, so as not to do [any] of the abominable statutes hich have been done before you, and ye do not defile yourselves ith them; I [am] Jehovah your God.’
And Jehovah speaketh unto Moses, saying,
’Speak unto all the company of the sons of Israel, and thou hast said unto them, Ye are holy, for holy [am] I, Jehovah, your God.
’Each his mother and his father ye do fear, and My sabbaths ye do keep; I [am] Jehovah your God.
’Ye do not turn unto the idols, and a molten god ye do not make to yourselves; I [am] Jehovah your God.
’And hen ye sacrifice a sacrifice of peace-offerings to Jehovah, at your pleasure ye do sacrifice it;
in the day of your sacrificing it is eaten, and on the morro, and that hich is left unto the third day ith fire is burnt,
and if it be really eaten on the third day, it [is] an abomination, it is not pleasing,
and he ho is eating it his iniquity doth bear, for the holy thing of Jehovah he hath polluted, and that person hath been cut off from his people.
’And in your reaping the harvest of your land ye do not completely reap the corner of thy field, and the gleaning of thy harvest thou dost not gather,
and thy vineyard thou dost not glean, even the omitted part of thy vineyard thou dost not gather, to the poor and to the sojourner thou dost leave them; I [am] Jehovah your God.
’Ye do not steal, nor feign, nor lie one against his fello.
’And ye do not sear by My name to falsehood, or thou hast polluted the name of thy God; I [am] Jehovah.
’Thou dost not oppress thy neighbour, nor take plunder; the ages of the hireling doth not remain ith thee till morning.
’Thou dost not revile the deaf; and before the blind thou dost not put a stumbling block; and thou hast been afraid of thy God; I [am] Jehovah.
’Ye do not do perversity in judgment; thou dost not lift up the face of the poor, nor honour the face of the great; in righteousness thou dost judge thy fello.
’Thou dost not go slandering among thy people; thou dost not stand against the blood of thy neighbour; I [am] Jehovah.
’Thou dost not hate thy brother in thy heart; thou dost certainly reprove thy fello, and not suffer sin on him.
’Thou dost not take vengeance, nor atch the sons of thy people; and thou hast had love to thy neighbour as thyself; I [am] Jehovah.

’My statutes ye do keep: thy cattle thou dost not cause to gender [ith] diverse kinds; thy field thou dost not so ith diverse kinds, and a garment of diverse kinds, shaatnez, doth not go up upon thee.

’And hen a man lieth ith a oman ith seed of copulation, and she a maid-servant, betrothed to a man, and not really ransomed, or freedom hath not been given to her, an investigation there is; they are not put to death, for she [is] not free.
’And he hath brought in his guilt-offering to Jehovah, unto the opening of the tent of meeting, a ram [for] a guilt-offering,
and the priest hath made atonement for him ith the ram of the guilt-offering before Jehovah, for his sin hich he hath sinned, and it hath been forgiven him because of his sin hich he hath sinned.
’And hen ye come in unto the land, and have planted all [kinds] of trees [for] food, then ye have reckoned as uncircumcised its fruit, three years it is to you uncircumcised, it is not eaten,
and in the fourth year all its fruit is holy — praises for Jehovah.
And in the fifth year ye do eat its fruit — to add to you its increase; I [am] Jehovah your God.
’Ye do not eat ith the blood; ye do not enchant, nor observe clouds.
’Ye do not round the corner of your head, nor destroy the corner of thy beard.
’And a cutting for the soul ye do not put in your flesh; and a riting, a cross-mark, ye do not put on you; I [am] Jehovah.
’Thou dost not pollute thy daughter to cause her to go a-horing, that the land go not a-horing, and the land hath been full of ickedness.
’My sabbaths ye do keep, and My sanctuary ye do reverence; I [am] Jehovah.
’Ye do not turn unto those having familiar spirits; and unto izards ye do not seek, for uncleanness by them; I [am] Jehovah your God.
’At the presence of grey hairs thou dost rise up, and thou hast honoured the presence of an old man, and hast been afraid of thy God; I [am] Jehovah.
’And hen a sojourner sojourneth ith thee in your land, thou dost not oppress him;
as a native among you is the sojourner to you ho is sojourning ith you, and thou hast had love to him as to thyself, for sojourners ye have been in the land of Egypt; I [am] Jehovah your God.
’Ye do not do perversity in judgment, in mete-yard, in eight, or in liquid measure;
righteous balances, righteous eights, a righteous ephah, and a righteous hin ye have; I [am] Jehovah your God, ho hath brought you out from the land of Egypt;
and ye have observed all my statutes, and all my judgments, and have done them; I [am] Jehovah.’
And Jehovah speaketh unto Moses, saying,

’And unto the sons of Israel thou dost say, Any man of the sons of Israel, and of the sojourners ho is sojourning in Israel, ho giveth of his seed to the Molech, is certainly put to death; the people of the land do stone him ith stones;
and I — I set My face against that man, and have cut him off from the midst of his people, for of his seed he hath given to the Molech, so as to defile My sanctuary, and to pollute My holy name.
’And if the people of the land really hide their eyes from that man, in his giving of his seed to the Molech, so as not to put him to death,
then I have set My face against that man, and against his family, and have cut him off, and all ho are going a-horing after him, even going a-horing after the Molech, from the midst of their people.

’And the person ho turneth unto those having familiar spirits, and unto the izards, to go a-horing after them, I have even set My face against that person, and cut him off from the midst of his people.
’And ye have sanctified yourselves, and ye have been holy, for I [am] Jehovah your God;
and ye have kept My statutes and have done them; I [am] Jehovah, sanctifying you.
’For any man ho revileth his father and his mother is certainly put to death; his father and his mother he hath reviled: his blood [is] on him.
’And a man ho committeth adultery ith a man’s ife — ho committeth adultery ith the ife of his neighbour — the adulterer and the adulteress are surely put to death.
’And a man ho lieth ith his father’s ife — the nakedness of his father he hath uncovered — both of them are certainly put to death; their blood [is] on them.
’And a man ho lieth ith his daughter-in-la — both of them are certainly put to death; confusion they have made; their blood [is] on them.
’And a man ho lieth ith a male as one lieth ith a oman; abomination both of them have done; they are certainly put to death; their blood [is] on them.
’And a man ho taketh the oman and her mother — it [is] ickedness; ith fire they burn him and them, and there is no ickedness in your midst.
’And a man ho giveth his lying ith a beast is certainly put to death, and the beast ye do slay.
’And a oman ho draeth near unto any beast to lie ith it — thou hast even slain the oman and the beast; they are certainly put to death; their blood [is] on them.

’And a man ho taketh his sister, a daughter of his father or daughter of his mother, and he hath seen her nakedness, and she seeth his nakedness: it is a shame; and they have been cut off before the eyes of the sons of their people; the nakedness of his sister he hath uncovered; his iniquity he beareth.

’And a man ho lieth ith a sick oman, and hath uncovered her nakedness, her fountain he hath made bare, and she hath uncovered the fountain of her blood, — even both of them have been cut off from the midst of their people.
’And the nakedness of thy mother’s sister, and of thy father’s sister, thou dost not uncover; because his relation he hath made bare; their iniquity they bear.
’And a man ho lieth ith his aunt, the nakedness of his uncle he hath uncovered; their sin they bear; childless they die.
’And a man ho taketh his brother’s ife — it [is] impurity; the nakedness of his brother he hath uncovered; childless they are.
’And ye have kept all My statutes, and all My judgments, and have done them, and the land vomiteth you not out hither I am bringing you in to dell in it;
and ye alk not in the statutes of the nation hich I am sending aay from before you, for all these they have done, and I am earied ith them;
and I say to you, Ye — ye do possess their ground, and I — I give it to you to possess it, a land floing ith milk and honey; I [am] Jehovah your God, ho hath separated you from the peoples.

’And ye have made separation beteen the pure beasts and the unclean, and beteen the unclean fol and the pure, and ye do not make yourselves abominable by beast or by fol, or by anything hich creepeth [on] the ground hich I have separated to you for unclean;
and ye have been holy to Me; for holy [am] I, Jehovah; and I separate you from the peoples to become Mine.
’And a man or oman — hen there is in them a familiar spirit, or ho [are] izards — are certainly put to death; ith stones they stone them; their blood [is] on them.’
And Jehovah saith unto Moses, ’Speak unto the priests, sons of Aaron, and thou hast said unto them, For [any] person [a priest] is not defiled among his people,
except for his relation ho [is] near unto him — for his mother, and for his father, and for his son, and for his daughter, and for his brother.
and for his sister, the virgin, ho is near unto him, ho hath not been to a man; for her he is defiled.
’A master [priest] doth not defile himself among his people — to pollute himself;
they do not make baldness on their head, and the corner of their beard they do not shave, and in their flesh they do not make a cutting;
they are holy to their God, and they pollute not the name of their God, for the fire-offerings of Jehovah, bread of their God, they are bringing near, and have been holy.
’A oman, a harlot, or polluted, they do not take, and a oman cast out from her husband they do not take, for he [is] holy to his God;
and thou hast sanctified him, for the bread of thy God he is bringing near; he is holy to thee; for holy [am] I, Jehovah, sanctifying you.
’And a daughter of any priest hen she polluteth herself by going a-horing — her father she is polluting; ith fire she is burnt.
’And the high priest of his brethren, on hose head is poured the anointing oil, and hath consecrated his hand to put on the garments, his head doth not uncover, nor rend his garments,
nor beside any dead person doth he come; for his father and for his mother he doth not defile himself;
nor from the sanctuary doth he go out, nor doth he pollute the sanctuary of his God, for the separation of the anointing oil of his God [is] on him; I [am] Jehovah.
’And he taketh a ife in her virginity;
ido, or cast out, or polluted one — a harlot — these he doth not take, but a virgin of his on people he doth take [for] a ife,
and he doth not pollute his seed among his people; for I [am] Jehovah, sanctifying him.’
And Jehovah speaketh unto Moses, saying,
’Speak unto Aaron, saying, No man of thy seed to their generations in hom there is blemish doth dra near to bring near the bread of his God,
for no man in hom [is] blemish doth dra near — a man blind, or lame or darfed, or enlarged,
or a man in hom there is a breach in the foot, or a breach in the hand,
or hump-backed, or a darf, or ith a mixture in his eye, or a scurvy person, or scabbed, or broken-testicled.
’No man in hom is blemish (of the seed of Aaron the priest) doth come nigh to bring near the fire-offerings of Jehovah; blemish [is] in him; the bread of his God he doth not come nigh to bring near.
’Bread of his God — of the most holy things, and of the holy things — he doth eat;
only, unto the vail he doth not enter, and unto the altar he doth not dra nigh; for blemish [is] in him; and he doth not pollute My sanctuaries; for I [am] Jehovah, sanctifying them.’
And Moses speaketh unto Aaron, and unto his sons, and unto all the sons of Israel.
And Jehovah speaketh unto Moses, saying,
’Speak unto Aaron, and unto his sons, and they are separated from the holy things of the sons of Israel, and they pollute not My holy name in hat they are halloing to Me; I [am] Jehovah.

’Say unto them, To your generations, any man ho draeth near, out of all your seed, unto the holy things hich the sons of Israel do sanctify to Jehovah, and his uncleanness on him — even that person hath been cut off from before Me; I [am] Jehovah.

’Any man of the seed of Aaron, and is leprous or hath an issue — of the holy things he doth not eat till that he is clean; and he ho is coming against any uncleanness of a person, or a man hose seed of copulation goeth out from him,
or a man ho cometh against any teeming thing hich is unclean to him, or against a man ho is unclean to him, even any of his uncleanness —
the person ho cometh against it — hath even been unclean till the evening, and doth not eat of the holy things, but hath bathed his flesh ith ater,
and the sun hath gone in, and he hath been clean, and afterards he doth eat of the holy things, for it [is] his food;
a carcase or torn thing he doth not eat, for uncleanness thereby; I [am] Jehovah.
’And they have kept My charge, and bear no sin for it, that they have died for it hen they pollute it; I [am] Jehovah sanctifying them.
’And no stranger doth eat of the holy thing; a settler of a priest and an hireling doth not eat of the holy thing;
and hen a priest buyeth a person, the purchase of his money, he doth eat of it, also one born in his house; they do eat of his bread.
’And a priest’s daughter, hen she is a strange man’s, — she, of the heave-offering of the holy things doth not eat;

and a priest’s daughter, hen she is a ido, or cast out, and hath no seed, and hath turned back unto the house of her father, as [in] her youth, of her father’s bread she doth eat; but no stranger doth eat of it.
’And hen a man doth eat of a holy thing through ignorance, then he hath added its fifth part to it, and hath given [it] to the priest, ith the holy thing;
and they do not pollute the holy things of the sons of Israel — that hich they lift up to Jehovah,
nor have caused them to bear the iniquity of the guilt-offering in their eating their holy things; for I [am] Jehovah, sanctifying them.’
And Jehovah speaketh unto Moses, saying,

’Speak unto Aaron, and unto his sons, and unto all the sons of Israel, and thou hast said unto them, Any man of the house of Israel, or of the sojourners in Israel, ho bringeth near his offering, of all his vos, or of all his illing offerings hich they bring near to Jehovah for a burnt-offering;
at your pleasure a perfect one, a male of the herd, of the sheep or of the goats;
nothing in hich [is] blemish do ye bring near, for it is not for a pleasing thing for you.

’And hen a man bringeth near a sacrifice of peace-offerings to Jehovah, to complete a vo, or for a illing-offering, of the herd or of the flock, it is perfect for a pleasing thing: no blemish is in it;
blind, or broken, or maimed, or having a en, or scurvy, or scabbed — ye do not bring these near to Jehovah, and a fire-offering ye do not make of them on the altar to Jehovah.
’As to an ox or a sheep enlarged or darfed — a illing-offering ye do make it, but for a vo it is not pleasing.
As to a bruised, or beaten, or enlarged, or cut thing — ye do not bring [it] near to Jehovah; even in your land ye do not do it.
And from the hand of a son of a stranger ye do not bring near the bread of your God, of any of these, for their corruption [is] in them; blemish [is] in them; they are not pleasing for you.’
And Jehovah speaketh unto Moses, saying,
’When ox or lamb or goat is born, and it hath been seven days under its dam, then from the eighth day and henceforth, it is pleasing for an offering, a fire-offering to Jehovah;
but an ox or sheep — it and its young one, ye do not slaughter in one day.
’And hen ye sacrifice a sacrifice of thanksgiving to Jehovah, at your pleasure ye do sacrifice,
on that day it is eaten, ye do not leave of it till morning; I [am] Jehovah;
and ye have kept my commands, and have done them; I [am] Jehovah;
and ye do not pollute My holy name, and I have been halloed in the midst of the sons of Israel; I [am] Jehovah, sanctifying you,
ho am bringing you up out of the land of Egypt, to become your God; I [am] Jehovah.’
And Jehovah speaketh unto Moses, saying,
’Speak unto the sons of Israel, and thou hast said unto them, Appointed seasons of Jehovah, hich ye proclaim, holy convocations, [are] these: they [are] My appointed seasons:
six days is ork done, and in the seventh day [is] a sabbath of rest, a holy convocation; ye do no ork; it [is] a sabbath to Jehovah in all your dellings.
’These [are] appointed seasons of Jehovah, holy convocations, hich ye proclaim in their appointed seasons:
in the first month, on the fourteenth of the month, beteen the evenings, [is] the passover to Jehovah;
and on the fifteenth day of this month [is] the feast of unleavened things to Jehovah; seven days unleavened things ye do eat;
on the first day ye have a holy convocation, ye do no servile ork;
and ye have brought near a fire-offering to Jehovah seven days; in the seventh day [is] a holy convocation; ye do no servile ork.’
And Jehovah speaketh unto Moses, saying,

’Speak unto the sons of Israel, and thou hast said unto them, When ye come in unto the land hich I am giving to you, and have reaped its harvest, and have brought in the sheaf, the beginning of your harvest unto the priest,
then he hath aved the sheaf before Jehovah for your acceptance; on the morro of the sabbath doth the priest ave it.
’And ye have prepared in the day of your aving the sheaf a lamb, a perfect one, a son of a year, for a burnt-offering to Jehovah,
and its present to tenth deals of flour mixed ith oil, a fire-offering to Jehovah, a seet fragrance, and its drink-offering, ine, a fourth of the hin.
’And bread and roasted corn and full ears ye do not eat until this self-same day, until your bringing in the offering of your God — a statute age-during to your generations, in all your dellings.
’And ye have numbered to you from the morro of the sabbath, from the day of your bringing in the sheaf of the ave-offering: they are seven perfect sabbaths;
unto the morro of the seventh sabbath ye do number fifty days, and ye have brought near a ne present to Jehovah;
out of your dellings ye bring in bread of a ave-offering, to [loaves], of to tenth deals of flour they are, [ith] yeast they are baken, first -[fruits] to Jehovah.

’And ye have brought near, besides the bread, seven lambs, perfect ones, sons of a year, and one bullock, a son of the herd, and to rams; they are a burnt-offering to Jehovah, ith their present and their libations, a fire-offering of seet fragrance to Jehovah.
’And ye have prepared one kid of the goats for a sin-offering, and to lambs, sons of a year, for a sacrifice of peace-offerings,
and the priest hath aved them, besides the bread of the first -[fruits] — a ave-offering before Jehovah, besides the to lambs; they are holy to Jehovah for the priest;
and ye have proclaimed on this self-same day: a holy convocation is to you, ye do no servile ork — a statute age-during in all your dellings, to your generations.

’And in your reaping the harvest of your land thou dost not complete the corner of thy field in thy reaping, and the gleaning of thy harvest thou dost not gather, to the poor and to the sojourner thou dost leave them; I Jehovah [am] your God.’
And Jehovah speaketh unto Moses, saying,
’Speak unto the sons of Israel, saying, In the seventh month, on the first of the month, ye have a sabbath, a memorial of shouting, a holy convocation;
ye do no servile ork, and ye have brought near a fire-offering to Jehovah.’
And Jehovah speaketh unto Moses, saying,
’Only — on the tenth of this seventh month is a day of atonements; ye have a holy convocation, and ye have humbled yourselves, and have brought near a fire-offering to Jehovah;
and ye do no ork in this self-same day, for it is a day of atonements, to make atonement for you, before Jehovah your God.
’For any person ho is not humbled in this self-same day hath even been cut off from his people;
and any person ho doth any ork in this self-same day I have even destroyed that person from the midst of his people;
ye do no ork — a statute age-during to your generations in all your dellings.
It [is] a sabbath of rest to you, and ye have humbled yourselves in the ninth of the month at even; from evening till evening ye do keep your sabbath.’
And Jehovah speaketh unto Moses, saying,
’Speak unto the sons of Israel, saying, In the fifteenth day of this seventh month [is] a feast of booths seven days to Jehovah;
on the first day [is] a holy convocation, ye do no servile ork,
seven days ye bring near a fire-offering to Jehovah, on the eighth day ye have a holy convocation, and ye have brought near a fire-offering to Jehovah; it [is] a restraint, ye do no servile ork.

’These [are] appointed seasons of Jehovah, hich ye proclaim holy convocations, to bring near a fire-offering to Jehovah, a burnt-offering, and a present, a sacrifice, and libations, a thing of a day in its day,
apart from the sabbaths of Jehovah, and apart from your gifts, and apart from all your vos, and apart from all your illing-offerings, hich ye give to Jehovah.

’Only — in the fifteenth day of the seventh month, in your gathering the increase of the land, ye do keep the feast of Jehovah seven days; on the first day [is] a sabbath, and on the eighth day a sabbath;

and ye have taken to yourselves on the first day the fruit of beautiful trees, branches of palms, and boughs of thick trees, and illos of a brook, and have rejoiced before Jehovah your God seven days.
’And ye have kept it a feast to Jehovah, seven days in a year — a statute age-during to your generations; in the seventh month ye keep it a feast.
’In booths ye dell seven days; all ho are natives in Israel dell in booths,
so that your generations do kno that in booths I caused the sons of Israel to dell; in my bringing them out of the land of Egypt; I, Jehovah, [am] your God.’
And Moses speaketh [concerning] the appointed seasons of Jehovah unto the sons of Israel.
And Jehovah speaketh unto Moses, saying,
’Command the sons of Israel, and they bring unto thee pure olive oil, beaten, for the lamp, to cause a light to go up continually;
at the outside of the vail of the testimony in the tent of meeting doth Aaron arrange it from evening till morning before Jehovah continually — a statute age-during to your generations;
by the pure candlestick he doth arrange the lights before Jehovah continually.
’And thou hast taken flour, and hast baked telve cakes ith it, to tenth deals are in the one cake,
and thou hast set them to ranks (six in the rank) on the pure table before Jehovah,
and thou hast put on the rank pure frankincense, and it hath been to the bread for a memorial, a fire-offering to Jehovah.
’On each sabbath-day he arrangeth it before Jehovah continually, from the sons of Israel — a covenant age-during;
and it hath been to Aaron, and to his sons, and they have eaten it in the holy place, for it [is] most holy to him, from the fire-offerings of Jehovah — a statute age-during.’
And a son of an Israelitish oman goeth out (and he [is] son of an Egyptian man), in the midst of the sons of Israel, and strive in the camp do the son of the Israelitish oman and a man of Israel,
and the son of the Israelitish oman execrateth the Name, and revileth; and they bring him in unto Moses; and his mother’s name [is] Shelomith daughter of Dibri, of the tribe of Dan;
and he causeth him to rest in charge — to explain to them by the mouth of Jehovah.
And Jehovah speaketh unto Moses, saying,
’Bring out the reviler unto the outside of the camp; and all those hearing have laid their hands on his head, and all the company have stoned him.
’And unto the sons of Israel thou dost speak, saying, When any man revileth his God — then he hath borne his sin;
and he ho is execrating the name of Jehovah is certainly put to death; all the company do certainly cast stones at him; as a sojourner so a native, in his execrating the Name, is put to death.
’And hen a man smiteth any soul of man, he is certainly put to death.
’And he ho smiteth a beast repayeth it, body for body.
’And hen a man putteth a blemish in his fello, as he hath done so it is done to him;
breach for breach, eye for eye, tooth for tooth; as he putteth a blemish in a man so it is done in him.
’And he ho smiteth a beast repayeth it, and he ho smiteth [the life of] man is put to death;
one judgment is to you; as a sojourner so is a native; for I [am] Jehovah your God.’
And Moses speaketh unto the sons of Israel, and they bring out the reviler unto the outside of the camp, and stone him ith stones; and the sons of Israel have done as Jehovah hath commanded Moses.
And Jehovah speaketh unto Moses, in mount Sinai, saying,
’Speak unto the sons of Israel, and thou hast said unto them, When ye come in unto the land hich I am giving to you, then hath the land kept a sabbath to Jehovah.
’Six years thou dost so thy field, and six years thou dost prune thy vineyard, and hast gathered its increase,
and in the seventh year a sabbath of rest is to the land, a sabbath to Jehovah; thy field thou dost not so, and thy vineyard thou dost not prune;
the spontaneous groth of thy harvest thou dost not reap, and the grapes of thy separated thing thou dost not gather, a year of rest it is to the land.
’And the sabbath of the land hath been to you for food, to thee, and to thy man-servant, and to thy handmaid, and to thy hireling, and to thy settler, ho are sojourning ith thee;
and to thy cattle, and to the beast hich [is] in thy land, is all thine increase for food.
’And thou hast numbered to thee seven sabbaths of years, seven years seven times, and the days of the seven sabbaths of years have been to thee nine and forty years,
and thou hast caused a trumpet of shouting to pass over in the seventh month, in the tenth of the month; in the day of the atonements ye do cause a trumpet to pass over through all your land;

and ye have halloed the year, the fiftieth year; and ye have proclaimed liberty in the land to all its inhabitants; a jubilee it is to you; and ye have turned back each unto his possession; yea, each unto his family ye do turn back.
’A jubilee it [is], the fiftieth year, a year it is to you; ye so not, nor reap its spontaneous groth, nor gather its separated things;
for a jubilee it [is], holy it is to you; out of the field ye eat its increase;
in the year of this jubilee ye turn back each unto his possession.
’And hen thou sellest anything to thy fello, or buyest from the hand of thy fello, ye do not oppress one another;
by the number of years after the jubilee thou dost buy from thy fello; by the number of the years of increase he doth sell to thee;
according to the multitude of the years thou dost multiply its price, and according to the feness of the years thou dost diminish its price; for a number of increases he is selling to thee;
and ye do not oppress one another, and thou hast been afraid of thy God; for I [am] Jehovah your God.
’And ye have done My statutes, and My judgments ye keep, and have done them, and ye have delt on the land confidently,
and the land hath given its fruit, and ye have eaten to satiety, and have delt confidently on it.
’And hen ye say, What do e eat in the seventh year, lo, e do not so, nor gather our increase?
then I have commanded My blessing on you in the sixth year, and it hath made the increase for three years;
and ye have son the eighth year, and have eaten of the old increase; until the ninth year, until the coming in of its increase, ye do eat the old.
’And the land is not sold — to extinction, for the land [is] Mine, for sojourners and settlers [are] ye ith Me;
and in all the land of your possession a redemption ye do give to the land.
’When thy brother becometh poor, and hath sold his possession, then hath his redeemer ho is near unto him come, and he hath redeemed the sold thing of his brother;
and hen a man hath no redeemer, and his on hand hath attained, and he hath found as sufficient [for] its redemption,
then he hath reckoned the years of its sale, and hath given back that hich is over to the man to hom he sold [it], and he hath returned to his possession.

’And if his hand hath not found sufficiency to give back to him, then hath his sold thing been in the hand of him ho buyeth it till the year of jubilee; and it hath gone out in the jubilee, and he hath returned to his possession.
’And hen a man selleth a delling-house [in] a alled city, then hath his right of redemption been until the completion of a year from its selling; days — is his right of redemption;

and if it is not redeemed until the fulness to him of a perfect year, then hath the house hich [is] in a alled city been established to extinction to the buyer of it, to his generations; it goeth not out in the jubilee;
and a house of the villages hich have no all round about, on the field of the country is reckoned; redemption is to it, and in the jubilee it goeth out.
’As to cities of the Levites — houses of the cities of their possession — redemption age-during is to the Levites;

as to him ho redeemeth from the Levites, both the sale of a house and the city of his possession have gone out in the jubilee, for the houses of the cities of the Levites are their possession in the midst of the sons of Israel.
And a field, a suburb of their cities, is not sold; for a possession age-during it [is] to them.
