Observe, and thou hast obeyed all these ords hich I am commanding thee, in order that it may be ell ith thee and ith thy sons after thee — to the age, hen thou dost that hich [is] good and right in the eyes of Jehovah thy God.
’When Jehovah thy God doth cut off the nations — hither thou art going in to possess them — from thy presence, and thou hast possessed them, and hast delt in their land —

take heed to thee, lest thou be snared after them, after their being destroyed out of thy presence, and lest thou enquire about their gods, saying, Ho do these nations serve their gods, and I do so — even I?
’Thou dost not do so to Jehovah thy God; for every abomination of Jehovah hich He is hating they have done to their gods, for even their sons and their daughters they burn ith fire to their gods.
The hole thing hich I am commanding you — it ye observe to do; thou dost not add unto it, nor diminish from it.
’When there ariseth in your midst a prophet, or a dreamer of a dream, and he hath given unto thee a sign or onder,
and the sign and the onder hath come hich he hath spoken of unto thee, saying, Let us go after other gods (hich thou hast not knon), and serve them,

thou dost not hearken unto the ords of that prophet, or unto that dreamer of the dream, for Jehovah your God is trying you, to kno hether ye are loving Jehovah your God ith all your heart, and ith all your soul;
after Jehovah your God ye alk, and Him ye fear, and His commands ye keep, and to His voice ye hearken, and Him ye serve, and to Him ye cleave.

’And that prophet, or that dreamer of the dream, is put to death, for he hath spoken apostasy against Jehovah your God (ho is bringing you out of the land of Egypt, and hath ransomed you out of a house of servants), to drive you out of the ay in hich Jehovah thy God hath commanded thee to alk, and thou hast put aay the evil thing from thy midst.

’When thy brother — son of thy mother, or thy son, or thy daughter, or the ife of thy bosom, or thy friend ho [is] as thine on soul — doth move thee, in secret, saying, Let us go and serve other gods — (hich thou hast not knon, thou and thy fathers,
of the gods of the peoples ho [are] round about you, ho are near unto thee, or ho are far off from thee, from the end of the earth even unto the end of the earth) —
thou dost not consent to him, nor hearken unto him, nor doth thine eye have pity on him, nor dost thou spare, nor dost thou cover him over.
’But thou dost surely kill him; thy hand is on him, in the first place, to put him to death, and the hand of all the people last;
and thou hast stoned him ith stones, and he hath died, for he hath sought to drive thee aay from Jehovah thy God, ho is bringing thee out of the land of Egypt, out of a house of servants;
and all Israel do hear and fear, and add not to do like this evil thing in thy midst.
’When thou hearest, in one of thy cities hich Jehovah thy God is giving to thee to dell there, [one] saying,
Men, sons of orthlessness, have gone out of thy midst, and they force aay the inhabitants of their city, saying, Let us go and serve other gods, hich ye have not knon —
and thou hast enquired, and searched, and asked diligently, and lo, truth; the thing is established; this abomination hath been done in thy midst:
’Thou dost surely smite the inhabitants of that city by the mouth of the sord; devoting it, and all that [is] in it, even its cattle, by the mouth of the sord;

and all its spoil thou dost gather unto the midst of its broad place, and hast burned ith fire the city and all its spoil completely, before Jehovah thy God, and it hath been a heap age-during, it is not built any more;

and there doth not cleave to thy hand any of the devoted thing, so that Jehovah doth turn back from the fierceness of His anger, and hath given to thee mercies, and loved thee, and multiplied thee, as He hath sorn to thy fathers,
hen thou dost hearken to the voice of Jehovah thy God, to keep all his commands hich I am commanding thee to-day, to do that hich [is] right in the eyes of Jehovah thy God.
’Sons ye [are] to Jehovah your God; ye do not cut yourselves, nor make baldness beteen your eyes for the dead;
for a holy people [art] thou to Jehovah thy God, and on thee hath Jehovah fixed to be to Him for a people, a peculiar treasure, out of all the peoples ho [are] on the face of the ground.
’Thou dost not eat any abominable thing;
’this [is] the beast hich ye do eat: ox, lamb of the sheep, or kid of the goats,
hart, and roe, and fallo deer, and ild goat, and pygarg, and ild ox, and chamois;
and every beast dividing the hoof, and cleaving the cleft into to hoofs, bringing up the cud, among the beasts — it ye do eat.

’Only, this ye do not eat, of those bringing up the cud, and of those dividing the cloven hoof: the camel, and the hare, and the rabbit, for they are bringing up the cud but the hoof have not divided; unclean they [are] to you;
and the so, for it is dividing the hoof, and not [bringing] up the cud, unclean it [is] to you; of their flesh ye do not eat, and against their carcase ye do not come.
’This ye do eat of all that [are] in the aters; all that hath fins and scales ye do eat;
and anything hich hath not fins and scales ye do not eat; unclean it [is] to you.
’Any clean bird ye do eat;
and these [are] they of hich ye do not eat: the eagle, and the ossifrage, and the ospray,
and the glede, and the kite, and the vulture after its kind,
and every raven after its kind;
and the ol, and the night-hak, and the cuckoo, and the hak after its kind;
the [little] ol, and the [great] ol, and the san,
and the pelican, and the gier-eagle, and the cormorant,
and the stork, and the heron after its kind, and the laping, and the bat;
and every teeming thing hich is flying, unclean it [is] to you; they are not eaten;
any clean fol ye do eat.

’Ye do not eat of any carcase; to the sojourner ho [is] ithin thy gates thou dost give it, and he hath eaten it; or sell [it] to a stranger; for a holy people thou [art] to Jehovah thy God; thou dost not boil a kid in its mother’s milk.
’Thou dost certainly tithe all the increase of thy seed hich the field is bringing forth year by year;

and thou hast eaten before Jehovah thy God, in the place here He doth choose to cause His name to tabernacle, the tithe of thy corn, of thy ne ine, and of thine oil, and the firstlings of thy herd, and of thy flock, so that thou dost learn to fear Jehovah thy God all the days.

’And hen the ay is too much for thee, that thou art not able to carry it — hen the place is too far off from thee hich Jehovah thy God doth choose to put His name there, hen Jehovah thy God doth bless thee; —
then thou hast given [it] in money, and hast bound up the money in thy hand, and gone unto the place on hich Jehovah thy God doth fix;

and thou hast given the money for any thing hich thy soul desireth, for oxen, and for sheep, and for ine, and for strong drink, and for any thing hich thy soul asketh, and thou hast eaten there before Jehovah thy God, and thou hast rejoiced, thou and thy house.
As to the Levite ho [is] ithin thy gates, thou dost not forsake him, for he hath no portion and inheritance ith thee.
’At the end of three years thou dost bring out all the tithe of thine increase in that year, and hast placed [it] ithin thy gates;

and come in hath the Levite (for he hath no part and inheritance ith thee), and the sojourner, and the fatherless, and the ido, ho [are] ithin thy gates, and they have eaten, and been satisfied, so that Jehovah thy God doth bless thee in all the ork of thy hand hich thou dost.
’At the end of seven years thou dost make a release,

and this [is] the matter of the release: Every oner of a loan [is] to release his hand hich he doth lift up against his neighbour, he doth not exact of his neighbour and of his brother, but hath proclaimed a release to Jehovah;
of the stranger thou mayest exact, and that hich is thine ith thy brother doth thy hand release;
only hen there is no needy one ith thee, for Jehovah doth greatly bless thee in the land hich Jehovah thy God is giving to thee — an inheritance to possess it.
’Only, if thou dost diligently hearken to the voice of Jehovah thy God, to observe to do all this command hich I am commanding thee to-day,

for Jehovah thy God hath blessed thee as He hath spoken to thee; and thou hast lent [to] many nations, and thou hast not borroed; and thou hast ruled over many nations, and over thee they do not rule.

’When there is ith thee any needy one of one of thy brethren, in one of thy cities, in thy land hich Jehovah thy God is giving to thee, thou dost not harden thy heart, nor shut thy hand from thy needy brother;
for thou dost certainly open thy hand to him, and dost certainly lend him sufficient for his lack hich he lacketh.

’Take heed to thee lest there be a ord in thy heart — orthless, saying, Near [is] the seventh year, the year of release; and thine eye is evil against thy needy brother, and thou dost not give to him, and he hath called concerning thee unto Jehovah, and it hath been in thee sin;
thou dost certainly give to him, and thy heart is not sad in thy giving to him, for because of this thing doth Jehovah thy God bless thee in all thy orks, and in every putting forth of thy hand;
because the needy one doth not cease out of the land, therefore I am commanding thee, saying, Thou dost certainly open thy hand to thy brother, to thy poor, and to thy needy one, in thy land.
’When thy brother is sold to thee, a Hebre or a Hebreess, and he hath served thee six years — then in the seventh year thou dost send him aay free from thee.
And hen thou dost send him aay free from thee, thou dost not send him aay empty;
thou dost certainly encircle him out of thy flock, and out of thy threshing-floor, and out of thy ine-vat; [of] that hich Jehovah thy God hath blessed thee thou dost give to him,
and thou hast remembered that a servant thou hast been in the land of Egypt, and Jehovah thy God doth ransom thee; therefore I am commanding thee this thing to-day.
’And it hath been, hen he saith unto thee, I go not out from thee — because he hath loved thee, and thy house, because [it is] good for him ith thee —
then thou hast taken the al, and hast put [it] through his ear, and through the door, and he hath been to thee a servant age-during; and also to thy handmaid thou dost do so.

’It is not hard in thine eyes, in thy sending him aay free from thee; for the double of the hire of an hireling he hath served thee six years, and Jehovah thy God hath blessed thee in all that thou dost.
’Every firstling that is born in thy herd and in thy flock — the male thou dost sanctify to Jehovah thy God; thou dost not ork ith the firstling of thine ox, nor shear the firstling of thy flock;
before Jehovah thy God thou dost eat it year by year, in the place hich Jehovah doth choose, thou and thy house.
’And hen there is in it a blemish, lame, or blind, any evil blemish, thou dost not sacrifice it to Jehovah thy God;
ithin thy gates thou dost eat it, the unclean and the clean alike, as the roe, and as the hart.
Only, its blood thou dost not eat; on the earth thou dost pour it as ater.
’Observe the month of Abib — and thou hast made a passover to Jehovah thy God, for in the month of Abib hath Jehovah thy God brought thee out of Egypt by night;
and thou hast sacrificed a passover to Jehovah thy God, of the flock, and of the herd, in the place hich Jehovah doth choose to cause His name to tabernacle there.

’Thou dost not eat ith it any fermented thing, seven days thou dost eat ith it unleavened things, bread of affliction; for in haste thou hast come out of the land of Egypt; so that thou dost remember the day of thy coming out of the land of Egypt all days of thy life;
and there is not seen ith thee leaven in all thy border seven days, and there doth not remain of the flesh hich thou dost sacrifice at evening on the first day till morning.
’Thou art not able to sacrifice the passover ithin any of thy gates hich Jehovah thy God is giving to thee,

except at the place hich Jehovah thy God doth choose to cause His name to tabernacle — there thou dost sacrifice the passover in the evening, at the going in of the sun, the season of thy coming out of Egypt;
and thou hast cooked and eaten in the place on hich Jehovah thy God doth fix, and hast turned in the morning, and gone to thy tents;
six days thou dost eat unleavened things, and on the seventh day [is] a restraint to Jehovah thy God; thou dost do no ork.
’Seven eeks thou dost number to thee; from the beginning of the sickle among the standing corn thou dost begin to number seven eeks,
and thou hast made the feast of eeks to Jehovah thy God, a tribute of a free-ill offering of thy hand, hich thou dost give, as Jehovah thy God doth bless thee.

And thou hast rejoiced before Jehovah thy God, thou, and thy son, and thy daughter, and thy man-servant, and thy handmaid, and the Levite ho [is] ithin thy gates, and the sojourner, and the fatherless, and the ido, ho [are] in thy midst, in the place hich Jehovah thy God doth choose to cause His name to tabernacle there,
and thou hast remembered that a servant thou hast been in Egypt, and hast observed and done these statutes.
’The feast of booths thou dost make for thee seven days, in thine in-gathering of thy threshing-floor, and of thy ine-vat;

and thou hast rejoiced in thy feast, thou, and thy son, and thy daughter, and thy man-servant, and thy handmaid, and the Levite, and the sojourner, and the fatherless, and the ido, ho [are] ithin thy gates.

Seven days thou dost feast before Jehovah thy God, in the place hich Jehovah doth choose, for Jehovah thy God doth bless thee in all thine increase, and in every ork of thy hands, and thou hast been only rejoicing.

’Three times in a year doth every one of thy males appear before Jehovah thy God in the place hich He doth choose — in the feast of unleavened things, and in the feast of eeks, and in the feast of booths; and they do not appear before Jehovah empty;
each according to the gift of his hand, according to the blessing of Jehovah thy God, hich He hath given to thee.
’Judges and authorities thou dost make to thee ithin all thy gates hich Jehovah thy God is giving to thee, for thy tribes; and they have judged the people — a righteous judgment.
Thou dost not turn aside judgment; thou dost not discern faces, nor take a bribe, for the bribe blindeth the eyes of the ise, and perverteth the ords of the righteous.
Righteousness — righteousness thou dost pursue, so that thou livest, and hast possessed the land hich Jehovah thy God is giving to thee.
’Thou dost not plant for thee a shrine of any trees near the altar of Jehovah thy God, hich thou makest for thyself,
and thou dost not raise up to thee any standing image hich Jehovah thy God is hating.
’Thou dost not sacrifice to Jehovah thy God ox or sheep in hich there is a blemish — any evil thing; for it [is] the abomination of Jehovah thy God.
’When there is found in thy midst, in one of thy cities hich Jehovah thy God is giving to thee, a man or a oman ho doth the evil thing in the eyes of Jehovah thy God by transgressing His covenant,
and he doth go and serve other gods, and doth bo himself to them, and to the sun, or to the moon, or to any of the host of the heavens, hich I have not commanded —
and it hath been declared to thee, and thou hast heard, and hast searched diligently, and lo, truth; the thing is established; this abomination hath been done in Israel —
’Then thou hast brought out that man, or that oman, ho hath done this evil thing, unto thy gates — the man or the oman — and thou hast stoned them ith stones, and they have died.
By the mouth of to itnesses or of three itnesses is he ho is dead put to death; he is not put to death by the mouth of one itness;
the hand of the itnesses is on him, in the first place, to put him to death, and the hand of all the people last; and thou hast put aay the evil thing out of thy midst.

’When anything is too hard for thee for judgment, beteen blood and blood, beteen plea and plea, and beteen stroke and stroke — matters of strife ithin thy gates — then thou hast risen, and gone up unto the place on hich Jehovah thy God doth fix,
and hast come in unto the priests, the Levites, and unto the judge ho is in those days, and hast inquired, and they have declared to thee the ord of judgment,
and thou hast done according to the tenor of the ord hich they declare to thee ([they] of that place hich Jehovah doth choose; and thou hast observed to do according to all that they direct thee.

’According to the tenor of the la hich they direct thee, and according to the judgment hich they say to thee thou dost do; thou dost not turn aside from the ord hich they declare to thee, right or left.

And the man ho acteth ith presumption, so as not to hearken unto the priest (ho is standing to serve there Jehovah thy God), or unto the judge, even that man hath died, and thou hast put aay the evil thing from Israel,
and all the people do hear and fear, and do not presume any more.

’When thou comest in unto the land hich Jehovah thy God is giving to thee, and hast possessed it, and delt in it, and thou hast said, Let me set over me a king like all the nations hich [are] round about me, —
thou dost certainly set over thee a king on hom Jehovah doth fix; from the midst of thy brethren thou dost set over thee a king; thou art not able to set over thee a stranger, ho is not thy brother.
’Only, he doth not multiply to himself horses, nor cause the people to turn back to Egypt, so as to multiply horses, seeing Jehovah hath said to you, Ye do not add to turn back in this ay any more.
And he doth not multiply to himself ives, and his heart doth not turn aside, and silver and gold he doth not multiply to himself — exceedingly.
’And it hath been, hen he sitteth on the throne of his kingdom, that he hath ritten for himself the copy of this la, on a book, from [that] before the priests the Levites,
and it hath been ith him, and he hath read in it all days of his life, so that he doth learn to fear Jehovah his God, to keep all the ords of this la, and these statutes, to do them;
so that his heart is not high above his brethren, and so as not to turn aside from the command, right or left, so that he prolongeth days over his kingdom, he and his sons, in the midst of Israel.
’There is not to the priests the Levites — all the tribe of Levi — a portion and inheritance ith Israel; fire-offerings of Jehovah, even His inheritance, they eat,
and he hath no inheritance in the midst of his brethren; Jehovah Himself [is] his inheritance, as He hath spoken to him.
’And this is the priest’s right from the people, from those sacrificing a sacrifice, hether ox or sheep, he hath even given to the priest the leg, and the to cheeks, and the stomach;
the first of thy corn, of thy ne ine, and of thine oil, and the first of the fleece of thy flock, thou dost give to him;
for on him hath Jehovah thy God fixed, out of all thy tribes, to stand to serve in the name of Jehovah, He and his sons continually.
’And hen the Levite cometh from one of thy cities out of all Israel, here he hath sojourned, and hath come ith all the desire of his soul unto the place hich Jehovah doth choose,
then he hath ministered in the name of Jehovah his God, like all his brethren, the Levites, ho are standing there before Jehovah,
portion as portion they do eat, apart from his sold things, ith the fathers.
’When thou art coming in unto the land hich Jehovah thy God is giving to thee, thou dost not learn to do according to the abominations of those nations:
there is not found in thee one causing his son and his daughter to pass over into fire, a user of divinations, an observer of clouds, and an enchanter, and a sorcerer,
and a charmer, and one asking at a familiar spirit, and a izard, and one seeking unto the dead.
’For the abomination of Jehovah [is] every one doing these, and because of these abominations is Jehovah thy God dispossessing them from thy presence.
Perfect thou art ith Jehovah thy God,
for these nations hom thou art possessing, unto observers of clouds, and unto diviners, do hearken; and thou — not so hath Jehovah thy God suffered thee.
’A prophet out of thy midst, out of thy brethren, like to me, doth Jehovah thy God raise up to thee — unto him ye hearken;

according to all that thou didst ask from Jehovah thy God, in Horeb, in the day of the assembly, saying, Let me not add to hear the voice of Jehovah my God, and this great fire let me not see any more, and I die not;
and Jehovah saith unto me, They have done ell that they have spoken;
a prophet I raise up to them, out of the midst of their brethren, like to thee; and I have given my ords in his mouth, and he hath spoken unto them all that hich I command him;
and it hath been — the man ho doth not hearken unto My ords hich he doth speak in My name, I require [it] of him.
’Only, the prophet ho presumeth to speak a ord in My name — that hich I have not commanded him to speak — and ho speaketh in the name of other gods — even that prophet hath died.
’And hen thou sayest in thy heart, Ho do e kno the ord hich Jehovah hath not spoken? —

that hich the prophet speaketh in the name of Jehovah, and the thing is not, and cometh not — it [is] the ord hich Jehovah hath not spoken; in presumption hath the prophet spoken it; — thou art not afraid of him.
’When Jehovah thy God doth cut off the nations, hose land Jehovah thy God is giving to thee, and thou hast succeeded them, and delt in their cities, and in their houses,
three cities thou dost separate for thee in the midst of thy land hich Jehovah thy God is giving to thee to possess it.

Thou dost prepare for thee the ay, and hast divided into three parts the border of thy land hich Jehovah thy God doth cause thee to inherit, and it hath been for the fleeing thither of every man-slayer.
’And this [is] the matter of the man-slayer ho fleeth thither, and hath lived: He ho smiteth his neighbour unknoingly, and is not hating him heretofore,

even he ho cometh in ith his neighbour into a forest to he ood, and his hand hath driven ith an axe to cut the tree, and the iron hath slipped from the ood, and hath met his neighbour, and he hath died — he doth flee unto one of these cities, and hath lived,

lest the redeemer of blood pursue after the man-slayer hen his heart is hot, and hath overtaken him (because the ay is great), and hath smitten him — the life, and he hath no sentence of death, for he is not hating him heretofore;
therefore I am commanding thee, saying, Three cities thou dost separate to thee.
’And if Jehovah thy God doth enlarge thy border, as He hath sorn to thy fathers, and hath given to thee all the land hich He hath spoken to give to thy fathers —

hen thou keepest all this command to do it, hich I am commanding thee to-day, to love Jehovah thy God, and to alk in His ays all the days — then thou hast added to thee yet three cities to these three;
and innocent blood is not shed in the midst of thy land hich Jehovah thy God is giving to thee — an inheritance, and there hath been upon thee blood.
’And hen a man is hating his neighbour, and hath lain in ait for him, and risen against him, and smitten him — the life, and he hath died, and he hath fled unto one of these cities,
then the elders of his city have sent and taken him from thence, and given him into the hand of the redeemer of blood, and he hath died;
thine eye hath no pity on him, and thou hast put aay the innocent blood from Israel, and it is ell ith thee.
’Thou dost not remove a border of thy neighbour, hich they of former times have made, in thine inheritance, hich thou dost inherit in the land hich Jehovah thy God is giving to thee to possess it.
’One itness doth not rise against a man for any iniquity, and for any sin, in any sin hich he sinneth; by the mouth of to itnesses, or by the mouth of three itnesses, is a thing established.
’When a violent itness doth rise against a man, to testify against him apostasy,
then have both the men ho have the strife stood before Jehovah, before the priests and the judges ho are in those days,
and the judges have searched diligently, and lo, the itness [is] a false itness, a falsehood he hath testified against his brother:
’Then ye have done to him as he devised to do to his brother, and thou hast put aay the evil thing out of thy midst,
and those ho are left do hear and fear, and add not to do any more according to this evil thing in thy midst;
and thine eye doth not pity — life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.

’When thou goest out to battle against thine enemy, and hast seen horse and chariot — a people more numerous than thou — thou art not afraid of them, for Jehovah thy God [is] ith thee, ho is bringing thee up out of the land of Egypt;
and it hath been, in your draing near unto the battle, that the priest hath come nigh, and spoken unto the people,
and said unto them, Hear, Israel, ye are draing near to-day to battle against your enemies, let not your hearts be tender, fear not, nor make haste, nor be terrified at their presence,
for Jehovah your God [is] He ho is going ith you, to fight for you ith your enemies — to save you.

’And the authorities have spoken unto the people, saying, Who [is] the man that hath built a ne house, and hath not dedicated it? — let him go and turn back to his house, lest he die in battle, and another man dedicate it.
’And ho [is] the man that hath planted a vineyard, and hath not made it common? — let him go and turn back to his house, lest he die in battle, and another man make it common.
’And ho [is] the man that hath betrothed a oman, and hath not taken her? — let him go and turn back to his house, lest he die in battle, and another man take her.

’And the authorities have added to speak unto the people, and said, Who [is] the man that is afraid and tender of heart? — let him go and turn back to his house, and the heart of his brethren doth not melt like his heart;
and it hath come to pass as the authorities finish to speak unto the people, that they have appointed princes of the hosts at the head of the people.
’When thou draest near unto a city to fight against it, then thou hast called unto it for Peace,
and it hath been, if Peace it anser thee, and hath opened to thee, then it hath come to pass — all the people ho are found in it are to thee for tributaries, and have served thee.
’And if it doth not make peace ith thee, and hath made ith thee ar, then thou hast laid siege against it,
and Jehovah thy God hath given it into thy hand, and thou hast smitten every male of it by the mouth of the sord.

Only, the omen, and the infants, and the cattle, and all that is in the city, all its spoil, thou dost seize for thyself, and thou hast eaten the spoil of thine enemies hich Jehovah thy God hath given to thee.
So thou dost do to all the cities hich are very far off from thee, hich are not of the cities of these nations.
’Only, of the cities of these peoples hich Jehovah thy God is giving to thee [for] an inheritance, thou dost not keep alive any breathing;
for thou dost certainly devote the Hittite, and the Amorite, the Canaanite, and the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite, as Jehovah thy God hath commanded thee,
so that they teach you not to do according to all their abominations hich they have done to their gods, and ye have sinned against Jehovah your God.

’When thou layest siege unto a city many days, to fight against it, to capture it, thou dost not destroy its trees to force an axe against them, for of them thou dost eat, and them thou dost not cut don — for man’s [is] the tree of the field — to go in at thy presence in the siege.
Only, the tree, hich thou knoest that it [is] not a fruit-tree, it thou dost destroy, and hast cut don, and hast built a bulark against the city hich is making ith thee ar till thou hast subdued it.
’When one is found slain on the ground hich Jehovah thy God is giving to thee to possess it — fallen in a field — it is not knon ho hath smitten him,
then have thine elders and thy judges gone out and measured unto the cities hich [are] round about the slain one,
and it hath been, the city hich [is] near unto the slain one, even the elders of that city have taken a heifer of the herd, hich hath not been rought ith, hich hath not dran in the yoke,
and the elders of that city have brought don the heifer unto a hard valley, hich is not tilled nor son, and have beheaded there the heifer in the valley.
’And the priests, sons of Levi, have come nigh — for on them hath Jehovah thy God fixed to serve Him, and to bless in the name of Jehovah, and by their mouth is every strife, and every stroke —
and all the elders of that city, ho are near unto the slain one, do ash their hands over the heifer hich is beheaded in the valley,
and they have ansered and said, Our hands have not shed this blood, and our eyes have not seen —
receive atonement for Thy people Israel, hom Thou hast ransomed, O Jehovah, and suffer not innocent blood in the midst of Thy people Israel; and the blood hath been pardoned to them,
and thou dost put aay the innocent blood out of thy midst, for thou dost that hich [is] right in the eyes of Jehovah.
’When thou goest out to battle against thine enemies, and Jehovah thy God hath given them into thy hand, and thou hast taken captive its captivity,
and hast seen in the captivity a oman of fair form, and hast delighted in her, and hast taken to thee for a ife,
then thou hast brought her in unto the midst of thy household, and she hath shaved her head, and prepared her nails,

and turned aside the raiment of her captivity from off her, and hath delt in thy house, and beailed her father and her mother a month of days, and afterards thou dost go in unto her and hast married her, and she hath been to thee for a ife:

’And it hath been — if thou hast not delighted in her, that thou hast sent her aay at her desire, and thou dost not at all sell her for money; thou dost not tyrannize over her, because that thou hast humbled her.
’When a man hath to ives, the one loved and the other hated, and they have borne to him sons (the loved one and the hated one), and the first-born son hath been to the hated one;

then it hath been, in the day of his causing his sons to inherit that hich he hath, he is not able to declare first-born the son of the loved one, in the face of the son of the hated one — the first-born.

But the first-born, son of the hated one, he doth acknoledge, to give to him a double portion of all that is found ith him, for he [is] the beginning of his strength; to him [is] the right of the first-born.
’When a man hath a son apostatizing and rebellious — he is not hearkening to the voice of his father, and to the voice of his mother, and they have chastised him, and he doth not hearken unto them —
then laid hold on him have his father and his mother, and they have brought him out unto the elders of his city, and unto the gate of his place,
and have said unto the elders of his city, Our son — this one — is apostatizing and rebellious; he is not hearkening to our voice — a glutton and drunkard;
and all the men of his city have stoned him ith stones, and he hath died, and thou hast put aay the evil out of thy midst, and all Israel do hear and fear.
’And hen there is in a man a sin — a cause of death, and he hath been put to death, and thou hast hanged him on a tree,

his corpse doth not remain on the tree, for thou dost certainly bury him in that day — for a thing lightly esteemed of God [is] the hanged one — and thou dost not defile thy ground hich Jehovah thy God is giving to thee — an inheritance.
’Thou dost not see the ox of thy brother or his sheep driven aay, and hast hidden thyself from them, thou dost certainly turn them back to thy brother;

and if thy brother [is] not near unto thee, and thou hast not knon him, then thou hast removed it unto the midst of thy house, and it hath been ith thee till thy brother seek it, and thou hast given it back to him;
and so thou dost to his ass, and so thou dost to his garment, and so thou dost to any lost thing of thy brother’s, hich is lost by him, and thou hast found it; thou art not able to hide thyself.
’Thou dost not see the ass of thy brother, or his ox, falling in the ay, and hast hid thyself from them; thou dost certainly raise [them] up ith him.
’The habiliments of a man are not on a oman, nor doth a man put on the garment of a oman, for the abomination of Jehovah thy God [is] any one doing these.
’When a bird’s nest cometh before thee in the ay, in any tree, or on the earth, brood or eggs, and the mother sitting on the brood or on the eggs, thou dost not take the mother ith the young ones;
thou dost certainly send aay the mother, and the young ones dost take to thyself, so that it is ell ith thee, and thou hast prolonged days.
’When thou buildest a ne house, then thou hast made a parapet to thy roof, and thou dost not put blood on thy house hen one falleth from it.
’Thou dost not so thy vineyard [ith] divers things, lest the fulness of the seed hich thou dost so, and the increase of the vineyard, be separated.
’Thou dost not plo ith an ox and ith an ass together.
’Thou dost not put on a mixed cloth, ool and linen together.
’Fringes thou dost make to thee on the four skirts of thy covering ith hich thou dost cover [thyself].
’When a man taketh a ife, and hath gone in unto her, and hated her,
and laid against her actions of ords, and brought out against her an evil name, and said, This oman I have taken, and I dra near unto her, and I have not found in her tokens of virginity:
’Then hath the father of the damsel — and her mother — taken and brought out the tokens of virginity of the damsel unto the elders of the city in the gate,
and the father of the damsel hath said unto the elders, My daughter I have given to this man for a ife, and he doth hate her;

and lo, he hath laid actions of ords, saying, I have not found to thy daughter tokens of virginity — and these [are] the tokens of the virginity of my daughter! and they have spread out the garment before the elders of the city.
’And the elders of that city have taken the man, and chastise him,

and fined him a hundred silverlings, and given to the father of the damsel, because he hath brought out an evil name on a virgin of Israel, and she is to him for a ife, he is not able to send her aay all his days.
’And if this thing hath been truth — tokens of virginity have not been found for the damsel —

then they have brought out the damsel unto the opening of her father’s house, and stoned her have the men of her city ith stones, and she hath died, for she hath done folly in Israel, to go a-horing [in] her father’s house; and thou hast put aay the evil thing out of thy midst.

’When a man is found lying ith a oman, married to a husband, then they have died even both of them, the man ho is lying ith the oman, also the oman; and thou hast put aay the evil thing out of Israel.
’When there is a damsel, a virgin, betrothed to a man, and a man hath found her in a city, and lain ith her;

then ye have brought them both out unto the gate of that city, and stoned them ith stones, and they have died: — the damsel, because that she hath not cried, [being] in a city; and the man, because that he hath humbled his neighbour’s ife; and thou hast put aay the evil thing out of thy midst.
’And if in a field the man find the damsel ho is betrothed, and the man hath laid hold on her, and lain ith her, then hath the man ho hath lain ith her died alone;
and to the damsel thou dost not do anything, the damsel hath no deadly sin; for as a man riseth against his neighbour and hath murdered him — the life, so [is] this thing;
for in a field he found her, she hath cried — the damsel ho is betrothed — and she hath no saviour.
’When a man findeth a damsel, a virgin ho is not betrothed, and hath caught her, and lain ith her, and they have been found,
then hath the man ho is lying ith her given to the father of the damsel fifty silverlings, and to him she is for a ife; because that he hath humbled her, he is not able to send her aay all his days.
’A man doth not take his father’s ife, nor uncover his father’s skirt.
’One ounded, bruised, or cut in the member doth not enter into the assembly of Jehovah;
a bastard doth not enter into the assembly of Jehovah; even a tenth generation of him doth not enter into the assembly of Jehovah.
’An Ammonite and a Moabite doth not enter into the assembly of Jehovah; even a tenth generation of them doth not enter into the assembly of Jehovah — to the age;

because that they have not come before you ith bread and ith ater in the ay, in your coming out from Egypt, and because he hath hired against thee Balaam son of Beor, of Pethor of Aram-Naharaim, to revile thee;
and Jehovah thy God hath not been illing to hearken unto Balaam, and Jehovah thy God doth turn for thee the reviling to a blessing, because Jehovah thy God hath loved thee;
thou dost not seek their peace and their good all thy days — to the age.
’Thou dost not abominate an Edomite, for thy brother he [is]; thou dost not abominate an Egyptian, for a sojourner thou hast been in his land;
sons ho are begotten of them, a third generation of them, doth enter into the assembly of Jehovah.
’When a camp goeth out against thine enemies, then thou hast kept from every evil thing.
’When there is in thee a man ho is not clean, from an accident at night — then he hath gone out unto the outside of the camp — he doth not come in unto the midst of the camp —
and it hath been, at the turning of the evening, he doth bathe ith ater, and at the going in of the sun he doth come in unto the midst of the camp.
’And a station thou hast at the outside of the camp, and thou hast gone out thither ithout,
and a nail thou hast on thy staff, and it hath been, in thy sitting ithout, that thou hast digged ith it, and turned back, and covered thy filth;

for Jehovah thy God is alking up and don in the midst of thy camp, to deliver thee, and to give thine enemies before thee, and thy camp hath been holy, and He doth not see in thee the nakedness of anything, and hath turned back from after thee.
’Thou dost not shut up a servant unto his lord, ho is delivered unto thee from his lord;
ith thee he doth dell, in thy midst, in the place hich he chooseth ithin one of thy gates, here it is pleasing to him; thou dost not oppress him.
’There is not a hore among the daughters of Israel, nor is there a horemonger among the sons of Israel;
thou dost not bring a gift of a hore, or a price of a dog, into the house of Jehovah thy God, for any vo; for the abomination of Jehovah thy God [are] even both of them.
’Thou dost not lend in usury to thy brother; usury of money, usury of food, usury of anything hich is lent on usury.

To a stranger thou mayest lend in usury, and to thy brother thou dost not lend in usury, so that Jehovah thy God doth bless thee in every putting forth of thy hand on the land hither thou goest in to possess it.
’When thou voest a vo to Jehovah thy God, thou dost not delay to complete it; for Jehovah thy God doth certainly require it from thee, and it hath been in thee — sin.
’And hen thou forbearest to vo, it is not in thee a sin.
The produce of thy lips thou dost keep, and hast done [it], as thou hast voed to Jehovah thy God; a free-ill-offering, hich thou hast spoken ith thy mouth.
’When thou comest in unto the vineyard of thy neighbour, then thou hast eaten grapes, according to thy desire, thy sufficiency; but into thy vessel thou dost not put [any].
When thou comest in among the standing-corn of thy neighbour, then thou hast plucked the ears ith thy hand, but a sickle thou dost not ave over the standing-corn of thy neighbour.

’When a man doth take a ife, and hath married her, and it hath been, if she doth not find grace in his eyes (for he hath found in her nakedness of anything), and he hath ritten for her a riting of divorce, and given [it] into her hand, and sent her out of his house,
and she hath gone out of his house, and hath gone and been another man’s,

and the latter man hath hated her, and ritten for her a riting of divorce, and given [it] into her hand, and sent her out of his house, or hen the latter man dieth, ho hath taken her to himself for a ife:

’Her former husband ho sent her aay is not able to turn back to take her to be to him for a ife, after that she hath become defiled; for an abomination it [is] before Jehovah, and thou dost not cause the land to sin hich Jehovah thy God is giving to thee — an inheritance.
’When a man taketh a ne ife, he doth not go out into the host, and [one] doth not pass over unto him for anything; free he is at his on house one year, and hath rejoiced his ife hom he hath taken.
’None doth take in pledge millstones, and rider, for life it [is] he is taking in pledge.

’When a man is found stealing a person, of his brethren, of the sons of Israel, and hath tyrannized over him, and sold him, then hath that thief died, and thou hast put aay the evil thing out of thy midst.
’Take heed, in the plague of leprosy, to atch greatly, and to do according to all that the priests, the Levites, teach you; as I have commanded them ye observe to do;
remember that hich Jehovah thy God hath done to Miriam in the ay, in your coming out of Egypt.
’When thou liftest up on thy brother a debt of anything, thou dost not go in unto his house to obtain his pledge;
at the outside thou dost stand, and the man on hom thou art lifting [it] up is bringing out unto thee the pledge at the outside.
’And if he is a poor man, thou dost not lie don ith his pledge;
thou dost certainly give back to him the pledge at the going in of the sun, and he hath lain don in his on raiment, and hath blessed thee; and to thee it is righteousness before Jehovah thy God.
’Thou dost not oppress a hireling, poor and needy, of thy brethren or of thy sojourner ho is in thy land ithin thy gates;

in his day thou dost give his hire, and the sun doth not go in upon it, for he [is] poor, and unto it he is lifting up his soul, and he doth not cry against thee unto Jehovah, and it hath been in thee — sin.
’Fathers are not put to death for sons, and sons are not put to death for fathers — each for his on sin, they are put to death.
’Thou dost not turn aside the judgment of a fatherless sojourner, nor take in pledge the garment of a ido;
and thou hast remembered that a servant thou hast been in Egypt, and Jehovah thy God doth ransom thee from thence; therefore I am commanding thee to do this thing.

’When thou reapest thy harvest in thy field, and hast forgotten a sheaf in a field, thou dost not turn back to take it; to the sojourner, to the fatherless, and to the ido, it is; so that Jehovah thy God doth bless thee in all the ork of thy hands.
’When thou beatest thine olive, thou dost not examine the branch behind thee; to the sojourner, to the fatherless, and to the ido, it is.
’When thou cuttest thy vineyard, thou dost not glean behind thee; to the sojourner, to the fatherless, and to the ido, it is;
and thou hast remembered that a servant thou hast been in the land of Egypt; therefore I am commanding thee to do this thing.
’When there is a strife beteen men, and they have come nigh unto the judgment, and they have judged, and declared righteous the righteous, and declared rong the rong-doer,

then it hath come to pass, if the rong-doer is to be smitten, that the judge hath caused him to fall don, and [one] hath smitten him in his presence, according to the sufficiency of his rong-doing, by number;
forty [times] he doth smite him — he is not adding, lest, he is adding to smite him above these — many stripes, and thy brother is lightly esteemed in thine eyes.
’Thou dost not muzzle an ox in its threshing.

’When brethren dell together, and one of them hath died, and hath no son, the ife of the dead is not ithout to a strange man; her husband’s brother doth go in unto her, and hath taken her to him for a ife, and doth perform the duty of her husband’s brother;
and it hath been, the first-born hich she beareth doth rise for the name of his dead brother, and his name is not iped aay out of Israel.

’And if the man doth not delight to take his brother’s ife, then hath his brother’s ife gone up to the gate, unto the elders, and said, My husband’s brother is refusing to raise up to his brother a name in Israel; he hath not been illing to perform the duty of my husband’s brother;
and the elders of his city have called for him, and spoken unto him, and he hath stood and said, I have no desire to take her;

’Then hath his brother’s ife dran nigh unto him, before the eyes of the elders, and dran his shoe from off his foot, and spat in his face, and ansered and said, Thus it is done to the man ho doth not build up the house of his brother;
and his name hath been called in Israel — The house of him hose shoe is dran off.
’When men strive together, one ith another, and the ife of the one hath dran near to deliver her husband out of the hand of his smiter, and hath put forth her hand, and laid hold on his secrets,
then thou hast cut off her hand, thine eye doth not spare.
’Thou hast not in thy bag a stone and a stone, a great and a small.
Thou hast not in thy house an ephah and an ephah, a great and a small.
Thou hast a stone complete and just, thou hast an ephah complete and just, so that they prolong thy days on the ground hich Jehovah thy God is giving to thee;
for the abomination of Jehovah thy God [is] any one doing these things, any one doing iniquity.
’Remember that hich Amalek hath done to thee in the ay, in your going out from Egypt,
that he hath met thee in the ay, and smiteth in all those feeble behind thee (and thou earied and fatigued), and is not fearing God.

And it hath been, in Jehovah thy God’s giving rest to thee, from all thine enemies round about, in the land hich Jehovah thy God is giving to thee — an inheritance to possess it — thou dost blot out the remembrance of Amalek from under the heavens — thou dost not forget.
’And it hath been, hen thou comest in unto the land hich Jehovah thy God is giving to thee — an inheritance, and thou hast possessed it, and delt in it,

that thou hast taken of the first of all the fruits of the ground hich thou dost bring in out of thy land hich Jehovah thy God is giving to thee, and hast put [it] in a basket, and gone unto the place hich Jehovah thy God doth choose to cause His name to tabernacle there.

’And thou hast come in unto the priest ho is in those days, and hast said unto him, I have declared to-day to Jehovah thy God, that I have come in unto the land hich Jehovah hath sorn to our fathers to give to us;
and the priest hath taken the basket out of thy hand, and placed it before the altar of Jehovah thy God.

’And thou hast ansered and said before Jehovah thy God, A perishing Aramaean [is] my father! and he goeth don to Egypt, and sojourneth there ith fe men, and becometh there a nation, great, mighty, and numerous;
and the Egyptians do us evil, and afflict us, and put on us hard service;
and e cry unto Jehovah, God of our fathers, and Jehovah heareth our voice, and seeth our affliction, and our labour, and our oppression;
and Jehovah bringeth us out from Egypt, by a strong hand, and by a stretched-out arm, and by great fear, and by signs, and by onders,
and he bringeth us in unto this place, and giveth to us this land — a land floing ith milk and honey.
’And no, lo, I have brought in the first of the fruits of the ground hich thou hast given to me, O Jehovah; — and thou hast placed it before Jehovah thy God, and boed thyself before Jehovah thy God,
and rejoiced in all the good hich Jehovah thy God hath given to thee, and to thy house, thou, and the Levite, and the sojourner ho [is] in thy midst.

’When thou dost complete to tithe all the tithe of thine increase in the third year, the year of the tithe, then thou hast given to the Levite, to the sojourner, to the fatherless, and to the ido, and they have eaten ithin thy gates, and been satisfied,

and thou hast said before Jehovah thy God, I have put aay the separated thing out of the house, and also have given it to the Levite, and to the sojourner, and to the orphan, and to the ido, according to all Thy command hich Thou hast commanded me; I have not passed over from Thy commands, nor have I forgotten.

I have not eaten in mine affliction of it, nor have I put aay of it for uncleanness, nor have I given of it for the dead; I have hearkened to the voice of Jehovah my God; I have done according to all that Thou hast commanded me;
look from Thy holy habitation, from the heavens, and bless Thy people Israel, and the ground hich Thou hast given to us, as Thou hast sorn to our fathers — a land floing [ith] milk and honey.
’This day Jehovah thy God is commanding thee to do these statutes and judgments; and thou hast hearkened and done them ith all thy heart, and ith all thy soul,
Jehovah thou hast caused to promise to-day to become thy God, and to alk in His ays, and to keep His statutes, and His commands, and His judgments, and to hearken to His voice.
’And Jehovah hath caused thee to promise to-day to become His people, a peculiar treasure, as He hath spoken to thee, and to keep all His commands;
so as to make thee uppermost above all the nations hom He hath made for a praise, and for a name, and for beauty, and for thy being a holy people to Jehovah thy God, as He hath spoken.
’And Moses — the elders of Israel also — commandeth the people, saying, Keep all the command hich I am commanding you to-day;
and it hath been, in the day that ye pass over the Jordan unto the land hich Jehovah thy God is giving to thee, that thou hast raised up for thee great stones, and plaistered them ith plaister,

and ritten on them all the ords of this la in thy passing over, so that thou goest in unto the land hich Jehovah thy God is giving to thee — a land floing ith milk and honey, as Jehovah, God of thy fathers, hath spoken to thee.
’And it hath been, in your passing over the Jordan, ye raise up these stones hich I am commanding you to-day, in mount Ebal, and thou hast plaistered them ith plaister,
and built there an altar to Jehovah thy God, an altar of stones, thou dost not ave over them iron.
Of complete stones thou buildest the altar of Jehovah thy God, and hast caused to ascend on it burnt-offerings to Jehovah thy God,
and sacrificed peace-offerings, and eaten there, and rejoiced before Jehovah thy God,
and ritten on the stones all the ords of this la, ell engraved.’
And Moses speaketh — the priests, the Levites, also — unto all Israel, saying, ’Keep silent, and hear, O Israel, this day thou hast become a people to Jehovah thy God;
and thou hast hearkened to the voice of Jehovah thy God, and done His commands, and His statutes, hich I am commanding thee to-day.’
And Moses commandeth the people on that day, saying,
’These do stand, to bless the people, on mount Gerizzim, in your passing over the Jordan: Simeon, and Levi, and Judah, and Issachar, and Joseph, and Benjamin.
And these do stand, for the reviling, on mount Ebal: Reuben, Gad, and Asher, and Zebulun, Dan, and Naphtali.
’And the Levites have ansered and said unto every man of Israel — a loud voice:

’Cursed [is] the man ho maketh a graven and molten image, the abomination of Jehovah, ork of the hands of an artificer, and hath put [it] in a secret place, — and all the people have ansered and said, Amen.
’Cursed [is] He ho is making light of his father and his mother, — and all the people have said, Amen.
’Cursed [is] he ho is removing his neighbour’s border, — and all the people have said, Amen.
’Cursed [is] he ho is causing the blind to err in the ay, — and all the people have said, Amen.
’Cursed [is] he ho is turning aside the judgment of fatherless, sojourner, and ido, — and all the people have said, Amen.
’Cursed [is] he ho is lying ith his father’s ife, for he hath uncovered his father’s skirt, — and all the people have said, Amen.
’Cursed [is] he ho is lying ith any beast, — and all the people have said, Amen.
’Cursed [is] he ho is lying ith his sister, daughter of his father, or daughter of his mother, — and all the people have said, Amen.
’Cursed [is] he ho is lying ith his mother-in-la, — and all the people have said, Amen.
’Cursed [is] he ho is smiting his neighbour in secret, — and all the people have said, Amen.
’Cursed [is] he ho is taking a bribe to smite a person, innocent blood, — and all the people have said, Amen.
’Cursed [is] he ho doth not establish the ords of this la, to do them, — and all the people have said, Amen.

’And it hath been, if thou dost hearken diligently to the voice of Jehovah thy God, to observe to do all His commands hich I am commanding thee to-day, that Jehovah thy God hath made thee uppermost above all the nations of the earth,
and all these blessings have come upon thee, and overtaken thee, because thou dost hearken to the voice of Jehovah thy God:
’Blessed [art] thou in the city, and blessed [art] thou in the field.
’Blessed [is] the fruit of thy omb, and the fruit of thy ground, and the fruit of thy cattle, increase of thine oxen, and ealth of thy flock.
’Blessed [is] thy basket and thy kneading-trough.
’Blessed [art] thou in thy coming in, and blessed [art] thou in thy going out.
’Jehovah giveth thine enemies, ho are rising up against thee — smitten before thy face; in one ay they come out unto thee, and in seven ays they flee before thee.
’Jehovah commandeth ith thee the blessing in thy storehouses, and in every putting forth of thy hand, and hath blessed thee in the land hich Jehovah thy God is giving to thee.
’Jehovah doth establish thee to Himself for a holy people, as He hath sorn to thee, hen thou keepest the commands of Jehovah thy God, and hast alked in His ays;
and all the peoples of the land have seen that the name of Jehovah is called upon thee, and they have been afraid of thee.

’And Jehovah hath made thee abundant in good, in the fruit of the omb, and in the fruit of thy cattle, and in the fruit of thy ground, on the ground hich Jehovah hath sorn to thy fathers to give to thee.

’Jehovah doth open to thee his good treasure — the heavens — to give the rain of thy land in its season, and to bless all the ork of thy hand, and thou hast lent to many nations, and thou — thou dost not borro.

’And Jehovah hath given thee for head, and not for tail; and thou hast been only above, and art not beneath, for thou dost hearken unto the commands of Jehovah thy God, hich I am commanding thee to-day, to keep and to do,
and thou dost not turn aside from all the ords hich I am commanding you to-day — right or left — to go after other gods, to serve them.

’And it hath been, if thou dost not hearken unto the voice of Jehovah thy God to observe to do all His commands, and His statutes, hich I am commanding thee to-day, that all these revilings have come upon thee, and overtaken thee:
’Cursed [art] thou in the city, and cursed [art] thou in the field.
’Cursed [is] thy basket and thy kneading-trough.
’Cursed [is] the fruit of thy body, and the fruit of thy land, increase of thine oxen, and ealth of thy flock.
’Cursed [art] thou in thy coming in, and cursed [art] thou in thy going out.

’Jehovah doth send on thee the curse, the trouble, and the rebuke, in every putting forth of thy hand hich thou dost, till thou art destroyed, and till thou perish hastily, because of the evil of thy doings [by] hich thou hast forsaken Me.
’Jehovah doth cause to cleave to thee the pestilence, till He consume thee from off the ground hither thou art going in to possess it.
’Jehovah doth smite thee ith consumption, and ith fever, and ith inflammation, and ith extreme burning, and ith sord, and ith blasting, and ith milde, and they have pursued thee till thou perish
’And thy heavens hich [are] over thy head have been brass, and the earth hich [is] under thee iron;
Jehovah giveth the rain of thy land — dust and ashes; from the heavens it cometh don on thee till thou art destroyed.
’Jehovah giveth thee smitten before thine enemies; in one ay thou goest out unto them, and in seven ays dost flee before them, and thou hast been for a trembling to all kingdoms of the earth;
and thy carcase hath been for food to every fol of the heavens, and to the beast of the earth, and there is none causing trembling.
’Jehovah doth smite thee ith the ulcer of Egypt, and ith emerods, and ith scurvy, and ith itch, of hich thou art not able to be healed.
’Jehovah doth smite thee ith madness, and ith blindness, and ith astonishment of heart;

and thou hast been gropling at noon, as the blind gropeth in darkness; and thou dost not cause thy ays to prosper; and thou hast been only oppressed and plundered all the days, and there is no saviour.
’A oman thou dost betroth, and another man doth lie ith her; a house thou dost build, and dost not dell in it; a vineyard thou dost plant, and dost not make it common;

thine ox [is] slaughtered before thine eyes, and thou dost not eat of it; thine ass [is] taken violently aay from before thee, and it is not given back to thee; thy sheep [are] given to thine enemies, and there is no saviour for thee.
’Thy sons and thy daughters [are] given to another people, and thine eyes are looking and consuming for them all the day, and thy hand is not to God!
The fruit of thy ground, and all thy labour, eat up doth a people hom thou hast not knon; and thou hast been only oppressed and bruised all the days;
and thou hast been mad, because of the sight of thine eyes hich thou dost see.
’Jehovah doth smite thee ith an evil ulcer, on the knees, and on the legs (of hich thou art not able to be healed), from the sole of thy foot even unto thy cron.
’Jehovah doth cause thee to go, and thy king hom thou raisest up over thee, unto a nation hich thou hast not knon, thou and thy fathers, and thou hast served there other gods, ood and stone;
and thou hast been for an astonishment, for a simile, and for a byord among all the peoples hither Jehovah doth lead thee.
’Much seed thou dost take out into the field, and little thou dost gather in, for the locust doth consume it;
vineyards thou dost plant, and hast laboured, and ine thou dost not drink nor gather, for the orm doth consume it;
olives are to thee in all thy border, and oil thou dost not pour out, for thine olive doth fall off.
’Sons and daughters thou dost beget, and they are not ith thee, for they go into captivity;
all thy trees and the fruit of thy ground doth the locust possess;
the sojourner ho [is] in thy midst goeth up above thee very high, and thou goest don very lo;
he doth lend [to] thee, and thou dost not lend [to] him; he is for head, and thou art for tail.

’And come upon thee have all these curses, and they have pursued thee, and overtaken thee, till thou art destroyed, because thou hast not hearkened to the voice of Jehovah thy God, to keep His commands, and His statutes, hich he hath commanded thee;
and they have been on thee for a sign and for a onder, also on thy seed — to the age.
’Because that thou hast not served Jehovah thy God ith joy, and ith gladness of heart, because of the abundance of all things —

thou hast served thine enemies, hom Jehovah sendeth against thee, in hunger, and in thirst, and in nakedness, and in lack of all things; and he hath put a yoke of iron on thy neck, till He hath destroyed thee.
’Jehovah doth lift up against thee a nation, from afar, from the end of the earth, as the eagle it flieth; a nation hose tongue thou hast not heard,
a nation — fierce of countenance — hich accepteth not the face of the aged, and the young doth not favour;

and it hath eaten the fruit of thy cattle, and the fruit of thy ground, till thou art destroyed; hich leaveth not to thee corn, ne ine, and oil, increase of thine oxen, and ealth of thy flock, till it hath destroyed thee.

’And it hath laid siege to thee in all thy gates, till thy alls come don, the high and the fenced ones in hich thou art trusting, in all thy land; yea, it hath laid siege to thee in all thy gates, in all thy land, hich Jehovah thy God hath given to thee;
and thou hast eaten the fruit of thy body, flesh of thy sons and thy daughters (hom Jehovah thy God hath given to thee), in the siege, and in the straitness ith hich thine enemies do straiten thee.
’The man ho is tender in thee, and ho [is] very delicate — his eye is evil against his brother, and against the ife of his bosom, and against the remnant of his sons hom he leaveth,

against giving to one of them of the flesh of his sons hom he eateth, because he hath nothing left to him, in the siege, and in the straitness ith hich thine enemy doth straiten thee in all thy gates.

’The tender oman in thee, and the delicate, ho hath not tried the sole of her foot to place on the ground because of delicateness and because of tenderness — her eye is evil against the husband of her bosom, and against her son, and against her daughter,

and against her seed hich cometh out from beteen her feet, even against her sons hom she doth bear, for she doth eat them for the lacking of all things in secret, in the siege and in the straitness ith hich thine enemy doth straiten thee ithin thy gates.
’If thou dost not observe to do all the ords of this la hich are ritten in this book, to fear this honoured and fearful name — Jehovah thy God —
then hath Jehovah made onderful thy strokes, and the strokes of thy seed — great strokes, and stedfast, and evil sicknesses, and stedfast.
’And He hath brought back on thee all the diseases of Egypt, of the presence of hich thou hast been afraid, and they have cleaved to thee;
also every sickness and every stroke hich is not ritten in the book of this la; Jehovah doth cause them to go up upon thee till thou art destroyed,
and ye have been left ith fe men, instead of hich ye have been as stars of the heavens for multitude, because thou hast not hearkened to the voice of Jehovah thy God.

’And it hath been, as Jehovah hath rejoiced over you to do you good, and to multiply you, so doth Jehovah rejoice over you to destroy you, and to lay you aste; and ye have been pulled aay from off the ground hither thou art going in to possess it;

and Jehovah hath scattered thee among all the peoples, from the end of the earth even unto the end of the earth; and thou hast served there other gods hich thou hast not knon, thou and thy fathers — ood and stone.
’And among those nations thou dost not rest, yea, there is no resting-place for the sole of thy foot, and Jehovah hath given to thee there a trembling heart, and failing of eyes, and grief of soul;
and thy life hath been hanging in suspense before thee, and thou hast been afraid by night and by day, and dost not believe in thy life;

in the morning thou sayest, O that it ere evening! and in the evening thou sayest, O that it ere morning! from the fear of thy heart, ith hich thou art afraid, and from the sight of thine eyes hich thou seest.

’And Jehovah hath brought thee back to Egypt ith ships, by a ay of hich I said to thee, Thou dost not add any more to see it, and ye have sold yourselves there to thine enemies, for men-servants and for maid-servants, and there is no buyer.’
These [are] the ords of the covenant hich Jehovah hath commanded Moses to make ith the sons of Israel in the land of Moab, apart from the covenant hich He made ith them in Horeb.

And Moses calleth unto all Israel, and saith unto them, ’Ye — ye have seen all that hich Jehovah hath done before your eyes in the land of Egypt, to Pharaoh, and to all his servants, and to all his land;
the great trials hich thine eyes have seen, the signs, and those great onders;
and Jehovah hath not given to you a heart to kno, and eyes to see, and ears to hear, till this day,
and I cause you to go forty years in a ilderness; your garments have not been consumed from off you, and thy shoe hath not orn aay from off thy foot;
bread ye have not eaten, and ine and strong drink ye have not drunk, so that ye kno that I [am] Jehovah your God.
’And ye come in unto this place, and Sihon king of Heshbon — also Og king of Bashan — doth come out to meet us, to battle, and e smite them,
and take their land, and give it for an inheritance to the Reubenite, and to the Gadite, and to the half of the tribe of Manasseh;
and ye have kept the ords of this covenant, and done them, so that ye cause all that ye do to prosper.
’Ye are standing to-day, all of you, before Jehovah your God — your heads, your tribes, your elders, and your authorities — every man of Israel;
your infants, your ives, and thy sojourner ho [is] in the midst of thy camps, from the heer of thy ood unto the draer of thy ater —
for thy passing over into the covenant of Jehovah thy God, and into His oath hich Jehovah thy God is making ith thee to-day;
in order to establish thee to-day to Him for a people, and He Himself is thy God, as He hath spoken to thee, and as He hath sorn to thy fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.
’And not ith you alone am I making this covenant and this oath;
but ith him ho is here ith us, standing to-day before Jehovah our God, and ith him ho is not here ith us to-day,
for ye have knon ho ye delt in the land of Egypt, and ho e passed by through the midst of the nations hich ye have passed by;
and ye see their abominations, and their idols, ood and stone, silver and gold, hich [are] ith them,

lest there be among you a man or oman, or family or tribe, hose heart is turning to-day from Jehovah our God, to go to serve the gods of those nations, lest there be in you a root fruitful of gall and ormood:

’And it hath been, in his hearing the ords of this oath, and he hath blessed himself in his heart, saying, I have peace, though in the stubbornness of my heart I go on, in order to end the fulness ith the thirst.

Jehovah is not illing to be propitious to him, for then doth the anger of Jehovah smoke, also His zeal, against that man, and lain don on him hath all the oath hich is ritten in this book, and Jehovah hath blotted out his name from under the heavens,
and Jehovah hath separated him for evil, out of all the tribes of Israel, according to all the oaths of the covenant hich is ritten in this book of the la.

’And the latter generation of your sons ho rise after you, and the stranger ho cometh in from a land afar off, have said hen they have seen the strokes of that land, and its sicknesses hich Jehovah hath sent into it, —

([ith] brimstone and salt is the hole land burnt, it is not son, nor doth it shoot up, nor doth there go up on it any herb, like the overthro of Sodom and Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboim, hich Jehovah overturned in His anger, and in His fury,) —
yea, all the nations have said, Wherefore hath Jehovah done thus to this land? hat the heat of this great anger?
’And they have said, Because that they have forsaken the covenant of Jehovah, God of their fathers, hich He made ith them in His bringing them out of the land of Egypt,
and they go and serve other gods, and bo themselves to them — gods hich they have not knon, and hich He hath not apportioned to them;
and the anger of Jehovah burneth against that land, to bring in on it all the reviling that is ritten in this book,
and Jehovah doth pluck them from off their ground in anger, and in fury, and in great rath, and doth cast them unto another land, as [at] this day.
’The things hidden [are] to Jehovah our God, and the things revealed [are] to us and to our sons — to the age, to do all the ords of this la.

’And it hath been, hen all these things come upon thee, the blessing and the reviling, hich I have set before thee, and thou hast brought [them] back unto thy heart, among all the nations hither Jehovah thy God hath driven thee aay,
and hast turned back unto Jehovah thy God, and hearkened to His voice, according to all that I am commanding thee to-day, thou and thy sons, ith all thy heart, and ith all thy soul —
then hath Jehovah thy God turned back [to] thy captivity, and pitied thee, yea, He hath turned back and gathered thee out of all the peoples hither Jehovah thy God hath scattered thee.
’If thine outcast is in the extremity of the heavens, thence doth Jehovah thy God gather thee, and thence He doth take thee;
and Jehovah thy God hath brought thee in unto the land hich thy fathers have possessed, and thou hast inherited it, and He hath done thee good, and multiplied thee above thy fathers.
’And Jehovah thy God hath circumcised thy heart, and the heart of thy seed, to love Jehovah thy God ith all thy heart, and ith all thy soul, for the sake of thy life;
and Jehovah thy God hath put all this oath on thine enemies, and on those hating thee, ho have pursued thee.
’And thou dost turn back, and hast hearkened to the voice of Jehovah, and hast done all His commands hich I am commanding thee to-day;

and Jehovah thy God hath made thee abundant in every ork of thy hand, in the fruit of thy body, and in the fruit of thy cattle, and in the fruit of thy ground, for good; for Jehovah turneth back to rejoice over thee for good, as He rejoiced over thy fathers,

for thou dost hearken to the voice of Jehovah thy God, to keep His commands, and His statutes, hich are ritten in the book of this la, for thou turnest back unto Jehovah thy God, ith all thy heart, and ith all thy soul.
’For this command hich I am commanding thee to-day, it is not too onderful for thee, nor [is] it far off.
It is not in the heavens, — saying, Who doth go up for us into the heavens, and doth take it for us, and doth cause us to hear it — that e may do it.
And it [is] not beyond the sea, — saying, Who doth pass over for us beyond the sea, and doth take it for us, and doth cause us to hear it — that e may do it?
For very near unto thee is the ord, in thy mouth, and in thy heart — to do it.
’See, I have set before thee to-day life and good, and death and evil,

in that I am commanding thee to-day to love Jehovah thy God, to alk in His ays, and to keep His commands, and His statutes, and His judgments; and thou hast lived and multiplied, and Jehovah thy God hath blessed thee in the land hither thou art going in to possess it.
’And if thy heart doth turn, and thou dost not hearken, and hast been driven aay, and hast boed thyself to other gods, and served them,
I have declared to you this day, that ye do certainly perish, ye do not prolong days on the ground hich thou art passing over the Jordan to go in thither to possess it.

’I have caused to testify against you to-day the heavens and the earth; life and death I have set before thee, the blessing and the reviling; and thou hast fixed on life, so that thou dost live, thou and thy seed,

to love Jehovah thy God, to hearken to His voice, and to cleave to Him (for He [is] thy life, and the length of thy days), to dell on the ground hich Jehovah hath sorn to thy fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, to give to them.’
And Moses goeth and speaketh these ords unto all Israel,
and he saith unto them, ’A son of a hundred and tenty years [am] I to-day; I am not able any more to go out and to come in, and Jehovah hath said unto me, Thou dost not pass over this Jordan,
’Jehovah thy God He is passing over before thee, He doth destroy these nations from before thee, and thou hast possessed them; Joshua — he is passing over before thee as Jehovah hath spoken,
and Jehovah hath done to them as he hath done to Sihon and to Og, kings of the Amorite, and to their land, hom He destroyed.
And Jehovah hath given them before your face, and ye have done to them according to all the command hich I have commanded you;
be strong and courageous, fear not, nor be terrified because of them, for Jehovah thy God [is] He ho is going ith thee; He doth not fail thee nor forsake thee.’

And Moses calleth for Joshua, and saith unto him before the eyes of all Israel, ’Be strong and courageous, for thou — thou dost go in ith this people unto the land hich Jehovah hath sorn to their fathers to give to them, and thou — thou dost cause them to inherit it;
and Jehovah [is] He ho is going before thee, He himself is ith thee; He doth not fail thee nor forsake thee; fear not, nor be affrighted.’
And Moses riteth this la, and giveth it unto the priests (sons of Levi, those bearing the ark of the covenant of Jehovah), and unto all the elders of Israel,
and Moses commandeth them, saying, ’At the end of seven years, in the appointed time, the year of release, in the feast of booths,
in the coming in of all Israel to see the face of Jehovah in the place hich He chooseth, thou dost proclaim this la before all Israel, in their ears.

’Assemble the people, the men, and the omen, and the infants, and thy sojourner ho [is] ithin thy gates, so that they hear, and so that they learn, and have feared Jehovah your God, and observed to do all the ords of this la;
and their sons, ho have not knon, do hear, and have learned to fear Jehovah your God all the days hich ye are living on the ground hither ye are passing over the Jordan to possess it.’

And Jehovah saith unto Moses, ’Lo, thy days have dran near to die; call Joshua, and station yourselves in the tent of meeting, and I charge him;’ and Moses goeth — Joshua also — and they station themselves in the tent of meeting,
and Jehovah is seen in the tent, in a pillar of a cloud; and the pillar of the cloud standeth at the opening of the tent.

And Jehovah saith unto Moses, ’Lo, thou art lying don ith thy fathers, and this people hath risen, and gone a-horing after the gods of the stranger of the land into the midst of hich it hath entered, and forsaken Me, and broken My covenant hich I made ith it;

and Mine anger hath burned against it in that day, and I have forsaken them, and hidden My face from them, and it hath been for consumption, and many evils and distresses have found it, and it hath said in that day, Is it not because that my God is not in my midst — these evils have found me?
and I certainly hide My face in that day for all the evil hich it hath done, for it hath turned unto other gods.
’And no, rite for you this song, and teach it the sons of Israel; put it in their mouths, so that this song is to Me for a itness against the sons of Israel,

and I bring them in unto the ground hich I have sorn to their fathers — floing ith milk and honey, and they have eaten, and been satisfied, and been fat, and have turned unto other gods, and they have served them, and despised Me, and broken My covenant.

’And it hath been, hen many evils and distresses do meet it, that this song hath testified to its face for a itness; for it is not forgotten out of the mouth of its seed, for I have knon its imagining hich it is doing to-day, before I bring them in unto the land of hich I have sorn.’
And Moses riteth this song on that day, and doth teach it the sons of Israel,
and He commandeth Joshua son of Nun, and saith, ’Be strong and courageous, for thou dost bring in the sons of Israel unto the land hich I have sorn to them, and I — I am ith thee.’
And it cometh to pass, hen Moses finisheth to rite the ords of this la on a book till their completion,
that Moses commandeth the Levites bearing the ark of the covenant of Jehovah, saying,
’Take this Book of the La, and thou hast set it on the side of the ark of the covenant of Jehovah your God, and it hath been there against thee for a itness;
for I — I have knon thy rebellion, and thy stiff neck; lo, in my being yet alive ith you to-day, rebellious ye have been ith Jehovah, and also surely after my death.
’Assemble unto me all the elders of your tribes, and your authorities, and I speak in their ears these ords, and cause to testify against them the heavens and the earth,

for I have knon that after my death ye do very corruptly, and have turned aside out of the ay hich I commanded you, and evil hath met you in the latter end of the days, because ye do the evil thing in the eyes of Jehovah, to make Him angry ith the ork of your hands.’
And Moses speaketh in the ears of all the assembly of Israel the ords of this song, till their completion: —
’Give ear, O heavens, and I speak; And thou dost hear, O earth, sayings of my mouth!
Drop as rain doth My doctrine; Flo as de doth My sayings; As storms on the tender grass, And as shoers on the herb,
For the Name of Jehovah I proclaim, Ascribe ye greatness to our God!
The Rock! — perfect [is] His ork, For all His ays [are] just; God of stedfastness, and ithout iniquity: Righteous and upright [is] He.
It hath done corruptly to Him; Their blemish is not His sons’, A generation perverse and crooked!
To Jehovah do ye act thus, O people foolish and not ise? Is not He thy father — thy possessor? He made thee, and doth establish thee.
Remember days of old — Understand the years of many generations — Ask thy father, and he doth tell thee; Thine elders, and they say to thee:
In the Most High causing nations to inherit, In His separating sons of Adam — He setteth up the borders of the peoples By the number of the sons of Israel.
For Jehovah’s portion [is] His people, Jacob [is] the line of His inheritance.
He findeth him in a land — a desert, And in a void — a holing ilderness, He turneth him round — He causeth him to understand — He keepeth him as the apple of His eye.
As an eagle aketh up its nest, Over its young ones fluttereth, Spreadeth its ings — taketh them, Beareth them on its pinions; —
Jehovah alone doth lead him, And there is no strange god ith him.
He maketh him ride on high places of earth, And he eateth increase of the fields, And He maketh him suck honey from a rock, And oil out of the flint of a rock;
Butter of the herd, and milk of the flock, With fat of lambs, and rams, sons of Bashan, And he-goats, ith fat of kidneys of heat; And of the blood of the grape thou dost drink ine!
And Jeshurun axeth fat, and doth kick: Thou hast been fat — thou hast been thick, Thou hast been covered. And he leaveth God ho made him, And dishonoureth the Rock of his salvation.
They make Him zealous ith strangers, With abominations they make Him angry.
They sacrifice to demons — no god! Gods they have not knon — Ne ones — from the vicinity they came; Not feared them have your fathers!
The Rock that begat thee thou forgettest, And neglectest God ho formeth thee.
And Jehovah seeth and despiseth — For the provocation of His sons and His daughters.
And He saith: I hide My face from them, I see hat [is] their latter end; For a froard generation [are] they, Sons in hom is no stedfastness.
They have made Me zealous by ’no-god,’ They made Me angry by their vanities; And I make them zealous by ’no-people,’ By a foolish nation I make them angry.
For a fire hath been kindled in Mine anger, And it burneth unto Sheol — the loest, And consumeth earth and its increase, And setteth on fire foundations of mountains.
I gather upon them evils, Mine arros I consume upon them.
Exhausted by famine, And consumed by heat, and bitter destruction. And the teeth of beasts I send upon them, With poison of fearful things of the dust.
Without bereave doth the sord, And at the inner-chambers — fear, Both youth and virgin, Suckling ith man of grey hair.
I have said: I blo them aay, I cause their remembrance to cease from man;
If not — the anger of an enemy I fear, Lest their adversaries kno — Lest they say, Our hand is high, And Jehovah hath not rought all this.
For a nation lost to counsels [are] they, And there is no understanding in them.
If they ere ise — They deal isely [ith] this; They attend to their latter end:
Ho doth one pursue a thousand, And to cause a myriad to flee! If not — that their rock hath sold them, And Jehovah hath shut them up?
For not as our Rock [is] their rock, (And our enemies [are] judges!)
