For of the vine of Sodom their vine [is], And of the fields of Gomorrah; Their grapes [are] grapes of gall — They have bitter clusters;
The poison of dragons [is] their ine And the fierce venom of asps.
Is it not laid up ith Me? Sealed among My treasures?
Mine [are] vengeance and recompense, At the due time — doth their foot slide; For near is a day of their calamity, And haste do things prepared for them.
For Jehovah doth judge His people, And for His servants doth repent Himself. For He seeth — the going aay of poer, And none is restrained and left.
And He hath said, Where [are] their gods — The rock in hich they trusted;
Which the fat of their sacrifices do eat, They drink the ine of their libation! Let them arise and help you, Let it be for you a hiding-place!
See ye, no, that I — I [am] He, And there is no god ith Me: I put to death, and I keep alive; I have smitten, and I heal; And there is not from My hand a deliverer,
For I lift up unto the heavens My hand, And have said, I live — to the age!
If I have sharpened the brightness of My sord, And My hand doth lay hold on judgment, I turn back vengeance to Mine adversaries, And to those hating Me — I repay!
I make drunk Mine arros ith blood, And My sord devoureth flesh, From the blood of the pierced and captive, From the head of the freemen of the enemy.
Sing ye nations — [ith] his people, For the blood of His servants He avengeth, And vengeance He turneth back on His adversaries, And hath pardoned His land — His people.’
And Moses cometh and speaketh all the ords of this song in the ears of the people, he and Hoshea son of Nun;
and Moses finisheth to speak all these ords unto all Israel,
and saith unto them, ’Set your heart to all the ords hich I am testifying against you to-day, that ye command your sons to observe to do all the ords of this la,
for it [is] not a vain thing for you, for it [is] your life, and by this thing ye prolong days on the ground hither ye are passing over the Jordan to possess it.’
And Jehovah speaketh unto Moses, in this self-same day, saying,
’Go up unto this mount Abarim, mount Nebo, hich [is] in the land of Moab, hich [is] on the front of Jericho, and see the land of Canaan hich I am giving to the sons of Israel for a possession;
and die in the mount hither thou art going up, and be gathered unto thy people, as Aaron thy brother hath died in the mount Hor, and is gathered unto his people:
’Because ye trespassed against me in the midst of the sons of Israel at the aters of Meribath-Kadesh, the ilderness of Zin — because ye sanctified Me not in the midst of the sons of Israel;
but over-against thou seest the land, and thither thou dost not go in, unto the land hich I am giving to the sons of Israel.’
And this [is] the blessing [ith] hich Moses the man of God blessed the sons of Israel before his death,
and he saith: — ’Jehovah from Sinai hath come, And hath risen from Seir for them; He hath shone from mount Paran, And hath come [ith] myriads of holy ones; At His right hand [are] springs for them.
Also He [is] loving the peoples; All His holy ones [are] in thy hand, And they — they sat don at thy foot, [Each] He lifteth up at thy ords.
A la hath Moses commanded us, A possession of the assembly of Jacob.
And he is in Jeshurun king, In the heads of the people gathering together, The tribes of Israel!
Let Reuben live, and not die, And let his men be a number.
And this [is] for Judah; and he saith: — Hear, O Jehovah, the voice of Judah, And unto his people do Thou bring him in; His hand hath striven for him, And an help from his adversaries art Thou.
And of Levi he said: — Thy Thummim and thy Urim [are] for thy pious one, Whom Thou hast tried in Massah, Thou dost strive ith Him at the aters of Meribah;
Who is saying of his father and his mother, I have not seen him; And his brethren he hath not discerned, And his sons he hath not knon; For they have observed Thy saying, And Thy covenant they keep.
They teach Thy judgments to Jacob, And Thy la to Israel; They put perfume in Thy nose, And hole burnt-offering on Thine altar.
Bless, O Jehovah, his strength, And the ork of his hands Thou acceptest, Smite the loins of his ithstanders, And of those hating him — that they rise not!
Of Benjamin he said: — The beloved of Jehovah doth tabernacle confidently by him, Covering him over all the day; Yea, beteen his shoulders He doth tabernacle.
And of Joseph he said: — Blessed of Jehovah [is] his land, By precious things of the heavens, By de, and by the deep crouching beneath,
And by precious things — fruits of the sun, And by precious things — cast forth by the moons,
And by chief things — of the ancient mountains, And by precious things — of the age-during heights,

And by precious things — of earth and its fulness, And the good pleasure Of Him ho is delling in the bush, — Let it come for the head of Joseph, And for the cron of him Who is separate from his brethren.

His honour [is] a firstling of his ox, And his horns [are] horns of a reem; By them peoples he doth push together To the ends of earth; And they [are] the myriads of Ephraim, And they [are] the thousands of Manasseh.
And of Zebulun he said: — Rejoice, O Zebulun, in thy going out, And, O Issachar, in thy tents;
Peoples [to] the mountain they call, There they sacrifice righteous sacrifices; For the abundance of the seas they suck, And hidden things hidden in the sand.
And of Gad he said: — Blessed of the Enlarger [is] Gad, As a lioness he doth tabernacle, And hath torn the arm — also the cron!

And he provideth the first part for himself, For there the portion of the lagiver is covered, And he cometh [ith] the heads of the people; The righteousness of Jehovah he hath done, And His judgments ith Israel.
And of Dan he said: — Dan [is] a lion’s help; he doth leap from Bashan.
And of Naphtali he said: — O Naphtali, satisfied ith pleasure, And full of the blessing of Jehovah, West and south possess thou.
And of Asher he said: — Blessed ith sons [is] Asher, Let him be accepted by his brethren, And dipping in oil his foot.
Iron and brass [are] thy shoes, And as thy days — thy strength.
There is none like the God of Jeshurun, Riding the heavens in thy help, And in His excellency the skies.
A habitation [is] the eternal God, And beneath [are] arms age-during. And He casteth out from thy presence the enemy, and saith, ’Destroy!’
And Israel doth tabernacle [in] confidence alone; The eye of Jacob [is] unto a land of corn and ine; Also His heavens drop don de.

O thy happiness, O Israel! ho is like thee? A people saved by Jehovah, The shield of thy help, And He ho [is] the sord of thine excellency: And thine enemies are subdued for thee, And thou on their high places dost tread.’
And Moses goeth up from the plains of Moab unto mount Nebo, the top of Pisgah, hich [is] on the front of Jericho, and Jehovah sheeth him all the land — Gilead unto Dan,
and all Naphtali, and the land of Ephraim, and Manasseh, and all the land of Judah unto the further sea,
and the south, and the circuit of the valley of Jericho, the city of palms, unto Zoar.

And Jehovah saith unto him, ’This [is] the land hich I have sorn to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, saying, To thy seed I give it; I have caused thee to see ith thine eyes, and thither thou dost not pass over.’
And Moses, servant of the Lord, dieth there, in the land of Moab, according to the command of Jehovah;
and He burieth him in a valley in the land of Moab, over-against Beth-Peor, and no man hath knon his burying place unto this day.
And Moses [is] a son of a hundred and tenty years hen he dieth; his eye hath not become dim, nor hath his moisture fled.
And the sons of Israel beail Moses in the plains of Moab thirty days; and the days of eeping [and] mourning for Moses are completed.
And Joshua son of Nun is full of the spirit of isdom, for Moses had laid his hands upon him, and the sons of Israel hearken unto him, and do as Jehovah commanded Moses.
And there hath not arisen a prophet any more in Israel like Moses, hom Jehovah hath knon face unto face,
in reference to all the signs and the onders hich Jehovah sent him to do in the land of Egypt, to Pharaoh, and to all his servants, and to all his land,
and in reference to all the strong hand, and to all the great fear hich Moses did before the eyes of all Israel.
And it cometh to pass after the death of Moses, servant of Jehovah, that Jehovah speaketh unto Joshua son of Nun, minister of Moses, saying,
’Moses my servant is dead, and no, rise, pass over this Jordan, thou, and all this people, unto the land hich I am giving to them, to the sons of Israel.
’Every place on hich the sole of your foot treadeth, to you I have given it, as I have spoken unto Moses.
From this ilderness and Lebanon, and unto the great river, the river Phrath, all the land of the Hittites, and unto the great Sea — the going in of the sun — is your border.
’No man doth station himself before thee all days of thy life; as I have been ith Moses, I am ith thee, I do not fail thee, nor forsake thee;
be strong and courageous, for thou — thou dost cause this people to inherit the land hich I have sorn to their fathers to give to them.

’Only, be strong and very courageous, to observe to do according to all the la hich Moses My servant commanded thee; thou dost not turn aside from it right or left, so that thou dost act isely in every [place] hither thou goest;

the book of this la doth not depart out of thy mouth, and thou hast meditated in it by day and by night, so that thou dost observe to do according to all that is ritten in it, for then thou dost cause thy ay to prosper, and then thou dost act isely.
’Have not I commanded thee? be strong and courageous; be not terrified nor affrighted, for ith thee [is] Jehovah thy God in every [place] hither thou goest.’
And Joshua commandeth the authorities of the people, saying,

’Pass over into the midst of the camp, and command the people, saying, Prepare for yourselves provision, for ithin three days ye are passing over this Jordan, to go in to possess the land hich Jehovah your God is giving to you to possess it.’
And to the Reubenite, and to the Gadite, and to the half of the tribe of Manasseh, hath Joshua spoken, saying,
’Remember the ord hich Moses, servant of Jehovah, commanded you, saying, Jehovah your God is giving rest to you, and He hath given to you this land;

your ives, your infants, and your substance, abide in the land hich Moses hath given to you beyond the Jordan, and ye — ye pass over by fifties, before your brethren, all the mighty ones of valour, and have helped them,

till that Jehovah giveth rest to your brethren as to yourselves, and they have possessed, even they, the land hich Jehovah your God is giving to them; then ye have turned back to the land of your possession, and have possessed it, hich Moses, servant of Jehovah, hath given to you beyond the Jordan, [at] the sun-rising.’
And they anser Joshua, saying, ’All that thou hast commanded us e do; and unto every [place] hither thou dost send us, e go;
according to all that e hearkened unto Moses [in], so e hearken unto thee; surely Jehovah thy God is ith thee as He hath been ith Moses.
Any man ho doth provoke thy mouth, and doth not hear thy ords, in all that thou dost command him, is put to death; only, be strong and courageous.’

And Joshua son of Nun sendeth from Shittim, to men, spies, silently, saying, ’Go, see the land — and Jericho;’ and they go and come into the house of a oman, a harlot, and her name [is] Rahab, and they lie don there.
And it is told to the king of Jericho, saying, ’Lo, men have come in hither to-night, from the sons of Israel, to search the land.
And the king of Jericho sendeth unto Rahab, saying, ’Bring out the men ho are coming in unto thee, ho have come into thy house, for to search the hole of the land they have come in.
And the oman taketh the to men, and hideth them, and saith thus: ’The men came in unto me, and I have not knon hence they [are];
and it cometh to pass — the gate is to [be] shut — in the dark, and the men have gone out; I have not knon hither the men have gone; pursue ye, hasten after them, for ye overtake them;’
and she hath caused them to go up on the roof, and hideth them ith the flax ood, hich is arranged for her on the roof.
And the men have pursued after them the ay of the Jordan, by the fords, and the gate they have shut afterards, hen the pursuers have gone out after them.
And — before they lie don — she hath gone up unto them on the roof,
and she saith unto the men, ’I have knon that Jehovah hath given to you the land, and that your terror hath fallen upon us, and that all the inhabitants of the land have melted at your presence.

’For e have heard ho Jehovah dried up the aters of the Red Sea at your presence, in your going out of Egypt, and that hich ye have done to the to kings of the Amorite ho [are] beyond the Jordan; to Sihon and to Og hom ye devoted.
And e hear, and melt doth our heart, and there hath not stood any more spirit in [any] man, from your presence, for Jehovah your God, He [is] God in the heavens above, and on the earth beneath.
’And no, sear ye, I pray you, to me by Jehovah — because I have done ith you kindness — that ye have done, even ye, kindness ith the house of my father, and have given to me a true token,
and have kept alive my father, and my mother, and my brothers, and my sisters, and all that they have, and have delivered our souls from death.’
And the men say to her, ’Our soul for yours — to die; if ye declare not this our matter, then it hath been, in Jehovah’s giving to us this land, that e have done ith thee kindness and truth.’
And she causeth them to go don by a rope through the indo, for her house [is] in the side of the all, and in the all she [is] delling;
and she saith to them, ’To the mountain go, lest the pursuers come upon you; and ye have been hidden there three days till the turning back of the pursuers, and afterards ye go on your ay.’
And the men say unto her, ’We are acquitted of this thine oath hich thou hast caused us to sear:

lo, e are coming into the land, this line of scarlet thread thou dost bind to the indo by hich thou hast caused us to go don, and thy father, and thy mother, and thy brethren, and all the house of thy father thou dost gather unto thee, to the house;

and it hath been, any one ho goeth out from the doors of thy house ithout, his blood [is] on his head, and e are innocent; and any one ho is ith thee in the house, his blood [is] on our head, if a hand is on him;
and if thou declare this our matter, then e have been acquitted from thine oath hich thou hast caused us to sear.’
And she saith, ’According unto your ords, so it [is];’ and she sendeth them aay, and they go; and she bindeth the scarlet line to the indo.
And they go, and come in to the mountain, and abide there three days until the pursuers have turned back; and the pursuers seek in all the ay, and have not found.
And the to men turn back, and come don from the hill, and pass over, and come in unto Joshua son of Nun, and recount to him all that hath come upon them;
and they say unto Joshua, ’Surely Jehovah hath given into our hand all the land; and also, all the inhabitants of the land have melted at our presence.’
And Joshua riseth early in the morning, and they journey from Shittim, and come in unto the Jordan, he and all the sons of Israel, and they lodge there before they pass over.
And it cometh to pass, at the end of three days, that the authorities pass over into the midst of the camp,
and command the people, saying, ’When ye see the ark of the covenant of Jehovah your God, and the priests, the Levites, bearing it, then ye journey from your place, and have gone after it;
only, a distance is beteen you and it, about to thousand cubits by measure; ye do not come near unto it, so that ye kno the ay in hich ye go, for ye have not passed over in the ay heretofore.’
And Joshua saith unto the people, ’Sanctify yourselves, for to-morro doth Jehovah do in your midst onders.’
And Joshua speaketh unto the priests, saying, ’Take up the ark of the covenant, and pass over before the people;’ and they take up the ark of the covenant, and go before the people.
And Jehovah saith unto Joshua, ’This day I begin to make thee great in the eyes of all Israel, so that they kno that as I as ith Moses I am ith thee;
and thou, thou dost command the priests bearing the ark of the covenant, saying, When ye come unto the extremity of the aters of the Jordan — in the Jordan ye stand.’
And Joshua saith unto the sons of Israel, ’Come nigh hither, and hear the ords of Jehovah your God;

and Joshua saith, ’By this ye kno that the living God [is] in your midst, and He doth certainly dispossess from before you the Canaanite, and the Hittite, and the Hivite, and the Perizzite, and the Girgashite, and the Amorite, and the Jebusite:
lo, the ark of the covenant of the Lord of all the earth is passing over before you into Jordan;
and no, take for you telve men out of the tribes of Israel, one man — one man for a tribe;

and it hath been, at the resting of the soles of the feet of the priests bearing the ark of Jehovah, Lord of all the earth, in the aters of the Jordan, the aters of the Jordan are cut off — the aters hich are coming don from above — and they stand — one heap.’
And it cometh to pass, in the journeying of the people from their tents to pass over the Jordan, and of the priests bearing the ark of the covenant before the people,

and at those bearing the ark coming in unto the Jordan, and the feet of the priests bearing the ark have been dipped in the extremity of the aters (and the Jordan is full over all its banks all the days of harvest) —

that the aters stand; those coming don from above have risen — one heap, very far above Adam the city, hich [is] at the side of Zaretan; and those going don by the sea of the plain, the Salt Sea, have been completely cut off; and the people have passed through over-against Jericho;

and the priests bearing the ark of the covenant of Jehovah stand on dry ground in the midst of the Jordan — established, and all Israel are passing over on dry ground till that all the nation hath completed to pass over the Jordan.
And it cometh to pass, hen all the nation hath completed to pass over the Jordan, that Jehovah speaketh unto Joshua, saying,
’Take for you out of the people telve men, one man — one man out of a tribe;

and command ye them, saying, Take up for you from this [place], from the midst of the Jordan, from the established standing-place of the feet of the priests, telve stones, and ye have removed them over ith you, and placed them in the lodging-place in hich ye lodge to-night.’
And Joshua calleth unto the telve men hom he prepared out of the sons of Israel, one man — one man out of a tribe;

and Joshua saith to them, ’Pass over before the ark of Jehovah your God unto the midst of the Jordan and lift up for you each, one stone on his shoulder, according to the number of the tribes of the sons of Israel,
so that this is a sign in your midst, hen your children ask hereafter, saying, What [are] these stones to you?

that ye have said to them, Because the aters of the Jordan ere cut off, at the presence of the ark of the covenant of Jehovah; in its passing over into the Jordan ere the aters of the Jordan cut off; and these stones have been for a memorial to the sons of Israel — to the age.’

And the sons of Israel do so as Joshua commanded, and take up telve stones out of the midst of the Jordan, as Jehovah hath spoken unto Joshua, according to the number of the tribes of the sons of Israel, and remove them over ith them unto the lodging-place, and place them there,
even the telve stones hath Joshua raised up out of the midst of the Jordan, the place of the standing of the feet of the priests bearing the ark of the covenant, and they are there unto this day.

And the priests bearing the ark are standing in the midst of the Jordan till the completion of the hole thing hich Jehovah commanded Joshua to speak unto the people, according to all that Moses commanded Joshua, and the people haste and pass over.
And it cometh to pass hen all the people have completed to pass over, that the ark of Jehovah passeth over, and the priests, in the presence of the people;
and the sons of Reuben, and the sons of Gad, and the half of the tribe of Manasseh, pass over, by fifties, before the sons of Israel, as Moses had spoken unto them;
about forty thousand, armed ones of the host, passed over before Jehovah for battle, unto the plains of Jericho.
On that day hath Jehovah made Joshua great in the eyes of all Israel, and they reverence him, as they reverenced Moses, all days of his life.
And Jehovah speaketh unto Joshua, saying,
’Command the priests bearing the ark of the testimony, and they come up out of the Jordan.’
And Joshua commandeth the priests, saying, ’Come ye up out of the Jordan.’

And it cometh to pass, in the coming up of the priests bearing the ark of the covenant of Jehovah out of the midst of the Jordan — the soles of the feet of the priests have been dran up into the dry ground — and the aters of the Jordan turn back to their place, and go as heretofore over all its banks.
And the people have come up out of the Jordan on the tenth of the first month, and encamp in Gilgal, in the extremity east of Jericho;
and these telve stones, hich they have taken out of the Jordan, hath Joshua raised up in Gilgal.
And he speaketh unto the sons of Israel, saying, ’When your sons ask their fathers hereafter, saying, What [are] these stones?
then ye have caused your sons to kno, saying, On dry land Israel passed over this Jordan;
because Jehovah your God dried up the aters of the Jordan at your presence, till your passing over, as Jehovah your God did to the Red Sea hich He dried up at our presence till our passing over;
so that all the people of the land do kno the hand of Jehovah that it [is] strong, so that ye have reverenced Jehovah your God all the days.’

And it cometh to pass hen all the kings of the Amorite hich [are] beyond the Jordan, toards the sea, and all the kings of the Canaanite hich [are] by the sea, hear ho that Jehovah hath dried up the aters of the Jordan at the presence of the sons of Israel till their passing over, that their heart is melted, and there hath not been in them any more spirit because of the presence of the sons of Israel.
At that time said Jehovah unto Joshua, ’Make for thee knives of flint, and turn back, circumcise the sons of Israel a second time;’
and Joshua maketh for him knives of flint, and circumciseth the sons of Israel at the height of the foreskins.

And this [is] the thing [for] hich Joshua circumciseth [them]: all the people ho are coming out of Egypt, ho are males, all the men of ar have died in the ilderness, in the ay, in their coming out of Egypt,
for all the people ho are coming out ere circumcised, and all the people ho [are] born in the ilderness, in the ay, in their coming out from Egypt, they have not circumcised;

for forty years have the sons of Israel gone in the ilderness, till all the nation of the men of ar ho are coming out of Egypt, ho hearkened not to the voice of Jehovah, to hom Jehovah hath sorn not to sho them the land hich Jehovah sare to their fathers to give to us, a land floing ith milk and honey, are consumed;
and their sons He raised up in their stead, them hath Joshua circumcised, for they have been uncircumcised, for they have not circumcised them in the ay.
And it cometh to pass hen all the nation have completed to be circumcised, that they abide in their places in the camp till their recovering;
and Jehovah saith unto Joshua, ’To-day I have rolled the reproach of Egypt from off you;’ and [one] calleth the name of that place Gilgal unto this day.
And the sons of Israel encamp in Gilgal, and make the passover on the fourteenth day of the month, at evening, in the plains of Jericho;
and they eat of the old corn of the land on the morro of the passover, unleavened things and roasted [corn], in this self-same day;

and the manna doth cease on the morro in their eating of the old corn of the land, and there hath been no more manna to the sons of Israel, and they eat of the increase of the land of Canaan in that year.

And it cometh to pass in Joshua’s being by Jericho, that he lifteth up his eyes, and looketh, and lo, one standing over-against him, and his dran sord in his hand, and Joshua goeth unto him, and saith to him, ’Art thou for us or for our adversaries?’

And He saith, ’No, for I [am] Prince of Jehovah’s host; no I have come;’ and Joshua falleth on his face to the earth, and doth obeisance, and saith to Him, ’What is my Lord speaking unto His servant?’
And the Prince of Jehovah’s host saith unto Joshua, ’Cast off thy shoe from off thy foot, for the place on hich thou art standing is holy;’ and Joshua doth so;
(And Jericho shutteth itself up, and is shut up, because of the presence of the sons of Israel — none going out, and none coming in;)
And Jehovah saith unto Joshua, ’See, I have given into thy hand Jericho and its king — mighty ones of valour,
and ye have compassed the city — all the men of battle — going round the city once; thus thou dost six days;
and seven priests do bear seven trumpets of the jubilee before the ark, and on the seventh day ye compass the city seven times, and the priests blo ith the trumpets,

and it hath been, in the prolongation of the horn of the jubilee, in your hearing the voice of the trumpet, all the people shout — a great shout, and the all of the city hath fallen under it, and the people have gone up, each over-against him.’
And Joshua son of Nun calleth unto the priests, and saith unto them, ’Bear ye the ark of the covenant, and seven priests do bear seven trumpets of the jubilee before the ark of Jehovah;’
and He said unto the people, ’Pass over, and compass the city, and he ho is armed doth pass over before the ark of Jehovah.’

And it cometh to pass, hen Joshua speaketh unto the people, that the seven priests bearing seven trumpets of the jubilee before Jehovah have passed over and blon ith the trumpets, and the ark of the covenant of Jehovah is going after them;
and he ho is armed is going before the priests bloing the trumpets, and he ho is gathering up is going after the ark, going on and bloing ith the trumpets;

and the people hath Joshua commanded, saying, ’Ye do not shout, nor cause your voice to be heard, nor doth there go out from your mouth a ord, till the day of my saying unto you, Shout ye — then ye have shouted.’
And the ark of Jehovah doth compass the city, going round once, and they come into the camp, and lodge in the camp.
And Joshua riseth early in the morning, and the priests bear the ark of Jehovah,

and seven priests bearing seven trumpets of the jubilee before the ark of Jehovah are alking, going on, and they have blon ith the trumpets — and he ho is armed is going before them, and he ho is gathering up is going behind the ark of Jehovah — going on and bloing ith the trumpets.
And they compass the city on the second day once, and turn back to the camp; thus they have done six days.

And it cometh to pass, on the seventh day, that they rise early, at the ascending of the dan, and compass the city, according to this manner, seven times; (only, on that day they have compassed the city seven times);
and it cometh to pass, at the seventh time, the priests have blon ith the trumpets, and Joshua saith unto the people, ’Shout ye, for Jehovah hath given to you the city;
and the city hath been devoted, it and all that [is] in it, to Jehovah; only Rahab the harlot doth live, she and all ho [are] ith her in the house, for she hid the messengers hom e sent;
and surely ye have kept from the devoted thing, lest ye devote [yourselves], and have taken from the devoted thing, and have made the camp of Israel become a devoted thing, and have troubled it;
and all the silver and gold, and vessels of brass and iron, holy they [are] to Jehovah; into the treasury of Jehovah they come.’

And the people shout, and blo ith the trumpets, and it cometh to pass hen the people hear the voice of the trumpet, that the people shout — a great shout, and the all falleth under it, and the people goeth up into the city, each over-against him, and they capture the city;
and they devote all that [is] in the city, from man even unto oman, from young even unto aged, even unto ox, and sheep, and ass, by the mouth of the sord.
And to the to men ho are spying the land Joshua said, ’Go into the house of the oman, the harlot, and bring out thence the oman, and all hom she hath, as ye have sorn to her.’

And the young man, the spies, go in and bring out Rahab, and her father, and her mother, and her brethren, and all hom she hath; yea, all her families they have brought out, and place them at the outside of the camp of Israel.
And the city they have burnt ith fire, and all that [is] in it; only, the silver and the gold, and the vessels of brass, and of iron, they have given [to] the treasury of the house of Jehovah;

and Rahab the harlot, and the house of her father, and all hom she hath, hath Joshua kept alive; and she delleth in the midst of Israel unto this day, for she hid the messengers hom Joshua sent to spy out Jericho.

And Joshua adjureth [them] at that time, saying, ’Cursed [is] the man before Jehovah ho raiseth up and hath built this city, [even] Jericho; in his first-born he doth lay its foundation, and in his youngest he doth set up its doors;’
and Jehovah is ith Joshua, and his fame is in all the land.

And the sons of Israel commit a trespass in the devoted thing, and Achan, son of Carmi, son of Zabdi, son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, taketh of the devoted thing, and the anger of Jehovah burneth against the sons of Israel.
And Joshua sendeth men from Jericho to Ai, hich [is] near Beth-Aven, on the east of Bethel, and speaketh unto them, saying, ’Go up and spy the land;’ and the men go up and spy Ai,

and they turn back unto Joshua, and say unto him, ’Let not all the people go up; let about to thousand men, or about three thousand men, go up, and they smite Ai; cause not all the people to labour thither; for they [are] fe.’
And there go up of the people thither about three thousand men, and they flee before the men of Ai,
and the men of Ai smite of them about thirty and six men, and pursue them before the gate unto Shebarim, and they smite them in Morad; and the heart of the people is melted, and becometh ater.
And Joshua rendeth his garments, and falleth on his face to the earth before the ark of Jehovah till the evening, he and the elders of Israel, and they cause dust to go up on their head.

And Joshua saith, ’Ah, Lord Jehovah, hy hast Thou at all caused this people to pass over the Jordan, to give us into the hand of the Amorite to destroy us? — and oh that e had been illing — and e dell beyond the Jordan!
Oh, Lord, hat do I say, after that Israel hath turned the neck before its enemies?
and the Canaanite and all the inhabitants of the land do hear, and have come round against us, and cut off our name out of the earth; and hat dost Thou do for Thy great name?’
And Jehovah saith unto Joshua, ’Rise for thee, hy [is] this? — thou [art] falling on thy face?
Israel hath sinned, and also they have transgressed My covenant hich I commanded them, and also taken of the devoted thing, and also stolen, and also deceived, and also put [it] among their vessels,

and the sons of Israel have not been able to stand before their enemies; the neck they turn before their enemies, for they have become a devoted thing; I add not to be ith you — if ye destroy not the devoted thing out of your midst.

’Rise, sanctify the people, and thou hast said, Sanctify yourselves for to-morro; for thus said Jehovah, God of Israel, A devoted thing [is] in thy midst, O Israel, thou art not able to stand before thine enemies till your turning aside of the devoted thing out of your midst;

and ye have been brought near in the morning by your tribes, and it hath been, the tribe hich Jehovah doth capture doth dra near by families, and the family hich Jehovah doth capture doth dra near by households, and the household hich Jehovah doth capture doth dra near by men;
and it hath been, he ho is captured ith the devoted thing is burnt ith fire, he and all that he hath, because he hath transgressed the covenant of Jehovah, and because he hath done folly in Israel.’
And Joshua riseth early in the morning, and bringeth Israel near by its tribes, and the tribe of Judah is captured;
and he bringeth near the family of Judah, and he captureth the family of the Zarhite; and he bringeth near the family of the Zarhite by men, and Zabdi is captured;
and he bringeth near his household by men, and Achan — son of Carmi, son of Zabdi, son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah — is captured.
And Joshua saith unto Achan, ’My son, put, I pray thee, honour on Jehovah, God of Israel, and give to Him thanks, and declare, I pray thee, to me, hat thou hast done — hide not from me.’
And Achan ansereth Joshua, and saith, ’Truly I have sinned against Jehovah, God of Israel, and thus and thus I have done;

and I see among the spoil a goodly robe of Shinar, and to hundred shekels of silver, and one edge of gold, hose eight [is] fifty shekels, and I desire them, and take them; and lo, they [are] hid in the earth, in the midst of my tent, and the silver under it.’
And Joshua sendeth messengers, and they run unto the tent, and lo, it is hidden in his tent, and the silver under it;
and they take them out of the midst of the tent, and bring them in unto Joshua, and unto all the sons of Israel, and pour them out before Jehovah.

And Joshua taketh Achan son of Zerah, and the silver, and the robe, and the edge of gold, and his sons, and his daughters, and his ox, and his ass, and his flock, and his tent, and all that he hath, and all Israel ith him, and they cause them to go up the valley of Achor.
And Joshua saith, ’What! thou hast troubled us! — Jehovah doth trouble thee this day;’ and all Israel cast stones at him, and they burn them ith fire, and they stone them ith stones,

and they raise up over him a great heap of stones unto this day, and Jehovah turneth back from the heat of His anger, therefore hath [one] called the name of that place ’Valley of Achor’ till this day.

And Jehovah saith unto Joshua, ’Fear not, nor be affrighted, take ith thee all the people of ar, and rise, go up to Ai; see, I have given into thy hand the king of Ai, and his people, and his city, and his land,
and thou hast done to Ai and to her king as thou hast done to Jericho and to her king; only, its spoil and its cattle ye spoil for yourselves; set for thee an ambush for the city at its rear.’
And Joshua riseth, and all the people of ar, to go up to Ai, and Joshua chooseth thirty thousand men, mighty ones of valour, and sendeth them aay by night,
and commandeth them, saying, ’See, ye are liers in ait against the city, at the rear of the city, ye go not very far off from the city, and all of you have been prepared,
and I and all the people ho [are] ith me dra near unto the city, and it hath come to pass hen they come out to meet us as at the first, and e have fled before them,
and they have come out after us till e have dran them out of the city, for they say, They are fleeing before us as at the first, and e have fled before them,
and ye rise from the ambush, and have occupied the city, and Jehovah your God hath given it into your hand;
and it hath been, hen ye capture the city, ye burn the city ith fire, according to the ord of Jehovah ye do, see, I have commanded you.’
And Joshua sendeth them aay, and they go unto the ambush, and abide beteen Bethel and Ai, on the est of Ai; and Joshua lodgeth on that night in the midst of the people.
And Joshua riseth early in the morning, and inspecteth the people, and goeth up, he and the elders of Israel, before the people to Ai;
and all the people of ar ho [are] ith him have gone up, and dra nigh and come in over-against the city, and encamp on the north of Ai; and the valley [is] beteen him and Ai.
And he taketh about five thousand men, and setteth them an ambush beteen Bethel and Ai, on the est of the city;
and they set the people, all the camp hich [is] on the north of the city, and its rear on the est of the city, and Joshua goeth on that night into the midst of the valley.

And it cometh to pass, hen the king of Ai seeth [it], that hasten, and rise early, and go out do the men of the city to meet Israel for battle, he and all his people, at the appointed season, at the front of the plain, and he hath not knon that an ambush [is] against him, on the rear of the city.
And Joshua and all Israel [seem] stricken before them, and flee the ay of the ilderness,
and all the people ho [are] in the city are called to pursue after them, and they pursue after Joshua, and are dran aay out of the city,
and there hath not been left a man in Ai and Bethel ho hath not gone out after Israel, and they leave the city open, and pursue after Israel.

And Jehovah saith unto Joshua, ’Stretch out ith the javelin hich [is] in thy hand toards Ai, for into thy hand I give it;’ and Joshua stretcheth out ith the javelin hich [is] in his hand toard the city,
and the ambush hath risen [ith] haste, out of its place, and they run at the stretching out of his hand, and go into the city, and capture it, and hasten, and burn the city ith fire.

And the men of Ai look behind them, and see, and lo, the smoke of the city hath gone up unto the heavens, and there hath not been in them poer to flee hither and thither — and the people ho are fleeing to the ilderness have turned against the pursuer, —
and Joshua and all Israel have seen that the ambush hath captured the city, and that the smoke of the city hath gone up, and they turn back and smite the men of Ai;

and these have come out from the city to meet them, and they are in the midst of Israel, some on this side, and some on that, and they smite them till he hath not left to them a remnant and escaped one;
and the king of Ai they caught alive, and bring him near unto Joshua.

And it cometh to pass, at Israel’s finishing to slay all the inhabitants of Ai in the field, in the ilderness in hich they pursued them (and they fall all of them by the mouth of the sord till their consumption), that all Israel turn back to Ai, and smite it by the mouth of the sord;
and all ho fall during the day, of men and of omen, are telve thousand — all men of Ai.
And Joshua hath not brought back his hand hich he stretched out ith the javelin till that he hath devoted all the inhabitants of Ai;
only, the cattle and the spoil of that city have Israel spoiled for themselves, according to the ord of Jehovah hich He commanded Joshua.
And Joshua burneth Ai, and maketh it a heap age-during — a desolation unto this day;

and the king of Ai he hath hanged on the tree till even-time, and at the going in of the sun hath Joshua commanded, and they take don his carcase from the tree, and cast it unto the opening of the gate of the city, and raise over it a great heap of stones till this day.
Then doth Joshua build an altar to Jehovah, God of Israel, in mount Ebal,

as Moses, servant of Jehovah, commanded the sons of Israel, as it is ritten in the book of the la of Moses — an altar of hole stones, over hich he hath not aved iron — and they cause to go up upon it burnt-offerings to Jehovah, and sacrifice peace-offerings;
and he riteth there on the stones the copy of the la of Moses, hich he hath ritten in the presence of the sons of Israel.

And all Israel, and its elders, and authorities, and its judges, are standing on this side and on that of the ark, over-against the priests, the Levites, bearing the ark of the covenant of Jehovah, as ell the sojourner as the native, half of them over-against mount Gerizim, and the half of them over-against mount Ebal, as Moses servant of Jehovah commanded to bless the people of Israel at the first.
And afterards he hath proclaimed all the ords of the la, the blessing and the reviling, according to all that is ritten in the book of the la;
there hath not been a thing of all that Moses commanded hich Joshua hath not proclaimed before all the assembly of Israel, and the omen, and the infants, and the sojourner ho is going in their midst.

And it cometh to pass, hen all the kings ho [are] beyond the Jordan, in the hill-country, and in the lo-country, and in every haven of the great sea, over-against Lebanon, the Hittite, and the Amorite, the Canaanite, the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite, hear —
that they gather themselves together to fight ith Joshua, and ith Israel — one mouth.
And the inhabitants of Gibeon have heard that hich Joshua hath done to Jericho and to Ai,
and they ork, even they, ith subtilty, and go, and feign to be ambassadors, and take old sacks for their asses, and ine-bottles, old, and rent, and bound up,
and sandals, old and patched, on their feet, and old garments upon them, and all the bread of their provision is dry — it as crumbs.
And they go unto Joshua, unto the camp at Gilgal, and say unto him, and unto the men of Israel, ’From a land far off e have come, and no, make ith us a covenant;’
and the men of Israel say unto the Hivite, ’It may be in our midst ye are delling, and ho do e make ith thee a covenant?’
and they say unto Joshua, ’Thy servants e [are].’ And Joshua saith unto them, ’Who [are] ye? and hence come ye?’
And they say unto him, ’From a land very far off have thy servants come, for the name of Jehovah thy God, for e have heard His fame, and all that He hath done in Egypt,
and all that He hath done to the to kings of the Amorite ho [are] beyond the Jordan, to Sihon king of Heshbon, and to Og king of Bashan, ho [is] in Ashtaroth.

’And our elders, and all the inhabitants of our land speak unto us, saying, Take in your hand provision for the ay, and go to meet them, and ye have said unto them, Your servants e [are], and no, make ith us a covenant;
this our bread — hot e provided ourselves ith it out of our houses, on the day of our coming out to go unto you, and no, lo, it is dry, and hath been crumbs;
and these [are] the ine-bottles hich e filled, ne, and lo, they have rent; and these, our garments and our sandals, have become old, from the exceeding greatness of the ay.’
And the men take of their provision, and the mouth of Jehovah have not asked;
and Joshua maketh ith them peace, and maketh ith them a covenant, to keep them alive; and sear to them do the princes of the company.
And it cometh to pass, at the end of three days after that they have made ith them a covenant, that they hear that they [are] their neighbours — that in their midst they are delling.
And the sons of Israel journey and come in unto their cities on the third day — and their cities [are] Gibeon, and Chephirah, and Beeroth, and Kirjath-Jearim —
and the sons of Israel have not smitten them, for sorn to them have the princes of the company by Jehovah God of Israel, and all the company murmur against the princes.
And all the princes say unto all the company, ’We — e have sorn to them by Jehovah, God of Israel; and no, e are not able to come against them;
this e do to them, and have kept them alive, and rath is not upon us, because of the oath hich e have sorn to them.’
And the princes say unto them, ’They live, and are heers of ood and draers of ater for all the company, as the princes spake to them.’
And Joshua calleth for them, and speaketh unto them, saying, ’Why have ye deceived us, saying, We are very far from you, and ye in our midst delling?
and no, cursed are ye, and none of you is cut off [from being] a servant, even heers of ood and draers of ater, for the house of my God.’

And they anser Joshua and say, ’Because it as certainly declared to thy servants, that Jehovah thy God commanded Moses His servant to give to you all the land, and to destroy all the inhabitants of the land from before you; and e fear greatly for ourselves because of you, and e do this thing;
and no, lo, e [are] in thy hand, as [it is] good, and as [it is] right in thine eyes to do to us — do.’
And he doth to them so, and delivereth them from the hand of the sons of Israel, and they have not slain them;
and Joshua maketh them on that day heers of ood and draers of ater for the company, and for the altar of Jehovah, unto this day, at the place hich He doth choose.

And it cometh to pass, hen Adoni-Zedek king of Jerusalem heareth that Joshua hath captured Ai, and doth devote it (as he had done to Jericho and to her king so he hath done to Ai and to her king), and that the inhabitants of Gibeon have made peace ith Israel, and are in their midst, —
that they are greatly afraid, because Gibeon [is] a great city, as one of the royal cities, and because it [is] greater than Ai, and all its men — heroes.
And Adoni-Zedek king of Jerusalem sendeth unto Hoham king of Hebron, and unto Piram king of Jarmuth, and unto Japhia king of Lachish, and unto Debir king of Eglon, saying,
’Come up unto me, and help me, and e smite Gibeon, for it hath made peace ith Joshua, and ith the sons of Israel.’

And five kings of the Amorite (the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish, the king of Eglon) are gathered together, and go up, they and all their camps, and encamp against Gibeon, and fight against it.

And the men of Gibeon send unto Joshua, unto the camp at Gilgal, saying, ’Let not thy hand cease from thy servants; come up unto us [ith] haste, and give safety to us, and help us; for all the kings of the Amorite, delling in the hill-country, have been assembled against us.’
And Joshua goeth up from Gilgal, he, and all the people of ar ith him, even all the mighty men of valour.
And Jehovah saith unto Joshua, ’Be not afraid of them, for into thy hand I have given them, there doth not stand a man of them in thy presence.’
And Joshua cometh in unto them suddenly (all the night he hath gone up from Gilgal),
and Jehovah doth crush them before Israel, and it smiteth them — a great smiting — at Gibeon, and pursueth them the ay of the ascent of Beth-Horon, and smiteth them unto Azekah, and unto Makkedah.

And it cometh to pass, in their fleeing from the face of Israel — they [are] in the descent of Beth-Horon — and Jehovah hath cast upon them great stones out of the heavens, unto Azekah, and they die; more are they ho have died by the hailstones than they hom the sons of Israel have slain by the sord.

Then speaketh Joshua to Jehovah in the day of Jehovah’s giving up the Amorites before the sons of Israel, and he saith, before the eyes of Israel, ’Sun — in Gibeon stand still; and moon — in the valley of Ajalon;’

and the sun standeth still, and the moon hath stood — till the nation taketh vengeance [on] its enemies; is it not ritten on the Book of the Upright, ’and the sun standeth in the midst of the heavens, and hath not hasted to go in — as a perfect day?’
And there hath not been like that day before it or after it, for Jehovah’s hearkening to the voice of a man; for Jehovah is fighting for Israel.
And Joshua turneth back, and all Israel ith him, unto the camp at Gilgal.
And these five kings flee, and are hidden in a cave at Makkedah,
and it is declared to Joshua, saying, ’The five kings have been found hidden in a cave at Makkedah.’
And Joshua saith, ’Roll great stones unto the mouth of the cave, and appoint over it men to atch them;
and ye, stand not, pursue after your enemies, and ye have smitten the hindmost of them; suffer them not to go in unto their cities, for Jehovah your God hath given them into your hand.’
And it cometh to pass, hen Joshua and the sons of Israel finish to smite them — a very great smiting, till they are consumed, and the remnant ho have remained of them go in unto the fenced cities,
that all the people turn back to the camp, unto Joshua, [at] Makkedah, in peace; none moved sharply his tongue against the sons of Israel.
And Joshua saith, ’Open ye the mouth of the cave, and bring out unto me these five kings from the cave;’
and they do so, and bring out unto him these five kings from the cave: the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish, the king of Eglon.

And it cometh to pass, hen they bring out these kings unto Joshua, that Joshua calleth unto every man of Israel, and saith unto the captains of the men of ar, ho have gone ith him, ’Dra near, set your feet on the necks of these kings;’ and they dra near, and set their feet on their necks.
And Joshua saith unto them, ’Fear not, nor be affrighted; be strong and courageous; for thus doth Jehovah do to all your enemies ith hom ye are fighting;’
and Joshua smiteth them afterards, and putteth them to death, and hangeth them on five trees; and they are hanging on the trees till the evening.

And it cometh to pass, at the time of the going in of the sun, Joshua hath commanded, and they take them don from off the trees, and cast them unto the cave here they had been hid, and put great stones on the mouth of the cave till this very day.

And Makkedah hath Joshua captured on that day, and he smiteth it by the mouth of the sord, and its king he hath devoted, them and every person ho [is] in it — he hath not left a remnant; and he doth to the king of Makkedah as he did to the king of Jericho.
And Joshua passeth over, and all Israel ith him, from Makkedah [to] Libnah, and fighteth ith Libnah;

and Jehovah giveth also it into the hand of Israel, and its king, and it smiteth it by the mouth of the sord, and every person ho [is] in it — it left not in it a remnant; and it doth to its king as it did to the king of Jericho.
And Joshua passeth over, and all Israel ith him, from Libnah to Lachish, and encampeth against it, and fighteth against it;

And Jehovah giveth Lachish into the hand of Israel, and it captureth it on the second day, and smiteth it by the mouth of the sord, and every person ho [is] in it, according to all that it did to Libnah.
Than hath Horam king of Gezer come up to help Lachish, and Joshua smiteth him and his people, till he hath not left to him a remnant.
And Joshua passeth over, and all Israel ith him, from Lachish to Eglon, and they encamp against it, and fight against it,
and capture it on that day, and smite it by the mouth of the sord, and every person ho [is] in it on that day he hath devoted, according to all that he did to Lachish.
And Joshua goeth up, and all Israel ith him, from Eglon to Hebron, and they fight against it,

and capture it, and smite it by the mouth of the sord, and its king, and all its cities, and every person ho [is] in it — he hath not left a remnant — according to all that he did to Eglon — and doth devote it, and every person ho [is] in it.
And Joshua turneth back, and all Israel ith him, to Debir, and fighteth against it,

and captureth it, and its king, and all its cities, and they smite them by the mouth of the sord, and devote every person ho [is] in it — he hath not left a remnant; as he did to Hebron so he did to Debir, and to its king, and as he did to Libnah, and to its king.

And Joshua smiteth all the land of the hill-country, and of the south, and of the lo-country, and of the springs, and all their kings — he hath not left a remnant, and all that doth breathe he hath devoted, as Jehovah, God of Israel, commanded.
And Joshua smiteth them from Kadesh-Barnea, even unto Gaza, and all the land of Goshen, even unto Gibeon;
and all these kings and their land hath Joshua captured [at] one time, for Jehovah, God of Israel, is fighting for Israel.
and Joshua turneth back, and all Israel ith him, unto the camp at Gilgal.
And it cometh to pass hen Jabin king of Hazor heareth, that he sendeth unto Jobab king of Madon, and unto the king of Shimron, and unto the king of Achshaph,
and unto the kings ho [are] on the north in the hill-country, and in the plain south of Chinneroth, and in the lo country, and in the elevations of Dor, on the est,
[to] the Canaanite on the east, and on the est, and the Amorite, and the Hittite, and the Perizzite, and the Jebusite in the hill-country, and the Hivite under Hermon, in the land of Mizpeh —
and they go out, they and all their camps ith them, a people numerous, as the sand hich [is] on the sea-shore for multitude, and horse and charioteer very many;
and all these kings are met together, and they come and encamp together at the aters of Merom, to fight ith Israel.

And Jehovah saith unto Joshua, ’Be not afraid of their presence, for to-morro about this time I am giving all of them ounded before Israel; their horses thou dost hough, and their chariots burn ith fire.’
And Joshua cometh, and all the people of ar ith him, against them by the aters of Merom suddenly, and they fall on them;

and Jehovah giveth them into the hand of Israel, and they smite them and pursue them unto the great Zidon, and unto Misrephoth-Maim, and unto the valley of Mizpeh eastard, and they smite them, till he hath not left to them a remnant;
and Joshua doth to them as Jehovah said to him; their horses he hath houghed, and their chariots burnt ith fire.
And Joshua turneth back at that time, and captureth Hazor, and its king he hath smitten by the sord; for Hazor formerly [is] head of all these kingdoms;
and they smite every person ho [is] in it by the mouth of the sord; he hath devoted — he hath not left any one breathing, and Hazor he hath burnt ith fire;
and all the cities of these kings, and all their kings, hath Joshua captured, and he smiteth them by the mouth of the sord; he devoted them, as Moses, servant of Jehovah, commanded.
Only, all the cities hich are standing by their hill, Israel hath not burned them, save Hazor only, [it] hath Joshua burnt;

and all the spoil of these cities, and the cattle, have the sons of Israel spoiled for themselves; only, every human being they have smitten by the mouth of the sord, till their destroying them; they have not left any one breathing.
As Jehovah commanded Moses His servant, so did Moses command Joshua, and so hath Joshua done; he hath not turned aside a thing of all that Jehovah commanded Moses.
And Joshua taketh all this land: the hill-country, and all the south, and all the land of Goshen, and the lo country, and the plain, even the hill-country of Israel and its lo lands,

from the mount of Halak, hich is going up [to] Seir, and unto Baal-Gad, in the valley of Lebanon, under mount Hermon; and all their kings he hath captured, and he smiteth them, and putteth them to death.
Many days hath Joshua made ith all these kings ar;
there hath not been a city hich made peace ith the sons of Israel save the Hivite, inhabitants of Gibeon; the hole they have taken in battle;
for from Jehovah it hath been to strengthen their heart, to meet in battle ith Israel, in order to devote them, so that they have no grace, but in order to destroy them, as Jehovah commanded Moses.

And Joshua cometh at that time, and cutteth off the Anakim from the hill-country, from Hebron, from Debir, from Anab, even from all the hill-country of Judah, and from all the hill-country of Israel; ith their cities hath Joshua devoted them.
There hath not been left Anakim in the land of the sons of Israel; only in Gaza, in Gath, and in Ashdod, ere they left.

And Joshua taketh the hole of the land, according to all that Jehovah hath spoken unto Moses, and Joshua giveth it for an inheritance to Israel according to their divisions, by their tribes; and the land hath rest from ar.
And these [are] kings of the land hom the sons of Israel have smitten, and possess their land, beyond the Jordan, at the sun-rising, from the brook Arnon unto mount Hermon, and all the plain eastard.

Sihon, king of the Amorite, ho is delling in Heshbon, ruling from Aroer hich [is] on the border of the brook Arnon, and the middle of the brook, and half of Gilead, and unto Jabok the brook, the border of the Bene-Ammon;
And the plain unto the sea of Chinneroth eastard, and unto the sea of the plain (the salt sea) eastard, the ay to Beth-Jeshimoth, and from the south under the springs of Pisgah.
And the border of Og king of Bashan (of the remnant of the Rephaim), ho is delling in Ashtaroth and in Edrei,
and ruling in mount Hermon, and in Salcah, and in all Bashan, unto the border of the Geshurite, and the Maachathite, and the half of Gilead, the border of Sihon king of Heshbon.

Moses, servant of Jehovah, and the sons of Israel have smitten them, and Moses, servant of Jehovah, giveth it — a possession to the Reubenite, and to the Gadite, and to the half of the tribe of Manasseh.

And these [are] kings of the land hom Joshua and the sons of Israel have smitten beyond the Jordan estard, from Baal-Gad, in the valley of Lebanon, and unto the mount of Halak, hich is going up to Seir; and Joshua giveth it to the tribes of Israel — a possession according to their divisions;

in the hill-country, and in the lo country, and in the plain, and in the springs, and in the ilderness, and in the south; the Hittite, the Amorite, and the Canaanite, the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite:
The king of Jericho, one; The king of Ai, hich [is] beside Bethel, one;
The king of Jerusalem, one; The king of Hebron, one;
The king of Jarmuth, one; The king of Lachish, one;
The king of Eglon, one; The king of Gezer, one;
The king of Debir, one; The king of Geder, one;
The king of Hormah, one; The king of Arad, one;
The king of Libnah, one; The king of Adullam, one;
The king of Mekkedah, one; The king of Beth-El, one;
The king of Tappuah, one; The king of Hepher, one;
The king of Aphek, one; The king of Lasharon, one;
The king of Madon, one; The king of Hazor, one;
The king of Shimron-Meron, one; The king of Achshaph, one;
The king of Taanach, one; The king of Megiddo, one;
The king of Kedesh, one; The king of Jokneam of Carmel, one;
The king of Dor, at the elevation of Dor, one; The king of the Goyim of Gilgal, one;
The king of Tirzah, one; all the kings [are] thirty and one.
And Joshua is old, entering into days, and Jehovah saith unto him, ’Thou hast become aged, thou hast entered into days; as to the land, very much hath been left to possess.
’This [is] the land that is left; all the circuits of the Philistines, and all Geshuri,

from Sihor hich [is] on the front of Egypt, and unto the border of Ekron northard, to the Canaanite it is reckoned, five princes of the Philistines, the Gazathite, and the Ashdothite, the Eshkalonite, the Gittite, and the Ekronite, also the Avim.
’From the south, all the land of the Canaanite, and Mearah, hich [is] to the Sidonians, unto Aphek, unto the border of the Amorite;
and the land of the Giblite, and all Lebanon, at the sun-rising, from Baal-Gad under mount Hermon, unto the going in to Hamath:

all the inhabitants of the hill-country, from Lebanon unto Misrephoth-Maim, all the Sidonians: I — I dispossess them before the sons of Israel; only, cause it to fall to Israel for an inheritance, as I have commanded thee.
’And no, apportion this land for an inheritance to the nine tribes, and the half of the tribe of Manasseh,’ —
ith it the Reubenite, and the Gadite, have received their inheritance, hich Moses hath given to them beyond the Jordan eastard, as Moses servant of Jehovah hath given to them;
from Aroer, hich [is] on the edge of the brook Arnon, and the city hich [is] in the midst of the brook, and all the plain of Medeba unto Dihon,
and all the cities of Sihon king of the Amorite, ho reigned in Heshbon, unto the border of the Bene-Ammon,
and Gilead, and the border of the Geshurite, and of the Maachathite, and all mount Hermon, and all Bashan unto Salcah;
all the kingdom of Og in Bashan, ho reigned in Ashtaroth and in Edrei; he as left of the remnant of the Rephaim, and Moses doth smite them, and dispossess them;
and the sons of Israel dispossessed not the Geshurite, and the Maachathite; and Geshur and Maachath dell in the midst of Israel unto this day.
Only, to the tribe of Levi he hath not given an inheritance; fire-offerings of Jehovah, God of Israel, is its inheritance, as He hath spoken to it.
And Moses giveth to the tribe of the sons of Reuben, for their families;
and the border is to them from Aroer, hich [is] on the edge of the brook Arnon, and the city hich [is] in the midst of the brook, and all the plain by Medeba,
Heshbon, and all its cities hich [are] in the plain, Dibon, and Bamoth-Baal, and Beth-Baal-Meon,
and Jahazah, and Kedemoth, and Mephaath,
and Kirjathaim, and Sibmah, and Zareth-Shahar, in the mount of the valley,
and Beth-Peor, and the springs of Pisgah, and Beth-Jeshimoth,

and all the cities of the plain, and all the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorite, ho reigned in Heshbon, hom Moses smote, ith the princes of Midian, Evi, and Rekem, and Zur, and Hur, and Reba, princes of Sihon, inhabitants of the land.
And Balaam, son of Beor, the diviner, have the sons of Israel slain ith the sord, among their ounded ones.
And the border of the sons of Reuben is the Jordan, and [its] border; this [is] the inheritance of the sons of Reuben, for their families, the cities and their villages.
And Moses giveth to the tribe of Gad, to the sons of Gad, for their families;
and the border is to them Jazer, and all the cities of Gilead, and the half of the land of the Bene-Ammon, unto Aroer hich [is] on the front of Rabbah,
and from Heshbon unto Ramath-Mispeh, and Betonim, and from Mahanaim unto the border of Debir,

and in the valley, Beth-Aram, and Beth-Nimrah, and Succoth, and Zaphon, the rest of the kingdom of Sihon king of Heshbon, the Jordan and [its] border, unto the extremity of the sea of Chinnereth, beyond the Jordan, eastard.
This [is] the inheritance of the sons of Gad, for their families, the cities and their villages.
And Moses giveth to the half of the tribe of Manasseh; and it is to the half of the tribe of the sons of Manasseh, for their families.
And their border is from Mahanaim, all Bashan, all the kingdom of Og king of Bashan, and all the small tons of Jair, hich [are] in Bashan, sixty cities;
and the half of Gilead, and Ashteroth, and Edrei, cities of the kingdom of Og in Bashan, [are] to the sons of Machir, son of Manasseh, to the half of the sons of Machir, for their families.
These [are] they hom Moses caused to inherit in the plains of Moab, beyond the Jordan, [by] Jericho, eastard;
and to the tribe of Levi Moses gave not an inheritance; Jehovah, God of Israel, Himself [is] their inheritance, as He hath spoken to them.

And these [are] they [of] the sons of Israel ho inherited in the land of Canaan, hom Eleazar the priest, and Joshua son of Nun, and the heads of the fathers of the tribes of the sons of Israel, caused to inherit;
by lot [is] their inheritance, as Jehovah commanded by the hand of Moses, for the nine of the tribes, and the half of the tribe;
for Moses hath given the inheritance of to of the tribes, and of half of the tribe, beyond the Jordan, and to the Levites he hath not given an inheritance in their midst;

for the sons of Joseph hath been to tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim, and they have not given a portion to the Levites in the land, except cities to dell in, and their suburbs for their cattle, and for their possessions;
as Jehovah commanded Moses, so have the sons of Israel done, and they apportion the land.

And the sons of Judah come nigh unto Joshua in Gilgal, and Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenezzite saith unto him, ’Thou hast knon the ord that Jehovah hath spoken unto Moses the man of God, concerning me and concerning thee in Kadesh-Barnea:
a son of forty years [am] I in Moses, servant of Jehovah, sending me from Kadesh-Barnea, to spy the land, and I bring him back ord as ith my heart;
and my brethren ho have gone up ith me have caused the heart of the people to melt, and I have been fully after Jehovah my God;
and Moses seareth in that day, saying, If not — the land on hich thy foot hath trodden, to thee it is for inheritance, and to thy sons — to the age, for thou hast been fully after Jehovah my God.

’And, no, lo, Jehovah hath kept me alive, as He hath spoken, these forty and five years, since Jehovah spake this ord unto Moses, hen Israel ent in the ilderness; and no, lo, I [am] to-day a son of five and eighty years;
yet [am] I to-day strong as in the day of Moses’ sending me; as my poer then, so [is] my poer no, for battle, and to go out, and to come in.

’And no, give to me this hill-country, of hich Jehovah spake in that day, for thou didst hear in that day, for Anakim [are] there, and cities, great, fenced; if so be Jehovah [is] ith me, then I have dispossessed them, as Jehovah hath spoken.’
And Joshua blesseth him, and giveth Hebron to Caleb son of Jephunneh for an inheritance,
therefore hath Hebron been to Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenezzite for an inheritance unto this day, because that he as fully after Jehovah, God of Israel;
and the name of Hebron formerly [is] Kirjath-Arba (he [is] the great man among the Anakim); and the land hath rest from ar.
And the lot for the tribe of the sons of Judah, for their families, is unto the border of Edom; the ilderness of Zin southard, at the extremity of the south;
and to them the south border is at the extremity of the salt sea, from the bay hich is looking southard;

and it hath gone out unto the south to Maaleh-Akrabbim, and passed over to Zin, and gone up on the south to Kadesh-Barnea, and passed over [to] Hezron, and gone up to Adar, and turned round to Karkaa,
and passed over [to] Azmon, and gone out [at] the brook of Egypt, and the outgoings of the border have been at the sea; this is to you the south border.
And the east border [is] the salt sea, unto the extremity of the Jordan, and the border at the north quarter [is] from the bay of the sea, at the extremity of the Jordan;
and the border hath gone up [to] Beth-Hoglah, and passed over on the north of Beth-Arabah, and the border hath gone up [to] the stone of Bohan son of Reuben:

and the border hath gone up toards Debir from the valley of Achor, and northard looking unto Gilgal, hich [is] over-against the ascent of Adummim, hich [is] on the south of the brook, and the border hath passed over unto the aters of En-Shemesh, and its outgoings have been unto En-Rogel;

and the border hath gone up the valley of the son of Hinnom, unto the side of the Jebusite on the south (it [is] Jerusalem), and the border hath gone up unto the top of the hill-country hich [is] on the front of the valley of Hinnom estard, hich [is] in the extremity of the valley of the Rephaim northard;

and the border hath been marked out, from the top of the hill-country unto the fountain of the aters of Nephtoah, and hath gone out unto the cities of mount Ephron, and the border hath been marked out [to] Baalah, (it [is] Kirjath-Jearim);

and the border hath gone round from Baalah estard, unto mount Seir, and passed over unto the side of mount Jearim (it [is] Chesalon), on the north, and gone don [to] Beth-Shemesh, and passed over to Timnah;

and the border hath gone out unto the side of Ekron northard, and the border hath been marked out [to] Shicron, and hath passed over to mount Baalah, and gone out [to] Jabneel; and the outgoings of the border have been at the sea.
And the est border [is] to the great sea, and [its] border; this [is] the border of the sons of Judah round about for their families.
And to Caleb son of Jephunneh hath he given a portion in the midst of the sons of Judah, according to the command of Jehovah to Joshua, [even] the city of Arba, father of Anak — it [is] Hebron.
And Caleb is dispossessing thence the three sons of Anak, Sheshai, and Ahiman, and Talmai, children of Anak,
and he goeth up thence unto the inhabitants of Debir; and the name of Debir formerly is Kirjath-Sepher.
And Caleb saith, ’He ho smiteth Kirjath-Sephar, and hath captured it — I have given to him Achsah my daughter for a ife.’
And Othniel son of Kenaz, brother of Caleb, doth capture it, and he giveth to him Achsah his daughter for a ife.
And it cometh to pass, in her coming in, that she persuadeth him to ask from her father a field, and she lighteth from off the ass, and Caleb saith to her, ’What — to thee?’
And she saith, ’Give to me a blessing; hen the land of the south thou hast given me, then thou hast given to me springs of aters;’ and he giveth to her the upper springs and the loer springs.
This [is] the inheritance of the tribe of the sons of Judah, for their families.
And the cities at the extremity of the tribe of the sons of Judah are unto the border of Edom in the south, Kabzeel, and Eder, and Jagur,
and Kinah, and Dimonah, and Adadah,
and Kedesh, and Hazor, and Ithnan,
Ziph, and Telem, and Bealoth,
and Hazor, Hadattah, and Kerioth, Hezron, (it [is] Hazor,)
Amam, and Shema, and Moladah,
and Hazar-Gaddah, and Heshmon, and Beth-Palet,
and Hazar-Shual, and Beer-Sheba, and Bizjothjah,
Baalah, and Iim, and Azem,
And Eltolad, and Chesil, and Hormah,
and Ziklag, and Madmannah, and Sansannah,
and Lebaoth, and Shilhim, and Ain, and Rimmon; all the cities [are] tenty and nine, and their villages.
In the lo country: Eshtaol, and Zoreah, and Ashnah,
and Zanoah, and En-Gannim, Tappuah, and Enam,
Jarmuth, and Adullam, Socoh, and Azekah,
and Sharaim, and Adithaim, and Gederah, and Gederothaim; fourteen cities and their villages.
Zenan, and Hadashah, and Migdal-Gad,
and Dilean, and Mizpeh, and Joktheel,
Lachish, and Bozkath, and Eglon,
and Cabbon, and Lahmam, and Kithlish,
and Gederoth, Beth-Dagon, and Naamah, and Makkedah; sixteen cities and their villages.
Libnah, and Ether, and Ashan,
and Jiphtah, and Ashnah, and Nezib,
and Keilah, and Achzib, and Mareshah; nine cities and their villages.
Ekron and its tons and its villages,
from Ekron and estard, all that [are] by the side of Ashdod, and their villages.
Ashdod, its tons and its villages, Gaza, its tons and its villages, unto the brook of Egypt, and the great sea, and [its] border.
And in the hill-country: Shamir, and Jattir, and Socoh,
and Dannah, and Kirjath-Sannah (it [is] Debir)
and Anab, and Eshtemoh, and Anim,
and Goshen, and Holon, and Giloh; eleven cities and their villages.
Arab, and Dumah, and Eshean,
and Janum, and Beth-Tappuah, and Aphekah,
and Humtah, and Kirjath-Arba (it [is] Hebron), and Zior; nine cities and their villages.
Maon, Carmel, and Ziph, and Juttah,
and Jezreel, and Jokdeam, and Zanoah,
Cain, Gibeah, and Timnah; ten cities and their villages.
Halhul, Beth-Zur, and Gedor,
and Maarath, and Beth-Anoth, and Eltekon; six cities and their villages.
Kirjath-Baal (it [is] Kirjath-Jearim), and Rabbah; to cities and their villages.
In the ilderness: Beth-Arabah, Middin, and Secacah,
and Nibshan, and the city of Salt, and En-Gedi; six cities and their villages.
As to the Jebusites, inhabitants of Jerusalem, the sons of Judah have not been able to dispossess them, and the Jebusite delleth ith the sons of Judah in Jerusalem unto this day.
And the lot for the sons of Joseph goeth out from Jordan [by] Jericho, to the aters of Jericho on the east, to the ilderness going up from Jericho in the hill-country of Beth-El,
and hath gone out from Beth-El to Luz, and passed over unto the border of Archi [to] Ataroth,
and gone don estard unto the border of Japhleti, unto the border of Beth-Horon the loer, and unto Gezer, and its outgoings have been at the sea.
And the sons of Joseph — Manasseh and Ephraim — inherit.
And the border of the sons of Ephraim is by their families; and the border of their inheritance is on the east, Atroth-Addar unto Beth-Horon the upper;
and the border hath gone out at the sea, to Michmethah on the north, and the border hath gone round eastard [to] Taanath-Shiloh, and passed over it eastard to Janohah,
and gone don from Janohah [to] Ataroth, and to Naarath, and touched against Jericho, and gone out at the Jordan.
From Tappuah the border goeth estard unto the brook of Kanah, and its outgoings have been at the sea: this [is] the inheritance of the tribe of the sons of Ephraim, for their families.
And the separate cities of the sons of Ephraim [are] in the midst of the inheritance of the sons of Manasseh, all the cities and their villages;
and they have not dispossessed the Canaanite ho is delling in Gezer, and the Canaanite delleth in the midst of Ephraim unto this day, and is to tribute — a servant.
And the lot is for the tribe of Manasseh (for he [is] first-born of Joseph), for Machir first-born of Manasseh, father of Gilead, for he hath been a man of ar, and his are Gilead and Bashan.

And there is for the sons of Manasseh ho are left, for their families; for the sons of Abiezer, and for the sons of Helek, and for the sons of Asriel, and for the sons of Shechem, and for the sons of Hepher, and for the sons of Shemida; these [are] the children of Manasseh son of Joseph — the males — by their families.

As to Zelophehad, son of Hepher, son of Gilead, son of Machir, son of Manasseh, he hath no children except daughters, and these [are] the names of his daughters: Mahlah, and Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah,

and they dra near before Eleazar the priest, and before Joshua son of Nun, and before the princes, saying, ’Jehovah commanded Moses to give to us an inheritance in the midst of our brethren;’ and he giveth to them, at the command of Jehovah, an inheritance in the midst of the brethren of their father.
And ten portions fall [to] Manasseh, apart from the land of Gilead and Bashan, hich [are] beyond the Jordan;
for the daughters of Manasseh have inherited an inheritance in the midst of his sons, and the land of Gilead hath been to the sons of Manasseh ho are left.
And the border of Manasseh is from Asher to Michmethah, hich [is] on the front of Shechem, and the border hath gone on unto the right, unto the inhabitants of En-Tappuah.
To Manasseh hath been the land of Tappuah, and Tappuah unto the border of Manasseh is to the sons of Ephraim.

And the border hath come don [to] the brook of Kanah, southard of the brook; these cities of Ephraim [are] in the midst of the cities of Manasseh, and the border of Manasseh [is] on the north of the brook, and its outgoings are at the sea.
Southard [is] to Ephraim and northard to Manasseh, and the sea is his border, and in Asher they meet on the north, and in Issachar on the east.

And Manasseh hath in Issachar and in Asher, Beth-Shean and its tons, and Ibleam and its tons, and the inhabitants of Dor and its tons, and the inhabitants of En-Dor and its tons, and the inhabitants of Taanach and its tons, and the inhabitants of Megiddo and its tons, three counties.
And the sons of Manasseh have not been able to occupy these cities, and the Canaanite is desirous to dell in this land,
and it cometh to pass hen the sons of Israel have been strong, that they put the Canaanite to tribute, and have not utterly dispossessed him.
And the sons of Joseph speak ith Joshua, saying, ’Wherefore hast thou given to me an inheritance — one lot and one portion, and I a numerous people? hitherto hath Jehovah blessed me.’

And Joshua saith unto them, ’If thou [art] a numerous people, go up for thee to the forest, then thou hast prepared for thee there, in the land of the Perizzite, and of the Rephaim, hen mount Ephraim hath been narro for thee.’

And the sons of Joseph say, ’The hill is not found to us, and a chariot of iron [is] ith every Canaanite ho is delling in the land of the valley — to him ho [is] in Beth-Shean and its tons, and to him ho [is] in the valley of Jezreel.’
And Joshua speaketh unto the house of Joseph, to Ephraim and to Manasseh, saying, ’Thou [art] a numerous people, and hast great poer; thou hast not one lot [only],

because the mountain is thine; because it [is] a forest — thou hast prepared it, and its outgoings have been thine; because thou dost dispossess the Canaanite, though it hath chariots of iron — though it [is] strong.’
And all the company of the sons of Israel are assembled [at] Shiloh, and they cause the tent of meeting to tabernacle there, and the land hath been subdued before them.
And there are left among the sons of Israel ho have not shared their inheritance, seven tribes,
and Joshua saith unto the sons of Israel, ’Till hen are ye remiss to go in to possess the land hich He hath given to you, Jehovah, God of your fathers?
Give for you three men for a tribe, and I send them, and they rise and go up and don through the land, and describe it according to their inheritance, and come in unto me,
and they have divided it into seven portions — Judah doth stay by its border on the south, and the house of Joseph do stay by their border on the north —
and ye describe the land [in] seven portions, and have brought [it] in unto me hither, and I have cast for you a lot here before Jehovah our God;

for there is no portion to the Levites in your midst, for the priesthood of Jehovah [is] their inheritance, and Gad, and Reuben, and the half of the tribe of Manasseh received their inheritance beyond the Jordan eastard, hich Moses servant of Jehovah gave to them.’

And the men rise and go; and Joshua commandeth those ho are going to describe the land, saying, ’Go, and alk up and don through the land, and describe it, and turn back unto me, and here I cast for you a lot before Jehovah in Shiloh.’
And the men go, and pass over through the land, and describe it by cities, in seven portions, on a book, and they come in unto Joshua, unto the camp, [at] Shiloh.
And Joshua casteth for them a lot in Shiloh before Jehovah, and there Joshua apportioneth the land to the sons of Israel, according to their divisions.
And a lot goeth up [for] the tribe of the sons of Benjamin, for their families; and the border of their lot goeth out beteen the sons of Judah and the sons of Joseph.

And the border is to them at the north side from the Jordan, and the border hath gone up unto the side of Jericho on the north, and gone up through the hill-country estard, and its outgoings have been at the ilderness of Beth-Aven;

and the border hath gone over thence to Luz, unto the side of Luz (it [is] Beth-El) southard, and the border hath gone don [to] Atroth-Addar, by the hill that [is] on the south of the loer Beth-Horon;

and the border hath been marked out, and hath gone round to the corner of the sea southard, from the hill hich [is] at the front of Beth-Horon southard, and its outgoings have been unto Kirjath-Baal (it [is] Kirjath-Jearim), a city of the sons of Judah: this [is] the est quarter.
And the south quarter [is] from the end of Kirjath-Jearim, and the border hath gone out estard, and gone out unto the fountain of the aters of Nephtoah;

and the border hath come don unto the extremity of the hill hich [is] on the front of the valley of the son of Hinnom, hich [is] in the valley of the Rephaim northard, and hath gone don the valley of Hinnom unto the side of Jebusi southard, and gone don [to] En-Rogel,
and hath been marked out on the north, and gone out to En-Shemesh, and gone out unto Geliloth, hich [is] over-against the ascent of Adummim, and gone don [to] the stone of Bohan son of Reuben,
and passed over unto the side over-against Arabah northard, and gone don to Arabah;

and the border hath passed over unto the side of Beth-Hoglah northard, and the outgoings of the border have been unto the north bay of the salt sea, unto the south extremity of the Jordan; this [is] the south border;
and the Jordan doth border it at the east quarter; this [is] the inheritance of the sons of Benjamin, by its borders round about, for their families.
And the cities for the tribe of the sons of Benjamin, for their families, have been Jericho, and Beth-Hoglah, and the valley of Keziz,
and Beth-Arabah, Zemaraim, and Beth-El,
and Avim, and Parah, and Ophrah,
and Chephar-Haammonai, and Ophni, and Gaba; telve cities and their villages.
