and he goeth through the ilderness, and compasseth the land of Edom and the land of Moab, and cometh in at the rising of the sun of the land of Moab, and they encamp beyond Arnon, and have not come into the border of Moab, for Arnon [is] the border of Moab.
’And Israel sendeth messengers unto Sihon, king of the Amorite, king of Heshbon, and Israel saith to him, Let us pass over, e pray thee, through thy land, unto my place,
and Sihon hath not trusted Israel to pass over through his border, and Sihon gathereth all his people, and they encamp in Jahaz, and fight ith Israel;
and Jehovah, God of Israel, giveth Sihon and all his people into the hand of Israel, and they smite them, and Israel possesseth all the land of the Amorite, the inhabitant of that land,
and they possess all the border of the Amorite from Arnon, and unto the Jabbok, and from the ilderness, and unto the Jordan.
’And no, Jehovah, God of Israel, hath dispossessed the Amorite from the presence of His people Israel, and thou ouldest possess it!
That hich Chemosh thy god causeth thee to possess — dost thou not possess it? and all that hich Jehovah our God hath dispossessed from our presence, — it e do possess.
’And no, [art] thou at all better than Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab? did he at all strive ith Israel? did he at all fight against them?

In Israel’s delling in Heshbon and in its tons, and in Aroer and in its tons, and in all the cities hich [are] by the sides of Arnon three hundred years — and herefore have ye not delivered them in that time?
And I — I have not sinned against thee, and thou art doing ith me evil — to fight against me. Jehovah, the Judge, doth judge to-day beteen the sons of Israel and the sons of Ammon.’
And the king of the Bene-Ammon hath not hearkened unto the ords of Jephthah hich he sent unto him,
and the Spirit of Jehovah is on Jephthah, and he passeth over Gilead and Manasseh, and passeth over Mizpeh of Gilead, and from Mizpeh of Gilead he hath passed over to the Bene-Ammon.
And Jephthah voeth a vo to Jehovah, and saith, ’If Thou dost at all give the Bene-Ammon into my hand —

then it hath been, that hich at all cometh out from the doors of my house to meet me in my turning back in peace from the Bene-Ammon — it hath been to Jehovah, or I have offered up for it — a burnt-offering.’
And Jephthah passeth over unto the Bene-Ammon to fight against them, and Jehovah giveth them into his hand,

and he smiteth them from Aroer, and unto thy going in to Minnith, tenty cities, and unto the meado of the vineyards — a very great smiting; and the Bene-Ammon are humbled at the presence of the sons of Israel.
And Jephthah cometh into Mizpeh, unto his house, and lo, his daughter is coming out to meet him ith timbrels, and ith choruses, and save her alone, he hath none, son or daughter.

And it cometh to pass, hen he seeth her, that he rendeth his garments, and saith, ’Alas, my daughter, thou hast caused me greatly to bend, and thou hast been among those troubling me; and I — I have opened my mouth unto Jehovah, and I am not able to turn back.’

And she saith unto him, ’My father — thou hast opened thy mouth unto Jehovah, do to me as it hath gone out from thy mouth, after that Jehovah hath done for thee vengeance on thine enemies, on the Bene-Ammon.’
And she saith unto her father, ’Let this thing be done to me; desist from me to months, and I go on, and have gone don on the hills, and I eep for my virginity — I and my friends.’
And he saith, ’Go;’ and he sendeth her aay to months, and she goeth, she and her friends, and she eepeth for her virginity on the hills;
and it cometh to pass at the end of to months that she turneth back unto her father, and he doth to her his vo hich he hath voed, and she kne not a man; and it is a statute in Israel:
from time to time the daughters of Israel go to talk to the daughter of Jephthah the Gileadite, four days in a year.

And the men of Ephraim are called together, and pass over northard, and say to Jephthah, ’Wherefore has thou passed over to fight against the Bene-Ammon, and on us hast not called to go ith thee? thy house e burn over thee ith fire.’
And Jephthah saith unto them, ’A man of great strife I have been (I and my people) ith the Bene-Ammon, and I call you, and ye have not saved me out of their hand,

and I see that thou art not a saviour, and I put my life in my hand, and pass over unto the Bene-Ammon, and Jehovah giveth them into my hand — and hy have ye come up unto me this day to fight against me?’

And Jephthah gathered all the men of Gilead, and fighteth ith Ephraim, and the men of Gilead smite Ephraim, because they said, ’Fugitives of Ephraim [are] ye Gileadites, in the midst of Ephraim — in the midst of Manasseh.’

And Gilead captureth the passages of the Jordan to Ephraim, and it hath been, hen [any of] the fugitives of Ephraim say, ’Let me pass over,’ and the men of Gilead say to him, ’An Ephramite thou?’ and he saith, ’No;’

that they say to him, ’Say, I pray thee, Shibboleth;’ and he saith, ’Sibboleth,’ and is not prepared to speak right — and they seize him, and slaughter him at the passages of the Jordan, and there fall at that time, of Ephraim, forty and to chiefs.
And Jephthah judged Israel six years, and Jephthah the Gileadite dieth, and is buried in [one of] the cities of Gilead.
And after him Ibzan of Beth-Lehem judgeth Israel,
and he hath thirty sons and thirty daughters, he hath sent ithout and thirty daughters hath brought in to his sons from ithout; and he judgeth Israel seven years.
And Ibzan dieth, and is buried in Beth-Lehem.
And after him Elon the Zebulunite judgeth Israel, and he judgeth Israel ten years,
and Elon the Zebulunite dieth, and is buried in Aijalon, in the land of Zebulun.
And after him, Abdon son of Hillel, the Pirathonite, judgeth Israel,
and he hath forty sons, and thirty grandsons, riding on seventy ass-colts, and he judgeth Israel eight years.
And Abdon son of Hillel, the Pirathonite, dieth, and is buried in Pirathon, in the land of Ephraim, in the hill-country of the Amalekite.
And the sons of Israel add to do the evil thing in the eyes of Jehovah, and Jehovah giveth them into the hand of the Philistines forty years.
And there is a certain man of Zorah, of the family of the Danite, and his name [is] Manoah, his ife [is] barren, and hath not borne;
and a messenger of Jehovah appeareth unto the oman, and saith unto her, ’Lo, I pray thee, thou [art] barren, and hast not borne; hen thou hast conceived, then thou hast borne a son.
And, no, take heed, I pray thee, and do not drink ine, and strong drink, and do not eat any unclean thing,

for, lo, thou art conceiving and bearing a son, and a razor doth not go up on his head, for a Nazarite to God is the youth from the omb, and he doth begin to save Israel out of the hand of the Philistines.’

And the oman cometh and speaketh to her husband, saying, ’A man of God hath come unto me, and his appearance [is] as the appearance of a messenger of God, very fearful, and I have not asked him hence he [is], and his name he hath not declared to me;

and he saith to me, Lo, thou art pregnant, and bearing a son, and no do not drink ine and strong drink, and do not eat any unclean thing, for a Nazarite to God is the youth from the omb till the day of his death.’
And Manoah maketh entreaty unto Jehovah, and saith, ’O, my Lord, the man of God hom Thou didst send, let him come in, I pray thee, again unto us, and direct us hat e do to the youth ho is born.’
And God hearkeneth to the voice of Manoah, and the messenger of God cometh again unto the oman, and she [is] sitting in a field, and Manoah her husband is not ith her,
and the oman hasteth, and runneth, and declareth to her husband, and saith unto him, ’Lo, he hath appeared unto me — the man ho came on [that] day unto me.’
And Manoah riseth, and goeth after his ife, and cometh unto the man, and saith to him, ’Art thou the man ho spake unto the oman?’ and he saith, ’I [am].’
And Manoah saith, ’No let thy ords come to pass; hat is the custom of the youth — and his ork?’
And the messenger of Jehovah saith unto Manoah, ’Of all that I said unto the oman let her take heed;
of anything hich cometh out from the ine-vine she doth not eat, and ine and strong drink she doth not drink, and any unclean thing she doth not eat; all that I have commanded her she doth observe.’
And Manoah saith unto the messenger of Jehovah, ’Let us detain thee, e pray thee, and prepare before thee a kid of the goats.’

And the messenger of Jehovah saith unto Manoah, ’If thou detain me — I do not eat of thy bread; and if thou prepare a burnt-offering — to Jehovah thou dost offer it;’ for Manoah hath not knon that He [is] a messenger of Jehovah.
And Manoah saith unto the messenger of Jehovah, ’What [is] thy name? hen thy ords come to pass, then e have honoured thee.’
And the messenger of Jehovah saith to him, ’Why [is] this — thou dost ask for My name? — and it [is] Wonderful.’
And Manoah taketh the kid of the goats, and the present, and offereth on the rock to Jehovah, and He is doing onderfully, and Manoah and his ife are looking on,

and it cometh to pass, in the going up of the flame from off the altar toard the heavens, that the messenger of Jehovah goeth up in the flame of the altar, and Manoah and his ife are looking on, and they fall on their faces to the earth,
and the messenger of Jehovah hath not added again to appear unto Manoah, and unto his ife, then hath Manoah knon that He [is] a messenger of Jehovah.
And Manoah saith unto his ife, ’We certainly die, for e have seen God.’

And his ife saith to him, ’If Jehovah ere desirous to put us to death, He had not received from our hands burnt-offering and present, nor sheed us all these things, nor as [at this] time caused us to hear [anything] like this.’
And the oman beareth a son, and calleth his name Samson, and the youth groeth, and Jehovah doth bless him,
and the Spirit of Jehovah beginneth to move him in the camp of Dan, beteen Zorah and Eshtaol.
And Samson goeth don to Timnath, and seeth a oman in Timnath of the daughters of the Philistines,
and cometh up and declareth to his father, and to his mother, and saith, ’A oman I have seen in Timnath, of the daughters of the Philistines; and no, take her for me for a ife.’

And his father saith to him — also his mother, ’Is there not among the daughters of thy brethren, and among all my people, a oman, that thou art going to take a oman from the uncircumcised Philistines?’ and Samson saith unto his father, ’Take her for me, for she is right in mine eyes.’
And his father and his mother have not knon that from Jehovah it [is], that a meeting he is seeking of the Philistines; and at that time the Philistines are ruling over Israel.
And Samson goeth don — also his father and his mother, to Timnath, and they come unto the vineyards of Timnath, and lo, a lion’s help roareth at meeting him,

and the Spirit of Jehovah prospereth over him, and he rendeth it as the rending of a kid, and there is nothing in his hand, and he hath not declared to his father and to his mother that hich he hath done.
And he goeth don and speaketh to the oman, and she is right in the eyes of Samson;
and he turneth back after [some] days to take her, and turneth aside to see the carcase of the lion, and lo, a company of bees [are] in the body of the lion — and honey.

And he taketh it don on to his hands, and goeth on, going and eating; and he goeth unto his father, and unto his mother, and giveth to them, and they eat, and he hath not declared to them that from the body of the lion he took don the honey.
And his father goeth don unto the oman, and Samson maketh there a banquet, for so the young men do;
and it cometh to pass hen they see him, that they take thirty companions, and they are ith him.

And Samson saith to them, ’Let me, I pray you, put forth to you a riddle; if ye certainly declare it to me [in] the seven days of the banquet, and have found [it] out, then I have given to you thirty linen shirts, and thirty changes of garments;
and if ye are not able to declare [it] to me, then ye have given to me thirty linen shirts, and thirty changes of garments.’ And they say to him, ’Put forth thy riddle, and e hear it!’
And he saith to them: ’Out of the eater came forth meat, And out of the strong came forth seetness;’ and they ere not able to declare the riddle [in] three days.

And it cometh to pass, on the seventh day, that they say to Samson’s ife, ’Entice thy husband, that he declare to us the riddle, lest e burn thee and the house of thy father ith fire; to possess us have ye called for us? is it not?’

And Samson’s ife eepeth for it, and saith, ’Thou hast only hated me, and hast not loved me; the riddle thou hast put forth to the sons of my people — and to me thou hast not declared it;’ and he saith to her, ’Lo, to my father and to my mother I have not declared [it] — and to thee I declare [it]!’

And she eepeth for it the seven days [in] hich their banquet hath been, and it cometh to pass on the seventh day that he declareth [it] to her, for she hath distressed him; and she declareth the riddle to the sons of her people.

And the men of the city say to him on the seventh day, before the sun goeth in: — ’What [is] seeter than honey? And hat stronger than a lion?’ And he saith to them: ’Unless ye had ploughed ith my heifer, Ye had not found out my riddle.’

And the Spirit of Jehovah prospereth over him, and he goeth don to Ashkelon, and smiteth of them thirty men, and taketh their armour, and giveth the changes to those declaring the riddle; and his anger burneth, and he goeth up to the house of his father;
and Samson’s ife becometh his companion’s, ho [is] his friend.

And it cometh to pass, after [some] days, in the days of heat-harvest, that Samson looketh after his ife, ith a kid of the goats, and saith, ’I go in unto my ife, to the inner chamber;’ and her father hath not permitted him to go in,

and her father saith, I certainly said, that thou didst certainly hate her, and I give her to thy companion; is not her sister — the young one — better than she? Let her be, I pray thee, to thee, instead of her.’
And Samson saith of them, ’I am more innocent this time than the Philistines, though I am doing ith them evil.’
And Samson goeth and catcheth three hundred foxes, and taketh torches, and turneth tail unto tail, and putteth a torch beteen the to tails, in the midst,
and kindleth fire in the torches, and sendeth [them] out into the standing corn of the Philistines, and burneth [it] from heap even unto standing corn, even unto vineyard — olive-yard.

And the Philistines say, ’Who hath done this?’ And they say, ’Samson, son-in-la of the Timnite, because he hath taken aay his ife, and giveth her to his companion;’ and the Philistines go up, and burn her and her father ith fire.
And Samson saith to them, ’Though ye do thus, nevertheless I am avenged on you, and afterards I cease!’
And he smiteth them hip and thigh — a great smiting, and goeth don and delleth in the cleft of the rock Etam.
And the Philistines go up, and encamp in Judah, and are spread out in Lehi,
and the men of Judah say, ’Why have ye come up against us?’ and they say, ’To bind Samson e have come up, to do to him as he hath done to us.’

And three thousand men of Judah go don unto the cleft of the rock Etam, and say to Samson, ’Hast thou no knon that the Philistines are rulers over us? and hat [is] this thou hast done to us?’ And he saith to them, ’As they did to me, so I did to them.’
And they say to him, ’To bind thee e have come don — to give thee into the hand of the Philistines.’ And Samson saith to them, ’Sear to me, lest ye fall upon me yourselves.’

And they speak to him, saying, No, but e certainly bind thee, and have given thee into their hand, and e certainly do not put thee to death;’ and they bind him ith to thick bands, ne ones, and bring him up from the rock.

He hath come unto Lehi — and the Philistines have shouted at meeting him — and the Spirit of Jehovah prospereth over him, and the thick bands hich [are] on his arms are as flax hich they burn ith fire, and his bands are asted from off his hands,
and he findeth a fresh ja-bone of an ass, and putteth forth his hand and taketh it, and smiteth ith it — a thousand men.
And Samson saith, ’With a ja-bone of the ass — an ass upon asses — ith a ja-bone of the ass I have smitten a thousand men.’
And it cometh to pass hen he finisheth speaking, that he casteth aay the ja-bone out of his hand, and calleth that place Ramath-Lehi;

and he thirsteth exceedingly, and calleth unto Jehovah, and saith, ’Thou — Thou hast given by the hand of Thy servant this great salvation; and no, I die ith thirst, and have fallen into the hand of the uncircumcised.’

And God cleaveth the hollo place hich [is] in Lehi, and aters come out of it, and he drinketh, and his spirit cometh back, and he reviveth; therefore hath [one] called its name ’The fountain of him ho is calling,’ hich [is] in Lehi unto this day.
And he judgeth Israel in the days of the Philistines tenty years.
And Samson goeth to Gaza, and seeth there a oman, a harlot, and goeth in unto her;

[it is told] to the Gazathites, saying, ’Samson hath come in hither;’ and they go round and lay ait for him all the night at the gate of the city, and keep themselves silent all the night, saying, ’Till the light of the morning — then e have slain him.’

And Samson lieth don till the middle of the night, and riseth in the middle of the night, and layeth hold on the doors of the gate of the city, and on the to side posts, and removeth them ith the bar, and putteth on his shoulders, and taketh them up unto the top of the hill, hich [is] on the front of Hebron.
And it cometh to pass afterards that he loveth a oman in the valley of Sorek, and her name [is] Delilah,

and the princes of the Philistines come up unto her, and say to her, ’Entice him, and see herein his great poer [is], and herein e are able for him — and e have bound him to afflict him, and e — e give to thee, each one, eleven hundred silverlings.’
And Delilah saith unto Samson, ’Declare, I pray thee, to me, herein thy great poer [is], and hereith thou art bound, to afflict thee.’
And Samson saith unto her, ’If they bind me ith seven green iths hich have not been dried, then I have been eak, and have been as one of the human race.’
And the princes of the Philistines bring up to her seven green iths hich have not been dried, and she bindeth him ith them.

And the ambush is abiding ith her in an inner chamber, and she saith unto him, ’Philistines [are] upon thee, Samson;’ and he breaketh the iths as a thread of to is broken in its smelling fire, and his poer hath not been knon.
And Delilah saith unto Samson, ’Lo, thou hast played upon me, and speakest unto me lies; no, declare, I pray thee, to me, hereith thou art bound.’
And he saith unto her, ’If they certainly bind me ith thick bands, ne ones, by hich ork hath not been done, then I have been eak, and have been as one of the human race.’

And Delilah taketh thick bands, ne ones, and bindeth him ith them, and saith unto him, ’Philistines [are] upon thee, Samson;’ and the ambush is abiding in an inner chamber, and he breaketh them from off his arms as a thread.

And Delilah saith unto Samson, ’Hitherto thou hast played upon me, and dost speak unto me lies; declare to me hereith thou art bound.’ And he saith unto her, ’If thou eavest the seven locks of my head ith the eb.’
And she fixeth [it] ith the pin, and saith unto him, ’Philistines [are] upon thee, Samson;’ and he aaketh out of his sleep, and journeyeth ith the pin of the eaving machine, and ith the eb.
And she saith unto him, ’Ho dost thou say, I have loved thee, and thy heart is not ith me? these three times thou hast played upon me, and hast not declared to me herein thy great poer [is].’
And it cometh to pass, because she distressed him ith her ords all the days, and doth urge him, and his soul is grieved to death,

that he declareth to her all his heart, and saith to her, ’A razor hath not gone up on my head, for a Nazarite to God I [am] from the omb of my mother; if I have been shaven, then hath my poer turned aside from me, and I have been eak, and have been as any of the human race.’

And Delilah seeth that he hath declared to her all his heart, and she sendeth and calleth for the princes of the Philistines, saying, ’Come up this time, for he hath declared to me all his heart;’ and the princes of the Philistines have come up unto her, and bring up the money in their hand.
and she maketh him sleep on her knees, and calleth for a man, and shaveth the seven locks of his head, and beginneth to afflict him, and his poer turneth aside from off him;

and she saith, ’Philistines [are] upon thee, Samson;’ and he aaketh out of his sleep, and saith, ’I go out as time by time, and shake myself;’ and he hath not knon that Jehovah hath turned aside from off him.
And the Philistines seize him, and pick out his eyes, and bring him don to Gaza, and bind him ith to brazen fetters; and he is grinding in the prison-house.
And the hair of his head beginneth to shoot up, hen he hath been shaven,
and the princes of the Philistines have been gathered together to sacrifice a great sacrifice to Dagon their god, and to rejoice; and they say, ’Our god hath given into our hand Samson our enemy.’
And the people see him, and praise their god, for they said, ’Our god hath given in our hand our enemy, and he ho is laying aste our land, and ho multiplied our ounded.’

And it cometh to pass, hen their heart [is] glad, that they say, ’Call for Samson, and he doth play before us;’ and they call for Samson out of the prison-house, and he playeth before them, and they cause him to stand beteen the pillars.
And Samson saith unto the young man ho is keeping hold on his hand, ’Let me alone, and let me feel the pillars on hich the house is established, and I lean upon them.’

And the house hath been full of men and of omen, and thither [are] all the princes of the Philistines, and on the roof [are] about three thousand men and omen, ho are looking on the playing of Samson.

And Samson calleth unto Jehovah, and saith, ’Lord Jehovah, remember me, I pray Thee, and strengthen me, I pray Thee, only this time, O God; and I am avenged — vengeance at once — because of my to eyes, on the Philistines.’
And Samson turneth aside [to] the to middle pillars, on hich the house is established, and on hich it is supported, [to] the one ith his right hand, and one ith his left;

and Samson saith, ’Let me die ith the Philistines,’ and he inclineth himself poerfully, and the house falleth on the princes, and on all the people ho [are] in it, and the dead hom he hath put to death in his death are more than those hom he put to death in his life.

And his brethren come don, and all the house of his father, and lift him up, and bring him up, and bury him beteen Zorah and Eshtaol, in the burying-place of Manoah his father; and he hath judged Israel tenty years.
And there is a man of the hill-country of Ephraim, and his name [is] Micah,

and he saith to his mother, ’The eleven hundred silverlings hich have been taken of thine, and [of hich] thou hast sorn, and also spoken in mine ears; lo, the silver [is] ith me, I have taken it;’ and his mother saith, ’Blessed [is] my son of Jehovah.’

And he giveth back the eleven hundred silverlings to his mother, and his mother saith, ’I had certainly sanctified the silver to Jehovah, from my hand, for my son, to make a graven image, and a molten image; and no, I give it back to thee.’

And he giveth back the money to his mother, and his mother taketh to hundred silverlings, and giveth them to a refiner, and he maketh them a graven image, and a molten image, and it is in the house of Micah.
As to the man Micah, he hath a house of gods, and he maketh an ephod, and teraphim, and consecrateth the hand of one of his sons, and he is to him for a priest;
in those days there is no king in Israel, each that hich is right in his on eyes doth.
And there is a young man of Beth-Lehem-Judah, of the family of Judah, and he [is] a Levite, and he [is] a sojourner there.
And the man goeth out of the city, out of Beth-Lehem-Judah, to sojourn here he doth find, and cometh to the hill-country of Ephraim, unto the house of Micah, to ork his ay.
And Micah saith to him, ’Whence comest thou?’ and he saith unto him, ’A Levite [am] I, of Beth-Lehem-Judah, and I am going to sojourn here I do find.’

And Micah saith to him, ’Dell ith me, and be to me for a father and for a priest, and I give to thee ten silverlings for the days, and a suit of garments, and thy sustenance;’ and the Levite goeth [in].
And the Levite is illing to dell ith the man, and the young man is to him as one of his sons.
And Micah consecrateth the hand of the Levite, and the young man is to him for a priest, and he is in the house of Micah,
and Micah saith, ’No I have knon that Jehovah doth good to me, for the Levite hath been to me for a priest.’

In those days there is no king in Israel, and in those days the tribe of the Danite is seeking for itself an inheritance to inhabit, for [that] hath not fallen to it unto that day in the midst of the tribes of Israel by inheritance.

And the sons of Dan send, out of their family, five men of them, men, sons of valour, from Zorah, and from Eshtaol, to traverse the land, and to search it, and they say unto them, ’Go, search the land;’ and they come into the hill-country of Ephraim, unto the house of Micah, and lodge there.

They [are] ith the household of Micah, and they have discerned the voice of the young man, the Levite, and turn aside there, and say to him, ’Who hath brought thee hither? and hat art thou doing in this [place?] and hat to thee here?’
And he saith unto them, ’Thus and thus hath Micah done to me; and he hireth me, and I am to him for a priest.’
And they say to him, ’Ask, e pray thee, at God, and e kno hether our ay is prosperous on hich e are going.’
And the priest saith to them, ’Go in peace; over-against Jehovah [is] your ay in hich ye go.’

And the five men go, and come in to Laish, and see the people hich [is] in its midst, delling confidently, according to the custom of Zidonians, quiet and confident; and there is none putting to shame in the land in [any] thing, possessing restraint, and they [are] far off from the Zidonians, and have no ord ith [any] man.
And they come in unto their brethren, at Zorah and Eshtaol, and their brethren say to them, ’What — ye?’
And they say, ’Rise, and e go up against them, for e have seen the land, and lo, very good; and ye are keeping silent! be not slothful to go — to enter to possess the land.
When ye go, ye come in unto a people confident, and the land [is] large on both hands, for God hath given it into your hand, a place here there is no lack of anything hich [is] in the land.’
And there journey thence, of the family of the Danite, from Zorah, and from Eshtaol, six hundred men girded ith eapons of ar.
And they go up and encamp in Kirjath-Jearim, in Judah, therefore they have called that place, ’Camp of Dan,’ till this day; lo, behind Kirjath-Jearim.
And they pass over thence [to] the hill-country of Ephraim, and come in unto the house of Micah.

And the five men, those going to traverse the land of Laish, anser and say unto their brethren, ’Have ye knon that there is in these houses an ephod, and teraphim, and graven image, and molten image? and no, kno hat ye do.’
And they turn aside thither, and come in unto the house of the young man the Levite, the house of Micah, and ask of him of elfare, —
(and the six hundred men girded ith their eapons of ar, ho [are] of the sons of Dan, are standing at the opening of the gate), —

yea, the five men, those going to traverse the land, go up — they have come in thither — they have taken the graven image, and the ephod, and the teraphim, and the molten image — and the priest is standing at the opening of the gate, and the six hundred men ho are girded ith eapons of ar —
yea, these have entered the house of Micah, and take the graven image, the ephod, and the teraphim, and the molten image; and the priest saith unto them, ’What are ye doing?’

and they say to him, ’Keep silent, lay thy hand on thy mouth, and go ith us, and be to us for a father and for a priest: is it better thy being a priest to the house of one man, or thy being priest to a tribe and to a family in Israel?’
And the heart of the priest is glad, and he taketh the ephod, and the teraphim, and the graven image, and goeth into the midst of the people,
and they turn and go, and put the infants, and the cattle, and the baggage, before them.
They have been far off from the house of Micah — and the men ho [are] in the houses hich [are] near the house of Micah have been called together, and overtake the sons of Dan,
and call unto the sons of Dan, and they turn round their faces, and say to Micah, ’What — to thee that thou hast been called together?’
And he saith, ’My gods hich I made ye have taken, and the priest, and ye go; and hat to me more? and hat [is] this ye say unto me, What — to thee!’
And the sons of Dan say unto him, ’Let not thy voice be heard ith us, lest men bitter in soul fall upon you, and thou hast gathered thy life, and the life of thy household;’
and the sons of Dan go on their ay, and Micah seeth that they are stronger than he, and turneth, and goeth back unto his house.

And they have taken that hich Micah had made, and the priest hom he had, and come in against Laish, against a people quiet and confident, and smite them by the mouth of the sord, and the city have burnt ith fire,
and there is no deliverer, for it [is] far off from Zidon, and they have no ord ith [any] man, and it [is] in the valley hich [is] by Beth-Rehob; and they build the city, and dell in it,
and call the name of the city Dan, by the name of Dan their father, ho as born to Israel; and yet Laish [is] the name of the city at the first.

And the sons of Dan raise up for themselves the graven image, and Jonathan son of Gershom, son of Manasseh, he and his sons have been priests to the tribe of the Danite, till the day of the removal of [the people] of the land.
And they appoint for them the graven image of Micah, hich he had made, all the days of the house of God being in Shiloh.

And it cometh to pass, in those days, hen there is no king in Israel, that there is a man a Levite, a sojourner in the sides of the hill-country of Ephraim, and he taketh to him a ife, a concubine, out of Beth-Lehem-Judah;
and commit horedom against him doth his concubine, and she goeth from him unto the house of her father, unto Beth-Lehem-Judah, and is there days — four months.

And her husband riseth and goeth after her, to speak unto her heart, to bring her back, and his young man [is] ith him, and a couple of asses; and she bringeth him into the house of her father, and the father of the young oman seeth him, and rejoiceth to meet him.
And keep hold on him doth his father-in-la, father of the young oman, and he abideth ith him three days, and they eat and drink, and lodge there.

And it cometh to pass, on the fourth day, that they rise early in the morning, and he riseth to go, and the father of the young oman saith unto his son-in-la, ’Support thy heart ith a morsel of bread, and afterard ye go on.’
And they sit and eat both of them together, and drink, and the father of the young oman saith unto the man, ’Be illing, I pray thee, and lodge all night, and let thy heart be glad.’
And the man riseth to go, and his father-in-la presseth on him, and he turneth back and lodgeth there.

And he riseth early in the morning, on the fifth day, to go, and the father of the young oman saith, ’Support, I pray thee, thy heart;’ and they have tarried till the turning of the day, and they eat, both of them.

And the man riseth to go, he and his concubine, and his young man, and his father-in-la, father of the young oman, saith to him, ’Lo, I pray thee, the day hath fallen toard evening, lodge all night, I pray thee; lo, the declining of the day! lodge here, and let thine heart be glad — and ye have risen early to-morro for your journey, and thou hast gone to thy tent.’

And the man hath not been illing to lodge all night, and he riseth, and goeth, and cometh in till over-against Jebus (It [is] Jerusalem), and ith him [are] a couple of asses saddled; and his concubine [is] ith him.
They [are] near Jebus, and the day hath gone greatly don, and the young man saith unto his lord, ’Come, I pray thee, and e turn aside unto this city of the Jebusite, and lodge in it.’
And his lord saith unto him, ’Let us not turn aside unto the city of a stranger, that is not of the sons of Israel, thither, but e have passed over unto Gibeah.’
And he saith to his young man, ’Come, and e dra near to one of the places, and have lodged in Gibeah, or in Ramah.’
And they pass over, and go on, and the sun goeth in upon them near Gibeah, hich is to Benjamin;
and they turn aside there to go in to lodge in Gibeah, and he goeth in and sitteth in a broad place of the city, and there is no man gathering them into the house to lodge.

And lo, a man, an aged one, hath come from his ork from the field in the evening, and the man [is] of the hill-country of Ephraim, and he [is] a sojourner in Gibeah, and the men of the place [are] Benjamites.
And he lifteth up his eyes, and seeth the man, the traveller, in a broad place of the city, and the aged man saith, ’Whither goest thou? and hence comest thou?’

And he saith unto him, ’We are passing over from Beth-Lehem-Judah unto the sides of the hill-country of Ephraim — thence I [am], and I go unto Beth-Lehem-Judah; and to the house of Jehovah I am going, and there is no man gathering me into the house,
and both stra and provender are for our asses, and also bread and ine there are for me, and for thy handmaid, and for the young man ith thy servants; there is no lack of anything.’
And the old man saith, ’Peace to thee; only, all thy lack [is] on me, only in the broad place lodge not.’
And he bringeth him in to his house, and mixeth [food] for the asses, and they ash their feet, and eat and drink.

They are making their heart glad, and lo, men of the city, men — sons of orthlessness — have gone round about the house, beating on the door, and they speak unto the old man, the master of the house, saying, ’Bring out the man ho hath come unto thine house, and e kno him.’
And the man, the master of the house, goeth out unto them, and saith unto them, ’Nay, my brethren, do not evil, I pray you, after that this man hath come in unto my house, do not this folly;
lo, my daughter, the virgin, and his concubine, let me bring them out, I pray you, and humble ye them, and do to them that hich is good in your eyes, and to this man do not this foolish thing.’

And the men have not been illing to hearken to him, and the man taketh hold on his concubine, and bringeth [her] out unto them ithout, and they kno her, and roll themselves upon her all the night, till the morning, and send her aay in the ascending of the dan;
and the oman cometh in at the turning of the morning, and falleth at the opening of the man’s house, here her lord [is], till the light.

And her lord riseth in the morning, and openeth the doors of the house, and goeth out to go on his ay, and lo, the oman, his concubine, is fallen at the opening of the house, and her hands [are] on the threshold,
and he saith unto her, ’Rise, and e go;’ and there is none ansering, and he taketh her on the ass, and the man riseth and goeth to his place,
and cometh in unto his house, and taketh the knife, and layeth hold on his concubine, and cutteth her in pieces to her bones — into telve pieces, and sendeth her into all the border of Israel.

And it hath come to pass, every one ho seeth hath said, ’There hath not been — yea, there hath not been seen like this, from the day of the coming up of the sons of Israel out of the land of Egypt till this day; set your [heart] upon it, take counsel, and speak.’
And all the sons of Israel go out, and the company is assembled as one man, from Dan even unto Beer-Sheba, and the land of Gilead, unto Jehovah, at Mizpeh.
And the chiefs of all the people, of all the tribes of Israel, station themselves in the assembly of the people of God, four hundred thousand footmen draing sord.
And the sons of Benjamin hear that the sons of Israel have gone up to Mizpeh. And the sons of Israel say, ’Speak ye, ho hath this evil been?’
And the man, the Levite, husband of the oman ho hath been murdered, ansereth and saith, ’Into Gibeah (hich [is] to Benjamin) I have come, I and my concubine, to lodge;
and rise against me do the masters of Gibeah — and they go round the house against me by night — me they thought to slay, and my concubine they have humbled, and she dieth;
and I lay hold on my concubine, and cut her in pieces, and send her into all the country of the inheritance of Israel; for they have done ickedness and folly in Israel;
lo, ye [are] all sons of Israel; give for you a ord and counsel here.’
And all the people rise as one man, saying, ’None of us doth go to his tent, and none of us doth turn aside to his house;
and no, this [is] the thing hich e do to Gibeah — against it by lot!

and e have taken ten men of a hundred, of all the tribes of Israel, and a hundred of a thousand, and a thousand of a myriad, to receive provision for the people, to do, at their coming to Gibeah of Benjamin, according to all the folly hich it hath done in Israel.’
And every man of Israel is gathered unto the city, as one man — companions.
And the tribes of Israel send men among all the tribes of Benjamin, saying, ’What [is] this evil hich hath been among you?

And no, give up the men — sons of orthlessness — hich [are] in Gibeah, and e put them to death, and e put aay evil from Israel.’ And [the sons of] Benjamin have not been illing to hearken to the voice of their brethren, the sons of Israel;
and the sons of Benjamin are gathered out of the cities to Gibeah, to go out to battle ith the sons of Israel.

And the sons of Benjamin number themselves on that day; out of the cities [are] tenty and six thousand men draing sord, apart from the inhabitants of Gibeah, [ho] numbered themselves, seven hundred chosen men;
among all this people [are] seven hundred chosen men, bound of their right hand, each of these slinging ith a stone at the hair, and he doth not err.
And the men of Israel numbered themselves, apart from Benjamin, four hundred thousand men, draing sord, each of these a man of ar.

And they rise and go up to Beth-El, and ask of God, and the sons of Israel say, ’Who doth go up for us at the commencement to battle ith the sons of Benjamin?’ and Jehovah saith, ’Judah — at the commencement.’
And the sons of Israel rise in the morning, and encamp against Gibeah,
and the men of Israel go out to battle ith Benjamin, and the men of Israel set themselves in array ith them, [for] battle against Gibeah,
and the sons of Benjamin come out from Gibeah, and destroy in Israel on that day to and tenty thousand men — to the earth.
And the people, the men of Israel, strengthen themselves, and add to set the battle in array in the place here they arranged themselves on the first day.

And the sons of Israel go up and eep before Jehovah till the evening, and ask of Jehovah, saying, ’Do I add to dra nigh to battle ith the sons of Benjamin, my brother?’ And Jehovah saith, ’Go up against him.’
And the sons of Israel dra near unto the sons of Benjamin on the second day,
and Benjamin cometh out to meet them from Gibeah on the second day, and destroy among the sons of Israel again eighteen thousand men — to the earth; all these are draing sord.

And all the sons of Israel go up, even all the people, and come in to Beth-El, and eep, and sit there before Jehovah, and fast on that day till the evening, and cause to ascend burnt-offerings and peace-offerings before Jehovah.
And the sons of Israel ask of Jehovah, — and there [is] the ark of the covenant of God in those days,

and Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron, is standing before it in those days — saying, ’Do I add again to go out to battle ith the sons of Benjamin, my brother, or do I cease?’ And Jehovah saith, ’Go up, for to-morro I give him into thy hand.’
And Israel setteth liers in ait against Gibeah, round about,
and the sons of Israel go up against the sons of Benjamin, on the third day, and arrange themselves against Gibeah, as time by time.

And the sons of Benjamin come out to meet the people; they have been dran aay out of the city, and begin to smite [some] of the people — ounded as time by time, in the highays (of hich one is going up to Beth-El, and the other to Gibeah in the field), [are] about thirty men of Israel.
And the sons of Benjamin say, ’They are smitten before us as at the beginning;’ but the sons of Israel said, ’Let us flee, and dra them aay out of the city, unto the highays.’
And all the men of Israel have risen from their place, and arrange themselves at Baal-Tamar, and the ambush of Israel is coming forth out of its place, out of the meado of Gibeah.
And they come in over against Gibeah — ten thousand chosen men out of all Israel — and the battle [is] grievous, and they have not knon that the evil is striking against them.
And Jehovah smiteth Benjamin before Israel, and the sons of Israel destroy in Benjamin, on that day, tenty and five thousand, and a hundred men; all these [are] draing sord.
And the sons of Benjamin see that they have been smitten — and the men of Israel give place to Benjamin, for they have trusted unto the ambush hich they had set against Gibeah,
and the ambush have hasted, and push against Gibeah, and the ambush draeth itself out, and smiteth the hole of the city by the mouth of the sord.
And there as the appointed sign to the men of Israel ith the ambush — their causing to go up a great volume of smoke from the city.

And the men of Israel turn in battle, and Benjamin hath begun to smite the ounded among the men of Israel, about thirty men, for they said, ’Surely they are utterly smitten before us, as [at] the first battle;
and the volume hath begun to go up from the city — a pillar of smoke — and Benjamin turneth behind, and lo, gone up hath the perfection of the city toard the heavens.
And the men of Israel have turned, and the men of Benjamin are troubled, for they have seen that the evil hath stricken against them —
and they turn before the men of Israel unto the ay of the ilderness, and the battle hath folloed them; and those ho [are] from the city are destroying them in their midst;
they have compassed the Benjamites — they have pursued them — ith ease they have trodden them don till over-against Gibeah, at the sun-rising.
And there fall of Benjamin eighteen thousand men — the hole of these [are] men of valour;
and they turn and flee toard the ilderness, unto the rock of Rimmon; and they glean of them in the highays five thousand men, and follo after them unto Gidom, and smite of them to thousand men.
And all those falling of Benjamin are tenty and five thousand men draing sord, on that day — the hole of these [are] men of valour;
and there turn and flee into the ilderness, unto the rock of Rimmon six hundred men, and they dell in the rock Rimmon four months.

And the men of Israel have turned back unto the sons of Benjamin, and smite them by the mouth of the sord out of the city, — men unto cattle, unto all that is found; also all the cities hich are found they have sent into fire.
And the men of Israel have sorn in Mizpeh, saying, ’None of us doth give his daughter to Benjamin for a ife.’
And the people come in to Beth-El, and sit there till the evening before God, and lift up their voice, and eep — a great eeping,
and say, ’Why, O Jehovah, God of Israel, hath this been in Israel — to be lacking to-day, from Israel, one tribe?’
And it cometh to pass on the morro, that the people rise early, and build there an altar, and cause to ascend burnt-offerings and peace-offerings.

And the sons of Israel say, ’Who [is] he that hath not come up in the assembly out of all the tribes of Israel unto Jehovah?’ for the great oath hath been concerning him ho hath not come up unto Jehovah to Mizpeh, saying, ’He is surely put to death.’
And the sons of Israel repent concerning Benjamin their brother, and say, ’There hath been to-day cut off one tribe from Israel,
hat do e do for them — for those ho are left — for ives, and e — e have sorn by Jehovah not to give to them of our daughters for ives?’
And they say, ’Who is [that] one out of the tribes of Israel ho hath not come up unto Jehovah to Mizpeh?’ and lo, none hath come in unto the camp from Jabesh-Gilead — unto the assembly.
And the people numbered themselves, and lo, there is not there a man of the inhabitants of Jabesh-Gilead.

And the company send there telve thousand men of the sons of valour, and command them, saying, ’Go — and ye have smitten the inhabitants of Jabesh-Gilead by the mouth of the sord, even the omen and the infants.
And this [is] the thing hich ye do; every male, and every oman knoing the lying of a male, ye devote.’

And they find out of the inhabitants of Jabesh-Gilead four hundred young omen, virgins, ho have not knon man by the lying of a male, and they bring them in unto the camp at Shiloh, hich [is] in the land of Canaan.
And all the company send, and speak, unto the sons of Benjamin ho [are] in the rock Rimmon, and proclaim to them peace;
and Benjamin turneth back at that time, and they give to them the omen hom they have kept alive of the omen of Jabesh-Gilead, and they have not found for [all of] them so.
And the people repented concerning Benjamin, for Jehovah had made a breach among the tribes of Israel.
And the elders of the company say, ’What do e do to the remnant for ives — for the omen have been destroyed out of Benjamin?’
And they say, ’A possession of an escaped party [is] to Benjamin, and a tribe is not blotted out from Israel;
and e — e are not able to give to them ives out of our daughters, for the sons of Israel have sorn, saying, Cursed [is] he ho is giving a ife to Benjamin.’

And they say, ’Lo, a festival of Jehovah [is] in Shiloh, from time to time, hich [is] on the north of Beth-El, at the rising of the sun, by the highay hich is going up from Beth-El to Shechem, and on the south of Lebonah.’
And they command the sons of Benjamin, saying, ’Go — and ye have laid ait in the vineyards,

and have seen, and lo, if the daughters of Shiloh come out to dance in dances — then ye have gone out from the vineyards, and caught for you each his ife out of the daughters of Shiloh, and gone to the land of Benjamin;

and it hath been, hen their fathers or their brethren come in to plead unto us, that e have said unto them, Favour us [by] them, for e have not taken [to] each his ife in battle, for ye — ye have not given to them at this time [that] ye are guilty.’

And the sons of Benjamin do so, and take omen according to their number, out of the dancers hom they have taken violently aay; and they go, and turn back unto their inheritance, and build the cities, and dell in them.
And the sons of Israel go up and don thence at that time, each to his tribe, and to his family; and they go out thence each to his inheritance.
In those days there is no king in Israel; each doth that hich is right in his on eyes.

And it cometh to pass, in the days of the judging of the judges, that there is a famine in the land, and there goeth a man from Beth-Lehem-Judah to sojourn in the fields of Moab, he, and his ife, and his to sons.

And the name of the man [is] Elimelech, and the name of his ife Naomi, and the name of his to sons Mahlon and Chilion, Ephrathites from Beth-Lehem-Judah; and they come into the fields of Moab, and are there.
And Elimelech husband of Naomi dieth, and she is left, she and her to sons;
and they take to them ives, Moabitesses: the name of the one [is] Orpah, and the name of the second Ruth; and they dell there about ten years.
And they die also, both of them — Mahlon and Chilion — and the oman is left of her to children and of her husband.
And she riseth, she and her daughters-in-la, and turneth back from the fields of Moab, for she hath heard in the fields of Moab that God hath looked after His people, — to give to them bread.
And she goeth out from the place here she hath been, and her to daughters-in-la ith her, and they go in the ay to turn back unto the land of Judah.
And Naomi saith to her to daughters-in-la, ’Go, turn back, each to the house of her mother; Jehovah doth ith you kindness as ye have done ith the dead, and ith me;
Jehovah doth grant to you, and find ye rest each in the house of her husband;’ and she kisseth them, and they lift up their voice and eep.
And they say to her, ’Surely ith thee e go back to thy people.’
And Naomi saith, ’Turn back, my daughters; hy do ye go ith me? are there yet to me sons in my boels that they have been to you for husbands?
Turn back, my daughters, go, for I am too aged to be to a husband; though I had said, There is for me hope, also, I have been to-night to a husband, and also I have borne sons:

for them do ye ait till that they gro up? for them do ye shut yourselves up, not to be to a husband? nay, my daughters, for more bitter to me than to you, for the hand of Jehovah hath gone out against me.’
And they lift up their voice, and eep again, and Orpah kisseth her mother-in-la, and Ruth hath cleaved to her.
And she saith, ’Lo, thy sister-in-la hath turned back unto her people, and unto her god, turn thou back after thy sister-in-la.’
And Ruth saith, ’Urge me not to leave thee — to turn back from after thee; for hither thou goest I go, and here thou lodgest I lodge; thy people [is] my people, and thy God my God.
Where thou diest I die, and there I am buried; thus doth Jehovah to me, and thus doth He add — for death itself doth part beteen me and thee.’
And she seeth that she is strengthening herself to go ith her, and she ceaseth to speak unto her;
and they go both of them till their coming in to Beth-Lehem; and it cometh to pass at their coming in to Beth-Lehem, that all the city is moved at them, and they say, ’Is this Naomi?’
And she saith unto them, ’Call me not Naomi; call me Mara, for the Almighty hath dealt very bitterly to me,
I ent out full, and empty hath Jehovah brought me back, hy do ye call me Naomi, and Jehovah hath testified against me, and the Almighty hath done evil to me?’
And Naomi turneth back, and Ruth the Moabitess her daughter-in-la ith her, ho hath turned back from the fields of Moab, and they have come in to Beth-Lehem at the commencement of barley-harvest.
And Naomi hath an acquaintance of her husband’s, a man mighty in ealth, of the family of Elimelech, and his name [is] Boaz.
And Ruth the Moabitess saith unto Naomi, ’Let me go, I pray thee, into the field, and I gather among the ears of corn after him in hose eyes I find grace;’ and she saith to her, ’Go, my daughter.’
And she goeth and cometh and gathereth in a field after the reapers, and her chance happeneth — the portion of the field is Boaz’s ho [is] of the family of Elimelech.
And lo, Boaz hath come from Beth-Lehem, and saith to the reapers, ’Jehovah [is] ith you;’ and they say to him, ’Jehovah doth bless thee.’
And Boaz saith to his young man ho is set over the reapers, ’Whose [is] this young person?’
And the young man ho is set over the reapers ansereth and saith, ’A young oman — Moabitess — she [is], ho came back ith Naomi from the fields of Moab,
and she saith, Let me glean, I pray thee — and I have gathered among the sheaves after the reapers; and she cometh and remaineth since the morning and till no; she sat in the house a little.
And Boaz saith unto Ruth, ’Hast thou not heard, my daughter? go not to glean in another field, and also, pass not over from this, and thus thou dost cleave to my young omen:

thine eyes [are] on the field hich they reap, and thou hast gone after them; have not I charged the young men not to touch thee? hen thou art athirst then thou hast gone unto the vessels, and hast drunk from that hich the young men dra.’
And she falleth on her face, and boeth herself to the earth, and saith unto him, ’Wherefore have I found grace in thine eyes, to discern me, and I a stranger?’

And Boaz ansereth and saith to her, ’It hath thoroughly been declared to me all that thou hast done ith thy mother-in-la, after the death of thy husband, and thou dost leave thy father, and thy mother, and the land of thy birth, and dost come in unto a people hich thou hast not knon heretofore.
Jehovah doth recompense thy ork, and thy reard is complete from Jehovah, God of Israel, under hose ings thou hast come to take refuge.’

And she saith, ’Let me find grace in thine eyes, my lord, because thou hast comforted me, and because thou hast spoken unto the heart of thy maid-servant, and I — I am not as one of thy maid-servants.’

And Boaz saith to her, ’At meal-time come nigh hither, and thou hast eaten of the bread, and dipped thy morsel in the vinegar.’ And she sitteth at the side of the reapers, and he reacheth to her roasted corn, and she eateth, and is satisfied, and leaveth.
And she riseth to glean, and Boaz chargeth his young men, saying, ’Even beteen the sheaves she doth glean, and ye do not cause her to blush;
and also ye do surely cast to her of the handfuls — and have left, and she hath gleaned, and ye do not push against her.’
And she gleaneth in the field till the evening, and beateth out that hich she hath gleaned, and it is about an ephah of barley;
and she taketh [it] up, and goeth into the city, and her mother-in-la seeth that hich she hath gleaned, and she bringeth out and giveth to her that hich she left from her satiety.

And her mother-in-la saith to her, ’Where hast thou gleaned to-day? and here hast thou rought? may he ho is discerning thee be blessed.’ And she declareth to her mother-in-la ith hom she hath rought, and saith, ’The name of the man ith hom I have rought to-day [is] Boaz.’

And Naomi saith to her daughter-in-la, ’Blessed [is] he of Jehovah ho hath not forsaken His kindness ith the living and ith the dead;’ and Naomi saith to her, ’The man is a relation of ours; he [is] of our redeemers.’
And Ruth the Moabitess saith, ’Also he surely said unto me, Near the young people hom I have thou dost cleave till they have completed the hole of the harvest hich I have.’
And Naomi saith unto Ruth her daughter-in-la, ’Good, my daughter, that thou goest out ith his young omen, and they come not against thee in another field.’
And she cleaveth to the young omen of Boaz to glean, till the completion of the barley-harvest, and of the heat-harvest, and she delleth ith her mother-in-la.
And Naomi her mother-in-la saith to her, ’My daughter, do not I seek for thee rest, that it may be ell ith thee?
and no, is not Boaz of our acquaintance, ith hose young omen thou hast been? lo, he is innoing the threshing-floor of barley to-night,
and thou hast bathed, and anointed thyself, and put thy garments upon thee, and gone don to the threshing-floor; let not thyself be knon to the man till he complete to eat and to drink;
and it cometh to pass hen he lieth don, that thou hast knon the place here he lieth don, and hast gone in, and uncovered his feet, and lain don, — and he doth declare to thee that hich thou dost do.’
And she saith unto her, ’All that thou sayest — I do.’
And she goeth don [to] the threshing-floor, and doth according to all that her mother-in-la commanded her
And Boaz eateth and drinketh, and his heart is glad; and he goeth in to lie don at the end of the heap; and she cometh in gently, and uncovereth his feet, and lieth don.
And it cometh to pass, at the middle of the night, that the man trembleth, and turneth himself, and lo, a oman is lying at his feet.
And he saith, ’Who [art] thou?’ and she saith, ’I [am] Ruth thy handmaid, and thou hast spread thy skirt over thy handmaid, for thou [art] a redeemer.’
And he saith, ’Blessed [art] thou of Jehovah, my daughter; thou hast dealt more kindly at the latter end than at the beginning — not to go after the young men, either poor or rich.
And no, my daughter, fear not, all that thou sayest I do to thee, for all the gate of my people doth kno that thou [art] a virtuous oman.
And no, surely, true, that I [am] a redeemer, but also there is a redeemer nearer than I.

Lodge to night, and it hath been in the morning, if he doth redeem thee, ell: he redeemeth; and if he delight not to redeem thee, then I have redeemed thee — I; Jehovah liveth! lie don till the morning.’
And she lieth don at his feet till the morning, and riseth before one doth discern another; and he saith, ’Let it not be knon that the oman hath come into the floor.’
And he saith, ’Give the covering hich [is] on thee, and keep hold on it;’ and she keepeth hold on it, and he measureth six [measures] of barley, and layeth [it] on her; and he goeth into the city.
And she cometh in unto her mother-in-la, and she saith, ’Who [art] thou, my daughter?’ and she declareth to her all that the man hath done to her.
And she saith, ’These six [measures] of barley he hath given to me, for he said, Thou dost not go in empty unto thy mother-in-la.’
And she saith, ’Sit still, my daughter, till thou dost kno ho the matter falleth, for the man doth not rest except he hath completed the matter to-day.’

And Boaz hath gone up to the gate, and sitteth there, and lo, the redeemer is passing by of hom Boaz had spoken, and he saith, ’Turn aside, sit don here, such a one, such a one;’ and he turneth aside and sitteth don.
And he taketh ten men of the elders of the city, and saith, ’Sit don here;’ and they sit don.
And he saith to the redeemer, ’A portion of the field hich [is] to our brother, to Elimelech, hath Naomi sold, ho hath come back from the fields of Moab;

and I said, I uncover thine ear, saying, Buy before the inhabitants, and before the elders of my people; if thou dost redeem — redeem, and if none doth redeem — declare to me, and I kno, for there is none save thee to redeem, and I after thee.’ And he saith, I redeem [it].’

And Boaz saith, ’In the day of thy buying the field from the hand of Naomi, then from Ruth the Moabitess, ife of the dead, thou hast bought [it], to raise up the name of the dead over his inheritance.’
And the redeemer saith, ’I am not able to redeem [it] for myself, lest I destroy mine inheritance; redeem for thyself — thou — my right of redemption, for I am not able to redeem.’
And this [is] formerly in Israel for redemption and for changing, to establish anything: a man hath dran off his sandal, and given [it] to his neighbour, and this [is] the testimony in Israel.
And the redeemer saith to Boaz, ’Buy [it] for thyself,’ and draeth off his sandal.
And Boaz saith to the elders, and [to] all the people, ’Witnesses [are] ye to-day that I have bought all that [is] to Elimelech, and all that [is] to Chilion and Mahlon, from the hand of Naomi;

and also Ruth the Moabitess, ife of Mahlon, I have bought to myself for a ife, to raise up the name of the dead over his inheritance; and the name of the dead is not cut off from among his brethren, and from the gate of his place; itnesses ye [are] to-day.’

And all the people ho [are] in the gate say — also the elders — ’Witnesses! Jehovah make the oman ho is coming in unto thy house as Rachel and as Leah, both of hom built the house of Israel; and do thou virtuously in Ephrathah, and proclaim the Name in Beth-Lehem;
and let thy house be as the house of Pharez (hom Tamar bare to Judah), of the seed hich Jehovah doth give to thee of this young oman.’
And Boaz taketh Ruth, and she becometh his ife, and he goeth in unto her, and Jehovah giveth to her conception, and she beareth a son.
And the omen say unto Naomi, ’Blessed [is] Jehovah ho hath not let a redeemer cease to thee to-day, and his name is proclaimed in Israel,
and he hath been to thee for a restorer of life, and for a nourisher of thine old age, for thy daughter-in-la ho hath loved thee — ho is better to thee than seven sons — hath borne him.’
And Naomi taketh the lad, and layeth him in her bosom, and is to him for a nurse;
and the neighbouring omen give to him a name, saying, ’There hath been a son born to Naomi,’ and they call his name Obed; he [is] father of Jesse, father of David.
And these are genealogies of Pharez: Pharez begat Hezron,
and Hezron begat Ram, and Ram begat Amminidab,
and Amminidab begat Nahshon, and Nahshon begat Salmon,
and Salmon begat Boaz, and Boaz begat Obed,
and Obed begat Jesse, and Jesse begat David.
And there is a certain man of Ramathaim-Zophim, of the hill-country of Ephraim, and his name [is] Elkanah, son of Jeroham, son of Elihu, son of Tohu, son of Zuph, and Ephrathite,
and he hath to ives, the name of the one [is] Hannah, and the name of the second Peninnah, and Peninnah hath children, and Hannah hath no children.

And that man hath gone up out of his city from time to time, to bo himself, and to sacrifice, before Jehovah of Hosts, in Shiloh, and there [are] to sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, priests to Jehovah.
And the day cometh, and Elkanah sacrificeth, and he hath given to Peninnah his ife, and to all her sons and her daughters, portions,
and to Hannah he giveth a certain portion — double, for he hath loved Hannah, and Jehovah hath shut her omb;
and her adversity hath also provoked her greatly, so as to make her tremble, for Jehovah hath shut up her omb.
And so he doth year by year, from the time of her going up into the house of Jehovah, so it provoketh her, and she eepeth, and doth not eat.
And Elkanah her husband saith to her, ’Hannah, hy eepest thou? and hy dost thou not eat? and hy is thy heart afflicted? am I not better to thee than ten sons?’
And Hannah riseth after eating in Shiloh, and after drinking, and Eli the priest is sitting on the throne by the side-post of the temple of Jehovah.
And she is bitter in soul, and prayeth unto Jehovah, and eepeth greatly,

and voeth a vo, and saith, ’Jehovah of Hosts, if Thou dost certainly look on the affliction of Thy handmaid, and hast remembered me, and dost not forget Thy handmaid, and hast given to Thy handmaid seed of men — then I have given him to Jehovah all days of his life, and a razor doth not go up upon his head.’
And it hath been, hen she multiplied praying before Jehovah, that Eli is atching her mouth,
and Hannah, she is speaking to her heart, only her lips are moving, and her voice is not heard, and Eli reckoneth her to be drunken.
And Eli saith unto her, ’Until hen are thou drunken? turn aside thy ine from thee.’
And Hannah ansereth and saith, ’No, my lord, A oman sharply pained in spirit I [am], and ine and strong drink I have not drunk, and I pour out my soul before Jehovah;
put not thy handmaid before a daughter of orthlessness, for from the abundance of my meditation, and of my provocation, I have spoken hitherto.’
And Eli ansereth and saith, ’Go in peace, and the God of Israel doth give thy petition hich thou hast asked of Him.’
And she saith, ’Let thy handmaid find grace in thine eyes;’ and the oman goeth on her ay, and eateth, and her countenance hath not been [sad] for it any more.
And they rise early in the morning, and bo themselves before Jehovah, and turn back, and come in unto their house in Ramah, and Elkanah knoeth Hannah his ife, and Jehovah remembereth her;
and it cometh to pass, at the revolution of the days, that Hannah conceiveth, and beareth a son, and calleth his name Samuel, ’for, from Jehovah I have asked him.’
And the man Elkanah goeth up, and all his house, to sacrifice to Jehovah the sacrifice of the days, and his vo.
And Hannah hath not gone up, for she said to her husband, ’Till the youth is eaned — then I have brought him in, and he hath appeared before the face of Jehovah, and delt there — unto the age.’

And Elkanah her husband saith to her, ’Do that hich is good in thine eyes; abide till thy eaning him; only, Jehovah establish His ord;’ and the oman abideth and suckleth her son till she hath eaned him,

and she causeth him to go up ith her hen she hath eaned him, ith three bullocks, and one ephah of flour, and a bottle of ine, and she bringeth him into the house of Jehovah at Shiloh, and the youth [is but] a youth.
And they slaughter the bullock, and bring in the youth unto Eli,
and she saith, ’O, my lord, thy soul liveth! my lord, I [am] the oman ho stood ith thee in this [place], to pray unto Jehovah;
for this youth I prayed, and Jehovah doth give to me my petition hich I asked of Him;
and also I have caused him to be asked for Jehovah, all the days that he hath lived — he is asked for Jehovah;’ and he boeth himself there before Jehovah.
And Hannah prayeth, and saith: ’My heart hath exulted in Jehovah, My horn hath been high in Jehovah, My mouth hath been large over mine enemies, For I have rejoiced in Thy salvation.
There is none holy like Jehovah, For there is none save Thee, And there is no rock like our God.
Ye multiply not — ye speak haughtily — The old saying goeth out from your mouth, For a God of knoledge [is] Jehovah, And by Him actions are eighed.
Bos of the mighty are broken, And the stumbling have girded on strength.
The satiated for bread hired themselves, And the hungry have ceased. While the barren hath borne seven, And she abounding ith sons hath languished.
Jehovah putteth to death, and keepeth alive, He bringeth don to Sheol, and bringeth up.
Jehovah dispossesseth, and He maketh rich, He maketh lo, yea, He maketh high.

He raiseth from the dust the poor, From a dunghill He lifteth up the needy, To cause [them] to sit ith nobles, Yea, a throne of honour He doth cause them to inherit, For to Jehovah [are] the fixtures of earth, And He setteth on them the habitable orld.
The feet of His saints He keepeth, And the icked in darkness are silent, For not by poer doth man become mighty.
Jehovah — broken don are His adversaries, Against them in the heavens He thundereth: Jehovah judgeth the ends of earth, And giveth strength to His king, And exalteth the horn of His anointed.’
And Elkanah goeth to Ramath, unto his house, and the youth hath been serving Jehovah, [in] the presence of Eli the priest;
and the sons of Eli [are] sons of orthlessness, they have not knon Jehovah.
And the custom of the priests ith the people [is]: any man sacrificing a sacrifice — then hath the servant of the priest come in hen the flesh is boiling, and the hook of three teeth in his hand,
and hath struck [it] into the pan, or kettle, or caldron, or pot; all that the hook bringeth up doth the priest take for himself; thus they do to all Israel ho are coming in, there, in Shiloh.

Also before they make perfume ith the fat — then hath the priest’s servant come in, and said to the man ho is sacrificing, ’Give flesh to roast for the priest, and he doth not take of thee flesh boiled, but ra;’

and the man saith unto him, ’Let them surely make a perfume (as to-day) ith the fat, then take to thee as thy soul desireth;’ and he hath said to him, ’Surely no thou dost give; and if not — I have taken by strength.’
And the sin of the young men is very great [in] the presence of Jehovah, for the men have despised the offering of Jehovah.
And Samuel is ministering [in] the presence of Jehovah, a youth girt [ith] an ephod of linen;
and a small upper coat doth his mother make to him, and she hath brought it up to him from time to time, in her coming up ith her husband to sacrifice the sacrifice of the time.
And Eli blessed Elkanah, and his ife, and said, ’Jehovah doth appoint for thee seed of this oman, for the petition hich she asked for Jehovah;’ and they have gone to their place.
When Jehovah hath looked after Hannah, then she conceiveth and beareth three sons and to daughters; and the youth Samuel groeth up ith Jehovah.
And Eli [is] very old, and hath heard all that his sons do to all Israel, and ho that they lie ith the omen ho are assembling [at] the opening of the tent of meeting,
and he saith to them, ’Why do ye things like these? for I am hearing of your evil ords from all the people — these!
Nay, my sons; for the report hich I am hearing is not good causing the people of Jehovah to transgress. —

If a man sin against a man, then hath God judged him; but if against Jehovah a man sin, ho doth pray for him?’ and they hearken not to the voice of their father, though Jehovah hath delighted to put them to death.
And the youth Samuel is going on and groing up, and [is] good both ith Jehovah, and also ith men.
And there cometh a man of God unto Eli, and saith unto him, ’Thus said Jehovah, Was I really revealed unto the house of thy father in their being in Egypt, before Pharaoh’s house,

even to choose him out of all the tribes of Israel to Me for a priest, to go up on Mine altar, to make a perfume, to bear an ephod before Me, and I give to the house of thy father all the fire-offerings of the sons of Israel?

Why do ye kick at My sacrifice, and at Mine offering hich I commanded [in] My habitation, and dost honour thy sons above Me, to make yourselves fat from the first part of every offering of Israel, of My people?

’Therefore — the affirmation of Jehovah, God of Israel — I certainly said, Thy house and the house of thy father, do alk up and don before Me to the age; and no — the affirmation of Jehovah — Far be it from Me! for he ho is honouring Me, I honour, and those despising Me, are lightly esteemed.
’Lo, days [are] coming, and I have cut off thine arm, and the arm of the house of thy father, that an old man is not in thy house;
and thou hast beheld an adversary [in My] habitation, in all that He doth good ith Israel, and there is not an old man in thy house all the days.
’And the man I cut not off of thine from Mine altar, [is] to consume thine eyes, and to grieve thy soul; and all the increase of thy house do die men;
and this [is] to thee the sign that cometh unto thy to sons, unto Hophni and Phinehas — in one day they die both of them;
and I have raised up for Me a stedfast priest; as in My heart and in My soul he doth do; and I have built for him a stedfast house, and he hath alked up and don before Mine anointed all the days;

and it hath been, every one ho is left in thy house doth come in to bo himself to him, for a age of silver, and a cake of bread, and hath said, Admit me, I pray thee, unto one of the priest’s offices, to eat a morsel of bread.’
And the youth Samuel is serving Jehovah before Eli, and the ord of Jehovah hath been precious in those days — there is no vision broken forth.
And it cometh to pass, at that time, that Eli is lying don in his place, and his eyes have begun to be dim — he is not able to see.
And the lamp of God is not yet extinguished, and Samuel is lying don in the temple of Jehovah, here the ark of God [is],
and Jehovah calleth unto Samuel, and he saith, ’Here [am] I.’
And he runneth unto Eli, and saith, ’Here [am] I, for thou hast called for me;’ and he saith, ’I called not; turn back, lie don;’ and he goeth and lieth don.
And Jehovah addeth to call again Samuel, and Samuel riseth and goeth unto Eli, and saith, ’Here [am] I, for thou hast called for me;’ and he saith, ’I have not called, my son, turn back, lie don.’
And Samuel hath not yet knon Jehovah, and the ord of Jehovah is not yet revealed unto him.
And Jehovah addeth to call Samuel the third time, and he riseth and goeth unto Eli, and saith, ’Here [am] I, for thou hast called for me;’ and Eli understandeth that Jehovah is calling to the youth.
And Eli saith to Samuel, ’Go, lie don, and it hath been, if He doth call unto thee, that thou hast said, Speak, Jehovah, for Thy servant is hearing;’ and Samuel goeth and lieth don in his place.
And Jehovah cometh, and stationeth Himself, and calleth as time by time, ’Samuel, Samuel;’ and Samuel saith, ’Speak, for Thy servant is hearing.’
And Jehovah saith unto Samuel, ’Lo, I am doing a thing in Israel, at hich the to ears of every one hearing it do tingle.
In that day I establish unto Eli all that I have spoken unto his house, beginning and completing;
and I have declared to him that I am judging his house — to the age, for the iniquity hich he hath knon, for his sons are making themselves vile, and he hath not restrained them,
and therefore I have sorn to the house of Eli: the iniquity of the house of Eli is not atoned for, by sacrifice, and by offering — unto the age.’
And Samuel lieth till the morning, and openeth the doors of the house of Jehovah, and Samuel is afraid of declaring the vision unto Eli.
And Eli calleth Samuel, and saith, ’Samuel, my son;’ and he saith, ’Here [am] I.’

And he saith, ’What [is] the ord hich He hath spoken unto thee? I pray thee, hide it not from me; so doth God do to thee, and so doth He add, if thou hidest from me a ord of all the ords that He hath spoken unto thee.’
And Samuel declareth to him the hole of the ords, and hath not hid from him; and he saith, ’It [is] Jehovah; that hich is good in His eyes He doth.’
And Samuel groeth up, and Jehovah hath been ith him, and hath not let fall any of his ords to the earth;
and all Israel kno, from Dan even unto Beer-Sheba, that Samuel is established for a prophet to Jehovah.
And Jehovah addeth to appear in Shiloh, for Jehovah hath been revealed unto Samuel, in Shiloh, by the ord of Jehovah.
And the ord of Samuel is to all Israel, and Israel goeth out to meet the Philistines for battle, and they encamp by Eben-Ezer, and the Philistines have encamped in Aphek,

and the Philistines set themselves in array to meet Israel, and the battle spreadeth itself, and Israel is smitten before the Philistines, and they smite among the ranks in the field about four thousand men.

And the people cometh in unto the camp, and the elders of Israel say, ’Why hath Jehovah smitten us to-day before the Philistines? e take unto us from Shiloh the ark of the covenant of Jehovah, and it cometh into our midst, and He doth save us out of the hand of our enemies.’

And the people sendeth to Shiloh, and they take up thence the ark of the covenant of Jehovah of Hosts, inhabiting the cherubs, and there [are] to sons of Eli, ith the ark of the covenant of God, Hophni and Phinehas.
And it cometh to pass, at the coming in of the ark of the covenant of Jehovah unto the camp, that all Israel shout — a great shout — and the earth is moved.
And the Philistines hear the noise of the shouting, and say, ’What [is] the noise of this great shout in the camp of the Hebres?’ and they perceive that the ark of Jehovah hath come in unto the camp.
And the Philistines are afraid, for they said, ’God hath come in unto the camp;’ and they say, ’Woe to us, for there hath not been like this heretofore.
Woe to us, ho doth deliver us out of the hand of these honourable gods? these [are] the gods ho are smiting the Egyptians ith every plague in the ilderness.
Strengthen yourselves, and become men, O Philistines, lest ye do service to Hebres, as they have done to you — then ye have become men, and have fought.’
And the Philistines fight, and Israel is smitten, and they flee each to his tents, and the blo is very great, and there fall of Israel thirty thousand footmen;
and the ark of God hath been taken, and the to sons of Eli have died, Hophni and Phinehas.
And a man of Benjamin runneth out of the ranks, and cometh into Shiloh, on that day, and his long robes [are] rent, and earth on his head;

and he cometh in, and lo, Eli is sitting on the throne by the side of the ay, atching, for his heart hath been trembling for the ark of God, and the man hath come in to declare [it] in the city, and all the city crieth out.
And Eli heareth the noise of the cry, and saith, ’What — the noise of this tumult!’ And the man hasted, and cometh in, and declareth to Eli.
And Eli is a son of ninety and eight years, and his eyes have stood, and he hath not been able to see.
And the man saith unto Eli, ’I [am] he ho hath come out of the ranks, and I out of the ranks have fled to-day;’ and he saith, ’What hath been the matter, my son?’

And he ho is bearing tidings ansereth and saith, ’Israel hath fled before the Philistines, and also a great slaughter hath been among the people, and also thy to sons have died — Hophni and Phinehas — and the ark of God hath been captured.’

And it cometh to pass, at his mentioning the ark of God, that he falleth from off the throne backard, by the side of the gate, and his neck is broken, and he dieth, for the man [is] old and heavy, and he hath judged Israel forty years.

And his daughter-in-la, ife of Phinehas, [is] pregnant, about to bear, and she heareth the report of the taking of the ark of God, that her father-in-la and her husband have died, and she boeth, and beareth, for her pains have turned upon her.
And at the time of her death, hen the omen ho are standing by her say, ’Fear not, for a son thou hast borne,’ she hath not ansered, nor set her heart [to it];
and she calleth the youth I-Chabod, saying, ’Honour hath removed from Israel,’ because of the taking of the ark of God, and because of her father-in-la and her husband.
And she saith, ’Honour hath removed from Israel, for the ark of God hath been taken.’
And the Philistines have taken the ark of God, and bring it in from Eben-Ezer to Ashdod,
and the Philistines take the ark of God and bring it into the house of Dagon, and set it near Dagon.
And the Ashdodites rise early on the morro, and lo, Dagon is fallen on its face to the earth, before the ark of Jehovah; and they take Dagon, and put it back to its place.

And they rise early in the morning on the morro, and lo, Dagon is fallen on its face to the earth, before the ark of Jehovah, and the head of Dagon, and the to palms of its hands are cut off at the threshold, only the fishy part hath been left to him;
therefore the priests of Dagon, and all those coming into the house of Dagon, tread not on the threshold of Dagon, in Ashdod, till this day.
And the hand of Jehovah is heavy on the Ashdodites, and He maketh them desolate, and smiteth them ith emerods, Ashdod and its borders.
And the men of Ashdod see that [it is] so, and have said, ’The ark of the God of Israel doth not abide ith us, for hard hath been His hand upon us, and upon Dagon our god.’

And they send and gather all the princes of the Philistines unto them, and say, ’What do e do to the ark of the God of Israel?’ and they say, ’To Gath let the ark of the God of Israel be brought round;’ and they bring round the ark of the God of Israel;

and it cometh to pass after they have brought it round, that the hand of Jehovah is against the city — a very great destruction; and He smiteth the men of the city, from small even unto great; and break forth on them do emerods.

And they send the ark of God to Ekron, and it cometh to pass, at the coming in of the ark of God to Ekron, that the Ekronites cry out, saying, ’They have brought round unto us the ark of the God of Israel, to put us to death — and our people.’

And they send and gather all the princes of the Philistines, and say, ’Send aay the ark of the God of Israel, and it turneth back to its place, and it doth not put us to death — and our people;’ for there hath been a deadly destruction throughout all the city, very heavy hath the hand of God been there,
and the men ho have not died have been smitten ith emerods, and the cry of the city goeth up into the heavens.
And the ark of Jehovah is in the field of the Philistines seven months,
and the Philistines call for priests and for diviners, saying, ’What do e do to the ark of Jehovah? let us kno hereith e send it to its place?’
