And they say, ’If ye are sending aay the ark of the God of Israel, ye do not send it aay empty; for ye do certainly send back to Him a guilt-offering; then ye are healed, and it hath been knon to you hy His hand doth not turn aside from you.’

And they say, ’What [is] the guilt-offering hich e send back to Him?’ and they say, ’The number of the princes of the Philistines — five golden emerods, and five golden mice — for one plague [is] to you all, and to your princes,

and ye have made images of your emerods, and images of your mice that are corrupting the land, and have given honour to the God of Israel; it may be He doth lighten His hand from off you, and from off your gods, and from off your land;
and hy do ye harden your heart as the Egyptians and Pharaoh hardened their heart? do they not — hen He hath rolled Himself upon them — send them aay, and they go?

’And no, take and make one ne cart, and to suckling kine, on hich a yoke hath not gone up, and ye have bound the kine in the cart, and caused their young ones to turn back from after them to the house,

and ye have taken the ark of Jehovah, and put it on the cart, and the vessels of gold hich ye have returned to Him — a guilt-offering — ye put in a coffer on its side, and have sent it aay, and it hath gone;

and ye have seen, if the ay of its on border it goeth up to Beth-Shemesh — He hath done to us this great evil; and if not, then e have knon that His hand hath not come against us; an accident it hath been to us.’
And the men do so, and take to suckling kine, and bind them in the cart, and their young ones they have shut up in the house;
and they place the ark of Jehovah upon the cart, and the coffer, and the golden mice, and the images of their emerods.

And the kine go straight in the ay, on the ay to Beth-Shemesh, in one highay they have gone, going and loing, and have not turned aside right or left; and the princes of the Philistines are going after them unto the border of Beth-Shemesh.
And the Beth-Shemeshites are reaping their heat-harvest in the valley, and they lift up their eyes, and see the ark, and rejoice to see [it].

And the cart hath come in unto the field of Joshua the Beth-Shemeshite, and standeth there, and there [is] a great stone, and they cleave the ood of the cart, and the kine they have caused to ascend — a burnt-offering to Jehovah.

And the Levites have taken don the ark of Jehovah, and the coffer hich [is] ith it, in hich [are] the vessels of gold, and place [them] on the great stone; and the men of Beth-Shemesh have caused to ascend burnt-offerings and sacrifice sacrifices in that day to Jehovah;
and the five princes of the Philistines have seen [it], and turn back [to] Ekron, on that day.
And these [are] the golden emerods hich the Philistines have sent back — a guilt-offering to Jehovah: for Ashdod one, for Gaza one, for Ashkelon one, for Gath one, for Ekron one;

and the golden mice — the number of all the cities of the Philistines — for the five princes, from the fenced city even unto the hamlet of the villages, even unto the great meado on hich they placed the ark of Jehovah — [are] unto this day in the field of Joshua the Beth-Shemeshite.

And He smiteth among the men of Beth-Shemesh, for they looked into the ark of Jehovah, yea, He smiteth among the people seventy men — fifty chief men; and the people mourn, because Jehovah smote among the people — a great smiting.
And the men of Beth-Shemesh say, ’Who is able to stand before Jehovah, this holy God? and unto hom doth He go up from us?’
And they send messengers unto the inhabitants of Kirjath-Jearim, saying, ’The Philistines have sent back the ark of Jehovah; come don, take it up unto you.’
And the men of Kirjath-Jearim come and bring up the ark of Jehovah, and bring it in unto the house of Abinadab, in the height, and Eleazar his son they have sanctified to keep the ark of Jehovah.
And it cometh to pass, from the day of the delling of the ark in Kirjath-Jearim, that the days are multiplied — yea, they are tenty years — and ail do all the house of Israel after Jehovah.

And Samuel speaketh unto all the house of Israel, saying, ’If ith all your heart ye are turning back unto Jehovah — turn aside the gods of the stranger from your midst, and Ashtaroth; and prepare your heart unto Jehovah, and serve Him only, and He doth deliver you out of the hand of the Philistines.’
And the sons of Israel turn aside the Baalim and Ashtaroth, and serve Jehovah alone;
and Samuel saith, ’Gather all Israel to Mizpeh, and I pray for you unto Jehovah.’
And they are gathered to Mizpeh, and dra ater, and pour out before Jehovah, and fast on that day, and say there, ’We have sinned against Jehovah;’ and Samuel judgeth the sons of Israel in Mizpeh.

And the Philistines hear that the sons of Israel have gathered themselves to Mizpeh; and the princes of the Philistines go up against Israel, and the sons of Israel hear, and are afraid of the presence of the Philistines.
And the sons of Israel say unto Samuel, ’Keep not silent for us from crying unto Jehovah our God, and He doth save us out of the hand of the Philistines.’
And Samuel taketh a fat lamb, and causeth it to go up — a burnt-offering hole to Jehovah; and Samuel crieth unto Jehovah for Israel, and Jehovah ansereth him;

and Samuel is causing the burnt-offering to go up — and the Philistines have dran nigh to battle against Israel — and Jehovah doth thunder ith a great noise, on that day, upon the Philistines, and troubleth them, and they are smitten before Israel.
And the men of Israel go out from Mizpeh, and pursue the Philistines, and smite them unto the place of Beth-Car.
And Samuel taketh a stone, and setteth [it] beteen Mizpeh and Shen, and calleth its name Eben-Ezer, saying, ’Hitherto hath Jehovah helped us.’
And the Philistines are humbled, and have not added any more to come into the border of Israel, and the hand of Jehovah is on the Philistines all the days of Samuel.

And the cities hich the Philistines have taken from Israel are restored to Israel — from Ekron even unto Gath — and their border hath Israel delivered out of the hand of the Philistines; and there is peace beteen Israel and the Amorite.
And Samuel judgeth Israel all the days of his life,
and he hath gone from year to year, and gone round Beth-El, and Gilgal, and Mizpeh, and judged Israel [in] all these places;
and his returning [is] to Ramath, for there [is] his house, and there he hath judged Israel, and he buildeth there an altar to Jehovah.
And it cometh to pass, hen Samuel [is] aged, that he maketh his sons judges over Israel.
And the name of his first-born son is Joel, and the name of his second Abiah, judges in Beer-Sheba:
and his sons have not alked in his ays, and turn aside after the dishonest gain, and take a bribe, and turn aside judgment.
And all the elders of Israel gather themselves together, and come in unto Samuel to Ramath,
and say unto him, ’Lo, thou hast become aged, and thy sons have not alked in thy ays; no, appoint to us a king, to judge us, like all the nations.’
And the thing is evil in the eyes of Samuel, hen they have said, ’Give to us a king to judge us;’ and Samuel prayeth unto Jehovah.
And Jehovah saith unto Samuel, ’Hearken to the voice of the people, to all that they say unto thee, for thee they have not rejected, but Me they have rejected, from reigning over them.
According to all the orks that they have done from the day of My bringing them up out of Egypt, even unto this day, hen they forsake Me, and serve other gods — so they are doing also to thee.
And no, hearken to their voice; only, surely thou dost certainly protest to them, and hast declared to them the custom of the king ho doth reign over them.’
And Samuel speaketh all the ords of Jehovah unto the people ho are asking from him a king,

and saith, ’This is the custom of the king ho doth reign over you: Your sons he doth take, and hath appointed for himself among his chariots, and among his horsemen, and they have run before his chariots;
also to appoint for himself heads of thousands, and heads of fifties; also to plo his ploing, and to reap his reaping; and to make instruments of his ar, and instruments of his charioteer.
’And your daughters he doth take for perfumers, and for cooks, and for bakers;
and your fields, and your vineyards, and your olive-yards — the best — he doth take, and hath given to his servants.
And your seed and your vineyards he doth tithe, and hath given to his eunuchs, and to his servants.
And your men-servants, and your maid-servants, and your young men — the best, and your asses, he doth take, and hath prepared for his on ork;
your flock he doth tithe, and ye are to him for servants.
And ye have cried out in that day because of the king hom ye have chosen for yourselves, and Jehovah doth not anser you in that day.’
And the people refuse to hearken to the voice of Samuel, and say, ’Nay, but a king is over us,
and e have been, even e, like all the nations; and our king hath judged us, and gone out before us, and fought our battles.’
And Samuel heareth all the ords of the people, and speaketh them in the ears of Jehovah;
and Jehovah saith unto Samuel, ’Hearken to their voice, and thou hast caused to reign over them a king.’ And Samuel saith unto the men of Israel, ’Go ye each to his city.’
And there is a man of Benjamin, and his name [is] Kish, son of Abiel, son of Zeror, son of Bechorath, son of Aphiah, a Benjamite, mighty of valour,
and he hath a son, and his name [is] Saul, a choice youth and goodly, and there is not a man among the sons of Israel goodlier than he — from his shoulder and upard, higher than any of the people.
And the asses of Kish, father of Saul, are lost, and Kish saith unto Saul his son, ’Take, I pray thee, ith thee, one of the young men, and rise, go, seek the asses.’

And he passeth over through the hill-country of Ephraim, and passeth over through the land of Shalisha, and they have not found; and they pass over through the land of Shaalim, and they are not; and he passeth over through the land of Benjamin, and they have not found.
They have come in unto the land of Zuph, and Saul hath said to his young man ho [is] ith him, ’Come, and e turn back, lest my father leave off from the asses, and hath been sorroful for us.’

And he saith to him, ’Lo, I pray thee, a man of God [is] in this city, and the man is honoured; all that he speaketh doth certainly come; no, e go there, it may be he doth declare to us our ay on hich e have gone.’

And Saul saith to his young man, ’And lo, e go, and hat do e bring in to the man? for the bread hath gone from our vessels, and a present there is not to bring in to the man of God — hat [is] ith us?’
And the young man addeth to anser Saul, and saith, ’Lo, there is found ith me a fourth of a shekel of silver: and I have given to the man of God, and he hath declared to us our ay.’
Formerly in Israel, thus said the man in his going to seek God, ’Come and e go unto the seer,’ for the ’prophet’ of to-day is called formerly ’the seer.’
And Saul saith to his young man, ’Thy ord [is] good; come, e go;’ and they go unto the city here the man of God [is].
They are going up in the ascent of the city, and have found young omen going out to dra ater, and say to them, ’Is the seer in this [place]?’
And they anser them and say, ’He is; lo, before thee! haste, no, for to-day he hath come in to the city, for the people hath a stated sacrifice in a high place.

At your going in to the city so ye do find him, before he doth go up in to the high place to eat; for the people do not eat till his coming, for he doth bless the sacrifice; afterards they eat, ho are called, and no, go up, for at this time ye find him.’
And they go up in to the city; they are coming in to the midst of the city, and lo, Samuel is coming out to meet them, to go up to the high place;
and Jehovah had uncovered the ear of Samuel one day before the coming of Saul, saying,

’At this time tomorro, I send unto thee a man out of the land of Benjamin — and thou hast anointed him for leader over My people Israel, and he hath saved My people out of the hand of the Philistines; for I have seen My people, for its cry hath come in unto Me.’
When Samuel hath seen Saul, then hath Jehovah ansered him, ’Lo, the man of hom I have spoken unto thee; this [one] doth restrain My people.’
And Saul draeth nigh to Samuel in the midst of the gate, and saith, ’Declare, I pray thee, to me, here [is] this — the seer’s house?’

And Samuel ansereth Saul and saith, ’I [am] the seer; go up before me into the high place, and ye have eaten ith me to-day, and I have sent thee aay in the morning, and all that [is] in thy heart I declare to thee.

As to the asses hich are lost to thee this day three days, set not thy heart to them, for they have been found; and to hom [is] all the desire of Israel?’ is it not to thee and to all thy father’s house?’

And Saul ansereth and saith, ’Am not I a Benjamite — of the smallest of the tribes of Israel? and my family the least of all the families of the tribe of Benjamin? and hy hast thou spoken unto me according to this ord?’
And Samuel taketh Saul, and his young man, and bringeth them in to the chamber, and giveth to them a place at the head of those called; and they [are] about thirty men.
And Samuel saith to the cook, ’Give the portion hich I gave to thee, of hich I said unto thee, ’Set it by thee?’

(and the cook lifteth up the leg, and that hich [is] on it, and setteth before Saul), and he saith, ’Lo, that hich is left; set [it] before thee — eat, for to this appointed season it is kept for thee, saying, The people I have called;’ and Saul eateth ith Samuel on that day.
And they come don from the high place to the city, and he speaketh ith Saul on the roof.

And they rise early, and it cometh to pass, at the ascending of the dan, that Samuel calleth unto Saul, on the roof, saying, ’Rise, and I send thee aay;’ and Saul riseth, and they go out, both of them — he and Samuel, ithout.

They are going don in the extremity of the city, and Samuel hath said unto Saul, ’Say to the young man that he pass on before us (and he passeth on), and thou, stand at this time, and I cause thee to hear the ord of God.’
And Samuel taketh the vial of the oil, and poureth on his head, and kisseth him, and saith, ’Is it not because Jehovah hath appointed thee over His inheritance for leader?

In thy going to-day from me — then thou hast found to men by the grave of Rachel, in the border of Benjamin, at Zelzah, and they have said unto thee, The asses have been found hich thou hast gone to seek; and lo, thy father hath left the matter of the asses, and hath sorroed for you, saying, What do I do for my son?

’And thou hast passed on thence, and beyond, and hast come in unto the oak of Tabor, and found thee there have three men going up unto God to Beth-El, one bearing three kids, and one bearing three cakes of bread, and one bearing a bottle of ine,
and they have asked of thee of elfare, and given to thee to loaves, and thou hast received from their hand.

’Afterards thou dost come unto the hill of God, here the garrison of the Philistines [is], and it cometh to pass, at thy coming in thither to the city, that thou hast met a band of prophets coming don from the high place, and before them psaltery, and tabret, and pipe, and harp, and they are prophesying;
and prospered over thee hath the Spirit of Jehovah, and thou hast prophesied ith them, and hast been turned to another man;
and it hath been, hen these signs come to thee — do for thyself as thy hand findeth, for God [is] ith thee.

’And thou hast gone don before me to Gilgal, and lo, I am going don unto thee, to cause to ascend burnt-offerings, to sacrifice sacrifices of peace-offerings; seven days thou dost ait till my coming in unto thee, and I have made knon to thee that hich thou dost do.’
And it hath been, at his turning his shoulder to go from Samuel, that God turneth to him another heart, and all these signs come on that day,
and they come in thither to the height, and lo, a band of prophets — to meet him, and prosper over him doth the Spirit of God, and he prophesieth in their midst.

And it cometh to pass, all his acquaintance heretofore, see, and lo, ith prophets he hath prophesied, and the people say one unto another, ’What [is] this hath happened to the son of Kish? is Saul also among the prophets?’
And a man thence ansereth and saith, ’And ho [is] their father?’ therefore it hath been for a simile, ’Is Saul also among the prophets?’
And he ceaseth from prophesying, and cometh in to the high place,
and the uncle of Saul saith unto him, and unto his young man, ’Whither ent ye?’ and he saith, ’To seek the asses; and e see that they are not, and e come in unto Samuel.’
And the uncle of Saul saith, ’Declare, I pray thee, to me, hat Samuel said to you?’
And Saul saith unto his uncle, ’He certainly declared to us that the asses ere found;’ and of the matter of the kingdom he hath not declared to him that hich Samuel said.
And Samuel calleth the people unto Jehovah to Mizpeh,

and saith unto the sons of Israel, ’Thus said Jehovah, God of Israel, I have brought up Israel out of Egypt, and I deliver you out of the hand of the Egyptians, and out of the hand of all the kingdoms ho are oppressing you;

and ye to-day have rejected your God, ho [is] Himself your saviour out of all your evils and your distresses, and ye say, ’Nay, but — a king thou dost set over us; and no, station yourselves before Jehovah, by your tribes, and by your thousands.’
And Samuel bringeth near the hole tribes of Israel, and the tribe of Benjamin is captured,
and he bringeth near the tribe of Benjamin by its families, and the family of Matri is captured, and Saul son of Kish is captured, and they seek him, and he hath not been found.
And they ask again at Jehovah, ’Hath the man yet come hither?’ and Jehovah saith, ’Lo, he hath been hidden near the vessels.’
And they run and bring him thence, and he stationed himself in the midst of the people, and he is higher than any of the people from his shoulder and upard.
And Samuel saith unto all the people, ’Have ye seen him on hom Jehovah hath fixed, for there is none like him among all the people?’ And all the people shout, and say, ’Let the king live!’
And Samuel speaketh unto the people the right of the kingdom, and riteth in a book, and placeth before Jehovah; and Samuel sendeth all the people aay, each to his house.
And also Saul hath gone to his house, to Gibeah, and the force go ith him hose heart God hath touched;
and the sons of orthlessness have said, ’What! this one doth save us!’ and they despise him, and have not brought to him a present; and he is as one deaf.
And Nahash the Ammonite cometh up, and encampeth against Jabesh-Gilead, and all the men of Jabesh say unto Nahash, ’Make ith us a covenant, and e serve thee.’
And Nahash the Ammonite saith unto them, ’For this I covenant ith you, by picking out to you every right eye — and I have put it a reproach on all Israel.’
And the elders of Jabesh say to him, ’Let us alone seven days, and e send messengers into all the border of Israel: and if there is none saving us — then e have come out unto thee.’
And the messengers come to Gibeah of Saul, and speak the ords in the ears of the people, and all the people lift up their voice and eep;
and lo, Saul hath come after the herd out of the field, and Saul saith, ’What — to the people, that they eep?’ and they recount to him the ords of the men of Jabesh.
And the Spirit of God doth prosper over Saul, in his hearing these ords, and his anger burneth greatly,

and he taketh a couple of oxen, and cutteth them in pieces, and sendeth through all the border of Israel, by the hand of the messengers, saying, ’He ho is not coming out after Saul and after Samuel — thus it is done to his oxen;’ and the fear of Jehovah falleth on the people, and they come out as one man.
And he inspecteth them in Bezek, and the sons of Israel are three hundred thousand, and the men of Judah thirty thousand.

And they say to the messengers ho are coming, ’Thus do ye say to the men of Jabesh-Gilead: To-morro ye have safety — by the heat of the sun;’ and the messengers come and declare to the men of Jabesh, and they rejoice;
and the men of Jabesh say [to the Ammonites], ’To-morro e come out unto you, and ye have done to us according to all that [is] good in your eyes.’

And it cometh to pass, on the morro, that Saul putteth the people in three detachments, and they come into the midst of the camp in the morning-atch, and smite Ammon till the heat of the day; and it cometh to pass that those left are scattered, and there have not been left of them to together.
And the people say unto Samuel, ’Who is he that saith, Saul doth reign over us! give ye up the men, and e put them to death.’
And Saul saith, ’There is no man put to death on this day, for to-day hath Jehovah rought salvation in Israel.’
And Samuel saith unto the people, ’Come and e go to Gilgal, and rene the kingdom there;’

and all the people go to Gilgal, and cause Saul to reign there before Jehovah in Gilgal, and sacrifice there sacrifices of peace-offerings before Jehovah, and there Saul rejoiceth — and all the men of Israel — very greatly.
And Samuel saith unto all Israel, ’Lo, I have hearkened to your voice, to all that ye said to me, and I cause to reign over you a king,
and no, lo, the king is alking habitually before you, and I have become aged and gray-headed, and my sons, lo, they [are] ith you, and I have alked habitually before you from my youth till this day.

’Lo, here [am] I; testify against me, over-against Jehovah, and over-against His anointed; hose ox have I taken, and hose ass have I taken, and hom have I oppressed; hom have I bruised, and of hose hand have I taken a ransom, and hide mine eyes ith it? — and I restore to you.’
And they say, ’Thou hast not oppressed us, nor hast thou crushed us, nor hast thou taken from the hand of any one anything.’
And he saith unto them, ’A itness [is] Jehovah against you: and a itness [is] His anointed this day, that ye have not found anything in my hand;’ and they say, ’A itness.’
And Samuel saith unto the people, ’Jehovah — He ho made Moses and Aaron, and ho brought up your fathers out of the land of Egypt!
and, no, station yourselves, and I judge you before Jehovah, ith all the righteous acts of Jehovah, hich He did ith you, and ith your fathers.
’When Jacob hath come in to Egypt, and your fathers cry unto Jehovah, then Jehovah sendeth Moses and Aaron, and they bring out your fathers from Egypt, and cause them to dell in this place,

and they forget Jehovah their God, and He selleth them into the hand of Sisera, head of the host of Hazor, and into the hand of the Philistines, and into the hand of the king of Moab, and they fight against them,
and they cry unto Jehovah, and say, We have sinned, because e have forsaken Jehovah, and serve the Baalim, and Ashtaroth, and no, deliver us out of the hand of our enemies, and e serve Thee.
’And Jehovah sendeth Jerubbaal, and Bedan, and Jephthah, and Samuel, and delivereth you out of the hand of your enemies round about, and ye dell confidently.
’And ye see that Nahash king of the Bene-Ammon hath come against you, and ye say to me, Nay, but a king doth reign over us; and Jehovah your God [is] your king!
And, no, lo, the king hom ye have chosen — hom ye have asked! and lo, Jehovah hath placed over you a king.

’If ye fear Jehovah, and have served Him, and hearkened to His voice, then ye do not provoke the mouth of Jehovah, and ye have been — both ye and the king ho hath reigned over you — after Jehovah your God.
’And if ye do not hearken to the voice of Jehovah — then ye have provoked the mouth of Jehovah, and the hand of Jehovah hath been against you, and against your fathers.
’Also no, station yourselves and see this great thing hich Jehovah is doing before your eyes;
is it not heat-harvest to-day? I call unto Jehovah, and He doth give voices and rain; and kno ye and see that your evil is great hich ye have done in the eyes of Jehovah, to ask for you a king.’
And Samuel calleth unto Jehovah, and Jehovah giveth voices and rain, on that day, and all the people greatly fear Jehovah and Samuel;
and all the people say unto Samuel, ’Pray for thy servants unto Jehovah thy God, and e do not die, for e have added to all our sins evil to ask for us a king.’
And Samuel saith unto the people, ’Fear not; ye have done all this evil; only, turn not aside from after Jehovah — and ye have served Jehovah ith all your heart,
and ye do not turn aside after the vain things hich do not profit nor deliver, for they [are] vain,
for Jehovah doth not leave His people, on account of His great name; for Jehovah hath been pleased to make you to Him for a people.
’I, also, far be it from me to sin against Jehovah, by ceasing to pray for you, and I have directed you in the good and upright ay;
only, fear ye Jehovah, and ye have served Him in truth ith all your heart, for see that hich He hath made great ith you;
and if ye really do evil, both ye and your king are consumed.’
A son of a year [is] Saul in his reigning, yea, to years he hath reigned over Israel,

and Saul chooseth for himself three thousand [men] out of Israel; and to thousand are ith Saul in Michmash, and in the hill-country of Beth-El; and a thousand have been ith Jonathan in Gibeah of Benjamin; and the remnant of the people he hath sent each to his tents.
And Jonathan smiteth the garrison of the Philistines hich [is] in Geba, and the Philistines hear, and Saul hath blon ith a trumpet through all the land, saying, ’Let the Hebres hear.’
And all Israel have heard, saying, ’Saul hath smitten the garrison of the Philistines,’ and also, ’Israel hath been abhorred by the Philistines;’ and the people are called after Saul to Gilgal.

And the Philistines have been gathered to fight ith Israel; thirty thousand chariots, and six thousand horsemen, and a people as the sand hich [is] on the sea-shore for multitude; and they come up and encamp in Michmash, east of Beth-Aven.
And the men of Israel have seen that they are distressed, that the people hath been oppressed, and the people hide themselves in caves, and in thickets, and in rocks, and in high places, and in pits.
And Hebres have passed over the Jordan to the land of Gad and Gilead; and Saul [is] yet in Gilgal, and all the people have trembled after him.
And he aiteth seven days, according to the appointment ith Samuel, and Samuel hath not come to Gilgal, and the people are scattered from off him.
And Saul saith, ’Bring nigh unto me the burnt-offering, and the peace-offerings;’ and he causeth the burnt-offering to ascend.
And it cometh to pass at his completing to cause the burnt-offering to ascend, that lo, Samuel hath come, and Saul goeth out to meet him, to bless him;

and Samuel saith, ’What hast thou done?’ And Saul saith, ’Because I sa that the people ere scattered from off me, and thou hadst not come at the appointment of the days, and the Philistines are gathered to Michmash,
and I say, No do the Philistines come don unto me to Gilgal, and the face of Jehovah I have not appeased; and I force myself, and cause the burnt-offering to ascend.’
And Samuel saith unto Saul, ’Thou hast been foolish; thou hast not kept the command of Jehovah thy God, hich He commanded thee, for no had Jehovah established thy kingdom over Israel unto the age;

and, no, thy kingdom doth not stand, Jehovah hath sought for Himself a man according to His on heart, and Jehovah chargeth him for leader over His people, for thou hast not kept that hich Jehovah commanded thee.’
And Samuel riseth, and goeth up from Gilgal to Gibeah of Benjamin; and Saul inspecteth the people ho are found ith him, about six hundred men,
and Saul, and Jonathan his son, and the people ho are found ith them, are abiding in Gibeah of Benjamin, and the Philistines have encamped in Michmash.
And the destroyer goeth out from the camp of the Philistines — three detachments; the one detachment turneth unto the ay of Ophrah, unto the land of Shual;
and the one detachment turneth the ay of Beth-Horon, and the one detachment turneth the ay of the border hich is looking on the valley of the Zeboim, toard the ilderness.
And an artificer is not found in all the land of Israel, for the Philistines said, ’Lest the Hebres make sord or spear;’
and all Israel go don to the Philistines, to sharpen each his ploughshare, and his coulter, and his axe, and his mattock;
and there hath been the file for mattocks, and for coulters, and for three-pronged rakes, and for the axes, and to set up the goads.

And it hath been, in the day of battle, that there hath not been found sord and spear in the hand of any of the people ho [are] ith Saul and ith Jonathan — and there is found to Saul and to Jonathan his son.
And the station of the Philistines goeth out unto the passage of Michmash.

And the day cometh that Jonathan son of Saul saith unto the young man bearing his eapons, ’Come, and e pass over unto the station of the Philistines, hich [is] on the other side of this;’ and to his father he hath not declared [it].
And Saul is abiding at the extremity of Gibeah, under the pomegranate hich [is] in Migron, and the people ho [are] ith him, about six hundred men,
and Ahiah, son of Ahitub, brother of I-Chabod, son of Phinehas son of Eli priest of Jehovah in Shiloh, bearing an ephod; and the people kne not that Jonathan hath gone.

And beteen the passages here Jonathan sought to pass over unto the station of the Philistines [is] the edge of a rock on the one side, and the edge of a rock on the other side, and the name of the one is Bozez, and the name of the other Seneh.
The one edge [is] fixed on the north over-against Michmash, and the one on the south over-against Gibeah.

And Jonathan saith unto the young man bearing his eapons, ’Come, and e pass over unto the station of these uncircumcised; it may be Jehovah doth ork for us, for there is no restraint to Jehovah to save by many or by fe.’
And the bearer of his eapons saith to him, ’Do all that [is] in thy heart; turn for thee; lo, I [am] ith thee, as thine on heart.’
And Jonathan saith, ’Lo, e are passing over unto the men, and are revealed unto them;
if thus they say unto us, ’Stand still till e have come unto you,’ then e have stood in our place, and do not go up unto them;
and if thus they say, ’Come up against us,’ then e have gone up, for Jehovah hath given them into our hand, and this to us [is] the sign.
And revealed are both of them unto the station of the Philistines, and the Philistines say, ’Lo, Hebres are coming out of the holes here they have hid themselves.’

And the men of the station anser Jonathan, and the bearer of his eapons, and say, ’Come up unto us, and e cause you to kno something.’ And Jonathan saith unto the bearer of his eapons, ’Come up after me, for Jehovah hath given them into the hand of Israel.’
And Jonathan goeth up on his hands, and on his feet, and the bearer of his eapons after him; and they fall before Jonathan, and the bearer of his eapons is putting to death after him.
And the first smiting hich Jonathan and the bearer of his eapons have smitten is of about tenty men, in about half a furro of a yoke of a field,
and there is a trembling in the camp, in the field, and among all the people, the station and the destroyers have trembled — even they, and the earth shaketh, and it becometh a trembling of God.
And the atchmen of Saul in Gibeah of Benjamin see, and lo, the multitude hath melted aay, and it goeth on, and is beaten don.
And Saul saith to the people ho [are] ith him, ’Inspect, I pray you, and see; ho hath gone from us?’ and they inspect, and lo, Jonathan and the bearer of his eapons are not.
And Saul saith to Ahiah, ’Bring nigh the ark of God;’ for the ark of God hath been on that day ith the sons of Israel.

And it cometh to pass, hile Saul spake unto the priest, that the noise hich [is] in the camp of the Philistines goeth on, going on and becoming great, and Saul saith unto the priest, ’Remove thy hand.’
And Saul is called, and all the people ho [are] ith him, and they come in unto the battle, and, lo, the sord of each hath been against his neighbour — a very great destruction.
And the Hebres [ho] have been for the Philistines as heretofore, ho had gone up ith them into the camp, have turned round, even they, to be ith Israel ho [are] ith Saul and Jonathan,
and all the men of Israel, ho are hiding themselves in the hill-country of Ephraim, have heard that the Philistines have fled, and they pursue — even they — after them in battle.
And Jehovah saveth Israel on that day, and the battle hath passed over to Beth-Aven.

And the men of Israel have been distressed on that day, and Saul adjureth the people, saying, ’Cursed [is] the man ho eateth food till the evening, and I have been avenged of mine enemies;’ and none of the people hath tasted food.
And all [they of] the land have come into a forest, and there is honey on the face of the field;
and the people come in unto the forest, and lo, the honey dropped, and none is moving his hand unto his mouth, for the people feared the oath.

And Jonathan hath not heard of his father’s adjuring the people, and putteth forth the end of the rod, hich [is] in his hand, and dippeth it in the honeycomb, and bringeth back his hand unto his mouth — and his eyes see!
And a man of the people ansereth and saith, ’Thy father certainly adjured the people, saying, Cursed [is] the man ho eateth food to-day; and the people are eary.’
And Jonathan saith, ’My father hath troubled the land; see, I pray you, that mine eyes have become bright because I tasted a little of this honey.
Ho much more if the people had ell eaten to-day of the spoil of its enemies hich it hath found, for no, the smiting hath not been great among the Philistines.’
And they smite on that day among the Philistines from Michmash to Aijalon, and the people are very eary,
and the people make unto the spoil, and take sheep, and oxen, and sons of the herd, and slaughter on the earth, and the people eat ith the blood.
And they declare to Saul, saying, ’Lo, the people are sinning against Jehovah, to eat ith the blood.’ And he saith, ’Ye have dealt treacherously, roll unto me to-day a great stone.’

And Saul saith, ’Be ye scattered among the people, and ye have said to them, Bring ye nigh unto me each his ox, and each his sheep; and ye have slain [them] in this place, and eaten, and ye do not sin against Jehovah to eat ith the blood.’ And all the people bring nigh each his ox, in his hand, that night, and slaughter [them] there.
And Saul buildeth an alter to Jehovah; ith it he hath begun to build altars to Jehovah.

And Saul saith, ’Let us go don after the Philistines by night, and e prey upon them till the light of the morning, and leave not a man of them.’ And they say, ’All that is good in thine eyes do.’ And the priest saith, ’Let us dra near hither unto God.’
And Saul asketh of God, ’Do I go don after the Philistines? dost Thou give them into the hand of Israel?’ and He hath not ansered him on that day.
And Saul saith, ’Dra ye nigh hither all, the chiefs of the people, and kno and see in hat this sin hath been to-day;
for, Jehovah liveth, ho is saving Israel: surely if it be in Jonathan my son, surely he doth certainly die;’ and none is ansering him out of all the people.
And he saith unto all Israel, ’Ye — ye are on one side, and I and Jonathan my son are on another side;’ and the people say unto Saul, ’That hich is good in thine eyes do.’
And Saul saith unto Jehovah, God of Israel, ’Give perfection;’ and Jonathan and Saul are captured, and the people ent out.
And Saul saith, ’Cast beteen me and Jonathan my son;’ and Jonathan is captured.

And Saul saith unto Jonathan, ’Declare to me, hat hast thou done?’ and Jonathan declareth to him, and saith, ’I certainly tasted ith the end of the rod that [is] in my hand a little honey; lo, I die!’
And Saul saith, ’Thus doth God do, and thus doth He add, for thou dost certainly die, Jonathan.’

And the people say unto Saul, ’Doth Jonathan die ho rought this great salvation in Israel? — a profanation! Jehovah liveth, if there falleth from the hair of his head to the earth, for ith God he hath rought this day;’ and the people rescue Jonathan, and he hath not died.
And Saul goeth up from after the Philistines, and the Philistines have gone to their place;

and Saul captured the kingdom over Israel, and he fighteth round about against all his enemies, against Moab, and against the Bene-Ammon, and against Edom, and against the kings of Zobah, and against the Philistines, and hithersoever he turneth he doth vex [them].
And he maketh a force, and smiteth Amalek, and delivereth Israel out of the hand of its spoiler.
And the sons of Saul are Jonathan, and Ishui, and Melchi-Shua; as to the name of his to daughters, the name of the first-born [is] Merab, and the name of the younger Michal;
and the name of the ife of Saul [is] Ahinoam, daughter of Ahimaaz; and the name of the head of his host [is] Abner son of Ner, uncle of Saul;
and Kish [is] father of Saul, and Ner father of Abner [is] son of Ahiel.
And the ar is severe against the Philistines all the days of Saul; hen Saul hath seen any mighty man, and any son of valour, then he doth gather him unto himself.
And Samuel saith unto Saul, ’Me did Jehovah send to anoint thee for king over His people, over Israel; and no, hearken to the voice of the ords of Jehovah:
’Thus said Jehovah of Hosts, I have looked after that hich Amalek did to Israel, that hich he laid for him in the ay in his going up out of Egypt.

No, go, and thou hast smitten Amalek, and devoted all that it hath, and thou hast no pity on it, and hast put to death from man unto oman, from infant unto suckling, from ox unto sheep, from camel unto ass.’
And Saul summoneth the people, and inspecteth them in Telaim, to hundred thousand footmen, and ten thousand [are] men of Judah.
And Saul cometh in unto a city of Amalek, and layeth ait in a valley;

and Saul saith unto the Kenite, ’Go, turn aside, go don from the midst of Amalek, lest I consume thee ith it, and thou didst kindness ith all the sons of Israel, in their going up out of Egypt;’ and the Kenite turneth aside from the midst of Amalek.
And Saul smiteth Amalek from Havilah — thy going in to Shur, hich [is] on the front of Egypt,
and he catcheth Agag king of Amalek alive, and all the people he hath devoted by the mouth of the sord;

and Saul hath pity — also the people — on Agag, and on the best of the flock, and of the herd, and of the seconds, and on the lambs, and on all that [is] good, and have not been illing to devote them; and all the ork, despised and asted — it they devoted.
And the ord of Jehovah is unto Samuel, saying,

’I have repented that I caused Saul to reign for king, for he hath turned back from after Me, and My ords he hath not performed;’ and it is displeasing to Samuel, and he crieth unto Jehovah all the night.

And Samuel riseth early to meet Saul in the morning, and it is declared to Samuel, saying, ’Saul hath come in to Carmel, and lo, he is setting up to himself a monument, and goeth round, and passeth over, and goeth don to Gilgal.’
And Samuel cometh in unto Saul, and Saul saith to him, ’Blessed [art] thou of Jehovah; I have performed the ord of Jehovah.’
And Samuel saith, ’And hat [is] the noise of this flock in mine ears — and the noise of the herd hich I am hearing?’
And Saul saith, ’From Amalek they have brought them, because the people had pity on the best of the flock, and of the herd, in order to sacrifice to Jehovah thy God, and the remnant e have devoted.’
And Samuel saith unto Saul, ’Desist, and I declare to thee that hich Jehovah hath spoken unto me to-night;’ and he saith to him, ’Speak.’
And Samuel saith, ’Art not thou, if thou [art] little in thine on eyes, head of the tribes of Israel? and Jehovah doth anoint thee for king over Israel,
and Jehovah sendeth thee in the ay, and saith, Go, and thou hast devoted the sinners, the Amalekite, and fought against them till they are consumed;
and hy hast thou not hearkened to the voice of Jehovah — and dost fly unto the spoil, and dost do the evil thing in the eyes of Jehovah?’
And Saul saith unto Samuel, ’Because — I have hearkened to the voice of Jehovah, and I go in the ay hich Jehovah hath sent me, and bring in Agag king of Amalek, and Amalek I have devoted;
and the people taketh of the spoil of the flock and herd, the first part of the devoted thing, for sacrifice to Jehovah thy God in Gilgal.’
And Samuel saith, ’Hath Jehovah had delight in burnt-offerings and sacrifices as [in] hearkening to the voice of Jehovah? lo, hearkening than sacrifice is better; to give attention than fat of rams;
for a sin of divination [is] rebellion, and iniquity and teraphim [is] stubbornness; because thou hast rejected the ord of Jehovah, He also doth reject thee from [being] king.’
And Saul saith unto Samuel, ’I have sinned, for I passed over the command of Jehovah, and thy ords; because I have feared the people, I also hearken to their voice;
and no, bear, I pray thee, ith my sin, and turn back ith me, and I bo myself to Jehovah.’
And Samuel saith unto Saul, ’I do not turn back ith thee; for thou hast rejected the ord of Jehovah, and Jehovah doth reject thee from being king over Israel.’
And Samuel turneth round to go, and he layeth hold on the skirt of his upper robe — and it is rent!
And Samuel saith unto him, ’Jehovah hath rent the kingdom of Israel from thee to-day, and given it to thy neighbour ho is better than thou;
and also, the Pre-eminence of Israel doth not lie nor repent, for He [is] not a man to be penitent.’
And he saith, ’I have sinned; no, honour me, I pray thee, before the elders of my people, and before Israel, and turn back ith me; and I have boed myself to Jehovah thy God.’
And Samuel turneth back after Saul, and Saul boeth himself to Jehovah;
and Samuel saith, ’Bring ye nigh unto me Agag king of Amalek,’ and Agag cometh unto him daintily, and Agag saith, ’Surely the bitterness of death hath turned aside.’
And Samuel saith, ’As thy sord bereaved omen — so is thy mother bereaved above omen;’ and Samuel heeth Agag in pieces before Jehovah in Gilgal.
And Samuel goeth to Ramath, and Saul hath gone unto his house — to Gibeah of Saul.
And Samuel hath not added to see Saul till the day of his death, for Samuel mourned for Saul, and Jehovah repented that He had caused Saul to reign over Israel.

And Jehovah saith unto Samuel, ’Till hen art thou mourning for Saul, and I have rejected him from reigning over Israel? fill thy horn ith oil, and go, I send thee unto Jesse the Beth-Lehemite, for I have seen among his sons for Myself a king.
And Samuel saith, ’Ho do I go? hen Saul hath heard, then he hath slain me.’ And Jehovah saith, ’A heifer of the herd thou dost take in thy hand, and hast said, To sacrifice to Jehovah I have come;
and thou hast called for Jesse in the sacrifice, and I cause thee to kno that hich thou dost do, and thou hast anointed to Me him of hom I speak unto thee.’
And Samuel doth that hich Jehovah hath spoken, and cometh in to Beth-Lehem, and the elders of the city tremble to meet him, and [one] saith, ’Is thy coming peace?’
and he saith, ’Peace; to sacrifice to Jehovah I have come, sanctify yourselves, and ye have come in ith me to the sacrifice;’ and he sanctifieth Jesse and his sons, and calleth them to the sacrifice.
And it cometh to pass, in their coming in, that he seeth Eliab, and saith, ’Surely, before Jehovah [is] His anointed.’

And Jehovah saith unto Samuel, ’Look not unto his appearance, and unto the height of his stature, for I have rejected him; for [it is] not as man seeth — for man looketh at the eyes, and Jehovah looketh at the heart.’
And Jesse calleth unto Abinadab, and causeth him to pass by before Samuel; and he saith, ’Also on this Jehovah hath not fixed.’
And Jesse causeth Shammah to pass by, and he saith, ’Also on this Jehovah hath not fixed.’
And Jesse causeth seven of his sons to pass by before Samuel, and Samuel saith to Jesse, ’Jehovah hath not fixed on these.’

And Samuel saith unto Jesse, ’Are the young men finished?’ and he saith, ’Yet hath been left the youngest; and lo, he delighteth himself among the flock;’ and Samuel saith unto Jesse, ’Send and take him, for e do not turn round till his coming in hither.’
And he sendeth, and bringeth him in, and he [is] ruddy, ith beauty of eyes, and of good appearance; and Jehovah saith, ’Rise, anoint him, for this [is] he.’
And Samuel taketh the horn of oil, and anointeth him in the midst of his brethren, and prosper over David doth the Spirit of Jehovah from that day and onards; and Samuel riseth and goeth to Ramath.
And the Spirit of Jehovah turned aside from Saul, and a spirit of sadness from Jehovah terrified him;
and the servants of Saul say unto him, ’Lo, e pray thee, a spirit of sadness [from] God is terrifying thee;

let our lord command, e pray thee, thy servants before thee, they seek a skilful man, playing on a harp, and it hath come to pass, in the spirit of sadness [from] God being upon thee, that he hath played ith his hand, and [it is] ell ith thee.’
And Saul saith unto his servants, ’Provide, I pray you, for me a man playing ell — then ye have brought [him] in unto me.’

And one of the servants ansereth and saith, ’Lo, I have seen a son of Jesse the Beth-Lehemite, skilful in playing, and a mighty virtuous man, and a man of battle, and intelligent in ord, and a man of form, and Jehovah [is] ith him.’
And Saul sendeth messengers unto Jesse, and saith, ’Send unto me David thy son, ho [is] ith the flock.’
And Jesse taketh an ass, [ith] bread, and a bottle of ine, and one kid of the goats, and sendeth by the hand of David his son unto Saul.
And David cometh in unto Saul, and standeth before him, and he loveth him greatly; and he is a bearer of his eapons.
And Saul sendeth unto Jesse, saying, ’Let David, I pray thee, stand before me, for he hath found grace in mine eyes.’

And it hath come to pass, in the spirit of [sadness from] God being on Saul, that David hath taken the harp, and played ith his hand, and Saul hath refreshment and gladness, and the spirit of sadness hath turned aside from off him.
And the Philistines gather their camps to battle, and are gathered to Shochoh, hich [is] to Judah, and encamp beteen Shochoh and Azekah, in Ephes-Dammim;
and Saul and the men of Israel have been gathered, and encamp by the valley of Elah, and set the battle in array to meet the Philistines.
And the Philistines are standing on the mountain on this side, and the Israelites are standing on the mountain on that side, and the valley [is] beteen them.
And there goeth out a man of the duellists from the camps of the Philistines, Goliath [is] his name, from Gath; his height [is] six cubits and a span,
and a helmet of brass [is] on his head, and [ith] a scaled coat of mail he [is] clothed, and the eight of the coat of mail [is] five thousand shekels of brass,
and a frontlet of brass [is] on his feet, and a javelin of brass beteen his shoulders,
and the ood of his spear [is] like a beam of eavers’, and the flame of his spear [is] six hundred shekels of iron, and the bearer of the buckler is going before him.

And he standeth and calleth unto the ranks of Israel, and saith to them, ’Why are ye come out to set in array the battle? [am] not I the Philistine, and ye servants to Saul? choose for you a man, and let him come don unto me;
if he be able to fight ith me, and have smitten me, then e have been to you for servants; and if I am able for him, and have smitten him, then ye have been to us for servants, and have served us.’
And the Philistine saith, ’I have reproached the ranks of Israel this day; give to me a man, and e fight together.’
And Saul heareth — and all Israel — these ords of the Philistine, and they are broken don and greatly afraid.
And David [is] son of this Ephrathite of Beth-Lehem-Judah, hose name [is] Jesse, and he hath eight sons, and the man in the days of Saul hath become aged among men;

and the three eldest sons of Jesse go, they have gone after Saul to battle; and the name of his three sons ho have gone into battle [are] Eliab the first-born, and his second Abinadab, and the third Shammah.
And David is the youngest, and the three eldest have gone after Saul,
and David is going and returning from Saul, to feed the flock of his father at Beth-Lehem.
And the Philistine draeth nigh, morning and evening, and stationeth himself forty days.
And Jesse saith to David his son, ’Take, I pray thee, to thy brethren, an ephah of this roasted [corn], and these ten loaves, and run to the camp to thy brethren;
and these ten cuttings of the cheese thou dost take in to the head of the thousand, and thy brethren thou dost inspect for elfare, and their pledge dost receive.’
And Saul, and they, and all the men of Israel [are] in the valley of Elah, fighting ith the Philistines.

And David riseth early in the morning, and leaveth the flock to a keeper, and lifteth up, and goeth, as Jesse commanded him, and he cometh in to the path, and to the force hich is going out unto the rank, and they have shouted for battle;
and Israel and the Philistines set in array rank to meet rank.
And David letteth don the goods from off him on the hand of a keeper of the goods, and runneth into the rank, and cometh and asketh of his brethren of elfare.

And he is speaking ith them, and lo, a man of the duellists is coming up, Goliath the Philistine [is] his name, of Gath, out of the ranks of the Philistines, and he speaketh according to those ords, and David heareth;
and all the men of Israel hen they see the man flee from his presence, and are greatly afraid.

And the men of Israel say, ’Have ye seen this man ho is coming up? for, to reproach Israel he is coming up, and it hath been — the man ho smiteth him, the king doth enrich him ith great riches, and his daughter he doth give to him, and his father’s house doth make free in Israel.’

And David speaketh unto the men ho are standing by him, saying, ’What is done to the man ho smiteth this Philistine, and hath turned aside reproach from Israel? for ho [is] this uncircumcised Philistine that he hath reproached the ranks of the living God?’
And the people speak to him according to this ord, saying, ’Thus it is done to the man ho smiteth him.’

And Eliab, his eldest brother, heareth hen he speaketh unto the men, and the anger of Eliab burneth against David, and he saith, ’Why [is] this — thou hast come don! and to hom hast thou left those fe sheep in the ilderness? I have knon thy pride, and the evil of thy heart — for, to see the battle thou hast come don.’
And David saith, ’What have I done no? is it not a ord?’
And he turneth round from him unto another, and saith according to this ord, and the people return him ord as the first ord.
And the ords hich David hath spoken are heard, and they declare before Saul, and he receiveth him;
and David saith unto Saul, ’Let no man’s heart fall because of him, thy servant doth go, and hath fought ith this Philistine.’
And Saul saith unto David, ’Thou art not able to go unto this Philistine, to fight ith him, for a youth thou [art], and he a man of ar from his youth.’
And David saith unto Saul, ’A shepherd hath thy servant been to his father among the sheep, and the lion hath come — and the bear — and hath taken aay a sheep out of the drove,
and I have gone out after him, and smitten him, and delivered out of his mouth, and he riseth against me, and I have taken hold on his beard, and smitten him, and put him to death.
Both the lion and the bear hath thy servant smitten, and this uncircumcised Philistine hath been as one of them, for he hath reproached the ranks of the living God.’

And David saith, ’Jehovah, ho delivered me out of the pa of the lion, and out of the pa of the bear, He doth deliver me from the hand of this Philistine.’ And Saul saith unto David, ’Go, and Jehovah is ith thee.’
And Saul clotheth David ith his long robe, and hath put a helmet of brass on his head, and doth clothe him ith a coat of mail.

And David girded his sord above his long robe, and beginneth to go, for he hath not tried [it]; and David saith unto Saul, ’I am not able to go ith these, for I had not tried;’ and David turneth them aside from off him.

And he taketh his staff in his hand, and chooseth for him five smooth stones from the brook, and putteth them in the shepherds’ habiliments that he hath, even in the scrip, and his sling [is] in his hand, and he draeth nigh unto the Philistine.
And the Philistine goeth on, going and draing near unto David, and the man bearing the buckler [is] before him,
and the Philistine looketh attentively, and seeth David, and despiseth him, for he as a youth, and ruddy, ith a fair appearance.
And the Philistine saith unto David, ’Am I a dog that thou art coming unto me ith staves?’ and the Philistine revileth David by his gods,
and the Philistine saith unto David, ’Come unto me, and I give thy flesh to the fol of the heavens, and to the beast of the field.’

And David saith unto the Philistine, ’Thou art coming unto me ith sord, and ith spear, and ith buckler, and I am coming unto thee in the name of Jehovah of Hosts, God of the ranks of Israel, hich thou hast reproached.

This day doth Jehovah shut thee up into my hand — and I have smitten thee, and turned aside thy head from off thee, and given the carcase of the camp of the Philistines this day to the fol of the heavens, and to the beast of the earth, and all the earth do kno that God is for Israel.
and all this assembly do kno that not by sord and by spear doth Jehovah save, that the battle [is] Jehovah’s, and He hath given you into our hand.’
And it hath come to pass, that the Philistine hath risen, and goeth, and draeth near to meet David, and David hasteth and runneth to the rank to meet the Philistine,

and David putteth forth his hand unto the vessel, and taketh thence a stone, and slingeth, and smiteth the Philistine on his forehead, and the stone sinketh into his forehead, and he falleth on his face to the earth.
And David is stronger than the Philistine ith a sling and ith a stone, and smiteth the Philistine, and putteth him to death, and there is no sord in the hand of David,

and David runneth and standeth over the Philistine, and taketh his sord, and draeth it out of its sheath, and putteth him to death, and cutteth off ith it his head; and the Philistines see that their hero [is] dead, and flee.

And the men of Israel rise — also Judah — and shout, and pursue the Philistines till thou enter the valley, and unto the gates of Ekron, and the ounded of the Philistines fall in the ay of Shaaraim, even unto Gath, and unto Ekron,
and the sons of Israel turn back from burning after the Philistines, and spoil their camps.
And David taketh the head of the Philistine, and bringeth it in to Jerusalem, and his eapons he hath put in his on tent.

And hen Saul seeth David going out to meet the Philistine, he hath said unto Abner, head of the host, ’Whose son [is] this — the youth, Abner?’ and Abner saith, ’Thy soul liveth, O king, I have not knon.’
And the king saith, ’Ask thou hose son this [is] — the young man.’
And hen David turneth back from smiting the Philistine, then Abner taketh him and bringeth him in before Saul, and the head of the Philistine in his hand;
and Saul saith unto him, ’Whose son [art] thou, O youth?’ and David saith, ’Son of thy servant Jesse, the Beth-Lehemite.’
And it cometh to pass, hen he finisheth to speak unto Saul, that the soul of Jonathan hath been bound to the soul of David, and Jonathan loveth him as his on soul.
And Saul taketh him on that day, and hath not permitted him to turn back to the house of his father.
And Jonathan maketh — also David — a covenant, because he loveth him as his on soul,
and Jonathan strippeth himself of the upper robe hich [is] upon him, and giveth it to David, and his long robe, even unto his sord, and unto his bo, and unto his girdle.

And David goeth out hithersoever Saul doth send him; he acted isely, and Saul setteth him over the men of ar, and it is good in the eyes of all the people, and also in the eyes of the servants of Saul.

And it cometh to pass, in their coming in, in David’s returning from smiting the Philistine, that the omen come out from all the cities of Israel to sing — also the dancers — to meet Saul the king, ith tabrets, ith joy, and ith three-stringed instruments;
and the omen anser — those playing, and say, ’Saul hath smitten among his thousands, And David among his myriads.’

And it is displeasing to Saul exceedingly, and this thing is evil in his eyes, and he saith, ’They have given to David myriads, and to me they have given the thousands, and more to him [is] only the kingdom;’
and Saul is eyeing David from that day and thenceforth.

And it cometh to pass, on the morro, that the spirit of sadness [from] God prospereth over Saul, and he prophesieth in the midst of the house, and David is playing ith his hand, as day by day, and the javelin [is] in the hand of Saul,
and Saul casteth the javelin, and saith, ’I smite through David, even through the all;’ and David turneth round out of his presence tice.
And Saul is afraid of the presence of David, for Jehovah hath been ith him, and from Saul He hath turned aside;
and Saul turneth him aside from him, and appointeth him to himself head of a thousand, and he goeth out an cometh in, before the people.
And David is in all his ays acting isely, and Jehovah [is] ith him,
and Saul seeth that he is acting very isely, and is afraid of him,
and all Israel and Judah love David hen he is going out and coming in before them.

And Saul saith unto David, ’Lo, my elder daughter Merab — her I give to thee for a ife; only, be to me for a son of valour, and fight the battles of Jehovah;’ and Saul said, ’Let not my hand be on him, but let the hand of the Philistines be upon him.’
And David saith unto Saul, ’Who [am] I? and hat my life — the family of my father in Israel — that I am son-in-la to the king?’
And it cometh to pass, at the time of the giving of Merab daughter of Saul to David, that she hath been given to Adriel the Meholathite for a ife.
And Michal daughter of Saul loveth David, and they declare to Saul, and the thing is right in his eyes,
and Saul saith, ’I give her to him, and she is to him for a snare, and the hand of the Philistines is on him;’ and Saul saith unto David, ’By the second — thou dost become my son-in-la to-day.’
And Saul commandeth his servants, ’Speak unto David gently, saying, Lo, the king hath delighted in thee, and all his servants have loved thee, and no, be son-in-la to the king.’
And the servants of Saul speak in the ears of David these ords, and David saith, ’Is it a light thing in your eyes to be son-in-la to the king — and I a poor man, and lightly esteemed?’
And the servants of Saul declare to him, saying, ’According to these ords hath David spoken.’

And Saul saith, ’Thus do ye say to David, There is no delight to the king in dory, but in a hundred foreskins of the Philistines — to be avenged on the enemies of the king;’ and Saul thought to cause David to fall by the hand of the Philistines.
And his servants declare to David these ords, and the thing is right in the eyes of David, to be son-in-la to the king; and the days have not been full,

and David riseth and goeth, he and his men, and smiteth among the Philistines to hundred men, and David bringeth in their foreskins, and they set them before the king, to be son-in-la to the king; and Saul giveth to him Michal his daughter for a ife.
And Saul seeth and knoeth that Jehovah [is] ith David, and Michal daughter of Saul hath loved him,
and Saul addeth to be afraid of the presence of David yet; and Saul is an enemy ith David all the days.
And the princes of the Philistines come out, and it cometh to pass from the time of their coming out, David hath acted more isely than any of the servants of Saul, and his name is very precious.
And Saul speaketh unto Jonathan his son, and unto all his servants, to put David to death,

and Jonathan son of Saul delighted exceedingly in David, and Jonathan declareth to David, saying, ’Saul my father is seeking to put thee to death, and, no, take heed, I pray thee, in the morning, and thou hast abode in a secret place, and been hidden,
and I — I go out, and have stood by the side of my father in the field here thou [art], and I speak of thee unto my father, and have seen hat [is coming], and have declared to thee.’

And Jonathan speaketh good of David unto Saul his father, and saith unto him, ’Let not the king sin against his servant, against David, because he hath not sinned against thee, and because his orks for thee [are] very good;

yea, he putteth his life in his hand, and smiteth the Philistine, and Jehovah orketh a great salvation for all Israel; thou hast seen, and dost rejoice, and hy dost thou sin against innocent blood, to put David to death for nought?’
And Saul hearkeneth to the voice of Jonathan, and Saul seareth, ’Jehovah liveth — he doth not die.’
And Jonathan calleth for David, and Jonathan declareth to him all these ords, and Jonathan bringeth in David unto Saul, and he is before him as heretofore.
And there addeth to be ar, and David goeth out and fighteth against the Philistines, and smiteth among them — a great smiting, and they flee from his face.
And a spirit of sadness [from] Jehovah is unto Saul, and he is sitting in his house, and his javelin in his hand, and David is playing ith the hand,

and Saul seeketh to smite ith the javelin through David, and through the all, and he freeth himself from the presence of Saul, and he smiteth the javelin through the all; and David hath fled and escapeth during that night.

And Saul sendeth messengers unto the house of David to atch him, and to put him to death in the morning; and Michal his ife declareth to David, saying, ’If thou art not delivering thy life to-night — tomorro thou art put to death.’
And Michal causeth David to go don through the indo, and he goeth on, and fleeth, and escapeth;
and Michal taketh the teraphim, and layeth on the bed, and the mattress of goats’ [hair] she hath put [for] his pillos, and covereth ith a garment.
And Saul sendeth messengers to take David, and she saith, ’He [is] sick.’
And Saul sendeth the messengers to see David, saying, ’Bring him up in the bed unto me,’ — to put him to death.
And the messengers come in, and lo, the teraphim [are] on the bed, and the mattress of goats’ [hair], [for] his pillos.

And Saul saith unto Michal, ’Why thus hast thou deceived me — that thou dost send aay mine enemy, and he is escaped?’ and Michal saith unto Saul, ’He said unto me, Send me aay: hy do I put thee to death?’
And David hath fled, and is escaped, and cometh in unto Samuel to Ramath, and declareth to him all that Saul hath done to him, and he goeth, he and Samuel, and they dell in Naioth.
And it is declared to Saul, saying, ’Lo, David [is] in Naioth in Ramah.’

And Saul sendeth messengers to take David, and they see the assembly of the prophets prophesying, and Samuel standing, set over them, and the Spirit of God is on Saul’s messengers, and they prophesy — they also.
And they declare [it] to Saul, and he sendeth other messengers, and they prophesy — they also; and Saul addeth and sendeth messengers a third time, and they prophesy — they also.
And he goeth — he also — to Ramath, and cometh in unto the great ell hich [is] in Sechu, and asketh, and saith, ’Where [are] Samuel and David?’ and [one] saith, ’Lo, in Naioth in Ramah.’
And he goeth thither — unto Naioth in Ramah, and the Spirit of God is upon him — him also; and he goeth, going on, and he prophesieth till his coming in to Naioth in Ramah,
and he strippeth off — he also — his garments, and prophesieth — he also — before Samuel, and falleth don naked all that day and all the night; therefore they say, ’Is Saul also among the prophets?’
And David fleeth from Naioth in Ramah, and cometh, and saith before Jonathan, ’What have I done? hat [is] mine iniquity? and hat my sin before thy father, that he is seeking my life?’

And he saith to him, ’Far be it! thou dost not die; lo, my father doth not do anything great or small and doth not uncover mine ear; and herefore doth my father hide from me this thing? this [thing] is not.’

And David seareth again, and saith, ’Thy father hath certainly knon that I have found grace in thine eyes, and he saith, Let not Jonathan kno this, lest he be grieved; and yet, Jehovah liveth, and thy soul liveth, but — as a step beteen me and death.’
And Jonathan saith to David, ’What doth thy soul say? — and I do it for thee.’
And David saith unto Jonathan, ’Lo, the ne moon [is] to-morro; and I do certainly sit ith the king to eat; and thou hast sent me aay, and I have been hidden in a field till the third evening;
if thy father at all look after me, and thou hast said, David asked earnestly of me to run to Beth-Lehem his city, for a sacrifice of the days [is] there for all the family.
If thus he say: Good; peace [is] for thy servant; and if it be very displeasing to him — kno that the evil hath been determined by him;

and thou hast done kindness, to thy servant, for into a covenant of Jehovah thou hast brought thy servant ith thee; — and if there is in me iniquity, put thou me to death; and unto thy father, hy is this — thou dost bring me in?’
And Jonathan saith, ’Far be it from thee! for I certainly do not kno that the evil hath been determined by my father to come upon thee, and I do not declare it to thee.’
And David saith unto Jonathan, ’Who doth declare to me? or hat [if] thy father doth anser thee sharply?’
And Jonathan saith unto David, ’Come, and e go out into the field;’ and they go out both of them into the field.

And Jonathan saith unto David, ’Jehovah, God of Israel — hen I search my father, about [this] time to-morro [or] the third [day], and lo, good [is] toards David, and I do not then send unto thee, and have uncovered thine ear —

thus doth Jehovah do to Jonathan, and thus doth He add; hen the evil concerning thee is good to my father, then I have uncovered thine ear, and sent thee aay, and thou hast gone in peace, and Jehovah is ith thee, as he as ith my father;
and not only hile I am alive dost thou do ith me the kindness of Jehovah, and I die not,
but thou dost not cut off thy kindness from my house unto the age, nor in Jehovah’s cutting off the enemies of David, each one from off the face of the ground.’
And Jonathan covenanteth ith the house of David, and Jehovah hath sought [it] from the hand of the enemies of David;
and Jonathan addeth to cause David to sear, because he loveth him, for ith the love of his on soul he hath loved him.
And Jonathan saith to him, ’To-morro [is] ne moon, and thou hast been looked after, for thy seat is looked after;
and on the third day thou dost certainly come don, and hast come in unto the place here thou ast hidden in the day of the ork, and hast remained near the stone Ezel.
’And I shoot three of the arros at the side, sending out for myself at a mark;

and lo, I send the youth: Go, find the arros. If I at all say to the youth, Lo, the arros [are] on this side of thee — take them, — then come thou, for peace [is] for thee, and there is nothing; Jehovah liveth.
And if thus I say to the young man, Lo, the arros [are] beyond thee, — go, for Jehovah hath sent thee aay;
as to the thing hich e have spoken, I and thou, lo, Jehovah [is] beteen me and thee — unto the age.’
And David is hidden in the field, and it is the ne moon, and the king sitteth don by the food to eat,
and the king sitteth on his seat, as time by time, on a seat by the all, and Jonathan riseth, and Abner sitteth at the side of Saul, and David’s place is looked after.
And Saul hath not spoken anything on that day, for he said, ’It [is] an accident; he is not clean — surely not clean.’

And it cometh to pass on the second morro of the ne moon, that David’s place is looked after, and Saul saith unto Jonathan his son, ’Wherefore hath the son of Jesse not come in, either yesterday or to-day, unto the food?’
And Jonathan ansereth Saul, ’David hath been earnestly asked of me unto Beth-Lehem,

and he saith, Send me aay, I pray thee, for a family sacrifice e have in the city, and my brother himself hath given command to me, and no, if I have found grace in thine eyes, let me go aay, I pray thee, and see my brethren; therefore he hath not come unto the table of the king.’

And the anger of Saul burneth against Jonathan, and he saith to him, ’Son of a perverse rebellious oman! have I not knon that thou art fixing on the son of Jesse to thy shame, and to the shame of the nakedness of thy mother?
for all the days that the son of Jesse liveth on the ground thou art not established, thou and thy kingdom; and no, send and bring him unto me, for he [is] a son of death.’
And Jonathan ansereth Saul his father, and saith unto him, ’Why is he put to death? hat hath he done?’
And Saul casteth the javelin at him to smite him, and Jonathan knoeth that it hath been determined by his father to put David to death.
And Jonathan riseth from the table in the heat of anger, and hath not eaten food on the second day of the ne moon, for he hath been grieved for David, for his father put him to shame.
And it cometh to pass in the morning, that Jonathan goeth out into the field for the appointment ith David, and a little youth [is] ith him.
And he saith to his youth, ’Run, find, I pray thee, the arros hich I am shooting;’ the youth is running, and he hath shot the arro, causing [it] to pass over him.
And the youth cometh unto the place of the arro hich Jonathan hath shot, and Jonathan calleth after the youth, and saith, ’Is not the arro beyond thee?’
and Jonathan calleth after the youth, ’Speed, haste, stand not;’ and Jonathan’s youth gathereth the arros, and cometh unto his lord.
And the youth hath not knon anything, only Jonathan and David kne the ord.
And Jonathan giveth his eapons unto the youth hom he hath, and saith to him, ’Go, carry into the city.’

The youth hath gone, and David hath risen from Ezel, at the south, and falleth on his face to the earth, and boeth himself three times, and they kiss one another, and they eep one ith another, till David exerted himself;

and Jonathan saith to David, ’Go in peace, in that e have sorn — e to — in the name of Jehovah, saying, Jehovah is beteen me and thee, and beteen my seed and thy seed — unto the age;’ and he riseth and goeth; and Jonathan hath gone in to the city.
And David cometh in to Nob, unto Ahimelech the priest, and Ahimelech trembleth at meeting David, and saith to him, ’Wherefore [art] thou thyself alone, and no man ith thee?’

And David saith to Ahimelech the priest, ’The king hath commanded me a matter, and he saith unto me, Let no man kno anything of the matter about hich I am sending thee, and hich I have commanded thee; and the young men I have caused to kno at such and such a place;
and no, hat is there under thy hand? five loaves give into my hand, or that hich is found.’
And the priest ansereth David, and saith, ’There is no common bread under my hand, but there is holy bread; if the youths have been kept only from omen.’

And David ansereth the priest, and saith to him, ’Surely, if omen have been restrained from us as heretofore in my going out, then the vessels of the young men are holy, and it [is] a common ay: and also, surely to-day it is sanctified in the vessel.’

And the priest giveth to him the holy thing, for there as no bread there except the bread of the Presence hich is turned aside from the presence of Jehovah to put hot bread in the day of its being taken aay.
And there [is] a man of the servants of Saul on that day detained before Jehovah, and his name [is] Doeg the Edomite, chief of the shepherds hom Saul hath.
And David saith to Ahimelech, ’And is there not here under thy hand spear or sord? for neither my sord nor my vessels have I taken in my hand, for the matter of the king as urgent.’

And the priest saith, ’The sord of Goliath the Philistine, hom thou didst smite in the valley of Elah, lo, it is rapped in a garment behind the ephod, if it thou dost take to thyself, take; for there is none other save it in this [place].’ And David saith, ’There is none like it — give it to me.’
And David riseth and fleeth on that day from the face of Saul, and cometh in unto Achish king of Gath;
and the servants of Achish say unto him, ’Is not this David king of the land? is it not of this one they sing in dances, saying, ’Saul smote among his thousands, and David among his myriads?’
And David layeth these ords in his heart, and is exceedingly afraid of the face of Achish king of Gath,
and changeth his behaviour before their eyes, and feigneth himself mad in their hand, and scribbleth on the doors of the gate, and letteth don his spittle unto his beard.
And Achish saith unto his servants, ’Lo, ye see a man acting as a madman; hy do ye bring him in unto me?
A lack of madmen [have] I, that ye have brought in this one to act as a madman by me! doth this one come in unto my house?’
And David goeth thence, and is escaped unto the cave of Adullam, and his brethren hear, and all the house of his father, and go don unto him thither;
and gather themselves unto him do every man in distress, and every man ho hath an exactor, and every man bitter in soul, and he is over them for head, and there are ith him about four hundred men.
And David goeth thence to Mizpeh of Moab, and saith unto the king of Moab, ’Let, I pray thee, my father and my mother go out ith you, till that I kno hat God doth for me;’
and he leadeth them before the king of Moab, and they dell ith him all the days of David’s being in the fortress.
And Gad the prophet saith unto David, ’Thou dost not abide in a fortress, go, and thou hast entered for thee the land of Judah;’ and David goeth and entereth the forest of Hareth.

And Saul heareth that David hath become knon, and the men ho [are] ith him, and Saul is abiding in Gibeah, under the grove in Ramah, and his spear [is] in his hand, and all his servants standing by him.

And Saul saith to his servants ho are standing by him, ’Hear, I pray you, ye Benjamites; also to all of you doth the son of Jesse give fields and vineyards! all of you he doth appoint heads of thousands and heads of hundreds!

for ye have conspired all of you against me, and there is none uncovering mine ear about my son’s covenanting ith the son of Jesse, and there is none of you grieving for me, and uncovering mine ear, that my son hath raised up my servant against me, to lie in ait as [at] this day.’
And anser doth Doeg the Edomite, ho is set over the servants of Saul, and saith, ’I have seen the son of Jesse coming in to Nob, unto Ahimelech son of Ahitub,
and he asketh for him at Jehovah, and provision hath given to him, and the sord of Goliath the Philistine hath given to him.
And the king sendeth to call Ahimelech son of Ahitub, the priest, and all the house of his father, the priests, ho [are] in Nob, and they come all of them unto the king;
and Saul saith, ’Hear, I pray thee, son of Ahitub;’ and he saith, ’Here [am] I, my lord.’

And Saul saith unto him, ’Why have ye conspired against me, thou and the son of Jesse, by thy giving to him bread and a sord, and to ask for him at God, to rise against me, to lie in ait, as [at] this day?’
And Ahimelech ansereth the king and saith, ’And ho among all thy servants [is] as David — faithful, and son-in-la of the king, and hath turned aside unto thy council, and is honoured in thy house?

To-day have I begun to ask for him at God? far be it from me! let not the king lay anything against his servant, against any of the house of my father, for thy servant hath knon nothing of all this, less or more.’
And the king saith, ’Thou dost surely die, Ahimelech, thou, and all the house of thy father.’

And the king saith to runners, those standing by him, ’Turn round, and put to death the priests of Jehovah, because their hand also [is] ith David, and because they have knon that he is fleeing, and have not uncovered mine ear;’ and the servants of the king have not been illing to put forth their hand to come against the priests of Jehovah.

And the king saith to Doeg, ’Turn round thou, and come against the priests;’ and Doeg the Edomite turneth round, and cometh himself against the priests, and putteth to death in that day eighty and five men bearing a linen ephod,
and Nob, the city of the priests, he hath smitten by the mouth of the sord, from man even unto oman, from infant even unto suckling, and ox, and ass, and sheep, by the mouth of the sord.
And there escapeth one son of Ahimelech, son of Ahitub, and his name [is] Abiathar, and he fleeth after David,
and Abiathar declareth to David that Saul hath slain the priests of Jehovah.

And David saith to Abiathar, ’I have knon on that day hen Doeg the Edomite [is] there, that he doth certainly declare [it] to Saul; I have brought [it] round to every person of the house of thy father;
dell ith me; fear not; for he ho seeketh my life seeketh thy life; for a charge [art] thou ith me.’
And they declare to David, saying, ’Lo, the Philistines are fighting against Keilah, and they are spoiling the threshing-floors.’
And David asketh at Jehovah, saying, ’Do I go? — and have I smitten among these Philistines?’ And Jehovah saith unto David, ’Go, and thou hast smitten among the Philistines, and saved Keilah.’
And David’s men say unto him, ’Lo, e here in Judah are afraid; and ho much more hen e go to Keilah, unto the ranks of the Philistines?’
And David addeth again to ask at Jehovah, and Jehovah ansereth him, and saith, ’Rise, go don to Keilah, for I am giving the Philistines into thy hand.’
And David goeth, and his men, to Keilah, and fighteth ith the Philistines, and leadeth aay their cattle, and smiteth among them — a great smiting, and David saveth the inhabitants of Keilah.
And it cometh to pass, in the fleeing of Abiathar son of Ahimelech unto David, to Keilah, an ephod came don in his hand.
And it is declared to Saul that David hath come in to Keilah, and Saul saith, ’God hath made him knon for my hand, for he hath been shut in, to enter into a city of doors and bar.’
And Saul summoneth the hole of the people to battle, to go don to Keilah, to lay siege unto David and unto his men.
And David knoeth that against him Saul is devising the evil, and saith unto Abiathar the priest, ’Bring nigh the ephod.’
And David saith, ’Jehovah, God of Israel, Thy servant hath certainly heard that Saul is seeking to come in unto Keilah, to destroy the city on mine account.

Do the possessors of Keilah shut me up into his hand? doth Saul come don as Thy servant hath heard? Jehovah, God of Israel, declare, I pray Thee, to Thy servant.’ And Jehovah saith, ’He doth come don.’
And David saith, ’Do the possessors of Keilah shut me up, and my men, into the hand of Saul?’ And Jehovah saith, ’They shut [thee] up.’

And David riseth — and his men — about six hundred men, and they go out from Keilah, and go up and don here they go up and don; and to Saul it hath been declared that David hath escaped from Keilah, and he ceaseth to go out.
And David abideth in the ilderness, in fortresses, and abideth in the hill-country, in the ilderness of Ziph; and Saul seeketh him all the days, and God hath not given him into his hand.
And David seeth that Saul hath come out to seek his life, and David [is] in the ilderness of Ziph, in a forest.
And Jonathan son of Saul riseth, and goeth unto David to the forest, and strengtheneth his hand in God,
