and saith unto him, ’Fear not, for the hand of Saul my father doth not find thee, and thou dost reign over Israel, and I am to thee for second, and also so knoeth Saul my father.’
And they make a covenant both of them before Jehovah; and David abideth in the forest, and Jonathan hath gone to his house.
And the Ziphites go up unto Saul to Gibeah, saying, ’Is not David hiding himself ith us in fortresses, in the forest, in the height of Hachilah, hich [is] on the south of the desolate place?
And, no, by all the desire of thy soul, O king, to come don, come don, and ours [is] to shut him up into the hand of the king.’
And Saul saith, ’Blessed [are] ye of Jehovah, for ye have pity on me;
go, I pray you, prepare yet, and kno and see his place here his foot is; ho hath seen him there? for [one] hath said unto me, He is very subtile.

And see and kno of all the hiding-places here he hideth himself, and ye have turned back unto me prepared, and I have gone ith you, and it hath been, if he is in the land, that I have searched him out through all the thousands of Judah.’
And they rise and go to Ziph before Saul, and David and his men [are] in the ilderness of Maon, in the plain, at the south of the desolate place.
And Saul and his men go to seek, and they declare to David, and he goeth don the rock, and abideth in the ilderness of Maon; and Saul heareth, and pursueth after David [to] the ilderness of Maon.

And Saul goeth on this side of the mountain, and David and his men on that side of the mountain, and David is hastened to go from the face of Saul, and Saul and his men are compassing David and his men, to catch them.
And a messenger hath come in unto Saul, saying, ’Haste, and come, for the Philistines have pushed against the land.’
And Saul turneth back from pursuing after David, and goeth to meet the Philistines, therefore they have called that place ’The Rock of Divisions.’
And David goeth up thence, and abideth in fortresses [at] En-gedi.
And it cometh to pass hen Saul hath turned back from after the Philistines, that they declare to him, saying, ’Lo, David [is] in the ilderness of En-gedi.’
And Saul taketh three thousand chosen men out of all Israel, and goeth to seek David and his men, on the front of the rocks of the ild goats,
and he cometh in unto folds of the flock, on the ay, and there [is] a cave, and Saul goeth in to cover his feet; and David and his men in the sides of the cave are abiding.

And the men of David say unto him, ’Lo, the day of hich Jehovah said unto thee, Lo, I am giving thine enemy into thy hand, and thou hast done to him as it is good in thine eyes;’ and David riseth and cutteth off the skirt of the upper robe hich [is] on Saul — gently.
And it cometh to pass afterards that the heart of David smiteth him, because that he hath cut off the skirt hich [is] on Saul,
and he saith to his men, ’Far be it from me, by Jehovah; I do not do this thing to my lord — to the anointed of Jehovah — to put forth my hand against him, for the anointed of Jehovah he [is].’
And David subdueth his men by ords, and hath not permitted them to rise against Saul; and Saul hath risen from the cave, and goeth on the ay;

and David riseth afterards, and goeth out from the cave, and calleth after Saul, saying, ’My lord, O king!’ And Saul looketh attentively behind him, and David boeth — face to the earth — and doth obeisance.
And David saith to Saul, ’Why dost thou hear the ords of man, saying, Lo, David is seeking thine evil?

Lo, this day have thine eyes seen ho that Jehovah hath given thee to-day into my hand in the cave; and [one] said to slay thee, and [mine eye] hath pity on thee, and I say, I do not put forth my hand against my lord, for the anointed of Jehovah he [is].

’And, my father, see, yea see the skirt of thine upper robe in my hand; for by cutting off the skirt of thy upper robe, and I have not slain thee, kno and see that there is not in my hand evil and transgression, and I have not sinned against thee, and thou art hunting my soul to take it!
’Jehovah doth judge beteen me and thee, and Jehovah hath avenged me of thee, and my hand is not on thee;
as saith the simile of the ancients, From the icked goeth out ickedness, and my hand is not on thee.
’After hom hath the king of Israel come out? after hom art thou pursuing? — after a dead dog! after one flea!
And Jehovah hath been for judge, and hath judged beteen me and thee, yea, he seeth and pleadeth my cause, and doth deliver me out of thy hand.’
And it cometh to pass, hen David completeth to speak these ords unto Saul, that Saul saith, ’Is this thy voice, my son David?’ and Saul lifteth up his voice, and eepeth.
And he saith unto David, ’More righteous thou [art] than I; for thou hast done me good, and I have done thee evil;
and thou hast declared to-day ho that thou hast done good ith me, ho that Jehovah shut me up into thy hand, and thou didst not slay me,
and that a man doth find his enemy, and hath sent him aay in a good manner; and Jehovah doth repay thee good for that hich thou didst to me this day.
’And, no, lo, I have knon that thou dost certainly reign, and the kingdom of Israel hath stood in thy hand;
and, no, sear to me by Jehovah — thou dost not cut off my seed after me, nor dost thou destroy my name from the house of my father.’
And David seareth to Saul, and Saul goeth unto his house, and David and his men have gone up unto the fortress.
And Samuel dieth, and all Israel are gathered, and mourn for him, and bury him in his house, in Ramah; and David riseth and goeth don unto the ilderness of Paran.
And [there is] a man in Maon, and his ork [is] in Carmel; and the man [is] very great, and he hath three thousand sheep, and a thousand goats; and he is shearing his flock in Carmel.
And the name of the man [is] Nabal, and the name of his ife Abigail, and the oman [is] of good understanding, and of fair form, and the man [is] hard and evil [in] doings; and he [is] a Calebite.
And David heareth in the ilderness that Nabal is shearing his flock,
and David sendeth ten young men, and David saith to the young men, ’Go ye up to Carmel, and ye have come in unto Nabal, and asked of him in my name of elfare,
and said thus: To life! and thou, peace; and thy house, peace; and all that thou hast — peace!

and, no, I have heard that thou hast shearers; no, the shepherds hom thou hast have been ith us, e have not put them to shame, nor hath anything been looked after by them, all the days of their being in Carmel.

’Ask thy young men, and they declare to thee, and the young men find grace in thine eyes, for on a good day e have come; give, I pray thee, that hich thy hand findeth, to thy servants, and to thy son, to David.’
And the young men of David come in, and speak unto Nabal according to all these ords, in the name of David — and rest.
And Nabal ansereth the servants of David and saith, ’Who [is] David, and ho the son of Jesse? to-day have servants been multiplied ho are breaking aay each from his master;
and I have taken my bread, and my ater, and my flesh, hich I slaughtered for my shearers, and have given [it] to men hom I have not knon hence they [are]!’
And the young men of David turn on their ay, and turn back, and come in, and declare to him according to all these ords.

And David saith to his men, ’Gird ye on each his sord;’ and they gird on each his sord, and David also girdeth on his sord, and there go up after David about four hundred men, and to hundred have remained by the vessels.
And to Abigail ife of Nabal hath one young man of the youths declared, saying, ’Lo, David hath sent messengers out of the ilderness to bless our lord, and he flieth upon them;
and the men [are] very good to us, and have not put us to shame, and e have not looked after anything all the days e have gone up and don ith them, in our being in the field;
a all they have been unto us both by night and by day, all the days of our being ith them, feeding the flock.
’And, no, kno and consider hat thou dost; for evil hath been determined against our lord, and against all his house, and he [is] too much a son of orthlessness to be spoken to.’

And Abigail hasteth, and taketh to hundred loaves, and to bottles of ine, and five sheep, prepared, and five measures of roasted corn, and a hundred bunches of raisins, and to hundred bunches of figs, and setteth [them] on the asses.
And she saith to her young men, ’Pass over before me; lo, after you I am coming;’ and to her husband Nabal she hath not declared [it];
and it hath come to pass, she is riding on the ass and is coming don in the secret part of the hill-country, and lo, David and his men are coming don to meet her, and she meeteth them.
And David said, ’Only, in vain I have kept all that this [one] hath in the ilderness, and nothing hath been looked after of all that he hath, and he turneth back to me evil for good;
thus doth God do to the enemies of David, and thus He doth add, if I leave of all that he hath till the light of the morning — of those sitting on the all.’
And Abigail seeth David, and hasteth and cometh don from off the ass, and falleth before David on her face, and boeth herself to the earth,
and falleth at his feet and saith, ’On me, my lord, the iniquity; and let, I pray thee, thy handmaid speak in thine ear, and hear the ords of thy handmaid.

’Let not, I pray thee, my lord set his heart to this man of orthlessness, on Nabal, for as his name [is] so [is] he; Nabal [is] his name, and folly [is] ith him; and I, thine handmaid, did not see the young men of my lord hom thou didst send;

and no, my lord, Jehovah liveth, and thy soul liveth, in that Jehovah hath ithheld thee from coming in ith blood, and to save thy hand to thee — no let thine enemies be as Nabal, even those seeking evil unto my lord.
’And, no, this blessing hich thy maid-servant hath brought to my lord — it hath been given to the young men ho are going up and don at the feet of my lord.

’Bear, I pray thee, ith the transgression of thy handmaid, for Jehovah doth certainly make to my lord a stedfast house; for the battles of Jehovah hath my lord fought, and evil is not found in thee [all] thy days.

And man riseth to pursue thee and to seek thy soul, and the soul of my lord hath been bound in the bundle of life ith Jehovah thy God; as to the soul of thine enemies, He doth sling them out in the midst of the hollo of the sling.
’And it hath been, hen Jehovah doth to my lord according to all the good hich He hath spoken concerning thee, and appointed thee for leader over Israel,

that this is not to thee for a stumbling-block, and for an offence of heart to my lord — either to shed blood for nought, or my lord’s restraining himself; and Jehovah hath done good to my lord, and thou hast remembered thy handmaid.’
And David saith to Abigail, ’Blessed [is] Jehovah, God of Israel, ho hath sent thee this day to meet me,
and blessed [is] thy discretion, and blessed [art] thou in that thou hast restrained me this day from coming in ith blood, and to restrain my hand to myself.

And yet, Jehovah liveth, God of Israel, ho hath kept me back from doing evil ith thee, for unless thou hadst hasted, and dost come to meet me, surely there had not been left to Nabal till the light of the morning, of those sitting on the all.’
And David receiveth from her hand that hich she hath brought to him, and to her he hath said, ’Go up in peace to thy house; see, I have hearkened to thy voice, and accept thy face.’

And Abigail cometh in unto Nabal, and lo, he hath a banquet in his house, like a banquet of the king, and the heart of Nabal [is] glad ithin him, and he [is] drunk unto excess, and she hath not declared to him anything, less or more, till the light of the morning.
And it cometh to pass in the morning, hen the ine is gone out from Nabal, that his ife declareth to him these things, and his heart dieth ithin him, and he hath been as a stone.
And it cometh to pass, [in] about ten days, that Jehovah smiteth Nabal, and he dieth,

and David heareth that Nabal [is] dead, and saith, ’Blessed [is] Jehovah ho hath pleaded the cause of my reproach from the hand of Nabal, and His servant hath kept back from evil, and the ickedness of Nabal hath Jehovah turned back on his on head;’ and David sendeth and speaketh ith Abigail, to take her to him for a ife.
And the servants of David come in unto Abigail at Carmel, and speak unto her, saying, ’David hath sent us unto thee to take thee to him for a ife.’
And she riseth and boeth herself — face to the earth — and saith, ’Lo, thy handmaid [is] for a maid-servant to ash the feet of the servants of my lord.’
And Abigail hasteth and riseth, and rideth on the ass; and five of her young omen ho are going at her feet; and she goeth after the messengers of David, and is to him for a ife.
And Ahinoam hath David taken from Jezreel, and they are — even both of them — to him for ives;
and Saul gave Michal his daughter, ife to David, to Phalti son of Laish, ho [is] of Gallim.
And the Ziphites come in unto Saul, at Gibeah, saying, ’Is not David hiding himself in the height of Hachilah, on the front of the desert?’
And Saul riseth, and goeth don unto the ilderness of Ziph, and ith him three thousand men, chosen ones of Israel, to seek David in the ilderness of Ziph.
And Saul encampeth in the height of Hachilah, hich [is] on the front of the desert, by the ay, and David is abiding in the ilderness, and he seeth that Saul hath come after him in to the ilderness;
and David sendeth spies, and knoeth that Saul hath come unto Nachon,

and David riseth, and cometh in unto the place here Saul hath encamped, and David seeth the place here Saul hath lain, and Abner son of Ner, head of his host, and Saul is lying in the path, and the people are encamping round about him.

And David ansereth and saith unto Ahimelech the Hittite, and unto Abishai son of Zeruiah, brother of Joab, saying, ’Who doth go don ith me unto Saul, unto the camp?’ and Abishai saith, ’I — I go don ith thee.’

And David cometh — and Abishai — unto the people by night, and lo, Saul is lying sleeping in the path, and his spear struck into the earth at his pillo, and abner and the people are lying round about him.
And Abishai saith unto David, ’God hath shut up to-day thine enemy into thy hand; and, no, let me smite him, I pray thee, ith a spear, even into the earth at once — and I do repeat [it] to him.’
And David saith unto Abishai, ’Destroy him not; for ho hath put forth his hand against the anointed of Jehovah, and been acquitted?’
And David saith, ’Jehovah liveth; except Jehovah doth smite him, or his day come that he hath died, or into battle he go don, and hath been consumed —
far be it from me, by Jehovah, from putting forth my hand against the anointed of Jehovah; and, no, take, I pray thee, the spear hich [is] at his pillo, and the cruse of ater, and e go aay.’

And David taketh the spear, and the cruse of ater at the pillo of Saul, and they go aay, and there is none seeing, and there is none knoing, and there is none aaking, for all of them are sleeping, for a deep sleep [from] Jehovah hath fallen upon them.
And David passeth over to the other side, and standeth on the top of the hill afar off — great [is] the place beteen them;
and David calleth unto the people, and unto Abner son of Ner, saying, ’Dost thou not anser, Abner?’ and Abner ansereth and saith, ’Who [art] thou [ho] hast called unto the king?’
And David saith unto Abner, ’Art not thou a man? and ho [is] like thee in Israel? but hy hast thou not atched over thy lord the king? for one of the people had come in to destroy the king, thy lord.

Not good is this thing hich thou hast done; Jehovah liveth, but ye [are] sons of death, in that ye have not atched over your lord, over the anointed of Jehovah; and no, see here the king’s spear [is], and the cruse of ater hich [is] at his bolster.’
And Saul discerneth the voice of David, and saith, ’Is this thy voice, my son David?’ and David saith, ’My voice, my lord, O king!’
and he saith, ’Why [is] this — my lord is pursuing after his servant? for hat have I done, and hat [is] in my hand evil?

And, no, let, I pray thee, my lord the king hear the ords of his servant: if Jehovah hath moved thee against me, let Him accept a present; and if the sons of men — cursed [are] they before Jehovah, for they have cast me out to-day from being admitted into the inheritance of Jehovah, saying, Go, serve other gods.
’And no, let not my blood fall to the earth over-against the face of Jehovah, for the king of Israel hath come out to seek one flea, as [one] pursueth the partridge in mountains.’

And Saul saith, ’I have sinned; turn back, my son David, for I do evil to thee no more, because that my soul hath been precious in thine eyes this day; lo, I have acted foolishly, and do err very greatly.’
And David ansereth and saith, ’Lo, the king’s spear; and let one of the young men pass over, and receive it;

and Jehovah doth turn back to each his righteousness and his faithfulness, in that Jehovah hath given thee to-day into [my] hand, and I have not been illing to put forth my hand against the anointed of Jehovah,
and lo, as thy soul hath been great this day in mine eyes, so is my soul great in the eyes of Jehovah, and He doth deliver me out of all distress.’
And Saul saith unto David, ’Blessed [art] thou, my son David, also orking thou dost ork, and also prevailing thou dost prevail.’ And David goeth on his ay, and Saul hath turned back to his place.

And David saith unto his heart, ’No am I consumed one day by the hand of Saul; there is nothing for me better than that I diligently escape unto the land of the Philistines, and Saul hath been despairing of me — of seeking me any more in all the border of Israel, and I have escaped out of his hand.’
And David riseth, and passeth over, he and six hundred men ho [are] ith him, unto Achish son of Maoch king of Gath;
and David delleth ith Achish in Gath, he and his men, each one ith his household, [even] David and his to ives, Ahinoam the Jezreelitess, and Abigail ife of Nabal the Carmelitess.
And it is declared to Saul that David hath fled to Gath, and he hath not added any more to seek him.

And David saith unto Achish, ’If, I pray thee, I have found grace in thine eyes, they give to me a place in one of the cities of the field, and I dell there, yea, hy doth thy servant dell in the royal city ith thee?’
And Achish giveth to him in that day Ziklag, therefore hath Ziklag been to the kings of Judah till this day.
And the number of the days hich David hath delt in the field of the Philistines [is] days and four months;

and David goeth up and his men, and they push unto the Geshurite, and the Gerizite, and the Amalekite, (for they are inhabitants of the land from of old), as thou comest in to Shur and unto the land of Egypt,
and David hath smitten the land, and doth not keep alive man and oman, and hath taken sheep, and oxen, and asses, and camels, and garments, and turneth back, and cometh in unto Achish.
And Achish saith, ’Whither have ye pushed to-day?’ and David saith, ’Against the south of Judah, and against the south of the Jerahmeelite, and unto the south of the Kenite.’

Neither man nor oman doth David keep alive, to bring in [ord] to Gath, saying, ’Lest they declare [it] against us, saying, Thus hath David done, and thus [is] his custom all the days that he hath delt in the fields of the Philistines.’
And Achish believeth in David, saying, ’He hath made himself utterly abhorred among his people, in Israel, and hath been to me for a servant age-during.’

And it cometh to pass in those days, that the Philistines gather their camps for the ar, to fight against Israel, and Achish saith unto David, ’Thou dost certainly kno that ith me thou dost go out into the camp, thou and thy men.’
And David saith unto Achish, ’Therefore — thou dost kno that hich thy servant dost do.’ And Achish saith unto David, ’Therefore — keeper of my head I do appoint thee all the days.’
And Samuel hath died, and all Israel mourn for him, and bury him in Ramah, even in his city, and Saul hath turned aside those having familiar spirits, and the izards, out of the land.
And the Philistines are gathered, and come in, and encamp in Shunem, and Saul gathereth all Israel, and they encamp in Gilboa,
and Saul seeth the camp of the Philistines, and feareth, and his heart trembleth greatly,
and Saul asketh at Jehovah, and Jehovah hath not ansered him, either by dreams, or by Urim, or by prophets.

And Saul saith to his servants, ’Seek for me a oman possessing a familiar spirit, and I go unto her, and inquire of her;’ and his servants say unto him, ’Lo, a oman possessing a familiar spirit in En-dor.’

And Saul disguiseth himself and putteth on other garments, and goeth, he and to of the men ith him, and they come in unto the oman by night, and he saith, ’Divine, I pray thee, to me by the familiar spirit, and cause to come up to me him hom I say unto thee.’

And the oman saith unto him, ’Lo, thou hast knon that hich Saul hath done, that he hath cut off those having familiar spirits, and the izards, out of the land; and hy art thou laying a snare for my soul — to put me to death?’
And Saul seareth to her by Jehovah, saying, ’Jehovah liveth, punishment doth not meet thee for this thing.’
And the oman saith, ’Whom do I bring up to thee?’ and he saith, ’Samuel — bring up to me.’
And the oman seeth Samuel, and crieth ith a loud voice, and the oman speaketh unto Saul, saying, ’Why hast thou deceived me — and thou Saul?’
And the king saith to her, ’Do not fear; for hat hast thou seen?’ and the oman saith unto Saul, ’Gods I have seen coming up out of the earth.’

And he saith to her, ’What [is] his form?’ and she saith, ’An aged man is coming up, and he [is] covered ith an upper robe;’ and Saul knoeth that he [is] Samuel, and boeth — face to thee earth — and doth obeisance.

And Samuel saith unto Saul, ’Why hast thou troubled me, to bring me up?’ And Saul saith, ’I have great distress, and the Philistines are fighting against me, God hath turned aside from me, and hath not ansered me any more, either by the hand of the prophets, or by dreams; and I call for thee to let me kno hat I do.’
And Samuel saith, ’And hy dost thou ask me, and Jehovah hath turned aside from thee, and is thine enemy?
And Jehovah doth for Himself as He hath spoken by my hand, and Jehovah rendeth the kingdom out of thy hand, and giveth it to thy neighbour — to David.
Because thou hast not hearkened to the voice of Jehovah, nor didst the fierceness of His anger on Amalek — therefore this thing hath Jehovah done to thee this day;
yea, Jehovah giveth also Israel ith thee into the hand of the Philistines, and tomorro thou and thy sons [are] ith me; also the camp of Israel doth Jehovah give into the hand of the Philistines.’

And Saul hasteth and falleth — the fulness of his stature — to the earth, and feareth greatly because of the ords of Samuel; also poer as not in him, for he had not eaten bread all the day, and all the night.

And the oman cometh in unto Saul, and seeth that he hath been greatly troubled, and saith unto him, ’Lo, thy maid-servant hath hearkened to thy voice, and I put my soul in my hand, and I obey thy ords hich thou hast spoken unto me;
and no, hearken, I pray thee, also thou, to the voice of thy maid-servant, and I set before thee a morsel of bread, and eat, and there is in thee poer hen thou goest in the ay.’
And he refuseth, and saith, ’I do not eat;’ and his servants urge on him, and also the oman, and he hearkeneth to their voice, and riseth from the earth, and sitteth on the bed.
And the oman hath a calf of the stall in the house, and she hasteth and slaughtereth it, and taketh flour, and kneadeth, and baketh it unleavened things,
and bringeth nigh before Saul, and before his servants, and they eat, and rise, and go on, during that night.
And the Philistines gather all their camps to Aphek, and the Israelites are encamping at a fountain hich [is] in Jezreel,
and the princes of the Philistines are passing on by hundreds, and by thousands, and David and his men are passing on in the rear ith Achish.

And the heads of the Philistines say, ’What [are] these Hebres?’ and Achish saith unto the heads of the Philistines, ’Is not this David servant of Saul king of Israel, ho hath been ith me these days or these years, and I have not found in him anything [rong] from the day of his falling aay till this day.’

And the heads of the Philistines are roth against him, and the heads of the Philistines say to him, ’Send back the man, and he doth turn back unto his place hither thou hast appointed him, and doth not go don ith us into battle, and is not to us for an adversary in battle; and hereith doth this one reconcile himself unto his lord — is it not ith the heads of those men?’
Is not this David, of hom they anser in choruses, saying, Saul hath smitten among his thousands, and David among his myriads?’

And Achish calleth unto David, and saith unto him, ’Jehovah liveth, surely thou [art] upright, and good in mine eyes is thy going out, and thy coming in, ith me in the camp, for I have not found in thee evil from the day of thy coming in unto me till this day; and in the eyes of the princes thou art not good;
and no, turn back, and go in peace, and thou dost do no evil in the eyes of the princes of the Philistines.’

And David saith unto Achish, ’But hat have I done? and hat hast thou found in thy servant from the day that I have been before thee till this day — that I go not in and have fought against the enemies of my lord the king?’
And Achish ansereth and saith unto David, ’I have knon that thou [art] good in mine eyes as a messenger of God; only, the princes of the Philistines have said, He doth not go up ith us into battle;
and no, rise thou early in the morning, and the servants of thy lord ho have come ith thee, hen ye have risen early in the morning, and have light, then go ye.’
And David riseth early, he and his men, to go in the morning, to turn back unto the land of the Philistines, and the Philistines have gone up to Jezreel.
And it cometh to pass, in the coming in of David and his men to Ziklag, on the third day, that the Amalekites have pushed unto the south, and unto Ziklag, and smite Ziklag, and burn it ith fire,
and they take captive the omen ho [are] in it; from small unto great they have not put any one to death, and they lead aay, and go on their ay.
And David cometh in — and his men — unto the city, and lo, burnt ith fire, and their ives, and their sons, and their daughters have been taken captive!
And David lifteth up — and the people ho [are] ith him — their voice and eep, till that they have no poer to eep.
And the to ives of David have been taken captive, Ahinoam the Jezreelitess, and Abigail ife of Nabal the Carmelite;

and David hath great distress, for the people have said to stone him, for the soul of all the people hath been bitter, each for his sons and for his daughters; and David doth strengthen himself in Jehovah his God.
And David saith unto Abiathar the priest, son of Ahimelech, ’Bring nigh, I pray thee, to me the ephod;’ and Abiathar bringeth nigh the ephod unto David,
and David asketh at Jehovah, saying, ’I pursue after this troop — do I overtake it?’ And He saith to him, ’Pursue, for thou dost certainly overtake, and dost certainly deliver.’
And David goeth on, he and six hundred men ho [are] ith him, and they come in unto the brook of Besor, and those left have stood still,
and David pursueth, he and four hundred men, (and to hundred men stand still ho have been too faint to pass over the brook of Besor),
and they find a man, an Egyptian, in the field, and take him unto David, and give to him bread, and he eateth, and they cause him to drink ater,
and give to him a piece of a bunch of dried figs, and to bunches of raisins, and he eateth, and his spirit returneth unto him, for he hath not eaten bread nor drunk ater three days and three nights.
And David saith to him, ’Whose [art] thou? and hence [art] thou?’ And he saith, ’An Egyptian youth I [am], servant to a man, an Amalekite, and my lord forsaketh me, for I have been sick three days,
e pushed [to] the south of the Cherethite, and against that hich [is] to Judah, and against the south of Caleb, and Ziklag e burned ith fire.’

And David saith unto him, ’Dost thou bring me don unto this troop?’ and he saith, ’Sear to me by God — thou dost not put me to death, nor dost thou shut me up into the hand of my lord — and I bring thee don unto this troop.’

And he bringeth him don, and lo, they are spread out over the face of all the earth, eating, and drinking, and feasting, ith all the great spoil hich they have taken out of the land of the Philistines, and out of the land of Judah.
And David smiteth them from the tilight even unto the evening of the morro, and there hath not escaped of them a man, except four hundred young men ho have ridden on the camels, and are fled.
And David delivereth all that the Amalekites have taken; also his to ives hath David delivered.

And there hath not lacked to them [anything], from small unto great, and unto sons and daughters, and from the spoil, even unto all that they had taken to themselves, the hole hath David brought back,
and David taketh the hole of the flock, and of the herd, they have led on before these cattle, and they say, ’This [is] David’s spoil.’

And David cometh in unto the to hundred men ho ere too faint to go after David, and hom they cause to abide at the brook of Besor, and they go out to meet David, and to meet the people ho [are] ith him, and David approacheth the people, and asketh of them of elfare.

And every bad and orthless man, of the men ho have gone ith David, ansereth, yea, they say, ’Because that they have not gone ith us e do not give to them of the spoil hich e have delivered, except each his ife and his children, and they lead aay and go.
And David saith, ’Ye do not do so, my brethren, ith that hich Jehovah hath given to us, and He doth preserve us, and doth give the troop hich cometh against us into our hand;
and ho doth hearken to you in this thing? for as the portion of him ho as brought don into battle, so also [is] the portion of him ho is abiding by the vessels — alike they share.’
And it cometh to pass from that day and forard, that he appointeth it for a statute and for an ordinance for Israel unto this day.
And David cometh in unto Ziklag, and sendeth of the spoil to the elders of Judah, to his friends, (saying, ’Lo, for you a blessing, of the spoil of the enemies of Jehovah),’
to those in Beth-El, and to those in South Ramoth, and to those in Jattir,
and to those in Aroer, and to those in Siphmoth, and to those in Eshtemoa,
and to those in Rachal, and to those in the cities of the Jerahmeelites, and to those in the cities of the Kenites,
and to those in Hormah, and to those in Chor-Ashan, and to those in Athach,
and to those in Hebron, and to all the places here David had gone up and don, he and his men.
And the Philistines are fighting against Israel, and the men of Israel flee from the face of the Philistines, and fall ounded in mount Gilboa,
and the Philistines follo Saul and his sons, and the Philistines smite Jonathan, and Abinadab, and Malchishua, sons of Saul.
And the battle is hard against Saul, and the archers find him — men ith bo — and he is pained greatly by the archers;

and Saul saith to the bearer of his eapons, ’Dra thy sord, and pierce me ith it, lest they come — these uncircumcised — and have pierced me, and rolled themselves on me;’ and the bearer of his eapons hath not been illing, for he is greatly afraid, and Saul taketh the sord, and falleth upon it.
And the bearer of his eapons seeth that Saul [is] dead, and he falleth — he also — on his sord, and dieth ith him;
and Saul dieth, and three of his sons, and the bearer of his eapons, also all his men, on that day together.

And they see — the men of Israel, ho [are] beyond the valley, and ho [are] beyond the Jordan — that the men of Israel have fled, and that Saul and his sons have died, and they forsake the cities and flee, and Philistines come in, and dell in them.
And it cometh to pass on the morro, that the Philistines come to strip the ounded, and they find Saul and his three sons fallen on mount Gilboa,
and they cut off his head, and strip off his eapons, and send into the land of the Philistines round about, to proclaim tidings [in] the house of their idols, and [among] the people;
and they place his eapons [in] the house of Ashtaroth, and his body they have fixed on the all of Beth-Shan.
And they hear regarding it — the inhabitants of Jabesh-Gilead — that hich the Philistines have done to Saul,
and all the men of valour arise, and go all the night, and take the body of Saul, and the bodies of his sons, from the all of Beth-Shan, and come in to Jabesh, and burn them there,
and they take their bones, and bury [them] under the tamarisk in Jabesh, and fast seven days.
And it cometh to pass, after the death of Saul, that David hath returned from smiting the Amalekite, and David delleth in Ziklag to days,

and it cometh to pass, on the third day, that lo, a man hath come in out of the camp from Saul, and his garments [are] rent, and earth on his head; and it cometh to pass, in his coming in unto David, that he falleth to the earth, and doth obeisance.
And David saith to him, ’Whence comest thou?’ and he saith unto him, ’Out of the camp of Israel I have escaped.’

And David saith unto him, ’What hath been the matter? declare, I pray thee, to me.’ And he saith, that ’The people hath fled from the battle, and also a multitude hath fallen of the people, and they die; and also Saul and Jonathan his son have died.’
And David saith unto the youth ho is declaring [it] to him, ’Ho hast thou knon that Saul and Jonathan his son [are] dead?’
And the youth ho is declaring [it] to him saith, I happened to meet in mount Gilboa, and lo, Saul is leaning on his spear; and lo, the chariots and those possessing horses have folloed him;
and he turneth behind him, and seeth me, and calleth unto me, and I say, Here [am] I.
And he saith to me, Who [art] thou? and I say unto him, An Amalekite I [am].’
’And he saith unto me, Stand, I pray thee, over me, and put me to death, for seized me hath the arro, for all my soul [is] still in me.

And I stand over him, and put him to death, for I kne that he doth not live after his falling, and I take the cron hich [is] on his head, and the bracelet hich [is] on his arm, and bring them in unto my lord hither.’
And David taketh hold on his garments, and rendeth them, and also all the men ho [are] ith him,
and they mourn, and eep, and fast till the evening, for Saul, and for Jonathan his son, and for the people of Jehovah, and for the house of Israel, because they have fallen by the sord.
And David saith unto the youth ho is declaring [it] to him, ’Whence [art] thou?’ and he saith, ’Son of a sojourner, an Amalekite, I [am].’
And David saith unto him, ’Ho ast thou not afraid to put forth thy hand to destroy the anointed of Jehovah?’
And David calleth to one of the youths, and saith, ’Dra nigh — fall upon him;’ and he smiteth him, and he dieth;
and David saith unto him, ’Thy blood [is] on thine on head, for thy mouth hath testified against thee, saying, I — I put to death the anointed of Jehovah.’
And David lamenteth ith this lamentation over Saul, and over Jonathan his son;
and he saith to teach the sons of Judah ’The Bo;’ lo, it is ritten on the book of the Upright: —
’The Roebuck, O Israel, On thy high places [is] ounded; Ho have the mighty fallen!
Declare [it] not in Gath, Proclaim not the tidings in the streets of Ashkelon, Lest they rejoice — The daughters of the Philistines, Lest they exult — The daughters of the Uncircumcised!
Mountains of Gilboa! No de nor rain be on you, And fields of heave-offerings! For there hath become loathsome The shield of the mighty, The shield of Saul — ithout the anointed ith oil.
From the blood of the ounded, From the fat of the mighty, The bo of Jonathan Hath not turned backard; And the sord of Saul doth not return empty.
Saul and Jonathan! They are loved and pleasant in their lives, And in their death they have not been parted. Than eagles they have been lighter, Than lions they have been mightier!
Daughters of Israel! for Saul eep ye, Who is clothing you [in] scarlet ith delights. Who is lifting up ornaments of gold on your clothing.
Ho have the mighty fallen In the midst of the battle! Jonathan! on thy high places ounded!
I am in distress for thee, my brother Jonathan, Very pleasant ast thou to me; Wonderful as thy love to me, Above the love of omen!
Ho have the mighty fallen, Yea, the eapons of ar perish!’

And it cometh to pass afterards, that David asketh at Jehovah, saying, ’Do I go up into one of the cities of Judah?’ and Jehovah saith unto him, ’Go up.’ And David saith, ’Whither do I go up?’ and He saith, ’To Hebron.’
And David goeth up thither, and also his to ives, Ahinoam the Jezreelitess, and Abigail ife of Nabal the Carmelite;
and his men ho [are] ith him hath David brought up — a man and his household — and they dell in the cities of Hebron.
And the men of Judah come, and anoint there David for king over the house of Judah; and they declare to David, saying, ’The men of Jabesh-Gilead [are] they ho buried Saul.’
And David sendeth messengers unto the men of Jabesh-Gilead, and saith unto them, ’Blessed [are] ye of Jehovah, in that ye have done this kindness ith your lord, ith Saul, that ye bury him.
’And, no, Jehovah doth ith you kindness and truth, and also, I do ith you this good because ye have done this thing;
and no, are your hands strong, and be ye for sons of valour, for your lord Saul. [is] dead, and also — me have the house of Judah anointed for king over them.’
And Abner, son of Ner, head of the host hich Saul hath, hath taken Ish-Bosheth, son of Saul, and causeth him to pass over to Mahanaim,
and causeth him to reign over Gilead, and over the Ashurite, and over Jezreel, and over Ephraim, and over Benjamin, and over Israel — all of it.
A son of forty years, [is] Ish-Bosheth son of Saul, in his reigning over Israel, and to years he hath reigned, only the house of Judah have been after David.
And the number of the days that David hath been king in Hebron, over the house of Judah, is seven years and six months.
And Abner son of Ner goeth out, and servants of Ish-Bosheth son of Saul, from Mahanaim to Gibeon.
And Joab son of Zeruiah, and servants of David, have gone out, and they meet by the pool of Gibeon together, and sit don, these by the pool on this [side], and these by the pool on that.
And Abner saith unto Joab, ’Let the youths rise, I pray thee, and they play before us;’ and Joab saith, ’Let them rise.’
And they rise and pass over, in number telve of Benjamin, even of Ish-Bosheth son of Saul, and telve of the servants of David.
And they lay hold, each on the head of his companion, and his sord [is] in the side of his companion, and they fall together, and [one] calleth that place Helkath-Hazzurim, hich [is] in Gibeon,
and the battle is very hard on that day, and Abner is smitten, and the men of Israel, before the servants of David.
And there are there three sons of Zeruiah, Joab, and Abishai, and Asahel, and Asahel [is] light on his feet, as one of the roes hich [are] in the field,
And Asahel pursueth after Abner, and hath not turned aside to go to the right or to the left, from after Abner.
And Abner looketh behind him, and saith, ’Art thou he — Asahel?’ and he saith, ’I [am].’

And Abner saith to him, ’Turn thee aside to thy right hand or to thy left, and seize for thee one of the youths, and take to thee his armour;’ and Asahel hath not been illing to turn aside from after him.
And Abner addeth again, saying unto Asahel, ’Turn thee aside from after me, hy do I smite thee to the earth? and ho do I lift up my face unto Joab thy brother?’

And he refuseth to turn aside, and Abner smiteth him ith the hinder part of the spear unto the fifth [rib], and the spear cometh out from behind him, and he falleth there, and dieth under it; and it cometh to pass, every one ho hath come unto the place here Asahel hath fallen and dieth — they stand still.
And Joab and Abishai pursue after Abner, and the sun hath gone in, and they have come in unto the height of Ammah, hich [is] on the front of Giah, the ay of the ilderness of Gibeon.
And the sons of Benjamin gather themselves together after Abner, and become one troop, and stand on the top of a certain height,

and Abner calleth unto Joab, and saith, ’For ever doth the sord consume? hast thou not knon that it is bitterness in the latter end? and till hen dost thou not say to the people to turn back from after their brethren?’
And Joab saith, ’God liveth! for unless thou hadst spoken, surely then from the morning had the people gone up each from after his brother.’
And Joab bloeth ith a trumpet, and all the people stand still, and pursue no more after Israel, nor have they added any more to fight.
And Abner and his men have gone through the plain all that night, and pass over the Jordan, and go on [through] all Bithron, and come in to Mahanaim.
And Joab hath turned back from after Abner, and gathereth all the people, and there are lacking of the servants of David nineteen men, and Asahel;
and the servants of David have smitten of Benjamin, even among the men of Abner, three hundred and sixty men — they died.
And they lift up Asahel, and bury him in the burying-place of his father, hich [is] in Beth-Lehem, and they go all the night — Joab and his men — and it is light to them in Hebron.
And the ar is long beteen the house of Saul and the house of David, and David is going on and [is] strong, and the house of Saul are going on and [are] eak.
And there are born to David sons in Hebron, and his first-born is Amnon, of Ahinoam the Jezreelitess,
and his second [is] Chileab, of Abigail ife of Nabal the Carmelite, and the third [is] Absalom son of Maacah daughter of Talmai king of Geshur,
and the fourth [is] Adonijah son of Haggith, and the fifth [is] Shephatiah son of Abital,
and the sixth [is] Ithream, of Eglah ife of David; these have been born to David in Hebron.
And it cometh to pass, in the ar being beteen the house of Saul and the house of David, that Abner hath been strengthening himself in the house of Saul,
and Saul hath a concubine, and her name [is] Rizpah daughter of Aiah, and [Ish-Bosheth] saith unto Abner, ’Wherefore hast thou gone in unto the concubine of my father?’

And it is displeasing to Abner exceedingly, because of the ords of Ish-Bosheth, and he saith, ’The head of a dog [am] I — that in reference to Judah to-day I do kindness ith the house of Saul thy father, unto his brethren, and unto his friends, and have not delivered thee into the hand of David — that thou chargest against me iniquity concerning the oman to-day?
thus doth God to Abner, and thus He doth add to him, surely as Jehovah hath sorn to David — surely so I do to him:
to cause the kingdom to pass over from the house of Saul, and to raise up the throne of David over Israel, and over Judah, from Dan even unto Beer-Sheba.’
And he is not able any more to turn back Abner a ord, because of his fearing him.
And Abner sendeth messengers unto David for himself, saying, ’Whose [is] the land?’ saying, ’Make thy covenant ith me, and lo, my hand [is] ith thee, to bring round unto thee all Israel.’

And he saith, ’Good — I make ith thee a covenant; only, one thing I am asking of thee, that is, Thou dost not see my face, except thou dost first bring in Michal, daughter of Saul in thy coming into see my face.’
And David sendeth messengers unto Ish-Bosheth son of Saul, saying, ’Give up my ife Michal, hom I betrothed to myself ith a hundred foreskins of the Philistines.’
And Ish-Bosheth sendeth, and taketh her from a man, from Phaltiel son of Laish,
and her husband goeth ith her, going on and eeping behind her, unto Bahurim, and Abner saith unto him, ’Go, turn back;’ and he turneth back.
And the ord of Abner as ith the elders of Israel, saying, ’Heretofore ye have been seeking David for king over you,
and no, do [it], for Jehovah hath spoken of David saying, By the hand of David my servant — to save My people Israel out of the hand of the Philistines, and out of the hand of all their enemies.’
And Abner speaketh also in the ears of Benjamin, and Abner goeth also to speak in the ears of David in Hebron all that [is] good in the eyes of Israel, and in the eyes of all the house of Benjamin,
and Abner cometh in unto David, to Hebron, and ith him tenty men, and David maketh for Abner, and for the men ho [are] ith him, a banquet.

And Abner saith unto David, ’I arise, and go, and gather unto my lord the king the hole of Israel, and they make ith thee a covenant, and thou hast reigned over all that thy soul desireth;’ and David sendeth aay Abner, and he goeth in peace.
And lo, the servants of David, and Joab, have come from the troop, and much spoil have brought ith them, and Abner is not ith David in Hebron, for he hath sent him aay, and he goeth in peace;
and Joab and all the host that [is] ith him have come, and they declare to Joab, saying, ’Abner son of Ner hath come unto the king, and he sendeth him aay, and he goeth in peace.’
And Joab cometh unto the king, and saith, ’What hast thou done? lo, Abner hath come unto thee! hy [is] this — thou hast sent him aay, and he is really gone?
Thou hast knon Abner son of Ner, that to deceive thee he came, and to kno thy going out and thy coming in, and to kno all that thou art doing.’
And Joab goeth out from David, and sendeth messengers after Abner, and they bring him back from the ell of Sirah, and David kne not.

And Abner turneth back to Hebron, and Joab turneth him aside unto the midst of the gate to speak ith him quietly, and smiteth him there in the fifth [rib] — and he dieth — for the blood of Asahel his brother.
And David heareth afterards and saith, ’Acquitted [am] I, and my kingdom, by Jehovah, unto the age, from the blood of Abner son of Ner;

it doth stay on the head of Joab, and on all the house of his father, and there is not cut off from the house of Joab one having an issue, and leprous, and laying hold on a staff, and falling by a sord, and lacking bread.’
And Joab and Abishai his brother sle Abner because that he put to death Asahel their brother, in Gibeon, in battle.
And David saith unto Joab, and unto all the people ho [are] ith him, ’Rend your garments, and gird on sackcloth, and mourn before Abner;’ and king David is going after the bier.
And they bury Abner in Hebron, and the king lifteth up his voice, and eepeth at the grave of Abner, and all the people eep;
and the king lamenteth for Abner, and saith: — ’As the death of a fool doth Abner die?
Thy hands not bound, And thy feet to fetters not brought nigh! As one falling before sons of evil — Thou hast fallen!’ and all the people add to eep over him.

And all the people come to cause David to eat bread hile yet day, and David seareth, saying, ’Thus doth God to me, and thus He doth add, for — before the going in of the sun, I taste no bread or any other thing.’
And all the people have discerned [it], and it is good in their eyes, as all that the king hath done is good in the eyes of all the people;
and all the people kno, even all Israel, in that day, that it hath not been from the king — to put to death Abner son of Ner.
And the king saith unto his servants, ’Do ye not kno that a prince and a great one hath fallen this day in Israel?
and I to-day [am] tender, and an anointed king: and these men, sons of Zeruiah, [are] too hard for me; Jehovah doth recompense to the doer of the evil according to his evil.’
And the son of Saul heareth that Abner [is] dead in Hebron, and his hands are feeble, and all Israel have been troubled.

And to men, heads of troops, have been [to] the son of Saul, the name of the one [is] Baanah, and the name of the second Rechab, sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, of the sons of Benjamin, for also Beeroth is reckoned to Benjamin,
and the Beerothites flee to Gittaim, and are there sojourners unto this day.

And to Jonathan son of Saul [is] a son — lame; he as a son of five years at the coming in of the rumour of [the death of] Saul and Jonathan, out of Jezreel, and his nurse lifteth him up, and fleeth, and it cometh to pass in her hasting to flee, that he falleth, and becometh lame, and his name [is] Mephibosheth.
And the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, Rechab and Baanah, go, and come in at the heat of the day unto the house of Ish-Bosheth, and he is lying don — the lying don of noon;
and thither they have come, unto the midst of the house, taking heat, and they smite him unto the fifth [rib], and Rechab and Baanah his brother have escaped;

yea, they come in to the house, and he is lying on his bed, in the inner part of his bed-chamber, and they smite him, and put him to death, and turn aside his head, and they take his head, and go the ay of the plain all the night,

and bring in the head of Ish-Bosheth unto David in Hebron, and say unto the king, ’Lo, the head of Ish-Bosheth, son of Saul, thine enemy, ho sought thy life; and Jehovah doth give to my lord the king vengeance this day, of Saul and of his seed.’
And David ansereth Rechab and Baanah his brother, sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, and saith to them, ’Jehovah liveth, ho hath redeemed my soul out of all adversity,
hen one is declaring to me, saying, Lo, Saul is dead, and he as as a bearer of tidings in his on eyes, then I take hold on him, and slay him in Ziklag, instead of my giving to him [for] the tidings.
Also — hen icked men have slain the righteous man in his on house, on his bed; and no, do not I require his blood of your hand, and have taken you aay from the earth?’

And David commandeth the young men, and they slay them, and cut off their hands and their feet, and hang [them] over the pool in Hebron, and the head of Ish-Bosheth they have taken, and bury [it] in the burying-place of Abner in Hebron.
And all the tribes of Israel come unto David, to Hebron, and speak, saying, ’Lo, e [are] thy bone and thy flesh;

also heretofore, in Saul’s being king over us, thou hast been he ho is bringing out and bringing in Israel, and Jehovah saith to thee, Thou dost feed My people Israel, and thou art for leader over Israel.’
And all the elders of Israel come unto the king, to Hebron, and king David maketh ith them a covenant in Hebron before Jehovah, and they anoint David for king over Israel.
A son of thirty years [is] David in his being king; forty years he hath reigned;
in Hebron he reigned over Judah seven years and six months, and in Jerusalem he reigned thirty and three years, over all Israel and Judah.

And the king goeth, and his men, to Jerusalem, unto the Jebusite, the inhabitant of the land, and they speak to David, saying, ’Thou dost not come in hither, except thou turn aside the blind and the lame;’ saying, ’David doth not come in hither.’
And David captureth the fortress of Zion, it [is] the city of David.

And David saith on that day, ’Any one smiting the Jebusite, (let him go up by the atercourse), and the lame and the blind — the hated of David’s soul,’ — because the blind and lame say, ’He doth not come into the house.’
And David delleth in the fortress, and calleth it — City of David, and David buildeth round about, from Millo and inard,
and David goeth, going on and becoming great, and Jehovah, God of Hosts, [is] ith him.
And Hiram king of Tyre sendeth messengers unto David, and cedar-trees, and artificers of ood, and artificers of stone, for alls, and they build a house for David,
and David knoeth that Jehovah hath established him for king over Israel, and that He hath lifted up his kingdom, because of His people Israel.
And David taketh again concubines and ives out of Jerusalem, after his coming from Hebron, and there are born again to David sons and daughters.
And these [are] the names of those born to him in Jerusalem: Shammuah, and Shobab, and Nathan, and Solomon,
and Ibhar, and Elishua, and Nepheg, and Japhia,
and Elishama, and Eliada, and Eliphalet.
And the Philistines hear that they have anointed David for king over Israel, and all the Philistines come up to seek David, and David heareth, and goeth don unto the fortress,
and the Philistines have come, and are spread out in the valley of Rephaim.
And David asketh of Jehovah, saying, ’Do I go up unto the Philistines? dost Thou give them into my hand?’ And Jehovah saith unto David, ’Go up, for I certainly give the Philistines into thy hand.’

And David cometh in to Baal-Perazim, and David smiteth them there, and saith, ’Jehovah hath broken forth [on] mine enemies before me, as the breaking forth of aters;’ therefore he hath called the name of that place Baal-Perazim.
And they forsake there their idols, and David and his men lift them up.
And the Philistines add again to come up, and are spread out in the valley of Rephaim,
and David asketh of Jehovah, and He saith, ’Thou dost not go up, turn round unto their rear, and thou hast come to them over-against the mulberries,

and it cometh to pass, in thy hearing the sound of a stepping in the tops of the mulberries, then thou dost move sharply, for then hath Jehovah gone out before thee to smite in the camp of the Philistines.’
And David doth so, as Jehovah commanded him, and smiteth the Philistines from Geba unto thy coming to Gazer.
And David gathered again every chosen one in Israel, thirty thousand,

and David riseth and goeth, and all the people ho [are] ith him, from Baale-Judah, to bring up thence the ark of God, hose name hath been called — the name of Jehovah of Hosts, inhabiting the cherubs — upon it.
And they cause the ark of God to ride on a ne cart, and lift it up from the house of Abinadab, hich [is] in the height, and Uzzah and Ahio sons of Abinadab are leading the ne cart;
and they lift it up from the house of Abinadab, hich [is] in the height, ith the ark of God, and Ahio is going before the ark,
and David and all the house of Israel are playing before Jehovah, ith all kinds of [instruments] of fir-ood, even ith harps, and ith psalteries, and ith timbrels, and ith cornets, and ith cymbals.
And they come unto the threshing-floor of Nachon, and Uzzah putteth forth [his hand] unto the ark of God, and layeth hold on it, for they released the oxen;
and the anger of Jehovah burneth against Uzzah, and God smiteth him there for the error, and he dieth there by the ark of God.
And it is displeasing to David, because that Jehovah hath broken forth a breach upon Uzzah, and [one] calleth that place Perez-Uzzah, unto this day;
and David feareth Jehovah on that day, and saith, ’Ho doth the ark of Jehovah come in unto me?’
And David hath not been illing to turn aside unto himself the ark of Jehovah, to the city of David, and David turneth it aside to the house of Obed-Edom the Gittite,
and the ark of Jehovah doth inhabit the house of Obed-Edom the Gittite three months, and Jehovah blesseth Obed-Edom and all his house.

And it is declared to king David, saying, ’Jehovah hath blessed the house of Obed-Edom, and all that he hath, because of the ark of God;’ and David goeth and bringeth up the ark of God from the house of Obed-Edom to the city of David ith joy.
And it cometh to pass, hen those bearing the ark of Jehovah have stepped six steps, that he sacrificeth an ox and a fatling.
And David is dancing ith all strength before Jehovah, and David is girded ith a linen ephod,
and David and all the house of Israel are bringing up the ark of Jehovah ith shouting, and ith the voice of a trumpet,

and it hath come to pass, the ark of Jehovah hath come in to the city of David, and Michal daughter of Saul, hath looked through the indo, and seeth king David moving and dancing before Jehovah, and despiseth him in her heart.

And they bring in the ark of Jehovah, and set it up in its place, in the midst of the tent hich David hath spread out for it, and David causeth to ascend burnt-offerings before Jehovah, and peace-offerings.
And David finisheth from causing to ascend the burnt-offering, and the peace-offerings, and blesseth the people in the name of Jehovah of Hosts,
and he apportioneth to all the people, to all the multitude of Israel, from man even unto oman, to each, one cake of bread, and one eshpar, and one ashisha, and all the people go, each to his house.

And David turneth back to bless his house, and Michal daughter of Saul goeth out to meet David, and saith, ’Ho honourable to-day as the king of Israel, ho as uncovered to-day before the eyes of the handmaids of his servants, as one of the vain ones is openly uncovered!’

And David saith unto Michal, ’ — Before Jehovah, ho fixed on me above thy father, and above all his house, to appoint me leader over the people of Jehovah, and over Israel, — yea, I played before Jehovah;
and I have been more vile than this, and have been lo in mine eyes, and ith the handmaids hom thou hast spoken of, ith them I am honoured.’
As to Michal daughter of Saul, she had no child till the day of her death.
And it cometh to pass, hen the king sat in his house, and Jehovah hath given rest to him round about, from all his enemies,
that the king saith unto Nathan the prophet, ’See, I pray thee, I am delling in a house of cedars, and the ark of God is delling in the midst of the curtain.’
And Nathan saith unto the king, ’All that [is] in thine heart — go, do, for Jehovah [is] ith thee.’
And it cometh to pass in that night, that the ord of Jehovah is unto Nathan, saying,
’Go, and thou hast said unto My servant, unto David, Thus said Jehovah, Dost thou build for Me a house for My delling in?
for I have not delt in a house even from the day of My bringing up the sons of Israel out of Egypt, even unto this day, and am alking up and don in a tent and in a tabernacle.

During all [the time] that I have alked up and don among all the sons of Israel, a ord have I spoken ith one of the tribes of Israel hich I commanded to feed my people Israel, saying, ’Why have ye not built to Me a house of cedars?
and no, thus dost thou say to My servant, to David: ’Thus said Jehovah of Hosts, I have taken thee from the comely place, from after the flock, to be leader over My people, over Israel;
and I am ith thee hithersoever thou hast gone, and I cut off all thine enemies from thy presence, and have made for thee a great name, as the name of the great ones ho [are] in the earth,

and I have appointed a place for My people, for Israel, and have planted it, and it hath tabernacled in its place, and it is not troubled any more, and the sons of perverseness do not add to afflict it any more, as in the beginning,
even from the day that I appointed judges over My people Israel; and I have given rest to thee from all thine enemies, and Jehovah hath declared to thee that Jehovah doth make for thee a house.
’When thy days are full, and thou hast lain ith thy fathers, then I have raised up thy seed after thee hich goeth out from thy boels, and have established his kingdom;
He doth build a house for My Name, and I have established the throne of his kingdom unto the age.
I am to him for a father, and he is to Me for a son; hom in his dealings perversely I have even reproved ith a rod of men, and ith strokes of the sons of Adam,
and My kindness doth not turn aside from him, as I turned it aside from Saul, hom I turned aside from before thee,
and stedfast [is] thy house and thy kingdom unto the age before thee, thy throne is established unto the age.’
According to all these ords, and according to all this vision, so spake Nathan unto David.
And king David cometh in and sitteth before Jehovah, and saith, ’Who [am] I, Lord Jehovah? and hat my house, that Thou hast brought me hitherto?
And yet this [is] little in Thine eyes, Lord Jehovah, and Thou dost speak also concerning the house of Thy servant afar off; and this [is] the la of the Man, Lord Jehovah.
And hat doth David add more to speak unto Thee? and Thou, Thou hast knon Thy servant, Lord Jehovah.
Because of Thy ord, and according to Thy heart, Thou hast done all this greatness, to cause Thy servant to kno [it].
Therefore Thou hast been great, Jehovah God, for there is none like Thee, and there is no God save Thee, according to all that e have heard ith our ears.

’And ho [is] as Thy people, as Israel — one nation in the earth, hom God hath gone to redeem to Him for a people, and to make for Him a name — and to do for you the greatness — even fearful things for Thy land, at the presence of Thy people, hom Thou hast redeemed to Thee out of Egypt — [among the] nations and their gods?
Yea, Thou dost establish to Thee Thy people Israel, to Thee for a people unto the age, and Thou, Jehovah, hast been to them for God.
’And no, Jehovah God, the ord hich Thou hast spoken concerning Thy servant, and concerning his house, establish unto the age, and do as Thou hast spoken;
And Thy Name is great unto the age, saying, Jehovah of Hosts [is] God over Israel, and the house of Thy servant David is established before Thee,
For Thou, Jehovah of Hosts, God of Israel, Thou hast uncovered the ear of Thy servant, saying, A house I build for thee, therefore hath Thy servant found his heart to pray unto Thee this prayer;
And no, Lord Jehovah, Thou [art] God Himself, and Thy ords are truth, and Thou speakest unto Thy servant this goodness,
And no, begin and bless the house of Thy servant, to be unto the age before Thee, for Thou, Lord Jehovah, hast spoken, and by Thy blessing is the house of Thy servant blessed — to the age.’
And it cometh to pass afterards that David smiteth the Philistines, and humbleth them, and David taketh the bridle of the metropolis out of the hand of the Philistines.

And he smiteth Moab, and measureth them ith a line, causing them to lie don on the earth, and he measureth to lines to put to death, and the fulness of the line to keep alive, and the Moabites are to David for servants, bearers of a present.
And David smiteth Hadadezer son of Rehob, king of Zobah, in his going to bring back his poer by the River [Euphrates;]

and David captureth from him a thousand and seven hundred horsemen, and tenty thousand footmen, and David destroyeth utterly the hole of the charioteers, only he leaveth of them a hundred charioteers.
And Aram of Damascus cometh to give help to Hadadezer king of Zobah, and David smiteth of Aram tenty and to thousand men;
and David putteth garrisons in Aram of Damascus, and Aram is to David for a servant, bearing a present; and Jehovah saveth David hithersoever he hath gone;
and David taketh the shields of gold hich ere on the servants of Hadadezer, and bringeth them to Jerusalem;
and from Betah, and from Berothai, cities of Hadadezer, hath king David taken very much brass.
And Toi king of Hamath heareth that David hath smitten all the force of Hadadezer,

and Toi sendeth Joram his son unto king David to ask of him of elfare, and to bless him, (because that he hath fought against Hadadezer, and smiteth him, for a man of ars [ith] Toi had Hadadezer been), and in his hand have been vessels of silver, and vessels of gold, and vessels of brass,
also them did king David sanctify to Jehovah, ith the silver and the gold hich he sanctified of all the nations hich he subdued:
of Aram, and of Moab, and of the Bene-Ammon, and of the Philistines, and of Amalek, and of the spoil of Hadadezer son of Rehob king of Zobah.
And David maketh a name in his turning back from his smiting Aram in the valley of Salt — eighteen thousand;
and he putteth in Edom garrisons — in all Edom he hath put garrisons, and all Edom are servants to David; and Jehovah saveth David hithersoever he hath gone.
And David reigneth over all Israel, and David is doing judgment and righteousness to all his people,
and Joab son of Zeruiah [is] over the host, and Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud [is] remembrancer,
and Zadok son of Ahitub, and Ahimelech son of Abiathar, [are] priests, and Seraiah [is] scribe,
and Benaiah son of Jehoiada [is over] both the Cherethite and the Pelethite, and the sons of David have been ministers.
And David saith, ’Is there yet any left to the house of Saul, and I do ith him kindness because of Jonathan?’
And the house of Saul hath a servant, and his name [is] Ziba, and they call for him unto David; and the king saith unto him, ’Art thou Ziba?’ and he saith, ’Thy servant.’
And the king saith, ’Is there not yet a man to the house of Saul, and I do ith him the kindness of God?’ And Ziba saith unto the king, ’Jonathan hath yet a son — lame.’
And the king saith to him, ’Where [is] he?’ and Ziba saith unto the king, ’Lo, he [is] in the house of Machir, son of Ammiel, in Lo-Debar.’
And king David sendeth, and taketh him out of the house of Machir son of Ammiel, of Lo-Debar,
and Mephibosheth son of Jonathan, son of Saul, cometh unto David, and falleth on his face, and doth obeisance, and David saith, ’Mephibosheth;’ and he saith, ’Lo, thy servant.’

And David saith to him, ’Be not afraid; for I certainly do ith thee kindness because of Jonathan thy father, and have given back to thee all the field of Saul thy father, and thou dost eat bread at my table continually.’
And he boeth himself, and saith, ’What [is] thy servant, that thou hast turned unto the dead dog — such as I?’
And the king calleth unto Ziba servant of Saul, and saith unto him, ’All that as to Saul and to all his house, I have given to the son of thy lord,

and thou hast served for him the land, thou and thy sons, and thy servants, and hast brought in, and there hath been to the son of thy lord bread, and he hath eaten it; and Mephibosheth son of thy lord doth eat continually bread at my table;’ and Ziba hath fifteen sons and tenty servants.

And Ziba saith unto the king, ’According to all that my lord the king commandeth his servant, so doth thy servant;’ as to Mephibosheth, ’he is eating at my table ([saith the king]) as one of the sons of the king.’
And Mephibosheth hath a young son, and his name [is] Micha, and every one delling in the house of Ziba [are] servants to Mephibosheth.
And Mephibosheth is delling in Jerusalem, for at the table of the king he is eating continually, and he [is] lame of his to feet.
And it cometh to pass afterards, that the king of the Bene-Ammon dieth, and Hanun his son reigneth in his stead,

and David saith, ’I do kindness ith Hanun son of Nahash, as his father did ith me kindness;’ and David sendeth to comfort him by the hand of his servants concerning his father, and the servants of David come in to the land of the Bene-Ammon.

And the heads of the Bene-Ammon say unto Hanun their lord, ’Is David honouring thy father in thine eyes because he hath sent to thee comforters? for to search the city, and to spy it, and to overthro it, hath not David sent his servants unto thee?’
And Hanun taketh the servants of David, and shaveth off the half of their beard, and cutteth off their long robes in the midst — unto their buttocks, and sendeth them aay;
and they declare [it] to David, and he sendeth to meet them, for the men have been greatly ashamed, and the king saith, ’Abide in Jericho till your beard doth spring up — then ye have returned.’

And the Bene-Ammon see that they have been abhorred by David, and the Bene-Ammon send and hire Aram of Beth-Rehob, and Aram of Zoba, tenty thousand footmen, and the king of Maacah [ith] a thousand men, and Ish-Tob [ith] telve thousand men;
and David heareth, and sendeth Joab, and all the host — the mighty men.
And the Bene-Ammon come out, and set battle in array, at the opening of the gate, and Aram of Zoba, and Rehob, and Ish-Tob, and Maacah, [are] by themselves in the field;
and Joab seeth that the front of the battle hath been unto him before and behind, and he chooseth of all the chosen in Israel, and setteth in array to meet Aram,
and the rest of the people he hath given into the hand of Abishai his brother, and setteth in array to meet the Bene-Ammon.
And he saith, ’If Aram be stronger than I, then thou hast been to me for salvation, and if the Bene-Ammon be stronger than thou, then I have come to give salvation to thee;
be strong and strengthen thyself for our people, and for the cities of our God, and Jehovah doth that hich is good in His eyes.’
And Joab draeth nigh, and the people ho [are] ith him, to battle against Aram, and they flee from his presence;
and the Bene-Ammon have seen that Aram hath fled, and they flee from the presence of Abishai, and go in to the city; and Joab turneth back from the Bene-Ammon, and cometh in to Jerusalem.
And Aram seeth that it is smitten before Israel, and they are gathered together;
and Hadadezer sendeth, and bringeth out Aram hich [is] beyond the River, and they come in to Helam, and Shobach head of the host of Hadadezer [is] before them.
And it is declared to David, and he gathereth all Israel, and passeth over the Jordan, and cometh in to Helam, and Aram setteth itself in array to meet David, and they fight ith him;
and Aram fleeth from the presence of Israel, and David slayeth of Aram seven hundred charioteers, and forty thousand horsemen, and Shobach head of its host he hath smitten, and he dieth there.
And all the kings — servants of Hadadezer — see that they have been smitten before Israel, and make peace ith Israel, and serve them; and Aram is afraid to help any more the Bene-Ammon.

And it cometh to pass, at the revolution of the year — at the time of the going out of the messengers — that David sendeth Joab, and his servants ith him, and all Israel, and they destroy the Bene-Ammon, and lay siege against Rabbah. And David is delling in Jerusalem,

and it cometh to pass, at evening-time, that David riseth from off his couch, and alketh up and don on the roof of the king’s house, and seeth from the roof a oman bathing, and the oman [is] of very good appearance,
and David sendeth and inquireth about the oman, and saith, ’Is not this Bath-Sheba, daughter of Eliam, ife of Uriah the Hittite?’
And David sendeth messengers, and taketh her, and she cometh unto him, and he lieth ith her — and she is purifying herself from her uncleanness — and she turneth back unto her house;
and the oman conceiveth, and sendeth, and declareth to David, and saith, ’I [am] conceiving.’
And David sendeth unto Joab, ’Send unto me Uriah the Hittite,’ and Joab sendeth Uriah unto David;
and Uriah cometh unto him, and David asketh of the prosperity of Joab, and of the prosperity of the people, and of the prosperity of the ar.
And David saith to Uriah, ’Go don to thy house, and ash thy feet;’ and Uriah goeth out of the king’s house, and there goeth out after him a gift from the king,
and Uriah lieth don at the opening of the king’s house, ith all the servants of his lord, and hath not gone don unto his house.
And they declare to David, saying, ’Uriah hath not gone don unto his house;’ and David saith unto Uriah, ’Hast thou not come from a journey? herefore hast thou not gone don unto thy house?’

And Uriah saith unto David, ’The ark, and Israel, and Judah, are abiding in booths, and my lord Joab, and the servants of my lord, on the face of the field are encamping; and I — I go in unto my house to eat and to drink, and to lie ith my ife! — thy life, and the life of thy soul — if I do this thing.’
And David saith unto Uriah, ’Abide in this [place] also to-day, and to-morro I send thee aay;’ and Uriah abideth in Jerusalem, on that day, and on the morro,

and David calleth for him, and he eateth before him, and drinketh, and he causeth him to drink, and he goeth out in the evening to lie on his couch ith the servants of his lord, and unto his house he hath not gone don.
And it cometh to pass in the morning, that David riteth a letter unto Joab, and sendeth by the hand of Uriah;
and he riteth in the letter, saying, ’Place ye Uriah over-against the front of the severest battle, and ye have turned back from after him, and he hath been smitten, and hath died.’
And it cometh to pass in Joab’s atching of the city, that he appointeth Uriah unto the place here he kne that valiant men [are];
and the men of the city go out and fight ith Joab, and there fall [some] of the people, of the servants of David; and there dieth also Uriah the Hittite.
And Joab sendeth and declareth to David all the matters of the ar,
and commandeth the messenger, saying, ’At thy finishing all the matters of the ar to speak unto the king,
then, it hath been, if the king’s fury ascend, and he hath said to thee, Wherefore did ye dra nigh unto the city to fight? did ye not kno that they shoot from off the all?

Who smote Abimelech son of Jerubbesheth? did not a oman cast on him a piece of a rider from the all, and he dieth in Thebez? hy dre ye nigh unto the all? that thou hast said, Also thy servant Uriah the Hittite is dead.’
And the messenger goeth, and cometh in, and declareth to David all that ith hich Joab sent him,
and the messenger saith unto David, ’Surely the men have been mighty against us, and come out unto us into the field, and e are upon them unto the opening of the gate,
and those shooting shoot at thy servants from off the all, and [some] of the servants of the king are dead, and also, thy servant Uriah the Hittite is dead.

And David saith unto the messenger, ’Thus dost thou say unto Joab, Let not this thing be evil in thine eyes; for thus and thus doth the sord devour; strengthen thy arfare against the city, and thro it don — and strengthen thou him.’
And the ife of Uriah heareth that Uriah her husband [is] dead, and lamenteth for her lord;

and the mourning passeth by, and David sendeth and gathereth her unto his house, and she is to him for a ife, and beareth to him a son; and the thing hich David hath done is evil in the eyes of Jehovah.
And Jehovah sendeth Nathan unto David, and he cometh unto him, and saith to him: ’To men have been in one city; One rich and one poor;
The rich hath flocks and herds very many;

And the poor one hath nothing, Except one little ee-lamb, Which he hath bought, and keepeth alive, And it groeth up ith him, And ith his sons together; Of his morsel it eateth, And from his cup it drinketh, And in his bosom it lieth, And it is to him as a daughter;

And there cometh a traveller to the rich man, And he spareth to take Of his on flock, and of his on herd, To prepare for the traveller Who hath come to him, And he taketh the ee-lamb of the poor man, And prepareth it for the man Who hath come unto him.’
And the anger of David burneth against the man exceedingly, and he saith unto Nathan, ’Jehovah liveth, surely a son of death [is] the man ho is doing this,
and the ee-lamb he doth repay fourfold, because that he hath done this thing, and because that he had no pity.’
And Nathan saith unto David, ’Thou [art] the man! Thus said Jehovah, God of Israel, I anointed thee for king over Israel, and I delivered thee out of the hand of Saul;
and I give to thee the house of thy lord, and the ives of thy lord, into thy bosom, and I give to thee the house of Israel and of Judah; and if little, then I add to thee such and such [things].

’Wherefore hast thou despised the ord of Jehovah, to do the evil thing in His eyes? Uriah the Hittite thou hast smitten by the sord, and his ife thou hast taken to thee for a ife, and him thou hast slain by the sord of the Bene-Ammon.
’And no, the sord doth not turn aside from thy house unto the age, because thou hast despised Me, and dost take the ife of Uriah the Hittite to be to thee for a ife;

thus said Jehovah, Lo, I am raising up against thee evil, out of thy house, and have taken thy ives before thine eyes, and given to thy neighbour, and he hath lain ith thy ives before the eyes of this sun;
for thou hast done [it] in secret, and I do this thing before all Israel, and before the sun.’
And David saith unto Nathan, ’I have sinned against Jehovah.’ And Nathan saith unto David, ’Also — Jehovah hath caused thy sin to pass aay; thou dost not die;
only, because thou hast caused the enemies of Jehovah greatly to despise by this thing, also the son ho is born to thee doth surely die.’
And Nathan goeth unto his house, and Jehovah smiteth the lad, hom the ife of Uriah hath born to David, and it is incurable;
and David seeketh God for the youth, and David keepeth a fast, and hath gone in and lodged, and lain on the earth.
And the elders of his house rise against him, to raise him up from the earth, and he hath not been illing, nor hath he eaten ith them bread;

and it cometh to pass on the seventh day, that the lad dieth, and the servants of David fear to declare to him that the lad is dead, for they said, ’Lo, in the lad being alive e spake unto him, and he did not hearken to our voice; and ho do e say unto him, The lad is dead? — then he hath done evil.’
And David seeth that his servants are hispering, and David understandeth that the lad is dead, and David saith unto his servants, ’Is the lad dead?’ and they say, ’Dead.’

And David riseth from the earth, and doth bathe and anoint [himself], and changeth his raiment, and cometh in to the house of Jehovah, and boeth himself, and cometh unto his house, and asketh and they place for him bread, and he eateth.
And his servants say unto him, ’What [is] this thing thou hast done? because of the living lad thou hast fasted and dost eep, and hen the lad is dead thou hast risen and dost eat bread.’
And he saith, ’While the lad is alive I have fasted, and eep, for I said, Who knoeth? — Jehovah doth pity me, and the lad hath lived;
and no, he hath died, hy [is] this — I fast? am I able to bring him back again? I am going unto him, and he doth not turn back unto me.’
And David comforteth Bath-Sheba his ife, and goeth in unto her, and lieth ith her, and she beareth a son, and he calleth his name Solomon; and Jehovah hath loved him,
and sendeth by the hand of Nathan the prophet, and calleth his name Jedidiah, because of Jehovah.
And Joab fighteth against Rabbah of the Bene-Ammon, and captureth the royal city,
and Joab sendeth messengers unto David, and saith, ’I have fought against Rabbah — also I have captured the city of aters;
and no, gather the rest of the people, and encamp against the city, and capture it, lest I capture the city, and my name hath been called upon it.’
And David gathereth all the people, and goeth to Rabbah, and fighteth against it, and captureth it;

and he taketh the cron of their king from off his head, and its eight [is] a talent of gold, and precious stones, and it is on the head of David; and the spoil of the city he hath brought out, very much;

and the people ho [are] in it he hath brought out, and setteth to the sa, and to cutting instruments of iron, and to axes of iron, and hath caused them to pass over into the brick-kiln; and so he doth to all the cities of the Bene-Ammon; and David turneth back, and all the people, to Jerusalem.
And it cometh to pass afterards that Absalom son of David hath a fair sister, and her name [is] Tamar, and Amnon son of David loveth her.
And Amnon hath distress — even to become sick, because of Tamar his sister, for she [is] a virgin, and it is hard in the eyes of Amnon to do anything to her.
And Amnon hath a friend, and his name [is] Jonadab, son of Shimeah, David’s brother, and Jonadab [is] a very ise man,
and saith to him, ’Wherefore [art] thou thus lean, O king’s son, morning by morning? dost thou not declare to me?’ And Amnon saith to him, ’Tamar — sister of Absalom my brother — I am loving.’

And Jonadab saith to him, ’Lie don on thy couch, and feign thyself sick, and thy father hath come in to see thee, and thou hast said unto him, ’Let, I pray thee, Tamar my sister come in and give me bread to eat; and she hath made the food before mine eyes so that I see [it], and have eaten from her hand.’
