And he saith, ’What have I sinned, that thou art giving thy servant into the hand of Ahab — to put me to death?

Jehovah thy God liveth, if there is a nation and kingdom hither my lord hath not sent to seek thee; and they said, He is not, then he caused the kingdom and the nation to sear, that it doth not find thee;
and no, thou art saying, Go, say to thy lord, Lo, Elijah;

and it hath been, I go from thee, and the Spirit of Jehovah doth lift thee up, hither I kno not, and I have come to declare to Ahab, and he doth not find thee, and he hath slain me; and thy servant is fearing Jehovah from my youth.

’Hath it not been declared to my lord that hich I have done in Jezebel’s slaying the prophets of Jehovah, that I hide of the prophets of Jehovah a hundred men, fifty by fifty in a cave, and sustained them ith bread and ater?
and no thou art saying, Go, say to my lord, Lo, Elijah — and he hath slain me!’
And Elijah saith, ’Jehovah of Hosts liveth, before hom I have stood, surely to-day I appear unto him.’
And Obadiah goeth to meet Ahab, and declareth [it] to him, and Ahab goeth to meet Elijah,
and it cometh to pass at Ahab’s seeing Elijah, that Ahab saith unto him, ’Art thou he — the troubler of Israel?’
And he saith, ’I have not troubled Israel, but thou and the house of thy father, in your forsaking the commands of Jehovah, and thou goest after the Baalim;
and no, send, gather unto me all Israel, unto the mount of Carmel, and the prophets of Baal four hundred and fifty, and the prophets of the shrine, four hundred — eating at the table of Jezebel.’
And Ahab sendeth among all the sons of Israel, and gathereth the prophets unto the mount of Carmel;

and Elijah cometh nigh unto all the people, and saith, ’Till hen are ye leaping on the to branches? — if Jehovah [is] God, go after Him; and if Baal, go after him;’ and the people have not ansered him a ord.
And Elijah saith unto the people, ’I — I have been left a prophet of Jehovah — by myself; and the prophets of Baal [are] four hundred and fifty men;

and let them give to us to bullocks, and they choose for themselves the one bullock, and cut it in pieces, and place [it] on the ood, and place no fire; and I — I prepare the other bullock, and have put [it] on the ood, and fire I do not place; —

and ye have called in the name of your god, and I — I call in the name of Jehovah, and it hath been, the god ho ansereth by fire — He [is] the God.’ And all the people anser and say, ’Good [is] the ord.’
And Elijah saith to the prophets of Baal, ’Choose for you the one bullock, and prepare first, for ye [are] the multitude, and call ye in the name of your god, and place no fire.’

And they take the bullock that [one] gave to them, and prepare, and call in the name of Baal from the morning even till the noon, saying, ’O Baal, anser us!’ and there is no voice, and there is none ansering; and they leap on the altar that one had made.

And it cometh to pass, at noon, that Elijah playeth on them, and saith, ’Call ith a loud voice, for he [is] a god, for he is meditating, or pursuing, or on a journey; it may be he is asleep, an doth aake.’
And they call ith a loud voice, and cut themselves, according to their ordinance, ith sords and ith spears, till a floing of blood [is] on them;

and it cometh to pass, at the passing by of the noon, that they feign themselves prophets till the going up of the present, and there is no voice, and there is none ansering, and there is none attending.
And Elijah saith to all the people, ’Come nigh unto me;’ and all the people come nigh unto him, and he repaireth the altar of Jehovah that is broken don;
and Elijah taketh telve stones, according to the number of the tribes of the sons of Jacob, unto hom the ord of Jehovah as, saying, ’Israel is thy name;’
and he buildeth ith the stones an altar, in the name of Jehovah, and maketh a trench, as about the space of to measures of seed, round about the altar.
And he arrangeth the ood, and cutteth in pieces the bullock, and placeth [it] on the ood, and saith, ’Fill ye four pitchers of ater, and pour on the burnt-offering, and on the ood;
and he saith, ’Do [it] a second time;’ and they do [it] a second time; and he saith, ’Do [it] a third time;’ and they do [it] a third time;
and the ater goeth round about the altar, and also, the trench he hath filled ith ater.

And it cometh to pass, at the going up of the [evening -]present, that Elijah the prophet cometh nigh and saith, ’Jehovah, God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, to-day let it be knon that Thou [art] God in Israel, and I Thy servant, that by Thy ord I have done the hole of these things;
anser me, O Jehovah, anser me, and this people doth kno that Thou [art] Jehovah God; and Thou hast turned their heart backard.’
And there falleth a fire of Jehovah, and consumeth the burnt-offering, and the ood, and the stones, and the dust, and the ater that [is] in the trench it hath licked up.
And all the people see, and fall on their faces, and say, ’Jehovah, He [is] the God, Jehovah, He [is] the God.’
And Elijah saith to them, ’Catch ye the prophets of Baal; let not a man escape of them;’ and they catch them, and Elijah bringeth them don unto the stream Kishon, and doth slaughter them there.
And Elijah saith to Ahab, ’Go up, eat and drink, because of the sound of the noise of the shoer.’
And Ahab goeth up to eat, and to drink, and Elijah hath gone up unto the top of Carmel, and he stretcheth himself out on the earth, and he placeth his face beteen his knees,
and saith unto his young man, ’Go up, I pray thee, look attentively the ay of the sea;’ and he goeth up and looketh attentively, and saith, ’There is nothing;’ and he saith, ’Turn back,’ seven times.

And it cometh to pass, at the seventh, that he saith, ’Lo, a little thickness as the palm of a man is coming up out of the sea.’ And he saith, ’Go up, say unto Ahab, ’Bind — and go don, and the shoer doth not restrain thee.’
And it cometh to pass, in the meantime, that the heavens have become black — thick clouds and ind — and the shoer is great; and Ahab rideth, and goeth to Jezreel,
and the hand of Jehovah hath been on Elijah, and he girdeth up his loins, and runneth before Ahab, till thine entering Jezreel.
And Ahab declareth to Jezebel all that Elijah did, and all ho he sle all the prophets by the sord,
and Jezebel sendeth a messenger unto Elijah, saying, ’Thus doth the gods, and thus do they add, surely about this time to-morro, I make thy life as the life of one of them.’
And he feareth, and riseth, and goeth for his life, and cometh in to Beer-Sheba, that [is] Judah’s, and leaveth his young man there,

and he himself hath gone into the ilderness a day’s Journey, and cometh and sitteth under a certain retem-tree, and desireth his soul to die, and saith, ’Enough, no, O Jehovah, take my soul, for I [am] not better than my fathers.’
And he lieth don and sleepeth under a certain retem-tree, and lo, a messenger cometh against him, and saith to him, ’Rise, eat;’
and he looketh attentively, and lo, at his bolster a cake [baken on] burning stones, and a dish of ater, and he eateth, and drinketh, and turneth, and lieth don.
And the messenger of Jehovah turneth back a second time, and cometh against him, and saith, ’Rise, eat, for the ay is too great for thee;’
and he riseth, and eateth, and drinketh, and goeth in the poer of that food forty days and forty nights, unto the mount of God — Horeb.
And he cometh in there, unto the cave, and lodgeth there, and lo, the ord of Jehovah [is] unto him, and saith to him, ’What — to thee, here, Elijah?’

And he saith, ’I have been very zealous for Jehovah, God of Hosts, for the sons of Israel have forsaken Thy covenant — Thine altars they have thron don, and Thy prophets they have slain by the sord, and I am left, I, by myself, and they seek my life — to take it.’

And He saith, ’Go out, and thou hast stood in the mount before Jehovah.’ And lo, Jehovah is passing by, and a ind — great and strong — is rending mountains, and shivering rocks before Jehovah: — not in the ind [is] Jehovah; and after the ind a shaking: — not in the shaking [is] Jehovah;
and after the shaking a fire: — not in the fire [is] Jehovah; and after the fire a voice still small;

and it cometh to pass, at Elijah’s hearing [it], that he rappeth his face in his robe, and goeth out, and standeth at the opening of the cave, and lo, unto him [is] a voice, and it saith, ’What — to thee, here, Elijah?’

And he saith, ’I have been very zealous for Jehovah, God of Hosts; for the sons of Israel have forsaken Thy covenant, Thine altars they have thron don, and Thy prophets they have slain by the sord, and I am left, I, by myself, and they seek my life — to take it.’
And Jehovah saith unto him, ’Go turn back on thy ay to the ilderness of Damascus, and thou hast gone in, and anointed Hazael for king over Aram,
and Jehu son of Nimshi thou dost anoint for king over Israel, and Elisha son of Shaphat, of Abel-Meholah, thou dost anoint for prophet in thy stead.
’And it hath been, him ho is escaped from the sord of Hazael, put to death doth Jehu, and him ho is escaped from the sord of Jehu put to death doth Elisha;
and I have left in Israel seven thousand, all the knees that have not boed to Baal, and every mouth that hath not kissed him.’
And he goeth thence, and findeth Elisha son of Shaphat, and he is ploing; telve yoke [are] before him, and he [is] ith the telfth; and Elijah passeth over unto him, and casteth his robe upon him,

and he forsaketh the oxen, and runneth after Elijah, and saith, ’Let me give a kiss, I pray thee, to my father and to my mother, and I go after thee.’ And he saith to him, ’Go, turn back, for hat have I done to thee?’

And he turneth back from after him, and taketh the yoke of oxen, and sacrificeth it, and ith instruments of the oxen he hath boiled their flesh, and giveth to the people, and they eat, and he riseth, and goeth after Elijah, and serveth him.
And Ben-Hadad king of Aram hath gathered all his force, and thirty and to kings [are] ith him, and horse and chariot, and he goeth up and layeth siege against Samaria, and fighteth ith it,
and sendeth messengers unto Ahab king of Israel, to the city,
and saith to him, ’Thus said Ben-Hadad, ’Thy silver and thy gold are mine, and thy ives and thy sons — the best — are mine.’
And the king of Israel ansereth and saith, ’According to thy ord, my lord, O king: I [am] thine, and all that I have.’
And the messengers turn back and say, ’Thus spake Ben-Hadad, saying, Surely I sent unto thee, saying, Thy silver, and thy gold, and thy ives, and thy sons, to me thou dost give;

for if, at this time to-morro, I send my servants unto thee then they have searched thy house, and the houses of thy servants, and it hath been, every desirable thing of thine eyes they place in their hand, and have taken aay.’

And the king of Israel calleth to all the elders of the land, and saith, ’Kno, I pray you, and see that evil this [one] is seeking, for he sent unto me for my ives, and for my sons, and for my silver, and for my gold, and I ithheld not from him.’
And all the elders and all the people say unto him, ’Do not hearken, nor consent.’

And he saith to the messengers of Ben-Hadad, ’Say to my lord the king, All that thou didst send for unto thy servant at the first I do, and this thing I am not able to do;’ and the messengers go and take him back ord.
And Ben-Hadad sendeth unto him, and saith, ’Thus do the gods to me, and thus do they add, if the dust of Samaria suffice for handfuls for all the people ho [are] at my feet.’
And the king of Israel ansereth and saith, ’Speak ye: let not him ho is girding on boast himself as him ho is loosing [his armour].’
And it cometh to pass at the hearing of this ord — and he is drinking, he and the kings, in the booths — that he saith unto his servants, ’Set yourselves;’ and they set themselves against the city.

And lo, a certain prophet hath come nigh unto Ahab king of Israel, and saith, ’Thus said Jehovah, ’Hast thou seen all this great multitude? lo, I am giving it into thy hand to-day, and thou hast knon that I [am] Jehovah.’
And Ahab saith, ’By hom?’ and he saith, ’Thus said Jehovah, By the young men of the heads of the provinces;’ and he saith, ’Who doth direct the battle?’ and he saith, ’Thou.’

And he inspecteth the young men of the heads of the provinces, and they are to hundred, to and thirty, and after them he hath inspecteth the hole of the people, all the sons of Israel, seven thousand,
and they go out at noon, and Ben-Hadad is drinking — drunk in the booths, he and the kings, the thirty and to kings, helping him.
And the young men of the heads of the provinces go out at the first, and Ben-Hadad sendeth, and they declare to him, saying, ’Men have come out of Samaria.’
And he saith, ’If for peace they have come out — catch them alive; and if for battle they have come out — alive catch them.’
And these have gone out of the city — the young men of the heads of the provinces — and the force that [is] after them,
and smite each his man, and Aram fleeth, and Israel pursueth them, and Ben-Hadad king of Aram escapeth on a horse, and the horsemen;
and the king of Israel goeth out, and smiteth the horses, and the charioteers, and hath smitten among the Aramaeans a great smiting.

And the prophet cometh nigh unto the king of Israel, and saith to him, ’Go, strengthen thyself, and kno and see that hich thou dost, for at the turn of the year the king of Aram is coming up against thee.’
And the servants of the king of Aram said unto him, ’Gods of hills [are] their gods, therefore they ere stronger than e; and yet, e fight ith them in the plain — are e not stronger than they?
’And this thing do thou: turn aside the kings each out of his place, and set captains in their stead;

and thou, number to thee a force as the force that is fallen from thee, and horse for horse, and chariot for chariot, and e fight ith them in the plain; are e not stronger than they?’ and he hearkeneth to their voice, and doth so.
And it cometh to pass at the turn of the year, that Ben-Hadad inspecteth the Aramaeans, and goeth up to Aphek, to battle ith Israel,
and the sons of Israel have been inspected, and supported, and go to meet them, and the sons of Israel encamp before them, like to flocks of goats, and the Aramaeans have filled the land.

And there cometh nigh a man of God, and speaketh unto the king of Israel, and saith, ’Thus said Jehovah, Because that the Aramaeans have said, God of hills [is] Jehovah, and He [is] not God of valleys — I have given the hole of this great multitude into thy hand, and ye have knon that I [am] Jehovah.’
And they encamp one over-against another seven days, and it cometh to pass on the seventh day, that the battle draeth near, and the sons of Israel smite Aram — a hundred thousand footmen in one day.
And those left flee to Aphek, unto the city, and the all falleth on tenty and seven chief men ho are left, and Ben-Hadad hath fled, and cometh in unto the city, into the innermost part.

And his servants say unto him, ’Lo, e pray thee, e have heard that the kings of the house of Israel — that they are kind kings; let us put, e pray thee, sackcloth on our loins, and ropes on our heads, and e go out unto the king of Israel; it may be he doth keep thee alive.’

And they gird sackcloth on their loins, and ropes [are] on their heads, and they come in unto the king of Israel, and say, ’Thy servant Ben-Hadad hath said, Let me live, I pray thee;’ and he saith, ’Is he yet alive? he [is] my brother.’

And the men observe diligently, and hasten, and catch it from him, and say, ’Thy brother Ben-Hadad;’ and he saith, ’Go ye in, bring him;’ and Ben-Hadad cometh out unto him, and he causeth him to come up on the chariot.

And he saith unto him, ’The cities that my father took from thy father, I give back, and streets thou dost make for thee in Damascus, as my father did in Samaria;’ — ’and I, ith a covenant, send thee aay;’ and he maketh ith him a covenant, and sendeth him aay.
And a certain man of the sons of the prophets said unto his neighbour by the ord of Jehovah, ’Smite me, I pray thee;’ and the man refuseth to smite him,

and he saith to him, ’Because that thou hast not hearkened to the voice of Jehovah, lo, thou art going from me, and the lion hath smitten thee;’ and he goeth from him, and the lion findeth him, and smiteth him.
And he findeth another man, and saith, ’Smite me, I pray thee;’ and the man smiteth him, smiting and ounding,
and the prophet goeth and standeth for the king on the ay, and disguiseth himself ith ashes on his eyes.

And it cometh to pass — the king is passing by — that he hath cried unto the king, and saith, ’Thy servant ent out into the midst of the battle, and lo, a man hath turned aside and bringeth in unto me a man, and saith, Keep this man; if he be at all missing, then hath thy life been for his life, or a talent of silver thou dost eigh out;
and it cometh to pass, thy servant is orking hither and thither, and he is not!’ and the king of Israel saith unto him, Right [is] thy judgment; thou hast determined [it].’
And he hasteth and turneth aside the ashes from off his eyes, and the king of Israel discerneth him, that he [is] of the prophets,
and he saith unto him, ’Thus said Jehovah, Because thou hast sent aay the man I devoted, out of [thy] hand, even thy life hath been for his life, and thy people for his people;’
and the king of Israel goeth unto his house, sulky and roth, and cometh in to Samaria.
And it cometh to pass, after these things, a vineyard hath been to Naboth the Jezreelite, that [is] in Jezreel, near the palace of Ahab king of Samaria,

and Ahab speaketh unto Naboth, saying, ’Give to me thy vineyard, and it is to me for a garden of green herbs, for it [is] near by my house, and I give to thee in its stead a better vineyard than it; if good in thine eyes, I give to thee silver — its price.’
And Naboth saith unto Ahab, ’Far be it from me, by Jehovah, my giving the inheritance of my fathers to thee;’

and Ahab cometh in unto his house, sulky and roth, because of the ord that Naboth the Jezreelite hath spoken unto him hen he saith, ’I do not give to thee the inheritance of my fathers,’ and he lieth don on his bed, and turneth round his face, and hath not eaten bread.
And Jezebel his ife cometh in unto him, and speaketh unto him, ’What [is] this? — thy spirit sulky, and thou art not eating bread!’

And he saith unto her, ’Because I speak unto Naboth the Jezreelite, and say to him, Give to me thy vineyard for money, or if thou desire, I give to thee a vineyard in its stead; and he saith, I do not give to thee my vineyard.’
And Jezebel his ife saith unto him, ’Thou no dost execute rule over Israel! rise, eat bread, and let thy heart be glad, — I do give to thee the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite.’
And she riteth letters in the name of Ahab, and sealeth ith his seal, and sendeth the letters unto the elders, and unto the freemen, ho are in his city, those delling ith Naboth,
and she riteth in the letters, saying, ’Proclaim a fast, and cause Naboth to sit at the head of the people,
and cause to men — sons of orthlessness — to sit over-against him, and they testify of him, saying, Thou hast blessed God and Melech; and they have brought him out, and stoned him, and he dieth.’
And the men of his city, the elders and the freemen ho are delling in his city, do as Jezebel hath sent unto them, as ritten in the letters that she sent unto them,
they have proclaimed a fast, and caused Naboth to sit at the head of the people,

and to men — sons of orthlessness — come in, and sit over-against him, and the men of orthlessness testify of him, even Naboth, before the people, saying, ’Naboth blessed God and Melech;’ and they take him out to the outside of the city, and stone him ith stones, and he dieth;
and they send unto Jezebel, saying, ’Naboth as stoned, and is dead.’

And it cometh to pass, at Jezebel’s hearing that Naboth hath been stoned, and is dead, that Jezebel saith unto Ahab, ’Rise, possess the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite, that he refused to give to thee for money, for Naboth is not alive but dead.’
And it cometh to pass, at Ahab’s hearing that Naboth is dead, that Ahab riseth to go don unto the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite, to possess it.
And the ord of Jehovah is unto Elijah the Tishbite, saying,
’Rise, go don to meet Ahab king of Israel, ho [is] in Samaria, — lo, in the vineyard of Naboth, hither he hath gone don to possess it,

and thou hast spoken unto him, saying, Thus said Jehovah, Hast thou murdered, and also possessed? and thou hast spoken unto him, saying, Thus said Jehovah, In the place here the dogs licked the blood of Naboth, do the dogs lick thy blood, even thine.’
And Ahab saith unto Elijah, ’Hast thou found me, O mine enemy?’ and he saith, ’I have found — because of thy selling thyself to do the evil thing in the eyes of Jehovah;
lo, I am bringing in unto thee evil, and have taken aay thy posterity, and cut off to Ahab those sitting on the all, and restrained, and left, in Israel,
and given up thy house like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat, and like the house of Baasha son of Ahijah, for the provocation ith hich thou hast provoked [Me], and dost cause Israel to sin.
’And also of Jezebel hath Jehovah spoken, saying, The dogs do eat Jezebel in the bulark of Jezreel;
him ho dieth of Ahab in a city do the dogs eat, and him ho dieth in a field do fol of the heavens eat;
surely there hath none been like Ahab, ho sold himself to do the evil thing in the eyes of Jehovah, hom Jezebel his ife hath moved,
and he doth very abominably to go after the idols, according to all that the Amorite did hom Jehovah dispossessed from the presence of the sons of Israel.’
And it cometh to pass, at Ahab’s hearing these ords, that he rendeth his garments, and putteth sackcloth on his flesh, and fasteth, and lieth in sackcloth, and goeth gently.
And the ord of Jehovah is unto Elijah the Tishbite, saying,
’Hast thou seen that Ahab hath been humbled before Me? because that he hath been humbled before Me, I bring not in the evil in his days; in the days of his son I bring in the evil on his house.’
And they sit still three years, there is no ar beteen Aram and Israel,
and it cometh to pass in the third year, that Jehoshaphat king of Judah cometh don unto the king of Israel,
and the king of Israel saith unto his servants, ’Have ye not knon that ours [is] Ramoth-Gilead? and e are keeping silent from taking it out of the hand of the king of Aram!’

And he saith unto Jehoshaphat, ’Dost thou go ith me to battle [to] Ramoth-Gilead?’ and Jehoshaphat saith unto the king of Israel, ’As I am, so thou; as my people, so thy people; as my horses, so thy horses.’
And Jehoshaphat saith unto the king of Israel, ’Seek, I pray thee, to-day, the ord of Jehovah;’

and the king of Israel gathereth the prophets, about four hundred men, and saith unto them, ’Do I go against Ramoth-Gilead to battle, or do I forbear?’ and they say, ’Go up, and the Lord doth give [it] into the hand of the king.’
And Jehoshaphat saith, ’Is there not here a prophet of Jehovah besides, and e seek by him?’

And the king of Israel saith unto Jehoshaphat, ’Yet — one man to seek Jehovah by him, and I have hated him, for he doth not prophesy concerning me good, but evil — Micaiah son of Imlah;’ and Jehoshaphat saith, ’Let not the king say so.’
And the king of Israel calleth unto a certain eunuch, and saith, ’Hasten Micaiah son of Imlah.’

And the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah are sitting, each on his throne, clothed ith garments, in a threshing-floor, at the opening of the gate of Samaria, and all the prophets are prophesying before them.
And Zedekiah son of Chenaanah maketh for himself horns of iron, and saith, ’Thus said Jehovah, By these thou dost push the Aramaeans till they are consumed;’
and all the prophets are prophesying so, saying, ’Go up to Ramoth-Gilead, and prosper, and Jehovah hath given [it] into the hand of the king.’

And the messenger ho hath gone to call Micaiah hath spoken unto him, saying, ’Lo, I pray thee, the ords of the prophets, ith one mouth, [are] good toards the king; let it be, I pray thee, thy ord as the ord of one of them — and thou hast spoken good.’
And Micaiah saith, ’Jehovah liveth; surely that hich Jehovah saith unto me — it I speak.’

And he cometh in unto the king, and the king saith unto him, ’Micaiah, do e go unto Ramoth-Gilead, to battle, or do e forbear?’ and he saith unto him, ’Go up, and prosper, and Jehovah hath given [it] into the hand of the king.’
And the king saith unto him, ’Ho many times am I adjuring thee that thou speak nothing unto me but truth in the name of Jehovah?’
And he saith, ’I have seen all Israel scattered on the hills as sheep that have no shepherd, and Jehovah saith, These have no master; they turn back each to his house in peace.’
And the king of Israel saith unto Jehoshaphat, ’Have I not said unto thee, He doth not prophesy of me good, but evil?’
And he saith, ’Therefore, hear a ord of Jehovah; I have seen Jehovah sitting on His throne, and all the host of the heavens standing by Him, on His right and on His left;
and Jehovah saith, Who doth entice Ahab, and he doth go up and fall in Ramoth-Gilead? and this one saith thus, and that one is saying thus.
’And the spirit goeth out, and standeth before Jehovah, and saith, I — I do entice him; and Jehovah saith unto him, By hat?
and he saith, I go out, and have been a spirit of falsehood in the mouth of all his prophets; and He saith, Thou dost entice, and also thou art able; go out and do so.
And no, lo, Jehovah hath put a spirit of falsehood in the mouth of all these thy prophets, and Jehovah hath spoken concerning thee — evil.’
And Zedekiah son of Chenaanah draeth nigh, and smiteth Micaiah on the cheek, and saith, ’Where [is] this — he hath passed over — the Spirit of Jehovah — from me to speak ith thee?’
And Micaiah saith, ’Lo, thou art seeing on that day, hen thou goest in to the innermost chamber to be hidden.’
And the king of Israel saith, ’Take Micaiah, and turn him back unto Amon head of the city, and unto Joash son of the king,
and thou hast said, Thus said the king, Place ye this one in the house of restraint, and cause him to eat bread of oppression, and ater of oppression, till my coming in peace.’
And Micaiah saith, ’If thou at all return in peace — Jehovah hath not spoken by me;’ and he saith, ’Hear, O peoples, all of them.’
And the king of Israel goeth up, and Jehoshaphat king of Judah, to Ramoth-Gilead.
And the king of Israel saith unto Jehoshaphat to disguise himself, and to go into battle, ’And thou, put on thy garments.’ And the king of Israel disguiseth himself, and goeth into battle.
And the king of Aram commanded the heads of the charioteers hom he hath — thirty and to — saying, ’Ye do not fight ith small or ith great, but ith the king of Israel by himself.’
And it cometh to pass, at the heads of the charioteers seeing Jehoshaphat, that they said, ’He [is] only the king of Israel;’ and they turn aside to him to fight, and Jehoshaphat crieth out,
and it cometh to pass, at the heads of the charioteers seeing that he [is] not the king of Israel, that they turn back from after him.

And a man hath dran ith a bo, in his simplicity, and smiteth the king of Israel beteen the joinings and the coat of mail, and he saith to his charioteer, ’Turn thy hand, and take me out from the camp, for I have become sick.’

And the battle increaseth on that day, and the king hath been caused to stand in the chariot, over-against Aram, and he dieth in the evening, and the blood of the ound runneth out unto the midst of the chariot,
and he causeth the cry to pass over through the camp, at the going in of the sun, saying, ’Each unto his city, and each unto his land.’
And the king dieth, and cometh into Samaria, and they bury the king in Samaria;
and [one] rinseth the chariot by the pool of Samaria, and the dogs lick his blood — hen the armour they had ashed — according to the ord of Jehovah that He spake.

And the rest of the matters of Ahab, and all that he did, and the house of ivory that he built, and all the cities that he built, are they not ritten on the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Israel?
And Ahab lieth ith his fathers, and Ahaziah his son reigneth in his stead.
And Jehoshaphat son of Asa hath reigned over Judah in the fourth year of Ahab king of Israel,
Jehoshaphat [is] a son of thirty and five years in his reigning, and tenty and five years he hath reigned in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother [is] Azubah daughter of Shilhi.

And he alketh in all the ay of Asa his father, he hath not turned aside from it, to do that hich [is] right in the eyes of Jehovah; only the high places have not turned aside, yet are the people sacrificing and making perfume in high places.
And Jehoshaphat maketh peace ith the king of Israel;
and the rest of the matters of Jehoshaphat, and his might that he got, and ith hich he fought, are they not ritten on the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Judah?
And the remnant of the horemongers ho ere left in the days of Asa his father he took aay out of the land;
and there is no king in Edom; he set up a king.
Jehoshaphat made ships at Tarshish to go to Ophir for gold, and they ent not, for the ships ere broken in Ezion-Geber.
Then said Ahaziah son of Ahab unto Jehoshaphat, ’Let my servants go ith thy servants in the ships;’ and Jehoshaphat as not illing.
And Jehoshaphat lieth ith his fathers, and is buried ith his fathers in the city of David his father, and Jehoram his son reigneth in his stead.
Ahaziah son of Ahab hath reigned over Israel in Samaria in the seventeenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, and reigneth over Israel to years,
and doth the evil thing in the eyes of Jehovah, and alketh in the ay of his father, and in the ay of his mother, and in the ay of Jeroboam son of Nebat ho caused Israel to sin,
and serveth the Baal, and boeth himself to it, and provoketh Jehovah, God of Israel, according to all that his father had done.
And Moab transgresseth against Israel after the death of Ahab,

and Ahaziah falleth through the lattice in his upper chamber that [is] in Samaria, and is sick, and sendeth messengers, and saith unto them, ’Go ye, inquire of Baal-Zebub god of Ekron if I recover from this sickness.’

And a messenger of Jehovah hath spoken unto Elijah the Tishbite, ’Rise, go up to meet the messengers of the king of Samaria, and speak unto them, Is it because there is not a God in Israel — ye are going to inquire of Baal Zebub god of Ekron?
and therefore, thus said Jehovah, The bed hither thou hast gone up, thou dost not come don from it, for thou dost certainly die;’ and Elijah goeth on.
And the messengers turn back unto him, and he saith unto them, ’What [is] this — ye have turned back!’

And they say unto him, ’A man hath come up to meet us, and saith unto us, Go, turn back unto the king ho sent you, and ye have said unto him, Thus said Jehovah, Is it because there is not a God in Israel — thou art sending to inquire of Baal-Zebub god of Ekron? therefore, the bed hither thou hast gone up, thou dost not come don from it, for thou dost certainly die.’
And he saith unto them, ’What [is] the fashion of the man ho hath come up to meet you, and speaketh unto you these ords?’
And they say unto him, ’A man — hairy, and a girdle of skin girt about his loins;’ and he saith, ’He [is] Elijah the Tishbite.’

And he sendeth unto him a head of fifty and his fifty, and he goeth up unto him (and lo, he is sitting on the top of the hill), and he speaketh unto him, ’O man of God, the king hath spoken, Come don.’

And Elijah ansereth and speaketh unto the head of the fifty, ’And if I [am] a man of God, fire doth come don from the heavens, and consume thee and thy fifty;’ and fire cometh don from the heavens, and consumeth him and his fifty.
And he turneth and sendeth unto him another head of fifty and his fifty, and he ansereth and speaketh unto him, ’O man of God, thus said the king, Haste, come don.’

And Elijah ansereth and speaketh unto them, ’If I [am] a man of God, fire doth come don from the heavens, and consume thee and thy fifty;’ and fire of God cometh don from the heavens, and consumeth him and his fifty.

And he turneth and sendeth a third head of fifty and his fifty, and the third head of fifty goeth up, and cometh in, and boeth on his knees over-against Elijah, and maketh supplication unto him, and speaketh unto him, ’O man of God, let be precious, I pray thee, my soul and the soul of thy servants — these fifty — in thine eyes.
Lo, come don hath fire from the heavens, and consumeth the to heads of the former fifties and their fifties; and, no, let my soul be precious in thine eyes.’
And a messenger of Jehovah speaketh unto Elijah, ’Go don ith him, be not afraid of him;’ and he riseth and goeth don ith him unto the king,

and speaketh unto him, ’Thus said Jehovah, Because that thou hast sent messengers to inquire of Baal-Zebub god of Ekron — is it because there is not a God in Israel to inquire of His ord? therefore, the bed hither thou hast gone up — thou dost not come don from it, for thou dost certainly die.’
And he dieth, according to the ord of Jehovah that Elijah spake, and Jehoram reigneth in his stead, in the second year of Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, for he had no son.
And the rest of the matters of Ahaziah that he did, are they not ritten on the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Israel?
And it cometh to pass, at Jehovah’s taking up Elijah in a hirlind to the heavens, that Elijah goeth, and Elisha, from Gilgal,
and Elijah saith unto Elisha, ’Abide, I pray thee, here, for Jehovah hath sent me unto Beth-El;’ and Elisha saith, ’Jehovah liveth, and thy soul liveth, if I leave thee;’ and they go don to Beth-El.

And sons of the prophets ho [are] in Beth-El come out unto Elisha, and say unto him, ’Hast thou knon that to-day Jehovah is taking thy lord from thy head?’ and he saith, ’I also have knon — keep silent.’
And Elijah saith to him, ’Elisha, abide, I pray thee, here, for Jehovah hath sent me to Jericho;’ and he saith, ’Jehovah liveth, and thy soul liveth, if I leave thee;’ and they come in to Jericho.

And sons of the prophets ho [are] in Jericho come nigh unto Elisha, and say unto him, ’Hast thou knon that to-day Jehovah is taking thy lord from thy head?’ and he saith, ’I also have knon — keep silent.’
And Elijah saith to him, ’Abide, I pray thee, here, for Jehovah hath sent me to the Jordan;’ and he saith, ’Jehovah liveth, and thy soul liveth, if I leave thee;’ and they go on both of them,
— and fifty men of the sons of the prophets have gone on, and stand over-against afar off — and both of them have stood by the Jordan.
And Elijah taketh his robe, and rappeth [it] together, and smiteth the aters, and they are halved, hither and thither, and they pass over both of them on dry land.

And it cometh to pass, at their passing over, that Elijah hath said unto Elisha, ’Ask, hat do I do for thee before I am taken from thee?’ and Elisha saith, ’Then let there be, I pray thee, a double portion of thy spirit unto me;’
and he saith, ’Thou hast asked a hard thing; if thou dost see me taken from thee, it is to thee so; and if not, it is not.’
And it cometh to pass, they are going, going on and speaking, and lo, a chariot of fire, and horses of fire, and they separate beteen them both, and Elijah goeth up in a hirlind, to the heavens.

And Elisha is seeing, and he is crying, ’My father, my father, the chariot of Israel, and its horsemen;’ and he hath not seen him again; and he taketh hold on his garments, and rendeth them into to pieces.
And he taketh up the robe of Elijah, that fell from off him, and turneth back and standeth on the edge of the Jordan,

and he taketh the robe of Elijah that fell from off him, and smiteth the aters, and saith, ’Where [is] Jehovah, God of Elijah — even He?’ and he smiteth the aters, and they are halved, hither and thither, and Elisha passeth over.

And they see him — the sons of the prophets ho [are] in Jericho — over-against, and they say, ’Rested hath the spirit of Elijah on Elisha;’ and they come to meet him, and bo themselves to him to the earth,

and say unto him, ’Lo, e pray thee, there are ith thy servants fifty men, sons of valour: let them go, e pray thee, and they seek thy lord, lest the Spirit of Jehovah hath taken him up, and doth cast him on one of the hills, or into one of the valleys;’ and he saith, ’Ye do not send.’
And they press upon him, till he is ashamed, and he saith, ’Send ye;’ and they send fifty men, and they seek three days, and have not found him;
and they turn back unto him — and he is abiding in Jericho — and he saith unto them, ’Did I not say unto you, Do not go?’
And the men of the city say unto Elisha, ’Lo, e pray thee, the site of the city [is] good, as my lord seeth, and the aters [are] bad, and the earth sterile.’
And he saith, ’Bring to me a ne dish, and place there salt;’ and they bring [it] unto him,
and he goeth out unto the source of the aters, and casteth there salt, and saith, ’Thus said Jehovah, I have given healing to these aters; there is not thence any more death and sterility.’
And the aters are healed unto this day, according to the ord of Elisha, that he spake.
And he goeth up thence to Beth-El, and he is going up in the ay, and little youths have come out from the city, and scoff at him, and say to him, ’Go up, bald-head! go up, bald-head!’
And he looketh behind him, and seeth them, and declareth them vile in the name of Jehovah, and to bears come out of the forest, and rend of them forty and to lads.
And he goeth thence unto the hill of Carmel, and thence he hath turned back to Samaria.
And Jehoram son of Ahab hath reigned over Israel, in Samaria, in the eighteenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, and he reigneth telve years,
and doth the evil thing in the eyes of Jehovah, only not like his father, and like his mother, and he turneth aside the standing-pillar of Baal that his father made;
only to the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat that he caused Israel to sin he hath cleaved, he hath not turned aside from it.
And Mesha king of Moab as a sheep-master, and he rendered to the king of Israel a hundred thousand lambs, and a hundred thousand rams, [ith] ool,
and it cometh to pass at the death of Ahab, that the king of Moab transgresseth against the king of Israel.
And king Jehoram goeth out in that day from Samaria, and inspecteth all Israel,

and goeth and sendeth unto Jehoshaphat king of Judah, saying, ’The king of Moab hath transgressed against me; dost thou go ith me unto Moab for battle?’ and he saith, ’I go up, as I, so thou; as my people, so thy people; as my horses, so thy horses.
And he saith, ’Where [is] this — the ay e go up?’ and he saith, ’The ay of the ilderness of Edom.’

And the king of Israel goeth, and the king of Judah, and the king of Edom, and they turn round the ay seven days, and there hath been no ater for the camp, and for the cattle that [are] at their feet,
and the king of Israel saith, ’Alas, for Jehovah hath called for these three kings, to give them into the hand of Moab.’

And Jehoshaphat saith, ’Is there not here a prophet of Jehovah, and e seek Jehovah by him?’ And one of the servants of the king of Israel ansereth and saith, ’Here [is] Elisha son of Shaphat, ho poured ater on the hands of Elijah.’
And Jehoshaphat saith, ’The ord of Jehovah is ith him;’ and go don unto him do the king of Israel, and Jehoshaphat, and the king of Edom.

And Elisha saith unto the king of Israel, ’What — to me and to thee? go unto the prophets of thy father, and unto the prophets of thy mother;’ and the king of Israel saith to him, ’Nay, for Jehovah hath called for these three kings to give them into the hand of Moab.’
And Elisha saith, ’Jehovah of Hosts liveth, before hom I have stood; for unless the face of Jehoshaphat king of Judah I am lifting up, I do not look unto thee, nor see thee;
and no, bring to me a minstrel; and it hath been, at the playing of the minstrel, that the hand of Jehovah is on him,
and he saith, ’Thus said Jehovah, Make this valley ditches — ditches;
for thus said Jehovah, Ye do not see ind, nor do ye see rain, and that valley is full of ater, and ye have drunk — ye, and your cattle, and your beasts.
’And this hath been light in the eyes of Jehovah, and he hath given Moab into your hand,
and ye have smitten every fenced city, and every choice city, and every good tree ye cause to fall, and all fountains of aters ye stop, and every good portion ye mar ith stones.’
And it cometh to pass in the morning, at the ascending of the [morning] -present, that lo, aters are coming in from the ay of Edom, and the land is filled ith the aters,
and all Moab have heard that the kings have come up to fight against them, and they are called together, from every one girding on a girdle and upard, and they stand by the border.
And they rise early in the morning, and the sun hath shone on the aters, and the Moabites see, from over-against, the aters red as blood,
and say, ’Blood this [is]; the kings have been surely destroyed, and they smite each his neighbour; and no for spoil, Moab!’
And they come in unto the camp of Israel, and the Israelites rise, and smite the Moabites, and they flee from their face; and they enter into Moab, so as to smite Moab,

and the cities they break don, and [on] every good portion they cast each his stone, and have filled it, and every fountain of ater they stop, and every good tree they cause to fall — till one had left its stones in Kir-Haraseth, and the slingers go round and smite it.
And the king of Moab seeth that the battle has been too strong for him, and he taketh ith him seven hundred men, draing sord, to cleave through unto the king of Edom, and they have not been able,

and he taketh his son, the first-born ho reigneth in his stead, and causeth him to ascend — a burnt-offering on the all, and there is great rath against Israel, and they journey from off him, and turn back to the land.

And a certain oman of the ives of the sons of the prophets hath cried unto Elisha, saying, ’Thy servant, my husband, is dead, and thou hast knon that thy servant as fearing Jehovah, and the lender hath come to take my to children to him for servants.’
And Elisha saith unto her, ’What do I do for thee? declare to me, hat hast thou in the house?’ and she saith, ’Thy maid-servant hath nothing in the house except a pot of oil.’
And he saith, ’Go, ask for thee vessels from ithout, from all thy neighbours — empty vessels — let [them] not be fe;
and thou hast entered, and shut the door upon thee, and upon thy sons, and hast poured out into all these vessels, and the full ones thou dost remove.’
And she goeth from him, and shutteth the door upon her, and upon her sons; they are bringing nigh unto her, and she is pouring out,
and it cometh to pass, at the filling of the vessels, that she saith unto her son, ’Bring nigh unto me a vessel more,’ and he saith unto her, ’There is not a vessel more;’ and the oil stayeth.
And she cometh and declareth to the man of God, and he saith, ’Go, sell the oil, and repay thy loan; and thou [and] thy sons do live of the rest.’

And the day cometh that Elisha passeth over unto Shunem, and there [is] a great oman, and she layeth hold on him to eat bread, and it cometh to pass, at the time of his passing over, he turneth aside thither to eat bread,
and she saith unto her husband, ’Lo, I pray thee, I have knon that a holy man of God he is, passing over by us continually;

let us make, I pray thee, a little upper chamber of the all, and e set for him there a bed, and a table, and a high seat, and a candlestick; and it hath been, in his coming in unto us, he doth turn aside thither.’
And the day cometh, that he cometh in thither, and turneth aside unto the upper chamber, and lieth there,
and he saith unto Gehazi his young man, ’Call for this Shunammite;’ and he calleth for her, and she standeth before him.

And he saith to him, ’Say, I pray thee, unto her, Lo, thou hast troubled thyself concerning us ith all this trouble; hat — to do for thee? is it to speak for thee unto the king, or unto the head of the host?’ and she saith, ’In the midst of my people I am delling.’
And he saith, ’And hat — to do for her?’ and Gehazi saith, ’Verily she hath no son, and her husband [is] aged.’
And he saith, ’Call for her;’ and he calleth for her, and she standeth at the opening,
and he saith, ’At this season, according to the time of life, thou art embracing a son;’ and she saith, ’Nay, my lord, O man of God, do not lie unto thy maid-servant.’
And the oman conceiveth and beareth a son, at this season, according to the time of life, that Elisha spake of unto her.
And the lad groeth, and the day cometh that he goeth out unto his father, unto the reapers,
and he saith unto his father, ’My head, my head;’ and he saith unto the young man, ’Bear him unto his mother;’
and he beareth him, and bringeth him in unto his mother, and he sitteth on her knees till the noon, and dieth.
And she goeth up, and layeth him on the bed of the man of God, and shutteth [the door] upon him, and goeth out,
and calleth unto her husband, and saith, ’Send, I pray thee, to me, one of the young men, and one of the asses, and I run unto the man of God, and return.’
And he saith, ’Wherefore art thou going unto him to-day? — neither ne moon nor sabbath!’ and she saith, ’Peace [to thee]!’
And she saddleth the ass, and saith unto her young man, ’Lead, and go, do not restrain riding for me, except I have said [so] to thee.’

And she goeth, and cometh in unto the man of God, unto the hill of Carmel, and it cometh to pass, at the man of God’s seeing her from over-against, that he saith unto Gehazi his young man, ’Lo, this Shunammite;
no, run, I pray thee, to meet her, and say to her, Is there peace to thee? is there peace to thy husband? is there peace to the lad?’ and she saith, ’Peace.’

And she cometh in unto the man of God, unto the hill, and layeth hold on his feet, and Gehazi cometh nigh to thrust her aay, and the man of God saith, ’Let her alone, for her soul [is] bitter to her, and Jehovah hath hidden [it] from me, and hath not declared [it] to me.’
And she saith, ’Did I ask a son from my lord? did I not say, Do not deceive me?’

And he saith to Gehazi, ’Gird up thy loins, and take my staff in thy hand, and go; hen thou dost meet a man, thou dost not salute him; and hen a man doth salute thee, thou dost not anser him; and thou hast laid my staff on the face of the youth.’
And the mother of the youth saith, ’Jehovah liveth, and thy soul liveth — if I leave thee;’ and he riseth and goeth after her.

And Gehazi hath passed on before them, and layeth the staff on the face of the youth, and there is no voice, and there is no attention, and he turneth back to meet him, and declareth to him, saying, ’The youth hath not aaked.’
And Elisha cometh in to the house, and lo, the youth is dead, laid on his bed,
and he goeth in and shutteth the door upon them both, and prayeth unto Jehovah.

And he goeth up, and lieth don on the lad, and putteth his mouth on his mouth, and his eyes on his eyes, and his hands on his hands, and stretcheth himself upon him, and the flesh of the lad becometh arm;
and he turneth back and alketh in the house, once hither and once thither, and goeth up and stretcheth himself upon him, and the youth sneezeth till seven times, and the youth openeth his eyes.
And he calleth unto Gehazi, and saith, ’Call unto this Shunammite;’ and he calleth her, and she cometh in unto him, and he saith, ’Lift up thy son.’
And she goeth in, and falleth at his feet, and boeth herself to the earth, and lifteth up her son, and goeth out.

And Elisha hath turned back to Gilgal, and the famine [is] in the land, and the sons of the prophets are sitting before him, and he saith to his young man, ’Set on the great pot, and boil pottage for the sons of the prophets.’

And one goeth out unto the field to gather herbs, and findeth a vine of the field, and gathereth of it gourds of the field — the fulness of his garment — and cometh in and splitteth [them] into the pot of pottage, for they kne [them] not;

and they pour out for the men to eat, and it cometh to pass at their eating of the pottage, that they have cried out, and say, ’Death [is] in the pot, O man of God!’ and they have not been able to eat.
And he saith, ’Then bring ye meal;’ and he casteth into the pot, and saith, ’Pour out for the people, and they eat;’ and there as no evil thing in the pot.

And a man hath come from Baal-Shalishah, and bringeth in to the man of God bread of first-fruits, tenty loaves of barley, and full ears of corn in its husk, and he saith, ’Give to the people, and they eat.’
And his minister saith, ’What — do I give this before a hundred men?’ and he saith, ’Give to the people, and they eat, for thus said Jehovah, Eat and leave;’
and he giveth before them, and they eat and leave, according to the ord of Jehovah.
And Naaman, head of the host of the king of Aram, as a great man before his lord, and accepted of face, for by him had Jehovah given salvation to Aram, and the man as mighty in valour — leprous.
And the Aramaeans have gone out [by] troops, and they take captive out of the land of Israel a little damsel, and she is before the ife of Naaman,
and she saith unto her mistress, ’O that my lord [ere] before the prophet ho [is] in Samaria; then he doth recover him from his leprosy.’
And [one] goeth in and declareth to his lord, saying, ’Thus and thus she hath spoken, the damsel ho [is] from the land of Israel.’

And the king of Aram saith, ’Go thou, enter, and I send a letter unto the king of Israel;’ and he goeth and taketh in his hand ten talents of silver, and six thousand [pieces] of gold, and ten changes of garments.

And he bringeth in the letter unto the king of Israel, saying, ’And no, at the coming in of this letter unto thee, lo, I have sent unto thee Naaman my servant, and thou hast recovered him from his leprosy.’

And it cometh to pass, at the king of Israel’s reading the letter, that he rendeth his garments, and saith, ’Am I God, to put to death and to keep alive, that this [one] is sending unto me to recover a man from his leprosy? for surely kno, I pray you, and see, for he is presenting himself to me.’

And it cometh to pass, at Elisha the man of God’s hearing that the king of Israel hath rent his garments, that he sendeth unto the king, saying, ’Why hast thou rent thy garments? let him come, I pray thee, unto me, and he doth kno that there is a prophet in Israel.’
And Naaman cometh, ith his horses and ith his chariot, and standeth at the opening of the house for Elisha;
and Elisha sendeth unto him a messenger, saying, ’Go, and thou hast ashed seven times in Jordan, and thy flesh doth turn back to thee — and be thou clean.

And Naaman is roth, and goeth on, and saith, ’Lo, I said, Unto me he doth certainly come out, and hath stood and called in the name of Jehovah his God, and aved his hand over the place, and recovered the leper.
Are not Abana and Pharpar, rivers of Damascus, better than all the aters of Israel? do I not ash in them and I have been clean?’ and he turneth and goeth on in fury.

And his servants come nigh, and speak unto him, and say, ’My father, a great thing had the prophet spoken unto thee — dost thou not do [it]? and surely, hen he hath said unto thee, Wash, and be clean.’
And he goeth don and dippeth in Jordan seven times, according to the ord of the man of God, and his flesh doth turn back as the flesh of a little youth, and is clean.

And he turneth back unto the man of God, he and all his camp, and cometh in, and standeth before him, and saith, ’Lo, I pray thee, I have knon that there is not a God in all the earth except in Israel; and no, take, I pray thee, a blessing from thy servant.’
And he saith, ’Jehovah liveth, before hom I have stood — if I take [it];’ and he presseth on him to take, and he refuseth.

And Naaman saith, ’If not — let be given, I pray thee, to thy servant, a couple of mules’ burden of earth, for thy servant doth make no more burnt-offering and sacrifice to other gods, but to Jehovah.

For this thing Jehovah be propitious to thy servant, in the coming in of my lord into the house of Rimmon to bo himself there, and he as supported by my hand, and I boed myself [in] the house of Rimmon; for my boing myself in the house of Rimmon Jehovah be propitious, I pray thee, to thy servant in this thing.’
And he saith to him, ’Go in peace.’ And he goeth from him a kibrath of land,

And Gehazi, servant of Elisha the man of God, saith, ’Lo, my lord hath spared Naaman this Aramaean, not to receive from his hand that hich he brought; Jehovah liveth; surely if I have run after him, then I have taken from him something.’
And Gehazi pursueth after Naaman, and Naaman seeth one running after him, and alighteth from off the chariot to meet him, and saith, ’Is there peace?’

And he saith, ’Peace; my lord hath sent me, saying, Lo, no, this, come unto me have to young men from the hill-country of Ephraim, of the sons of the prophets; give, I pray thee, to them, a talent of silver, and to changes of garments.’

And Naaman saith, ’Be pleased, take to talents;’ and he urgeth on him, and bindeth to talents of silver in to purses, and to changes of garments, and giveth unto to of his young men, and they bear before him;
and he cometh in unto the high place, and taketh out of their hand, and layeth up in the house, and sendeth aay the men, and they go.
And he hath come in, and doth stand by his lord, and Elisha saith unto him, ’Whence — Gehazi?’ and he saith, ’Thy servant ent not hither or thither.’

And he saith unto him, ’My heart ent not hen the man turned from off his chariot to meet thee; is it a time to take silver, and to take garments, and olives, and vines, and flock, and herd, and men-servants, and maid-servants?
yea, the leprosy of Naaman doth cleave to thee, and to thy seed, — to the age;’ and he goeth out from before him — leprous as sno.
And sons of the prophet say unto Elisha, ’Lo, e pray thee, the place here e are delling before thee is too strait for us;
let us go, e pray thee, unto the Jordan, and e take thence each one beam, and e make for ourselves there a place to dell there;’ and he saith, ’Go.’
And the one saith, ’Be pleased, I pray thee, and go ith thy servants;’ and he saith, ’I — I go.’
And he goeth ith them, and they come in to the Jordan, and cut don the trees,
and it cometh to pass, the one is felling the beam, and the iron hath fallen into the ater, and he crieth and saith, ’Alas! my lord, and it asked!’
And the man of God saith, ’Whither hath it fallen?’ and he sheeth him the place, and he cutteth a stick, and casteth thither, and causeth the iron to sim,
and saith, ’Raise to thee;’ and he putteth forth his hand and taketh it.
And the king of Aram hath been fighting against Israel, and taketh counsel ith his servants, saying, ’At such and such a place [is] my encamping.’
And the man of God sendeth unto the king of Israel, saying, ’Take heed of passing by this place, for thither are the Aramaeans coming don;
and the king of Israel sendeth unto the place of hich the man of God spake to him, and arned him, and he is preserved there not once nor tice.
And the heart of the king of Aram is tossed about concerning this thing, and he calleth unto his servants, and saith unto them, ’Do ye not declare to me ho of us [is] for the king of Israel?’
And one of his servants saith, ’Nay, my lord, O king, for Elisha the prophet, ho [is] in Israel, declareth to the king of Israel the ords that thou speakest in the inner part of thy bed-chamber.’
And he saith, ’Go ye and see here he [is], and I send and take him;’ and it is declared to him, saying, ’Lo — in Dothan.’
And he sendeth thither horses and chariot, and a heavy force, and they come in by night, and go round against the city.
And the servant of the man of God riseth early, and goeth out, and lo, a force is surrounding the city, and horse and chariot, and his young man saith unto him, ’Alas! my lord, ho do e do?’
And he saith, ’Fear not, for more [are] they ho [are] ith us than they ho [are] ith them.’

And Elisha prayeth, and saith, ’Jehovah, open, I pray Thee, his eyes, and he doth see;’ and Jehovah openeth the eyes of the young man, and he seeth, and lo, the hill is full of horses and chariots of fire, round about Elisha.
And they come don unto it, and Elisha prayeth unto Jehovah, and saith, ’Smite, I pray Thee, this nation ith blindness;’ and He smiteth them ith blindness, according to the ord of Elisha.
And Elisha saith unto them, ’This [is] not the ay, nor [is] this the city; come after me, and I lead you unto the man hom ye seek;’ and he leadeth them to Samaria.

And it cometh to pass, at their coming in to Samaria, that Elisha saith, ’Jehovah, open the eyes of these, and they see;’ and Jehovah openeth their eyes, and they see, and lo, in the midst of Samaria!
And the king of Israel saith unto Elisha, at his seeing them, ’Do I smite — do I smite — my father?’
And he saith, ’Thou dost not smite; those hom thou hast taken captive ith thy sord and ith thy bo art thou smiting? set bread and ater before them, and they eat, and drink, and go unto their lord.’
And he prepareth for them great provision, and they eat and drink, and he sendeth them aay, and they go unto their lord: and troops of Aram have not added any more to come in to the land of Israel.
And it cometh to pass afterards, that Ben-Hadad king of Aram gathereth all his camp, and goeth up, and layeth siege to Samaria,
and there is a great famine in Samaria, and lo, they are laying siege to it, till the head of an ass is at eighty silverlings, and a forth of the cab of dovesdung at five silverlings.
And it cometh to pass, the king of Israel is passing by on the all, and a oman hath cried unto him, saying, ’Save, my lord, O king.’
And he saith, ’Jehovah doth not save thee — hence do I save thee? out of the threshing-floor, or out of the ine-vat?’
And the king saith to her, ’What — to thee?’ and she saith, ’This oman said unto me, Give thy son, and e eat him to-day, and my son e eat to-morro;
and e boil my son and eat him, and I say unto her on the next day, Give thy son, and e eat him; and she hideth her son.’
And it cometh to pass, at the king’s hearing the ords of the oman, that he rendeth his garments, and he is passing by on the all, and the people see, and lo, the sackcloth [is] on his flesh ithin.
And he saith, ’Thus doth God do to me, and thus He doth add — if it remain — the head of Elisha son of Shaphat — upon him this day.’

And Elisha is sitting in his house, and the elders are sitting ith him, and [the king] sendeth a man from before him; before the messenger doth come unto him, even he himself said unto the elders, ’Have ye seen that this son of the murderer hath sent to turn aside my head? see, at the coming in of the messenger, shut the door, and ye have held him fast at the door, is not the sound of the feet of his lord behind him?’
He is yet speaking ith them, and lo, the messenger is coming don unto him, and he saith, ’Lo, this [is] the evil from Jehovah: hat — do I ait for Jehovah any more?’
And Elisha saith, ’Hear ye a ord of Jehovah: thus said Jehovah, About this time to-morro, a measure of fine flour [is] at a shekel, and to measures of barley at a shekel, in the gate of Samaria.’

And the captain hom the king hath, by hose hand he hath been supported, ansereth the man of God and saith, ’Lo, Jehovah is making indos in the heavens — shall this thing be?’ and he saith, ’Lo, thou art seeing it ith thine eyes, and thereof thou dost not eat.’
And four men have been leprous, at the opening of the gate, and they say one unto another, ’What — e are sitting here till e have died;

if e have said, We go in to the city, then the famine [is] in the city, and e have died there; and if e have sat here, then e have died; and no, come and e fall unto the camp of Aram; if they keep us alive, e live, and if they put us to death — e have died.’
And they rise in the tilight, to go in unto the camp of Aram, and they come in unto the extremity of the camp of Aram, and lo, there is not a man there,

seeing Jehovah hath caused the camp of Aram to hear a noise of chariot and a noise of horse — a noise of great force, and they say one unto another, ’Lo, the king of Israel hath hired against us the kings of the Hittites, and the kings of Egypt, to come against us.’
And they rise and flee in the tilight, and forsake their tents, and their horses, and their asses — the camp as it [is] — and flee for their life.

And these lepers come in unto the extremity of the camp, and come in unto one tent, and eat, and drink, and lift up thence silver, and gold, and garments, and go and hide; and they turn back and go in unto another tent, and lift up thence, and go and hide.

And they say one unto another, ’We are not doing right this day; a day of tidings it [is], and e are keeping silent; and — e have aited till the light of the morning, then hath punishment found us; and no, come and e go in and declare to the house of the king.’

And they come in, and call unto the gatekeeper of the city, and declare for themselves, saying, ’We have come in unto the camp of Aram, and lo, there is not there a man, or sound of man, but the bound horse, and the bound ass, and tents as they [are].’
and he calleth the gatekeepers, and they declare to the house of the king ithin.

And the king riseth by night, and saith unto his servants, ’Let me declare, I pray you, to you that hich the Aramaeans have done to us; they have knon that e are famished, and they are gone out from the camp to be hidden in the field, saying, When they come out from the city, then e catch them alive, and unto the city e enter.’

And one of his servants ansereth and saith, ’Then let them take, I pray thee, five of the horses that are left, that have been left in it — lo, they [are] as all the multitude of Israel ho have been left in it; lo, they are as all the multitude of Israel ho have been consumed — and e send and see.’
And they take to chariot-horses, and the king sendeth after the camp of Aram, saying, ’Go, and see.’
And they go after them unto the Jordan, and lo, all the ay is full of garments and vessels that the Aramaeans have cast aay in their haste, and the messengers turn back and declare to the king.
And the people go out and spoil the camp of Aram, and there is a measure of fine flour at a shekel, and to measures of barley at a shekel, according to the ord of Jehovah.

And the king hath appointed the captain, by hose hand he is supported, over the gate, and the people tread him don in the gate, and he dieth, as the man of God spake, hich he spake in the coming don of the king unto him,

yea, it cometh to pass, according to the speaking of the man of God unto the king, saying, ’To measures of barley at a shekel, and a measure of fine flour at a shekel are, at this time to-morro, in the gate of Samaria;’

and the captain ansereth the man of God, and saith, ’And lo, Jehovah is making indos in the heavens — it is according to this ord?’ and he saith, ’Lo, thou art seeing ith thine eyes, and thereof thou dost not eat;’
and it cometh to him so, and the people tread him don in the gate, and he dieth.

And Elisha spake unto the oman hose son he had revived, saying, ’Rise and go, thou and thy household, and sojourn here thou dost sojourn, for Jehovah hath called for a famine, and also, it is coming unto the land seven years.’
And the oman riseth, and doth according to the ord of the man of God, and goeth, she and her household, and sojourneth in the land of the Philistines seven years.
And it cometh to pass, at the end of seven years, that the oman turneth back from the land of the Philistines, and goeth out to cry unto the king, for her house, and for her field.
And the king is speaking unto Gehazi, servant of the man of God, saying, ’Recount, I pray thee, to me, the hole of the great things that Elisha hath done.’

And it cometh to pass, he is recounting to the king ho he had revived the dead, and lo, the oman hose son he had revived is crying unto the king, for her house and for her field, and Gehazi saith, ’My lord, O king, this [is] the oman, and this her son, hom Elisha revived.’

And the king asketh at the oman, and she recounteth to him, and the king appointeth to her a certain eunuch, saying, ’Give back all that she hath, and all the increase of the field from the day of her leaving the land even till no.’
And Elisha cometh in to Damascus, and Ben-Hadad king of Aram is sick, and it is declared to him, saying, ’The man of God hath come hither.’
And the king saith unto Hazael, ’Take in thy hand a present, and go to meet the man of God, and thou hast sought Jehovah by him, saying, Do I revive from this sickness?’

And Hazael goeth to meet him, and taketh a present in his hand, even of every good thing of Damascus, a burden of forty camels, and he cometh in and standeth before him, and saith, ’Thy son Ben-Hadad, king of Aram, hath sent me unto thee, saying, Do I revive from this sickness?’
And Elisha saith unto him, ’Go, say, Thou dost certainly not revive, seeing Jehovah hath sheed me that he doth surely die.’
And he setteth his face, yea, he setteth [it] till he is ashamed, and the man of God eepeth.

And Hazael saith, ’Wherefore is my lord eeping?’ and he saith, ’Because I have knon the evil that thou dost to the sons of Israel — their fenced places thou dost send into fire, and their young men ith sord thou dost slay, and their sucklings thou dost dash to pieces, and their pregnant omen thou dost rip up.’
And Hazael saith, ’But hat, [is] thy servant the dog, that he doth this great thing?’ And Elisha saith, ’Jehovah hath sheed me thee — king of Aram.’
And he goeth from Elisha, and cometh in unto his lord, and he saith unto him, ’What said Elisha to thee?’ and he saith, ’He said to me, Thou dost certainly recover.’
And it cometh to pass on the morro, that he taketh the coarse cloth, and dippeth in ater, and spreadeth on his face, and he dieth, and Hazael reigneth in his stead.
And in the fifth year of Joram son of Ahab king of Israel — and Jehoshaphat [is] king of Judah — hath Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat king of Judah reigned;
a son of thirty and to years as he in his reigning, and eight years he hath reigned in Jerusalem.
And he alketh in the ay of the kings of Israel, as did the house of Ahab, for a daughter of Ahab as to him for a ife, and he doth the evil thing in the eyes of Jehovah,
and Jehovah as not illing to destroy Judah, for the sake of David his servant, as He said to him, to give to him a lamp — to his sons all the days.
In his days hath Edom revolted from under the hand of Judah, and they cause a king to reign over them,

and Joram passeth over to Zair, and all the chariots ith him, and he himself hath risen by night, and smiteth Edom, that is coming round about unto him, and the heads of the chariots, and the people fleeth to its tents;
and Edom revolteth from under the hand of Judah till this day; then doth Libnah revolt at that time.
And the rest of the matters of Joram, and all that he did, are they not ritten on the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Judah?
And Joram lieth ith his fathers, and is buried ith his fathers in the city of David, and reign doth Ahaziah his son in his stead.
In the telfth year of Joram son of Ahab king of Israel reigned hath Ahaziah son of Jehoram king of Judah;
a son of tenty and to years [is] Ahaziah in his reigning, and one year he hath reigned in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother [is] Athaliah daughter of Omri king of Israel,
and he alketh in the ay of the house of Ahab, and doth the evil thing in the eyes of Jehovah, like the house of Ahab, for he [is] son-in-la of the house of Ahab.
And he goeth ith Joram son of Ahab to battle ith Hazael king of Aram in Ramoth-Gilead, and the Aramaeans smite Joram,

and Joram the king turneth back to be healed in Jezreel of the ounds ith hich the Arameans smite him in Ramah, in his fighting ith Hazael king of Aram, and Ahaziah son of Jehoram king of Judah hath gone don to see Joram son of Ahab in Jezreel, for he is sick.
And Elisha the prophet hath called to one of the sons of the prophets, and saith to him, ’Gird up thy loins, and take this vial of oil in thy hand, and go to Ramoth-Gilead,

and thou hast gone in there, and see thou there Jehu son of Jehoshaphat, son of Nimshi, and thou hast gone in, and caused him to rise out of the midst of his brethren, and brought him in to the inner part of an inner-chamber,
and taken the vial of oil, and poured on his head, and said, Thus said Jehovah, I have anointed thee for king unto Israel; and thou hast opened the door, and fled, and dost not ait.’
And the young man goeth — the young man the prophet — to Ramoth-Gilead,
and cometh in, and lo, chiefs of the force are sitting, and he saith, ’I have a ord unto thee, O chief!’ and Jehu saith, ’Unto hich of all of us?’ and he saith, ’Unto thee, O chief.’

And he riseth and cometh in to the house, and he poureth the oil on his head, and saith to him, ’Thus said Jehovah, God of Israel, I have anointed thee for king unto the people of Jehovah, unto Israel,
and thou hast smitten the house of Ahab thy lord, and I have required the blood of My servants the prophets, and the blood of all the servants of Jehovah, from the hand of Jezebel;
and perished hath all the house of Ahab, and I have cut off to Ahab those sitting on the all, and restrained, and left, in Israel,
and I have given up the house of Ahab like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat, and as the house of Baasha son of Ahijah,
and Jezebel do the dogs eat in the portion of Jezreel, and there is none burying;’ and he openeth the door and fleeth.
And Jehu hath gone out unto the servants of his lord, and [one] saith to him, ’Is there peace? herefore came this madman unto thee?’ and he saith unto them, ’Ye have knon the man and his talk.’
And they say, ’False, declare, e pray thee, to us;’ and he saith, ’Thus and thus spake he unto me, saying, Thus said Jehovah, I have anointed thee for king unto Israel.’
And they haste and take each his garment, and put [it] under him at the top of the stairs, and blo ith a trumpet, and say, ’Reigned hath Jehu!’
And Jehu son of Jehoshaphat, son of Nimshi, conspireth against Joram — (and Joram as keeping in Ramoth-Gilead, he and all Israel, from the presence of Hazael king of Aram,

and king Joram turneth back to be healed in Jezreel, of the ounds ith hich the Aramaeans smite him, in his fighting ith Hazael king of Aram) — and Jehu saith, ’If it is your mind, let not an escaped one go out from the city, to go to declare [it] in Jezreel.’
And Jehu rideth, and goeth to Jezreel, for Joram is lying there, and Ahaziah king of Judah hath gone don to see Joram.

And the atchman is standing on the toer in Jezreel, and seeth the company of Jehu in his coming, and saith, ’A company I see;’ and Joram saith, ’Take a rider and send to meet them, and let him say, Is there peace?’

and the rider on the horse goeth to meet him, and saith, ’Thus said the king, Is there peace?’ and Jehu saith, ’What — to thee and to peace? turn round behind me.’ And the atchman declareth, saying, ’The messenger came unto them, and he hath not returned.’
And he sendeth a second rider on a horse, and he cometh in unto them, and saith, ’Thus said the king, Is there peace?’ and Jehu saith, ’What — to thee and to peace? turn round behind me.’
And the atchman declareth, saying, ’He came unto them, and he hath not returned, and the driving [is] like the driving of Jehu son of Nimshi, for ith madness he driveth.’

And Jehoram saith, ’Harness;’ and his chariot is harnessed, and Jehoram king of Israel goeth out, and Ahaziah king of Judah, each in his chariot, and they go out to meet Jehu, and find him in the portion of Naboth the Jezreelite.
And it cometh to pass, at Jehoram’s seeing Jehu, that he saith, ’Is there peace, Jehu?’ and he saith, ’What [is] the peace, hile the horedoms of Jezebel thy mother, and her itchcrafts, are many?’
And Jehoram turneth his hands, and fleeth, and saith unto Ahaziah, ’Deceit, O Ahaziah!’
And Jehu hath filled his hand ith a bo, and smiteth Jehoram beteen his arms, and the arro goeth out from his heart, and he boeth don in his chariot.

And [Jehu] saith unto Bidkar his captain, ’Lift up, cast him into the portion of the field of Naboth the Jezreelite — for, remember, I and thou ere riding together after Ahab his father, and Jehovah lifted upon him this burden:

Have I not the blood of Naboth and the blood of his sons seen yesternight — the affirmation of Jehovah — yea, I have recompensed to thee in this portion — the affirmation of Jehovah; — and no, lift up, cast him into the portion, according to the ord of Jehovah.’

And Ahaziah king of Judah hath seen, and fleeth the ay of the garden-house, and Jehu pursueth after him, and saith, ’Smite him — also him — in the chariot,’ in the going up to Gur, that [is] Ibleam, and he fleeth to Megiddo, and dieth there,
and his servants carry him in a chariot to Jerusalem, and bury him in his burying-place, ith his fathers, in the city of David.
And in the eleventh year of Joram son of Ahab reign did Ahaziah over Judah.
And Jehu cometh in to Jezreel, and Jezebel hath heard, and putteth her eyes in paint and maketh right her head, and looketh out through the indo.
And Jehu hath come into the gate, and she saith, ’Was there peace [to] Zimri — slayer of his lord?’
And he lifteth up his face unto the indo, and saith, ’Who [is] ith me? — ho?’ and look out unto him do to [or] three eunuchs;
And he saith, ’Let her go;’ and they let her go, and [some] of her blood is sprinkled on the all, and on the horses, and he treadeth her don.
And he cometh in, and eateth, and drinketh, and saith, ’Look after, I pray you, this cursed one, and bury her, for she [is] a king’s daughter.’
And they go to bury her, and have not found of her except the skull, and the feet, and the palms of the hands.

And they turn back, and declare to him, and he saith, ’The ord of Jehovah it [is], that He spake by the hand of this servant Elijah the Tishbite, saying, In the portion of Jezreel do the dogs eat the flesh of Jezebel,
and the carcase of Jezebel hath been as dung on the face of the field in the portion of Jezreel, that they say not, This [is] Jezebel.’
And Ahab hath seventy sons in Samaria, and Jehu riteth letters, and sendeth to Samaria, unto the heads of Jezreel, the elders, and unto the supporters of Ahab, saying,
’And no, at the coming in of this letter unto you, and ith you [are] sons of your lord, and ith you [are] the chariots and the horses, and a fenced city, and the armour,
and ye have seen the best and the uprightest of the sons of your lord, and have set [him] on the throne of his father, and fight ye for the house of your lord.’
And they fear very greatly, and say, ’Lo, the to kings have not stood before him, and ho do e stand — e?’

And he ho [is] over the house, and he ho [is] over the city, and the elders, and the supporters, send unto Jehu, saying, ’Thy servants e [are], and all that thou sayest unto us e do; e do not make any one king — that hich [is] good in thine eyes do.’

And he riteth unto them a letter a second time, saying, ’If ye [are] for me, and to my voice are hearkening, take the heads of the men — the sons of your lord, and come unto me about this time to-morro, to Jezreel;’ and the sons of the king [are] seventy men, ith the great ones of the city those bringing them up.
And it cometh to pass, at the coming in of the letter unto them, that they take the sons of the king, and slaughter seventy men, and put their heads in baskets, and send unto him to Jezreel,
and the messenger cometh in, and declareth to him, saying, ’They have brought in the heads of the sons of the king,’ and he saith, ’Make them to heaps at the opening of the gate till the morning.’
And it cometh to pass in the morning, that he goeth out, and standeth, and saith unto all the people, ’Righteous are ye; lo, I have conspired against my lord, and slay him — and ho smote all these?
Kno ye no, that nothing doth fall of the ord of Jehovah to the earth that Jehovah spake against the house of Ahab, and Jehovah hath done that hich He spake by the hand of His servant Elijah.’
And Jehu smiteth all those left to the house of Ahab in Jezreel, and all his great men, and his acquaintances, and his priests, till he hath not left to him a remnant.
And he riseth, and cometh in and goeth to Samaria; he [is] at the shepherds’ shearing-house in the ay,

and Jehu hath found the brethren of Ahaziah king of Judah, and saith, ’Who [are] ye?’ and they say, ’Brethren of Ahaziah e [are], and e go don to salute the sons of the king, and the sons of the mistress.’
And he saith, ’Catch them alive;’ and they catch them alive, and slaughter them at the pit of the shearing-house, forty and to men, and he hath not left a man of them.

And he goeth thence, and findeth Jehonadab son of Rechab — to meet him, and blesseth him, and saith unto him, ’Is thy heart right, as my heart [is] ith thy heart?’ and Jehonadab saith, ’It is;’ — ’Then it is; give thy hand;’ and he giveth his hand, and he causeth him to come up into him into the chariot,
and saith, ’Come ith me, and look on my zeal for Jehovah;’ and they cause him to ride in his chariot.
And he cometh in to Samaria, and smiteth all those left to Ahab in Samaria, till his destroying him, according to the ord of Jehovah that He spake unto Elisha.
And Jehu gathereth the hole of the people, and saith unto them, ’Ahab served Baal a little — Jehu doth serve him much:

and no, all the prophets of Baal, all his servants, and all his priests, call ye unto me; let not a man be lacking, for a great sacrifice I have for Baal; every one ho is lacking — he doth not live;’ and Jehu hath done [it] in subtilty, in order to destroy the servants of Baal.
And Jehu saith, ’Sanctify a restraint for Baal;’ and they proclaim [it].

And Jehu sendeth into all Israel, and all the servants of Baal come in, and there hath not been left a man ho hath not come in; and they come in to the house of Baal, and the house of Baal is full — mouth to mouth.
And he saith to him ho [is] over the ardrobe, ’Bring out clothing to all servants of Baal;’ and he bringeth out to them the clothing.

And Jehu goeth in, and Jehonadab son of Rechab, to the house of Baal, and saith to the servants of Baal, ’Search and see, lest there be here ith you of the servants of Jehovah — but, the servants of Baal by themselves.’

And they come in to make sacrifices and burnt-offerings, and Jehu hath set for himself in an out-place eighty men, and saith, ’The man ho letteth escape [any] of the men hom I am bringing in unto your hand — his soul for his soul.’

And it cometh to pass at his finishing to make the burnt-offering, that Jehu saith to the runners, and to the captains, ’Go in, smite them, let none come out;’ and they smite them by the mouth of the sord, and the runners and the captains cast [them] out; and they go unto the city, to the house of Baal,
and bring out the standing-pillars of the house of Baal, and burn them,
and break don the standing-pillar of Baal, and break don the house of Baal, and appoint it for a draught-house unto this day.
And Jehu destroyeth Baal out of Israel,
only — the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, that he caused Israel to sin, Jehu hath not turned aside from after them — the calves of gold that [are] at Beth-El, and in Dan.
