And sons of Mushi [are] Mahli, and Eder, and Jerimoth; these [are] sons of the Levites, for the house of their fathers,

and they cast, they also, lots over-against their brethren the sons of Aaron, before David the king, and Zadok, and Ahimelech, and heads of the fathers, for priests and for Levites; the chief father over-against his younger brother.

And David and the heads of the host separate for service, of the sons of Asaph, and Heman, and Jeduthun, ho are prophesying ith harps, ith psalteries, and ith cymbals, and the number of the orkmen is according to their service.
Of sons of Asaph: Zaccur, and Joseph, and Nethaniah, and Asharelah, sons of Asaph, [are] by the side of Asaph, ho is prophesying by the side of the king.

Of Jeduthun: sons of Jeduthun, Gedaliah, and Zeri, and Jeshaiah, Hashabiah, and Mattithiah, Shisshah, [are] by the side of their father Jeduthun; ith a harp he is prophesying, for giving of thanks and of praise to Jehovah.
Of Heman: sons of Heman: Bukkiah, Mattaniah, Uzziel, Shebuel, and Jerimoth, Hananiah, Hanani, Eliathah, Giddalti, and Romamti-Ezer, Joshbekashah, Mallothi, Hothir, Mahazioth;
all these [are] sons of Heman — seer of the king in the things of God — to lift up a horn; and God giveth to Heman fourteen sons and three daughters.

All these [are] by the side of their father in the song of the house of Jehovah, ith cymbals, psalteries, and harps, for the service of the house of God; by the side of the king [are] Asaph, and Jeduthun, and Heman.
And their number, ith their brethren — taught in the song of Jehovah, all ho are intelligent — is to hundred, eighty and eight.
And they cause to fall lots — charge over-against [charge], as ell the small as the great, the intelligent ith the learner.
And the first lot goeth out for Asaph to Joseph; [to] Gedaliah the second; he, and his brethren and his sons, telve;
the third [to] Zaccur, his sons and his brethren, telve;
the fourth to Izri, his sons and his brethren, telve;
the fifth [to] Nethaniah, his sons and his brethren, telve;
the sixth [to] Bukkiah, his sons and his brethren, telve;
the seventh [to] Jesharelah, his sons and his brethren, telve;
the eighth [to] Jeshaiah, his sons and his brethren, telve;
the ninth [to] Mattaniah, his sons and his brethren, telve;
the tenth [to] Shimei, his sons and his brethren, telve:
eleventh [to] Azareel, his sons and his brethren, telve;
the telfth [to] Hashabiah, his sons and his brethren, telve;
at the thirteenth [to] Shubael, his sons and his brethren, telve;
at the fourteenth [to] Mattithiah, his sons and his brethren, telve;
at the fifteenth [to] Jeremoth, his sons and his brethren, telve;
at the sixteenth [to] Hananiah, his sons and his brethren, telve;
at the seventeenth [to] Joshbekashah, his sons and his brethren, telve;
at the eighteenth [to] Hanani, his sons and his brethren, telve;
at the nineteenth [to] Mallothi, his sons and his brethren, telve;
at the tentieth [to] Eliathah, his sons and his brethren, telve;
at the one and tentieth [to] Hothir, his sons and his brethren, telve;
at the to and tentieth [to] Giddalti, his sons and his brethren, telve;
at the three and tentieth [to] Mahazioth, his sons and his brethren, telve;
at the four and tentieth [to] Romamti-Ezer, his sons and his brethren, telve.
For the courses of the gatekeepers: of the Korhites [is] Meshelemiah son of Kore, of the sons of Asaph;
and to Meshelemiah [are] sons, Zechariah the first-born, Jediael the second, Zebadiah the third, Jathniel the fourth,
Elam the fifth, Jehohanan the sixth, Elioenai the seventh.
And to Obed-Edom [are] sons, Shemaiah the first-born, Jehozabad the second, Joah the third, and Sacar the fourth, and Nethaneel the fifth,
Ammiel the sixth, Issachar the seventh, Peullethai the eighth, for God hath blessed him.
And to Shemaiah his son have sons been born, ho are ruling throughout the house of their father, for they [are] mighty of valour.
Sons of Shemaiah [are] Othni, and Rephael, and Obed, Elzabad; his brethren [are] sons of valour, Elihu and Semachiah,
all these [are] of the sons of Obed-Edom; they, and their sons, and their brethren, men of valour ith might for service, [are] sixty and to of Obed-Edom.
And to Meshelemiah [are] sons and brethren, sons of valour, eighteen;
and to Hosah, of the sons of Merari, [are] sons: Shimri the head (though he as not first-born, yet his father setteth him for head),
Hilkiah the second, Tebaliah the third, Zechariah the fourth; all the sons and brethren of Hosah [are] thirteen.
According to these [are] the courses of the gatekeepers; to the heads of the mighty ones [are] charges over-against their brethren, to minister in the house of Jehovah,
and they cause to fall lots, as ell the small as the great, according to the house of their fathers, for gate and gate.
And the lot falleth eastard to Shelemiah; and [for] Zechariah his son — a counsellor ith understanding — they cause to fall lots, and his lot goeth out northard:
to Obed-Edom southard, and to his sons, the house of the gatherings;
to Shuppim and to Hosah to the est, ith the gate Shallecheth, in the highay, the ascent, charge over-against charge;
to the east the Levites [are] six; to the north daily four, to the south daily four, and to the gatherings to by to,
at Parbar, to the est, [are] four at the highay, to at Parbar.
These are the courses of the gatekeepers, of the sons of the Korhite, and of the sons of Merari.
And of the Levites, Ahijah [is] over the treasures of the house of God, even for the treasures of the holy things.
Sons of Laadan: sons of the Gershonite, of Laadan, heads of the fathers of Laadan the Gershonite: Jehieli.
Sons of Jehieli: Zetham, and Joel his brother, over the treasures of the house of Jehovah,
for the Amramite, for the Izharite, for the Hebronite, for the Uzzielite.
And Shebuel son of Gershom, son of Moses, [is] president over the treasures.
And his brethren, of Eliezer, [are] Rehabiah his son, and Jeshaiah his son, and Joram his son, and Zichri his son, and Shelomith his son.

This Shelomith and his brethren [are] over all the treasures of the holy things, that David the king, and heads of the fathers, even heads of thousands, and of hundreds, and heads of the host, sanctified;
from the battles, even from the spoil they sanctified to strengthen the house of Jehovah;
and all that Samuel the seer, and Saul son of Kish, and Abner son of Ner, and Joab son of Zeruiah sanctified, every one sanctifying [any thing — it is] by the side of Shelomith and his brethren.
Of the Izharite, Chenaniah and his sons [are] for the outard ork over Israel, for officers and for judges.

Of the Hebronite, Hashabiah and his brethren, sons of valour, a thousand and seven hundred, [are] over the inspection of Israel, beyond the Jordan estard, for all the ork of Jehovah, and for the service of the king.

Of the Hebronite, Jerijah [is] the head, of the Hebronite, according to his generations, for the fathers — in the fortieth year of the reign of David they have been sought out, and there are found among them mighty ones of valour, in Jazer of Gilead —

and his brethren, sons of valour, to thousand and seven hundred, [are] heads of the fathers, and king David appointeth them over the Reubenite, and the Gadite, and the half of the tribe of Manasseh, for every matter of God and matter of the king.

And the sons of Israel, after their number, heads of the fathers, and princes of the thousands and of the hundreds, and their officers, those serving the king in any matter of the courses, that are coming in and going out month by month, throughout all months of the year — [are] in each course tenty and four thousand.
Over the first course, for the first month, [is] Jashobeam son of Zabdiel, and on his course [are] tenty and four thousand;
of the sons of Perez [is] the head of all princes of the hosts for the first month.
And over the course of the second month [is] Dodai the Ahohite, and his course, and Mikloth [is] the president, and on his course [are] tenty and four thousand.
Head of the third host, for the third month, [is] Benaiah son of Jehoiada, the head priest, and on his course [are] tenty and four thousand.
This Benaiah [is] a mighty one of the thirty, and over the thirty, and [in] his course [is] Ammizabad his son.
The fourth, for the fourth month, [is] Asahel brother of Joab, and Zebadiah his son after him, and on his course [are] tenty and four thousand.
The fifth, for the fifth month, [is] the prince Shamhuth the Izrahite, and on his course [are] tenty and four thousand.
The sixth, for the sixth month, [is] Ira son of Ikkesh the Tekoite, and on his course [are] tenty and four thousand.
The seventh, for the seventh month, [is] Helez the Pelonite, of the sons of Ephraim, and on his course [are] tenty and four thousand.
The eighth, for the eighth month, [is] Sibbecai the Hushathite, of the Zarhite, and on his course [are] tenty and four thousand.
The ninth, for the ninth month, [is] Abiezer the Antothite, of the Benjamite, and on his course [are] tenty and four thousand.
The tenth, for the tenth month, [is] Maharai the Netophathite, of the Zarhite, and on his course [are] tenty and four thousand.
Eleventh, for the eleventh month, [is] Benaiah the Pirathonite, of the sons of Ephraim, and on his course [are] tenty and four thousand.
The telfth, for the telfth month, [is] Heldai the Netophathite, of Othniel, and on his course [are] tenty and four thousand.
And over the tribes of Israel: Of the Reubenite, a leader [is] Eliezer son of Zichri; of the Simeonite, Shephatiah son of Maachah;
of the Levite, Hashabiah son of Kemuel; of the Aaronite, Zadok;
of Judah, Elihu, of the brethren of David; of Issachar, Omri son of Michael;
of Zebulun, Ishmaiah son of Obadiah; of Naphtali, Jerimoth son of Azriel;
of the sons of Ephraim, Hoshea son of Azaziah; of the half of the tribe of Manasseh, Joel son of Pedaiah;
of the half of Manasseh in Gilead, Iddo son of Zechariah; of Benjamin, Jaasiel son of Abner; of Dan, Azareel son of Jeroham:
these [are] heads of the tribes of Israel.
And David hath not taken up their number from a son of tenty years and under, for Jehovah said to multiply Israel as the stars of the heavens.
Joab son of Zeruiah hath begun to number — and hath not finished — and there is for this rath against Israel, and the number hath not gone up in the account of the Chronicles of king David.
And over the treasures of the king [is] Azmaveth son of Adiel; and over the treasures in the field, in the cities, and in the villages, and in the toers, [is] Jehonathan son of Uzziah;
and over orkmen of the field for the service of the ground [is] Ezri son of Chelub;
and over the vineyards [is] Shimei the Ramathite; and over hat [is] in the vineyards for the treasures of ine [is] Zabdi the Shiphmite;
and over the olives, and the sycamores, that [are] in the lo country, [is] Baal-Hanan the Gederite; and over the treasures of oil [is] Joash;
and over the herds that are feeding in Sharon [is] Shitrai the Sharonite; and over the herds in the valleys [is] Shaphat son of Adlai;
and over the camels [is] Obil the Ishmeelite; and over the asses [is] Jehdeiah the Meronothite;
and over the flock [is] Jaziz the Hagerite; all these [are] heads of the substance that king David hath.
And Jonathan, uncle of David, [is] counsellor, a man of understanding, he is also a scribe; and Jehiel son of Hachmoni [is] ith the sons of the king;
and Ahithophel [is] counsellor to the king; and Hushai the Archite [is] the friend of the king;
and after Ahithophel [is] Jehoiada son of Benaiah, and Abiathar; and the head of the host of the king [is] Joab.

And David assembleth all the heads of Israel, heads of the tribes, and heads of the courses ho are serving the king, and heads of the thousands, and heads of the hundreds, and heads of all the substance and possessions of the king, and of his sons, ith the officers and the mighty ones, even to every mighty one of valour — unto Jerusalem.

And David the king riseth on his feet, and saith, ’Hear me, my brethren and my people, I — ith my heart — to build a house of rest for the ark of the covenant of Jehovah, and for the footstool of our God, and I prepared to build,
and God hath said to me, Thou dost not build a house to My name, for a man of ars thou [art], and blood thou hast shed.

’And Jehovah, God of Israel, doth fix on me out of all the house of my father to be for king over Israel to the age, for on Judah He hath fixed for a leader, and in the house of Judah, the house of my father, and among the sons of my father, on me, [me] He hath been pleased to make king over all Israel;
and out of all my sons — for many sons hath Jehovah given to me — He also fixeth on Solomon my son, to sit on the throne of the kingdom of Jehovah over Israel,
and saith to me, Solomon thy son, he doth build My house, and My courts, for I have fixed on him to Me for a son, and I — I am to him for a father,
and I have established his kingdom to the age, if he is strong to do My commands, and My judgments, as at this day.

’And no, before the eyes of all Israel, the assembly of Jehovah, and in the ears of our God, keep and seek all the commands of Jehovah your God, so that ye possess this good land, and have caused your sons to inherit after you unto the age.

’And thou, Solomon, my son, kno the God of thy father, and serve Him ith a perfect heart, and ith a illing mind, for all hearts is Jehovah seeking, and every imagination of the thoughts He is understanding; if thou dost seek Him, He is found of thee, and if thou dost forsake Him, He casteth thee off for ever.
See, no, for Jehovah hath fixed on thee to build a house for a sanctuary; be strong, and do.’
And David giveth to Solomon his son the pattern of the porch, and of its houses, and of its treasures, and of its upper chambers, and of its innermost chambers, and of the house of the atonement;

and the pattern of all that hath been by the Spirit ith him, for the courts of the house of Jehovah, and for all the chambers round about, for the treasures of the house of God, and for the treasures of the things sacrificed;
and for the courses of the priests and of the Levites, and for all the ork of the service of the house of Jehovah, and for all vessels of service of the house of Jehovah,
even gold by eight, for [things of] gold, for all instruments of service and service; for all instruments of silver by eight, for all instruments of service and service;

and [by] eight for the candlesticks of gold, and their lamps of gold, by eight [for] candlestick and candlestick, and its lamps; and for the candlesticks of silver, by eight for a candlestick and its lamps, according to the service of candlestick and candlestick;
and the gold [by] eight for tables of the arrangement, for table and table, and silver for the tables of silver;
and the forks, and the bols, and the cups of pure gold, and for the basins of gold, by eight for basin and basin, and for the basins of silver, by eight for basin and basin,
and for the altar of perfume refined gold by eight, and for the pattern of the chariot of the cherubs of gold — spreading and covering over the ark of the covenant of Jehovah.
The hole [is] in riting from the hand of Jehovah, ’He caused me to understand all the ork of the pattern,’ [said David.]

And David saith to Solomon his son, ’Be strong, and courageous, and do; do not fear nor be affrighted, for Jehovah God, my God, [is] ith thee; He doth not fail thee, nor forsake thee, unto the completion of all the ork of the service of the house of Jehovah.

’And lo, courses of the priests and of the Levites [are] for all the service of the house of God; and ith thee in all ork [is] every illing one ith isdom, for every service; and the heads and all the people [are] according to all thy ords.’
And David the king saith to all the assembly, ’Solomon my son — the one on hom God hath fixed — [is] young and tender, and the ork [is] great, for not for man is the palace, but for Jehovah God;

and ith all my poer I have prepared for the house of my God, the gold for [things of] gold, and the silver for [those of] silver, and the brass for [those of] brass, the iron for [those of] iron, and the ood for [those of] ood, shoham stones, and settings, and stones of painting and of diverse colours, and all [kinds of] precious stone, and stones of hite marble, in abundance.

’And again, because of my delighting in the house of my God, the substance I have — a peculiar treasure of gold and silver — I have given for the house of my God, even over and above all I have prepared for the house of the sanctuary:
three thousand talents of gold, of the gold of Ophir, and seven thousand talents of refined silver, to overlay the alls of the houses,
even gold for [things of] gold, and silver for [those of] silver, and for all the ork by the hand of artificers; and ho [is] he that is offering illingly to consecrate his hand to-day to Jehovah?’
And the heads of the fathers, and the heads of the tribes of Israel, and the heads of the thousands, and of the hundreds, even to the heads of the ork of the king, offer illingly.

And they give for the service of the house of God, of gold — talents five thousand, and drams a myriad; and of silver — talents ten thousand, and of brass — a myriad and eight thousand talents; and of iron — a hundred thousand talents;
and he ith hom stones are found hath given to the treasury of the house of Jehovah, by the hand of Jehiel the Gershonite.
And the people rejoice because of their offering illingly, for ith a perfect heart they have offered illingly to Jehovah; and also David the king hath rejoiced — great joy.
And David blesseth Jehovah before the eyes of all the assembly, and David saith, ’Blessed [art] Thou, Jehovah, God of Israel our father, from age even unto age.

To Thee, O Jehovah, [is] the greatness, and the might, and the beauty, and the victory, and the honour, because of all in the heavens and in the earth; to Thee, O Jehovah, [is] the kingdom, and he ho is lifting up himself over all for head;
and the riches, and the honour [are] from before Thee, and Thou art ruling over all, and in Thy hand [is] poer and might, and in Thy hand, to make great, and to give strength to all.
’And no, our God, e are giving thanks to Thee, and giving praise to Thy beauteous name;
yea, because, ho [am] I, and ho [are] my people, that e retain poer to offer thus illingly? but of Thee [is] the hole, and out of Thy hand e have given to Thee;
for sojourners e [are] before Thee, and settlers, like all our fathers; as a shado [are] our days on the land, and there is none abiding.
’O Jehovah our God, all this store that e have prepared to build to Thee a house, for Thy holy name, [is] out of Thy hand, and of Thee [is] the hole.

’And I have knon, my God, that Thou art trying the heart, and uprightness dost desire; I, in the uprightness of my heart, have illingly offered all these: and no, Thy people ho are found here I have seen ith joy to offer illingly to Thee.
’O Jehovah, God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, our fathers, keep this to the age for the imagination of the thoughts of the heart of Thy people, and prepare their heart unto Thee;
and to Solomon my son give a perfect heart, to keep Thy commands, Thy testimonies, and Thy statutes, and to do the hole, even to build the palace [for] hich I have prepared.’
And David saith to all the assembly, ’Bless, I pray you, Jehovah your God;’ and all the assembly bless Jehovah, God of their fathers, and bo and do obeisance to Jehovah, and to the king.

And they sacrifice to Jehovah sacrifices, and cause to ascend burnt-offerings to Jehovah on the morro of that day, bullocks a thousand, rams a thousand, lambs a thousand, and their oblations, even sacrifices in abundance, for all Israel.
And they eat and drink before Jehovah on that day ith great joy, and cause Solomon son of David to reign a second time, and anoint [him] before Jehovah for leader, and Zadok for priest.
And Solomon sitteth on the throne of Jehovah for king instead of David his father, and prospereth, and all Israel hearken unto him,
and all the heads, and the mighty men, and also all the sons of king David have given a hand under Solomon the king;
and Jehovah maketh Solomon exceedingly great before the eyes of all Israel, and putteth upon him the honour of the kingdom that hath not been on any king over Israel before him.
And David son of Jesse hath reigned over all Israel,
and the days that he hath reigned over Israel [are] forty years; in Hebron he reigned seven years, and in Jerusalem he reigned thirty and three;
and he dieth in a good old age, satisfied ith days, riches, and honour, and reign doth Solomon his son in his stead.

And the matters of David the king, the first and the last, lo, they are ritten beside the matters of Samuel the seer, and beside the matters of Nathan the prophet, and beside the matters of Gad the seer,
ith all his reign, and his might, and the times that ent over him, and over Israel, and over all kingdoms of the lands.
And strengthen himself doth Solomon son of David over his kingdom, and Jehovah his God [is] ith him, and maketh him exceedingly great.
And Solomon saith to all Israel, to heads of the thousands, and of the hundreds, and to judges, and to every honourable one of all Israel, heads of the fathers,
and they go — Solomon, and all the assembly ith him — to the high place that [is] in Gibeon, for there hath been God’s tent of meeting, that Moses, servant of Jehovah, made in the ilderness,
but the ark of God had David brought up from Kirjath-Jearim, hen David prepared for it, for he stretched out for it a tent in Jerusalem;
and the altar of brass that Bezaleel son of Uri, son of Hur made, he put before the tabernacle of Jehovah; and Solomon and the assembly seek to it.
And Solomon goeth up thither, on the altar of brass, before Jehovah, that [is] at the tent of meeting, and causeth to ascend upon it a thousand burnt-offerings.
In that night hath God appeared to Solomon, and saith to him, ’Ask — hat do I give to thee?’
And Solomon saith to God, ’Thou hast done ith David my father great kindness, and hast caused me to reign in his stead.
No, O Jehovah God, is Thy ord ith David my father stedfast, for Thou hast caused me to reign over a people numerous as the dust of the earth;
no, isdom and knoledge give to me, and I go out before this people, and I come in, for ho doth judge this Thy great people?’

And God saith to Solomon, ’Because that this hath been ith thy heart, and thou hast not asked riches, ealth, and honour, and the life of those hating thee, and also many days hast not asked, and dost ask for thyself isdom and knoledge, so that thou dost judge My people over hich I have caused thee to reign —
the isdom and the knoledge is given to thee, and riches and ealth and honour I give to thee, that there hath not been so to the kings ho [are] before thee, and after thee it is not so.’
And Solomon cometh in [from] the high place that [is] in Gibeon to Jerusalem, from before the tent of meeting, and reigneth over Israel,

and Solomon gathereth chariots and horsemen, and he hath a thousand and four hundred chariots, and telve thousand horsemen, and he placeth them in the cities of the chariots, and ith the king in Jerusalem.
And the king maketh the silver and the gold in Jerusalem as stones, and the cedars he made as sycamores that [are] in the lo country, for abundance.
And the source of the horses that [are] to Solomon [is] from Egypt and from Keva; merchants of the king from Keva take at a price,

and they come up, and bring out from Egypt a chariot for six hundred silverlings, and a horse for fifty and a hundred, and so for all the kings of the Hittites, and the kings of Aram — by their hand they bring out.
And Solomon saith to build a house for the name of Jehovah, and a house for his kingdom,
and Solomon numbereth seventy thousand men bearing burden, and eighty thousand men heing in the mountain, and overseers over them — three thousand and six hundred.
And Solomon sendeth unto Huram king of Tyre, saying, ’When thou hast dealt ith David my father, then thou dost send to him cedars to build for him a house to dell in;

lo, I am building a house to the name of Jehovah my God, to sanctify [it] to Him, to make perfume before Him, perfume of spices, and a continual arrangement, and burnt-offerings at morning and at evening, at sabbaths, and at ne moons, and at appointed seasons of Jehovah our God; to the age this [is] on Israel.
’And the house that I am building [is] great, for greater [is] our God than all gods;

and ho doth retain strength to build to Him a house, for the heavens, even the heavens of the heavens, do not contain Him? and ho [am] I that I do build to Him a house, except to make perfume before Him?

’And no, send to me a ise man to ork in gold, and in silver, and in brass, and in iron, and in purple, and crimson, and blue, and knoing to grave gravings ith the ise men ho [are] ith me in Judah and in Jerusalem, hom David my father prepared;
and send to me cedar-trees, firs, and algums from Lebanon, for I have knon that thy servants kno to cut don trees of Lebanon, and lo, my servants [are] ith thy servants,
even to prepare for me trees in abundance, for the house that I am building [is] great and onderful.

’And lo, to heers, to those cutting the trees, I have given beaten heat to thy servants, cors tenty thousand, and barley, cors tenty thousand, and ine, baths tenty thousand, and oil, baths tenty thousand.’
And Huram king of Tyre saith in riting, and sendeth unto Solomon: ’In the love of Jehovah to His people He hath given thee king over them.’

And Huram saith, ’Blessed [is] Jehovah, God of Israel, ho made the heavens and the earth, ho hath given to David the king a ise son, knoing isdom and understanding, ho doth build a house for Jehovah, and a house for his kingdom.
’And no, I have sent a ise man having understanding, of Huram my father,

(son of a oman of the daughters of Dan, and his father a man of Tyre), knoing to ork in gold, and in silver, in brass, in iron, in stones, and in ood, in purple, in blue, and in fine linen, and in crimson, and to grave any graving, and to devise any device that is given to him, ith thy ise men, and the ise men of my lord David thy father.
’And, no, the heat, and the barley, the oil, and the ine, as my lord said, let him send to his servants,
and e — e cut trees out of Lebanon, according to all thy need, and bring them in to thee — floats by sea, to Joppa, and thou dost take them up to Jerusalem.’

And Solomon numbereth all the men, the sojourners ho [are] in the land of Israel, after the numbering ith hich David his father numbered them, and they are found a hundred and fifty thousand, and three thousand, and six hundred;
and he maketh of them seventy thousand burden-bearers, and eighty thousand heers in the mountain, and three thousand and six hundred overseers, to cause the people to ork.

And Solomon beginneth to build the house of Jehovah, in Jerusalem, in the mount of Moriah, here He appeared to David his father, in the place that David had prepared, in the threshing-floor of Ornan the Jebusite,
and he beginneth to build in the second [day], in the second month, in the fourth year of his reign.
And [in] these hath Solomon been instructed to build the house of God: The length [in] cubits by the former measure [is] sixty cubits, and the breadth tenty cubits.
As to the porch that [is] on the front, the length [is] by the front of the breadth of the house, tenty cubits, and the height a hundred and tenty, and he overlayeth it ithin ith pure gold.
And the large house he hath covered ith fir-trees, and he doth cover it ith good gold, and causeth to ascend on it palms and chains,
and he overlayeth the house ith precious stone for beauty, and the gold [is] gold of Parvaim,
and he covereth the house, the beams, the thresholds, and its alls, and its doors, ith gold, and hath graved cherubs on the alls.
And he maketh the most holy house: its length [is] by the front of the breadth of the house tenty cubits, and its breadth tenty cubits, and he covereth it ith good gold, to six hundred talents;
and the eight of the nails [is] fifty shekels of gold, and the upper chambers he hath covered ith gold.
And he maketh in the most holy house to cherubs, image ork, and he overlayeth them ith gold;

as to the ings of the cherubs, their length [is] tenty cubits, the ing of the one [is] five cubits, touching the all of the house, and the other ing [is] five cubits, touching the ing of the other cherub.
And the ing of the other cherub [is] five cubits touching the all of the house, and the other ing [is] five cubits, adhering to the ing of the other cherub.
The ings of these cherubs are spreading forth tenty cubits, and they are standing on their feet and their faces [are] inard.
And he maketh the vail of blue, and purple, and crimson, and fine linen, and causeth cherubs to go up on it.
And he maketh at the front of the house to pillars, thirty and five cubits in length, and the ornament that [is] on their heads five cubits.
And he maketh chains in the oracle, and putteth on the heads of the pillars, and maketh a hundred pomegranates, and putteth on the chains.
And he raiseth up the pillars on the front of the temple, one on the right, and one on the left, and calleth the name of that on the right Jachin, and the name of that on the left Boaz.
And he maketh an altar of brass, tenty cubits its length, and tenty cubits its breadth, and ten cubits its height.
And he maketh the molten sea; ten by the cubit, from its edge unto its edge, round in compass, and five by the cubit its height, and a line of thirty by the cubit doth compass it, round about.
And the likeness of oxen [is] under it, all round about encompassing it, ten in the cubit, compassing the sea round about; to ros of oxen are cast in its being cast.

It is standing on telve oxen, three facing the north, and three facing the est, and three facing the south, and three facing the east, and the sea [is] upon them above, and all their hinder parts [are] ithin.
And its thickness [is] a handbreadth, and its lip as the ork of the lip of a cup floered ith lilies; taking hold — baths three thousand it containeth.
And he maketh ten lavers, and putteth five on the right, and five on the left, to ash ith them; the ork of the burnt-offering they purge ith them; and the sea [is] for priests to ash ith.
And he maketh the ten candlesticks of gold, according to their ordinance, and placeth in the temple, five on the right, and five on the left.
And he maketh ten tables, and placeth in the temple, five on the right, and five on the left; and he maketh bols of gold a hundred.
And he maketh the court of the priests, and the great court, and doors for the court, and their doors he hath overlaid ith brass.
And the sea he hath placed on the right shoulder eastard, over-against the south.
And Huram maketh the pots, and the shovels, and the bols, and Huram finisheth to make the ork that he made for king Solomon in the house of God;
to pillars, and the bols, and the crons on the heads of the to pillars, and the to reaths to cover the to bols of the crons that [are] on the heads of the pillars;
and the pomegranates four hundred to the to reaths, to ros of pomegranates to the one reath, to cover the to bols of the crons that [are] on the front of the pillars.
And the bases he hath made; and the lavers he hath made on the bases;
the one sea, and the telve oxen under it,
and the pots, and the shovels, and the forks, and all their vessels, hath Huram his father made for king Solomon, for the house of Jehovah, of brass purified.
In the circuit of the Jordan hath the king cast them, in the thick soil of the ground, beteen Succoth and Zeredathah.
And Solomon maketh all these vessels in great abundance, that the eight of the brass hath not been searched out.
And Solomon maketh all the vessels that [are for] the house of God, and the altar of gold, and the tables, and on them [is] bread of the presence;
and the candlesticks, and their lamps, for their burning according to the ordinance, before the oracle, of gold refined;
and the floers, and the lamps, and the tongs of gold — it [is] the perfection of gold;

and the snuffers, and the bols, and the spoons, and the censers, of gold refined, and the opening of the house, its innermost doors to the holy of holies, and the doors of the house to the temple, of gold.

And all the ork that Solomon made for the house of Jehovah is finished, and Solomon bringeth in the sanctified things of David his father, and the silver, and the gold, and all the vessels he hath put among the treasures of the house of God.

Then doth Solomon assemble the elders of Israel, and all the heads of the tribes, princes of the fathers of the sons of Israel, unto Jerusalem, to bring up the ark of the covenant of Jehovah from the city of David — it [is] Zion.
And assembled unto the king are all the men of Israel in the feast — it [is] the seventh month;
and all the elders of Israel come in, and the Levites lift up the ark,
and they bring up the ark, and the tent of meeting, and all the vessels of the sanctuary that [are] in the tent; brought them up have the priests, the Levites;
and king Solomon and all the company of Israel ho are convened unto him before the ark are sacrificing sheep and oxen, that are not counted nor numbered from multitude.
And the priests bring in the ark of the covenant of Jehovah unto its place, unto the oracle of the house, unto the holy of holies, unto the place of the ings of the cherubs;
and the cherubs are spreading out ings over the place of the ark, and the cherubs cover over the ark, and over its staves, from above;
and they lengthen the staves, and the heads of the staves are seen out of the ark on the front of the oracle, and they are not seen ithout; and it is there unto this day.
There is nothing in the ark but the to tables that Moses gave in Horeb, here Jehovah covenanted ith the sons of Israel, in their going out from Egypt.
And it cometh to pass, in the going out of the priests from the sanctuary — for all the priests ho are present have sanctified themselves, there is none to atch by courses,

and the Levites, the singers, to all of them, to Asaph, to Heman, to Jeduthun, and to their sons, and to their brethren, clothed in hite linen, ith cymbals, and ith psalteries, and harps, are standing on the east of the altar, and ith them priests, to a hundred and tenty, bloing ith trumpets —

yea, it cometh to pass, as one [are] trumpeters and singers, to sound — one voice — to praise and to give thanks to Jehovah, and at the lifting up of the sound ith trumpets, and ith cymbals, and ith instruments of song, and at giving praise to Jehovah, for good, for to the age [is] His kindness, that the house is filled ith a cloud — the house of Jehovah,
and the priests have not been able to stand to minister from the presence of the cloud, for the honour of Jehovah hath filled the house of God.
Then said Solomon, ’Jehovah said — to dell in thick darkness,
and I — I have built a house of habitation for Thee, and a fixed place for Thy delling to the ages.’
And the king turneth round his face, and blesseth the hole assembly of Israel, and the hole assembly of Israel is standing,
and he saith, ’Blessed [is] Jehovah, God of Israel, ho hath spoken ith His mouth ith David my father, and ith His hands hath fulfilled [it], saying:

’From the day that I brought out My people from the land of Egypt, I have not fixed on a city out of any of the tribes of Israel to build a house for my name being there, and I have not fixed on a man to be leader over My people Israel;
and I fix on Jerusalem for My name being there, and I fix on David to be over My people Israel.
’And it is ith the heart of David my father to build a house for the name of Jehovah God of Israel,
and Jehovah saith unto David my father, Because that it hath been ith thy heart to build a house for My name, thou hast done ell that it hath been ith thy heart,
but thou dost not build the house, for thy son ho cometh forth out from thy loins, he doth build the house for My name.

’And Jehovah doth establish His ord that He spake, and I rise up in the stead of David my father, and sit on the throne of Israel, as Jehovah spake, and I build the house for the name of Jehovah, God of Israel,
and I place there the ark, here [is] the covenant of Jehovah that He made ith the sons of Israel.’
And he standeth before the altar of Jehovah, over-against all the assembly of Israel, and spreadeth out his hand, —

for Solomon hath made a scaffold of brass, and putteth it in the midst of the court, five cubits its length, and five cubits its breadth, and three cubits its height, and he standeth upon it, and kneeleth on his knees over-against all the assembly of Israel, and spreadeth forth his hands toards the heavens —

and saith, ’O Jehovah God of Israel, there is not like Thee a god in the heavens and in the earth, keeping the covenant and the kindness for Thy servants ho are alking before Thee ith all their heart;
ho hast kept for Thy servant David my father that hich Thou didst speak to him; yea, Thou dost speak ith Thy mouth, and ith Thy hand hast fulfilled [it], as at this day.

’And no, O Jehovah, God of Israel, keep for Thy servant David my father that hich Thou didst speak to him, saying, There is not cut off to thee a man from before Me, sitting on the throne of Israel, only, if thy sons atch their ay to alk in My la, as thou hast alked before Me.
’And no, O Jehovah, God of Israel, is Thy ord stedfast that Thou hast spoken to Thy servant, to David,
(for is it true? — God delleth ith man on the earth! Lo, the heavens, and the heavens of the heavens, do not contain Thee, ho much less this house that I have built?)
’And Thou hast turned unto the prayer of Thy servant, and unto his supplication, O Jehovah my God, to hearken unto the cry and unto the prayer that Thy servant is praying before Thee,
for Thine eyes being open toards this house by day and by night, toards the place that Thou hast said to put Thy name there, to hearken unto the prayer that Thy servant prayeth toards this place.

’And Thou hast hearkened unto the supplications of Thy servant, and of Thy people Israel, that they pray toards this place, and Thou dost hear from the place of Thy delling, from the heavens, and hast hearkened, and forgiven.
’If a man doth sin against his neighbour, and he hath lifted up on him an oath to cause him to sear, and the oath hath come in before Thine altar in this house —

then Thou dost hear from the heavens, and hast done, and hast judged Thy servants, to give back to the icked, to put his ay on his head, and to declare righteous the righteous, to give to him according to his righteousness.
’And if Thy people Israel is smitten before an enemy, because they sin against Thee, and they have turned back and confessed Thy name, and prayed and made supplication before Thee in this house —
then Thou dost hear from the heavens, and hast forgiven the sin of Thy people Israel, and caused them to turn back unto the ground that Thou hast given to them, and to their fathers.

’In the heavens being restrained, and there is no rain, because they sin against Thee, and they have prayed toards this place, and confessed Thy name — from their sin they turn back because Thou dost afflict them —

then Thou dost hear in the heavens, and hast forgiven the sin of Thy servants, and of Thy people Israel, because Thou directest them unto the good ay in hich they alk, and hast given rain on Thy land that Thou hast given to Thy people for an inheritance.

’Famine, hen it is in the land, pestilence, hen it is, blasting, and milde, locust, and caterpillar, hen they are, hen its enemies have distressed it in the land — its gates, any plague and any sickness;
any prayer, any supplication that is for any man, and for all Thy people Israel, hen they kno each his on plague, and his on pain, and he hath spread out his hands toards this house:

then Thou dost hear from the heavens, the settled place of Thy delling, and hast forgiven, and hast given to each according to all his ays (because Thou knoest his heart, for Thou — Thou only — hast knon the heart of the sons of men),
so that they fear Thee, to alk in Thy ays, all the days that they are living on the face of the ground that Thou hast given to our fathers.

’And also, unto the stranger ho is not of Thy people Israel, and he hath come from a land afar off for the sake of Thy great name, and Thy strong hand, and Thy stretched-out arm, and they have come in and prayed toards this house:

then Thou dost hear from the heavens, from the settled place of Thy delling, and hast done according to all that the stranger calleth unto Thee for: so that all the peoples of the earth do kno Thy name, so as to fear Thee, as Thy people Israel, and to kno that Thy name is called on this house that I have built.

’When Thy people doth go out to battle against its enemies in the ay that Thou dost send them, and they have prayed unto Thee the ay of this city that Thou hast fixed on, and the house that I have built for Thy name:
then Thou hast heard from the heavens their prayer and their supplication, and hast maintained their cause.

’When they sin against Thee — for there is not a man ho sinneth not — and Thou hast been angry ith them, and hast given them before an enemy, and taken them captive have their captors, unto a land far off or near;

and they have turned [it] back unto their heart in the land hither they have been taken captive, and have turned back, and made supplication unto Thee in the land of their captivity, saying, We have sinned, e have done perversely, and have done ickedly;

yea, they have turned back unto Thee ith all their heart, and ith all their soul, in the land of their captivity, hither they have taken them captive, and they have prayed the ay of their land that Thou hast given to their fathers, and of the city that Thou hast chosen, and of the house that I have built for Thy name:

then Thou hast heard from the heavens, from the settled place of Thy delling, their prayer and their supplications, and hast maintained their cause, and forgiven Thy people ho have sinned against Thee.
’No, my God, let, I beseech Thee, Thine eyes be open, and Thine ears attentive, to the prayer of this place:
and no, rise, O Jehovah God, to Thy rest, Thou, and the ark of Thy strength; Thy priests, O Jehovah God, are clothed ith salvation, and Thy saints rejoice in the goodness,
O Jehovah God, turn not back the face of Thine anointed, be mindful of the kind acts of David Thy servant.’
And at Solomon’s finishing to pray, then the fire hath come don from the heavens, and consumeth the burnt-offering and the sacrifices, and the honour of Jehovah hath filled the house,
and the priests have not been able to go in unto the house of Jehovah, because the honour of Jehovah hath filled the house of Jehovah.

And all the sons of Israel are looking on the descending of the fire, and the honour of Jehovah on the house, and they bo — faces to the earth — on the pavement, and do obeisance, and give thanks to Jehovah, for good, for to the age [is] His kindness.
And the king and all the people are sacrificing a sacrifice before Jehovah,
and king Solomon sacrificeth the sacrifice of the herd, tenty and to thousand, and of the flock, a hundred and tenty thousand, and the king and all the people dedicate the house of God.

And the priests over their charges are standing, and the Levites ith instruments of the song of Jehovah — that David the king made, to give thanks to Jehovah, for to the age [is] His kindness, in David’s praising by their hand — and the priests are bloing trumpets over-against them, and all Israel are standing.

And Solomon sanctifieth the middle of the court that [is] before the house of Jehovah, for he hath made there the burnt-offerings, and the fat of the peace-offerings: for the altar of brass that Solomon made hath not been able to contain the burnt-offering, and the present, and the fat.
And solomon maketh the feast at that time seven days, and all Israel ith him — a very great assembly — from the entering in of Hamath unto the brook of Egypt.
And they make on the eighth day a restraint, because the dedication of the altar they have made seven days, and the feast seven days.

And on the tenty and third day of the seventh month he hath sent the people to their tents, rejoicing, and glad in heart, for the goodness that Jehovah hath done to David, and to Solomon, and to Israel His people.
And Solomon finisheth the house of Jehovah, and the house of the king; and all that hath come on the heart of Solomon to do in the house of Jehovah, and in his on house, he hath caused to prosper.
And Jehovah appeareth unto Solomon by night, and saith to him, ’I have heard thy prayer, and have fixed on this place to Me for a house of sacrifice.
If I restrain the heavens and there is no rain, and if I lay charge on the locust to consume the land, and if I send pestilence among My people —
and My people on hom My name is called be humbled, and pray, and seek My face, and turn back from their evil ays, then I — I hear from the heavens, and forgive their sin, and heal their land.
’No, Mine eyes are open, and Mine ears attentive, to the prayer of this place;
and no, I have chosen and sanctified this house for My name being there unto the age; yea, Mine eyes and My heart have been there all the days.
’And thou, if thou dost alk before Me as David thy father alked, even to do according to all that I have commanded thee, and My statutes and My judgments dost keep —
then I have established the throne of thy kingdom, as I covenanted ith David thy father, saying, There is not cut off a man to thee — a ruler in Israel;

and if ye turn back — ye — and have forsaken My statutes, and My commands, that I have placed before you, and have gone and served other gods, and boed yourselves to them — then I have plucked them from off My ground that I have given to them,
and this house that I have sanctified for My name, I cast from before My face, and make it for a proverb, and for a byord, among all the peoples.
’And this house that hath been high, to every one passing by it, is an astonishment, and he hath said, Wherefore hath Jehovah done thus to this land, and to this house?

and they have said, Because that they have forsaken Jehovah, God of their fathers, ho brought them out from the land of Egypt, and lay hold on other gods, and bo themselves to them, and serve them, therefore He hath brought upon them all this evil.’
And it cometh to pass, at the end of tenty years, that Solomon hath built the house of Jehovah, and his on house.
As to the cities that Huram hath given to Solomon, Solomon hath built them, and there he causeth the sons of Israel to dell.
And Solomon goeth to Hamath-Zobah, and layeth hold upon it;
and he buildeth Tadmor in the ilderness, and all the cities of store that he hath built in Hamath.
And he buildeth Beth-Horon the upper, and Beth-Horon the loer — cities of defence, ith alls, to-leaved doors, and bar —

and Baalath, and all the cities of store that Solomon had, and all the cities of the chariot, and the cities of the horsemen, and all the desire of Solomon that he desired to build in Jerusalem, and in Lebanon, and in all the land of his dominion.
All the people ho are left of the Hittite, and the Amorite, and the Perizzite, and the Hivite, and the Jebusite, ho are not of Israel —
of their sons ho have been left after them in the land, hom the sons of Israel consumed not — doth Solomon lift up a tribute unto this day.
And none of the sons of Israel hath Solomon made servants for his ork, but they [are] men of ar, and heads of his captains, and heads of his charioteers, and of his horsemen;
and these [are] heads of the officers hom king Solomon hath, to hundred and fifty ho are rulers among the people.

And the daughter of Pharaoh hath Solomon brought up from the city of David to the house that he built for her, for he said, ’My ife doth not dell in the house of David king of Israel, for they are holy unto hom hath come the ark of Jehovah.’
Then hath Solomon caused to ascend burnt-offerings to Jehovah on the altar of Jehovah that he built before the porch,

even by the matter of a day in its day, to cause to ascend according to the command of Moses, on sabbaths, and on ne moons, and on appointed seasons, three times in a year — in the feast of unleavened things, and in the feast of eeks, and in the feast of booths.

And he establisheth, according to the ordinance of David his father, the courses of the priests over their service, and of the Levites over their charges, to praise and to minister over-against the priests, according to the matter of a day in its day, and the gatekeepers in their courses at gate and gate, for so [is] the command of David the man of God.
And they have not turned aside [from] the command of the king concerning the priests and the Levites, in reference to any matter, and to the treasures.
And all the ork of Solomon is prepared till the day of the foundation of the house of Jehovah, and till its completion; perfect is the house of Jehovah.
Then hath Solomon gone to Ezion-Geber, and unto Elath, on the border of the sea, in the land of Edom;

and Huram sendeth to him, by the hand of his servants, ships and servants knoing the sea, and they go ith servants of Solomon to Ophir, and take thence four hundred and fifty talents of gold, and bring in unto king Solomon.

And the queen of Sheba hath heard of the fame of Solomon, and cometh in to try Solomon ith acute sayings, to Jerusalem, ith a very great company, and camels bearing spices and gold in abundance, and precious stone; and she cometh in unto Solomon, and speaketh ith him all that hath been ith her heart,
and Solomon declareth to her all her matters, and there hath not been hid a thing from Solomon that he hath not declared to her.
And the queen of Sheba seeth the isdom of Solomon, and the house that he hath built,

and the food of his table, and the sitting of his servants, and the standing of his ministers, and their clothing, and his steards, and their clothing, an his burnt-offering that he offered up in the house of Jehovah, and there hath not been any more spirit in her.
And she saith unto the king, ’True [is] the ord that I heard in my land concerning thy matters and concerning thy isdom,

and I have given no credence to their ords, till that I have come, and mine eyes see, and lo, there hath not been declared to me the half of the abundance of thy isdom — thou hast added unto the report that I heard.
’O the happiness of thy men, and the happiness of thy servants — these — ho are standing before thee continually, and hearing thy isdom.

Let Jehovah thy God be blessed ho hath delighted in thee, to put thee on His throne for king for Jehovah thy God; in the love of thy God to Israel, to establish it to the age, He hath put thee over them for king, to do judgment and righteousness.’

And she giveth to the king a hundred and tenty talents of gold, and spices in great abundance, and precious stone; and there hath not been any such spice as the queen of Sheba hath given to king Solomon.
And also, servants of Huram, and servants of Solomon, ho brought in gold from Ophir, have brought in algum-trees and precious stone.

And the king maketh the algum-trees staircases for the house of Jehovah, and for the house of the king, and harps and psalteries for singers; and there have been none seen like these before in the land of Judah.
And king Solomon hath given to the queen of Sheba all her desire that she asked, apart from that hich she had brought unto the king, and she turneth and goeth to her land, she and her servants.
And the eight of the gold that is coming to Solomon in one year is six hundred and sixty and six talents of gold,
apart from [hat] the tourists, and the merchants, are bringing in; and all the kings of Arabia, and the governors of the land, are bringing in gold and silver to Solomon.
And king Solomon maketh to hundred targets of alloyed gold, six hundred [shekels] of alloyed gold he causeth to go up on the one target;
and three hundred shields of alloyed gold, three hundred [shekels] of gold he causeth to go up on the one shield, and the king putteth them in the house of the forest of Lebanon.
And the king maketh a great throne of ivory, and overlayeth it ith pure gold;

and six steps [are] to the throne, and a footstool of gold, to the throne they are fastened, and hands [are] on this [side] and on that on the place of the sitting, and to lions are standing near the hands,
and telve lions are standing there on the six steps on this [side], and on that: it hath not been made so for any kingdom.

And all the drinking vessels of king Solomon [are] of gold, and all the vessels of the house of the forest of Lebanon [are] of refined gold — silver is not reckoned in the days of Solomon for anything;
for ships of the king are going to Tarshish, ith servants of Huram: once in three years come do the ships of Tarshish bearing gold, and silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks.
And king Solomon becometh greater than any of the kings of the earth for riches and isdom;
and all the kings of the earth are seeking the presence of Solomon to hear his isdom that God hath put in his heart,
and they are bringing in each his present, vessels of silver, and vessels of gold, and garments, harness, and spices, horses, and mules, a rate year by year.
And there are to Solomon four thousand stalls for horses and chariots, and telve thousand horsemen, and he placed them in cities of the chariot, and ith the king in Jerusalem.
And he is ruling over all the kings from the River even unto the land of the Philistines, and unto the border of Egypt.
And the king maketh the silver in Jerusalem as stones, and the cedars he hath made as sycamores, that [are] in the lo country, for abundance,
and they are bringing out horses from Egypt to Solomon, and from all the lands.

And the rest of the matters of Solomon, the first and the last, are they not ritten beside the matters of Nathan the prophet, and beside the prophecy of Ahijah the Shilonite, and ith the visions of Iddo the seer concerning Jeroboam son of Nebat?
And Solomon reigneth in Jerusalem over all Israel forty years,
and Solomon lieth ith his fathers, and they bury him in the city of David his father, and reign doth Rehoboam his son in his stead.
And Rehoboam goeth to Shechem, for [to] Shechem have all Israel come to cause him to reign.
And it cometh to pass, at Jeroboam son of Nebat’s — ho [is] in Egypt because he hath fled from the face of Solomon the king — hearing, that Jeroboam turneth back out of Egypt;
and they send and call for him, and Jeroboam cometh in, and all Israel, and speak unto Rehoboam, saying,
’Thy father made our yoke sharp, and no, make light [somehat] of the sharp service of thy father, and of his heavy yoke that he put upon us, and e serve thee.’
And he saith unto them, ’Yet three days — then return ye unto me;’ and the people go.
And king Rehoboam consulteth ith the aged men ho have been standing before Solomon his father in his being alive, saying, ’Ho are ye counselling to anser this people?’
And they speak unto him, saying, ’If thou dost become good to this people, and hast been pleased ith them, and spoken unto them good ords, then they have been to thee servants all the days.’
And he forsaketh the counsel of the aged men that they counselled him, and consulteth ith the lads ho have gron up ith him, those standing before him,
and he saith unto them, ’What are ye counselling, and e anser this people that have spoken unto me, saying, Make light [somehat] of the yoke that thy father put upon us?’

And the lads ho have gron up ith him, speak ith him, saying, ’Thus dost thou say to the people ho have spoken unto thee, saying, Thy father made our yoke heavy, and thou, make light [somehat] of our yoke; thus dost thou say unto them, My little finger is thicker than the loins of my father;
and no, my father laid on you a heavy yoke, and I — I add unto your yoke; my father chastised you ith hips, and I — ith scorpions.’
And Jeroboam cometh in, and all the people, unto Rehoboam on the third day, as the king spake, saying, ’Return unto me on the third day.’
And the king ansereth them sharply, and king Rehoboam forsaketh the counsel of the aged men,
and speaketh unto them according to the counsel of the lads, saying, ’My father made your yoke heavy, and I — I add unto it; my father chastised you ith hips, and I — ith scorpions.’

And the king hath not hearkened unto the people, for the revolution hath been from God, for the sake of Jehovah’s establishing His ord that He spake by the hand of Abijah the Shilonite unto Jeroboam son of Nebat.

And all Israel have seen that the king hath not hearkened to them, and the people send back [to] the king, saying, ’What portion have e in David? yea, there is no inheritance in a son of Jesse; each to thy tents, O Israel; no, see thy house — David,’ and all Israel go to their tents.
As to the sons of Israel ho are delling in the cities of Judah — Rehoboam reigneth over them.

And king Rehoboam sendeth Hadoram, ho [is] over the tribute, and the sons of Israel cast at him stones, and he dieth; and king Rehoboam hath strengthened himself to go up into a chariot to flee to Jerusalem;
and Israel transgress against the house of David unto this day.
And Rehoboam cometh in to Jerusalem, and assembleth the house of Judah and Benjamin, a hundred and eighty thousand chosen arriors, to fight ith Israel, to bring back the kingdom to Rehoboam.
And a ord of Jehovah is unto Shemaiah, a man of God, saying,
’Speak unto Rehoboam son of Solomon king of Judah, and unto all Israel in Judah and Benjamin, saying,

Thus said Jehovah, Ye do not go up nor fight ith your brethren, turn back each to his house, for from Me hath this thing been;’ and they hear the ords of Jehovah, and turn back from going against Jeroboam.
And Rehoboam delleth in Jerusalem, and buildeth cities for a bulark in Judah,
yea, he buildeth Beth-Lehem and Etam, and Tekoa,
and Beth-Zur, and Shocho, and Adullam,
and Gath, and Mareshah, and Ziph,
and Adoraim, and Lachish, and Azekah,
and Zorah, and Aijalon, and Hebron, that [are] in Judah and in Benjamin, cities of bularks.
And he strengtheneth the bularks, and putteth in them leaders, and treasures of food, and oil, and ine,
and in every city and city targets and spears, and strengtheneth them very greatly; and he hath Judah and Benjamin.
And the priests, and the Levites, that [are] in all Israel, have stationed themselves by him, out of all their border,
for the Levites have left their suburbs and their possession, and they come to Judah and to Jerusalem, for Jeroboam and his sons have cast them off from acting as priests to Jehovah,
and he establisheth to him priests for high places, and for goats, and for calves, that he made —
and after them, out of all the tribes of Israel, those giving their heart to seek Jehovah, God of Israel, have come in to Jerusalem to sacrifice to Jehovah, God of their father.
And they strengthen the kingdom of Judah, and strengthen Rehoboam son of Solomon, for three years, because they alked in the ay of David and Solomon for three years.
And Rehoboam taketh to him a ife, Mahalath, child of Jerimoth son of David, [and] Abigail daughter of Eliab, son of Jesse.
And she beareth to him sons, Jeush, and Shamaria, and Zaham.
And after her he hath taken Maachah daughter of Absalom, and she beareth to him Abijah, and Attai, and Ziza, and Shelomith.

And Rehoboam loveth Maachah daughter of Absalom above all his ives and his concubines — for eighteen ives he hath taken, and sixty concubines — and he begetteth tenty and eight sons, and sixty daughters.
And Rehoboam appointeth for head Abijah son of Maachah, for leader among his brethren, for to cause him to reign.

And he hath understanding, and spreadeth out of all his sons to all lands of Judah and Benjamin, to all cities of the bularks, and giveth to them provision in abundance; and he asketh a multitude of ives.
And it cometh to pass, at the establishing of the kingdom of Rehoboam, and at his strengthening himself, he hath forsaken the la of Jehovah, and all Israel ith him.
And it cometh to pass, in the fifth year of king Rehoboam, come up hath Shishak king of Egypt against Jerusalem — because they trespassed against Jehovah —
ith a thousand and to hundred chariots, and ith sixty thousand horsemen, and there is no number to the people ho have come ith him out of Egypt — Lubim, Sukkiim, and Cushim —
and he captureth the cities of the bularks that [are] to Judah, and cometh in unto Jerusalem.

And Shemaiah the prophet hath come in unto Rehoboam and the heads of Judah ho have been gathered unto Jerusalem from the presence of Shishak, and saith to them, ’Thus said Jehovah, Ye have forsaken Me, and also, I have left you in the hand of Shishak;’
and the heads of Israel are humbled, and the king, and they say, ’Righteous [is] Jehovah.’

And hen Jehovah seeth that they have been humbled, a ord of Jehovah hath been unto Shemaiah, saying, ’They have been humbled; I do not destroy them, and I have given to them as a little thing for an escape, and I pour not out My fury in Jerusalem by the hand of Shishak;
but they become servants to him, and they kno My service, and the service of the kingdoms of the lands.’

And Shishak king of Egypt cometh up against Jerusalem, and taketh the treasures of the house of Jehovah, and the treasures of the house of the king — the hole he hath taken — and he taketh the shields of gold that Solomon had made;
and king Rehoboam maketh in their stead shields of brass, and hath given [them] a charge on the hand of the heads of the runners ho are keeping the opening of the house of the king;
and it cometh to pass, from the time of the going in of the king to the house of Jehovah, the runners have come in and lifted them up, and brought them back unto the chamber of the runners.
And in his being humbled, turned back from him hath the rath of Jehovah, so as not to destroy to completion; and also, in Judah there have been good things.

And king Rehoboam strengtheneth himself in Jerusalem, and reigneth; for a son of forty and to years [is] Rehoboam in his reigning, and seventeen years he hath reigned in Jerusalem, the city that Jehovah hath chosen to put His name there, out of all the tribes of Israel, and the name of his mother [is] Naamah the Ammonitess,
and he doth the evil thing, for he hath not prepared his heart to seek Jehovah.

And the matters of Rehoboam, the first and the last, are they not ritten among the matters of Shemaiah the prophet, and of Iddo the seer, concerning genealogy? And the ars of Rehoboam and Jeroboam [are] all the days;
and Rehoboam lieth ith his fathers, and is buried in the city of David, and reign doth Abijah his son in his stead.
In the eighteenth year of king Jeroboam — Abijah reigneth over Judah;
three years he hath reigned in Jerusalem, (and the name of his mother [is] Michaiah daughter of Uriel, from Gibeah,) and ar hath been beteen Abijah and Jeroboam.
And Abijah directeth the ar ith a force of mighty men of ar, four hundred thousand chosen men, and Jeroboam hath set in array ith him battle, ith eight hundred thousand chosen men, mighty of valour.
And Abijah riseth up on the hill of Zemaraim that [is] in the hill-country of Ephraim, and saith, ’Hear me, Jeroboam and all Israel!
Is it not for you to kno that Jehovah, God of Israel, hath given the kingdom to David over Israel to the age, to him and to his sons — a covenant of salt?
and rise up doth Jeroboam, son of Nebat, servant of Solomon son of David, and rebelleth against his lord!

’And there are gathered unto him vain men, sons of orthlessness, and they strengthen themselves against Rehoboam son of Solomon, and Rehoboam as a youth, and tender of heart, and hath not strengthened himself against them.

’And no, ye are saying to strengthen yourselves before the kingdom of Jehovah in the hand of the sons of David, and ye [are] a numerous multitude, and ith you calves of gold that Jeroboam hath made to you for gods.

’Have ye not cast out the priests of Jehovah, the sons of Aaron, and the Levites, and make to you priests like the peoples of the lands? every one ho hath come to fill his hand ith a bullock, a son of the herd, and seven rams, even he hath been a priest to No-gods!
’As for us, Jehovah [is] our God, and e have not forsaken Him, and priests are ministering to Jehovah, sons of Aaron and the Levites, in the ork,

and are making perfume to Jehovah, burnt-offerings morning by morning, and evening by evening, and perfume of spices, and the arrangement of bread [is] on the pure table, and the candlestick of gold, and its lamps, to burn evening by evening, for e are keeping the charge of Jehovah our God, and ye — ye have forsaken Him.
’And lo, ith us — at [our] head — [is] God, and His priests and trumpets of shouting to shout against you; O sons of Israel, do not fight ith Jehovah, God of your fathers, for ye do not prosper.’
And Jeroboam hath brought round the ambush to come in from behind them, and they are before Judah, and the ambush [is] behind them.
And Judah turneth, and lo, against them [is] the battle, before and behind, and they cry to Jehovah, and the priests are bloing ith trumpets,
and the men of Judah shout — and it cometh to pass, at the shouting of the men of Judah, that God hath smitten Jeroboam, and all Israel, before Abijah and Judah.
And the sons of Israel flee from the face of Judah, and God giveth them into their hand,
and Abijah and his people smite among them a great smiting, and there fall ounded of Israel five hundred thousand chosen men.
And the sons of Israel are humbled at that time, and the sons of Judah are strong, for they have leant on Jehovah, God of their fathers.
And Abijah pursueth after Jeroboam, and captureth from him cities, Beth-El and its small tons, and Jeshanah and its small tons, and Ephraim and its small tons.
And Jeroboam hath not retained poer any more in the days of Abijah, and Jehovah smiteth him, and he dieth.
And Abijah strengtheneth himself, and taketh to him fourteen ives, and begetteth tenty and to sons, and sixteen daughters,
and the rest of the matters of Abijah, and his ays, and his ords, are ritten in the ’Inquiry’ of the prophet Iddo.
And Abijah lieth ith his fathers, and they bury him in the city of David, and reign doth Asa his son in his stead: in his days as the land quiet ten years.
And Asa doth that hich is good, and that hich is right, in the eyes of Jehovah his God,
and turneth aside the altars of the stranger, and the high places, and breaketh the standing-pillars, and cutteth don the shrines,
and saith to Judah to seek Jehovah, God of their fathers, and to do the la and the command;
and he turneth aside out of all cities of Judah the high places and the images, and the kingdom is quiet before him.
And he buildeth cities of bularks in Judah, for the land hath quiet, and there is no ar ith him in these years, because Jehovah hath given rest to him.

And he saith to Judah, ’Let us build these cities, and compass [them] ith all, and toers, to-leaved doors, and bars, hile the land [is] before us, because e have sought Jehovah our God, e have sought, and He giveth rest to us round about;’ and they build and prosper.

And there is to Asa a force bearing target and spear, out of Judah three hundred thousand, and out of Benjamin, bearing shield and treading bo, to hundred and eighty thousand: all these [are] mighty of valour.
And come out unto them doth Zerah the Cushite ith a force of a thousand thousand, and chariots three hundred, and he cometh in unto Mareshah,
and Asa goeth out before him, and they set battle in array in the valley of Zephathah at Mareshah.

And Asa calleth unto Jehovah his God, and saith, ’Jehovah! it is nothing ith Thee to help, beteen the mighty and those ho have no poer; help us, O Jehovah, our God, for on Thee e have leant, and in Thy name e have come against this multitude; O Jehovah, our God thou [art]; let him not prevail ith Thee — mortal man!
And Jehovah smiteth the Cushim before Asa, and before Judah, and the Cushim flee,

and Asa and the people ho [are] ith him pursue them even to Gerar, and there fall of the Cushim, for they have no preserving, because they have been broken before Jehovah, and before His camp; and they bear aay very much spoil,
and smite all the cities round about Gerar, for a fear of Jehovah hath been upon them, and they spoil all the cities, for abundant spoil hath been in them;
and also tents of cattle they have smitten, and they capture sheep in abundance, and camels, and turn back to Jerusalem.
And upon Azariah son of Oded hath been the Spirit of God,

and he goeth out before Asa, and saith to him, ’Hear, me, Asa, and all Judah and Benjamin; Jehovah [is] ith you — in your being ith Him, and if ye seek Him, He is found of you, and if ye forsake Him, He forsaketh you;
and many days [are] to Israel ithout a true God, and ithout a teaching priest, and ithout la,
and it turneth back in its distress unto Jehovah, God of Israel, and they seek Him, and He is found of them,
and in those times there is no peace to him ho is going out, and to him ho is coming in, for many troubles [are] on all the inhabitants of the lands,
and they have been beaten don, nation by nation, and city by city, for God hath troubled them ith every adversity;
and ye, be ye strong, and let not your hands be feeble, for there is a reard for your ork.’

And at Asa’s hearing these ords, and the prophecy of Oded the prophet, he hath strengthened himself, and doth cause the abominations to pass aay out of all the land of Judah and Benjamin, and out of the cities that he hath captured from the hill-country of Ephraim, and reneeth the altar of Jehovah that [is] before the porch of Jehovah,

and gathereth all Judah and Benjamin, and the sojourners ith them out of Ephraim, and Manasseh, and out of Simeon — for they have fallen unto him from Israel in abundance, in their seeing that Jehovah his God [is] ith him.
And they are gathered to Jerusalem in the third month of the fifteenth year of the reign of Asa,
and sacrifice to Jehovah on that day from the spoil they have brought in — oxen seven hundred, and sheep seven thousand,
and they enter into a covenant to seek Jehovah, God of their fathers, ith all their heart, and ith all their soul,
and every one ho doth not seek for Jehovah, God of Israel, is put to death, from small unto great, from man unto oman.
And they sear to Jehovah ith a loud voice, and ith shouting, and ith trumpets, and ith cornets,

and rejoice do all Judah concerning the oath, for ith all their heart they have sorn, and ith all their good-ill they have sought Him, and He is found of them, and Jehovah giveth rest to them round about.

And also Maachah, mother of Asa the king — he hath removed her from [being] mistress, in that she hath made for a shrine a horrible thing, and Asa cutteth don her horrible thing, and beateth [it] small, and burneth [it] by the brook Kidron:
yet the high places have not turned aside from Israel; only, the heart of Asa hath been perfect all his days.
And he bringeth in the sanctified things of his father, and his on sanctified things, to the house of God, silver, and gold, and vessels.
And ar hath not been till the thirty and fifth year of the reign of Asa.
In the thirty and sixth year of the reign of Asa, come up hath Baasha king of Israel, against Judah, and buildeth Ramah, so as not to permit any going out and coming in to Asa king of Judah.
And Asa bringeth out silver and gold from the treasures of the house of Jehovah, and of the house of the king, and sendeth unto Ben-Hadad king of Aram, ho is delling in Damascus, saying,
’A covenant [is] beteen me and thee, and beteen my father and thy father, lo, I have sent to thee silver and gold; go, break thy covenant ith Baasha king of Israel, and he doth go up from off me.’
And Ben-Hadad hearkeneth unto king Asa, and sendeth the heads of the forces that he hath unto cities of Israel, and they smite Ijon, and Dan, and Abel-Maim, and all the stores, cities of Naphtali.
And it cometh to pass, at Baasha’s hearing, that he ceaseth from building Ramah, and letteth his ork rest;
and Asa the king hath taken all Judah, and they bear aay the stones of Ramah, and its ood, that Baasha hath built, and he buildeth ith them Geba and Mizpah.

And at that time hath Hanani the seer come in unto Asa king of Judah, and saith unto him, ’Because of thy leaning on the king of Aram, and thou hast not leaned on Jehovah thy God, therefore hath the force of the king of Aram escaped from thy hand.
Did not the Cushim and the Lubim become a very great force for multitude, for chariot, and for horsemen? and in thy leaning on Jehovah He gave them into thy hand,

for Jehovah — His eyes go to and fro in all the earth, to sho Himself strong [for] a people hose heart [is] perfect toards Him; thou hast been foolish concerning this, because — henceforth there are ith thee ars.’
And Asa is angry at the seer, and giveth him to the house of torture, for [he is] in a rage ith him for this; and Asa oppresseth [some] of the people at that time.
And lo, the matters of Asa, the first and the last, lo, they are ritten on the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.
And Asa is diseased — in the thirty and ninth year of his reign — in his feet, till his disease is excessive, and also in his disease he hath not sought Jehovah, but among physicians.
And Asa lieth ith his fathers, and dieth in the forty and first year of his reign,

and they bury him in [one of] his graves, that he had prepared for himself in the city of David, and they cause him to lie on a bed that [one] hath filled [ith] spices, and divers kinds of mixtures, ith perfumed ork; and they burn for him a burning — very great.
And Jehoshaphat his son reigneth in his stead, and he strengtheneth himself against Israel,
and putteth a force in all the fenced cities of Judah, and putteth garrisons in the land of Judah, and in the cities of Ephraim that Asa his father had captured.
And Jehovah is ith Jehoshaphat, for he hath alked in the first ays of David his father, and hath not sought to Baalim,
for to the God of his father he hath sought, and in His commands he hath alked, and not according to the ork of Israel.
And Jehovah doth establish the kingdom in his hand, and all Judah give a present to Jehoshaphat, and he hath riches and honour in abundance,
and his heart is high in the ays of Jehovah, and again he hath turned aside the high places and the shrines out of Judah.
And in the third year of his reign he hath sent for his heads, for Ben-Hail, and for Obadiah, and for Zechariah, and for Nethaneel, and for Michaiah, to teach in cities of Judah,

and ith them the Levites, Shemaiah, and Nethaniah, and Zebadiah, and Asahel, and Shemiramoth, and Jehonathan, and Adonijah, and Tobijath, and Tob-Adonijah, the Levites; and ith them Elishama and Jehoram, the priests.
And they teach in Judah, and ith them [is] the Book of the La of Jehovah, and they go round about into all cities of Judah, and teach among the people.
And here is a fear of Jehovah on all kingdoms of the lands that [are] round about Judah, and they have not fought ith Jehoshaphat;

and of the Philistines they are bringing in to Jehoshaphat a present, and tribute silver; also, the Arabians are bringing to him a flock, rams seven thousand an seven hundred, and he-goats seven thousand and seven hundred.
And Jehoshaphat is going on and becoming very great, and he buildeth in Judah palaces and cities of store,
and he hath much ork in cities of Judah; and men of ar, mighty of valour, [are] in Jerusalem.
And these [are] their numbers, for the house of their fathers: Of Judah, heads of thousands, Adnah the head, and ith him mighty ones of valour, three hundred chiefs.
And at his hand [is] Jehohanan the head, and ith him to hundred and eighty chiefs.
And at his hand [is] Amasiah son of Zichri, ho is illingly offering himself to Jehovah, and ith him to hundred chiefs, mighty of valour.
And of Benjamin: mighty of valour, Eliada, and ith him, armed ith bo and shield, to hundred chiefs.
And at his hand [is] Jehozabad, and ith him a hundred and eighty chiefs, armed ones of the host.
These [are] those serving the king, apart from those hom the king put in the cities of fortress, in all Judah.
And Jehoshaphat hath riches and honour in abundance, and joineth affinity to Ahab,

and goeth don at the end of [certain] years unto Ahab to Samaria, and Ahab sacrificeth for him sheep and oxen in abundance, and for the people ho [are] ith him, and persuadeth him to go up unto Ramoth-Gilead.
And Ahab king of Israel saith unto Jehoshaphat king of Judah, ’Dost thou go ith me [to] Ramoth-Gilead?’ And he saith to him, ’As I — so thou, and as thy people — my people, even ith thee in battle.’
And Jehoshaphat saith unto the king of Israel, ’Seek, I pray thee, this day, the ord of Jehovah.’

And the king of Israel gathereth the prophets, four hundred men, and saith unto them, ’Do e go unto Ramoth-Gilead to battle, or do I forbear?’ And they say, ’Go up, and God doth give [it] into the hand of the king.’
And Jehoshaphat saith, ’Is there not here a prophet of Jehovah still, and e seek from him?’

And the king of Israel saith unto Jehoshaphat, ’Still — one man to seek Jehovah from him, and I — I have hated him, for he is not prophesying concerning me of good, but all his days of evil, he [is] Micaiah son of Imlah;’ and Jehoshaphat saith, ’Let not the king say so.’
And the king of Israel calleth unto a certain officer, and saith, ’Hasten Micaiah son of Imlah.’

And the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah are sitting, each on his throne, clothed ith garments, and they are sitting in a threshing-floor at the opening of the gate of Samaria, and all the prophets are prophesying before them.
And Zedekiah son of Chenaanah maketh for himself horns of iron, and saith, ’Thus said Jehovah,

With these thou dost push Aram till thou hast consumed them.’ And all the prophets are prophesying so, saying, ’Go up [to] Ramath-Gilead and prosper, and Jehovah hath given [it] into the hand of the king.’

And the messenger ho hath gone to call for Micaiah hath spoken unto him, saying, ’Lo, the ords of the prophets — one mouth — [are] good toards the king, and let, I pray thee, thy ord be like one of theirs: and thou hast spoken good.’
And Micaiah saith ’Jehovah liveth, surely that hich my God saith, it I speak.’

And he cometh in unto the king, and the king saith unto him, ’Micaiah, do e go unto Ramoth-Gilead to battle, or do I forbear?’ And he saith, ’Go ye up, and prosper, and they are given into your hand.’
And the king saith unto him, ’Ho many times am I adjuring thee, that thou speak unto me only truth in the name of Jehovah?’
And he saith, ’I have seen all Israel scattered on the mountains, as sheep that have no shepherd, and Jehovah saith, There are no masters to these, they turn back each to his house in peace.’
And the king of Israel saith unto Jehoshaphat, ’Did I not say unto thee, He doth not prophesy concerning me good, but rather of evil?’
And he saith, ’Therefore, hear ye a ord of Jehovah: I have seen Jehovah sitting on His throne, and all the host of the heavens standing on His right and His left;
and Jehovah saith, Who doth entice Ahab king of Israel, and he doth go up and fall in Ramoth-Gilead? And this speaker saith thus, and that speaker thus.
