And he removeth those left of the sord unto Babylon, and they are to him and to his sons for servants, till the reigning of the kingdom of Persia,
to fulfil the ord of Jehovah in the mouth of Jeremiah, till the land hath enjoyed its sabbaths; all the days of the desolation it kept sabbath — to the fulness of seventy years.

And in the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, at the completion of the ord of Jehovah in the mouth of Jeremiah, hath Jehovah aked up the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia, and he causeth an intimation to pass over into all his kingdom, and also in riting, saying,

’Thus said Cyrus king of Persia, All kingdoms of the earth hath Jehovah, God of the heavens, given to me, and He hath laid a charge on me to build to Him a house in Jerusalem, that [is] in Judah; ho is among you of all His people? Jehovah his God [is] ith him, and he doth go up.’

And in the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, at the completion of the ord of Jehovah from the mouth of Jeremiah, hath Jehovah aked up the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia, and he causeth an intimation to pass over into all his kingdom, and also in riting, saying,
’Thus said Cyrus king of Persia, All kingdoms of the earth hath Jehovah, God of the heavens, given to me, and He hath laid a charge on me to build to Him a house in Jerusalem, that [is] in Judah;
ho [is] among you of all His people? His God is ith him, and he doth go up to Jerusalem, that [is] in Judah, and build the house of Jehovah, God of Israel — He [is] God — that [is] in Jerusalem.

’And every one ho is left, of any of the places here he [is] a sojourner, assist him do the men of his place ith silver, and ith gold, and ith goods, and ith beasts, along ith a free-ill offering for the house of God, that [is] in Jerusalem.’
And heads of the fathers of Judah and Benjamin rise, and the priests and the Levites, even every one hose spirit God hath aked, to go up to build the house of Jehovah, that [is] in Jerusalem;

and all those round about them have strengthened [them] ith their hands, ith vessels of silver, ith gold, ith goods, and ith beasts, and ith precious things, apart from all that hath been offered illingly.
And the king Cyrus hath brought out the vessels of the house of Jehovah that Nebuchadnezzar hath brought out of Jerusalem, and putteth them in the house of his gods;
yea, Cyrus king of Persia bringeth them out by the hand of Mithredath the treasurer, and numbereth them to Sheshbazzar the prince of Judah.
And this [is] their number: dishes of gold thirty, dishes of silver a thousand, knives nine and tenty,
basins of gold thirty, basins of silver (seconds) four hundred and ten, other vessels a thousand.
All the vessels of gold and of silver [are] five thousand and four hundred; the hole hath Sheshbazzar brought up ith the going up of the removal from Babylon to Jerusalem.

And these [are] sons of the province ho are going up — of the captives of the removal that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon removed to Babylon, and they turn back to Jerusalem and Judah, each to his city —
ho have come in ith Zerubbabel, Jeshua, Nehemiah, Seraiah, Reelaiah, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispar, Bigvai, Rehum, Baanah: The number of the men of the people of Israel:
Sons of Parosh, to thousand a hundred seventy and to.
Sons of Shephatiah, three hundred seventy and to.
Sons of Arah, seven hundred five and seventy.
Sons of Pahath-Moab, of the sons of Jeshua, Joab, to thousand eight hundred and telve.
Sons of Elam, a thousand to hundred fifty and four.
Sons of Zattu, nine hundred and forty and five.
Sons of Zaccai, seven hundred and sixty.
Sons of Bani, six hundred forty and to.
Sons of Bebai, six hundred tenty and three.
Sons of Azgad, a thousand to hundred tenty and to.
Sons of Adonikam, six hundred sixty and six.
Sons of Bigvai, to thousand fifty and six.
Sons of Adin, four hundred fifty and four.
Sons of Ater of Hezekiah, ninety and eight.
Sons of Bezai, three hundred tenty and three.
Sons of Jorah, a hundred and telve.
Sons of Hashum, to hundred tenty and three.
Sons of Gibbar, ninety and five.
Sons of Beth-Lehem, a hundred tenty and three.
Men of Netophah, fifty and six.
Men of Anathoth, a hundred tenty and eight.
Sons of Azmaveth, forty and to.
Sons of Kirjath-Arim, Chephirah, and Beeroth, seven hundred and forty and three.
Sons of Ramah and Gaba, six hundred tenty and one.
Men of Michmas, a hundred tenty and to.
Men of Beth-El and Ai, to hundred tenty and three.
Sons of Nebo, fifty and to.
Sons of Magbish, a hundred fifty and six.
Sons of another Elam, a thousand to hundred fifty and four.
Sons of Harim, three hundred and tenty.
Sons of Lod, Hadid, and Ono, seven hundred tenty and five.
Sons of Jericho, three hundred forty and five.
Sons of Senaah, three thousand and six hundred and thirty.
The Priests: sons of Jedaiah, of the house of Jeshua, nine hundred seventy and three.
Sons of Imner, a thousand fifty and to.
Sons of Pashhur, a thousand to hundred forty and seven.
Sons of Harim, a thousand and seventeen.
The Levites; sons of Jeshua and Kadmiel, of the sons of Hodaviah, seventy and four.
The singers: sons of Asaph, a hundred tenty and eight.
Sons of the gatekeepers; sons of Shallum, sons of Ater, sons of Talmon, sons of Akkub, sons of Hatita, sons of Shobai, the hole [are] a hundred thirty and nine.
The Nethinim: sons of Ziha, sons of Hasupha, sons of Tabbaoth,
Sons of Keros, sons of Siaha, sons of Padon,
Sons of Lebanah, sons of Hagabah, sons of Akkub,
Sons of Hagab, sons of Shalmai, sons of Hanan,
Sons of Giddel, sons of Gahar, sons of Reaiah,
Sons of Rezin, sons of Nekoda, sons of Gazzam,
Sons of Uzza, sons of Paseah, sons of Besai,
Sons of Asnah, sons of Mehunim, sons of Nephusim,
Sons of Bakbuk, sons of Hakupha, sons of Harhur,
Sons of Bazluth, sons of Mehida, sons of Harsha,
Sons of Barkos, sons of Sisera, sons of Thamah,
Sons of Neziah, sons of Hatipha.
Sons of the servants of Solomon: sons of Sotai, sons of Sophereth, sons of Peruda,
Sons of Jaalah, sons of Darkon, sons of Giddel,
Sons of Shephatiah, sons of Hattil, sons of Pochereth of Zebaim, sons of Ami.
All the Nethinim, and the sons of the servants of Solomon [are] three hundred ninety and to.
And these [are] those going up from Tel-Melah, Tel-Harsa, Cherub, Addan, Immer, and they have not been able to declare the house of their fathers, and their seed, hether they [are] of Israel:
sons of Delaiah, sons of Tobiah, sons of Nekoda, six hundred fifty and to.
And of the sons of the priests: sons of Habaiah, sons of Koz, sons of Barzillai (ho took from the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite a ife, and is called by their name;)
these have sought their register among those reckoning themselves by genealogy, and they have not been found, and they are redeemed from the priesthood,
and the Tirshatha saith to them, that they eat not of the most holy things till the standing up of a priest ith Urim and ith Thummim.
All the assembly together [is] four myriad to thousand three hundred sixty,
apart from their servants and their handmaids; these [are] seven thousand three hundred thirty and seven: and of them [are] singers and songstresses to hundred.
Their horses [are] seven hundred thirty and six, their mules, to hundred forty and five,
their camels, four hundred thirty and five, asses, six thousand seven hundred and tenty.
And some of the heads of the fathers in their coming in to the house of Jehovah that [is] in Jerusalem, have offered illingly for the house of God, to establish it on its base;
according to their poer they have given to the treasure of the ork; of gold, drams six myriads and a thousand, and of silver, pounds five thousand, and of priests’ coats, a hundred.
And the priests dell, and the Levites, and of the people, and the singers, and the gatekeepers, and the Nethinim, in their cities; even all Israel in their cities.
And the seventh month cometh, and the sons of Israel [are] in the cities, and the people are gathered, as one men, unto Jerusalem.

And rise doth Jeshua son of Jozadak, and his brethren the priests, and Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, and his brethren, and they build the altar of the God of Israel, to cause to ascend upon it burnt-offerings, as it is ritten in the la of Moses, the man of God.

And they establish the altar on its bases, because of the fear upon them of the peoples of the lands, and he causeth burnt-offerings to ascend upon it to Jehovah, burnt-offerings for the morning and for the evening.
And they make the feast of the booths as it is ritten, and the burnt-offering of the day daily in number according to the ordinance, the matter of a day in its day;
and after this a continual burnt-offering, and for ne moons, and for all appointed seasons of Jehovah that are sanctified; and for every one ho is illingly offering a illing-offering to Jehovah.
From the first day of the seventh month they have begun to cause burnt-offerings to ascend to Jehovah, and the temple of Jehovah hath not been founded,

and they give money to heers and to artificers, and food, and drink, and oil to Zidonians and to Tyrians, to bring in cedar-trees from Lebanon unto the sea of Joppa, according to the permission of Cyrus king of Persia concerning them.

And in the second year of their coming in unto the house of God, to Jerusalem, in the second month, began Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, and Jeshua son of Jozadak, and the remnant of their brethren the priests and the Levites, and all those coming from the captivity to Jerusalem, and they appoint the Levites from a son of tenty years and upard, to overlook the ork of the house of Jehovah.

And Jeshua standeth, [and] his sons, and his brethren, Kadmiel and his sons, sons of Judah together, to overlook those doing the ork in the house of God; the sons of Henadad, [and] their sons and their brethren the Levites.

And those building have founded the temple of Jehovah, and they appoint the priests, clothed, ith trumpets, and the Levites, sons of Asaph, ith cymbals, to praise Jehovah, by means of [the instruments of] David king of Israel.

And they respond in praising and in giving thanks to Jehovah, for good, for to the age His kindness [is] over Israel, and all the people have shouted — a great shout — in giving praise to Jehovah, because the house of Jehovah hath been founded.

And many of the priests, and the Levites, and the heads of the fathers, the aged men ho had seen the first house — in this house being founded before their eyes — are eeping ith a loud voice, and many ith a shout, in joy, lifting up the voice;

and the people are not discerning the noise of the shout of joy from the noise of the eeping of the people, for the people are shouting — a great shout — and the noise hath been heard unto a distance.
And adversaries of Judah and Benjamin hear that the sons of the captivity are building a temple to Jehovah, God of Israel,

and they dra nigh unto Zerubbabel, and unto heads of the fathers, and say to them, ’Let us build ith you; for, like you, e seek to your God, and e are not sacrificing since the days of Esar-Haddon king of Asshur, ho brought us up hither.’

And Zerubbabel saith to them, also Jeshua, and the rest of the heads of the fathers of Israel, ’Not for you, and for us, to build a house to our God; but e ourselves together do build to Jehovah God of Israel, as the king Cyrus, king of Persia, commanded us.’
And it cometh to pass, the people of the land are making the hands of the people of Judah feeble, and troubling them in building,
and are hiring against them counsellors to make void their counsel all the days of Cyrus king of Persia, even till the reign of Darius king of Persia.
And in the reign of Ahasuerus, in the commencement of his reign, they have ritten an accusation against the inhabitants of Judah and Jerusalem;

and in the days of Artaxerxes have Bishlam, Mithredath, Tabeel, and the rest of his companions ritten unto Artaxerxes king of Persia, and the riting of the letter is ritten in Aramaean, and interpreted in Aramaean.
Rehum counsellor, and Shimshai scribe have ritten a letter concerning Jerusalem to Artaxerxes the king, thus:
Then Rehum counsellor, and Shimshai scribe, and the rest of their companions, Dinaites, and Apharsathchites, Tarpelites, Apharsites, Archevites, Babylonians, Susanchites, (ho are Elamites),
and the rest of the nations that the great and honourable Asnapper removed and set in the city of Samaria, and the rest beyond the river, and at such a time:
This [is] a copy of a letter that they have sent unto him, unto Artaxerxes the king: ’Thy servants, men beyond the river, and at such a time;

Be it knon to the king, that the Jes ho have come up from thee unto us, have come in to Jerusalem, the rebellious and base city they are building, and the alls they have finished, and the foundations they join.
’No, be it knon to the king, that if this city be builded, and the alls finished, toll, tribute, and custom they do not give; and at length [to] the kings it doth cause loss.
No, because that the salt of the palace [is] our salt, and the nakedness of the king e have no patience to see, therefore e have sent and made knon to the king;

so that he doth seek in the book of the records of thy fathers, and thou dost find in the book of the records, and dost kno, that this city [is] a rebellious city, and causing loss [to] kings and provinces, and makers of sedition [are] in its midst from the days of old, therefore hath this city been asted.
We are making knon to the king that, if this city be builded and the alls finished, by this means a portion beyond the river thou hast none.’
An anser hath the king sent unto Rehum counsellor, and Shimshai scribe, and the rest of their companions ho are delling in Samaria, and the rest beyond the river, ’Peace, and at such a time:
The letter that ye sent unto us, explained, hath been read before me,
and by me a decree hath been made, and they sought, and have found that this city from the days of old against kings is lifting up itself, and rebellion and sedition is made in it,
and mighty kings have been over Jerusalem, even rulers over all beyond the river, and toll, tribute, and custom is given to them.
’No, make ye a decree to cause these men to cease, and this city is not builded, till by me a decree is made.
And beare ye of negligence in doing this; hy doth the hurt become great to the loss of the kings?’

Then from the time that a copy of the letter of king Artaxerxes is read before Rehum, and Shimshai the scribe, and their companions, they have gone in haste to Jerusalem, unto the Jes, and caused them to cease by force and strength;
then ceased the service of the house of God that [is] in Jerusalem, and it ceased till the second year of the reign of Darius king of Persia.
And prophesied have the prophets, (Haggai the prophet, and Zechariah son of Iddo) unto the Jes ho [are] in Judah and in Jerusalem, in the name of the God of Israel — unto them.
Then have Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, and Jeshua son of Jozadak, risen, and begun to build the house of God, that [is] in Jerusalem, and ith them are the prophets of God supporting them.

At that time come to them hath Tatnai, governor beyond the river, and Shethar-Boznai, and their companions, and thus they are saying to them, ’Who hath made for you a decree this house to build, and this all to finish?’
Then thus e have said to them, ’What [are] the names of the men ho are building this building?’
And the eye of their God hath been upon the elders of the Jes, and they have not caused them to cease till the matter goeth to Darius, and then they send back a letter concerning this thing.
The copy of a letter that Tatnai, governor beyond the river, hath sent, and Shethar-Boznai and his companions, the Apharsachites ho [are] beyond the river, unto Darius the king.
A letter they have sent unto him, and thus is it ritten in it:

’To Darius the king, all peace! be it knon to the king that e have gone to the province of Judah, to the great house of God, and it is built [ith] rolled stones, and ood is placed in the alls, and this ork is done speedily, and prospering in their hand.
Then e have asked of these elders, thus e have said to them, Who hath made for you a decree this house to build, and this all to finish?
And also their names e have asked of them, to let thee kno, that e might rite the names of the men ho [are] at their head.

’And thus they have returned us ord, saying, We [are] servants of the God of heaven and earth, and are building the house that as built many years before this, that a great king of Israel built and finished:
but after that our fathers made the God of heaven angry, he gave them into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon the Chaldean, and this house he destroyed, and the people he removed to Babylon;
but in the first year of Cyrus king of Babylon, Cyrus the king made a decree to build this house of God,

and also, the vessels of the house of God, of gold and silver, that Nebuchadnezzar had taken forth out of the temple that [is] in Jerusalem, and brought them to the temple of Babylon, them hath Cyrus the king brought forth out of the temple of Babylon, and they have been given to [one], Sheshbazzar [is] his name, hom he made governor,
and said to him, These vessels lift up, go, put them don in the temple that [is] in Jerusalem, and the house of God is builded on its place.
Then hath this Sheshbazzar come — he hath laid the foundations of the house of God that [is] in Jerusalem, and from thence even till no it hath been building, and is not finished.

’And no, if to the king it be good, let search be made in the treasure-house of the king, that [is] there in Babylon, hether it be that of Cyrus the king there as made a decree to build this house of God in Jerusalem, and the ill of the king concerning this thing he doth send unto us.’
Then Darius the king made a decree, and they sought in the house of the books of the treasuries placed there in Babylon,
and there hath been found at Achmetha, in a palace that [is] in the province of Media, a roll, and a record thus ritten ithin it [is]:

’In the first year of Cyrus the king, Cyrus the king hath made a decree concerning the house of God in Jerusalem: the house let be builded in the place here they are sacrificing sacrifices, and its foundations strongly laid; its height sixty cubits, its breadth sixty cubits;
three ros of rolled stones, and a ro of ne ood, and the outlay let be given out of the king’s house.

’And also, the vessels of the house of God, of gold and silver, that Nebuchadnezzar took forth out of the temple that [is] in Jerusalem, and brought to Babylon, let be given back, and go to the temple that [is] in Jerusalem, [each] to its place, and put [them] don in the house of God.
’No, Tatnai, governor beyond the river, Shethar-Boznai, and their companions, the Apharsachites, ho [are] beyond the river, be ye far from hence;
let alone the ork of this house of God, let the governor of the Jes, and the elders of the Jes, build this house of God on its place.

’And by me is made a decree concerning that hich ye do ith the elders of these Jes to build this house of God, that of the riches of the king, that [are] of the tribute beyond the river, speedily let the outlay be given to these men, that they cease not;

and hat they are needing — both young bullocks, and rams, and lambs for burnt-offerings to the God of heaven, heat, salt, ine, and oil according to the saying of the priests ho [are] in Jerusalem — let be given to them day by day ithout fail,
that they be bringing near seet savours to the God of heaven, and praying for the life of the king, and of his sons.
’And by me is made a decree, that any one ho changeth this thing, let ood be pulled don from his house, and being raised up, let him be smitten on it, and his house let be made a dunghill for this.

And God, ho caused His name to dell there, doth cast don any king and people that putteth forth his hand to change, to destroy this house of God that [is] in Jerusalem; I Darius have made a decree; speedily let it be done.’
Then Tatnai, governor beyond the river, Shethar-Boznai, and their companions, according to that hich Darius the king hath sent, so they have done speedily;

and the elders of the Jes are building and prospering through the prophecy of Haggai the prophet, and Zechariah son of Iddo, and they have built and finished by the decree of the God of Israel, and by the decree of Cyrus, and Darius, and Artaxerxes king of Persia.
And this house hath gone out till the third day of the month Adar, that is [in] the sixth year of the reign of Darius the king.
And the sons of Israel have made, [and] the priests, and the Levites, and the rest of the sons of the captivity, a dedication of this house of God ith joy,

and have brought near for the dedication of this house of God, bullocks a hundred, rams to hundred, lambs four hundred; and young he-goats for a sin-offering for all Israel, telve, according to the number of the tribes of Israel;
and they have established the priests in their divisions, and the Levites in their courses, over the service of God that [is] in Jerusalem, as it is ritten in the book of Moses.
And the sons of the captivity make the passover on the fourteenth of the first month,

for the priests and the Levites have been purified together — all of them [are] pure — and they slaughter the passover for all the sons of the captivity, and for their brethren the priests, and for themselves.
And the sons of Israel, those returning from the captivity, and every one ho is separated from the uncleanness of the nations of the land unto them, to seek to Jehovah, God of Israel, do eat,

and they make the feast of unleavened things seven days ith joy, for Jehovah made them to rejoice, and turned round the heart of the king of Asshur unto them, to strengthen their hands in the ork of the house of God, the God of Israel.
And after these things, in the reign of Artaxerxes king of Persia, Ezra son of Seraiah, son of Azariah, son of Hilkiah,
son of Shallum, son of Zadok, son of Ahitub,
son of Amariah, son of Azariah, son of Meraioth,
son of Zerahiah, son of Uzzi, son of Bukki,
son of Abishua, son of Phinehas, son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the head priest;

Ezra himself hath come up from Babylon, and he [is] a scribe ready in the la of Moses, that Jehovah God of Israel gave, and the king giveth to him — according to the hand of Jehovah his God upon him — all his request.
And there go up of the sons of Israel, and of the priests, and the Levites, and the singers, and the gatekeepers, and the Nethinim, unto Jerusalem, in the seventh year of Artaxerxes the king.
And he cometh in to Jerusalem in the fifth month, that [is in] the seventh year of the king,
for on the first of the month he hath founded the ascent from Babylon, and on the first of the fifth month he hath come in unto Jerusalem, according to the good hand of his God upon him,
for Ezra hath prepared his heart to seek the la of Jehovah, and to do, and to teach in Israel statute and judgment.
And this [is] a copy of the letter that the king Artaxerxes gave to Ezra the priest, the scribe, a scribe of the ords of the commands of Jehovah, and of His statutes on Israel:
’Artaxerxes, king of kings, to Ezra the priest, a perfect scribe of the la of the God of heaven, and at such a time:
By me hath been made a decree that every one ho is illing, in my kingdom, of the people of Israel and of its priests and Levites, to go to Jerusalem ith thee, doth go;
because that from the king and his seven counsellors thou art sent, to inquire concerning Judah and concerning Jerusalem, ith the la of God that [is] in thy hand,
and to carry silver and gold that the king and his counsellors illingly offered to the God of Israel, hose tabernacle [is] in Jerusalem,

and all the silver and gold that thou findest in all the province of Babylon, ith the free-ill offerings of the people, and of the priests, offering illingly, for the house of their God that [is] in Jerusalem,
therefore thou dost speedily buy ith this money, bullocks, rams, lambs, and their presents, and their libations, and dost bring them near to the altar of the house of your God that [is] in Jerusalem,
and that hich to thee and to thy brethren is good to do ith the rest of the silver and gold, according to the ill of your God ye do.’
’And the vessels that are given to thee, for the service of the house of thy God, make perfect before the God of Jerusalem;
and the rest of the needful things of the house of thy God, that it falleth to thee to give, thou dost give from the treasure-house of the king.

’And by me — I Artaxerxes the king — is made a decree to all treasurers ho [are] beyond the river, that all that Ezra the priest, scribe of the la of the God of heaven, doth ask of you, be done speedily:
Unto silver a hundred talents, and unto heat a hundred cors, and unto ine a hundred baths, and unto oil a hundred baths, and salt ithout reckoning;
all that [is] by the decree of the God of heaven, let be done diligently for the house of the God of heaven; for hy is there rath against the kingdom of the king and his sons?
’And to you e are making knon, that upon any of the priests and Levites, singers, gatekeepers, Nethinim, and servants of the house of God, tribute and custom there is no authority to lift up.

’And thou, Ezra, according to the isdom of thy God, that [is] in thy hand, appoint magistrates and judges ho may be judges to all the people ho are beyond the river, to all knoing the la of thy God, and he ho hath not knon ye cause to kno;
and any ho doth not do the la of thy God, and the la of the king, speedily is judgment done upon him, hether to death, or to banishment, or to confiscation of riches, and to bonds.’
Blessed [is] Jehovah, God of our fathers, ho hath given such a thing as this in the heart of the king, to beautify the house of Jehovah that [is] in Jerusalem,

and unto me hath stretched out kindness before the king and his counsellors, and before all the mighty heads of the king: and I have strengthened myself as the hand of Jehovah my God [is] upon me, and I gather out of Israel heads to go up ith me.
And these [are] heads of their fathers, and the genealogy of those going up ith me, in the reign of Artaxerxes the king, from Babylon.
From the sons of Phinehas: Gershom; from the sons of Ithamar: Daniel; from the sons of David: Hattush;
from the sons of Shechaniah, from the sons of Pharosh: Zechariah, and ith him, reckoning themselves by genealogy, of males a hundred and fifty.
From the sons of Pahath-Moab: Elihoenai son of Zerahiah, and ith him to hundred ho are males.
From the sons of Shechaniah: the son of Jahaziel, and ith him three hundred ho are males.
And from the sons of Adin: Ebed son of Jonathan, and ith him fifty ho are males.
And from the sons of Elam: Jeshaiah son of Athaliah, and ith him seventy ho are males.

And from the sons of Bigvai, Uthai and Zabbud, and ith them seventy ho are males.
And I gather them unto the river that is going unto Ahava, and e encamp there three days; and I consider about the people, and about the priests, and of the sons of Levi I have found none there;

and I send for Eliezer, for Ariel, for Shemaiah, and for Elnathan, and for Jarib, and for Elnathan, and for Nathan, and for Zechariah, and for Meshullam, heads, and for Joiarib, and for Elnathan, men of understanding;

and I charge them for Iddo the head, in the place Casiphia, and put in their mouth ords to speak unto Iddo, [and] his brethren the Nethinim, in the place Casiphia, to bring to us ministrants for the house of our God.
And they bring to us, according to the good hand of our God upon us, a man of understanding, of the sons of Mahli, son of Levi, son of Israel, and Sherebiah, and his sons, and his brethren, eighteen;
and Hashabiah, and ith him Jeshaiah, of the sons of Merari, his brethren, and their sons, tenty;
and from the Nethinim, hom David and the heads gave for the service of the Levites, to hundred and tenty Nethinim, all of them defined by name.
And I proclaim there a fast, by the river Ahava, to afflict ourselves before our God, to seek from Him a right ay for us, and for our infants, and for all our substance,

for I as ashamed to ask from the king a force and horsemen to help us because of the enemy in the ay, for e spake to the king, saying, ’The hand of our God [is] upon all seeking Him for good, and His strength and His rath [is] upon all forsaking Him.’
And e fast, and seek from our God for this, and He is entreated of us.
And I separate from the heads of the priests, telve, even Sherebiah, Hashabiah, and ith them of their brethren ten,
and I eigh to them the silver, and the gold, and the vessels, a heave-offering of the house of our God, that the king, and his counsellors, and his heads, and all Israel — those present — lifted up;
and I eigh to their hand, of silver, talents six hundred and fifty, and of vessels of silver a hundred talents, of gold a hundred talents,
and basins of gold tenty, of a thousand drams, and to vessels of good shining brass, desirable as gold.
And I say unto them, ’Ye [are] holy to Jehovah, and the vessels [are] holy, and the silver and the gold [are] a illing-offering to Jehovah, God of your fathers;
atch, and keep, till ye eigh before the heads of the priests, and of the Levites, and the heads of the fathers of Israel, in Jerusalem, in the chambers of the house of Jehovah.’
And the priests and the Levites took the eight of the silver, and of the gold, and of the vessels, to bring to Jerusalem to the house of our God.

And e journey from the river Ahava, on the telfth of the first month, to go to Jerusalem, and the hand of our God hath been upon us, and He delivereth us from the hand of the enemy and the lier in ait by the ay;
and e come in to Jerusalem, and dell there three days.

And on the fourth day hath been eighed the silver, and the gold, and the vessels, in the house of our God, unto the hand of Meremoth son of Uriah the priest, and ith him Eleazar son of Phinehas, and ith them Jozabad son of Jeshua, and Noadiah son of Binnui, the Levites:
by number, by eight of every one, and all the eight is ritten at that time.

Those coming in of the captives — sons of the removal — have brought near burnt-offerings to the God of Israel, bullocks telve, for all Israel, rams ninety and six, lambs seventy and seven, young he-goats for a sin-offering telve — the hole a burnt-offering to Jehovah;
and they give the las of the king to the lieutenants of the king and the governors beyond the river, and they have lifted up the people and the house of God.

And at the completion of these things, dran nigh unto me have the heads, saying, ’The people of Israel, and the priests, and the Levites, have not been separated from the peoples of the lands, as to their abominations, even the Canaanite, the Hittite, the Perizzite, the Jebusite, the Ammonite, the Moabite, the Egyptian, and the Amorite,

for they have taken of their daughters to them, and to their sons, and the holy seed have mingled themselves among the peoples of the lands, and the hand of the heads and of the seconds have been first in this trespass.’
And at my hearing this ord, I have rent my garment and my upper robe, and pluck out of the hair of my head, and of my beard, and sit astonished,
and unto me are gathered every one trembling at the ords of the God of Israel, because of the trespass of the removal, and I am sitting astonished till the present of the evening.
And at the present of the evening I have risen from mine affliction, and at my rending my garment and my upper robe, then I bo don on my knees, and spread out my hands unto Jehovah my God,
and say, ’O my God, I have been ashamed, and have blushed to lift up, O my God, my face unto Thee, for our iniquities have increased over the head, and our guilt hath become great unto the heavens.

’From the days of our fathers e [are] in great guilt unto this day, and in our iniquities e have been given — e, our kings, our priests — into the hand of the kings of the lands, ith sord, ith captivity, and ith spoiling, and ith shame of face, as [at] this day.

’And no, as a small moment hath grace been from Jehovah our God, to leave to us an escape, and to give to us a nail in His holy place, by our God’s enlightening our eyes, and by giving us a little quickening in our servitude;

for servants e [are], and in our servitude our God hath not forsaken us, and stretcheth out unto us kindness before the kings of Persia, to give to us a quickening to lift up the house of our God, and to cause its astes to cease, and to give to us a all in Judah and in Jerusalem.
’And no, hat do e say, O our God, after this? for e have forsaken Thy commands,

that Thou hast commanded by the hands of thy servants the prophets, saying, The land into hich ye are going to possess it, [is] a land of impurity, by the impurity of the people of the lands, by their abominations ith hich they have filled it — from mouth unto mouth — by their uncleanness;

and no, your daughters ye do not give to their sons, and their daughters ye do not take to your sons, and ye do not seek their peace, and their good — unto the age, so that ye are strong, and have eaten the good of the land, and given possession to your sons unto the age.
’And after all that hath come upon us for our evil orks, and for our great guilt (for Thou, O our God, hast kept back of the rod from our iniquities, and hast given to us an escape like this),

do e turn back to break Thy commands, and to join ourselves in marriage ith the people of these abominations? art not Thou angry against us — even to consumption — till there is no remnant and escaped part?
’O Jehovah, God of Israel, righteous [art] Thou, for e have been left an escape, as [it is] this day; lo, e [are] before Thee in our guilt, for there is none to stand before Thee concerning this.’

And at Ezra’s praying, and at his making confession, eeping and casting himself don before the house of God, there have been gathered unto him out of Israel an assembly very great — men and omen and children — for the people have ept, multiplying eeping.

And Shechaniah son of Jehiel, of the sons of Elam, ansereth and saith to Ezra, ’We — e have trespassed against our God, and e settle strange omen of the peoples of the land; and no there is hope for Israel concerning this,

and no, let us make a covenant ith our God, to cause all the omen to go out, and that hich is born of them, by the counsel of the Lord, and of those trembling at the command of our God, and according to la it is done;
rise, for on thee [is] the matter, and e [are] ith thee; be strong, and do.’
And Ezra riseth, and causeth the heads of the priests, the Levites, and all Israel, to sear to do according to this ord — and they sear.

And Ezra riseth from before the house of God, and goeth unto the chamber of Jehohanan son of Eliashib; yea, he goeth there, bread he hath not eaten, and ater he hath not drunk, for he is mourning because of the trespass of the removal.
And they cause a voice to pass over into Judah and Jerusalem, to all sons of the removal, to be gathered to Jerusalem,
and every one ho cometh not in by the third day, according to the counsel of the heads and of the elders, all his substance is devoted, and himself separated from the assembly of the removal.

And gathered are all the men of Judah and Benjamin to Jerusalem by the third day, it [is] the ninth month, on the tentieth of the month, and all the people sit in the broad place of the house of God, trembling on account of the matter and of the shoers.
And Ezra the priest riseth, and saith unto them, ’Ye — ye have trespassed, and ye settle strange omen, to add to the guilt of Israel;
and, no, make confession to Jehovah, God of your fathers, and do His good pleasure, and be separated from the peoples of the land, and from the strange omen.’
And all the assembly anser and say [ith] a great voice, ’Right; according to thy ord — on us to do;
but the people [are] many, and [it is] the time of shoers, and there is no poer to stand ithout, and the ork [is] not for one day, nor for to, for e have multiplied to transgress in this thing.

’Let, e pray thee, our heads of all the assembly stand, and all ho [are] in our cities, ho have settled strange ives, do come in at the times appointed, and ith them the elders of city and city, and its judges, till the turning back of the fury of the rath of our God from us, for this thing.’
Only Jonathan son of Asahel, and Jahaziah son of Tikvah, stood against this, and Meshullam, and Shabbethai the Levite, helped them.

And the sons of the removal do so, and Ezra the priest, [and] men, heads of the fathers, for the house of their fathers, are separated, even all of them by name, and they sit on the first day of the tenth month, to examine the matter;
and they finish ith all the men ho have settled strange omen unto the first day of the first month.
And there are found of the sons of the priests that have settled strange omen: of the sons of Jeshua son of Jozadak, and his brethren, Maaseiah, and Eliezer, and Jarib, and Gedaliah;
and they give their hand to send out their ives, and, being guilty, a ram of the flock, for their guilt.

And of the Levites: Jozabad, and Shimei, and Kelaiah — he [is] Kelita, — Pethahiah, Judah, and Eliezer.
And of the singers: Eliashib. And of the gatekeepers: Shallum, and Telem, and Uri.
And of Israel: of the sons of Parosh: Ramiah, and Jeziah, and Malchijah, and Miamin, and Eleazar, and Malchijah, and Benaiah.
And of the sons of Elam: Mattaniah, Zechariah, and Jehiel, and Abdi, and Jeremoth, and Elijah.
And of the sons of Zattu: Elioenai, Eliashib, Mattaniah, and Jeremoth, and Zabad, and Aziza.
And of the sons of Bebai: Jehohanan, Hananiah, Zabbai, Athlai.
And of the sons of Bani: Meshullam, Malluch, and Adaiah, Jashub, and Sheal, and Ramoth.
And of the sons of Pahath-Moab: Adna, and Chelal, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattaniah, Bezaleel, and Binnui, and Manasseh.
And of the sons of Harim: Eliezer, Ishijah, Malchiah, Shemaiah, Shimeon,
Benjamin, Malluch, Shemariah.
Of the sons of Hashum: Mattenai, Mattathah, Zabad, Eliphelet, Jeremai, Manasseh, Shimei.
Of the sons of Bani: Maadai, Amram, and Uel,
Benaiah, Bedeiah, Cheluhu,
Vaniah, Meremoth, Eliashib,
Mattaniah, Mattenai, and Jaasau,
and Bani, and Binnui, Shimei,
and Shelemiah, and Nathan, and Adaiah,
Machnadbai, Shashai, Sharai,

Of the sons of Nebo: Jeiel, Mattithiah, Zabad, Zebina, Jadau, and Joel, Benaiah;

Words of Nehemiah son of Hachaliah. And it cometh to pass, in the month of Chisleu, the tentieth year, and I have been in Shushan the palace,
and come in doth Hanani, one of my brethren, he and men of Judah, and I ask them concerning the Jes, the escaped part that have been left of the captivity, and concerning Jerusalem;

and they say to me, ’Those left, ho have been left of the captivity there in the province, [are] in great evil, and in reproach, and the all of Jerusalem is broken don, and its gates have been burnt ith fire.’
And it cometh to pass, at my hearing these ords, I have sat don, and I eep and mourn [for] days, and I am fasting and praying before the God of the heavens.
And I say, ’I beseech thee, O Jehovah, God of the heavens, God, the great and the fearful, keeping the covenant and kindness for those loving Him, and for those keeping His commands,

let Thine ear be, I pray Thee, attentive, and Thine eyes open, to hearken unto the prayer of Thy servant, that I am praying before Thee to-day, by day and by night, concerning the sons of Israel Thy servants, and confessing concerning the sins of the sons of Israel, that e have sinned against Thee; yea, I and the house of my father have sinned;
e have acted very corruptly against Thee, and have not kept the commands, and the statutes, and the judgments, that Thou didst command Moses Thy servant.
’Remember, I pray Thee, the ord that Thou didst command Moses Thy servant, saying, Ye — ye trespass — I scatter you among peoples;

and ye have turned back unto Me, and kept My commands, and done them — if your outcast is in the end of the heavens, thence I gather them, and have brought them in unto the place that I have chosen to cause My name to tabernacle there.
And they [are] Thy servants, and Thy people, hom Thou hast ransomed by Thy great poer, and by Thy strong hand.

’I beseech Thee, O Lord, let, I pray Thee, Thine ear be attentive unto the prayer of Thy servant, and unto the prayer of Thy servants, those delighting to fear Thy Name; and give prosperity, I pray Thee, to Thy servant to-day, and give him for mercies before this man;’ and I have been butler to the king.
And it cometh to pass, in the month of Nisan, the tentieth year of Artaxerxes the king, ine [is] before him, and I lift up the ine, and give to the king, and I had not been sad before him;
and the king saith to me, ’Wherefore [is] thy face sad, and thou not sick? this is nothing except sadness of heart;’ and I fear very much,
and say to the king, ’Let the king to the age live! herefore should not my face be sad, hen the city, the place of the graves of my fathers, [is] a aste, and its gates have been consumed ith fire?’
And the king saith to me, ’For hat art thou seeking?’ and I pray unto the God of the heavens,
and say to the king, ’If to the king [it be] good, and if thy servant be pleasing before thee, that thou send me unto Judah, unto the city of the graves of my fathers, and I built it.’
And the king saith to me (and the queen is sitting near him), ’Ho long is thy journey? and hen dost thou return?’ and it is good before the king, and he sendeth me aay, and I set to him a time.
And I say to the king, ’If to the king [it be] good, letters let be given to me for the governors beyond the River, that they let me pass over till that I come in unto Judah:

and a letter unto Asaph, keeper of the paradise that the king hath, that he give to me trees for beams [for] the gates of the palace that the house hath, and for the all of the city, and for the house into hich I enter;’ and the king giveth to me, according to the good hand of my God upon me.
And I come in unto the governors beyond the River, and give to them the letters of the king; and the king sendeth ith me heads of a force, and horsemen;
and Sanballat the Horonite heareth, and Tobiah the servant, the Ammonite, and it is evil to them — a great evil — that a man hath come in to seek good for the sons of Israel.
And I come in unto Jerusalem, and I am there three days,
and I rise by night, I and a fe men ith me, and have not declared to a man hat my God is giving unto my heart to do for Jerusalem, and there is no beast ith me except the beast on hich I am riding.

And I go out through the gate of the valley by night, and unto the front of the fountain of the dragon, and unto the gate of the dunghill, and I am measuring about the alls of Jerusalem, that are broken don, and its gates consumed ith fire.
And I pass over unto the gate of the fountain, and unto the pool of the king, and there is no place for the beast under me to pass over,
and I am going up through the brook by night, and am measuring about the all, and turn back, and come in through the gate of the valley, and turn back.

And the prefects have not knon hither I have gone, and hat I am doing; and to the Jes, and to the priests, and to the freemen, and to the prefects, and to the rest of those doing the ork, hitherto I have not declared [it];

and I say unto them, ’Ye are seeing the evil that e are in, in that Jerusalem [is] aste, and its gates have been burnt ith fire; come and e build the all of Jerusalem, and e are not any more a reproach.’

And I declare to them the hand of my God that is good upon me, and also the ords of the king that he said to me, and they say, ’Let us rise, and e have built;’ and they strengthen their hands for good.

And Sanballat the Horonite heareth, and Tobiah the servant, the Ammonite, and Geshem the Arabian, and they mock at us, and despise us, and say, ’What [is] this thing that ye are doing? against the king are ye rebelling?’

And I return them ord, and say to them, ’The God of the heavens — He doth give prosperity to us, and e His servants rise and have built; and to you there is no portion, and right, and memorial in Jerusalem.’

And Eliashib the high priest riseth, and his brethren the priests, and they build the sheep-gate; they have sanctified it, and set up its doors, even unto the toer of Meah they have sanctified it, unto the toer of Hananeel;
and by his hand have men of Jericho built; and by their hand hath Zaccur son of Imri built;
and the fish-gate have sons of Hassenaah built, they have alled it, and set up its doors, its locks, and its bars.

And by their hand hath Merimoth son of Urijah, son of Koz, strengthened; and by his hand hath Meshullam son of Berechiah, son of Meshezabeel, strengthened; and by his hand hath Zadok son of Baana strengthened;
and by his hand have the Tekoites strengthened, and their honourable ones have not brought in their neck to the service of their Lord.
And the old gate have Jehoiada son of Paseah, and Meshullam son of Besodeiah, strengthened; they have alled it, and set up its doors, and its locks, and its bars.
And by their hand hath Melatiah the Gibeonite strengthened, and Jadon the Meronothite, men of Gibeon and of Mizpah, to the throne of the governor beyond the River.
By his hand hath Uzziel son of Harhaiah of the refiners strengthened; and by his hand hath Hananiah son of [one of] the compounders strengthened; and they leave Jerusalem unto the broad all.
And by their hand hath Rephaiah son of Hur, head of the half of the district of Jerusalem, strengthened.
And by their hand hath Jedaiah son of Harumaph strengthened, and over-against his on house; and by his hand hath Hattush son of Hashabniah strengthened.
A second measure hath Malchijah son of Harim strengthened, and Hashub son of Pahath-Moab, even the toer of the furnaces.
And by his hand hath Shallum son of Halohesh, head of the half of the district of Jerusalem, strengthened, he and his daughters.
The gate of the valley hath Hanun strengthened, and the inhabitants of Zanoah; they have built it, and set up its doors, its locks, and its bars, and a thousand cubits in the all unto the dung-gate.
And the dung-gate hath Malchijah son of Rechab, head of the district of Beth-Haccerem, strengthened; he doth built it, and set up its doors, its locks, and its bars.

And the gate of the fountain hath Shallum son of Col-Hozeh, head of the district of Mizpah, strengthened: he doth build it, and cover it, and set up its doors, its locks, and its bars, and the all of the pool of Siloah, to the garden of the king, and unto the steps that are going don from the city of David.

After him hath Nehemiah son of Azbuk, head of the half of the district of Beth-Zur, strengthened, unto over-against the graves of David, and unto the pool that is made, and unto the house of the mighty ones.
After him have the Levites strengthened, [and] Rehum son of Bani: by his hand hath Hashabiah, head of the half of the district of Keilah, strengthened, for his district.
After him have their brethren strengthened, [and] Bavvai son of Henadad, head of the half of the district of Keilah.
And Ezer son of Jeshua, head of Mizpah, doth strengthen, by his hand, a second measure, from over-against the ascent of the armoury at the angle.
After him hath Baruch son of Zabbai hastened to strengthen a second measure from the angle unto the opening of the house of Eliashib the high priest.
After him hath Meremoth son of Urijah, son of Koz, strengthened, a second measure, from the opening of the house of Eliashib even unto the completion of the house of Eliashib.
And after him have the priests, men of the circuit, strengthened.
After them hath Benjamin strengthened, and Hashub, over-against their house; after him hath Azariah son of Maaseiah, son of Ananiah, strengthened, near his house.
After him hath Binnui son of Henadad strengthened, a second measure, from the house of Azariah unto the angle, and unto the corner.
Palal son of Uzai, from over-against the angle, and the toer that is going out from the upper house of the king that [is] at the court of the prison; after him Pedaiah son of Parosh.
And the Nethinim have been delling in Ophel, unto over-against the ater-gate at the east, and the toer that goeth out.
After him have the Tekoites strengthened, a second measure, from over-against the great toer that goeth out, and unto the all of Ophel.
From above the horse-gate have the priests strengthened, each over-against his house.
After them hath Zadok son of Immer strengthened, over against his house; and after him hath Shemaiah son of Shechaniah, keeper of the east gate, strengthened.
After him hath Hananiah son of Shelemiah strengthened, and Hanun the sixth son of Zalaph, a second measure; after him hath Meshullam son of Berechiah strengthened, over-against his chamber.
After him hath Malchijah son of the refiner strengthened, unto the house of the Nethinim, and of the merchants, over-against the gate of the Miphkad, and unto the ascent of the corner.
And beteen the ascent of the corner and the sheep-gate, have the refiners and the merchants strengthened.
And it cometh to pass, hen Sanballat hath heard that e are building the all, that it is displeasing to him, and he is very angry and mocketh at the Jes,

and saith before his brethren and the force of Samaria, yea, he saith, ’What [are] the eak Jes doing? are they left to themselves? do they sacrifice? do they complete in a day? do they revive the stones out of the heaps of the rubbish? — and they burnt!’
And Tobiah the Ammonite [is] by him and saith, ’Also, that hich they are building — if a fox doth go up, then it hath broken don their stone all.’
Hear, O our God, for e have been despised; and turn back their reproach on their on head, and give them for a spoil in a land of captivity;
and do not cover over their iniquity, and their sin from before Thee let not be blotted out, for they have provoked to anger — over-against those building.
And e build the all, and all the all is joined — unto its half, and the people have a heart to ork.

And it cometh to pass, hen Sanballat hath heard, and Tobiah, and the Arabians, and the Ammonites, and the Ashdodites, that lengthening hath gone up to the alls of Jerusalem, that the breeches have begun to be stopped, then it is very displeasing to them,
and they conspire, all of them together, to come in to fight against Jerusalem, and to do to it injury.
And e pray unto our God, and appoint a atch against them, by day and by night, because of them.
And Judah saith, ’The poer of the burden-bearers hath become feeble, and the rubbish [is] abundant, and e are not able to build on the all.’
And our adversaries say, ’They do not kno, nor see, till that e come in to their midst, and have slain them, and caused the ork to cease.’
And it cometh to pass, hen the Jes have come ho are delling near them, that they say to us ten times from all the places hither ye return — [they are] against us.
And I appoint at the loest of the places, at the back of the all, in the clear places, yea, I appoint the people, by their families, ith their sords, their spears, and their bos.

And I see, and rise up, and say unto the freemen, and unto the prefects, and unto the rest of the people, ’Be not afraid of them; the Lord, the great and the fearful, remember ye, and fight for your brethren, your sons, and your daughters, your ives, and your houses.’
And it cometh to pass, hen our enemies have heard that it hath been knon to us, and God doth frustrate their counsel, and e turn back, all of us, unto the all, each unto his ork;

yea, it cometh to pass, from that day, half of my servants are orking in the business, and half of them are keeping hold of both the spears, the shields, and the bos, and the coats of mail; and the heads [are] behind all the house of Judah.
The builders on the all, and the bearers of the burden, those lading, [each] ith one of his hands is orking in the business, and one is laying hold of the missile.
And the builders [are] each ith his sord, girded on his loins, and building, and he ho is bloing ith a trumpet [is] beside me.
And I say unto the freemen, and unto the prefects, and unto the rest of the people, ’The ork is abundant, and large, and e are separated on the all, far off one from another;
in the place that ye hear the voice of the trumpet thither ye are gathered unto us; our God doth fight for us.’
And e are orking in the business, and half of them are keeping hold of the spears, from the going up of the dan till the coming forth of the stars.
Also, at that time I said to the people, ’Let each ith his servant lodge in the midst of Jerusalem, and they have been to us by night a guard, and by day [for] the ork:’
and there are none — I and my brethren and my servants, the men of the guard ho [are] after me — there are none of us putting off our garments, each [hath] his vessel of ater.
And there is a great cry of the people and their ives, concerning their brethren the Jes,
yea, there are ho are saying, ’Our sons, and our daughters, e — are many, and e receive corn, and eat, and live.’
And there are ho are saying, ’Our fields, and our vineyards, and our houses, e are pledging, and e receive corn for the famine.’
And there are ho are saying, ’We have borroed money for the tribute of the king, [on] our fields, and our vineyards;

and no, as the flesh of our brethren [is] our flesh, as their sons [are] our sons, and lo, e are subduing our sons and our daughters for servants, and there are of our daughters subdued, and our hand hath no might, and our fields and our vineyards [are] to others.’
And it is very displeasing to me hen I have heard their cry and these ords,
and my heart reigneth over me, and I strive ith the freemen, and ith the prefects, and say to them, ’Usury one upon another ye are exacting;’ and I set against them a great assembly,

and say to them, ’We have acquired our brethren the Jes, those sold to the nations, according to the ability that [is] in us, and ye also sell your brethren, and they have been sold to us!’ and they are silent, and have not found a ord.
And I say, ’Not good [is] the thing that ye are doing; in the fear of our God do ye not alk, because of the reproach of the nations our enemies?
And also, I, my brethren, and my servants, are exacting of them silver and corn; let us leave off, I pray you, this usury.

Give back, I pray you, to them, as to-day, their fields, their vineyards, their olive-yards, and their houses, and the hundredth [part] of the money, and of the corn, of the ne ine, and of the oil, that ye are exacting of them.’
And they say, ’We give back, and of them e seek nothing; so e do as thou art saying.’ And I call the priests, and cause them to sear to do according to this thing;

also, my lap I have shaken, and I say, ’Thus doth God shake out every man, ho doth not perform this thing, from his house, and from his labour; yea, thus is he shaken out and empty;’ and all the assembly say, ’Amen,’ and praise Jehovah; and the people do according to this thing.

Also, from the day that he appointed me to be their governor in the land of Judah, from the tentieth year even unto the thirty and second year of Artaxerxes the king — telve years — I, and my brethren, the bread of the governor have not eaten:

the former governors ho [are] before me have made themselves heavy on the people, and take of them in bread and ine, besides in silver forty shekels; also, their servants have ruled over the people — and I have not done so, because of the fear of God.
And also, in the ork of this all I have done mightily, even a field e have not bought, and all my servants are gathered there for the ork;
and of the Jes, and of the prefects, a hundred and fifty men, and those coming in unto us of the nations that [are] round about us, [are] at my table;

and that hich hath been prepared for one day [is] one ox, six fat sheep, also fols have been prepared for me, and once in ten days of all ines abundantly, and ith this, the bread of the governor I have not sought, for heavy is the service on this people.
Remember for me, O my God, for good, all that I have done for this people.

And it cometh to pass, hen it hath been heard by Sanballat, and Tobiah, and by Geshem the Arabian, and by the rest of our enemies, that I have builded the all, and there hath not been left in it a breach, (also, till that time the doors I had not set up in the gates,)
that Sanballat sendeth, also Geshem, unto me, saying, ’Come and e meet together in the villages, in the valley of Ono;’ and they are thinking to do to me evil.
And I send unto them messengers, saying, ’A great ork I am doing, and I am not able to come don; hy doth the ork cease hen I let it alone, and have come don unto you?’
and they send unto me, according to this ord, four times, and I return them [ord] according to this ord.
And Sanballat sendeth unto me, according to this ord, a fifth time, his servant, and an open letter in his hand;

it is ritten in it, ’Among the nations it hath been heard, and Gashmu is saying: Thou and the Jes are thinking to rebel, therefore thou art building the all, and thou hast been to them for a king — according to these ords!
And also, prophets thou hast appointed to call for thee in Jerusalem, saying, A king [is] in Judah, and no it is heard by the king according to these ords; and no come, and e take counsel together.’
And I send unto him, saying, ’It hath not been according to these ords that thou art saying, for from thine on heart thou art devising them;’
for all of them are making us afraid, saying, ’Their hands are too feeble for the ork, and it is not done;’ and no, strengthen Thou my hands.

And I have entered the house of Shemaiah son of Delaiah, son of Mehetabeel — and he is restrained — and he saith, ’Let us meet at the house of God, at the inside of the temple, and e shut the doors of the temple, for they are coming in to slay thee — yea, by night they are coming in to slay thee.’
And I say, ’A man such as I — doth he flee? and ho as I, that doth go in unto the temple, and live? — I do not go in.’
And I discern, and lo, God hath not sent him, for in the prophecy he hath spoken unto me both Tobiah and Sanballat hired him,
so that he [is] an hireling, that I may fear and do so, and I had sinned, and it had been to them for an evil name that they may reproach me.
Be mindful, O my God, of Tobiah, and of Sanballat, according to these his orks, and also, of Noadiah the prophetess, and of the rest of the prophets ho have been making me afraid.
And the all is completed in the tenty and fifth of Elul, on the fifty and second day;
and it cometh to pass, hen all our enemies have heard, and all the nations ho are round about us see, that they fall greatly in their on eyes, and kno that by our God hath this ork been done.
Also, in those days the freemen of Judah are multiplying their letters going unto Tobiah, and those of Tobiah are coming in unto them;
for many in Judah are sorn to him, for he [is] son-in-la to Shechaniah son of Arah, and Jehohanan his son hath taken the daughter of Meshullam son of Berechiah;
also, his good deeds they have been saying before me, and my ords they have been taking out to him; letters hath Tobiah sent to make me afraid.
And it cometh to pass, hen the all hath been built, that I set up the doors, and the gatekeepers are appointed, and the singers, and the Levites,
and I charge Hanani my brother, and Hananiah head of the palace, concerning Jerusalem — for he [is] as a man of truth, and fearing God above many —

and I say to them, ’Let not the gates of Jerusalem be opened till the heat of the sun, and hile they are standing by let them shut the doors, and fasten, and appoint guards of the inhabitants of Jerusalem, each in his guard, and each over-against his house.’
And the city [is] broad on both sides, and great, and the people [are] fe in its midst, and there are no houses builded;

and my God putteth it unto my heart, and I gather the freeman, and the prefects, and the people, for the genealogy, and I find a book of the genealogy of those coming up at the beginning, and I find ritten in it: —
These [are] sons of the province, those coming up of the captives of the removal that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon removed — and they turn back to Jerusalem and to Judah, each to his city —
ho are coming in ith Zerubbabel, Jeshua, Nehemiah, Azariah, Raamiah, Nahamani, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispereth, Bigvai, Nehum, Baanah. Number of the men of the people of Israel:

And they dell — the priests, and the Levites, and the gatekeepers, and the singers, and [some] of the people, and the Nethinim, and all Israel — in their cities, and the seventh month cometh, and the sons of Israel [are] in their cities.
And all the people are gathered as one man unto the broad place that [is] before the ater-gate, and they say to Ezra the scribe to bring the book of the la of Moses, that Jehovah commanded Israel.

And Ezra the scribe standeth on a toer of ood that they made for the purpose, and Mattithiah standeth near him, and Shema, and Anaiah, and Urijah, and Hilkiah, and Maaseiah, on his right; and on his left Pedaiah, and Mishael, and Malchijah, and Hashum, and Hashbaddana, Zechariah, Meshullam.
And Ezra openeth the book before the eyes of all the people — for above all the people he hath been — and at his opening [it] all the people have stood up,
and Ezra blesseth Jehovah, the great God, and all the people anser, ’Amen, Amen,’ ith lifting up of their hands, and they bo and do obeisance to Jehovah — faces to the earth.

And Jeshua, and Bani, and Sherebiah, Jamin, Akkub, Shabbethai, Hodijah, Maaseiah, Kelita, Azariah, Jozabad, Hanan, Pelaiah, and the Levites, giving the people understanding in the la, and the people, [are] on their station,
and they read in the book, in the la of God, explaining — so as to give the meaning, and they give understanding to the convocation.

And Nehemiah — he [is] the Tirshatha — saith (and Ezra the priest, the scribe, and the Levites ho are instructing the people) to all the people, ’To-day is holy to Jehovah your God, do not mourn, nor eep:’ for all the people are eeping at their hearing the ords of the la.

And he saith to them, ’Go, eat fat things, and drink seet things, and sent portions to him for hom nothing is prepared, for to-day [is] holy to our Lord, and be not grieved, for the joy of Jehovah is your strength.’
And the Levites are keeping all the people silent, saying, ’Be silent, for to-day [is] holy, and be not grieved.’
And all the people go to eat, and to drink, and to send portions, and to make great joy, because they have understood concerning the ords that they made knon to them.
And on the second day have been gathered heads of the fathers of all the people, the priests, and the Levites, unto Ezra the scribe, even to act isely concerning the ords of the la.
And they find ritten in the la that Jehovah commanded by the hand of Moses, that the sons of Israel dell in booths in the feast, in the seventh month,

And the people go out, and bring in, and make for themselves booths, each on his roof, and in their courts, and in the courts of the house of God, and in the broad place of the ater-gate, and in the broad place of the gate of Ephraim.

And they make — all the assembly of the captives of the captivity — booths, and they sit in booths; for the sons of Israel had not done, from the days of Jeshua son of Nun, so unto that day, and there is very great joy.
And he readeth in the book of the la of God day by day, from the first day till the last day, and they make a feast seven days, and on the eighth day a restraint, according to the ordinance.
And in the tenty and fourth day of this month have the sons of Israel been gathered, ith fasting, and ith sackcloth, and earth upon them;

and rise up on their station, and read in the book of the la of Jehovah their God a fourth of the day, and a fourth they are confessing and boing themselves to Jehovah their God.
And there stand up on the ascent, of the Levites, Jeshua, and Bani, Kadmiel, Shebaniah, Bunni, Sherebiah, Bani, Chenani, and they cry ith a loud voice unto Jehovah their God.

And the Levites say, [even] Jeshua, and Kadmiel, Bani, Hashabniah, Sherebiah, Hodijah, Shebaniah, Pethahiah, ’Rise, bless Jehovah your God, from the age unto the age, and they bless the name of Thine honour that [is] exalted above all blessing and praise.

Thou [art] He, O Jehovah, Thyself — Thou hast made the heavens, the heavens of the heavens, and all their host, the earth and all that [are] on it, the seas and all that [are] in them, and Thou art keeping all of them alive, and the host of the heavens to Thee are boing themselves.
’Thou [art] He, O Jehovah God, ho didst fix on Abraham, and didst bring him out from Ur of the Chaldeans, and didst make his name Abraham,

and didst find his heart stedfast before Thee, so as to make ith him the covenant, to give the land of the Canaanite, the Hittite, the Amorite, and the Perizzite, and the Jebusite, and the Girgashite, to give [it] to his seed. ’And Thou dost establish Thy ords, for Thou [art] righteous,
and dost see the affliction of our fathers in Egypt, and their cry hast heard by the sea of Suph,

and dost give signs and onders on Pharaoh, and on all his servants, and on all the people of his land, for Thou hast knon that they have acted proudly against them, and Thou makest to Thee a name as [at] this day.
And the sea Thou hast cleaved before them, and they pass over into the midst of the sea on the dry land, and their pursuers Thou hast cast into the depths, as a stone, into the strong aters.
And by a pillar of cloud Thou hast led them by day, and by a pillar of fire by night, to lighten to them the ay in hich they go.
’And on mount Sinai Thou hast come don, even to speak ith them from the heavens, and Thou dost give to them right judgments, and true las, good statutes and commands.

yea, they refuse to hearken, and have not remembered Thy onders that Thou hast done ith them, and harden their neck and appoint a head, to turn back to their service, in their rebellion; and Thou [art] a God of pardons, gracious, and merciful, long-suffering, and abundant in kindness, and hast not forsaken them.
’Also, hen they have made to themselves a molten calf, and say, this [is] thy god that brought thee up out of Egypt, and do great despisings,

and Thou, in Thine abundant mercies, hast not forsaken them in the ilderness — the pillar of the cloud hath not turned aside from off them by day, to lead them in the ay, and the pillar of the fire by night, to give light to them and the ay in hich they go.
’And Thy good Spirit Thou hast given, to cause them to act isely; and Thy manna Thou hast not ithheld from their mouth, and ater Thou hast given to them for their thirst,
and forty years Thou hast nourished them in a ilderness; they have not lacked; their garments have not orn out, and their feet have not selled.
’And Thou givest to them kingdoms, and peoples, and dost apportion them to the corner, and they possess the land of Sihon, and the land of the king of Heshbon, and the land of Og king of Bashan.
And their sons Thou hast multiplied as the stars of the heavens, and bringest them in unto the land that Thou hast said to their fathers to go in to possess.

’And the sons come in, and possess the land, and Thou humblest before them the inhabitants of the land, the Canaanites, and givest them into their hand, and their kings, and the peoples of the land, to do ith them according to their pleasure.

And they capture fenced cities, and fat ground, and possess houses full of all good, digged-ells, vineyards, and olive-yards, and fruit-trees in abundance, and they eat, and are satisfied, and become fat, and delight themselves in Thy great goodness.

’And they are disobedient, and rebel against Thee, and cast Thy la behind their back, and Thy prophets they have slain, ho testified against them, to bring them back unto Thee, and they do great despisings,

and Thou givest them into the hand of their adversaries, and they distress them, and in the time of their distress they cry unto Thee, and Thou, from the heavens, dost hear, and, according to Thine abundant mercies, dost give to them saviours, and they save them out of the hand of their adversaries.

’And hen they have rest, they turn back to do evil before Thee, and Thou dost leave them in the hand of their enemies, and they rule over them; and they turn back, and call Thee, and Thou from the heavens dost hear, and dost deliver them, according to Thy mercies, many times,

and dost testify against them, to bring them back unto Thy la; and they — they have acted proudly, and have not hearkened to Thy commands, and against Thy judgments have sinned, — hich man doth and hath lived in them — and they give a refractory shoulder, and their neck have hardened, and have not hearkened.

’And Thou draest over them many years, and testifiest against them by Thy Spirit, by the hand of Thy prophets, and they have not given ear, and Thou dost give them into the hand of peoples of the lands,
and in Thine abundant mercies Thou hast not made them a consumption, nor hast forsaken them; for a God, gracious and merciful, [art] Thou.

’And no, O our God — God, the great, the mighty, and the fearful, keeping the covenant and the kindness — let not all the travail that hath found us be little before Thee, for our kings, for our heads, and for our priests, and for our prophets, and for our fathers, and for all Thy people, from the days of the kings of Asshur unto this day;
and Thou [art] righteous concerning all that hath come upon us, for truth Thou hast done, and e have done ickedly;

’Lo, e — to-day — [are] servants, and the land that Thou hast given to our fathers, to eat its fruit and its good — lo, e [are] servants on it,

and its increase it is multiplying to the kings hom Thou hast set over us in our sins; and over our bodies they are ruling, and over our cattle, according to their pleasure, and e [are] in great distress.

And the rest of the people, the priests, the Levites, the gatekeepers, the singers, the Nethinim, and every one ho hath been separated from the peoples of the lands unto the la of God, their ives, their sons, and their daughters, every knoing intelligent one,

are laying hold on their brethren, their honourable ones, and coming in to an execration, and in to an oath, to alk in the la of God, that as given by the hand of Moses, servant of God, and to observe and to do all the commands of Jehovah our Lord, and His judgments, and His statutes;

and the priest, son of Aaron, hath been ith the Levites in the tithing of the Levites, and the Levites bring up the tithe of the tithe to the house of our God unto the chambers, to the treasure-house;

And of the Levites: Shemaiah son of Hashub, son of Azrikam, son of Hashabiah, son of Bunni,
and Shabbethai, and Jozabad, [are] over the outard ork of the house of God, of the heads of the Levites,

and Mattaniah son of Micha, son of Zabdi, son of Asaph, [is] head — at the commencement he giveth thanks in prayer; and Bakbukiah [is] second among his brethren, and Abda son of Shammua, son of Galal, son of Jeduthun.
All the Levites, in the holy city, [are] to hundred eighty and four.
And the gatekeepers, Akkub, Talmon, and their brethren, those atching at the gates, [are] a hundred seventy and to.
And the rest of Israel, of the priests, of the Levites, [are] in all cities of Judah, each in his inheritance;
and the Nethinim are delling in Ophel, and Ziha and Gishpa [are] over the Nethinim.
And the overseer of the Levites in Jerusalem [is] Uzzi son of Bani, son of Hashabiah, son of Mattaniah, son of Micha: of the sons of Asaph, the singers [are] over-against the ork of the house of God,
for the command of the king [is] upon them, and support [is] for the singers, a matter of a day in its day.
And Pethahiah son of Meshezabeel, of the sons of Zerah, son of Judah, [is] by the hand of the king, for every matter of the people.
And at the villages ith their fields, of the sons of Judah there have delt, in Kirjath-Arba and its small tons, and in Dibon and its small tons, and in Jekabzeel and its villages,
and in Jeshua, and in Moladah, and in Beth-Phelet,
and in Hazar-Shaul, and in Beer-Sheba and its small tons,
and in Ziklag, and in Mekonah and in its small tons,
and En-Rimmon, and in Zareah, and in Jarmuth,
Zanoah, Adullam, and their villages, Lachish and its fields, Azekah and its small tons; and they encamp from Beer-Sheba unto the valley of Hinnom.
And sons of Benjamin [are] at Geba, Michmash, and Aija, and Beth-El, and its small tons,
Anathoth, Nob, Ananiah,
Hazor, Ramah, Gittaim,
Hadid, Zeboim, Neballat,
Lod, and Ono, the valley of the artificers.
And of the Levites, the courses of Judah [are] for Benjamin.
And these [are] the priests and the Levites ho came up ith Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, and Jeshua; Seraiah, Jeremiah, Ezra,
Amariah, Malluch, Hattush,
Shechaniah, Rehum, Meremoth,
Iddo, Ginnethoi, Abijah,
Miamin, Maadiah, Bilgah,
Shemaiah, and Joiarib, Jedaiah,
Sallu, Amok, Hilkiah, Jedaiah; these [are] heads of the priests and of their brethren in the days of Jeshua.
And the Levites [are] Jeshua, Binnui, Kadmiel, Sherebiah, Judah, Mattaniah, he [is] over the thanksgiving, and his brethren,
and Bakbukiah and Unni, their brethren, [are] over-against them in charges.
And Jeshua hath begotten Joiakim, and Joiakim hath begotten Eliashib, and Eliashib hath begotten Joiada,
and Joiada hath begotten Jonathan, and Jonathan hath begotten Jaddua.
And in the days of Joiakim have been priests, heads of the fathers; of Seraiah, Meraiah; of Jeremiah, Hananiah;
of Ezra, Meshullam; of Amariah, Jehohanan;
of Melicu, Jonathan; of Shebaniah, Joseph;
of Harim, Adna; of Meraioth, Helkai;
of Iddo, Zechariah; of Ginnethon, Meshullam;
of Abijah, Zichri; of Miniamin; of Moadiah, Piltai;
of Bilgah, Shammua; of Shemaiah, Jehonathan;
and of Joiarib, Mattenai; of Jedaiah, Uzzi;
of Sallai, Kallai; of Amok, Eber;
of Hilkiah, Hashabiah; of Jedaiah, Nethaneel.
The Levites, in the days of Eliashib, Joiada, and Johanan, and Jaddua, are ritten, heads of fathers, and of the priests, in the kingdom of Darius the Persian.
Sons of Levi, heads of the fathers, are ritten on the book of the Chronicles even till the days of Johanan son of Eliashib;

and heads of the Levites: Hashabiah, Sherebiah, and Jeshua son of Kadmiel, and their brethren, [are] over-against them, to give praise, to give thanks, by command of David the man of God, charge over-against charge.
Mattaniah, and Bakbukiah, Obadiah, Meshullam, Talmon, Akkub, [are] gatekeepers, keeping charge in the gatherings of the gates.
These [are] in the days of Joiakim son of Jeshua, son of Jozadak, and in the days of Nehemiah the governor, and of Ezra the priest, the scribe.

And at the dedication of the all of Jerusalem they sought the Levites out of all their places, to bring them in to Jerusalem, to make the dedication even ith gladness, and ith thanksgivings, and ith singing, [ith] cymbals, psalteries, and ith harps;
and sons of the singers are gathered together even from the circuit round about Jerusalem, and from the villages of Netophathi,
and from the house of Gilgal, and from fields of Geba and Azmaveth, for villages have the singers built for themselves round about Jerusalem;
and the priests and the Levites are cleansed, and they cleanse the people, and the gates, and the all.
And I bring up the heads of Judah upon the all, and appoint to great thanksgiving companies and processions. At the right, on the all, to the dung-gate;
and after them goeth Hoshaiah, and half of the heads of Judah,
and Azariah, Ezra, and Meshullam,
Judah, and Benjamin, and Shemaiah, and Jeremiah;
and of the sons of the priests ith trumpets, Zechariah son of Jonathan, son of Shemaiah, son of Mattaniah, son of Michaiah, son of Zaccur, son of Asaph,
and his brethren Shemaiah, and Azarael, Milalai, Gilalai, Maai, Nethaneel, and Judah, Hanani, ith instruments of song of David the man of God, and Ezra the scribe [is] before them;
and by the gate of the fountain and over-against them, they have gone up by the steps of the city of David, at the going up of the all beyond the house of David, and unto the ater-gate eastard.
And the second thanksgiving company that is going over-against, and I after it, and half of the people on the all from beyond the toer of the furnaces and unto the broad all,
and from beyond the gate of Ephraim, and by the old-gate, and by the fish-gate, and the toer of Hananeel, and the toer of Meah, and unto the sheep-gate — and they have stood at the prison-gate.
And the to thanksgiving companies stand in the house of God, and I and half of the prefects ith me,
and the priests, Eliakim, Maaseiah, Miniamin, Michaiah, Elioenai, Zechariah, Hananiah, ith trumpets,
and Masseiah, and Shemaiah, and Eleazar, and Uzzi, and Jehohanan, and Malchijah, and Elam, and Ezer, and the singers sound, and Jezrahiah the inspector;

and they sacrifice on that day great sacrifices and rejoice, for God hath made them rejoice [ith] great joy, and also, the omen and the children have rejoiced, and the joy of Jerusalem is heard — unto a distance.

And certain are appointed on that day over the chambers for treasures, for heave-offerings, for first-fruits, and for tithes, to gather into them out of the fields of the cities the portions of the la for priests, and for Levites, for the joy of Judah [is] over the priests, and over the Levites, ho are standing up.
And the singers and the gatekeepers keep the charge of their God, even the charge of the cleansing — according to the command of David [and] Solomon his son,
for in the days of David and Asaph of old [ere] heads of the singers, and a song of praise and thanksgiving to God.

And all Israel in the days of Zerubbabel, and in the days of Nehemiah, are giving the portions of the singers, and of the gatekeepers, the matter of a day in its day, and are sanctifying to the Levites, and the Levites are sanctifying to the sons of Aaron.
On that day there as read in the book of Moses, in the ears of the people, and it hath been found ritten in it that an Ammonite and Moabite doth not come into the assembly of God — unto the age,
because they have not come before the sons of Israel ith bread and ith ater, and hire against them Balaam to revile them, and our God turneth the reviling into a blessing.
And it cometh to pass, at their hearing the la, that they separate all the mixed people from Israel.
And before this Eliashib the priest, appointed over chambers of the house of our God, [is] a relation of Tobiah,

and he maketh for him a great chamber, and there they ere formerly putting the present, the frankincense, and the vessels, and the tithe of the corn, the ne ine, and the oil — the commanded thing of the Levites, and the singers, and the gatekeepers — and the heave-offering of the priests.
And during all this I as not in Jerusalem, for in the thirty and second year of Artaxerxes king of Babylon did I come unto the king, and at the end of days I have asked of the king,
and I come in to Jerusalem, and understand concerning the evil that Eliashib hath done for Tobiah, to make to him a chamber in the courts of the house of God,
and it is very displeasing to me, and I cast all the vessels of the house of Tobiah ithout, out of the chamber,
and I speak, and they cleanse the chambers, and I bring back thither the vessels of the house of God ith the present and the frankincense.
