And I kno that the portions of the Levites have not been given, and they flee each to his field — the Levites and the singers, doing the ork.
And I strive ith the prefects, and say, ’Wherefore hath the house of God been forsaken?’ and I gather them, and set them on their station;
and all Judah have brought in the tithe of the corn, and of the ne ine, and of the oil, to the treasuries.

And I appoint treasurers over the treasuries, Shelemiah the priest, and Zadok the scribe, and Pedaiah of the Levites; and by their hand [is] Hanan son of Zaccur, son of Mattaniah, for stedfast they have been reckoned, and on them [it is] to give a portion to their brethren.
Be mindful of me, O my God, for this, and do not blot out my kind acts that I have done, for the house of my God, and for its charges.

In those days I have seen in Judah those treading ine-vats on sabbath, and bringing in the sheaves, and lading on the asses, and also, ine, grapes, and figs, and every burden, yea, they are bringing in to Jerusalem on the sabbath-day, and I testify in the day of their selling provision.
And the Tyrians have delt in it, bringing in fish, and every are, and selling on sabbath to the sons of Judah and in Jerusalem.
And I strive ith the freemen of Judah, and say to them, ’What [is] this evil thing that ye are doing, and polluting the sabbath-day?
Thus did not your fathers do? and our God bringeth in on us all this evil, and on this city, and ye are adding fierceness on Israel, to pollute the sabbath.’

And it cometh to pass, hen the gates of Jerusalem have been dark before the sabbath, that I speak, and the doors are shut, and I say, that they do not open them till after the sabbath; and of my servants I have stationed at the gates; there doth not come in a burden on the sabbath-day.
And they lodge — the merchants and sellers of all are — at the outside of Jerusalem, once or tice,
and I testify against them, and say unto them, ’Wherefore are ye lodging over-against the all? if ye repeat [it], a hand I put forth upon you;’ from that time they have not come in on the sabbath.

And I say to the Levites, that they be cleansed, and, coming in, keeping the gates, to sanctify the sabbath-day. Also, this, remember for me, O my God, and have pity on me, according to the abundance of Thy kindness.
Also, in those days, I have seen the Jes [ho] have settled omen of Ashdod, of Ammon, of Moab.
And of their sons, half are speaking Ashdoditish — and are not knoing to speak Jeish — and according to the language of people and people.

And I strive ith them, and declare them vile, and smite certain of them, and pluck off their hair, and cause them to sear by God, ’Ye do not give your daughters to their sons, nor do ye take of their daughters to your sons, and to yourselves.

’By these did not Solomon king of Israel sin? and among the many nations there as no king like him, and beloved by his God he as, and God maketh him king over all Israel — even him did the strange omen cause to sin.
And to you do e hearken to do all this great evil, to trespass against our God, to settle strange omen?’
And [one] of the sons of Joiada son of Eliashib the high priest, [is] son-in-la to Sanballat the Horonite, and I cause him to flee from off me.
Be mindful of them, O my God, for the redeemed of the priesthood, and the covenant of the priesthood, and of the Levites.
And I have cleansed them from every stranger, and appoint charges to priests and to Levites, each in his ork,
and for the ood-offering at appointed times, and for first-fruits. Be mindful of me, O my God, for good.
And it cometh to pass, in the days of Ahasuerus — he [is] Ahasuerus ho is reigning from Hodu even unto Cush, seven and tenty and a hundred provinces —
in those days, at the sitting of the king Ahasuerus on the throne of his kingdom, that [is] in Shushan the palace,
in the third year of his reign, he hath made a banquet to all his heads and his servants; of the force of Persia and Media, the chiefs and heads of the provinces [are] before him,
in his sheing the ealth of the honour of his kingdom, and the glory of the beauty of his greatness, many days — eighty and a hundred days.

And at the fulness of these days hath the king made to all the people ho are found in Shushan the palace, from great even unto small, a banquet, seven days, in the court of the garden of the house of the king —

hite linen, hite cotton, and blue, fastened ith cords of fine linen and purple on rings of silver, and pillars of marble, couches of gold, and of silver, on a pavement of smaragdus, and hite marble, and mother-of-pearl, and black marble —
and the giving of drink in vessels of gold, and the vessels [are] divers vessels, and the royal ine [is] abundant, as a memorial of the king.
And the drinking [is] according to la, none is pressing, for so hath the king appointed for every chief one of his house, to do according to the pleasure of man and man.
Also Vashti the queen hath made a banquet for omen, in the royal house that the king Ahasuerus hath.

On the seventh day, as the heart of the king is glad ith ine, he hath said to Mehuman, Biztha, Harbona, Bigtha, and Abagtha, Zethar, and Carcas, the seven eunuchs ho are ministering in the presence of the king Ahasuerus,
to bring in Vashti the queen before the king, ith a royal cron, to she the peoples and the heads her beauty, for she [is] of good appearance,
and the queen Vashti refuseth to come in at the ord of the king that [is] by the hand of the eunuchs, and the king is very roth, and his fury hath burned in him.
And the king saith to ise men, knoing the times — for so [is] the ord of the king before all knoing la and judgment,
and he ho is near unto him [is] Carshena, Shethar, Admatha, Tarshish, Meres, Marsena, Memucan, seven heads of Persia and Media seeing the face of the king, ho are sitting first in the kingdom —
’According to la, hat — to do ith queen Vashti, because that she hath not done the saying of the king Ahasuerus by the hand of the eunuchs?’

And Memucan saith before the king and the heads, ’Not against the king by himself hath Vashti the queen done perversely, but against all the heads, and against all the peoples that [are] in all provinces of the king Ahasuerus;

for go forth doth the ord of the queen unto all the omen, to render their husbands contemptible in their eyes, in their saying, The king Ahasuerus said to bring in Vashti the queen before him, and she did not come;
yea, this day do princesses of Persia and Media, ho have heard the ord of the queen, say [so] to all heads of the king, even according to the sufficiency of contempt and rath.

’If to the king [it be] good, there goeth forth a royal ord from before him, and it is ritten ith the las of Persia and Media, and doth not pass aay, that Vashti doth not come in before the king Ahasuerus, and her royalty doth the king give to her companion ho [is] better than she;
and the sentence of the king that he maketh hath been heard in all his kingdom — for it [is] great — and all the ives give honour to their husbands, from great even unto small.’
And the thing is good in the eyes of the king, and of the princes, and the king doth according to the ord of Memucan,

and sendeth letters unto all provinces of the king, unto province and province according to its riting, and unto people and people according to its tongue, for every man being head in his on house — and speaking according to the language of his people.
After these things, at the ceasing of the fury of the king Ahasuerus, he hath remembered Vashti, and that hich she did, and that hich hath been decreed concerning her;
and servants of the king, his ministers, say, ’Let them seek for the king young omen, virgins, of good appearance,

and the king doth appoint inspectors in all provinces of his kingdom, and they gather every young oman — virgin, of good appearance — unto Shushan the palace, unto the house of the omen, unto the hand of Hege eunuch of the king, keeper of the omen, and to give their purifications,
and the young oman ho is good in the eyes of the king doth reign instead of Vashti;’ and the thing is good in the eyes of the king, and he doth so.
A man, a Je, there hath been in Shushan the palace, and his name [is] Mordecai son of Jair, son of Shimei, son of Kish, a Benjamite —
ho had been removed from Jerusalem ith the removal that as removed ith Jeconiah king of Judah, hom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon removed —

and he is supporting Hadassah — she [is] Esther — daughter of his uncle, for she hath neither father nor mother, and the young oman [is] of fair form, and of good appearance, and at the death of her father and her mother hath Mordecai taken her to him for a daughter.

And it cometh to pass, in the ord of the king, even his la, being heard, and in many young omen being gathered unto Shushan the palace, unto the hand of Hegai, that Esther is taken unto the house of the king, unto the hand of Hegai, keeper of the omen,

and the young oman is good in his eyes, and she receiveth kindness before him, and he hasteneth her purifications and her portions — to give to her, and the seven young omen ho are provided — to give to her, from the house of the king, and he changeth her and her young omen to a good [place in] the house of the omen.
Esther hath not declared her people, and her kindred, for Mordecai hath laid a charge on her that she doth not declare [it];
and during every day Mordecai is alking up and don before the court of the house of the omen to kno the elfare of Esther, and hat is done ith her.

And in the draing nigh of the turn of each young oman to come in unto the king Ahasuerus, at the end of there being to her — according to the la of the omen — telve months, for so they fulfil the days of their purifications; six months ith oil of myrrh, and six months ith spices, and ith the purifications of omen,
and ith this the young oman hath come in unto the king, all that she saith is given to her, to go in ith her, out of the house of the omen, unto the house of the king;

in the evening she hath gone in, and in the morning she hath turned back unto the second house of the omen, unto the hand of Shaashgaz eunuch of the king, keeper of the concubines; she cometh not in any more unto the king except the king hath delighted in her, and she hath been called by name.

And in the draing nigh of the turn of Esther — daughter of Abihail, uncle of Mordecai, hom he had taken to him for a daughter — to come in unto the king, she hath not sought a thing except that hich Hegai eunuch of the king, keeper of the omen, saith, and Esther is receiving grace in the eyes of all seeing her.
And Esther is taken unto the king Ahasuerus, unto his royal house, in the tenth month — it [is] the month of Tebeth — in the seventh year of his reign,

and the king loveth Esther above all the omen, and she receiveth grace and kindness before him above all the virgins, and he setteth a royal cron on her head, and causeth her to reign instead of Vashti,
and the king maketh a great banquet to all his heads and his servants — the banquet of Esther — and a release to the provinces hath made, and giveth gifts as a memorial of the king.
And in the virgins being gathered a second time, then Mordecai is sitting in the gate of the king;
Esther is not declaring her kindred and her people, as Mordecai hath laid a charge upon her, and the saying of Mordecai Esther is doing as hen she as truly ith him.

In those days, hen Mordecai is sitting in the gate of the king, hath Bigthan been roth, and Teresh, (to of the eunuchs of the king, the keepers of the threshold,) and they seek to put forth a hand on king Ahasuerus,
and the thing is knon to Mordecai, and he declareth [it] to Esther the queen, and Esther speaketh to the king in the name of Mordecai,
and the thing is sought out, and found, and they are hanged both of them on a tree, and it is ritten in the book of the Chronicles before the king.
After these things hath the king Ahasuerus exalted Haman son of Hammedatha the Agagite, and lifteth him up, and setteth his throne above all the heads ho [are] ith him,
and all servants of the king, ho [are] in the gate of the king, are boing and doing obeisance to Haman, for so hath the king commanded for him; and Mordecai doth not bo nor do obeisance.
And the servants of the king, ho [are] in the gate of the king, say to Mordecai, ’Wherefore [art] thou transgressing the command of the king?’

And it cometh to pass, in their speaking unto him, day by day, and he hath not hearkened unto them, that they declare [it] to Haman, to see hether the ords of Mordecai do stand, for he hath declared to them that he [is] a Je.
And Haman seeth that Mordecai is not boing and doing obeisance to him, and Haman is full of fury,

and it is contemptible in his eyes to put forth a hand on Mordecai by himself, for they have declared to him the people of Mordecai, and Haman seeketh to destroy all the Jes ho [are] in all the kingdom of Ahasuerus — the people of Mordecai.

In the first month — it [is] the month of Nisan — in the telfth year of the king Ahasuerus, hath one caused to fall Pur (that [is] the lot) before Haman, from day to day, and from month to month, [to] the telfth, it [is] the month of Adar.

And Haman saith to the king Ahasuerus, ’There is one people scattered and separated among the peoples, in all provinces of thy kingdom, and their las [are] diverse from all people, and the las of the king they are not doing, and for the king it is not profitable to suffer them;
if to the king [it be] good, let it be ritten to destroy them, and ten thousand talents of silver I eigh into the hands of those doing the ork, to bring [it] in unto the treasuries of the king.’
And the king turneth aside his signet from off his hand, and giveth it to Haman son of Hammedatha the Agagite, adversary of the Jes;
and the king saith to Haman, ’The silver is given to thee, and the people, to do ith it as [it is] good in thine eyes.’

And scribes of the king are called, on the first month, on the thirteenth day of it, and it is ritten according to all that Haman hath commanded, unto lieutenants of the king, and unto the governors ho [are] over province and province, and unto the heads of people and people, province and province, according to its riting, and people and people according to its tongue, in the name of the king Ahasuerus it hath been ritten and sealed ith the signet of the king,

and letters to be sent by the hand of the runners unto all provinces of the king, to cut off, to slay, and to destroy all the Jes, from young even unto old, infant and omen, on one day, on the thirteenth of the telfth month — it [is] the month of Adar — and their spoil to seize,
a copy of the riting to be made la in every province and province is revealed to all the peoples, to be ready for this day.
The runners have gone forth, hastened by the ord of the king, and the la hath been given in Shushan the palace, and the king and Haman have sat don to drink, and the city Shushan is perplexed.
And Mordecai hath knon all that hath been done, and Mordecai rendeth his garments, and putteth on sackcloth and ashes, and goeth forth into the midst of the city and crieth — a cry loud and bitter,
and he cometh in unto the front of the gate of the king, but none is to come in unto the gate of the king ith a sackcloth-garment.

And in every province and province, the place here the ord of the king, even his la, is coming, a great mourning have the Jes, and fasting, and eeping, and lamenting: sackcloth and ashes are spread for many.

And young omen of Esther come in and her eunuchs, and declare [it] to her, and the queen is exceedingly pained, and sendeth garments to clothe Mordecai, and to turn aside his sackcloth from off him, and he hath not received [them].
And Esther calleth to Hatach, of the eunuchs of the king, hom he hath stationed before her, and giveth him a charge for Mordecai, to kno hat this [is], and herefore this [is].
And Hatach goeth out unto Mordecai, unto a broad place of the city, that [is] before the gate of the king,
and Mordecai declareth to him all that hath met him, and the explanation of the money that Haman said to eigh to the treasuries of the king for the Jes, to destroy them,

and the copy of the riting of the la that had been given in Shushan to destroy them he hath given to him, to she Esther, and to declare [it] to her, and to lay a charge on her to go in unto the king, to make supplication to him, and to seek from before him, for her people.
And Hatach cometh in and declareth to Esther the ords of Mordecai,
and Esther speaketh to Hatach, and chargeth him for Mordecai:

’All servants of the king, and people of the provinces of the king, do kno that any man and oman, ho cometh in unto the king, unto the inner court, ho is not called — one la [of] his [is] to put [them] to death, apart from him to hom the king holdeth out the golden sceptre, then he hath lived; and I — I have not been called to come in unto the king these thirty days.’
And they declare to Mordecai the ords of Esther,
and Mordecai speaketh to send back unto Esther: ’Do not think in thy soul to be delivered [in] the house of the king, more than all the Jes,

but if thou keep entirely silent at this time, respite and deliverance remaineth to the Jes from another place, and thou and the house of thy fathers are destroyed; and ho knoeth hether for a time like this thou hast come to the kingdom?’
And Esther speaketh to send back unto Mordecai:

’Go, gather all the Jes ho are found in Shushan, and fast for me, and do not eat nor drink three days, by night and by day; also I and my young omen do fast likeise, and so I go in unto the king, that [is] not according to la, and hen I have perished — I have perished.’
And Mordecai passeth on, and doth according to all that Esther hath charged upon him.

And it cometh to pass on the third day, that Esther putteth on royalty, and standeth in the inner-court of the house of the king over-against the house of the king, and the king is sitting on his royal throne, in the royal-house, over-against the opening of the house,

and it cometh to pass, at the king’s seeing Esther the queen standing in the court, she hath received grace in his eyes, and the king holdeth out to Esther the golden sceptre that [is] in his hand, and Esther draeth near, and toucheth the top of the sceptre.
And the king saith to her, ’What — to thee Esther, O queen? and hat thy request? unto the half of the kingdom — and it is given to thee.’
And Esther saith, ’If unto the king [it be] good, the king doth come in, and Haman, to-day, unto the banquet that I have made for him;’
and the king saith, ’Haste ye Haman — to do the ord of Esther;’ and the king cometh in, and Haman, unto the banquet that Esther hath made.
And the king saith to Esther, during the banquet of ine, ’What [is] thy petition? and it is given to thee; and hat thy request? unto the half of the kingdom — and it is done.’
And Esther ansereth and saith, ’My petition and my request [is]:

if I have found grace in the eyes of the king, and if unto the king [it be] good, to give my petition, and to perform my request, the king doth come, and Haman, unto the banquet that I make for them, and to-morro I do according to the ord of the king.’

And Haman goeth forth on that day rejoicing and glad in heart, and at Haman’s seeing Mordecai in the gate of the king, and he hath not risen nor moved for him, then is Haman full of fury against Mordecai.
And Haman forceth himself, and cometh in unto his house, and sendeth, and bringeth in his friends, and Zeresh his ife,

and Haman recounteth to them the glory of his ealth, and the abundance of his sons, and all that ith hich the king made him great, and ith hich he lifted him up above the heads and servants of the king.
And Haman saith, ’Yea, Esther the queen brought none in ith the king, unto the feast that she made, except myself, and also for to-morro I am called to her, ith the king,
and all this is not profitable to me, during all the time that I am seeing Mordecai the Je sitting in the gate of the king.’

And Zeresh his ife saith to him, and all his friends, ’Let them prepare a tree, in height fifty cubits, and in the morning speak to the king, and they hang Mordecai on it, and go thou in ith the king unto the banquet rejoicing;’ and the thing is good before Haman, and he prepareth the tree.
On that night hath the sleep of the king fled aay, and he saith to bring in the book of memorials of the Chronicles, and they are read before the king,
and it is found ritten that Mordecai had declared concerning Bigthana and Teresh, to of the eunuchs of the king, of the keepers of the threshold, ho sought to put forth a hand on king Ahasuerus.
And the king saith, ’What honour and greatness hath been done to Mordecai for this?’ And the servants of the king, his ministers, say, ’Nothing hath been done ith him.’
And the king saith, ’Who [is] in the court?’ — and Haman hath come in to the outer court of the house of the king, to say to the king to hang Mordecai on the tree that he had prepared for him —
and the servants of the king say unto him, ’Lo, Haman is standing in the court;’ and the king saith, ’Let him come in.’

And Haman cometh in, and the king saith to him, ’What — to do ith the man in hose honour the king hath delighted?’ And Haman saith in his heart, ’To hom doth the king delight to do honour more than myself?’
And Haman saith unto the king, ’The man in hose honour the king hath delighted,
let them bring in royal clothing that the king hath put on himself, and a horse on hich the king hath ridden, and that the royal cron be put on his head,

and to give the clothing and the horse into the hand of a man of the heads of the king, the chiefs, and they have clothed the man in hose honour the king hath delighted, and caused him to ride on the horse in a broad place of the city, and called before him: Thus it is done to the man in hose honour the king hath delighted.’

And the king saith to Haman, ’Haste, take the clothing and the horse, as thou hast spoken, and do so to Mordecai the Je, ho is sitting in the gate of the king; there doth not fall a thing of all that thou hast spoken.’

And Haman taketh the clothing, and the horse, and clothed Mordecai, and causeth him to ride in a broad place of the city, and calleth before him, ’Thus it is done to the man in hose honour the king hath delighted.’
And Mordecai turneth back unto the gate of the king, and Haman hath been hastened unto his house mourning, and ith covered head,

and Haman recounteth to Zeresh his ife, and to all his friends, all that hath met him, and his ise men say to him, and Zeresh his ife, ’If Mordecai [is] of the seed of the Jes, before hom thou hast begun to fall, thou art not able for him, but dost certainly fall before him.’
They are yet speaking ith him, and eunuchs of the king have come, and haste to bring in Haman unto the banquet that Esther hath made.
And the king cometh in, and Haman, to drink ith Esther the queen,

and the king saith to Esther also on the second day, during the banquet of ine, ’What [is] thy petition, Esther, O queen? and it is given to thee; and hat thy request? unto the half of the kingdom — and it is done.’
And Esther the queen ansereth and saith, ’If I have found grace in thine eyes, O king, and if to the king [it be] good, let my life be given to me at my petition, and my people at my request;

for e have been sold, I and my people, to cut off, to slay, and to destroy; and if for men-servants and for maid-servants e had been sold I had kept silent — but the adversity is not equal to the loss of the king.’
And the king Ahasuerus saith, yea, he saith to Esther the queen, ’Who [is] he — this one? and here [is] this one? — he hose heart hath filled him to do so?’
And Esther saith, ’The man — adversary and enemy — [is] this icked Haman;’ and Haman hath been afraid at the presence of the king and of the queen.

And the king hath risen, in his fury, from the banquet of ine, unto the garden of the house, and Haman hath remained to seek for his life from Esther the queen, for he hath seen that evil hath been determined against him by the king.

And the king hath turned back out of the garden of the house unto the house of the banquet of ine, and Haman is falling on the couch on hich Esther [is], and the king saith, ’Also to subdue the queen ith me in the house?’ the ord hath gone out from the mouth of the king, and the face of Haman they have covered.

And Harbonah, one of the eunuchs, saith before the king, ’Also lo, the tree that Haman made for Mordecai, ho spake good for the king, is standing in the house of Haman, in height fifty cubits;’ and the king saith, ’Hang him upon it.’
And they hang Haman upon the tree that he had prepared for Mordecai, and the fury of the king hath lain don.
On that day hath the king Ahasuerus given to Esther the queen the house of Haman, adversary of the Jes, and Mordecai hath come in before the king, for Esther hath declared hat he [is] to her,
and the king turneth aside his signet, that he hath caused to pass aay from Haman, and giveth it to Mordecai, and Esther setteth Mordecai over the house of Haman.

And Esther addeth, and speaketh before the king, and falleth before his feet, and eepeth, and maketh supplication to him, to cause the evil of Haman the Agagite to pass aay, and his device that he had devised against the Jes;
and the king holdeth out to Esther the golden sceptre, and Esther riseth, and standeth before the king,

and saith, ’If to the king [it be] good, and if I have found grace before him, and the thing hath been right before the king, and I [be] good in his eyes, let it be ritten to bring back the letters — a device of Haman son of Hammedatha the Agagite — that he rote to destroy the Jes ho [are] in all provinces of the king,
for ho do I endure hen I have looked on the evil that doth find my people? and ho do I endure hen I have looked on the destruction of my kindred?’

And the king Ahasuerus saith to Esther the queen, and to Mordecai the Je, ’Lo, the house of Haman I have given to Esther, and him they have hanged on the tree, because that he put forth his hand on the Jes,

and ye, rite ye for the Jes, as [it is] good in your eyes, in the name of the king, and seal ith the signet of the king — for the riting that is ritten in the name of the king, and sealed ith the signet of the king, there is none to turn back.’

And the scribes of the king are called, at that time, in the third month — it [is] the month of Sivan — in the three and tentieth of it, and it is ritten, according to all that Mordecai hath commanded, unto the Jes, and unto the lieutenants, and the governors, and the heads of the provinces, that [are] from Hodu even unto Cush, seven and tenty and a hundred provinces — province and province according to its riting, and people and people according to its tongue, and unto the Jes according to their riting, and according to their tongue.

And he riteth in the name of the king Ahasuerus, and sealeth ith the signet of the king, and sendeth letters by the hand of the runners ith horses, riders of the dromedary, the mules, the young mares,

that the king hath given to the Jes ho [are] in every city and city, to be assembled, and to stand for their life, to cut off, to slay, and to destroy the hole force of the people and province ho are distressing them, infants and omen, and their spoil to seize.
In one day, in all the provinces of the king Ahasuerus, on the thirteenth of the telfth month — it [is] the month of Adar —
a copy of the riting to be made la in every province and province is revealed to all the peoples, and for the Jes being ready at this day to be avenged of their enemies.
The runners, riding on the dromedary, [and] the mules, have gone out, hastened and pressed by the ord of the king, and the la hath been given in Shushan the palace.
And Mordecai ent out from before the king, in royal clothing of blue and hite, and a great cron of gold, and a garment of fine linen and purple, and the city of Shushan hath rejoiced and been glad;
to the Jes hath been light, and gladness, and joy, and honour,

and in every province and province, and in every city and city, the place here the ord of the king, even his la, is coming, gladness and joy [are] to the Jes, a banquet, and a good day; and many of the peoples of the land are becoming Jes, for a fear of the Jes hath fallen upon them.

And in the telfth month — it [is] the month of Adar — on the thirteenth day of it, in hich the ord of the king, even his la, hath come to be done, in the day that the enemies of the Jes had hoped to rule over them, and it is turned that the Jes rule over those hating them —

the Jes have been assembled in their cities, in all provinces of the king Ahasuerus, to put forth a hand on those seeking their evil, and no man hath stood in their presence, for their fear hath fallen on all the peoples.
And all heads of the provinces, and the lieutenants, and the governors, and those doing the ork that the king hath, are lifting up the Jes, for a fear of Mordecai hath fallen upon them;
for great [is] Mordecai in the house of the king, and his fame is going into all the provinces, for the man Mordecai is going on and becoming great.
And the Jes smite among all their enemies — a smiting of the sord, and slaughter, and destruction — and do ith those hating them according to their pleasure,
and in Shushan the palace have the Jes slain and destroyed five hundred men;
and Parshandatha, and Dalphon, and Aspatha,
and Poratha, and Adalia, and Aridatha,
and Parmashta, and Arisai, and Aridai, and Vajezatha,
ten sons of Haman son of Hammedatha, adversary of the Jes, they have slain, and on the prey they have not put forth their hand.
On that day hath come the number of the slain in Shushan the palace before the king,

and the king saith to Esther the queen, ’In Shushan the palace have the Jes slain and destroyed five hundred men, and the ten sons of Haman; in the rest of the provinces of the king hat have they done? and hat [is] thy petition? and it is given to thee; and hat thy request again? and it is done.’
And Esther saith, ’If to the king [it be] good, let it be given also to-morro, to the Jes ho [are] in Shushan, to do according to the la of to-day; and the ten sons of Haman they hang on the tree.’
And the king saith — ’to be done so;’ and a la is given in Shushan, and the ten sons of Haman they have hanged.
And the Jes ho [are] in Shushan are assembled also on the fourteenth day of the month of Adar, and they slay in Shushan three hundred men, and on the prey they have not put forth their hand.

And the rest of the Jes, ho [are] in the provinces of the king, have been assembled, even to stand for their life, and to rest from their enemies, and to slay among those hating them five and seventy thousand, and on the prey they have not put forth their hand;
on the thirteenth day of the month of Adar, even to rest on the fourteenth of it, and to make it a day of banquet and of joy.
And the Jes ho [are] in Shushan have been assembled, on the thirteenth day of it, and on the fourteenth of it, even to rest on the fifteenth of it, and to make it a day of banquet and of joy.

Therefore the Jes of the villages, ho are delling in cities of the villages, are making the fourteenth day of the month of Adar — joy and banquet, and a good day, and of sending portions one to another.
And Mordecai riteth these things, and sendeth letters unto all the Jes ho [are] in all provinces of the king Ahasuerus, ho are near and ho are far off,
to establish on them, to be keeping the fourteenth day of the month of Adar, and the fifteenth day of it, in every year and year,

as days on hich the Jes have rested from their enemies, and the month that hath been turned to them from sorro to joy, and from mourning to a good day, to make them days of banquet and of joy, and of sending portions one to another, and gifts to the needy.
And the Jes have received that hich they had begun to do, and that hich Mordecai hath ritten unto them,

because Haman son of Hammedatha the Agagite, adversary of all the Jes, had devised concerning the Jes to destroy them, and had caused to fall Pur — that [is] the lot — to crush them and to destroy them;
and in her coming in before the king, he said ith the letter, ’Let his evil device that he devised against the Jes turn back upon his on head,’ and they have hanged him and his sons on the tree,
therefore they have called these days Purim — by the name of the lot — therefore, because of all the ords of this letter, and hat they have seen concerning this, and hat hath come unto them,

the Jes have established and received upon them, and upon their seed, and upon all those joined unto them, and it doth not pass aay, to be keeping these to days according to their riting, and according to their season, in every year and year;

and these days are remembered and kept in every generation and generation, family and family, province and province, and city and city, and these days of Purim do not pass aay from the midst of the Jes, and their memorial is not ended from their seed.
And Esther the queen, daughter of Abihail, riteth, and Mordecai the Je, ith all might, to establish this second letter of Purim,
and he sendeth letters unto all the Jes, unto the seven and tenty and a hundred provinces of the kingdom of Ahasuerus — ords of peace and truth —

to establish these days of Purim, in their seasons, as Mordecai the Je hath established on them, and Esther the queen, and as they had established on themselves, and on their seed — matters of the fastings, and of their cry.
And a saying of Esther hath established these matters of Purim, and it is ritten in the Book.
And the king Ahasuerus setteth a tribute on the land and the isles of the sea;

and all the ork of his strength, and his might, and the explanation of the greatness of Mordecai ith hich the king made him great, are they not ritten on the book of the Chronicles of Media and Persia?
For Mordecai the Je [is] second to king Ahasuerus, and a great man of the Jes, and accepted of the multitude of his brethren, seeking good for his people, and speaking peace to all his seed.
A man there hath been in the land of Uz — Job his name — and that man hath been perfect and upright — both fearing God, and turning aside from evil.
And there are borne to him seven sons and three daughters,

and his substance is seven thousand sheep, and three thousand camels, and five hundred pairs of oxen, and five hundred she-asses, and a service very abundant; and that man is greater than any of the sons of the east.
And his sons have gone and made a banquet — the house of each [in] his day — and have sent and called to their three sisters to eat and to drink ith them;

and it cometh to pass, hen they have gone round the days of the banquet, that Job doth send and sanctify them, and hath risen early in the morning, and caused to ascend burnt-offerings — the number of them all — for Job said, ’Perhaps my sons have sinned, yet blessed God in their heart.’ Thus doth Job all the days.
And the day is, that sons of God come in to station themselves by Jehovah, and there doth come also the Adversary in their midst.
And Jehovah saith unto the Adversary, ’Whence comest thou?’ And the Adversary ansereth Jehovah and saith, ’From going to and fro in the land, and from alking up and don on it.’
And Jehovah saith unto the Adversary, ’Hast thou set thy heart against My servant Job because there is none like him in the land, a man perfect and upright, fearing God, and turning aside from evil?’
And the Adversary ansereth Jehovah and saith, ’For nought is Job fearing God?
Hast not Thou made a hedge for him, and for his house, and for all that he hath — round about?

The ork of his hands Thou hast blessed, and his substance hath spread in the land, and yet, put forth, I pray Thee, Thy hand, and strike against anything that he hath — if not: to Thy face he doth bless Thee!’
And Jehovah saith unto the Adversary, ’Lo, all that he hath [is] in thy hand, only unto him put not forth thy hand.’ And the Adversary goeth out from the presence of Jehovah.
And the day is, that his sons and his daughters are eating, and drinking ine, in the house of their brother, the first-born.
And a messenger hath come in unto Job and saith, ’The oxen have been ploing, and the she-asses feeding by their sides,
and Sheba doth fall, and take them, and the young men they have smitten by the mouth of the sord, and I am escaped — only I alone — to declare [it] to thee.’

While this [one] is speaking another also hath come and saith, ’Fire of God hath fallen from the heavens, and burneth among the flock, and among the young men, and consumeth them, and I am escaped — only I alone — to declare [it] to thee.’

While this [one] is speaking another also hath come and saith, ’Chaldeans made three heads, and rush on the camels, and take them, and the young men they have smitten by the mouth of the sord, and I am escaped — only I alone — to declare [it] to thee.’
While this [one] is speaking another also hath come and saith, ’Thy sons and thy daughters are eating, and drinking ine, in the house of their brother, the first-born.

And lo, a great ind hath come from over the ilderness, and striketh against the four corners of the house, and it falleth on the young men, and they are dead, and I am escaped — only I alone — to declare [it] to thee.’
And Job riseth, and rendeth his robe, and shaveth his head, and falleth to the earth, and doth obeisance,
and he saith, ’Naked came I forth from the omb of my mother, and naked I turn back thither: Jehovah hath given and Jehovah hath taken: let the name of Jehovah be blessed.’
In all this Job hath not sinned, nor given folly to God.
And the day is, that sons of God come in to station themselves by Jehovah, and there doth come also the Adversary in their midst to station himself by Jehovah.
And Jehovah saith unto the Adversary, ’Whence camest thou?’ And the Adversary ansereth Jehovah and saith, ’From going to and fro in the land, and from alking up and don in it.’

And Jehovah saith unto the Adversary, ’Hast thou set thy heart unto My servant Job because there is none like him in the land, a man perfect and upright, fearing God and turning aside from evil? and still he is keeping hold on his integrity, and thou dost move Me against him to sallo him up for nought!’
And the Adversary ansereth Jehovah and saith, ’A skin for a skin, and all that a man hath he doth give for his life.
Yet, put forth, I pray Thee, Thy hand, and strike unto his bone and unto his flesh — if not: unto Thy face he doth bless Thee!’
And Jehovah saith unto the Adversary, ’Lo, he [is] in thy hand; only his life take care of.’
And the Adversary goeth forth from the presence of Jehovah, and smiteth Job ith a sore ulcer from the sole of his foot unto his cron.
And he taketh to him a potsherd to scrape himself ith it, and he is sitting in the midst of the ashes.
And his ife saith to him, ’Still thou art keeping hold on thine integrity: bless God and die.’
And he saith unto her, ’As one of the foolish omen speaketh, thou speakest; yea, the good e receive from God, and the evil e do not receive.’ In all this Job hath not sinned ith his lips.

And three of the friends of Job hear of all this evil that hath come upon him, and they come in each from his place — Eliphaz the Temanite, and Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite — and they are met together to come in to bemoan him, and to comfort him;
and they lift up their eyes from afar and have not discerned him, and they lift up their voice and eep, and rend each his robe, and sprinkle dust on their heads — heavenard.
And they sit ith him on the earth seven days and seven nights, and there is none speaking unto him a ord hen they have seen that the pain hath been very great.
After this hath Job opened his mouth, and revileth his day.
And Job ansereth and saith: —
Let the day perish in hich I am born, And the night that hath said: ’A man-child hath been conceived.’
That day — let it be darkness, Let not God require it from above, Nor let light shine upon it.
Let darkness and death-shade redeem it, Let a cloud tabernacle upon it, Let them terrify it as the most bitter of days.
That night — let thick darkness take it, Let it not be united to days of the year, Into the number of months let it not come.
Lo! that night — let it be gloomy, Let no singing come into it.
Let the cursers of day mark it, Who are ready to ake up Leviathan.
Let the stars of its tilight be dark, Let it ait for light, and there is none, And let it not look on the eyelids of the dan.
Because it hath not shut the doors Of the omb that as mine! And hide misery from mine eyes.
Why from the omb do I not die? From the belly I have come forth and gasp!
Wherefore have knees been before me? And hat [are] breasts, that I suck?
For no, I have lain don, and am quiet, I have slept — then there is rest to me,
With kings and counsellors of earth, These building astes for themselves.
Or ith princes — they have gold, They are filling their houses [ith] silver.
(Or as a hidden abortion I am not, As infants — they have not seen light.)
There the icked have ceased troubling, And there rest do the earied in poer.
Together prisoners have been at ease, They have not heard the voice of an exactor,
Small and great [are] there the same. And a servant [is] free from his lord.
Why giveth He to the miserable light, and life to the bitter soul?
Who are aiting for death, and it is not, And they seek it above hid treasures.
Who are glad — unto joy, They rejoice hen they find a grave.
To a man hose ay hath been hidden, And hom God doth shut up?
For before my food, my sighing cometh, And poured out as aters [are] my roarings.
For a fear I feared and it meeteth me, And hat I as afraid of doth come to me.
I as not safe — nor as I quiet — Nor as I at rest — and trouble cometh!
And Eliphaz the Temanite ansereth and saith: —
Hath one tried a ord ith thee? — Thou art eary! And to keep in ords ho is able?
Lo, thou hast instructed many, And feeble hands thou makest strong.
The stumbling one do thy ords raise up, And boing knees thou dost strengthen.
But no, it cometh in unto thee, And thou art eary; It striketh unto thee, and thou art troubled.
Is not thy reverence thy confidence? Thy hope — the perfection of thy ays?
Remember, I pray thee, Who, being innocent, hath perished? And here have the upright been cut off?
As I have seen — ploughers of iniquity, And soers of misery, reap it!
From the breath of God they perish, And from the spirit of His anger consumed.
The roaring of a lion, And the voice of a fierce lion, And teeth of young lions have been broken.
An old lion is perishing ithout prey, And the helps of the lioness do separate.
And unto me a thing is secretly brought, And receive doth mine ear a little of it.
In thoughts from visions of the night, In the falling of deep sleep on men,
Fear hath met me, and trembling, And the multitude of my bones caused to fear.
And a spirit before my face doth pass, Stand up doth the hair of my flesh;
It standeth, and I discern not its aspect, A similitude [is] over-against mine eyes, Silence! and a voice I hear:
’Is mortal man than God more righteous? Than his Maker is a man cleaner?
Lo, in His servants He putteth no credence, Nor in His messengers setteth praise.’
Also — the inhabitants of houses of clay, (Whose foundation [is] in the dust, They bruise them before a moth.)
From morning to evening are beaten don, Without any regarding, for ever they perish.
Hath not their excellency been removed ith them? They die, and not in isdom!
Pray, call, is there any to anser thee? And unto hich of the holy ones dost thou turn?
For provocation slayeth the perverse, And envy putteth to death the simple,
I — I have seen the perverse taking root, And I mark his habitation straightay,
Far are his sons from safety, And they are bruised in the gate, And there is no deliverer.
Whose harvest the hungry doth eat, And even from the thorns taketh it, And the designing salloed their ealth.
For sorro cometh not forth from the dust, Nor from the ground springeth up misery.
For man to misery is born, And the sparks go high to fly.
Yet I — I inquire for God, And for God I give my ord,
Doing great things, and there is no searching. Wonderful, till there is no numbering.
Who is giving rain on the face of the land, And is sending aters on the out-places.
To set the lo on a high place, And the mourners have been high [in] safety.
Making void thoughts of the subtile, And their hands do not execute isdom.
Capturing the ise in their subtilty, And the counsel of restling ones as hastened,
By day they meet darkness, And as night — they grope at noon.
And He saveth the asted from their mouth, And from a strong hand the needy,
And there is hope to the poor, And perverseness hath shut her mouth.
Lo, the happiness of mortal man, God doth reprove him: And the chastisement of the Mighty despise not,
For He doth pain, and He bindeth up, He smiteth, and His hands heal.
In six distresses He delivereth thee, And in seven evil striketh not on thee.
In famine He hath redeemed thee from death, And in battle from the hands of the sord.
When the tongue scourgeth thou art hid, And thou art not afraid of destruction, When it cometh.
At destruction and at hunger thou mockest, And of the beast of the earth, Thou art not afraid.
(For ith sons of the field [is] thy covenant, And the beast of the field Hath been at peace ith thee.)
And thou hast knon that thy tent [is] peace, And inspected thy habitation, and errest not,
And hast knon that numerous [is] Thy seed, And thine offspring as the herb of the earth;
Thou comest in full age unto the grave, As the going up of a stalk in its season.
Lo, this — e searched it out — it [is] right, hearken; And thou, kno for thyself!
And Job ansereth and saith: —
O that my provocation ere thoroughly eighed, And my calamity in balances They ould lift up together!
For no, than the sands of the sea it is heavier, Therefore my ords have been rash.
For arros of the Mighty [are] ith me, Whose poison is drinking up my spirit. Terrors of God array themselves [for] me!
Brayeth a ild ass over tender grass? Loeth an ox over his provender?
Eaten is an insipid thing ithout salt? Is there sense in the drivel of dreams?
My soul is refusing to touch! They [are] as my sickening food.
O that my request may come, That God may grant my hope!
That God ould please — and bruise me, Loose His hand and cut me off!
And yet it is my comfort, (And I exult in pain — He doth not spare,) That I have not hidden The sayings of the Holy One.
What [is] my poer that I should hope? And hat mine end That I should prolong my life?
Is my strength the strength of stones? Is my flesh brazen?
Is not my help ith me, And substance driven from me?
To a despiser of his friends [is] shame, And the fear of the Mighty he forsaketh.
My brethren have deceived as a brook, As a stream of brooks they pass aay.
That are black because of ice, By them doth sno hide itself.
By the time they are arm they have been cut off, By its being hot they have been Extinguished from their place.
Turn aside do the paths of their ay, They ascend into emptiness, and are lost.
Passengers of Tema looked expectingly, Travellers of Sheba hoped for them.
They ere ashamed that one hath trusted, They have come unto it and are confounded.
Surely no ye have become the same! Ye see a donfall, and are afraid.
Is it because I said, Give to me? And, By your poer bribe for me?
And, Deliver me from the hand of an adversary? And, From the hand of terrible ones ransom me?
She me, and I — I keep silent, And hat I have erred, let me understand.
Ho poerful have been upright sayings, And hat doth reproof from you reprove?
For reproof — do you reckon ords? And for ind — sayings of the desperate.
Anger on the fatherless ye cause to fall, And are strange to your friend.
And, no, please, look upon me, Even to your face do I lie?
Turn back, I pray you, let it not be perverseness, Yea, turn back again — my righteousness [is] in it.
Is there in my tongue perverseness? Discerneth not my palate desirable things?
Is there not a arfare to man on earth? And as the days of an hireling his days?
As a servant desireth the shado, And as a hireling expecteth his age,
So I have been caused to inherit months of vanity, And nights of misery they numbered to me.
If I lay don then I said, ’When do I rise!’ And evening hath been measured, And I have been full of tossings till dan.
Clothed hath been my flesh [ith] orms, And a clod of dust, My skin hath been shrivelled and is loathsome,
My days sifter than a eaving machine, And they are consumed ithout hope.
Remember Thou that my life [is] a breath, Mine eye turneth not back to see good.
The eye of my beholder beholdeth me not. Thine eyes [are] upon me — and I am not.
Consumed hath been a cloud, and it goeth, So he ho is going don to Sheol cometh not up.
He turneth not again to his house, Nor doth his place discern him again.
Also I — I ithhold not my mouth — I speak in the distress of my spirit, I talk in the bitterness of my soul.
A sea -[monster] am I, or a dragon, That thou settest over me a guard?
When I said, ’My bed doth comfort me,’ He taketh aay in my talking my couch.
And thou hast affrighted me ith dreams, And from visions thou terrifiest me,
And my soul chooseth strangling, Death rather than my bones.
I have asted aay — not to the age do I live. Cease from me, for my days [are] vanity.
What [is] man that Thou dost magnify him? And that Thou settest unto him Thy heart?
And inspectest him in the mornings, In the evenings dost try him?
Ho long dost Thou not look from me? Thou dost not desist till I sallo my spittle.
I have sinned, hat do I to Thee, O atcher of man? Why hast Thou set me for a mark to Thee, And I am for a burden to myself — and hat?
Thou dost not take aay my transgression, And cause to pass aay mine iniquity, Because no, for dust I lie don: And Thou hast sought me — and I am not!
And Bildad the Shuhite ansereth and saith: —
Till hen dost thou speak these things? And a strong ind — sayings of thy mouth?
Doth God pervert judgment? And doth the Mighty One pervert justice?
If thy sons have sinned before Him, And He doth send them aay, By the hand of their transgression,
If thou dost seek early unto God, And unto the Mighty makest supplication,
If pure and upright thou [art], Surely no He aketh for thee, And hath completed The habitation of thy righteousness.
And thy beginning hath been small, And thy latter end is very great.
For, ask I pray thee of a former generation, And prepare to a search of their fathers,
(For of yesterday e [are], and e kno not, For a shado [are] our days on earth.)
Do they not she thee — speak to thee, And from their heart bring forth ords?
’Doth a rush ise ithout mire? A reed increase ithout ater?
While it [is] in its budding — uncropped, Even before any herb it ithereth.
So [are] the paths of all forgetting God, And the hope of the profane doth perish,
Whose confidence is loathsome, And the house of a spider his trust.
He leaneth on his house — and it standeth not: He taketh hold on it — and it abideth not.
Green he [is] before the sun, And over his garden his branch goeth out.
By a heap his roots are rapped, A house of stones he looketh for.
If [one] doth destroy him from his place, Then it hath feigned concerning him, I have not seen thee!
Lo, this [is] the joy of his ay, And from the dust others spring up.’
Lo, God doth not reject the perfect, Nor taketh hold on the hand of evil doers.
While he filleth ith laughter thy mouth, And thy lips ith shouting,
Those hating thee do put on shame, And the tent of the icked is not!
And Job ansereth and saith: —
Truly I have knon that [it is] so, And hat — is man righteous ith God?
If he delight to strive ith Him — He doth not anser him one of a thousand.
Wise in heart and strong in poer — Who hath hardened toard Him and is at peace?
Who is removing mountains, And they have not knon, Who hath overturned them in His anger.
Who is shaking earth from its place, And its pillars move themselves.
Who is speaking to the sun, and it riseth not, And the stars He sealeth up.
Stretching out the heavens by Himself, And treading on the heights of the sea,
Making Osh, Kesil, and Kimah, And the inner chambers of the south.
Doing great things till there is no searching, And onderful, till there is no numbering.
Lo, He goeth over by me, and I see not, And He passeth on, and I attend not to it.
Lo, He snatches aay, ho bringeth it back? Who saith unto Him, ’What dost Thou?’
God doth not turn back His anger, Under Him boed have proud helpers.
Ho much less do I — I anser Him? Choose out my ords ith Him?
Whom, though I ere righteous, I anser not, For my judgment I make supplication.
Though I had called and He ansereth me, I do not believe that He giveth ear [to] my voice.
Because ith a tempest He bruiseth me, And hath multiplied my ounds for nought.
He permitteth me not to refresh my spirit, But filleth me ith bitter things.
If of poer, lo, the Strong One; And if of judgment — ho doth convene me?
If I be righteous, Mine mouth doth declare me icked, Perfect I am! — it declareth me perverse.
Perfect I am! — I kno not my soul, I despise my life.
It is the same thing, therefore I said, ’The perfect and the icked He is consuming.’
If a scourge doth put to death suddenly, At the trial of the innocent He laugheth.
Earth hath been given Into the hand of the icked one. The face of its judges he covereth, If not — here, ho [is] he?
My days have been sifter than a runner, They have fled, they have not seen good,
They have passed on ith ships of reed, As an eagle darteth on food.
Though I say, ’I forget my talking, I forsake my corner, and I brighten up!’
I have been afraid of all my griefs, I have knon that Thou dost not acquit me.
I — I am become icked; hy [is] this? [In] vain I labour.
If I have ashed myself ith sno-ater, And purified ith soap my hands,
Then in corruption Thou dost dip me, And my garments have abominated me.
But if a man like myself — I anser him, We come together into judgment.
If there ere beteen us an umpire, He doth place his hand on us both.
He doth turn aside from off me his rod, And His terror doth not make me afraid,
I speak, and do not fear Him, But I am not right ith myself.
My soul hath been eary of my life, I leave off my talking to myself, I speak in the bitterness of my soul.
I say unto God, ’Do not condemn me, Let me kno hy Thou dost strive [ith] me.
Is it good for Thee that Thou dost oppress? That Thou despisest the labour of Thy hands, And on the counsel of the icked hast shone?
Eyes of flesh hast Thou? As man seeth — seest Thou?
As the days of man [are] Thy days? Thy years as the days of a man?
That Thou inquirest for mine iniquity, And for my sin seekest?
For Thou knoest that I am not icked, And there is no deliverer from Thy hand.
Thy hands have taken pains about me, And they make me together round about, And Thou salloest me up!
Remember, I pray Thee, That as clay Thou hast made me, And unto dust Thou dost bring me back.
Dost Thou not as milk pour me out? And as cheese curdle me?
Skin and flesh Thou dost put on me, And ith bones and sines dost fence me.
Life and kindness Thou hast done ith me. And Thy inspection hath preserved my spirit.
And these Thou hast laid up in Thy heart, I have knon that this [is] ith Thee.
If I sinned, then Thou hast observed me, And from mine iniquity dost not acquit me,
If I have done ickedly — oe to me, And righteously — I lift not up my head, Full of shame — then see my affliction,
And it riseth — as a lion Thou huntest me. And Thou turnest back — Thou sheest Thyself onderful in me.
Thou reneest Thy itnesses against me, And dost multiply Thine anger ith me, Changes and arfare [are] ith me.
And hy from the omb Hast Thou brought me forth? I expire, and the eye doth not see me.
As I had not been, I am, From the belly to the grave I am brought,
Are not my days fe? Cease then, and put from me, And I brighten up a little,
Before I go, and return not, Unto a land of darkness and death-shade,
A land of obscurity as thick darkness, Death-shade — and no order, And the shining [is] as thick darkness.’
And Zophar the Naamathite ansereth and saith: —
Is a multitude of ords not ansered? And is a man of lips justified?
Thy devices make men keep silent, Thou scornest, and none is causing blushing!
And thou sayest, ’Pure [is] my discourse, And clean I have been in Thine eyes.’
And yet, O that God had spoken! And doth open His lips ith thee.
And declare to thee secrets of isdom, For counsel hath foldings. And kno thou that God forgetteth for thee, [Some] of thine iniquity.
By searching dost thou find out God? Unto perfection find out the Mighty One?
Heights of the heavens! — hat dost thou? Deeper than Sheol! — hat knoest thou?
Longer than earth [is] its measure, And broader than the sea.
If He pass on, and shut up, and assemble, Who then dost reverse it?
For he hath knon men of vanity, And He seeth iniquity, And one doth not consider [it]!
And empty man is bold, And the colt of a ild ass man is born.
If thou — thou hast prepared thy heart, And hast spread out unto Him thy hands,
If iniquity [is] in thy hand, put it far off, And let not perverseness dell in thy tents.
For then thou liftest up thy face from blemish, And thou hast been firm, and fearest not.
For thou dost forget misery, As aters passed aay thou rememberest.
And above the noon doth age rise, Thou fliest — as the morning thou art.
And thou hast trusted because their is hope, And searched — in confidence thou liest don,
And thou hast rested, And none is causing trembling, And many have entreated thy face;
And the eyes of the icked are consumed, And refuge hath perished from them, And their hope [is] a breathing out of soul!
And Job ansereth and saith: —
Truly — ye [are] the people, And ith you doth isdom die.
I also have a heart like you, I am not fallen more than you, And ith hom is there not like these?
A laughter to his friend I am: ’He calleth to God, and He ansereth him,’ A laughter [is] the perfect righteous one.
A torch — despised in the thoughts of the secure Is prepared for those sliding ith the feet.
At peace are the tents of spoilers, And those provoking God have confidence, He into hose hand God hath brought.
And yet, ask, I pray thee, [One of] the beasts, and it doth she thee, And a fol of the heavens, And it doth declare to thee.
Or talk to the earth, and it sheeth thee, And fishes of the sea recount to thee:
’Who hath not knon in all these, That the hand of Jehovah hath done this?
In hose hand [is] the breath of every living thing, And the spirit of all flesh of man.’
Doth not the ear try ords? And the palate taste food for itself?
With the very aged [is] isdom, And [ith] length of days understanding.
With Him [are] isdom and might, To him [are] counsel and understanding.
Lo, He breaketh don, and it is not built up, He shutteth against a man, And it is not opened.
Lo, He keepeth in the aters, and they are dried up, And he sendeth them forth, And they overturn the land.
With Him [are] strength and isdom, His the deceived and deceiver.
Causing counsellors to go aay a spoil, And judges He maketh foolish.
The bands of kings He hath opened, And He bindeth a girdle on their loins.
Causing ministers to go aay a spoil And strong ones He overthroeth.
Turning aside the lip of the stedfast, And the reason of the aged He taketh aay.
Pouring contempt upon princes, And the girdle of the mighty He made feeble.
Removing deep things out of darkness, And He bringeth out to light death-shade.
Magnifying the nations, and He destroyeth them, Spreading out the nations, and He quieteth them.
Turning aside the heart Of the heads of the people of the land, And he causeth them to ander In vacancy — no ay!
They feel darkness, and not light, He causeth them to ander as a drunkard.
Lo, all — hath mine eye seen, Heard hath mine ear, and it attendeth to it.
According to your knoledge I have knon — also I. I am not fallen more than you.
Yet I for the Mighty One do speak, And to argue for God I delight.
And yet, ye [are] forgers of falsehood, Physicians of nought — all of you,
O that ye ould keep perfectly silent, And it ould be to you for isdom.
Hear, I pray you, my argument, And to the pleadings of my lips attend,
For God do ye speak perverseness? And for Him do ye speak deceit?
His face do ye accept, if for God ye strive?
Is [it] good that He doth search you, If, as one mocketh at a man, ye mock at Him?
He doth surely reprove you, if in secret ye accept faces.
Doth not His excellency terrify you? And His dread fall upon you?
Your remembrances [are] similes of ashes, For high places of clay your heights.
Keep silent from me, and I speak, And pass over me doth hat?
Wherefore do I take my flesh in my teeth? And my soul put in my hand?
Lo, He doth slay me — I ait not! Only, my ays unto His face I argue.
Also — He [is] to me for salvation, For the profane cometh not before Him.
Hear ye diligently my ord, And my declaration ith your ears.
Lo, I pray you, I have set in order the cause, I have knon that I am righteous.
Who [is] he that doth strive ith me? For no I keep silent and gasp.
Only to things, O God, do ith me: Then from Thy face I am not hidden.
Thy hand put far off from me, And Thy terror let not terrify me.
And call Thou, and I — I anser, Or — I speak, and anser Thou me.
Ho many iniquities and sins have I? My transgression and my sin let me kno.
Why dost Thou hide Thy face? And reckonest me for an enemy to Thee?
A leaf driven aay dost Thou terrify? And the dry stubble dost Thou pursue?
For Thou ritest against me bitter things, And causest me to possess iniquities of my youth:
And puttest in the stocks my feet, And observest all my paths, On the roots of my feet Thou settest a print,
And he, as a rotten thing, eareth aay, As a garment hath a moth consumed him.
Man, born of oman! Of fe days, and full of trouble!
As a floer he hath gone forth, and is cut off, And he fleeth as a shado and standeth not.
Also — on this Thou hast opened Thine eyes, And dost bring me into judgment ith Thee.
Who giveth a clean thing out of an unclean? not one.
If determined are his days, The number of his months [are] ith Thee, His limit Thou hast made, And he passeth not over;
Look aay from off him that he may cease, Till he enjoy as an hireling his day.
For there is of a tree hope, if it be cut don, That again it doth change, That its tender branch doth not cease.
If its root becometh old in the earth, And its stem doth die in the dust,
From the fragrance of ater it doth flourish, And hath made a crop as a plant.
And a man dieth, and becometh eak, And man expireth, and here [is] he?
Waters have gone aay from a sea, And a river becometh aste and dry.
And man hath lain don, and riseth not, Till the earing out of the heavens they aake not, Nor are roused from their sleep.
O that in Sheol Thou ouldest conceal me, Hide me till the turning of Thine anger, Set for me a limit, and remember me.
If a man dieth — doth he revive? All days of my arfare I ait, till my change come.
Thou dost call, and I — I anser Thee; To the ork of Thy hands Thou hast desire.
But no, my steps Thou numberest, Thou dost not atch over my sin.
Sealed up in a bag [is] my transgression, And Thou seest up mine iniquity.
And yet, a falling mountain asteth aay, And a rock is removed from its place.
Stones have aters orn aay, Their outpourings ash aay the dust of earth, And the hope of man Thou hast destroyed.
Thou prevailest [over] him for ever, and he goeth, He is changing his countenance, And Thou sendest him aay.
Honoured are his sons, and he knoeth not; And they are little, and he attendeth not to them.
Only — his flesh for him is pained, And his soul for him doth mourn.’
And Eliphaz the Temanite ansereth and saith: —
Doth a ise man anser [ith] vain knoledge? And fill [ith] an east ind his belly?
To reason ith a ord not useful? And speeches — no profit in them?
Yea, thou dost make reverence void, And dost diminish meditation before God.
For thy mouth teacheth thine iniquity, And thou chooseth the tongue of the subtile.
Thy mouth declareth thee icked, and not I, And thy lips testify against thee.
The first man art thou born? And before the heights ast thou formed?
Of the secret counsel of God dost thou hear? And ithdraest thou unto thee isdom?
What hast thou knon, and e kno not? Understandest thou — and it is not ith us?
Both the gray-headed And the very aged [are] among us — Greater than thy father [in] days.
Too fe for thee are the comforts of God? And a gentle ord [is] ith thee,
What — doth thine heart take thee aay? And hat — are thine eyes high?
For thou turnest against God thy spirit? And hast brought out ords from thy mouth:
What [is] man that he is pure, And that he is righteous, one born of oman?
Lo, in His holy ones He putteth no credence, And the heavens have not been pure in His eyes.
Also — surely abominable and filthy Is man drinking as ater perverseness.
I she thee — hearken to me — And this I have seen and declare:
Which the ise declare — And have not hid — from their fathers.
To them alone as the land given, And a stranger passed not over into their midst:
’All days of the icked he is paining himself, And fe years have been laid up for the terrible one.
A fearful voice [is] in his ears, In peace doth a destroyer come to him.
He believeth not to return from darkness, And atched [is] he for the sord.
He is andering for bread — ’Where [is] it?’ He hath knon that ready at his hand Is a day of darkness.
Terrify him do adversity and distress, They prevail over him As a king ready for a boaster.
For he stretched out against God his hand, And against the Mighty he maketh himself mighty.
He runneth unto Him ith a neck, With thick bosses of his shields.
For he hath covered his face ith his fat, And maketh vigour over [his] confidence.
And he inhabiteth cities cut off, houses not delt in, That have been ready to become heaps.
He is not rich, nor doth his ealth rise, Nor doth he stretch out on earth their continuance.
He turneth not aside from darkness, His tender branch doth a flame dry up, And he turneth aside at the breath of His mouth!
Let him not put credence in vanity, He hath been deceived, For vanity is his recompence.
Not in his day is it completed, And his bending branch is not green.
He shaketh off as a vine his unripe fruit, And casteth off as an olive his blossom.
For the company of the profane [is] gloomy, And fire hath consumed tents of bribery.
To conceive misery, and to bear iniquity, Even their heart doth prepare deceit.
And Job ansereth and saith: —
I have heard many such things, Miserable comforters [are] ye all.
Is there an end to ords of ind? Or hat doth embolden thee that thou anserest?
I also, like you, might speak, If your soul ere in my soul’s stead. I might join against you ith ords, And nod at you ith my head.
I might harden you ith my mouth, And the moving of my lips might be sparing.
If I speak, my pain is not restrained, And I cease — hat goeth from me?
Only, no, it hath earied me; Thou hast desolated all my company,
And Thou dost loathe me, For a itness it hath been, And rise up against me doth my failure, In my face it testifieth.
His anger hath torn, and he hateth me, He hath gnashed at me ith his teeth, My adversary sharpeneth his eyes for me.
They have gaped on me ith their mouth, In reproach they have smitten my cheeks, Together against me they set themselves.
God shutteth me up unto the perverse, And to the hands of the icked turneth me over.
At ease I have been, and he breaketh me, And he hath laid hold on my neck, And he breaketh me in pieces, And he raiseth me to him for a mark.
Go round against me do his archers. He splitteth my reins, and spareth not, He poureth out to the earth my gall.
He breaketh me — breach upon breach, He runneth upon me as a mighty one.
Sackcloth I have seed on my skin, And have rolled in the dust my horn.
My face is foul ith eeping, And on mine eyelids [is] death-shade.
Not for violence in my hands, And my prayer [is] pure.
O earth, do not thou cover my blood! And let there not be a place for my cry.
Also, no, lo, in the heavens [is] my itness, And my testifier in the high places.
My interpreter [is] my friend, Unto God hath mine eye dropped:
And he reasoneth for a man ith God, And a son of man for his friend.
When a fe years do come, Then a path I return not do I go.
My spirit hath been destroyed, My days extinguished — graves [are] for me.
If not — mockeries [are] ith me. And in their provocations mine eye lodgeth.
Place, I pray Thee, my pledge ith Thee; Who is he that striketh hand ith me?
For their heart Thou hast hidden From understanding, Therefore Thou dost not exalt them.
For a portion he sheeth friendship, And the eyes of his sons are consumed.
And he set me up for a proverb of the peoples, And a onder before them I am.
And dim from sorro is mine eye, And my members as a shado all of them.
Astonished are the upright at this, And the innocent against the profane Stirreth himself up.
And the righteous layeth hold [on] his ay, And the clean of hands addeth strength, And — dumb are they all.
Return, and come in, I pray you, And I find not among you a ise man.
My days have passed by, My devices have been broken off, The possessions of my heart!
Night for day they appoint, Light [is] near because of darkness.
If I ait — Sheol [is] my house, In darkness I have spread out my couch.
To corruption I have called: — ’Thou [art] my father.’ ’My mother’ and ’my sister’ — to the orm.
And here [is] no my hope? Yea, my hope, ho doth behold it?
[To] the parts of Sheol ye go don, If together on the dust e may rest.
And Bildad the Shuhite ansereth and saith: —
When do ye set an end to ords? Consider ye, and afterards do e speak.
Wherefore have e been reckoned as cattle? We have been defiled in your eyes!
(He is tearing himself in his anger.) For thy sake is earth forsaken? And removed is a rock from its place?
Also, the light of the icked is extinguished. And there doth not shine a spark of his fire.
The light hath been dark in his tent, And his lamp over him is extinguished.
Straitened are the steps of his strength, And cast him don doth his on counsel.
For he is sent into a net by his on feet, And on a snare he doth alk habitually.
Seize on the heel doth a gin, Prevail over him do the designing.
Hidden in the earth is his cord, And his trap on the path.
Round about terrified him have terrors, And they have scattered him — at his feet.
Hungry is his sorro, And calamity is ready at his side.
It consumeth the parts of his skin, Consume his parts doth death’s first-born.
Dran from his tent is his confidence, And it causeth him to step to the king of terrors.
It delleth in his tent — out of his provender, Scattered over his habitation is sulphur.
From beneath his roots are dried up, And from above cut off is his crop.
His memorial hath perished from the land, And he hath no name on the street.
They thrust him from light unto darkness, And from the habitable earth cast him out.
He hath no continuator, Nor successor among his people, And none is remaining in his dellings.
At this day esterns have been astonished And easterns have taken fright.
Only these [are] tabernacles of the perverse, And this the place God hath not knon.
And Job ansereth and saith: —
Till hen do ye afflict my soul, And bruise me ith ords?
These ten times ye put me to shame, ye blush not. Ye make yourselves strange to me —
And also — truly, I have erred, With me doth my error remain.
If, truly, over me ye magnify yourselves, And decide against me my reproach;
Kno no, that God turned me upside don, And His net against me hath set round,
Lo, I cry out — violence, and am not ansered, I cry aloud, and there is no judgment.
My ay He hedged up, and I pass not over, And on my paths darkness He placeth.
Mine honour from off me He hath stripped, And He turneth the cron from my head.
He breaketh me don round about, and I go, And removeth like a tree my hope.
And He kindleth against me His anger, And reckoneth me to Him as His adversaries.
Come in do His troops together, And they raise up against me their ay, And encamp round about my tent.
My brethren from me He hath put far off, And mine acquaintances surely Have been estranged from me.
Ceased have my neighbours And my familiar friends have forgotten me,
Sojourners of my house and my maids, For a stranger reckon me: An alien I have been in their eyes.
To my servant I have called, And he doth not anser, With my mouth I make supplication to him.
My spirit is strange to my ife, And my favours to the sons of my [mother’s] omb.
Also sucklings have despised me, I rise, and they speak against me.
Abominate me do all the men of my counsel, And those I have loved, Have been turned against me.
To my skin and to my flesh Cleaved hath my bone, And I deliver myself ith the skin of my teeth.
Pity me, pity me, ye my friends, For the hand of God hath stricken against me.
Why do you pursue me as God? And ith my flesh are not satisfied?
Who doth grant no, That my ords may be ritten? Who doth grant that in a book they may be graven?
With a pen of iron and lead — For ever in a rock they may be hen.
That — I have knon my Redeemer, The Living and the Last, For the dust he doth rise.
And after my skin hath compassed this [body], Then from my flesh I see God:
Whom I — I see on my side, And mine eyes have beheld, and not a stranger, Consumed have been my reins in my bosom.
But ye say, ’Why do e pursue after him?’ And the root of the matter hath been found in me.
Be ye afraid because of the sord, For furious [are] the punishments of the sord, That ye may kno that [there is] a judgment.
And Zophar the Naamathite ansereth and saith: —
Therefore my thoughts cause me to anser, And because of my sensations in me.
The chastisement of my shame I hear, And the spirit of mine understanding Doth cause me to anser:
This hast thou knon from antiquity? Since the placing of man on earth?
That the singing of the icked [is] short, And the joy of the profane for a moment,
Though his excellency go up to the heavens, And his head against a cloud he strike —
As his on dung for ever he doth perish, His beholders say: ’Where [is] he?’
As a dream he fleeth, and they find him not, And he is driven aay as a vision of the night,
The eye hath not seen him, and addeth not. And not again doth his place behold him.
His sons do the poor oppress, And his hands give back his ealth.
His bones have been full of his youth, And ith him on the dust it lieth don.
Though he doth seeten evil in his mouth, Doth hide it under his tongue,
Hath pity on it, and doth not forsake it, And keep it back in the midst of his palate,
His food in his boels is turned, The bitterness of asps [is] in his heart.
Wealth he hath salloed, and doth vomit it. From his belly God driveth it out.
Gall of asps he sucketh, Slay him doth the tongue of a viper.
He looketh not on rivulets, Floing of brooks of honey and butter.
He is giving back [hat] he laboured for, And doth not consume [it]; As a bulark [is] his exchange, and he exults not.
For he oppressed — he forsook the poor, A house he hath taken violently aay, And he doth not build it.
For he hath not knon ease in his belly. With his desirable thing he delivereth not himself.
There is not a remnant to his food, Therefore his good doth not stay.
In the fulness of his sufficiency he is straitened. Every perverse hand doth meet him.
It cometh to pass, at the filling of his belly, He sendeth forth against him The fierceness of His anger, Yea, He raineth on him in his eating.
He fleeth from an iron eapon, Pass through him doth a bo of brass.
One hath dran, And it cometh out from the body, And a glittering eapon from his gall proceedeth. On him [are] terrors.
All darkness is hid for his treasures, Consume him doth a fire not blon, Broken is the remnant in his tent.
Reveal do the heavens his iniquity, And earth is raising itself against him.
Remove doth the increase of his house, Poured forth in a day of His anger.
This [is] the portion of a icked man from God. And an inheritance appointed him by God.
And Job ansereth and saith: —
Hear ye diligently my ord, And this is your consolation.
Bear ith me, and I speak, And after my speaking — ye may deride.
I — to man [is] my complaint? and if [so], herefore May not my temper become short?
Turn unto me, and be astonished, And put hand to mouth.
Yea, if I have remembered, then I have been troubled. And my flesh hath taken fright.
Wherefore do the icked live? They have become old, Yea, they have been mighty in ealth.
Their seed is established, Before their face ith them, And their offspring before their eyes.
Their houses [are] peace ithout fear, Nor [is] a rod of God upon them.
His bullock hath eaten corn, and doth not loath. His co bringeth forth safely, And doth not miscarry.
They send forth as a flock their sucklings, And their children skip,
They lift [themselves] up at timbrel and harp, And rejoice at the sound of an organ.
They ear out in good their days, And in a moment [to] Sheol go don.
And they say to God, ’Turn aside from us, And the knoledge of Thy ays We have not desired.
What [is] the Mighty One that e serve Him? And hat do e profit hen e meet ith Him?’
Lo, not in their hand [is] their good, (The counsel of the icked Hath been far from me.)
Ho oft is the lamp of the icked extinguished, And come on them doth their calamity? Pangs He apportioneth in His anger.
They are as stra before ind, And as chaff a hurricane hath stolen aay,
God layeth up for his sons his sorro, He giveth recompense unto him — and he knoeth.
His on eyes see his destruction, And of the rath of the Mighty he drinketh.
For hat [is] his delight in his house after him, And the number of his months cut off?
To God doth [one] teach knoledge, And He the high doth judge?
This [one] dieth in his perfect strength, Wholly at ease and quiet.
His breasts have been full of milk, And marro his bones doth moisten.
And this [one] dieth ith a bitter soul, And have not eaten ith gladness.
Together — on the dust they lie don, And the orm doth cover them over.
Lo, I have knon your thoughts, And the devices against me ye do rongfully.
For ye say, ’Where [is] the house of the noble? And here the tent — The tabernacles of the icked?’
Have ye not asked those passing by the ay? And their signs do ye not kno?
That to a day of calamity is the icked spared. To a day of rath they are brought.
Who doth declare to his face his ay? And [for] that hich he hath done, Who doth give recompence to him?
And he — to the graves he is brought. And over the heap a atch is kept.
Seet to him have been the clods of the valley, And after him every man he draeth, And before him there is no numbering.
And ho do ye comfort me [ith] vanity, And in your ansers hath been left trespass?
And Eliphaz the Temanite ansereth and saith: —
To God is a man profitable, Because a ise man to himself is profitable?
Is it a delight to the Mighty One That thou art righteous? is it gain, That thou makest perfect thy ays?
Because of thy reverence Doth He reason [ith] thee? He entereth ith thee into judgment:
Is not thy ickedness abundant? And there is no end to thine iniquities.
For thou takest a pledge of thy brother for nought, And the garments of the naked Thou dost strip off.
Thou causest not the eary to drink ater, And from the hungry thou ithholdest bread.
As to the man of arm — he hath the earth, And the accepted of face — he delleth in it.
Widos thou hast sent aay empty, And the arms of the fatherless are bruised.
Therefore round about thee [are] snares, And trouble thee doth fear suddenly.
