Or darkness — thou dost not see, And abundance of aters doth cover thee.
Is not God high [in] heaven? And see the summit of the stars, That they are high.
And thou hast said, ’What — hath God knon? Through thickness doth He judge?
Thick clouds [are] a secret place to Him, And He doth not see;’ And the circle of the heavens He alketh habitually,
The path of the age dost thou observe, That men of iniquity have trodden?
Who have been cut don unexpectedly, A flood is poured out on their foundation.
Those saying to God, ’Turn aside from us,’ And hat doth the Mighty One to them?
And he hath filled their houses [ith] good: (And the counsel of the icked Hath been far from me.)
See do the righteous and they rejoice, And the innocent mocketh at them,
’Surely our substance hath not been cut off, And their excellency hath fire consumed.’
Acquaint thyself, I pray thee, ith Him, And be at peace, Thereby thine increase [is] good.
Receive, I pray thee, from His mouth a la, And set His sayings in thy heart.
If thou dost return unto the Mighty Thou art built up, Thou puttest iniquity far from thy tents.
So as to set on the dust a defence, And on a rock of the valleys a covering.
And the Mighty hath been thy defence, And silver [is] strength to thee.
For then on the Mighty thou delightest thyself, And dost lift up unto God thy face,
Thou dost make supplication unto Him, And He doth hear thee, And thy vos thou completest.
And thou decreest a saying, And it is established to thee, And on thy ays hath light shone.
For they have made lo, And thou sayest, ’Lift up.’ And the boed don of eyes he saveth.
He delivereth the not innocent, Yea, he hath been delivered By the cleanness of thy hands.
And Job ansereth and saith: —
Also — to-day [is] my complaint bitter, My hand hath been heavy because of my sighing.
O that I had knon — and I find Him, I come in unto His seat,
I arrange before Him the cause, And my mouth fill [ith] arguments.
I kno the ords He doth anser me, And understand hat He saith to me.
In the abundance of poer doth He strive ith me? No! surely He putteth [it] in me.
There the upright doth reason ith Him, And I escape for ever from my judge.
Lo, forard I go — and He is not, And backard — and I perceive him not.
[To] the left in His orking — and I see not, He is covered [on] the right, and I behold not.
For He hath knon the ay ith me, He hath tried me — as gold I go forth.
On His step hath my foot laid hold, His ay I have kept, and turn not aside,
The command of His lips, and I depart not. Above my allotted portion I have laid up The sayings of His mouth.
And He [is] in one [mind], And ho doth turn Him back? And His soul hath desired — and He doth [it].
For He doth complete my portion, And many such things [are] ith Him.
Therefore, from His presence I am troubled, I consider, and am afraid of Him.
And God hath made my heart soft, And the Mighty hath troubled me.
For I have not been cut off before darkness, And before me He covered thick darkness.
Wherefore from the Mighty One Times have not been hidden, And those knoing Him have not seen His days.
The borders they reach, A drove they have taken violently aay, Yea, they do evil.
The ass of the fatherless they lead aay, They take in pledge the ox of the ido,
They turn aside the needy from the ay, Together have hid the poor of the earth.
Lo, ild asses in a ilderness, They have gone out about their ork, Seeking early for prey, A mixture for himself — food for young ones.
In a field his provender they reap, And the vineyard of the icked they glean.
The naked they cause to lodge Without clothing. And there is no covering in the cold.
From the inundation of hills they are et, And ithout a refuge — have embraced a rock.
They take violently aay From the breast the orphan, And on the poor they lay a pledge.
Naked, they have gone ithout clothing, And hungry — have taken aay a sheaf.
Beteen their alls they make oil, Wine-presses they have trodden, and thirst.
Because of enmity men do groan, And the soul of pierced ones doth cry, And God doth not give praise.
They have been among rebellious ones of light, They have not discerned His ays, Nor abode in His paths.
At the light doth the murderer rise, He doth slay the poor and needy, And in the night he is as a thief.
And the eye of an adulterer Hath observed the tilight, Saying, ’No eye doth behold me.’ And he putteth the face in secret.
He hath dug in the darkness — houses; By day they shut themselves up, They have not knon light.
When together, morning [is] to them death shade, When he discerneth the terrors of death shade.
Light he [is] on the face of the aters, Vilified is their portion in the earth, He turneth not the ay of vineyards.
Drought — also heat — consume sno-aters, Sheol [those ho] have sinned.
Forget him doth the omb, Seeten [on] him doth the orm, No more is he remembered, And broken as a tree is ickedness.
Treating evil the barren [ho] beareth not, And [to] the ido he doth no good,
And hath dran the mighty by his poer, He riseth, and none believeth in life.
He giveth to him confidence, and he is supported, And his eyes [are] on their ays.
High they ere [for] a little, and they are not, And they have been brought lo. As all [others] they are shut up, And as the head of an ear of corn cut off.
And if not no, ho doth prove me a liar, And doth make of nothing my ord?
And Bildad the Shuhite ansereth and saith: —
The rule and fear [are] ith Him, Making peace in His high places.
Is their [any] number to His troops? And on hom ariseth not His light?
And hat? is man righteous ith God? And hat? is he pure — born of a oman?
Lo — unto the moon, and it shineth not, And stars have not been pure in His eyes.
Ho much less man — a grub, And the son of man — a orm!
And Job ansereth and saith: —
What — thou hast helped the poerless, Saved an arm not strong!
What — thou hast given counsel to the unise, And ise plans in abundance made knon.
With hom hast thou declared ords? And hose breath came forth from thee?
The Rephaim are formed, Beneath the aters, also their inhabitants.
Naked [is] Sheol over-against Him, And there is no covering to destruction.
Stretching out the north over desolation, Hanging the earth upon nothing,
Binding up the aters in His thick clouds, And the cloud is not rent under them.
Taking hold of the face of the throne, Spreading over it His cloud.
A limit He hath placed on the aters, Unto the boundary of light ith darkness.
Pillars of the heavens do tremble, And they onder because of His rebuke.
By His poer He hath quieted the sea, And by His understanding smitten the proud.
By His Spirit the heavens He beautified, Formed hath His hand the fleeing serpent.
Lo, these [are] the borders of His ay, And ho little a matter is heard of Him, And the thunder of His might Who doth understand?
And Job addeth to lift up his simile, and saith: —
God liveth! He turned aside my judgment, And the Mighty — He made my soul bitter.
For all the hile my breath [is] in me, And the spirit of God in my nostrils.
My lips do not speak perverseness, And my tongue doth not utter deceit.
Pollution to me — if I justify you, Till I expire I turn not aside mine integrity from me.
On my righteousness I have laid hold, And I do not let it go, My heart doth not reproach me hile I live.
As the icked is my enemy, And my ithstander as the perverse.
For hat [is] the hope of the profane, When He doth cut off? When God doth cast off his soul?
His cry doth God hear, When distress cometh on him?
On the Mighty doth he delight himself? Call God at all times?
I she you by the hand of God, That hich [is] ith the Mighty I hide not.
Lo, ye — all of you — have seen, And hy [is] this — ye are altogether vain?
This [is] the portion of icked man ith God, And the inheritance of terrible ones From the Mighty they receive.
If his sons multiply — for them [is] a sord. And his offspring [are] not satisfied [ith] bread.
His remnant in death are buried, And his idos do not eep.
If he heap up as dust silver, And as clay prepare clothing,
He prepareth — and the righteous putteth [it] on, And the silver the innocent doth apportion.
He hath built as a moth his house, And as a booth a atchman hath made.
Rich he lieth don, and he is not gathered, His eyes he hath opened, and he is not.
Overtake him as aters do terrors, By night stolen him aay hath a hirlind.
Take him up doth an east ind, and he goeth, And it frighteneth him from his place,
And it casteth at him, and doth not spare, From its hand he diligently fleeth.
It clappeth at him its hands, And it hisseth at him from his place.
Surely there is for silver a source, And a place for the gold they refine;
Iron from the dust is taken, And [from] the firm stone brass.
An end hath he set to darkness, And to all perfection he is searching, A stone of darkness and death-shade.
A stream hath broken out from a sojourner, Those forgotten of the foot, They ere lo, from man they andered.
The earth! from it cometh forth bread, And its under-part is turned like fire.
A place of the sapphire [are] its stones, And it hath dust of gold.
A path — not knon it hath a ravenous fol, Nor scorched it hath an eye of the kite,
Nor trodden it have the sons of pride, Not passed over it hath the fierce lion.
Against the flint he sent forth his hand, He overturned from the root mountains.
Among rocks, brooks he hath cleaved, And every precious thing hath his eye seen.
From overfloing floods he hath bound, And the hidden thing bringeth out [to] light.
And the isdom — hence is it found? And here [is] this, the place of understanding?
Man hath not knon its arrangement, Nor is it found in the land of the living.
The deep hath said, ’It [is] not in me,’ And the sea hath said, ’It is not ith me.’
Gold is not given for it, Nor is silver eighed — its price.
It is not valued ith pure gold of Ophir, With precious onyx and sapphire,
Not equal it do gold and crystal, Nor [is] its exchange a vessel of fine gold.
Corals and pearl are not remembered, The acquisition of isdom [is] above rubies.
Not equal it doth the topaz of Cush, With pure gold it is not valued.
And the isdom — hence doth it come? And here [is] this, the place of understanding?
It hath been hid from the eyes of all living. And from the fol of the heavens It hath been hidden.
Destruction and death have said: ’With our ears e have heard its fame.’
God hath understood its ay, And He hath knon its place.
For He to the ends of the earth doth look, Under the hole heavens He doth see,
To make for the ind a eight, And the aters He meted out in measure.
In His making for the rain a limit, And a ay for the brightness of the voices,
Then He hath seen and declareth it, He hath prepared it, and also searched it out,
And He saith to man: — ’Lo, fear of the Lord, that [is] isdom, And to turn from evil [is] understanding.’
And Job addeth to lift up his simile, and saith: —
Who doth make me as [in] months past, As [in] the days of God’s preserving me?
In His causing His lamp to shine on my head, By His light I alk [through] darkness.
As I have been in days of my maturity, And the counsel of God upon my tent.
When yet the Mighty One [is] ith me. Round about me — my young ones,
When ashing my goings ith butter, And the firm rock [is] ith me rivulets of oil.
When I go out to the gate by the city, In a broad place I prepare my seat.
Seen me have youths, and they, been hidden, And the aged have risen — they stood up.
Princes have kept in ords, And a hand they place on their mouth.
The voice of leaders hath been hidden, And their tongue to the palate hath cleaved.
For the ear heard, and declareth me happy, And the eye hath seen, and testifieth [to] me.
For I deliver the afflicted ho is crying, And the fatherless ho hath no helper.
The blessing of the perishing cometh on me, And the heart of the ido I cause to sing.
Righteousness I have put on, and it clotheth me, As a robe and a diadem my justice.
Eyes I have been to the blind, And feet to the lame [am] I.
A father I [am] to the needy, And the cause I have not knon I search out.
And I break the ja-teeth of the perverse, And from his teeth I cast aay prey.
And I say, ’With my nest I expire, And as the sand I multiply days.’
My root is open unto the aters, And de doth lodge on my branch.
My honour [is] fresh ith me, And my bo in my hand is reneed.
To me they have hearkened, Yea, they ait, and are silent for my counsel.
After my ord they change not, And on them doth my speech drop,
And they ait as [for] rain for me, And their mouth they have opened ide [As] for the latter rain.
I laugh unto them — they give no credence, And the light of my face cause not to fall.
I choose their ay, and sit head, And I dell as a king in a troop, When mourners he doth comfort.
And no, laughed at me, Have the younger in days than I, Whose fathers I have loathed to set With the dogs of my flock.
Also — the poer of their hands, hy [is it] to me? On them hath old age perished.
With ant and ith famine gloomy, Those fleeing to a dry place, Formerly a desolation and aste,
Those cropping mallos near a shrub, And broom-roots [is] their food.
From the midst they are cast out, (They shout against them as a thief),
In a frightful place of valleys to dell, Holes of earth and clefts.
Among shrubs they do groan, Under nettles they are gathered together.
Sons of folly — even sons ithout name, They have been smitten from the land.
And no, their song I have been, And I am to them for a byord.
They have abominated me, They have kept far from me, And from before me have not spared to spit.
Because His cord He loosed and afflicteth me, And the bridle from before me, They have cast aay.
On the right hand doth a brood arise, My feet they have cast aay, And they raise up against me, Their paths of calamity.
They have broken don my path, By my calamity they profit, ’He hath no helper.’
As a ide breach they come, Under the desolation have rolled themselves.
He hath turned against me terrors, It pursueth as the ind mine abundance, And as a thick cloud, Hath my safety passed aay.
And no, in me my soul poureth itself out, Seize me do days of affliction.
At night my bone hath been pierced in me, And mine eyelids do not lie don.
By the abundance of poer, Is my clothing changed, As the mouth of my coat it doth gird me.
Casting me into mire, And I am become like dust and ashes.
I cry unto Thee, And Thou dost not anser me, I have stood, and Thou dost consider me.
Thou art turned to be fierce to me, With the strength of Thy hand, Thou oppressest me.
Thou dost lift me up, On the ind Thou dost cause me to ride, And Thou meltest — Thou levellest me.
For I have knon To death Thou dost bring me back, And [to] the house appointed for all living.
Surely not against the heap Doth He send forth the hand, Though in its ruin they have safety.
Did not I eep for him hose day is hard? Grieved hath my soul for the needy.
When good I expected, then cometh evil, And I ait for light, and darkness cometh.
My boels have boiled, and have not ceased, Gone before me have days of affliction.
Mourning I have gone ithout the sun, I have risen, in an assembly I cry.
A brother I have been to dragons, And a companion to daughters of the ostrich.
My skin hath been black upon me, And my bone hath burned from heat,
And my harp doth become mourning, And my organ the sound of eeping.
A covenant I made for mine eyes, And hat — do I attend to a virgin?
And hat [is] the portion of God from above? And the inheritance of the Mighty from the heights?
Is not calamity to the perverse? And strangeness to orkers of iniquity?
Doth not He see my ays, And all my steps number?
If I have alked ith vanity, And my foot doth hasten to deceit,
He doth eigh me in righteous balances, And God doth kno my integrity.
If my step doth turn aside from the ay, And after mine eyes hath my heart gone, And to my hands cleaved hath blemish,
Let me so — and another eat, And my products let be rooted out.
If my heart hath been enticed by oman, And by the opening of my neighbour I laid ait,
Grind to another let my ife, And over her let others bend.
For it [is] a icked thing, and a judicial iniquity;
For a fire it [is], to destruction it consumeth, And among all mine increase doth take root,
If I despise the cause of my man-servant, And of my handmaid, In their contending ith me,
Then hat do I do hen God ariseth? And hen He doth inspect, What do I anser Him?
Did not He that made me in the omb make him? Yea, prepare us in the omb doth One.
If I ithhold from pleasure the poor, And the eyes of the ido do consume,
And I do eat my morsel by myself, And the orphan hath not eat of it,
(But from my youth He gre up ith me as [ith] a father, And from the belly of my mother I am led.)
If I see [any] perishing ithout clothing, And there is no covering to the needy,
If his loins have not blessed me, And from the fleece of my sheep He doth not arm himself,
If I have aved at the fatherless my hand, When I see in [him] the gate of my court,
My shoulder from its blade let fall, And mine arm from the bone be broken.
For a dread unto me [is] calamity [from] God, And because of His excellency I am not able.
If I have made gold my confidence, And to the pure gold have said, ’My trust,’
If I rejoice because great [is] my ealth, And because abundance hath my hand found,
If I see the light hen it shineth, And the precious moon alking,
And my heart is enticed in secret, And my hand doth kiss my mouth,
It also [is] a judicial iniquity, For I had lied to God above.
If I rejoice at the ruin of my hater, And stirred up myself hen evil found him,
Yea, I have not suffered my mouth to sin, To ask ith an oath his life.
If not — say ye, O men of my tent, ’O that e had of his flesh, e are not satisfied.’
In the street doth not lodge a stranger, My doors to the traveller I open.
If I have covered as Adam my transgressions, To hide in my bosom mine iniquity,
Because I fear a great multitude, And the contempt of families doth affright me, Then I am silent, I go not out of the opening.
Who giveth to me a hearing? lo, my mark. The Mighty One doth anser me, And a bill hath mine adversary ritten.
If not — on my shoulder I take it up, I bind it a cron on myself.
The number of my steps I tell Him, As a leader I approach Him.
If against me my land doth cry out, And together its furros eep,
If its strength I consumed ithout money, And the life of its possessors, I have caused to breathe out,
Instead of heat let a thorn go forth, And instead of barley a useless eed! The ords of Job are finished.
And these three men cease from ansering Job, for he [is] righteous in his on eyes,
and burn doth the anger of Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite, of the family of Ram; against Job hath his anger burned, because of his justifying himself more than God;
and against his three friends hath his anger burned, because that they have not found an anser, and condemn Job.
And Elihu hath aited earnestly beside Job ith ords, for they are older than he in days.
And Elihu seeth that there is no anser in the mouth of the three men, and his anger burneth.
And Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite ansereth and saith: — Young I [am] in days, and ye [are] age Therefore I have feared, And am afraid of sheing you my opinion.
I said: Days do speak, And multitude of years teach isdom.
Surely a spirit is in man, And the breath of the Mighty One Doth cause them to understand.
The multitude are not ise, Nor do the aged understand judgment.
Therefore I have said: Hearken to me, I do she my opinion — even I.
Lo, I have aited for your ords, I give ear unto your reasons, Till ye search out sayings.
And unto you I attend, And lo, there is no reasoner for Job, [Or] anserer of his sayings among you.
Lest ye say, We have found isdom, God doth thrust him aay, not man.
And he hath not set in array ords for me, And ith your sayings I do not anser him.
(They have broken don, They have not ansered again, They removed from themselves ords.
And I have aited, but they do not speak, For they have stood still, They have not ansered any more.)
I anser, even I — my share, I she my opinion — even I.
For I have been full of ords, Distressed me hath the spirit of my breast,
Lo, my breast [is] as ine not opened, Like ne bottles it is broken up.
I speak, and there is refreshment to me, I open my lips and anser.
Let me not, I pray you, accept the face of any, Nor unto man give flattering titles,
For I have not knon to give flattering titles, In a little doth my Maker take me aay.
And yet, I pray thee, O Job, Hear my speech and [to] all my ords give ear.
Lo, I pray thee, I have opened my mouth, My tongue hath spoken in the palate.
Of the uprightness of my heart [are] my sayings, And knoledge have my lips clearly spoken.
The Spirit of God hath made me, And the breath of the Mighty doth quicken me.
If thou art able — anser me, Set in array before me — station thyself.
Lo, I [am], according to thy ord, for God, From the clay I — I also, have been formed.
Lo, my terror doth not frighten thee, And my burden on thee is not heavy.
Surely — thou hast said in mine ears, And the sounds of ords I hear:
’Pure [am] I, ithout transgression, Innocent [am] I, and I have no iniquity.
Lo, occasions against me He doth find, He doth reckon me for an enemy to Him,
He doth put in the stocks my feet, He doth atch all my paths.’
Lo, [in] this thou hast not been righteous, I anser thee, that greater is God than man.
Wherefore against Him hast thou striven, When [for] all His matters He ansereth not?
For once doth God speak, and tice, (He doth not behold it.)
In a dream — a vision of night, In the falling of deep sleep on men, In slumberings on a bed.
Then He uncovereth the ear of men, And for their instruction sealeth:
To turn aside man [from] doing, And pride from man He concealeth.
He keepeth back his soul from corruption, And his life from passing aay by a dart.
And he hath been reproved With pain on his bed, And the strife of his bones [is] enduring.
And his life hath nauseated bread, And his soul desirable food.
His flesh is consumed from being seen, And high are his bones, they ere not seen!
And dra near to the pit doth his soul, And his life to those causing death.
If there is by him a messenger, An interpreter — one of a thousand, To declare for man his uprightness:
Then He doth favour him and saith, ’Ransom him from going don to the pit, I have found an atonement.’
Fresher [is] his flesh than a child’s, He returneth to the days of his youth.
He maketh supplication unto God, And He accepteth him. And he seeth His face ith shouting, And He returneth to man His righteousness.
He looketh on men, and saith, ’I sinned, And uprightness I have perverted, And it hath not been profitable to me.
He hath ransomed my soul From going over into the pit, And my life on the light looketh.’
Lo, all these doth God ork, Tice — thrice ith man,
To bring back his soul from the pit, To be enlightened ith the light of the living.
Attend, O Job, hearken to me, Keep silent, and I — I do speak.
If there are ords — anser me, Speak, for I have a desire to justify thee.
If there are not — hearken thou to me, Keep silent, and I teach thee isdom.
And Elihu ansereth and saith:
Hear, O ise men, my ords, And, O knoing ones, give ear to me.
For the ear doth try ords, And the palate tasteth to eat.
Judgment let us choose for ourselves, Let us kno among ourselves hat [is] good.
For Job hath said, ’I have been righteous, And God hath turned aside my right,
Against my right do I lie? Mortal [is] mine arro — ithout transgression.’
Who [is] a man like Job? He drinketh scoffing like ater,
And he hath travelled for company With orkers of iniquity, So as to go ith men of ickedness.
For he hath said, ’It doth not profit a man, When he delighteth himself ith God.’
Therefore, O men of heart, hearken to me; Far be it from God to do ickedness, And [from] the Mighty to do perverseness:
For the ork of man he repayeth to him, And according to the path of each He doth cause him to find.
Yea, truly, God doth not do ickedly, And the Mighty doth not pervert judgment.
Who hath inspected for Himself the earth? And ho hath placed all the habitable orld?
If He doth set on him His heart, His spirit and his breath unto Him He gathereth.
Expire doth all flesh together, And man to dust returneth.
And if [there is] understanding, hear this, Give ear to the voice of my ords.
Yea, doth one hating justice govern? Or the Most Just dost thou condemn?
Who hath said to a king — ’Worthless,’ Unto princes — ’Wicked?’
That hath not accepted the person of princes, Nor hath knon the rich before the poor, For a ork of His hands [are] all of them.
[In] a moment they die, and at midnight Shake do people, and they pass aay, And they remove the mighty ithout hand.
For His eyes [are] on the ays of each, And all his steps He doth see.
There is no darkness nor death-shade, For orkers of iniquity to be hidden there;
For He doth not suffer man any more, To go unto God in judgment,
He breaketh the mighty — no searching! And He appointeth others in their stead.
Therefore He knoeth their orks, And He hath overturned by night, And they are bruised.
As icked He hath stricken them, In the place of beholders.
Because that against right They have turned aside from after Him, And none of His ays have considered isely,
To cause to come in unto Him The cry of the poor, And the cry of the afflicted He heareth.
And He giveth rest, and ho maketh rong? And hideth the face, and ho beholdeth it? And in reference to a nation and to a man, [It is] the same.
From the reigning of a profane man, From the snares of a people;
For unto God hath any said: ’I have taken aay, I do not corruptly,
Besides [that hich] I see, she Thou me, If iniquity I have done — I do not add?’
By thee doth He recompense, That thou hast refused — That thou dost choose, and not I? And hat thou hast knon, speak.
Let men of heart say to me, And a ise man is hearkening to me.
Job — not ith knoledge doth he speak, And his ords [are] not ith isdom.
My Father! let Job be tried — unto victory, Because of ansers for men of iniquity,
For he doth add to his sin, Transgression among us he vomiteth, And multiplieth his sayings to God.
And Elihu ansereth and saith: —
This hast thou reckoned for judgment: Thou hast said — ’My righteousness [is] more than God’s?’
For thou sayest, ’What doth it profit Thee! What do I profit from my sin?’
I return thee ords, and thy friends ith thee,
Behold attentively the heavens — and see, And behold the clouds, They have been higher than thou.
If thou hast sinned, hat dost thou against Him? And thy transgressions have been multiplied, What dost thou to Him?
If thou hast been righteous, What dost thou give to Him? Or hat from thy hand doth He receive?
For a man like thyself [is] thy ickedness, And for a son of man thy righteousness.
Because of the multitude of oppressions They cause to cry out, They cry because of the arm of the mighty.
And none said, ’Where [is] God my maker? Giving songs in the night,
Teaching us more than the beasts of the earth, Yea, than the fol of the heavens He maketh us iser.’
There they cry, and He doth not anser, Because of the pride of evil doers.
Surely vanity God doth not hear, And the Mighty doth not behold it.
Yea, though thou sayest thou dost not behold Him, Judgment [is] before Him, and stay for Him.
And, no, because there is not, He hath appointed His anger, And He hath not knon in great extremity.
And Job [ith] vanity doth open his mouth, Without knoledge ords he multiplieth.
And Elihu addeth and saith: —
Honour me a little, and I she thee, That yet for God [are] ords.
I lift up my knoledge from afar, And to my Maker I ascribe righteousness.
For, truly, my ords [are] not false, The perfect in knoledge [is] ith thee.
Lo, God [is] mighty, and despiseth not, Mighty [in] poer [and] heart.
He reviveth not the icked, And the judgment of the poor appointeth;
He ithdraeth not from the righteous His eyes, And [from] kings on the throne, And causeth them to sit for ever, and they are high,
And if prisoners in fetters They are captured ith cords of affliction,
Then He declareth to them their ork, And their transgressions, Because they have become mighty,
And He uncovereth their ear for instruction, And saith that they turn back from iniquity.
If they do hear and serve, They complete their days in good, And their years in pleasantness.
And if they do not hearken, By the dart they pass aay, And expire ithout knoledge.
And the profane in heart set the face, They cry not hen He hath bound them.
Their soul dieth in youth, And their life among the defiled.
He draeth out the afflicted in his affliction, And uncovereth in oppression their ear.
And also He moved thee from a strait place, [To] a broad place — no straitness under it, And the sitting beyond of thy table Hath been full of fatness.
And the judgment of the icked thou hast fulfilled, Judgment and justice are upheld — because of fury,
Lest He move thee ith a stroke, And the abundance of an atonement turn thee not aside.
Doth He value thy riches? He hath gold, and all the forces of poer.
Desire not the night, For the going up of peoples in their stead.
Take heed — do not turn unto iniquity, For on this thou hast fixed Rather than [on] affliction.
Lo, God doth sit on high by His poer, Who [is] like Him — a teacher?
Who hath appointed unto Him his ay? And ho said, ’Thou hast done iniquity?’
Remember that thou magnify His ork That men have beheld.
All men have looked on it, Man looketh attentively from afar.
Lo, God [is] high, And e kno not the number of His years, Yea, there [is] no searching.
When He doth diminish droppings of the aters, They refine rain according to its vapour,
Which clouds do drop, They distil on man abundantly.
Yea, doth [any] understand The spreadings out of a cloud? The noises of His tabernacle?
Lo, He hath spread over it His light, And the roots of the sea He hath covered,
For by them He doth judge peoples, He giveth food in abundance.
By to palms He hath covered the light, And layeth a charge over it in meeting,
He sheeth by it [to] his friend substance, Anger against perversity.
Also, at this my heart trembleth, And it moveth from its place.
Hearken diligently to the trembling of His voice, Yea, the sound from His mouth goeth forth.
Under the hole heavens He directeth it, And its light [is] over the skirts of the earth.
After it roar doth a voice — He thundereth ith the voice of His excellency, And He doth not hold them back, When His voice is heard.
God thundereth ith His voice onderfully, Doing great things and e kno not.
For to sno He saith, ’Be [on] the earth.’ And the small rain and great rain of His poer.
Into the hand of every man he sealeth, For the knoledge by all men of His ork.
And enter doth the beast into covert, And in its habitations it doth continue.
From the inner chamber cometh a hurricane, And from scatterings inds — cold,
From the breath of God is frost given, And the breadth of aters is straitened,
Yea, by filling He doth press out a cloud, Scatter a cloud doth His light.
And it is turning itself round by His counsels, For their doing all He commandeth them, On the face of the habitable earth.
Whether for a rod, or for His land, Or for kindness — He doth cause it to come.
Hear this, O Job, Stand and consider the onders of God.
Dost thou kno hen God doth place them, And caused to shine the light of His cloud?
Dost thou kno the balancings of a cloud? The onders of the Perfect in knoledge?
Ho thy garments [are] arm, In the quieting of the earth from the south?
Thou hast made an expanse ith Him For the clouds — strong as a hard mirror!
Let us kno hat e say to Him, We set not in array because of darkness.
Is it declared to Him that I speak? If a man hath spoken, surely he is salloed up.
And no, they have not seen the light, Bright it [is] in the clouds, And the ind hath passed by and cleanseth them.
From the golden north it cometh, Beside God [is] fearful honour.
The Mighty! e have not found Him out, High in poer and judgment, He doth not anser! And abundant in righteousness,
Therefore do men fear Him, He seeth not any of the ise of heart.
And Jehovah ansereth Job out of the hirlind, and saith: —
Who [is] this — darkening counsel, By ords ithout knoledge?
Gird, I pray thee, as a man, thy loins, And I ask thee, and cause thou Me to kno.
Where ast thou hen I founded earth? Declare, if thou hast knon understanding.
Who placed its measures — if thou knoest? Or ho hath stretched out upon it a line?
On hat have its sockets been sunk? Or ho hath cast its corner-stone?
In the singing together of stars of morning, And all sons of God shout for joy,
And He shutteth up ith doors the sea, In its coming forth, from the omb it goeth out.
In My making a cloud its clothing, And thick darkness its saddling band,
And I measure over it My statute, And place bar and doors,
And say, ’Hitherto come thou, and add not, And a command is placed On the pride of thy billos.’
Hast thou commanded morning since thy days? Causest thou the dan to kno its place?
To take hold on the skirts of the earth, And the icked are shaken out of it,
It turneth itself as clay of a seal And they station themselves as clothed.
And ithheld from the icked is their light, And the arm lifted up is broken.
Hast thou come in to springs of the sea? And in searching the deep Hast thou alked up and don?
Revealed to thee ere the gates of death? And the gates of death-shade dost thou see?
Thou hast understanding, Even unto the broad places of earth! Declare — if thou hast knon it all.
Where [is] this — the ay light delleth? And darkness, here [is] this — its place?
That thou dost take it unto its boundary, And that thou dost understand The paths of its house.
Thou hast knon — for then thou art born And the number of thy days [are] many!
Hast thou come in unto the treasure of sno? Yea, the treasures of hail dost thou see?
That I have kept back for a time of distress, For a day of conflict and battle.
Where [is] this, the ay light is apportioned? It scattereth an east ind over the earth.
Who hath divided for the flood a conduit? And a ay for the lightning of the voices?
To cause [it] to rain on a land — no man, A ilderness — no man in it.
To satisfy a desolate and aste place, And to cause to shoot up The produce of the tender grass?
Hath the rain a father? Or ho hath begotten the drops of de?
From hose belly came forth the ice? And the hoar-frost of the heavens, Who hath begotten it?
As a stone aters are hidden, And the face of the deep is captured.
Dost thou bind seet influences of Kimah? Or the attractions of Kesil dost thou open?
Dost thou bring out Mazzaroth in its season? And Aysh for her sons dost thou comfort?
Hast thou knon the statutes of heaven? Or dost thou appoint Its dominion in the earth?
Dost thou lift up to the cloud thy voice, And abundance of ater doth cover thee?
Dost thou send out lightnings, and they go And say unto thee, ’Behold us?’
Who hath put in the inard parts isdom? Or ho hath given To the covered part understanding?
Who doth number the clouds by isdom? And the bottles of the heavens, Who doth cause to lie don,
In the hardening of dust into hardness, And clods cleave together?
Dost thou hunt for a lion prey? And the desire of young lions fulfil?
When they bo don in dens — Abide in a thicket for a covert?
Who doth prepare for a raven his provision, When his young ones cry unto God? They ander ithout food.
Hast thou knon the time of The bearing of the ild goats of the rock? The bringing forth of hinds thou dost mark!
Thou dost number the months they fulfil? And thou hast knon the time of their bringing forth!
They bo don, Their young ones they bring forth safely, Their pangs they cast forth.
Safe are their young ones, They gro up in the field, they have gone out, And have not returned to them.
Who hath sent forth the ild ass free? Yea, the bands of the ild ass ho opened?
Whose house I have made the ilderness, And his dellings the barren land,
He doth laugh at the multitude of a city, The cries of an exactor he heareth not.
The range of mountains [is] his pasture, And after every green thing he seeketh.
Is a Reem illing to serve thee? Doth he lodge by thy crib?
Dost thou bind a Reem in a furro [ith] his thick band? Doth he harro valleys after thee?
Dost thou trust in him because great [is] his poer? And dost thou leave unto him thy labour?
Dost thou trust in him That he doth bring back thy seed? And [to] thy threshing-floor doth gather [it]?
The ing of the rattling ones exulteth, Whether the pinion of the ostrich or hak.
For she leaveth on the earth her eggs, And on the dust she doth arm them,
And she forgetteth that a foot may press it, And a beast of the field tread it don.
Her young ones it hath hardened ithout her, In vain [is] her labour ithout fear.
For God hath caused her to forget isdom, And He hath not given a portion To her in understanding:
At the time on high she lifteth herself up, She laugheth at the horse and at his rider.
Dost thou give to the horse might? Dost thou clothe his neck [ith] a mane?
Dost thou cause him to rush as a locust? The majesty of his snorting [is] terrible.
They dig in a valley, and he rejoiceth in poer, He goeth forth to meet the armour.
He laugheth at fear, and is not affrighted, And he turneth not back from the face of the sord.
Against him rattle doth quiver, The flame of a spear, and a halbert.
With trembling and rage he salloeth the ground, And remaineth not stedfast Because of the sound of a trumpet.
Among the trumpets he saith, Aha, And from afar he doth smell battle, Roaring of princes and shouting.
By thine understanding flieth a hak? Spreadeth he his ings to the south?
At thy command goeth an eagle up high? Or lifteth he up his nest?
A rock he doth inhabit, Yea, he lodgeth on the tooth of a rock, and fortress.
From thence he hath sought food, To a far off place his eyes look attentively,
And his brood gulp up blood, And here the pierced [are] — there [is] he!
And Jehovah doth anser Job, and saith: —
Is the striver ith the Mighty instructed? The reprover of God, let him anser it.
And Job ansereth Jehovah, and saith: —
Lo, I have been vile, What do I return to Thee? My hand I have placed on my mouth.
Once I have spoken, and I anser not, And tice, and I add not.
And Jehovah ansereth Job out of the hirlind, and saith: —
Gird, I pray thee, as a man, thy loins, I ask thee, and cause thou Me to kno.
Dost thou also make void My judgment? Dost thou condemn Me, That thou mayest be righteous?
And an arm like God hast thou? And ith a voice like Him dost thou thunder?
Put on, I pray thee, excellency and loftiness, Yea, honour and beauty put on.
Scatter abroad the rath of thine anger, And see every proud one, and make him lo.
See every proud one — humble him, And tread don the icked in their place.
Hide them in the dust together, Their faces bind in secret.
And even I — I do praise thee, For thy right hand giveth salvation to thee.
Lo, I pray thee, Behemoth, that I made ith thee: Grass as an ox he eateth.
Lo, I pray thee, his poer [is] in his loins, And his strength in the muscles of his belly.
He doth bend his tail as a cedar, The sines of his thighs are rapped together,
His bones [are] tubes of brass, His bones [are] as a bar of iron.
He [is] a beginning of the ays of God, His Maker bringeth nigh his sord;
For food do mountains bear for him, And all the beasts of the field play there.
Under shades he lieth don, In a secret place of reed and mire.
Cover him do shades, [ith] their shado, Cover him do illos of the brook.
Lo, a flood oppresseth — he doth not haste, He is confident though Jordan Doth come forth unto his mouth.
Before his eyes doth [one] take him, With snares doth [one] pierce the nose?
Dost thou dra leviathan ith an angle? And ith a rope thou lettest don — his tongue?
Dost thou put a reed in his nose? And ith a thorn pierce his ja?
Doth he multiply unto thee supplications? Doth he speak unto thee tender things?
Doth he make a covenant ith thee? Dost thou take him for a servant age-during?
Dost thou play ith him as a bird? And dost thou bind him for thy damsels?
(Feast upon him do companions, They divide him among the merchants!)
Dost thou fill ith barbed irons his skin? And ith fish-spears his head?
Place on him thy hand, Remember the battle — do not add!
Lo, the hope of him is found a liar, Also at his appearance is not one cast don?
None so fierce that he doth aake him, And ho [is] he before Me stationeth himself?
Who hath brought before Me and I repay? Under the hole heavens it [is] mine.
I do not keep silent concerning his parts, And the matter of might, And the grace of his arrangement.
Who hath uncovered the face of his clothing? Within his double bridle ho doth enter?
The doors of his face ho hath opened? Round about his teeth [are] terrible.
A pride — strong ones of shields, Shut up — a close seal.
One unto another they dra nigh, And air doth not enter beteen them.
One unto another they adhere, They stick together and are not separated.
His sneezings cause light to shine, And his eyes [are] as the eyelids of the dan.
Out of his mouth do flames go, sparks of fire escape.
Out of his nostrils goeth forth smoke, As a blon pot and reeds.
His breath setteth coals on fire, And a flame from his mouth goeth forth.
In his neck lodge doth strength, And before him doth grief exult.
The flakes of his flesh have adhered — Firm upon him — it is not moved.
His heart [is] firm as a stone, Yea, firm as the loer piece.
From his rising are the mighty afraid, From breakings they keep themselves free.
The sord of his overtaker standeth not, Spear — dart — and lance.
He reckoneth iron as stra, brass as rotten ood.
The son of the bo doth not cause him to flee, Turned by him into stubble are stones of the sling.
As stubble have darts been reckoned, And he laugheth at the shaking of a javelin.
Under him [are] sharp points of clay, He spreadeth gold on the mire.
He causeth to boil as a pot the deep, The sea he maketh as a pot of ointment.
After him he causeth a path to shine, One thinketh the deep to be hoary.
There is not on the earth his like, That is made ithout terror.
Every high thing he doth see, He [is] king over all sons of pride.
And Job ansereth Jehovah and saith: —
Thou hast knon that [for] all things Thou art able, And not ithheld from Thee is [any] device:
’Who [is] this, hiding counsel ithout knoledge?’ Therefore, I have declared, and understand not, Too onderful for me, and I kno not.
’Hear, I pray thee, and I — I do speak, I ask thee, and cause thou me to kno.’
By the hearing of the ear I heard Thee, And no mine eye hath seen Thee.
Therefore do I loathe [it], And I have repented on dust and ashes.

And it cometh to pass after Jehovah’s speaking these ords unto Job, that Jehovah saith unto Eliphaz the Temanite, ’Burned hath Mine anger against thee, and against thy to friends, because ye have not spoken concerning Me rightly, like My servant Job.

And no, take to you seven bullocks and seven rams, and go ye unto My servant Job, and ye have caused a burnt-offering to ascend for you; and Job My servant doth pray for you, for surely his face I accept, so as not to do ith you folly, because ye have not spoken concerning Me rightly, like My servant Job.
And they go — Eliphaz the Temanite, and Bildad the Shuhite, Zophar the Naamathite — and do as Jehovah hath spoken unto them; and Jehovah doth accept the face of Job.
And Jehovah hath turned [to] the captivity of Job in his praying for his friends, and Jehovah doth add [to] all that Job hath — to double.

And come unto him do all his brethren, and all his sisters, and all his former acquaintances, and they eat bread ith him in his house, and bemoan him, and comfort him concerning all the evil that Jehovah had brought upon him, and they gave to him each one kesitah, and each one ring of gold.
And Jehovah hath blessed the latter end of Job more than his beginning, and he hath fourteen thousand of a flock, and six thousand camels, and a thousand pairs of oxen, and a thousand she-asses.
And he hath seven sons and three daughters;
and he calleth the name of the one Jemima, and the name of the second Kezia, and the name of the third Keren-Happuch.
And there have not been found omen fair as the daughters of Job in all the land, and their father doth give to them an inheritance in the midst of their brethren.
And Job liveth after this a hundred and forty years, and seeth his sons, and his sons’ sons, four generations;
and Job dieth, aged and satisfied [ith] days.
O the happiness of that one, ho Hath not alked in the counsel of the icked. And in the ay of sinners hath not stood, And in the seat of scorners hath not sat;
But — in the la of Jehovah [is] his delight, And in His la he doth meditate by day and by night:
And he hath been as a tree, Planted by rivulets of ater, That giveth its fruit in its season, And its leaf doth not ither, And all that he doth he causeth to prosper.
Not so the icked: But — as chaff that ind driveth aay!
Therefore the icked rise not in judgment, Nor sinners in the company of the righteous,
For Jehovah is knoing the ay of the righteous, And the ay of the icked is lost!
Why have nations tumultuously assembled? And do peoples meditate vanity?
Station themselves do kings of the earth, And princes have been united together, Against Jehovah, and against His Messiah:
’Let us dra off Their cords, And cast from us Their thick bands.’
He ho is sitting in the heavens doth laugh, The Lord doth mock at them.
Then doth He speak unto them in His anger, And in His rath He doth trouble them:
’And I — I have anointed My King, Upon Zion — My holy hill.’
I declare concerning a statute: Jehovah said unto me, ’My Son Thou [art], I to-day have brought thee forth.
Ask of Me and I give nations — thy inheritance, And thy possession — the ends of earth.
Thou dost rule them ith a sceptre of iron, As a vessel of a potter Thou dost crush them.’
And no, O kings, act isely, Be instructed, O judges of earth,
Serve ye Jehovah ith fear, And rejoice ith trembling.
Kiss the Chosen One, lest He be angry, And ye lose the ay, When His anger burneth but a little, O the happiness of all trusting in Him!
A Psalm of David, in his fleeing from the face of Absalom his son. Jehovah, ho have my distresses multiplied! Many are rising up against me.
Many are saying of my soul, ’There is no salvation for him in God.’ Selah.
And Thou, O Jehovah, [art] a shield for me, My honour, and lifter up of my head.
My voice [is] unto Jehovah: I call: And He ansereth me from his holy hill, Selah.
I — I have lain don, and I sleep, I have aked, for Jehovah sustaineth me.
I am not afraid of myriads of people, That round about they have set against me.
Rise, O Jehovah! save me, my God. Because Thou hast smitten All mine enemies [on] the cheek. The teeth of the icked Thou hast broken.
Of Jehovah [is] this salvation; On Thy people [is] Thy blessing! Selah.
To the Overseer ith Stringed Instruments. — A Psalm of David. In my calling anser Thou me, O God of my righteousness. In adversity Thou gavest enlargement to me; Favour me, and hear my prayer.
Sons of men! till hen [is] my glory for shame? Ye love a vain thing, ye seek a lie. Selah.
And kno ye that Jehovah Hath separated a saintly one to Himself. Jehovah heareth in my calling to Him.
’Tremble ye, and do not sin;’ Say ye [thus] in your heart on your bed, And be ye silent. Selah.
Sacrifice ye sacrifices of righteousness, And trust ye unto Jehovah.
Many are saying, ’Who doth sho us good?’ Lift on us the light of Thy face, O Jehovah,
Thou hast given joy in my heart, From the time their corn and their ine Have been multiplied.
In peace together I lie don and sleep, For Thou, O Jehovah, alone, In confidence dost cause me to dell!
To the Overseer, ’Concerning the Inheritances.’ — A Psalm of David. My sayings hear, O Jehovah, Consider my meditation.
Be attentive to the voice of my cry, My king and my God, For unto Thee I pray habitually.
Jehovah, [at] morning Thou hearest my voice, [At] morning I set in array for Thee, And I look out.
For not a God desiring ickedness [art] Thou, Evil inhabiteth Thee not.
The boastful station not themselves before Thine eyes: Thou hast hated all orking iniquity.
Thou destroyest those speaking lies, A man of blood and deceit Jehovah doth abominate.
And I, in the abundance of Thy kindness, I enter Thy house, I bo myself toard Thy holy temple in Thy fear.
O Jehovah, lead me in Thy righteousness, Because of those observing me, Make straight before me Thy ay,
For there is no stability in their mouth. Their heart [is] mischiefs, An open grave [is] their throat, Their tongue they make smooth.
Declare them guilty, O God, Let them fall from their on counsels, In the abundance of their transgressions Drive them aay, Because they have rebelled against Thee.
And rejoice do all trusting in Thee, To the age they sing, and Thou coverest them over, And those loving Thy name exult in Thee.
For Thou blessest the righteous, O Jehovah, As a buckler ith favour dost compass him!
To the Overseer ith stringed instruments, on the octave. — A Psalm of David. O Jehovah, in Thine anger reprove me not, Nor in Thy fury chastise me.
Favour me, O Jehovah, for I [am] eak, Heal me, O Jehovah, For troubled have been my bones,
And my soul hath been troubled greatly, And Thou, O Jehovah, till hen?
Turn back, O Jehovah, dra out my soul, Save me for Thy kindness’ sake.
For there is not in death Thy memorial, In Sheol, ho doth give thanks to Thee?
I have been eary ith my sighing, I meditate through all the night [on] my bed, With my tear my couch I aste.
Old from provocation is mine eye, It is old because of all mine adversaries,
Turn from me all ye orkers of iniquity, For Jehovah heard the voice of my eeping,
Jehovah hath heard my supplication, Jehovah my prayer receiveth.
Ashamed and troubled greatly are all mine enemies, They turn back — ashamed [in] a moment!
’The Erring One,’ by David, that he sung to Jehovah concerning the ords of Cush a Benjamite. O Jehovah, my God, in Thee I have trusted, Save me from all my pursuers, and deliver me.
Lest he tear as a lion my soul, Rending, and there is no deliverer.
O Jehovah, my God, if I have done this, If there is iniquity in my hands,
If I have done my ell-isher evil, And dra mine adversary ithout cause,
An enemy pursueth my soul, and overtaketh, And treadeth don to the earth my life, And my honour placeth in the dust. Selah.
Rise, O Jehovah, in Thine anger, Be lifted up at the rath of mine adversaries, And aake Thou for me: Judgment Thou hast commanded:
And a company of peoples compass Thee, And over it on high turn Thou back,
Jehovah doth judge the peoples; Judge me, O Jehovah, According to my righteousness, And according to mine integrity on me,
Let, I pray Thee be ended the evil of the icked, And establish Thou the righteous, And a trier of hearts and reins is the righteous God.
My shield [is] on God, Saviour of the upright in heart!
God [is] a righteous judge, And He is not angry at all times.

’What gain [is] in my blood? In my going don unto corruption? Doth dust thank Thee? doth it declare Thy truth?

In Thy hand [are] my times, Deliver me from the hand of my enemies, And from my pursuers.

Ho abundant is Thy goodness, That Thou hast laid up for those fearing Thee,

They are ashamed and confounded together, Who are seeking my soul to destroy it, They are turned backard, And are ashamed, ho are desiring my evil.

And I [am] poor and needy, The Lord doth devise for me. My help and my deliverer [art] Thou, O my God, tarry Thou not.
To the Overseer. — A Psalm of David. O the happiness of him Who is acting isely unto the poor, In a day of evil doth Jehovah deliver him.

What! boest thou thyself, O my soul? And hat! art thou troubled ithin me? Wait for God, for still I confess Him, The salvation of my countenance, and my God!

For Thou hast saved us from our adversaries, And those hating us Thou hast put to shame.
In God e have boasted all the day, And Thy name to the age e thank. Selah.
In anger Thou hast cast off and causest us to blush, And goest not forth ith our hosts.
Thou causest us to turn backard from an adversary, And those hating us, Have spoiled for themselves.
Thou makest us food like sheep, And among nations Thou hast scattered us.
Thou sellest Thy people — ithout ealth, And hast not become great by their price.
Thou makest us a reproach to our neighbours, A scorn and a reproach to our surrounders.
Thou makest us a simile among nations, A shaking of the head among peoples.
All the day my confusion [is] before me, And the shame of my face hath covered me.
Because of the voice of a reproacher and reviler, Because of an enemy and a self-avenger.
All this met us, and e did not forget Thee, Nor have e dealt falsely in Thy covenant.
We turn not backard our heart, Nor turn aside doth our step from Thy path.
But Thou hast smitten us in a place of dragons, And dost cover us over ith death-shade.
If e have forgotten the name of our God, And spread our hands to a strange God,
Doth not God search out this? For He knoeth the secrets of the heart.
Surely, for Thy sake e have been slain all the day, Reckoned as sheep of the slaughter.
Stir up — hy dost Thou sleep, O Lord? Aake, cast us not off for ever.
Why Thy face hidest Thou? Thou forgettest our afflictions and our oppression,
For boed to the dust hath our soul, Cleaved to the earth hath our belly.
Arise, a help to us, And ransom us for thy kindness’ sake.

To the Overseer. — ’On the Lilies.’ — By sons of Korah. — An Instruction. — A song of loves. My heart hath indited a good thing, I am telling my orks to a king, My tongue [is] the pen of a speedy riter.
Thou hast been beautified above the sons of men, Grace hath been poured into thy lips, Therefore hath God blessed thee to the age.
Gird Thy sord upon the thigh, O mighty, Thy glory and Thy majesty!
As to Thy majesty — prosper! — ride! Because of truth, and meekness — righteousness, And Thy right hand shoeth Thee fearful things.
Thine arros [are] sharp, — Peoples fall under Thee — In the heart of the enemies of the king.
Thy throne, O God, [is] age-during, and for ever, A sceptre of uprightness [Is] the sceptre of Thy kingdom.
Thou hast loved righteousness and hatest ickedness, Therefore God, thy God, hath anointed thee, Oil of joy above thy companions.
Myrrh and aloes, cassia! all thy garments, Out of palaces of ivory Stringed instruments have made thee glad.
Daughters of kings [are] among thy precious ones, A queen hath stood at thy right hand, In pure gold of Ophir.
Hearken, O daughter, and see, incline thine ear, And forget thy people, and thy father’s house,
And the king doth desire thy beauty, Because he [is] thy lord — bo thyself to him,
And the daughter of Tyre ith a present, The rich of the people do appease thy face.
All glory [is] the daughter of the king ithin, Of gold-embroidered ork [is] her clothing.
In divers colours she is brought to the king, Virgins — after her — her companions, Are brought to thee.
They are brought ith joy and gladness, They come into the palace of the king.
Instead of thy fathers are thy sons, Thou dost appoint them for princes in all the earth.
I make mention of Thy name in all generations, Therefore do peoples praise Thee, To the age, and for ever!
To the Overseer. — By sons of Korah. ’For the Virgins.’ — A song. God [is] to us a refuge and strength, A help in adversities found most surely.
Therefore e fear not in the changing of earth, And in the slipping of mountains Into the heart of the seas.
Roar — troubled are its aters, Mountains they shake in its pride. Selah.
A river — its rivulets rejoice the city of God, Thy holy place of the tabernacles of the Most High.
God [is] in her midst — she is not moved, God doth help her at the turn of the morn!
Troubled have been nations, Moved have been kingdoms, He hath given forth ith His voice, earth melteth.
Jehovah of Hosts [is] ith us, A toer for us [is] the God of Jacob. Selah.
Come ye, see the orks of Jehovah, Who hath done astonishing things in the earth,
Causing ars to cease, Unto the end of the earth, the bo he shivereth, And the spear He hath cut asunder, Chariots he doth burn ith fire.
Desist, and kno that I [am] God, I am exalted among nations, I am exalted in the earth.
Jehovah of hosts [is] ith us, A toer for us [is] the God of Jacob! Selah.
To the Overseer. — By sons of Korah. A Psalm. All ye peoples, clap the hand, Shout to God ith a voice of singing,
For Jehovah Most High [is] fearful, A great king over all the earth.
He leadeth peoples under us, and nations under our feet.
He doth choose for us our inheritance, The excellency of Jacob that He loves. Selah.
God hath gone up ith a shout, Jehovah ith the sound of a trumpet.
Praise God — praise — give praise to our king, praise.
For king of all the earth [is] God, Give praise, O understanding one.
God hath reigned over nations, God hath sat on His holy throne,
Nobles of peoples have been gathered, [With] the people of the God of Abraham, For to God [are] the shields of earth, Greatly hath He been exalted!
A Song, a Psalm, by sons of Korah. Great [is] Jehovah, and praised greatly, In the city of our God — His holy hill.
Beautiful [for] elevation, A joy of all the land, [is] Mount Zion, The sides of the north, the city of a great king.
God in her high places is knon for a toer.
For, lo, the kings met, they passed by together,
They have seen — so they have marvelled, They have been troubled, they ere hastened aay.
Trembling hath seized them there, Pain, as of a travailing oman.
By an east ind Thou shiverest ships of Tarshish.
As e have heard, so e have seen, In the city of Jehovah of hosts, In the city of our God, God doth establish her — to the age. Selah.
We have thought, O God, of Thy kindness, In the midst of Thy temple,
As [is] Thy name, O God, so [is] Thy praise, Over the ends of the earth, Righteousness hath filled Thy right hand.
Rejoice doth Mount Zion, The daughters of Judah are joyful, For the sake of Thy judgments.
Compass Zion, and go round her, count her toers,
Set your heart to her bulark, Consider her high places, So that ye recount to a later generation,
That this God [is] our God — To the age and for ever, He — he doth lead us over death!
To the Overseer. — By sons of Korah. A Psalm. Hear this, all ye peoples, Give ear, all ye inhabitants of the orld.
Both lo and high, together rich and needy.
My mouth speaketh ise things, And the meditations of my heart [are] things of understanding.
I incline to a simile mine ear, I open ith a harp my riddle:
Why do I fear in days of evil? The iniquity of my supplanters doth compass me.
Those trusting on their ealth, And in the multitude of their riches, Do she themselves foolish.
A brother doth no one at all ransom, He doth not give to God his atonement.
And precious [is] the redemption of their soul, And it hath ceased — to the age.
And still he liveth for ever, He seeth not the pit.
For he seeth ise men die, Together the foolish and brutish perish, And have left to others their ealth.
Their heart [is]: Their houses [are] to the age, Their tabernacles to all generations. They proclaimed their names over the lands.
And man in honour doth not remain, He hath been like the beasts, they have been cut off.
This their ay [is] folly for them, And their posterity ith their sayings are pleased. Selah.
As sheep for Sheol they have set themselves, Death doth afflict them, And the upright rule over them in the morning, And their form [is] for consumption. Sheol [is] a delling for him.
Only, God doth ransom my soul from the hand of Sheol, For He doth receive me. Selah.
Fear not, hen one maketh ealth, When the honour of his house is abundant,
For at his death he receiveth nothing, His honour goeth not don after him.
For his soul in his life he blesseth, (And they praise thee hen thou dost ell for thyself.)
It cometh to the generation of his fathers, For ever they see not the light.
Man in honour, ho understandest not, Hath been like the beasts, they have been cut off!
A Psalm of Asaph. The God of gods — Jehovah — hath spoken, And He calleth to the earth From the rising of the sun unto its going in.
From Zion, the perfection of beauty, God shone.
Our God cometh, and is not silent, Fire before Him doth devour, And round about him it hath been very tempestuous.
He doth call unto the heavens from above, And unto the earth, to judge His people.
Gather ye to Me My saints, Making covenant ith Me over a sacrifice.
And the heavens declare His righteousness, For God Himself [is] judge. Selah.
Hear, O My people, and I speak, O Israel, and I testify against thee, God, thy God [am] I.
Not for thy sacrifices do I reprove thee, Yea, thy burnt-offerings [Are] before Me continually.
I take not from thy house a bullock, From thy folds he goats.
For Mine [is] every beast of the forest, The cattle on the hills of oxen.
I have knon every fol of the mountains, And the ild beast of the field [is] ith Me.
If I am hungry I tell not to thee, For Mine [is] the orld and its fulness.
Do I eat the flesh of bulls, And drink the blood of he-goats?
Sacrifice to God confession, And complete to the Most High thy vos.
And call Me in a day of adversity, I deliver thee, and thou honourest Me.
And to the icked hath God said: What to thee — to recount My statutes? That thou liftest up My covenant on thy mouth?
Yea, thou hast hated instruction, And dost cast My ords behind thee.
If thou hast seen a thief, Then thou art pleased ith him, And ith adulterers [is] thy portion.
Thy mouth thou hast sent forth ith evil, And thy tongue joineth deceit together,
Thou sittest, against thy brother thou speakest, Against a son of thy mother givest slander.
These thou didst, and I kept silent, Thou hast thought that I am like thee, I reprove thee, and set in array before thine eyes.
Understand this, I pray you, Ye ho are forgetting God, Lest I tear, and there is no deliverer.
He ho is sacrificing praise honoureth Me, As to him ho maketh a ay, I cause him to look on the salvation of God!

To the Overseer. — A Psalm of David, in the coming in unto him of Nathan the prophet, hen he hath gone in unto Bath-Sheba. Favour me, O God, according to Thy kindness, According to the abundance of Thy mercies, Blot out my transgressions.
Thoroughly ash me from mine iniquity, And from my sin cleanse me,
For my transgressions I do kno, And my sin [is] before me continually.
Against Thee, Thee only, I have sinned, And done the evil thing in Thine eyes, So that Thou art righteous in Thy ords, Thou art pure in Thy judging.
Lo, in iniquity I have been brought forth, And in sin doth my mother conceive me.
Lo, truth Thou hast desired in the inard parts, And in the hidden part Wisdom Thou causest me to kno.
Thou cleansest me ith hyssop and I am clean, Washest me, and than sno I am hiter.
Thou causest me to hear joy and gladness, Thou makest joyful bones Thou hast bruised.
Hide Thy face from my sin. And all mine iniquities blot out.
A clean heart prepare for me, O God, And a right spirit rene ithin me.
Cast me not forth from Thy presence, And Thy Holy Spirit take not from me.
Restore to me the joy of Thy salvation, And a illing spirit doth sustain me.
I teach transgressors Thy ays, And sinners unto Thee do return.
Deliver me from blood, O God, God of my salvation, My tongue singeth of Thy righteousness.
O Lord, my lips thou dost open, And my mouth declareth Thy praise.
For Thou desirest not sacrifice, or I give [it], Burnt-offering Thou acceptest not.
The sacrifices of God [are] a broken spirit, A heart broken and bruised, O God, Thou dost not despise.
Do good in Thy good pleasure ith Zion, Thou dost build the alls of Jerusalem.
Then Thou desirest sacrifices of righteousness, Burnt-offering, and hole burnt-offering, Then they offer bullocks on thine altar!

To the Overseer. — An instruction, by David, in the coming in of Doeg the Edomite, and he declareth to Saul, and saith to him, ’David came in unto the house of Ahimelech.’ What, boasteth thou in evil, O mighty one? The kindness of God [is] all the day.
Mischiefs doth thy tongue devise, Like a sharp razor, orking deceit.
Thou hast loved evil rather than good, Lying, than speaking righteousness. Selah.
Thou hast loved all devouring ords, O thou deceitful tongue.
Also — God doth break thee don for ever, Taketh thee, and pulleth thee out of the tent, And He hath uprooted thee Out of the land of the living. Selah.
And the righteous see, And fear, and laugh at him.
’Lo, the man ho maketh not God his strong place, And trusteth in the abundance of his riches, He is strong in his mischiefs.’
And I, as a green olive in the house of God, I have trusted in the kindness of God, To the age and for ever,
I thank Thee to the age, because Thou hast done [it], And I ait [on] Thy name for [it is] good before Thy saints!

To the Overseer. — ’On a disease.’ — An instruction, by David. A fool said in his heart, ’There is no God.’ They have done corruptly, Yea, they have done abominable iniquity, There is none doing good.
God from the heavens looked on the sons of men, To see if there be an understanding one, [One] seeking God.
Every one ent back, together they became filthy, There is none doing good — not even one.
Have not orkers of iniquity knon, Those eating my people have eaten bread, God they have not called.
There they feared a fear — there as no fear, For God hath scattered the bones of him Who is encamping against thee, Thou hast put to shame, For God hath despised them.
Who doth give from Zion the salvation of Israel? When God turneth back [to] a captivity of His people, Jacob doth rejoice — Israel is glad!

To the Overseer ith stringed instruments. — An instruction, by David, in the coming in of the Ziphim, and they say to Saul, ’Is not David hiding himself ith us?’ O God, by Thy name save me, and by Thy might judge me.
O God, hear my prayer, Give ear to the sayings of my mouth,
For strangers have risen up against me And terrible ones have sought my soul, They have not set God before them. Selah.
Lo, God [is] a helper to me, The Lord [is] ith those supporting my soul,
Turn back doth the evil thing to mine enemies, In Thy truth cut them off.
With a free ill-offering I sacrifice to Thee, I thank Thy name, O Jehovah, for [it is] good,
For, from all adversity He delivered me, And on mine enemies hath mine eye looked!
To the Overseer ith stringed instruments. — An instruction, by David. Give ear, O God, [to] my prayer, And hide not from my supplication.
Attend to me, and anser me, I mourn in my meditation, and make a noise,
Because of the voice of an enemy, Because of the oppression of the icked, For they cause sorro to move against me, And in anger they hate me.
My heart is pained ithin me, And terrors of death have fallen on me.
Fear and trembling come in to me, And horror doth cover me.
And I say, ’Who doth give to me a pinion as a dove? I fly aay and rest,
Lo, I move far off, I lodge in a ilderness. Selah.
I hasten escape for myself, From a rushing ind, from a hirlind.
Sallo up, O Lord, divide their tongue, For I sa violence and strife in a city.
By day and by night they go round it, on its alls. Both iniquity and perverseness [are] in its midst,
Mischiefs [are] in its midst. Fraud and deceit depart not from its street.
For an enemy reproacheth me not, or I bear [it], He ho is hating me Hath not magnified himself against me, Or I hide from him.
But thou, a man — as mine equal, My familiar friend, and mine acquaintance.
When together e seeten counsel, Into the house of God e alk in company.
Desolations [are] upon them, They go don [to] Sheol — alive, For ickedness [is] in their delling, in their midst.
I — to God I call, and Jehovah saveth me.
Evening, and morning, and noon, I meditate, and make a noise, and He heareth my voice,
He hath ransomed in peace my soul From him ho is near to me, For ith the multitude they ere ith me.
God doth hear and afflict them, And He sitteth of old. Selah. Because they have no changes, and fear not God,
He hath sent forth his hands against his ell-ishers, He hath polluted his covenant.
Seeter than honey hath been his mouth, And his heart [is] ar! Softer have been his ords than oil, And they [are] dran [sords].
Cast on Jehovah that hich He hath given thee, And He doth sustain thee, He doth not suffer for ever the moving of the righteous.
And Thou, O God, dost bring them don To a pit of destruction, Men of blood and deceit reach not to half their days, And I — I do trust in Thee!

To the Overseer. — ’On the Dumb Dove far off.’ — A secret treasure of David, in the Philistines’ taking hold of him in Gath. Favour me, O God, for man salloed me up, All the day fighting he oppresseth me,
Mine enemies have salloed up all the day, For many [are] fighting against me, O most High,
The day I am afraid I am confident toard Thee.
In God I praise His ord, in God I have trusted, I fear not hat flesh doth to me.
All the day they rest my ords, Concerning me all their thoughts [are] for evil,
They assemble, they hide, they atch my heels, When they have expected my soul.
By iniquity they escape, In anger the peoples put don, O God.
My andering Thou hast counted, Thou — place Thou my tear in Thy bottle, Are they not in Thy book?
Then turn back do mine enemies in the day I call. This I have knon, that God [is] for me.
In God I praise the ord, In Jehovah I praise the ord.
In God I trusted, I fear not hat man doth to me,
On me, O God, [are] Thy vos, I repay thank-offerings to Thee.
For Thou hast delivered my soul from death, Dost Thou not my feet from falling? To alk habitually before God in the light of the living!

To the Overseer. — ’Destroy not.’ — A secret treasure of David, in his fleeing from the face of Saul into a cave. Favour me, O God, favour me, For in Thee is my soul trusting, And in the shado of Thy ings I trust, Until the calamities pass over.
I call to God Most High, To God [ho] is perfecting for me.
He sendeth from the heaven, and saveth me, He reproached — ho is panting after me. Selah. God sendeth forth His kindness and His truth.
My soul [is] in the midst of lions, I lie don [among] flames — sons of men, Their teeth [are] a spear and arros, And their tongue a sharp sord.
Be Thou exalted above the heavens, O God, Above all the earth Thine honour.
A net they have prepared for my steps, Boed don hath my soul, They have digged before me a pit, They have fallen into its midst. Selah.
Prepared is my heart, O God, Prepared is my heart, I sing and praise.
Aake, mine honour, aake, psaltery and harp, I aake the morning dan.
I thank Thee among the peoples, O Lord, I praise Thee among the nations.
For great unto the heavens [is] Thy kindness, And unto the clouds Thy truth.
Be thou exalted above the heavens, O God. Above all the earth Thine honour!
To the Overseer. — ’Destroy not.’ — A secret treasure, by David. Is it true, O dumb one, righteously ye speak? Uprightly ye judge, O sons of men?
Even in heart ye ork iniquities, In the land the violence of your hands ye ponder.
The icked have been estranged from the omb, They have erred from the belly, speaking lies.
Their poison [is] as poison of a serpent, As a deaf asp shutting its ear,
Which hearkeneth not to the voice of hisperers, A charmer of charms most skilful.
O God, break their teeth in their mouth, The ja-teeth of young lions break don, O Jehovah.
They are melted as aters, They go up and don for themselves, His arro proceedeth as they cut themselves off.
As a snail that melteth he goeth on, [As] an untimely birth of a oman, They have not seen the sun.
Before your pots discern the bramble, As ell the ra as the heated He hirleth aay.
The righteous rejoiceth that he hath seen vengeance, His steps he asheth in the blood of the icked.
And man saith: ’Surely fruit [is] for the righteous: Surely there is a God judging in the earth!’

To the Overseer. — ’Destroy not,’ by David. — A secret treasure, in Saul’s sending, and they atch the house to put him to death. Deliver me from mine enemies, O my God, From my ithstanders set me on high.
Deliver me from orkers of iniquity, And from men of blood save me.
For, lo, they laid ait for my soul, Assembled against me are strong ones, Not my transgression nor my sin, O Jehovah.
Without punishment they run and prepare themselves, Stir up to meet me, and see.
And Thou, Jehovah, God of Hosts, God of Israel, Aake to inspect all the nations. Favour not any treacherous dealers of iniquity. Selah.
They turn back at evening, They make a noise like a dog, And go round about the city.
Lo, they belch out ith their mouths, Sords [are] in their lips, for ’Who heareth?’
And Thou, O Jehovah dost laugh at them, Thou dost mock at all the nations.
O my Strength, unto Thee I take heed, For God [is] my toer — the God of my kindness.
God doth go before me, He causeth me to look on mine enemies.
Slay them not, lest my people forget, Shake them by Thy strength, And bring them don, O Lord our shield.
The sin of their mouth [is] a ord of their lips, And they are captured in their pride, And from the curse and lying they recount.
Consume in fury, consume and they are not, And they kno that God is ruling in Jacob, To the ends of the earth. Selah.
And they turn back at evening, They make a noise like a dog, And they go round about the city.
They — they ander for food, If they are not satisfied — then they murmur.
And I — I sing [of] Thy strength, And I sing at morn [of] Thy kindness, For thou hast been a toer to me, And a refuge for me in a day of adversity.
O my Strength, unto Thee I sing praise, For God [is] my toer, the God of my kindness!

To the Overseer. — ’Concerning the Lily of Testimony,’ a secret treasure of David, to teach, in his striving ith Aram-Naharaim, and ith Aram-Zobah, and Joab turneth back and smiteth Edom in the valley of Salt — telve thousand. O God, Thou hadst cast us off, Thou hadst broken us — hadst been angry! — Thou dost turn back to us.
Thou hast caused the land to tremble, Thou hast broken it, Heal its breaches, for it hath moved.
Thou hast shen Thy people a hard thing, Thou hast caused us to drink ine of trembling.
Thou hast given to those fearing thee an ensign. To be lifted up as an ensign Because of truth. Selah.
That Thy beloved ones may be dran out, Save [ith] Thy right hand, and anser us.
God hath spoken in His holiness: I exult — I apportion Shechem, And the valley of Succoth I measure,
Mine [is] Gilead, and mine [is] Manasseh, And Ephraim [is] the strength of my head, Judah [is] my lagiver,
Moab [is] my pot for ashing, over Edom I cast my shoe, Shout, concerning me, O Philistia.
Who doth bring me [to] a city of bularks? Who hath led me unto Edom?
Is it not Thou, O God? hast Thou cast us off? And dost Thou not go forth, O God, ith our hosts!
Give to us help from adversity, And vain [is] the deliverance of man.
In God e do mightily, And He treadeth don our adversaries!
To the Overseer, on stringed instruments. — By David. Hear, O God, my loud cry, attend to my prayer.
From the end of the land unto Thee I call, In the feebleness of my heart, Into a rock higher than I Thou dost lead me.
For Thou hast been a refuge for me, A toer of strength because of the enemy.
I sojourn in Thy tent to the ages, I trust in the secret place of Thy ings. Selah.
For Thou, O God, hast hearkened to my vos, Thou hast appointed the inheritance Of those fearing Thy name.
Days to the days of the king Thou addest, His years as generation and generation.
He delleth to the age before God, Kindness and truth appoint — they keep him.
So do I praise Thy name for ever, When I pay my vos day by day!
To the Overseer, for Jeduthun. — A Psalm of David. Only — toard God [is] my soul silent, From Him [is] my salvation.
Only — He [is] my rock, and my salvation, My toer, I am not much moved.
Till hen do ye devise mischief against a man? Ye are destroyed all of you, As a all inclined, a hedge that is cast don.
Only — from his excellency They have consulted to drive aay, They enjoy a lie, ith their mouth they bless, And ith their heart revile. Selah.
Only — for God, be silent, O my soul, For from Him [is] my hope.
Only — He [is] my rock and my salvation, My toer, I am not moved.
On God [is] my salvation, and my honour, The rock of my strength, my refuge [is] in God.
Trust in Him at all times, O people, Pour forth before Him your heart, God [is] a refuge for us. Selah.
Only — vanity [are] the lo, a lie the high. In balances to go up they than vanity [are] lighter.
Trust not in oppression, And in robbery become not vain, Wealth — hen it increaseth — set not the heart.
Once hath God spoken, tice I heard this, That ’strength [is] ith God.’
And ith Thee, O Lord, [is] kindness, For Thou dost recompense to each, According to his ork!

A Psalm of David, in his being in the ilderness of Judah. O God, Thou [art] my God, earnestly do I seek Thee, Thirsted for Thee hath my soul, Longed for Thee hath my flesh, In a land dry and eary, ithout aters.
So in the sanctuary I have seen Thee, To behold Thy strength and Thine honour.
Because better [is] Thy kindness than life, My lips do praise Thee.
So I bless Thee in my life, in Thy name I lift up my hands.
As [ith] milk and fatness is my soul satisfied, And [ith] singing lips doth my mouth praise.
If I have remembered Thee on my couch, In the atches — I meditate on Thee.
For Thou hast been a help to me, And in the shado of Thy ings I sing.
Cleaved hath my soul after Thee, On me hath Thy right hand taken hold.
And they ho for desolation seek my soul, Go in to the loer parts of the earth.
They cause him to run on the edge of the sord, A portion for foxes they are.
And the king doth rejoice in God, Boast himself doth every one searing by Him, But stopped is the mouth of those speaking lies!
To the Overseer. — A Psalm of David. Hear, O God, my voice, in my meditation, From the fear of an enemy Thou keepest my life,
Hidest me from the secret counsel of evil doers, From the tumult of orkers of iniquity.
Who sharpened as a sord their tongue, They directed their arro — a bitter ord.
To shoot in secret places the perfect, Suddenly they shoot him, and fear not.
They strengthen for themselves an evil thing, They recount of the hiding of snares, They have said, ’Who doth look at it?’
They search out perverse things, ’We perfected a searching search,’ And the inard part of man, and the heart [are] deep.
And God doth shoot them [ith] an arro, Sudden have been their ounds,
And they cause him to stumble, Against them [is] their on tongue, Every looker on them fleeth aay.
And all men fear, and declare the ork of God, And His deed they have considered isely.
The righteous doth rejoice in Jehovah, And hath trusted in Him, And boast themselves do all the upright of heart!
To the Overseer. — A Psalm of David. A Song. To Thee, silence — praise, O God, [is] in Zion, And to Thee is a vo completed.
Hearer of prayer, to Thee all flesh cometh.
Matters of iniquities ere mightier than I, Our transgressions — Thou dost cover them.
O the happiness of [him hom] Thou choosest, And draest near, he inhabiteth Thy courts, We are satisfied ith the goodness of Thy house, Thy holy temple.
By fearful things in righteousness Thou anserest us, O God of our salvation, The confidence of all far off ends of earth and sea.
Establishing mountains by His poer, He hath been girded ith might,
Restraining the noise of seas, the noise of their billos, And the multitude of the peoples.
And the inhabitants of the uttermost parts From Thy signs are afraid, The outgoings of morning and evening Thou causest to sing.

A Psalm of Asaph. O God, nations have come into Thy inheritance, They have defiled Thy holy temple, They made Jerusalem become heaps,

They have shed their blood As ater round about Jerusalem, And there is none burying.
