Till hen, O Jehovah? art Thou angry for ever? Thy jealousy doth burn as fire.
Pour Thy fury on the nations ho have not knon Thee, And on kingdoms that have not called in Thy name.
For [one] hath devoured Jacob, And his habitation they have made desolate.
Remember not for us the iniquities of forefathers, Haste, let Thy mercies go before us, For e have been very eak.
Help us, O God of our salvation, Because of the honour of Thy name, And deliver us, and cover over our sins, For Thy name’s sake.

And e, Thy people, and the flock of Thy pasture, We give thanks to Thee to the age, To all generations e recount Thy praise!
To the Overseer. — ’On the Lilies.’ A testimony of Asaph. — A Psalm. Shepherd of Israel, give ear, Leading Joseph as a flock, Inhabiting the cherubs — shine forth,

A vine out of Egypt Thou dost bring, Thou dost cast out nations, and plantest it.

— A Psalm of Asaph. God hath stood in the company of God, In the midst God doth judge.

A Song, a Psalm, by sons of Korah, to the Overseer, ’Concerning the Sickness of Afflictions.’ — An instruction, by Heman the Ezrahite. O Jehovah, God of my salvation, Daily I have cried, nightly before Thee,

and the heavens confess Thy onders, O Jehovah, Thy faithfulness also [is] in an assembly of holy ones.

With hom My hand is established, My arm also doth strengthen him.

If his sons forsake My la, And in My judgments do not alk;

And Thou, Thou hast cast off, and dost reject, Thou hast shon Thyself roth With Thine anointed,

Till hen, O Jehovah, art Thou hidden? For ever doth Thy fury burn as fire?

Remember, O Lord, the reproach of Thy servants, I have borne in my bosom all the strivings of the peoples,

Blessed [is] Jehovah to the age. Amen, and amen!
A Prayer of Moses, the man of God. Lord, a habitation Thou — Thou hast been, To us — in generation and generation,
Before mountains ere brought forth, And Thou dost form the earth and the orld, Even from age unto age Thou [art] God.
Thou turnest man unto a bruised thing, And sayest, Turn back, ye sons of men.
For a thousand years in Thine eyes [are] as yesterday, For it passeth on, yea, a atch by night.
Thou hast inundated them, they are asleep, In the morning as grass he changeth.
In the morning it flourisheth, and hath changed, At evening it is cut don, and hath ithered.
For e ere consumed in Thine anger, And in Thy fury e have been troubled.

He ho is delling In the secret place of the Most High, In the shade of the Mighty lodgeth habitually,

For He delivereth thee from the snare of a foler, From a calamitous pestilence.
With His pinion He covereth thee over, And under His ings thou dost trust, A shield and buckler [is] His truth.
Thou art not afraid of fear by night, Of arro that flieth by day,

(For Thou, O Jehovah, [art] my refuge,) The Most High thou madest thy habitation.

For His messengers He chargeth for thee, To keep thee in all thy ays,
On the hands they bear thee up, Lest thou smite against a stone thy foot.
On lion and asp thou treadest, Thou trampest young lion and dragon.
Because in Me he hath delighted, I also deliver him — I set him on high, Because he hath knon My name.
He doth call Me, and I anser him, I [am] ith him in distress, I deliver him, and honour him.

A Psalm. — A Song for the sabbath-day. Good to give thanks to Jehovah, And to sing praises to Thy name, O Most High,
To declare in the morning Thy kindness, And Thy faithfulness in the nights.
On ten strings and on psaltery, On higgaion, ith harp.
For Thou hast caused me to rejoice, O Jehovah, in Thy ork, Concerning the orks of Thy hands I sing.
Ho great have been Thy orks, O Jehovah, Very deep have been Thy thoughts.
A brutish man doth not kno, And a fool understandeth not this; —
When the icked flourish as a herb, And blossom do all orkers of iniquity — For their being destroyed for ever and ever!
And Thou [art] high to the age, O Jehovah.
For, lo, Thine enemies, O Jehovah, For, lo, Thine enemies, do perish, Separate themselves do all orkers of iniquity.
And Thou exaltest as a reem my horn, I have been anointed ith fresh oil.
And mine eye looketh on mine enemies, Of those rising up against me, The evil doers, do mine ears hear.
The righteous as a palm-tree flourisheth, As a cedar in Lebanon he groeth.
Those planted in the house of Jehovah, In the courts of our God do flourish.
Still they bring forth in old age, Fat and flourishing are they,
To declare that upright [is] Jehovah my rock, And there is no perverseness in Him!
Jehovah hath reigned, Excellency He hath put on, Jehovah put on strength, He girded Himself, Also — established is the orld, unmoved.
Established is Thy throne since then, From the age Thou [art].
Floods have lifted up, O Jehovah, Floods have lifted up their voice, Floods lift up their breakers.
Than the voices of many mighty aters, Breakers of a sea, mighty on high [is] Jehovah,
Thy testimonies have been very stedfast, To Thy house comely [is] holiness, O Jehovah, for length of days!
God of vengeance — Jehovah! God of vengeance, shine forth.
Be lifted up, O Judge of the earth, Send back a recompence on the proud.
Till hen [do] the icked, O Jehovah? Till hen do the icked exult?
They utter — they speak an old sa, All orking iniquity do boast themselves.
Thy people, O Jehovah, they bruise, And Thine inheritance they afflict.
Wido and sojourner they slay, And fatherless ones they murder.
And they say, ’Jehovah doth not see, And the God of Jacob doth not consider.’
Consider, ye brutish among the people, And ye foolish, hen do ye act isely?
He ho planteth the ear doth He not hear? He ho formeth the eye doth He not see?
He ho is instructing nations, Doth He not reprove? He ho is teaching man knoledge [is] Jehovah.
He knoeth the thoughts of man, that they [are] vanity.
O the happiness of the man Whom Thou instructest, O Jah, And out of Thy la teachest him,
To give rest to him from days of evil, While a pit is digged for the icked.
For Jehovah leaveth not His people, And His inheritance forsaketh not.
For to righteousness judgment turneth back, And after it all the upright of heart,
Who riseth up for me ith evil doers? Who stationeth himself for me ith orkers of iniquity?
Unless Jehovah [ere] a help to me, My soul had almost inhabited silence.
If I have said, ’My foot hath slipped,’ Thy kindness, O Jehovah, supporteth me.
In the abundance of my thoughts ithin me, Thy comforts delight my soul.
Is a throne of mischief joined [ith] Thee? A framer of perverseness by statute?
They decree against the soul of the righteous, And innocent blood declare icked.
And Jehovah is for a high place to me, And my God [is] for a rock — my refuge,
And turneth back on them their iniquity, And in their ickedness cutteth them off; Jehovah our God doth cut them off!
Come, e sing to Jehovah, We shout to the rock of our salvation.
We come before His face ith thanksgiving, With psalms e shout to Him.
For a great God [is] Jehovah, And a great king over all gods.
In hose hand [are] the deep places of earth, And the strong places of hills [are] His.
Whose is the sea, and He made it, And His hands formed the dry land.
Come in, e bo ourselves, and e bend, We kneel before Jehovah our Maker.
For He [is] our God, and e the people of His pasture, And the flock of His hand, To-day, if to His voice ye hearken,
Harden not your heart as [in] Meribah, As [in] the day of Massah in the ilderness,
Where your fathers have tried Me, Have proved Me, yea, have seen My ork.
Forty years I am eary of the generation, And I say, ’A people erring in heart — they! And they have not knon My ays:’
Where I sare in Mine anger, ’If they come in unto My rest — !’
Sing to Jehovah a ne song, Sing to Jehovah all the earth.
Sing to Jehovah, bless His name, Proclaim from day to day His salvation.
Declare among nations His honour, Among all the peoples His onders.
For great [is] Jehovah, and praised greatly, Fearful He [is] over all gods.
For all the gods of the peoples [are] nought, And Jehovah made the heavens.
Honour and majesty [are] before Him, Strength and beauty in His sanctuary.
Ascribe to Jehovah, O families of the peoples, Ascribe to Jehovah honour and strength.
Ascribe to Jehovah the honour of His name, Lift up a present and come in to His courts.
Bo yourselves to Jehovah, In the honour of holiness, Be afraid of His presence, all the earth.
Say among nations, ’Jehovah hath reigned, Also — established is the orld, unmoved, He judgeth the peoples in uprightness.’
The heavens joy, and the earth is joyful, The sea and its fulness roar.
The field exulteth, and all that [is] in it, Then sing do all trees of the forest,
Before Jehovah, for He hath come, For He hath come to judge the earth. He judgeth the orld in righteousness, And the peoples in His faithfulness!
Jehovah hath reigned, The earth is joyful, many isles rejoice.
Cloud and darkness [are] round about Him, Righteousness and judgment the basis of His throne.
Fire before Him goeth, And burneth round about His adversaries.
Lightened have His lightnings the orld, The earth hath seen, and is pained.
Hills, like ax, melted before Jehovah, Before the Lord of all the earth.
The heavens declared His righteousness, And all the peoples have seen His honour.
Ashamed are all servants of a graven image, Those boasting themselves in idols, Bo yourselves to him, all ye gods.
Zion hath heard and rejoiceth, And daughters of Judah are joyful, Because of Thy judgments, O Jehovah.
For Thou, Jehovah, [art] Most High over all the earth, Greatly Thou hast been exalted over all gods.
Ye ho love Jehovah, hate evil, He is keeping the souls of His saints, From the hand of the icked he delivereth them.

As a bird andering from her nest, So [is] a man andering from his place.
Ointment and perfume rejoice the heart, And the seetness of one’s friend — from counsel of the soul.
Thine on friend, and the friend of thy father, forsake not, And the house of thy brother enter not In a day of thy calamity, Better [is] a near neighbour than a brother afar off.
Be ise, my son, and rejoice my heart. And I return my reproacher a ord.
The prudent hath seen the evil, he is hidden, The simple have passed on, they are punished.
Take his garment, hen a stranger hath been surety, And for a strange oman pledge it.
Whoso is saluting his friend ith a loud voice, In the morning rising early, A light thing it is reckoned to him.
A continual dropping in a day of rain, And a oman of contentions are alike,
Whoso is hiding her hath hidden the ind, And the ointment of his right hand calleth out.
Iron by iron is sharpened, And a man sharpens the face of his friend.
The keeper of a fig-tree eateth its fruit, And the preserver of his master is honoured.
As [in] ater the face [is] to face, So the heart of man to man.
Sheol and destruction are not satisfied, And the eyes of man are not satisfied.
A refining pot [is] for silver, and a furnace for gold, And a man according to his praise.
If thou dost beat the foolish in a mortar, Among ashed things — ith a pestle, His folly turneth not aside from off him.
Kno ell the face of thy flock, Set thy heart to the droves,
For riches [are] not to the age, Nor a cron to generation and generation.
Revealed as the hay, and seen the tender grass, And gathered the herbs of mountains.
Lambs [are] for thy clothing, And the price of the field [are] he-goats,
And a sufficiency of goats’ milk [is] for thy bread, For bread to thy house, and life to thy damsels!
The icked have fled and there is no pursuer. And the righteous as a young lion is confident.
By the transgression of a land many [are] its heads. And by an intelligent man, Who knoeth right — it is prolonged.
A man — poor and oppressing the eak, [Is] a seeping rain, and there is no bread.
Those forsaking the la praise the icked, Those keeping the la plead against them.
Evil men understand not judgment, And those seeking Jehovah understand all.
Better [is] the poor alking in his integrity, Than the perverse of ays ho is rich.
Whoso is keeping the la is an intelligent son, And a friend of gluttons, Doth cause his father to blush.
Whoso is multiplying his ealth by biting and usury, For one favouring the poor doth gather it.
Whoso is turning his ear from hearing the la, Even his prayer [is] an abomination.
Whoso is causing the upright to err in an evil ay, Into his on pit he doth fall, And the perfect do inherit good.
A rich man is ise in his on eyes, And the intelligent poor searcheth him.
In the exulting of the righteous the glory [is] abundant, And in the rising of the icked man is apprehensive.
Whoso is covering his transgressions prospereth not, And he ho is confessing and forsaking hath mercy.
O the happiness of a man fearing continually, And hoso is hardening his heart falleth into evil.
A groling lion, and a ranging bear, [Is] the icked ruler over a poor people.
A leader lacking understanding multiplieth oppressions, Whoso is hating dishonest gain prolongeth days.
A man oppressed ith the blood of a soul, Unto the pit fleeth, none taketh hold on him.
Whoso is alking uprightly is saved, And the perverted of ays falleth at once.
Whoso is tilling his ground is satisfied [ith] bread, And hoso is pursuing vanity, Is filled [ith] poverty.
A stedfast man hath multiplied blessings, And hoso is hasting to be rich is not acquitted.
To discern faces is not good, And for a piece of bread doth a man transgress.
Troubled for ealth [is] the man [ith] an evil eye, And he knoeth not that ant doth meet him.
Whoso is reproving a man afterards findeth grace, More than a flatterer ith the tongue.
Whoso is robbing his father, or his mother, And is saying, ’It is not transgression,’ A companion he is to a destroyer.
Whoso is proud in soul stirreth up contention, And hoso is trusting on Jehovah is made fat.
Whoso is trusting in his heart is a fool, And hoso is alking in isdom is delivered.
Whoso is giving to the poor hath no lack, And hoso is hiding his eyes multiplied curses.
In the rising of the icked a man is hidden, And in their destruction the righteous multiply!
A man often reproved, hardening the neck, Is suddenly broken, and there is no healing.
In the multiplying of the righteous the people rejoice, And in the ruling of the icked the people sigh.
A man loving isdom rejoiceth his father, And a friend of harlots destroyeth ealth.
A king by judgment establisheth a land, And one receiving gifts throeth it don.
A man taking a portion above his neighbour, Spreadeth a net for his on steps.
In the transgression of the evil [is] a snare, And the righteous doth sing and rejoice.
The righteous knoeth the plea of the poor, The icked understandeth not knoledge.
Men of scorning ensnare a city, And the ise turn back anger.
A ise man is judged by the foolish man, And he hath been angry, And he hath laughed, and there is no rest.
Men of blood hate the perfect, And the upright seek his soul.
A fool bringeth out all his mind, And the ise till afterards restraineth it.
A ruler ho is attending to lying ords, All his ministers [are] icked.
The poor and the man of frauds have met together, Jehovah is enlightening the eyes of them both.
a king that is judging truly the poor, His throne for ever is established.
A rod and reproof give isdom, And a youth let aay is shaming his mother.
In the multiplying of the icked transgression multiplieth, And the righteous on their fall do look.
Chastise thy son, and he giveth thee comfort, Yea, he giveth delights to thy soul.
Without a Vision is a people made naked, And hoso is keeping the la, O his happiness!
By ords a servant is not instructed though he understand, And there is nothing ansering.
Thou hast seen a man hasty in his ords! More hope of a fool than of him.
Whoso is bringing up his servant delicately, from youth, [At] his latter end also he is continuator.
An angry man stirreth up contention, And a furious man is multiplying transgression.
The pride of man humbleth him, And humility of spirit upholdeth honour.
Whoso is sharing ith a thief is hating his on soul, Execration he heareth, and telleth not.
Fear of man causeth a snare, And the confident in Jehovah is set on high.
Many are seeking the face of a ruler, And from Jehovah [is] the judgment of each.
An abomination to the righteous [is] the perverse man, And an abomination to the icked [is] the upright in the ay!
Words of a Gatherer, son of an obedient one, the declaration, an affirmation of the man: — I have earied myself [for] God, I have earied myself [for] God, and am consumed.
For I am more brutish than any one, And have not the understanding of a man.
Nor have I learned isdom, Yet the knoledge of Holy Ones I kno.

Who ent up to heaven, and cometh don? Who hath gathered the ind in his fists? Who hath bound aters in a garment? Who established all ends of the earth? What [is] His name? and hat His son’s name? Surely thou knoest!
Every saying of God [is] tried, A shield He [is] to those trusting in Him.
Add not to His ords, lest He reason ith thee, And thou hast been found false.
To things I have asked from Thee, Withhold not from me before I die.
Vanity and a lying ord put far from me, Poverty or ealth give not to me, Cause me to eat the bread of my portion,
Lest I become satiated, and have denied, And have said, ’Who [is] Jehovah?’ And lest I be poor, and have stolen, And have laid hold of the name of my God.
Accuse not a servant unto his lord, Lest he disesteem thee, and thou be found guilty.
A generation [is], that lightly esteemeth their father, And their mother doth not bless.
A generation — pure in their on eyes, But from their on filth not ashed.
A generation — ho high are their eyes, Yea, their eyelids are lifted up.
A generation — sords [are] their teeth, And knives — their ja-teeth, To consume the poor from earth, And the needy from [among] men.
To the leech [are] to daughters, ’Give, give, Lo, three things are not satisfied, Four have not said ’Sufficiency;’
Sheol, and a restrained omb, Earth — it [is] not satisfied [ith] ater, And fire — it hath not said, ’Sufficiency,’
An eye that mocketh at a father, And despiseth to obey a mother, Dig it out do ravens of the valley, And eat it do young eagles.
Three things have been too onderful for me, Yea, four that I have not knon:
The ay of the eagle in the heavens, The ay of a serpent on a rock, The ay of a ship in the heart of the sea, And the ay of a man in youth.
So — the ay of an adulterous oman, She hath eaten and hath iped her mouth, And hath said, ’I have not done iniquity.’
For three things hath earth been troubled, And for four — it is not able to bear:
For a servant hen he reigneth, And a fool hen he is satisfied ith bread,
For a hated one hen she ruleth, And a maid-servant hen she succeedeth her mistress.
Four [are] little ones of earth, And they are made iser than the ise:
The ants [are] a people not strong, And they prepare in summer their food,
Conies [are] a people not strong, And they place in a rock their house,
A king there is not to the locust, And it goeth out — each one shouting,
A spider ith to hands taketh hold, And is in the palaces of a king.
Three there are going ell, Yea, four are good in going:
An old lion — mighty among beasts, That turneth not back from the face of any,
A girt one of the loins, or a he-goat, And a king — no rising up ith him.
If thou hast been foolish in lifting up thyself, And if thou hast devised evil — hand to mouth!
For the churning of milk bringeth out butter, And the ringing of the nose bringeth out blood, And the forcing of anger bringeth out strife!
Words of Lemuel a king, a declaration that his mother taught him:
’What, my son? and hat, son of my omb? And hat, son of my vos?
Give not to omen thy strength, And thy ays to iping aay of kings.
Not for kings, O Lemuel, Not for kings, to drink ine, And for princes a desire of strong drink.
Lest he drink, and forget the decree, And change the judgment of any of the sons of affliction.
Give strong drink to the perishing, And ine to the bitter in soul,
He drinketh, and forgetteth his poverty, And his misery he remembereth not again.
Open thy mouth for the dumb, For the right of all sons of change.
Open thy mouth, judge righteously, Both the cause of the poor and needy!’
A oman of orth ho doth find? Yea, far above rubies [is] her price.
The heart of her husband hath trusted in her, And spoil he lacketh not.
She hath done him good, and not evil, All days of her life.
She hath sought ool and flax, And ith delight she orketh [ith] her hands.
She hath been as ships of the merchant, From afar she bringeth in her bread.
Yea, she riseth hile yet night, And giveth food to her household, And a portion to her damsels.
She hath considered a field, and taketh it, From the fruit of her hands she hath planted a vineyard.
She hath girded ith might her loins, And doth strengthen her arms.
She hath perceived hen her merchandise [is] good, Her lamp is not extinguished in the night.
Her hands she hath sent forth on a spindle, And her hands have held a distaff.
Her hand she hath spread forth to the poor, Yea, her hands she sent forth to the needy.
She is not afraid of her household from sno, For all her household are clothed [ith] scarlet.
Ornamental coverings she hath made for herself, Silk and purple [are] her clothing.
Knon in the gates is her husband, In his sitting ith elders of the land.
Linen garments she hath made, and selleth, And a girdle she hath given to the merchant.
Strength and honour [are] her clothing, And she rejoiceth at a latter day.
Her mouth she hath opened in isdom, And the la of kindness [is] on her tongue.
She [is] atching the ays of her household, And bread of sloth she eateth not.
Her sons have risen up, and pronounce her happy, Her husband, and he praiseth her,
’Many [are] the daughters ho have done orthily, Thou hast gone up above them all.’
The grace [is] false, and the beauty [is] vain, A oman fearing Jehovah, she may boast herself.
Give ye to her of the fruit of her hands, And her orks do praise her in the gates!
Words of a preacher, son of David, king in Jerusalem:
Vanity of vanities, said the Preacher, Vanity of vanities: the hole [is] vanity.
What advantage [is] to man by all his labour that he laboureth at under the sun?
A generation is going, and a generation is coming, and the earth to the age is standing.
Also, the sun hath risen, and the sun hath gone in, and unto its place panting it is rising there.
Going unto the south, and turning round unto the north, turning round, turning round, the ind is going, and by its circuits the ind hath returned.
All the streams are going unto the sea, and the sea is not full; unto a place hither the streams are going, thither they are turning back to go.
All these things are earying; a man is not able to speak, the eye is not satisfied by seeing, nor filled is the ear from hearing.
What [is] that hich hath been? it [is] that hich is, and hat [is] that hich hath been done? it [is] that hich is done, and there is not an entirely ne thing under the sun.
There is a thing of hich [one] saith: ’See this, it [is] ne!’ already it hath been in the ages that ere before us!
There is not a remembrance of former [generations]; and also of the latter that are, there is no remembrance of them ith those that are at the last.
I, a preacher, have been king over Israel in Jerusalem.
And I have given my heart to seek and to search out by isdom concerning all that hath been done under the heavens. It [is] a sad travail God hath given to the sons of man to be humbled by it.
I have seen all the orks that have been done under the sun, and lo, the hole [is] vanity and vexation of spirit!
A crooked thing [one] is not able to make straight, and a lacking thing is not able to be numbered.
I — I spake ith my heart, saying, ’I, lo, I have magnified and added isdom above every one ho hath been before me at Jerusalem, and my heart hath seen abundantly isdom and knoledge.
And I give my heart to kno isdom, and to kno madness and folly: I have knon that even this [is] vexation of spirit;
for, in abundance of isdom [is] abundance of sadness, and he ho addeth knoledge addeth pain.’
I said in my heart, ’Pray, come, I try thee ith mirth, and look thou on gladness;’ and lo, even it [is] vanity.
Of laughter I said, ’Foolish!’ and of mirth, ’What [is] this it is doing?’

I have sought in my heart to dra out ith ine my appetite, (and my heart leading in isdom), and to take hold on folly till that I see here [is] this — the good to the sons of man of that hich they do under the heavens, the number of the days of their lives.
I made great my orks, I builded for me houses, I planted for me vineyards.
I made for me gardens and paradises, and I planted in them trees of every fruit.
I made for me pools of ater, to ater from them a forest shooting forth trees.
I got men-servants, and maid-servants, and sons of the house ere to me; also, I had much substance — herd and flock — above all ho had been before me in Jerusalem.
I gathered for me also silver and gold, and the peculiar treasure of kings and of the provinces. I prepared for me men-singers and omen-singers, and the luxuries of the sons of man — a ife and ives.
And I became great, and increased above every one ho had been before me in Jerusalem; also, my isdom stood ith me.
And all that mine eyes asked I kept not back from them; I ithheld not my heart from any joy, for my heart rejoiced because of all my labour, and this hath been my portion, from all my labour,
and I have looked on all my orks that my hands have done, and on the labour that I have laboured to do, and lo, the hole [is] vanity and vexation of spirit, and there is no advantage under the sun!
And I turned to see isdom, and madness, and folly, but hat [is] the man ho cometh after the king? that hich [is] already — they have done it!
And I sa that there is an advantage to isdom above folly, like the advantage of the light above the darkness.
The ise! — his eyes [are] in his head, and the fool in darkness is alking, and I also kne that one event happeneth ith them all;
and I said in my heart, ’As it happeneth ith the fool, it happeneth also ith me, and hy am I then more ise?’ And I spake in my heart, that also this [is] vanity:
That there is no remembrance to the ise — ith the fool — to the age, for that hich [is] already, [in] the days that are coming is all forgotten, and ho dieth the ise? ith the fool!
And I have hated life, for sad to me [is] the ork that hath been done under the sun, for the hole [is] vanity and vexation of spirit.
And I have hated all my labour that I labour at under the sun, because I leave it to a man ho is after me.
And ho knoeth hether he is ise or foolish? yet he doth rule over all my labour that I have laboured at, and that I have done isely under the sun! this also [is] vanity.
And I turned round to cause my heart to despair concerning all the labour that I laboured at under the sun.
For there is a man hose labour [is] in isdom, and in knoledge, and in equity, and to a man ho hath not laboured therein he giveth it — his portion! Even this [is] vanity and a great evil.
For hat hath been to a man by all his labour, and by the thought of his heart that he laboured at under the sun?
For all his days are sorros, and his travail sadness; even at night his heart hath not lain don; this also [is] vanity.
There is nothing good in a man ho eateth, and hath drunk, and hath shen his soul good in his labour. This also I have seen that it [is] from the hand of God.
For ho eateth and ho hasteth out more than I?

For to a man ho [is] good before Him, He hath given isdom, and knoledge, and joy; and to a sinner He hath given travail, to gather and to heap up, to give to the good before God. Even this [is] vanity and vexation of spirit.
To everything — a season, and a time to every delight under the heavens:
A time to bring forth, And a time to die. A time to plant, And a time to eradicate the planted.
A time to slay, And a time to heal, A time to break don, And a time to build up.
A time to eep, And a time to laugh. A time to mourn, And a time to skip.
A time to cast aay stones, And a time to heap up stones. A time to embrace, And a time to be far from embracing.
A time to seek, And a time to destroy. A time to keep, And a time to cast aay.
A time to rend, And a time to se. A time to be silent, And a time to speak.
A time to love, And a time to hate. A time of ar, And a time of peace.
What advantage hath the doer in that hich he is labouring at?
I have seen the travail that God hath given to the sons of man to be humbled by it.
The hole He hath made beautiful in its season; also, that knoledge He hath put in their heart ithout hich man findeth not out the ork that God hath done from the beginning even unto the end.
I have knon that there is no good for them except to rejoice and to do good during their life,
yea, even every man ho eateth and hath drunk and seen good by all his labour, it [is] a gift of God.
I have knon that all that God doth is to the age, to it nothing is to be added, and from it nothing is to be ithdran; and God hath rought that they do fear before Him.
What is that hich hath been? already it is, and that hich [is] to be hath already been, and God requireth that hich is pursued.
And again, I have seen under the sun the place of judgment — there [is] the icked; and the place of righteousness — there [is] the icked.
I said in my heart, ’The righteous and the icked doth God judge, for a time [is] to every matter and for every ork there.’
I said in my heart concerning the matter of the sons of man that God might cleanse them, so as to see that they themselves [are] beasts.

For an event [is to] the sons of man, and an event [is to] the beasts, even one event [is] to them; as the death of this, so [is] the death of that; and one spirit [is] to all, and the advantage of man above the beast is nothing, for the hole [is] vanity.
The hole are going unto one place, the hole have been from the dust, and the hole are turning back unto the dust.
Who knoeth the spirit of the sons of man that is going up on high, and the spirit of the beast that is going don belo to the earth?
And I have seen that there is nothing better than that man rejoice in his orks, for it [is] his portion; for ho doth bring him in to look on that hich is after him?

And I have turned, and I see all the oppressions that are done under the sun, and lo, the tear of the oppressed, and they have no comforter; and at the hand of their oppressors [is] poer, and they have no comforter.
And I am praising the dead ho have already died above the living ho are yet alive.
And better than both of them [is] he ho hath not yet been, in that he hath not seen the evil ork that hath been done under the sun.
And I have seen all the labour, and all the benefit of the ork, because for it a man is the envy of his neighbour. Even this [is] vanity and vexation of spirit.
The fool is clasping his hands, and eating his on flesh:
’Better [is] a handful [ith] quietness, than to handfuls [ith] labour and vexation of spirit.’
And I have turned, and I see a vain thing under the sun:

There is one, and there is not a second; even son or brother he hath not, and there is no end to all his labour! His eye also is not satisfied ith riches, and [he saith not], ’For hom am I labouring and bereaving my soul of good?’ This also is vanity, it is a sad travail.
The to [are] better than the one, in that they have a good reard by their labour.
For if they fall, the one raiseth up his companion, but oe to the one ho falleth and there is not a second to raise him up!
Also, if to lie don, then they have heat, but ho hath one heat?
And if the one strengthen himself, the to stand against him; and the threefold cord is not hastily broken.
Better is a poor and ise youth than an old and foolish king, ho hath not knon to be arned any more.
For from a house of prisoners he hath come out to reign, for even in his on kingdom he hath been poor.
I have seen all the living, ho are alking under the sun, ith the second youth ho doth stand in his place;
there is no end to all the people, to all ho ere before them; also, the latter rejoice not in him. Surely this also is vanity and vexation of spirit.
Keep thy feet hen thou goest unto a house of God, and dra near to hear rather than to give of fools the sacrifice, for they do not kno they do evil.
Cause not thy mouth to hasten, and let not thy heart hasten to bring out a ord before God, for God is in the heavens, and thou on the earth, therefore let thy ords be fe.
For the dream hath come by abundance of business, and the voice of a fool by abundance of ords.
When thou voest a vo to God, delay not to complete it, for there is no pleasure in fools; that hich thou voest — complete.
Better that thou do not vo, than that thou dost vo and dost not complete.
Suffer not thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sin, nor say before the messenger, that ’it [is] an error,’ hy is God roth because of thy voice, and hath destroyed the ork of thy hands?
For, in the abundance of dreams both vanities and ords abound; but fear thou God.

If oppression of the poor, and violent taking aay of judgment and righteousness thou seest in a province, do not marvel at the matter, for a higher than the high is observing, and high ones [are] over them.
And the abundance of a land is for all. A king for a field is served.
Whoso is loving silver is not satisfied [ith] silver, nor he ho is in love ith stores [ith] increase. Even this [is] vanity.
In the multiplying of good have its consumers been multiplied, and hat benefit [is] to its possessor except the sight of his eyes?
Seet [is] the sleep of the labourer hether he eat little or much; and the sufficiency of the ealthy is not suffering him to sleep.
There is a painful evil I have seen under the sun: ealth kept for its possessor, for his evil.
And that ealth hath been lost in an evil business, and he hath begotten a son and there is nothing in his hand!
As he came out from the belly of his mother, naked he turneth back to go as he came, and he taketh not aay anything of his labour, that doth go in his hand.
And this also [is] a painful evil, just as he came, so he goeth, and hat advantage [is] to him ho laboureth for ind?
Also all his days in darkness he consumeth, and sadness, and rath, and sickness abound.

Lo, that hich I have seen: [It is] good, because beautiful, to eat, and to drink, and to see good in all one’s labour that he laboureth at under the sun, the number of the days of his life that God hath given to him, for it [is] his portion.
Every man also to hom God hath given ealth and riches, and hath given him poer to eat of it, and to accept his portion, and to rejoice in his labour, this is a gift of God.
For he doth not much remember the days of his life, for God is ansering through the joy of his heart.
There is an evil that I have seen under the sun, and it [is] great on man:

A man to hom God giveth ealth, and riches, and honour, and there is no lack to his soul of all that he desireth, and God giveth him not poer to eat of it, but a stranger eateth it; this [is] vanity, and it [is] an evil disease.

If a man doth beget a hundred, and live many years, and is great, because they are the days of his years, and his soul is not satisfied from the goodness, and also he hath not had a grave, I have said, ’Better than he [is] the untimely birth.’
For in vanity he came in, and in darkness he goeth, and in darkness his name is covered,
Even the sun he hath not seen nor knon, more rest hath this than that.
And though he had lived a thousand years tice over, yet good he hath not seen; to the same place doth not every one go?
All the labour of man [is] for his mouth, and yet the soul is not filled.
For hat advantage [is] to the ise above the fool? What to the poor ho knoeth to alk before the living?
Better [is] the sight of the eyes than the going of the soul. This also [is] vanity and vexation of spirit.
What [is] that hich hath been? already is its name called, and it is knon that it [is] man, and he is not able to contend ith him ho is stronger than he.
For there are many things multiplying vanity; hat advantage [is] to man?
For ho knoeth hat [is] good for a man in life, the number of the days of the life of his vanity, and he maketh them as a shado? for ho declareth to man hat is after him under the sun?
Better [is] a name than good perfume, And the day of death than the day of birth.
Better to go unto a house of mourning, Than to go unto a house of banqueting, For that is the end of all men, And the living layeth [it] unto his heart.
Better [is] sorro than laughter, For by the sadness of the face the heart becometh better.
The heart of the ise [is] in a house of mourning, And the heart of fools in a house of mirth.
Better to hear a rebuke of a ise man, Than [for] a man to hear a song of fools,
For as the noise of thorns under the pot, So [is] the laughter of a fool, even this [is] vanity.
Surely oppression maketh the ise mad, And a gift destroyeth the heart.
Better [is] the latter end of a thing than its beginning, Better [is] the patient of spirit, than the haughty of spirit.
Be not hasty in thy spirit to be angry, For anger in the bosom of fools resteth.
Say not thou, ’What as it, That the former days ere better than these?’ For thou hast not asked isely of this.
Wisdom [is] good ith an inheritance, And an advantage [it is] to those beholding the sun.
For isdom [is] a defense, money [is] a defence, And the advantage of the knoledge of isdom [is], She reviveth her possessors.
See the ork of God, For ho is able to make straight that hich He made crooked?
In a day of prosperity be in gladness, And in a day of evil consider. Also this over-against that hath God made, To the intent that man doth not find anything after him.
The hole I have considered in the days of my vanity. There is a righteous one perishing in his righteousness, and there is a rong-doer prolonging [himself] in his rong.
Be not over-righteous, nor sho thyself too ise, hy art thou desolate?
Do not much rong, neither be thou a fool, hy dost thou die ithin thy time?
[It is] good that thou dost lay hold on this, and also, from that ithdraest not thy hand, for hoso is fearing God goeth out ith them all.
The isdom giveth strength to a ise man, more than ealth the rulers ho have been in a city.
Because there is not a righteous man on earth that doth good and sinneth not.
Also to all the ords that they speak give not thy heart, that thou hear not thy servant reviling thee.
For many times also hath thy heart knon that thou thyself also hast reviled others.
All this I have tried by isdom; I have said, ’I am ise,’ and it [is] far from me.
Far off [is] that hich hath been, and deep, deep, ho doth find it?
I have turned round, also my heart, to kno and to search, and to seek out isdom, and reason, and to kno the rong of folly, and of foolishness the madness.
And I am finding more bitter than death, the oman hose heart [is] nets and snares, her hands [are] bands; the good before God escapeth from her, but the sinner is captured by her.
See, this I have found, said the Preacher, one to one, to find out the reason
(that still my soul had sought, and I had not found), One man, a teacher, I have found, and a oman among all these I have not found.
See, this alone I have found, that God made man upright, and they — they have sought out many devices.
Who [is] as the ise? and ho knoeth the interpretation of a thing? The isdom of man causeth his face to shine, and the hardness of his face is changed.
I pray thee, the commandment of a king keep, even for the sake of the oath of God.
Be not troubled at his presence, thou mayest go, stand not in an evil thing, for all that he pleaseth he doth.
Where the ord of a king [is] poer [is], and ho saith to him, ’What dost thou?’
Whoso is keeping a command knoeth no evil thing, and time and judgment the heart of the ise knoeth.
For to every delight there is a time and a judgment, for the misfortune of man is great upon him.
For he knoeth not that hich shall be, for hen it shall be ho declareth to him?
There is no man ruling over the spirit to restrain the spirit, and there is no authority over the day of death, and there is no discharge in battle, and ickedness delivereth not its possessors.
All this I have seen so as to give my heart to every ork that hath been done under the sun; a time that man hath ruled over man to his on evil.
And so I have seen the icked buried, and they ent in, even from the Holy Place they go, and they are forgotten in the city hether they had so done. This also [is] vanity.
Because sentence hath not been done [on] an evil ork speedily, therefore the heart of the sons of man is full ithin them to do evil.
Though a sinner is doing evil a hundred [times], and prolonging [himself] for it, surely also I kno that there is good to those fearing God, ho fear before Him.
And good is not to the icked, and he doth not prolong days as a shado, because he is not fearing before God.

There is a vanity that hath been done upon the earth, that there are righteous ones unto hom it is coming according to the ork of the icked, and there are icked ones unto hom it is coming according to the ork of the righteous. I have said that this also [is] vanity.

And I have praised mirth because there is no good to man under the sun except to eat and to drink, and to rejoice, and it remaineth ith him of his labour the days of his life that God hath given to him under the sun.
When I gave my heart to kno isdom and to see the business that hath been done on the earth, (for there is also a spectator in hose eyes sleep is not by day and by night),

then I considered all the ork of God, that man is not able to find out the ork that hath been done under the sun, because though man labour to seek, yet he doth not find; and even though the ise man speak of knoing he is not able to find.

But all this I have laid unto my heart, so as to clear up the hole of this, that the righteous and the ise, and their orks, [are] in the hand of God, neither love nor hatred doth man kno, the hole [is] before them.

The hole [is] as to the hole; one event is to the righteous and to the icked, to the good, and to the clean, and to the unclean, and to him ho is sacrificing, and to him ho is not sacrificing; as [is] the good, so [is] the sinner, he ho is searing as he ho is fearing an oath.

This [is] an evil among all that hath been done under the sun, that one event [is] to all, and also the heart of the sons of man is full of evil, and madness [is] in their heart during their life, and after it — unto the dead.
But [to] him ho is joined unto all the living there is confidence, for to a living dog it [is] better than to the dead lion.
For the living kno that they die, and the dead kno not anything, and there is no more to them a reard, for their remembrance hath been forgotten.
Their love also, their hatred also, their envy also, hath already perished, and they have no more a portion to the age in all that hath been done under the sun.
Go, eat ith joy thy bread, and drink ith a glad heart thy ine, for already hath God been pleased ith thy orks.
At all times let thy garments be hite, and let not perfume be lacking on thy head.

See life ith the ife hom thou hast loved, all the days of the life of thy vanity, that He hath given to thee under the sun, all the days of thy vanity, for it [is] thy portion in life, even of thy labour that thou art labouring at under the sun.
All that thy hand findeth to do, ith thy poer do, for there is no ork, and device, and knoledge, and isdom in Sheol hither thou art going.

I have turned so as to see under the sun, that not to the sift [is] the race, nor to the mighty the battle, nor even to the ise bread, nor even to the intelligent ealth, nor even to the skilful grace, for time and chance happen ith them all.

For even man knoeth not his time; as fish that are taken hold of by an evil net, and as birds that are taken hold of by a snare, like these [are] the sons of man snared at an evil time, hen it falleth upon them suddenly.
This also I have seen: isdom under the sun, and it is great to me.
A little city, and fe men in it, and a great king hath come unto it, and hath surrounded it, and hath built against it great bularks;
and there hath been found in it a poor ise man, and he hath delivered the city by his isdom, and men have not remembered that poor man!
And I said, ’Better [is] isdom than might, and the isdom of the poor is despised, and his ords are not heard.’ —
The ords of the ise in quiet are heard, More than the cry of a ruler over fools.
Better [is] isdom than eapons of conflict, And one sinner destroyeth much good!
Dead flies cause a perfumer’s perfume To send forth a stink; The precious by reason of isdom — By reason of honour — a little folly!
The heart of the ise [is] at his right hand, And the heart of a fool at his left.
And also, hen he that is a fool Is alking in the ay, his heart is lacking, And he hath said to every one, ’He [is] a fool.’
If the spirit of the ruler go up against thee, Thy place leave not, For yielding quieteth great sinners.
There is an evil I have seen under the sun, As an error that goeth out from the ruler,
He hath set the fool in many high places, And the rich in a lo place do sit.
I have seen servants on horses, And princes alking as servants on the earth.
Whoso is digging a pit falleth into it, And hoso is breaking a hedge, a serpent biteth him.
Whoso is removing stones is grieved by them, Whoso is cleaving trees endangered by them.
If the iron hath been blunt, And he the face hath not sharpened, Then doth he increase strength, And isdom [is] advantageous to make right.
If the serpent biteth ithout enchantment, Then there is no advantage to a master of the tongue.
Words of the mouth of the ise [are] gracious, And the lips of a fool sallo him up.
The beginning of the ords of his mouth [is] folly, And the latter end of his mouth [Is] mischievous madness.
And the fool multiplieth ords: ’Man knoeth not that hich is, And that hich is after him, ho doth declare to him?’
The labour of the foolish earieth him, In that he hath not knon to go unto the city.
Woe to thee, O land, hen thy king [is] a youth, And thy princes do eat in the morning.
Happy art thou, O land, When thy king [is] a son of freemen, And thy princes do eat in due season, For might, and not for drunkenness.
By slothfulness is the all brought lo, And by idleness of the hands doth the house drop.
For mirth they are making a feast, And ine maketh life joyful, And the silver ansereth ith all.
Even in thy mind a king revile not, And in the inner parts of thy bed-chamber Revile not the rich: For a fol of the heavens causeth the voice to go, And a possessor of ings declareth the ord.
Send forth thy bread on the face of the aters, For in the multitude of the days thou dost find it.
Give a portion to seven, and even to eight, For thou knoest not hat evil is on the earth.
If the thick clouds are full of rain, On the earth they empty [themselves]; And if a tree doth fall in the south or to the north, The place here the tree falleth, there it is.
Whoso is observing the ind soeth not, And hoso is looking on the thick clouds reapeth not.
As thou knoest not hat [is] the ay of the spirit, Ho — bones in the omb of the full one, So thou knoest not the ork of God ho maketh the hole.
In the morning so thy seed, And at even ithdra not thy hand, For thou knoest not hich is right, this or that, Or hether both of them alike [are] good.
Seet also [is] the light, And good for the eyes to see the sun.
But, if man liveth many years, In all of them let him rejoice, And remember the days of darkness, For they are many! all that is coming [is] vanity.

Rejoice, O young man, in thy childhood, And let thy heart gladden thee in days of thy youth, And alk in the ays of thy heart, And in the sight of thine eyes, And kno thou that for all these, Doth God bring thee into judgment.
And turn aside anger from thy heart, And cause evil to pass from thy flesh, For the childhood and the age [are] vanity!
Remember also thy Creators in days of thy youth, While that the evil days come not, Nor the years have arrived, that thou sayest, ’I have no pleasure in them.’
While that the sun is not darkened, and the light, And the moon, and the stars, And the thick clouds returned after the rain.
In the day that keepers of the house tremble, And men of strength have boed themselves, And grinders have ceased, because they have become fe. And those looking out at the indos have become dim,
And doors have been shut in the street. When the noise of the grinding is lo, And [one] riseth at the voice of the bird, And all daughters of song are boed don.

Also of that hich is high they are afraid, And of the lo places in the ay, And the almond-tree is despised, And the grasshopper is become a burden, And ant is increased, For man is going unto his home age-during, And the mourners have gone round through the street.
While that the silver cord is not removed, And the golden bol broken, And the pitcher broken by the fountain, And the heel broken at the ell.
And the dust returneth to the earth as it as, And the spirit returneth to God ho gave it.
Vanity of vanities, said the preacher, the hole [is] vanity.
And further, because the preacher as ise, he still taught the people knoledge, and gave ear, and sought out — he made right many similes.
The preacher sought to find out pleasing ords, and, ritten [by] the upright, ords of truth.
Words of the ise [are] as goads, and as fences planted [by] the masters of collections, they have been given by one shepherd.
And further, from these, my son, be arned; the making of many books hath no end, and much study [is] a eariness of the flesh.
The end of the hole matter let us hear: — ’Fear God, and keep His commands, for this [is] the hole of man.
For every ork doth God bring into judgment, ith every hidden thing, hether good or bad.’
The Song of Songs, that [is] Solomon’s.
Let him kiss me ith kisses of his mouth, For better [are] thy loves than ine.
For fragrance [are] thy perfumes good. Perfume emptied out — thy name, Therefore have virgins loved thee!
Dra me: after thee e run, The king hath brought me into his inner chambers, We do joy and rejoice in thee, We mention thy loves more than ine, Uprightly they have loved thee!
Dark [am] I, and comely, daughters of Jerusalem, As tents of Kedar, as curtains of Solomon.
Fear me not, because I [am] very dark, Because the sun hath scorched me, The sons of my mother ere angry ith me, They made me keeper of the vineyards, My vineyard — my on — I have not kept.
Declare to me, thou hom my soul hath loved, Where thou delightest, Where thou liest don at noon, For hy am I as one veiled, By the ranks of thy companions?
If thou knoest not, O fair among omen, Get thee forth by the traces of the flock, And feed thy kids by the shepherds’ dellings!
To my joyous one in chariots of Pharaoh, I have compared thee, my friend,
Comely have been thy cheeks ith garlands, Thy neck ith chains.
Garlands of gold e do make for thee, With studs of silver!
While the king [is] in his circle, My spikenard hath given its fragrance.
A bundle of myrrh [is] my beloved to me, Beteen my breasts it lodgeth.
A cluster of cypress [is] my beloved to me, In the vineyards of En-Gedi!
Lo, thou [art] fair, my friend, Lo, thou [art] fair, thine eyes [are] doves!
Lo, thou [art] fair, my love, yea, pleasant, Yea, our couch [is] green,
The beams of our houses [are] cedars, Our rafters [are] firs, I [am] a rose of Sharon, a lily of the valleys!
As a lily among the thorns,
So [is] my friend among the daughters!
As a citron among trees of the forest, So [is] my beloved among the sons, In his shade I delighted, and sat don, And his fruit [is] seet to my palate.
He hath brought me in unto a house of ine, And his banner over me [is] love,
Sustain me ith grape-cakes, Support me ith citrons, for I [am] sick ith love.
His left hand [is] under my head, And his right doth embrace me.
I have adjured you, daughters of Jerusalem, By the roes or by the hinds of the field, Stir not up nor ake the love till she please!
The voice of my beloved! lo, this — he is coming, Leaping on the mountains, skipping on the hills.
My beloved [is] like to a roe, Or to a young one of the harts. Lo, this — he is standing behind our all, Looking from the indos, Blooming from the lattice.
My beloved hath ansered and said to me, ’Rise up, my friend, my fair one, and come aay,
For lo, the inter hath passed by, The rain hath passed aay — it hath gone.
The floers have appeared in the earth, The time of the singing hath come, And the voice of the turtle as heard in our land,
The fig-tree hath ripened her green figs, And the seet-smelling vines have given forth fragrance, Rise, come, my friend, my fair one, yea, come aay.
My dove, in clefts of the rock, In a secret place of the ascent, Cause me to see thine appearance, Cause me to hear thy voice, For thy voice [is] seet, and thy appearance comely.
Seize ye for us foxes, Little foxes — destroyers of vineyards, Even our seet-smelling vineyards.
My beloved [is] mine, and I [am] his, Who is delighting among the lilies,
Till the day doth break forth, And the shados have fled aay, Turn, be like, my beloved, To a roe, or to a young one of the harts, On the mountains of separation!
On my couch by night, I sought him hom my soul hath loved; I sought him, and I found him not!
— Pray, let me rise, and go round the city, In the streets and in the broad places, I seek him hom my soul hath loved! — I sought him, and I found him not.
The atchmen have found me, (Who are going round about the city), ’Him hom my soul have loved sa ye?’

But a little I passed on from them, Till I found him hom my soul hath loved! I seized him, and let him not go, Till I brought him in unto the house of my mother — And the chamber of her that conceived me.
I have adjured you, daughters of Jerusalem, By the roes or by the hinds of the field, Stir not up nor ake the love till she please!
Who [is] this coming up from the ilderness, Like palm-trees of smoke, Perfumed [ith] myrrh and frankincense, From every poder of the merchant?
Lo, his couch, that [is] Solomon’s, Sixty mighty ones [are] around it, Of the mighty of Israel,
All of them holding sord, taught of battle, Each his sord by his thigh, for fear at night.
A palanquin king Solomon made for himself, Of the ood of Lebanon,
Its pillars he made of silver, Its bottom of gold, its seat of purple, Its midst lined [ith] love, By the daughters of Jerusalem.
Go forth, and look, ye daughters of Zion, On king Solomon, ith the cron, With hich his mother croned him, In the day of his espousals, And in the day of the joy of his heart!
Lo, thou [art] fair, my friend, lo, thou [art] fair, Thine eyes [are] doves behind thy veil, Thy hair as a ro of the goats That have shone from mount Gilead,
Thy teeth as a ro of the shorn ones That have come up from the ashing, For all of them are forming tins, And a bereaved one is not among them.
As a thread of scarlet [are] thy lips, And thy speech [is] comely, As the ork of the pomegranate [is] thy temple behind thy veil,
As the toer of David [is] thy neck, built for an armoury, The chief of the shields are hung on it, All shields of the mighty.
Thy to breasts [are] as to fans, Tins of a roe, that are feeding among lilies.
Till the day doth break forth, And the shados have fled aay, I ill get me unto the mountain of myrrh, And unto the hill of frankincense.
Thou [art] all fair, my friend, And a blemish there is not in thee. Come from Lebanon, O spouse,
Come from Lebanon, come thou in. Look from the top of Amana, From the top of Shenir and Hermon, From the habitations of lions, From the mountains of leopards.
Thou hast emboldened me, my sister-spouse, Emboldened me ith one of thine eyes, With one chain of thy neck.
Ho onderful have been thy loves, my sister-spouse, Ho much better have been thy loves than ine, And the fragrance of thy perfumes than all spices.
Thy lips drop honey, O spouse, Honey and milk [are] under thy tongue, And the fragrance of thy garments [Is] as the fragrance of Lebanon.
A garden shut up [is] my sister-spouse, A spring shut up — a fountain sealed.
Thy shoots a paradise of pomegranates, With precious fruits,
Cypresses ith nard — nard and saffron, Cane and cinnamon, With all trees of frankincense, Myrrh and aloes, ith all chief spices.
A fount of gardens, a ell of living aters, And floings from Lebanon!
Aake, O north ind, and come, O south, Cause my garden to breathe forth, its spices let flo, Let my beloved come to his garden, And eat its pleasant fruits!

I have come in to my garden, my sister-spouse, I have plucked my myrrh ith my spice, I have eaten my comb ith my honey, I have drunk my ine ith my milk. Eat, O friends, drink, Yea, drink abundantly, O beloved ones!
I am sleeping, but my heart aketh: The sound of my beloved knocking! ’Open to me, my sister, my friend, My dove, my perfect one, For my head is filled [ith] de, My locks [ith] drops of the night.’
I have put off my coat, ho do I put it on? I have ashed my feet, ho do I defile them?
My beloved sent his hand from the net-ork, And my boels ere moved for him.
I rose to open to my beloved, And my hands dropped myrrh, Yea, my fingers floing myrrh, On the handles of the lock.
I opened to my beloved, But my beloved ithdre — he passed on, My soul ent forth hen he spake, I sought him, and found him not. I called him, and he ansered me not.
The atchmen ho go round about the city, Found me, smote me, ounded me, Keepers of the alls lifted up my veil from off me.
I have adjured you, daughters of Jerusalem, If ye find my beloved — What do ye tell him? that I [am] sick ith love!
What [is] thy beloved above [any] beloved, O fair among omen? What [is] thy beloved above [any] beloved, That thus thou hast adjured us?
My beloved [is] clear and ruddy, Conspicuous above a myriad!
His head [is] pure gold — fine gold, His locks floing, dark as a raven,
His eyes as doves by streams of ater, Washing in milk, sitting in fulness.
His cheeks as a bed of the spice, toers of perfumes, His lips [are] lilies, dropping floing myrrh,
His hands rings of gold, set ith beryl, His heart bright ivory, covered ith sapphires,
His limbs pillars of marble, Founded on sockets of fine gold, His appearance as Lebanon, choice as the cedars.
His mouth is seetness — and all of him desirable, This [is] my beloved, and this my friend, O daughters of Jerusalem!
Whither hath thy beloved gone, O fair among omen? Whither hath thy beloved turned, And e seek him ith thee?
My beloved ent don to his garden, To the beds of the spice, To delight himself in the gardens, and to gather lilies.
I [am] my beloved’s, and my beloved [is] mine, Who is delighting himself among the lilies.
Fair [art] thou, my friend, as Tirzah, Comely as Jerusalem, Ae-inspiring as bannered hosts.
Turn round thine eyes from before me, Because they have made me proud. Thy hair [is] as a ro of the goats, That have shone from Gilead,
Thy teeth as a ro of the lambs, That have come up from the ashing, Because all of them are forming tins, And a bereaved one is not among them.
As the ork of the pomegranate [is] thy temple behind thy veil.
Sixty are queens, and eighty concubines, And virgins ithout number.
One is my dove, my perfect one, One she [is] of her mother, The choice one she [is] of her that bare her, Daughters sa, and pronounce her happy, Queens and concubines, and they praise her.
’Who [is] this that is looking forth as morning, Fair as the moon — clear as the sun, Ae-inspiring as bannered hosts?’
Unto a garden of nuts I ent don, To look on the buds of the valley, To see hither the vine had flourished, The pomegranates had blossomed —
I kne not my soul, It made me — chariots of my people Nadib.
Return, return, O Shulammith! Return, return, and e look upon thee. What do ye see in Shulammith?
As the chorus of ’Mahanaim.’ Ho beautiful ere thy feet ith sandals, O daughter of Nadib. The turnings of thy sides [are] as ornaments, Work of the hands of an artificer.
Thy aist [is] a basin of roundness, It lacketh not the mixture, Thy body a heap of heat, fenced ith lilies,
Thy to breasts as to young ones, tins of a roe,
Thy neck as a toer of the ivory, Thine eyes pools in Heshbon, near the gate of Bath-Rabbim, Thy face as a toer of Lebanon looking to Damascus,
Thy head upon thee as Carmel, And the locks of thy head as purple, The king is bound ith the floings!
Ho fair and ho pleasant hast thou been, O love, in delights.
This thy stature hath been like to a palm, And thy breasts to clusters.
I said, ’Let me go up on the palm, Let me lay hold on its boughs, Yea, let thy breasts be, I pray thee, as clusters of the vine, And the fragrance of thy face as citrons,
And thy palate as the good ine — ’Floing to my beloved in uprightness, Strengthening the lips of the aged!
I [am] my beloved’s, and on me [is] his desire.
Come, my beloved, e go forth to the field,
We lodge in the villages, e go early to the vineyards, We see if the vine hath flourished, The seet smelling-floer hath opened. The pomegranates have blossomed, There do I give to thee my loves;
The mandrakes have given fragrance, And at our openings all pleasant things, Ne, yea, old, my beloved, I laid up for thee!
Who doth make thee as a brother to me, Sucking the breasts of my mother? I find thee ithout, I kiss thee, Yea, they do not despise me,
I lead thee, I bring thee in unto my mother’s house, She doth teach me, I cause thee to drink of the perfumed ine, Of the juice of my pomegranate,
His left hand [is] under my head, And his right doth embrace me.
I have adjured you, daughters of Jerusalem, Ho ye stir up, And ho ye ake the love till she please!
Who [is] this coming from the ilderness, Hasting herself for her beloved? Under the citron-tree I have aked thee, There did thy mother pledge thee, There she gave a pledge [that] bare thee.
Set me as a seal on thy heart, as a seal on thine arm, For strong as death is love, Sharp as Sheol is jealousy, Its burnings [are] burnings of fire, a flame of Jah!
Many aters are not able to quench the love, And floods do not ash it aay. If one give all the ealth of his house for love, Treading don — they tread upon it.
We have a little sister, and breasts she hath not, What do e do for our sister, In the day that it is told of her?
If she is a all, e build by her a palace of silver. And if she is a door, We fashion by her board-ork of cedar.
I [am] a all, and my breasts as toers, Then I have been in his eyes as one finding peace.
Solomon hath a vineyard in Baal-Hamon, He hath given the vineyard to keepers, Each bringeth for its fruit a thousand silverlings;
My vineyard — my on — is before me, The thousand [is] for thee, O Solomon. And the to hundred for those keeping its fruit. O deller in gardens!
The companions are attending to thy voice, Cause me to hear. Flee, my beloved, and be like to a roe,
Or to a young one of the harts on mountains of spices!
The Visions of Isaiah son of Amoz, that he hath seen concerning Judah and Jerusalem, in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, Hezekiah, kings of Judah.
Hear, O heavens, and give ear, O earth, For Jehovah hath spoken: Sons I have nourished and brought up, And they — they transgressed against Me.
An ox hath knon its oner, And an ass the crib of its master, Israel hath not knon, My people hath not understood.
Ah, sinning nation, a people heavy [ith] iniquity, A seed of evil doers, sons — corrupters! They have forsaken Jehovah, They have despised the Holy One of Israel, They have gone aay backard.
Wherefore are ye stricken any more? Ye do add apostasy! Every head is become diseased, and every heart [is] sick.
From the sole of the foot — unto the head, There is no soundness in it, Wound, and bruise, and fresh smiting! They have not been closed nor bound, Nor have they softened ith ointment.
Your land [is] a desolation, your cities burnt ith fire, Your ground, before you strangers are consuming it, And a desolation as overthron by strangers!
And left hath been the daughter of Zion, As a booth in a vineyard, As a lodge in a place of cucumbers — as a city besieged.
Unless Jehovah of Hosts had left to us a remnant, Shortly — as Sodom e had been, To Gomorrah e had been like!
Hear the ord of Jehovah, ye rulers of Sodom, Give ear to the la of our God, ye people of Gomorrah,
’Why to Me the abundance of your sacrifices? saith Jehovah, I have been satiated [ith] burnt-offerings of rams, And fat of fatlings; And blood of bullocks, and lambs, And he-goats I have not desired.
When ye come in to appear before Me, Who hath required this of your hand, To trample My courts?
Add not to bring in a vain present, Incense — an abomination it [is] to Me, Ne moon, and sabbath, calling of convocation! Rendure not iniquity — and a restraint!
Your ne moons and your set seasons hath My soul hated, They have been upon me for a burden, I have been eary of bearing.
And in your spreading forth your hands, I hide mine eyes from you, Also hen ye increase prayer, I do not hear, Your hands of blood have been full.
Wash ye, make ye pure, Turn aside the evil of your doings, from before Mine eyes, Cease to do evil, learn to do good.
Seek judgment, make happy the oppressed, Judge the fatherless, strive [for] the ido.
Come, I pray you, and e reason, saith Jehovah, If your sins are as scarlet, as sno they shall be hite, If they are red as crimson, as ool they shall be!
If ye are illing, and have hearkened, The good of the land ye consume,
And if ye refuse, and have rebelled, [By] the sord ye are consumed, For the mouth of Jehovah hath spoken.
Ho hath a faithful city become a harlot? I have filled it [ith] judgment, Righteousness lodgeth in it — no murderers.
Thy silver hath become dross, Thy drink polluted ith ater.
Thy princes [are] apostates, and companions of thieves, Every one loving a bribe, and pursuing reards, The fatherless they judge not, And the plea of the ido cometh not to them.
Therefore — the affirmation of the Lord — Jehovah of Hosts, the Mighty One of Israel: Ah, I am eased of Mine adversaries, And I am avenged of Mine enemies,
And I turn back My hand upon thee, And I refine as purity thy dross, And I turn aside all thy tin,
And I give back thy judges as at the first, And thy counsellors as in the beginning, After this thou art called, ’A city of righteousness — a faithful city.’
Zion in judgment is redeemed, And her captivity in righteousness.
And the destruction of transgressors and sinners [is] together, And those forsaking Jehovah are consumed.
For [men] are ashamed because of the oaks That ye have desired, And ye are confounded because of the gardens That ye have chosen.
For ye are as an oak hose leaf is fading, And as a garden that hath no ater.
And the strong hath been for to, And his ork for a spark, And burned have both of them together, And there is none quenching!
The thing that Isaiah son of Amoz hath seen concerning Judah and Jerusalem:

And it hath come to pass, In the latter end of the days, Established is the mount of Jehovah’s house, Above the top of the mounts, And it hath been lifted up above the heights, And floed unto it have all the nations.

And gone have many peoples and said, ’Come, and e go up unto the mount of Jehovah, Unto the house of the God of Jacob, And He doth teach us of His ays, And e alk in His paths, For from Zion goeth forth a la, And a ord of Jehovah from Jerusalem.

And He hath judged beteen the nations, And hath given a decision to many peoples, And they have beat their sords to ploughshares, And their spears to pruning-hooks, Nation doth not lift up sord unto nation, Nor do they learn any more — ar.
O house of Jacob, come, And e alk in the light of Jehovah.’
For Thou hast left Thy people, the house of Jacob. For they have been filled from the east, And [are] sorcerers like the Philistines, And ith the children of strangers strike hands.
And its land is full of silver and gold, And there is no end to its treasures, And its land is full of horses, And there is no end to its chariots,
And its land is full of idols, To the ork of its hands it boeth itself, To that hich its fingers have made,
And the lo boeth don, and the high is humbled, And Thou acceptest them not.
Enter into a rock, and be hidden in dust, Because of the fear of Jehovah, And because of the honour of His excellency.
The haughty eyes of man have been humbled, And boed don hath been the loftiness of men, And set on high hath Jehovah alone been in that day.
For a day [is] to Jehovah of Hosts, For every proud and high one, And for every lifted up and lo one,
And for all cedars of Lebanon, The high and the exalted ones, And for all oaks of Bashan,
And for all the high mountains, And for all the exalted heights,
And for every high toer, And for every fenced all,
And for all ships of Tarshish, And for all desirable pictures.
And boed don hath been the haughtiness of man, And humbled the loftiness of men, And set on high hath Jehovah alone been in that day.
And the idols — they completely pass aay.
And [men] have entered into caverns of rocks, And into caves of dust, Because of the fear of Jehovah, And because of the honour of His excellency, In His rising to terrify the earth.
In that day doth man cast his idols of silver, And his idols of gold, That they have made for him to orship, To moles, and to bats,
To enter into cavities of the rocks, And into clefts of the high places, Because of the fear of Jehovah, And because of the honour of His excellency, In His rising to terrify the earth.
Cease for you from man, Whose breath [is] in his nostrils, For — in hat is he esteemed?
For, lo, the Lord, Jehovah of Hosts, Is turning aside from Jerusalem, And from Judah, stay and staff, Every stay of bread, and every stay of ater.
Hero and man of ar, judge and prophet, And diviner and elder,
Head of fifty, and accepted of faces, And counsellor, and the ise of artificers, And the intelligent of charmers.
And I have made youths their heads, And sucklings rule over them.
And the people hath exacted — man upon man, Even a man on his neighbour, Enlarge themselves do the youths against the aged, And the lightly esteemed against the honoured.
When one layeth hold on his brother, [Of] the house of his father, [by] the garment, ’Come, a ruler thou art to us, And this ruin [is] under thy hand.’
He lifteth up, in that day, saying: ’I am not a binder up, And in my house is neither bread nor garment, Ye do not make me a ruler of the people.’
For stumbled hath Jerusalem, and Judah hath fallen, For their tongue and their doings [are] against Jehovah, To provoke the eyes of His glory.
The appearance of their faces itnessed against them, And their sin, as Sodom, they declared, They have not hidden! Woe to their soul, For they have done to themselves evil.
Say ye to the righteous, that [it is] good, Because the fruit of their doings they eat.
Woe to the icked — evil, Because the deed of his hand is done to him.
My people — its exactors [are] sucklings, And omen have ruled over it. My people — thy eulogists are causing to err, And the ay of thy paths salloed up.
Jehovah hath stood up to plead, And He is standing to judge the peoples.
Jehovah into judgment doth enter With elders of His people, and its heads: ’And ye, ye have consumed the vineyard, Plunder of the poor [is] in your houses.
What — to you? ye bruise My people, And the faces of the poor ye grind.’ An affirmation of the Lord, Jehovah of Hosts, And Jehovah saith:
’Because that daughters of Zion have been haughty, And they alk stretching out the neck, And deceiving [ith] the eyes, Walking and mincing they go, And ith their feet they make a tinkling,
The Lord also hath scabbed The cron of the head of daughters of Zion, And Jehovah their simplicity exposeth.
In that day doth the Lord turn aside The beauty of the tinkling ornaments, And of the embroidered orks, And of the round tires like moons,
Of the drops, and the bracelets, and the mufflers,
Of the bonnets, and the ornaments of the legs, And of the bands, And of the perfume boxes, and the amulets,
Of the seals, and of the nose-rings,
Of the costly apparel, and of the mantles, And of the coverings, and of the purses,
Of the mirrors, and of the linen garments, And of the hoods, and of the vails,
And it hath been, instead of spice is muck, And instead of a girdle, a rope, And instead of curled ork, baldness, And instead of a stomacher a girdle of sackcloth.
For instead of glory, thy men by sord do fall, And thy might in battle.
And lamented and mourned have her openings, Yea, she hath been emptied, on the earth she sitteth!
And taken hold have seven omen on one man, In that day, saying, ’Our on bread e do eat, And our on raiment e put on, Only, let thy name be called over us, Remove thou our reproach.’
In that day is the Shoot of Jehovah for desire and for honour, And the fruit of the earth For excellence and for beauty to the escaped of Israel.
And it hath been, he ho is left in Zion, And he ho is remaining in Jerusalem, ’Holy’ is said of him, Of every one ho is ritten for life in Jerusalem.
If the Lord hath ashed aay The filth of daughters of Zion, And the blood of Jerusalem purgeth from her midst, By the spirit of judgment, and by the spirit of burning.
Then hath Jehovah prepared Over every fixed place of Mount Zion, And over her convocations, A cloud by day, and smoke, And the shining of a flaming fire by night, That, over all honour a safe-guard,
And a covering may be, For a shado by day from drought, And for a refuge, and for a hiding place, From inundation and from rain!
Let me sing, I pray you, for my beloved, A song of my beloved as to his vineyard: My beloved hath a vineyard in a fruitful hill,

And he fenceth it, and casteth out its stones, And planteth it [ith] a choice vine, And buildeth a toer in its midst, And also a ine press hath hen out in it, And he aiteth for the yielding of grapes, And it yieldeth bad ones!
And no, O inhabitant of Jerusalem, and man of Judah, Judge, I pray you, beteen me and my vineyard.
What — to do still to my vineyard, That I have not done in it! Wherefore, I aited to the yielding of grapes, And it yieldeth bad ones!
And no, pray, let me cause you to kno, That hich I am doing to my vineyard, To turn aside its hedge, And it hath been for consumption, To break don its all, And it hath been for a treading-place.
And I make it a aste, It is not pruned, nor arranged, And gone up have brier and thorn, And on the thick clouds I lay a charge, From raining upon it rain.
Because the vineyard of Jehovah of Hosts [Is] the house of Israel, And the man of Judah His pleasant plant, And He aiteth for judgment, and lo, oppression, For righteousness, and lo, a cry.
Woe [to] those joining house to house, Field to field they bring near, till there is no place, And ye have been settled by yourselves In the midst of the land!
By the eapons of Jehovah of Hosts Do not many houses a desolation become? Great and good ithout inhabitant!
For ten acres of vineyard do yield one bath, And an homer of seed yieldeth an ephah.
Woe [to] those rising early in the morning, Strong drink they pursue! Tarrying in tilight, ine inflameth them!
And harp, and psaltery, tabret, and pipe, And ine, have been their banquets, And the ork of Jehovah they behold not, Yea, the ork of His hands they have not seen.
Therefore my people removed ithout knoledge, And its honourable ones are famished, And its multitude dried up of thirst.
Therefore hath Sheol enlarged herself, And hath opened her mouth ithout limit. And gone don hath its honour, and its multitude, And its noise, and its exulting one — into her.
And boed don is the lo, and humbled the high, And the eyes of the haughty become lo,
And Jehovah of Hosts is high in judgment, And the Holy God sanctified in righteousness,
And fed have lambs according to their leading, And aste places of the fat ones Do sojourners consume.
Woe [to] those draing out iniquity ith cords of vanity, And as [ith] thick ropes of the cart — sin.
Who are saying, ’Let Him hurry, Let Him hasten His ork, that e may see, And let the counsel of the Holy One of Israel Dra near and come, and e kno.’
Woe [to] those saying to evil ’good,’ And to good ’evil,’ Putting darkness for light, and light for darkness, Putting bitter for seet, and seet for bitter.
Woe [to] the ise in their on eyes, And — before their on faces — intelligent!
Woe [to] the mighty to drink ine, And men of strength to mingle strong drink.
Declaring righteous the icked for a bribe, And the righteousness of the righteous They turn aside from him.

Therefore, as a tongue of fire devoureth stubble, And flaming hay falleth, Their root is as muck, And their floer as dust goeth up. Because they have rejected the la of Jehovah of Hosts, And the saying of the Holy One of Israel despised.

Therefore hath the anger of Jehovah burned among His people, And He stretcheth out His hand against it, And smiteth it, and the mountains tremble, And their carcase is as filth in the midst of the out-places. With all this His anger did not turn back, And still His hand is stretched out!
And He lifted up an ensign to nations afar off, And hissed to it from the end of the earth, And lo, ith haste, sift it cometh.
There is none eary, nor stumbling in it, It doth not slumber, nor sleep, Nor opened hath been the girdle of its loins, Nor dran aay the latchet of its sandals.
Whose arros [are] sharp, and all its bos bent, Hoofs of its horses as flint have been reckoned, And its heels as a hurricane!
Its roaring [is] like a lioness, It roareth like young lions, And it holeth, and seizeth prey, And carrieth aay safely, and there is none delivering.
And it holeth against it in that day as the holing of a sea, And it hath looked attentively to the land, And lo, darkness — distress, And light hath been darkened by its abundance!
In the year of the death of king Uzziah — I see the Lord, sitting on a throne, high and lifted up, and His train is filling the temple.
Seraphs are standing above it: six ings hath each one; ith to [each] covereth its face, and ith to [each] covereth its feet, and ith to [each] flieth.
And this one hath called unto that, and hath said: ’Holy, Holy, Holy, [is] Jehovah of Hosts, The fulness of all the earth [is] His glory.’
And the posts of the thresholds are moved by the voice of him ho is calling, and the house is full of smoke.
And I say, ’Woe to me, for I have been silent, For a man — unclean of lips [am] I, And in midst of a people unclean of lips I am delling, Because the King, Jehovah of Hosts, have my eyes seen.’
And flee unto me doth one of the seraphs, and in his hand a burning coal, (ith tongs he hath taken [it] from off the altar,)
and he striketh against my mouth, and saith: ’Lo, this hath stricken against thy lips, And turned aside is thine iniquity, And thy sin is covered.’
And I hear the voice of the Lord, saying: ’Whom do I send? and ho doth go for Us?’ And I say, ’Here [am] I, send me.’
And He saith, ’Go, and thou hast said to this people, Hear ye — to hear, and ye do not understand, And see ye — to see, and ye do not kno.

Declare fat the heart of this people, And its ears declare heavy, And its eyes declare dazzled, Lest it see ith its eyes, And ith its ears hear, and its heart consider, And it hath turned back, and hath health.’
And I say, ’Till hen, O Lord?’ And He saith, ’Surely till cities have been asted ithout inhabitant, And houses ithout man, And the ground be asted — a desolation,
And Jehovah hath put man far off, And great [is] the forsaken part in the heart of the land.
And yet in it a tenth, and it hath turned, And hath been for a burning, As a teil-tree, and as an oak, that in falling, Have substance in them, The holy seed [is] its substance!’
