And it cometh to pass in the days of Ahaz, son of Jotham, son of Uzziah, king of Judah, gone up hath Rezin king of Aram, and Pekah, son of Remaliah, king of Israel, to Jerusalem, to battle against it, and he is not able to fight against it.
And it is declared to the house of David, saying, ’Aram hath been led toards Ephraim,’ And his heart and the heart of his people is moved, like the moving of trees of a forest by the presence of ind.
And Jehovah saith unto Isaiah, ’Go forth, I pray thee, to meet Ahaz, thou, and Shear-Jashub thy son, unto the end of the conduit of the upper pool, unto the highay of the fuller’s field,

and thou hast said unto him: ’Take heed, and be quiet, fear not, And let not thy heart be timid, Because of these to tails of smoking brands, For the fierceness of the anger of Rezin and Aram, And the son of Remaliah.
Because that Aram counselled against thee evil, Ephraim and the son of Remaliah, saying:
We go up into Judah, and e vex it, And e rend it unto ourselves, And e cause a king to reign in its midst — The son of Tabeal.
Thus said the Lord Jehovah: It doth not stand, nor shall it be!
For the head of Aram [is] Damascus, And the head of Damascus [is] Rezin, And ithin sixty and five years Is Ephraim broken from [being] a people.
And the head of Ephraim [is] Samaria, And the head of Samaria [is] the son of Remaliah. If ye do not give credence, Surely ye are not stedfast.’
And Jehovah addeth to speak unto Ahaz, saying:
’Ask for thee a sign from Jehovah thy God, Make deep the request, or make [it] high upards.’
And Ahaz saith, ’I do not ask nor try Jehovah.’
And he saith, ’Hear, I pray you, O house of David, Is it a little thing for you to eary men, That ye eary also my God?
Therefore the Lord Himself giveth to you a sign, Lo, the Virgin is conceiving, And is bringing forth a son, And hath called his name Immanuel,
Butter and honey he doth eat, When he knoeth to refuse evil, and to fix on good.
For before the youth doth kno To refuse evil, and to fix on good, Forsaken is the land thou art vexed ith, because of her to kings.
Jehovah bringeth on thee, and on thy people, And on the house of thy father, Days that have not come, Even from the day of the turning aside of Ephraim from Judah, By the king of Asshur.
And it hath come to pass, in that day, Jehovah doth hiss for a fly that [is] in the extremity of the brooks of Egypt, And for a bee that [is] in the land of Asshur.
And they have come, and rested all of them in the desolate valleys, And in holes of the rocks, and on all the thorns, And on all the commendable things.
In that day doth the Lord shave, By a razor that is hired beyond the river, By the king of Asshur, The head, and the hair of the feet, Yea, also the beard it consumeth.
And it hath come to pass, in that day, A man keepeth alive a heifer of the herd, And to of the flock,
And it hath come to pass, From the abundance of the yielding of milk he eateth butter, For butter and honey doth every one eat Who is left in the heart of the land.
And it hath come to pass, in that day, Every place here there are a thousand vines, At a thousand silverlings, Is for briers and for thorns.
With arros and ith bo he cometh thither, Because all the land is brier and thorn.
And all the hills that ith a mattock are kept in order, Thither cometh not the fear of brier and thorn, And it hath been for the sending forth of ox, And for the treading of sheep!’
And Jehovah saith unto me, ’Take to thee a great tablet, and rite upon it ith a graving tool of man, To haste spoil, enjoy prey.’
And I cause faithful itnesses to testify to me, Uriah the priest, and Zechariah son of Jeberechiah.
And I dra near unto the prophetess, and she conceiveth, and beareth a son; and Jehovah saith unto me, ’Call his name Maher-shalal-hash-baz,
for before the youth doth kno to cry, My father, and My mother, one taketh aay the ealth of Damascus and the spoil of Samaria, before the king of Asshur.’
And Jehovah addeth to speak unto me again, saying:
’Because that this people hath refused The aters of Shiloah that go softly, And is rejoicing ith Rezin and the son of Remaliah,

Therefore, lo, the Lord is bringing up on them, The aters of the river, the mighty and the great, (The king of Asshur, and all his glory,) And it hath gone up over all its streams, And hath gone on over all its banks.
And it hath passed on into Judah, It hath overflon and passed over, Unto the neck it cometh, And the stretching out of its ings Hath been the fulness of the breadth of thy land, O Emmanu-El!
Be friends, O nations, and be broken, And give ear, all ye far off ones of earth, Gird yourselves, and be broken, Gird yourselves, and be broken.
Take counsel, and it is broken, Speak a ord, and it doth not stand, Because of Emmanu-El!’
For thus hath Jehovah spoken unto me ith strength of hand, and instructeth me against alking in the ay of this people, saying,
’Ye do not say, A confederacy, To all to hom this people saith, A confederacy, And its fear ye do not fear, Nor declare fearful.
Jehovah of Hosts — Him ye do sanctify, And He [is] your Fear, and He your Dread,
And He hath been for a sanctuary, And for a stone of stumbling, and for a rock of falling, To the to houses of Israel, For a gin and for a snare to the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
And many among them have stumbled and fallen, And been broken, and snared, and captured.
Bind up the testimony, Seal the la among My disciples.
And I have aited for Jehovah, Who is hiding His face from the house of Jacob, And I have looked for Him.
Lo, I, and the children hom Jehovah hath given to me, [Are] for signs and for onders in Israel, From Jehovah of Hosts, ho is delling in Mount Zion.
And hen they say unto you, ’Seek unto those having familiar spirits, And unto izards, ho chatter and mutter, Doth not a people seek unto its God? — For the living unto the dead!
To the la and to the testimony! If not, let them say after this manner, ’That there is no dan to it.’
— And it hath passed over into it, hardened and hungry, And it hath come to pass, That it is hungry, and hath been roth, And made light of its king, and of its God, And hath looked upards.
And unto the land it looketh attentively, And lo, adversity and darkness! — Dimness, distress, and thick darkness is driven aay, But not the dimness for hich she is in distress!
As the former time made light The land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, So the latter hath honoured the ay of the sea, Beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations.
The people ho are alking in darkness Have seen a great light, Dellers in a land of death-shade, Light hath shone upon them.
Thou hast multiplied the nation, Thou hast made great its joy, They have joyed before Thee as the joy in harvest, As [men] rejoice in their apportioning spoil.
Because the yoke of its burden, And the staff of its shoulder, the rod of its exactor, Thou hast broken as [in] the day of Midian.
For every battle of a arrior [is] ith rushing, and raiment rolled in blood, And it hath been for burning — fuel of fire.

For a Child hath been born to us, A Son hath been given to us, And the princely poer is on his shoulder, And He doth call his name Wonderful, Counsellor, Mighty God, Father of Eternity, Prince of Peace.

To the increase of the princely poer, And of peace, there is no end, On the throne of David, and on his kingdom, To establish it, and to support it, In judgment and in righteousness, Henceforth, even unto the age, The zeal of Jehovah of Hosts doth this.
A ord hath the Lord sent into Jacob, And it hath fallen in Israel.
And the people have knon — all of it, Ephraim, and the inhabitant of Samaria, In pride and in greatness of heart, saying,
’Bricks have fallen, and hen ork e build, Sycamores have been cut don, and cedars e rene.’
And Jehovah setteth the adversaries of Rezin on high above him, And his enemies he joineth together,
Aram from before, and Philistia from behind, And they devour Israel ith the hole mouth. With all this not turned back hath His anger, And still His hand is stretched out.
And the people hath not turned back unto Him ho is smiting it, And Jehovah of Hosts they have not sought.
And Jehovah cutteth off from Israel head and tail, Branch and reed — the same day,
Elder, and accepted of face, he [is] the head, Prophet, teacher of falsehood, he [is] the tail.
And the eulogists of this people are causing to err, And its eulogised ones are consumed.

Therefore, over its young men the Lord rejoiceth not, And its orphans, and its idos He pitieth not, For every one [is] profane, and an evil doer, And every mouth is speaking folly. With all this not turned back hath His anger, And still His hand is stretched out.
For burned as a fire hath ickedness, Brier and thorn it devoureth, And it kindleth in thickets of the forest, And they lift themselves up, an exaltation of smoke!
In the rath of Jehovah of Hosts Hath the land been consumed, And the people is as fuel of fire; A man on his brother hath no pity,
And cutteth don on the right, and hath been hungry, And he devoureth on the left, And they have not been satisfied, Each the flesh of his on arm they devour.
Manasseh — Ephraim, and Ephraim — Manasseh, Together they [are] against Judah, With all this not turned back hath His anger. And still His hand is stretched out!
Woe [to] those decreeing decrees of iniquity, And riters ho have prescribed perverseness.
To turn aside from judgment the poor, And to take violently aay the judgment Of the afflicted of My people, That idos may be their prey, That the fatherless they may spoil.
And hat do ye at a day of inspection? And at desolation? — from afar it cometh. Near hom do ye flee for help? And here do ye leave your honour?
Without Me it hath boed don In the place of a bound one, And in the place of the slain they fall. With all this not turned back hath His anger, And still His hand is stretched out.
Woe [to] Asshur, a rod of Mine anger, And a staff in their hand [is] Mine indignation.
Against a profane nation I send him, And concerning a people of My rath I charge him, To spoil spoil, and to seize prey, And to make it a treading-place as the clay of out places.
And he — he thinketh not so, And his heart reckoneth not so, For — to destroy [is] in his heart, And to cut off nations not a fe.
For he saith, ’Are not my princes altogether kings?
Is not Calno as Carchemish? Is not Hamath as Arpad? Is not Samaria as Damascus?
As my hand hath got to the kingdoms of a orthless thing, and their graven images, [Greater] than Jerusalem and than Samaria,
Do I not — as I have done to Samaria, And to her orthless things, So do to Jerusalem and to her grievous things?

And it hath come to pass, When the Lord doth fulfil all His ork In mount Zion and in Jerusalem, I see concerning the fruit of the greatness Of the heart of the king of Asshur. And concerning the glory of the height of his eyes.

For he hath said, ’By the poer of my hand I have rought, And by my isdom, for I have been intelligent, And I remove borders of the peoples, And their chief ones I have spoiled, And I put don as a mighty one the inhabitants,

And my hand as to a nest Getteth to the ealth of the peoples, And as a gathering of forsaken eggs All the earth I — I have gathered, And there hath not been one moving ing, Or opening mouth, or hispering.’
— Doth the axe glorify itself Against him ho is heing ith it? Doth the sa magnify itself Against him ho is shaking it? As a rod aving those lifting it up! As a staff lifting up that hich is not ood!
Therefore doth the Lord, the Lord of Hosts, Send among his fat ones leanness, And under his honour He kindleth a burning As the burning of a fire.
And the light of Israel hath been for a fire, And his Holy One for a flame, And it hath burned, and devoured his thorn And his brier in one day.
And the honour of his forest, and his fruitful field, From soul even unto flesh He doth consume, And it hath been as the fainting of a standard-bearer.
And the rest of the trees of his forest [are] fe, And a youth doth rite them.

And it hath come to pass, in that day, The remnant of Israel, And the escaped of the house of Jacob, Do not add any more to lean on its smiter, And have leant on Jehovah, The Holy One of Israel, in truth.
A remnant returneth — a remnant of Jacob, Unto the Mighty God.
For though thy people Israel be as the sand of the sea, A remnant doth return of it, A consumption determined, Overfloing [ith] righteousness.
For a consumption that is determined, The Lord, Jehovah of Hosts, Is making in the midst of all the land.

Therefore, thus said the Lord, Jehovah of Hosts, ’Be not afraid, my people, inhabiting Zion, because of Asshur, With a rod he doth smite thee, And his staff lifteth up against thee, in the ay of Egypt.
For yet a very little, And the indignation hath been completed, And Mine anger by their earing out.
And aaking for him is Jehovah of Hosts, A scourge like the smiting of Midian at the rock Oreb, And his rod [is] over the sea, And he hath lifted it in the ay of Egypt.
And it hath come to pass, in that day, Turned is his burden from off thy shoulder, And his yoke from off thy neck, And destroyed hath been the yoke, because of prosperity.
He hath come in against Aiath, He hath passed over into Migron, At Michmash he looketh after his vessels.
They have gone over the passage, Geba they have made a lodging place, Trembled hath Rama, Gibeah of Saul fled.
Cry aloud [ith] thy voice, daughter of Gallim, Give attention, Laish! anser her, Anathoth.
Fled aay hath Madmenah, The inhabitants of the high places have hardened themselves.
Yet to-day in Nob to remain, Wave its hand doth the mount of the daughter of Zion, The hill of Jerusalem.
Lo, the Lord, Jehovah of Hosts, Is lopping a branch ith violence, And the high of stature are cut don, And the lofty are become lo,
And He hath gone round the thickets of the forest ith iron, And Lebanon by a mighty one falleth!
And a rod hath come out from the stock of Jesse, And a branch from his roots is fruitful.
Rested on him hath the Spirit of Jehovah, The spirit of isdom and understanding, The spirit of counsel and might, The spirit of knoledge and fear of Jehovah.
To refresh him in the fear of Jehovah, And by the sight of his eyes he judgeth not, Nor by the hearing of his ears decideth.

And he hath judged in righteousness the poor, And decided in uprightness for the humble of earth, And hath smitten earth ith the rod of his mouth, And ith the breath of his lips he putteth the icked to death.
And righteousness hath been the girdle of his loins, And faithfulness — the girdle of his reins.
And a olf hath sojourned ith a lamb, And a leopard ith a kid doth lie don, And calf, and young lion, and fatling [are] together, And a little youth is leader over them.
And co and bear do feed, Together lie don their young ones, And a lion as an ox eateth stra.
And played hath a suckling by the hole of an asp, And on the den of a cockatrice Hath the eaned one put his hand.
Evil they do not, nor destroy in all My holy mountain, For full hath been the earth ith the knoledge of Jehovah, As the aters are covering the sea.
And there hath been, in that day, A root of Jesse that is standing for an ensign of peoples, Unto him do nations seek, And his rest hath been — honour!

And it hath come to pass, in that day, The Lord addeth a second time his poer, To get the remnant of His people that is left, From Asshur, and from Egypt, And from Pathros, and from Cush, And from Elam, and from Shinar, And from Hamath, and from isles of the sea,
And He hath lifted up an ensign to nations, And gathereth the driven aay of Israel, And the scattered of Judah He assembleth, From the four ings of the earth.
And turned aside hath the envy of Ephraim, And the adversaries of Judah are cut off, Ephraim doth not envy Judah, And Judah doth not distress Ephraim.
And they have flon on the shoulder of the Philistines estard, Together they spoil the sons of the east, Edom and Moab sending forth their hand, And sons of Ammon obeying them.

And Jehovah hath devoted to destruction The tongue of the sea of Egypt, And hath aved His hand over the river, In the terror of his ind, And hath smitten it at the seven streams, And hath caused [men] to tread [it] ith shoes.
And there hath been a highay, For the remnant of His people that is left, from Asshur, As there as for Israel in the day of his coming up out of the land of Egypt!
And thou hast said in that day: ’I thank thee, O Jehovah, Though Thou hast been angry ith me, Turn back doth Thine anger, And Thou dost comfort me.
Lo, God [is] my salvation, I trust, and fear not, For my strength and song [is] Jah Jehovah, And He is to me for salvation.
And ye have dran aters ith joy Out of the fountains of salvation,
And ye have said in that day, Give ye praise to Jehovah, call in His name. Make knon among the peoples His acts. Make mention that set on high is His name.
Praise ye Jehovah, for excellence He hath done, Knon is this in all the earth.
Cry aloud, and sing, O inhabitant of Zion, For great in thy midst [is] the Holy One of Israel!’
The burden of Babylon that Isaiah son of Amoz hath seen:
’On a high mountain lift ye up an ensign, Raise the voice to them, ave the hand, And they go in to the openings of nobles.
I have given charge to My sanctified ones, Also I have called My mighty ones for Mine anger, Those rejoicing at Mine excellency.’
A voice of a multitude in the mountains, A likeness of a numerous people, A voice of noise from the kingdoms of nations ho are gathered, Jehovah of Hosts inspecting a host of battle!
They are coming in from a land afar off, From the end of the heavens, Jehovah and the instruments of His indignation, To destroy all the land.
Hol ye, for near [is] the day of Jehovah, As destruction from the Mighty it cometh.
Therefore, all hands do fail, And every heart of man doth melt.
And they have been troubled, Pains and pangs they take, As a travailing oman they are pained, A man at his friend they marvel, The appearance of flames — their faces!
Lo, the day of Jehovah doth come, Fierce, ith rath, and heat of anger, To make the land become a desolation, Yea, its sinning ones He destroyeth from it.
For the stars of the heavens, and their constellations, Cause not their light to shine, Darkened hath been the sun in its going out, And the moon causeth not its light to come forth.
And I have appointed on the orld evil, And on the icked their iniquity, And have caused to cease the excellency of the proud, And the excellency of the terrible I make lo.
I make man more rare than fine gold, And a common man than pure gold of Ophir.
Therefore the heavens I cause to tremble, And the earth doth shake from its place, In the rath of Jehovah of Hosts, And in a day of the heat of his anger.
And it hath been, as a roe driven aay, And as a flock that hath no gatherer, Each unto his people — they turn, And each unto his land — they flee.
Every one ho is found is thrust through, And every one ho is added falleth by sord.
And their sucklings are dashed to pieces before their eyes, Spoiled are their houses, and their ives lain ith.
Lo, I am stirring up against them the Medes, Who silver esteem not, And gold — they delight not in it.
And bos dash young men to pieces, And the fruit of the omb they pity not, On sons their eye hath no pity.
And Babylon, the beauty of kingdoms, The glory, the excellency of the Chaldeans, Hath been as overthron by God, With Sodom and ith Gomorrah.
She doth not sit for ever, Nor continueth unto many generations, Nor doth Arab pitch tent there, And shepherds lie not don there.
And Ziim have lain don there, And full have been their houses of holings, And delt there have daughters of an ostrich, And goats do skip there.
And Aiim have responded in his forsaken habitations, And dragons in palaces of delight, And near to come [is] her time, And her days are not dran out!
Because Jehovah loveth Jacob, And hath fixed again on Israel, And given them rest on their on land, And joined hath been the sojourner to them, And they have been admitted to the house of Jacob.

And peoples have taken them, And have brought them in unto their place, And the house of Israel have inherited them, On the land of Jehovah, For men-servants and for maid-servants, And they have been captors of their captors, And have ruled over their exactors.
And it hath come to pass, In the day of Jehovah’s giving rest to thee, From thy grief, and from thy trouble, And from the sharp bondage, That hath been served upon thee,
That thou hast taken up this simile Concerning the king of Babylon, and said, Ho hath the exactor ceased,
Ceased hath the golden one. Broken hath Jehovah the staff of the icked, The sceptre of rulers.
He ho is smiting peoples in rath, A smiting ithout intermission, He ho is ruling in anger nations, Pursuing ithout restraint!
At rest — quiet hath been all the earth, They have broken forth [into] singing.
Even firs have rejoiced over thee, Cedars of Lebanon — [saying]: Since thou hast lain don, The heer cometh not up against us.
Sheol beneath hath been troubled at thee, To meet thy coming in, It is aking up for thee Rephaim, All chiefs ones of earth, It hath raised up from their thrones All kings of nations.
All of them anser and say unto thee, Even thou hast become eak like us! Unto us thou hast become like!
Brought don to Sheol hath been thine excellency, The noise of thy psaltery, Under thee spread out hath been the orm, Yea, covering thee is the orm.
Ho hast thou fallen from the heavens, O shining one, son of the dan! Thou hast been cut don to earth, O eakener of nations.
And thou saidst in thy heart: the heavens I go up, Above stars of God I raise my throne, And I sit in the mount of meeting in the sides of the north.
I go up above the heights of a thick cloud, I am like to the Most High.
Only — unto Sheol thou art brought don, Unto the sides of the pit.
Thy beholders look to thee, to thee they attend, Is this the man causing the earth to tremble, Shaking kingdoms?
He hath made the orld as a ilderness, And his cities he hath broken don, Of his bound ones he opened not the house.
All kings of nations — all of them, Have lain don in honour, each in his house,
And — thou hast been cast out of thy grave, As an abominable branch, raiment of the slain, Thrust through ones of the sord, Going don unto the sons of the pit, As a carcase trodden don.
Thou art not united ith them in burial, For thy land thou hast destroyed, Thy people thou hast slain, Not named to the age is the seed of evil doers.
Prepare ye for his sons slaughter; Because of the iniquity of their fathers, They rise not, nor have possessed the land, Nor filled the face of the orld [ith] cities.
And I have risen up against them, (The affirmation of Jehovah of Hosts,) And have cut off, in reference to Babylon, Name and remnant, and continuator and successor, The affirmation of Jehovah.
And have made it for a possession of a bittern, And ponds of aters, And daubed it ith the mire of destruction, The affirmation of Jehovah of Hosts!
Sorn hath Jehovah of Hosts, saying, ’As I thought — so hath it not been? And as I counselled — it standeth;
To break Asshur in My land, And on My mountains I tread him don, And turned from off them hath his yoke, Yea, his burden from off their shoulder turneth aside.
This [is] the counsel that is counselled for all the earth, And this [is] the hand that is stretched out for all the nations.
For Jehovah of Hosts hath purposed, And ho doth make void? And His hand that is stretched out, Who doth turn it back?’
In the year of the death of king Ahaz as this burden:
Rejoice not thou, Philistia, all of thee, That broken hath been the rod of thy smiter, For from the root of a serpent cometh out a viper, And its fruit [is] a flying saraph.
And delighted have the first-born of the poor, And the needy in confidence lie don, And I have put to death ith famine thy root, And thy remnant it slayeth.
Hol, O gate; cry, O city, Melted art thou, Philistia, all of thee, For from the north smoke hath come, And there is none alone in his set places.
And hat doth one anser the messengers of a nation? ’That Jehovah hath founded Zion, And in it do the poor of His people trust!’
The burden of Moab. Because in a night destroyed as Ar of Moab — It hath been cut off, Because in a night destroyed as Kir of Moab — It hath been cut off.
He hath gone up to Bajith and Dibon, The high places — to eep, On Nebo and on Medeba Moab holeth, On all its heads [is] baldness, every beard cut off.
In its out-places they girded on sackcloth, On its pinnacles, and in its broad places, Every one holeth — going don ith eeping.
And cry doth Heshbon and Elealeh, Unto Jahaz heard hath been their voice, Therefore the armed ones of Moab do shout, His life hath been grievous to him.

My heart [is] toard Moab, Cry do her fugitives unto Zoar, a heifer of the third [year], For — the ascent of Luhith — With eeping he goeth up in it, For, in the ay of Horonaim, A cry of destruction they ake up.
For, the aters of Nimrim are desolations, For, ithered hath been the hay, Finished hath been the tender grass, A green thing there hath not been.
Therefore the abundance he made, and their store, Unto the brook of the illos they carry.
For gone round hath the cry the border of Moab, Unto Eglaim [is] its holing, And to Beer-Elim [is] its holing.
For the aters of Dimon have been full of blood, For I set on Dimon additions, For the escaped of Moab a lion, And for the remnant of Adamah!
Send ye a lamb [to] the ruler of the land, From Selah in the ilderness, Unto the mount of the daughter of Zion.
And it hath come to pass, As a andering bird, a nest cast out, Are daughters of Moab, [at] fords of Arnon.
Bring ye in counsel, do judgment, Make as night thy shado in the midst of noon, Hide outcasts, the anderer reveal not.

Sojourn in thee do My outcasts, O Moab, Be a secret hiding-place to them, From the face of a destroyer, For ceased hath the extortioner, Finished hath been a destroyer, Consumed the treaders don out of the land.
And established in kindness is the throne, And [one] hath sat on it in truth, in the tent of David, Judging and seeking judgment, and hasting righteousness.
We have heard of the pride of Moab — very proud, His pride, and his arrogance, and his rath, Not right [are] his devices.
Therefore hol doth Moab for Moab, all of it doth hol, For the grape-cakes of Kir-Hareseth it meditateth, Surely they are smitten.

Because fields of Heshbon languish, The vine of Sibmah, Lords of nations did beat her choice vines, Unto Jazer they have come, They have andered in a ilderness, Her plants have spread themselves, They have passed over a sea.
Therefore I eep ith the eeping of Jazer, The vine of Sibmah, I ater thee [ith] my tear, O Heshbon and Elealeh, For — for thy summer fruits, and for thy harvest, The shouting hath fallen.
And removed have been gladness and joy from the fruitful field, And in vineyards they sing not, nor shout, Wine in the presses treadeth not the treader, Shouting I have caused to cease.
Therefore my boels for Moab as a harp do sound, And mine inard parts for Kir-Haresh.
And it hath come to pass, hen it hath been seen, That eary hath been Moab on the high place, And he hath come unto his sanctuary to pray, And is not able.
This [is] the ord that Jehovah hath spoken unto Moab from that time,
And no hath Jehovah spoken, saying, ’In three years, as years of an hireling, Lightly esteemed is the honour of Moab, With all the great multitude, And the remnant [is] little, small, not mighty!’
The burden of Damascus. Lo, Damascus is taken aay from [being] a city, And it hath been a heap — a ruin.
Forsaken are the cities of Aroer, For droves they are, and they have lain don, And there is none troubling.
And ceased hath the fortress from Ephraim, And the kingdom from Damascus, And the remnant of Aram are as the honour of the sons of Israel, The affirmation of Jehovah of Hosts!
And it hath come to pass, in that day, Wax poor doth the honour of Jacob, And the fatness of his flesh doth ax lean.
And it hath come to pass, As the gathering by the reaper of the standing corn, And his arm the ears reapeth, And it hath come to pass, As the gathering of the ears in the valley of Rephaim,
And left in him have been gleanings, As the compassing of an olive, To — three berries on the top of a branch, Four — five on the fruitful boughs, The affirmation of Jehovah, God of Israel!
In that day doth man look to His Maker, Yea, his eyes to the Holy One of Israel look,
And he looketh not unto the altars. The ork of his on hands, And that hich his on fingers made He seeth not — the shrines and the images.
In that day are the cities of his strength As the forsaken thing of the forest, And the branch that they have left, Because of the sons of Israel, It also hath been a desolation.
Because thou hast forgotten the God of thy salvation, And the rock of thy strength hast not remembered, Therefore thou plantest plants of pleasantness, And ith a strange slip soest it,
In the day thy plant thou causest to become great, And in the morning thy seed makest to flourish, A heap [is] the harvest in a day of overfloing, And of mortal pain.
Woe [to] the multitude of many peoples, As the sounding of seas they sound; And [to] the asting of nations, As the asting of mighty aters they are asted.
Nations as the asting of many aters are asted, And He hath pushed against it, And it hath fled afar off, And been pursued as chaff of hills before ind, And as a rolling thing before a hurricane.
At even-time, lo, terror, before morning it is not, This [is] the portion of our spoilers, And the lot of our plunderers!
Ho, land shadoed [ith] ings, That [is] beyond the rivers of Cush,

That is sending by sea ambassadors, Even ith implements of reed on the face of the aters, — Go, ye light messengers, Unto a nation dran out and peeled, Unto a people fearful from its beginning and onards, A nation meeting out by line, and treading don, Whose land floods have spoiled.
All ye inhabitants of the orld, And ye dellers of earth, At the lifting up of an ensign on hills ye look, And at the bloing of a trumpet ye hear.
For thus said Jehovah unto me, ’I rest, and I look on My settled place, As a clear heat on an herb. As a thick cloud of de in the heat of harvest.
For before harvest, hen the floer is perfect, And the blossom is producing unripe fruit, Then hath [one] cut the sprigs ith pruning hooks, And the branches he hath turned aside, cut don.
They are left together to the ravenous fol of the mountains, And to the beast of the earth, And summered on them hath the ravenous fol, And every beast of the earth intereth on them.

At that time brought is a present to Jehovah of Hosts, A nation dran out and peeled. Even of a people fearful from the beginning hitherto, A nation meting out by line, and treading don, Whose land floods have spoiled, Unto the place of the name of Jehovah of Hosts — mount Zion!’
The burden of Egypt. Lo, Jehovah is riding on a sift thick cloud, And He hath entered Egypt, And moved have been the idols of Egypt at His presence, And the heart of Egypt melteth in its midst.
And I armed Egyptians against Egyptians, And they fought, each against his brother, And each against his neighbour, City against city, kingdom against kingdom.

And emptied out hath been in its midst the spirit of Egypt. And its counsel I sallo up, And they have sought unto the idols, And unto the charmers, And unto those having familiar spirits, And unto the izards.
And I have delivered the Egyptians Into the hand of a hard lord, And a strong king doth rule over them, An affirmation of the Lord, Jehovah of Hosts.
And failed have aters from the sea, And a river is asted and dried up.
And they have turned aay the floings, Weak and dried up have been brooks of the bulark, Reed and flag have ithered.
Exposed things by the brook, by the edge of the brook, And every son thing of the brook, hath ithered, It hath been driven aay, and is not.
And lamented have the fishers, And mourned have all casting angle into a brook, And those spreading nets on the face of the aters have languished.
And ashamed have been makers of fine flax, And eavers of net-orks.
And its foundations have been smitten, All making ages [are] afflicted in soul.
Only, fools [are] the princes of Zoan, The counsel of the ise ones of the counsellors of Pharaoh hath become brutish. Ho say ye unto Pharaoh, ’A son of the ise am I, a son of kings of antiquity?’
Where [are] they no, thy ise ones? Yea, let them tell to thee, I pray thee, And they kno hat Jehovah of Hosts hath counselled against Egypt!
Foolish have been princes of Zoan, Lifted up have been princes of Noph, And they have caused Egypt to err, The chief of her tribes.
Jehovah hath mingled in her midst A spirit of perverseness, And they have caused Egypt to err in all its ork, As a drunkard erreth in his vomit.
And there is no ork to Egypt, That head or tail, branch or reed, may do.
In that day is Egypt like omen, And it hath mourned, and been afraid, Because of the aving of the hand of Jehovah of Hosts, That He is aving over it.
And the land of Judah hath been to Egypt for a cause of staggering, Every one ho doth mention it, for himself feareth, Because of the counsel of Jehovah of Hosts, That He is counselling against it.
In that day there are five cities in the land of Egypt, Speaking the lip of Canaan, And searing to Jehovah of Hosts, ’The city of destruction,’ is said of one.
In that day there is an altar to Jehovah In the midst of the land of Egypt, And a standing pillar near its border to Jehovah,

And it hath been for a sign and for a testimony, To Jehovah of Hosts in the land of Egypt, For they cry unto Jehovah from the face of oppressors, And He sendeth to them a saviour, Even a great one, and hath delivered them.
And knon hath been Jehovah to Egypt, And the Egyptians have knon Jehovah in that day, And done sacrifice and present, And voed a vo to Jehovah, and completed [it].
And Jehovah hath smitten Egypt, smiting and healing, And they have turned back unto Jehovah, And He hath been entreated of them, And hath healed them.
In that day is a highay out of Egypt to Asshur, And come in have the Assyrians to Egypt, And the Egyptians into Asshur, And the Egyptians have served ith the Assyrians.
In that day is Israel third, After Egypt, and after Asshur, A blessing in the heart of the earth.
In that Jehovah of Hosts did bless it, saying, ’Blessed [is] My people — Egypt, And the ork of My hands — Asshur, And Mine inheritance — Israel!’
In the year of the coming in of Tartan to Ashdod, hen Sargon king of Asshur sendeth him, and he fighteth against Ashdod, and captureth it,

at that time spake Jehovah by the hand of Isaiah son of Amoz, saying, ’Go, and thou hast loosed the sackcloth from off thy loins, and thy sandal thou dost dra from off thy foot,’ and he doth so, going naked and barefoot.
And Jehovah saith, ’As My servant Isaiah hath gone naked and barefoot three years, a sign and a onder for Egypt and for Cush,
so doth the king of Asshur lead the captivity of Egypt, and the removal of Cush, young and old, naked and barefoot, ith seat uncovered — the nakedness of Egypt;
and they have been affrighted and ashamed of Cush their confidence, and of Egypt their beauty,
and the inhabitant of this isle hath said in that day — Lo, thus [is] our trust, Whither e have fled for help, To be delivered from the king of Asshur, And ho do e escape — e?’
The burden of the ilderness of the sea. ’Like hurricanes in the south for passing through, From the ilderness it hath come, From a fearful land.
A hard vision hath been declared to me, The treacherous dealer is dealing treacherously, And the destroyer is destroying. Go up, O Elam, besiege, O Media, All its sighing I have caused to cease.
Therefore filled have been my loins [ith] great pain, Pangs have seized me as pangs of a travailing oman, I have been bent don by hearing, I have been troubled by seeing.
Wandered hath my heart, trembling hath terrified me, The tilight of my desire He hath made a fear to me,
Arrange the table, atch in the atch-toer, Eat, drink, rise, ye heads, anoint the shield,
For thus said the Lord unto me: ’Go, station the atchman, That hich he seeth let him declare.’
And he hath seen a chariot — a couple of horsemen, The rider of an ass, the rider of a camel, And he hath given attention — He hath increased attention!
And he crieth — a lion, ’On a atch-toer my lord, I am standing continually by day, And on my ard I am stationed hole nights.
And lo, this, the chariot of a man is coming, A couple of horsemen.’ And he ansereth and saith: ’Fallen, fallen hath Babylon, And all the graven images of her gods He hath broken to the earth.
O my threshing, and the son of my floor, That hich I heard from Jehovah of Hosts, God of Israel, I have declared to you!’
The burden of Dumah. Unto me is [one] calling from Seir ’Watchman, hat of the night? Watchman, hat of the night?’
The atchman hath said, ’Come hath morning, and also night, If ye inquire, inquire ye, turn back, come.’
The burden on Arabia. In a forest in Arabia ye lodge, O travellers of Dedanim.
To meet the thirsty brought ater have Inhabitants of the land of Tema, With his bread they came before a fugitive.
For from the face of destructions they fled, From the face of a stretched-out sord, And from the face of a trodden bo, And from the face of the grievousness of battle.
For thus said the Lord unto me: ’Within a year, as years of a hireling, Consumed hath been all the honour of Kedar.
And the remnant of the number of bo-men, The mighty of the sons of Kedar are fe, For Jehovah, God of Israel, hath spoken!’
The burden of the Valley of Vision. What — to thee, no, that thou hast gone up, All of thee — to the roofs?
Full of stirs — a noisy city — an exulting city, Thy pierced are not pierced of the sord, Nor dead in battle.
All thy rulers fled together from the bo, Bound have been all found of thee, They have been kept bound together, Afar off they have fled.
Therefore I said, ’Look ye from me, I am bitter in my eeping, Haste not to comfort me, For the destruction of the daughter of my people.’
For a day of noise, and of treading don, And of perplexity, [is] to the Lord, Jehovah of Hosts, In the valley of vision, digging don a all, And crying unto the mountain.
And Elam hath borne a quiver, In a chariot of men — horsemen, And Kir hath exposed a shield.
And it cometh to pass, The choice of thy valleys have been full of chariots, And the horsemen place themselves diligently at the gate.
And one removeth the covering of Judah, And thou lookest in that day Unto the armour of the house of the forest,
And the breaches of the city of David ye have seen, For they have become many, And ye gather the aters of the loer pool,
And the houses of Jerusalem ye did number, And ye break don the houses to fence the all.
And a ditch ye made beteen the to alls, For the aters of the old pool, And ye have not looked unto its Maker, And its Framer of old ye have not seen.
And call doth the Lord, Jehovah of Hosts, In that day, to eeping and to lamentation, And to baldness and to girding on of sackcloth,
And lo, joy and gladness, slaying of oxen, And slaughtering of sheep, Eating of flesh, and drinking of ine, Eat and drink, for to-morro e die.
And revealed it hath been in mine ears, [By] Jehovah of Hosts: Not pardoned is this iniquity to you, Till ye die, said the Lord, Jehovah of Hosts.
Thus said the Lord, Jehovah of Hosts: ’Go, enter in unto this steard, Unto Shebna, ho [is] over the house:
What — to thee here? And ho — to thee here? That thou hast hen out to thee here — a sepulchre? Heing on high his sepulchre, Graving in a rock a delling for himself.
Lo, Jehovah is casting thee up and don, A casting up and don, O mighty one,
And thy coverer covering, rapping round, Wrappeth thee round, O babbler, On a land broad of sides — there thou diest, And there the chariots of thine honour [Are] the shame of the house of thy lord.
And I have thrust thee from thy station, And from thine office he throeth thee don.
And it hath come to pass, in that day, That I have called to my servant, To Eliakim son of Hilkiah.

And I have clothed him ith thy coat, And ith thy girdle I strengthen him, And thy garment I give into his hand, And he hath been for a father to the inhabitant of Jerusalem, And to the house of Judah.
And I have placed the key Of the house of David on his shoulder, And he hath opened, and none is shutting, And hath shut, and none is opening.
And I have fixed him a nail in a stedfast place, And he hath been for a throne of honour To the house of his father.
And they have hanged on him All the honour of the house of his father, The offspring and the issue, All vessels of small quality, From vessels of basins to all vessels of flagons.

In that day — an affirmation of Jehovah of Hosts, Moved is the nail that is fixed In a stedfast place, Yea, it hath been cut don, and hath fallen, And cut off hath been the burden that [is] on it, For Jehovah hath spoken!’
The Burden of Tyre. Hol, ye ships of Tarshish, For it hath been destroyed, Without house, ithout entrance, From the land of Chittim it as revealed to them.
Be silent, ye inhabitants of the isle, Trader of Zidon, passing the sea, they filled thee.
And in many aters [is] the seed of Sihor, The harvest of the brook [is] her increase, And she is a mart of nations.
Be ashamed, O Zidon; for the sea spake, The strength of the sea, saying: ’I have not been pained, nor have I brought forth, Nor have I nourished young men, [nor] brought up virgins.’
As [at] the report of Egypt they are pained, So [at] the report of Tyre.
Pass over to Tarshish, hol, ye inhabitants of the isle,
Is this your exulting one? From the days of old [is] her antiquity, Carry her do her on feet afar off to sojourn.
Who hath counselled this against Tyre, The croning one, hose traders [are] princes, Her merchants the honoured of earth?’
Jehovah of Hosts hath counselled it, To pollute the excellency of all beauty, To make light all the honoured of earth.
Pass through thy land as a brook, Daughter of Tarshish, there is no more a girdle.
His hand He hath stretched out over the sea, He hath caused kingdoms to tremble, Jehovah hath charged concerning the merchant one, To destroy her strong places.
And He saith, ’Thou dost not add any more to exult, O oppressed one, virgin daughter of Zidon, To Chittim arise, pass over, Even there — there is no rest for thee.’
Lo, the land of the Chaldeans — this people as not, Asshur founded it for the Ziim, They raised its atch-toers, They lifted up her palaces, — He hath appointed her for a ruin!
Hol, ye ships of Tarshish, For your strength hath been destroyed.
And it hath come to pass, in that day, That forgotten is Tyre seventy years, According to the days of one king. At the end of seventy years there is to Tyre as the song of the harlot.
Take a harp, go round the city, O forgotten harlot, play ell, Multiply song that thou mayest be remembered.

And it hath come to pass, At the end of seventy years Jehovah inspecteth Tyre, And she hath repented of her gift, That she committed fornication With all kingdoms of the earth on the face of the ground.
And her merchandise and her gift have been holy to Jehovah, Not treasured up nor stored, For to those sitting before Jehovah is her merchandise, To eat to satiety, and for a lasting covering!
Lo, Jehovah is emptying the land, And is making it aste, And hath overturned [it on] its face, And hath scattered its inhabitants.

And it hath been — as a people so a priest, As the servant so his master, As the maid-servant so her mistress, As the buyer so the seller, As the lender so the borroer, As the usurer so he ho is lifting [it] on himself.
Utterly emptied is the land, and utterly spoiled, For Jehovah hath spoken this ord:
Mourned, faded hath the land, Languished, faded hath the orld, Languished have they — the high place of the people of the land.
And the land hath been defiled under its inhabitants, Because they have transgressed las, They have changed a statute, They have made void a covenant age-during.
Therefore a curse hath consumed the land, And the inhabitants in it are become desolate, Therefore consumed have been inhabitants of the land, And fe men have been left.
Mourned hath the ne ine, languished the vine, Sighed have all the joyful of heart.
Ceased hath the joy of tabrets, Ceased hath the noise of exulting ones, Ceased hath the joy of a harp.
With a song they drink not ine, Bitter is strong drink to those drinking it.
It as broken don — a city of emptiness, Shut hath been every house from entrance.
A cry over the ine [is] in out-places, Darkened hath been all joy, Removed hath been the joy of the land.
Left in the city [is] desolation, And [ith] asting is the gate smitten.
When thus it is in the heart of the land, In the midst of the peoples, As the compassing of the olive, As gleanings hen harvest hath been finished,
They — they lift up their voice, They sing of the excellency of Jehovah, They have cried aloud from the sea.
Therefore in prosperity honour ye Jehovah, In isles of the sea, the name of Jehovah, God of Israel.

From the skirt of the earth e heard songs, The desire of the righteous. And I say, ’Leanness [is] to me, Leanness [is] to me, oe [is] to me.’ Treacherous dealers dealt treacherously, Yea, treachery, treacherous dealers dealt treacherously.
Fear, and a snare, and a gin, [Are] on thee, O inhabitant of the land.

And it hath come to pass, He ho is fleeing from the noise of the fear Doth fall into the snare, And he ho is coming up from the midst of the snare, Is captured by the gin, For indos on high have been opened, And shaken are foundations of the land.
Utterly broken don hath been the land, Utterly broken hath been the land, Utterly moved hath been the land.
Stagger greatly doth the land as a drunkard, And it hath been moved as a lodge, And heavy on it hath been its transgression, And it hath fallen, and addeth not to rise.
And it hath come to pass, in that day, Jehovah layeth a charge on the host of the high place in the high place, And on the kings of the land on the land.
And they have been gathered — A gathering of bound ones in a pit, And shut up they have been in a prison, And after a multitude of days are inspected.
And confounded hath been the moon, And ashamed hath been the sun, For reigned hath Jehovah of Hosts In mount Zion, and in Jerusalem, And over-against His elders — honour!
O Jehovah, my God [art] Thou, I exalt Thee, I confess Thy name, For Thou hast done a onderful thing, Counsels of old, stedfastness, O stedfast One.
For Thou didst make of a city a heap, Of a fenced city a ruin, A high place of strangers from [being] a city, To the age it is not built.
Therefore honour Thee do a strong people, A city of the terrible nations feareth Thee.
For Thou hast been a stronghold for the poor, A stronghold for the needy in his distress, A refuge from storm, a shado from heat, When the spirit of the terrible [is] as a storm — a all.
As heat in a dry place, The noise of strangers Thou humblest, Heat ith the shado of a thick cloud, The singing of the terrible is humbled.
And made hath Jehovah of Hosts, For all the peoples in this mount, A banquet of fat things, a banquet of preserved things, Fat things full of marro, preserved things refined.
And salloed up hath He in this mountain The face of the rapping that is rapped over all the peoples, And of the covering that is spread over all the nations.
He hath salloed up death in victory, And iped hath the Lord Jehovah, The tear from off all faces, And the reproach of His people He turneth aside from off all the earth, For Jehovah hath spoken.
And [one] hath said in that day, ’Lo, this [is] our God, We aited for Him, and He saveth us, This [is] Jehovah, e have aited for Him, We joy and rejoice in His salvation.’
For rest doth the hand of Jehovah on this mountain, And trodden don is Moab under Him, As trodden don is stra on a dunghill.
And he spread out his hands in its midst, As spread out doth the simmer to sim; And He hath humbled his excellency With the machinations of his hands.
And the fortress of the high place of thy alls He hath boed don — He hath made lo, He hath caused [it] to come to the earth, — unto dust.
In that day sung is this song in the land of Judah: ’We have a strong city, Salvation He doth make alls and bulark.
Open ye the gates, that enter may a righteous nation, Preserving stedfastness.
An imagination supported Thou fortifiest peace — peace! For in Thee it is confident.
Trust ye in Jehovah for ever, For in Jah Jehovah [is] a rock of ages,
For He boed don the dellers on high, A city set on high He maketh lo, He maketh it lo unto the earth, He causeth it to come unto the dust,
Tread it don doth a foot, Feet of the poor — steps of the eak.
The path for the righteous [is] uprightness, O upright One, The path of the righteous Thou dost ponder.
Also, [in] the path of Thy judgments, O Jehovah, e have aited [for] Thee, To Thy name and to Thy remembrance [Is] the desire of the soul.
[With] my soul I desired Thee in the night, Also, [ith] my spirit ithin me I seek Thee earnestly, For hen Thy judgments [are] on the earth, The inhabitants of the orld have learned righteousness.
The icked findeth favour, He hath not learned righteousness, In a land of straightforardness he dealeth perversely, And seeth not the excellency of Jehovah.
O Jehovah, high [is] Thy hand — they see not, They see the zeal of the people, and are ashamed, Also, the fire — Thine adversaries, consumeth them.
O Jehovah, Thou appointest peace to us, For, all our orks also Thou hast rought for us.
O Jehovah our God, lords have ruled us besides Thee, Only, by Thee e make mention of Thy name.
Dead — they live not, Rephaim, they rise not, Therefore Thou hast inspected and dost destroy them, Yea, thou destroyest all their memory.
Thou hast added to the nation, O Jehovah, Thou hast added to the nation, Thou hast been honoured, Thou hast put far off all the ends of earth.
O Jehovah, in distress they missed Thee, They have poured out a hisper, Thy chastisement [is] on them.
When a pregnant oman cometh near to the birth, She is pained — she crieth in her pangs, So e have been from Thy face, O Jehovah.
We have conceived, e have been pained. We have brought forth as it ere ind, Salvation e do not ork in the earth, Nor do the inhabitants of the orld fall.
’Thy dead live — My dead body they rise. Aake and sing, ye dellers in the dust, For the de of herbs [is] thy de, And the land of Rephaim thou causest to fall.
Come, My people, enter into thy inner chambers, And shut thy doors behind thee, Hide thyself shortly a moment till the indignation pass over.
For, lo, Jehovah is coming out of His place, To charge the iniquity of the inhabitant of the earth upon him, And revealed hath the earth her blood, Nor doth she cover any more her slain!’

In that day lay a charge doth Jehovah, With his sord — the sharp, and the great, and the strong, On leviathan — a fleeing serpent, And on leviathan — a crooked serpent, And He hath slain the dragon that [is] in the sea.
In that day, ’A desirable vineyard,’ respond ye to her,
I, Jehovah, am its keeper, every moment I ater it, Lest any lay a charge against it, Night and day I keep it!
Fury is not in Me; Who giveth Me a brier — a thorn in battle? I step into it, I burn it at once.
Or — he doth take hold on My strength, He doth make peace ith Me, Peace he doth make ith Me.
Those coming in He causeth to take root, Jacob doth blossom, and flourished hath Israel, And they have filled the face of the orld [ith] increase.
As the smiting of his smiter hath He smitten him? As the slaying of his slain doth He slay?
In measure, in sending it forth, thou strivest ith it, He hath taken aay by His sharp ind, In the day of an east ind,

Therefore by this is the iniquity of Jacob covered, And this [is] all the fruit — To take aay his sin, in His setting all the stones of an altar, As chalkstones beaten in pieces, They rise not — shrines and images.
For the fenced city [is] alone, A habitation cast out and forsaken as a ilderness, There doth the calf delight, And there it lieth don, And hath consumed its branches.

In the ithering of its branch it is broken off, Women are coming in setting it on fire, For it [is] not a people of understanding, Therefore pity it not doth its Maker, And its Former doth not favour it.
And it hath come to pass, in that day, Beat out doth Jehovah from the branch of the river, Unto the stream of Egypt, And ye are gathered one by one, O sons of Israel.

And it hath come to pass, in that day, It is blon ith a great trumpet, And come in have those perishing in the land of Asshur, And those cast out in the land of Egypt, And have boed themselves to Jehovah, In the holy mount — in Jerusalem!
Woe [to] the proud cron of the drunkards of Ephraim. And the fading floer of the beauty of his glory, That [is] on the head of the fat valley of the broken don of ine.
Lo, a mighty and strong one [is] to the Lord, As a storm of hail — a destructive shoer, As an inundation of mighty aters overfloing, He cast don to the earth ith the hand.
By feet trodden don is the proud cron of the drunkards of Ephraim,

And the fading floer of the beauty of his glory That [is] on the head of the fat valley, Hath been as its first-fruit before summer, That its beholder seeth, While it [is] yet in his hand he salloeth it.
In that day is Jehovah of Hosts For a cron of beauty, and for a diadem of glory, To the remnant of His people.
And for a spirit of judgment To him ho is sitting in the judgment, And for might [to] those turning back the battle to the gate.

And even these through ine have erred, And through strong drink have andered, Priest and prophet erred through strong drink, They have been salloed up of the ine, They andered because of the strong drink, They have erred in seeing, They have stumbled judicially.
For all tables have been full of vomit, Filth — ithout place!
By hom doth He teach knoledge? And by hom doth He cause to understand the report? The eaned from milk, the removed from breasts,
For rule [is] on rule, rule on rule, line on line, line on line, A little here, a little there,
For by scorned lip, and by another tongue, Doth He speak unto this people.
Unto hom He hath said, ’This [is] the rest, give ye rest to the eary, And this — the refreshing:’ And they have not been illing to hear,

And to hom a ord of Jehovah hath been, Rule on rule, rule on rule, line on line, line on line, A little here, a little there, So that they go and have stumbled backard, And been broken, and snared, and captured.
Therefore, hear a ord of Jehovah, ye men of scorning, Ruling this people that [is] in Jerusalem.

Because ye have said: ’We have made a covenant ith death, And ith Sheol e have made a provision, An overfloing scourge, hen it passeth over, Doth not meet us, Though e have made a lie our refuge, And in falsehood have been hidden.’
Therefore, thus said the Lord Jehovah: ’Lo, I am laying a foundation in Zion, A stone — a tried stone, a corner stone precious, a settled foundation, He ho is believing doth not make haste.
And I have put judgment for a line, And righteousness for a plummet, And seep aay doth hail the refuge of lies, And the secret hiding-place do aters overflo.
And disannulled hath been your covenant ith death, And your provision ith Sheol doth not stand, An overfloing scourge, hen it passeth over, Then ye have been to it for a treading-place.
From the fulness of its passing over it taketh you, For morning by morning it passeth over, By day and by night, And it hath been only a trembling to consider the report.
For shorter hath been the bed Than to stretch one’s self out in, And the covering hath been narroer Than to rap one’s self up in.
For as [at] mount Perazim rise doth Jehovah, As [at] the valley in Gibeon He is troubled, To do His ork — strange [is] His ork, And to do His deed — strange [is] His deed.’
And no, sho not yourselves scorners, Lest strong be your bands, For a consumption, that is determined, I have heard, by the Lord, Jehovah of Hosts, [Is] for all the land.
Give ear, and hear my voice, Attend, and hear my saying:
The hole day plougheth the ploughman to so? He openeth and harroeth his ground!
Hath he not, if he have made level its face, Then scattered fitches, and cummin sprinkle, And hath placed the principal heat, And the appointed barley, And the rie [in] its on border?
And instruct him for judgment doth his God, He doth direct him.
For not ith a sharp-pointed thing threshed are fitches, And the heel of a cart on cummin turned round, For ith a staff beaten out are fitches, And cummin ith a rod.
Bread -[corn] is beaten small, For not for ever doth he sorely thresh it, Nor crushed [it] hath a heel of his cart, Nor do his hoofs beat it small.
Even this from Jehovah of Hosts hath gone out, He hath made counsel onderful, He hath made isdom great!
Woe [to] Ariel, Ariel, The city of the encampment of David! Add year to year, let festivals go round.
And I have sent distress to Ariel, And it hath been lamentation and mourning, And it hath been to me as Ariel.
And I encamped, O babbler, against thee, And I laid siege against thee — a camp. And I raised up against thee bularks.

And thou hast been lo, From the earth thou speakest, And from the dust makest thy saying lo, And thy voice hath been from the earth, As one having a familiar spirit, And from the dust thy saying hisperest,
And as small dust hath been The multitude of those scattering thee, And as chaff passing on the multitude of the terrible, And it hath been at an instant — suddenly.
By Jehovah of Hosts thou art inspected, With thunder, and ith an earthquake, And great noise, hurricane, and hirlind, And flame of devouring fire.
And as a dream, a vision of night, hath been The multitude of all the nations Who are arring against Ariel, And all its arriors, and its bulark, Even of those distressing her.

And it hath been, as hen the hungry dreameth, And lo, he is eating, And he hath aked, and empty [is] his soul, And as hen the thirsty dreameth, And lo, he is drinking, and he hath aked, And lo, he is eary, and his soul is longing, So is the multitude of all the nations Who are arring against mount Zion.
Tarry and onder, look ye, yea, look, Be drunk, and not ith ine, Stagger, and not ith strong drink.
For poured out on you hath Jehovah a spirit of deep sleep, And He closeth your eyes — the prophets, And your heads — the seers — He covered.
And the vision of the hole is to you, As ords of the sealed book, That they give unto one knoing books, Saying, ’Read this, e pray thee,’ And he hath said, ’I am not able, for it [is] sealed;’
And the book is given to him ho hath not knon books, Saying, ’Read this, e pray thee,’ And he hath said, ’I have not knon books.’

And the Lord saith: Because dran near hath this people, ith its mouth, And ith its lips they have honoured Me, And its heart it hath put far off from Me, And their fear of Me is — A precept of men is taught!
Therefore, lo, I am adding to do onderfully ith this people, A onder, and a marvel, And perished hath the isdom of its ise ones, And the understanding of its intelligent ones hideth itself.’
Woe [to] those going deep from Jehovah to hide counsel, And hose orks have been in darkness. And they say, ’Who is seeing us? And ho is knoing us?’
Your perversion! as clay is the potter esteemed? That the ork saith of its maker, ’He hath not made me?’ And the framed thing said of its framer, ’He did not understand?’
Is it not yet a very little, And turned hath Lebanon to a fruitful field, And the fruitful field for a forest is reckoned?
And heard in that day have the deaf the ords of a book, And out of thick darkness, and out of darkness, The eyes of the blind do see.
And the humble have added joy in Jehovah, And the poor among men In the Holy One of Israel rejoice.
For ceased hath the terrible one, And consumed hath been the scorner, And cut off have been all atching for iniquity,
Causing men to sin in ord, And for a reprover in the gate lay a snare, And turn aside into emptiness the righteous.
Therefore, thus said Jehovah, Who ransomed Abraham, Concerning the house of Jacob: ’Not no ashamed is Jacob, Nor no doth his face become pale,
For in his seeing his children, The ork of My hand, in his midst, They sanctify My name, And have sanctified the Holy One of Jacob, And the God of Israel they declare fearful.
And the erring in spirit have knon understanding, And murmurers learn doctrine!’
Woe [to] apostate sons, The affirmation of Jehovah! To do counsel, and not from Me, And to spread out a covering, and not of My spirit, So as to add sin to sin.
Who are alking to go don to Egypt, And My mouth have not asked, To be strong in the strength of Pharaoh, And to trust in the shado of Egypt.
And the strength of Pharaoh Hath been to you for shame, And the trust in the shado of Egypt confusion,
For in Zoan ere his princes, And his messengers reach Hanes.
All he made ashamed of a people that profit not, Neither for help, not for profit, But for shame, and also for reproach!

The burden of the beasts of the south. Into a land of adversity and distress, Of young lion and of old lion, Whence [are] viper and flying saraph, They carry on the shoulder of asses their ealth, And on the hump of camels their treasures, Unto a people not profitable.
Yea, Egyptians [are] vanity, and in vain do help, Therefore I have cried concerning this: ’Their strength [is] to sit still.’
No, go in, rite it on a tablet ith them, And on a book engrave it, And it is for a latter day, for a itness unto the age,
That a rebellious people [is] this, sons — liars, Sons not illing to hear the la of Jehovah.
Who have said to seers, ’Ye do not see,’ And to prophets, ’Ye do not prophesy to us Straightforard things, Speak to us smooth things, prophesy deceits,
Turn aside from the ay, decline from the path, Cause to cease from before us the Holy One of Israel.’
Therefore, thus said the Holy One of Israel, Because of your kicking against this ord, And ye trust in oppression, And perverseness, and rely on it,
Therefore is this iniquity to you as a breach falling, Selled out in a all set on high, Whose destruction suddenly, at an instant cometh.

And He hath broken it As the breaking of the potters’ bottle, Beaten don — He doth not spare, Nor is there found, in its beating don, A potsherd to take fire from the burning, And to dra out aters from a ditch.
For thus said the Lord Jehovah, The Holy One of Israel: ’In returning and rest ye are saved, In keeping quiet and in confidence is your might, And ye have not been illing.
And ye say, No, for on a horse e flee? Therefore ye flee, And on the sift e ride! Therefore sift are your pursuers.
One thousand because of the rebuke of one, Because of the rebuke of five ye flee, Till ye have been surely left as a pole On the top of the mountain, And as an ensign on the height.
And therefore doth ait Jehovah to favour you, And therefore He is exalted to pity you, For a God of judgment [is] Jehovah, O the blessedness of all aiting for Him.
For the people in Zion dell in Jerusalem, Weep thou not, eeping, Pitying, He pitieth thee at the voice of thy cry, When He heareth He ansereth thee.
And the Lord hath given to you bread of adversity, And ater of oppression. And thy directors remove no more, And thine eyes have seen thy directors,
And thine ear heareth a ord behind thee, Saying, ’This [is] the ay, go ye in it,’ When ye turn to the right, And hen ye turn to the left.
And ye have defiled the covering of Thy graven images of silver, And the ephod of thy molten image of gold, Thou scatterest them as a sickening thing, ’Go out,’ thou sayest to it.

And He hath given rain [for] thy seed, With hich thou dost so the ground, And bread, the increase of the ground, And it hath been fat and plenteous, Enjoy do thy cattle in that day an enlarged pasture.
And the oxen and the young asses serving the ground, Fermented provender do eat, That one is innoing ith shovel and fan.
And there hath been on every high mount, And on every exalted hill, Rivulets — streams of aters, In a day of much slaughter, in the falling of toers.

And the light of the moon hath been as the light of the sun, And the light of the sun is sevenfold, As the light of seven days, In the day of Jehovah’s binding up the breach of His people, When the stroke of its ound He healeth.
Lo, the name of Jehovah is coming from far, Burning is His anger, and great the flame, His lips have been full of indignation, And His tongue [is] as a devouring fire.
And His breath [is] as an overfloing stream, Unto the neck it divideth, To sift nations ith a sieve of vanity, And a bridle causing to err, [Is] on the jas of the peoples.
Singing is to you as in a night sanctified for a festival, And joy of heart as he ho is going ith a pipe, To go in to the mountain of Jehovah, Unto the rock of Israel.

And caused to be heard hath Jehovah The honour of His voice, And the coming don of His arm He doth she ith the raging of anger, And the flame of a consuming fire, Scattering, and inundation, and hailstone.
For from the voice of Jehovah broken don [is] Asshur, With a rod He smiteth.
And every passage of the settled staff, That Jehovah causeth to rest on him, Hath been ith tabrets, and ith harps, And in battles of shaking he hath fought ith it.

For, arranged from former time is Tophet, Even it for the king is prepared, He hath made deep, He hath made large, Its pile [is] fire and much ood, The breath of Jehovah, As a stream of brim stone, is burning in it!

Woe [to] those going don to Egypt for help, And on horses lean, And trust on chariots, because many, And on horsemen, because very strong, And have not looked on the Holy One of Israel, And Jehovah have not sought.
And He also [is] ise, and bringeth in evil, And His ords He hath not turned aside, And He hath risen against a house of evil doers, And against the help of orkers of iniquity.

And the Egyptians [are men], and not God, And their horses [are] flesh, and not spirit, And Jehovah stretcheth out His hand, And stumbled hath the helper, And fallen hath the helped one, And together all of them are consumed.

For thus said Jehovah unto me: ’As grol doth the lion and the young lion over his prey, Called against hom is a multitude of shepherds, From their voice he is not affrighted, And from their noise he is not humbled; So come don doth Jehovah of Hosts To ar on mount Zion, and on her height.
As birds flying, so doth Jehovah of Hosts Cover over Jerusalem, covering and delivering, Passing over, and causing to escape.’
Turn back to Him from hom sons of Israel Have deepened apostasy.
For in that day despise doth each His idols of silver, and his idols of gold, That your hands made to you — a sin.
And fallen hath Asshur by sord, not of the high, Yea, a sord — not of the lo, doth consume him, And he hath fled for himself from the face of a sord, And his young men become tributary.
And [to] his rock from fear he passeth on, And affrighted by the ensign have been his princes — an affirmation of Jehovah, Who hath a light in Zion, And ho hath a furnace in Jerusalem!
Lo, for righteousness doth a king reign, As to princes, for judgment they rule.
And each hath been as a hiding-place [from] ind, And as a secret hiding-place [from] inundation, As rivulets of aters in a dry place, As a shado of a heavy rock in a eary land.
And not dazzled are the eyes of beholders, And the ears of hearers do attend.
And the heart of those hastened Understandeth to kno, And the tongue of stammerers hasteth to speak clearly.
A fool is no more called ’noble,’ And to a miser it is not said, ’rich;’
For a fool speaketh folly, And his heart doth iniquity, to do profanity, And to speak concerning Jehovah error, To empty the soul of the hungry, Yea, drink of the thirsty he causeth to lack.
And the miser — his instruments [are] evil, He hath counselled icked devices, To corrupt the poor ith lying sayings, Even hen the needy speaketh justly.
And the noble counselled noble things, And he for noble things riseth up.
Women, easy ones, rise, hear my voice, Daughters, confident ones, give ear [to] my saying,
Days and a year ye are troubled, O confident ones, For consumed hath been harvest, The gathering cometh not.
Tremble ye omen, ye easy ones, Be troubled, ye confident ones, Strip and make bare, ith a girdle on the loins,
For breasts they are lamenting, For fields of desire, for the fruitful vine.
Over the ground of my people thorn — brier goeth up, Surely over all houses of joy of the exulting city,
Surely the palace hath been left, The multitude of the city forsaken, Fort and atch-toer hath been for dens unto the age, A joy of ild asses — a pasture of herds;
Till emptied out on us is the Spirit from on high, And a ilderness hath become a fruitful field, And the fruitful field for a forest is reckoned.
And delt in the ilderness hath judgment, And righteousness in the fruitful field remaineth.
And a ork of the righteousness hath been peace, And a service of the righteousness — Keeping quiet and confidence unto the age.
And delt hath My people in a peaceful habitation, And in stedfast tabernacles, And in quiet resting-places.
And it hath hailed in the going don of the forest, And in the valley is the city lo.
Happy [are] ye soing by all aters, Sending forth the foot of the ox and the ass!

Woe, spoiler! and thou not spoiled, And treacherous! and they dealt not treacherously ith thee, When thou dost finish, O spoiler, thou art spoiled, When thou dost finish dealing treacherously, They deal treacherously ith thee.
O Jehovah, favour us, for thee e have aited, Be their arm, in the mornings, Yea, our salvation in time of adversity.
From the voice of a multitude fled have peoples, From thine exaltation scattered have been nations.
And gathered hath been your spoil, A gathering of the caterpillar, As a running to and fro of locusts is he running on it.
Set on high is Jehovah, for He is delling on high, He filled Zion [ith] judgment and righteousness,
And hath been the stedfastness of thy times, The strength of salvation, isdom, and knoledge, Fear of Jehovah — it [is] His treasure.
Lo, ’Their Ariel,’ they have cried ithout, Messengers of peace do eep bitterly.
Desolated have been highays, Ceased hath he ho passeth along the path, He hath broken covenant, He hath despised enemies, He hath not esteemed a man.
Mourned, languished hath the land, Confounded hath been Lebanon, Withered hath been Sharon as a ilderness, And shaking are Bashan and Carmel.
No, do I arise, saith Jehovah, No I am exalted, no I am lifted up.
Ye conceive chaff, ye bear stubble, Your spirit! — fire devoureth you.
And peoples have been [as] burnings of lime, Thorns, as seepings, ith fire they burn.
Hear, ye far off, that hich I have done, And kno, ye near ones, My might.
Afraid in Zion have been sinners, Seized hath trembling the profane: Who doth dell for us — consuming fire, Who doth dell for us — burnings of the age?

Whoso is alking righteously, And is speaking uprightly, Kicking against gain of oppressions, Shaking his hands from taking hold on a bribe, Stopping his ear from hearing of blood, And shutting his eyes from looking on evil,
He high places doth inhabit, Strongholds of rock [are] his high toer, His bread hath been given, his aters stedfast.
A king in his beauty, see do thine eyes, They see a land afar off.
Thy heart doth meditate terror, Where [is] he ho is counting? Where [is] he ho is eighing? Where [is] he ho is counting the toers?
The strong people thou seest not, A people deeper of lip than to be understood, Of a scorned tongue, there is no understanding.
See Zion, the city of our meetings, Thine eyes see Jerusalem a quiet habitation, A tent not taken don, Not removed are its pins for ever, And none of its cords are broken.
But there mighty [is] Jehovah for us, A place of rivers — streams broad of sides, No ship ith oars doth go into it, And a mighty ship doth not pass over it.
For Jehovah our judge, Jehovah our lagiver, Jehovah our king — He doth save us.
Left have been thy ropes, They strengthen not rightly their mast, They have not spread out a sail, Then apportioned hath been a prey of much spoil, The lame have taken spoil.
Nor doth an inhabitant say, ’I as sick,’ The people that is delling in it, is forgiven of iniquity!
Come near, ye nations, to hear, And ye peoples, give attention, Hear doth the earth and its fulness, The orld, and all its productions.
For rath [is] to Jehovah against all the nations, And fury against all their host, He hath devoted them to destruction, He hath given them to slaughter.
And their ounded are cast out, And their carcases cause their stench to ascend, And melted have been mountains from their blood.

And consumed have been all the host of the heavens, And rolled together as a book have been the heavens, And all their hosts do fade, As the fading of a leaf of a vine, And as the fading one of a fig-tree.
For soaked in the heavens as My sord, Lo, on Edom it cometh don, On the people of My curse for judgment.

A sord [is] to Jehovah — it hath been full of blood, It hath been made fat ith fatness, With blood of lambs and he-goats. With fat of kidneys of rams, For a sacrifice [is] to Jehovah in Bozrah, And a great slaughter in the land of Edom.
And come don have reems ith them, And bullocks ith bulls, And soaked hath been their land from blood, And their dust from fatness is made fat.
(For a day of vengeance [is] to Jehovah, A year of recompences for Zion’s strife,)
And turned have been her streams to pitch, And her dust to brimstone, And her land hath become burning pitch.
By night and by day she is not quenched, To the age go up doth her smoke, From generation to generation she is aste, For ever and ever, none is passing into her.
And possess her do pelican and hedge-hog, And ol and raven dell in her, And He hath stretched out over her A line of vacancy, and stones of emptiness.
[To] the kingdom her freemen they call, But there are none there, And all her princes are at an end.
And gone up her palaces have thorns, Nettle and bramble [are] in her fortresses, And it hath been a habitation of dragons, A court for daughters of an ostrich.
And met have Ziim ith Aiim, And the goat for its companion calleth, Only there rested hath the night-ol, And hath found for herself a place of rest.
There made her nest hath the bittern, Yea, she layeth, and hath hatched, And hath gathered under her shado, Only there gathered have been vultures, Each ith its companion.
Seek out of the book of Jehovah, and read, One of these hath not been lacking, None hath missed its companion, For My mouth — it hath commanded, And His spirit — He hath gathered them.
And He hath cast for them a lot, And His hand hath apportioned [it] to them by line, Unto the age they possess it, To all generations they dell in it!
They joy from the ilderness and dry place, And rejoice doth the desert, and flourish as the rose,

Flourishing it doth flourish, and rejoice, Yea, [ith] joy and singing, The honour of Lebanon hath been given to it, The beauty of Carmel and Sharon, They — they see the honour of Jehovah, The majesty of our God.
Strengthen ye the feeble hands, Yea, the stumbling knees strengthen.
Say to the hastened of heart, ’Be strong, Fear not, lo, your God; vengeance cometh, The recompence of God, He Himself doth come and save you.’
Then opened are eyes of the blind, And ears of the deaf are unstopped,
Then leap as a hart doth the lame, And sing doth the tongue of the dumb, For broken up in a ilderness have been aters, And streams in a desert.
And the mirage hath become a pond, And the thirsty land fountains of aters, In the habitation of dragons, Its place of couching don, a court for reed and rush.
And a highay hath been there, and a ay, And the ’ay of holiness’ is called to it, Not pass over it doth the unclean, And He Himself [is] by them, Whoso is going in the ay — even fools err not.
No lion is there, yea, a destructive beast Ascendeth it not, it is not found there, And alked have the redeemed,
And the ransomed of Jehovah return, And have entered Zion ith singing. And joy age-during on their head, Joy and gladness they attain, And fled aay have sorro and sighing!
And it cometh to pass, in the fourteenth year of king Hezekiah, come up hath Sennacherib king of Asshur against all the fenced cities of Judah, and seizeth them.
And the king of Asshur sendeth Rabshakeh from Lachish to Jerusalem, unto the king Hezekiah, ith a heavy force, and he standeth by the conduit of the upper pool, in the highay of the fuller’s field,
and go forth unto him doth Eliakim son of Hilkiah, ho [is] over the house, and Shebna the scribe, and Joah son of Asaph, the remembrancer.
And Rabshakeh saith unto them, ’Say ye, I pray you, unto Hezekiah, ’Thus said the great king, the king of Asshur, What [is] this confidence in hich thou hast confided?
I have said: Only, a ord of the lips! counsel and might [are] for battle: no, on hom hast thou trusted, that thou hast rebelled against me?

’Lo, thou hast trusted on the staff of this broken reed — on Egypt — hich a man leaneth on, and it hath gone into his hand, and pierced it — so [is] Pharaoh king of Egypt to all those trusting on him.

’And dost thou say unto me, Unto Jehovah our God e have trusted? is it not He, hose high places and hose altars Hezekiah hath turned aside, and saith to Judah and to Jerusalem, Before this altar ye do bo yourselves?
’And no, negotiate, I pray thee, ith my lord the king of Asshur, and I give to thee to thousand horses, if thou art able to put for thee riders on them.
And ho dost thou turn back the face of one captain of the least of the servants of my lord, and dost trust for thee on Egypt, for chariot and for horsemen?
And no, ithout Jehovah have I come up against this land to destroy it? Jehovah said unto me, Go up unto this land, and thou hast destroyed it.’

And Eliakim saith — and Shebna and Joah — unto Rabshakeh, ’Speak, e pray thee, unto thy servants [in] Aramaean, for e are understanding; and do not speak unto us [in] Jeish, in the ears of the people ho [are] on the all.’

And Rabshakeh saith, ’Unto thy lord, and unto thee, hath my lord sent me to speak these ords? is it not for the men — those sitting on the all to eat their on dung and to drink their on ater ith you?’
And Rabshakeh standeth and calleth ith a great voice [in] Jeish, and saith, ’Hear ye the ords of the great king, the king of Asshur:
Thus said the king, Let not Hezekiah lift you up, for he is not able to deliver you;
and let not Hezekiah make you trust unto Jehovah, saying, Jehovah doth certainly deliver us, this city is not given into the hand of the king of Asshur.

’Do not hearken unto Hezekiah, for thus said the king of Asshur, Make ye ith me a blessing, and come out unto me, and eat ye each of his vine, and each of his fig-tree, and drink ye each the aters of his on ell,
till my coming in, and I have taken you unto a land like your on land, a land of corn and ine, a land of bread and vineyards;
lest Hezekiah doth persuade you, saying, Jehovah doth deliver us. ’Have the gods of the nations delivered each his land out of the hand of the king of Asshur?
Where [are] the gods of Hamath and Arpad? Where the gods of Sepharvaim, that they have delivered Samaria out of my hand?
Who among all the gods of these lands [are] they ho have delivered their land out of my hand, that Jehovah doth deliver Jerusalem out of my hand?’
And they keep silent, and have not ansered him a ord, for a command of the king is, saying, ’Do not anser him.’
