And Eliakim son of Hilkiah, ho [is] over the house, cometh in, and Shebna the scribe, and Joah son of Asaph, the remembrancer, unto Hezekiah ith rent garments, and they declare to him the ords of Rabshakeh.
And it cometh to pass, at the king Hezekiah’s hearing, that he rendeth his garments, and covereth himself ith sackcloth, and entereth the house of Jehovah,
and sendeth Eliakim, ho [is] over the house, and Shebna the scribe, and the elders of the priests, covering themselves ith sackcloth, unto Isaiah son of Amoz the prophet,
and they say unto him, ’Thus said Hezekiah, A day of distress, and rebuke, and despising, [is] this day; for come have sons unto the birth, and poer there is not to bear.

’It may be Jehovah thy God doth hear the ords of Rabshakeh ith hich the king of Asshur his lord hath sent him to reproach the living God, and hath decided concerning the ords that Jehovah thy God hath heard, and thou hast lifted up prayer for the remnant that is found.’
And the servants of king Hezekiah come in unto Isaiah,
and Isaiah saith unto them, ’Thus do ye say unto your lord, Thus said Jehovah, Be not afraid because of the ords that thou hast heard, ith hich the servants of the king of Asshur have reviled Me.
Lo, I am giving in him a spirit, and he hath heard a report, and hath turned back unto his land, and I have caused him to fall by the sord in his land.’
And Rabshakeh turneth back and findeth the king of Asshur fighting against Libnah, for he hath heard that he hath journeyed from Lachish.
And he heareth concerning Tirhakah king of Cush, saying, ’He hath come out to fight ith thee;’ and he heareth, and sendeth messengers unto Hezekiah, saying,
’Thus do ye speak unto Hezekiah king of Judah, saying, Let not thy God lift thee up in hom thou art trusting, saying, Jerusalem is not given into the hand of the king of Asshur.
Lo, thou hast heard that hich the kings of Asshur have done to all the lands — to devote them — and thou art delivered!
Did the gods of the nations deliver them hom my fathers destroyed — Gozan, and Haran, and Rezeph, and the sons of Eden, ho [are] in Telassar?
Where [is] the king of Hamath, and the king of Arpad, and the king of the city of Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah?’
And Hezekiah taketh the letters out of the hand of the messengers, and readeth them, and Hezekiah goeth up to the house of Jehovah, and Hezekiah spreadeth it before Jehovah.
And Hezekiah prayeth unto Jehovah, saying,
’Jehovah of Hosts, God of Israel, inhabiting the cherubs, Thou [art] God Himself — Thyself alone — to all kingdoms of the earth, Thou hast made the heavens and the earth.
Incline, O Jehovah, Thine ear, and hear; open, O Jehovah, Thine eyes and see; and hear Thou all the ords of Sennacherib that he hath sent to reproach the living God.
’Truly, O Jehovah, kings of Asshur have laid aste all the lands and their land,
so as to put their gods into fire — for they [are] no gods, but ork of the hands of man, ood and stone — and they destroy them.
And no, Jehovah our God, save us from his hand, and all kingdoms of the earth do kno that Thou [art] Jehovah, Thyself alone.’
And Isaiah son of Amoz sendeth unto Hezekiah, saying, ’Thus said Jehovah, God of Israel, That hich thou hast prayed unto me concerning Sennacherib king of Asshur —
this [is] the ord that Jehovah spake concerning him: Trampled on thee, laughed at thee, Hath the virgin daughter of Zion, Behind thee shaken the head hath the daughter of Jerusalem.
Whom hast thou reproached and reviled? And against hom lifted up the voice? Yea, thou dost lift up on high thine eyes Against the Holy One of Israel.

By the hand of thy servants Thou hast reviled the Lord, and sayest: In the multitude of my chariots I have come up to a high place of hills, The sides of Lebanon, And I cut don the height of its cedars, The choice of its firs, And I enter the high place of its extremity, The forest of its Carmel.
I — I have dug and drunk aters, And I dry up ith the sole of my steps All floods of a bulark.
Hast thou not heard from afar? — it I did, From days of old — that I formed it. No, I have brought it in, And it is to make desolate, Ruinous heaps — fenced cities,

And their inhabitants are feeble-handed, They ere broken don, and are dried up. They have been the herb of the field, And the greenness of the tender grass, Grass of the roofs, And blasted corn, before it hath risen up.
And thy sitting don, and thy going out, And thy coming in, I have knon, And thy anger toards Me.

Because of thy anger toards Me, And thy noise — it came up into Mine ears, I have put My hook in thy nose, And My bridle in thy lips, And I have caused thee to turn back In the ay in hich thou camest.
— And this to thee [is] the sign, Food of the year [is] self-son grain, And in the second year the spontaneous groth, And in the third year, so ye and reap, And plant vineyards, and eat their fruit.
And it hath continued — the escaped Of the house of Judah that hath been left — To take root beneath, And it hath made fruit upard.
For from Jerusalem goeth forth a remnant, And an escape from mount Zion, The zeal of Jehovah of Hosts doth this.

Therefore, thus said Jehovah, Concerning the king of Asshur: He doth not come in unto this city, Nor doth he shoot there an arro, Nor doth he come before it [ith] shield, Nor doth he pour out against it a mount.
In the ay that he came, in it he turneth back, And unto this city he doth not come in, An affirmation of Jehovah,
And I have covered over this city, To save it, for Mine on sake, And for the sake of David My servant.’
And a messenger of Jehovah goeth out, and smiteth in the camp of Asshur a hundred and eighty and five thousand; and [men] rise early in the morning, and lo, all of them [are] dead corpses.
And journey, and go, and turn back doth Sennacherib king of Asshur, and delleth in Nineveh.

And it cometh to pass, he is boing himself in the house of Nisroch his god, and Adrammelech and Sharezer his sons have smitten him ith the sord, and they have escaped to the land of Ararat, and Esar-Haddon his son reigneth in his stead.

In those days hath Hezekiah been sick unto death, and come in unto him doth Isaiah son of Amoz, the prophet, and saith unto him, ’Thus said Jehovah: Give a charge to thy house, for thou [art] dying, and dost not live.’
And Hezekiah turneth round his face unto the all, and prayeth unto Jehovah,

and saith, ’I pray thee, O Jehovah, remember, I pray Thee, ho I have alked habitually before Thee in truth, and ith a perfect heart, and that hich [is] good in thine eyes I have done;’ and Hezekiah eepeth — a great eeping.
And a ord of Jehovah is unto Isaiah, saying,
Go, and thou hast said to Hezekiah, Thus said Jehovah, God of David thy father, ’I have heard thy prayer, I have seen thy tear, lo, I am adding to thy days fifteen years,
and out of the hand of the king of Asshur I deliver thee and this city, and have covered over this city.
And this [is] to thee the sign from Jehovah, that Jehovah doth this thing that He hath spoken.

Lo, I am bringing back the shado of the degrees that it hath gone don on the degrees of Ahaz, by the sun, backard ten degrees:’ and the sun turneth back ten degrees in the degrees that it had gone don.
A riting of Hezekiah king of Judah concerning his being sick, hen he reviveth from his sickness:
’I — I said in the cutting off of my days, I go in to the gates of Sheol, I have numbered the remnant of mine years.
I said, I do not see Jah — Jah! In the land of the living, I do not behold man any more, With the inhabitants of the orld.
My sojourning hath departed, And been removed from me as a shepherd’s tent, I have dran together, as a eaver, my life, By eakness it cutteth me off, From day unto night Thou dost end me.
I have set [Him] till morning as a lion, So doth He break all my bones, From day unto night Thou dost end me.
As a crane — a sallo — so I chatter, I mourn as a dove, Dran up have been mine eyes on high, O Jehovah, oppression [is] on me, be my surety.
— What do I say? seeing He said to me, And He Himself hath rought, I go softly all my years for the bitterness of my soul.
Lord, by these do [men] live, And by all in them [is] the life of my spirit, And Thou savest me, make me also to live,
Lo, to peace He changed for me bitterness, And Thou hast delighted in my soul ithout corruption, For Thou hast cast behind Thy back all my sins.
For Sheol doth not confess Thee, Death doth not praise Thee, Those going don to the pit hope not for Thy truth.
The living, the living, he doth confess Thee.
Like myself to-day — a father to sons Doth make knon of Thy faithfulness, O Jehovah — to save me: And my songs e sing all days of our lives In the house of Jehovah.’
And Isaiah saith, ’Let them take a bunch of figs, and plaster over the ulcer, and he liveth.’
And Hezekiah saith, ’What [is] the sign that I go up to the house of Jehovah!’
At that time hath Merodach-Baladan, son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent letters and a present unto Hezekiah, hen he heareth that he hath been sick, and is become strong.

And Hezekiah rejoiceth over them, and sheeth them the house of his spices, the silver, and the gold, and the spices, and the good ointment, and all the house of his vessels, and all that hath been found in his treasures; there hath not been a thing in his house, and in all his dominion, that Hezekiah hath not sheed them.

And Isaiah the prophet cometh in unto king Hezekiah, and saith unto him, ’What said these men? and hence come they unto thee?’ And Hezekiah saith, ’From a land afar off they have come unto me — from Babylon.’
And he saith, ’What sa they in thy house?’ and Hezekiah saith, ’All that [is] in my house they sa; there hath not been a thing that I have not sheed them among my treasures.’
And Isaiah saith unto Hezekiah, ’Hear a ord of Jehovah of Hosts:
Lo, days are coming, and borne hath been all that [is] in thy house, and that thy fathers have treasured up till this day, to Babylon; there is not left a thing, said Jehovah;
and of thy sons ho come forth from thee, hom thou begettest, they take, and they have been eunuchs in a palace of the king of Babylon.’
And Hezekiah saith unto Isaiah, ’Good [is] the ord of Jehovah that thou hast spoken;’ and he saith, ’Because there is peace and truth in my days.’
Comfort ye, comfort ye, My people, saith your God.
Speak to the heart of Jerusalem, and call to her, That her arfare hath been completed, That accepted hath been her punishment, That she hath received from the hand of Jehovah Double for all her sins.
A voice is crying — in a ilderness — Prepare ye the ay of Jehovah, Make straight in a desert a highay to our God.
Every valley is raised up, And every mountain and hill become lo, And the crooked place hath become a plain, And the entangled places a valley.
And revealed hath been the honour of Jehovah, And seen [it] have all flesh together, For the mouth of Jehovah hath spoken.
A voice is saying, ’Call,’ And he said, ’What do I call?’ All flesh [is] grass, and all its goodliness [is] As a floer of the field:
Withered hath grass, faded the floer, For the Spirit of Jehovah ble upon it, Surely the people [is] grass;
Withered hath grass, faded the floer, But a ord of our God riseth for ever.
On a high mountain get thee up, O Zion, Proclaiming tidings, Lift up ith poer thy voice, O Jerusalem, proclaiming tidings, Lift up, fear not, say to cities of Judah, ’Lo, your God.’
Lo, the Lord Jehovah ith strength cometh, And His arm is ruling for Him, Lo, His hire [is] ith Him, and His age before Him.
As a shepherd His flock He feedeth, With His arm He gathereth lambs, And in His bosom He carrieth [them]: Suckling ones He leadeth.

Who hath measured in the hollo of his hand the aters? And the heavens by a span hath meted out, And comprehended in a measure the dust of the earth, And hath eighed in scales the mountains, And the hills in a balance?
Who hath meted out the Spirit of Jehovah, And, [being] His counsellor, doth teach Him!
With hom consulted He, That he causeth Him to understand? And teacheth Him in the path of judgment, And teacheth Him knoledge? And the ay of understanding causeth Him to kno?
Lo, nations as a drop from a bucket, And as small dust of the balance, have been reckoned, Lo, isles as a small thing He taketh up.
And Lebanon is not sufficient to burn, Nor its beasts sufficient for a burnt-offering.
All the nations [are] as nothing before Him, Less than nothing and emptiness, They have been reckoned to Him.
And unto hom do ye liken God, And hat likeness do ye compare to Him?
The graven image poured out hath a artisan, And a refiner ith gold spreadeth it over, And chains of silver he is refining.
He ho is poor [by] heave-offerings, A tree not rotten doth choose, A skilful artisan he seeketh for it, To establish a graven image — not moved.
Do ye not kno — do ye not hear? Hath it not been declared from the first to you? Have ye not understood [From] the foundations of the earth?
He ho is sitting on the circle of the earth, And its inhabitants [are] as grasshoppers, He ho is stretching out as a thin thing the heavens, And spreadeth them as a tent to dell in.
He ho is making princes become nothing, Judges of earth as emptiness hath made;

Yea, they have not been planted, Yea, they have not been son, Yea, not taking root in the earth is their stock, And also He hath blon upon them, and they ither, And a hirlind as stubble taketh them aay.
And unto hom do ye liken Me, And [am] I equal? saith the Holy One.

Lift up on high your eyes, And see — ho hath prepared these? He ho is bringing out by number their host, To all of them by name He calleth, By abundance of strength (And [he is] strong in poer) not one is lacking.
Why sayest thou, O Jacob? and speakest thou, O Israel? ’My ay hath been hid from Jehovah, And from my God my judgment passeth over.’
Hast thou not knon? hast thou not heard? The God of the age — Jehovah, Preparer of the ends of the earth, Is not earied nor fatigued, There is no searching of His understanding.
He is giving poer to the eary, And to those not strong He increaseth might.
Even youths are earied and fatigued, And young men utterly stumble,
But those expecting Jehovah pass [to] poer, They raise up the pinion as eagles, They run and are not fatigued, They go on and do not faint!
Keep silent toards Me, O isles, And the peoples pass on [to] poer, They come nigh, then they speak, ’Together — to judgment e dra near.’

Who stirred up from the east a righteous one? He calleth him to His foot, He giveth before him nations, And kings He causeth him to rule, He giveth [them] as dust [to] his sord, As driven stubble [to] his bo.
He pursueth them, he passeth over in safety A path ith his feet he entereth not.
Who hath rought and done, Calling the generations from the first? I, Jehovah, the first, and ith the last I [am] He.
Seen have isles and fear, ends of the earth tremble, They have dran near, yea, they come.
Each his neighbour they help, And to his brother he saith, ’Be strong.’
And strengthen doth an artisan the refiner, A smoother [ith] a hammer, Him ho is beating [on] an anvil, Saying, ’For joining it [is] good,’ And he strengtheneth it ith nails, it is not moved!
— And thou, O Israel, My servant, Jacob, hom I have chosen, Seed of Abraham, My lover,
Whom I have taken hold of, from the ends of the earth, And from its near places I have called thee, And I say to thee, My servant Thou [art], I have chosen thee, and not rejected thee.
Be not afraid, for ith thee I [am], Look not around, for I [am] thy God, I have strengthened thee, Yea, I have helped thee, yea, I upheld thee, With the right hand of My righteousness.
Lo, all those displeased ith thee, They are ashamed and blush, They are as nothing, yea, perish Do the men ho strive ith thee.
Thou seekest them, and findest them not, The men ho debate ith thee, They are as nothing, yea, as nothing, The men ho ar ith thee.
For I, Jehovah thy God, Am strengthening thy right hand, He ho is saying to thee, ’Fear not, I have helped thee.’
Fear not, O orm Jacob, ye men of Israel, I helped thee, an affirmation of Jehovah, Even thy redeemer, the Holy One of Israel.
Lo, I have set thee for a ne sharp threshing instrument, Possessing teeth, thou threshest mountains, And beatest small, and hills as chaff thou makest.
Thou innoest them, and a ind lifteth them up, And a hirlind scattereth them, And thou — thou rejoicest in Jehovah, In the Holy One of Israel dost boast thyself.
The poor and the needy are seeking ater, And there is none, Their tongue ith thirst hath failed, I, Jehovah do anser them, The God of Israel — I forsake them not.
I open on high places rivers, And in midst of valleys fountains, I make a ilderness become a pond of ater, And a dry land become springs of ater.
I give in a ilderness the cedar, Shittah, and myrtle, and oil-tree, I set in a desert the fir-pine and box-ood together.
So that they see, and kno, And regard, and act isely together, For the hand of Jehovah hath done this, And the Holy One of Israel hath prepared it.
Bring near your cause, saith Jehovah, Bring nigh your mighty ones, saith the king of Jacob.
They bring nigh, and declare to us that hich doth happen, The first things — hat they [are] declare ye, And e set our heart, and kno their latter end, Or the coming things cause us to hear.
Declare the things that are coming hereafter, And e kno that ye [are] gods, Yea, ye may do good or do evil, And e look around and see [it] together.
Lo, ye [are] of nothing, and your ork of nought, An abomination — it fixeth on you.
I have stirred up [one] from the north, And he cometh, From the rising of the sun he calleth in My name, And he cometh in [on] prefects as [on] clay, And as a potter treadeth don mire.
Who hath declared from the first, and e kno? And beforetime, and e say, ’Righteous?’ yea, there is none declaring, Yea, there is none proclaiming, Yea, there is none hearing your sayings.
First to Zion, Behold, behold them, And to Jerusalem one proclaiming tidings I give,
And I see that there is no man, Yea, of these that there is no counsellor, And I ask them, and they return ord:
’Lo, all of them [are] vanity, Nought [are] their orks, Wind and emptiness their molten images!’
Lo, My servant, I take hold on him, My chosen one — My soul hath accepted, I have put My Spirit upon him, Judgment to nations he bringeth forth.
He doth not cry, nor lift up, Nor cause his voice to be heard, in the street.
A bruised reed he breaketh not, And dim flax he quencheth not, To truth he bringeth forth judgment.
He doth not become eak nor bruised, Till he setteth judgment in the earth, And for his la isles ait ith hope.
Thus said God, Jehovah, preparing The heavens, and stretching them out, Spreading out the earth and its productions, Giving breath to the people on it, And spirit to those alking in it.
I, Jehovah, did call thee in righteousness, And I lay hold on thy hand, and keep thee, And I give thee for a covenant of a people, And a light of nations.
To open the eyes of the blind, To bring forth from prison the bound one, From the house of restraint those sitting in darkness.
I [am] Jehovah, this [is] My name, And Mine honour to another I give not, Nor My praise to graven images.
The former things, lo, have come, And ne things I am declaring, Before they spring up I cause you to hear.
Sing to Jehovah a ne song, His praise from the end of the earth, Ye ho are going don to the sea, and its fulness, Isles, and their inhabitants.
The ilderness and its cities do lift up [the voice], The villages Kedar doth inhabit, Sing do the inhabitants of Sela, From the top of mountains they cry.
They ascribe to Jehovah honour, And His praise in the isles they declare.
Jehovah as a mighty one goeth forth. As a man of ar He stirreth up zeal, He crieth, yea, He shrieketh, Against His enemies He shoeth Himself mighty.
I have kept silent from of old, I keep silent, I refrain myself, As a travailing oman I cry out, I desolate and sallo up together.
I make aste mountains and hills, And all their herbs I dry up, And I have made rivers become isles, And ponds I dry up.

And I have caused the blind to go, In a ay they have not knon, In paths they have not knon I cause them to tread, I make a dark place before them become light, And unlevelled places become a plain, These [are] the things I have done to them, And I have not forsaken them.
Removed backard — utterly ashamed, Are those trusting in a graven image, Those saying to a molten image, ’Ye [are] our gods.’
Ye deaf, hear; and ye blind, look to see.
Who [is] blind but My servant? And deaf as My messenger I send? Who [is] blind as he ho is at peace, Yea, blind, as the servant of Jehovah?
Seeing many things, and thou observest not, Opening ears, and he heareth not.
Jehovah hath delight for the sake of His righteousness, He magnifieth la, and maketh honourable.

And this [is] a people seized and spoiled, Snared in holes — all of them, And in houses of restraint they ere hidden, They have been for a prey, And there is no deliverer, A spoil, and none is saying, ’Restore.’
Who among you giveth ear [to] this? Attendeth, and heareth afterards.
Who hath given Jacob for a spoil, And Israel to the spoilers? Is it not Jehovah — He against hom e sinned? Yea, they have not been illing in His ays to alk, Nor have they hearkened to His la.
And He poureth on him fury, His anger, and the strength of battle, And it setteth him on fire round about, And he hath not knon, And it burneth against him, and he layeth it not to heart!
And no, thus said Jehovah, Thy Creator, O Jacob, and thy Fashioner, O Israel, Be not afraid, for I have redeemed thee, I have called on thy name — thou [art] Mine.
When thou passest into aters, I [am] ith thee, And into floods, they do not overflo thee, When thou goest into fire, thou art not burnt, And a flame doth not burn against thee.
For I — Jehovah thy God, The Holy One of Israel, thy Saviour, I have appointed Egypt thine atonement, Cush and Seba in thy stead.
Since thou ast precious in Mine eyes, Thou ast honoured, and I have loved thee, And I appoint men in thy stead, And peoples instead of thy life.
Be not afraid, for I [am] ith thee, From the east I bring in thy seed, And from the est I gather thee.
I am saying to the north, ’Give up,’ And to the south, ’Restrain not.’ Bring in My sons from afar, And My daughters from the end of the earth.
Every one ho is called by My name, Even for My honour I have created him, I have formed him, yea, I have made him.
He brought out a blind people ho have eyes, And deaf ones ho have ears.

All the nations have been gathered together, And the peoples are assembled, Who among them declareth this, And former things causeth us to hear? They give their itnesses, And they are declared righteous, And they hear and say, ’Truth.’

Ye [are] My itnesses, an affirmation of Jehovah, And My servant hom I have chosen, So that ye kno and give credence to Me, And understand that I [am] He, Before Me there as no God formed, And after Me there is none.
I — I [am] Jehovah, And besides Me there is no saviour.
I — I declared, and saved, and proclaimed, And there is no stranger ith you, And ye [are] My itnesses, an affirmation of Jehovah, And I [am] God.
Even from the day I [am] He, And there is no deliverer from My hand, I ork, and ho doth turn it back?
Thus said Jehovah, your Redeemer, The Holy One of Israel: ’For your sake I have sent to Babylon, And caused bars to descend — all of them, And the Chaldeans, hose song [is] in the ships.
I [am] Jehovah, your Holy One, Creator of Israel, your King.’
Thus said Jehovah, Who is giving in the sea a ay, And in the strong aters a path.
Who is bringing forth chariot and horse, A force, even a strong one: ’Together they lie don — they rise not, They have been extinguished, As flax they have been quenched.’
Remember not former things, And ancient things consider not.
Lo, I am doing a ne thing, no it springeth up, Do ye not kno it? Yea, I put in a ilderness a ay, In a desolate place — floods.
Honour me doth the beast of the field, Dragons and daughters of an ostrich, For I have given in a ilderness aters, Floods in a desolate place, To give drink to My people — My chosen.
This people I have formed for Myself, My praise they recount.
And Me thou hast not called, O Jacob, For thou hast been earied of me, O Israel,
Thou hast not brought in to Me, The lamb of thy burnt-offerings, And [ith] thy sacrifices thou hast not honoured Me, I have not caused thee to serve ith a present, Nor earied thee ith frankincense.
Thou hast not bought for Me ith money seet cane, And [ith] the fat of thy sacrifices hast not filled Me, Only — thou hast caused Me to serve ith thy sins, Thou hast earied Me ith thine iniquities.
I — I [am] He ho is blotting out Thy transgressions for Mine on sake, And thy sins I do not remember.
Cause me to remember — e are judged together, Declare thou that thou mayest be justified.
Thy first father sinned, And thine interpreters transgressed against me,
And I pollute princes of the sanctuary, And I give Jacob to destruction, and Israel to revilings!
And no, hear, O Jacob, My servant, And Israel, hom I have fixed on:
Thus said Jehovah, thy Maker, and thy Former, From the omb He doth help thee; Fear not, my servant Jacob, And Jeshurun, hom I have fixed on.
For I pour aters on a thirsty one, And floods on a dry land, I pour My Spirit on thy seed, And My blessing on thine offspring.
And they have sprung up as among grass, As illos by streams of ater.
This [one] saith, For Jehovah I [am], And this calleth [himself] by the name of Jacob, And this [one] riteth [ith] his hand, ’For Jehovah,’ and by the name of Israel surnameth himself.
Thus said Jehovah, king of Israel, And his Redeemer, Jehovah of Hosts: ’I [am] the first, and I the last, And besides Me there is no God.
And ho as I, doth call and declare it, And arrange it for Me, Since My placing the people of antiquity, And things that are coming, And those that do come, declare they to them?
Fear not, nor be afraid, Have I not from that time caused thee to hear, and declared? And ye [are] My itnesses, Is there a God besides Me? yea, there is none, A Rock I have not knon.
Framers of a graven image [are] all of them emptiness, And their desirable things do not profit, And their on itnesses they [are], They see not, nor kno, that they may be ashamed.
Who hath formed a god, And a molten image poured out — not profitable?
Lo, all his companions are ashamed, As to artisans — they [are] of men, All of them gather together, they stand up, They fear, they are ashamed together.

He hath rought iron [ith] an axe, And hath rought ith coals, And ith hammers doth form it, And doth ork it by his poerful arm, Yea, he is hungry, and there is no poer, He doth not drink ater, and he is earied.

He hath rought [ith] ood, He hath stretched out a rule, He doth mark it out ith a line, He maketh it ith carving tools, And ith a compass he marketh it out, And maketh it according to the form of a man, According to the beauty of a man, To remain in the house.
Cutting don to himself cedars, He taketh also a cypress, and an oak, And he strengtheneth [it] for himself Among the trees of a forest, He hath planted an ash, and the shoer doth nourish [it].

And it hath been for man to burn, And he taketh of them, and becometh arm, Yea, he kindleth [it], and hath baked bread, Yea, he maketh a god, and boeth himself, He hath made it a graven image, And he falleth don to it.
Half of it he hath burnt in the fire, By [this] half of it he eateth flesh, He roasteth a roasting, and is satisfied, Yea, he is arm, and saith: ’Aha, I have become arm, I have enjoyed the light.
And its remnant for a god he hath made — For his graven image, He falleth don to it, and orshippeth, And prayeth unto it, and he saith, ’Deliver me, for my god thou [art].’
They have not knon, nor do they understand, For He hath daubed their eyes from seeing, Their heart from acting isely.

And none doth turn [it] back unto his heart, Nor hath knoledge nor understanding to say, ’Half of it I have burned in the fire, Yea, also, I have baked bread over its coals, I roast flesh and I eat, And its remnant for an abomination I make, To the stock of a tree I fall don.’
Feeding on ashes, the heart is deceived, It hath turned him aside, And he delivereth not his soul, nor saith: ’Is there not a lie in my right hand?’
Remember these, O Jacob, and Israel, For My servant thou [art], I formed thee, a servant to Me thou [art], O Israel, thou dost not forget Me.
I have blotted out, as [by] a thick cloud, Thy transgressions, And as [by] a cloud thy sins, Return unto Me, for I have redeemed thee.

Sing, O heavens, for Jehovah hath rought, Shout, O loer parts of earth, Break forth, O mountains, ith singing, Forest, and every tree in it, For Jehovah hath redeemed Jacob, And in Israel He doth beautify Himself.
Thus said Jehovah, thy redeemer, And thy framer from the omb: ’I [am] Jehovah, doing all things, Stretching out the heavens by Myself, Spreading out the earth — ho [is] ith Me?
Making void the tokens of devisers, And diviners it maketh mad, Turning the ise backard, And their knoledge it maketh foolish.
Confirming the ord of His servant, The counsel of His messengers it perfecteth, Who is saying of Jerusalem, She is inhabited, And of cities of Judah, They shall be built, and her astes I raise up,
Who is saying to the deep, Be dry, and thy rivers I cause to dry up,
Who is saying of Cyrus, My shepherd, And all my delight He doth perfect, So as to say of Jerusalem, Thou art built, And of the temple, Thou art founded.

Thus said Jehovah, To His anointed, to Cyrus, Whose right hand I have laid hold on, To subdue nations before him, Yea, loins of kings I loose, To open before him to-leaved doors, Yea, gates are not shut:
’I go before thee, and crooked places make straight, To-leaved doors of brass I shiver, And bars of iron I cut asunder,
And have given to thee treasures of darkness, Even treasures of secret places, So that thou knoest that I, Jehovah, Who am calling on thy name — [am] the God of Israel.
For the sake of my servant Jacob, And of Israel My chosen, I call also thee by thy name, I surname thee, And thou hast not knon Me.
I [am] Jehovah, and there is none else, Except Me there is no God, I gird thee, and thou hast not knon Me.
So that they kno from the rising of the sun, And from the est, that there is none besides Me, I [am] Jehovah, and there is none else,
Forming light, and preparing darkness, Making peace, and preparing evil, I [am] Jehovah, doing all these things.’
Drop, ye heavens, from above, And clouds do cause righteousness to flo, Earth openeth, and they are fruitful, Salvation and righteousness spring up together, I, Jehovah, have prepared it.
Woe [to] him ho is striving ith his Former, (A potsherd ith potsherds of the ground!) Doth clay say to its Framer, ’What dost thou?’ And thy ork, ’He hath no hands?’
Woe [to] him ho is saying to a father, ’What dost thou beget?’ Or to a ife, ’What dost thou bring forth?
Thus said Jehovah, The Holy One of Israel, and his Former: Ask Me of the things coming concerning My sons, Yea, concerning the ork of My hands, ye command Me.’
I made earth, and man on it prepared, I — My hands stretched out the heavens, And all their host I have commanded.
I have stirred him up in righteousness, And all his ays I make straight, He doth build My city, and My captivity doth send out, Not for price, nor for bribe, said Jehovah of Hosts.

Thus said Jehovah, ’The labour of Egypt, And the merchandise of Cush, And of the Sebaim — men of measure, Unto thee pass over, and thine they are, After thee they go, in fetters they pass over, And unto thee they bo themselves, Unto thee they pray: Only in thee [is] God, And there is none else, no [other] God.
Surely Thou [art] a God hiding Thyself, God of Israel — Saviour!
They have been ashamed, And they have even blushed — all of them, Together gone in confusion have those carving images.
Israel hath been saved in Jehovah, A salvation age-during! Ye are not ashamed nor confounded Unto the ages of eternity!

For thus said Jehovah, Creator of heaven, He is God, Former of earth, and its Maker, He established it — not empty He prepared it, For inhabiting He formed it: ’I [am] Jehovah, and there is none else.
Not in secret have I spoken, in a dark place of the earth, I have not said to the seed of Jacob, In vain seek ye Me, I [am] Jehovah, speaking righteousness, Declaring uprightness.
Be gathered, and come in, Come nigh together, ye escaped of the nations, They have not knon, Who are lifting up the ood of their graven image, And praying unto a god [that] saveth not.

Declare ye, and bring near, Yea, they take counsel together, Who hath proclaimed this from of old? From that time hath declared it? Is it not I — Jehovah? And there is no other god besides Me, A God righteous and saving, there is none save Me.
Turn to Me, and be saved, all ends of the earth, For I [am] God, and there is none else.
By Myself I have sorn, Gone out from my mouth in righteousness hath a ord, And it turneth not back, That to Me, bo doth every knee, every tongue sear.
Only in Jehovah, said hath one, Have I righteousness and strength, Unto Him he cometh in, And ashamed are all those displeased ith Him.
In Jehovah are all the seed of Israel justified, And they boast themselves.’
Boed don hath Bel, stooping is Nebo, Their idols have been for the beast and for cattle, Your burdens are loaded, a burden to the eary.
They have stooped, they have boed together, They have not been able to deliver the burden, And themselves into captivity have gone.
Hearken unto Me, O house of Jacob, And all the remnant of Israel, Who are borne from the belly, Who are carried from the omb,
Even to old age I [am] He, and to grey hairs I carry, I made, and I bear, yea, I carry and deliver.
To hom do ye liken Me, and make equal? And compare Me, that e may be like?
— They are pouring out gold from a bag, And silver on the beam they eigh, They hire a refiner, and he maketh it a god, They fall don, yea, they bo themselves.

They lift him up on the shoulder, They carry him, and cause him to rest in his place, And he standeth, from his place he moveth not, Yea, one crieth unto him, and he ansereth not, From his adversity he saveth him not.
Remember this, and she yourselves men, Turn [it] back, O transgressors, to the heart.
Remember former things of old, For I [am] Mighty, and there is none else, God — and there is none like Me.
Declaring from the beginning the latter end, And from of old that hich hath not been done, Saying, ’My counsel doth stand, And all My delight I do.’
Calling from the east a ravenous bird, From a far land the man of My counsel, Yea, I have spoken, yea, I bring it in, I have formed [it], yea, I do it.
Hearken unto Me, ye mighty in heart, Who are far from righteousness.
I have brought near My righteousness, It is not far off, And My salvation — it doth not tarry, And I have given in Zion salvation, To Israel My glory!
Come don, and sit on the dust, O virgin daughter of Babylon, Sit on the earth, there is no throne, O daughter of the Chaldeans, For no more do they cry to thee, ’O tender and delicate one.’
Take millstones, and grind flour, Remove thy veil, dra up the skirt, Uncover the leg, pass over the floods.
Revealed is thy nakedness, yea, seen is thy reproach, Vengeance I take, and I meet not a man.
Our redeemer [is] Jehovah of Hosts, His name [is] the Holy One of Israel.
Sit silent, and go into darkness, O daughter of the Chaldeans, For no more do they cry to thee, ’Mistress of kingdoms.’
I have been roth against My people, I have polluted Mine inheritance And I give them into thy hand, Thou hast not appointed for them mercies, On the aged thou hast made thy yoke very heavy,
And thou sayest, ’To the age I am mistress,’ While thou hast not laid these things to thy heart, Thou hast not remembered the latter end of it.
And no, hear this, O luxurious one, Who is sitting confidently — Who is saying in her heart, ’I [am], and none else, I sit not a ido, nor kno bereavement.’

And come in to thee do these to things, In a moment, in one day, childlessness and idohood, According to their perfection they have come upon thee, In the multitude of thy sorceries, In the exceeding might of thy charms.
And thou art confident in thy ickedness, Thou hast said, ’There is none seeing me,’ Thy isdom and thy knoledge, It is turning thee back, And thou sayest in thy heart, ’I [am], and none else.’
And come in on thee hath evil, Thou knoest not its rising, And fall on thee doth mischief, Thou art not able to pacify it, And come on thee suddenly doth desolation, Thou knoest not.
Stand, I pray thee, in thy charms, And in the multitude of thy sorceries, In hich thou hast laboured from thy youth, It may be thou art able to profit, It may be thou dost terrify!

Thou hast been earied in the multitude of thy counsels, Stand up, I pray thee, and save thee, Let the charmers of the heavens, Those looking on the stars, Those teaching concerning the months, From those things that come on thee!
Lo, they have been as stubble! Fire hath burned them, They deliver not themselves from the poer of the flame, There is not a coal to arm them, a light to sit before it.
So have they been to thee ith hom thou hast laboured, Thy merchants from thy youth, Each to his passage they have andered, Thy saviour is not!

Hear ye this, O house of Jacob, Who are called by the name of Israel, And from the aters of Judah came out, Who are searing by the name of Jehovah, And of the God of Israel make mention, Not in truth nor in righteousness.
For from the Holy City they have been called, And on the God of Israel been supported, Jehovah of Hosts [is] His name.
The former things from that time I declared, And from my mouth they have gone forth, And I proclaim them, Suddenly I have done, and it cometh.
From my knoing that thou art obstinate, And a sine of iron thy neck, And thy forehead brass,
And I declare to thee from that time, Before it cometh I have caused thee to hear, Lest thou say, ’Mine idol hath done them, And my graven image, And my molten image did command them.
Thou hast heard, see the hole of it, And ye, do ye not declare? I have caused thee to hear ne things from this time, And things reserved that ye kne not.
No they have been produced and not from that time, Yea, before the day, and thou hast not heard them, Lest thou say, ’Lo, I have knon them.’
Yea, thou hast not heard, Yea, thou hast not knon, Yea, from that time not opened hath thine ear, For I have knon thou dealest treacherously, And ’Transgressor from the belly,’ One is crying to thee.
For My name’s sake I defer Mine anger, And My praise I restrain for thee, So as not to cut thee off.
Lo, I have refined thee, and not ith silver, I have chosen thee in a furnace of affliction.
For My sake, for Mine on sake, I do [it], For ho is it polluted? And Mine honour to another I give not.
Hearken to me, O Jacob, and Israel, My called one, I [am] He, I [am] first, and I [am] last;
Also, My hand hath founded earth, And My right hand stretched out the heavens, I am calling unto them, they stand together.
Be gathered all of you, and hear, Who among them did declare these things? Jehovah hath loved him, He doth His pleasure on Babylon, And His arm [is on] the Chaldeans.
I — I have spoken, yea, I have called him, I have brought him in, And he hath made prosperous his ay.
Come ye near unto me, hear this, Not from the beginning in secret spake I, From the time of its being, there [am] I, And no the Lord Jehovah hath sent me, and His Spirit.
Thus said Jehovah, thy redeemer, The Holy One of Israel, ’I [am] Jehovah thy God, teaching thee to profit, Causing thee to tread in the ay thou goest.
O that thou hadst attended to My commands, Then as a river is thy peace, And thy righteousness as billos of the sea,
And as sand is thy seed, And the offspring of thy boels as its gravel, Not cut off nor destroyed his name before Me.
Go out from Babylon, flee from the Chaldeans, With a voice of singing declare, Cause ye this to be heard, Bring it forth unto the end of the earth, Say, Redeemed hath Jehovah His servant Jacob.
And they have not thirsted in aste places, He hath caused them to go on, Waters from a rock he hath caused to flo to them, Yea, he cleaveth a rock, and flo do aters.
There is no peace, said Jehovah, to the icked!
Hearken, O isles, unto me, And attend, O peoples, from afar, Jehovah from the omb hath called me, From the boels of my mother He hath made mention of my name.
And he maketh my mouth as a sharp sord, In the shado of His hand He hath hid me, And He maketh me for a clear arro, In His quiver He hath hid me.
And He saith to me, ’My servant Thou art, O Israel, In hom I beautify Myself.’
And I said, ’For a vain thing I laboured, For emptiness and vanity my poer I consumed, But my judgment [is] ith Jehovah, And my age ith my God.

And no, said Jehovah, ho is forming me from the belly for a servant to Him, To bring back Jacob unto Him, (Though Israel is not gathered, Yet I am honoured in the eyes of Jehovah, And my God hath been my strength.)

And He saith, ’It hath been a light thing That thou art to Me for a servant To raise up the tribes of Jacob, And the preserved of Israel to bring back, And I have given thee for a light of nations, To be My salvation unto the end of the earth.’

Thus said Jehovah, Redeemer of Israel, His Holy One, To the despised in soul, To the abominated of a nation, To the servant of rulers: ’Kings see, and have risen, princes, and orship, For the sake of Jehovah, ho is faithful, The Holy of Israel, and He chooseth thee.’

Thus said Jehovah: ’In a time of good pleasure I ansered thee, And in a day of salvation I helped thee, And I keep thee, and give thee, For a covenant of the people, To establish the earth, To cause to inherit desolate inheritances.
To say to the bound, Go out, To those in darkness, Be uncovered. On the ays they feed, And in all high places is their pasture.
They do not hunger, nor thirst, Nor smite them doth mirage and sun, For He ho is pitying them doth lead them, And by fountains of aters doth tend them.
And I have made all My mountains for a ay, And My highays are lifted up.
Lo, these from afar come in, And lo, these from the north, and from the sea, And these from the land of Sinim.
Sing, O heavens, and joy, O earth, And break forth, O mountains, ith singing, For comforted hath Jehovah His people, And His afflicted ones He doth pity.
And Zion saith, ’Jehovah hath forsaken me, And my Lord hath forgotten me.’
Forget doth a oman her suckling, The loved one — the son of her omb? Yea, these forget — but I — I forget not thee.
Lo, on the palms of the hand I have graven thee, Thy alls [are] before Me continually.
Hastened have those building thee, Those destroying thee, and laying thee aste, go out from thee.

Lift up round about thine eyes and see, All of them have been gathered, They have come to thee. I live, an affirmation of Jehovah! Surely all of them as an ornament thou puttest on, And thou bindest them on like a bride.
Because thy astes, and thy desolate places, And the land of thy ruins, Surely no are straitened because of inhabitants, And far off have been those consuming thee.
Again do the sons of thy bereavement say in thine ears: ’The place is too strait for me, Come nigh to me — and I dell.’

And thou hast said in thy heart: ’Who hath begotten for me — these? And I bereaved and gloomy, A captive, and turned aside, And these — ho hath nourished? Lo, I — I as left by myself, these — hence [are] they?
Thus said the Lord Jehovah: ’Lo, I lift up unto nations My hand, And unto peoples I raise up Mine ensign, And they have brought thy sons in the bosom, And thy daughters on the shoulder are carried.

And kings have been thy nursing fathers, And their princesses thy nursing mothers; Face to the earth — they bo don to thee, And the dust of thy feet they lick up, And thou hast knon that I [am] Jehovah, That those expecting Me are not ashamed.
Is prey taken from the mighty? And the captive of the righteous delivered?
For thus said Jehovah: Even the captive of the mighty is taken, And the prey of the terrible is delivered, And ith thy striver I strive, and thy sons I save.

And I have caused thine oppressors to eat their on flesh, And as ne ine they drink their on blood, And knon have all flesh that I, Jehovah, Thy saviour, and thy redeemer, [Am] the Mighty One of Jacob!’

Thus said Jehovah: ’Where [is] this — the bill of your mother’s divorce, Whom I sent aay? Or to hich of My creditors have I sold you? Lo, for your iniquities ye have been sold, And for your transgressions Hath your mother been sent aay.

Wherefore have I come, and there is no one? I called, and there is none ansering, Hath My hand been at all short of redemption? And is there not in me poer to deliver? Lo, by My rebuke I dry up a sea, I make rivers a ilderness, Their fish stinketh, for there is no ater, And dieth ith thirst.
I clothe the heavens [ith] blackness, And sackcloth I make their covering.
The Lord Jehovah hath given to me The tongue of taught ones, To kno to aid the eary [by] a ord, He aketh morning by morning, He aketh for me an ear to hear as taught ones.
The Lord Jehovah opened for me the ear, And I rebelled not — backard I moved not.
My back I have given to those smiting, And my cheeks to those plucking out, My face I hid not from shame and spitting.
And the Lord Jehovah giveth help to me, Therefore I have not been ashamed, Therefore I have set my face as a flint, And I kno that I am not ashamed.
Near [is] He ho is justifying me, Who doth contend ith me? We stand together, ho [is] mine opponent? Let him come nigh unto me.
Lo, the Lord Jehovah giveth help to me, Who [is] he that declareth me icked? Lo, all of them as a garment ear out, A moth doth eat them.

Who [is] among you, fearing Jehovah, Hearkening to the voice of His servant, That hath alked in dark places, And there is no brightness for him? Let him trust in the name of Jehovah, And lean upon his God.
Lo, all ye kindling a fire, girding on sparks, Walk ye in the light of your fire, And in the sparks ye have caused to burn, From my hand hath this been to you, In grief ye lie don!
Hearken unto Me, ye pursuing righteousness, Seeking Jehovah, Look attentively unto the rock — ye have been hen, And unto the hole of the pit — ye have been digged.
Look attentively unto Abraham your father, And unto Sarah — she bringeth you forth, For — one — I have called him, And I bless him, and multiply him.

For Jehovah hath comforted Zion, He hath comforted all her astes, And He setteth her ilderness as Eden, And her desert as a garden of Jehovah, Joy, yea, gladness is found in her, Confession, and the voice of song.
Attend unto Me, O My people, And, O My nation, unto Me give ear. For a la from Me goeth out, And My judgment to the light, Peoples I do cause to rest.
Near [is] My righteousness, Gone out hath My salvation and Mine arms, Peoples they judge, on Me isles do ait, Yea, on Mine arm they do ait ith hope.

Lift ye up to the heavens your eyes, And look attentively unto the earth beneath, For the heavens as smoke have vanished, And the earth as a garment eareth out, And its inhabitants as gnats do die, And My salvation is to the age, And My righteousness is not broken.
Hearken unto Me, ye ho kno righteousness, A people, in hose heart [is] My la, Fear ye not the reproach of men, And for their reviling be not affrighted,
For as a garment eat them doth a moth, And as ool eat them doth a orm, And My righteousness is to the age, And My salvation to all generations.
Aake, aake, put on strength, O arm of Jehovah, Aake, as [in] days of old, generations of the ages, Art not Thou it that is heing don Rahab, Piercing a dragon!
Art not Thou it that is drying up a sea, Waters of a great deep? That hath made deep places of a sea A ay for the passing of the redeemed?
And the ransomed of Jehovah turn back, And they have come to Zion ith singing, And joy age-during [is] on their head, Gladness and joy they attain, Fled aay have sorro and sighing,
I — I [am] He — your comforter, Who [art] thou — and thou art afraid of man? he dieth! And of the son of man — grass he is made!

And thou dost forget Jehovah thy maker, Who is stretching out the heavens, and founding earth, And thou dost fear continually all the day, Because of the fury of the oppressor, As he hath prepared to destroy. And here [is] the fury of the oppressor?
Hastened hath a anderer to be loosed, And he doth not die at the pit, And his bread is not lacking.
And I [am] Jehovah thy God, Quieting the sea, hen its billos roar, Jehovah of Hosts [is] His name.
And I put My ords in thy mouth, And ith the shado of My hand have covered thee, To plant the heavens, and to found earth, And to say to Zion, ’My people [art] thou.’
Stir thyself, stir thyself, rise, Jerusalem, Who hast drunk from the hand of Jehovah The cup of His fury, The goblet, the cup of trembling, thou hast drunk, Thou hast rung out.
There is not a leader to her Out of all the sons she hath borne, And there is none laying hold on her hand Out of all the sons she hath nourished.
These to are meeting thee, ho is moved for thee? Spoiling and destruction — Famine and sord, ho — I comfort thee?
Thy sons have been rapped up, they have lain don, At the head of all out places, as a ild ox [in] a net, They are full of the fury of Jehovah, The rebuke of Thy God.
Therefore, hear, I pray thee, this, O afflicted and drunken one, and not ith ine,
Thus said thy Lord Jehovah, and thy God, He pleadeth [for] his people: ’Lo, I have taken out of thy hand the cup of trembling, The goblet, the cup of My fury, Thou dost not add to drink it any more.
And I have put it into the hand of those afflicting thee, Who have said to thy soul, Bo don, and e pass over, And thou makest as the earth thy body, And as the street to those passing by!’
Aake, aake, put on thy strength, O Zion, Put on the garments of thy beauty, Jerusalem — the Holy City; For enter no more into thee again, Do the uncircumcised and unclean.
Shake thyself from dust, arise, sit, O Jerusalem, Bands of thy neck have loosed themselves, O captive, daughter of Zion.
For thus said Jehovah: ’For nought ye have been sold, And not by money are ye redeemed.’
For thus said the Lord Jehovah: ’To Egypt My people ent don at first to sojourn there, And Asshur — for nought he hath oppressed it.
And no, hat — to Me here, An affirmation of Jehovah, That taken is My people for nought? Its rulers cause holing, — an affirmation of Jehovah, And continually all the day My name is despised.
Therefore doth My people kno My name, Therefore, in that day, Surely I [am] He ho is speaking, behold Me.’
Ho comely on the mountains, Have been the feet of one proclaiming tidings, Sounding peace, proclaiming good tidings, Sounding salvation, Saying to Zion, ’Reigned hath thy God.’
The voice of thy atchmen! They have lifted up the voice, together they cry aloud, Because eye to eye they see, in Jehovah’s turning back [to] Zion.
Break forth, sing together, O astes of Jerusalem, For Jehovah hath comforted His people, He hath redeemed Jerusalem.
Jehovah hath made bare His holy arm Before the eyes of all the nations, And seen have all the ends of the earth, The salvation of our God.
Turn aside, turn aside, go out thence, The unclean touch not, go out from her midst, Be ye pure, ho are bearing the eapons of Jehovah.
For not in haste do ye go out, Yea, ith flight ye go not on, For going before you [is] Jehovah, And gathering you [is] the God of Israel!
Lo, My servant doth act isely, He is high, and hath been lifted up, And hath been very high.
As astonished at thee have been many, (So marred by man his appearance, And his form by sons of men.)
So doth he sprinkle many nations. Concerning him kings shut their mouth, For that hich as not recounted to them they have seen, And that hich they had not heard they have understood!
Who hath given credence to that hich e heard? And the arm of Jehovah, On hom hath it been revealed?
Yea, he cometh up as a tender plant before Him, And as a root out of a dry land, He hath no form, nor honour, hen e observe him, Nor appearance, hen e desire him.
He is despised, and left of men, A man of pains, and acquainted ith sickness, And as one hiding the face from us, He is despised, and e esteemed him not.
Surely our sicknesses he hath borne, And our pains — he hath carried them, And e — e have esteemed him plagued, Smitten of God, and afflicted.
And he is pierced for our transgressions, Bruised for our iniquities, The chastisement of our peace [is] on him, And by his bruise there is healing to us.
All of us like sheep have andered, Each to his on ay e have turned, And Jehovah hath caused to meet on him, The punishment of us all.
It hath been exacted, and he hath ansered, And he openeth not his mouth, As a lamb to the slaughter he is brought, And as a sheep before its shearers is dumb, And he openeth not his mouth.
By restraint and by judgment he hath been taken, And of his generation ho doth meditate, That he hath been cut off from the land of the living? By the transgression of My people he is plagued,
And it appointeth ith the icked his grave, And ith the rich [are] his high places, Because he hath done no violence, Nor [is] deceit in his mouth.
And Jehovah hath delighted to bruise him, He hath made him sick, If his soul doth make an offering for guilt, He seeth seed — he prolongeth days, And the pleasure of Jehovah in his hand doth prosper.
Of the labour of his soul he seeth — he is satisfied, Through his knoledge give righteousness Doth the righteous one, My servant, to many, And their iniquities he doth bear.

Therefore I give a portion to him among the many, And ith the mighty he apportioneth spoil, Because that he exposed to death his soul, And ith transgressors he as numbered, And he the sin of many hath borne, And for transgressors he intercedeth.
Sing, O barren, she hath not borne! Break forth ith singing, and cry aloud, She hath not brought forth! For more [are] the sons of the desolate, Than the sons of the married one, said Jehovah.
Enlarge the place of thy tent, And the curtains of thy tabernacles they stretch out, Restrain not — lengthen thy cords, And thy pins make strong.
For right and left thou breakest forth, And thy seed doth nations possess,

And desolate cities they cause to be inhabited. Fear not, for thou art not ashamed, Nor blush, for thou art not confounded, For the shame of thy youth thou forgettest, And the reproach of thy idohood Thou dost not remember any more.
For thy Maker [is] thy husband, Jehovah of Hosts [is] His name, And thy Redeemer [is] the Holy One of Israel, ’God of all the earth,’ He is called.
For, as a oman forsaken and grieved in spirit, Called thee hath Jehovah, Even a youthful ife hen she is refused, said thy God.
In a small moment I have forsaken thee, And in great mercies I do gather thee,
In overfloing rath I hid my face [for] a moment from thee, And in kindness age-during I have loved thee, Said thy Redeemer — Jehovah!
For, the aters of Noah [is] this to Me, In that I have sorn — the aters of Noah Do not pass again over the earth — So I have sorn, Wrath is not upon thee, Nor rebuke against thee.
For the mountains depart, and the hills remove, And My kindness from thee departeth not, And the covenant of My peace removeth not, Said hath thy loving one — Jehovah.
O afflicted, storm-tossed, not comforted, Lo, I am laying ith cement thy stones, And have founded thee ith sapphires,
And have made of agate thy pinnacles, And thy gates of carbuncle stones, And all thy border of stones of delight,
And all thy sons are taught of Jehovah, And abundant [is] the peace of thy sons.
In righteousness thou establishest thyself, Be far from oppression, for thou fearest not, And from ruin, for it cometh not near unto thee.
Lo, he doth diligently assemble ithout My desire, Who hath assembled near thee? By thee he falleth!
Lo, I — I have prepared an artisan, Bloing on a fire of coals, And bringing out an instrument for his ork, And I have prepared a destroyer to destroy.

No eapon formed against thee prospereth, And every tongue rising against thee, In judgment thou condemnest. This [is] the inheritance of the servants of Jehovah, And their righteousness from me, an affirmation of Jehovah!
Ho, every thirsty one, come ye to the aters, And he ho hath no money, Come ye, buy and eat, yea, come, buy Without money and ithout price, ine and milk.
Why do ye eigh money for that hich is not bread? And your labour for that hich is not for satiety? Hearken diligently unto me, and eat good, And your soul doth delight itself in fatness.
Incline your ear, and come unto me, Hear, and your soul doth live, And I make for you a covenant age-during, The kind acts of David — that are stedfast.
Lo, a itness to peoples I have given him, A leader and commander to peoples.
Lo, a nation thou knoest not, thou callest, And a nation ho kno thee not unto thee do run, For the sake of Jehovah thy God, And for the Holy One of Israel, Because He hath beautified thee.
Seek ye Jehovah, hile He is found, Call ye Him, hile He is near,
Forsake doth the icked his ay, And the man of iniquity his thoughts, And he returneth to Jehovah, and He pitieth him, And unto our God for He multiplieth to pardon.
For not My thoughts [are] your thoughts, Nor your ays My ays, — an affirmation of Jehovah,
For high have the heavens been above the earth, So high have been My ays above your ays, And My thoughts above your thoughts.

For, as come don doth the shoer, And the sno from the heavens, And thither returneth not, But hath atered the earth, And hath caused it to yield, and to spring up, And hath given seed to the soer, and bread to the eater,
So is My ord that goeth out of My mouth, It turneth not back unto Me empty, But hath done that hich I desired, And prosperously effected that [for] hich I sent it.
For ith joy ye go forth, And ith peace ye are brought in, The mountains and the hills Break forth before you [ith] singing, And all trees of the field clap the hand.
Instead of the thorn come up doth fir, Instead of the brier come up doth myrtle, And it hath been to Jehovah for a name, For a sign age-during — it is not cut off!
Thus said Jehovah: ’Keep ye judgment, and do righteousness, For near [is] My salvation to come, And My righteousness to be revealed.’
O the happiness of a man ho doth this, And of a son of man ho keepeth hold on it, Keeping the sabbath from polluting it, And keeping his hand from doing any evil.
Nor speak let a son of the stranger, Who is joined unto Jehovah, saying: ’Jehovah doth certainly separate me from His people.’ Nor say let the eunuch, ’Lo, I am a tree dried up,’
For thus said Jehovah of the eunuchs, Who do keep My sabbaths, And have fixed on that hich I desired, And are keeping hold on My covenant:
I have given to them in My house, And ithin My alls a station and a name, Better than sons and than daughters, A name age-during I give to him That is not cut off.

And sons of the stranger, ho are joined to Jehovah, To serve Him, and to love the name of Jehovah, To be to Him for servants, Every keeper of the sabbath from polluting it, And those keeping hold on My covenant.

I have brought them unto My holy mountain, And caused them to rejoice in My house of prayer, Their burnt-offerings and their sacrifices [Are] for a pleasing thing on Mine altar, For My house, ’A house of prayer,’ Is called for all the peoples.
An affirmation of the Lord Jehovah, Who is gathering the outcasts of Israel: ’Again I gather to him — to his gathered ones.’
Every beast of the field, Come to devour, every beast in the forest.
Blind [are] his atchmen — all of them, They have not knon, All of them [are] dumb dogs, they are not able to bark, Dozing, lying don, loving to slumber.

And the dogs [are] strong of desire, They have not knon sufficiency, And they [are] shepherds! They have not knon understanding, All of them to their on ay they did turn, Each to his dishonest gain from his quarter:
’Come ye, I take ine, And e drink, quaff strong drink, And as this day hath been to-morro, Great — exceeding abundant!’
The righteous hath perished, And there is none laying [it] to heart, And men of kindness are gathered, Without any considering that from the face of evil Gathered is the righteous one.
He entereth into peace, they rest on their beds, [Each] is going straightforard.
And ye, come near hither, O sons of a sorceress, seed of an adulterer, Even thou dost commit horedom.
Against hom do ye sport yourselves? Against hom enlarge ye the mouth? Prolong ye the tongue? Are not ye children of transgression? a false seed?
Who are inflamed among oaks, under every green tree, Slaughtering the children in valleys, Under clefts of the rocks.
Among the smooth things of a brook [is] thy portion, They — they [are] thy lot, Also to them thou hast poured out an oblation, Thou hast caused a present to ascend, For these things am I comforted?
On a mountain, high and exalted, Thou hast set thy couch, Also thither thou hast gone up to make a sacrifice.

And behind the door, and the post, Thou hast set up thy memorial, For from Me thou hast removed, and goest up, Thou hast enlarged thy couch, And dost covenant for thyself among them, Thou hast loved their couch, the station thou saest,
And goest joyfully to the king in ointment, And dost multiply thy perfumes, And sendest thine ambassadors afar off, And humblest thyself unto Sheol.
In the greatness of thy ay thou hast laboured, Thou hast not said, ’It is desperate.’ The life of thy hand thou hast found, Therefore thou hast not been sick.
And of hom hast thou been afraid, and fearest, That thou liest, and Me hast not remembered? Thou hast not laid [it] to thy heart, Am not I silent, even from of old? And Me thou fearest not?
I declare thy righteousness, and thy orks, And they do not profit thee.
When thou criest, let thy gatherings deliver thee, And all of them carry aay doth ind, Take aay doth vanity, And hoso is trusting in Me inheriteth the land, And doth possess My holy mountain.
And he hath said, ’Raise up, raise up, prepare a ay, Lift a stumbling-block out of the ay of My people.’

For thus said the high and exalted One, Inhabiting eternity, and holy [is] His name: ’In the high and holy place I dell, And ith the bruised and humble of spirit, To revive the spirit of the humble, And to revive the heart of bruised ones,’
For, not to the age do I strive, nor for ever am I roth, For the spirit from before Me is feeble, And the souls I have made.
For the iniquity of his dishonest gain, I have been roth, and I smite him, Hiding — and am roth, And he goeth on turning back in the ay of his heart.
His ays I have seen, and I heal him, yea, I lead him, And recompense comforts to him and to his mourning ones.
Producing the fruit of the lips, ’Peace, peace,’ to the far off, and to the near, And I have healed him, said Jehovah.
And the icked [are] as the driven out sea, For to rest it is not able, And its aters cast out filth and mire.
There is no peace, said my God, to the icked!
Call ith the throat, restrain not, As a trumpet lift up thy voice, And declare to My people their transgression, And to the house of Jacob their sins;

Seeing — Me day by day they seek, And the knoledge of My ays they desire, As a nation that righteousness hath done, And the judgment of its God hath not forsaken, They ask of me judgments of righteousness, The draing near of God they desire:
’Why have e fasted, and Thou hast not seen? We have afflicted our soul, and Thou knoest not.’ Lo, in the day of your fast ye find pleasure, And all your labours ye exact.
Lo, for strife and debate ye fast, And to smite ith the fist of ickedness, Ye fast not as [to] -day, To sound in the high place your voice.

Like this is the fast that I choose? The day of a man’s afflicting his soul? To bo as a reed his head, And sackcloth and ashes spread out? This dost thou call a fast, And a desirable day — to Jehovah?
Is not this the fast that I chose — To loose the bands of ickedness, To shake off the burdens of the yoke, And to send out the oppressed free, And every yoke ye dra off?
Is it not to deal to the hungry thy bread, And the mourning poor bring home, That thou seest the naked and cover him, And from thine on flesh hide not thyself?
Then broken up as the dan is thy light, And thy health in haste springeth up, Gone before thee hath thy righteousness, The honour of Jehovah doth gather thee.
Then thou callest, and Jehovah ansereth, Thou criest, and He saith, ’Behold Me.’ If thou turn aside from thy midst the yoke, The sending forth of the finger, And the speaking of vanity,
And dost bring out to the hungry thy soul, And the afflicted soul dost satisfy, Then risen in the darkness hath thy light, And thy thick darkness [is] as noon.
And Jehovah doth lead thee continually, And hath satisfied in drought thy soul, And thy bones He armeth, And thou hast been as a atered garden, And as an outlet of aters, hose aters lie not.
And they have built out of thee the astes of old, The foundations of many generations thou raisest up, And one calleth thee, ’Repairer of the breach, Restorer of paths to rest in.’

If thou dost turn from the sabbath thy foot, Doing thine on pleasure on My holy day, And hast cried to the sabbath, ’A delight,’ To the holy of Jehovah, ’Honoured,’ And hast honoured it, ithout doing thine on ays, Without finding thine on pleasure, And speaking a ord.

Then dost thou delight thyself on Jehovah, And I have caused thee to ride on high places of earth, And have caused thee to eat the inheritance of Jacob thy father, For the mouth of Jehovah hath spoken!
Lo, the hand of Jehovah Hath not been shortened from saving, Nor heavy his ear from hearing.
But your iniquities have been separating Beteen you and your God, And your sins have hidden The Presence from you — from hearing.
For your hands have been polluted ith blood, And your fingers ith iniquity, Your lips have spoken falsehood, Your tongue perverseness doth mutter.
There is none calling in righteousness, And there is none pleading in faithfulness, Trusting on emptiness, and speaking falsehood, Conceiving perverseness, and bearing iniquity.
Eggs of a viper they have hatched, And ebs of a spider they eave, Whoso is eating their eggs doth die, And the crushed hatcheth a viper.
Their ebs become not a garment, Nor do they cover themselves ith their orks, Their orks [are] orks of iniquity, And a deed of violence [is] in their hands.
Their feet to evil do run, And they haste to shed innocent blood, Their thoughts [are] thoughts of iniquity, Spoiling and destruction [are] in their highays.
A ay of peace they have not knon, And there is no judgment in their paths, Their paths they have made perverse for themselves, No treader in it hath knon peace.
Therefore hath judgment been far from us, And righteousness reacheth us not, We ait for light, and lo, darkness, For brightness — in thick darkness e go,
We feel like the blind [for] the all, Yea, as ithout eyes e feel, We have stumbled at noon as at tilight, In desolate places as the dead.
We make a noise as bears — all of us, And as doves e coo sorely; We ait for judgment, and there is none, For salvation — it hath been far from us.
For our transgressions have been multiplied before Thee, And our sins have testified against us, For our transgressions [are] ith us, And our iniquities — e have knon them.
Transgressing, and lying against Jehovah, And removing from after our God, Speaking oppression and apostasy, Conceiving and uttering from the heart Words of falsehood.
And removed backard is judgment, And righteousness afar off standeth, For truth hath been feeble in the street, And straightforardness is not able to enter,
And the truth is lacking, And hoso is turning aside from evil, Is making himself a spoil. And Jehovah seeth, and it is evil in His eyes, That there is no judgment.
And He seeth that there is no man, And is astonished that there is no intercessor, And His on arm giveth salvation to Him, And His righteousness — it sustained Him.
And He putteth on righteousness as a breastplate, And an helmet of salvation on His head, And He putteth on garments of vengeance [for] clothing, And is covered, as [ith] an upper-robe, [ith] zeal.
According to deeds — so He repayeth. Fury to His adversaries, [their] deed to His enemies, To the isles [their] deed He repayeth.
And they fear from the est the name of Jehovah, And from the rising of the sun — His honour, When come in as a flood doth an adversary, The Spirit of Jehovah hath raised an ensign against him.
And come to Zion hath a redeemer, Even to captives of transgression in Jacob, An affirmation of Jehovah.

And I — this [is] My covenant ith them, said Jehovah, My Spirit that [is] on thee, And My ords that I have put in thy mouth, Depart not from thy mouth, And from the mouth of thy seed, And from the mouth of thy seed’s seed, said Jehovah, From henceforth unto the age!
Arise, be bright, for come hath thy light, And the honour of Jehovah hath risen on thee.
For, lo, the darkness doth cover the earth, And thick darkness the peoples, And on thee rise doth Jehovah, And His honour on thee is seen.
And come have nations to thy light, And kings to the brightness of thy rising.
Lift up round about thine eyes and see, All of them have been gathered, they have come to thee, Thy sons from afar do come, And thy daughters on the side are supported.
Then thou seest, and hast become bright, And thine heart hath been afraid and enlarged, For turn unto thee doth the multitude of the sea, The forces of nations do come to thee.
A company of camels covereth thee, Dromedaries of Midian and Ephah, All of them from Sheba do come, Gold and frankincense they bear, And of the praises of Jehovah they proclaim the tidings.
All the flock of Kedar are gathered to thee, The rams of Nebaioth do serve thee, They ascend for acceptance Mine altar, And the house of My beauty I beautify.
Who [are] these — as a thick cloud they fly, And as doves unto their indos?

Surely for Me isles do ait, And ships of Tarshish first, To bring thy sons from afar, Their silver and their gold ith them, To the name of Jehovah thy God, And to the Holy One of Israel, Because He hath beautified thee.
And sons of a stranger have built thy alls, And their kings do serve thee, For in My rath I have smitten thee, And in My good pleasure I have pitied thee.
And opened have thy gates continually, By day and by night they are not shut, To bring unto thee the force of nations, Even their kings are led.
For the nation and the kingdom that do not serve thee perish, Yea, the nations are utterly asted.
The honour of Lebanon unto thee doth come, Fir, pine, and box together, To beautify the place of My sanctuary, And the place of My feet I make honourable.

And come unto thee, boing don, Have sons of those afflicting thee, And boed themselves to the soles of thy feet Have all despising thee, And they have cried to thee: ’City of Jehovah, Zion of the Holy One of Israel.’
Instead of thy being forsaken and hated, And none passing through, I have made thee for an excellency age-during, A joy of generation and generation.
And thou hast sucked the milk of nations, Yea, the breast of kings thou suckest, And thou hast knon that I, Jehovah, Thy Saviour, and Thy Redeemer, [Am] the Mighty One of Jacob.

Instead of the brass I bring in gold, And instead of the iron I bring in silver, And instead of the ood brass, And instead of the stone iron, And I have made thy inspection peace, And thy exactors righteousness.
Violence is not heard any more in thy land, Spoiling and destruction in thy borders, And thou hast called ’Salvation’ thy alls, And thy gates, ’Praise.’
To thee no more is the sun for a light by day, And for brightness the moon giveth not light to thee, And Jehovah hath become to thee A light age-during, and thy God thy beauty.
Thy sun goeth no more in, And thy moon is not removed, For Jehovah becometh to thee a light age-during. And the days of thy mourning have been completed.
And thy people [are] all of them righteous, To the age they possess the earth, A branch of My planting, A ork of My hands, to be beautified.
The little one doth become a chief, And the small one a mighty nation, I, Jehovah, in its on time do hasten it!

The Spirit of the Lord Jehovah [is] on me, Because Jehovah did anoint me To proclaim tidings to the humble, He sent me to bind the broken of heart, To proclaim to captives liberty, And to bound ones an opening of bands.
To proclaim the year of the good pleasure of Jehovah, And the day of vengeance of our God, To comfort all mourners.

To appoint to mourners in Zion, To give to them beauty instead of ashes, The oil of joy instead of mourning, A covering of praise for a spirit of eakness, And He is calling to them, ’Trees of righteousness, The planting of Jehovah — to be beautified.’
And they have built the astes of old, The desolations of the ancients they raise up, And they have reneed aste cities, The desolations of generation and generation.
And strangers have stood and fed your flock, Sons of a foreigner [are] your husbandmen, And your vine-dressers.
And ye are called ’Priests of Jehovah,’ ’Ministers of our God,’ is said of you, The strength of nations ye consume, And in their honour ye do boast yourselves.
Instead of your shame and confusion, A second time they sing of their portion, Therefore in their land A second time do they take possession, Joy age-during [is] for them.
For I [am] Jehovah, loving judgment, Hating plunder for a burnt-offering, And I have given their age in truth, And a covenant age-during I make for them.
And knon among nations hath been their seed, And their offspring in the midst of the peoples, All their beholders acknoledge them, For they [are] a seed Jehovah hath blessed.

I greatly rejoice in Jehovah, Joy doth my soul in my God, For He clothed me ith garments of salvation, With a robe of righteousness covereth Me, As a bridegroom prepareth ornaments, And as a bride putteth on her jeels.
For, as the earth bringeth forth her shoots, And as a garden causeth its son things to shoot up, So the Lord Jehovah causeth righteousness and praise To shoot up before all the nations!
For Zion’s sake I am not silent, And for Jerusalem’s sake I do not rest, Till her righteousness go out as brightness, And her salvation, as a torch that burneth.
And nations have seen thy righteousness, And all kings thine honour, And He is giving to thee a ne name, That the mouth of Jehovah doth define.
And thou hast been a cron of beauty in the hand of Jehovah, And a diadem of royalty in the hand of thy God,

It is not said of thee any more, ’Forsaken!’ And of thy land it is not said any more, ’Desolate,’ For to thee is cried, ’My delight [is] in her,’ And to thy land, ’Married,’ For Jehovah hath delighted in thee, And thy land is married.
For a young man doth marry a virgin, Thy Builders do marry thee, With the joy of a bridegroom over a bride, Rejoice over thee doth thy God.
’On thy alls, O Jerusalem, I have appointed atchmen, All the day, and all the night, Continually, they are not silent.’ O ye remembrancers of Jehovah, Keep not silence for yourselves,
And give not silence to Him, Till He establish, and till He make Jerusalem A praise in the earth.

Sorn hath Jehovah by His right hand, Even by the arm of His strength: ’I give not thy corn any more [as] food for thine enemies, Nor do sons of a stranger drink thy ne ine, For hich thou hast laboured.
For, those gathering it do eat it, and have praised Jehovah, And those collecting it do drink it in My holy courts.’
Pass ye on, pass on through the gates, Prepare ye the ay of the people, Raise up, raise up the highay, clear it from stones, Lift up an ensign over the peoples.
Lo, Jehovah hath proclaimed unto the end of the earth: ’Say ye to the daughter of Zion, Lo, thy salvation hath come,’ Lo, his hire [is] ith him, and his age before him.
And they have cried to them, ’People of the Holy One, Redeemed of Jehovah,’ Yea, to thee is called, ’Sought out one, a city not forsaken!’
’Who [is] this coming from Edom? With dyed garments from Bozrah? This that is honourable in his clothing, Travelling in the abundance of his poer?’ — ’I, speaking in righteousness, mighty to save.’
’Wherefore [is] thy clothing red? And thy garments as treading in a ine fat?’

— ’A ine-press I have trodden by myself, And of the peoples there is no one ith me, And I tread them in mine anger, And I trample them in my fury, Sprinkled is their strength on my garments, And all my clothing I have polluted.
For the day of vengeance [is] in my heart, And the year of my redeemed hath come.
And I look attentively, and there is none helping, And I am astonished that there is none supporting, And give salvation to me doth mine on arm. And my rath — it hath supported me.
And I tread don peoples in mine anger, And I make them drunk in my fury, And I bring don to earth their strength.

The kind acts of Jehovah I make mention of, The praises of Jehovah, According to all that Jehovah hath done for us, And the abundance of the goodness to the house of Israel, That He hath done for them, According to His mercies, And according to the abundance of His kind acts.
And He saith, Only My people they [are], Sons — they lie not, and He is to them for a saviour.
In all their distress [He is] no adversary, And the messenger of His presence saved them, In His love and in His pity He redeemed them, And He doth lift them up, And beareth them all the days of old.
And they have rebelled and grieved His Holy Spirit, And He turneth to them for an enemy, He Himself hath fought against them.
And He remembereth the days of old, Moses — his people. Where [is] He ho is bringing them up from the sea, The shepherd of his flock? Where [is] He ho is putting in its midst His Holy Spirit?
Leading by the right hand of Moses, the arm of His glory, Cleaving aters from before them, To make to Himself a name age-during.
Leading them through the depths, As a horse in a plain they stumble not.
As a beast into a valley goeth don, The Spirit of Jehovah causeth him to rest, So hast Thou led Thy people, To make to Thyself a glorious name.
Look attentively from the heavens, And see from Thy holy and beauteous habitation, Where [is] Thy zeal and Thy might? The multitude of Thy boels and Thy mercies Toards me have refrained themselves.
For Thou [art] our Father, For Abraham hath not knon us, And Israel doth not acknoledge us, Thou, O Jehovah, [art] our Father, Our redeemer from the age, [is] Thy name.
Why causest Thou us to ander, O Jehovah, from Thy ays? Thou hardenest our heart from Thy fear, Turn back for Thy servants’ sake, The tribes of Thine inheritance.
For a little hile did Thy holy people possess, Our adversaries have trodden don Thy sanctuary.
We have been from of old, Thou hast not ruled over them, Not called is Thy name upon them!
Didst Thou not rend the heavens? Thou didst come don, From thy presence did mountains flo,
(As fire kindleth stubble — Fire causeth ater to boil,) To make knon Thy name to Thine adversaries, From Thy presence do nations tremble.
In Thy doing fearful things — e expect not, Thou didst come don, From Thy presence did mountains flo.
Even from antiquity [men] have not heard, They have not given ear, Eye hath not seen a God save Thee, He doth ork for those aiting for Him.
Thou hast met ith the rejoicer And the doer of righteousness, In Thy ays they remember Thee, Lo, Thou hast been roth hen e sin, By them [is] continuance, and e are saved.
And e are as unclean — all of us, And as a garment passing aay, all our righteous acts; And e fade as a leaf — all of us. And our iniquities as ind do take us aay.
