from the presence of the Chaldeans, for they have been afraid of them, for Ishmael son of Nethaniah had smitten Gedaliah son of Ahikam, hom the king of Babylon had appointed over the land.
And they come nigh — all the heads of the forces, and Johanan son of Kareah, and Jezaniah son of Hoshaiah, and all the people from the least even unto the greatest —

and they say unto Jeremiah the prophet, ’Let, e pray thee, our supplication fall before thee, and pray for us unto Jehovah thy God, for all this remnant; for e have been left a fe out of many, as thine eyes do see us;
and Jehovah thy God doth declare to us the ay in hich e alk, and the thing that e do.’

And Jeremiah the prophet saith unto them, ’I have heard: lo, I am praying unto Jehovah your God according to your ords, and it hath come to pass, the hole ord that Jehovah ansereth you, I declare to you — I do not ithhold from you a ord.’
And they have said to Jeremiah, ’Jehovah is against us for a itness true and faithful, if — according to all the ord ith hich Jehovah thy God doth send thee unto us — e do not so.
Whether good or evil, to the voice of Jehovah our God, to hom e are sending thee, e do hearken; because it is good for us hen e hearken to the voice of Jehovah our God.’
And it cometh to pass, at the end of ten days, that there is a ord of Jehovah unto Jeremiah,
and he calleth unto Johanan son of Kareah, and unto all the heads of the forces that [are] ith him, and to all the people, from the least even unto the greatest,
and he saith unto them, ’Thus said Jehovah, God of Israel, unto hom ye sent me, to cause your supplication to fall before Him:
’If ye do certainly dell in this land, then I have builded you up, and I thro not don; and I have planted you, and I pluck not up; for I have repented concerning the evil that I have done to you.
Be not afraid of the king of Babylon, hom ye are afraid of; be not afraid of him — an affirmation of Jehovah — for ith you [am] I, to save you, and to deliver you from his hand.
And I give to you mercies, and he hath pitied you, and caused you to turn back unto your on ground.
’And if ye are saying, We do not dell in this land — not to hearken to the voice of Jehovah your God,
saying, No; but the land of Egypt e enter, that e see no ar, and the sound of a trumpet do not hear, and for bread be not hungry; and there do e dell.
And no, therefore, hear ye a ord of Jehovah, O remnant of Judah: Thus said Jehovah of Hosts, God of Israel: If ye really set your faces to enter Egypt, and have gone in to sojourn there,

then it hath come to pass, the sord that ye are afraid of, doth there overtake you, in the land of Egypt; and the hunger, because of hich ye are sorroful, doth there cleave after you in Egypt, and there ye die.

’Thus are all the men ho have set their faces to enter Egypt to sojourn there; they die — by sord, by hunger, and by pestilence, and there is not to them a remnant and an escaped one, because of the evil that I am bringing in upon them;

for thus said Jehovah of Hosts, God of Israel: As poured out hath been Mine anger and My fury on the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so poured out is My fury upon you in your entering Egypt, and ye have been for an execration, and for an astonishment, and for a reviling, and for a reproach, and ye do not see any more this place.
’Jehovah hath spoken against you, O remnant of Judah, do not enter Egypt: kno certainly that I have testified against you to-day;

for ye have sheed yourselves perverse in your souls, for ye sent me unto Jehovah your God, saying, Pray for us unto Jehovah our God, and according to all that Jehovah our God saith, so declare to us, and e have done [it];
and I declare to you to-day, and ye have not hearkened to the voice of Jehovah your God, and to anything ith hich He hath sent me unto you.
And no, kno ye certainly that by sord, by famine, and by pestilence ye die, in the place that ye have desired to go in to sojourn there.’
And it cometh to pass, hen Jeremiah doth finish to speak unto all the people all the ords of Jehovah their God, ith hich Jehovah their God hath sent him unto them — all these ords —

that Azariah son of Hoshaiah, and Johanan son of Kareah, and all the proud men, speak unto Jeremiah, saying, ’Falsehood thou art speaking; Jehovah our God hath not sent thee to say, Do not enter Egypt to sojourn there;
for Baruch son of Neriah is moving thee against us, in order to give us up into the hand of the Chaldeans, to put us to death, and to remove us to Babylon.’
And Johanan son of Kareah, and all the heads of the forces, and all the people, have not hearkened to the voice of Jehovah, to dell in the land of Judah;
and Johanan son of Kareah, and all the heads of the forces, take all the remnant of Judah ho have turned from all the nations hither they ere driven to sojourn in the land of Judah,

the men, and the omen, and the infant, and the daughters of the king, and every person that Nebuzar-Adan, chief of the executioners, had left ith Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, and Jeremiah the prophet, and Baruch son of Neriah,
and they enter the land of Egypt, for they have not hearkened to the voice of Jehovah, and they enter unto Tahpanhes.
And there is a ord of Jehovah unto Jeremiah in Tahpanhes, saying,
’Take in thy hand great stones, and thou hast hidden them, in the clay, in the brick-kiln, that [is] at the opening of the house of Pharaoh in Tahpanhes, before the eyes of the men of Judah,

and thou hast said unto them: Thus said Jehovah of Hosts, God of Israel: ’Lo, I am sending, and I have taken Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, My servant, and I have set his throne above these stones that I have hid, and he hath stretched out his pavilion over them,
and he hath come, and smitten the land of Egypt — those ho [are] for death to death, and those ho [are] for captivity to captivity, and those ho [are] for the sord to the sord.

And I have kindled a fire in the houses of the gods of Egypt, and it hath burned them, and he hath taken them captive, and covered himself ith the land of Egypt, as cover himself doth the shepherd ith his garment, and he hath gone forth thence in peace;
and he hath broken the standing pillars of the house of the sun, that [is] in the land of Egypt, and the houses of the gods of Egypt he doth burn ith fire.’
The ord that hath been unto Jeremiah concerning all the Jes ho are delling in the land of Egypt — ho are delling in Migdol, and in Tahpanhes, and in Noph, and in the land of Pathros — saying,

’Thus said Jehovah of Hosts, God of Israel: Ye — ye have seen all the evil that I have brought in on Jerusalem, and on all the cities of Judah, and lo, they [are] a aste this day, and there is none delling in them,
because of their ickedness that they have done, by provoking Me to anger, by going to make perfume, by serving other gods, that they kne not, they, ye, and your fathers.
’And I send unto you all my servants, the prophets, rising early and sending, saying: I pray you, do not this abomination that I have hated —
and they have not hearkened nor inclined their ear, to turn back from their ickedness, not to make perfume to other gods,
and poured out is My fury, and Mine anger, and it burneth in cities of Judah, and in streets of Jerusalem, and they are for a aste, for a desolation, as [at] this day.

’And, no, thus said Jehovah of Hosts, God of Israel: Why are ye doing great evil unto your on souls, to cut off to you man and oman, infant and suckling, from the midst of Judah, so as not to leave to you a remnant:

by provoking Me to anger by the orks of your hands, by making perfume to other gods in the land of Egypt, hither ye are going in to sojourn, so as to cut yourselves off, and so as to your being for a reviling and for a reproach among all nations of the earth?

’Have ye forgotten the ickedness of your fathers, and the ickedness of the kings of Judah, and the ickedness of their ives, and your on ickedness, and the ickedness of your ives, that they have done in the land of Judah, and in streets of Jerusalem?
They have not been humbled unto this day, nor have they been afraid, nor have they alked in My la, and in My statutes, that I have set before you and before your fathers.
’Therefore, thus said Jehovah of Hosts, God of Israel: Lo, I am setting my face against you for evil, even to cut off all Judah,

and I have taken the remnant of Judah, ho have set their faces to enter the land of Egypt to sojourn there, and they have all been consumed in the land of Egypt; they fall by sord, by famine they are consumed, from the least even unto the greatest, by sord and by famine they die, and they have been for an execration, for an astonishment, and for a reviling, and for a reproach.
’And I have seen after those delling in the land of Egypt, as I sa after Jerusalem, ith sord, ith famine, and ith pestilence,

and there is not an escaped and remaining one of the remnant of Judah, ho are entering into the land of Egypt to sojourn there, even to turn back to the land of Judah, hither they are lifting up their soul to return to dell, for they do not turn back, except those escaping.’

And they anser Jeremiah — all the men ho are knoing that their ives are making perfume to other gods, and all the omen ho are remaining, a great assembly, even all the people ho are delling in the land of Egypt, in Pathros — saying:
’The ord that thou hast spoken unto us in the name of Jehovah — e are not hearkening unto thee;

for e certainly do everything that hath gone out of our mouth, to make perfume to the queen of the heavens, and to pour out to her libations, as e have done, e, and our fathers, our kings, and our heads, in cities of Judah, and in streets of Jerusalem, and — e are satisfied ith bread, and e are ell, and evil e have not seen.
’And from the time e have ceased to make perfume to the queen of the heavens, and to pour out to her libations, e have lacked all, and by sord and by famine e have been consumed,
and hen e are making perfume to the queen of the heavens, and pouring out to her libations — ithout our husbands have e made for her cakes to idolize her, and to pour out to her libations?’
And Jeremiah saith unto all the people, concerning the men and concerning the omen, and concerning all the people ho are ansering him, saying:

’The perfume that ye made in the cities of Judah, and in the streets of Jerusalem, ye, and your fathers, your kings, and your heads, and the people of the land, hath not Jehovah remembered it? yea, it cometh up on His heart.

And Jehovah is not able any more to accept [you], because of the evil of your doings, because of the abominations that ye have done, and your land is for a aste, and for an astonishment, and for a reviling, ithout inhabitant, as [at] this day.

’Because that ye have made perfume, and because ye have sinned against Jehovah, and have not hearkened to the voice of Jehovah, and in His la, and in His statutes, and in His testimonies ye have not alked, therefore hath this evil met you as [at] this day.’
And Jeremiah saith unto all the people, and unto all the omen, ’Hear ye a ord of Jehovah, all Judah ho [are] in the land of Egypt,

Thus spake Jehovah of Hosts, God of Israel, saying: Ye and your ives both speak ith your mouth, and ith your hands have fulfilled, saying: We certainly execute our vos that e have voed, to make perfume to the queen of the heavens, and to pour out to her libations, ye do certainly establish your vos, and certainly execute your vos.

’Therefore, hear ye a ord of Jehovah, all Judah ho are delling in the land of Egypt: Lo, I — I have sorn by My great name, said Jehovah, My name is no more proclaimed by the mouth of any man of Judah, saying, Live doth the Lord Jehovah — in all the land of Egypt.
Lo, I am atching over them for evil, and not for good, and consumed have been all the men of Judah ho [are] in the land of Egypt, by sord and by famine, till their consumption.

’And the escaped of the sord turn back out of the land of Egypt to the land of Judah, fe in number, and knon have all the remnant of Judah ho are coming into the land of Egypt to sojourn there, hose ord is established, Mine or theirs.
’And this [is] to you the sign — an affirmation of Jehovah — that I am seeing after you in this place, so that ye kno that My ords are certainly established against you for evil;

Thus said Jehovah, Lo, I am giving Pharaoh-Hophra king of Egypt into the hand of his enemies, and into the hand of those seeking his life, as I have given Zedekiah king of Judah into the hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, his enemy, and ho is seeking his life.’

The ord that Jeremiah the prophet hath spoken unto Baruch son of Neriah, in his riting these ords on a book from the mouth of Jeremiah, in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah king of Judah, saying:
’Thus said Jehovah, God of Israel, concerning thee, O Baruch:
’Thou hast said, Woe to me, no, for Jehovah hath added sorro to my pain, I have been earied ith my sighing, and rest I have not found.
Thus dost thou say unto him: Thus said Jehovah: Lo, that hich I have built I am throing don, and that hich I have planted I am plucking up, even the hole land itself.

And thou — thou seekest for thee great things — do not seek, for lo, I am bringing in evil on all flesh — an affirmation of Jehovah — and I have given to thee thy life for a spoil, in all places hither thou goest.’
That hich hath been the ord of Jehovah unto Jeremiah the prophet concerning the nations,

For Egypt, concerning the force of Pharaoh-Necho king of Egypt, that hath been by the river Phrat, in Carchemish, that Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon hath smitten, in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah king of Judah:
’Set ye in array shield and buckler, And dra nigh to battle.
Gird the horses, and go up, ye horsemen, And station yourselves ith helmets, Polish the javelins, put on the coats of mail.

Wherefore have I seen them dismayed — They are turned backard, And their mighty ones are beaten don, And [to] a refuge they have fled, and not turned the face? Fear [is] round about — an affirmation of Jehovah.
The sift do not flee, nor do the mighty escape, Northard, by the side of the river Phrat, They have stumbled and fallen.
Who is this? as a flood he cometh up, As rivers do his aters shake themselves!
Egypt, as a flood cometh up, And as rivers the aters shake themselves. And he saith, I go up; I cover the land, I destroy the city and the inhabitants in it.
Go up, ye horses; and boast yourselves, ye chariots, And go forth, ye mighty, Cush and Phut handling the shield, And Lud handling — treading the bo.

And that day [is] to the Lord Jehovah of Hosts A day of vengeance, To be avenged of His adversaries, And the sord hath devoured, and been satisfied, And it hath been atered from their blood, For a sacrifice [is] to the Lord Jehovah of Hosts, In the land of the north, by the river Phrat.
Go up to Gilead, and take balm, O virgin daughter of Egypt, In vain thou hast multiplied medicines, Healing there is none for thee.
Nations have heard of thy shame, And thy cry hath filled the land, For the mighty on the mighty did stumble, Together they have fallen — both of them!’
The ord that Jehovah hath spoken unto Jeremiah the prophet concerning the coming in of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, to smite the land of Egypt:
’Declare ye in Egypt, and sound in Migdol, Yea, sound in Noph, and in Tahpanhes say: Station thyself, yea, prepare for thee, For a sord hath devoured around thee,
Wherefore hath thy bull been sept aay? He hath not stood, because Jehovah thrust him aay.
He hath multiplied the stumbling, Yea one hath fallen upon his neighbour, And they say: Rise, and e turn back to our people, And unto the land of our birth, Because of the oppressing sord.
They have cried there: Pharaoh king of Egypt [is] a desolation, Passed by hath the appointed time.
I live — an affirmation of the King, Jehovah of Hosts [is] His name, Surely as Tabor [is] among mountains, And as Carmel by the sea — he cometh in,
Goods for removal make for thee, O inhabitant, daughter of Egypt, For Noph becometh a desolation, And hath been burnt up, ithout inhabitant.
A heifer very fair [is] Egypt, Rending from the north doth come into her.

Even her hired ones in her midst [are] as calves of the stall, For even they have turned, They have fled together, they have not stood, For the day of their calamity hath come on them, The time of their inspection.
Its voice as a serpent goeth on, For ith a force they go, And ith axes they have come in to her, As heers of trees.
They have cut don her forest, An affirmation of Jehovah — for it is not searched, For they have been more than the grasshopper, And they have no numbering.
Ashamed hath been the daughter of Egypt, She hath been given into the hand of the people of the north.

Said hath Jehovah of Hosts, God of Israel: Lo, I am seeing after Amon of No, And after Pharaoh, and after Egypt, And after her gods, and after her kings, And after Pharaoh, and after those trusting in him,

And I have given them into the hand of those seeking their life, And into the hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, And into the hand of his servants, And afterards it is inhabited, As [in] days of old — an affirmation of Jehovah.

And thou, thou dost not fear, my servant Jacob, Nor [art] thou dismayed, O Israel, For lo, I am saving thee from afar, And thy seed from the land of their captivity, And Jacob hath turned back, And hath been at rest, and been at ease, And there is none disturbing.

Thou, thou dost not fear, My servant Jacob, An affirmation of Jehovah — for ith thee I [am], For I make an end of all the nations Whither I have driven thee, And of thee I do not make an end, And I have reproved thee in judgment, And do not entirely acquit thee!’
That hich hath been the ord of Jehovah unto Jeremiah concerning the Philistines, before Pharaoh smiteth Gaza:

’Thus said Jehovah: Lo, aters are coming up from the north, And have been for an overfloing stream, And they overflo the land and its fulness, The city, and the inhabitants in it, And men have cried out, And holed hath every inhabitant of the land.
From the sound of the stamping of the hoofs of his mighty ones, From the rushing of his chariot, the noise of his heels, Fathers have not turned unto sons, From feebleness of hands,
Because of the day that hath come to spoil all the Philistines, To cut off to Tyre and to Zidon every helping remnant. For Jehovah is spoiling the Philistines, The remnant of the isle of Caphtor.
Come hath baldness unto Gaza, Cut off hath been Ashkelon, O remnant of their valley, Till hen dost thou cut thyself?
Ho, sord of Jehovah, till hen art thou not quiet? Be removed unto thy sheath, rest and cease.
Ho shall it be quiet, And Jehovah hath given a charge to it, Against Ashkelon, and against the sea shore? There hath He appointed it!’

Concerning Moab: ’Thus said Jehovah of Hosts, God of Israel: Woe unto Nebo, for it is spoiled, Put to shame, captured hath been Kiriathaim, Put to shame hath been the high toer, Yea, it hath been broken don.
There is no more praise of Moab, In Heshbon they devised against it evil: Come, and e cut it off from [being] a nation, Also, O Madmen, thou art cut off, After thee goeth a sord.
A voice of a cry [is] from Horonaim, Spoiling and great destruction.
Destroyed hath been Moab, Caused a cry to be heard have her little ones.
For the ascent of Luhith ith eeping, Go up doth eeping, For in the descent of Horonaim Adversaries a cry of desolation have heard.
Flee ye, deliver yourselves, Ye are as a naked thing in a ilderness.
For, because of thy trusting in thy orks, And in thy treasures, even thou art captured, And gone out hath Chemosh in a removal, His priests and his heads together.
And come in doth a spoiler unto every city, And no city doth escape, And perished hath the valley, And destroyed been the plain, as Jehovah said.
Give ings to Moab, for she utterly goeth out, And her cities are for a desolation, Without an inhabitant in them.
Cursed [is] he ho is doing the ork of Jehovah slothfully, And cursed [is] he Who is ithholding his sord from blood.

Secure is Moab from his youth, And at rest [is] he for his preserved things, And he hath not been emptied out from vessel unto vessel, And into captivity he hath not gone, Therefore hath his taste remained in him, And his fragrance hath not been changed.
Therefore, lo, days are coming, An affirmation of Jehovah, And I have sent to him anderers, And they have caused him to ander, And his vessels they empty out, And his bottles they dash in pieces.
And ashamed hath been Moab because of Chemosh, As the house of Israel have been ashamed Because of Beth-El their confidence.
Ho do ye say, We [are] mighty, And men of strength for battle?
Spoiled is Moab, and her cities hath one gone up, And the choice of its young men Have gone don to slaughter, An affirmation of the King, Jehovah of Hosts [is] His name.
Near is the calamity of Moab to come, And his affliction hath hasted exceedingly.
Bemoan for him, all ye round about him, And all knoing his name, say ye: Ho hath it been broken, the staff of strength, The rod of beauty.
Come don from honour, sit in thirst, O inhabitant, daughter of Dibon, For a spoiler of Moab hath come up to thee, He hath destroyed thy fenced places.
On the ay stand, and atch, O inhabitant of Aroer, Ask the fugitive and escaped, Say, What hath happened?
Put to shame hath been Moab, For it hath been broken don, Hol and cry, declare ye in Arnon, For spoiled is Moab,
And judgment hath come in unto the land of the plain — unto Holon, And unto Jahazah, and on Mephaath,
And on Dibon, and on Nebo, And on Beth-Diblathaim, and on Kirathaim,
And on Beth-Gamul, and on Beth-Meon,
And on Kerioth, and on Bozrah, And on all cities of the land of Moab, The far off and the near.
Cut don hath been the horn of Moab, And his arm hath been broken, An affirmation of Jehovah.
Declare ye him drunk, For against Jehovah he made himself great And Moab hath stricken in his vomit, And he hath been for a derision — even he.
And as not Israel the derision to thee? Among thieves as he found? For since thy ords concerning him, Thou dost bemoan thyself.
Forsake cities, and dell in a rock, Ye inhabitants of Moab, And be as a dove making a nest in the passages of a pit’s mouth.
We have heard of the arrogance of Moab, Exceeding proud! His haughtiness, and his arrogance, And his pride, and the height of his heart,
I — I have knon, an affirmation of Jehovah, His rath, and [it is] not right, His devices — not right they have done.
Therefore for Moab I hol, even for Moab — all of it, I cry for men of Kir-Heres, it doth mourn,
With the eeping of Jazer, I eep for thee, O vine of Sibmah, Thy branches have passed over a sea, Unto the sea of Jazer they have come, On thy summer fruits, and on thy harvest, A spoiler hath fallen.
And removed hath been joy and gladness From the fruitful field, Even from the land of Moab, And ine from ine-presses I have caused to cease, Shouting doth not proceed, The shouting [is] no shouting!
Because of the cry of Heshbon unto Elealeh, Unto Jahaz they have given their voice, From Zoar unto Horonaim, A heifer of the third [year], For even aters of Nimrim become desolations.
And I have caused to cease to Moab, An affirmation of Jehovah, Him ho is offering in a high place, And him ho is making perfume to his god.
Therefore my heart for Moab as pipes doth sound, And my heart for men of Kir-Heres As pipes doth sound, Therefore the abundance he made did perish.
For every head [is] bald, and every beard diminished, On all hands cuttings, and on the loins — sackcloth.
On all roofs of Moab, and in her broad-places, All of it — [is] lamentation, For I have broken Moab as a vessel in hich there is no pleasure, An affirmation of Jehovah.
Ho hath it been broken don! they have holed, Ho hath Moab turned the neck ashamed, And Moab hath been for a derision. And for a terror to all round about her.
For thus said Jehovah: Lo, as an eagle he doth flee, And hath spread his ings unto Moab.
Captured have been the cities, And the strongholds are caught, And the heart of the mighty of Moab Hath been in that day as the heart of a distressed oman.
And Moab hath been destroyed from [being] a people, For against Jehovah he exerted himself.
Fear, and a snare, and a gin, [are] for thee, O inhabitant of Moab — an affirmation of Jehovah,

Whoso is fleeing because of the fear falleth into the snare, And hoso is coming up from the snare is captured by the gin, For I bring in unto her — unto Moab — The year of their inspection, An affirmation of Jehovah.
In the shado of Heshbon stood poerless have fugitives, For fire hath gone forth from Heshbon, And a flame from ithin Sihon, And it consumeth the corner of Moab, And the cron of the sons of Shaon.
Woe to thee, O Moab, Perished hath the people of Chemosh, For thy sons ere taken ith the captives, And thy daughters ith the captivity.
And I have turned back [to] the captivity of Moab, In the latter end of the days, An affirmation of Jehovah! Hitherto [is] the judgment of Moab.
Concerning the sons of Ammon: ’Thus said Jehovah: Sons — hath Israel none? heir — hath he none? Wherefore hath Malcam possessed Gad? And his people in its cities have delt?

Therefore, lo, days are coming, An affirmation of Jehovah, And I have sounded unto Rabbah of the sons of Ammon a shout of battle, And it hath been for a heap — a desolation, And her daughters ith fire are burnt, And Israel hath succeeded its heirs, Said hath Jehovah.
Hol, Heshbon, for spoiled is Ai, Cry, daughters of Rabbah, gird on sackcloth, Lament, and go to and fro by the hedges, For Malcam into captivity doth go, His priests and his princes together.
What — dost thou boast thyself in valleys? Floed hath thy valley, O backsliding daughter, Who is trusting in her treasures: Who doth come in unto me?
Lo, I am bringing in upon thee a fear, An affirmation of the Lord Jehovah of Hosts, From all round about thee, And ye have been driven out each before it, And there is no gatherer of the andering.
And after this I turn back the captivity of the sons of Ammon, An affirmation of Jehovah.’
Concerning Edom: ’Thus said Jehovah of Hosts: Is isdom no more in Teman? Perished hath counsel from the intelligent? Vanished hath their isdom?
Flee, turn, go deep to dell, ye inhabitants of Dedan, For the calamity of Esau I brought in upon him, The time I inspected him.
If gatherers have come in to thee, They do not leave gleanings, If thieves in the night, They have destroyed their sufficiency!
For I — I have made Esau bare, I have uncovered his secret places, And to be hidden he is not able, Spoiled [is] his seed, and his brethren, And his neighbours, and he is not.
Leave thine orphans — I do keep alive, And thy idos — on Me trust ye,
For thus said Jehovah: They hose judgment is not to drink of the cup, Do certainly drink, And thou [art] he that is entirely acquitted! Thou art not acquitted, for thou certainly drinkest.
For, by Myself, I have sorn, An affirmation of Jehovah, That for a desolation, for a reproach, For a aste, and for a reviling — is Bozrah, And all her cities are for astes age-during.
A report I have heard from Jehovah, And an ambassador among nations is sent, Gather yourselves and come in against her, And rise ye for battle.
For, lo, little I have made thee among nations, Despised among men.

Thy terribleness hath lifted thee up, The pride of thy heart, O deller in clefts of the rock, Holding the high place of the height, For thou makest high as an eagle thy nest, From thence I bring thee don, An affirmation of Jehovah.
And Edom hath been for a desolation, Every passer by her is astonished, And doth hiss because of all her plagues.
As the overthro of Sodom and Gomorrah, And its neighbours, said Jehovah, No one doth dell there, Nor sojourn in her doth a son of man.

Lo, as a lion he cometh up, Because of the rising of the Jordan, Unto the enduring habitation, But I cause to rest, I cause him to run from off her, And ho is chosen? concerning her I lay a charge, For ho is like Me? and ho conveneth Me? And ho [is] this shepherd ho standeth before Me?

Therefore, hear ye the counsel of Jehovah, That He hath counselled concerning Edom, And His devices that He hath devised Concerning the inhabitants of Teman: Drag them out do not little ones of the flock, Make desolate over them doth he not their habitation?
From the noise of their fall hath the earth shaken, The cry — at the sea of Suph is its voice heard.
Lo, as an eagle he cometh up, and flieth, And he spreadeth his ings over Bozrah, And the heart of the mighty of Edom hath been in that day, As the heart of a distressed oman!’
Concerning Damascus: Ashamed hath been Hamath and Arpad, For an evil report they have heard, They have been melted, in the sea [is] sorro, To be quiet it is not able.
Feeble hath been Damascus, She turned to flee, and fear strengthened her, Distress and pangs have seized her, as a travailing oman.
Ho is it not left — the city of praise, The city of my joy!
Therefore fall do her young men in her broad places, And all the men of ar are cut off in that day, An affirmation of Jehovah of Hosts.
And I have kindled a fire against the all of Damascus, And it consumed palaces of Ben-Hadad!’
Concerning Kedar, and concerning the kingdoms of Hazor, that Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon hath smitten: ’Thus said Jehovah: Arise ye, go ye up unto Kedar, And spoil the sons of the east.
Their tents and their flock they do take, Their curtains, and all their vessels, And their camels, they bear aay for themselves, And they called concerning them, Fear [is] round about.
Flee, bemoan mightily, go deep to dell, Ye inhabitants of Hazor — an affirmation of Jehovah, For given counsel against you hath Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, Yea, he deviseth against them a device.
Rise ye, go up unto a nation at rest, Delling confidently, an affirmation of Jehovah, It hath no to-leaved doors nor bar, Alone they do dell.

And their camels have been for a prey, And the multitude of their cattle for a spoil, And I have scattered them to every ind, Who cut off the corner [of the beard], And from all its passages I bring in their calamity, An affirmation of Jehovah.
And Hazor hath been for a habitation of dragons, A desolation — unto the age, No one doth dell there, nor sojourn in it doth a son of man!’
That hich hath been the ord of Jehovah unto Jeremiah the prophet concerning Elam, in the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah, saying:
’Thus said Jehovah of Hosts: Lo, I am breaking the bo of Elam, The beginning of their might.
And I have brought in to Elam four inds, From the four ends of the heavens, And have scattered them to all these inds, And there is no nation hither outcasts of Elam come not in.

And I have affrighted Elam before their enemies, And before those seeking their life, And I have brought in against them evil, The heat of Mine anger, An affirmation of Jehovah, And I have sent after them the sord, Till I have consumed them;
And I have set My throne in Elam, And I have destroyed thence King and princes — an affirmation of Jehovah.
And it hath come to pass, in the latter end of the days, I turn back [to] the captivity of Elam, An affirmation of Jehovah!’
The ord that Jehovah hath spoken concerning Babylon, concerning the land of the Chaldeans, by the hand of Jeremiah the prophet:

’Declare ye among nations, and sound, And lift up an ensign, sound, do not hide, Say ye: Captured hath been Babylon, Put to shame hath been Bel, Broken hath been Merodach, Put to shame have been her grievous things, Broken have been her idols.
For come up against her hath a nation from the north, It maketh her land become a desolation, And there is not an inhabitant in it. From man even unto beast, They have moved, they have gone.
In those days, and at that time, An affirmation of Jehovah, Come in do sons of Israel, They and sons of Judah together, Going on and eeping they go, And Jehovah their God they seek.
[To] Zion they ask the ay, Thitherard [are] their faces: Come in, and e are joined unto Jehovah, A covenant age-during — not forgotten.

A perishing flock hath My people been, Their shepherds have caused them to err, [To] the mountains causing them to go back, From mountain unto hill they have gone, They have forgotten their crouching-place.

All finding them have devoured them, And their adversaries have said: We are not guilty, Because that they sinned against Jehovah, The habitation of righteousness, And the hope of their fathers — Jehovah.
Move ye from the midst of Babylon, And from the land of the Chaldeans go out. And be as he-goats before a flock.

For, lo, I am stirring up, And am causing to come up against Babylon, An assembly of great nations from a land of the north, And they have set in array against her, From thence she is captured, Its arro — as a skilful hero — returneth not empty,
And Chaldea hath been for a spoil, All her spoilers are satisfied, An affirmation of Jehovah.
Because thou rejoicest, because thou exultest, O spoilers of Mine inheritance, Because thou increasest as a heifer [at] the tender grass, And dost cry aloud as bulls,
Ashamed hath been your mother greatly, Confounded hath she been that bare you, Lo, the hindermost of nations [is] a ilderness, A dry land, and a desert.
Because of the rath of Jehovah it is not inhabited, And it hath been a desolation — all of it. Every passer by at Babylon is astonished, And doth hiss because of all her plagues.
Set yourselves in array against Babylon round about, All ye treading a bo, Shoot at her, have no pity on the arro, For against Jehovah she hath sinned.

Shout against her round about, She hath given forth her hand, Fallen have her foundations, Thron don have been her alls, For it [is] the vengeance of Jehovah, Be avenged of her, as she did — do ye to her.
Cut off the soer from Babylon, And him handling the sickle in the time of harvest, Because of the oppressing sord, Each unto his people — they turn, And each to his land — they flee.
A scattered sheep is Israel, lions have driven aay, At first, devour him did the king of Asshur, And no, at last, broken his bone Hath Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon.
Therefore thus said Jehovah of Hosts, God of Israel: Lo, I am seeing after the king of Babylon, And after his land, As I have seen after the king of Asshur;
And I have brought back Israel unto his habitation, And he hath fed on Carmel, and on Bashan. And in mount Ephraim, and on Gilead is his soul satisfied.
In those days, and at that time, An affirmation of Jehovah, Sought is the iniquity of Israel, and it is not, And the sin of Judah, and it is not found, For I am propitious to those hom I leave!
Against the land of Merathaim: Go up against it, and unto the inhabitants of Pekod, Waste and devote their posterity, An affirmation of Jehovah, And do according to all that I have commanded thee.
A noise of battle [is] in the land, and of great destruction.
Ho hath it been cut and broken, The hammer of the hole earth! Ho hath Babylon been for a desolation among nations!
I have laid a snare for thee, And also — thou art captured, O Babylon, And thou — thou hast knon, Thou hast been found, and also art caught, For against Jehovah thou hast stirred thyself up.
Jehovah hath opened His treasury, And He bringeth out the eapons of His indignation, For a ork [is] to the Lord Jehovah of Hosts, In the land of the Chaldeans.
Come ye in to her from the extremity, Open ye her storehouses, Raise her up as heaps, and devote her, Let her have no remnant.
Slay all her kine, they go don to slaughter, Woe [is] on them, for come hath their day, The time of their inspection.
A voice of fugitives and escaped ones [Is] from the land of Babylon, To declare in Zion the vengeance of Jehovah our God, The vengeance of His temple.

Summon unto Babylon archers, all treading the bo, Encamp against her round about, Let [her] have no escape; Recompense to her according to her ork, According to all that she did — do to her, For unto Jehovah she hath been proud, Unto the Holy One of Israel.
Therefore fall do her young men in her broad places, And all her men of ar are cut off in that day, An affirmation of Jehovah.
Lo, I [am] against thee, O pride, An affirmation of the Lord Jehovah of Hosts, For thy day hath come, the time of thy inspection.
And stumbled hath pride, And he hath fallen, and hath no raiser up, And I have kindled a fire in his cities, And it hath devoured all round about him.
Thus said Jehovah of Hosts: Oppressed are the sons of Israel, And the sons of Judah together, And all their captors have kept hold on them, They have refused to send them aay.
Their Redeemer [is] strong, Jehovah of Hosts [is] His name, He doth thoroughly plead their cause, So as to cause the land to rest, And He hath given trouble to the inhabitants of Babylon.
A sord [is] for the Chaldeans, An affirmation of Jehovah, And it [is] on the inhabitants of Babylon, And on her heads, and on her ise men;
A sord [is] on the princes, And they have become foolish; A sord [is] on her mighty ones, And they have been broken don;
A sord [is] on his horses and on his chariot, And on all the rabble ho [are] in her midst, And they have become omen; A sord [is] on her treasuries, And they have been spoiled;
A sord [is] on her aters, and they have been dried up, For it [is] a land of graven images, And in idols they do boast themselves.
Therefore dell do Ziim ith Iim, Yea, delt in her have daughters of the ostrich, And it is not inhabited any more for ever, Nor delt in unto all generations.
As overthron by God ith Sodom, And ith Gomorrah, and ith its neighbours, An affirmation of Jehovah, none doth dell there, Nor sojourn in her doth a son of man.
Lo, a people hath come from the north, Even a great nation, And many kings are stirred up from the sides of the earth.
Bo and halbert they seize, Cruel [are] they, and they have no mercy, Their voice as a sea soundeth, and on horses they ride, Set in array as a man for battle, Against thee, O daughter of Babylon.
Heard hath the king of Babylon their report, And feeble have been his hands, Distress hath seized him; pain as a travailing oman.

Lo, as a lion he cometh up, Because of the rising of the Jordan, Unto the enduring habitation, But I cause to rest, I cause them to run from off her. And ho is chosen? on her I lay a charge, For ho [is] like Me? And ho doth convene Me? And ho [is] this shepherd ho standeth before Me?

Therefore, hear ye the counsel of Jehovah, That He counselled concerning Babylon, And His devices that He hath devised Concerning the land of the Chaldeans; Drag them out do not little ones of the flock, Doth He not make desolate over them the habitation?
From the voice: Captured as Babylon, Hath the earth been shaken, And a cry among nations hath been heard!
Thus said Jehovah: Lo, I am stirring up against Babylon, And the inhabitants of Leb — My ithstanders, A destroying ind,
And I have sent to Babylon fanners, And they have fanned it, and they empty its land, For they have been against it, Round about — in the day of evil.
Let not the treader tread his bo, Nor lift himself up in his coat of mail, Nor have ye pity on her young men, Devote ye to destruction all her host.
And fallen have the ounded in the land of the Chaldeans, And the pierced-through in her streets.
For, not forsaken is Israel and Judah, By its God — by Jehovah of Hosts, For their land hath been full of guilt, Against the Holy One of Israel.
Flee ye from the midst of Babylon, And deliver ye each his soul, Be not cut off in its iniquity, For a time of vengeance it [is] to Jehovah, Recompence He is rendering to her.
A golden cup [is] Babylon in the hand of Jehovah, Making drunk all the earth, Of its ine drunk have nations, Therefore boast themselves do nations.
Suddenly hath Babylon fallen, Yea, it is broken, hol ye for it, Take balm for her pain, if so be it may be healed.
We healed Babylon, and she as not healed, Forsake her, and e go, each to his land, For come unto the heavens hath its judgment, And it hath been lifted up unto the clouds.
Jehovah hath brought forth our righteousnesses, Come, and e recount in Zion the ork of Jehovah our God.

Cleanse ye the arros, fill the shields, Stirred up hath Jehovah the spirit of the kings of Madia, For against Babylon His device [is] to destroy it, For the vengeance of Jehovah it [is], The vengeance of His temple.

Unto the alls of Babylon lift up an ensign, Strengthen the atch, Establish the atchers, prepare the ambush, For Jehovah hath both devised and done that hich He spake, Concerning the inhabitants of Babylon.
O deller on many aters, abundant in treasures, Come in hath thine end, the measure of thy dishonest gain.
Sorn hath Jehovah of Hosts by Himself, That, Surely I have filled thee [ith] men as the cankerorm, And they have cried against thee — shouting.
The maker of earth by His poer, The establisher of the orld by His isdom, Who by His understanding stretched out the heavens,

At the voice He giveth forth, A multitude of aters [are] in the heavens, And He causeth vapours to come up from the end of the earth, Lightnings for rain He hath made, And He bringeth out ind from His treasures.
Brutish hath been every man by knoledge, Put to shame hath been every refiner by a graven image, For false [is] his molten image, And there is no breath in them.
Vanity [are] they — ork of errors, In the time of their inspection they perish.
Not like these [is] the portion of Jacob, For He [is] former of all things, And [Israel is] the rod of His inheritance, Jehovah of Hosts [is] His name.
An axe [art] thou to me — eapons of ar, And I have broken in pieces by thee nations, And I have destroyed by thee kingdoms,
And I have broken in pieces by thee horse and its rider, And I have broken in pieces by thee chariot and its charioteer,
And I have broken in pieces by thee man and oman, And I have broken in pieces by thee old and young, And I have broken in pieces by thee young man and virgin,
And I have broken in pieces by thee shepherd and his drove, And I have broken in pieces by thee husbandman and his team, And I have broken in pieces by thee governors and prefects.
And I have recompensed to Babylon, And to all inhabitants of Chaldea, All the evil that they have done in Zion, Before your eyes — an affirmation of Jehovah.

Lo, I [am] against thee, O destroying mount, An affirmation of Jehovah, That is destroying all the earth, And I have stretched out My hand against thee, And I have rolled thee from the rocks, And given thee for a burnt mountain.
And they take not out of thee a stone for a corner, And a stone for foundations, For desolations age-during art thou, An affirmation of Jehovah.

Lift ye up an ensign in the land, Blo a trumpet among nations, Sanctify against it nations, Summon against it the kingdoms of Ararat, Minni, and Ashkenaz, Appoint against it an infant head, Cause the horse to ascend as the rough cankerorm.
Sanctify against it the nations ith the kings of Media, Its governors and all its prefects, And all the land of its dominion.
And shake doth the land, and it is pained, For stood against Babylon have the purposes of Jehovah, To make the land of Babylon a desolation ithout inhabitant.
Ceased have the mighty of Babylon to fight, They have remained in strongholds, Failed hath their might, they have become oman, They have burnt her tabernacles, Broken have been her bars.
Runner to meet runner doth run, And announcer to meet announcer, To announce to the king of Babylon, For, captured hath been his city — at the extremity.
And the passages have been captured, And the reeds they have burnt ith fire, And the men of ar have been troubled.
For thus said Jehovah of Hosts, God of Israel, The daughter of Babylon [is] as a threshing-floor, The time of her threshing — yet a little, And come hath the time of her harvest.
Devoured us, crushed us, hath Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, He hath set us [as] an empty vessel, He hath salloed us as a dragon, He hath filled his belly ith my dainties, He hath driven us aay.
My rong, and [that of] my flesh [is] on Babylon, Say doth the inhabitant of Zion, And my blood [is] on the inhabitants of Chaldea, Say doth Jerusalem.
Therefore, thus said Jehovah: Lo, I am pleading thy cause, And I have avenged thy vengeance, And dried up its sea, and made its fountains dry.
And Babylon hath been for heaps, A habitation of dragons, An astonishment, and a hissing, ithout inhabitant.
Together as young lions they roar, They have shaken themselves as lions’ helps.
In their heat I make their banquets, And I have caused them to drink, so that they exult, And have slept a sleep age-during, And aake not — an affirmation of Jehovah.
I cause them to go don as lambs to slaughter, As rams ith he-goats.
Ho hath Sheshach been captured, Yea, caught is the praise of the hole earth, Ho hath Babylon been for an astonishment among nations.
Come up against Babylon hath the sea, With a multitude of its billos it hath been covered.
Its cities have been for a desolation, A dry land, and a ilderness, A land — none doth dell in them, Nor pass over into them doth a son of man.
And I have seen after Bel in Babylon, And I have brought forth that hich he salloed — from his mouth, And flo no more unto him do nations, Also the all of Babylon hath fallen.
Go forth from its midst, O My people, And deliver ye, each his soul, Because of the fierceness of the anger of Jehovah,

And lest your heart be tender, And ye be afraid of the report that is heard in the land, And come in a year hath the report, And after it in a year the report, And violence [is] in the land, ruler against ruler;
Therefore, lo, days are coming, And I have seen after the graven images of Babylon. And all its land is ashamed, And all its pierced ones do fall in its midst.
And cried aloud against Babylon Have heavens and earth, and all that [is] in them, For, from the north come to it do the spoilers, An affirmation of Jehovah.
Even Babylon [is] to fall, ye pierced of Israel, Even they of Babylon have fallen, Ye pierced of all the earth.
Ye escaped of the sord, go on, stand not, Remember ye from afar Jehovah, And let Jerusalem come up on your heart.
We have been ashamed, for e heard reproach, Covered hath shame our faces, For come in have strangers, against the sanctuaries of the house of Jehovah.
Therefore, lo, days are coming, An affirmation of Jehovah, And I have seen after its graven images, And in all its land groan doth the ounded.
Because Babylon goeth up to the heavens, And because it fenceth the high place of its strength, From Me come into it do spoilers, An affirmation of Jehovah.
A voice of a cry [is] from Babylon, And of great destruction from the land of the Chaldean.
For Jehovah is spoiling Babylon, And hath destroyed out of it a great voice, And sounded have its billos as many aters, Given forth a noise hath their voice.
For come in against it — against Babylon — hath a spoiler, And captured have been its mighty ones, Broken have been their bos, For the God of recompences — Jehovah — doth certainly repay.

And I have caused its princes to drink, And its ise men, its governors, And its prefects, and its mighty ones, And they have slept a sleep age-during, And they aake not — an affirmation of the king, Jehovah of Hosts [is] His name.
Thus said Jehovah of Hosts, the all of Babylon — The broad one — is utterly made bare, And her high gates ith fire are burnt, And peoples labour in vain, And nations in fire, and have been eary!

The ord that Jeremiah the prophet hath commanded Seraiah son of Neriah, son of Maaseiah, in his going ith Zedekiah king of Judah to Babylon, in the fourth year of his reign — and Seraiah [is] a quiet prince;
and Jeremiah riteth all the evil that cometh unto Babylon on one book — all these ords that are ritten concerning Babylon.
And Jeremiah saith unto Seraiah, ’When thou dost enter Babylon, then thou hast seen, and hast read all these ords,
and hast said: Jehovah, Thou, Thou hast spoken concerning this place, to cut it off, that there is none delling in it, from man even unto cattle, for it is a desolation age-during.
And it hath come to pass, hen thou dost finish reading this book, thou dost bind to it a stone, and hast cast it into the midst of Phrat,
and said, Thus sink doth Babylon, and it doth not arise, because of the evil that I am bringing in against it, and they have been eary.’ Hitherto [are] ords of Jeremiah.
A son of tenty and one years [is] Zedekiah in his reigning, and eleven years he hath reigned in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother [is] Hamutal daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah.
and he doth the evil thing in the eyes of Jehovah, according to all that Jehoiakim hath done,
for, because of the anger of Jehovah, it hath been in Jerusalem and Judah till He hath cast them from before His face, and Zedekiah doth rebel against the king of Babylon.

And it cometh to pass, in the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, in the tenth of the month, come hath Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon — he and all his force — against Jerusalem, and they encamp against it, and build against it a fortification round about;
and the city cometh into siege till the eleventh year of king Zedekiah.
In the fourth month, in the ninth of the month, hen the famine is severe in the city, and there hath been no bread for the people of the land,

then is the city broken up, and all the men of ar flee, and go forth from the city by night, the ay of the gate beteen the to alls, that [is] by the king’s garden — and the Chaldeans [are] by the city round about — and they go the ay of the plain.
And the forces of the Chaldeans pursue after the king, and overtake Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho, and all his forces have been scattered from him,
and they capture the king, and bring him up unto the king of Babylon to Riblah, in the land of Hamath, and he speaketh ith him — judgments.
And the king of Babylon slaughtereth the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes, and also all the princes of Judah hath he slaughtered in Riblah;
and the eyes of Zedekiah he hath blinded, and he bindeth him in brazen fetters, and the king of Babylon bringeth him to Babylon, and putteth him in the house of inspection unto the day of his death.

And in the fifth month, in the tenth of the month — it [is] the nineteenth year of king Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon — come hath Nebuzar-Adan, chief of the executioners; he hath stood before the king of Babylon in Jerusalem,
and he burneth the house of Jehovah, and the house of the king, and all the houses of Jerusalem, even every great house he hath burned ith fire,
and all the alls of Jerusalem round about broken don have all the forces of the Chaldeans that [are] ith the chief of the executioners.

And of the poor of the people, and the remnant of the people ho are left in the city, and those ho are falling aay, ho have fallen unto the king of Babylon, and the remnant of the multitude, hath Nebuzar-Adan chief of the executioners, removed;
and of the poor of the land hath Nebuzar-Adan, chief of the executioners, left for vine-dressers and for husbandmen.

And the pillars of brass that [are] to the house of Jehovah, and the bases, and the brasen sea that [is] in the house of Jehovah, have the Chaldeans broken, and they bear aay all the brass of them to Babylon;
and the pots, and the shovels, and the snuffers, and the bols, and the spoons, and all the vessels of brass ith hich they minister, they have taken aay;

and the basins, and the fire-pans, and the bols, and the pots, and the candlesticks, and the spoons, and the cups, the gold of that hich [is] gold, and the silver of that hich [is] silver, hath the chief of the executioners taken.
The to pillars, the one sea, and the telve brazen oxen that [are] beneath the bases, that king Solomon made for the house of Jehovah, there as no eighing of the brass of all these vessels.
As to the pillars, eighteen cubits [is] the height of the one pillar, and a cord of telve cubits doth compass it, and its thickness [is] four fingers hollo.

And the chapiter upon it [is] of brass, and the height of the one chapiter [is] five cubits, and net-ork and pomegranates [are] on the chapiter round about, the hole [is] of brass; and like these have the second pillar, and pomegranates.
And the pomegranates are ninety and six on a side, all the pomegranates [are] a hundred on the net-ork round about.
And the chief of the executioners taketh Seraiah the head priest, and Zephaniah the second priest, and the three keepers of the threshold,

and out of the city he hath taken a certain eunuch, ho hath been inspector over the men of ar, and seven men of those seeing the king’s face, ho have been found in the city, and the head scribe of the host, ho mustereth the people of the land, and sixty men of the people of the land, ho are found in the midst of the city;
and Nebuzar-Adan, chief of the executioners, taketh them, and bringeth them unto the king of Babylon to Riblah,
and the king of Babylon smiteth them, and putteth them to death in Riblah, in the land of Hamath, and he removeth Judah from off its on ground.
This [is] the people hom Nebuchadrezzar hath removed: in the seventh year, of Jes, three thousand and tenty and three;
in the eighteenth year of Nebuchadrezzar — from Jerusalem, souls, eight hundred thirty and to;
in the three and tentieth year of Nebuchadrezzar, hath Nebuzar-Adan chief of the guard removed of Jeish souls, seven hundred forty and five; all the souls [are] four thousand and six hundred.

And it cometh to pass, in the thirty and seventh year of the removal of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the telfth month, in the tenty and fifth of the month, hath Evil-Merodach king of Babylon lifted up, in the year of his reign, the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah, and bringeth him out from the house of restraint,
and speaketh ith him good things, and setteth his throne above the throne of the kings ho [are] ith him in Babylon,
and he hath changed his prison garments, and he hath eaten bread before him continually, all the days of his life.
And his alloance — a continual alloance — hath been given to him by the king of Babylon, the matter of a day in its day, till the day of his death — all days of his life.
Ho hath she sat alone, The city abounding ith people! She hath been as a ido, The mighty among nations! Princes among provinces, She hath become tributary!
She eepeth sore in the night, And her tear [is] on her cheeks, There is no comforter for her out of all her lovers, All her friends dealt treacherously by her, They have been to her for enemies.
Removed hath Judah because of affliction, And because of the abundance of her service; She hath delt among nations, She hath not found rest, All her pursuers have overtaken her beteen the straits.
The ays of Zion are mourning, Without any coming at the appointed time, All her gates are desolate, her priests sigh, Her virgins are afflicted — and she hath bitterness.
Her adversaries have become chief, Her enemies have been at ease, For Jehovah hath afflicted her, For the abundance of her transgressions, Her infants have gone captive before the adversary.
And go out from the daughter of Zion doth all her honour, Her princes have been as harts — They have not found pasture, And they go poerless before a pursuer.

Remembered hath Jerusalem [In] the days of her affliction and her mournings, all her desirable things that ere from the days of old, In the falling of her people into the hand of an adversary, And she hath no helper; Seen her have adversaries, They have laughed at her cessation.
A sin hath Jerusalem sinned, Therefore impure she hath become, All ho honoured her have esteemed her lightly, For they have seen her nakedness, Yea, she herself hath sighed and turneth backard.

Her uncleanness [is] in her skirts, She hath not remembered her latter end, And she cometh don onderfully, There is no comforter for her. See, O Jehovah, mine affliction, For exerted himself hath an enemy.

His hand spread out hath an adversary On all her desirable things, For she hath seen — Nations have entered her sanctuary, Concerning hich Thou didst command, ’They do not come into the assembly to thee.’
All her people are sighing — seeking bread, They have given their desirable things For food to refresh the body; See, O Jehovah, and behold attentively, For I have been lightly esteemed.

[Is it] nothing to you, all ye passing by the ay? Look attentively, and see, If there is any pain like my pain, That He is rolling to me? Whom Jehovah hath afflicted In the day of the fierceness of His anger.
From above He hath sent fire into my bone, And it subdueth it, He hath spread a net for my feet, He hath turned me backard, He hath made me desolate — all the day sick.

Bound hath been the yoke of my transgressions by His hand, They are rapped together, They have gone up on my neck, He hath caused my poer to stumble, The Lord hath given me into hands, I am not able to rise.
Trodden don all my mighty ones hath the Lord in my midst, He proclaimed against me an appointed time, To destroy my young men, A ine-press hath the Lord trodden, To the virgin daughter of Judah.
For these I am eeping, My eye, my eye, is running don ith aters, For, far from me hath been a comforter, Refreshing my soul, My sons have been desolate, For mighty hath been an enemy.
Spread forth hath Zion her hands, There is no comforter for her, Jehovah hath charged concerning Jacob, His neighbours [are] his adversaries, Jerusalem hath become impure among them.
Righteous is Jehovah, For His mouth I have provoked. Hear, I pray you, all ye peoples, and see my pain, My virgins and my young men have gone into captivity.
I called for my lovers, they — they have deceived me, My priests and my elders in the city have expired; When they have sought food for themselves, Then they give back their soul.

See, O Jehovah, for distress [is] to me, My boels have been troubled, Turned hath been my heart in my midst, For I have greatly provoked, From ithout bereaved hath the sord, In the house [it is] as death.

They have heard that I have sighed, There is no comforter for me, All my enemies have heard of my calamity, They have rejoiced that Thou hast done [it], Thou hast brought in the day Thou hast called, And they are like to me.
Come in doth all their evil before Thee, And one is doing to them as Thou hast done to me, For all my transgressions, For many [are] my sighs, and my heart [is] sick!
Ho doth the Lord cloud in His anger the daughter of Zion, He hath cast from heaven [to] earth the beauty of Israel, And hath not remembered His footstool in the day of His anger.

Salloed up hath the Lord, He hath not pitied any of the pleasant places of Jacob, He hath broken don in His rath The fortresses of the daughter of Judah, He hath caused to come to the earth, He polluted the kingdom and its princes.

He hath cut off in the heat of anger every horn of Israel, He hath turned backard His right hand From the face of the enemy, And He burneth against Jacob as a flaming fire, It hath devoured round about.

He hath trodden His bo as an enemy, Stood hath His right hand as an adversary, And He slayeth all the desirable ones of the eye, In the tent of the daughter of Zion, He hath poured out as fire His fury.
The Lord hath been as an enemy, He hath salloed up Israel, He hath salloed up all her palaces, He hath destroyed His fortresses, And He multiplieth in the daughter of Judah Mourning and moaning.

And He shaketh as a garden His tabernacle, He hath destroyed His appointed place, Jehovah hath forgotten in Zion the appointed time and sabbath, And despiseth, in the indignation of His anger, king and priest.

The Lord hath cast off His altar, He hath rejected His sanctuary, He hath shut up into the hand of the enemy The alls of her palaces, A noise they have made in the house of Jehovah Like a day of appointment.

Devised hath Jehovah to destroy the all of the daughter of Zion, He hath stretched out a line, He hath not turned His hand from destroying, And He causeth bulark and all to mourn, Together — they have been eak.
Sunk into the earth have her gates, He hath destroyed and broken her bars, Her king and her princes [are] among the nations, There is no la, also her prophets Have not found vision from Jehovah.

Sit on the earth — keep silent do the elders of the daughter of Zion, They have caused dust to go up on their head, They have girded on sackcloth, Put don to the earth their head have the virgins of Jerusalem.

Consumed by tears have been my eyes, Troubled have been my boels, Poured out to the earth hath been my liver, For the breach of the daughter of my people; In infant and suckling being feeble, In the broad places of the city,
To their mothers they say, ’Where [are] corn and ine?’ In their becoming feeble as a pierced one In the broad places of the city, In their soul pouring itself out into the bosom of their mothers.

What do I testify [to] thee, hat do I liken to thee, O daughter of Jerusalem? What do I equal to thee, and I comfort thee, O virgin daughter of Zion? For great as a sea [is] thy breach, Who doth give healing to thee?
Thy prophets have seen for thee a false and insipid thing, And have not revealed concerning thine iniquity, To turn back thy captivity, And they see for thee false burdens and causes of expulsion.

Clapped hands at thee have all passing by the ay, They have hissed — and they shake the head At the daughter of Jerusalem: ’Is this the city of hich they said: The perfection of beauty, a joy to all the land?’

Opened against thee their mouth have all thine enemies, They have hissed, yea, they gnash the teeth, They have said: ’We have salloed [her] up, Surely this [is] the day that e looked for, We have found — e have seen.’

Jehovah hath done that hich He devised, He hath fulfilled His saying That He commanded from the days of old, He hath broken don and hath not pitied, And causeth an enemy to rejoice over thee, He lifted up the horn of thine adversaries.
Cried hath their heart unto the Lord; O all of the daughter of Zion, Cause to go don as a stream tears daily and nightly, Give not rest to thyself, Let not the daughter of thine eye stand still.

Arise, cry aloud in the night, At the beginning of the atches. Pour out as ater thy heart, Over against the face of the Lord, Lift up unto Him thy hands, for the soul of thine infants, Who are feeble ith hunger at the head of all out-places.
See, O Jehovah, and look attentively, To hom Thou hast acted thus, Do omen eat their fruit, infants of a handbreadth? Slain in the sanctuary of the Lord are priest and prophet?
Lain on the earth [in] out-places have young and old, My virgins and my young men have fallen by the sord, Thou hast slain in a day of Thine anger, Thou hast slaughtered — Thou hast not pitied.

Thou dost call as [at] a day of appointment, My fears from round about, And there hath not been in the day of the anger of Jehovah, An escaped and remaining one, They hom I stretched out and nourished, My enemy hath consumed!
I [am] the man [ho] hath seen affliction By the rod of His rath.
Me He hath led, and causeth to go [in] darkness, and ithout light.
Surely against me He turneth back, He turneth His hand all the day.
He hath orn out my flesh and my skin. He hath broken my bones.
He hath built up against me, And setteth round poverty and eariness.
In dark places He hath caused me to dell, As the dead of old.
He hath hedged me about, and I go not out, He hath made heavy my fetter.
Also hen I call and cry out, He hath shut out my prayer.
He hath hedged my ays ith hen ork, My paths He hath made crooked.
A bear lying in ait He [is] to me, A lion in secret hiding-places.
My ays He is turning aside, and He pulleth me in pieces, He hath made me a desolation.
He hath trodden His bo, And setteth me up as a mark for an arro.
He hath caused to enter into my reins The sons of His quiver.
I have been a derision to all my people, Their song all the day.
He hath filled me ith bitter things, He hath filled me [ith] ormood.
And He breaketh ith gravel my teeth, He hath covered me ith ashes.
And Thou castest off from peace my soul, I have forgotten prosperity.
And I say, Perished hath my strength and my hope from Jehovah.
Remember my affliction and my mourning, Wormood and gall!
Remember ell, and bo don doth my soul in me.
This I turn to my heart — therefore I hope.
The kindnesses of Jehovah! For e have not been consumed, For not ended have His mercies.
Ne every morning, abundant [is] thy faithfulness.
My portion [is] Jehovah, hath my soul said, Therefore I hope for Him.
Good [is] Jehovah to those aiting for Him, To the soul [that] seeketh Him.
Good! hen one doth stay and stand still For the salvation of Jehovah.
Good for a man that he beareth a yoke in his youth.
He sitteth alone, and is silent, For He hath laid [it] upon him.
He putteth in the dust his mouth, if so be there is hope.
He giveth to his smiter the cheek, He is filled ith reproach.
For the Lord doth not cast off to the age.
For though He afflicted, yet He hath pitied, According to the abundance of His kindness.
For He hath not afflicted ith His heart, Nor doth He grieve the sons of men.
To bruise under one’s feet any bound ones of earth,
To turn aside the judgment of a man, Over-against the face of the Most High,
To subvert a man in his cause, the Lord hath not approved.
Who [is] this — he hath said, and it is, [And] the Lord hath not commanded [it]?
From the mouth of the Most High Go not forth the evils and the good.
What — sigh habitually doth a living man, A man for his sin?
We search our ays, and investigate, And turn back unto Jehovah.
We lift up our heart on the hands unto God in the heavens.
We — e have transgressed and rebelled, Thou — Thou hast not forgiven.
Thou hast covered Thyself ith anger, And dost pursue us; Thou hast slain — Thou hast not pitied.
Thou hast covered Thyself ith a cloud, So that prayer doth not pass through.
Offscouring and refuse Thou dost make us In the midst of the peoples.
Opened against us their mouth have all our enemies.
Fear and a snare hath been for us, Desolation and destruction.
Rivulets of ater go don my eye, For the destruction of the daughter of my people.
Mine eye is poured out, And doth not cease ithout intermission,
Till Jehovah looketh and seeth from the heavens,
My eye affecteth my soul, Because of all the daughters of my city.
Hunted me sore as a bird have my enemies ithout cause.
They have cut off in a pit my life, And they cast a stone against me.
Floed have aters over my head, I have said, I have been cut off.
I called Thy name, O Jehovah, from the loer pit.
My voice Thou hast heard, Hide not Thine ear at my breathing — at my cry.
Thou hast dran near in the day I call Thee, Thou hast said, Fear not.
Thou hast pleaded, O Lord, the pleadings of my soul, Thou hast redeemed my life.
Thou hast seen, O Jehovah, my overthro, Judge Thou my cause.
Thou hast seen all their vengeance, All their thoughts of me.
Thou hast heard their reproach, O Jehovah, All their thoughts against me,
The lips of my ithstanders, Even their meditation against me all the day.
Their sitting don, and their rising up, Behold attentively, I [am] their song.
Thou returnest to them the deed, O Jehovah, According to the ork of their hands.
Thou givest to them a covered heart, Thy curse to them.
Thou pursuest in anger, and destroyest them, From under the heavens of Jehovah!
Ho is the gold become dim, Changed the best — the pure gold? Poured out are stones of the sanctuary At the head of all out-places.
The precious sons of Zion, Who are comparable ith fine gold, Ho have they been reckoned earthen bottles, Work of the hands of a potter.
Even dragons have dran out the breast, They have suckled their young ones, The daughter of my people is become cruel, Like the ostriches in a ilderness.
Cleaved hath the tongue of a suckling unto his palate ith thirst, Infants asked bread, a dealer out they have none.
Those eating of dainties have been desolate in out-places, Those supported on scarlet have embraced dunghills.
And greater is the iniquity of the daughter of my people, Than the sin of Sodom, That as overturned as [in] a moment, And no hands ere stayed on her.
Purer ere her Nazarites than sno, Whiter than milk, ruddier of body than rubies, Of sapphire their form.
Darker than blackness hath been their visage, They have not been knon in out-places, Cleaved hath their skin unto their bone, It hath ithered — it hath been as ood.
Better have been the pierced of a sord Than the pierced of famine, For these flo aay, pierced through, Without the increase of the field.
The hands of merciful omen have boiled their on children, They have been for food to them, In the destruction of the daughter of my people.
Completed hath Jehovah His fury, He hath poured out the fierceness of His anger, And he kindleth a fire in Zion, And it devoureth her foundations.
Believe not did the kings of earth, And any of the inhabitants of the orld, That come ould an adversary and enemy Into the gates of Jerusalem.
Because of the sins of her prophets, The iniquities of her priests, Who are shedding in her midst the blood of the righteous,
They have andered naked in out-places, They have been polluted ith blood, Without [any] being able to touch their clothing,
’Turn aside — unclean,’ they called to them, ’Turn aside, turn aside, touch not,’ For they fled — yea, they have andered, They have said among nations: ’They do not add to sojourn.’
The face of Jehovah hath divided them, He doth not add to behold them, The face of priests they have not lifted up, Elders they have not favoured.
While e exist — consumed are our eyes for our vain help, In our atch-toer e have atched for a nation [that] saveth not.
They have hunted our steps from going in our broad-places, Near hath been our end, fulfilled our days, For come hath our end.
Sifter have been our pursuers, Than the eagles of the heavens, On the mountains they have burned [after] us, In the ilderness they have laid ait for us.
The breath of our nostrils — the anointed of Jehovah, Hath been captured in their pits, of hom e said: ’In his shado e do live among nations.’
Joy and rejoice, O daughter of Edom, Delling in the land of Uz, Even unto thee pass over doth a cup, Thou art drunk, and makest thyself naked.
Completed [is] thy iniquity, daughter of Zion, He doth not add to remove thee, He hath inspected thy iniquity, O daughter of Edom, He hath removed [thee] because of thy sins!
Remember, O Jehovah, hat hath befallen us, Look attentively, and see our reproach.
Our inheritance hath been turned to strangers, Our houses to foreigners.
Orphans e have been — ithout a father, our mothers [are] as idos.
Our ater for money e have drunk, Our ood for a price doth come.
For our neck e have been pursued, We have laboured — there hath been no rest for us.
[To] Egypt e have given a hand, [To] Asshur, to be satisfied ith bread.
Our fathers have sinned — they are not, We their iniquities have borne.
Servants have ruled over us, A deliverer there is none from their hand.
With our lives e bring in our bread, Because of the sord of the ilderness.
Our skin as an oven hath been burning, Because of the raging of the famine.
Wives in Zion they have humbled, Virgins — in cities of Judah.
Princes by their hand have been hanged, The faces of elders have not been honoured.
Young men to grind they have taken, And youths ith ood have stumbled.
The aged from the gate have ceased, Young men from their song.
Ceased hath the joy of our heart, Turned to mourning hath been our dancing.
Fallen hath the cron [from] our head, Woe [is] no to us, for e have sinned.
For this hath our heart been sick, For these have our eyes been dim.
For the mount of Zion — that is desolate, Foxes have gone up on it.
Thou, O Jehovah, to the age remainest, Thy throne to generation and generation.
Why for ever dost Thou forget us? Thou forsakest us for length of days!
Turn us back, O Jehovah, unto Thee, And e turn back, rene our days as of old.
For hast Thou utterly rejected us? Thou hast been roth against us — exceedingly?

And it cometh to pass, in the thirtieth year, in the fourth [month], in the fifth of the month, and I [am] in the midst of the Removed by the river Chebar, the heavens have been opened, and I see visions of God.
In the fifth of the month — it is the fifth year of the removal of the king Jehoiachin —
hath the ord of Jehovah certainly been unto Ezekiel son of Buzi the priest, in the land of the Chaldeans, by the river Chebar, and there is on him there a hand of Jehovah.

And I look, and lo, a tempestuous ind is coming from the north, a great cloud, and fire catching itself, and brightness to it round about, and out of its midst as the colour of copper, out of the midst of the fire.
And out of its midst [is] a likeness of four living creatures, and this [is] their appearance; a likeness of man [is] to them,
and four faces [are] to each, and four ings [are] to each of them,
and their feet [are] straight feet, and the sole of their feet [is] as a sole of a calf’s foot, and they are sparkling as the colour of bright brass;
and hands of man under their ings — on their four sides, and their faces and their ings — [are] to them four;
joining one unto another [are] their ings, they turn not round in their going, each straight forard they go.

As to the likeness of their faces, the face of a man, and the face of a lion, toard the right [are] to them four, and the face of an ox on the left [are] to them four, and the face of an eagle [are] to them four.
And their faces and their ings are separate from above, to each [are] to joining together, and to are covering their bodies.
And each straight forard they go, hither the spirit is to go, they go, they turn not round in their going.

As to the likeness of the living creatures, their appearances [are] as coals of fire — burning as the appearance of lamps; it is going up and don beteen the living creatures, and brightness [is] to the fire, and out of the fire is going forth lightning.
And the living creatures are running, and turning back, as the appearance of the flash.
And I see the living creatures, and lo, one heel [is] in the earth, near the living creatures, at its four faces.
The appearance of the heels and their orks [is] as the colour of beryl, and one likeness [is] to them four, and their appearances and their orks [are] as it ere the heel in the midst of the heel.
On their four sides, in their going they go, they turn not round in their going.
As to their rings, they are both high and fearful, and their rings [are] full of eyes round about them four.
And in the going of the living creatures, the heels go beside them, and in the living creatures being lifted up from off the earth, lifted up are the heels.
Whither the spirit is to go, they go, thither the spirit [is] to go, and the heels are lifted up over-against them, for a living spirit [is] in the heels.
In their going, they go; and in their standing, they stand; and in their being lifted up from off the earth, lifted up are the heels over-against them; for a living spirit [is] in the heels.
And a likeness [is] over the heads of the living creatures of an expanse, as the colour of the fearful ice, stretched out over their heads from above.
And under the expanse their ings [are] straight, one toard the other, to each are to covering on this side, and to each are to covering on that side — their bodies.

And I hear the noise of their ings, as the noise of many aters, as the noise of the Mighty One, in their going — the noise of tumult, as the noise of a camp, in their standing they let fall their ings.
And there is a voice from above the expanse, that [is] above their head: in their standing they let fall their ings.

And above the expanse that [is] over their head, as an appearance of a sapphire stone, [is] the likeness of a throne, and on the likeness of the throne a likeness, as the appearance of man upon it from above.

And I see as the colour of copper, as the appearance of fire ithin it round about, from the appearance of his loins and upard, and from the appearance of his loins and donard, I have seen as the appearance of fire, and brightness [is] to it round about.
As the appearance of the bo that is in a cloud in a day of rain, so [is] the appearance of the brightness round about.

It [is] the appearance of the likeness of the honour of Jehovah, and I see, and fall on my face, and I hear a voice speaking, and He saith unto me, ’Son of man, stand on thy feet, and I speak ith thee.’
And there doth come into me a spirit, hen He hath spoken unto me, and it causeth me to stand on my feet, and I hear Him ho is speaking unto me.

And He saith unto Me, ’Son of man, I am sending thee unto the sons of Israel, unto nations ho are rebels, ho have rebelled against Me; they and their fathers have transgressed against Me, unto this self-same day.
And the sons [are] brazen-faced and hard-hearted to hom I am sending thee, and thou hast said unto them: Thus said the Lord Jehovah:
and they — hether they hear, or hether they forbear, for a rebellious house they [are] — have knon that a prophet hath been in their midst.

’And thou, son of man, thou art not afraid of them, yea, of their ords thou art not afraid, for briers and thorns are ith thee, and near scorpions thou art delling, of their ords thou art not afraid, and of their faces thou art not affrighted, for they [are] a rebellious house,
And thou hast spoken My ords unto them, hether they hear or hether they forbear, for they [are] rebellious.
’And thou, son of man, hear that hich I am speaking unto thee: Thou art not rebellious like the rebellious house, open thy mouth, and eat that hich I am giving unto thee.’
And I look, and lo, a hand [is] sent forth unto me, and lo, in it a roll of a book,
and He spreadeth it before me, and it is ritten in front and behind, and ritten on it [are] lamentations, and mourning, and oe!
And He saith unto me, ’Son of man, that hich thou findest eat, eat this roll, and go, speak unto the house of Israel.’
And I open my mouth, and He causeth me to eat this roll.
And He saith unto me, ’Son of man, thy belly thou dost feed, and thy boels thou dost fill ith this roll that I am giving unto thee;’ and I eat it, and it is in my mouth as honey for seetness.
And He saith unto me, ’Son of man, go, enter in unto the house of Israel, and thou hast spoken ith My ords unto them.
For, not unto a people deep of lip and heavy of tongue [art] thou sent — unto the house of Israel;
not unto many peoples, deep of lip and heavy of tongue, hose ords thou dost not understand. If I had not sent thee unto them — they, they do hearken unto thee,
but the house of Israel are not illing to hearken unto thee, for they are not illing to hearken unto Me, for all the house of Israel are brazen-faced and strong-hearted.
’Lo, I have made thy face strong against their face, and thy forehead strong against their forehead.
As an adamant harder than a rock I have made thy forehead; thou dost not fear them, nor art thou affrighted before them, for a rebellious house [are] they.’
And He saith unto me, ’Son of man, all My ords, that I speak unto thee, receive ith thy heart, and ith thine ears hear;
and go, enter in unto the Removed, unto the sons of thy people, and thou hast spoken unto them, and hast said unto them: Thus said the Lord Jehovah: hether they hear, or hether they forbear.’
And lift me up doth a spirit, and I hear behind me a noise, a great rushing — ’Blessed [is] the honour of Jehovah from His place!’ —
even a noise of the ings of the living creatures touching one another, and a noise of the heels over-against them, even a noise of a great rushing.
