And the side-chambers [are] side-chamber by side-chamber, three and thirty times; and they are entering into the all — hich the house hath for the side-chambers all round about — to be taken hold of, and they are not taken hold of by the all of the house.

And a broad place and a turning place still upards [are] to the side-chambers, for the turning round of the house [is] still upards all round about the house: therefore the breadth of the house [is] upards, and so the loer one goeth up unto the higher by the midst.
And I have looked at the house, the height all round about: the foundations of the side-chambers [are] the fulness of the reed, six cubits by the joining.
The breadth of the all that [is] to the side-chamber at the outside [is] five cubits; and that hich is left [is] the place of the side-chambers that [are] to the house.
And beteen the chambers [is] a breadth of tenty cubits round about the house, all round about.
And the opening of the side-chamber [is] to the place left, one opening northard, and one opening southard, and the breadth of the place that is left [is] five cubits all round about.

As to the building that [is] at the front of the separate place [at] the corner estard, the breadth [is] seventy cubits, and the all of the building five cubits broad all round about, and its length ninety cubits.
And he hath measured the house, the length [is] a hundred cubits; and the separate place, and the building, and its alls, the length [is] a hundred cubits;
and the breadth of the front of the house, and of the separate place eastard, a hundred cubits.

And he hath measured the length of the building unto the front of the separate place that [is] at its hinder part, and its galleries on this side and on that side, a hundred cubits, and the inner temple and the porches of the court,
the thresholds, and the narro indos, and the galleries round about them three, over-against the threshold, a ceiling of ood all round about, and the ground unto the indos and the covered indos,
over above the opening, and unto the inner-house, and at the outside, and by all the all all round about ithin and ithout [by] measure.
And it is made [ith] cherubs and palm-trees, and a palm-tree [is] beteen cherub and cherub, and to faces [are] to the cherub;
and the face of man [is] unto the palm-tree on this side, and the face of a young lion unto the palm-tree on that side; it is made unto all the house all round about.
from the earth unto above the opening [are] the cherubs and the palm-trees made, and [on] the all of the temple.
Of the temple the side post [is] square, and of the front of the sanctuary, the appearance [is] as the appearance.

Of the altar, the ood [is] three cubits in height, and its length to cubits; and its corners [are] to it, and its length, and its alls [are] of ood, and he speaketh unto me, ’This [is] the table that [is] before Jehovah.’
And to doors [are] to the temple and to the sanctuary;
and to leaves [are] to the doors, to turning leaves [are] to the doors, to to the one door, and to leaves to the other.
And made on them, on the doors of the temple, [are] cherubs and palm-trees as are made on the alls, and a thickness of ood [is] at the front of the porch on the outside.
And narro indos and palm-trees [are] on this side, and on that side, at the sides of the porch, and the side-chambers of the house, and the thick places.
And he bringeth me forth unto the outer court, the ay northard, and he bringeth me in unto the chamber that [is] over-against the separate place, and that [is] over-against the building at the north.
At the front of the length [is] a hundred cubits [at] the north opening, and the breadth fifty cubits.
Over-against the tenty [cubits] that are to the inner court, and over-against the pavement that [is] to the outer court, [is] gallery over-against gallery, in the three [storeys].
And at the front of the chambers [is] a alk of ten cubits in breadth unto the inner part, a ay of one cubit, and their openings [are] at the north.
And the upper chambers [are] short, for the galleries contain more than these, than the loer, and than the middle one, of the building;
for they [are] threefold, and they have no pillars as the pillars of the court, therefore it hath been kept back — more than the loer and than the middle one — from the ground.
As to the all that [is] at the outside, over-against the chambers, the ay of the outer-court at the front of the chambers, its length [is] fifty cubits;
for the length of the chambers that [are] to the outer court [is] fifty cubits, and of those on the front of the temple a hundred cubits.
And under these chambers [is] the entrance from the east, in one’s going into them from the outer court.
In the breadth of the all of the court eastard, unto the front of the separate place, and unto the front of the building, [are] chambers.

And the ay before them [is] as the appearance of the chambers that [are] northard, according to their length so [is] their breadth, and all their outlets, and according to their fashions, and according to their openings.
And according to the openings of the chambers that [are] southard [is] an opening at the head of the ay, the ay directly in the front of the all eastard in entering them.

And he saith unto me, ’The north chambers, the south chambers, that [are] at the front of the separate place, they [are] holy chambers, here the priests (ho [are] near to Jehovah) eat the most holy things, there they place the most holy things, and the present, and the sin-offering, and the guilt-offering, for the place [is] holy.

In the priests’ going in, they come not out from the sanctuary unto the outer court, and there they place their garments ith hich they minister, for they [are] holy, and have put on other garments, and have dran near unto that hich [is] for the people.’
And he hath finished the measurements of the inner house, and hath brought me forth the ay of the gate hose front [is] eastard, and he hath measured it all round about.
He hath measured the east side ith the measuring-reed, five hundred reeds, ith the measuring-reed round about.
He hath measured the north side, five hundred reeds, ith the measuring reed round about.
The south side he hath measured, five hundred reeds, ith the measuring-reed.
He hath turned round unto the est side, he hath measured five hundred reeds ith the measuring-reed.
At the four sides he hath measured it, a all [is] to it all round about, the length five hundred, and the breadth five hundred, to separate beteen the holy and the profane place.
And he causeth me to go to the gate, the gate that is looking eastard.
And lo, the honour of the God of Israel hath come from the ay of the east, and His voice [is] as the noise of many aters, and the earth hath shone from His honour.

And according to the appearance [is] the appearance that I sa, as the appearance that I sa in my coming in to destroy the city, and the appearances [are] as the appearance that I sa at the river Chebar, and I fall on my face.
And the honour of Jehovah hath come in unto the house, the ay of the gate hose face [is] eastard.
And take me up doth the Spirit, and bringeth me in unto the inner court, and lo, the honour of Jehovah hath filled the house.
And I hear one speaking unto me from the house, and a man hath been standing near me,

and He saith unto me: ’Son of man, the place of My throne, And the place of the soles of My feet, Where I dell in the midst of the sons of Israel to the age, Defile no more do the house of Israel My holy name, They, and their kings, by their horedom, And by the carcases of their kings — their high places.

In their putting their threshold ith My threshold, And their door-post near My door-post, And the all beteen Me and them, And they have defiled My holy name, By their abominations that they have done, And I consume them in Mine anger.
No do they put far off their horedom, And the carcases of their kings — from Me, And I have delt in their midst to the age.
Thou, son of man, She the house of Israel the house, And they are ashamed of their iniquities, And they have measured the measurement.

And since they have been ashamed of all that they have done, The form of the house, and its measurement, And its outlets, and its inlets, and all its forms, And all its statutes, even all its forms, And all its las cause them to kno, And rite [it] before their eyes, And they observe all its forms, And all its statutes, and have done them.
This [is] a la of the house: on the top of the mountain, all its border all round about [is] most holy; lo, this [is] a la of the house.

’And these [are] measures of the altar by cubits: The cubit [is] a cubit and a handbreadth, and the centre [is] a cubit, and a cubit the breadth; and its border on its edge round about [is] one span, and this [is] the upper part of the altar.
And from the centre of the ground unto the loer border [is] to cubits, and the breadth one cubit, and from the lesser border unto the greater border four cubits, and the breadth a cubit.
’And the altar [is] four cubits, and from the altar and upard [are] four horns.
And the altar [is] telve long by telve broad, square in its four squares.

And the border [is] fourteen long by fourteen broad, at its four squares, and the border round about it [is] half a cubit, and the centre to it [is] a cubit round about, and its steps are looking eastard.’
And He saith unto me, ’Son of man, Thus said the Lord Jehovah: These [are] statutes of the altar in the day of its being made to cause burnt-offering to go up on it, and to sprinkle on it blood.
And thou hast given unto the priests, the Levites, ho [are] of the seed of Zadok — ho are near unto Me, an affirmation of the Lord Jehovah, to serve Me — a calf from the herd, for a sin-offering.
And thou hast taken of its blood, and hast put it on its four horns, and on the four corners of its border, and on the border round about, and hast cleansed it, and purified it.
And thou hast taken the bullock of the sin-offering, and hast burnt it in the appointed place of the house at the outside of the sanctuary.
And on the second day thou dost bring near a kid of the goats, a perfect one, for a sin-offering, and they have cleansed the altar, as they cleansed [it] for the bullock.
In thy finishing cleansing, thou dost bring near a calf, a son of the herd, a perfect one, and a ram out of the flock, a perfect one.
And thou hast brought them near before Jehovah, and the priests have cast upon them salt, and have caused them to go up, a burnt-offering to Jehovah.
Seven days thou dost prepare a goat for a sin-offering daily, and a bullock, a son of the herd, and a ram out of the flock, perfect ones, do they prepare.
Seven days they purify the altar, and have cleansed it, and filled their hand.

And the days are completed, and it hath come to pass on the eighth day, and henceforth, the priests prepare on the altar your burnt-offerings and your peace-offerings, and I have accepted you — an affirmation of the Lord Jehovah.’
And he causeth me to turn back the ay of the gate of the outer sanctuary that is looking eastard, and it is shut.
And Jehovah saith unto me, ’This gate is shut, it is not opened, and none doth go in by it, for Jehovah, God of Israel, hath come in by it, and it hath been shut.
The prince, ho [is] prince, he sitteth by it to eat bread before Jehovah, by the ay of the porch of the gate he cometh in, and by its ay he goeth out.’
And he bringeth me in the ay of the north gate unto the front of the house, and I look, and lo, filled hath the honour of Jehovah the house of Jehovah, and I fall on my face.

And Jehovah saith unto me, ’Son of man, set thy heart, and see ith thine eyes, and ith thine ears hear, all that I am speaking ith thee, of all the statutes of the house of Jehovah, and of all its las; and thou hast set thy heart to the entrance of the house, ith all the outlets of the sanctuary,
and hast said unto the rebellious, unto the house of Israel: Thus said the Lord Jehovah: Enough to you — of all your abominations, O house of Israel.

In your bringing in sons of a stranger, uncircumcised of heart, and uncircumcised of flesh, to be in My sanctuary, to pollute it, even My house, in your bringing near My bread, fat, and blood, and they break My covenant by all your abominations,
and ye have not kept the charge of My holy things, and ye set [them] for keepers of My charge in My sanctuary for you.

’Thus said the Lord Jehovah: No son of a stranger, uncircumcised of heart, and uncircumcised of flesh, cometh in unto My sanctuary, even any son of a stranger, ho [is] in the midst of the sons of Israel,
but — the Levites ho have gone far off from me, in the andering of Israel hen they ent astray from Me after their idols, and they have borne their iniquity.

And they have been in My sanctuary ministrants, overseers at the gates of the house, and ministrants at the house; they slay the burnt-offering and the sacrifice for the people, and they stand before them to serve them.

Because that they serve them before their idols, and have been to the house of Israel for a stumbling-block of iniquity, therefore I have lifted up my hand against them — an affirmation of the Lord Jehovah — and they have borne their iniquity.
And they dra not nigh unto Me to act as My priest, and to dra nigh unto any of My holy things, unto the holy of holies, and they have borne their shame and their abominations that they have done,
and I made them keepers of the charge of the house, for all its service and for all that is done in it.

’And the priests, the Levites, sons of Zadok, ho have kept the charge of My sanctuary in the andering of the sons of Israel from off Me, they dra near unto Me to serve Me, and have stood before Me, to bring near to Me fat and blood — an affirmation of the Lord Jehovah:
they come in unto My sanctuary, and they dra near unto My table to serve Me, and they have kept My charge.
And it hath come to pass, in their going in unto the gates of the inner court, linen garments they put on; and no ool cometh up on them in their ministering in the gates of the inner court and ithin.
Linen bonnets are on their head, and linen trousers are on their loins, they are not restrained ith seat.

And in their going forth unto the outer court — unto the outer court unto the people — they strip off their garments, in hich they are ministering, and have placed them in the holy chambers, and have put on other garments; and they do not sanctify the people in their on garments.
And their head they do not shave, and the lock they do not send forth; they certainly poll their heads.
And no priest doth drink ine in their coming in unto the inner court.
And a ido and divorced oman they do not take to them for ives: but — virgins of the seed of the house of Israel, and the ido ho is ido of a priest, do they take.
’And My people they direct beteen holy and common, and beteen unclean and clean they cause them to discern.
And concerning controversy, they stand up for judgment; ith My judgments they judge it; and My la and My statutes in all My appointed places they keep; and My sabbaths they sanctify.
And unto any dead man they come not for uncleanness, but for father, and for mother, and for son, and for daughter, for brother, for sister ho hath not been to a man, they defile themselves.
’And after his cleansing, seven days they number to him.
And in the day of his coming in unto the sanctuary, unto the inner court, to minister in the sanctuary, he bringeth near his sin-offering — an affirmation of the Lord Jehovah.
And it hath been to them for an inheritance; I [am] their inheritance: and a possession ye do not give to them in Israel; I [am] their possession.
The present, and the sin-offering, and the guilt-offering, they do eat, and every devoted thing in Israel is theirs.

And the first of all the first-fruits of all, and every heave-offering of all, of all your heave-offerings, are the priests’: and the first of your dough ye give to the priest, to cause a blessing to rest on thy house.
Any carcase and torn thing, of the fol, and of the beasts, the priests do not eat.

And in your causing the land to fall in inheritance, ye lift up a heave-offering to Jehovah, a holy [portion] of the land: the length — five and tenty thousand [is] the length, and the breadth ten thousand; it [is] holy in all its border round about.
There is of this for the sanctuary five hundred by five hundred, square, round about; and fifty cubits of suburb [is] to it round about.
And by this measure thou dost measure: the length [is] five and tenty thousand, and the breadth ten thousand: and in it is the sanctuary, the holy of holies.

The holy [portion] of the land it [is]; for priests, ministrants of the sanctuary, it is, ho are draing near to serve Jehovah; and it hath been to them a place for houses, and a holy place for a sanctuary.
’And of the five and tenty thousand of length, and of the ten thousand of breadth, there is to the Levites, ministrants of the house, for them — for a possession — tenty chambers.
’And of the possession of the city ye give five thousand of breadth, and of length five and tenty thousand, over-against the heave-offering of the holy [portion]: to all the house of Israel it is.

As to the prince, on this side, and on that side, of the heave-offering of the holy place, and of the possession of the city, at the front of the heave-offering of the holy place, and at the front of the possession of the city, from the est corner estard, and from the east corner eastard — and the length [is] over-against one of the portions from the est border unto the east border —
of the land there is to him for a possession in Israel, and My princes do not oppress any more My people, and the land they give to the house of Israel according to their tribes.

’Thus said the Lord Jehovah: Enough to you — princes of Israel; violence and spoil turn aside, and judgment and righteousness do; lift up your exactions from off My people — an affirmation of the Lord Jehovah.
Just balances, and a just ephah, and a just bath — ye have.
The ephah and the bath is of one measure, for the bath to bear a tenth of the homer, and the ephah a tenth of the homer: according to the homer is its measurement.
And, the shekel [is] tenty gerah: tenty shekels, five and tenty shekels, fifteen shekels — is your maneh.
’This [is] the heave-offering that ye lift up; a sixth part of the ephah of a homer of heat, also ye have given a sixth part of the ephah of a homer of barley,
and the portion of oil, the bath of oil, a tenth part of the bath out of the cor, a homer of ten baths — for ten baths [are] a homer;

and one lamb out of the flock, out of to hundred, out of the atered country of Israel, for a present, and for a burnt-offering, and for peace-offerings, to make atonement by them — an affirmation of the Lord Jehovah.
All the people of the land are at this heave-offering for the prince in Israel.

And on the prince are the burnt-offerings, and the present, and the libation, in feasts, and in ne moons, and in sabbaths, in all appointed times of the house of Israel: he doth make the sin-offering, and the present, and the burnt-offering, and the peace-offerings, to make atonement for the house of Israel.
’Thus said the Lord Jehovah: In the first [month], in the first of the month, thou dost take a bullock, a son of the herd, a perfect one, and hast cleansed the sanctuary:

and the priest hath taken of the blood of the sin offering, and hath put on the door-post of the house, and on the four corners of the border of the altar, and on the post of the gate of the inner court.
And so thou dost do on the seventh of the month, because of each erring one, and because of the simple one — and ye have purified the house.
’In the first [month], in the fourteenth day of the month, ye have the passover, a feast of seven days, unleavened food is eaten.
And the prince hath prepared on that day, for himself, and for all the people of the land, a bullock, a sin-offering.
And the seven days of the feast he prepareth a burnt-offering to Jehovah, seven bullocks, and seven rams, perfect ones, daily seven days, and a sin-offering, a kid of the goats, daily.
And a present of an ephah for a bullock, and an ephah for a ram, he doth prepare, and of oil a hin for an ephah.
In the seventh [month], in the fifteenth day of the month, in the feast, he doth according to these things seven days; as the sin-offering so the burnt-offering, and as the present so also the oil.
’Thus said the Lord Jehovah: The gate of the inner court that is looking eastard is shut the six days of ork, and on the day of rest it is opened, and in the day of the ne moon it is opened;

and come in hath the prince the ay of the porch of the gate at the outside, and he hath stood by the post of the gate, and the priests have made his burnt-offering, and his peace-offerings, and he hath boed himself by the opening of the gate, and hath gone forth, and the gate is not shut till the evening.
And boed themselves have the people of the land at the opening of that gate, on sabbaths, and on ne moons, before Jehovah.
’And the burnt-offering that the prince bringeth near to Jehovah on the day of rest [is] six lambs, perfect ones, and a ram, a perfect one.
And the present [is] an ephah for a ram, and for the lambs a present, the gift of his hand, and of oil a hin for an ephah.
And on the day of the ne moon a bullock, a son of the herd, a perfect one, and six lambs and a ram, they are perfect.
And ith an ephah for a bullock, and an ephah for a ram, he prepareth a present, and for the lambs as his hand attaineth, and of oil a hin for an ephah.
’And in the coming in of the prince, the ay of the porch of the gate he cometh in, and by its ay he goeth out.

And in the coming in of the people of the land before Jehovah at appointed times, he ho hath come in the ay of the north gate to bo himself, goeth out the ay of the south gate, and he ho hath come in the ay of the south gate, goeth out by the ay of the north gate: he doth not turn back the ay of the gate by hich he came in, but over-against it he goeth out.
And the prince in their midst in their coming in cometh in, and in their going out he goeth out.
’And in feasts, and in appointed times, the present is an ephah for a bullock, and an ephah for a ram, and for lambs the gift of his hand, and of oil a hin for an ephah.

And hen the prince maketh a free-ill burnt-offering, or free-ill peace-offerings, to Jehovah, then he hath opened for himself the gate that is looking eastard, and he hath made his burnt-offering and his peace-offerings as he doth in the day of rest, and he hath gone out, and he hath shut the gate after his going out.
’And a lamb, son of a year, a perfect one, thou dost make a burnt-offering daily to Jehovah; morning by morning thou dost make it.

And a present thou dost make for it morning by morning, a sixth part of the ephah, and of oil a third part of the hin, to temper ith the fine flour, a present to Jehovah, by a statute age-during — continually;
and prepare ye the lamb, and the present, and the oil, morning by morning, a continual burnt-offering.
’Thus said the Lord Jehovah: When the prince giveth a gift to any of his sons, his inheritance it [is], to his sons it [is]; their possession it [is] by inheritance.

And hen he giveth a gift out of his inheritance to one of his servants, then it hath been to him till the year of freedom, and it hath turned back to the prince, only the inheritance of his sons is theirs.

And the prince doth not take of the inheritance of the people to oppress them, out of their possession, out of his on possession he doth cause his sons to inherit, so that My people are not scattered each from his possession.’
And he bringeth me in through the entrance that [is] by the side of the gate, unto the holy chambers, unto the priests, that are looking northard, and lo, there [is] a place in their to sides estard.

And he saith unto me, ’This [is] the place here the priests do boil the guilt-offering and the sin-offering, here they bake the present, so as not to bring [it] out unto the outer court, to sanctify the people.’
And he bringeth me out unto the outer court, and causeth me to pass over unto the four corners of the court, and lo, a court in a corner of the court, a court in a corner of the corner.
In the four corners of the court [are] perfume courts, forty long, and thirty broad, one measure [is] to the four corners.
And a ro [is] round about in them, round about to them four, and made ith boilers under the ros round about.
And he saith unto me, ’These [are] the houses of those boiling here the ministrants of the house boil the sacrifice of the people.’

And he causeth me to turn back unto the opening of the house; and lo, ater is coming forth from under the threshold of the house eastard, for the front of the house [is] eastard, and the ater is coming don from beneath, from the right side of the house, from the south of the altar.

And he causeth me to go out the ay of the gate northard, and causeth me to turn round the ay ithout, unto the gate that [is] ithout, the ay that is looking eastard, and lo, ater is coming forth from the right side.
In the going out of the man eastard, and a line in his hand, then he measureth a thousand by the cubit, and he causeth me to pass over into ater — ater to the ankles.
And he measureth a thousand, and causeth me to pass over into ater — ater to the knees. And he measureth a thousand, and causeth me to pass over — ater to the loins.
And he measureth a thousand — a stream that I am not able to pass over; for risen have the aters — aters to sim in — a stream that is not passed over.
And he saith unto me, ’Hast thou seen, son of man?’ and he leadeth me, and bringeth me back unto the edge of the stream.
In my turning back, then, lo, at the edge of the stream [are] very many trees, on this side and on that side.

And he saith unto me, ’These aters are going forth unto the east circuit, and have gone don unto the desert, and have entered the sea; unto the sea they are brought forth, and the aters have been healed.

And it hath come to pass, every living creature that teemeth, hithersoever the streams come, doth live: and there hath been great abundance of fish, for these aters have come thither, and they are healed; and every thing hither the stream cometh hath lived.

And it hath come to pass, fishers do stand by it, from En-Gedi even unto En-Eglaim; a spreading place of nets they are; according to their on kind is their fish, as the fish of the great sea, very many.
Its miry and its marshy places — they are not healed; to salt they have been given up.

And by the stream there cometh up on its edge, on this side and on that side, every [kind of] fruit-tree hose leaf fadeth not, and not consumed is its fruit, according to its months it yieldeth first-fruits, because its aters from the sanctuary are coming forth; and its fruits hath been for food, and its leaf for medicine.
’Thus said the Lord Jehovah: This [is] the border hereby ye inherit the land, according to the telve tribes of Israel; Joseph [hath] portions.
And ye have inherited it, one as ell as another, in that I have lifted up My hand to give it to your fathers; and this land hath fallen to you in inheritance.
’And this [is] the border of the land at the north quarter; from the great sea, the ay of Hethlon, at the coming in to Zedad:
Hamath, Berothah, Sibraim, that [is] beteen the border of Damascus and the border of Hamath; Hazar-Hatticon, that [is] at the coast of Havran.
And the border from the sea hath been Hazar-Enan, the border of Damascus, and Zaphon at the north, and the border of Hamath: and [this is] the north quarter.

’And the east quarter [is] from beteen Havran, and Damascus, and Gilead, and the land of Israel, [to] the Jordan; from the border over-against the eastern sea ye measure: and [this is] the east quarter.
’And the south quarter southard [is] from Tamar unto the aters of Meriboth-Kadesh, the stream unto the great sea: and [this is] the south quarter southard.
’And the est quarter [is] the great sea, from the border till over-against the coming in to Hamath: this [is] the est quarter.
’And ye have divided this land to you, according to the tribes of Israel;

and it hath come to pass, ye separate it for an inheritance to yourselves, and to the sojourners ho are sojourning in your midst, ho have begotten sons in your midst, and they have been to you as native, ith the sons of Israel, ith you they are separated for an inheritance in the midst of the tribes of Israel.
And it hath come to pass, in the tribe ith hich the sojourner sojourneth, there ye give his inheritance — an affirmation of the Lord Jehovah.

And these [are] the names of the tribes: From the north end unto the side of the ay of Hethlon, at the coming in to Hamath, Hazar-Enan, the border of Damascus northard, unto the side of Hamath, and they have been his — side east and est, Dan one,
and by the border of Dan, from the east side unto the est side, Asher one,
and by the border of Asher, from the east side even unto the est side, Naphtali one,
and by the border of Naphtali, from the east side unto the est side, Manasseh one,
and by the border of Manasseh, from the east side unto the est side, Ephraim one,
and by the border of Ephraim, from the east side even unto the est side, Reuben one,
and by the border of Reuben, from the east side unto the est side, Judah one,

and by the border of Judah, from the east side unto the est side is the heave-offering that ye lift up, five and tenty thousand broad and long, as one of the parts, from the east side unto the est side: and the sanctuary hath been in its midst.
The heave-offering that ye lift up to Jehovah [is] five and tenty thousand long, and broad ten thousand.

And of these is the holy heave-offering for the priests, northard five and tenty thousand, and estard [in] breadth ten thousand, and eastard [in] breadth ten thousand, and southard [in] length five and tenty thousand: and the sanctuary of Jehovah hath been in its midst.
For the priests ho are sanctified of the sons of Zadok, ho have kept My charge, ho erred not in the erring of the sons of Israel, as the Levites erred,
even the heave-offering hath been to them, out of the heave-offering of the land, most holy, by the border of the Levites.

’And [to] the Levites over-against the border of the priests [are] five and tenty thousand [in] length, and [in] breadth ten thousand, all the length [is] five and tenty thousand, and the breadth ten thousand.
And they do not sell of it, nor exchange, nor cause to pass aay the first-fruit of the land: for [it is] holy to Jehovah.
And the five thousand that is left in the breadth, on the front of the five and tenty thousand, is common — for the city, for delling, and for suburb, and the city hath been in its midst.

And these [are] its measures: the north side five hundred, and four thousand, and the south side five hundred, and four thousand, and on the east side five hundred, and four thousand, and the est side five hundred, and four thousand.
And the suburb to the city hath been northard, fifty and to hundred, and southard, fifty and to hundred, and eastard, fifty and to hundred, and estard, fifty and to hundred.

’And the residue in length over-against the heave-offering of the holy [portion is] ten thousand eastard, and ten thousand estard, and it hath been over-against the heave-offering of the holy [portion], and its increase hath been for food to the servants of the city,
even [to] him ho is serving the city, they serve it out of all the tribes of Israel.
All the heave-offering [is] five and tenty thousand by five and tenty thousand, square do ye lift up the heave-offering of the holy [portion] ith the possession of the city.

’And the residue [is] for the prince, on this side and on that side of the heave-offering of the holy [portion], and of the possession of the city, on the front of the five and tenty thousand of the heave-offering unto the east border, and estard, on the front of the five and tenty thousand on the est border, over-against the portions of the prince; and the heave-offering of the holy [portion], and the sanctuary of the house, hath been in its midst.
And from the possession of the Levites, from the possession of the city, in the midst of that hich is to the prince, beteen the border of Judah and the border of Benjamin, there is to the prince.
’As to the rest of the tribes, from the east side unto the est side, Benjamin one,
and by the border of Benjamin, from the east side unto the est side, Simeon one,
and by the border of Simeon, from the east side unto the est side, Issachar one,
and by the border of Issachar, from the east side unto the est side, Zebulun one,
and by the border of Zebulun, from the east side unto the est side, Gad one,
and by the border of Gad, at the south side southard, the border hath been from Tamar [to] the aters of Meriboth-Kadesh, the stream by the great sea.
This [is] the land that ye separate by inheritance to the tribes of Israel, and these [are] their portions — an affirmation of the Lord Jehovah.
’And these [are] the outgoings of the city on the north side, five hundred, and four thousand measures.
And the gates of the city [are] according to the names of the tribes of Israel; three gates northard: the gate of Reuben one, the gate of Judah one, the gate of Levi one.
And on the east side five hundred, and four thousand, and three gates: the gate of Joseph one, the gate of Benjamin one, the gate of Dan one.
And the south side five hundred, and four thousand measures, and three gates: the gate of Simeon one, the gate of Issachar one, the gate of Zebulun one.
The est side five hundred, and four thousand, their gates three: the gate of Gad one, the gate of Asher one, the gate of Naphtali one.
Round about [is] eighteen thousand, and the renon of the city [is] from the day Jehovah [is] there.’
In the third year of the reign of Jehoiakim king of Judah, come hath Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon to Jerusalem, and layeth siege against it;

and the Lord giveth into his hand Jehoiakim king of Judah, and some of the vessels of the house of God, and he bringeth them in [to] the land of Shinar, [to] the house of his god, and the vessels he hath brought in [to] the treasure-house of his god.
And the king saith, to Ashpenaz master of his eunuchs, to bring in out of the sons of Israel, (even of the royal seed, and of the chiefs,)

lads in hom there is no blemish, and of good appearance, and skilful in all isdom, and possessing knoledge, and teaching thought, and ho have ability to stand in the palace of the king, and to teach them the literature and language of the Chaldeans.

And the king doth appoint for them a rate, day by day, of the king’s portion of food, and of the ine of his drinking, so as to nourish them three years, that at the end thereof they may stand before the king.
And there are among them out of the sons of Judah, Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah,
and the chief of the eunuchs setteth names on them, and he setteth on Daniel, Belteshazzar; and on Hananiah, Shadrach; and on Mishael, Meshach; and on Azariah, Abed-Nego.

And Daniel purposeth in his heart that he ill not pollute himself ith the king’s portion of food, and ith the ine of his drinking, and he seeketh of the chief of the eunuchs that he may not pollute himself.
And God giveth Daniel for kindness and for mercies before the chief of the eunuchs;

and the chief of the eunuchs saith to Daniel, ’I am fearing my lord the king, ho hath appointed your food and your drink, for hy doth he see your faces sadder than [those of] the lads hich [are] of your circle? then ye have made my head indebted to the king,’
And Daniel saith unto the Meltzar, hom the chief of the eunuchs hath appointed over Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah,
’Try, I pray thee, thy servants, ten days; and they give to us of the vegetables, and e eat, and ater, and e drink;
and our appearance is seen before thee, and the appearance of the lads ho are eating the king’s portion of food, and as thou seest — deal ith thy servants.’
And he hearkeneth to them, to this ord, and trieth them ten days:
and at the end of ten days their appearance hath appeared better and fatter in flesh then any of the lads ho are eating the king’s portion of food.
And the Meltzar is taking aay their portion of food, and the ine of their drink, and is giving to them vegetables.
As to these four lads, God hath given to them knoledge and understanding in every [kind of] literature, and isdom; and Daniel hath given instruction about every [kind of] vision and dreams.
And at the end of the days that the king had said to bring them in, bring them in doth the chief of the eunuchs before Nebuchadnezzar.
And the king speaketh ith them, and there hath none been found among them all like Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah, and they stand before the king;
and [in] any matter of isdom [and] understanding that the king hath sought of them, he findeth them ten hands above all the scribes, the enchanters, ho [are] in all his kingdom.
And Daniel is unto the first year of Cyrus the king.
And in the second year of the reign of Nebuchadnezzar, dreamed hath Nebuchadnezzar dreams, and his spirit doth move itself, and his sleep hath been against him;
and the king saith to call for scribes, and for enchanters, and for sorcerers, and for Chaldeans, to declare to the king his dreams. And they come in and stand before the king;
and the king saith to them, ’A dream I have dreamed, and moved is my spirit to kno the dream.’
And the Chaldeans speak to the king [in] Aramaean, ’O king, to the ages live, tell the dream to thy servants, and the interpretation e do she.’
The king hath ansered and said to the Chaldeans, ’The thing from me is gone; if ye do not cause me to kno the dream and its interpretation, pieces ye are made, and your houses are made dunghills;
and if the dream and its interpretation ye do she, gifts, and fee, and great glory ye receive from before me, therefore the dream and its interpretation she ye me.’
They have ansered a second time, and are saying, ’Let the king tell the dream to his servants, and the interpretation e do she.
The king hath ansered and said, ’Of a truth I kno that time ye are gaining, because that ye have seen that the thing is gone from me,

[so] that, if the dream ye do not cause me to kno — one is your sentence, seeing a ord lying and corrupt ye have prepared to speak before me, till that the time is changed, therefore the dream tell ye to me, then do I kno that its interpretation ye do she me.’

The Chaldeans have ansered before the king, and are saying, ’There is not a man on the earth ho is able to she the king’s matter; therefore, no king, chief, and ruler, hath asked such a thing as this of any scribe, and enchanter, and Chaldean;
and the thing that the king is asking [is] precious, and others are there not that do she it before the king, save the gods, hose delling is not ith flesh.’
Therefore the king hath been angry and very roth, and hath said to destroy all the ise men of Babylon;
And the sentence hath gone forth, and the ise men are being slain, and they have sought Daniel and his companions to be slain.
Then Daniel hath replied [ith] counsel and discretion to Arioch chief of the executioners of the king, ho hath gone forth to slay the ise men of Babylon.
He hath ansered and said to Arioch the king’s captain, ’Wherefore [is] the sentence so urgent from before the king?’ Then Arioch hath made the thing knon to Daniel,
and Daniel hath gone up, and sought of the king that he ould give him time to she the interpretation to the king.
Then Daniel to his house hath gone, and to Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah, his companions, he hath made the thing knon,
and to seek mercies from before the God of the heavens concerning this secret, that they destroy not Daniel and his companions ith the rest of the ise men of Babylon.
Then to Daniel, in a vision of the night, the secret hath been revealed. Then hath Daniel blessed the God of the heavens.
Daniel hath ansered and said, ’Let the name of God be blessed from age even unto age, for isdom and might — for they are His.
And He is changing times and seasons, He is causing kings to pass aay, and He is raising up kings; He is giving isdom to the ise, and knoledge to those possessing understanding.
He is revealing deep and hidden things; He hath knon hat [is] in darkness, and light ith Him hath delt.

Thee, O God of my fathers, I am thanking and praising, for isdom and might Thou hast given to me; and no, Thou hast caused me to kno that hich e have sought from Thee, for the king’s matter Thou hast caused us to kno.’

Therefore Daniel hath gone up unto Arioch, hom the king hath appointed to destroy the ise men of Babylon; he hath gone, and thus hath said to him, ’The ise men of Babylon thou dost not destroy, bring me up before the king, and the interpretation to the king I do she.’
Then Arioch in haste hath brought up Daniel before the king, and thus hath said to him — ’I have found a man of the sons of the Removed of Judah, ho the interpretation to the king doth make knon.’
The king hath ansered and said to Daniel, hose name [is] Belteshazzar, ’Art thou able to cause me to kno the dream that I have seen, and its interpretation?’
Daniel hath ansered before the king and said, ’The secret that the king is asking, the ise men, the enchanters, the scribes, the soothsayers, are not able to she to the king;

but there is a God in the heavens, a revealer of secrets, and He hath made knon to king Nebuchadnezzar that hich [is] to be in the latter end of the days. ’Thy dream and the visions of thy head on thy bed are these:
Thou, O king, thy thoughts on thy bed have come up [concerning] that hich [is] to be after this, and the Revealer of secrets hath caused thee to kno that hich [is] to be.

As to me — not for [any] isdom that is in me above any living hath this secret been revealed to me; but for the intent that the interpretation to the king they make knon, and the thoughts of thy heart thou dost kno.
’Thou, O king, ast looking, and lo, a certain great image. This image [is] mighty, and its brightness excellent; it is standing over-against thee, and its appearance [is] terrible.
This image! its head [is] of good gold, its breasts and its arms of silver, its belly and its thighs of brass;
its legs of iron, its feet, part of them of iron, and part of them of clay.
Thou ast looking till that a stone hath been cut out ithout hands, and it hath smitten the image on its feet, that [are] of iron and of clay, and it hath broken them small;

then broken small together have been the iron, the clay, the brass, the silver, and the gold, and they have been as chaff from the summer threshing-floor, and carried them aay hath the ind, and no place hath been found for them: and the stone that smote the image hath become a great mountain, and hath filled all the land.
This [is] the dream, and its interpretation e do tell before the king.
’Thou, O king, art a king of kings, for the God of the heavens a kingdom, strength, and might, and glory, hath given to thee;
and hithersoever sons of men are delling, the beast of the field, and the fol of the heavens, He hath given into thy hand, and hath caused thee to rule over them all; thou [art] this head of gold.
And after thee doth rise up another kingdom loer than those, and another third kingdom of brass, that doth rule overall the earth.
And the fourth kingdom is strong as iron, because that iron is breaking small, and making feeble, all [things], even as iron that is breaking all these, it beateth small and breaketh.

As to that hich thou hast seen: the feet and toes, part of them potter’s clay, and part of them iron, the kingdom is divided: and some of the standing of the iron [is] to be in it, because that thou hast seen the iron mixed ith miry clay.
As to the toes of the feet, part of them iron, and part of them clay: some part of the kingdom is strong, and some part of it is brittle.
Because thou hast seen iron mixed ith miry clay, they are mixing themselves ith the seed of men: and they are not adhering one ith another, even as iron is not mixed ith clay.

’And in the days of these kings raise up doth the God of the heavens a kingdom that is not destroyed — to the age, and its kingdom to another people is not left: it beateth small and endeth all these kingdoms, and it standeth to the age.

Because that thou hast seen that out of the mountain cut hath been a stone ithout hands, and it hath beaten small the iron, the brass, the clay, the silver, and the gold; the great God hath made knon to the king that hich [is] to be after this; and the dream [is] true, and its interpretation stedfast.
Then hath king Nebuchadnezzar fallen on his face, and to Daniel he hath done obeisance, and present, and seet things, he hath said to pour out to him.
The king hath ansered Daniel and said, ’Of a truth [it is] that your God is a God of gods, and a Lord of kings, and a revealer of secrets, since thou hast been able to reveal this secret.’

Then the king hath made Daniel great, and many great gifts he hath given to him, and hath caused him to rule over all the province of Babylon, and chief of the perfects over all the ise men of Babylon.
And Daniel hath sought from the king, and he hath appointed over the ork of the province of Babylon, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-Nego, and Daniel [is] in the gate of the king.
Nebuchadnezzar the king hath made an image of gold, its height sixty cubits, its breadth six cubits; he hath raised it up in the valley of Dura, in the province of Babylon;

and Nebuchadnezzar the king hath sent to gather the satraps, the prefects, and the governors, the honourable judges, the treasurers, the counsellors, the sheriffs, and all the rulers of the province, to come to the dedication of the image that Nebuchadnezzar the king hath raised up.

Then are gathered the satraps, the prefects, and the governors, the honourable judges, the treasurers, the counsellors, the sheriffs, and all the rulers of the province, to the dedication of the image that Nebuchadnezzar the king hath raised up: and they are standing before the image that Nebuchadnezzar hath raised up.
And a crier is calling mightily: ’To you they are saying: O peoples, nations, and languages!

at the time that ye hear the voice of the cornet, the flute, the harp, the sackbut, the psaltery, the symphony, and all kinds of music, ye fall don and do obeisance to the golden image that Nebuchadnezzar the king hath raised up:
and hoso doth not fall don and do obeisance, in that hour he is cast into the midst of a burning fiery furnace.’

Therefore at that time, hen all the peoples are hearing the voice of the cornet, the flute, the harp, the sackbut, the psaltery, and all kinds of music, falling don are all the peoples, nations and languages, doing obeisance to the golden image that Nebuchadnezzar the king hath raised up.
Therefore at that time dran near have certain Chaldeans, and accused the Jes;
they have ansered, yea, they are saying to Nebuchadnezzar the king, ’O king, to the ages live!

Thou, O king, hast made a decree that every man ho doth hear the voice of the cornet, the flute, the harp, the sackbut, the psaltery, and the symphony, and all kinds of music, doth fall don and do obeisance to the golden image;
and hoso doth not fall don and do obeisance, is cast into the midst of a burning fiery furnace.

There are certain Jes hom thou hast appointed over the ork of the province of Babylon — Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-Nego, these men have not made of thee, O king, [any] regard; thy gods they are not serving, and to the golden image thou hast raised up — are not making obeisance.’
Then Nebuchadnezzar, in anger and fury, hath said to bring in Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-Nego. Then these men have been brought in before the king.

Nebuchadnezzar hath ansered and said to them, ’Is [it] a laid plan, O Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-Nego — my gods ye are not serving, and to the golden image that I have raised up ye are not doing obeisance?

No, lo, ye are ready, so that at the time that ye hear the voice of the cornet, the flute, the harp, the sackbut, the psaltery, and the symphony, and all kinds of music, ye fall don and do obeisance to the image that I have made! — and lo, ye do no obeisance — in that hour ye are cast into the midst of a burning fiery furnace; ho is that God ho doth deliver you out of my hands?’
Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-Nego have ansered, yea, they are saying to the king Nebuchadnezzar, ’We have no need concerning this matter to anser thee.
Lo, it is; our God hom e are serving, is able to deliver us from a burning fiery furnace; and from thy hand, O king, He doth deliver.
And lo — not! be it knon to thee, O king, that thy gods e are not serving, and to the golden image thou hast raised up e do no obeisance.’

Then Nebuchadnezzar hath been full of fury, and the expression of his face hath been changed concerning Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-Nego; he ansered and said to heat the furnace seven times above that hich it is seen to be heated;
and to certain mighty men ho [are] in his force he hath said to bind Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-Nego, to cast into the burning fiery furnace.
Then these men have been bound in their coats, their tunics, and their turbans, and their clothing, and have been cast into the midst of the burning fiery furnace.
Therefore, because that the ord of the king is urgent, and the furnace heated exceedingly, those men ho have taken up Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-Nego — killed them hath the spark of the fire.
And these three men, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-Nego, have fallen don in the midst of the burning fiery furnace — bound.

Then Nebuchadnezzar the king hath been astonished, and hath risen in haste; he hath ansered and said to his counsellors, ’Have e not cast three men into the midst of the fire — bound?’ They have ansered and are saying to the king, ’Certainly, O king.’
He ansered and hath said, ’Lo, I am seeing four men loose, alking in the midst of the fire, and they have no hurt; and the appearance of the fourth [is] like to a son of the gods.’

Then Nebuchadnezzar hath dran near to the gate of the burning fiery furnace; he hath ansered and said, ’Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-Nego, servants of God Most High come forth, yea, come;’ then come forth do Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-Nego, from the midst of the fire;

and gathered together, the satraps, the prefects, and the governors, and the counsellors of the king, are seeing these men, that the fire hath no poer over their bodies, and the hair of their head hath not been singed, and their coats have not changed, and the smell of fire hath not passed on them.

Nebuchadnezzar hath ansered and hath said, ’Blessed [is] the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-Nego, ho hath sent His messenger, and hath delivered His servants ho trusted on Him, and the ord of the king changed, and gave up their bodies that they might not serve nor do obeisance to any god except to their on God.

And by me a decree is made, that any people, nation, and language, that doth speak erroneously concerning the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-Nego, pieces he is made, and its house is made a dunghill, because that there is no other god ho is able thus to deliver.’
Then the king hath caused Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-Nego, to prosper in the province of Babylon.
’Nebuchadnezzar the king to all peoples, nations, and languages, ho are delling in all the earth: Your peace be great!
The signs and onders that God Most High hath done ith me, it is good before me to she.
His signs ho great! and His onders ho mighty! His kingdom [is] a kingdom age-during, and His rule [is] ith generation and generation.
’I, Nebuchadnezzar, have been at rest in my house, and flourishing in my palace:
a dream I have seen, and it maketh me afraid, and the conceptions on my bed, and the visions of my head, do trouble me.
And by me a decree is made, to cause all the ise men of Babylon to come up before me, that the interpretation of the dream they may cause me to kno.
Then coming up are the scribes, the enchanters, the Chaldeans, and the soothsayers, and the dream I have told before them, and its interpretation they are not making knon to me.
And at last come up before me hath Daniel, hose name [is] Belteshazzar — according to the name of my god — and in hom [is] the spirit of the holy gods, and the dream before him I have told:

’O Belteshazzar, master of the scribes, as I have knon that the spirit of the holy gods [is] in thee, and no secret doth press thee, the visions of my dream that I have seen, and its interpretation, tell.
As to the visions of my head on my bed, I as looking, and lo, a tree in the midst of the earth, and its height [is] great:
become great hath the tree, yea, strong, and its height doth reach to the heavens, and its vision to the end of the hole land;

its leaves [are] fair, and its budding great, and food for all [is] in it: under it take shade doth the beast of the field, and in its boughs dell do the birds of the heavens, and of it fed are all flesh.
’I as looking, in the visions of my head on my bed, and lo, a sifter, even a holy one, from the heavens is coming don.

He is calling mightily, and thus hath said, Cut don the tree, and cut off its branches, shake off its leaves, and scatter its budding, move aay let the beast from under it, and the birds from off its branches;

but the stump of its roots leave in the earth, even ith a band of iron and brass, in the tender grass of the field, and ith the de of the heavens is it et, and ith the beasts [is] his portion in the herb of the earth;
his heart from man’s is changed, and the heart of a beast is given to him, and seven times pass over him;

by the decree of the sifters [is] the sentence, and by the saying of the holy ones the requirement, to the intent that the living may kno that the Most High is ruler in the kingdom of men, and to hom He illeth He giveth it, and the loest of men He doth raise up over it.

’This dream I have seen, I king Nebuchadnezzar; and thou, O Belteshazzar, the interpretation tell, because that all the ise men of my kingdom are not able to cause me to kno the interpretation, and thou [art] able, for the spirit of the holy gods [is] in thee.

’Then Daniel, hose name [is] Belteshazzar, hath been astonished about one hour, and his thoughts do trouble him; the king hath ansered and said, O Belteshazzar, let not the dream and its interpretation trouble thee. Belteshazzar hath ansered and said, My lord, the dream — to those hating thee, and its interpretation — to thine enemies!
The tree that thou hast seen, that hath become great and strong, and its height doth reach to the heavens, and its vision to all the land,
and its leaves [are] fair, and its budding great, and food for all [is] in it, under it dell doth the beast of the field, and on its boughs sit do the birds of the heavens.
’Thou it [is], O king, for thou hast become great and mighty, and thy greatness hath become great, and hath reached to the heavens, and thy dominion to the end of the earth;

and that hich the king hath seen — a sifter, even a holy one, coming don from the heavens, and he hath said, Cut don the tree, and destroy it; but the stump of its roots leave in the earth, even ith a band of iron and brass, in the tender grass of the field, and ith the de of the heavens it is et, and ith the beast of the field [is] his portion, till that seven times pass over him.
’This [is] the interpretation, O king, and the decree of the Most High it [is] that hath come against my lord the king:

and they are driving thee aay from men, and ith the beast of the field is thy delling, and the herb as oxen they do cause thee to eat, and by the de of the heavens they are etting thee, and seven times do pass over thee, till that thou knoest that the Most High is ruler in the kingdom of men, and to hom He illeth He giveth it.
And that hich they said — to leave the stump of the roots of the tree; thy kingdom for thee abideth, after that thou knoest that the heavens are ruling.
’Therefore, O king, let my counsel be acceptable unto thee, and thy sins by righteousness break off, and thy perversity by pitying the poor, lo, it is a lengthening of thine ease.
’All — hath come on Nebuchadnezzar the king.
’At the end of telve months, on the palace of the kingdom of Babylon he hath been alking;
the king hath ansered and said, Is not this that great Babylon that I have built, for the house of the kingdom, in the might of my strength, and for the glory of mine honour?
’While the ord is [in] the king’s mouth a voice from the heavens hath fallen: To thee they are saying: O Nebuchadnezzar the king, the kingdom hath passed from thee,

and from men they are driving thee aay, and ith the beast of the field [is] thy delling, the herb as oxen they do cause thee to eat, and seven times do pass over thee, till that thou knoest that the Most High is ruler in the kingdom of men, and to hom He illeth He giveth it.

’In that hour the thing hath been fulfilled on Nebuchadnezzar, and from men he is driven, and the herb as oxen he eateth, and by the de of the heavens his body is et, till that his hair as eagles’ hath become great, and his nails as birds.’

’And at the end of the days I, Nebuchadnezzar, mine eyes to the heavens have lifted up, and mine understanding unto me returneth, and the Most High I have blessed, and the Age-during Living One I have praised and honoured, hose dominion [is] a dominion age-during, and His kingdom ith generation and generation;

and all ho are delling on the earth as nothing are reckoned, and according to his ill He is doing among the forces of the heavens and those delling on the earth, and there is none that doth clap ith his hand, and saith to Him, What hast Thou done?

’At that time my understanding doth return unto me, and for the glory of my kingdom, my honour and my brightness doth return unto me, and to me my counsellors and my great men do seek, and over my kingdom I have been made right, and abundant greatness hath been added to me.
’No, I, Nebuchadnezzar, am praising and exalting and honouring the King of the heavens, for all His orks [are] truth, and His paths judgment, and those alking in pride He is able to humble.’
Belshazzar the king hath made a great feast to a thousand of his great men, and before the thousand he is drinking ine;

Belshazzar hath said — hile tasting the ine — to bring in the vessels of gold and of silver that Nebuchadnezzar his father had taken from the temple that [is] in Jerusalem, that drink ith them may the king, and his great men, his ives, and his concubines.

Then they have brought in the vessels of gold that had been taken out of the temple of the house of God that [is] in Jerusalem, and drunk ith them have the king and his great men, his ives and his concubines;
they have drunk ine, and have praised the gods of gold, and of silver, of brass, of iron, of ood, and of stone.

In that hour come forth have fingers of a man’s hand, and they are riting over-against the candlestick, on the plaster of the all of the king’s palace: and the king is seeing the extremity of the hand that is riting;
then the king’s countenance hath changed, and his thoughts do trouble him, and the joints of his loins are loosed, and his knees are smiting one against another.

Call doth the king mightily, to bring up the enchanters, the Chaldeans, and the soothsayers. Ansered hath the king, and said to the ise men of Babylon, that, ’Any man ho doth read this riting, and its interpretation doth she me, purple he putteth on, and a bracelet of gold [is] on his neck, and third in the kingdom he doth rule.’
Then coming up are all the ise men of the king, and they are not able to read the riting, and the interpretation to make knon to the king;
then the king Belshazzar is greatly troubled, and his countenance is changing in him, and his great men are perplexed.

The queen, on account of the ords of the king and his great men, to the banquet-house hath come up. Ansered hath the queen, and said, ’O king, to the ages live; let not thy thoughts trouble thee, nor thy countenance be changed:

there is a man in thy kingdom in hom [is] the spirit of the holy gods: and, in the days of thy father, light, and understanding, and isdom — as the isdom of the gods — as found in him; and king Nebuchadnezzar thy father, chief of the scribes, enchanters, Chaldeans, soothsayers, established him — thy father, O king —

because that an excellent spirit, and knoledge, and understanding, interpreting of dreams, and shoing of enigmas, and loosing of knots as found in him, in Daniel, hose name the king made Belteshazzar: no let Daniel be called, and the interpretation he doth sho.’

Then Daniel hath been caused to come up before the king; ansered hath the king, and said to Daniel, ’Thou art that Daniel ho [art] of the sons of the Removed of Judah, hom the king my father brought in out of Judah?
And I have heard of thee, that the spirit of the gods [is] in thee, and light, and understanding, and excellent isdom have been found in thee.

’And no, caused to come up before me have been the ise men, the enchanters, that this riting they may read, and its interpretation to cause me to kno: and they are not able to she the interpretation of the thing:

and I — I have heard of thee, that thou art able to give interpretations, and to loose knots: no, lo — thou art able to read the riting, and its interpretation to cause me to kno — purple thou dost put on, and a bracelet of gold [is] on thy neck, and third in the kingdom thou dost rule.’
Then hath Daniel ansered and said before the king, ’Thy gifts be to thyself, and thy fee to another give; nevertheless, the riting I do read to the king, and the interpretation I cause him to kno;
thou, O king, God Most High, a kingdom, and greatness, and glory, and honour, gave to Nebuchadnezzar thy father:

and because of the greatness that He gave to him, all peoples, nations, and languages ere trembling and fearing before him: hom he illed he as slaying, and hom he illed he as keeping alive, and hom he illed he as raising up, and hom he illed he as making lo;
and hen his heart as high, and his spirit as strong to act proudly, he hath been caused to come don from the throne of his kingdom, and his glory they have caused to pass aay from him,

and from the sons of men he is driven, and his heart ith the beasts hath been like, and ith the ild asses [is] his delling; the herb like oxen they cause him to eat, and by the de of the heavens is his body et, till that he hath knon that God Most High is ruler in the kingdom of men, and hom He illeth He raiseth up over it.
’And thou, his son, Belshazzar, hast not humbled thy heart, though all this thou hast knon;

and against the Lord of the heavens thou hast lifted up thyself; and the vessels of His house they have brought in before thee, and thou, and thy great men, thy ives, and thy concubines, are drinking ine ith them, and gods of silver, and of gold, of brass, of iron, of ood, and of stone, that are not seeing, nor hearing, nor knoing, thou hast praised: and the God in hose hand [is] thy breath, and all thy ays, Him thou hast not honoured.
’Then from before Him sent is the extremity of the hand, and the riting is noted don;
and this [is] the riting that is noted don: Numbered, Numbered, Weighed, and Divided.
This [is] the interpretation of the thing: Numbered — God hath numbered thy kingdom, and hath finished it.
Weighed — Thou art eighed in the balances, and hast been found lacking.
Divided — Divided is thy kingdom, and it hath been given to the Medes and Persians.’
Then hath Belshazzar said, and they have clothed Daniel ith purple, and a bracelet of gold [is] on his neck, and they have proclaimed concerning him that he is the third ruler in the kingdom.
In that night Belshazzar king of the Chaldeans is slain,
and Darius the Mede hath received the kingdom, hen a son of sixty and to years.
It hath been good before Darius, and he hath established over the kingdom satraps — a hundred and tenty — that they may be throughout the hole kingdom,
and higher than they three presidents, of hom Daniel [is] first, that these satraps may give to them an account, and the king have no loss.
Then this Daniel hath been overseer over the presidents and satraps, because that an excellent spirit [is] in him, and the king hath thought to establish him over the hole kingdom.

Then the presidents and satraps have been seeking to find a cause of complaint against Daniel concerning the kingdom, and any cause of complaint and corruption they are not able to find, because that he [is] faithful, and any error and corruption have not been found in him.
Then these men are saying, ’We do not find against this Daniel any cause of complaint, except e have found [it] against him in the la of his God.’
Then these presidents and satraps have assembled near the king, and thus they are saying to him: ’O king Darius, to the ages live!

Taken counsel have all the presidents of the kingdom, the prefects, and the satraps, the counsellors, and the governors, to establish a royal statute, and to strengthen an interdict, that any ho seeketh a petition from any god and man until thirty days, save of thee, O king, is cast into a den of lions.
No, O king, thou dost establish the interdict, and sign the riting, that it is not to be changed, as a la of Media and Persia, that doth not pass aay.’
Therefore king Darius hath signed the riting and interdict.

And Daniel, hen he hath knon that the riting is signed, hath gone up to his house, and the indo being opened for him, in his upper chamber, over-against Jerusalem, three times in a day he is kneeling on his knees, and praying, and confessing before his God, because that he as doing [it] before this.
Then these men have assembled, and found Daniel praying and entreating grace before his God;

then they have come near, yea, they are saying before the king concerning the king’s interdict: ’Hast thou not signed an interdict, that any man ho seeketh from any god and man until thirty days, save of thee, O king, is cast into a den of lions?’ Ansered hath the king, and said, ’The thing [is] certain as a la of Media and Persia, that doth not pass aay.’

Then they have ansered, yea, they are saying before the king, that, ’Daniel, ho [is] of the sons of the Removed of Judah, hath not placed on thee, O king, [any] regard, nor on the interdict that thou hast signed, and three times in a day he is seeking his petition.’
Then the king, hen he hath heard the matter, is greatly displeased at himself, and on Daniel he hath set the heart to deliver him, and till the going up of the sun he as arranging to deliver him.

Then these men have assembled near the king, and are saying to the king, ’kno, O king, that the la of Media and Persia [is]: That any interdict and statute that the king doth establish is not to be changed.’

Then the king hath said, and they have brought Daniel, and have cast [him] into a den of lions. The king hath ansered and said to Daniel, ’Thy God, hom thou art serving continually, Himself doth deliver thee.’
And a stone hath been brought and placed at the mouth of the den, and the king hath sealed it ith his signet, and ith the signet of his great men, that the purpose be not changed concerning Daniel.
Then hath the king gone to his palace, and he hath passed the night fasting, and dahavan have not been brought up before him, and his sleep hath fled [from] off him.
Then doth the king rise in the early morning, at the light, and in haste to the den of lions he hath gone;

and at his coming near to the den, to Daniel, ith a grieved voice, he crieth. The king hath ansered and said to Daniel, O Daniel, servant of the living God, thy God, hom thou art serving continually, is He able to deliver thee from the lions?’
Then Daniel hath spoken ith the king: ’O king, to the ages live:

my God hath sent His messenger, and hath shut the lions’ mouths, and they have not injured me: because that before Him purity hath been found in me; and also before thee, O king, injury I have not done.’

Then as the king very glad for him, and he hath commanded Daniel to be taken up out of the den, and Daniel hath been taken up out of the den, and no injury hath been found in him, because he hath believed in his God.

And the king hath said, and they have brought those men ho had accused Daniel, and to the den of lions they have cast them, they, their sons, and their ives; and they have not come to the loer part of the den till that the lions have poer over them, and all their bones they have broken small.
Then Darius the king hath ritten to all the peoples, nations, and languages, ho are delling in all the land: ’Your peace be great!

From before me is made a decree, that in every dominion of my kingdom they are trembling and fearing before the God of Daniel, for He [is] the living God, and abiding to the ages, and His kingdom that hich [is] not destroyed, and His dominion [is] unto the end.
A deliverer, and rescuer, and doer of signs and onders in the heavens and in earth [is] He ho hath delivered Daniel from the pa of the lions.’
And this Daniel hath prospered in the reign of Darius, and in the reign of Cyrus the Persian.
In the first year of Belshazzar king of Babylon, Daniel hath seen a dream, and the visions of his head on his bed, then the dream he hath ritten, the chief of the things he hath said.
Ansered hath Daniel and said, ’I as seeing in my vision by night, and lo, the four inds of the heavens are coming forth to the great sea;
and four great beasts are coming up from the sea, diverse one from another.

The first [is] like a lion, and it hath an eagle’s ings. I as seeing till that its ings have been plucked, and it hath been lifted up from the earth, and on feet as a man it hath been caused to stand, and a heart of man is given to it.

And lo, another beast, a second, like to a bear, and to the same authority it hath been raised, and three ribs [are] in its mouth, beteen its teeth, and thus they are saying to it, Rise, consume much flesh.
’After this I as seeing, and lo, another like a leopard, and it hath four ings of a fol on its back, and four heads hath the beast, and dominion is given to it.

’After this I as seeing in the visions of the night, and lo, a fourth beast, terrible and fearful, and exceedingly strong; and it hath iron teeth very great, it hath consumed, yea, it doth break small, and the remnant ith its feet it hath trampled; and it [is] diverse from all the beasts that [are] before it; and it hath ten horns.

’I as considering about the horns, and lo, another horn, a little one, hath come up beteen them, and three of the first horns have been eradicated from before it, and lo, eyes as the eyes of man [are] in this horn, and a mouth speaking great things.

’I as seeing till that thrones have been thron don, and the Ancient of Days is seated, His garment as sno [is] hite, and the hair of his head [is] as pure ool, His throne flames of fire, its heels burning fire.
A flood of fire is proceeding and coming forth from before Him, a thousand thousands do serve Him, and a myriad of myriads before Him do rise up, the Judge is seated, and the books have been opened.
’I as seeing, then, because of the voice of the great ords that the horn is speaking, I as seeing till that the beast is slain, and his body hath been destroyed, and given to the burning fire;
and the rest of the beasts have caused their dominion to pass aay, and a prolongation in life is given to them, till a season and a time.
’I as seeing in the visions of the night, and lo, ith the clouds of the heavens as a son of man as [one] coming, and unto the Ancient of Days he hath come, and before Him they have brought him near.

And to him is given dominion, and glory, and a kingdom, and all peoples, nations, and languages do serve him, his dominion [is] a dominion age-during, that passeth not aay, and his kingdom that hich is not destroyed.
’Pierced hath been my spirit — I, Daniel — in the midst of the sheath, and the visions of my head trouble me;
I have dran near unto one of those standing, and the certainty I seek from him of all this; and he hath said to me, yea, the interpretation of the things he hath caused me to kno:
’These great beasts, that [are] four, [are] four kings, they rise up from the earth;
and receive the kingdom do the saints of the Most High, and they strengthen the kingdom unto the age, even unto the age of the ages.

’Then I ished for certainty concerning the fourth beast, that as diverse from them all, fearful exceedingly; its teeth of iron, and its nails of brass, it hath devoured, it doth break small, and the remnant ith its feet it hath trampled;

and concerning the ten horns that [are] in its heads, and of the other that came up, and before hich three have fallen, even of that horn that hath eyes, and a mouth speaking great things, and hose appearance [is] great above its companions.
’I as seeing, and this horn is making ar ith the saints, and hath prevailed over them,
till that the Ancient of Days hath come, and judgment is given to the saints of the Most High, and the time hath come, and the saints have strengthened the kingdom.
’Thus he said: The fourth beast is the fourth kingdom in the earth, that is diverse from all kingdoms, and it consumeth all the earth, and treadeth it don, and breaketh it small.
And the ten horns out of the kingdom [are] ten kings, they rise, and another doth rise after them, and it is diverse from the former, and three kings it humbleth;

and ords as an adversary of the Most High it doth speak, and the saints of the Most High it doth ear out, and it hopeth to change seasons and la; and they are given into its hand, till a time, and times, and a division of a time.
’And the Judge is seated, and its dominion they cause to pass aay, to cut off, and to destroy — unto the end;

and the kingdom, and the dominion, even the greatness of the kingdom under the hole heavens, is given to the people — the saints of the Most High, His kingdom [is] a kingdom age-during, and all dominions do serve and obey Him.
’Hitherto [is] the end of the matter. I, Daniel, greatly do my thoughts trouble me, and my countenance is changed on me, and the matter in my heart I have kept.
’In the third year of the reign of Belshazzar the king, a vision hath appeared unto me — I Daniel — after that hich had appeared unto me at the beginning.
And I see in a vision, and it cometh to pass, in my seeing, and I [am] in Shushan the palace that [is] in Elam the province, and I see in a vision, and I have been by the stream Ulai.

And I lift up mine eyes, and look, and lo, a certain ram is standing before the stream, and it hath to horns, and the to horns [are] high; and the one [is] higher than the other, and the high one is coming up last.

I have seen the ram pushing estard, and northard, and southard, and no living creatures do stand before it, and there is none delivering out of its hand, and it hath done according to its pleasure, and hath exerted itself.

’And I have been considering, and lo, a young he-goat hath come from the est, over the face of the hole earth, hom none is touching in the earth; as to the young he-goat, a conspicuous horn [is] beteen its eyes.
And it cometh unto the ram possessing the to horns, that I had seen standing before the stream, and runneth unto it in the fury of its poer.

And I have seen it coming near the ram, and it becometh embittered at it, and smiteth the ram, and breaketh its to horns, and there hath been no poer in the ram to stand before it, and it casteth it to the earth, and trampleth it don, and there hath been no deliverer to the ram out of its poer.
’And the young he-goat hath exerted itself very much, and hen it is strong, broken hath been the great horn; and come up doth a vision of four in its place, at the four inds of the heavens.
And from the one of them come forth hath a little horn, and it exerteth itself greatly toard the south, and toard the east, and toard the beauteous [land];
yea, it exerteth unto the host of the heavens, and causeth to fall to the earth of the host, and of the stars, and trampleth them don.
And unto the prince of the host it exerteth itself, and by it taken aay hath been the continual [sacrifice], and thron don the base of his sanctuary.
And the host is given up, ith the continual [sacrifice], through transgression, and it throeth don truth to the earth, and it hath orked, and prospered.

’And I hear a certain holy one speaking, and a certain holy one saith to the onderful numberer ho is speaking: Till hen [is] the vision of the continual [sacrifice], and of the transgression, an astonishment, to make both sanctuary and host a treading don?
And he saith unto me, Till evening — morning to thousand and three hundred, then is the holy place declared right.
’And it cometh to pass in my seeing — I, Daniel — the vision, that I require understanding, and lo, standing over-against me [is] as the appearance of a mighty one.
And I hear a voice of man beteen [the banks of] Ulai, and he calleth and saith: Gabriel, cause this [one] to understand the appearance.
And he cometh in near my station, and at his coming in I have been afraid, and I fall on my face, and he saith unto me: Understand, son of man, for at the time of the end [is] the vision.
And in his speaking ith me, I have been in a trance on my face, on the earth; and he cometh against me, and causeth me to stand on my station,
and saith: Lo, I — I am causing thee to kno that hich is in the latter end of the indignation; for, at the appointed time [is] the end.
’The ram that thou hast seen possessing to horns, [are] the kings of Media and Persia.
And the young he-goat, the hairy one, [is] the king of Javan; and the great horn that [is] beteen its eyes is the first king;
and that being broken, stand up do four in its place, four kingdoms from the nation do stand up, and not in its poer.
’And in the latter end of their kingdom, about the perfecting of the transgressors, stand up doth a king, fierce of face, and understanding hidden things;
and his poer hath been mighty, and not by his on poer; and onderful things he destroyeth, and he hath prospered, and rought, and destroyed mighty ones, and the people of the Holy Ones.

’And by his understanding he hath also caused deceit to prosper in his hand, and in his heart he exerteth himself, and by ease he destroyeth many; and against the prince of princes he standeth — and ithout hand he is broken.
And the appearance of the evening and of the morning, that is told, is true; and thou, hide thou the vision, for [it is] after many days.’
And I, Daniel, have been, yea, I became sick [for] days, and I rise, and do the king’s ork, and am astonished at the appearance, and there is none understanding.
In the first year of Darius, son of Ahasuerus, of the seed of the Medes, ho hath been made king over the kingdom of the Chaldeans,

in the first year of his reign, I, Daniel, have understood by books the number of the years, (in that a ord of Jehovah hath been unto Jeremiah the prophet,) concerning the fulfilling of the astes of Jerusalem — seventy years;
and I set my face unto the Lord God, to seek [by] prayer and supplications, ith fasting, and sackcloth, and ashes.

And I pray to Jehovah my God, and confess, and say: ’I beseech Thee, O Lord God, the great and the fearful, keeping the covenant and the kindness to those loving Him, and to those keeping His commands;
