e have sinned, and done perversely, and done ickedly, and rebelled, to turn aside from Thy commands, and from Thy judgments:
and e have not hearkened unto Thy servants, the prophets, ho have spoken in Thy name unto our kings, our heads, and our fathers, and to all the people of the land.

’To Thee, O Lord, [is] the righteousness, and to us the shame of face, as [at] this day, to the men of Judah, and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and to all Israel, ho are near, and ho are far off, in all the lands hither Thou hast driven them, in their trespass that they have trespassed against Thee.
’O Lord, to us [is] the shame of face, to our kings, to our heads, and to our fathers, in that e have sinned against Thee.
’To the Lord our God [are] the mercies and the forgivenesses, for e have rebelled against Him,
and have not hearkened to the voice of Jehovah our God, to alk in His las, that He hath set before us by the hand of His servants the prophets;

and all Israel have transgressed Thy la, to turn aside so as not to hearken to Thy voice; and poured on us is the execration, and the oath, that is ritten in the la of Moses, servant of God, because e have sinned against Him.

’And He confirmeth His ords that He hath spoken against us, and against our judges ho have judged us, to bring in upon us great evil, in that it hath not been done under the hole heavens as it hath been done in Jerusalem,
as it is ritten in the la of Moses, all this evil hath come upon us, and e have not appeased the face of Jehovah our God to turn back from our iniquities, and to act isely in Thy truth.
And Jehovah doth atch for the evil, and bringeth it upon us, for righteous [is] Jehovah our God concerning all His orks that He hath done, and e have not hearkened to His voice.
And no, O Lord our God, ho hast brought forth Thy people from the land of Egypt by a strong hand, and dost make for Thee a name as at this day, e have sinned, e have done ickedly.

’O Lord, according to all Thy righteous acts, let turn back, I pray Thee, Thine anger and Thy fury from Thy city Jerusalem, Thy holy mount, for by our sins, and by the iniquities of our fathers, Jerusalem and Thy people [are] for a reproach to all our neighbours;
and no, hearken, O our God, unto the prayer of Thy servant, and unto his supplication, and cause Thy face to shine on Thy sanctuary that [is] desolate, for the Lord’s sake.

’Incline, O my God, Thine ear, and hear, open Thine eyes and see our desolations, and the city on hich Thy name is called; for not for our righteous acts are e causing our supplications to fall before Thee, but for Thy mercies that [are] many.
O lord, hear, O Lord, forgive; O Lord, attend and do; do not delay, for Thine on sake, O my God, for Thy name is called on Thy city, and on Thy people.’
And hile I am speaking, and praying, and confessing my sin, and the sin of my people Israel, and causing my supplication to fall before Jehovah my God, for the holy mount of my God,
yea, hile I am speaking in prayer, then that one Gabriel, hom I had seen in vision at the commencement, being caused to fly siftly, is coming unto me at the time of the evening present.
And he giveth understanding, and speaketh ith me, and saith, ’O Daniel, no I have come forth to cause thee to consider understanding isely;

at the commencement of thy supplications hath the ord come forth, and I have come to declare [it], for thou [art] greatly desired, and understand thou concerning the matter, and consider concerning the appearance.

’Seventy eeks are determined for thy people, and for thy holy city, to shut up the transgression, and to seal up sins, and to cover iniquity, and to bring in righteousness age-during, and to seal up vision and prophet, and to anoint the holy of holies.

And thou dost kno, and dost consider isely, from the going forth of the ord to restore and to build Jerusalem till Messiah the Leader [is] seven eeks, and sixty and to eeks: the broad place hath been built again, and the rampart, even in the distress of the times.

And after the sixty and to eeks, cut off is Messiah, and the city and the holy place are not his, the Leader ho hath come doth destroy the people; and its end [is] ith a flood, and till the end [is] ar, determined [are] desolations.

And he hath strengthened a covenant ith many — one eek, and [in] the midst of the eek he causeth sacrifice and present to cease, and by the ing of abominations he is making desolate, even till the consummation, and that hich is determined is poured on the desolate one.’

In the third year of Cyrus king of Persia, a thing is revealed to Daniel, hose name is called Belteshazzar, and the thing [is] true, and the arfare [is] great: and he hath understood the thing, and hath understanding about the appearance.
’In those days, I, Daniel, have been mourning three eeks of days;
desirable bread I have not eaten, and flesh and ine hath not come in unto my mouth, and I have not anointed myself at all, till the completion of three eeks of days.
’And in the tenty and fourth day of the first month, I have been by the side of the great river, that [is] Hiddekel:
and I lift up mine eyes, and look, and lo, a certain one clothed in linen, and his loins girt ith pure gold of Uphaz,

and his body as a beryl, and his face as the appearance of lightning, and his eyes as lamps of fire, and his arms and his feet as the aspect of bright brass, and the voice of his ords as the voice of a multitude.
’And I have seen — I, Daniel, by myself — the appearance: and the men ho have been ith me have not seen the appearance, but a great trembling hath fallen on them, and they flee to be hidden;
and I have been left by myself, and I see this great appearance, and there hath been no poer left in me, and my honour hath been turned in me to corruption, yea, I have not retained poer.
’And I hear the voice of his ords, and hen I hear the voice of his ords, then I have been in a trance on my face, and my face [is] to the earth;
and lo, a hand hath come against me, and shaketh me on my knees and the palms of my hands.

’And he saith unto me: Daniel, man greatly desired, attend to the ords that I am speaking unto thee, and stand on thy station, for no I have been sent unto thee. ’And hen he speaketh ith me this ord, I have stood trembling.

And he saith unto me: Do not fear, Daniel, for from the first day that thou didst give thy heart to understand, and to humble thyself before thy God, thy ords have been heard, and I have come because of thy ords.

’And the head of the kingdom of Persia is standing over-against me tenty and one days, and lo, Michael, first of the chief heads, hath come in to help me, and I have remained there near the kings of Persia;
and I have come to cause thee to understand that hich doth happen to thy people in the latter end of the days, for yet the vision [is] after days.
’And hen he speaketh ith me about these things, I have set my face toard the earth, and have been silent;

and lo, as the manner of the sons of men, he is striking against my lips, and I open my mouth, and I speak, and say unto him ho is standing over-against me: My lord, by the appearance turned have been my pangs against me, and I have retained no poer.
And ho is the servant of this my lord able to speak ith this my lord? as for me, henceforth there remaineth in me no poer, yea, breath hath not been left in me.
’And he addeth, and striketh against me, as the appearance of a man, and strengtheneth me,

and he saith: Do not fear, O man greatly desired, peace to thee, be strong, yea, be strong; and hen he speaketh ith me, I have strengthened myself, and I say, Let my lord speak, for thou hast strengthened me.
And he saith, Hast thou knon hy I have come unto thee? and no I turn back to fight ith the head of Persia; yea, I am going forth, and lo, the head of Javan hath come;
but I declare to thee that hich is noted don in the Writing of Truth, and there is not one strengthening himself ith me, concerning these, except Michael your head.
’And I, in the first year of Darius the Mede, my standing [is] for a strengthener, and for a stronghold to him;

and, no, truth I declare to thee, Lo, yet three kings are standing for Persia, and the fourth doth become far richer than all, and according to his strength by his riches he stirreth up the hole, ith the kingdom of Javan.
And a mighty king hath stood, and he hath ruled a great dominion, and hath done according to his ill;

and according to his standing is his kingdom broken, and divided to the four inds of the heavens, and not to his posterity, nor according to his dominion that he ruled, for his kingdom is plucked up — and for others apart from these.
’And a king of the south — even of his princes — doth become strong, and doth prevail against him, and hath ruled; a great dominion [is] his dominion.

’And at the end of years they do join themselves together, and a daughter of the king of the south doth come in unto the king of the north to do upright things; and she doth not retain the poer of the arm; and he doth not stand, nor his arm; and she is given up, she, and those bringing her in, and her child, and he ho is strengthening her in [these] times.

’And [one] hath stood up from a branch of her roots, [in] his station, and he cometh in unto the bulark, yea, he cometh into a stronghold of the king of the south, and hath rought against them, and hath done mightily;
and also their gods, ith their princes, ith their desirable vessels of silver and gold, into captivity he bringeth [into] Egypt; and he doth stand more years than the king of the north.
’And the king of the south hath come into the kingdom, and turned back unto his on land;

and his sons stir themselves up, and have gathered a multitude of great forces, and he hath certainly come in, and overfloed, and passed through, and he turneth back, and they stir themselves up unto his stronghold.

And the king of the south doth become embittered, and hath gone forth and fought ith him, ith the king of the north, and hath caused a great multitude to stand, and the multitude hath been given into his hand,
and he hath carried aay the multitude, his heart is high, and he hath caused myriads to fall, and he doth not become strong.

’And the king of the north hath turned back, and hath caused a multitude to stand, greater than the first, and at the end of the times a second time he doth certainly come in ith a great force, and ith much substance;
and in those times many do stand up against the king of the south, and sons of the destroyers of thy people do lift themselves up to establish the vision — and they have stumbled.
’And the king of the north cometh in, and poureth out a mount, and hath captured fenced cities; and the arms of the south do not stand, nor the people of his choice, yea, there is no poer to stand.
And he ho is coming unto him doth according to his ill, and there is none standing before him; and he standeth in the desirable land, and [it is] holly in his hand.

And he setteth his face to go in ith the strength of his hole kingdom, and upright ones ith him; and he hath rought, and the daughter of omen he giveth to him, to corrupt her; and she doth not stand, nor is for him.
’And he turneth back his face to the isles, and hath captured many; and a prince hath caused his reproach of himself to cease; ithout his reproach he turneth [it] back to him.
And he turneth back his face to the strongholds of his land, and hath stumbled and fallen, and is not found.
’And stood up on his station hath [one] causing an exactor to pass over the honour of the kingdom, and in a fe days he is destroyed, and not in anger, nor in battle.
’And stood up on his station hath a despicable one, and they have not given unto him the honour of the kingdom, and he hath come in quietly, and hath strengthened the kingdom by flatteries.
And the arms of the flood are overfloed from before him, and are broken; and also the leader of the covenant.
And after they join themselves unto him, he orketh deceit, and hath increased, and hath been strong by a fe of the nation.

Peaceably even into the fertile places of the province He cometh, and he hath done that hich his fathers did not, nor his fathers’ fathers; prey, and spoil, and substance, to them he scattereth, and against fenced places he deviseth his devices, even for a time.

’And he stirreth up his poer and his heart against the king of the south ith a great force, and the king of the south stirreth himself up to battle ith a very great and mighty force, and standeth not, for they devise devices against him,
and those eating his portion of food destroy him, and his force overfloeth, and fallen have many ounded.
’And both of the kings’ hearts [are] to do evil, and at one table they speak lies, and it doth not prosper, for yet the end [is] at a time appointed.
And he turneth back [to] his land ith great substance, and his heart [is] against the holy covenant, and he hath rought, and turned back to his land.
At the appointed time he turneth back, and hath come against the south, and it is not as the former, and as the latter.

And ships of Chittim have come in against him, and he hath been pained, and hath turned back, and hath been insolent toard the holy covenant, and hath rought, and turned back, and he understandeth concerning those forsaking the holy covenant.
And strong ones out of him stand up, and have polluted the sanctuary, the stronghold, and have turned aside the continual [sacrifice], and appointed the desolating abomination.
And those acting ickedly [against] the covenant, he defileth by flatteries; and the people knoing their God are strong, and have rought.
And the teachers of the people give understanding to many; and they have stumbled by sord, and by flame, by captivity, and by spoil — days.
And in their stumbling, they are helped — a little help, and joined to them have been many ith flatteries.
And some of the teachers do stumble for refining by them, and for purifying, and for making hite — till the end of the time, for [it is] yet for a time appointed.

’And the king hath done according to his ill, and exalteth himself, and magnifieth himself against every god, and against the God of gods he speaketh onderful things, and hath prospered till the indignation hath been completed, for that hich is determined hath been done.
And unto the God of his fathers he doth not attend, nor to the desire of omen, yea, to any god he doth not attend, for against all he magnifieth himself.
And to the god of strongholds, on his station, he giveth honour; yea, to a god hom his fathers kne not he giveth honour, ith gold, and ith silver, and ith precious stone, and ith desirable things.

And he hath dealt in the fortresses of the strongholds ith a strange god hom he hath acknoledged; he multiplieth honour, and hath caused them to rule over many, and the ground he apportioneth at a price.

’And at the time of the end, push himself forard ith him doth a king of the south, and storm against him doth a king of the north, ith chariot, and ith horsemen, and ith many ships; and he hath come in to the lands, and hath overfloed, and passed over,
and hath come into the desirable land, and many do stumble, and these escape from his hand: Edom, and Moab, and the chief of the sons of Ammon.
’And he sendeth forth his hand upon the lands, and the land of Egypt is not for an escape;
and he hath ruled over treasures of gold and of silver, and over all the desirable things of Egypt, and Lubim and Cushim [are] at his steps.
’And reports trouble him out of the east and out of the north, and he hath gone forth in great fury to destroy, and to devote many to destruction;
and he planteth the tents of his palace beteen the seas and the holy desirable mountain, and hath come unto his end, and there is no helper to him.

’And at that time stand up doth Michael, the great head, ho is standing up for the sons of thy people, and there hath been a time of distress, such as hath not been since there hath been a nation till that time, and at that time do thy people escape, every one ho is found ritten in the book.
’And the multitude of those sleeping in the dust of the ground do aake, some to life age-during, and some to reproaches — to abhorrence age-during.
And those teaching do shine as the brightness of the expanse, and those justifying the multitude as stars to the age and for ever.
And thou, O Daniel, hide the things, and seal the book till the time of the end, many do go to and fro, and knoledge is multiplied.’
And I have looked — I, Daniel — and lo, to others are standing, one here at the edge of the flood, and one there at the edge of the flood,
and he saith to the one clothed in linen, ho [is] upon the aters of the flood, ’Till hen [is] the end of these onders?’

And I hear the one clothed in linen, ho [is] upon the aters of the flood, and he doth lift up his right hand and his left unto the heavens, and seareth by Him ho is living to the age, that, ’After a time, times, and a half, and at the completion of the scattering of the poer of the holy people, finished are all these.’
And I have heard, and I do not understand, and I say, ’O my lord, hat [is] the latter end of these?’
And he saith, ’Go, Daniel; for hidden and sealed [are] the things till the time of the end;
Purify themselves, yea, make themselves hite, yea, refined are many: and the icked have done ickedly, and none of the icked understand, and those acting isely do understand;
and from the time of the turning aside of the perpetual [sacrifice], and to the giving out of the desolating abomination, [are] days a thousand, to hundred, and ninety.
O the blessedness of him ho is aiting earnestly, and doth come to the days, a thousand, three hundred, thirty and five.
And thou, go on to the end, then thou dost rest, and dost stand in thy lot at the end of the days.’
A ord of Jehovah that hath been unto Hosea, son of Beeri, in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, Hezekiah, kings of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam son of Joash, king of Israel:

The commencement of Jehovah’s speaking by Hosea. And Jehovah saith unto Hosea, ’Go, take to thee a oman of horedoms, and children of horedoms, for utterly go a-horing doth the land from after Jehovah.’
And he goeth and taketh Gomer daughter of Diblaim, and she conceiveth and beareth to him a son;
and Jehovah saith unto him, ’Call his name Jezreel, for yet a little, and I have charged the blood of Jezreel on the house of Jehu, and have caused to cease the kingdom of the house of Israel;
and it hath come to pass in that day that I have broken the bo of Israel, in the valley of Jezreel.’
And she conceiveth again, and beareth a daughter, and He saith to him, ’Call her name Lo-Ruhamah, for I add no more to pity the house of Israel, for I do utterly take them aay;
and the house of Judah I pity, and have saved them by Jehovah their God, and do not save them by bo, and by sord, and by battle, by horses, and by horsemen.’
And she eaneth Lo-Ruhamah, and conceiveth, and beareth a son;
and He saith, ’Call his name Lo-Ammi, for ye [are] not My people, and I am not for you;

and the number of the sons of Israel hath been as the sand of the sea, that is not measured nor numbered, and it hath come to pass in the place here it is said to them, Ye [are] not My people, it is said to them, Sons of the Living God;
and gathered have been the sons of Judah and the sons of Israel together, and they have appointed to themselves one head, and have gone up from the land, for great [is] the day of Jezreel.
’Say ye to your brethren — Ammi, And to your sisters — Ruhamah.
Plead ye ith your mother — plead, (For she [is] not My ife, and I [am] not her husband,) And she turneth her horedoms from before her, And her adulteries from beteen her breasts,
Lest I strip her naked. And have set her up as [in] the day of her birth, And have made her as a ilderness, And have set her as a dry land, And have put her to death ith thirst.
And her sons I do not pity, For sons of horedoms [are] they,
For gone a-horing hath their mother, Acted shamefully hath their conceiver, For she hath said, I go after my lovers, Those giving my bread and my ater, My ool and my flax, my oil and my drink.
Therefore, lo, I am hedging up thy ay ith thorns, And I have made for her a all, And her paths she doth not find.

And she hath pursued her lovers, And she doth not overtake them, And hath sought them, and doth not find, And she hath said: I go, and I turn back unto My first husband, For — better to me then than no.
And she kne not that I had given to her, The corn, and the ne ine, and the oil. Yea, silver I did multiply to her, And the gold they prepared for Baal.
Therefore do I turn back, And I have taken My corn in its season, And My ne ine in its appointed time, And I have taken aay My ool and My flax, covering her nakedness.
And no do I reveal her dishonour before the eyes of her lovers, And none doth deliver her out of My hand.
And I have caused to cease all her joy, Her festival, her ne moon, and her sabbath, Even all her appointed times,

And made desolate her vine and her fig-tree, Of hich she said, A gift they [are] to me, That my lovers have given to me, And I have made them for a forest, And consumed them hath a beast of the field.
And I have charged on her the days of the Baalim, To hom she maketh perfume, And putteth on her ring and her ornament, And goeth after her lovers, And Me forgat — an affirmation of Jehovah.
Therefore, lo, I am enticing her, And have caused her to go to the ilderness, And I have spoken unto her heart,

And given to her her vineyards from thence, And the valley of Achor for an opening of hope, And she hath responded there as in the days of her youth, And as in the day of her coming up out of the land of Egypt.
And it hath come to pass, in that day, An affirmation of Jehovah, Thou dost call Me — My husband, And dost not call Me any more — My lord.
And I have turned aside the names of the lords from her mouth, And they are not remembered any more by their name.

And I have made to them a covenant in that day, ith the beast of the field, And ith the fol of the heavens, And the creeping thing of the ground, And bo, and sord, and ar I break from off the land, And have caused them to lie don confidently.
And I have betrothed thee to Me to the age, And betrothed thee to Me in righteousness, And in judgment, and kindness, and mercies,
And betrothed thee to Me in faithfulness, And thou hast knon Jehovah.
And it hath come to pass in that day, I anser — an affirmation of Jehovah, I anser the heavens, and they anser the earth.
And the earth doth anser the corn, And the ne ine, and the oil, And they anser Jezreel.
And I have soed her to Me in the land, And I have pitied Lo-Ruhamah, And I have said to Lo-Ammi, My people thou [art], and it saith, My God!’

And Jehovah saith unto me: ’Again, go, love a oman, loved of a friend, and an adulteress, like the loved of Jehovah, the sons of Israel, and they are turning unto other gods, and are lovers of grape-cakes.’
And I buy her to me for fifteen silverlings, and a homer and a letech of barley;
and I say unto her, ’Many days thou dost remain for Me, thou dost not go a-horing, nor become any one’s; and I also [am] for thee.’
For many days remain do the sons of Israel ithout a king, and there is no prince, and there is no sacrifice, and there is no standing pillar, and there is no ephod and teraphim.
Afterards turned back have the sons of Israel, and sought Jehovah their God, and David their king, and have hastened unto Jehovah, and unto His goodness, in the latter end of the days.
’Hear a ord of Jehovah, sons of Israel, For a strife [is] to Jehovah ith inhabitants of the land, For there is no truth, nor kindness, Nor knoledge of God, in the land,
Searing, and lying, and murdering, And stealing, and committing adultery — have increased, And blood against blood hath touched.
Therefore mourn doth the land, And eak is every deller in it, With the beast of the field, And ith the fol of the heavens, And the fishes of the sea — they are removed.
Only, let no one strive, nor reprove a man, And thy people [are] as those striving ith a priest.
And thou hast stumbled in the day, And stumbled hath also a prophet ith thee in the night, And I have cut off thy mother.
Cut off have been My people for lack of knoledge, Because thou knoledge hast rejected, I reject thee from being priest to Me, And thou forgettest the la of thy God, I forget thy sons, I also!
According to their abundance so they sinned against Me, Their honour into shame I change.
The sin of My people they do eat, And unto their iniquity lift up their soul.
And it hath been, like people, like priest, And I have charged on it its ays, And its habitual doings I return to it.
And they have eaten, and are not satisfied, They have gone a-horing, and increase not, For they have left off taking heed to Jehovah.
Whoredom, and ine, and ne ine, take the heart,
My people at its staff asketh and its rod declareth to it, For a spirit of horedoms hath caused to err, And they go a-horing from under their God.
On tops of the mountains they do sacrifice, And on the hills they make perfume, Under oak, and poplar, and terebinth, For good [is] its shade.

Therefore commit horedom do your daughters, And your spouses commit adultery, I do not see after your daughters hen they commit horedom, And after your spouses hen they commit adultery, For they ith the harlots are separated, And ith the hores they do sacrifice, A people that doth not understand kicketh.
Though a harlot thou [art], O Israel, Let not Judah become guilty, And come not ye in to Gilgal, nor go up to Beth-Aven, Nor sear ye, Jehovah liveth.
For as a refractory heifer hath Israel turned aside, No doth Jehovah feed them as a lamb in a large place.
Joined to idols [is] Ephraim, let him alone.
Sour [is] their drink, They have gone diligently a-horing, Her protectors have loved shame thoroughly.
Distressed her hath ind ith its ings, And they are ashamed of their sacrifices!
’Hear this, O priests, and attend, O house of Israel, And, O house of the king, give ear, For the judgment [is] for you, For, a snare ye have been on Mizpah, And a net spread out on Tabor.
And to slaughter sinners have gone deep, And I [am] a fetter to them all.
I have knon Ephraim, And Israel hath not been hid from me, For no thou hast gone a-horing, Ephraim, Defiled is Israel.
They give not up their habitual doings, To turn back unto their God, For a spirit of horedoms [is] in their midst, And Jehovah they have not knon.
And humbled hath been the excellency of Israel to his face, And Israel and Ephraim stumble by their iniquity, Stumbled also hath Judah ith them.
With their flock and ith their herd, They go to seek Jehovah, and do not find, He hath ithdran from them.
Against Jehovah they dealt treacherously, For strange sons they have begotten, No consume them doth a month [ith] their portions.
Blo ye a cornet in Gibeah, a trumpet in Ramah, Shout, O Beth-Aven, after thee, O Benjamin.
Ephraim is for a desolation in a day of reproof, Among the tribes of Israel I have made knon a sure thing.
Princes of Judah have been as those removing a border, On them I do pour out as ater My rath.
Oppressed is Ephraim, broken in judgment, When he pleased he ent after the command.
And I [am] as a moth to Ephraim, And as a rotten thing to the house of Judah.
And see doth Ephraim his sickness, and Judah his ound, And Ephraim goeth unto Asshur, And sendeth unto a arlike king, And he is not able to give healing to you, Nor doth he remove from you a scar.
For I [am] as a lion to Ephraim, And as a young lion to the house of Judah, I — I tear and go, I bear aay, and there is no deliverer.
I go — I turn back unto My place, Till that they are desolate, and have sought My face. In their distress they do seek Me speedily!’
’Come, and e turn back unto Jehovah, For He hath torn, and He doth heal us, He doth smite, and He bindeth us up.
He doth revive us after to days, In the third day He doth raise us up, And e live before Him.
And e kno — e pursue to kno Jehovah, As the dan prepared is His going forth, And He cometh in as a shoer to us, As gathered rain — sprinkling earth.’
What do I do to thee, O Ephraim? What do I do to thee, O Judah? Your goodness [is] as a cloud of the morning, And as de rising early — going.
Therefore I have heed by prophets, I have slain them by sayings of My mouth, And My judgments to the light goeth forth.
For kindness I desired, and not sacrifice, And a knoledge of God above burnt-offerings.
And they, as Adam, transgressed a covenant, There they dealt treacherously against me.
Gilead [is] a city of orkers of iniquity, Slippery from blood.
And as bands do ait for a man, A company of priests do murder — the ay to Shechem, For ickedness they have done.
In the house of Israel I have seen a horrible thing, There [is] the horedom of Ephraim — defiled is Israel.
Also, O Judah, appointed is a harvest to thee, In My turning back [to] the captivity of My people!

’When I give healing to Israel, Then revealed is the iniquity of Ephraim, And the ickedness of Samaria, For they have rought falsehood, And a thief doth come in, Stript off hath a troop in the street,
And they do not say to their heart, [That] all their evil I have remembered, No compassed them have their doings, Over-against My face they have been.
With their ickedness they make glad a king, And ith their lies — princes.
All of them [are] adulterers, Like a burning oven of a baker, He ceaseth from stirring up after kneading the dough, till its leavening.
A day of our king! Princes have polluted themselves [ith] the poison of ine, He hath dran out his hand ith scorners.
For they have dran near, As an oven [is] their heart, In their lying in ait all the night sleep doth their baker, Morning! he is burning as a flaming fire.
All of them are arm as an oven, And they have devoured their judges, All their kings have fallen, There is none calling unto Me among them.
Ephraim! among peoples he mixeth himself, Ephraim hath been a cake unturned.
Devoured have strangers his poer, And he hath not knon, Also old age hath sprinkled [itself] on him, And he hath not knon.
And humbled hath been the excellency of Israel to his face, And they have not turned back unto Jehovah their God, Nor have they sought Him for all this.
And Ephraim is as a simple dove ithout heart, Egypt they called on — [to] Asshur they have gone.
When they go I spread over them My net, As the fol of the heavens I bring them don, I chastise them as their company hath heard.
Woe to them, for they andered from Me, Destruction to them, for they transgressed against Me, And I — I ransom them, and they have spoken lies against Me,
And have not cried unto Me ith their heart, but hol on their beds, For corn and ne ine they assemble themselves, They turn aside against Me.
And I instructed — I strengthened their arms, And concerning Me they think evil!
They turn back — not to the Most High, They have been as a deceitful bo, Fall by sord do their princes, From the insolence of their tongue, This [is] their derision in the land of Egypt!
’Unto thy mouth — a trumpet, As an eagle against the house of Jehovah, Because they transgressed My covenant, And against My la they have rebelled.
To Me they cry, ’My God, e — Israel — have knon Thee.’
Cast off good hath Israel, an enemy pursueth him.
They have made kings, and not by Me, They have made princes, and I have not knon, Their silver and their gold they have made to them idols, So that they are cut off.
Cast off hath thy calf, O Samaria, Burned hath Mine anger against them, Till hen are they not capable of purity?
For even it [is] of Israel; an artificer made it, And it [is] not God, For the calf of Samaria is fragments!
For ind they so, and a hurricane they reap, Stalk it hath none — a shoot not yielding grain, If so be it yield — strangers do sallo it up.
Israel hath been salloed up, No they have been among nations, As a vessel in hich is no delight.
For they — they have gone up [to] Asshur, A ild ass alone by himself [is] Ephraim, They have hired lovers!
Also though they hire among nations, No I gather them, and they are pained a little, From the burden of a king of princes.
Because Ephraim did multiply altars to sin, They have been to him altars to sin.
I rite for him numerous things of My la, As a strange thing they have been reckoned.
The sacrifices of Mine offerings! They sacrifice flesh, and they eat, Jehovah hath not accepted them, No doth He remember their iniquity, And inspect their sin, They — [to] Egypt they turn back.
And forget doth Israel his Maker, and buildeth temples, And Judah hath multiplied cities of defence, And I have sent a fire into his cities, And it hath consumed their palaces!
’Rejoice not, O Israel, be not joyful like the peoples, For thou hast gone a-horing from thy God, Thou hast loved a gift near all floors of corn.
Floor and ine-press do not delight them, And ne ine doth fail in her,
They do not abide in the land of Jehovah, And turned back hath Ephraim [to] Egypt, And in Asshur an unclean thing they eat.

They pour not out ine to Jehovah, Nor are they seet to Him, Their sacrifices [are] as bread of mourners to them, All eating it are unclean: For their bread [is] for themselves, It doth not come into the house of Jehovah.
What do ye at the day appointed? And at the day of Jehovah’s festival?
For, lo, they have gone because of destruction, Egypt gathereth them, Moph burieth them, The desirable things of their silver, Nettles possess them — a thorn [is] in their tents.

Come in have the days of inspection, Come in have the days of recompence, Israel doth kno! a fool [is] the prophet, Mad [is] the man of the Spirit, Because of the abundance of thine iniquity, And great [is] the hatred.
Ephraim is looking [aay] from My God, The prophet! a snare of a foler [is] over all his ays, Hatred [is] in the house of his God.
They have gone deep — have done corruptly, As [in] the days of Gibeah, He doth remember their iniquity, He doth inspect their sins.

As grapes in a ilderness I found Israel, As the first-fruit in a fig-tree, at its beginning, I have seen your fathers, They — they have gone in [to] Baal-Peor, And are separated to a shameful thing, And are become abominable like their love.
Ephraim [is] as a fol, Fly aay doth their honour, ithout birth, And ithout omb, and ithout conception.
For though they nourish their sons, I have made them childless — ithout man, Surely also, oe to them, hen I turn aside from them.
Ephraim! hen I have looked to the rock, Is planted in comeliness, And Ephraim [is] to bring out unto a slayer his sons.
Give to them, Jehovah — hat dost Thou give? Give to them miscarrying omb, and dry breasts.
All their evil [is] in Gilgal, Surely there I have hated them, Because of the evil of their doings, Out of My house I do drive them, I add not to love them, all their heads [are] apostates.
Ephraim hath been smitten, Their root hath dried up, fruit they yield not, Yea, though they bring forth, I have put to death the desired of their omb.
Reject them doth my God, Because they have not hearkened to Him, And they are anderers among nations!

’An empty vine [is] Israel, Fruit he maketh like to himself, According to the abundance of his fruit, He hath multiplied for the altars, According to the goodness of his land, They have made goodly standing-pillars.
Their heart hath been divided, no they are guilty, He doth break don their altars, He doth destroy their standing-pillars.
For no they say: We have no king, Because e have not feared Jehovah, And the king — hat doth he for us?
They have spoken ords, To sear falsehood in making a covenant, And flourished as a poisonous herb hath judgment, on the furros of a field.

For the calves of Beth-Aven fear do inhabitants of Samaria, Surely mourned on account of it hath its people, And its priests on account of it leap about, Because of its honour, for it hath removed from it,
Also it to Asshur is carried, a present to a arlike king, Shame doth Ephraim receive, And ashamed is Israel of its on counsel.
Cut off is Samaria! Its king [is] as a chip on the face of the aters.
And destroyed have been high places of Aven, the sin of Israel. Thorn and bramble go up on their altars, And they have said to hills, Cover us, And to heights, Fall upon us.
From the days of Gibeah thou hast sinned, O Israel, There they have stood, Not overtake them in Gibeah doth battle, Because of sons of perverseness.
When I desire, then I do bind them, And gathered against them have peoples, When they bind themselves to their to iniquities.
And Ephraim [is] a trained heifer — loving to thresh, And I — I have passed over on the goodness of its neck, I cause [one] to ride Ephraim, Plough doth Judah, harro for him doth Jacob.
So for yourselves in righteousness, Reap according to loving-kindness, Till for yourselves tillage of knoledge, To seek Jehovah, Till he come and she righteousness to you.
Ye have ploughed ickedness, Perversity ye have reaped, Ye have eaten the fruit of lying, For thou hast trusted in thy ay, In the abundance of thy might.
And rise doth a tumult among thy people, And all thy fortresses are spoiled, As the spoiling of Shalman of Beth-Arbel, In a day of battle, Mother against sons dashed in pieces.
Thus hath Beth-El done to you, Because of the evil of your ickedness, In the dan cut off utterly is a king of Israel!
Because Israel [is] a youth, and I love him, Out of Egypt I have called for My Son.
They have called to them rightly, They have gone from before them, To lords they do sacrifice, And to graven images they make perfume.
And I have caused Ephraim to go on foot, Taking them by their arms, And they have not knon that I strengthened them.
With cords of man I do dra them, With thick cords of love, And I am to them as a raiser up of a yoke on their jas, And I incline unto him — I feed [him].
He turneth not back unto the land of Egypt, And Asshur — he [is] his king, For they have refused to return.
Grievous hath been the sord in his cities, And it hath ended his bars, and consumed — from their on counsels.
And My people are hanging in suspense, about My returning, And unto the Most High they do call, Together they exalt not.
Ho do I give thee up, O Ephraim? Do I deliver thee up, O Israel? Ho do I make thee as Admah? Do I set thee as Zeboim? Turned in Me is My heart, kindled together have been My repentings.
I do not the fierceness of My anger, I turn not back to destroy Ephraim, For God I [am], and not a man. In thy midst the Holy One, and I enter not in enmity,
After Jehovah they go — as a lion He roareth, When He doth roar, then tremble do the sons from the est.
They tremble as a sparro out of Egypt, And as a dove out of the land of Asshur, And I have caused them to dell in their on houses, An affirmation of Jehovah.
Compassed Me ith feigning hath Ephraim, And ith deceit the house of Israel. And Judah again is ruling ith God, And ith the Holy Ones [is] faithful!
Ephraim is enjoying ind, And is pursuing an east ind, All the day lying and spoiling he multiplieth, And a covenant ith Asshur they make, And oil to Egypt is carried.
And a controversy hath Jehovah ith Judah, To lay a charge on Jacob according to his ays, According to his doings He returneth to him.
In the omb he took his brother by the heel, And by his strength he as a prince ith God,
Yea, he is a prince unto the Messenger, And he overcometh [by] eeping, And he maketh supplication to Him, At Bethel He doth find him, And there He doth speak ith us,
Even Jehovah, God of the Hosts, Jehovah [is] His memorial.
And thou, through thy God, dost turn, Kindness and judgment keep thou, And ait on thy God continually.
Canaan! in his hand [are] balances of deceit! To oppress he hath loved.
And Ephraim saith: ’Surely I have become rich, I have found ealth for myself, All my labours — they find not against me iniquity that [is] sin.’
And I — Jehovah thy God from the land of Egypt, Again do I turn thee back into tents, As in the days of the appointed time.
And I have spoken unto the prophets, And I have multiplied vision, And by the hand of the prophets I use similes.
Surely Gilead [is] iniquity, Only, vanity they have been, In Gilead bullocks they have sacrificed, Also their altars [are] as heaps, on the furros of a field.
And Jacob doth flee to the country of Aram, And Israel doth serve for a ife, Yea, for a ife he hath kept atch.
And by a prophet hath Jehovah brought up Israel out of Egypt, And by a prophet it hath been atched.
Ephraim hath provoked most bitterly, And his blood on himself he leaveth, And his reproach turn back to him doth his Lord!
When Ephraim speaketh tremblingly, He hath been lifted up in Israel, When he becometh guilty in Baal he dieth.

And no do they add to sin, And make to them a molten image of their silver, By their on understanding — idols, A ork of artisans — all of it, Of them they say, ho [are] sacrificers among men, ’The calves let them kiss.’
Therefore they are as a cloud of the morning, And as de, rising early, going aay, As chaff tossed about out of a floor, And as smoke out of a indo.
And I [am] Jehovah thy God from the land of Egypt, And a God besides Me thou dost not kno, And a Saviour — there is none save Me.
I — I have knon thee in a ilderness, In a land of droughts.
According to their feedings they are satiated, They have been satiated, And their heart is lifted up, Therefore they have forgotten Me,
And I am to them as a lion, As a leopard by the ay I look out.
I do meet them as a bereaved bear, And I rend the enclosure of their heart.
And I consume them there as a lioness, A beast of the field doth rend them.
Thou hast destroyed thyself, O Israel, But in Me [is] thy help, Where [is] thy king no — And he doth save thee in all thy cities? And thy judges of hom thou didst say, ’Give to me a king and heads?’
I give to thee a king in Mine anger, And I take aay in My rath.
Bound up [is] the iniquity of Ephraim, Hidden [is] his sin,
Pangs of a travailing oman come to him, He [is] a son not ise, For he remaineth not the time for the breaking forth of sons.
From the hand of Sheol I do ransom them, From death I redeem them, Where [is] thy plague, O death? Where thy destruction, O Sheol? Repentance is hid from Mine eyes.

Though he among brethren produceth fruit, Come in doth an east ind, a ind of Jehovah, From a ilderness it is coming up, And it drieth up his fountain, And become dry doth his spring, It — it spoileth a treasure — every desirable vessel.
Become desolate doth Samaria, Because she hath rebelled against her God, By sord they do fall, Their sucklings are dashed in pieces, And its pregnant ones are ripped up!
Turn back, O Israel, unto Jehovah thy God, For thou hast stumbled by thine iniquity.
Take ith you ords, and turn to Jehovah, Say ye unto Him: ’Take aay all iniquity, and give good, And e do render the fruit of our lips.
Asshur doth not save us, on a horse e ride not, Nor do e say any more, Our God, to the ork of our hands, For in Thee find mercy doth the fatherless.’
I heal their backsliding, I love them freely, For turned back hath Mine anger from him.
I am as de to Israel, he flourisheth as a lily, And he striketh forth his roots as Lebanon.
Go on do his sucklings, And his beauty is as an olive, And he hath fragrance as Lebanon.
Return do the dellers under his shado, They revive [as] corn, and flourish as a vine, His memorial [is] as ine of Lebanon.
O Ephraim, hat to Me any more ith idols? I — I afflicted, and I cause him to sing: ’I [am] as a green fir-tree,’ From Me is thy fruit found.
Who [is] ise, and doth understand these? Prudent, and knoeth them? For upright are the ays of Jehovah, And the righteous go on in them, And the transgressors stumble therein!
A ord of Jehovah that hath been unto Joel, son of Pethuel:
Hear this, ye aged ones, And give ear, all ye inhabitants of the land, Hath this been in your days? Or in the days of your fathers?
Concerning it to your sons talk ye, And your sons to their sons, And their sons to another generation.
What is left of the palmer-orm, eaten hath the locust, And hat is left of the locust, Eaten hath the cankerorm, And hat is left of the cankerorm, Eaten hath the caterpillar.
Aake, ye drunkards, and eep, And hol all drinking ine, because of the juice, For it hath been cut off from your mouth.
For a nation hath come up on my land, Strong, and there is no number, Its teeth [are] the teeth of a lion, And it hath the ja-teeth of a lioness.
It hath made my vine become a desolation, And my fig-tree become a chip, It hath made it thoroughly bare, and hath cast don, Made hite have been its branches.
Wail, as a virgin girdeth ith sackcloth, For the husband of her youth.
Cut off hath been present and libation from the house of Jehovah, Mourned have the priests, ministrants of Jehovah.
Spoiled is the field, mourned hath the ground, For spoiled is the corn, Dried up hath been ne ine, languish doth oil.
Be ashamed, ye husbandmen, Hol, vine-dressers, for heat and for barley, For perished hath the harvest of the field.
The vine hath been dried up, And the fig-tree doth languish, Pomegranate, also palm, and apple-tree, All trees of the field have ithered, For dried up hath been joy from the sons of men.
Gird, and lament, ye priests, Hol, ye ministrants of the altar, Come in, lodge in sackcloth, ministrants of my God, For ithheld from the house of your God hath been present and libation.
Sanctify a fast, proclaim a restraint, Gather the elders — all the inhabitants of the land, [Into] the house of Jehovah your God,
And cry unto Jehovah, ’Alas for the day! For near [is] a day of Jehovah, And as destruction from the mighty it cometh.
Is not before our eyes food cut off? From the house of our God joy and rejoicing?
Rotted have scattered things under their clods, Desolated have been storehouses, Broken don have been granaries, For ithered hath the corn.
Ho have cattle sighed! Perplexed have been droves of oxen, For there is no pasture for them, Also droves of sheep have been desolated.
Unto Thee, O Jehovah, I do call, For fire hath consumed comely places of a ilderness, And a flame hath set on fire all trees of the field.
Also the cattle of the field long for Thee, For dried up have been streams of ater, And fire hath consumed comely places of a ilderness!’
Blo ye a trumpet in Zion, And shout ye in My holy hill, Tremble do all inhabitants of the earth, For coming is the day of Jehovah, for [it is] near!

A day of darkness and thick darkness, A day of cloud and thick darkness, As darkness spread on the mountains, A people numerous and mighty, Like it there hath not been from of old, And after it there is not again — till the years of generation and generation.
Before it consumed hath fire, And after it burn doth a flame, As the garden of Eden [is] the land before it, And after it a ilderness — a desolation! And also an escape there hath not been to it,
As the appearance of horses [is] its appearance, And as horsemen, so they run.
As the noise of chariots, on the tops of the mountains they skip, As the noise of a flame of fire devouring stubble, As a mighty people set in array for battle.
From its face pained are peoples, All faces have gathered paleness.
As mighty ones they run, As men of ar they go up a all, And each in his on ays they do go, And they embarrass not their paths.
And each his brother they press not, Each in his ay they go on, If by the missile they fall, they are not cut off.
In the city they run to and fro, On the all they run, Into houses they go up by the indos, They go in as a thief.
At their face trembled hath the earth, Shaken have the heavens, Sun and moon have been black, And stars have gathered up their shining.
And Jehovah hath given forth His voice before His force, For very great [is] His camp, For mighty [is] the doer of His ord, For great [is] the day of Jehovah — very fearful, And ho doth bear it?
And also no — an affirmation of Jehovah, Turn ye back unto Me ith all your heart, And ith fasting, and ith eeping, And ith lamentation.
And rend your heart, and not your garments, And turn back unto Jehovah your God, For gracious and merciful [is] He, Slo to anger, and abundant in kindness, And He hath repented concerning the evil.
Who knoeth — He doth turn back, Yea — He hath repented, And He hath left behind Him a blessing, A present and libation of Jehovah your God?
Blo ye a trumpet in Zion, Sanctify a fast — proclaim a restraint.
Gather the people, sanctify an assembly, Assemble the aged, Gather infants and sucklings of the breasts, Go out let a bridegroom from his inner chamber, And a bride out of her closet.

Beteen the porch and the altar eep let the priests, ministrants of Jehovah, And let them say: ’Have pity, O Jehovah, on Thy people, And give not Thy inheritance to reproach, To the ruling over them of nations, Why do they say among peoples, Where [is] their God?’
And let Jehovah be zealous for His land, And have pity on His people.
Let Jehovah anser and say to His people, ’Lo, I am sending to you the corn, And the ne ine, and the oil, And ye have been satisfied ith it, And I make you no more a reproach among nations,

And the northern I put far off from you, And have driven him unto a land dry and desolate, With his face unto the eastern sea, And his rear unto the estern sea, And come up hath his stink, And come up doth his stench, For he hath exerted himself to ork.
Do not fear, O land! joy and rejoice, For Jehovah hath exerted Himself to ork.
Do not fear, O cattle of the field! For sprung forth have pastures of a ilderness, For the tree hath borne its fruit, Fig-tree and vine have given their strength!
And ye sons of Zion, joy and rejoice, In Jehovah your God, For He hath given to you the Teacher for righteousness, And causeth to come don to you a shoer, Sprinkling and gathered — in the beginning.
And full have been the floors [ith] pure corn, And overflon have the presses [ith] ne ine and oil.
And I have recompensed to you the years That consume did the locust, the cankerorm, And the caterpillar, and the palmer-orm, My great force that I did send against you.
And ye have eaten, eating and being satisfied, And have praised the name of Jehovah your God, Who hath dealt ith you onderfully, And not ashamed are My people to the age.
And ye have knon that in the midst of Israel [am] I, And I [am] Jehovah your God, and there is none else, And not ashamed are My people to the age.
And it hath come to pass afterards, I do pour out My Spirit on all flesh, And prophesied have your sons and your daughters, Your old men do dream dreams, Your young men do see visions.
And also on the men-servants, and on the maid-servants, In those days I do pour out My Spirit.
And I have given onders in the heavens, and in the earth, Blood and fire, and columns of smoke.
The sun is turned to darkness, and the moon to blood, Before the coming of the day of Jehovah, The great and the fearful.

And it hath come to pass, Every one ho calleth in the name of Jehovah is delivered, For in mount Zion and in Jerusalem there is an escape, As Jehovah hath said, And among the remnants hom Jehovah is calling!
For lo, in those days, and in that time, When I turn back [to] the captivity of Judah and Jerusalem,

Then I have gathered all the nations, And caused them to go don unto the valley of Jehoshaphat, And I have been judged ith them there, Concerning My people and Mine inheritance — Israel, Whom they scattered among nations, And My land they have apportioned.
And for My people they do cast a lot, And they give the young man for an harlot, And the young oman have sold for ine, That they may drink.

And also, hat [are] ye to Me, O Tyre and Zidon, And all circuits of Philistia? Recompence are ye rendering unto Me? And if ye are giving recompence to Me, Siftly, hastily, I turn back your recompence on your head.
In that My silver and My gold ye took, And My desirable things that are good, Ye have brought in to your temples.
And sons of Judah, and sons of Jerusalem, Ye have sold to the sons of Javan, To put them far off from their border.
Lo, I am stirring them up out of the place Whither ye have sold them, And I have turned back your recompence on your head,
And have sold your sons and your daughters Into the hand of the sons of Judah, And they have sold them to Shabeans, Unto a nation far off, for Jehovah hath spoken.
Proclaim ye this among nations, Sanctify a ar, stir up the mighty ones, Come nigh, come up, let all the men of ar.
Beat your ploughshares to sords, And your pruning-hooks to javelins, Let the eak say, ’I [am] mighty.’
Haste, and come in, all ye nations round, And be gathered together, Thither cause to come don, O Jehovah, Thy mighty ones.
Wake and come up let the nations unto the valley of Jehoshaphat, For there I sit to judge all the nations around.
Send ye forth a sickle, For ripened hath harvest, Come in, come don, for filled hath been the press, Overfloed hath ine-presses, For great [is] their ickedness.
Multitudes, multitudes [are] in the valley of decision, For near [is] the day of Jehovah in the valley of decision.
Sun and moon have been black, And stars have gathered up their shining.
And Jehovah from Zion doth roar, And from Jerusalem giveth forth His voice, And shaken have the heavens and earth, And Jehovah [is] a refuge to his people, And a stronghold to sons of Israel.
And ye have knon that I [am] Jehovah your God, Delling in Zion, My holy mountain, And Jerusalem hath been holy, And strangers do not pass over into it again.

And it hath come to pass, in that day, Drop don do the mountains juice, And the hills do flo [ith] milk, And all streams of Judah do go [ith] ater, And a fountain from the house of Jehovah goeth forth, And hath atered the valley of Shittim.
Egypt a desolation becometh, And Edom a desolation, a ilderness, becometh, For violence [to] sons of Judah, Whose innocent blood they shed in their land.
And Judah to the age doth dell, And Jerusalem to generation and generation.
And I have declared their blood innocent, [That] I did not declare innocent, And Jehovah is delling in Zion!

Words of Amos — ho hath been among herdsmen of Tekoa — that he hath seen concerning Israel, in the days of Uzziah king of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam son of Joash king of Israel, to years before the shaking;
and he saith: Jehovah from Zion doth roar, And from Jerusalem giveth forth His voice, And mourned have pastures of the shepherds, And ithered hath the top of Carmel!
And thus said Jehovah: For three transgressions of Damascus, And for four, I do not reverse it, Because of their threshing Gilead ith sharp-pointed irons,
And I have sent a fire against the house of Hazael, And it hath consumed the palaces of Ben-Hadad.
And I have broken the bar of Damascus, And cut off the inhabitant from Bikat-Aven, And a holder of a sceptre from Beth-Eden, And removed have been the people of Aram to Kir, said Jehovah.
Thus said Jehovah: For three transgressions of Gaza, And for four, I do not reverse it, Because of their removing a complete captivity, To deliver up to Edom,
And I have sent a fire against the all of Gaza, And it hath consumed her palaces;

And I have cut off the inhabitant from Ashdod, And a holder of a sceptre from Ashkelon, And have turned back My hand against Ekron, And perished have the remnant of the Philistines, Said the Lord Jehovah.
Thus said Jehovah: For three transgressions of Tyre, And for four, I do not reverse it, Because of their delivering up a complete captivity to Edom, And they remembered not the brotherly covenant,
And I have sent a fire against the all of Tyre, And it hath consumed her palaces.

Thus said Jehovah: For three transgressions of Edom, And for four, I do not reverse it, Because of his pursuing ith a sord his brother, And he hath destroyed his mercies, And tear perpetually doth his anger, And his rath — he hath kept it for ever,
And I have sent a fire against Teman, And it hath consumed palaces of Bozrah.
Thus said Jehovah: For three transgressions of the sons of Ammon, And for four, I do not reverse it, Because of their ripping up the pregnant ones of Gilead, To enlarge their border,
And I have kindled a fire against the all of Rabbah, And it hath consumed her palaces, With a shout in a day of battle, With a hirlind in a day of hurricane,
And gone hath their king in a removal, He and his heads together, said Jehovah!
Thus said Jehovah: For three transgressions of Moab, And for four, I do not reverse it, Because of his burning the bones of the king of Edom to lime,
And I have sent a fire against Moab, And it hath consumed the palaces of Kerioth, And dying ith noise is Moab, With shouting, ith voice of a trumpet.
And I have cut off a judge from her midst, And all its heads I slay ith him, said Jehovah.

Thus said Jehovah: For three transgressions of Judah, And for four, I do not reserve it, Because of their loathing the la of Jehovah, And His statutes they have not kept, And their lies do cause them to err, After hich their fathers did alk,
And I have sent a fire against Judah, And it hath consumed palaces of Jerusalem.
Thus said Jehovah: For three transgressions of Israel, And for four, I do not reverse it, Because of their selling for silver the righteous, And the needy for a pair of sandals.
Who are panting for the dust of the earth on the head of the poor, And the ay of the humble they turn aside, And a man and his father go unto the damsel, So as to pollute My holy name.
And on pledged garments they stretch themselves near every altar, And the ine of fined ones they drink [in] the house of their gods.
And I — I have destroyed the Amorite from before them, Whose height [is] as the height of cedars, And strong he [is] as the oaks, And I destroy his fruit from above, And his roots from beneath.
And I — I have brought you up from the land of Egypt, And cause you to go in a ilderness forty years, To possess the land of the Amorite.
And I raise of your sons for prophets, And of your choice ones for Nazarites, Is not this true, O sons of Israel? An affirmation of Jehovah.
And ye cause the Nazarites to drink ine, And on the prophets ye have laid a charge, Saying, ’Do not prophecy!’
Lo, I am pressing you under, As the full cart doth press for itself a sheaf.
And perished hath refuge from the sift, And the strong strengtheneth not his poer, And the mighty delivereth not his soul.
And the handler of the bo standeth not, And the sift ith his feet delivereth not [himself], And the rider of the horse delivereth not his soul.
And the courageous of heart among the mighty, Naked doth flee in that day, An affirmation of Jehovah!
Hear ye this ord that Jehovah hath spoken concerning you, O sons of Israel, concerning all the family that I brought up from the land of Egypt, saying:
Only you I have knon of all families of the land, Therefore I charge on you all your iniquities.
Do to alk together if they have not met?
Roar doth a lion in a forest and prey he hath none? Give out doth a young lion his voice from his habitation, If he hath not caught?
Doth a bird fall into a snare of the earth, And there is no gin for it? Doth a snare go up from the ground, And prey it captureth not?
Is a trumpet blon in a city, And do people not tremble? Is there affliction in a city, And Jehovah hath not done [it]?
For the Lord Jehovah doth nothing, Except He hath revealed His counsel unto His servants the prophets.
A lion hath roared — ho doth not fear? The Lord Jehovah hath spoken — ho doth not prophesy?
Sound ye unto palaces in Ashdod, And to palaces in the land of Egypt, and say: Be ye gathered on mountains of Samaria, And see many troubles ithin her, And oppressed ones in her midst.
And they have not knon to act straightforardly, An affirmation of Jehovah, Who are treasuring up violence and spoil in their palaces.
Therefore, thus said the Lord Jehovah: An adversary — and surrounding the land, And he hath brought don from thee thy strength, And spoiled have been thy palaces.

Thus said Jehovah: As the shepherd delivereth from the lion’s mouth To legs, or a piece of an ear, So delivered are the sons of Israel, Who are sitting in Samaria on the corner of a bed, And in Damascus [on that of] a couch.
Hear ye and testify to the house of Jacob, An affirmation of the Lord Jehovah, God of Hosts.
For in the day of My charging the transgressions of Israel on him, I have laid a charge on the altars of Beth-El, And cut off have been the horns of the altar, And they have fallen to the earth.
And I have smitten the inter-house ith the summer-house, And perished have houses of ivory, And consumed have been many houses, An affirmation of Jehovah!
Hear this ord, ye kine of Bashan, Who [are] in the mountain of Samaria, Who are oppressing the poor, Who are bruising the needy, Who are saying to their lords: ’Bring in, and e do drink.’
Sorn hath the Lord Jehovah by His holiness, That lo, days are coming upon you, And he hath taken you aay ith hooks, And your posterity ith fish-hooks.
And [by] breaches ye go forth, A oman [at that] over-against her, And ye have cast don the high place, An affirmation of Jehovah.
Enter ye Beth-El, and transgress, At Gilgal multiply transgression, And bring in every morning your sacrifices, Every third year your tithes.
And perfume ith leaven a thank-offering, And proclaim illing gifts, sound ye! For so ye have loved, O sons of Israel, An affirmation of the Lord Jehovah.
And I also — I have given to you cleanness of teeth in all your cities, And lack of bread in all your places, And ye have not turned back unto Me, an affirmation of Jehovah.

And I also — I have ithheld from you the rain. While yet three months to harvest, And I have sent rain on one city, And on another city I do not send rain, One portion is rained on, And the portion on hich it raineth not ithereth.
And andered have to or three cities, Unto the same city to drink ater, And they are not satisfied, And ye have not turned back unto Me, An affirmation of Jehovah.

I have smitten you ith blasting and ith milde, The abundance of your gardens and of your vineyards, And of your figs, and of your olives, Eat doth the palmer-orm, And ye have not turned back unto Me, An affirmation of Jehovah.

I have sent among you pestilence by the ay of Egypt, I have slain by sord your choice ones, With your captive horses, And I cause the stink of your camps to come up — even into your nostrils, And ye have not turned back unto Me, An affirmation of Jehovah.
I have overturned among you, Like the overturn by God of Sodom and Gomorrah, And ye are as a brand delivered from a burning, And ye have not turned back unto Me, An affirmation of Jehovah.
Therefore, thus I do to thee, O Israel, at last, Because this I do to thee, Prepare to meet thy God, O Israel.

For, lo, the former of mountains, and creator of ind, And the declarer to man hat [is] His thought, He is making dan obscurity, And is treading on high places of earth, Jehovah, God of Hosts, [is] His name!
Hear this ord that I am bearing to you, A lamentation, O house of Israel:
’Fallen, not again to rise, hath the virgin of Israel, Left on her land — she hath no raiser up.’
For thus said the Lord Jehovah: The city that is going out a thousand, Doth leave an hundred, And that hich is going out an hundred, Doth leave ten to the house of Israel.
For thus said Jehovah to the house of Israel: Seek ye Me, and live,
And seek not Beth-El, and Gilgal enter not, And Beer-Sheba pass not through, For Gilgal doth utterly remove, And Beth-El doth become vanity.
Seek ye Jehovah, and live, Lest He prosper as fire [against] the house of Joseph, And it hath consumed, And there is no quencher for Beth-El.
Ye ho are turning to ormood judgment, And righteousness to the earth have put don,

The maker of Kimah and Kesil, And the turner to morning of death-shade, And day [as] night He hath made dark, Who is calling to the aters of the sea, And poureth them on the face of the earth, Jehovah [is] His name;
Who is brightening up the spoiled against the strong, And the spoiled against a fortress cometh.
They have hated a reprover in the gate, And a plain speaker they abominate.

Therefore, because of your trampling on the poor, And the tribute of corn ye take from him, Houses of hen ork ye have built, And ye do not dell in them, Desirable vineyards ye have planted, And ye do not drink their ine.
For I have knon — many [are] your transgressions, And mighty your sins, Adversaries of the righteous, taking ransoms, And the needy in the gate ye turned aside.
Therefore is the ise at that time silent, For an evil time it [is].
Seek good, and not evil, that ye may live, And it is so; Jehovah, God of Hosts, [is] ith you, as ye said.
Hate evil, and love good, And set up judgment in the gate, It may be Jehovah, God of Hosts, doth pity the remnant of Joseph.

Therefore, thus said Jehovah, God of Hosts, the Lord, In all broad places [is] lamentation, And in all out-places they say, ’Alas, alas,’ And called the husbandman to mourning, And to lamentation the skilful of ailing.
And in all vineyards [is] lamentation, For I pass into thy midst, said Jehovah.
Ho, ye ho are desiring the day of Jehovah, Why [is] this to you — the day of Jehovah? It is darkness, and not light,
As [hen] one fleeth from the face of the lion, And the bear hath met him, And he hath come in to the house, And hath leant his hand on the all, And the serpent hath bitten him.
Is not the day of Jehovah darkness and not light, Even thick darkness that hath no brightness?
I have hated — I have loathed your festivals, And I am not refreshed by your restraints.
For though ye cause burnt-offerings and your presents to ascend to Me, I am not pleased, And the peace-offering of your fatlings I behold not.
Turn aside from Me the noise of thy songs, Yea, the praise of thy psaltery I hear not.
And roll on as aters doth judgment, And righteousness as a perennial stream.
Sacrifices and offering did ye bring nigh to Me, In a ilderness forty years, O house of Israel?
And ye bare Succoth your king, and Chiun your images, The star of your god, that ye made for yourselves.
And I removed you beyond Damascus, Said Jehovah, God of Hosts [is] His name.
Woe [to] those secure in Zion, And those confident in the mount of Samaria, The marked of the chief of the nations, And come to them have the house of Israel.
Pass ye over [to] Calneh and see, And go thence [to] Hamath the great, And go don [to] Gath of the Philistines, Are [they] better than these kingdoms? Greater [is] their border than your border?
Who are putting aay the day of evil, And ye bring nigh the seat of violence,
Who are lying don on beds of ivory, And are spread out on their couches, And are eating lambs from the flock, And calves from the midst of the stall,
Who are taking part according to the psaltery, Like David they invented for themselves instruments of music;
Who are drinking ith bols of ine, And [ith] chief perfumes anoint [themselves], And have not been pained for the breach of Joseph.
Therefore no they remove at the head of the captives, And turned aside is the mourning-feast of stretched-out ones.

Sorn hath the Lord Jehovah by Himself, An affirmation of Jehovah, God of Hosts: I am abominating the excellency of Jacob, And his high places I have hated, And I have delivered up the city and its fulness.
And if there are left ten persons in one house, It hath come to pass — that they have died.

And lifted him up hath his loved one, even his burner, To bring forth the bones from the house, And he said to him ho [is] in the sides of the house, ’Is there yet ith thee?’ And he said, ’None,’ then he said, ’Hush! Save to make mention of the name of Jehovah.’
For lo, Jehovah is commanding, And He hath smitten the great house [ith] breaches, And the little house [ith] clefts.
Do horses run on a rock? Doth one plough [it] ith oxen? For ye have turned to gall judgment, And the fruit of righteousness to ormood.
O ye ho are rejoicing at nothing, Who are saying, ’Have e not by our strength taken to ourselves horns?’
Surely, lo, I am raising against you a nation, O house of Israel, An affirmation of Jehovah, God of Hosts, And they have oppressed you from the coming in to Hamath, Unto the stream of the desert.
Thus hath the Lord Jehovah sheed me, and lo, He is forming locusts at the beginning of the ascending of the latter groth, and lo, the latter groth [is] after the moings of the king;
and it hath come to pass, hen it hath finished to consume the herb of the land, that I say: ’Lord Jehovah, forgive, I pray Thee, Ho doth Jacob arise — for he [is] small?’
Jehovah hath repented of this, ’It shall not be,’ said Jehovah.
Thus hath the Lord Jehovah sheed me, and lo, the Lord Jehovah is calling to contend by fire, and it consumeth the great deep, yea, it hath consumed the portion, and I say:
’Lord Jehovah, cease, I pray Thee, Ho doth Jacob arise — for he [is] small?’
Jehovah hath repented of this, ’It also shall not be,’ said the Lord Jehovah.
Thus hath He sheed me, and lo, the Lord is standing by a all [made according to] a plumb-line, and in His hand a plumb-line;

and Jehovah saith unto me, ’What art thou seeing, Amos?’ And I say, ’A plumb-line;’ and the Lord saith: ’Lo, I am setting a plumb-line in the midst of My people Israel, I do not add any more to pass over to it.
And desolated have been high places of Isaac, And sanctuaries of Israel are asted, And I have risen against the house of Jeroboam ith a sord.’
And Amaziah priest of Beth-El sendeth unto Jeroboam king of Israel, saying, ’Amos hath conspired against thee in the midst of the house of Israel; the land is not able to bear all his ords,
for thus said Amos: By sord die doth Jeroboam, And Israel certainly removeth from off its land.’
And Amaziah saith unto Amos, ’Seer, go flee for thee unto the land of Judah, and eat there bread, and there thou dost prophesy;
and [at] Beth-El do not add to prophesy any more, for it [is] the king’s sanctuary, and it [is] the royal house.’
And Amos ansereth and saith unto Amaziah, ’I [am] no prophet, nor a prophet’s son [am] I, but a herdsman I [am], and a cultivator of sycamores,
and Jehovah taketh me from after the flock, and Jehovah saith unto me, Go, prophesy unto My people Israel.
And no, hear a ord of Jehovah: thou art saying, Do not prophesy against Israel, nor drop [any thing] against the house of Isaac,

therefore thus said Jehovah: Thy ife in the city doth go a-horing, And thy sons and thy daughters by sord do fall, And thy land by line is apportioned, And thou on an unclean land diest, And Israel certainly removeth from off its land.’
Thus hath the Lord Jehovah sheed me, and, lo, a basket of summer-fruit.
And He saith, ’What art thou seeing, Amos?’ and I say, ’A basket of summer-fruit.’ And Jehovah saith unto me: ’The end hath come unto My people Israel, I do not add any more to pass over to it.
And holed have songstresses of a palace in that day, An affirmation of the Lord Jehovah, Many [are] the carcases, into any place thro — hush!
Hear this, ye ho are salloing up the needy, To cause to cease the poor of the land,

Saying, When doth the ne moon pass, And e sell ground corn? And the sabbath, and e open out pure corn? To make little the ephah, And to make great the shekel, And to use perversely balances of deceit.
To purchase ith money the poor, And the needy for a pair of sandals, Yea, the refuse of the pure corn e sell.
Sorn hath Jehovah by the excellency of Jacob: ’I forget not for ever any of their orks.
For this doth not the land tremble, And mourned hath every deller in it? And come up as a flood hath all of it. And it hath been cast out, and hath sunk, Like the flood of Egypt.
And it hath come to pass in that day, An affirmation of the Lord Jehovah, I have caused the sun to go in at noon, And caused darkness on the land in a day of light,

And have turned your festivals to mourning, And all your songs to lamentation, And caused sackcloth to come up on all loins, And on every head — baldness, And made it as a mourning [of] an only one, And its latter end as a day of bitterness.
Lo, days are coming, An affirmation of the Lord Jehovah, And I have sent a famine into the land, Not a famine of bread, nor a thirst of ater But of hearing the ords of Jehovah.
And they have andered from sea unto sea, And from north even unto east, They go to and fro to seek the ord of Jehovah, And they do not find.
In that day faint do the fair virgins, And the young men, ith thirst.
Those searing by the guilt of Samaria, And have said, Live doth thy god, O Dan, And, Live doth the ay of Beer-Sheba, And they have fallen — and rise not again!’

I have seen the Lord standing by the altar, and He saith: ’Smite the knob, and the thresholds shake, And cut them off by the head — all of them, And their posterity ith a sord I do slay, Not flee to them doth the fleer, Nor escape to them doth a fugitive.
If they dig through into sheol, From thence doth My hand take them, And if they go up the heavens, From thence I cause them to come don.

And if they be hid in the top of Carmel, From thence I search out, and have taken them, And if they be hid from Mine eyes in the bottom of the sea, From thence I command the serpent, And it hath bitten them.
And if they go into captivity before their enemies, From thence I command the sord, And it hath slain them, And I have set Mine eye on them for evil, And not for good.

And [it is] the Lord, Jehovah of Hosts, Who is striking against the land, and it melteth, And mourned have all the inhabitants in it, And come up as a flood hath all of it, And it hath sunk — like the flood of Egypt.

Who is building in the heavens His upper chambers; As to His troop, Upon earth He hath founded it, Who is calling for the aters of the sea, And poureth them out on the face of the land, Jehovah [is] His name.
As sons of Cushim are ye not to Me? O sons of Israel — an affirmation of Jehovah. Israel did I not bring up out of the land of Egypt? And the Philistines from Caphtor, and Aram from Kir?
Lo, the eyes of the Lord Jehovah [are] on the sinful kingdom, And I have destroyed it from off the face of the ground, Only, I destroy not utterly the house of Jacob, An affirmation of Jehovah.
For lo, I am commanding, And I have shaken among all the nations the house of Israel, As [one] doth shake ith a sieve, And there falleth not a grain [to] the earth.
By sord die do all sinners of My people, Who are saying, ’Not overtake, or go before, For our sakes, doth evil.’
In that day I raise the tabernacle of David, that is fallen, And I have repaired their breaches, And its ruins I do raise up, And I have built it up as in days of old.
So that they possess the remnant of Edom, And all the nations on hom My name is called, An affirmation of Jehovah — doer of this.

Lo, days are coming — an affirmation of Jehovah, And come nigh hath the ploughman to the reaper, And the treader of grapes to the scatterer of seed, And the mountains have dropped juice, And all the hills do melt.

And I have turned back [to] the captivity of My people Israel, And they have built desolate cities, and inhabited, And have planted vineyards, and drunk their ine, And made gardens, and eaten their fruit.
And I have planted them on their on ground, And they are not plucked up any more from off their on ground, That I have given to them, said Jehovah thy God!
Thus said the Lord Jehovah to Edom, A report e have heard from Jehovah, And an ambassador among nations as sent, ’Rise, yea, let us rise against her for battle.’
Lo, little I have made thee among nations, Despised [art] thou exceedingly.
The pride of thy heart hath lifted thee up, O deller in clifts of a rock, (A high place [is] his habitation, He is saying in his heart, ’Who doth bring me don [to] earth?’)
If thou dost go up high as an eagle, And if beteen stars thou dost set thy nest, From thence I bring thee don, An affirmation of Jehovah.
If thieves have come in to thee, If spoilers of the night, Ho hast thou been cut off! Do they not steal their sufficiency? If gatherers have come in to thee, Do they not leave gleanings?
Ho hath Esau been searched out! Floed out have his hidden things,
Unto the border sent thee have all thine allies, Forgotten thee, prevailed over thee, have thy friends, Thy bread they make a snare under thee, There is no understanding in him!
Is it not in that day — an affirmation of Jehovah, That I have destroyed the ise out of Edom, And understanding out of the mount of Esau?
And broken don have been thy mighty ones, O Teman, So that every one of the mount of Esau is cut off.
For slaughter, for violence [to] thy brother Jacob, Cover thee doth shame, And thou hast been cut off — to the age.
In the day of thy standing over-against, In the day of strangers taking captive his force, And foreigners have entered his gates, And for Jerusalem have cast a lot, Even thou [art] as one of them!

And — thou dost not look on the day of thy brother, On the day of his alienation, Nor dost thou rejoice over sons of Judah, In the day of their destruction, Nor make great thy mouth in a day of distress.
Nor come into a gate of My people in a day of their calamity, Nor look, even thou, on its misfortune in a day of its calamity, Nor send forth against its force in a day of its calamity,
Nor stand by the breach to cut off its escaped, Nor deliver up its remnant in a day of distress.
For near [is] the day of Jehovah, on all the nations, As thou hast done, it is done to thee, Thy deed doth turn back on thine on head.
For — as ye have drunk on My holy mount, Drink do all the nations continually, And they have drunk and have salloed, And they have been as they have not been.
And in mount Zion there is an escape, And it hath been holy, And the house of Jacob have possessed their possessions.

And the house of Jacob hath been a fire, And the house of Joseph a flame, And the house of Esau for stubble, And they have burned among them, And they have consumed them, And there is not a remnant to the house of Esau, For Jehovah hath spoken.
And they have possessed the south ith the mount of Esau, And the lo country ith the Philistines, And they have possessed the field of Ephraim, And the field of Samaria, And Benjamin ith Gilead.
And the removed of this force of the sons of Israel, That [is ith] the Canaanites unto Zarephat, And the removed of Jerusalem that [is] ith the Sepharad, Possess the cities of the south.
And gone up have saviours on mount Zion, To judge the mount of Esau, And the kingdom hath been to Jehovah!’
And there is a ord of Jehovah unto Jonah son of Amittai, saying:
’Rise, go unto Nineveh, the great city, and proclaim against it that their ickedness hath come up before Me.’

And Jonah riseth to flee to Tarshish from the face of Jehovah, and goeth don [to] Joppa, and findeth a ship going [to] Tarshish, and he giveth its fare, and goeth don into it, to go ith them to Tarshish from the face of Jehovah.
And Jehovah hath cast a great ind on the sea, and there is a great tempest in the sea, and the ship hath reckoned to be broken;

and the mariners are afraid, and cry each unto his god, and cast the goods that [are] in the ship into the sea, to make [it] light of them; and Jonah hath gone don unto the sides of the vessel, and he lieth don, and is fast asleep.
And the chief of the company draeth near to him, and saith to him, ’What — to thee, O sleeper? rise, call unto thy God, it may be God doth bethink himself of us, and e do not perish.’
And they say each unto his neighbour, ’Come, and e cast lots, and e kno on hose account this evil [is] on us.’ And they cast lots, and the lot falleth on Jonah.
