Changed is all the land as a plain, From Gebo to Rimmon, south of Jerusalem, And she hath been high, and hath delt in her place, Even from the gate of Benjamin To the place of the first gate, unto the front gate, And from the toer of Hananeel, Unto the ine-vats of the king.
And they have delt in her, And destruction is no more, And Jerusalem hath delt confidently.

And this is the plague ith hich Jehovah Doth plague all the peoples ho have arred against Jerusalem, He hath consumed aay its flesh, And it is standing on its feet, And its eyes are consumed in their holes, And its tongue is consumed in their mouth.

And it hath come to pass, in that day, A great destruction [from] Jehovah is among them, And they have seized each the hand of his neighbour, And gone up hath his hand against the hand of his neighbour.
And also Judah is fought ith in Jerusalem, And gathered hath been the force of all the nations round about, Gold, and silver, and apparel, in great abundance.
And so is the plague of the horse, of the mule, Of the camel, and of the ass, And of all the cattle that are in these camps, As this plague.

And it hath come to pass, Every one ho hath been left of all the nations, Who are coming in against Jerusalem, They have also gone up from year to year, To bo themselves to the King, Jehovah of Hosts, And to celebrate the feast of the booths.
And it hath come to pass, That he ho doth not go up of the families of the land unto Jerusalem, To bo himself to the King, Jehovah of Hosts, Even on them there is no shoer.
And if the family of Egypt go not up, nor come in, Then not on them is the plague With hich Jehovah doth plague the nations That go not up to celebrate the feast of booths.
This is the punishment of the sin of Egypt, And the punishment of the sin of all the nations, That go not up to celebrate the feast of booths.
In that day there is on bells of the horse, ’Holy to Jehovah,’ And the pots in the house of Jehovah Have been as bols before the altar.

And every pot in Jerusalem, and in Judah, Have been holy to Jehovah of Hosts, And all those sacrificing have come in, And have taken of them, and boiled in them, And there is no merchant any more in the house of Jehovah of Hosts in that day!
The burden of a ord of Jehovah unto Israel by the hand of Malachi:
I have loved you, said Jehovah, And ye have said, ’In hat hast Thou loved us?’
Is not Esau Jacob’s brother? — an affirmation of Jehovah, And I love Jacob, and Esau I have hated, And I make his mountains a desolation, And his inheritance for dragons of a ilderness.

Because Edom saith, ’We have been made poor, And e turn back and e build the astes,’ Thus said Jehovah of Hosts: They do build, and I do destroy, And [men] have called to them, ’O region of ickedness,’ ’O people hom Jehovah defied to the age.’
And your eyes do see, and ye say, ’Magnified is Jehovah beyond the border of Israel,

A son honoureth a father, and a servant his master. And if I [am] a father, here [is] Mine honour? And if I [am] a master, here [is] My fear? Said Jehovah of Hosts to you, O priests, despising My name! And ye have said: ’In hat have e despised Thy name?’
Ye are bringing nigh on Mine altar polluted bread, And ye have said: ’In hat have e polluted Thee?’ In your saying: ’The table of Jehovah — it [is] despicable,’

And hen ye bring nigh the blind for sacrifice, ’There is no evil,’ And hen ye bring nigh the lame and sick, ’There is no evil;’ Bring it near, I pray thee, to thy governor — Doth he accept thee? or doth he lift up thy face? Said Jehovah of Hosts.
And no, appease, I pray thee, the face of God, And He doth favour us; From your on hand hath this been, Doth He accept of you appearances? Said Jehovah of Hosts.

Who [is] even among you, And he shutteth the to-leaved doors? Yea, ye do not kindle Mine altar for nought, I have no pleasure in you, said Jehovah of Hosts, And a present I do not accept of your hand.

For, from the rising of the sun to its going in, Great [is] My name among nations, And in every place perfume is brought nigh to My name, and a pure present, For great [is] My name among nations, Said Jehovah of Hosts.
And ye are polluting it in your saying, ’The table of Jehovah — it is polluted, As to its fruit — despicable is its food.’

And ye have said, ’Lo, hat a eariness,’ And ye have puffed at it, said Jehovah of Hosts, And ye have brought in plunder, And the lame and the sick, And ye have brought in the present! Do I accept it from your hand? said Jehovah.

And cursed [is] a deceiver, ho hath in his drove a male, And is voing, and is sacrificing a marred thing to the Lord, For a great king [am] I, said Jehovah of Hosts, And My name [is] revered among nations!
And no, to you [is] this charge, O priests,

If ye hearken not, and if ye lay [it] not to heart, To give honour to My name, said Jehovah of Hosts, I have sent against you the curse, And I have cursed your blessings, Yea, I have also cursed it, Because ye are not laying [it] to heart.
Lo, I am pushing aay before you the seed, And have scattered dung before your faces, Dung of your festivals, And it hath taken you aay ith it.
And ye have knon that I have sent unto you this charge, For My covenant being ith Levi, Said Jehovah of Hosts.
My covenant hath been ith him of life and of peace, And I make them to him a fear, and he doth fear Me, And because of My name he hath been affrighted.
The la of truth hath been in his mouth, And perverseness hath not been found in his lips, In peace and in uprightness he alked ith Me, And many he brought back from iniquity.
For the lips of a priest preserve knoledge, And la they do seek from his mouth, For a messenger of Jehovah of Hosts he [is].
And ye, ye have turned from the ay, Ye have caused many to stumble in the la, Ye have corrupted the covenant of Levi, Said Jehovah of Hosts.
And I also, I have made you despised and lo before all the people, Because ye are not keeping My ays, And are accepting persons in the la.
Have e not all one father? Hath not our God prepared us? Wherefore do e deal treacherously, Each against his brother, To pollute the covenant of our fathers?

Dealt treacherously hath Judah, And abomination hath been done in Israel, and in Jerusalem, For polluted hath Judah the holy thing of Jehovah, That He hath loved, and hath married the daughter of a strange god.
Cut off doth Jehovah the man ho doth it, Tempter and tempted — from the tents of Jacob, Even he ho is bringing nigh a present to Jehovah of Hosts.
And this a second time ye do, Covering ith tears the altar of Jehovah, With eeping and groaning, Because there is no more turning unto the present, Or receiving of a pleasing thing from your hand.
And ye have said, ’Wherefore?’ Because Jehovah hath testified beteen thee And the ife of thy youth, That thou hast dealt treacherously against her, And she thy companion, and thy covenant-ife.

And He did not make one [only], And He hath the remnant of the Spirit. And hat [is] the one [alone]! He is seeking a godly seed. And ye have been atchful over your spirit, And ith the ife of thy youth, None doth deal treacherously.

For [I] hate sending aay, said Jehovah, God of Israel, And He [ho] hath covered violence ith his clothing, said Jehovah of Hosts, And ye have been atchful over your spirit, And ye do not deal treacherously.

Ye have earied Jehovah ith your ords, And ye have said: ’In hat have e earied Him?’ In your saying: ’Every evil-doer [is] good in the eyes of Jehovah, And in them He is delighting,’ Or, ’Where [is] the God of judgment?’

Lo, I am sending My messenger, And he hath prepared a ay before Me, And suddenly come in unto his temple Doth the Lord hom ye are seeking, Even the messenger of the covenant, Whom ye are desiring, Lo, he is coming, said Jehovah of Hosts.
And ho is bearing the day of his coming? And ho is standing in his appearing? For he [is] as fire of a refiner, And as soap of a fuller.

And he hath sat, a refiner and purifier of silver, And he hath purified the sons of Levi, And hath refined them as gold and as silver, And they have been to Jehovah bringing nigh a present in righteousness.
And seet to Jehovah hath been the present of Judah and Jerusalem, As in days of old, and as in former years.

And I have dran near to you for judgment, And I have been a itness, Making haste against sorcerers, And against adulterers, And against searers to a falsehood, And against oppressors of the hire of an hireling, Of a ido, and of a fatherless one, And those turning aside a sojourner, And ho fear Me not, said Jehovah of Hosts.
For I [am] Jehovah, I have not changed, And ye, the sons of Jacob, Ye have not been consumed.

Even from the days of your fathers Ye have turned aside from My statutes, And ye have not taken heed. Turn back unto Me, and I turn back to you, Said Jehovah of Hosts. And ye have said, ’In hat do e turn back?’
Doth man deceive God? but ye are deceiving Me, And ye have said: ’In hat have e deceived Thee?’ The tithe and the heave-offering!
With a curse ye are cursed! And Me ye are deceiving — this nation — all of it.

Bring in all the tithe unto the treasure-house, And there is food in My house; When ye have tried Me, no, ith this, Said Jehovah of Hosts, Do not I open to you the indos of heaven? Yea, I have emptied on you a blessing till there is no space.
And I have pushed for you against the consumer, And He doth not destroy to you the fruit of the ground, Nor miscarry to you doth the vine in the field, Said Jehovah of Hosts.
And declared you happy have all the nations, For ye are a delightful land, said Jehovah of Hosts.
Hard against Me have been your ords, Said Jehovah, and ye have said: ’What have e spoken against Thee?’
Ye have said, ’A vain thing to serve God! And hat gain hen e kept His charge? And hen e have gone in black, Because of Jehovah of Hosts?
And no, e are declaring the proud happy, Yea, built up have been those doing ickedness, Yea they have tempted God, and escape.’
Then have those fearing Jehovah spoken one to another, And Jehovah doth attend and hear, And ritten is a book of memorial before Him Of those fearing Jehovah, And of those esteeming His name.
And they have been to Me, said Jehovah of Hosts, In the day that I am appointing — a peculiar treasure, And I have had pity on them, As one hath pity on his son ho is serving him.
And ye have turned back and considered, Beteen the righteous and the icked, Beteen the servant of God and him ho is not His servant.

For, lo, the day hath come, burning as a furnace, And all the proud, and every icked doer, have been stubble, And burnt them hath the day that came, Said Jehovah of Hosts, That there is not left to them root or branch,
And risen to you, ye ho fear My name, Hath the sun of righteousness — and healing in its ings, And ye have gone forth, and have increased as calves of a stall.
And ye have trodden don the icked, For they are ashes under the soles of your feet, In the day that I am appointing, Said Jehovah of Hosts.
Remember ye the la of Moses My servant, That I did command him in Horeb, For all Israel — statutes and judgments.
Lo, I am sending to you Elijah the prophet, Before the coming of the day of Jehovah, The great and the fearful.
And he hath turned back the heart of fathers to sons, And the heart of sons to their fathers, Before I come and have utterly smitten the land!
A roll of the birth of Jesus Christ, son of David, son of Abraham.
Abraham begat Isaac, and Isaac begat Jacob, and Jacob begat Judah and his brethren,
and Judah begat Pharez and Zarah of Tamar, and Pharez begat Hezron, and Hezron begat Ram,
and Ram begat Amminadab, and Amminadab begat Nahshon, and Nahshon begat Salmon,
and Salmon begat Boaz of Rahab, and Boaz begat Obed of Ruth, and Obed begat Jesse,
and Jesse begat David the king. And David the king begat Solomon, of her [ho had been] Uriah’s,
and Solomon begat Rehoboam, and Rehoboam begat Abijah, and Abijah begat Asa,
and Asa begat Jehoshaphat, and Jehoshaphat begat Joram, and Joram begat Uzziah,
and Uzziah begat Jotham, and Jotham begat Ahaz, and Ahaz begat Hezekiah,
and Hezekiah begat Manasseh, and Manasseh begat Amon, and Amon begat Josiah,
and Josiah begat Jeconiah and his brethren, at the Babylonian removal.
And after the Babylonian removal, Jeconiah begat Shealtiel, and Shealtiel begat Zerubbabel,
and Zerubbabel begat Abiud, and Abiud begat Eliakim, and Eliakim begat Azor,
and Azor begat Sadok, and Sadok begat Achim, and Achim begat Eliud,
and Eliud begat Eleazar, and Eleazar begat Matthan, and Matthan begat Jacob,
and Jacob begat Joseph, the husband of Mary, of hom as begotten Jesus, ho is named Christ.

All the generations, therefore, from Abraham unto David [are] fourteen generations, and from David unto the Babylonian removal fourteen generations, and from the Babylonian removal unto the Christ, fourteen generations.
And of Jesus Christ, the birth as thus: For his mother Mary having been betrothed to Joseph, before their coming together she as found to have conceived from the Holy Spirit,
and Joseph her husband being righteous, and not illing to make her an example, did ish privately to send her aay.

And on his thinking of these things, lo, a messenger of the Lord in a dream appeared to him, saying, ’Joseph, son of David, thou mayest not fear to receive Mary thy ife, for that hich in her as begotten [is] of the Holy Spirit,
and she shall bring forth a son, and thou shalt call his name Jesus, for he shall save his people from their sins.’
And all this hath come to pass, that it may be fulfilled that as spoken by the Lord through the prophet, saying,
’Lo, the virgin shall conceive, and she shall bring forth a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel,’ hich is, being interpreted ’With us [he is] God.’
And Joseph, having risen from the sleep, did as the messenger of the Lord directed him, and received his ife,
and did not kno her till she brought forth her son — the first-born, and he called his name Jesus.
And Jesus having been born in Beth-Lehem of Judea, in the days of Herod the king, lo, mages from the east came to Jerusalem,
saying, ’Where is he ho as born king of the Jes? for e sa his star in the east, and e came to bo to him.’
And Herod the king having heard, as stirred, and all Jerusalem ith him,
and having gathered all the chief priests and scribes of the people, he as inquiring from them here the Christ is born.
And they said to him, ’In Beth-Lehem of Judea, for thus it hath been ritten through the prophet,
And thou, Beth-Lehem, the land of Judah, thou art by no means the least among the leaders of Judah, for out of thee shall come one leading, ho shall feed My people Israel.’
Then Herod, privately having called the mages, did inquire exactly from them the time of the appearing star,
and having sent them to Beth-Lehem, he said, ’Having gone — inquire ye exactly for the child, and henever ye may have found, bring me back ord, that I also having come may bo to him.’
And they, having heard the king, departed, and lo, the star, that they did see in the east, did go before them, till, having come, it stood over here the child as.
And having seen the star, they rejoiced ith exceeding great joy,

and having come to the house, they found the child ith Mary his mother, and having fallen don they boed to him, and having opened their treasures, they presented to him gifts, gold, and frankincense, and myrrh,
and having been divinely arned in a dream not to turn back unto Herod, through another ay they ithdre to their on region.

And on their having ithdran, lo, a messenger of the Lord doth appear in a dream to Joseph, saying, ’Having risen, take the child and his mother, and flee to Egypt, and be thou there till I may speak to thee, for Herod is about to seek the child to destroy him.’
And he, having risen, took the child and his mother by night, and ithdre to Egypt,

verily I say to you, It shall be more tolerable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrah in the day of judgment than for that city.
’Lo, I do send you forth as sheep in the midst of olves, be ye therefore ise as the serpents, and simple as the doves.
And, take ye heed of men, for they ill give you up to sanhedrims, and in their synagogues they ill scourge you,
and before governors and kings ye shall be brought for my sake, for a testimony to them and to the nations.
’And henever they may deliver you up, be not anxious ho or hat ye may speak, for it shall be given you in that hour hat ye shall speak;
for ye are not the speakers, but the Spirit of your Father that is speaking in you.
’And brother shall deliver up brother to death, and father child, and children shall rise up against parents, and shall put them to death,
and ye shall be hated by all because of my name, but he ho hath endured to the end, he shall be saved.
’And henever they may persecute you in this city, flee to the other, for verily I say to you, ye may not have completed the cities of Israel till the Son of Man may come.
’A disciple is not above the teacher, nor a servant above his lord;
sufficient to the disciple that he may be as his teacher, and the servant as his lord; if the master of the house they did call Beelzeboul, ho much more those of his household?
’Ye may not, therefore, fear them, for there is nothing covered, that shall not be revealed, and hid, that shall not be knon;
that hich I tell you in the darkness, speak in the light, and that hich you hear at the ear, proclaim on the house-tops.
’And be not afraid of those killing the body, and are not able to kill the soul, but fear rather Him ho is able both soul and body to destroy in gehenna.
’Are not to sparros sold for an assar? and one of them shall not fall on the ground ithout your Father;
and of you — even the hairs of the head are all numbered;
be not therefore afraid, than many sparros ye are better.
’Every one, therefore, ho shall confess in me before men, I also ill confess in him before my Father ho is in the heavens;
and hoever shall deny me before men, I also ill deny him before my Father ho is in the heavens.
’Ye may not suppose that I came to put peace on the earth; I did not come to put peace, but a sord;
for I came to set a man at variance against his father, and a daughter against her mother, and a daughter-in-la against her mother-in-la,
and the enemies of a man are those of his household.
’He ho is loving father or mother above me, is not orthy of me, and he ho is loving son or daughter above me, is not orthy of me,
and hoever doth not receive his cross and follo after me, is not orthy of me.
’He ho found his life shall lose it, and he ho lost his life for my sake shall find it.
’He ho is receiving you doth receive me, and he ho is receiving me doth receive Him ho sent me,
he ho is receiving a prophet in the name of a prophet, shall receive a prophet’s reard, and he ho is receiving a righteous man in the name of a righteous man, shall receive a righteous man’s reard,
and hoever may give to drink to one of these little ones a cup of cold ater only in the name of a disciple, verily I say to you, he may not lose his reard.’
And it came to pass, hen Jesus ended directing his telve disciples, he departed thence to teach and to preach in their cities.
And John having heard in the prison the orks of the Christ, having sent to of his disciples,
said to him, ’Art thou He ho is coming, or for another do e look?’
And Jesus ansering said to them, ’Having gone, declare to John the things that ye hear and see,
blind receive sight, and lame alk, lepers are cleansed, and deaf hear, dead are raised, and poor have good nes proclaimed,
and happy is he ho may not be stumbled in me.’
And as they are going, Jesus began to say to the multitudes concerning John, ’What ent ye out to the ilderness to vie? — a reed shaken by the ind?
’But hat ent ye out to see? — a man clothed in soft garments? lo, those earing the soft things are in the kings’ houses.
’But hat ent ye out to see? — a prophet? yes, I say to you, and more than a prophet,
for this is he of hom it hath been ritten, Lo, I do send My messenger before thy face, ho shall prepare thy ay before thee.
Verily I say to you, there hath not risen, among those born of omen, a greater than John the Baptist, but he ho is least in the reign of the heavens is greater than he.
’And, from the days of John the Baptist till no, the reign of the heavens doth suffer violence, and violent men do take it by force,
for all the prophets and the la till John did prophesy,
and if ye are illing to receive [it], he is Elijah ho as about to come;
he ho is having ears to hear — let him hear.
’And to hat shall I liken this generation? it is like little children in market-places, sitting and calling to their comrades,
and saying, We piped unto you, and ye did not dance, e lamented to you, and ye did not smite the breast.
’For John came neither eating nor drinking, and they say, He hath a demon;
the Son of Man came eating and drinking, and they say, Lo, a man, a glutton, and a ine-drinker, a friend of tax-gatherers and sinners, and isdom as justified of her children.’
Then began he to reproach the cities in hich ere done most of his mighty orks, because they did not reform.
’Woe to thee, Chorazin! oe to thee, Bethsaida! because, if in Tyre and Sidon had been done the mighty orks that ere done in you, long ago in sackcloth and ashes they had reformed;
but I say to you, to Tyre and Sidon it shall be more tolerable in a day of judgment than for you.
’And thou, Capernaum, hich unto the heaven ast exalted, unto hades shalt be brought don, because if in Sodom had been done the mighty orks that ere done in thee, it had remained unto this day;
but I say to you, to the land of Sodom it shall be more tolerable in a day of judgment than to thee.’

At that time Jesus ansering said, ’I do confess to Thee, Father, Lord of the heavens and of the earth, that thou didst hide these things from ise and understanding ones, and didst reveal them to babes.
Yes, Father, because so it as good pleasure before Thee.
’All things ere delivered to me by my Father, and none doth kno the Son, except the Father, nor doth any kno the Father, except the Son, and he to hom the Son may ish to reveal [Him].
’Come unto me, all ye labouring and burdened ones, and I ill give you rest,
take up my yoke upon you, and learn from me, because I am meek and humble in heart, and ye shall find rest to your souls,
for my yoke [is] easy, and my burden is light.’
At that time did Jesus go on the sabbaths through the corn, and his disciples ere hungry, and they began to pluck ears, and to eat,
and the Pharisees having seen, said to him, ’Lo, thy disciples do that hich it is not laful to do on a sabbath.’
And he said to them, ’Did ye not read hat David did, hen he as hungry, himself and those ith him —
ho he ent into the house of God, and the loaves of the presentation did eat, hich it is not laful to him to eat, nor to those ith him, except to the priests alone?
’Or did ye not read in the La, that on the sabbaths the priests in the temple do profane the sabbath, and are blameless?
and I say to you, that a greater than the temple is here;
and if ye had knon hat is: Kindness I ill, and not sacrifice — ye had not condemned the blameless,
for the son of man is lord even of the sabbath.’
And having departed thence, he ent to their synagogue,
and lo, there as a man having the hand ithered, and they questioned him, saying, ’Is it laful to heal on the sabbaths?’ that they might accuse him.
And he said to them, ’What man shall be of you, ho shall have one sheep, and if this may fall on the sabbaths into a ditch, ill not lay hold on it and raise [it]?
Ho much better, therefore, is a man than a sheep? — so that it is laful on the sabbaths to do good.’
Then saith he to the man, ’Stretch forth thy hand,’ and he stretched [it] forth, and it as restored hole as the other.
And the Pharisees having gone forth, held a consultation against him, ho they might destroy him,
and Jesus having knon, ithdre thence, and there folloed him great multitudes, and he healed them all,
and did charge them that they might not make him manifest,
that it might be fulfilled that as spoken through Isaiah the prophet, saying,
’Lo, My servant, hom I did choose, My beloved, in hom My soul did delight, I ill put My Spirit upon him, and judgment to the nations he shall declare,
he shall not strive nor cry, nor shall any hear in the broad places his voice,
a bruised reed he shall not break, and smoking flax he shall not quench, till he may put forth judgment to victory,
and in his name shall nations hope.’
Then as brought to him a demoniac, blind and dumb, and he healed him, so that the blind and dumb both spake and sa.
And all the multitudes ere amazed, and said, ’Is this the Son of David?’
but the Pharisees having heard, said, ’This one doth not cast out demons, except by Beelzeboul, ruler of the demons.’
And Jesus, knoing their thoughts, said to them, ’Every kingdom having been divided against itself is desolated, and no city or house having been divided against itself, doth stand,
and if the Adversary doth cast out the Adversary, against himself he as divided, ho then doth his kingdom stand?
’And if I, by Beelzeboul, do cast out the demons, your sons — by hom do they cast out? because of this they — they shall be your judges.
’But if I, by the Spirit of God, do cast out the demons, then come already unto you did the reign of God.
’Or ho is one able to go into the house of the strong man, and to plunder his goods, if first he may not bind the strong man? and then his house he ill plunder.
’He ho is not ith me is against me, and he ho is not gathering ith me, doth scatter.
Because of this I say to you, all sin and evil speaking shall be forgiven to men, but the evil speaking of the Spirit shall not be forgiven to men.

And hoever may speak a ord against the Son of Man it shall be forgiven to him, but hoever may speak against the Holy Spirit, it shall not be forgiven him, neither in this age, nor in that hich is coming.
’Either make the tree good, and its fruit good, or make the tree bad, and its fruit bad, for from the fruit is the tree knon.
’Brood of vipers! ho are ye able to speak good things — being evil? for out of the abundance of the heart doth the mouth speak.
The good man out of the good treasure of the heart doth put forth the good things, and the evil man out of the evil treasure doth put forth evil things.
’And I say to you, that every idle ord that men may speak, they shall give for it a reckoning in a day of judgment;
for from thy ords thou shalt be declared righteous, and from thy ords thou shalt be declared unrighteous.’
Then ansered certain of the scribes and Pharisees, saying, ’Teacher, e ill to see a sign from thee.’
And he ansering said to them, ’A generation, evil and adulterous, doth seek a sign, and a sign shall not be given to it, except the sign of Jonah the prophet;
for, as Jonah as in the belly of the fish three days and three nights, so shall the Son of Man be in the heart of the earth three days and three nights.
’Men of Nineveh shall stand up in the judgment ith this generation, and shall condemn it, for they reformed at the proclamation of Jonah, and lo, a greater than Jonah here!

’A queen of the south shall rise up in the judgment ith this generation, and shall condemn it, for she came from the ends of the earth to hear the isdom of Solomon, and lo, a greater than Solomon here!
’And, hen the unclean spirit may go forth from the man, it doth alk through dry places seeking rest, and doth not find;
then it saith, I ill turn back to my house hence I came forth; and having come, it findeth [it] unoccupied, sept, and adorned:

then doth it go, and take ith itself seven other spirits more evil than itself, and having gone in they dell there, and the last of that man doth become orse than the first; so shall it be also to this evil generation.’
And hile he as yet speaking to the multitudes, lo, his mother and brethren had stood ithout, seeking to speak to him,
and one said to him, ’Lo, thy mother and thy brethren do stand ithout, seeking to speak to thee.’
And he ansering said to him ho spake to him, ’Who is my mother? and ho are my brethren?’
And having stretched forth his hand toard his disciples, he said, ’Lo, my mother and my brethren!
for hoever may do the ill of my Father ho is in the heavens, he is my brother, and sister, and mother.’
And in that day Jesus, having gone forth from the house, as sitting by the sea,
and gathered together unto him ere many multitudes, so that he having gone into the boat did sit don, and all the multitude on the beach did stand,
and he spake to them many things in similes, saying: ’Lo, the soer ent forth to so,
and in his soing, some indeed fell by the ay, and the fols did come and devour them,
and others fell upon the rocky places, here they had not much earth, and immediately they sprang forth, through not having depth of earth,
and the sun having risen they ere scorched, and through not having root, they ithered,
and others fell upon the thorns, and the thorns did come up and choke them,
and others fell upon the good ground, and ere giving fruit, some indeed a hundredfold, and some sixty, and some thirty.
He ho is having ears to hear — let him hear.’
And the disciples having come near, said to him, ’Wherefore in similes dost thou speak to them?’
And he ansering said to them that — ’To you it hath been given to kno the secrets of the reign of the heavens, and to these it hath not been given,
for hoever hath, it shall be given to him, and he shall have overabundance, and hoever hath not, even that hich he hath shall be taken from him.
’Because of this, in similes do I speak to them, because seeing they do not see, and hearing they do not hear, nor understand,
and fulfilled on them is the prophecy of Isaiah, that saith, With hearing ye shall hear, and ye shall not understand, and seeing ye shall see, and ye shall not perceive,

for made gross as the heart of this people, and ith the ears they heard heavily, and their eyes they did close, lest they might see ith the eyes, and ith the ears might hear, and ith the heart understand, and turn back, and I might heal them.
’And happy are your eyes because they see, and your ears because they hear,
for verily I say to you, that many prophets and righteous men did desire to see that hich ye look on, and they did not see, and to hear that hich ye hear, and they did not hear.
’Ye, therefore, hear ye the simile of the soer:
Every one hearing the ord of the reign, and not understanding — the evil one doth come, and doth catch that hich hath been son in his heart; this is that son by the ay.
’And that son on the rocky places, this is he ho is hearing the ord, and immediately ith joy is receiving it,
and he hath not root in himself, but is temporary, and persecution or tribulation having happened because of the ord, immediately he is stumbled.
’And that son toard the thorns, this is he ho is hearing the ord, and the anxiety of this age, and the deceitfulness of the riches, do choke the ord, and it becometh unfruitful.
’And that son on the good ground: this is he ho is hearing the ord, and is understanding, ho indeed doth bear fruit, and doth make, some indeed a hundredfold, and some sixty, and some thirty.’
Another simile he set before them, saying: ’The reign of the heavens as likened to a man soing good seed in his field,
and, hile men are sleeping, his enemy came and soed darnel in the midst of the heat, and ent aay,
and hen the herb sprang up, and yielded fruit, then appeared also the darnel.
’And the servants of the householder, having come near, said to him, Sir, good seed didst thou not so in thy field? hence then hath it the darnel?
And he saith to them, A man, an enemy, did this; and the servants said to him, Wilt thou, then, [that] having gone aay e may gather it up?
’And he said, No, lest — gathering up the darnel — ye root up ith it the heat,

suffer both to gro together till the harvest, and in the time of the harvest I ill say to the reapers, Gather up first the darnel, and bind it in bundles, to burn it, and the heat gather up into my storehouse.’
Another simile he set before them, saying: ’The reign of the heavens is like to a grain of mustard, hich a man having taken, did so in his field,
hich less, indeed, is than all the seeds, but hen it may be gron, is greatest of the herbs, and becometh a tree, so that the birds of the heaven do come and rest in its branches.’
Another simile spake he to them: ’The reign of the heavens is like to leaven, hich a oman having taken, hid in three measures of meal, till the hole as leavened.’
All these things spake Jesus in similes to the multitudes, and ithout a simile he as not speaking to them,

Then having let aay the multitudes, Jesus came to the house, and his disciples came near to him, saying, ’Explain to us the simile of the darnel of the field.’
And he ansering said to them, ’He ho is soing the good seed is the Son of Man,

’As, then, the darnel is gathered up, and is burned ith fire, so shall it be in the full end of this age,

and shall cast them to the furnace of the fire; there shall be the eeping and the gnashing of the teeth.
’Then shall the righteous shine forth as the sun in the reign of their Father. He ho is having ears to hear — let him hear.
’Again, the reign of the heavens is like to treasure hid in the field, hich a man having found did hide, and from his joy goeth, and all, as much as he hath, he selleth, and buyeth that field.
’Again, the reign of the heavens is like to a man, a merchant, seeking goodly pearls,
ho having found one pearl of great price, having gone aay, hath sold all, as much as he had, and bought it.
’Again, the reign of the heavens is like to a net that as cast into the sea, and did gather together of every kind,
hich, hen it as filled, having dran up again upon the beach, and having sat don, they gathered the good into vessels, and the bad they did cast out,

Jesus saith to them, ’Did ye understand all these?’ They say to him, ’Yes, sir.’

And he said to them, ’Because of this every scribe having been discipled in regard to the reign of the heavens, is like to a man, a householder, ho doth bring forth out of his treasure things ne and old.’
And it came to pass, hen Jesus finished these similes, he removed thence,

For Herod having laid hold on John, did bind him, and did put him in prison, because of Herodias his brother Philip’s ife,

And Jesus having come forth, sa a great multitude, and as moved ith compassion upon them, and did heal their infirm;

and evening having come, his disciples came to him, saying, ’The place is desolate, and the hour hath no past, let aay the multitudes that, having gone to the villages, they may buy to themselves food.’
And Jesus said to them, ’They have no need to go aay — give ye them to eat.’
And they say to him, ’We have not here except five loaves, and to fishes.’
And he said, ’Bring ye them to me hither.’

And having commanded the multitudes to recline upon the grass, and having taken the five loaves and the to fishes, having looked up to the heaven, he did bless, and having broken, he gave the loaves to the disciples, and the disciples to the multitudes,
and they did all eat, and ere filled, and they took up hat as over of the broken pieces telve hand-baskets full;
and those eating ere about five thousand men, apart from omen and children.
And immediately Jesus constrained his disciples to go into the boat, and to go before him to the other side, till he might let aay the multitudes;
and having let aay the multitudes, he ent up to the mountain by himself to pray, and evening having come, he as there alone,
and the boat as no in the midst of the sea, distressed by the aves, for the ind as contrary.
