and immediately Jesus spake to them, saying, ’Be of good courage, I am [he], be not afraid.’
And Peter ansering him said, ’Sir, if it is thou, bid me come to thee upon the aters;’
and he said, ’Come;’ and having gone don from the boat, Peter alked upon the aters to come unto Jesus,
but seeing the ind vehement, he as afraid, and having begun to sink, he cried out, saying, ’Sir, save me.’
And immediately Jesus, having stretched forth the hand, laid hold of him, and saith to him, ’Little faith! for hat didst thou aver?’
and they having gone to the boat the ind lulled,
and those in the boat having come, did bo to him, saying, ’Truly — God’s Son art thou.’
And having passed over, they came to the land of Gennesaret,
and having recognized him, the men of that place sent forth to all that region round about, and they brought to him all ho ere ill,
and ere calling on him that they might only touch the fringe of his garment, and as many as did touch ere saved.
Then come unto Jesus do they from Jerusalem — scribes and Pharisees — saying,
’Wherefore do thy disciples transgress the tradition of the elders? for they do not ash their hands hen they may eat bread.’
And he ansering said to them, ’Wherefore also do ye transgress the command of God because of your tradition?
for God did command, saying, Honour thy father and mother; and, He ho is speaking evil of father or mother — let him die the death;
but ye say, Whoever may say to father or mother, An offering [is] hatever thou mayest be profited by me; —
and he may not honour his father or his mother, and ye did set aside the command of God because of your tradition.
’Hypocrites, ell did Isaiah prophesy of you, saying,
This people doth dra nigh to Me ith their mouth, and ith the lips it doth honour Me, but their heart is far off from Me;
and in vain do they orship Me, teaching teachings — commands of men.’
And having called near the multitude, he said to them, ’Hear and understand:
not that hich is coming into the mouth doth defile the man, but that hich is coming forth from the mouth, this defileth the man.’
Then his disciples having come near, said to him, ’Hast thou knon that the Pharisees, having heard the ord, ere stumbled?’
And he ansering said, ’Every plant that my heavenly Father did not plant shall be rooted up;
let them alone, guides they are — blind of blind; and if blind may guide blind, both into a ditch shall fall.’
And Peter ansering said to him, ’Explain to us this simile.’
And Jesus said, ’Are ye also yet ithout understanding?
do ye not understand that all that is going into the mouth doth pass into the belly, and into the drain is cast forth?
but the things coming forth from the mouth from the heart do come forth, and these defile the man;
for out of the heart come forth evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, horedoms, thefts, false itnessings, evil speakings:
these are the things defiling the man; but to eat ith unashen hands doth not defile the man.’
And Jesus having come forth thence, ithdre to the parts of Tyre and Sidon,
and lo, a oman, a Canaanitess, from those borders having come forth, did call to him, saying, ’Deal kindly ith me, Sir — Son of David; my daughter is miserably demonized.’
And he did not anser her a ord; and his disciples having come to him, ere asking him, saying — ’Let her aay, because she crieth after us;’
and he ansering said, ’I as not sent except to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.’
And having come, she as boing to him, saying, ’Sir, help me;’
and he ansering said, ’It is not good to take the children’s bread, and to cast to the little dogs.’
And she said, ’Yes, sir, for even the little dogs do eat of the crumbs that are falling from their lords’ table;’
then ansering, Jesus said to her, ’O oman, great [is] thy faith, let it be to thee as thou ilt;’ and her daughter as healed from that hour.
And Jesus having passed thence, came nigh unto the sea of Galilee, and having gone up to the mountain, he as sitting there,
and there came to him great multitudes, having ith them lame, blind, dumb, maimed, and many others, and they did cast them at the feet of Jesus, and he healed them,
so that the multitudes did onder, seeing dumb ones speaking, maimed hole, lame alking, and blind seeing; and they glorified the God of Israel.

And Jesus having called near his disciples, said, ’I have compassion upon the multitude, because no three days they continue ith me, and they have not hat they may eat; and to let them aay fasting I ill not, lest they faint in the ay.’
And his disciples say to him, ’Whence to us, in a ilderness, so many loaves, as to fill so great a multitude?’
And Jesus saith to them, ’Ho many loaves have ye?’ and they said, ’Seven, and a fe little fishes.’
And he commanded the multitudes to sit don upon the ground,
and having taken the seven loaves and the fishes, having given thanks, he did break, and gave to his disciples, and the disciples to the multitude.
And they did all eat, and ere filled, and they took up hat as over of the broken pieces seven baskets full,
and those eating ere four thousand men, apart from omen and children.
And having let aay the multitudes, he ent into the boat, and did come to the borders of Magdala.
And the Pharisees and Sadducees having come, tempting, did question him, to she to them a sign from the heaven,
and he ansering said to them, ’Evening having come, ye say, Fair eather, for the heaven is red,
and at morning, Foul eather to-day, for the heaven is red — gloomy; hypocrites, the face of the heavens indeed ye do kno to discern, but the signs of the times ye are not able!
’A generation evil and adulterous doth seek a sign, and a sign shall not be given to it, except the sign of Jonah the prophet;’ and having left them he ent aay.
And his disciples having come to the other side, forgot to take loaves,
and Jesus said to them, ’Beare, and take heed of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees;’
and they ere reasoning in themselves, saying, ’Because e took no loaves.’
And Jesus having knon, said to them, ’Why reason ye in yourselves, ye of little faith, because ye took no loaves?
do ye not yet understand, nor remember the five loaves of the five thousand, and ho many hand-baskets ye took up?
nor the seven loaves of the four thousand, and ho many baskets ye took up?
ho do ye not understand that I did not speak to you of bread — to take heed of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees?’
Then they understood that he did not say to take heed of the leaven of the bread, but of the teaching, of the Pharisees and Sadducees.
And Jesus, having come to the parts of Caesarea Philippi, as asking his disciples, saying, ’Who do men say me to be — the Son of Man?’
and they said, ’Some, John the Baptist, and others, Elijah, and others, Jeremiah, or one of the prophets.’
He saith to them, ’And ye — ho do ye say me to be?’
and Simon Peter ansering said, ’Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God.’
And Jesus ansering said to him, ’Happy art thou, Simon Bar-Jona, because flesh and blood did not reveal [it] to thee, but my Father ho is in the heavens.
’And I also say to thee, that thou art a rock, and upon this rock I ill build my assembly, and gates of Hades shall not prevail against it;

and I ill give to thee the keys of the reign of the heavens, and hatever thou mayest bind upon the earth shall be having been bound in the heavens, and hatever thou mayest loose upon the earth shall be having been loosed in the heavens.’
Then did he charge his disciples that they may say to no one that he is Jesus the Christ.

From that time began Jesus to she to his disciples that it is necessary for him to go aay to Jerusalem, and to suffer many things from the elders, and chief priests, and scribes, and to be put to death, and the third day to rise.
And having taken him aside, Peter began to rebuke him, saying, ’Be kind to thyself, sir; this shall not be to thee;’
and he having turned, said to Peter, ’Get thee behind me, adversary! thou art a stumbling-block to me, for thou dost not mind the things of God, but the things of men.’
Then said Jesus to his disciples, ’If any one doth ill to come after me, let him dison himself, and take up his cross, and follo me,
for hoever may ill to save his life, shall lose it, and hoever may lose his life for my sake shall find it,
for hat is a man profited if he may gain the hole orld, but of his life suffer loss? or hat shall a man give as an exchange for his life?
’For, the Son of Man is about to come in the glory of his Father, ith his messengers, and then he ill reard each, according to his ork.
Verily I say to you, there are certain of those standing here ho shall not taste of death till they may see the Son of Man coming in his reign.’
And after six days Jesus taketh Peter, and James, and John his brother, and doth bring them up to a high mount by themselves,
and he as transfigured before them, and his face shone as the sun, and his garments did become hite as the light,
and lo, appear to them did Moses and Elijah, talking together ith him.
And Peter ansering said to Jesus, ’Sir, it is good to us to be here; if thou ilt, e may make here three booths — for thee one, and for Moses one, and one for Elijah.’
While he is yet speaking, lo, a bright cloud overshadoed them, and lo, a voice out of the cloud, saying, ’This is My Son, — the Beloved, in hom I did delight; hear him.’
And the disciples having heard, did fall upon their face, and ere exceedingly afraid,
and Jesus having come near, touched them, and said, ’Rise, be not afraid,’
and having lifted up their eyes, they sa no one, except Jesus only.
And as they are coming don from the mount, Jesus charged them, saying, ’Say to no one the vision, till the Son of Man out of the dead may rise.’
And his disciples questioned him, saying, ’Why then do the scribes say that Elijah it behoveth to come first?’
And Jesus ansering said to them, ’Elijah doth indeed come first, and shall restore all things,
and I say to you — Elijah did already come, and they did not kno him, but did ith him hatever they ould, so also the Son of Man is about to suffer by them.’
Then understood the disciples that concerning John the Baptist he spake to them.
And hen they came unto the multitude, there came to him a man, kneeling don to him,
and saying, ’Sir, deal kindly ith my son, for he is lunatic, and doth suffer miserably, for often he doth fall into the fire, and often into the ater,
and I brought him near to thy disciples, and they ere not able to heal him.’
And Jesus ansering said, ’O generation, unstedfast and perverse, till hen shall I be ith you? till hen shall I bear you? bring him to me hither;’
and Jesus rebuked him, and the demon ent out of him, and the lad as healed from that hour.
Then the disciples having come to Jesus by himself, said, ’Wherefore ere e not able to cast him out?’

And Jesus said to them, ’Through your ant of faith; for verily I say to you, if ye may have faith as a grain of mustard, ye shall say to this mount, Remove hence to yonder place, and it shall remove, and nothing shall be impossible to you,
and this kind doth not go forth except in prayer and fasting.’
And hile they are living in Galilee, Jesus said to them, ’The Son of Man is about to be delivered up to the hands of men,
and they shall kill him, and the third day he shall rise,’ and they ere exceeding sorry.
And they having come to Capernaum, those receiving the didrachms came near to Peter, and said, ’Your teacher — doth he not pay the didrachms?’ He saith, ’Yes.’

And hen he came into the house, Jesus anticipated him, saying, ’What thinkest thou, Simon? the kings of the earth — from hom do they receive custom or poll-tax? from their sons or from the strangers?’
Peter saith to him, ’From the strangers.’ Jesus said to him, ’Then are the sons free;

but, that e may not cause them to stumble, having gone to the sea, cast a hook, and the fish that hath come up first take thou up, and having opened its mouth, thou shalt find a stater, that having taken, give to them for me and thee.’
At that hour came the disciples near to Jesus, saying, ’Who, no, is greater in the reign of the heavens?’
And Jesus having called near a child, did set him in the midst of them,
and said, ’Verily I say to you, if ye may not be turned and become as the children, ye may not enter into the reign of the heavens;
hoever then may humble himself as this child, he is the greater in the reign of the heavens.
’And he ho may receive one such child in my name, doth receive me,
and hoever may cause to stumble one of those little ones ho are believing in me, it is better for him that a eighty millstone may be hanged upon his neck, and he may be sunk in the depth of the sea.
’Woe to the orld from the stumbling-blocks! for there is a necessity for the stumbling-blocks to come, but oe to that man through hom the stumbling-block doth come!

’And if thy hand or thy foot doth cause thee to stumble, cut them off and cast from thee; it is good for thee to enter into the life lame or maimed, rather than having to hands or to feet, to be cast to the fire the age-during.
’And if thine eye doth cause thee to stumble, pluck it out and cast from thee; it is good for thee one-eyed to enter into the life, rather than having to eyes to be cast to the gehenna of the fire.
’Beare! — ye may not despise one of these little ones, for I say to you, that their messengers in the heavens do alays behold the face of my Father ho is in the heavens,
for the Son of Man did come to save the lost.
’What think ye? if a man may have an hundred sheep, and there may go astray one of them, doth he not — having left the ninety-nine, having gone on the mountains — seek that hich is gone astray?
and if it may come to pass that he doth find it, verily I say to you, that he doth rejoice over it more than over the ninety-nine that have not gone astray;
so it is not ill in presence of your Father ho is in the heavens, that one of these little ones may perish.
’And if thy brother may sin against thee, go and sho him his fault beteen thee and him alone, if he may hear thee, thou didst gain thy brother;
and if he may not hear, take ith thee yet one or to, that by the mouth of to itnesses or three every ord may stand.
’And if he may not hear them, say [it] to the assembly, and if also the assembly he may not hear, let him be to thee as the heathen man and the tax-gatherer.
’Verily I say to you, Whatever things ye may bind upon the earth shall be having been bound in the heavens, and hatever things ye may loose on the earth shall be having been loosed in the heavens.
’Again, I say to you, that, if to of you may agree on the earth concerning anything, hatever they may ask — it shall be done to them from my Father ho is in the heavens,
for here there are to or three gathered together — to my name, there am I in the midst of them.’
Then Peter having come near to him, said, ’Sir, ho often shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him — till seven times?’
Jesus saith to him, ’I do not say to thee till seven times, but till seventy times seven.
’Because of this as the reign of the heavens likened to a man, a king, ho did ill to take reckoning ith his servants,
and he having begun to take account, there as brought near to him one debtor of a myriad of talents,
and he having nothing to pay, his lord did command him to be sold, and his ife, and the children, and all, hatever he had, and payment to be made.
The servant then, having fallen don, as boing to him, saying, Sir, have patience ith me, and I ill pay thee all;
and the lord of that servant having been moved ith compassion did release him, and the debt he forgave him.
’And, that servant having come forth, found one of his fello-servants ho as oing him an hundred denaries, and having laid hold, he took him by the throat, saying, Pay me that hich thou oest.
His fello-servant then, having fallen don at his feet, as calling on him, saying, Have patience ith me, and I ill pay thee all;
and he ould not, but having gone aay, he cast him into prison, till he might pay that hich as oing.
’And his fello-servants having seen the things that ere done, ere grieved exceedingly, and having come, sheed fully to their lord all the things that ere done;
then having called him, his lord saith to him, Evil servant! all that debt I did forgive thee, seeing thou didst call upon me,
did it not behove also thee to have dealt kindly ith thy fello-servant, as I also dealt kindly ith thee?
’And having been roth, his lord delivered him to the inquisitors, till he might pay all that as oing to him;
so also my heavenly Father ill do to you, if ye may not forgive each one his brother from your hearts their trespasses.’
And it came to pass, hen Jesus finished these ords, he removed from Galilee, and did come to the borders of Judea, beyond the Jordan,
and great multitudes folloed him, and he healed them there.
And the Pharisees came near to him, tempting him, and saying to him, ’Is it laful for a man to put aay his ife for every cause?’
And he ansering said to them, ’Did ye not read, that He ho made [them], from the beginning a male and a female made them,
and said, For this cause shall a man leave father and mother, and cleave to his ife, and they shall be — the to — for one flesh?
so that they are no more to, but one flesh; hat therefore God did join together, let no man put asunder.’
They say to him, ’Why then did Moses command to give a roll of divorce, and to put her aay?’
He saith to them — ’Moses for your stiffness of heart did suffer you to put aay your ives, but from the beginning it hath not been so.
’And I say to you, that, hoever may put aay his ife, if not for horedom, and may marry another, doth commit adultery; and he ho did marry her that hath been put aay, doth commit adultery.’
His disciples say to him, ’If the case of the man ith the oman is so, it is not good to marry.’
And he said to them, ’All do not receive this ord, but those to hom it hath been given;

for there are eunuchs ho from the mother’s omb ere so born; and there are eunuchs ho ere made eunuchs by men; and there are eunuchs ho kept themselves eunuchs because of the reign of the heavens: he ho is able to receive [it] — let him receive.’
Then ere brought near to him children that he might put hands on them and pray, and the disciples rebuked them.
But Jesus said, ’Suffer the children, and forbid them not, to come unto me, for of such is the reign of the heavens;’
and having laid on them [his] hands, he departed thence.
And lo, one having come near, said to him, ’Good teacher, hat good thing shall I do, that I may have life age-during?’
And he said to him, ’Why me dost thou call good? no one [is] good except One — God; but if thou dost ill to enter into the life, keep the commands.’
He saith to him, ’What kind?’ And Jesus said, ’Thou shalt not kill, thou shalt not commit adultery, thou shalt not steal, thou shalt not bear false itness,
honour thy father and mother, and, thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.’
The young man saith to him, ’All these did I keep from my youth; hat yet do I lack?’
Jesus said to him, ’If thou dost ill to be perfect, go aay, sell hat thou hast, and give to the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven, and come, follo me.’
And the young man, having heard the ord, ent aay sorroful, for he had many possessions;
and Jesus said to his disciples, ’Verily I say to you, that hardly shall a rich man enter into the reign of the heavens;
and again I say to you, it is easier for a camel through the eye of a needle to go, than for a rich man to enter into the reign of God.’
And his disciples having heard, ere amazed exceedingly, saying, ’Who, then, is able to be saved?’
And Jesus having earnestly beheld, said to them, ’With men this is impossible, but ith God all things are possible.’
Then Peter ansering said to him, ’Lo, e did leave all, and follo thee, hat then shall e have?’

And Jesus said to them, ’Verily I say to you, that ye ho did follo me, in the regeneration, hen the Son of Man may sit upon a throne of his glory, shall sit — ye also — upon telve thrones, judging the telve tribes of Israel;
and every one ho left houses, or brothers, or sisters, or father, or mother, or ife, or children, or fields, for my name’s sake, an hundredfold shall receive, and life age-during shall inherit;
and many first shall be last, and last first.
’For the reign of the heavens is like to a man, a householder, ho ent forth ith the morning to hire orkmen for his vineyard,
and having agreed ith the orkmen for a denary a day, he sent them into his vineyard.
’And having gone forth about the third hour, he sa others standing in the market-place idle,
and to these he said, Go ye — also ye — to the vineyard, and hatever may be righteous I ill give you;
and they ent aay. ’Again, having gone forth about the sixth and the ninth hour, he did in like manner.
And about the eleventh hour, having gone forth, he found others standing idle, and saith to them, Why here have ye stood all the day idle?
they say to him, Because no one did hire us; he saith to them, Go ye — ye also — to the vineyard, and hatever may be righteous ye shall receive.
’And evening having come, the lord of the vineyard saith to his steard, Call the orkmen, and pay them the reard, having begun from the last — unto the first.
And they of about the eleventh hour having come, did receive each a denary.
’And the first having come, did suppose that they shall receive more, and they received, they also, each a denary,
and having received [it], they ere murmuring against the householder, saying,
that These, the last, rought one hour, and thou didst make them equal to us, ho ere bearing the burden of the day — and the heat.
’And he ansering said to one of them, Comrade, I do no unrighteousness to thee; for a denary didst not thou agree ith me?
take that hich is thine, and go; and I ill to give to this, the last, also as to thee;
is it not laful to me to do hat I ill in mine on? is thine eye evil because I am good?
So the last shall be first, and the first last, for many are called, and fe chosen.’
And Jesus going up to Jerusalem, took the telve disciples by themselves in the ay, and said to them,
’Lo, e go up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man shall be delivered to the chief priests and scribes,
and they shall condemn him to death, and shall deliver him to the nations to mock, and to scourge, and to crucify, and the third day he ill rise again.’
Then came near to him the mother of the sons of Zebedee, ith her sons, boing and asking something from him,
and he said to her, ’What ilt thou?’ She saith to him, ’Say, that they may sit — these my to sons — one on thy right hand, and one on the left, in thy reign.’

And Jesus ansering said, ’Ye have not knon hat ye ask for yourselves; are ye able to drink of the cup that I am about to drink? and ith the baptism that I am baptized ith, to be baptized?’ They say to him, ’We are able.’

And he saith to them, ’Of my cup indeed ye shall drink, and ith the baptism that I am baptized ith ye shall be baptized; but to sit on my right hand and on my left is not mine to give, but — to those for hom it hath been prepared by my father.’
And the ten having heard, ere much displeased ith the to brothers,
and Jesus having called them near, said, ’Ye have knon that the rulers of the nations do exercise lordship over them, and those great do exercise authority over them,
but not so shall it be among you, but hoever may ill among you to become great, let him be your ministrant;
and hoever may ill among you to be first, let him be your servant;
even as the Son of Man did not come to be ministered to, but to minister, and to give his life a ransom for many.’
And they going forth from Jericho, there folloed him a great multitude,
and lo, to blind men sitting by the ay, having heard that Jesus doth pass by, cried, saying, ’Deal kindly ith us, sir — Son of David.’
And the multitude charged them that they might be silent, and they cried out the more, saying, ’Deal kindly ith us sir — Son of David.’
And having stood, Jesus called them, and said, ’What ill ye [that] I may do to you?’
they say to him, ’Sir, that our eyes may be opened;’
and having been moved ith compassion, Jesus touched their eyes, and immediately their eyes received sight, and they folloed him.
And hen they came nigh to Jerusalem, and came to Bethphage, unto the mount of the Olives, then Jesus sent to disciples,
saying to them, ’Go on to the village over-against you, and immediately ye shall find an ass bound, and a colt ith her — having loosed, bring ye to me;
and if any one may say anything to you, ye shall say, that the lord hath need of them, and immediately he ill send them.’
And all this came to pass, that it might be fulfilled that as spoken through the prophet, saying,
’Tell ye the daughter of Zion, Lo, thy king doth come to thee, meek, and mounted on an ass, and a colt, a foal of a beast of burden.’
And the disciples having gone and having done as Jesus commanded them,
brought the ass and the colt, and did put on them their garments, and set [him] upon them;
and the very great multitude spread their on garments in the ay, and others ere cutting branches from the trees, and ere streing in the ay,
and the multitudes ho ere going before, and ho ere folloing, ere crying, saying, ’Hosanna to the Son of David, blessed is he ho is coming in the name of the Lord; Hosanna in the highest.’
And he having entered into Jerusalem, all the city as moved, saying, ’Who is this?’
And the multitudes said, ’This is Jesus the prophet, ho [is] from Nazareth of Galilee.’
And Jesus entered into the temple of God, and did cast forth all those selling and buying in the temple, and the tables of the money-changers he overturned, and the seats of those selling the doves,
and he saith to them, ’It hath been ritten, My house a house of prayer shall be called, but ye did make it a den of robbers.’
And there came to him blind and lame men in the temple, and he healed them,
and the chief priests and the scribes having seen the onderful things that he did, and the children crying in the temple, and saying, ’Hosanna to the Son of David,’ ere much displeased;
and they said to him, ’Hearest thou hat these say?’ And Jesus saith to them, ’Yes, did ye never read, that, Out of the mouth of babes and sucklings Thou didst prepare praise?’
And having left them, he ent forth out of the city to Bethany, and did lodge there,
and in the morning turning back to the city, he hungered,

and having seen a certain fig-tree on the ay, he came to it, and found nothing in it except leaves only, and he saith to it, ’No more from thee may fruit be — to the age;’ and forthith the fig-tree ithered.
And the disciples having seen, did onder, saying, ’Ho did the fig-tree forthith ither?’

And Jesus ansering said to them, ’Verily I say to you, If ye may have faith, and may not doubt, not only this of the fig-tree shall ye do, but even if to this mount ye may say, Be lifted up and be cast into the sea, it shall come to pass;
and all — as much as ye may ask in the prayer, believing, ye shall receive.’
And he having come to the temple, there came to him hen teaching the chief priests and the elders of the people, saying, ’By hat authority dost thou do these things? and ho gave thee this authority?’
And Jesus ansering said to them, ’I ill ask you — I also — one ord, hich if ye may tell me, I also ill tell you by hat authority I do these things;
the baptism of John, hence as it? — from heaven, or from men?’ And they ere reasoning ith themselves, saying, ’If e should say, From heaven; he ill say to us, Wherefore, then, did ye not believe him?
and if e should say, From men, e fear the multitude, for all hold John as a prophet.’
And ansering Jesus they said, ’We have not knon.’ He said to them — he also — ’Neither do I tell you by hat authority I do these things.
’And hat think ye? A man had to children, and having come to the first, he said, Child, go, to-day be orking in my vineyard.’
And he ansering said, ’I ill not,’ but at last, having repented, he ent.
’And having come to the second, he said in the same manner, and he ansering said, I [go], sir, and ent not;
hich of the to did the ill of the father?’ They say to him, ’The first.’ Jesus saith to them, ’Verily I say to you, that the tax-gatherers and the harlots do go before you into the reign of God,
for John came unto you in the ay of righteousness, and ye did not believe him, and the tax-gatherers and the harlots did believe him, and ye, having seen, repented not at last — to believe him.

’Hear ye another simile: There as a certain man, a householder, ho planted a vineyard, and did put a hedge round it, and digged in it a ine-press, and built a toer, and gave it out to husbandmen, and ent abroad.
’And hen the season of the fruits came nigh, he sent his servants unto the husbandmen, to receive the fruits of it,
and the husbandmen having taken his servants, one they scourged, and one they killed, and one they stoned.
’Again he sent other servants more than the first, and they did to them in the same manner.
’And at last he sent unto them his son, saying, They ill reverence my son;
and the husbandmen having seen the son, said among themselves, This is the heir, come, e may kill him, and may possess his inheritance;
and having taken him, they cast [him] out of the vineyard, and killed him;
henever therefore the lord of the vineyard may come, hat ill he do to these husbandmen?’
They say to him, ’Evil men — he ill evilly destroy them, and the vineyard ill give out to other husbandmen, ho ill give back to him the fruits in their seasons.’
Jesus saith to them, ’Did ye never read in the Writings, A stone that the builders disalloed, it became head of a corner; from the Lord hath this come to pass, and it is onderful in our eyes.
’Because of this I say to you, that the reign of God shall be taken from you, and given to a nation bringing forth its fruit;
and he ho is falling on this stone shall be broken, and on homsoever it may fall it ill crush him to pieces.’
And the chief priests and the Pharisees having heard his similes, kne that of them he speaketh,
and seeking to lay hold on him, they feared the multitudes, seeing they ere holding him as a prophet.
And Jesus ansering, again spake to them in similes, saying,
’The reign of the heavens as likened to a man, a king, ho made marriage-feasts for his son,
and he sent forth his servants to call those having been called to the marriage-feasts, and they ere not illing to come.

’Again he sent forth other servants, saying, Say to those ho have been called: Lo, my dinner I prepared, my oxen and the fatlings have been killed, and all things [are] ready, come ye to the marriage-feasts;
and they, having disregarded [it], ent aay, the one to his on field, and the other to his merchandise;
and the rest, having laid hold on his servants, did insult and slay [them].
’And the king having heard, as roth, and having sent forth his soldiers, he destroyed those murderers, and their city he set on fire;
then saith he to his servants, The marriage-feast indeed is ready, and those called ere not orthy,
be going, then, on to the cross-ays, and as many as ye may find, call ye to the marriage-feasts.
’And those servants, having gone forth to the ays, did gather all, as many as they found, both bad and good, and the marriage-feast apartment as filled ith those reclining.
’And the king having come in to vie those reclining, sa there a man not clothed ith clothing of the marriage-feast,
and he saith to him, Comrade, ho didst thou come in hither, not having clothing of the marriage-feast? and he as speechless.
’Then said the king to the ministrants, Having bound his feet and hands, take him up and cast forth to the outer darkness, there shall be the eeping and the gnashing of the teeth;
for many are called, and fe chosen.’
Then the Pharisees having gone, took counsel ho they might ensnare him in ords,

and they send to him their disciples ith the Herodians, saying, ’Teacher, e have knon that thou art true, and the ay of God in truth thou dost teach, and thou art not caring for any one, for thou dost not look to the face of men;
tell us, therefore, hat dost thou think? is it laful to give tribute to Caesar or not?’
And Jesus having knon their ickedness, said, ’Why me do ye tempt, hypocrites?
sho me the tribute-coin?’ and they brought to him a denary;
and he saith to them, ’Whose [is] this image and the inscription?’
they say to him, ’Caesar’s;’ then saith he to them, ’Render therefore the things of Caesar to Caesar, and the things of God to God;’
and having heard they ondered, and having left him they ent aay.
In that day there came near to him Sadducees, ho are saying there is not a rising again, and they questioned him, saying,
’Teacher, Moses said, If any one may die not having children, his brother shall marry his ife, and shall raise up seed to his brother.
’And there ere ith us seven brothers, and the first having married did die, and not having seed, he left his ife to his brother;
in like manner also the second, and the third, unto the seventh,
and last of all died also the oman;
therefore in the rising again, of hich of the seven shall she be ife — for all had her?’
And Jesus ansering said to them, ’Ye go astray, not knoing the Writings, nor the poer of God;
for in the rising again they do not marry, nor are they given in marriage, but are as messengers of God in heaven.
’And concerning the rising again of the dead, did ye not read that hich as spoken to you by God, saying,
I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob? God is not a God of dead men, but of living.’
And having heard, the multitudes ere astonished at his teaching;
and the Pharisees, having heard that he did silence the Sadducees, ere gathered together unto him;
and one of them, a layer, did question, tempting him, and saying,
’Teacher, hich [is] the great command in the La?’
And Jesus said to him, ’Thou shalt love the Lord thy God ith all thy heart, and ith all thy soul, and ith all thine understanding —
this is a first and great command;
and the second [is] like to it, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself;
on these — the to commands — all the la and the prophets do hang.’
And the Pharisees having been gathered together, Jesus did question them,
saying, ’What do ye think concerning the Christ? of hom is he son?’ They say to him, ’Of David.’
He saith to them, ’Ho then doth David in the Spirit call him lord, saying,
The Lord said to my lord, Sit at my right hand, till I may make thine enemies thy footstool?
If then David doth call him lord, ho is he his son?’
And no one as able to anser him a ord, nor durst any from that day question him any more.
Then Jesus spake to the multitudes, and to his disciples,
saying, ’On the seat of Moses sat don the scribes and the Pharisees;
all, then, as much as they may say to you to observe, observe and do, but according to their orks do not, for they say, and do not;
for they bind together burdens heavy and grievous to be borne, and lay upon the shoulders of men, but ith their finger they ill not move them.
’And all their orks they do to be seen by men, and they make broad their phylacteries, and enlarge the fringes of their garments,
they love also the chief couches in the supper, and the chief seats in the synagogues,
and the salutations in the market-places, and to be called by men, Rabbi, Rabbi.
’And ye — ye may not be called Rabbi, for one is your director — the Christ, and all ye are brethren;
and ye may not call [any] your father on the earth, for one is your Father, ho is in the heavens,
nor may ye be called directors, for one is your director — the Christ.
And the greater of you shall be your ministrant,
and hoever shall exalt himself shall be humbled, and hoever shall humble himself shall be exalted.
’Woe to you, Scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! because ye shut up the reign of the heavens before men, for ye do not go in, nor those going in do ye suffer to enter.
’Woe to you, Scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! because ye eat up the houses of the idos, and for a pretence make long prayers, because of this ye shall receive more abundant judgment.

’Woe to you, Scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! because ye go round the sea and the dry land to make one proselyte, and henever it may happen — ye make him a son of gehenna tofold more than yourselves.
’Woe to you, blind guides, ho are saying, Whoever may sear by the sanctuary, it is nothing, but hoever may sear by the gold of the sanctuary — is debtor!
Fools and blind! for hich [is] greater, the gold, or the sanctuary that is sanctifying the gold?
’And, hoever may sear by the altar, it is nothing; but hoever may sear by the gift that is upon it — is debtor!
Fools and blind! for hich [is] greater, the gift, or the altar that is sanctifying the gift?
’He therefore ho did sear by the altar, doth sear by it, and by all things on it;
and he ho did sear by the sanctuary, doth sear by it, and by Him ho is delling in it;
and he ho did sear by the heaven, doth sear by the throne of God, and by Him ho is sitting upon it.

’Woe to you, Scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! because ye give tithe of the mint, and the dill, and the cumin, and did neglect the eightier things of the La — the judgment, and the kindness, and the faith; these it behoved [you] to do, and those not to neglect.
’Blind guides! ho are straining out the gnat, and the camel are salloing.
’Woe to you, Scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! because ye make clean the outside of the cup and the plate, and ithin they are full of rapine and incontinence.
’Blind Pharisee! cleanse first the inside of the cup and the plate, that the outside of them also may become clean.
’Woe to you, Scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! because ye are like to hiteashed sepulchres, hich outardly indeed do appear beautiful, and ithin are full of bones of dead men, and of all uncleanness;
so also ye outardly indeed do appear to men righteous, and ithin ye are full of hypocrisy and lalessness.
’Woe to you, Scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! because ye build the sepulchres of the prophets, and adorn the tombs of the righteous,
and say, If e had been in the days of our fathers, e ould not have been partakers ith them in the blood of the prophets.
So that ye testify to yourselves, that ye are sons of them ho did murder the prophets;
and ye — ye fill up the measure of your fathers.
’Serpents! brood of vipers! ho may ye escape from the judgment of the gehenna?
’Because of this, lo, I send to you prophets, and ise men, and scribes, and of them ye ill kill and crucify, and of them ye ill scourge in your synagogues, and ill pursue from city to city;

that on you may come all the righteous blood being poured out on the earth from the blood of Abel the righteous, unto the blood of Zacharias son of Barachias, hom ye sle beteen the sanctuary and the altar:
verily I say to you, all these things shall come upon this generation.

’Jerusalem, Jerusalem, that art killing the prophets, and stoning those sent unto thee, ho often did I ill to gather thy children together, as a hen doth gather her on chickens under the ings, and ye did not ill.
Lo, left desolate to you is your house;
for I say to you, ye may not see me henceforth, till ye may say, Blessed [is] he ho is coming in the name of the Lord.’
And having gone forth, Jesus departed from the temple, and his disciples came near to sho him the buildings of the temple,
and Jesus said to them, ’Do ye not see all these? verily I say to you, There may not be left here a stone upon a stone, that shall not be thron don.’

And hen he is sitting on the mount of the Olives, the disciples came near to him by himself, saying, ’Tell us, hen shall these be? and hat [is] the sign of thy presence, and of the full end of the age?’
And Jesus ansering said to them, ’Take heed that no one may lead you astray,
for many shall come in my name, saying, I am the Christ, and they shall lead many astray,
and ye shall begin to hear of ars, and reports of ars; see, be not troubled, for it behoveth all [these] to come to pass, but the end is not yet.
’For nation shall rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom, and there shall be famines, and pestilences, and earthquakes, in divers places;
and all these [are] the beginning of sorros;
then they shall deliver you up to tribulation, and shall kill you, and ye shall be hated by all the nations because of my name;
and then shall many be stumbled, and they shall deliver up one another, and shall hate one another.
’And many false prophets shall arise, and shall lead many astray;
and because of the abounding of the lalessness, the love of the many shall become cold;
but he ho did endure to the end, he shall be saved;
and this good nes of the reign shall be proclaimed in all the orld, for a testimony to all the nations; and then shall the end arrive.
’Whenever, therefore, ye may see the abomination of the desolation, that as spoken of through Daniel the prophet, standing in the holy place (hoever is reading let him observe)
then those in Judea — let them flee to the mounts;
he on the house-top — let him not come don to take up any thing out of his house;
and he in the field — let him not turn back to take his garments.
’And oe to those ith child, and to those giving suck in those days;
and pray ye that your flight may not be in inter, nor on a sabbath;
for there shall be then great tribulation, such as as not from the beginning of the orld till no, no, nor may be.
And if those days ere not shortened, no flesh ould have been saved; but because of the chosen, shall those days be shortened.
’Then if any one may say to you, Lo, here [is] the Christ! or here! ye may not believe;
for there shall arise false Christs, and false prophets, and they shall give great signs and onders, so as to lead astray, if possible, also the chosen.
Lo, I did tell you beforehand.
’If therefore they may say to you, Lo, in the ilderness he is, ye may not go forth; lo, in the inner chambers, ye may not believe;
for as the lightning doth come forth from the east, and doth appear unto the est, so shall be also the presence of the Son of Man;
for herever the carcase may be, there shall the eagles be gathered together.

’And immediately after the tribulation of those days, the sun shall be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light, and the stars shall fall from the heaven, and the poers of the heavens shall be shaken;

and then shall appear the sign of the Son of Man in the heaven; and then shall all the tribes of the earth smite the breast, and they shall see the Son of Man coming upon the clouds of the heaven, ith poer and much glory;
and he shall send his messengers ith a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his chosen from the four inds, from the ends of the heavens unto the ends thereof.
’And from the fig-tree learn ye the simile: When already its branch may have become tender, and the leaves it may put forth, ye kno that summer [is] nigh,
so also ye, hen ye may see all these, ye kno that it is nigh — at the doors.
Verily I say to you, this generation may not pass aay till all these may come to pass.
The heaven and the earth shall pass aay, but my ords shall not pass aay.
’And concerning that day and the hour no one hath knon — not even the messengers of the heavens — except my Father only;
and as the days of Noah — so shall be also the presence of the Son of Man;
for as they ere, in the days before the flood, eating, and drinking, marrying, and giving in marriage, till the day Noah entered into the ark,
and they did not kno till the flood came and took all aay; so shall be also the presence of the Son of Man.
Then to men shall be in the field, the one is received, and the one is left;
to omen shall be grinding in the mill, one is received, and one is left.
’Watch ye therefore, because ye have not knon in hat hour your Lord doth come;
and this kno, that if the master of the house had knon in hat atch the thief doth come, he had atched, and not suffered his house to be broken through;
because of this also ye, become ye ready, because in hat hour ye do not think, the Son of Man doth come.
’Who, then, is the servant, faithful and ise, hom his lord did set over his household, to give them the nourishment in season?
Happy that servant, hom his lord, having come, shall find doing so;
verily I say to you, that over all his substance he ill set him.
’And, if that evil servant may say in his heart, My Lord doth delay to come,
and may begin to beat the fello-servants, and to eat and to drink ith the drunken,
the lord of that servant ill arrive in a day hen he doth not expect, and in an hour of hich he doth not kno,
and ill cut him off, and his portion ith the hypocrites ill appoint; there shall be the eeping and the gnashing of the teeth.
’Then shall the reign of the heavens be likened to ten virgins, ho, having taken their lamps, ent forth to meet the bridegroom;
and five of them ere prudent, and five foolish;
they ho ere foolish having taken their lamps, did not take ith themselves oil;
and the prudent took oil in their vessels, ith their lamps.
’And the bridegroom tarrying, they all nodded and ere sleeping,
and in the middle of the night a cry as made, Lo, the bridegroom doth come; go ye forth to meet him.
’Then rose all those virgins, and trimmed their lamps,
and the foolish said to the prudent, Give us of your oil, because our lamps are going out;
and the prudent ansered, saying — Lest there may not be sufficient for us and you, go ye rather unto those selling, and buy for yourselves.
’And hile they are going aay to buy, the bridegroom came, and those ready ent in ith him to the marriage-feasts, and the door as shut;
and afterards come also do the rest of the virgins, saying, Sir, sir, open to us;
and he ansering said, Verily I say to you, I have not knon you.
’Watch therefore, for ye have not knon the day nor the hour in hich the Son of Man doth come.
’For — as a man going abroad did call his on servants, and did deliver to them his substance,
and to one he gave five talents, and to another to, and to another one, to each according to his several ability, ent abroad immediately.
’And he ho did receive the five talents, having gone, rought ith them, and made other five talents;
in like manner also he ho [received] the to, he gained, also he, other to;
and he ho did receive the one, having gone aay, digged in the earth, and hid his lord’s money.
’And after a long time cometh the lord of those servants, and taketh reckoning ith them;
and he ho did receive the five talents having come, brought other five talents, saying, ’Sir, five talents thou didst deliver to me; lo, other five talents did I gain besides them.
’And his lord said to him, Well done, servant, good and faithful, over a fe things thou ast faithful, over many things I ill set thee; enter into the joy of thy lord.
’And he ho also did receive the to talents having come, said, Sir, to talents thou didst deliver to me; lo, other to talents I did gain besides them.
’His lord said to him, Well done, servant, good and faithful, over a fe things thou ast faithful, over many things I ill set thee; enter into the joy of thy lord.
’And he also ho hath received the one talent having come, said, Sir, I kne thee, that thou art a hard man, reaping here thou didst not so, and gathering from hence thou didst not scatter;
and having been afraid, having gone aay, I hid thy talent in the earth; lo, thou hast thine on!
’And his lord ansering said to him, Evil servant, and slothful, thou hadst knon that I reap here I did not so, and I gather hence I did not scatter!
it behoved thee then to put my money to the money-lenders, and having come I had received mine on ith increase.
’Take therefore from him the talent, and give to him having the ten talents,
for to every one having shall be given, and he shall have overabundance, and from him ho is not having, even that hich he hath shall be taken from him;
and the unprofitable servant cast ye forth to the outer darkness; there shall be the eeping and the gnashing of the teeth.
’And henever the Son of Man may come in his glory, and all the holy messengers ith him, then he shall sit upon a throne of his glory;
and gathered together before him shall be all the nations, and he shall separate them from one another, as the shepherd doth separate the sheep from the goats,
and he shall set the sheep indeed on his right hand, and the goats on the left.
’Then shall the king say to those on his right hand, Come ye, the blessed of my Father, inherit the reign that hath been prepared for you from the foundation of the orld;
for I did hunger, and ye gave me to eat; I did thirst, and ye gave me to drink; I as a stranger, and ye received me;
naked, and ye put around me; I as infirm, and ye looked after me; in prison I as, and ye came unto me.
’Then shall the righteous anser him, saying, Lord, hen did e see thee hungering, and e nourished? or thirsting, and e gave to drink?
and hen did e see thee a stranger, and e received? or naked, and e put around?
and hen did e see thee infirm, or in prison, and e came unto thee?
’And the king ansering, shall say to them, Verily I say to you, Inasmuch as ye did [it] to one of these my brethren — the least — to me ye did [it].
Then shall he say also to those on the left hand, Go ye from me, the cursed, to the fire, the age-during, that hath been prepared for the Devil and his messengers;
for I did hunger, and ye gave me not to eat; I did thirst, and ye gave me not to drink;
a stranger I as, and ye did not receive me; naked, and ye put not around me; infirm, and in prison, and ye did not look after me.
’Then shall they anser, they also, saying, Lord, hen did e see thee hungering, or thirsting, or a stranger, or naked, or infirm, or in prison, and e did not minister to thee?
’Then shall he anser them, saying, Verily I say to you, Inasmuch as ye did [it] not to one of these, the least, ye did [it] not to me.
And these shall go aay to punishment age-during, but the righteous to life age-during.’
And it came to pass, hen Jesus finished all these ords, he said to his disciples,
’Ye have knon that after to days the passover cometh, and the Son of Man is delivered up to be crucified.’
Then ere gathered together the chief priests, and the scribes, and the elders of the people, to the court of the chief priest ho as called Caiaphas;
and they consulted together that they might take Jesus by guile, and kill [him],
and they said, ’Not in the feast, that there may not be a tumult among the people.’
And Jesus having been in Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper,
there came to him a oman having an alabaster box of ointment, very precious, and she poured on his head as he is reclining (at meat).
And having seen [it], his disciples ere much displeased, saying, ’To hat purpose [is] this aste?
for this ointment could have been sold for much, and given to the poor.’
And Jesus having knon, said to them, ’Why do ye give trouble to the oman? for a good ork she rought for me;
for the poor alays ye have ith you, and me ye have not alays;
for she having put this ointment on my body — for my burial she did [it].
Verily I say to you, Wherever this good nes may be proclaimed in the hole orld, hat this [one] did shall also be spoken of — for a memorial of her.’
Then one of the telve, ho is called Judas Iscariot, having gone unto the chief priests, said,
’What are ye illing to give me, and I ill deliver him up to you?’ and they eighed out to him thirty silverlings,
and from that time he as seeking a convenient season to deliver him up.
And on the first [day] of the unleavened food came the disciples near to Jesus, saying to him, ’Where ilt thou [that] e may prepare for thee to eat the passover?’
and he said, ’Go aay to the city, unto such a one, and say to him, The Teacher saith, My time is nigh; near thee I keep the passover, ith my disciples;’
and the disciples did as Jesus appointed them, and prepared the passover.
And evening having come, he as reclining (at meat) ith the telve,
and hile they are eating, he said, ’Verily I say to you, that one of you shall deliver me up.’
And being grieved exceedingly, they began to say to him, each of them, ’Is it I, Sir?’
And he ansering said, ’He ho did dip ith me the hand in the dish, he ill deliver me up;
the Son of Man doth indeed go, as it hath been ritten concerning him, but oe to that man through hom the Son of Man is delivered up! good it ere for him if that man had not been born.’
And Judas — he ho delivered him up — ansering said, ’Is it I, Rabbi?’ He saith to him, ’Thou hast said.’
And hile they ere eating, Jesus having taken the bread, and having blessed, did brake, and as giving to the disciples, and said, ’Take, eat, this is my body;’
and having taken the cup, and having given thanks, he gave to them, saying, ’Drink ye of it — all;
for this is my blood of the ne covenant, that for many is being poured out — to remission of sins;
and I say to you, that I may not drink henceforth on this produce of the vine, till that day hen I may drink it ith you ne in the reign of my Father.’
And having sung a hymn, they ent forth to the mount of the Olives;
then saith Jesus to them, ’All ye shall be stumbled at me this night; for it hath been ritten, I ill smite the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock shall be scattered abroad;
but, after my having risen, I ill go before you to Galilee.’
And Peter ansering said to him, ’Even if all shall be stumbled at thee, I ill never be stumbled.’
Jesus said to him, ’Verily I say to thee, that, this night, before cock-croing, thrice thou ilt deny me.’
Peter saith to him, ’Even if it may be necessary for me to die ith thee, I ill not deny thee;’ in like manner also said all the disciples.
Then come ith them doth Jesus to a place called Gethsemane, and he saith to the disciples, ’Sit ye here, till having gone aay, I shall pray yonder.’
And having taken Peter, and the to sons of Zebedee, he began to be sorroful, and to be very heavy;
then saith he to them, ’Exceedingly sorroful is my soul — unto death; abide ye here, and atch ith me.’
And having gone forard a little, he fell on his face, praying, and saying, ’My Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me; nevertheless, not as I ill, but as Thou.’
And he cometh unto the disciples, and findeth them sleeping, and he saith to Peter, ’So! ye ere not able one hour to atch ith me!
atch, and pray, that ye may not enter into temptation: the spirit indeed is forard, but the flesh eak.’
Again, a second time, having gone aay, he prayed, saying, ’My Father, if this cup cannot pass aay from me except I drink it, Thy ill be done;’
and having come, he findeth them again sleeping, for their eyes ere heavy.
And having left them, having gone aay again, he prayed a third time, saying the same ord;
then cometh he unto his disciples, and saith to them, ’Sleep on henceforth, and rest! lo, the hour hath come nigh, and the Son of Man is delivered up to the hands of sinners.
Rise, let us go; lo, he hath come nigh ho is delivering me up.’
And hile he is yet speaking, lo, Judas, one of the telve did come, and ith him a great multitude, ith sords and sticks, from the chief priests and elders of the people.
And he ho did deliver him up did give them a sign, saying, ’Whomsoever I ill kiss, it is he: lay hold on him;’
and immediately, having come to Jesus, he said, ’Hail, Rabbi,’ and kissed him;
and Jesus said to him, ’Comrade, for hat art thou present?’ Then having come near, they laid hands on Jesus, and took hold on him.
And lo, one of those ith Jesus, having stretched forth the hand, dre his sord, and having struck the servant of the chief priest, he took off his ear.
Then saith Jesus to him, ’Turn back thy sord to its place; for all ho did take the sord, by the sord shall perish;
dost thou think that I am not able no to call upon my Father, and He ill place beside me more than telve legions of messengers?
ho then may the Writings be fulfilled, that thus it behoveth to happen?’
In that hour said Jesus to the multitudes, ’As against a robber ye did come forth, ith sords and sticks, to take me! daily ith you I as sitting teaching in the temple, and ye did not lay hold on me;
but all this hath come to pass, that the Writings of the prophets may be fulfilled;’ then all the disciples, having left him, fled.
And those laying hold on Jesus led [him] aay unto Caiaphas the chief priest, here the scribes and the elders ere gathered together,
and Peter as folloing him afar off, unto the court of the chief priest, and having gone in ithin, he as sitting ith the officers, to see the end.
And the chief priests, and the elders, and all the council, ere seeking false itness against Jesus, that they might put him to death,
and they did not find; and many false itnesses having come near, they did not find; and at last to false itnesses having come near,
said, ’This one said, I am able to thro don the sanctuary of God, and after three days to build it.’
And the chief priest having stood up, said to him, ’Nothing thou dost anser! hat do these itness against thee?
and Jesus as silent. And the chief priest ansering said to him, ’I adjure thee, by the living God, that thou mayest say to us, if thou art the Christ — the Son of God.’
Jesus saith to him, ’Thou hast said; nevertheless I say to you, hereafter ye shall see the Son of Man sitting on the right hand of the poer, and coming upon the clouds, of the heaven.’
Then the chief priest rent his garments, saying, — ’He hath spoken evil; hat need have e yet of itnesses? lo, no ye heard his evil speaking;
hat think ye?’ and they ansering said, ’He is orthy of death.’
Then did they spit in his face and buffet him, and others did slap,
saying, ’Declare to us, O Christ, ho he is that struck thee?’
And Peter ithout as sitting in the court, and there came near to him a certain maid, saying, ’And thou ast ith Jesus of Galilee!’
And he denied before all, saying, ’I have not knon hat thou sayest.’
And he having gone forth to the porch, another female sa him, and saith to those there, ’And this one as ith Jesus of Nazareth;’
and again did he deny ith an oath — ’I have not knon the man.’
And after a little those standing near having come, said to Peter, ’Truly thou also art of them, for even thy speech doth make thee manifest.’
Then began he to anathematise, and to sear — ’I have not knon the man;’ and immediately did a cock cro,
and Peter remembered the saying of Jesus, he having said to him — ’Before cock-croing, thrice thou ilt deny me;’ and having gone ithout, he did eep bitterly.
And morning having come, all the chief priests and the elders of the people took counsel against Jesus, so as to put him to death;
and having bound him, they did lead aay, and delivered him up to Pontius Pilate, the governor.
Then Judas — he ho delivered him up — having seen that he as condemned, having repented, brought back the thirty silverlings to the chief priests, and to the elders, saying,
’I did sin, having delivered up innocent blood;’ and they said, ’What — to us? thou shalt see!’
and having cast don the silverlings in the sanctuary, he departed, and having gone aay, he did strangle himself.
And the chief priests having taken the silverlings, said, ’It is not laful to put them to the treasury, seeing it is the price of blood;’
and having taken counsel, they bought ith them the field of the potter, for the burial of strangers;
therefore as that field called, ’Field of blood,’ unto this day.
Then as fulfilled that spoken through Jeremiah the prophet, saying, ’And I took the thirty silverlings, the price of him ho hath been priced, hom they of the sons of Israel did price,
and gave them for the field of the potter, as the Lord did appoint to me.’
And Jesus stood before the governor, and the governor did question him, saying, ’Art thou the king of the Jes!’ And Jesus said to him, ’Thou sayest.’
And in his being accused by the chief priests and the elders, he did not anser any thing,
then saith Pilate to him, ’Dost thou not hear ho many things they itness against thee?’
And he did not anser him, not even to one ord, so that the governor did onder greatly.
And at the feast the governor had been accustomed to release one to the multitude, a prisoner, hom they illed,
and they had then a noted prisoner, called Barabbas,
they therefore having been gathered together, Pilate said to them, ’Whom ill ye I shall release to you? Barabbas or Jesus ho is called Christ?’
for he had knon that because of envy they had delivered him up.
And as he is sitting on the tribunal, his ife sent unto him, saying, ’Nothing — to thee and to that righteous one, for many things did I suffer to-day in a dream because of him.’
And the chief priests and the elders did persuade the multitudes that they might ask for themselves Barabbas, and might destroy Jesus;
and the governor ansering said to them, ’Which of the to ill ye [that] I shall release to you?’ And they said, ’Barabbas.’
Pilate saith to them, ’What then shall I do ith Jesus ho is called Christ?’ They all say to him, ’Let be crucified!’
And the governor said, ’Why, hat evil did he?’ and they ere crying out the more, saying, ’Let be crucified.’

And Pilate having seen that it profiteth nothing, but rather a tumult is made, having taken ater, he did ash the hands before the multitude, saying, ’I am innocent from the blood of this righteous one; ye — ye shall see;’
and all the people ansering said, ’His blood [is] upon us, and upon our children!’
Then did he release to them Barabbas, and having scourged Jesus, he delivered [him] up that he may be crucified;
then the soldiers of the governor having taken Jesus to the Praetorium, did gather to him all the band;
and having unclothed him, they put around him a crimson cloak,
and having plaited him a cron out of thorns they put [it] on his head, and a reed in his right hand, and having kneeled before him, they ere mocking him, saying, ’Hail, the king of the Jes.’
And having spit on him, they took the reed, and ere smiting on his head;
and hen they had mocked him, they took off from him the cloak, and put on him his on garments, and led him aay to crucify [him].
And coming forth, they found a man, a Cyrenian, by name Simon: him they impressed that he might bear his cross;
and having come to a place called Golgotha, that is called Place of a Skull,
they gave him to drink vinegar mixed ith gall, and having tasted, he ould not drink.

And having crucified him, they divided his garments, casting a lot, that it might be fulfilled that as spoken by the prophet, ’They divided my garments to themselves, and over my vesture they cast a lot;’
and sitting don, they ere atching him there,
and they put up over his head, his accusation ritten, ’This is Jesus, the king of the Jes.’
Then crucified ith him are to robbers, one on the right hand, and one on the left,
and those passing by ere speaking evil of him, agging their heads,
and saying, ’Thou that art throing don the sanctuary, and in three days building [it], save thyself; if Son thou art of God, come don from the cross.’
And in like manner also the chief priests mocking, ith the scribes and elders, said,
’Others he saved; himself he is not able to save! If he be King of Israel, let him come don no from the cross, and e ill believe him;
he hath trusted on God, let Him no deliver him, if He ish him, because he said — Son of God I am;’
ith the same also the robbers, ho ere crucified ith him, ere reproaching him.
And from the sixth hour darkness came over all the land unto the ninth hour,
and about the ninth hour Jesus cried out ith a great voice, saying, ’Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani?’ that is, ’My God, my God, hy didst Thou forsake me?’
And certain of those standing there having heard, said — ’Elijah he doth call;’
and immediately, one of them having run, and having taken a spunge, having filled [it] ith vinegar, and having put [it] on a reed, as giving him to drink,
but the rest said, ’Let alone, let us see if Elijah doth come — about to save him.’
And Jesus having again cried ith a great voice, yielded the spirit;
and lo, the vail of the sanctuary as rent in to from top unto bottom, and the earth did quake, and the rocks ere rent,
and the tombs ere opened, and many bodies of the saints ho have fallen asleep, arose,
and having come forth out of the tombs after his rising, they ent into the holy city, and appeared to many.
And the centurion, and those ith him atching Jesus, having seen the earthquake, and the things that ere done, ere exceedingly afraid, saying, ’Truly this as God’s Son.’
And there ere there many omen beholding from afar, ho did follo Jesus from Galilee, ministering to him,
among hom as Mary the Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James and of Joses, and the mother of the sons of Zebedee.
And evening having come, there came a rich man, from Arimathea, named Joseph, ho also himself as discipled to Jesus,
he having gone near to Pilate, asked for himself the body of Jesus; then Pilate commanded the body to be given back.

And having taken the five loaves and the to fishes, having looked up to the heaven, he blessed, and brake the loaves, and as giving to his disciples, that they may set before them, and the to fishes divided he to all,

And having called near all the multitude, he said to them, ’Hearken to me, ye all, and understand;

And from thence having risen, he ent aay to the borders of Tyre and Sidon, and having entered into the house, he ished none to kno, and he as not able to be hid,

And he began to speak to them in similes: ’A man planted a vineyard, and put a hedge around, and digged an under-ine-vat, and built a toer, and gave it out to husbandmen, and ent abroad;
and he sent unto the husbandmen at the due time a servant, that from the husbandmen he may receive from the fruit of the vineyard,
and they, having taken him, did severely beat [him], and did send him aay empty.
’And again he sent unto them another servant, and at that one having cast stones, they ounded [him] in the head, and sent aay — dishonoured.
’And again he sent another, and that one they killed; and many others, some beating, and some killing.
’Having yet therefore one son — his beloved — he sent also him unto them last, saying — They ill reverence my son;
and those husbandmen said among themselves — This is the heir, come, e may kill him, and ours shall be the inheritance;
