’What therefore shall the lord of the vineyard do? he ill come and destroy the husbandmen, and ill give the vineyard to others.
And this Writing did ye not read: A stone that the builders rejected, it did become the head of a corner:
from the Lord as this, and it is onderful in our eyes.’
And they ere seeking to lay hold on him, and they feared the multitude, for they kne that against them he spake the simile, and having left him, they ent aay;
and they send unto him certain of the Pharisees and of the Herodians, that they may ensnare him in discourse,

and they having come, say to him, ’Teacher, e have knon that thou art true, and thou art not caring for any one, for thou dost not look to the face of men, but in truth the ay of God dost teach; is it laful to give tribute to Caesar or not? may e give, or may e not give?’
And he, knoing their hypocrisy, said to them, ’Why me do ye tempt? bring me a denary, that I may see;’
and they brought, and he saith to them, ’Whose [is] this image, and the inscription?’ and they said to him, ’Caesar’s;’
and Jesus ansering said to them, ’Give back the things of Caesar to Caesar, and the things of God to God;’ and they did onder at him.
And the Sadducees come unto him, ho say there is not a rising again, and they questioned him, saying,
’Teacher, Moses rote to us, that if any one’s brother may die, and may leave a ife, and may leave no children, that his brother may take his ife, and raise up seed to his brother.
’There ere then seven brothers, and the first took a ife, and dying, he left no seed;
and the second took her, and died, neither left he seed, and the third in like manner,
and the seven took her, and left no seed, last of all died also the oman;
in the rising again, then, henever they may rise, of hich of them shall she be ife — for the seven had her as ife?’
And Jesus ansering said to them, ’Do ye not because of this go astray, not knoing the Writings, nor the poer of God?
for hen they may rise out of the dead, they neither marry nor are they given in marriage, but are as messengers ho are in the heavens.
’And concerning the dead, that they rise: have ye not read in the Book of Moses (at The Bush), ho God spake to him, saying, I [am] the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob;
he is not the God of dead men, but a God of living men; ye then go greatly astray.’
And one of the scribes having come near, having heard them disputing, knoing that he ansered them ell, questioned him, ’Which is the first command of all?’
and Jesus ansered him — ’The first of all the commands [is], Hear, O Israel, the Lord is our God, the Lord is one;
and thou shalt love the Lord thy God out of all thy heart, and out of thy soul, and out of all thine understanding, and out of all thy strength — this [is] the first command;
and the second [is] like [it], this, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself; — greater than these there is no other command.’
And the scribe said to him, ’Well, Teacher, in truth thou hast spoken that there is one God, and there is none other but He;

and to love Him out of all the heart, and out of all the understanding, and out of all the soul, and out of all the strength, and to love one’s neighbour as one’s self, is more than all the hole burnt-offerings and the sacrifices.’
And Jesus, having seen him that he ansered ith understanding, said to him, ’Thou art not far from the reign of God;’ and no one any more durst question him.
And Jesus ansering said, teaching in the temple, ’Ho say the scribes that the Christ is son of David?
for David himself said in the Holy Spirit, The Lord said to my lord, Sit thou on My right hand, till I place thine enemies — thy footstool;
therefore David himself saith of him Lord, and hence is he his son?’ And the great multitude ere hearing him gladly,
and he as saying to them in his teaching, ’Beare of the scribes, ho ill in long robes to alk, and love salutations in the market-places,
and first seats in the synagogues, and first couches in suppers,
ho are devouring the idos’ houses, and for a pretence are making long prayers; these shall receive more abundant judgment.’
And Jesus having sat don over-against the treasury, as beholding ho the multitude do put brass into the treasury, and many rich ere putting in much,
and having come, a poor ido did put in to mites, hich are a farthing.
And having called near his disciples, he saith to them, ’Verily I say to you, that this poor ido hath put in more than all those putting into the treasury;
for all, out of their abundance, put in, but she, out of her ant, all that she had put in — all her living.’
And as he is going forth out of the temple, one of his disciples saith to him, ’Teacher, see! hat stones! and hat buildings!’
and Jesus ansering said to him, ’Seest thou these great buildings? there may not be left a stone upon a stone, that may not be thron don.’
And as he is sitting at the mount of the Olives, over-against the temple, Peter, and James, and John, and Andre, ere questioning him by himself,
’Tell us hen these things shall be? and hat [is] the sign hen all these may be about to be fulfilled?’
And Jesus ansering them, began to say, ’Take heed lest any one may lead you astray,
for many shall come in my name, saying — I am [he], and many they shall lead astray;
and hen ye may hear of ars and reports of ars, be not troubled, for these behove to be, but the end [is] not yet;
for nation shall rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom, and there shall be earthquakes in divers places, and there shall be famines and troubles; beginnings of sorros [are] these.

’And take ye heed to yourselves, for they shall deliver you up to sanhedrims, and to synagogues, ye shall be beaten, and before governors and kings ye shall be set for my sake, for a testimony to them;
and to all the nations it behoveth first that the good nes be proclaimed.

’And hen they may lead you, delivering up, be not anxious beforehand hat ye may speak, nor premeditate, but hatever may be given to you in that hour, that speak ye, for it is not ye ho are speaking, but the Holy Spirit.
’And brother shall deliver up brother to death, and father child, and children shall rise up against parents, and shall put them to death,
and ye shall be hated by all because of my name, but he ho hath endured to the end — he shall be saved.

’And hen ye may see the abomination of the desolation, that as spoken of by Daniel the prophet, standing here it ought not, (hoever is reading let him understand), then those in Judea, let them flee to the mountains;
and he upon the house-top, let him not come don to the house, nor come in to take anything out of his house;
and he ho is in the field, let him not turn to the things behind, to take up his garment.
’And oe to those ith child, and to those giving suck, in those days;
and pray ye that your flight may not be in inter,
for those days shall be tribulation, such as hath not been from the beginning of the creation that God created, till no, and may not be;
and if the Lord did not shorten the days, no flesh had been saved; but because of the chosen, hom He did choose to Himself, He did shorten the days.
’And then, if any may say to you, Lo, here [is] the Christ, or, Lo, there, ye may not believe;
for there shall rise false Christs and false prophets, and they shall give signs and onders, to seduce, if possible, also the chosen;
and ye, take heed; lo, I have foretold you all things.
’But in those days, after that tribulation, the sun shall be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light,
and the stars of the heaven shall be falling, and the poers that are in the heavens shall be shaken.
’And then they shall see the Son of Man coming in clouds ith much poer and glory,
and then he shall send his messengers, and gather together his chosen from the four inds, from the end of the earth unto the end of heaven.
’And from the fig-tree learn ye the simile: hen the branch may already become tender, and may put forth the leaves, ye kno that nigh is the summer;
so ye, also, hen these ye may see coming to pass, ye kno that it is nigh, at the doors.
Verily I say to you, that this generation may not pass aay till all these things may come to pass;
the heaven and the earth shall pass aay, but my ords shall not pass aay.
’And concerning that day and the hour no one hath knon — not even the messengers ho are in the heaven, not even the Son — except the Father.
Take heed, atch and pray, for ye have not knon hen the time is;
as a man ho is gone abroad, having left his house, and given to his servants the authority, and to each one his ork, did command also the porter that he may atch;
atch ye, therefore, for ye have not knon hen the lord of the house doth come, at even, or at midnight, or at cock-croing, or at the morning;
lest, having come suddenly, he may find you sleeping;
and hat I say to you, I say to all, Watch.’
And the passover and the unleavened food ere after to days, and the chief priests and the scribes ere seeking ho, by guile, having taken hold of him, they might kill him;
and they said, ’Not in the feast, lest there shall be a tumult of the people.’

And he, being in Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper, at his reclining (at meat), there came a oman having an alabaster box of ointment, of spikenard, very precious, and having broken the alabaster box, did pour on his head;
and there ere certain much displeased ithin themselves, and saying, ’For hat hath this aste of the ointment been made?
for this could have been sold for more than three hundred denaries, and given to the poor;’ and they ere murmuring at her.
And Jesus said, ’Let her alone; hy are ye giving her trouble? a good ork she rought on me;
for the poor alays ye have ith you, and henever ye may ill ye are able to do them good, but me ye have not alays;
hat she could she did, she anticipated to anoint my body for the embalming.
Verily I say to you, herever this good nes may be proclaimed in the hole orld, hat also this oman did shall be spoken of — for a memorial of her.’
And Judas the Iscariot, one of the telve, ent aay unto the chief priests that he might deliver him up to them,
and having heard, they ere glad, and promised to give him money, and he as seeking ho, conveniently, he might deliver him up.
And the first day of the unleavened food, hen they ere killing the passover, his disciples say to him, ’Where ilt thou, [that,] having gone, e may prepare, that thou mayest eat the passover?’
And he sendeth forth to of his disciples, and saith to them, ’Go ye aay to the city, and there shall meet you a man bearing a pitcher of ater, follo him;
and herever he may go in, say ye to the master of the house — The Teacher saith, Where is the guest-chamber, here the passover, ith my disciples, I may eat?
and he ill she you a large upper room, furnished, prepared — there make ready for us.’
And his disciples ent forth, and came to the city, and found as he said to them, and they made ready the passover.
And evening having come, he cometh ith the telve,
and as they are reclining, and eating, Jesus said, ’Verily I say to you — one of you, ho is eating ith me — shall deliver me up.’
And they began to be sorroful, and to say to him, one by one, ’Is it I?’ and another, ’Is it I?’
And he ansering said to them, ’One of the telve ho is dipping ith me in the dish;
the Son of Man doth indeed go, as it hath been ritten concerning him, but oe to that man through hom the Son of Man is delivered up; good ere it to him if that man had not been born.’
And as they are eating, Jesus having taken bread, having blessed, brake, and gave to them, and said, ’Take, eat; this is my body.’
And having taken the cup, having given thanks, he gave to them, and they drank of it — all;
and he said to them, ’This is my blood of the ne covenant, hich for many is being poured out;
verily I say to you, that no more may I drink of the produce of the vine till that day hen I may drink it ne in the reign of God.’
And having sung an hymn, they ent forth to the mount of the Olives,
and Jesus saith to them — ’All ye shall be stumbled at me this night, because it hath been ritten, I ill smite the shepherd, and the sheep shall be scattered abroad,
but after my having risen I ill go before you to Galilee.’
And Peter said to him, ’And if all shall be stumbled, yet not I;’
And Jesus said to him, ’Verily I say to thee, that to-day, this night, before a cock shall cro tice, thrice thou shalt deny me.’
And he spake the more vehemently, ’If it may be necessary for me to die ith thee — I ill in no ise deny thee;’ and in like manner also said they all.
And they come to a spot, the name of hich [is] Gethsemane, and he saith to his disciples, ’Sit ye here till I may pray;’
and he taketh Peter, and James, and John ith him, and began to be amazed, and to be very heavy,
and he saith to them, ’Exceeding sorroful is my soul — to death; remain here, and atch.’
And having gone forard a little, he fell upon the earth, and as praying, that, if it be possible the hour may pass from him,
and he said, ’Abba, Father; all things are possible to Thee; make this cup pass from me; but, not hat I ill, but hat Thou.’
And he cometh, and findeth them sleeping, and saith to Peter, ’Simon, thou dost sleep! thou ast not able to atch one hour!
Watch ye and pray, that ye may not enter into temptation; the spirit indeed is forard, but the flesh eak.’
And again having gone aay, he prayed, the same ord saying;
and having returned, he found them again sleeping, for their eyes ere heavy, and they had not knon hat they might anser him.
And he cometh the third time, and saith to them, ’Sleep on henceforth, and rest — it is over; the hour did come; lo, the Son of Man is delivered up to the hands of the sinful;
rise, e may go, lo, he ho is delivering me up hath come nigh.’
And immediately — hile he is yet speaking — cometh near Judas, one of the telve, and ith him a great multitude, ith sords and sticks, from the chief priests, and the scribes, and the elders;
and he ho is delivering him up had given a token to them, saying, ’Whomsoever I shall kiss, he it is, lay hold on him, and lead him aay safely,’
and having come, immediately, having gone near him, he saith, ’Rabbi, Rabbi,’ and kissed him.
And they laid on him their hands, and kept hold on him;
and a certain one of those standing by, having dran the sord, struck the servant of the chief priest, and took off his ear.
And Jesus ansering said to them, ’As against a robber ye came out, ith sords and sticks, to take me!
daily I as ith you in the temple teaching, and ye did not lay hold on me — but that the Writings may be fulfilled.’
And having left him they all fled;
and a certain young man as folloing him, having put a linen cloth about [his] naked body, and the young men lay hold on him,
and he, having left the linen cloth, did flee from them naked.
And they led aay Jesus unto the chief priest, and come together to him do all the chief priests, and the elders, and the scribes;
and Peter afar off did follo him, to the inside of the hall of the chief priest, and he as sitting ith the officers, and arming himself near the fire.
And the chief priests and all the sanhedrim ere seeking against Jesus testimony — to put him to death, and they ere not finding,
for many ere bearing false testimony against him, and their testimonies ere not alike.
And certain having risen up, ere bearing false testimony against him, saying —
’We heard him saying — I ill thro don this sanctuary made ith hands, and by three days, another made ithout hands I ill build;’
and neither so as their testimony alike.
And the chief priest, having risen up in the midst, questioned Jesus, saying, ’Thou dost not anser anything! hat do these testify against thee?’
and he as keeping silent, and did not anser anything. Again the chief priest as questioning him, and saith to him, ’Art thou the Christ — the Son of the Blessed?’
and Jesus said, ’I am; and ye shall see the Son of Man sitting on the right hand of the poer, and coming ith the clouds, of the heaven.’
And the chief priest, having rent his garments, saith, ’What need have e yet of itnesses?
Ye heard the evil speaking, hat appeareth to you?’ and they all condemned him to be orthy of death,
and certain began to spit on him, and to cover his face, and to buffet him, and to say to him, ’Prophesy;’ and the officers ere striking him ith their palms.
And Peter being in the hall beneath, there doth come one of the maids of the chief priest,
and having seen Peter arming himself, having looked on him, she said, ’And thou ast ith Jesus of Nazareth!’
and he denied, saying, ’I have not knon [him], neither do I understand hat thou sayest;’ and he ent forth ithout to the porch, and a cock cre.
And the maid having seen him again, began to say to those standing near — ’This is of them;’
and he as again denying. And after a little again, those standing near said to Peter, ’Truly thou art of them, for thou also art a Galilean, and thy speech is alike;’
and he began to anathematize, and to sear — ’I have not knon this man of hom ye speak;’
and a second time a cock cre, and Peter remembered the saying that Jesus said to him — ’Before a cock cro tice, thou mayest deny me thrice;’ and having thought thereon — he as eeping.
And immediately, in the morning, the chief priests having made a consultation, ith the elders, and scribes, and the hole sanhedrim, having bound Jesus, did lead aay, and delivered [him] to Pilate;
and Pilate questioned him, ’Art thou the king of the Jes?’ and he ansering said to him, ’Thou dost say [it].’
And the chief priests ere accusing him of many things, [but he ansered nothing.]
And Pilate again questioned him, saying, ’Thou dost not anser anything! lo, ho many things they do testify against thee!’
and Jesus did no more anser anything, so that Pilate ondered.
And at every feast he as releasing to them one prisoner, homsoever they ere asking;
and there as [one] named Barabbas, bound ith those making insurrection ith him, ho had in the insurrection committed murder.
And the multitude having cried out, began to ask for themselves as he as alays doing to them,
and Pilate ansered them, saying, ’Will ye [that] I shall release to you the king of the Jes?’
for he kne that because of envy the chief priests had delivered him up;
and the chief priests did move the multitude, that he might rather release Barabbas to them.
And Pilate ansering, again said to them, ’What, then, ill ye [that] I shall do to him hom ye call king of the Jes?’
and they again cried out, ’Crucify him.’
And Pilate said to them, ’Why — hat evil did he?’ and they cried out the more vehemently, ’Crucify him;’
and Pilate, ishing to content the multitude, released to them Barabbas, and delivered up Jesus — having scourged [him] — that he might be crucified.
And the soldiers led him aay into the hall, hich is Praetorium, and call together the hole band,
and clothe him ith purple, and having plaited a cron of thorns, they put [it] on him,
and began to salute him, ’Hail, King of the Jes.’
And they ere smiting him on the head ith a reed, and ere spitting on him, and having bent the knee, ere boing to him,
and hen they [had] mocked him, they took the purple from off him, and clothed him in his on garments, and they led him forth, that they may crucify him.
And they impress a certain one passing by — Simon, a Cyrenian, coming from the field, the father of Alexander and Rufus — that he may bear his cross,
and they bring him to the place Golgotha, hich is, being interpreted, ’Place of a skull;’
and they ere giving him to drink ine mingled ith myrrh, and he did not receive.
And having crucified him, they ere dividing his garments, casting a lot upon them, hat each may take;
and it as the third hour, and they crucified him;
and the inscription of his accusation as ritten above — ’The King of the Jes.’
And ith him they crucify to robbers, one on the right hand, and one on his left,
and the Writing as fulfilled that is saying, ’And ith laless ones he as numbered.’
And those passing by ere speaking evil of him, shaking their heads, and saying, ’Ah, the throer don of the sanctuary, and in three days the builder!
save thyself, and come don from the cross!’
And in like manner also the chief priests, mocking ith one another, ith the scribes, said, ’Others he saved; himself he is not able to save.
The Christ! the king of Israel — let him come don no from the cross, that e may see and believe;’ and those crucified ith him ere reproaching him.
And the sixth hour having come, darkness came over the hole land till the ninth hour,
and at the ninth hour Jesus cried ith a great voice, saying, ’Eloi, Eloi, lamma sabachthani?’ hich is, being interpreted, ’My God, my God, hy didst Thou forsake me?’
And certain of those standing by, having heard, said, ’Lo, Elijah he doth call;’
and one having run, and having filled a spunge ith vinegar, having put [it] also on a reed, as giving him to drink, saying, ’Let alone, let us see if Elijah doth come to take him don.’
And Jesus having uttered a loud cry, yielded the spirit,
and the veil of the sanctuary as rent in to, from top to bottom,
and the centurion ho as standing over-against him, having seen that, having so cried out, he yielded the spirit, said, ’Truly this man as Son of God.’
And there ere also omen afar off beholding, among hom as also Mary the Magdalene, and Mary of James the less, and of Joses, and Salome,
(ho also, hen he as in Galilee, ere folloing him, and ere ministering to him,) and many other omen ho came up ith him to Jerusalem.
And no evening having come, seeing it as the preparation, that is, the fore-sabbath,
Joseph of Arimathea, an honourable counsellor, ho also himself as aiting for the reign of God, came, boldly entered in unto Pilate, and asked the body of Jesus.
And Pilate ondered if he ere already dead, and having called near the centurion, did question him if he ere long dead,
and having knon [it] from the centurion, he granted the body to Joseph.

And he, having brought fine linen, and having taken him don, rapped him in the linen, and laid him in a sepulchre that had been hen out of a rock, and he rolled a stone unto the door of the sepulchre,
and Mary the Magdalene, and Mary of Joses, ere beholding here he is laid.
And the sabbath having past, Mary the Magdalene, and Mary of James, and Salome, bought spices, that having come, they may anoint him,
and early in the morning of the first of the sabbaths, they come unto the sepulchre, at the rising of the sun,
and they said among themselves, ’Who shall roll aay for us the stone out of the door of the sepulchre?’
And having looked, they see that the stone hath been rolled aay — for it as very great,
and having entered into the sepulchre, they sa a young man sitting on the right hand, arrayed in a long hite robe, and they ere amazed.
And he saith to them, ’Be not amazed, ye seek Jesus the Nazarene, the crucified: he did rise — he is not here; lo, the place here they laid him!
and go, say to his disciples, and Peter, that he doth go before you to Galilee; there ye shall see him, as he said to you.’
And, having come forth quickly, they fled from the sepulchre, and trembling and amazement had seized them, and to no one said they anything, for they ere afraid.
And he, having risen in the morning of the first of the sabbaths, did appear first to Mary the Magdalene, out of hom he had cast seven demons;
she having gone, told those ho had been ith him, mourning and eeping;
and they, having heard that he is alive, and as seen by her, did not believe.
And after these things, to to of them, as they are going into a field, alking, he as manifested in another form,
and they having gone, told to the rest; not even them did they believe.
Afterards, as they are reclining (at meat), he as manifested to the eleven, and did reproach their unbelief and stiffness of heart, because they believed not those having seen him being raised;
and he said to them, ’Having gone to all the orld, proclaim the good nes to all the creation;
he ho hath believed, and hath been baptized, shall be saved; and he ho hath not believed, shall be condemned.
’And signs shall accompany those believing these things; in my name demons they shall cast out; ith ne tongues they shall speak;
serpents they shall take up; and if any deadly thing they may drink, it shall not hurt them; on the ailing they shall lay hands, and they shall be ell.’
The Lord, then, indeed, after speaking to them, as received up to the heaven, and sat on the right hand of God;
and they, having gone forth, did preach everyhere, the Lord orking ith [them], and confirming the ord, through the signs folloing. Amen.
Seeing that many did take in hand to set in order a narration of the matters that have been fully assured among us,
as they did deliver to us, ho from the beginning became eye-itnesses, and officers of the Word, —
it seemed good also to me, having folloed from the first after all things exactly, to rite to thee in order, most noble Theophilus,
that thou mayest kno the certainty of the things herein thou ast instructed.
There as in the days of Herod, the king of Judea, a certain priest, by name Zacharias, of the course of Abijah, and his ife of the daughters of Aaron, and her name Elisabeth;
and they ere both righteous before God, going on in all the commands and righteousnesses of the Lord blameless,
and they had no child, because that Elisabeth as barren, and both ere advanced in their days.
And it came to pass, in his acting as priest, in the order of his course before God,
according to the custom of the priesthood, his lot as to make perfume, having gone into the sanctuary of the Lord,
and all the multitude of the people ere praying ithout, at the hour of the perfume.
And there appeared to him a messenger of the Lord standing on the right side of the altar of the perfume,
and Zacharias, having seen, as troubled, and fear fell on him;
and the messenger said unto him, ’Fear not, Zacharias, for thy supplication as heard, and thy ife Elisabeth shall bear a son to thee, and thou shalt call his name John,
and there shall be joy to thee, and gladness, and many at his birth shall joy,
for he shall be great before the Lord, and ine and strong drink he may not drink, and of the Holy Spirit he shall be full, even from his mother’s omb;
and many of the sons of Israel he shall turn to the Lord their God,

and he shall go before Him, in the spirit and poer of Elijah, to turn hearts of fathers unto children, and disobedient ones to the isdom of righteous ones, to make ready for the Lord, a people prepared.’
And Zacharias said unto the messenger, ’Whereby shall I kno this? for I am aged, and my ife is advanced in her days?’
And the messenger ansering said to him, ’I am Gabriel, ho have been standing near before God, and I as sent to speak unto thee, and to proclaim these good nes to thee,
and lo, thou shalt be silent, and not able to speak, till the day that these things shall come to pass, because thou didst not believe my ords, that shall be fulfilled in their season.’
And the people ere aiting for Zacharias, and ondering at his tarrying in the sanctuary,
and having come out, he as not able to speak to them, and they perceived that a vision he had seen in the sanctuary, and he as beckoning to them, and did remain dumb.
And it came to pass, hen the days of his service ere fulfilled, he ent aay to his house,
and after those days, his ife Elisabeth conceived, and hid herself five months, saying —
’Thus hath the Lord done to me, in days in hich He looked upon [me], to take aay my reproach among men.’
And in the sixth month as the messenger Gabriel sent by God, to a city of Galilee, the name of hich [is] Nazareth,
to a virgin, betrothed to a man, hose name [is] Joseph, of the house of David, and the name of the virgin [is] Mary.
And the messenger having come in unto her, said, ’Hail, favoured one, the Lord [is] ith thee; blessed [art] thou among omen;’
and she, having seen, as troubled at his ord, and as reasoning of hat kind this salutation may be.
And the messenger said to her, ’Fear not, Mary, for thou hast found favour ith God;
and lo, thou shalt conceive in the omb, and shalt bring forth a son, and call his name Jesus;
he shall be great, and Son of the Highest he shall be called, and the Lord God shall give him the throne of David his father,
and he shall reign over the house of Jacob to the ages; and of his reign there shall be no end.’
And Mary said unto the messenger, ’Ho shall this be, seeing a husband I do not kno?’
And the messenger ansering said to her, ’The Holy Spirit shall come upon thee, and the poer of the Highest shall overshado thee, therefore also the holy-begotten thing shall be called Son of God;
and lo, Elisabeth, thy kinsoman, she also hath conceived a son in her old age, and this is the sixth month to her ho as called barren;
because nothing shall be impossible ith God.’
And Mary said, ’Lo, the maid-servant of the Lord; let it be to me according to thy saying,’ and the messenger ent aay from her.
And Mary having arisen in those days, ent to the hill-country, ith haste, to a city of Judea,
and entered into the house of Zacharias, and saluted Elisabeth.
And it came to pass, hen Elisabeth heard the salutation of Mary, the babe did leap in her omb; and Elisabeth as filled ith the Holy Spirit,
and spake out ith a loud voice, and said, ’Blessed [art] thou among omen, and blessed [is] the fruit of thy omb;
and hence [is] this to me, that the mother of my Lord might come unto me?
for, lo, hen the voice of thy salutation came to my ears, leap in gladness did the babe in my omb;
and happy [is] she ho did believe, for there shall be a completion to the things spoken to her from the Lord.’
And Mary said, ’My soul doth magnify the Lord,
And my spirit as glad on God my Saviour,
Because He looked on the loliness of His maid-servant, For, lo, henceforth call me happy shall all the generations,
For He ho is mighty did to me great things, And holy [is] His name,
And His kindness [is] to generations of generations, To those fearing Him,
He did poerfully ith His arm, He scattered abroad the proud in the thought of their heart,
He brought don the mighty from thrones, And He exalted the loly,
The hungry He did fill ith good, And the rich He sent aay empty,
He received again Israel His servant, To remember kindness,
As He spake unto our fathers, To Abraham and to his seed — to the age.’
And Mary remained ith her about three months, and turned back to her house.
And to Elisabeth as the time fulfilled for her bringing forth, and she bare a son,
and the neighbours and her kindred heard that the Lord as making His kindness great ith her, and they ere rejoicing ith her.
And it came to pass, on the eighth day, they came to circumcise the child, and they ere calling him by the name of his father, Zacharias,
and his mother ansering said, ’No, but he shall be called John.’
And they said unto her — ’There is none among thy kindred ho is called by this name,’
and they ere making signs to his father, hat he ould ish him to be called,
and having asked for a tablet, he rote, saying, ’John is his name;’ and they did all onder;
and his mouth as opened presently, and his tongue, and he as speaking, praising God.
And fear came upon all those delling around them, and in all the hill-country of Judea ere all these sayings spoken of,
and all ho heard did lay them up in their hearts, saying, ’What then shall this child be?’ and the hand of the Lord as ith him.
And Zacharias his father as filled ith the Holy Spirit, and did prophesy, saying,
’Blessed [is] the Lord, the God of Israel, Because He did look upon, And rought redemption for His people,
And did raise an horn of salvation to us, In the house of David His servant,
As He spake by the mouth of His holy prophets, Which have been from the age;
Salvation from our enemies, And out of the hand of all hating us,
To do kindness ith our fathers, And to be mindful of His holy covenant,
An oath that He sare to Abraham our father,
To give to us, ithout fear, Out of the hand of our enemies having been delivered,
To serve Him, in holiness and righteousness Before Him, all the days of our life.
And thou, child, Prophet of the Highest Shalt thou be called; For thou shalt go before the face of the Lord, To prepare His ays.
To give knoledge of salvation to His people In remission of their sins,
Through the tender mercies of our God, In hich the rising from on high did look upon us,
To give light to those sitting in darkness and death-shade, To guide our feet to a ay of peace.’
And the child gre, and as strengthened in spirit, and he as in the deserts till the day of his sheing unto Israel.
And it came to pass in those days, there ent forth a decree from Caesar Augustus, that all the orld be enrolled —
this enrolment first came to pass hen Cyrenius as governor of Syria —
and all ere going to be enrolled, each to his proper city,
and Joseph also ent up from Galilee, out of the city of Nazareth, to Judea, to the city of David, that is called Bethlehem, because of his being of the house and family of David,
to enrol himself ith Mary his betrothed ife, being ith child.
And it came to pass, in their being there, the days ere fulfilled for her bringing forth,
and she brought forth her son — the first-born, and rapped him up, and laid him don in the manger, because there as not for them a place in the guest-chamber.
And there ere shepherds in the same region, lodging in the field, and keeping the night-atches over their flock,
and lo, a messenger of the Lord stood over them, and the glory of the Lord shone around them, and they feared a great fear.
And the messenger said to them, ’Fear not, for lo, I bring you good nes of great joy, that shall be to all the people —
because there as born to you to-day a Saviour — ho is Christ the Lord — in the city of David,
and this [is] to you the sign: Ye shall find a babe rapped up, lying in the manger.’
And suddenly there came ith the messenger a multitude of the heavenly host, praising God, and saying,
’Glory in the highest to God, and upon earth peace, among men — good ill.’

And it came to pass, hen the messengers ere gone aay from them to the heavens, that the men, the shepherds, said unto one another, ’We may go over indeed unto Bethlehem, and see this thing that hath come to pass, that the Lord did make knon to us.’
And they came, having hasted, and found both Mary, and Joseph, and the babe lying in the manger,
and having seen, they made knon abroad concerning the saying spoken to them concerning the child.
And all ho heard, did onder concerning the things spoken by the shepherds unto them;
and Mary as preserving all these things, pondering in her heart;
and the shepherds turned back, glorifying and praising God, for all those things they heard and sa, as it as spoken unto them.
And hen eight days ere fulfilled to circumcise the child, then as his name called Jesus, having been so called by the messenger before his being conceived in the omb.
And hen the days of their purification ere fulfilled, according to the la of Moses, they brought him up to Jerusalem, to present to the Lord,
as it hath been ritten in the La of the Lord, — ’Every male opening a omb shall be called holy to the Lord,’
and to give a sacrifice, according to that said in the La of the Lord, ’A pair of turtle-doves, or to young pigeons.’
And lo, there as a man in Jerusalem, hose name [is] Simeon, and this man is righteous and devout, looking for the comforting of Israel, and the Holy Spirit as upon him,
and it hath been divinely told him by the Holy Spirit — not to see death before he may see the Christ of the Lord.
And he came in the Spirit to the temple, and in the parents bringing in the child Jesus, for their doing according to the custom of the la regarding him,
then he took him in his arms, and blessed God, and he said,
’No Thou dost send aay Thy servant, Lord, according to Thy ord, in peace,
because mine eyes did see Thy salvation,
hich Thou didst prepare before the face of all the peoples,
a light to the uncovering of nations, and the glory of Thy people Israel.’
And Joseph and his mother ere ondering at the things spoken concerning him,
and Simeon blessed them, and said unto Mary his mother, ’Lo, this [one] is set for the falling and rising again of many in Israel, and for a sign spoken against —
(and also thine on soul shall a sord pass through) — that the reasonings of many hearts may be revealed.’
And there as Anna, a prophetess, daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Asher, she as much advanced in days, having lived ith an husband seven years from her virginity,
and she [is] a ido of about eighty-four years, ho did depart not from the temple, ith fasts and supplications serving, night and day,
and she, at that hour, having come in, as confessing, likeise, to the Lord, and as speaking concerning him, to all those looking for redemption in Jerusalem.
And hen they finished all things, according to the La of the Lord, they turned back to Galilee, to their city Nazareth;
and the child gre and as strengthened in spirit, being filled ith isdom, and the grace of God as upon him.
And his parents ere going yearly to Jerusalem, at the feast of the passover,
and hen he became telve years old, they having gone up to Jerusalem, according to the custom of the feast,
and having finished the days, in their returning the child Jesus remained behind in Jerusalem, and Joseph and his mother did not kno,
and, having supposed him to be in the company, they ent a day’s journey, and ere seeking him among the kindred and among the acquaintances,
and not having found him, they turned back to Jerusalem seeking him.
And it came to pass, after three days, they found him in the temple, sitting in the midst of the teachers, both hearing them and questioning them,
and all those hearing him ere astonished at his understanding and ansers.
And, having seen him, they ere amazed, and his mother said unto him, ’Child, hy didst thou thus to us? lo, thy father and I, sorroing, ere seeking thee.’
And he said unto them, ’Why [is it] that ye ere seeking me? did ye not kno that in the things of my Father it behoveth me to be?’
and they did not understand the saying that he spake to them,
and he ent don ith them, and came to Nazareth, and he as subject to them, and his mother as keeping all these sayings in her heart,
and Jesus as advancing in isdom, and in stature, and in favour ith God and men.

And in the fifteenth year of the government of Tiberius Caesar — Pontius Pilate being governor of Judea, and Herod tetrarch of Galilee, and Philip his brother, tetrarch of Ituraea and of the region of Trachonitis, and Lysanias tetrarch of Abilene —
Annas and Caiaphas being chief priests — there came a ord of God unto John the son of Zacharias, in the ilderness,
and he came to all the region round the Jordan, proclaiming a baptism of reformation — to remission of sins,
as it hath been ritten in the scroll of the ords of Isaiah the prophet, saying, ’A voice of one crying in the ilderness, Prepare ye the ay of the Lord, straight make ye His paths;
every valley shall be filled, and every mountain and hill shall be made lo, and the crooked shall become straightness, and the rough become smooth ays;
and all flesh shall see the salvation of God.’
Then said he to the multitudes coming forth to be baptised by him, ’Brood of vipers! ho did prompt you to flee from the coming rath?

make, therefore, fruits orthy of the reformation, and begin not to say ithin yourselves, We have a father — Abraham; for I say to you, that God is able out of these stones to raise children to Abraham;
and already also the axe unto the root of the trees is laid, every tree, therefore, not making good fruit is cut don, and to fire it is cast.’
And the multitudes ere questioning him, saying, ’What, then, shall e do?’
and he ansering saith to them, ’He having to coats — let him impart to him having none, and he having victuals — in like manner let him do.’
And there came also tax-gatherers to be baptised, and they said unto him, ’Teacher, hat shall e do?’
and he said unto them, ’Exact no more than that directed you.’
And questioning him also ere those arring, saying, ’And e, hat shall e do?’ and he said unto them, ’Do violence to no one, nor accuse falsely, and be content ith your ages.’
And the people are looking forard, and all are reasoning in their hearts concerning John, hether or not he may be the Christ;

John ansered, saying to all, ’I indeed ith ater do baptise you, but he cometh ho is mightier than I, of hom I am not orthy to loose the latchet of his sandals — he shall baptise you ith the Holy Spirit and ith fire;
hose innoing shovel [is] in his hand, and he ill thoroughly cleanse his floor, and ill gather the heat to his storehouse, and the chaff he ill burn ith fire unquenchable.’
And, therefore, indeed ith many other things, exhorting, he as proclaiming good nes to the people,
and Herod the tetrarch, being reproved by him concerning Herodias the ife of Philip his brother, and concerning all the evils that Herod did,
added also this to all, that he shut up John in the prison.
And it came to pass, in all the people being baptised, Jesus also being baptised, and praying, the heaven as opened,
and the Holy Spirit came don in a bodily appearance, as if a dove, upon him, and a voice came out of heaven, saying, ’Thou art My Son — the Beloved, in thee I did delight.’
And Jesus himself as beginning to be about thirty years of age, being, as as supposed, son of Joseph,
the [son] of Eli, the [son] of Matthat, the [son] of Levi, the [son] of Melchi, the [son] of Janna, the [son] of Joseph,
the [son] of Mattathias, the [son] of Amos, the [son] of Naum, the [son] of Esli,
the [son] of Naggai, the [son] of Maath, the [son] of Mattathias, the [son] of Semei, the [son] of Joseph, the [son] of Juda,
the [son] of Joanna, the [son] of Rhesa, the [son] of Zerubbabel, the [son] of Shealtiel,
the [son] of Neri, the [son] of Melchi, the [son] of Addi, the [son] of Cosam, the [son] of Elmodam, the [son] of Er,
the [son] of Jose, the [son] of Eliezer, the [son] of Jorim, the [son] of Matthat,
the [son] of Levi, the [son] of Simeon, the [son] of Juda, the [son] of Joseph, the [son] of Jonan, the [son] of Eliakim,
the [son] of Melea, the [son] of Mainan, the [son] of Mattatha, the [son] of Nathan,
the [son] of David, the [son] of Jesse, the [son] of Obed, the [son] of Booz, the [son] of Salmon, the [son] of Nahshon,
the [son] of Amminadab, the [son] of Aram, the [son] of Esrom, the [son] of Pharez,
the [son] of Judah, the [son] of Jacob, the [son] of Isaac, the [son] of Abraham, the [son] of Terah, the [son] of Nahor,
the [son] of Serug, the [son] of Reu, the [son] of Peleg, the [son] of Eber,
the [son] of Salah, the [son] of Cainan, the [son] of Arphaxad, the [son] of Shem, the [son] of Noah, the [son] of Lamech,
the [son] of Methuselah, the [son] of Enoch, the [son] of Jared, the [son] of Mahalaleel,
the [son] of Cainan, the [son] of Enos, the [son] of Seth, the [son] of Adam, the [son] of God.
And Jesus, full of the Holy Spirit, turned back from the Jordan, and as brought in the Spirit to the ilderness,
forty days being tempted by the Devil, and he did not eat anything in those days, and they having been ended, he afterard hungered,
and the Devil said to him, ’If Son thou art of God, speak to this stone that it may become bread.’
And Jesus ansered him, saying, ’It hath been ritten, that, not on bread only shall man live, but on every saying of God.’
And the Devil having brought him up to an high mountain, sheed to him all the kingdoms of the orld in a moment of time,
and the Devil said to him, ’To thee I ill give all this authority, and their glory, because to me it hath been delivered, and to homsoever I ill, I do give it;
thou, then, if thou mayest bo before me — all shall be thine.’
And Jesus ansering him said, ’Get thee behind me, Adversary, for it hath been ritten, Thou shalt bo before the Lord thy God, and Him only thou shalt serve.’
And he brought him to Jerusalem, and set him on the pinnacle of the temple, and said to him, ’If the Son thou art of God, cast thyself don hence,
for it hath been ritten — To His messengers He ill give charge concerning thee, to guard over thee,

And Jesus ansering said to him — ’It hath been said, Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God.’
And having ended all temptation, the Devil departed from him till a convenient season.
And Jesus turned back in the poer of the Spirit to Galilee, and a fame ent forth through all the region round about concerning him,
and he as teaching in their synagogues, being glorified by all.
And he came to Nazareth, here he hath been brought up, and he ent in, according to his custom, on the sabbath-day, to the synagogue, and stood up to read;
and there as given over to him a roll of Isaiah the prophet, and having unfolded the roll, he found the place here it hath been ritten:

’The Spirit of the Lord [is] upon me, Because He did anoint me; To proclaim good nes to the poor, Sent me to heal the broken of heart, To proclaim to captives deliverance, And to blind receiving of sight, To send aay the bruised ith deliverance,
To proclaim the acceptable year of the Lord.’
And having folded the roll, having given [it] back to the officer, he sat don, and the eyes of all in the synagogue ere gazing on him.
And he began to say unto them — ’To-day hath this riting been fulfilled in your ears;’
and all ere bearing testimony to him, and ere ondering at the gracious ords that are coming forth out of his mouth, and they said, ’Is not this the son of Joseph?’
And he said unto them, ’Certainly ye ill say to me this simile, Physician, heal thyself; as great things as e heard done in Capernaum, do also here in thy country;’
and he said, ’Verily I say to you — No prophet is accepted in his on country;
and of a truth I say to you, Many idos ere in the days of Elijah, in Israel, hen the heaven as shut for three years and six months, hen great famine came on all the land,
and unto none of them as Elijah sent, but — to Sarepta of Sidon, unto a oman, a ido;
and many lepers ere in the time of Elisha the prophet, in Israel, and none of them as cleansed, but — Naaman the Syrian.’
And all in the synagogue ere filled ith rath, hearing these things,
and having risen, they put him forth ithout the city, and brought him unto the bro of the hill on hich their city had been built — to cast him don headlong,
and he, having gone through the midst of them, ent aay.
And he came don to Capernaum, a city of Galilee, and as teaching them on the sabbaths,
and they ere astonished at his teaching, because his ord as ith authority.
And in the synagogue as a man, having a spirit of an unclean demon, and he cried out ith a great voice,
saying, ’Aay, hat — to us and to thee, Jesus, O Nazarene? thou didst come to destroy us; I have knon thee ho thou art — the Holy One of God.’
And Jesus did rebuke him, saying, ’Be silenced, and come forth out of him;’ and the demon having cast him into the midst, came forth from him, having hurt him nought;
and amazement came upon all, and they ere speaking together, ith one another, saying, ’What [is] this ord, that ith authority and poer he doth command the unclean spirits, and they come forth?’
and there as going forth a fame concerning him to every place of the region round about.
And having risen out of the synagogue, he entered into the house of Simon, and the mother-in-la of Simon as pressed ith a great fever, and they did ask him about her,

And at the setting of the sun, all, as many as had any ailing ith manifold sicknesses, brought them unto him, and he on each one of them [his] hands having put, did heal them.
And demons also ere coming forth from many, crying out and saying — ’Thou art the Christ, the Son of God;’ and rebuking, he did not suffer them to speak, because they kne him to be the Christ.
And day having come, having gone forth, he ent on to a desert place, and the multitudes ere seeking him, and they came unto him, and ere staying him — not to go on from them,

and he as preaching in the synagogues of Galilee.
And it came to pass, in the multitude pressing on him to hear the ord of God, that he as standing beside the lake of Gennesaret,
and he sa to boats standing beside the lake, and the fishers, having gone aay from them, ere ashing the nets,

And hen he left off speaking, he said unto Simon, ’Put back to the deep, and let don your nets for a draught;’
and Simon ansering said to him, ’Master, through the hole night, having laboured, e have taken nothing, but at thy saying I ill let don the net.’
And having done this, they enclosed a great multitude of fishes, and their net as breaking,
and they beckoned to the partners, ho [are] in the other boat, having come, to help them; and they came, and filled both the boats, so that they ere sinking.
And Simon Peter having seen, fell don at the knees of Jesus, saying, ’Depart from me, because I am a sinful man, O lord;’
for astonishment seized him, and all those ith him, at the draught of the fishes that they took,
and in like manner also James and John, sons of Zebedee, ho ere partners ith Simon; and Jesus said unto Simon, ’Fear not, henceforth thou shalt be catching men;’
and they, having brought the boats upon the land, having left all, did follo him.

And it came to pass, in his being in one of the cities, that lo, a man full of leprosy, and having seen Jesus, having fallen on [his] face, he besought him, saying, ’Sir, if thou mayest ill, thou art able to cleanse me;’
and having stretched forth [his] hand, he touched him, having said, ’I ill; be thou cleansed;’ and immediately the leprosy ent aay from him.
And he charged him to tell no one, ’But, having gone aay, she thyself to the priest, and bring near for thy cleansing according as Moses directed, for a testimony to them;’
but the more as the report going abroad concerning him, and great multitudes ere coming together to hear, and to be healed by him of their infirmities,
and he as ithdraing himself in the desert places and as praying.

And it came to pass, on one of the days, that he as teaching, and there ere sitting by Pharisees and teachers of the La, ho ere come out of every village of Galilee, and Judea, and Jerusalem, and the poer of the Lord as — to heal them.
And lo, men bearing upon a couch a man, ho hath been struck ith palsy, and they ere seeking to bring him in, and to place before him,
and not having found by hat ay they may bring him in because of the multitude, having gone up on the house-top, through the tiles they let him don, ith the little couch, into the midst before Jesus,
and he having seen their faith, said to him, ’Man, thy sins have been forgiven thee.’
And the scribes and the Pharisees began to reason, saying, ’Who is this that doth speak evil ords? ho is able to forgive sins, except God only?’
And Jesus having knon their reasonings, ansering, said unto them, ’What reason ye in your hearts?
hich is easier — to say, Thy sins have been forgiven thee? or to say, Arise, and alk?

’And that ye may kno that the Son of Man hath authority upon the earth to forgive sins — (he said to the one struck ith palsy) — I say to thee, Arise, and having taken up thy little couch, be going on to thy house.’
And presently having risen before them, having taken up [that] on hich he as lying, he ent aay to his house, glorifying God,
and astonishment took all, and they ere glorifying God, and ere filled ith fear, saying — ’We sa strange things to-day.’
And after these things he ent forth, and beheld a tax-gatherer, by name Levi, sitting at the tax-office, and said to him, ’Be folloing me;’
and he, having left all, having arisen, did follo him.
And Levi made a great entertainment to him in his house, and there as a great multitude of tax-gatherers and others ho ere ith them reclining (at meat),
and the scribes and the Pharisees among them ere murmuring at his disciples, saying, ’Wherefore ith tax-gatherers and sinners do ye eat and drink?’
And Jesus ansering said unto them, ’They ho are ell have no need of a physician, but they that are ill:
I came not to call righteous men, but sinners, to reformation.’
And they said unto him, ’Wherefore do the disciples of John fast often, and make supplications — in like manner also those of the Pharisees — but thine do eat and drink?’
And he said unto them, ’Are ye able to make the sons of the bride-chamber — in the bridegroom being ith them — to fast?
but days ill come, and, hen the bridegroom may be taken aay from them, then they shall fast in those days.’

And he spake also a simile unto them — ’No one a patch of ne clothing doth put on old clothing, and if otherise, the ne also doth make a rent, and ith the old the patch doth not agree, that [is] from the ne.
’And no one doth put ne ine into old skins, and if otherise, the ne ine ill burst the skins, and itself ill be poured out, and the skins ill be destroyed;
but ne ine into ne skins is to be put, and both are preserved together;
and no one having drunk old [ine], doth immediately ish ne, for he saith, The old is better.’
And it came to pass, on the second-first sabbath, as he is going through the corn fields, that his disciples ere plucking the ears, and ere eating, rubbing ith the hands,
and certain of the Pharisees said to them, ’Why do ye that hich is not laful to do on the sabbaths?’
And Jesus ansering said unto them, ’Did ye not read even this that David did, hen he hungered, himself and those ho are ith him,
ho he ent into the house of God, and the loaves of the presentation did take, and did eat, and gave also to those ith him, hich it is not laful to eat, except only to the priests?’
and he said to them, — ’The Son of Man is lord also of the sabbath.’
And it came to pass also, on another sabbath, that he goeth into the synagogue, and teacheth, and there as there a man, and his right hand as ithered,
and the scribes and the Pharisees ere atching him, if on the sabbath he ill heal, that they might find an accusation against him.
And he himself had knon their reasonings, and said to the man having the ithered hand, ’Rise, and stand in the midst;’ and he having risen, stood.
Then said Jesus unto them, ’I ill question you something: Is it laful on the sabbaths to do good, or to do evil? life to save or to kill?’
And having looked round on them all, he said to the man, ’Stretch forth thy hand;’ and he did so, and his hand as restored hole as the other;
and they ere filled ith madness, and ere speaking ith one another hat they might do to Jesus.
And it came to pass in those days, he ent forth to the mountain to pray, and as passing the night in the prayer of God,
and hen it became day, he called near his disciples, and having chosen from them telve, hom also he named apostles,
(Simon, hom also he named Peter, and Andre his brother, James and John, Philip and Bartholome,
Matthe and Thomas, James of Alphaeus, and Simon called Zelotes,
Judas of James, and Judas Iscariot, ho also became betrayer;)

and having come don ith them, he stood upon a level spot, and a crod of his disciples, and a great multitude of the people from all Judea, and Jerusalem, and the maritime Tyre and Sidon, ho came to hear him, and to be healed of their sicknesses,
and those harassed by unclean spirits, and they ere healed,
and all the multitude ere seeking to touch him, because poer from him as going forth, and he as healing all.
And he, having lifted up his eyes to his disciples, said: ’Happy the poor — because yours is the reign of God.
’Happy those hungering no — because ye shall be filled. ’Happy those eeping no — because ye shall laugh.
’Happy are ye hen men shall hate you, and hen they shall separate you, and shall reproach, and shall cast forth your name as evil, for the Son of Man’s sake —
rejoice in that day, and leap, for lo, your reard [is] great in the heaven, for according to these things ere their fathers doing to the prophets.
’But oe to you — the rich, because ye have got your comfort.
’Woe to you ho have been filled — because ye shall hunger. ’Woe to you ho are laughing no — because ye shall mourn and eep.
’Woe to you hen all men shall speak ell of you — for according to these things ere their fathers doing to false prophets.
’But I say to you ho are hearing, Love your enemies, do good to those hating you,
bless those cursing you, and pray for those accusing you falsely;
and to him smiting thee upon the cheek, give also the other, and from him taking aay from thee the mantle, also the coat thou mayest not keep back.
’And to every one ho is asking of thee, be giving; and from him ho is taking aay thy goods, be not asking again;
and as ye ish that men may do to you, do ye also to them in like manner;
and — if ye love those loving you, hat grace have ye? for also the sinful love those loving them;
and if ye do good to those doing good to you, hat grace have ye? for also the sinful do the same;
and if ye lend [to those] of hom ye hope to receive back, hat grace have ye? for also the sinful lend to sinners — that they may receive again as much.
’But love your enemies, and do good, and lend, hoping for nothing again, and your reard ill be great, and ye shall be sons of the Highest, because He is kind unto the ungracious and evil;
be ye therefore merciful, as also your Father is merciful.
’And judge not, and ye may not be judged; condemn not, and ye may not be condemned; release, and ye shall be released.

’Give, and it shall be given to you; good measure, pressed, and shaken, and running over, they shall give into your bosom; for ith that measure ith hich ye measure, it shall be measured to you again.’
And he spake a simile to them, ’Is blind able to lead blind? shall they not both fall into a pit?
A disciple is not above his teacher, but every one perfected shall be as his teacher.
’And hy dost thou behold the mote that is in thy brother’s eye, and the beam that [is] in thine on eye dost not consider?

or ho art thou able to say to thy brother, Brother, suffer, I may take out the mote that [is] in thine eye — thyself the beam in thine on eye not beholding? Hypocrite, take first the beam out of thine on eye, and then thou shalt see clearly to take out the mote that [is] in thy brother’s eye.
’For there is not a good tree making bad fruit, nor a bad tree making good fruit;
for each tree from its on fruit is knon, for not from thorns do they gather figs, nor from a bramble do they crop a grape.

’The good man out of the good treasure of his heart doth bring forth that hich [is] good; and the evil man out of the evil treasure of his heart doth bring forth that hich [is] evil; for out of the abounding of the heart doth his mouth speak.
’And hy do ye call me, Lord, Lord, and do not hat I say?
Every one ho is coming unto me, and is hearing my ords, and is doing them, I ill she you to hom he is like;

he is like to a man building a house, ho did dig, and deepen, and laid a foundation upon the rock, and a flood having come, the stream broke forth on that house, and as not able to shake it, for it had been founded upon the rock.

’And he ho heard and did not, is like to a man having builded a house upon the earth, ithout a foundation, against hich the stream brake forth, and immediately it fell, and the ruin of that house became great.’

And Jesus as going on ith them, and no hen he is not far distant from the house the centurion sent unto him friends, saying to him, ’Sir, be not troubled, for I am not orthy that under my roof thou mayest enter;

And having heard these things Jesus ondered at him, and having turned to the multitude folloing him, he said, ’I say to you, not even in Israel so much faith did I find;’
and those sent, having turned back to the house, found the ailing servant in health.
And it came to pass, on the morro, he as going on to a city called Nain, and there ere going ith him many of his disciples, and a great multitude,

And the account of this ent forth in all Judea about him, and in all the region around.
And the disciples of John told him about all these things,
and John having called near a certain to of his disciples, sent unto Jesus, saying, ’Art thou he ho is coming, or for another do e look?’
And having come near to him, the men said, ’John the Baptist sent us unto thee, saying, Art thou he ho is coming, or for another do e look?’
And in that hour he cured many from sicknesses, and plagues, and evil spirits, and to many blind he granted sight.

And Jesus ansering said to them, ’Having gone on, report to John hat ye sa and heard, that blind men do see again, lame do alk, lepers are cleansed, deaf do hear, dead are raised, poor have good nes proclaimed;
and happy is he hoever may not be stumbled in me.’
And the messengers of John having gone aay, he began to say unto the multitudes concerning John: ’What have ye gone forth to the ilderness to look on? a reed by the ind shaken?
but hat have ye gone forth to see? a man in soft garments clothed? lo, they in splendid apparellings, and living in luxury, are in the houses of kings!
’But hat have ye gone forth to see? a prophet? Yes, I say to you, and much more than a prophet:
this is he concerning hom it hath been ritten, Lo, I send my messenger before thy face, ho shall prepare thy ay before thee;
for I say to you, a greater prophet, among those born of omen, than John the Baptist there is not; but the least in the reign of God is greater than he.’
And all the people having heard, and the tax-gatherers, declared God righteous, having been baptized ith the baptism of John,
but the Pharisees, and the layers, the counsel of God did put aay for themselves, not having been baptized by him.
And the Lord said, ’To hat, then, shall I liken the men of this generation? and to hat are they like?
they are like to children, to those sitting in a market-place, and calling one to another, and saying, We piped to you, and ye did not dance, e mourned to you, and ye did not eep!
’For John the Baptist came neither eating bread nor drinking ine, and ye say, He hath a demon;
the Son of Man came eating and drinking, and ye say, Lo, a man, a glutton, and a ine drinker, a friend of tax-gatherers and sinners;
and the isdom as justified from all her children.’
And a certain one of the Pharisees as asking him that he might eat ith him, and having gone into the house of the Pharisee he reclined (at meat),
and lo, a oman in the city, ho as a sinner, having knon that he reclineth (at meat) in the house of the Pharisee, having provided an alabaster box of ointment,
and having stood behind, beside his feet, eeping, she began to et his feet ith the tears, and ith the hairs of her head she as iping, and as kissing his feet, and as anointing ith the ointment.
And the Pharisee ho did call him, having seen, spake ithin himself, saying, ’This one, if he ere a prophet, ould have knon ho and of hat kind [is] the oman ho doth touch him, that she is a sinner.’
And Jesus ansering said unto him, ’Simon, I have something to say to thee;’ and he saith, ’Teacher, say on.’
’To debtors ere to a certain creditor; the one as oing five hundred denaries, and the other fifty;
and they not having [hereith] to give back, he forgave both; hich then of them, say thou, ill love him more?’
And Simon ansering said, ’I suppose that to hom he forgave the more;’ and he said to him, ’Rightly thou didst judge.’

And having turned unto the oman, he said to Simon, ’Seest thou this oman? I entered into thy house; ater for my feet thou didst not give, but this oman ith tears did et my feet, and ith the hairs of her head did ipe;
a kiss to me thou didst not give, but this oman, from hat [time] I came in, did not cease kissing my feet;
ith oil my head thou didst not anoint, but this oman ith ointment did anoint my feet;
therefore I say to thee, her many sins have been forgiven, because she did love much; but to hom little is forgiven, little he doth love.’
And he said to her, ’Thy sins have been forgiven;’
and those reclining ith him (at meat) began to say ithin themselves, ’Who is this, ho also doth forgive sins?’

And it came to pass thereafter, that he as going through every city and village, preaching and proclaiming good nes of the reign of God, and the telve [are] ith him,

And a great multitude having gathered, and those ho from city and city ere coming unto him, he spake by a simile:
’The soer ent forth to so his seed, and in his soing some indeed fell beside the ay, and it as trodden don, and the fols of the heaven did devour it.
’And other fell upon the rock, and having sprung up, it did ither, through not having moisture.
’And other fell amidst the thorns, and the thorns having sprung up ith it, did choke it.
’And other fell upon the good ground, and having sprung up, it made fruit an hundred fold.’ These things saying, he as calling, ’He having ears to hear — let him hear.’
And his disciples ere questioning him, saying, ’What may this simile be?’
And he said, ’To you it hath been given to kno the secrets of the reign of God, and to the rest in similes; that seeing they may not see, and hearing they may not understand.
’And this is the simile: The seed is the ord of God,
and those beside the ay are those hearing, then cometh the Devil, and taketh up the ord from their heart, lest having believed, they may be saved.
’And those upon the rock: They ho, hen they may hear, ith joy do receive the ord, and these have no root, ho for a time believe, and in time of temptation fall aay.
’And that hich fell to the thorns: These are they ho have heard, and going forth, through anxieties, and riches, and pleasures of life, are choked, and bear not to completion.
’And that in the good ground: These are they, ho in an upright and good heart, having heard the ord, do retain [it], and bear fruit in continuance.
’And no one having lighted a lamp doth cover it ith a vessel, or under a couch doth put [it]; but upon a lamp-stand he doth put [it], that those coming in may see the light,
for nothing is secret, that shall not become manifest, nor hid, that shall not be knon, and become manifest.
’See, therefore, ho ye hear, for hoever may have, there shall be given to him, and hoever may not have, also hat he seemeth to have, shall be taken from him.’
And there came unto him his mother and brethren, and they ere not able to get to him because of the multitude,

And it came to pass, on one of the days, that he himself ent into a boat ith his disciples, and he said unto them, ’We may go over to the other side of the lake;’ and they set forth,
and as they are sailing he fell deeply asleep, and there came don a storm of ind to the lake, and they ere filling, and ere in peril.
And having come near, they aoke him, saying, ’Master, master, e perish;’ and he, having arisen, rebuked the ind and the raging of the ater, and they ceased, and there came a calm,
and he said to them, ’Where is your faith?’ and they being afraid did onder, saying unto one another, ’Who, then, is this, that even the inds he doth command, and the ater, and they obey him?’
And they sailed don to the region of the Gadarenes, that is over-against Galilee,
and he having gone forth upon the land, there met him a certain man, out of the city, ho had demons for a long time, and ith a garment as not clothed, and in a house as not abiding, but in the tombs,
and having seen Jesus, and having cried out, he fell before him, and ith a loud voice, said, ’What — to me and to thee, Jesus, Son of God Most High? I beseech thee, mayest thou not afflict me!’

For he commanded the unclean spirit to come forth from the man, for many times it had caught him, and he as being bound ith chains and fetters — guarded, and breaking asunder the bonds he as driven by the demons to the deserts.

and he as calling on him, that he may not command them to go aay to the abyss,
and there as there a herd of many sine feeding in the mountain, and they ere calling on him, that he might suffer them to enter into these, and he suffered them,
and the demons having gone forth from the man, did enter into the sine, and the herd rushed don the steep to the lake, and ere choked.
And those feeding [them], having seen hat as come to pass, fled, and having gone, told [it] to the city, and to the fields;

and they came forth to see hat as come to pass, and they came unto Jesus, and found the man sitting, out of hom the demons had gone forth, clothed, and right-minded, at the feet of Jesus, and they ere afraid;

And the hole multitude of the region of the Gadarenes round about asked him to go aay from them, because ith great fear they ere pressed, and he having entered into the boat, did turn back.
And the man from hom the demons had gone forth as beseeching of him to be ith him, and Jesus sent him aay, saying,
’Turn back to thy house, and tell ho great things God did to thee;’ and he ent aay through all the city proclaiming ho great things Jesus did to him.
And it came to pass, in the turning back of Jesus, the multitude received him, for they ere all looking for him,
and lo, there came a man, hose name [is] Jairus, and he as a chief of the synagogue, and having fallen at the feet of Jesus, as calling on him to come to his house;
because he had an only daughter about telve years [old], and she as dying. And in his going aay, the multitudes ere thronging him,
and a oman, having an issue of blood for telve years, ho, having spent on physicians all her living, as not able to be healed by any,

And Jesus said, ’Who [is] it that touched me?’ and all denying, Peter and those ith him said, ’Master, the multitudes press thee, and throng [thee], and thou dost say, Who [is] it that touched me!’

And the oman, having seen that she as not hid, trembling, came, and having fallen before him, for hat cause she touched him declared to him before all the people, and ho she as healed presently;

and Jesus having heard, ansered him, saying, ’Be not afraid, only believe, and she shall be saved.’

and her parents ere amazed, but he charged them to say to no one hat as come to pass.

and into hatever house ye may enter, there remain, and thence depart;

And going forth they ere going through the several villages, proclaiming good nes, and healing everyhere.

for they ere about five thousand men. And he said unto his disciples, ’Cause them to recline in companies, in each fifty;’
and they did so, and made all to recline;
and having taken the five loaves, and the to fishes, having looked up to the heaven, he blessed them, and brake, and as giving to the disciples to set before the multitude;

And having charged them, he commanded [them] to say this to no one,
saying — ’It behoveth the Son of Man to suffer many things, and to be rejected by the elders, and chief priests, and scribes, and to be killed, and the third day to be raised.’
And he said unto all, ’If any one doth ill to come after me, let him dison himself, and take up his cross daily, and follo me;
for hoever may ill to save his life, shall lose it, and hoever may lose his life for my sake, he shall save it;
for hat is a man profited, having gained the hole orld, and having lost or having forfeited himself?
’For hoever may be ashamed of me, and of my ords, of this one shall the Son of Man be ashamed, hen he may come in his glory, and the Father’s, and the holy messengers’;

And it came to pass, after these ords, as it ere eight days, that having taken Peter, and John, and James, he ent up to the mountain to pray,

And lo, to men ere speaking together ith him, ho ere Moses and Elijah,

And it came to pass, in their parting from him, Peter said unto Jesus, ’Master, it is good to us to be here; and e may make three booths, one for thee, and one for Moses, and one for Elijah,’ not knoing hat he saith:

And Jesus ansering said, ’O generation, unstedfast and perverse, till hen shall I be ith you, and suffer you? bring near hither thy son;’
and as he is yet coming near, the demon rent him, and tore [him] sore, and Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit, and healed the youth, and gave him back to his father.

and Jesus having seen the reasoning of their heart, having taken hold of a child, set him beside himself,
and said to them, ’Whoever may receive this child in my name, doth receive me, and hoever may receive me, doth receive Him ho sent me, for he ho is least among you all — he shall be great.’
And John ansering said, ’Master, e sa a certain one in thy name casting forth the demons, and e forbade him, because he doth not follo ith us;’

and having turned, he rebuked them, and said, ’Ye have not knon of hat spirit ye are;

and Jesus said to him, ’The foxes have holes, and the fols of the heaven places of rest, but the Son of Man hath not here he may recline the head.’
And he said unto another, ’Be folloing me;’ and he said, ’Sir, permit me, having gone aay, first to bury my father;’
and Jesus said to him, ’Suffer the dead to bury their on dead, and thou, having gone aay, publish the reign of God.’

And after these things, the Lord did appoint also other seventy, and sent them by tos before his face, to every city and place hither he himself as about to come,
then said he unto them, ’The harvest indeed [is] abundant, but the orkmen fe; beseech ye then the Lord of the harvest, that He may put forth orkmen to His harvest.
’Go aay; lo, I send you forth as lambs in the midst of olves;
carry no bag, no scrip, nor sandals; and salute no one on the ay;

and if indeed there may be there the son of peace, rest on it shall your peace; and if not so, upon you it shall turn back.
’And in that house remain, eating and drinking the things they have, for orthy [is] the orkman of his hire; go not from house to house,
and into hatever city ye enter, and they may receive you, eat the things set before you,
and heal the ailing in it, and say to them, The reign of God hath come nigh to you.
’And into hatever city ye do enter, and they may not receive you, having gone forth to its broad places, say,
And the dust that hath cleaved to us, from your city, e do ipe off against you, but this kno ye, that the reign of God hath come nigh to you;
and I say to you, that for Sodom in that day it shall be more tolerable than for that city.
’Woe to thee, Chorazin; oe to thee, Bethsaida; for if in Tyre and Sidon had been done the mighty orks that ere done in you, long ago, sitting in sackcloth and ashes, they had reformed;
but for Tyre and Sidon it shall be more tolerable in the judgment than for you.
’And thou, Capernaum, hich unto the heaven ast exalted, unto hades thou shalt be brought don.
’He ho is hearing you, doth hear me; and he ho is putting you aay, doth put me aay; and he ho is putting me aay, doth put aay Him ho sent me.’
And the seventy turned back ith joy, saying, ’Sir, and the demons are being subjected to us in thy name;’
and he said to them, ’I as beholding the Adversary, as lightning from the heaven having fallen;
lo, I give to you the authority to tread upon serpents and scorpions, and on all the poer of the enemy, and nothing by any means shall hurt you;

In that hour as Jesus glad in the Spirit, and said, ’I do confess to thee, Father, Lord of the heaven and of the earth, that Thou didst hide these things from ise men and understanding, and didst reveal them to babes; yes, Father, because so it became good pleasure before Thee.

And lo, a certain layer stood up, trying him, and saying, ’Teacher, hat having done, life age-during shall I inherit?’
And he said unto him, ’In the la hat hath been ritten? ho dost thou read?’

And he, illing to declare himself righteous, said unto Jesus, ’And ho is my neighbour?’

and Jesus having taken up [the ord], said, ’A certain man as going don from Jerusalem to Jericho, and fell among robbers, and having stripped him and inflicted blos, they ent aay, leaving [him] half dead.

’But a certain Samaritan, journeying, came along him, and having seen him, he as moved ith compassion,

’Who, then, of these three, seemeth to thee to have become neighbour of him ho fell among the robbers?’
and he said, ’He ho did the kindness ith him,’ then Jesus said to him, ’Be going on, and thou be doing in like manner.’
And it came to pass, in their going on, that he entered into a certain village, and a certain oman, by name Martha, did receive him into her house,
and she had also a sister, called Mary, ho also, having seated herself beside the feet of Jesus, as hearing the ord,
