And Jesus ansering said to her, ’Martha, Martha, thou art anxious and disquieted about many things,
but of one thing there is need, and Mary the good part did choose, that shall not be taken aay from her.’
And it came to pass, in his being in a certain place praying, as he ceased, a certain one of his disciples said unto him, ’Sir, teach us to pray, as also John taught his disciples.’
And he said to them, ’When ye may pray, say ye: Our Father ho art in the heavens; halloed be Thy name: Thy reign come; Thy ill come to pass, as in heaven also on earth;
our appointed bread be giving us daily;
and forgive us our sins, for also e ourselves forgive every one indebted to us; and mayest Thou not bring us into temptation; but do Thou deliver us from the evil.’
And he said unto them, ’Who of you shall have a friend, and shall go on unto him at midnight, and may say to him, Friend, lend me three loaves,
seeing a friend of mine came out of the ay unto me, and I have not hat I shall set before him,
and he from ithin ansering may say, Do not give me trouble, already the door hath been shut, and my children ith me are in the bed, I am not able, having risen, to give to thee.
’I say to you, even if he ill not give to him, having risen, because of his being his friend, yet because of his importunity, having risen, he ill give him as many as he doth need;
and I say to you, Ask, and it shall be given to you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened to you;
for every one ho is asking doth receive; and he ho is seeking doth find; and to him ho is knocking it shall be opened.
’And of hich of you — the father — if the son shall ask a loaf, a stone ill he present to him? and if a fish, ill he instead of a fish, a serpent present to him?
and if he may ask an egg, ill he present to him a scorpion?
If, then, ye, being evil, have knon good gifts to be giving to your children, ho much more shall the Father ho is from heaven give the Holy Spirit to those asking Him!’
And he as casting forth a demon, and it as dumb, and it came to pass, the demon having gone forth, the dumb man spake, and the multitudes ondered,
and certain of them said, ’By Beelzeboul, ruler of the demons, he doth cast forth the demons;’
and others, tempting, a sign out of heaven from him ere asking.
And he, knoing their thoughts, said to them, ’Every kingdom having been divided against itself is desolated; and house against house doth fall;
and if also the Adversary against himself as divided, ho shall his kingdom be made to stand? for ye say, by Beelzeboul is my casting forth the demons.
’But if I by Beelzeboul cast forth the demons — your sons, by hom do they cast forth? because of this your judges they shall be;
but if by the finger of God I cast forth the demons, then come unaares upon you did the reign of God.
’When the strong man armed may keep his hall, in peace are his goods;
but hen the stronger than he, having come upon [him], may overcome him, his hole-armour he doth take aay in hich he had trusted, and his spoils he distributeth;
he ho is not ith me is against me, and he ho is not gathering ith me doth scatter.
’When the unclean spirit may go forth from the man it alketh through aterless places seeking rest, and not finding, it saith, I ill turn back to my house hence I came forth;
and having come, it findeth [it] sept and adorned;
then doth it go, and take to it seven other spirits more evil than itself, and having entered, they dell there, and the last of that man becometh orst than the first.’
And it came to pass, in his saying these things, a certain oman having lifted up the voice out of the multitude, said to him, ’Happy the omb that carried thee, and the paps that thou didst suck!’
And he said, ’Yea, rather, happy those hearing the ord of God, and keeping [it]!’
And the multitudes croding together upon him, he began to say, ’This generation is evil, a sign it doth seek after, and a sign shall not be given to it, except the sign of Jonah the prophet,
for as Jonah became a sign to the Ninevites, so also shall the Son of Man be to this generation.

’A queen of the south shall rise up in the judgment ith the men of this generation, and shall condemn them, because she came from the ends of the earth to hear the isdom of Solomon; and lo, greater than Solomon here!
’Men of Nineveh shall stand up in the judgment ith this generation, and shall condemn it, because they reformed at the proclamation of Jonah; and lo, greater than Jonah here!
’And no one having lighted a lamp, doth put [it] in a secret place, nor under the measure, but on the lamp-stand, that those coming in may behold the light.
’The lamp of the body is the eye, hen then thine eye may be simple, thy hole body also is lightened; and hen it may be evil, thy body also is darkened;
take heed, then, lest the light that [is] in thee be darkness;
if then thy hole body is lightened, not having any part darkened, the hole shall be lightened, as hen the lamp by the brightness may give thee light.’
And in [his] speaking, a certain Pharisee as asking him that he might dine ith him, and having gone in, he reclined (at meat),
and the Pharisee having seen, did onder that he did not first baptize himself before the dinner.
And the Lord said unto him, ’No do ye, the Pharisees, the outside of the cup and of the plate make clean, but your inard part is full of rapine and ickedness;
unthinking! did not He ho made the outside also the inside make?
But hat ye have give ye [as] alms, and, lo, all things are clean to you.

’But oe to you, the Pharisees, because ye tithe the mint, and the rue, and every herb, and ye pass by the judgment, and the love of God; these things it behoveth to do, and those not to be neglecting.
’Woe to you, the Pharisees, because ye love the first seats in the synagogues, and the salutations in the market-places.
’Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because ye are as the unseen tombs, and the men alking above have not knon.’
And one of the layers ansering, saith to him, ’Teacher, these things saying, us also thou dost insult;’
and he said, ’And to you, the layers, oe! because ye burden men ith burdens grievous to be borne, and ye yourselves ith one of your fingers do not touch the burdens.
’Woe to you, because ye build the tombs of the prophets, and your fathers killed them.
Then do ye testify, and are ell pleased ith the orks of your fathers, because they indeed killed them, and ye do build their tombs;
because of this also the isdom of God said: I ill send to them prophets, and apostles, and some of them they shall kill and persecute,
that the blood of all the prophets, that is being poured forth from the foundation of the orld, may be required from this generation;
from the blood of Abel unto the blood of Zacharias, ho perished beteen the altar and the house; yes, I say to you, It shall be required from this generation.
’Woe to you, the layers, because ye took aay the key of the knoledge; yourselves ye did not enter; and those coming in, ye did hinder.’
And in his speaking these things unto them, the scribes and the Pharisees began fearfully to urge and to press him to speak about many things,
laying ait for him, and seeking to catch something out of his mouth, that they might accuse him.

At hich time the myriads of the multitude having been gathered together, so as to tread upon one another, he began to say unto his disciples, first, ’Take heed to yourselves of the leaven of the Pharisees, hich is hypocrisy;
and there is nothing covered, that shall not be revealed; and hid, that shall not be knon;
because hatever in the darkness ye said, in the light shall be heard: and hat to the ear ye spake in the inner-chambers, shall be proclaimed upon the house-tops.
’And I say to you, my friends, be not afraid of those killing the body, and after these things are not having anything over to do;
but I ill sho to you, hom ye may fear; Fear him ho, after the killing, is having authority to cast to the gehenna; yes, I say to you, Fear ye Him.
’Are not five sparros sold for to assars? and one of them is not forgotten before God,
but even the hairs of your head have been all numbered; therefore fear ye not, than many sparros ye are of more value.
’And I say to you, Every one — hoever may confess ith me before men, the Son of Man also shall confess ith him before the messengers of God,
and he ho hath denied me before men, shall be denied before the messengers of God,
and every one hoever shall say a ord to the Son of Man, it shall be forgiven to him, but to him ho to the Holy Spirit did speak evil, it shall not be forgiven.
’And hen they bring you before the synagogues, and the rulers, and the authorities, be not anxious ho or hat ye may reply, or hat ye may say,
for the Holy Spirit shall teach you in that hour hat it behoveth [you] to say.’
And a certain one said to him, out of the multitude, ’Teacher, say to my brother to divide ith me the inheritance.’
And he said to him, ’Man, ho set me a judge or a divider over you?’
And he said unto them, ’Observe, and beare of the covetousness, because not in the abundance of one’s goods is his life.’
And he spake a simile unto them, saying, ’Of a certain rich man the field brought forth ell;
and he as reasoning ithin himself, saying, What shall I do, because I have not here I shall gather together my fruits?
and he said, This I ill do, I ill take don my storehouses, and greater ones I ill build, and I ill gather together there all my products and my good things,
and I ill say to my soul, Soul, thou hast many good things laid up for many years, be resting, eat, drink, be merry.
’And God said to him, Unthinking one! this night thy soul they shall require from thee, and hat things thou didst prepare — to hom shall they be?
so [is] he ho is treasuring up to himself, and is not rich toard God.’
And he said unto his disciples, ’Because of this, to you I say, Be not anxious for your life, hat ye may eat; nor for the body, hat ye may put on;
the life is more than the nourishment, and the body than the clothing.
’Consider the ravens, that they so not, nor reap, to hich there is no barn nor storehouse, and God doth nourish them; ho much better are ye than the fols?
and ho of you, being anxious, is able to add to his age one cubit?
If, then, ye are not able for the least — hy for the rest are ye anxious?
’Consider the lilies, ho do they gro? they labour not, nor do they spin, and I say to you, not even Solomon in all his glory as arrayed as one of these;
and if the herbage in the field, that to-day is, and to-morro into an oven is cast, God doth so clothe, ho much more you — ye of little faith?
’And ye — seek not hat ye may eat, or hat ye may drink, and be not in suspense,
for all these things do the nations of the orld seek after, and your Father hath knon that ye have need of these things;
but, seek ye the reign of God, and all these things shall be added to you.
’Fear not, little flock, because your Father did delight to give you the reign;
sell your goods, and give alms, make to yourselves bags that become not old, a treasure unfailing in the heavens, here thief doth not come near, nor moth destroy;
for here your treasure is, there also your heart ill be.
’Let your loins be girded, and the lamps burning,
and ye like to men aiting for their lord, hen he shall return out of the edding feasts, that he having come and knocked, immediately they may open to him.

’Happy those servants, hom the lord, having come, shall find atching; verily I say to you, that he ill gird himself, and ill cause them to recline (at meat), and having come near, ill minister to them;
and if he may come in the second atch, and in the third atch he may come, and may find [it] so, happy are those servants.
’And this kno, that if the master of the house had knon hat hour the thief doth come, he ould have atched, and ould not have suffered his house to be broken through;
and ye, then, become ye ready, because at the hour ye think not, the Son of Man doth come.’
And Peter said to him, ’Sir, unto us this simile dost thou speak, or also unto all?’
And the Lord said, ’Who, then, is the faithful and prudent steard hom the lord shall set over his household, to give in season the heat measure?
Happy that servant, hom his lord, having come, shall find doing so;
truly I say to you, that over all his goods he ill set him.
’And if that servant may say in his heart, My lord doth delay to come, and may begin to beat the men-servants and the maid-servants, to eat also, and to drink, and to be drunken;
the lord of that servant ill come in a day in hich he doth not look for [him], and in an hour that he doth not kno, and ill cut him off, and his portion ith the unfaithful he ill appoint.
’And that servant, ho having knon his lord’s ill, and not having prepared, nor having gone according to his ill, shall be beaten ith many stripes,

and he ho, not having knon, and having done things orthy of stripes, shall be beaten ith fe; and to every one to hom much as given, much shall be required from him; and to hom they did commit much, more abundantly they ill ask of him.
’Fire I came to cast to the earth, and hat ill I if already it as kindled?
but I have a baptism to be baptized ith, and ho am I pressed till it may be completed!
’Think ye that peace I came to give in the earth? no, I say to you, but rather division;
for there shall be henceforth five in one house divided — three against to, and to against three;

a father shall be divided against a son, and a son against a father, a mother against a daughter, and a daughter against a mother, a mother-in-la against her daughter-in-la, and a daughter-in-la against her mother-in-la.’
And he said also to the multitudes, ’When ye may see the cloud rising from the est, immediately ye say, A shoer doth come, and it is so;
and hen — a south ind bloing, ye say, that there ill be heat, and it is;
hypocrites! the face of the earth and of the heaven ye have knon to make proof of, but this time — ho do ye not make proof of [it]?
’And hy, also, of yourselves, judge ye not hat is righteous?

for, as thou art going aay ith thy opponent to the ruler, in the ay give diligence to be released from him, lest he may drag thee unto the judge, and the judge may deliver thee to the officer, and the officer may cast thee into prison;
I say to thee, thou mayest not come forth thence till even the last mite thou mayest give back.’
And there ere present certain at that time, telling him about the Galileans, hose blood Pilate did mingle ith their sacrifices;
and Jesus ansering said to them, ’Think ye that these Galileans became sinners beyond all the Galileans, because they have suffered such things?
No — I say to you, but, if ye may not reform, all ye even so shall perish.
’Or those eighteen, on hom the toer in Siloam fell, and killed them; think ye that these became debtors beyond all men ho are delling in Jerusalem?
No — I say to you, but, if ye may not reform, all ye in like manner shall perish.’
And he spake this simile: ’A certain one had a fig-tree planted in his vineyard, and he came seeking fruit in it, and he did not find;
and he said unto the vine-dresser, Lo, three years I come seeking fruit in this fig-tree, and do not find, cut it off, hy also the ground doth it render useless?
’And he ansering saith to him, Sir, suffer it also this year, till that I may dig about it, and cast in dung;
and if indeed it may bear fruit — ;and if not so, thereafter thou shalt cut it off.’
And he as teaching in one of the synagogues on the sabbath,
and lo, there as a oman having a spirit of infirmity eighteen years, and she as boed together, and not able to bend back at all,
and Jesus having seen her, did call [her] near, and said to her, ’Woman, thou hast been loosed from thy infirmity;’
and he laid on her [his] hands, and presently she as set upright, and as glorifying God.

And the chief of the synagogue ansering — much displeased that on the sabbath Jesus healed — said to the multitude, ’Six days there are in hich it behoveth [us] to be orking; in these, then, coming, be healed, and not on the sabbath-day.’
Then the Lord ansered him and said, ’Hypocrite, doth not each of you on the sabbath loose his ox or ass from the stall, and having led aay, doth ater [it]?
and this one, being a daughter of Abraham, hom the Adversary bound, lo, eighteen years, did it not behove to be loosed from this bond on the sabbath-day?’
And he saying these things, all ho ere opposed to him ere being ashamed, and all the multitude ere rejoicing over all the glorious things that are being done by him.
And he said, ’To hat is the reign of God like? and to hat shall I liken it?
It is like to a grain of mustard, hich a man having taken, did cast into his garden, and it increased, and came to a great tree, and the fols of the heavens did rest in its branches.’
And again he said, ’To hat shall I liken the reign of God?
It is like leaven, hich a oman, having taken, did hide in three measures of meal, till that all as leavened.’
And he as going through cities and villages, teaching, and making progress toard Jerusalem;
and a certain one said to him, ’Sir, are those saved fe?’ and he said unto them,
’Be striving to go in through the straight gate, because many, I say to you, ill seek to go in, and shall not be able;

from the time the master of the house may have risen up, and may have shut the door, and ye may begin ithout to stand, and to knock at the door, saying, Lord, lord, open to us, and he ansering shall say to you, I have not knon you hence ye are,
then ye may begin to say, We did eat before thee, and did drink, and in our broad places thou didst teach;
and he shall say, I say to you, I have not knon you hence ye are; depart from me, all ye orkers of the unrighteousness.
’There shall be there the eeping and the gnashing of the teeth, hen ye may see Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, and all the prophets, in the reign of God, and yourselves being cast out ithout;
and they shall come from east and est, and from north and south, and shall recline in the reign of God,
and lo, there are last ho shall be first, and there are first ho shall be last.’
On that day there came near certain Pharisees, saying to him, ’Go forth, and be going on hence, for Herod doth ish to kill thee;’
and he said to them, ’Having gone, say to this fox, Lo, I cast forth demons, and perfect cures to-day and to-morro, and the third [day] I am being perfected;
but it behoveth me to-day, and to-morro, and the [day] folloing, to go on, because it is not possible for a prophet to perish out of Jerusalem.
’Jerusalem, Jerusalem, that is killing the prophets, and stoning those sent unto her, ho often did I ill to gather together thy children, as a hen her brood under the ings, and ye did not ill.
’Lo, your house is being left to you desolate, and verily I say to you — ye may not see me, till it may come, hen ye may say, Blessed [is] he ho is coming in the name of the Lord.’
And it came to pass, on his going into the house of a certain one of the chiefs of the Pharisees, on a sabbath, to eat bread, that they ere atching him,
and lo, there as a certain dropsical man before him;
and Jesus ansering spake to the layers and Pharisees, saying, ’Is it laful on the sabbath-day to heal?’
and they ere silent, and having taken hold of [him], he healed him, and let [him] go;
and ansering them he said, ’Of hich of you shall an ass or ox fall into a pit, and he ill not immediately dra it up on the sabbath-day?’
and they ere not able to anser him again unto these things.
And he spake a simile unto those called, marking ho they ere choosing out the first couches, saying unto them,
’When thou mayest be called by any one to marriage-feasts, thou mayest not recline on the first couch, lest a more honourable than thou may have been called by him,
and he ho did call thee and him having come shall say to thee, Give to this one place, and then thou mayest begin ith shame to occupy the last place.

’But, hen thou mayest be called, having gone on, recline in the last place, that hen he ho called thee may come, he may say to thee, Friend, come up higher; then thou shalt have glory before those reclining ith thee;
because every one ho is exalting himself shall be humbled, and he ho is humbling himself shall be exalted.’

And he said also to him ho did call him, ’When thou mayest make a dinner or a supper, be not calling thy friends, nor thy brethren, nor thy kindred, nor rich neighbours, lest they may also call thee again, and a recompense may come to thee;
but hen thou mayest make a feast, be calling poor, maimed, lame, blind,
and happy thou shalt be, because they have not to recompense thee, for it shall be recompensed to thee in the rising again of the righteous.’
And one of those reclining ith him, having heard these things, said to him, ’Happy [is] he ho shall eat bread in the reign of God;’
and he said to him, ’A certain man made a great supper, and called many,
and he sent his servant at the hour of the supper to say to those having been called, Be coming, because no are all things ready.
’And they began ith one consent all to excuse themselves: The first said to him, A field I bought, and I have need to go forth and see it; I beg of thee, have me excused.
’And another said, Five yoke of oxen I bought, and I go on to prove them; I beg of thee, have me excused:
and another said, A ife I married, and because of this I am not able to come.

’And that servant having come, told to his lord these things, then the master of the house, having been angry, said to his servant, Go forth quickly to the broad places and lanes of the city, and the poor, and maimed, and lame, and blind, bring in hither.
’And the servant said, Sir, it hath been done as thou didst command, and still there is room.
’And the lord said unto the servant, Go forth to the ays and hedges, and constrain to come in, that my house may be filled;
for I say to you, that none of those men ho have been called shall taste of my supper.’
And there ere going on ith him great multitudes, and having turned, he said unto them,
’If any one doth come unto me, and doth not hate his on father, and mother, and ife, and children, and brothers, and sisters, and yet even his on life, he is not able to be my disciple;
and hoever doth not bear his cross, and come after me, is not able to be my disciple.
’For ho of you, illing to build a toer, doth not first, having sat don, count the expence, hether he have the things for completing?
lest that he having laid a foundation, and not being able to finish, all ho are beholding may begin to mock him,
saying — This man began to build, and as not able to finish.
’Or hat king going on to engage ith another king in ar, doth not, having sat don, first consult if he be able ith ten thousand to meet him ho ith tenty thousand is coming against him?
and if not so — he being yet a long ay off — having sent an embassy, he doth ask the things for peace.
’So, then, every one of you ho doth not take leave of all that he himself hath, is not able to be my disciple.
’The salt [is] good, but if the salt doth become tasteless, ith hat shall it be seasoned?
neither for land nor for manure is it fit — they cast it ithout. He ho is having ears to hear — let him hear.’
And all the tax-gatherers and the sinners ere coming nigh to him, to hear him,
and the Pharisees and the scribes ere murmuring, saying — This one doth receive sinners, and doth eat ith them.’
And he spake unto them this simile, saying,
’What man of you having a hundred sheep, and having lost one out of them, doth not leave behind the ninety-nine in the ilderness, and go on after the lost one, till he may find it?
and having found, he doth lay [it] on his shoulders rejoicing,
and having come to the house, he doth call together the friends and the neighbours, saying to them, Rejoice ith me, because I found my sheep — the lost one.
’I say to you, that so joy shall be in the heaven over one sinner reforming, rather than over ninety-nine righteous men, ho have no need of reformation.
’Or hat oman having ten drachms, if she may lose one drachm, doth not light a lamp, and seep the house, and seek carefully till that she may find?
and having found, she doth call together the female friends and the neighbours, saying, Rejoice ith me, for I found the drachm that I lost.
’So I say to you, joy doth come before the messengers of God over one sinner reforming.’
And he said, ’A certain man had to sons,
and the younger of them said to the father, Father, give me the portion of the substance falling to [me], and he divided to them the living.
’And not many days after, having gathered all together, the younger son ent abroad to a far country, and there he scattered his substance, living riotously;
and he having spent all, there came a mighty famine on that country, and himself began to be in ant;
and having gone on, he joined himself to one of the citizens of that country, and he sent him to the fields to feed sine,
and he as desirous to fill his belly from the husks that the sine ere eating, and no one as giving to him.
’And having come to himself, he said, Ho many hirelings of my father have a superabundance of bread, and I here ith hunger am perishing!
having risen, I ill go on unto my father, and ill say to him, Father, I did sin — to the heaven, and before thee,
and no more am I orthy to be called thy son; make me as one of thy hirelings.
’And having risen, he ent unto his on father, and he being yet far distant, his father sa him, and as moved ith compassion, and having ran he fell upon his neck and kissed him;
and the son said to him, Father, I did sin — to the heaven, and before thee, and no more am I orthy to be called thy son.
’And the father said unto his servants, Bring forth the first robe, and clothe him, and give a ring for his hand, and sandals for the feet;
and having brought the fatted calf, kill [it], and having eaten, e may be merry,
because this my son as dead, and did live again, and he as lost, and as found; and they began to be merry.
’And his elder son as in a field, and as, coming, he dre nigh to the house, he heard music and dancing,
and having called near one of the young men, he as inquiring hat these things might be,
and he said to him — Thy brother is arrived, and thy father did kill the fatted calf, because in health he did receive him back.
’And he as angry, and ould not go in, therefore his father, having come forth, as entreating him;
and he ansering said to the father, Lo, so many years I do serve thee, and never thy command did I transgress, and to me thou didst never give a kid, that ith my friends I might make merry;
but hen thy son — this one ho did devour thy living ith harlots — came, thou didst kill to him the fatted calf.
’And he said to him, Child, thou art alays ith me, and all my things are thine;
but to be merry, and to be glad, it as needful, because this thy brother as dead, and did live again, he as lost, and as found.’
And he said also unto his disciples, ’A certain man as rich, ho had a steard, and he as accused to him as scattering his goods;
and having called him, he said to him, What [is] this I hear about thee? render the account of thy steardship, for thou mayest not any longer be steard.
’And the steard said in himself, What shall I do, because my lord doth take aay the steardship from me? to dig I am not able, to beg I am ashamed: —
I have knon hat I shall do, that, hen I may be removed from the steardship, they may receive me to their houses.
’And having called near each one of his lord’s debtors, he said to the first, Ho much dost thou oe to my lord?
and he said, A hundred baths of oil; and he said to him, Take thy bill, and having sat don rite fifty.
’Afterard to another he said, And thou, ho much dost thou oe? and he said, A hundred cors of heat; and he saith to him, Take thy bill, and rite eighty.
’And the lord commended the unrighteous steard that he did prudently, because the sons of this age are more prudent than the sons of the light, in respect to their generation.
and I say to you, Make to yourselves friends out of the mammon of unrighteousness, that hen ye may fail, they may receive you to the age-during tabernacles.
’He ho is faithful in the least, [is] also faithful in much; and he ho in the least [is] unrighteous, is also unrighteous in much;
if, then, in the unrighteous mammon ye became not faithful — the true ho ill entrust to you?
and if in the other’s ye became not faithful — your on, ho shall give to you?

’No domestic is able to serve to lords, for either the one he ill hate, and the other he ill love; or one he ill hold to, and of the other he ill be heedless; ye are not able to serve God and mammon.’
And also the Pharisees, being lovers of money, ere hearing all these things, and ere deriding him,
and he said to them, ’Ye are those declaring yourselves righteous before men, but God doth kno your hearts; because that hich among men is high, [is] abomination before God;
the la and the prophets [are] till John; since then the reign of God is proclaimed good nes, and every one doth press into it;
and it is easier to the heaven and the earth to pass aay, than of the la one tittle to fall.
’Every one ho is sending aay his ife, and marrying another, doth commit adultery; and every one ho is marrying her sent aay from a husband doth commit adultery.
’And — a certain man as rich, and as clothed in purple and fine linen, making merry sumptuously every day,
and there as a certain poor man, by name Lazarus, ho as laid at his porch, full of sores,
and desiring to be filled from the crumbs that are falling from the table of the rich man; yea, also the dogs, coming, ere licking his sores.
’And it came to pass, that the poor man died, and that he as carried aay by the messengers to the bosom of Abraham — and the rich man also died, and as buried;
and in the hades having lifted up his eyes, being in torments, he doth see Abraham afar off, and Lazarus in his bosom,
and having cried, he said, Father Abraham, deal kindly ith me, and send Lazarus, that he may dip the tip of his finger in ater, and may cool my tongue, because I am distressed in this flame.
’And Abraham said, Child, remember that thou did receive — thou — thy good things in thy life, and Lazarus in like manner the evil things, and no he is comforted, and thou art distressed;

Jesus saith to her, ’Woman, believe me, that there doth come an hour, hen neither in this mountain, nor in Jerusalem, shall ye orship the Father;

but, there cometh an hour, and it no is, hen the true orshippers ill orship the Father in spirit and truth, for the Father also doth seek such to orship him;
God [is] a Spirit, and those orshipping Him, in spirit and truth it doth behove to orship.’
The oman saith to him, ’I have knon that Messiah doth come, ho is called Christ, hen that one may come, he ill tell us all things;’
Jesus saith to her, ’I am [he], ho am speaking to thee.’
And upon this came his disciples, and ere ondering that ith a oman he as speaking, no one, hoever, said, ’What seekest thou?’ or ’Why speakest thou ith her?’
The oman then left her ater-jug, and ent aay to the city, and saith to the men,
’Come, see a man, ho told me all things — as many as I did; is this the Christ?’
They ent forth therefore out of the city, and ere coming unto him.
And in the meanhile his disciples ere asking him, saying, ’Rabbi, eat;’
and he said to them, ’I have food to eat that ye have not knon.’
The disciples then said one to another, ’Did any one bring him anything to eat?’
Jesus saith to them, ’My food is, that I may do the ill of Him ho sent me, and may finish His ork;
do not say that it is yet four months, and the harvest cometh; lo, I say to you, Lift up your eyes, and see the fields, that they are hite unto harvest already.
’And he ho is reaping doth receive a reard, and doth gather fruit to life age-during, that both he ho is soing and he ho is reaping may rejoice together;
for in this the saying is the true one, that one is the soer and another the reaper.
I sent you to reap that on hich ye have not laboured; others laboured, and ye into their labour have entered.
And from that city many believed in him, of the Samaritans, because of the ord of the oman testifying, — ’He told me all things — as many as I did.’
When, then, the Samaritans came unto him, they ere asking him to remain ith them, and he remained there to days;
and many more did believe because of his ord,
and said to the oman — ’No more because of thy speaking do e believe; for e ourselves have heard and knon that this is truly the Saviour of the orld — the Christ.’
And after the to days he ent forth thence, and ent aay to Galilee,
for Jesus himself testified that a prophet in his on country shall not have honour;
hen then, he came to Galilee, the Galileans received him, having seen all things that he did in Jerusalem in the feast — for they also ent to the feast.
Jesus came, therefore, again to Cana of Galilee, here he made the ater ine, and there as a certain courtier, hose son as ailing in Capernaum,
he, having heard that Jesus is come out of Judea to Galilee, ent aay unto him, and as asking him that he may come don and may heal his son, for he as about to die.
Jesus then said unto him, ’If signs and onders ye may not see, ye ill not believe.’
The courtier saith unto him, ’Sir, come don before my child die;’
Jesus saith to him, ’Be going on; thy son doth live.’ And the man believed the ord that Jesus said to him, and as going on,
and he no going don, his servants met him, and told, saying — ’Thy child doth live;’
he inquired then of them the hour in hich he became better, and they said to him — ’Yesterday at the seventh hour the fever left him;’
then the father kne that [it as] in that hour in hich Jesus said to him — ’Thy son doth live,’ and he himself believed, and his hole house;
this again a second sign did Jesus, having come out of Judea to Galilee.
After these things there as a feast of the Jes, and Jesus ent up to Jerusalem,
and there is in Jerusalem by the sheep -[gate] a pool that is called in Hebre Bethesda, having five porches,
in these ere lying a great multitude of the ailing, blind, lame, ithered, aiting for the moving of the ater,
for a messenger at a set time as going don in the pool, and as troubling the ater, the first then having gone in after the troubling of the ater, became hole of hatever sickness he as held.
and there as a certain man there being in ailment thirty and eight years,
him Jesus having seen lying, and having knon that he is already a long time, he saith to him, ’Dost thou ish to become hole?’
The ailing man ansered him, ’Sir, I have no man, that, hen the ater may be troubled, he may put me into the pool, and hile I am coming, another doth go don before me.’
Jesus saith to him, ’Rise, take up thy couch, and be alking;’
and immediately the man became hole, and he took up his couch, and as alking, and it as a sabbath on that day,
the Jes then said to him that hath been healed, ’It is a sabbath; it is not laful to thee to take up the couch.’
He ansered them, ’He ho made me hole — that one said to me, Take up thy couch, and be alking;’
they questioned him, then, ’Who is the man ho is saying to thee, Take up thy couch and be alking?’
But he that as healed had not knon ho he is, for Jesus did move aay, a multitude being in the place.
After these things, Jesus findeth him in the temple, and said to him, ’Lo, thou hast become hole; sin no more, lest something orse may happen to thee.’
The man ent aay, and told the Jes that it is Jesus ho made him hole,
and because of this ere the Jes persecuting Jesus, and seeking to kill him, because these things he as doing on a sabbath.
And Jesus ansered them, ’My Father till no doth ork, and I ork;’
because of this, then, ere the Jes seeking the more to kill him, because not only as he breaking the sabbath, but he also called God his on Father, making himself equal to God.

Jesus therefore responded and said to them, ’Verily, verily, I say to you, The Son is not able to do anything of himself, if he may not see the Father doing anything; for hatever things He may do, these also the Son in like manner doth;
for the Father doth love the Son, and doth she to him all things that He himself doth; and greater orks than these He ill she him, that ye may onder.
’For, as the Father doth raise the dead, and doth make alive, so also the Son doth make alive hom he illeth;
for neither doth the Father judge any one, but all the judgment He hath given to the Son,
that all may honour the Son according as they honour the Father; he ho is not honouring the Son, doth not honour the Father ho sent him.
’Verily, verily, I say to you — He ho is hearing my ord, and is believing Him ho sent me, hath life age-during, and to judgment he doth not come, but hath passed out of the death to the life.
’Verily, verily, I say to you — There cometh an hour, and it no is, hen the dead shall hear the voice of the Son of God, and those having heard shall live;
for, as the Father hath life in himself, so He gave also to the Son to have life in himself,
and authority He gave him also to do judgment, because he is Son of Man.
’Wonder not at this, because there doth come an hour in hich all those in the tombs shall hear his voice,
and they shall come forth; those ho did the good things to a rising again of life, and those ho practised the evil things to a rising again of judgment.
’I am not able of myself to do anything; according as I hear I judge, and my judgment is righteous, because I seek not my on ill, but the ill of the Father ho sent me.
’If I testify concerning myself, my testimony is not true;
another there is ho is testifying concerning me, and I have knon that the testimony that he doth testify concerning me is true;
ye have sent unto John, and he hath testified to the truth.
’But I do not receive testimony from man, but these things I say that ye may be saved;
he as the burning and shining lamp, and ye did ill to be glad, for an hour, in his light.
’But I have the testimony greater than John’s, for the orks that the Father gave me, that I might finish them, the orks themselves that I do, they testify concerning me, that the Father hath sent me.
’And the Father ho sent me Himself hath testified concerning me; ye have neither heard His voice at any time, nor His appearance have ye seen;
and His ord ye have not remaining in you, because hom He sent, him ye do not believe.
’Ye search the Writings, because ye think in them to have life age-during, and these are they that are testifying concerning me;
and ye do not ill to come unto me, that ye may have life;
glory from man I do not receive,
but I have knon you, that the love of God ye have not in yourselves.
’I have come in the name of my Father, and ye do not receive me; if another may come in his on name, him ye ill receive;
ho are ye able — ye — to believe, glory from one another receiving, and the glory that [is] from God alone ye seek not?
’Do not think that I ill accuse you unto the Father; there is ho is accusing you, Moses — in hom ye have hoped;
for if ye ere believing Moses, ye ould have been believing me, for he rote concerning me;
but if his ritings ye believe not, ho shall ye believe my sayings?’
After these things Jesus ent aay beyond the sea of Galilee (of Tiberias),
and there as folloing him a great multitude, because they ere seeing his signs that he as doing on the ailing;
and Jesus ent up to the mount, and he as there sitting ith his disciples,
and the passover as nigh, the feast of the Jes.
Jesus then having lifted up [his] eyes and having seen that a great multitude doth come to him, saith unto Philip, ’Whence shall e buy loaves, that these may eat?’ —
and this he said, trying him, for he himself had knon hat he as about to do.
Philip ansered him, ’To hundred denaries’ orth of loaves are not sufficient to them, that each of them may receive some little;’
one of his disciples — Andre, the brother of Simon Peter — saith to him,
’There is one little lad here ho hath five barley loaves, and to fishes, but these — hat are they to so many?’
And Jesus said, ’Make the men to sit don;’ and there as much grass in the place, the men then sat don, in number, as it ere, five thousand,
and Jesus took the loaves, and having given thanks he distributed to the disciples, and the disciples to those reclining, in like manner, also of the little fishes as much as they ished.
And hen they ere filled, he saith to his disciples, ’Gather together the broken pieces that are over, that nothing may be lost;’
they gathered together, therefore, and filled telve hand-baskets ith broken pieces, from the five barley loaves that ere over to those having eaten.
The men, then, having seen the sign that Jesus did, said — ’This is truly the Prophet, ho is coming to the orld;’
Jesus, therefore, having knon that they are about to come, and to take him by force that they may make him king, retired again to the mountain himself alone.
And hen evening came, his disciples ent don to the sea,
and having entered into the boat, they ere going over the sea to Capernaum, and darkness had already come, and Jesus had not come unto them,
the sea also — a great ind bloing — as being raised,
having pushed onards, therefore, about tenty-five or thirty furlongs, they behold Jesus alking on the sea, and coming nigh to the boat, and they ere afraid;
and he saith to them, ’I am [he], be not afraid;’
they ere illing then to receive him into the boat, and immediately the boat came unto the land to hich they ere going.

On the morro, the multitude that as standing on the other side of the sea, having seen that there as no other little boat there except one — that into hich his disciples entered — and that Jesus ent not in ith his disciples into the little boat, but his disciples ent aay alone,
(and other little boats came from Tiberias, nigh the place here they did eat the bread, the Lord having given thanks),
hen therefore the multitude sa that Jesus is not there, nor his disciples, they also themselves did enter into the boats, and came to Capernaum seeking Jesus;
and having found him on the other side of the sea, they said to him, ’Rabbi, hen hast thou come hither?’
Jesus ansered them and said, ’Verily, verily, I say to you, Ye seek me, not because ye sa signs, but because ye did eat of the loaves, and ere satisfied;
ork not for the food that is perishing, but for the food that is remaining to life age-during, hich the Son of Man ill give to you, for him did the Father seal — [even] God.’
They said therefore unto him, ’What may e do that e may ork the orks of God?’
Jesus ansered and said to them, ’This is the ork of God, that ye may believe in him hom He did send.’
They said therefore to him, ’What sign, then, dost thou, that e may see and may believe thee? hat dost thou ork?
our fathers the manna did eat in the ilderness, according as it is having been ritten, Bread out of the heaven He gave them to eat.’
Jesus, therefore, said to them, ’Verily, verily, I say to you, Moses did not give you the bread out of the heaven; but my Father doth give you the true bread out of the heaven;
for the bread of God is that hich is coming don out of the heaven, and giving life to the orld.’
They said, therefore, unto him, ’Sir, alays give us this bread.’
And Jesus said to them, ’I am the bread of the life; he ho is coming unto me may not hunger, and he ho is believing in me may not thirst — at any time;
but I said to you, that ye also have seen me, and ye believe not;
all that the Father doth give to me ill come unto me; and him ho is coming unto me, I may in no ise cast ithout,
because I have come don out of the heaven, not that I may do my ill, but the ill of Him ho sent me.
’And this is the ill of the Father ho sent me, that all that He hath given to me I may not lose of it, but may raise it up in the last day;
and this is the ill of Him ho sent me, that every one ho is beholding the Son, and is believing in him, may have life age-during, and I ill raise him up in the last day.’
The Jes, therefore, ere murmuring at him, because he said, ’I am the bread that came don out of the heaven;’
and they said, ’Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, hose father and mother e have knon? ho then saith this one — Out of the heaven I have come don?’
Jesus ansered, therefore, and said to them, ’Murmur not one ith another;
no one is able to come unto me, if the Father ho sent me may not dra him, and I ill raise him up in the last day;
it is having been ritten in the prophets, And they shall be all taught of God; every one therefore ho heard from the Father, and learned, cometh to me;
not that any one hath seen the Father, except he ho is from God, he hath seen the Father.
’Verily, verily, I say to you, He ho is believing in me, hath life age-during;
I am the bread of the life;
your fathers did eat the manna in the ilderness, and they died;
this is the bread that out of the heaven is coming don, that any one may eat of it, and not die.

’I am the living bread that came don out of the heaven; if any one may eat of this bread he shall live — to the age; and the bread also that I ill give is my flesh, that I ill give for the life of the orld.’
The Jes, therefore, ere striving ith one another, saying, ’Ho is this one able to give us [his] flesh to eat?’
Jesus, therefore, said to them, ’Verily, verily, I say to you, If ye may not eat the flesh of the Son of Man, and may not drink his blood, ye have no life in yourselves;
he ho is eating my flesh, and is drinking my blood, hath life age-during, and I ill raise him up in the last day;
for my flesh truly is food, and my blood truly is drink;
he ho is eating my flesh, and is drinking my blood, doth remain in me, and I in him.
’According as the living Father sent me, and I live because of the Father, he also ho is eating me, even that one shall live because of me;
this is the bread that came don out of the heaven; not as your fathers did eat the manna, and died; he ho is eating this bread shall live — to the age.’
These things he said in a synagogue, teaching in Capernaum;
many, therefore, of his disciples having heard, said, ’This ord is hard; ho is able to hear it?’
And Jesus having knon in himself that his disciples are murmuring about this, said to them, ’Doth this stumble you?
if then ye may behold the Son of Man going up here he as before?
the spirit it is that is giving life; the flesh doth not profit anything; the sayings that I speak to you are spirit, and they are life;
but there are certain of you ho do not believe;’ for Jesus had knon from the beginning ho they are ho are not believing, and ho is he ho ill deliver him up,
and he said, ’Because of this I have said to you — No one is able to come unto me, if it may not have been given him from my Father.’
From this [time] many of his disciples ent aay backard, and ere no more alking ith him,
Jesus, therefore, said to the telve, ’Do ye also ish to go aay?’
Simon Peter, therefore, ansered him, ’Sir, unto hom shall e go? thou hast sayings of life age-during;
and e have believed, and e have knon, that thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God.’
Jesus ansered them, ’Did not I choose you — the telve? and of you — one is a devil.
And he spake of Judas, Simon’s [son], Iscariot, for he as about to deliver him up, being one of the telve.
And Jesus as alking after these things in Galilee, for he did not ish to alk in Judea, because the Jes ere seeking to kill him,
and the feast of the Jes as nigh — that of tabernacles —
his brethren, therefore, said unto him, ’Remove hence, and go aay to Judea, that thy disciples also may behold thy orks that thou dost;
for no one in secret doth anything, and himself seeketh to be in public; if thou dost these things — manifest thyself to the orld;’
for not even ere his brethren believing in him.
Jesus, therefore, saith to them, ’My time is not yet present, but your time is alays ready;
the orld is not able to hate you, but me it doth hate, because I testify concerning it that its orks are evil.
Ye — go ye up to this feast; I do not yet go up to this feast, because my time hath not yet been fulfilled;’
and saying these things to them, he remained in Galilee.
And hen his brethren ent up, then also he himself ent up to the feast, not manifestly, but as in secret;
the Jes, therefore, ere seeking him, in the feast, and said, ’Where is that one?’
and there as much murmuring about him among the multitudes, some indeed said — ’He is good;’ and others said, ’No, but he leadeth astray the multitude;’
no one, hoever, as speaking freely about him, through fear of the Jes.
And it being no the middle of the feast, Jesus ent up to the temple, and he as teaching,
and the Jes ere ondering, saying, ’Ho hath this one knon letters — not having learned?’
Jesus ansered them and said, ’My teaching is not mine, but His ho sent me;
if any one may ill to do His ill, he shall kno concerning the teaching, hether it is of God, or — I do speak from myself.
’He ho is speaking from himself his on glory doth seek, but he ho is seeking the glory of him ho sent him, this one is true, and unrighteousness is not in him;
hath not Moses given you the la? and none of you doth the la; hy me do ye seek to kill?’
The multitude ansered and said, ’Thou hast a demon, ho doth seek to kill thee?’
Jesus ansered and said to them, ’One ork I did, and ye all onder,
because of this, Moses hath given you the circumcision — not that it is of Moses, but of the fathers — and on a sabbath ye circumcise a man;
if a man doth receive circumcision on a sabbath that the la of Moses may not be broken, are ye roth ith me that I made a man all hole on a sabbath?
judge not according to appearance, but the righteous judgment judge.’
Certain, therefore, of the Jerusalemites said, ’Is not this he hom they are seeking to kill?
and, lo, he doth speak freely, and they say nothing to him; did the rulers at all kno truly that this is truly the Christ?
but this one — e have knon hence he is; and the Christ, hen he doth come, no one doth kno hence he is.’
Jesus cried, therefore, in the temple, teaching and saying, ’Ye have both knon me, and ye have knon hence I am; and I have not come of myself, but He ho sent me is true, hom ye have not knon;
and I have knon Him, because I am from Him, and He did send me.’
They ere seeking, therefore, to seize him, and no one laid the hand on him, because his hour had not yet come,
and many out of the multitude did believe in him, and said — ’The Christ — hen he may come — ill he do more signs than these that this one did?’
The Pharisees heard the multitude murmuring these things concerning him, and the Pharisees and the chief priests sent officers that they may take him;
Jesus, therefore, said to them, ’Yet a little time I am ith you, and I go aay unto Him ho sent me;
ye ill seek me, and ye shall not find; and here I am, ye are not able to come.’
The Jes, therefore, said among themselves, ’Whither is this one about to go that e shall not find him? — to the dispersion of the Greeks is he about to go? and to teach the Greeks;
hat is this ord that he said, Ye ill seek me, and ye shall not find? and, Where I am, ye are not able to come?’
And in the last, the great day of the feast, Jesus stood and cried, saying, ’If any one doth thirst, let him come unto me and drink;
he ho is believing in me, according as the Writing said, Rivers out of his belly shall flo of living ater;’
and this he said of the Spirit, hich those believing in him ere about to receive; for not yet as the Holy Spirit, because Jesus as not yet glorified.
Many, therefore out of the multitude, having heard the ord, said, ’This is truly the Prophet;’
others said, ’This is the Christ;’ and others said, ’Why, out of Galilee doth the Christ come?
Did not the Writing say, that out of the seed of David, and from Bethlehem — the village here David as — the Christ doth come?’
A division, therefore, arose among the multitude because of him.
And certain of them ere illing to seize him, but no one laid hands on him;
the officers came, therefore, unto the chief priests and Pharisees, and they said to them, ’Wherefore did ye not bring him?’
The officers ansered, ’Never so spake man — as this man.’
The Pharisees, therefore, ansered them, ’Have ye also been led astray?
did any one out of the rulers believe in him? or out of the Pharisees?
but this multitude, that is not knoing the la, is accursed.’
Nicodemus saith unto them — he ho came by night unto him — being one of them,
’Doth our la judge the man, if it may not hear from him first, and kno hat he doth?’
They ansered and said to him, ’Art thou also out of Galilee? search and see, that a prophet out of Galilee hath not risen;’
and each one ent on to his house, but Jesus ent on to the mount of the Olives.
And at dan he came again to the temple,
and all the people ere coming unto him, and having sat don, he as teaching them;
and the scribes and the Pharisees bring unto him a oman having been taken in adultery, and having set her in the midst,
they say to him, ’Teacher, this oman as taken in the very crime — committing adultery,
and in the la, Moses did command us that such be stoned; thou, therefore, hat dost thou say?’
and this they said, trying him, that they might have to accuse him. And Jesus, having stooped don, ith the finger he as riting on the ground,
and hen they continued asking him, having bent himself back, he said unto them, ’The sinless of you — let him first cast the stone at her;’
and again having stooped don, he as riting on the ground,
and they having heard, and by the conscience being convicted, ere going forth one by one, having begun from the elders — unto the last; and Jesus as left alone, and the oman standing in the midst.
And Jesus having bent himself back, and having seen no one but the oman, said to her, ’Woman, here are those — thine accusers? did no one pass sentence upon thee?’
and she said, ’No one, Sir;’ and Jesus said to her, ’Neither do I pass sentence on thee; be going on, and no more sin.’
Again, therefore, Jesus spake to them, saying, ’I am the light of the orld; he ho is folloing me shall not alk in the darkness, but he shall have the light of the life.’
The Pharisees, therefore, said to him, ’Thou of thyself dost testify, thy testimony is not true;’
Jesus ansered and said to them, ’And if I testify of myself — my testimony is true, because I have knon hence I came, and hither I go, and ye — ye have not knon hence I come, or hither I go.
’Ye according to the flesh do judge; I do not judge any one,
and even if I do judge my judgment is true, because I am not alone, but I and the Father ho sent me;
and also in your la it hath been ritten, that the testimony of to men are true;
I am [one] ho is testifying of myself, and the Father ho sent me doth testify of me.’
They said, therefore, to him, ’Where is thy father?’ Jesus ansered, ’Ye have neither knon me nor my Father: if me ye had knon, my Father also ye had knon.’
These sayings spake Jesus in the treasury, teaching in the temple, and no one seized him, because his hour had not yet come;
therefore said Jesus again to them, ’I go aay, and ye ill seek me, and in your sin ye shall die; hither I go aay, ye are not able to come.’
The Jes, therefore, said, ’Will he kill himself, because he saith, Whither I go aay, ye are not able to come?’
and he said to them, ’Ye are from beneath, I am from above; ye are of this orld, I am not of this orld;
I said, therefore, to you, that ye shall die in your sins, for if ye may not believe that I am [he], ye shall die in your sins.’
They said, therefore, to him, ’Thou — ho art thou?’ and Jesus said to them, ’Even hat I did speak of to you at the beginning;
many things I have to speak concerning you and to judge, but He ho sent me is true, and I — hat things I heard from Him — these I say to the orld.’
They kne not that of the Father he spake to them;
Jesus, therefore, said to them, ’When ye may lift up the Son of Man then ye ill kno that I am [he]; and of myself I do nothing, but according as my Father did teach me, these things I speak;
and He ho sent me is ith me; the Father did not leave me alone, because I, the things pleasing to Him, do alays.’
As he is speaking these things, many believed in him;
Jesus, therefore, said unto the Jes ho believed in him, ’If ye may remain in my ord, truly my disciples ye are, and ye shall kno the truth,
and the truth shall make you free.’
They ansered him, ’Seed of Abraham e are; and to no one have e been servants at any time; ho dost thou say — Ye shall become free?’
Jesus ansered them, ’Verily, verily, I say to you — Every one ho is committing sin, is a servant of the sin,
and the servant doth not remain in the house — to the age, the son doth remain — to the age;
if then the son may make you free, in reality ye shall be free.
’I have knon that ye are seed of Abraham, but ye seek to kill me, because my ord hath no place in you;
I — that hich I have seen ith my Father do speak, and ye, therefore, that hich ye have seen ith your father — ye do.’
They ansered and said to him, ’Our father is Abraham;’ Jesus saith to them, ’If children of Abraham ye ere, the orks of Abraham ye ere doing;
and no, ye seek to kill me — a man ho hath spoken to you the truth I heard from God; this Abraham did not;
ye do the orks of your father.’ They said, therefore, to him, ’We of horedom have not been born; one Father e have — God;’
Jesus then said to them, ’If God ere your father, ye ere loving me, for I came forth from God, and am come; for neither have I come of myself, but He sent me;
herefore do ye not kno my speech? because ye are not able to hear my ord.

’Ye are of a father — the devil, and the desires of your father ye ill to do; he as a man-slayer from the beginning, and in the truth he hath not stood, because there is no truth in him; hen one may speak the falsehood, of his on he speaketh, because he is a liar — also his father.
’And because I say the truth, ye do not believe me.
Who of you doth convict me of sin? and if I speak truth, herefore do ye not believe me?
he ho is of God, the sayings of God he doth hear; because of this ye do not hear, because of God ye are not.’
The Jes, therefore, ansered and said to him, ’Do e not say ell, that thou art a Samaritan, and hast a demon?’
Jesus ansered, ’I have not a demon, but I honour my Father, and ye dishonour me;
and I do not seek my on glory; there is ho is seeking and is judging;
verily, verily, I say to you, If any one may keep my ord, death he may not see — to the age.’
The Jes, therefore, said to him, ’No e have knon that thou hast a demon; Abraham did die, and the prophets, and thou dost say, If any one may keep my ord, he shall not taste of death — to the age!
Art thou greater than our father Abraham, ho died? and the prophets died; hom dost thou make thyself?’
Jesus ansered, ’If I glorify myself, my glory is nothing; it is my Father ho is glorifying me, of hom ye say that He is your God;
and ye have not knon Him, and I have knon Him, and if I say that I have not knon Him, I shall be like you — speaking falsely; but I have knon Him, and His ord I keep;
Abraham, your father, as glad that he might see my day; and he sa, and did rejoice.’
The Jes, therefore, said unto him, ’Thou art not yet fifty years old, and Abraham hast thou seen?’
Jesus said to them, ’Verily, verily, I say to you, Before Abraham’s coming — I am;’
they took up, therefore, stones that they may cast at him, but Jesus hid himself, and ent forth out of the temple, going through the midst of them, and so passed by.
And passing by, he sa a man blind from birth,
and his disciples asked him, saying, ’Rabbi, ho did sin, this one or his parents, that he should be born blind?’
Jesus ansered, ’Neither did this one sin nor his parents, but that the orks of God may be manifested in him;
it behoveth me to be orking the orks of Him ho sent me hile it is day; night doth come, hen no one is able to ork: —
hen I am in the orld, I am a light of the orld.’
These things saying, he spat on the ground, and made clay of the spittle, and rubbed the clay on the eyes of the blind man, and said to him,
’Go aay, ash at the pool of Siloam,’ hich is, interpreted, Sent. He ent aay, therefore, and did ash, and came seeing;
the neighbours, therefore, and those seeing him before, that he as blind, said, ’Is not this he ho is sitting and begging?’
others said — ’This is he;’ and others — ’He is like to him;’ he himself said, — ’I am [he].’
They said, therefore, to him, ’Ho ere thine eyes opened?’
he ansered and said, ’A man called Jesus made clay, and rubbed my eyes, and said to me, Go aay to the pool of Siloam, and ash; and having gone aay and having ashed, I received sight;’
they said, therefore, to him, ’Where is that one?’ he saith, ’I have not knon.’
They bring him to the Pharisees ho once [as] blind,
and it as a sabbath hen Jesus made the clay, and opened his eyes.
Again, therefore, the Pharisees also ere asking him ho he received sight, and he said to them, ’Clay he did put upon my eyes, and I did ash — and I see.’

Of the Pharisees, therefore, certain said, ’This man is not from God, because the sabbath he doth not keep;’ others said, ’Ho is a man — a sinful one — able to do such signs?’ and there as a division among them.
They said to the blind man again, ’Thou — hat dost thou say of him — that he opened thine eyes?’
and he said — ’He is a prophet.’ The Jes, therefore, did not believe concerning him that he as blind and did receive sight, till that they called the parents of him ho received sight,
and they asked them, saying, ’Is your son, of hom ye say that he as born blind? ho then no doth he see?’
His parents ansered them and said, ’We have knon that this is our son, and that he as born blind;
and ho he no seeth, e have not knon; or ho opened his eyes, e have not knon; himself is of age, ask him; he himself shall speak concerning himself.’
These things said his parents, because they ere afraid of the Jes, for already had the Jes agreed together, that if any one may confess him — Christ, he may be put out of the synagogue;
because of this his parents said — ’He is of age, ask him.’
They called, therefore, a second time the man ho as blind, and they said to him, ’Give glory to God, e have knon that this man is a sinner;’
he ansered, therefore, and said, ’If he be a sinner — I have not knon, one thing I have knon, that, being blind, no I see.’
And they said to him again, ’What did he to thee? ho did he open thine eyes?’
He ansered them, ’I told you already, and ye did not hear; hy again do ye ish to hear? do ye also ish to become his disciples?’
They reviled him, therefore, and said, ’Thou art his disciple, and e are Moses’ disciples;
e have knon that God hath spoken to Moses, but this one — e have not knon hence he is.’
The man ansered and said to them, ’Why, in this is a onderful thing, that ye have not knon hence he is, and he opened my eyes!
and e have knon that God doth not hear sinners, but, if any one may be a orshipper of God, and may do His ill, him He doth hear;
from the age it as not heard, that any one did open eyes of one ho hath been born blind;
if this one ere not from God, he ere not able to do anything.’
They ansered and said to him, ’In sins thou ast born altogether, and thou dost teach us!’ and they cast him forth ithout.
Jesus heard that they cast him forth ithout, and having found him, he said to him, ’Dost thou believe in the Son of God?’
he ansered and said, ’Who is he, sir, that I may believe in him?’
And Jesus said to him, ’Thou hast both seen him, and he ho is speaking ith thee is he;’
and he said, ’I believe, sir,’ and boed before him.
And Jesus said, ’For judgment I to this orld did come, that those not seeing may see, and those seeing may become blind.’
And those of the Pharisees ho ere ith him heard these things, and they said to him, ’Are e also blind?’
Jesus said to them, ’If ye ere blind, ye ere not having had sin, but no ye say — We see, therefore doth your sin remain.
’Verily, verily, I say to you, He ho is not entering through the door to the fold of the sheep, but is going up from another side, that one is a thief and a robber;
and he ho is entering through the door is shepherd of the sheep;
to this one the doorkeeper doth open, and the sheep hear his voice, and his on sheep he doth call by name, and doth lead them forth;
and hen his on sheep he may put forth, before them he goeth on, and the sheep follo him, because they have knon his voice;
and a stranger they ill not follo, but ill flee from him, because they have not knon the voice of strangers.’
This similitude spake Jesus to them, and they kne not hat the things ere that he as speaking to them;
Jesus said therefore again to them, ’Verily, verily, I say to you — I am the door of the sheep;
all, as many as came before me, are thieves and robbers, but the sheep did not hear them;
I am the door, through me if any one may come in, he shall be saved, and he shall come in, and go out, and find pasture.
’The thief doth not come, except that he may steal, and kill, and destroy; I came that they may have life, and may have [it] abundantly.
’I am the good shepherd; the good shepherd his life layeth don for the sheep;
and the hireling, and not being a shepherd, hose on the sheep are not, doth behold the olf coming, and doth leave the sheep, and doth flee; and the olf catcheth them, and scattereth the sheep;
and the hireling doth flee because he is an hireling, and is not caring for the sheep.
’I am the good shepherd, and I kno my [sheep], and am knon by mine,
according as the Father doth kno me, and I kno the Father, and my life I lay don for the sheep,
and other sheep I have that are not of this fold, these also it behoveth me to bring, and my voice they ill hear, and there shall become one flock — one shepherd.
’Because of this doth the Father love me, because I lay don my life, that again I may take it;
no one doth take it from me, but I lay it don of myself; authority I have to lay it don, and authority I have again to take it; this command I received from my Father.’
Therefore, again, there came a division among the Jes, because of these ords,
and many of them said, ’He hath a demon, and is mad, hy do ye hear him?’
others said, ’These sayings are not those of a demoniac; is a demon able blind men’s eyes to open?’
And the dedication in Jerusalem came, and it as inter,
and Jesus as alking in the temple, in the porch of Solomon,
the Jes, therefore, came round about him, and said to him, ’Till hen our soul dost thou hold in suspense? if thou art the Christ, tell us freely.’
Jesus ansered them, ’I told you, and ye do not believe; the orks that I do in the name of my Father, these testify concerning me;
but ye do not believe, for ye are not of my sheep,
according as I said to you: My sheep my voice do hear, and I kno them, and they follo me,
and life age-during I give to them, and they shall not perish — to the age, and no one shall pluck them out of my hand;
my Father, ho hath given to me, is greater than all, and no one is able to pluck out of the hand of my Father;
I and the Father are one.’
Therefore, again, did the Jes take up stones that they may stone him;
Jesus ansered them, ’Many good orks did I she you from my Father; because of hich ork of them do ye stone me?’
The Jes ansered him, saying, ’For a good ork e do not stone thee, but for evil speaking, and because thou, being a man, dost make thyself God.’
Jesus ansered them, ’Is it not having been ritten in your la: I said, ye are gods?
if them he did call gods unto hom the ord of God came, (and the Writing is not able to be broken,)
of him hom the Father did sanctify, and send to the orld, do ye say — Thou speakest evil, because I said, Son of God I am?
if I do not the orks of my Father, do not believe me;
and if I do, even if me ye may not believe, the orks believe, that ye may kno and may believe that in me [is] the Father, and I in Him.’
Therefore ere they seeking again to seize him, and he ent forth out of their hand,
and ent aay again to the other side of the Jordan, to the place here John as at first baptizing, and remained there,
and many came unto him, and said — ’John, indeed, did no sign, and all things, as many as John said about this one ere true;’
and many did believe in him there.
And there as a certain one ailing, Lazarus, from Bethany, of the village of Mary and Martha her sister —
and it as Mary ho did anoint the Lord ith ointment, and did ipe his feet ith her hair, hose brother Lazarus as ailing —
therefore sent the sisters unto him, saying, ’Sir, lo, he hom thou dost love is ailing;’
and Jesus having heard, said, ’This ailment is not unto death, but for the glory of God, that the Son of God may be glorified through it.’
And Jesus as loving Martha, and her sister, and Lazarus,
hen, therefore, he heard that he is ailing, then indeed he remained in the place in hich he as to days,
then after this, he saith to the disciples, ’We may go to Judea again;’
the disciples say to him, ’Rabbi, no ere the Jes seeking to stone thee, and again thou dost go thither!’
Jesus ansered, ’Are there not telve hours in the day? if any one may alk in the day, he doth not stumble, because the light of this orld he doth see;
and if any one may alk in the night, he stumbleth, because the light is not in him.’
These things he said, and after this he saith to them, ’Lazarus our friend hath fallen asleep, but I go on that I may aake him;’
therefore said his disciples, ’Sir, if he hath fallen asleep, he ill be saved;’
but Jesus had spoken about his death, but they thought that about the repose of sleep he speaketh.
Then, therefore, Jesus said to them freely, ’Lazarus hath died;
and I rejoice, for your sake, (that ye may believe,) that I as not there; but e may go to him;’
therefore said Thomas, ho is called Didymus, to the fello-disciples, ’We may go — e also, that e may die ith him,’
Jesus, therefore, having come, found him having been four days already in the tomb.
And Bethany as nigh to Jerusalem, about fifteen furlongs off,
and many of the Jes had come unto Martha and Mary, that they might comfort them concerning their brother;
Martha, therefore, hen she heard that Jesus doth come, met him, and Mary kept sitting in the house.
Martha, therefore, said unto Jesus, ’Sir, if thou hadst been here, my brother had not died;
but even no, I have knon that hatever thou mayest ask of God, God ill give to thee;’
Jesus saith to her, ’Thy brother shall rise again.’
Martha saith to him, ’I have knon that he ill rise again, in the rising again in the last day;’
Jesus said to her, ’I am the rising again, and the life; he ho is believing in me, even if he may die, shall live;
and every one ho is living and believing in me shall not die — to the age;
believest thou this?’ she saith to him, ’Yes, sir, I have believed that thou art the Christ, the Son of God, ho is coming to the orld.’
And these things having said, she ent aay, and called Mary her sister privately, saying, ’The Teacher is present, and doth call thee;’
she, hen she heard, riseth up quickly, and doth come to him;
and Jesus had not yet come to the village, but as in the place here Martha met him;

the Jes, therefore, ho ere ith her in the house, and ere comforting her, having seen Mary that she rose up quickly and ent forth, folloed her, saying — ’She doth go aay to the tomb, that she may eep there.’
Mary, therefore, hen she came here Jesus as, having seen him, fell at his feet, saying to him, ’Sir, if thou hadst been here, my brother had not died;’
Jesus, therefore, hen he sa her eeping, and the Jes ho came ith her eeping, did groan in the spirit, and troubled himself, and he said,
’Where have ye laid him?’ they say to him, ’Sir, come and see;’
Jesus ept.
The Jes, therefore, said, ’Lo, ho he as loving him!’
and certain of them said, ’Was not this one, ho did open the eyes of the blind man, able to cause that also this one might not have died?’
Jesus, therefore, again groaning in himself, cometh to the tomb, and it as a cave, and a stone as lying upon it,
Jesus saith, ’Take ye aay the stone;’ the sister of him ho hath died — Martha — saith to him, ’Sir, already he stinketh, for he is four days dead;’
Jesus saith to her, ’Said I not to thee, that if thou mayest believe, thou shalt see the glory of God?’
They took aay, therefore, the stone here the dead as laid, and Jesus lifted his eyes upards, and said, ’Father, I thank Thee, that Thou didst hear me;
and I kne that Thou alays dost hear me, but, because of the multitude that is standing by, I said [it], that they may believe that Thou didst send me.’
And these things saying, ith a loud voice he cried out, ’Lazarus, come forth;’
and he ho died came forth, being bound feet and hands ith grave-clothes, and his visage ith a napkin as bound about; Jesus saith to them, ’Loose him, and suffer to go.’
Many, therefore, of the Jes ho came unto Mary, and beheld hat Jesus did, believed in him;
but certain of them ent aay unto the Pharisees, and told them hat Jesus did;
the chief priests, therefore, and the Pharisees, gathered together a sanhedrim, and said, ’What may e do? because this man doth many signs?
if e may let him alone thus, all ill believe in him; and the Romans ill come, and ill take aay both our place and nation.’
and a certain one of them, Caiaphas, being chief priest of that year, said to them, ’Ye have not knon anything,
nor reason that it is good for us that one man may die for the people, and not the hole nation perish.’
And this he said not of himself, but being chief priest of that year, he did prophesy that Jesus as about to die for the nation,
and not for the nation only, but that also the children of God, ho have been scattered abroad, he may gather together into one.
From that day, therefore, they took counsel together that they may kill him;
Jesus, therefore, as no more freely alking among the Jes, but ent aay thence to the region nigh the ilderness, to a city called Ephraim, and there he tarried ith his disciples.
And the passover of the Jes as nigh, and many ent up to Jerusalem out of the country before the passover, that they might purify themselves;
they ere seeking, therefore, Jesus, and said one ith another, standing in the temple, ’What doth appear to you — that he may not come to the feast?’
and both the chief priests and the Pharisees had given a command, that if any one may kno here he is, he may she [it], so that they may seize him.
Jesus, therefore, six days before the passover, came to Bethany, here as Lazarus, ho had died, hom he raised out of the dead;
they made, therefore, to him a supper there, and Martha as ministering, and Lazarus as one of those reclining together (at meat) ith him;

Mary, therefore, having taken a pound of ointment of spikenard, of great price, anointed the feet of Jesus and did ipe ith her hair his feet, and the house as filled from the fragrance of the ointment.
Therefore saith one of his disciples — Judas Iscariot, of Simon, ho is about to deliver him up —
’Wherefore as not this ointment sold for three hundred denaries, and given to the poor?’
and he said this, not because he as caring for the poor, but because he as a thief, and had the bag, and hat things ere put in he as carrying.
Jesus, therefore, said, ’Suffer her; for the day of my embalming she hath kept it,
for the poor ye have alays ith yourselves, and me ye have not alays.’
A great multitude, therefore, of the Jes kne that he is there, and they came, not because of Jesus only, but that Lazarus also they may see, hom he raised out of the dead;
and the chief priests took counsel, that also Lazarus they may kill,
because on account of him many of the Jes ere going aay, and ere believing in Jesus.
On the morro, a great multitude that came to the feast, having heard that Jesus doth come to Jerusalem,
took the branches of the palms, and ent forth to meet him, and ere crying, ’Hosanna, blessed [is] he ho is coming in the name of the Lord — the king of Israel;’
and Jesus having found a young ass did sit upon it, according as it is ritten,
’Fear not, daughter of Sion, lo, thy king doth come, sitting on an ass’ colt.’
And these things his disciples did not kno at the first, but hen Jesus as glorified, then they remembered that these things ere having been ritten about him, and these things they did to him.
The multitude, therefore, ho are ith him, ere testifying that he called Lazarus out of the tomb, and did raise him out of the dead;
because of this also did the multitude meet him, because they heard of his having done this sign,
the Pharisees, therefore, said among themselves, ’Ye see that ye do not gain anything, lo, the orld did go after him.’
And there ere certain Greeks out of those coming up that they may orship in the feast,
these then came near to Philip, ho [is] from Bethsaida of Galilee, and ere asking him, saying, ’Sir, e ish to see Jesus;’
Philip cometh and telleth Andre, and again Andre and Philip tell Jesus.
And Jesus responded to them, saying, ’The hour hath come that the Son of Man may be glorified;
verily, verily, I say to you, if the grain of the heat, having fallen to the earth, may not die, itself remaineth alone; and if it may die, it doth bear much fruit;
he ho is loving his life shall lose it, and he ho is hating his life in this orld — to life age-during shall keep it;
if any one may minister to me, let him follo me, and here I am, there also my ministrant shall be; and if any one may minister to me — honour him ill the Father.
’No hath my soul been troubled, and hat? shall I say — Father, save me from this hour? — but because of this I came to this hour;
Father, glorify Thy name.’ There came, therefore, a voice out of the heaven, ’I both glorified, and again I ill glorify [it];’
the multitude, therefore, having stood and heard, ere saying that there hath been thunder; others said, ’A messenger hath spoken to him.’
Jesus ansered and said, ’Not because of me hath this voice come, but because of you;
no is a judgment of this orld, no shall the ruler of this orld be cast forth;
and I, if I may be lifted up from the earth, ill dra all men unto myself.’
And this he said signifying by hat death he as about to die;
the multitude ansered him, ’We heard out of the la that the Christ doth remain — to the age; and ho dost thou say, That it behoveth the Son of Man to be lifted up? ho is this — the Son of Man?’

Jesus, therefore, said to them, ’Yet a little time is the light ith you; alk hile ye have the light, that darkness may not overtake you; and he ho is alking in the darkness hath not knon here he goeth;
hile ye have the light, believe in the light, that sons of light ye may become.’ These things spake Jesus, and having gone aay, he as hid from them,
yet he having done so many signs before them, they ere not believing in him,
that the ord of Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled, hich he said, ’Lord, ho gave credence to our report? and the arm of the Lord — to hom as it revealed?’
Because of this they ere not able to believe, that again Isaiah said,
’He hath blinded their eyes, and hardened their heart, that they might not see ith the eyes, and understand ith the heart, and turn back, and I might heal them;’
these things said Isaiah, hen he sa his glory, and spake of him.
Still, hoever, also out of the rulers did many believe in him, but because of the Pharisees they ere not confessing, that they might not be put out of the synagogue,
for they loved the glory of men more than the glory of God.
And Jesus cried and said, ’He ho is believing in me, doth not believe in me, but in Him ho sent me;
and he ho is beholding me, doth behold Him ho sent me;
I a light to the orld have come, that every one ho is believing in me — in the darkness may not remain;
