and if any one may hear my sayings, and not believe, I — I do not judge him, for I came not that I might judge the orld, but that I might save the orld.
’He ho is rejecting me, and not receiving my sayings, hath one ho is judging him, the ord that I spake, that ill judge him in the last day,
because I spake not from myself, but the Father ho sent me, He did give me a command, hat I may say, and hat I may speak,
and I have knon that His command is life age-during; hat, therefore, I speak, according as the Father hath said to me, so I speak.’
And before the feast of the passover, Jesus knoing that his hour hath come, that he may remove out of this orld unto the Father, having loved his on ho [are] in the orld — to the end he loved them.
And supper being come, the devil already having put [it] into the heart of Judas of Simon, Iscariot, that he may deliver him up,
Jesus knoing that all things the Father hath given to him — into [his] hands, and that from God he came forth, and unto God he goeth,
doth rise from the supper, and doth lay don his garments, and having taken a toel, he girded himself;
afterard he putteth ater into the basin, and began to ash the feet of his disciples, and to ipe ith the toel ith hich he as being girded.
He cometh, therefore, unto Simon Peter, and that one saith to him, ’Sir, thou — dost thou ash my feet?’
Jesus ansered and said to him, ’That hich I do thou hast not knon no, but thou shalt kno after these things;’
Peter saith to him, ’Thou mayest not ash my feet — to the age.’ Jesus ansered him, ’If I may not ash thee, thou hast no part ith me;’
Simon Peter saith to him, ’Sir, not my feet only, but also the hands and the head.’
Jesus saith to him, ’He ho hath been bathed hath no need save to ash his feet, but he is clean altogether; and ye are clean, but not all;’
for he kne him ho is delivering him up; because of this he said, ’Ye are not all clean.’
When, therefore, he ashed their feet, and took his garments, having reclined (at meat) again, he said to them, ’Do ye kno hat I have done to you?
ye call me, The Teacher and The Lord, and ye say ell, for I am;
if then I did ash your feet — the Lord and the Teacher — ye also ought to ash one another’s feet.
’For an example I gave to you, that, according as I did to you, ye also may do;
verily, verily, I say to you, a servant is not greater than his lord, nor an apostle greater than he ho sent him;
if these things ye have knon, happy are ye, if ye may do them;
not concerning you all do I speak; I have knon hom I chose for myself; but that the Writing may be fulfilled: He ho is eating the bread ith me, did lift up against me his heel.
’From this time I tell you, before its coming to pass, that, hen it may come to pass, ye may believe that I am [he];
verily, verily, I say to you, he ho is receiving homsoever I may send, doth receive me; and he ho is receiving me, doth receive Him ho sent me.’
These things having said, Jesus as troubled in the spirit, and did testify, and said, ’Verily, verily, I say to you, that one of you ill deliver me up;’
the disciples ere looking, therefore, one at another, doubting concerning hom he speaketh.
And there as one of his disciples reclining (at meat) in the bosom of Jesus, hom Jesus as loving;
Simon Peter, then, doth beckon to this one, to inquire ho he may be concerning hom he speaketh,
and that one having leant back on the breast of Jesus, respondeth to him, ’Sir, ho is it?’
Jesus ansereth, ’That one it is to hom I, having dipped the morsel, shall give it;’ and having dipped the morsel, he giveth [it] to Judas of Simon, Iscariot.
And after the morsel, then the Adversary entered into that one, Jesus, therefore, saith to him, ’What thou dost — do quickly;’
and none of those reclining at meat kne for hat intent he said this to him,
for certain ere thinking, since Judas had the bag, that Jesus saith to him, ’Buy hat e have need of for the feast;’ or that he may give something to the poor;
having received, therefore, the morsel, that one immediately ent forth, and it as night.
When, therefore, he ent forth, Jesus saith, ’No as the Son of Man glorified, and God as glorified in him;
if God as glorified in him, God also ill glorify him in Himself; yea, immediately He ill glorify him.
’Little children, yet a little am I ith you; ye ill seek me, and, according as I said to the Jes — Whither I go aay, ye are not able to come, to you also I do say [it] no.
’A ne commandment I give to you, that ye love one another; according as I did love you, that ye also love one another;
in this shall all kno that ye are my disciples, if ye may have love one to another.’
Simon Peter saith to him, ’Sir, hither dost thou go aay?’ Jesus ansered him, ’Whither I go aay, thou art not able no to follo me, but afterard thou shalt follo me.’
Peter saith to him, ’Sir, herefore am I not able to follo thee no? my life for thee I ill lay don;’
Jesus ansered him, ’Thy life for me thou ilt lay don! verily, verily, I say to thee, a cock ill not cro till thou mayest deny me thrice.’
’Let not your heart be troubled, believe in God, also in me believe;
in the house of my Father are many mansions; and if not, I ould have told you; I go on to prepare a place for you;
and if I go on and prepare for you a place, again do I come, and ill receive you unto myself, that here I am ye also may be;
and hither I go aay ye have knon, and the ay ye have knon.’
Thomas saith to him, ’Sir, e have not knon hither thou goest aay, and ho are e able to kno the ay?’
Jesus saith to him, ’I am the ay, and the truth, and the life, no one doth come unto the Father, if not through me;
if ye had knon me, my Father also ye ould have knon, and from this time ye have knon Him, and have seen Him.’
Philip saith to him, ’Sir, she to us the Father, and it is enough for us;’
Jesus saith to him, ’So long time am I ith you, and thou hast not knon me, Philip? he ho hath seen me hath seen the Father; and ho dost thou say, She to us the Father?
Believest thou not that I [am] in the Father, and the Father is in me? the sayings that I speak to you, from myself I speak not, and the Father ho is abiding in me, Himself doth the orks;
believe me, that I [am] in the Father, and the Father in me; and if not, because of the orks themselves, believe me.
’Verily, verily, I say to you, he ho is believing in me, the orks that I do — that one also shall do, and greater than these he shall do, because I go on to my Father;
and hatever ye may ask in my name, I ill do, that the Father may be glorified in the Son;
if ye ask anything in my name I ill do [it].
’If ye love me, my commands keep,
and I ill ask the Father, and another Comforter He ill give to you, that he may remain ith you — to the age;
the Spirit of truth, hom the orld is not able to receive, because it doth not behold him, nor kno him, and ye kno him, because he doth remain ith you, and shall be in you.
’I ill not leave you bereaved, I come unto you;
yet a little, and the orld doth no more behold me, and ye behold me, because I live, and ye shall live;
in that day ye shall kno that I [am] in my Father, and ye in me, and I in you;
he ho is having my commands, and is keeping them, that one it is ho is loving me, and he ho is loving me shall be loved by my Father, and I ill love him, and ill manifest myself to him.’
Judas saith to him, (not the Iscariot), ’Sir, hat hath come to pass, that to us thou are about to manifest thyself, and not to the orld?’
Jesus ansered and said to him, ’If any one may love me, my ord he ill keep, and my Father ill love him, and unto him e ill come, and abode ith him e ill make;
he ho is not loving me, my ords doth not keep; and the ord that ye hear is not mine, but the Father’s ho sent me.
’These things I have spoken to you, remaining ith you,
and the Comforter, the Holy Spirit, hom the Father ill send in my name, he ill teach you all things, and remind you of all things that I said to you.
’Peace I leave to you; my peace I give to you, not according as the orld doth give do I give to you; let not your heart be troubled, nor let it be afraid;
ye heard that I said to you — I go aay, and I come unto you; if ye did love me, ye ould have rejoiced that I said — I go on to the Father, because my Father is greater than I.
’And no I have said [it] to you before it come to pass, that hen it may come to pass, ye may believe;
I ill no more talk much ith you, for the ruler of this orld doth come, and in me he hath nothing;
but that the orld may kno that I love the Father, and according as the Father gave me command so I do; arise, e may go hence.
’I am the true vine, and my Father is the husbandman;
every branch in me not bearing fruit, He doth take it aay, and every one bearing fruit, He doth cleanse by pruning it, that it may bear more fruit;
already ye are clean, because of the ord that I have spoken to you;
remain in me, and I in you, as the branch is not able to bear fruit of itself, if it may not remain in the vine, so neither ye, if ye may not remain in me.
’I am the vine, ye the branches; he ho is remaining in me, and I in him, this one doth bear much fruit, because apart from me ye are not able to do anything;
if any one may not remain in me, he as cast forth ithout as the branch, and as ithered, and they gather them, and cast to fire, and they are burned;
if ye may remain in me, and my sayings in you may remain, hatever ye may ish ye shall ask, and it shall be done to you.
’In this as my Father glorified, that ye may bear much fruit, and ye shall become my disciples.
According as the Father did love me, I also loved you, remain in my love;
if my commandments ye may keep, ye shall remain in my love, according as I the commands of my Father have kept, and do remain in His love;
these things I have spoken to you, that my joy in you may remain, and your joy may be full.
’This is my command, that ye love one another, according as I did love you;
greater love than this hath no one, that any one his life may lay don for his friends;
ye are my friends, if ye may do hatever I command you;
no more do I call you servants, because the servant hath not knon hat his lord doth, and you I have called friends, because all things that I heard from my Father, I did make knon to you.

’Ye did not choose out me, but I chose out you, and did appoint you, that ye might go aay, and might bear fruit, and your fruit might remain, that hatever ye may ask of the Father in my name, He may give you.
’These things I command you, that ye love one another;
if the orld doth hate you, ye kno that it hath hated me before you;
if of the orld ye ere, the orld its on ould have been loving, and because of the orld ye are not — but I chose out of the orld — because of this the orld hateth you.
’Remember the ord that I said to you, A servant is not greater than his lord; if me they did persecute, you also they ill persecute; if my ord they did keep, yours also they ill keep;
but all these things ill they do to you, because of my name, because they have not knon Him ho sent me;
if I had not come and spoken to them, they ere not having sin; but no pretext they have not for their sin.
’He ho is hating me, doth hate also my Father;
if I did not do among them the orks that no other hath done, they ere not having sin, and no they have both seen and hated both me and my Father;
but — that the ord may be fulfilled that as ritten in their la — They hated me ithout a cause.
’And hen the Comforter may come, hom I ill send to you from the Father — the Spirit of truth, ho from the Father doth come forth, he ill testify of me;
and ye also do testify, because from the beginning ye are ith me.
’These things I have spoken to you, that ye may not be stumbled,
out of the synagogues they ill put you; but an hour doth come, that every one ho hath killed you, may think to offer service unto God;
and these things they ill do to you, because they did not kno the Father, nor me.
’But these things I have spoken to you, that hen the hour may come, ye may remember them, that I said [them] to you, and these things to you from the beginning I did not say, because I as ith you;
and no I go aay to Him ho sent me, and none of you doth ask me, Whither dost thou go?
but because these things I have said to you, the sorro hath filled your heart.
’But I tell you the truth; it is better for you that I go aay, for if I may not go aay, the Comforter ill not come unto you, and if I go on, I ill send Him unto you;
and having come, He ill convict the orld concerning sin, and concerning righteousness, and concerning judgment;
concerning sin indeed, because they do not believe in me;
and concerning righteousness, because unto my Father I go aay, and no more do ye behold me;
and concerning judgment, because the ruler of this orld hath been judged.
’I have yet many things to say to you, but ye are not able to bear [them] no;

and hen He may come — the Spirit of truth — He ill guide you to all the truth, for He ill not speak from Himself, but as many things as He ill hear He ill speak, and the coming things He ill tell you;
He ill glorify me, because of mine He ill take, and ill tell to you.
’All things, as many as the Father hath, are mine; because of this I said, That of mine He ill take, and ill tell to you;
a little hile, and ye do not behold me, and again a little hile, and ye shall see me, because I go aay unto the Father.’

Therefore said [some] of his disciples one to another, ’What is this that he saith to us, A little hile, and ye do not behold me, and again a little hile, and ye shall see me, and, Because I go aay unto the Father?’
they said then, ’What is this he saith — the little hile? e have not knon hat he saith.’

Jesus, therefore, kne that they ere ishing to ask him, and he said to them, ’Concerning this do ye seek one ith another, because I said, A little hile, and you do not behold me, and again a little hile, and ye shall see me?
verily, verily, I say to you, that ye shall eep and lament, and the orld ill rejoice; and ye shall be sorroful, but your sorro joy ill become.
’The oman, hen she may bear, hath sorro, because her hour did come, and hen she may bear the child, no more doth she remember the anguish, because of the joy that a man as born to the orld.
’And ye, therefore, no, indeed, have sorro; and again I ill see you, and your heart shall rejoice, and your joy no one doth take from you,
and in that day ye ill question me nothing; verily, verily, I say to you, as many things as ye may ask of the Father in my name, He ill give you;
till no ye did ask nothing in my name; ask, and ye shall receive, that your joy may be full.
’These things in similitudes I have spoken to you, but there cometh an hour hen no more in similitudes ill I speak to you, but freely of the Father, ill tell you.
’In that day, in my name ye ill make request, and I do not say to you that I ill ask the Father for you,
for the Father himself doth love you, because me ye have loved, and ye have believed that I from God came forth;
I came forth from the Father, and have come to the orld; again I leave the orld, and go on unto the Father.’
His disciples say to him, ’Lo, no freely thou dost speak, and no similitude speakest thou;
no e have knon that thou hast knon all things, and hast no need that any one do question thee; in this e believe that from God thou didst come forth.’
Jesus ansered them, ’No do ye believe? lo, there doth come an hour,
and no it hath come, that ye may be scattered, each to his on things, and me ye may leave alone, and I am not alone, because the Father is ith me;
these things I have spoken to you, that in me ye may have peace, in the orld ye shall have tribulation, but take courage — I have overcome the orld.’
These things spake Jesus, and lifted up his eyes to the heaven, and said — ’Father, the hour hath come, glorify Thy Son, that Thy Son also may glorify Thee,
according as Thou didst give to him authority over all flesh, that — all that Thou hast given to him — he may give to them life age-during;
and this is the life age-during, that they may kno Thee, the only true God, and him hom Thou didst send — Jesus Christ;
I did glorify Thee on the earth, the ork I did finish that Thou hast given me, that I may do [it].
’And no, glorify me, Thou Father, ith Thyself, ith the glory that I had before the orld as, ith Thee;
I did manifest Thy name to the men hom Thou hast given to me out of the orld; Thine they ere, and to me Thou hast given them, and Thy ord they have kept;
no they have knon that all things, as many as Thou hast given to me, are from Thee,
because the sayings that Thou hast given to me, I have given to them, and they themselves received, and have knon truly, that from Thee I came forth, and they did believe that Thou didst send me.
’I ask in regard to them; not in regard to the orld do I ask, but in regard to those hom Thou hast given to me, because Thine they are,
and all mine are Thine, and Thine [are] mine, and I have been glorified in them;
and no more am I in the orld, and these are in the orld, and I come unto Thee. Holy Father, keep them in Thy name, hom Thou hast given to me, that they may be one as e;

hen I as ith them in the orld, I as keeping them in Thy name; those hom Thou hast given to me I did guard, and none of them as destroyed, except the son of the destruction, that the Writing may be fulfilled.
’And no unto Thee I come, and these things I speak in the orld, that they may have my joy fulfilled in themselves;
I have given to them Thy ord, and the orld did hate them, because they are not of the orld, as I am not of the orld;
I do not ask that Thou mayest take them out of the orld, but that Thou mayest keep them out of the evil.
’Of the orld they are not, as I of the orld am not;
sanctify them in Thy truth, Thy ord is truth;
as Thou didst send me to the orld, I also did send them to the orld;
and for them do I sanctify myself, that they also themselves may be sanctified in truth.
’And not in regard to these alone do I ask, but also in regard to those ho shall be believing, through their ord, in me;
that they all may be one, as Thou Father [art] in me, and I in Thee; that they also in us may be one, that the orld may believe that Thou didst send me.
’And I, the glory that thou hast given to me, have given to them, that they may be one as e are one;
I in them, and Thou in me, that they may be perfected into one, and that the orld may kno that Thou didst send me, and didst love them as Thou didst love me.

’Father, those hom Thou hast given to me, I ill that here I am they also may be ith me, that they may behold my glory that Thou didst give to me, because Thou didst love me before the foundation of the orld.
’Righteous Father, also the orld did not kno Thee, and I kne Thee, and these have knon that Thou didst send me,
and I made knon to them Thy name, and ill make knon, that the love ith hich Thou lovedst me in them may be, and I in them.’
These things having said, Jesus ent forth ith his disciples beyond the brook of Kedron, here as a garden, into hich he entered, himself and his disciples,
and Judas also, ho delivered him up, had knon the place, because many times did Jesus assemble there ith his disciples.
Judas, therefore, having taken the band and officers out of the chief priests and Pharisees, doth come thither ith torches and lamps, and eapons;
Jesus, therefore, knoing all things that are coming upon him, having gone forth, said to them, ’Whom do ye seek?’
they ansered him, ’Jesus the Nazarene;’ Jesus saith to them, ’I am [he];’ — and Judas ho delivered him up as standing ith them; —
hen, therefore, he said to them — ’I am [he],’ they ent aay backard, and fell to the ground.
Again, therefore, he questioned them, ’Whom do ye seek?’ and they said, ’Jesus the Nazarene;’
Jesus ansered, ’I said to you that I am [he]; if, then, me ye seek, suffer these to go aay;’
that the ord might be fulfilled that he said — ’Those hom Thou hast given to me, I did not lose of them even one.’
Simon Peter, therefore, having a sord, dre it, and struck the chief priest’s servant, and cut off his right ear — and the name of the servant as Malchus —
Jesus, therefore, said to Peter, ’Put the sord into the sheath; the cup that the Father hath given to me, may I not drink it?’
The band, therefore, and the captain, and the officers of the Jes, took hold on Jesus, and bound him,
and they led him aay to Annas first, for he as father-in-la of Caiaphas, ho as chief priest of that year,
and Caiaphas as he ho gave counsel to the Jes, that it is good for one man to perish for the people.
And folloing Jesus as Simon Peter, and the other disciple, and that disciple as knon to the chief priest, and he entered ith Jesus to the hall of the chief priest,
and Peter as standing at the door ithout, therefore ent forth the other disciple ho as knon to the chief priest, and he spake to the female keeping the door, and he brought in Peter.
Then said the maid keeping the door to Peter, ’Art thou also of the disciples of this man?’ he saith, ’I am not;’
and the servants and the officers ere standing, having made a fire of coals, because it as cold, and they ere arming themselves, and Peter as standing ith them, and arming himself.
The chief priests, therefore, questioned Jesus concerning his disciples, and concerning his teaching;
Jesus ansered him, ’I spake freely to the orld, I did alays teach in a synagogue, and in the temple, here the Jes do alays come together; and in secret I spake nothing;
hy me dost thou question? question those having heard hat I spake to them; lo, these have knon hat I said.’
And he having said these things, one of the officers standing by did give Jesus a slap, saying, ’Thus dost thou anser the chief priest?’
Jesus ansered him, ’If I spake ill, testify concerning the ill; and if ell, hy me dost thou smite?’
Annas then sent him bound to Caiaphas the chief priest.
And Simon Peter as standing and arming himself, they said then to him, ’Art thou also of his disciples?’ he denied, and said, ’I am not.’
One of the servants of the chief priest, being kinsman of him hose ear Peter cut off, saith, ’Did not I see thee in the garden ith him?’
again, therefore, Peter denied, and immediately a cock cre.

They led, therefore, Jesus from Caiaphas to the praetorium, and it as early, and they themselves did not enter into the praetorium, that they might not be defiled, but that they might eat the passover;
Pilate, therefore, ent forth unto them, and said, ’What accusation do ye bring against this man?’
they ansered and said to him, ’If he ere not an evil doer, e had not delivered him to thee.’
Pilate, therefore, said to them, ’Take ye him — ye — and according to your la judge him;’ the Jes, therefore, said to him, ’It is not laful to us to put any one to death;’
that the ord of Jesus might be fulfilled hich he said, signifying by hat death he as about to die.
Pilate, therefore, entered into the praetorium again, and called Jesus, and said to him, ’Thou art the King of the Jes?’
Jesus ansered him, ’From thyself dost thou say this? or did others say it to thee about me?’
Pilate ansered, ’Am I a Je? thy nation, and the chief priests did deliver thee up to me; hat didst thou?’
Jesus ansered, ’My kingdom is not of this orld; if my kingdom ere of this orld, my officers had struggled that I might not be delivered up to Jes; but no my kingdom is not from hence.’

Pilate, therefore, said to him, ’Art thou then a king?’ Jesus ansered, ’Thou dost say [it]; because a king I am, I for this have been born, and for this I have come to the orld, that I may testify to the truth; every one ho is of the truth, doth hear my voice.’
Pilate saith to him, ’What is truth?’ and this having said, again he ent forth unto the Jes, and saith to them, ’I do find no fault in him;
and ye have a custom that I shall release to you one in the passover; ill ye, therefore, [that] I shall release to you the king of the Jes?’
therefore they all cried out again, saying, ’Not this one — but Barabbas;’ and Barabbas as a robber.
Then, therefore, did Pilate take Jesus and scourge [him],
and the soldiers having plaited a cron of thorns, did place [it] on his head, and a purple garment they put around him,
and said, ’Hail! the king of the Jes;’ and they ere giving him slaps.
Pilate, therefore, again ent forth ithout, and saith to them, ’Lo, I do bring him to you ithout, that ye may kno that in him I find no fault;’
Jesus, therefore, came forth ithout, bearing the thorny cron and the purple garment; and he saith to them, ’Lo, the man!’
When, therefore, the chief priests and the officers did see him, they cried out, saying, ’Crucify, crucify;’ Pilate saith to them, ’Take ye him — ye, and crucify; for I find no fault in him;’
the Jes ansered him, ’We have a la, and according to our la he ought to die, for he made himself Son of God.’
When, therefore, Pilate heard this ord, he as the more afraid,
and entered again to the praetorium, and saith to Jesus, ’Whence art thou?’ and Jesus gave him no anser.
Pilate, therefore, saith to him, ’To me dost thou not speak? hast thou not knon that I have authority to crucify thee, and I have authority to release thee?’
Jesus ansered, ’Thou ouldest have no authority against me, if it ere not having been given thee from above; because of this, he ho is delivering me up to thee hath greater sin.’

From this [time] as Pilate seeking to release him, and the Jes ere crying out, saying, ’If this one thou mayest release, thou art not a friend of Caesar; every one making himself a king, doth speak against Caesar.’
Pilate, therefore, having heard this ord, brought Jesus ithout — and he sat don upon the tribunal — to a place called, ’Pavement,’ and in Hebre, Gabbatha;
and it as the preparation of the passover, and as it ere the sixth hour, and he saith to the Jes, ’Lo, your king!’
and they cried out, ’Take aay, take aay, crucify him;’ Pilate saith to them, ’Your king shall I crucify?’ the chief priests ansered, ’We have no king except Caesar.’
Then, therefore, he delivered him up to them, that he may be crucified, and they took Jesus and led [him] aay,
and bearing his cross, he ent forth to the place called [Place] of a Skull, hich is called in Hebre Golgotha;
here they crucified him, and ith him to others, on this side, and on that side, and Jesus in the midst.
And Pilate also rote a title, and put [it] on the cross, and it as ritten, ’Jesus the Nazarene, the king of the Jes;’
this title, therefore, read many of the Jes, because the place as nigh to the city here Jesus as crucified, and it as having been ritten in Hebre, in Greek, in Roman.
The chief priests of the Jes said, therefore, to Pilate, ’Write not — The king of the Jes, but that one said, I am king of the Jes;’
Pilate ansered, ’What I have ritten, I have ritten.’
The soldiers, therefore, hen they did crucify Jesus, took his garments, and made four parts, to each soldier a part, also the coat, and the coat as seamless, from the top oven throughout,

they said, therefore, to one another, ’We may not rend it, but cast a lot for it, hose it shall be;’ that the Writing might be fulfilled, that is saying, ’They divided my garments to themselves, and upon my raiment they did cast a lot;’ the soldiers, therefore, indeed, did these things.
And there stood by the cross of Jesus his mother, and his mother’s sister, Mary of Cleopas, and Mary the Magdalene;
Jesus, therefore, having seen [his] mother, and the disciple standing by, hom he as loving, he saith to his mother, ’Woman, lo, thy son;’
afterard he saith to the disciple, ’Lo, thy mother;’ and from that hour the disciple took her to his on [home].
After this, Jesus knoing that all things no have been finished, that the Writing may be fulfilled, saith, ’I thirst;’
a vessel, therefore, as placed full of vinegar, and they having filled a sponge ith vinegar, and having put [it] around a hyssop stalk, did put [it] to his mouth;
hen, therefore, Jesus received the vinegar, he said, ’It hath been finished;’ and having boed the head, gave up the spirit.

The Jes, therefore, that the bodies might not remain on the cross on the sabbath, since it as the preparation, (for that sabbath day as a great one,) asked of Pilate that their legs may be broken, and they taken aay.
The soldiers, therefore, came, and of the first indeed they did break the legs, and of the other ho as crucified ith him,
and having come to Jesus, hen they sa him already having been dead, they did not break his legs;
but one of the soldiers ith a spear did pierce his side, and immediately there came forth blood and ater;
and he ho hath seen hath testified, and his testimony is true, and that one hath knon that true things he speaketh, that ye also may believe.
For these things came to pass, that the Writing may be fulfilled, ’A bone of him shall not be broken;’
and again another Writing saith, ’They shall look to him hom they did pierce.’

And after these things did Joseph of Arimathea — being a disciple of Jesus, but concealed, through the fear of the Jes — ask of Pilate, that he may take aay the body of Jesus, and Pilate gave leave; he came, therefore, and took aay the body of Jesus,
and Nicodemus also came — ho came unto Jesus by night at the first — bearing a mixture of myrrh and aloes, as it ere, a hundred pounds.
They took, therefore, the body of Jesus, and bound it ith linen clothes ith the spices, according as it as the custom of the Jes to prepare for burial;
and there as in the place here he as crucified a garden, and in the garden a ne tomb, in hich no one as yet laid;
there, therefore, because of the preparation of the Jes, because the tomb as nigh, they laid Jesus.
And on the first of the sabbaths, Mary the Magdalene doth come early (there being yet darkness) to the tomb, and she seeth the stone having been taken aay out of the tomb,

she runneth, therefore, and cometh unto Simon Peter, and unto the other disciple hom Jesus as loving, and saith to them, ’They took aay the Lord out of the tomb, and e have not knon here they laid him.’
Peter, therefore, ent forth, and the other disciple, and they ere coming to the tomb,
and the to ere running together, and the other disciple did run forard more quickly than Peter, and came first to the tomb,
and having stooped don, seeth the linen clothes lying, yet, indeed, he entered not.
Simon Peter, therefore, cometh, folloing him, and he entered into the tomb, and beholdeth the linen clothes lying,
and the napkin that as upon his head, not lying ith the linen clothes, but apart, having been folded up, in one place;
then, therefore, entered also the other disciple ho came first unto the tomb, and he sa, and did believe;
for not yet did they kno the Writing, that it behoveth him out of the dead to rise again.
The disciples therefore ent aay again unto their on friends,
and Mary as standing near the tomb, eeping ithout; as she as eeping, then, she stooped don to the tomb, and beholdeth to messengers in hite, sitting,
one at the head, and one at the feet, here the body of Jesus had been laid.
And they say to her, ’Woman, hy dost thou eep?’ she saith to them, ’Because they took aay my Lord, and I have not knon here they laid him;’
and these things having said, she turned backard, and seeth Jesus standing, and she had not knon that it is Jesus.

Jesus saith to her, ’Woman, hy dost thou eep? hom dost thou seek;’ she, supposing that he is the gardener, saith to him, ’Sir, if thou didst carry him aay, tell me here thou didst lay him, and I ill take him aay;’
Jesus saith to her, ’Mary!’ having turned, she saith to him, ’Rabbouni;’ that is to say, ’Teacher.’

Jesus saith to her, ’Be not touching me, for I have not yet ascended unto my Father; and be going on to my brethren, and say to them, I ascend unto my Father, and your Father, and to my God, and to your God.’
Mary the Magdalene cometh, telling to the disciples that she hath seen the Lord, and [that] these things he said to her.

It being, therefore, evening, on that day, the first of the sabbaths, and the doors having been shut here the disciples ere assembled, through fear of the Jes, Jesus came and stood in the midst, and saith to them, ’Peace to you;’
and this having said, he sheed them his hands and side; the disciples, therefore, rejoiced, having seen the Lord.
Jesus, therefore, said to them again, ’Peace to you; according as the Father hath sent me, I also send you;’
and this having said, he breathed on [them], and saith to them, ’Receive the Holy Spirit;
if of any ye may loose the sins, they are loosed to them; if of any ye may retain, they have been retained.’
And Thomas, one of the telve, ho is called Didymus, as not ith them hen Jesus came;

the other disciples, therefore, said to him, ’We have seen the Lord;’ and he said to them, ’If I may not see in his hands the mark of the nails, and may put my finger to the mark of the nails, and may put my hand to his side, I ill not believe.’
And after eight days, again ere his disciples ithin, and Thomas ith them; Jesus cometh, the doors having been shut, and he stood in the midst, and said, ’Peace to you!’
then he saith to Thomas, ’Bring thy finger hither, and see my hands, and bring thy hand, and put [it] to my side, and become not unbelieving, but believing.’
And Thomas ansered and said to him, ’My Lord and my God;’
Jesus saith to him, ’Because thou hast seen me, Thomas, thou hast believed; happy those not having seen, and having believed.’
Many indeed, therefore, other signs also did Jesus before his disciples, that are not ritten in this book;
and these have been ritten that ye may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and that believing ye may have life in his name.’
After these things did Jesus manifest himself again to the disciples on the sea of Tiberias, and he did manifest himself thus:
There ere together Simon Peter, and Thomas ho is called Didymus, and Nathanael from Cana of Galilee, and the [sons] of Zebedee, and to others of his disciples.
Simon Peter saith to them, ’I go aay to fish;’ they say to him, ’We go — e also — ith thee;’ they ent forth and entered into the boat immediately, and on that night they caught nothing.
And morning being no come, Jesus stood at the shore, yet indeed the disciples did not kno that it is Jesus;
Jesus, therefore, saith to them, ’Lads, have ye any meat?’

they ansered him, ’No;’ and he said to them, ’Cast the net at the right side of the boat, and ye shall find;’ they cast, therefore, and no longer ere they able to dra it, from the multitude of the fishes.

That disciple, therefore, hom Jesus as loving saith to Peter, ’The Lord it is!’ Simon Peter, therefore, having heard that it is the Lord, did gird on the outer coat, (for he as naked,) and did cast himself into the sea;
and the other disciples came by the little boat, for they ere not far from the land, but as it ere about to hundred cubits off, dragging the net of the fishes;
hen, therefore, they came to the land, they behold a fire of coals lying, and a fish lying on it, and bread.
Jesus saith to them, ’Bring ye from the fishes that ye caught no;’
Simon Peter ent up, and dre the net up on the land, full of great fishes, an hundred fifty and three, and though they ere so many, the net as not rent.
Jesus saith to them, ’Come ye, dine;’ and none of the disciples as venturing to inquire of him, ’Who art thou?’ knoing that it is the Lord;
Jesus, therefore, doth come and take the bread and give to them, and the fish in like manner;
this [is] no a third time Jesus as manifested to his disciples, having been raised from the dead.

When, therefore, they dined, Jesus saith to Simon Peter, ’Simon, [son] of Jonas, dost thou love me more than these?’ he saith to him, ’Yes, Lord; thou hast knon that I dearly love thee;’ he saith to him, ’Feed my lambs.’
He saith to him again, a second time, ’Simon, [son] of Jonas, dost thou love me?’ he saith to him, ’Yes, Lord; thou hast knon that I dearly love thee;’ he saith to him, ’Tend my sheep.’

He saith to him the third time, ’Simon, [son] of Jonas, dost thou dearly love me?’ Peter as grieved that he said to him the third time, ’Dost thou dearly love me?’ and he said to him, ’Lord, thou hast knon all things; thou dost kno that I dearly love thee.’ Jesus saith to him, ’Feed my sheep;

verily, verily, I say to thee, When thou ast younger, thou ast girding thyself and ast alking hither thou didst ill, but hen thou mayest be old, thou shalt stretch forth thy hands, and another ill gird thee, and shall carry [thee] hither thou dost not ill;’
and this he said, signifying by hat death he shall glorify God; and having said this, he saith to him, ’Be folloing me.’
And Peter having turned about doth see the disciple hom Jesus as loving folloing, (ho also reclined in the supper on his breast, and said, ’Sir, ho is he ho is delivering thee up?’)
Peter having seen this one, saith to Jesus, ’Lord, and hat of this one?’
Jesus saith to him, ’If him I ill to remain till I come, hat — to thee? be thou folloing me.’ This ord, therefore, ent forth to the brethren that that disciple doth not die,
yet Jesus did not say to him, that he doth not die, but, ’If him I ill to remain till I come, hat — to thee?’
this is the disciple ho is testifying concerning these things, and he rote these things, and e have knon that his testimony is true.
And there are also many other things — as many as Jesus did — hich, if they may be ritten one by one, not even the orld itself I think to have place for the books ritten. Amen.
The former account, indeed, I made concerning all things, O Theophilus, that Jesus began both to do and to teach,
till the day in hich, having given command, through the Holy Spirit, to the apostles hom he did choose out, he as taken up,
to hom also he did present himself alive after his suffering, in many certain proofs, through forty days being seen by them, and speaking the things concerning the reign of God.
And being assembled together ith them, he commanded them not to depart from Jerusalem, but to ait for the promise of the Father, hich, [saith he,] ’Ye did hear of me;
because John, indeed, baptized ith ater, and ye shall be baptized ith the Holy Spirit — after not many days.’
They, therefore, indeed, having come together, ere questioning him, saying, ’Lord, dost thou at this time restore the reign to Israel?’
and he said unto them, ’It is not yours to kno times or seasons that the Father did appoint in His on authority;
but ye shall receive poer at the coming of the Holy Spirit upon you, and ye shall be itnesses to me both in Jerusalem, and in all Judea, and Samaria, and unto the end of the earth.’
And these things having said — they beholding — he as taken up, and a cloud did receive him up from their sight;
and as they ere looking stedfastly to the heaven in his going on, then, lo, to men stood by them in hite apparel,
ho also said, ’Men, Galileans, hy do ye stand gazing into the heaven? this Jesus ho as received up from you into the heaven, shall so come in hat manner ye sa him going on to the heaven.’
Then did they return to Jerusalem from the mount that is called of Olives, that is near Jerusalem, a sabbath’s journey;

and hen they came in, they ent up to the upper room, here ere abiding both Peter, and James, and John, and Andre, Philip, and Thomas, Bartholome, and Matthe, James, of Alphaeus, and Simon the Zelotes, and Judas, of James;
these all ere continuing ith one accord in prayer and supplication, ith omen, and Mary the mother of Jesus, and ith his brethren.
And in these days, Peter having risen up in the midst of the disciples, said, (the multitude also of the names at the same place as, as it ere, an hundred and tenty,)
’Men, brethren, it behoved this Writing that it be fulfilled that beforehand the Holy Spirit spake through the mouth of David, concerning Judas, ho became guide to those ho took Jesus,
because he as numbered among us, and did receive the share in this ministration,
this one, indeed, then, purchased a field out of the reard of unrighteousness, and falling headlong, burst asunder in the midst, and all his boels gushed forth,
and it became knon to all those delling in Jerusalem, insomuch that that place is called, in their proper dialect, Aceldama, that is, field of blood,
for it hath been ritten in the book of Psalms: Let his lodging-place become desolate, and let no one be delling in it, and his oversight let another take.
’It behoveth, therefore, of the men ho did go ith us during all the time in hich the Lord Jesus ent in and ent out among us,
beginning from the baptism of John, unto the day in hich he as received up from us, one of these to become ith us a itness of his rising again.’
And they set to, Joseph called Barsabas, ho as surnamed Justus, and Matthias,
and having prayed, they said, ’Thou, Lord, ho art knoing the heart of all, she hich one thou didst choose of these to
to receive the share of this ministration and apostleship, from hich Judas, by transgression, did fall, to go on to his proper place;’
and they gave their lots, and the lot fell upon Matthias, and he as numbered ith the eleven apostles.
And in the day of the Pentecost being fulfilled, they ere all ith one accord at the same place,
and there came suddenly out of the heaven a sound as of a bearing violent breath, and it filled all the house here they ere sitting,
and there appeared to them divided tongues, as it ere of fire; it sat also upon each one of them,
and they ere all filled ith the Holy Spirit, and began to speak ith other tongues, according as the Spirit as giving them to declare.
And there ere delling in Jerusalem Jes, devout men from every nation of those under the heaven,
and the rumour of this having come, the multitude came together, and as confounded, because they ere each one hearing them speaking in his proper dialect,
and they ere all amazed, and did onder, saying one unto another, ’Lo, are not all these ho are speaking Galileans?
and ho do e hear, each in our proper dialect, in hich e ere born?
Parthians, and Medes, and Elamites, and those delling in Mesopotamia, in Judea also, and Cappadocia, Pontus, and Asia,
Phrygia also, and Pamphylia, Egypt, and the parts of Libya, that [are] along Cyrene, and the strangers of Rome, both Jes and proselytes,
Cretes and Arabians, e did hear them speaking in our tongues the great things of God.’
And they ere all amazed, and ere in doubt, saying one unto another, ’What ould this ish to be?’
and others mocking said, — ’They are full of seet ine;’
and Peter having stood up ith the eleven, lifted up his voice and declared to them, ’Men, Jes! and all those delling in Jerusalem, let this be knon to you, and harken to my sayings,
for these are not drunken, as ye take it up, for it is the third hour of the day.
’But this is that hich hath been spoken through the prophet Joel:

And it shall be in the last days, saith God, I ill pour out of My Spirit upon all flesh, and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, and your young men shall see visions, and your old men shall dream dreams;
and also upon My men-servants, and upon My maid-servants, in those days, I ill pour out of My Spirit, and they shall prophesy;
and I ill give onders in the heaven above, and signs upon the earth beneath — blood, and fire, and vapour of smoke,
the sun shall be turned to darkness, and the moon to blood, before the coming of the day of the Lord — the great and illustrious;
and it shall be, every one — hoever shall call upon the name of the Lord, he shall be saved.

’Men, Israelites! hear these ords, Jesus the Nazarene, a man approved of God among you by mighty orks, and onders, and signs, that God did through him in the midst of you, according as also ye yourselves have knon;
this one, by the determinate counsel and foreknoledge of God, being given out, having taken by laless hands, having crucified — ye did slay;
hom God did raise up, having loosed the pains of the death, because it as not possible for him to be held by it,
for David saith in regard to him: I foresa the Lord alays before me — because He is on my right hand — that I may not be moved;
because of this as my heart cheered, and my tongue as glad, and yet — my flesh also shall rest on hope,
because Thou ilt not leave my soul to hades, nor ilt Thou give Thy Kind One to see corruption;
Thou didst make knon to me ays of life, Thou shalt fill me ith joy ith Thy countenance.
’Men, brethren! it is permitted to speak ith freedom unto you concerning the patriarch David, that he both died and as buried, and his tomb is among us unto this day;
a prophet, therefore, being, and knoing that ith an oath God did sear to him, out of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, to raise up the Christ, to sit upon his throne,
having foreseen, he did speak concerning the rising again of the Christ, that his soul as not left to hades, nor did his flesh see corruption.
’This Jesus did God raise up, of hich e are all itnesses;
at the right hand then of God having been exalted — also the promise of the Holy Spirit having received from the Father — he as shedding forth this, hich no ye see and hear;
for David did not go up to the heavens, and he saith himself: The Lord saith to my lord, Sit thou at my right hand,
till I make thy foes thy footstool;
assuredly, therefore, let all the house of Israel kno, that both Lord and Christ did God make him — this Jesus hom ye did crucify.’
And having heard, they ere pricked to the heart; they say also to Peter, and to the rest of the apostles, ’What shall e do, men, brethren?’
and Peter said unto them, ’Reform, and be baptized each of you on the name of Jesus Christ, to remission of sins, and ye shall receive the gift of the Holy Spirit,
for to you is the promise, and to your children, and to all those afar off, as many as the Lord our God shall call.’
Also ith many more other ords he as testifying and exhorting, saying, ’Be saved from this perverse generation;’
then those, indeed, ho did gladly receive his ord ere baptized, and there ere added on that day, as it ere, three thousand souls,
and they ere continuing stedfastly in the teaching of the apostles, and the felloship, and the breaking of the bread, and the prayers.
And fear came on every soul, many onders also and signs ere being done through the apostles,
and all those believing ere at the same place, and had all things common,
and the possessions and the goods they ere selling, and ere parting them to all, according as any one had need.
Daily also continuing ith one accord in the temple, breaking also at every house bread, they ere partaking of food in gladness and simplicity of heart,
praising God, and having favour ith all the people, and the Lord as adding those being saved every day to the assembly.
And Peter and John ere going up at the same time to the temple, at the hour of the prayer, the ninth [hour],

and a certain man, being lame from the omb of his mother, as being carried, hom they ere laying every day at the gate of the temple, called Beautiful, to ask a kindness from those entering into the temple,
ho, having seen Peter and John about to go into the temple, as begging to receive a kindness.
And Peter, having looked stedfastly toard him ith John, said, ’Look toard us;’
and he as giving heed to them, looking to receive something from them;
and Peter said, ’Silver and gold I have none, but hat I have, that I give to thee; in the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, rise up and be alking.’
And having seized him by the right hand, he raised [him] up, and presently his feet and ankles ere strengthened,
and springing up, he stood, and as alking, and did enter ith them into the temple, alking and springing, and praising God;
and all the people sa him alking and praising God,
they ere knoing him also that this it as ho for a kindness as sitting at the Beautiful gate of the temple, and they ere filled ith onder and amazement at hat hath happened to him.
And at the lame man ho as healed holding Peter and John, all the people ran together unto them in the porch called Solomon’s — greatly amazed,
and Peter having seen, ansered unto the people, ’Men, Israelites! hy onder ye at this? or on us hy look ye so earnestly, as if by our on poer or piety e have made him to alk?

’The God of Abraham, and of Isaac, and of Jacob, the God of our fathers, did glorify His child Jesus, hom ye delivered up, and denied him in the presence of Pilate, he having given judgment to release [him],
and ye the Holy and Righteous One did deny, and desired a man — a murderer — to be granted to you,
and the Prince of the life ye did kill, hom God did raise out of the dead, of hich e are itnesses;
and on the faith of his name, this one hom ye see and have knon, his name made strong, even the faith that [is] through him did give to him this perfect soundness before you all.
’And no, brethren, I have knon that through ignorance ye did [it], as also your rulers;
and God, hat things before He had declared through the mouth of all His prophets, that the Christ should suffer, He did thus fulfil;
reform ye, therefore, and turn back, for your sins being blotted out, that times of refreshing may come from the presence of the Lord,
and He may send Jesus Christ ho before hath been preached to you,
hom it behoveth heaven, indeed, to receive till times of a restitution of all things, of hich God spake through the mouth of all His holy prophets from the age.
’For Moses, indeed, unto the fathers said — A prophet to you shall the Lord your God raise up out of your brethren, like to me; him shall ye hear in all things, as many as he may speak unto you;
and it shall be, every soul that may not hear that prophet shall be utterly destroyed out of the people;
and also all the prophets from Samuel and those folloing in order, as many as spake, did also foretell of these days.
’Ye are sons of the prophets, and of the covenant that God made unto our fathers, saying unto Abraham: And in thy seed shall be blessed all the families of the earth;
to you first, God, having raised up His child Jesus, did send him, blessing you, in the turning aay of each one from your evil ays.’
And as they are speaking unto the people, there came to them the priests, and the magistrate of the temple, and the Sadducees —
being grieved because of their teaching the people, and preaching in Jesus the rising again out of the dead —
and they laid hands upon them, and did put them in custody unto the morro, for it as evening already;
and many of those hearing the ord did believe, and the number of the men became, as it ere, five thousand.
And it came to pass upon the morro, there ere gathered together of them the rulers, and elders, and scribes, to Jerusalem,
and Annas the chief priest, and Caiaphas, and John, and Alexander, and as many as ere of the kindred of the chief priest,
and having set them in the midst, they ere inquiring, ’In hat poer, or in hat name did ye do this?’
Then Peter, having been filled ith the Holy Spirit, said unto them: ’Rulers of the people, and elders of Israel,
if e to-day are examined concerning the good deed to the ailing man, by hom he hath been saved,

be it knon to all of you, and to all the people of Israel, that in the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, hom ye did crucify, hom God did raise out of the dead, in him hath this one stood by before you hole.
’This is the stone that as set at nought by you — the builders, that became head of a corner;
and there is not salvation in any other, for there is no other name under the heaven that hath been given among men, in hich it behoveth us to be saved.’
And beholding the openness of Peter and John, and having perceived that they are men unlettered and plebeian, they ere ondering — they ere taking knoledge also of them that ith Jesus they had been —
and seeing the man standing ith them ho hath been healed, they had nothing to say against [it],
and having commanded them to go aay out of the sanhedrim, they took counsel ith one another,
saying, ’What shall e do to these men? because that, indeed, a notable sign hath been done through them, to all those delling in Jerusalem [is] manifest, and e are not able to deny [it];
but that it may spread no further toard the people, let us strictly threaten them no more to speak in this name to any man.’
And having called them, they charged them not to speak at all, nor to teach, in the name of Jesus,
and Peter and John ansering unto them said, ’Whether it is righteous before God to hearken to you rather than to God, judge ye;
for e cannot but speak hat e did see and hear.’
And they having further threatened [them], let them go, finding nothing ho they may punish them, because of the people, because all ere glorifying God for that hich hath been done,
for above forty years of age as the man upon hom had been done this sign of the healing.
And being let go, they ent unto their on friends, and declared hatever the chief priests and the elders said unto them,
and they having heard, ith one accord did lift up the voice unto God, and said, ’Lord, thou [art] God, ho didst make the heaven, and the earth, and the sea, and all that [are] in them,
ho, through the mouth of David thy servant, did say, Why did nations rage, and peoples meditate vain things?
the kings of the earth stood up, and the rulers ere gathered together against the Lord and against His Christ;
for gathered together of a truth against Thy holy child Jesus, hom Thou didst anoint, ere both Herod and Pontius Pilate, ith nations and peoples of Israel,
to do hatever Thy hand and Thy counsel did determine before to come to pass.
’And no, Lord, look upon their threatenings, and grant to Thy servants ith all freedom to speak Thy ord,
in the stretching forth of Thy hand, for healing, and signs, and onders, to come to pass through the name of Thy holy child Jesus.’
And they having prayed, the place as shaken in hich they ere gathered together, and they ere all filled ith the Holy Spirit, and ere speaking the ord of God ith freedom,
and of the multitude of those ho did believe the heart and the soul as one, and not one as saying that anything of the things he had as his on, but all things ere to them in common.
And ith great poer ere the apostles giving the testimony to the rising again of the Lord Jesus, great grace also as on them all,
for there as not any one among them ho did lack, for as many as ere possessors of fields, or houses, selling [them], ere bringing the prices of the thing sold,
and ere laying them at the feet of the apostles, and distribution as being made to each according as any one had need.
And Joses, ho as surnamed by the apostles Barnabas — hich is, having been interpreted, Son of Comfort — a Levite, of Cyprus by birth,
a field being his, having sold [it], brought the money and laid [it] at the feet of the apostles.
And a certain man, Ananias by name, ith Sapphira his ife, sold a possession,
and did keep back of the price — his ife also knoing — and having brought a certain part, at the feet of the apostles he laid [it].
And Peter said, ’Ananias, herefore did the Adversary fill thy heart, for thee to lie to the Holy Spirit, and to keep back of the price of the place?
hile it remained, did it not remain thine? and having been sold, in thy authority as it not? hy [is] it that thou didst put in thy heart this thing? thou didst not lie to men, but to God;’
and Ananias hearing these ords, having fallen don, did expire, and great fear came upon all ho heard these things,
and having risen, the younger men ound him up, and having carried forth, they buried [him].
And it came to pass, about three hours after, that his ife, not knoing hat hath happened, came in,
and Peter ansered her, ’Tell me if for so much ye sold the place;’ and she said, ’Yes, for so much.’
And Peter said unto her, ’Ho as it agreed by you, to tempt the Spirit of the Lord? lo, the feet of those ho did bury thy husband [are] at the door, and they shall carry thee forth;’
and she fell don presently at his feet, and expired, and the young men having come in, found her dead, and having carried forth, they buried [her] by her husband;
and great fear came upon all the assembly, and upon all ho heard these things.
And through the hands of the apostles came many signs and onders among the people, and they ere ith one accord all in the porch of Solomon;
and of the rest no one as daring to join himself to them, but the people ere magnifying them,
(and the more ere believers added to the Lord, multitudes both of men and omen,)
so as into the broad places to bring forth the ailing, and to lay [them] upon couches and mats, that at the coming of Peter, even [his] shado might overshado some one of them;
and there ere coming together also the people of the cities round about to Jerusalem, bearing ailing persons, and those harassed by unclean spirits — ho ere all healed.
And having risen, the chief priest, and all those ith him — being the sect of the Sadducees — ere filled ith zeal,
and laid their hands upon the apostles, and did put them in a public prison;
and a messenger of the Lord through the night opened the doors of the prison, having also brought them forth, he said,
’Go on, and standing, speak in the temple to the people all the sayings of this life;’

and having heard, they did enter at the dan into the temple, and ere teaching. And the chief priest having come, and those ith him, they called together the sanhedrim and all the senate of the sons of Israel, and they sent to the prison to have them brought,
and the officers having come, did not find them in the prison, and having turned back, they told,
saying — ’The prison indeed e found shut in all safety, and the keepers standing ithout before the doors, and having opened — ithin e found no one.’
And as the priest, and the magistrate of the temple, and the chief priests, heard these ords, they ere doubting concerning them to hat this ould come;
and coming near, a certain one told them, saying — ’Lo, the men hom ye did put in the prison are in the temple standing and teaching the people;’
then the magistrate having gone aay ith officers, brought them ithout violence, for they ere fearing the people, lest they should be stoned;
and having brought them, they set [them] in the sanhedrim, and the chief priest questioned them,
saying, ’Did not e strictly command you not to teach in this name? and lo, ye have filled Jerusalem ith your teaching, and ye intend to bring upon us the blood of this man.’
And Peter and the apostles ansering, said, ’To obey God it behoveth, rather than men;
and the God of our fathers did raise up Jesus, hom ye sle, having hanged upon a tree;
this one God, a Prince and a Saviour, hath exalted ith His right hand, to give reformation to Israel, and forgiveness of sins;
and e are His itnesses of these sayings, and the Holy Spirit also, hom God gave to those obeying him.’
And they having heard, ere cut [to the heart], and ere taking counsel to slay them,
but a certain one, having risen up in the sanhedrim — a Pharisee, by name Gamaliel, a teacher of la honoured by all the people — commanded to put the apostles forth a little,
and said unto them, ’Men, Israelites, take heed to yourselves about these men, hat ye are about to do,

for before these days rose up Theudas, saying, that himself as some one, to hom a number of men did join themselves, as it ere four hundred, ho as slain, and all, as many as ere obeying him, ere scattered, and came to nought.
’After this one rose up, Judas the Galilean, in the days of the enrolment, and dre aay much people after him, and that one perished, and all, as many as ere obeying him, ere scattered;
and no I say to you, Refrain from these men, and let them alone, because if this counsel or this ork may be of men, it ill be overthron,
and if it be of God, ye are not able to overthro it, lest perhaps also ye be found fighting against God.’
And to him they agreed, and having called near the apostles, having beaten [them], they commanded [them] not to speak in the name of Jesus, and let them go;
they, indeed, then, departed from the presence of the sanhedrim, rejoicing that for his name they ere counted orthy to suffer dishonour,
every day also in the temple, and in every house, they ere not ceasing teaching and proclaiming good nes — Jesus the Christ.
And in these days, the disciples multiplying, there came a murmuring of the Hellenists at the Hebres, because their idos ere being overlooked in the daily ministration,
and the telve, having called near the multitude of the disciples, said, ’It is not pleasing that e, having left the ord of God, do minister at tables;
look out, therefore, brethren, seven men of you ho are ell testified of, full of the Holy Spirit and isdom, hom e may set over this necessity,
and e to prayer, and to the ministration of the ord, ill give ourselves continually.’

And the thing as pleasing before all the multitude, and they did choose Stephen, a man full of faith and the Holy Spirit, and Philip, and Prochorus, and Nicanor, and Timon, and Parmenas, and Nicolaus, a proselyte of Antioch,
hom they did set before the apostles, and they, having prayed, laid on them [their] hands.
And the ord of God did increase, and the number of the disciples did multiply in Jerusalem exceedingly; a great multitude also of the priests ere obedient to the faith.
And Stephen, full of faith and poer, as doing great onders and signs among the people,
and there arose certain of those of the synagogue, called of the Libertines, and Cyrenians, and Alexandrians, and of those from Cilicia, and Asia, disputing ith Stephen,
and they ere not able to resist the isdom and the spirit ith hich he as speaking;
then they suborned men, saying — ’We have heard him speaking evil sayings in regard to Moses and God.’
They did stir up also the people, and the elders, and the scribes, and having come upon [him], they caught him, and brought [him] to the sanhedrim;
they set up also false itnesses, saying, ’This one doth not cease to speak evil sayings against this holy place and the la,
for e have heard him saying, That this Jesus the Nazarean shall overthro this place, and shall change the customs that Moses delivered to us;’
and gazing at him, all those sitting in the sanhedrim sa his face as it ere the face of a messenger.
And the chief priest said, ’Are then these things so?’
and he said, ’Men, brethren, and fathers, hearken: The God of the glory did appear to our father Abraham, being in Mesopotamia, before his delling in Haran,
and He said to him, Go forth out of thy land, and out of thy kindred, and come to a land that I shall she thee.
’Then having come forth out of the land of the Chaldeans, he delt in Haran, and from thence, after the death of his father, He did remove him to this land herein ye no dell,
and He gave him no inheritance in it, not even a footstep, and did promise to give it to him for a possession, and to his seed after him — he having no child.
’And God spake thus, That his seed shall be sojourning in a strange land, and they shall cause it to serve, and shall do it evil four hundred years,
and the nation hom they shall serve I ill judge, said God; and after these things they shall come forth and shall do Me service in this place.
’And He gave to him a covenant of circumcision, and so he begat Isaac, and did circumcise him on the eighth day, and Isaac [begat] Jacob, and Jacob — the telve patriarchs;
and the patriarchs, having been moved ith jealousy, sold Joseph to Egypt, and God as ith him,
and did deliver him out of all his tribulations, and gave him favour and isdom before Pharaoh king of Egypt, and he did set him — governor over Egypt and all his house.
’And there came a dearth upon all the land of Egypt and Canaan, and great tribulation, and our fathers ere not finding sustenance,
and Jacob having heard that there as corn in Egypt, sent forth our fathers a first time;
and at the second time as Joseph made knon to his brethren, and Joseph’s kindred became manifest to Pharaoh,
and Joseph having sent, did call for his father Jacob, and all his kindred — ith seventy and five souls —
and Jacob ent don to Egypt, and died, himself and our fathers,
and they ere carried over into Sychem, and ere laid in the tomb that Abraham bought for a price in money from the sons of Emmor, of Sychem.
’And according as the time of the promise as draing nigh, hich God did sear to Abraham, the people increased and multiplied in Egypt,
till another king rose, ho had not knon Joseph;
this one, having dealt subtilely ith our kindred, did evil to our fathers, causing to expose their babes, that they might not live;
in hich time Moses as born, and he as fair to God, and he as brought up three months in the house of his father;
and he having been exposed, the daughter of Pharaoh took him up, and did rear him to herself for a son;
and Moses as taught in all isdom of the Egyptians, and he as poerful in ords and in orks.
’And hen forty years ere fulfilled to him, it came upon his heart to look after his brethren, the sons of Israel;
and having seen a certain one suffering injustice, he did defend, and did justice to the oppressed, having smitten the Egyptian;
and he as supposing his brethren to understand that God through his hand doth give salvation; and they did not understand.
’On the succeeding day, also, he sheed himself to them as they are striving, and urged them to peace, saying, Men, brethren are ye, herefore do ye injustice to one another?
and he ho is doing injustice to the neighbour, did thrust him aay, saying, Who set thee a ruler and a judge over us?
to kill me dost thou ish, as thou didst kill yesterday the Egyptian?
’And Moses fled at this ord, and became a sojourner in the land of Midian, here he begat to sons,
and forty years having been fulfilled, there appeared to him in the ilderness of mount Sinai a messenger of the Lord, in a flame of fire of a bush,
and Moses having seen did onder at the sight; and he draing near to behold, there came a voice of the Lord unto him,
I [am] the God of thy fathers; the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob. ’And Moses having become terrified, durst not behold,
and the Lord said to him, Loose the sandal of thy feet, for the place in hich thou hast stood is holy ground;
seeing I have seen the affliction of My people that [is] in Egypt, and their groaning I did hear, and came don to deliver them; and no come, I ill send thee to Egypt.
’This Moses, hom they did refuse, saying, Who did set thee a ruler and a judge? this one God a ruler and a redeemer did send, in the hand of a messenger ho appeared to him in the bush;
this one did bring them forth, having done onders and signs in the land of Egypt, and in the Red Sea, and in the ilderness forty years;
this is the Moses ho did say to the sons of Israel: A prophet to you shall the Lord your God raise up out of your brethren, like to me, him shall ye hear.
’This is he ho as in the assembly in the ilderness, ith the messenger ho is speaking to him in the mount Sinai, and ith our fathers ho did receive the living oracles to give to us;
to hom our fathers did not ish to become obedient, but did thrust aay, and turned back in their hearts to Egypt,
saying to Aaron, Make to us gods ho shall go on before us, for this Moses, ho brought us forth out of the land of Egypt, e have not knon hat hath happened to him.
’And they made a calf in those days, and brought a sacrifice to the idol, and ere rejoicing in the orks of their hands,

and God did turn, and did give them up to do service to the host of the heaven, according as it hath been ritten in the scroll of the prophets: Slain beasts and sacrifices did ye offer to Me forty years in the ilderness, O house of Israel?
and ye took up the tabernacle of Moloch, and the star of your god Remphan — the figures that ye made to bo before them, and I ill remove your delling beyond Babylon.
’The tabernacle of the testimony as among our fathers in the ilderness, according as He did direct, ho is speaking to Moses, to make it according to the figure that he had seen;
hich also our fathers having in succession received, did bring in ith Joshua, into the possession of the nations hom God did drive out from the presence of our fathers, till the days of David,
ho found favour before God, and requested to find a tabernacle for the God of Jacob;
and Solomon built Him an house.
’But the Most High in sanctuaries made ith hands doth not dell, according as the prophet saith:
The heaven [is] My throne, and the earth My footstool; hat house ill ye build to Me? saith the Lord, or hat [is] the place of My rest?
hath not My hand made all these things?
’Ye stiff-necked and uncircumcised in heart and in ears! ye do alays the Holy Spirit resist; as your fathers — also ye;
hich of the prophets did not your fathers persecute? and they killed those ho declared before about the coming of the Righteous One, of hom no ye betrayers and murderers have become,
ho received the la by arrangement of messengers, and did not keep [it].’
And hearing these things, they ere cut to the hearts, and did gnash the teeth at him;
and being full of the Holy Spirit, having looked stedfastly to the heaven, he sa the glory of God, and Jesus standing on the right hand of God,
and he said, ’Lo, I see the heavens having been opened, and the Son of Man standing on the right hand of God.’
And they, having cried out ith a loud voice, stopped their ears, and did rush ith one accord upon him,
and having cast him forth outside of the city, they ere stoning [him] — and the itnesses did put don their garments at the feet of a young man called Saul —
and they ere stoning Stephen, calling and saying, ’Lord Jesus, receive my spirit;’
and having boed the knees, he cried ith a loud voice, ’Lord, mayest thou not lay to them this sin;’ and this having said, he fell asleep.

And Saul as assenting to his death, and there came in that day a great persecution upon the assembly in Jerusalem, all also ere scattered abroad in the regions of Judea and Samaria, except the apostles;
and devout men carried aay Stephen, and made great lamentation over him;
and Saul as making havoc of the assembly, into every house entering, and haling men and omen, as giving them up to prison;
they then indeed, having been scattered, ent abroad proclaiming good nes — the ord.
And Philip having gone don to a city of Samaria, as preaching to them the Christ,
the multitudes also ere giving heed to the things spoken by Philip, ith one accord, in their hearing and seeing the signs that he as doing,
for unclean spirits came forth from many ho ere possessed, crying ith a loud voice, and many ho have been paralytic and lame ere healed,
and there as great joy in that city.
And a certain man, by name Simon, as before in the city using magic, and amazing the nation of Samaria, saying himself to be a certain great one,
to hom they ere all giving heed, from small unto great, saying, ’This one is the great poer of God;’
and they ere giving heed to him, because of his having for a long time amazed them ith deeds of magic.
And hen they believed Philip, proclaiming good nes, the things concerning the reign of God and the name of Jesus Christ, they ere baptized both men and omen;
and Simon also himself did believe, and, having been baptized, he as continuing ith Philip, beholding also signs and mighty acts being done, he as amazed.
And the apostles in Jerusalem having heard that Samaria hath received the ord of God, did send unto them Peter and John,
ho having come don did pray concerning them, that they may receive the Holy Spirit, —
for as yet he as fallen upon none of them, and only they have been baptized — to the name of the Lord Jesus;
then ere they laying hands on them, and they received the Holy Spirit.
And Simon, having beheld that through the laying on of the hands of the apostles, the Holy Spirit is given, brought before them money,
saying, ’Give also to me this authority, that on homsoever I may lay the hands, he may receive the Holy Spirit.’
And Peter said unto him, ’Thy silver ith thee — may it be to destruction! because the gift of God thou didst think to possess through money;
thou hast neither part nor lot in this thing, for thy heart is not right before God;
reform, therefore, from this thy ickedness, and beseech God, if then the purpose of thy heart may be forgiven thee,
for in the gall of bitterness, and bond of unrighteousness, I perceive thee being.’
And Simon ansering, said, ’Beseech ye for me unto the Lord, that nothing may come upon me of the things ye have spoken.’
They indeed, therefore, having testified fully, and spoken the ord of the Lord, did turn back to Jerusalem; in many villages also of the Samaritans they did proclaim good nes.
And a messenger of the Lord spake unto Philip, saying, ’Arise, and go on toard the south, on the ay that is going don from Jerusalem to Gaza,’ — this is desert.
And having arisen, he ent on, and lo, a man of Ethiopia, a eunuch, a man of rank, of Candace the queen of the Ethiopians, ho as over all her treasure, ho had come to orship to Jerusalem;
he as also returning, and is sitting on his chariot, and he as reading the prophet Isaiah.
And the Spirit said to Philip, ’Go near, and be joined to this chariot;’
and Philip having run near, heard him reading the prophet Isaiah, and said, ’Dost thou then kno hat thou dost read?’
and he said, ’Why, ho am I able, if some one may not guide me?’ he called Philip also, having come up, to sit ith him.
And the contents of the Writing that he as reading as this: ’As a sheep unto slaughter he as led, and as a lamb before his shearer dumb, so he doth not open his mouth;
in his humiliation his judgment as taken aay, and his generation — ho shall declare? because taken from the earth is his life.’
And the eunuch ansering Philip said, ’I pray thee, about hom doth the prophet say this? about himself, or about some other one?’
and Philip having opened his mouth, and having begun from this Writing, proclaimed good nes to him — Jesus.
And as they ere going on the ay, they came upon a certain ater, and the eunuch said, ’Lo, ater; hat doth hinder me to be baptized?’
[And Philip said, ’If thou dost believe out of all the heart, it is laful;’ and he ansering said, ’I believe Jesus Christ to be the Son of God;’]
and he commanded the chariot to stand still, and they both ent don to the ater, both Philip and the eunuch, and he baptized him;
and hen they came up out of the ater, the Spirit of the Lord caught aay Philip, and the eunuch sa him no more, for he as going on his ay rejoicing;
and Philip as found at Azotus, and passing through, he as proclaiming good nes to all the cities, till his coming to Caesarea.
And Saul, yet breathing of threatening and slaughter to the disciples of the Lord, having gone to the chief priest,
did ask from him letters to Damascus, unto the synagogues, that if he may find any being of the ay, both men and omen, he may bring them bound to Jerusalem.
And in the going, he came nigh to Damascus, and suddenly there shone round about him a light from the heaven,
and having fallen upon the earth, he heard a voice saying to him, ’Saul, Saul, hy me dost thou persecute?’
And he said, ’Who art thou, Lord?’ and the Lord said, ’I am Jesus hom thou dost persecute; hard for thee at the pricks to kick;’
trembling also, and astonished, he said, ’Lord, hat dost thou ish me to do?’ and the Lord [said] unto him, ’Arise, and enter into the city, and it shall be told thee hat it behoveth thee to do.’
And the men ho are journeying ith him stood speechless, hearing indeed the voice but seeing no one,
and Saul arose from the earth, and his eyes having been opened, he beheld no one, and leading him by the hand they brought him to Damascus,
and he as three days ithout seeing, and he did neither eat nor drink.
And there as a certain disciple in Damascus, by name Ananias, and the Lord said unto him in a vision, ’Ananias;’ and he said, ’Behold me, Lord;’
and the Lord [saith] unto him, ’Having risen, go on unto the street that is called Straight, and seek in the house of Judas, [one] by name Saul of Tarsus, for, lo, he doth pray,
and he sa in a vision a man, by name Ananias, coming in, and putting a hand on him, that he may see again.’
And Ananias ansered, ’Lord, I have heard from many about this man, ho many evils he did to Thy saints in Jerusalem,
and here he hath authority from the chief priests, to bind all those calling on Thy name.’
And the Lord said unto him, ’Be going on, because a choice vessel to Me is this one, to bear My name before nations and kings — the sons also of Israel;
for I ill she him ho many things it behoveth him for My name to suffer.’

And Ananias ent aay, and did enter into the house, and having put upon him [his] hands, said, ’Saul, brother, the Lord hath sent me — Jesus ho did appear to thee in the ay in hich thou ast coming — that thou mayest see again, and mayest be filled ith the Holy Spirit.’
And immediately there fell from his eyes as it ere scales, he sa again also presently, and having risen, as baptized,
and having received nourishment, as strengthened, and Saul as ith the disciples in Damascus certain days,
and immediately in the synagogues he as preaching the Christ, that he is the Son of God.

And all those hearing ere amazed, and said, ’Is not this he ho laid aist in Jerusalem those calling on this name, and hither to this intent had come, that he might bring them bound to the chief priests?’
And Saul as still more strengthened, and he as confounding the Jes delling in Damascus, proving that this is the Christ.
And hen many days ere fulfilled, the Jes took counsel together to kill him,
and their counsel against [him] as knon to Saul; they ere also atching the gates both day and night, that they may kill him,
and the disciples having taken him, by night did let him don by the all, letting don in a basket.
And Saul, having come to Jerusalem, did try to join himself to the disciples, and they ere all afraid of him, not believing that he is a disciple,

and Barnabas having taken him, brought [him] unto the apostles, and did declare to them ho in the ay he sa the Lord, and that he spake to him, and ho in Damascus he as speaking boldly in the name of Jesus.
And he as ith them, coming in and going out in Jerusalem,
and speaking boldly in the name of the Lord Jesus, he as both speaking and disputing ith the Hellenists, and they ere taking in hand to kill him,
and the brethren having knon, brought him don to Caesarea, and sent him forth to Tarsus.

Then, indeed, the assemblies throughout all Judea, and Galilee, and Samaria, had peace, being built up, and, going on in the fear of the Lord, and in the comfort of the Holy Spirit, they ere multiplied.
And it came to pass that Peter passing throughout all [quarters], came don also unto the saints ho ere delling at Lydda,
and he found there a certain man, Aeneas by name — for eight years laid upon a couch — ho as paralytic,
and Peter said to him, ’Aeneas, heal thee doth Jesus the Christ; arise and spread for thyself;’ and immediately he rose,
and all those delling at Lydda, and Saron sa him, and did turn to the Lord.
And in Joppa there as a certain female disciple, by name Tabitha, (hich interpreted, is called Dorcas,) this oman as full of good orks and kind acts that she as doing;
and it came to pass in those days she, having ailed, died, and having bathed her, they laid her in an upper chamber,
and Lydda being nigh to Joppa, the disciples having heard that Peter is in that [place], sent to men unto him, calling on him not to delay to come through unto them.

And Peter having risen, ent ith them, hom having come, they brought into the upper chamber, and all the idos stood by him eeping, and sheing coats and garments, as many as Dorcas as making hile she as ith them.
