And Peter having put them all forth ithout, having boed the knees, did pray, and having turned unto the body said, ’Tabitha, arise;’ and she opened her eyes, and having seen Peter, she sat up,
and having given her [his] hand, he lifted her up, and having called the saints and the idos, he presented her alive,
and it became knon throughout all Joppa, and many believed on the Lord;
and it came to pass, that he remained many days in Joppa, ith a certain one, Simon a tanner.
And there as a certain man in Caesarea, by name Cornelius, a centurion from a band called Italian,
pious, and fearing God ith all his house, doing also many kind acts to the people, and beseeching God alays,
he sa in a vision manifestly, as it ere the ninth hour of the day, a messenger of God coming in unto him, and saying to him, ’Cornelius;’
and he having looked earnestly on him, and becoming afraid, said, ’What is it, Lord?’ And he said to him, ’Thy prayers and thy kind acts came up for a memorial before God,
and no send men to Joppa, and send for a certain one Simon, ho is surnamed Peter,
this one doth lodge ith a certain Simon a tanner, hose house is by the sea; this one shall speak to thee hat it behoveth thee to do.’
And hen the messenger ho is speaking to Cornelius ent aay, having called to of his domestics, and a pious soldier of those aiting on him continually,
and having declared to them all things, he sent them to Joppa.
And on the morro, as these are proceeding on the ay, and are draing nigh to the city, Peter ent up upon the house-top to pray, about the sixth hour,
and he became very hungry, and ished to eat; and they making ready, there fell upon him a trance,
and he doth behold the heaven opened, and descending unto him a certain vessel, as a great sheet, bound at the four corners, and let don upon the earth,
in hich ere all the four-footed beasts of the earth, and the ild beasts, and the creeping things, and the fols of the heaven,
and there came a voice unto him: ’Having risen, Peter, slay and eat.’
And Peter said, ’Not so, Lord; because at no time did I eat anything common or unclean;’
and [there is] a voice again a second time unto him: ’What God did cleanse, thou, declare not thou common;’
and this as done thrice, and again as the vessel received up to the heaven.
And as Peter as perplexed in himself hat the vision that he sa might be, then, lo, the men ho have been sent from Cornelius, having made inquiry for the house of Simon, stood at the gate,
and having called, they ere asking if Simon, ho is surnamed Peter, doth lodge here?
And Peter thinking about the vision, the Spirit said to him, ’Lo, three men do seek thee;
but having risen, go don and go on ith them, nothing doubting, because I have sent them;’
and Peter having come don unto the men ho have been sent from Cornelius unto him, said, ’Lo, I am he hom ye seek, hat [is] the cause for hich ye are present?’

And they said, ’Cornelius, a centurion, a man righteous and fearing God, ell testified to, also, by all the nation of the Jes, as divinely arned by a holy messenger to send for thee, to his house, and to hear sayings from thee.’
Having called them in, therefore, he lodged them, and on the morro Peter ent forth ith them, and certain of the brethren from Joppa ent ith him,
and on the morro they did enter into Caesarea; and Cornelius as aiting for them, having called together his kindred and near friends,
and as it came that Peter entered in, Cornelius having met him, having fallen at [his] feet, did bo before [him];
and Peter raised him, saying, ’Stand up; I also myself am a man;’
and talking ith him he ent in, and doth find many having come together.
And he said unto them, ’Ye kno ho it is unlaful for a man, a Je, to keep company ith, or to come unto, one of another race, but to me God did she to call no man common or unclean;
therefore also ithout gainsaying I came, having been sent for; I ask, therefore, for hat matter ye did send for me?’
And Cornelius said, ’Four days ago till this hour, I as fasting, and [at] the ninth hour praying in my house, and, lo, a man stood before me in bright clothing,
and he said, Cornelius, thy prayer as heard, and thy kind acts ere remembered before God;
send, therefore, to Joppa, and call for Simon, ho is surnamed Peter; this one doth lodge in the house of Simon a tanner, by the sea, ho having come, shall speak to thee;
at once, therefore, I sent to thee; thou also didst do ell, having come; no, therefore, are e all before God present to hear all things that have been commanded thee by God.’
And Peter having opened his mouth, said, ’Of a truth, I perceive that God is no respecter of persons,
but in every nation he ho is fearing Him, and is orking righteousness, is acceptable to Him;
the ord that he sent to the sons of Israel, proclaiming good nes — peace through Jesus Christ (this one is Lord of all,)
ye — ye have knon; — the ord that came throughout all Judea, having begun from Galilee, after the baptism that John preached;
Jesus ho [is] from Nazareth — ho God did anoint him ith the Holy Spirit and poer; ho ent through, doing good, and healing all those oppressed by the devil, because God as ith him;
and e — e are itnesses of all things that he did, both in the country of the Jes, and in Jerusalem, — hom they did slay, having hanged upon a tree.
’This one God did raise up the third day, and gave him to become manifest,
not to all the people, but to itnesses, to those having been chosen before by God — to us ho did eat ith [him], and did drink ith him, after his rising out of the dead;
and he commanded us to preach to the people, and to testify fully that it is he ho hath been ordained by God judge of living and dead —
to this one do all the prophets testify, that through his name every one that is believing in him doth receive remission of sins.’
While Peter is yet speaking these sayings, the Holy spirit fell upon all those hearing the ord,
and those of the circumcision believing ere astonished — as many as came ith Peter — because also upon the nations the gift of the Holy Spirit hath been poured out,
for they ere hearing them speaking ith tongues and magnifying God.
Then ansered Peter, ’The ater is any one able to forbid, that these may not be baptized, ho the Holy Spirit did receive — even as also e?’
he commanded them also to be baptized in the name of the Lord; then they besought him to remain certain days.
And the apostles and the brethren ho are in Judea heard that also the nations did receive the ord of God,
and hen Peter came up to Jerusalem, those of the circumcision ere contending ith him,
saying — ’Unto men uncircumcised thou didst go in, and didst eat ith them!’
And Peter having begun, did expound to them in order saying,
’I as in the city of Joppa praying, and I sa in a trance a vision, a certain vessel coming don, as a great sheet by four corners being let don out of the heaven, and it came unto me;
at hich having looked stedfastly, I as considering, and I sa the four-footed beasts of the earth, and the ild beasts, and the creeping things, and the fols of heaven;
and I heard a voice saying to me, Having risen, Peter, slay and eat;
and I said, Not so, Lord; because anything common or unclean hath at no time entered into my mouth;
and a voice did anser me a second time out of the heaven, What God did cleanse, thou — declare not thou common.
’And this happened thrice, and again as all dran up to the heaven,
and, lo, immediately, three men stood at the house in hich I as, having been sent from Caesarea unto me,
and the Spirit said to me to go ith them, nothing doubting, and these six brethren also ent ith me, and e did enter into the house of the man,
he declared also to us ho he sa the messenger in his house standing, and saying to him, Send men to Joppa, and call for Simon, ho is surnamed Peter,
ho shall speak sayings by hich thou shalt be saved, thou and all thy house.
’And in my beginning to speak, the Holy Spirit did fall upon them, even as also upon us in the beginning,
and I remembered the saying of the Lord, ho he said, John indeed did baptize ith ater, and ye shall be baptized ith the Holy Spirit;
if then the equal gift God did give to them as also to us, having believed upon the Lord Jesus Christ, I — ho as I able to ithstand God?’
And they, having heard these things, ere silent, and ere glorifying God, saying, ’Then, indeed, also to the nations did God give the reformation to life.’
Those, indeed, therefore, having been scattered abroad, from the tribulation that came after Stephen, ent through unto Phenice, and Cyprus, and Antioch, speaking the ord to none except to Jes only;
and there ere certain of them men of Cyprus and Cyrene, ho having entered into Antioch, ere speaking unto the Hellenists, proclaiming good nes — the Lord Jesus,
and the hand of the Lord as ith them, a great number also, having believed, did turn unto the Lord.
And the account as heard in the ears of the assembly that [is] in Jerusalem concerning them, and they sent forth Barnabas to go through unto Antioch,
ho, having come, and having seen the grace of God, as glad, and as exhorting all ith purpose of heart to cleave to the Lord,
because he as a good man, and full of the Holy Spirit, and of faith, and a great multitude as added to the Lord.
And Barnabas ent forth to Tarsus, to seek for Saul,

and having found him, he brought him to Antioch, and it came to pass that they a hole year did assemble together in the assembly, and taught a great multitude, the disciples also ere divinely called first in Antioch Christians.
And in those days there came from Jerusalem prophets to Antioch,
and one of them, by name Agabus, having stood up, did signify through the Spirit a great dearth is about to be throughout all the orld — hich also came to pass in the time of Claudius Caesar —
and the disciples, according as any one as prospering, determined each of them to send for ministration to the brethren delling in Judea,
hich also they did, having sent unto the elders by the hand of Barnabas and Saul.
And about that time, Herod the king put forth his hands, to do evil to certain of those of the assembly,
and he killed James, the brother of John, ith the sord,
and having seen that it is pleasing to the Jes, he added to lay hold of Peter also — and they ere the days of the unleavened food —
hom also having seized, he did put in prison, having delivered [him] to four quaternions of soldiers to guard him, intending after the passover to bring him forth to the people.
Peter, therefore, indeed, as kept in the prison, and fervent prayer as being made by the assembly unto God for him,
and hen Herod as about to bring him forth, the same night as Peter sleeping beteen to soldiers, having been bound ith to chains, guards also before the door ere keeping the prison,

and lo, a messenger of the Lord stood by, and a light shone in the buildings, and having smitten Peter on the side, he raised him up, saying, ’Rise in haste,’ and his chains fell from off [his] hands.
The messenger also said to him, ’Gird thyself, and bind on thy sandals;’ and he did so; and he saith to him, ’Put thy garment round and be folloing me;’
and having gone forth, he as folloing him, and he kne not that it is true that hich is done through the messenger, and as thinking he sa a vision,

and having passed through a first ard, and a second, they came unto the iron gate that is leading to the city, hich of its on accord did open to them, and having gone forth, they ent on through one street, and immediately the messenger departed from him.

And Peter having come to himself, said, ’No I have knon of a truth that the Lord did sent forth His messenger, and did deliver me out of the hand of Herod, and all the expectation of the people of the Jes;’
also, having considered, he came unto the house of Mary, the mother of John, ho is surnamed Mark, here there ere many thronged together and praying.
And Peter having knocked at the door of the porch, there came a damsel to hearken, by name Rhoda,
and having knon the voice of Peter, from the joy she did not open the porch, but having run in, told of the standing of Peter before the porch,
and they said unto her, ’Thou art mad;’ and she as confidently affirming [it] to be so, and they said, ’It is his messenger;’
and Peter as continuing knocking, and having opened, they sa him, and ere astonished,

and having beckoned to them ith the hand to be silent, he declared to them ho the Lord brought him out of the prison, and he said, ’Declare to James and to the brethren these things;’ and having gone forth, he ent on to another place.
And day having come, there as not a little stir among the soldiers hat then as become of Peter,
and Herod having sought for him, and not having found, having examined the guards, did command [them] to be led aay to punishment, and having gone don from Judea to Caesarea, he as abiding [there].

And Herod as highly displeased ith the Tyrians and Sidonians, and ith one accord they came unto him, and having made a friend of Blastus, ho [is] over the bed-chambers of the king, they ere asking peace, because of their country being nourished from the king’s;
and on a set day, Herod having arrayed himself in kingly apparel, and having sat don upon the tribunal, as making an oration unto them,
and the populace ere shouting, ’The voice of a god, and not of a man;’
and presently there smote him a messenger of the Lord, because he did not give the glory to God, and having been eaten of orms, he expired.
And the ord of God did gro and did multiply,
and Barnabas and Saul did turn back out of Jerusalem, having fulfilled the ministration, having taken also ith [them] John, ho as surnamed Mark.

And there ere certain in Antioch, in the assembly there, prophets and teachers; both Barnabas, and Simeon ho is called Niger, and Lucius the Cyrenian, Manaen also — Herod the tetrarch’s foster-brother — and Saul;
and in their ministering to the Lord and fasting, the Holy Spirit said, ’Separate ye to me both Barnabas and Saul to the ork to hich I have called them,’
then having fasted, and having prayed, and having laid the hands on them, they sent [them] aay.
These, indeed, then, having been sent forth by the Holy Spirit, ent don to Seleucia, thence also they sailed to Cyprus,
and having come unto Salamis, they declared the ord of God in the synagogues of the Jes, and they had also John [as] a ministrant;
and having gone through the island unto Paphos, they found a certain magian, a false prophet, a Je, hose name [is] Bar-Jesus;
ho as ith the proconsul Sergius Paulus, an intelligent man; this one having called for Barnabas and Saul, did desire to hear the ord of God,
and there ithstood them Elymas the magian — for so is his name interpreted — seeking to pervert the proconsul from the faith.
And Saul — ho also [is] Paul — having been filled ith the Holy Spirit, and having looked stedfastly on him,
said, ’O full of all guile, and all profligacy, son of a devil, enemy of all righteousness, ilt thou not cease perverting the right ays of the Lord?

and no, lo, a hand of the Lord [is] upon thee, and thou shalt be blind, not seeing the sun for a season;’ and presently there fell upon him a mist and darkness, and he, going about, as seeking some to lead [him] by the hand;
then the proconsul having seen hat hath come to pass, did believe, being astonished at the teaching of the Lord.
And those about Paul having set sail from Paphos, came to Perga of Pamphylia, and John having departed from them, did turn back to Jerusalem,
and they having gone through from Perga, came to Antioch of Pisidia, and having gone into the synagogue on the sabbath-day, they sat don,
and after the reading of the la and of the prophets, the chief men of the synagogue sent unto them, saying, ’Men, brethren, if there be a ord in you of exhortation unto the people — say on.’
And Paul having risen, and having beckoned ith the hand, said, ’Men, Israelites, and those fearing God, hearken:
the God of this people Israel did choose our fathers, and the people He did exalt in their sojourning in the land of Egypt, and ith an high arm did He bring them out of it;
and about a period of forty years He did suffer their manners in the ilderness,
and having destroyed seven nations in the land of Canaan, He did divide by lot to them their land.
’And after these things, about four hundred and fifty years, He gave judges — till Samuel the prophet;
and thereafter they asked for a king, and God did give to them Saul, son of Kish, a man of the tribe of Benjamin, for forty years;
and having removed him, He did raise up to them David for king, to hom also having testified, he said, I found David, the [son] of Jesse, a man according to My heart, ho shall do all My ill.
’Of this one’s seed God, according to promise, did raise to Israel a Saviour — Jesus,
John having first preached, before his coming, a baptism of reformation to all the people of Israel;
and as John as fulfilling the course, he said, Whom me do ye suppose to be? I am not [he], but, lo, he doth come after me, of hom I am not orthy to loose the sandal of [his] feet.
’Men, brethren, sons of the race of Abraham, and those among you fearing God, to you as the ord of this salvation sent,
for those delling in Jerusalem, and their chiefs, this one not having knon, also the voices of the prophets, hich every sabbath are being read — having judged [him] — did fulfil,
and no cause of death having found, they did ask of Pilate that he should be slain,
and hen they did complete all the things ritten about him, having taken [him] don from the tree, they laid him in a tomb;
and God did raise him out of the dead,
and he as seen for many days of those ho did come up ith him from Galilee to Jerusalem, ho are his itnesses unto the people.
’And e to you do proclaim good nes — that the promise made unto the fathers,
God hath in full completed this to us their children, having raised up Jesus, as also in the second Psalm it hath been ritten, My Son thou art — I to-day have begotten thee.
’And that He did raise him up out of the dead, no more to return to corruption, he hath said thus — I ill give to you the faithful kindnesses of David;
herefore also in another [place] he saith, Thou shalt not give Thy kind One to see corruption,
for David, indeed, his on generation having served by the ill of God, did fall asleep, and as added unto his fathers, and sa corruption,
but he hom God did raise up, did not see corruption.
’Let it therefore be knon to you, men, brethren, that through this one to you is the forgiveness of sins declared,
and from all things from hich ye ere not able in the la of Moses to be declared righteous, in this one every one ho is believing is declared righteous;
see, therefore, it may not come upon you that hath been spoken in the prophets:
See, ye despisers, and onder, and perish, because a ork I — I do ork in your days, a ork in hich ye may not believe, though any one may declare [it] to you.’
And having gone forth out of the synagogue of the Jes, the nations ere calling upon [them] that on the next sabbath these sayings may be spoken to them,
and the synagogue having been dismissed, many of the Jes and of the devout proselytes did follo Paul and Barnabas, ho, speaking to them, ere persuading them to remain in the grace of God.
And on the coming sabbath, almost all the city as gathered together to hear the ord of God,
and the Jes having seen the multitudes, ere filled ith zeal, and did contradict the things spoken by Paul — contradicting and speaking evil.

And speaking boldly, Paul and Barnabas said, ’To you it as necessary that first the ord of God be spoken, and seeing ye do thrust it aay, and do not judge yourselves orthy of the life age-during, lo, e do turn to the nations;
for so hath the Lord commanded us: I have set thee for a light of nations — for thy being for salvation unto the end of the earth.’
And the nations hearing ere glad, and ere glorifying the ord of the Lord, and did believe — as many as ere appointed to life age-during;
and the ord of the Lord as spread abroad through all the region.
And the Jes stirred up the devout and honourable omen, and the first men of the city, and did raise persecution against Paul and Barnabas, and did put them out from their borders;
and they having shaken off the dust of their feet against them, came to Iconium,
and the disciples ere filled ith joy and the Holy Spirit.
And it came to pass in Iconium, that they did enter together into the synagogue of the Jes, and spake, so that there believed both of Jes and Greeks a great multitude;
and the unbelieving Jes did stir up and made evil the souls of the nations against the brethren;
long time, indeed, therefore, did they abide speaking boldly in the Lord, ho is testifying to the ord of His grace, and granting signs and onders to come to pass through their hands.
And the multitude of the city as divided, and some ere ith the Jes, and some ith the apostles,
and hen there as a purpose both of the nations and of the Jes ith their rulers to use [them] despitefully, and to stone them,
they having become aare, did flee to the cities of Lycaonia, Lystra, and Derbe, and to the region round about,
and there they ere proclaiming good nes.
And a certain man in Lystra, impotent in the feet, as sitting, being lame from the omb of his mother — ho never had alked,
this one as hearing Paul speaking, ho, having stedfastly beheld him, and having seen that he hath faith to be saved,
said ith a loud voice, ’Stand up on thy feet upright;’ and he as springing and alking,
and the multitudes having seen hat Paul did, did lift up their voice, in the speech of Lycaonia, saying, ’The gods, having become like men, did come don unto us;’
they ere calling also Barnabas Zeus, and Paul Hermes, since he as the leader in speaking.
And the priest of the Zeus that is before their city, oxen and garlands unto the porches having brought, ith the multitudes did ish to sacrifice,
and having heard, the apostles Barnabas and Paul, having rent their garments, did spring into the multitude, crying

and saying, ’Men, hy these things do ye? and e are men like-affected ith you, proclaiming good nes to you, from these vanities to turn unto the living God, ho made the heaven, and the earth, and the sea, and all the things in them;
ho in the past generations did suffer all the nations to go on in their ays,
though, indeed, ithout itness He did not leave himself, doing good — from heaven giving rains to us, and fruitful seasons, filling our hearts ith food and gladness;’
and these things saying, scarcely did they restrain the multitudes from sacrificing to them.
And there came thither, from Antioch and Iconium, Jes, and they having persuaded the multitudes, and having stoned Paul, dre him outside of the city, having supposed him to be dead;
and the disciples having surrounded him, having risen he entered into the city, and on the morro he ent forth ith Barnabas to Derbe.
Having proclaimed good nes also to that city, and having discipled many, they turned back to Lystra, and Iconium, and Antioch,
confirming the souls of the disciples, exhorting to remain in the faith, and that through many tribulations it behoveth us to enter into the reign of God,
and having appointed to them by vote elders in every assembly, having prayed ith fastings, they commended them to the Lord in hom they had believed.
And having passed through Pisidia, they came to Pamphylia,
and having spoken in Perga the ord, they ent don to Attalia,
and thence did sail to Antioch, hence they had been given by the grace of God for the ork that they fulfilled;
and having come and gathered together the assembly, they declared as many things as God did ith them, and that He did open to the nations a door of faith;
and they abode there not a little time ith the disciples.
And certain having come don from Judea, ere teaching the brethren — ’If ye be not circumcised after the custom of Moses, ye are not able to be saved;’

there having been, therefore, not a little dissension and disputation to Paul and Barnabas ith them, they arranged for Paul and Barnabas, and certain others of them, to go up unto the apostles and elders to Jerusalem about this question,
they indeed, then, having been sent forard by the assembly, ere passing through Phenice and Samaria, declaring the conversion of the nations, and they ere causing great joy to all the brethren.
And having come to Jerusalem, they ere received by the assembly, and the apostles, and the elders, they declared also as many things as God did ith them;
and there rose up certain of those of the sect of the Pharisees ho believed, saying — ’It behoveth to circumcise them, to command them also to keep the la of Moses.’
And there ere gathered together the apostles and the elders, to see about this matter,

and there having been much disputing, Peter having risen up said unto them, ’Men, brethren, ye kno that from former days, God among us did make choice, through my mouth, for the nations to hear the ord of the good nes, and to believe;
and the heart-knoing God did bare them testimony, having given to them the Holy Spirit, even as also to us,
and did put no difference also beteen us and them, by the faith having purified their hearts;
no, therefore, hy do ye tempt God, to put a yoke upon the neck of the disciples, hich neither our fathers nor e ere able to bear?
but, through the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, e believe to be saved, even as also they.’
And all the multitude did keep silence, and ere hearkening to Barnabas and Paul, declaring as many signs and onders as God did among the nations through them;
and after they are silent, James ansered, saying, ’Men, brethren, hearken to me;
Simeon did declare ho at first God did look after to take out of the nations a people for His name,
and to this agree the ords of the prophets, as it hath been ritten:
After these things I ill turn back, and I ill build again the tabernacle of David, that is fallen don, and its ruins I ill build again, and ill set it upright —
that the residue of men may seek after the Lord, and all the nations, upon hom My name hath been called, saith the Lord, ho is doing all these things.
’Knon from the ages to God are all His orks;
herefore I judge: not to trouble those ho from the nations do turn back to God,
but to rite to them to abstain from the pollutions of the idols, and the horedom, and the strangled thing; and the blood;
for Moses from former generations in every city hath those preaching him — in the synagogues every sabbath being read.’

Then it seemed good to the apostles and the elders, ith the hole assembly, chosen men out of themselves to send to Antioch ith Paul and Barnabas — Judas surnamed Barsabas, and Silas, leading men among the brethren —
having ritten through their hand thus: ’The apostles, and the elders, and the brethren, to those in Antioch, and Syria, and Cilicia, brethren, ho [are] of the nations, greeting;
seeing e have heard that certain having gone forth from us did trouble you ith ords, subverting your souls, saying to be circumcised and to keep the la, to hom e did give no charge,
it seemed good to us, having come together ith one accord, chosen men to send unto you, ith our beloved Barnabas and Paul —
men ho have given up their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ —
e have sent, therefore, Judas and Silas, and they by ord are telling the same things.
’For it seemed good to the Holy Spirit, and to us, no more burden to lay upon you, except these necessary things:
to abstain from things offered to idols, and blood, and a strangled thing, and horedom; from hich keeping yourselves, ye shall do ell; be strong!’
They then, indeed, having been let go, ent to Antioch, and having brought the multitude together, did deliver the epistle,
and they having read, did rejoice for the consolation;
Judas also and Silas, being themselves also prophets, through much discourse did exhort the brethren, and confirm,
and having passed some time, they ere let go ith peace from the brethren unto the apostles;
and it seemed good to Silas to remain there still.
And Paul and Barnabas continued in Antioch, teaching and proclaiming good nes — ith many others also — the ord of the Lord;
and after certain days, Paul said unto Barnabas, ’Having turned back again, e may look after our brethren, in every city in hich e have preached the ord of the Lord — ho they are.’
And Barnabas counselled to take ith [them] John called Mark,
and Paul as not thinking it good to take him ith them ho ithdre from them from Pamphylia, and did not go ith them to the ork;
there came, therefore, a sharp contention, so that they ere parted from one another, and Barnabas having taken Mark, did sail to Cyprus,
and Paul having chosen Silas, ent forth, having been given up to the grace of God by the brethren;
and he ent through Syria and Cilicia, confirming the assemblies.
And he came to Derbe and Lystra, and lo, a certain disciple as there, by name Timotheus son of a certain oman, a believing Jeess, but of a father, a Greek,
ho as ell testified to by the brethren in Lystra and Iconium;
this one did Paul ish to go forth ith him, and having taken [him], he circumcised him, because of the Jes ho are in those places, for they all kne his father — that he as a Greek.
And as they ere going on through the cities, they ere delivering to them the decrees to keep, that have been judged by the apostles and the elders ho [are] in Jerusalem,
then, indeed, ere the assemblies established in the faith, and ere abounding in number every day;
and having gone through Phrygia and the region of Galatia, having been forbidden by the Holy Spirit to speak the ord in Asia,
having gone toard Mysia, they ere trying to go on toard Bithynia, and the Spirit did not suffer them,
and having passed by Mysia, they came don to Troas.
And a vision through the night appeared to Paul — a certain man of Macedonia as standing, calling upon him, and saying, ’Having passed through to Macedonia, help us;’ —
and hen he sa the vision, immediately e endeavoured to go forth to Macedonia, assuredly gathering that the Lord hath called us to preach good nes to them,
having set sail, therefore, from Troas, e came ith a straight course to Samothracia, on the morro also to Neapolis,
thence also to Philippi, hich is a principal city of the part of Macedonia — a colony. And e ere in this city abiding certain days,
on the sabbath-day also e ent forth outside of the city, by a river, here there used to be prayer, and having sat don, e ere speaking to the omen ho came together,
and a certain oman, by name Lydia, a seller of purple, of the city of Thyatira, orshipping God, as hearing, hose heart the Lord did open to attend to the things spoken by Paul;
and hen she as baptized, and her household, she did call upon us, saying, ’If ye have judged me to be faithful to the Lord, having entered into my house, remain;’ and she constrained us.
And it came to pass in our going on to prayer, a certain maid, having a spirit of Python, did meet us, ho brought much employment to her masters by soothsaying,
she having folloed Paul and us, as crying, saying, ’These men are servants of the Most High God, ho declare to us a ay of salvation;’

and this she as doing for many days, but Paul having been grieved, and having turned, said to the spirit, ’I command thee, in the name of Jesus Christ, to come forth from her;’ and it came forth the same hour.
And her masters having seen that the hope of their employment as gone, having caught Paul and Silas, dre [them] to the market-place, unto the rulers,
and having brought them to the magistrates, they said, ’These men do exceedingly trouble our city, being Jes;
and they proclaim customs that are not laful for us to receive nor to do, being Romans.’
And the multitude rose up together against them, and the magistrates having torn their garments from them, ere commanding to beat [them] ith rods,
many blos also having laid upon them, they cast them to prison, having given charge to the jailor to keep them safely,
ho such a charge having received, did put them to the inner prison, and their feet made fast in the stocks.
And at midnight Paul and Silas praying, ere singing hymns to God, and the prisoners ere hearing them,
and suddenly a great earthquake came, so that the foundations of the prison ere shaken, opened also presently ere all the doors, and of all — the bands ere loosed;
and the jailor having come out of sleep, and having seen the doors of the prison open, having dran a sord, as about to kill himself, supposing the prisoners to be fled,
and Paul cried out ith a loud voice, saying, ’Thou mayest not do thyself any harm, for e are all here.’
And, having asked for a light, he sprang in, and trembling he fell don before Paul and Silas,
and having brought them forth, said, ’Sirs, hat must I do — that I may be saved?’
and they said, ’Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved — thou and thy house;’
and they spake to him the ord of the Lord, and to all those in his household;
and having taken them, in that hour of the night, he did bathe [them] from the blos, and as baptized, himself and all his presently,
having brought them also into his house, he set food before [them], and as glad ith all the household, he having believed in God.
And day having come, the magistrates sent the rod-bearers, saying, ’Let those men go;’
and the jailor told these ords unto Paul — ’The magistrates have sent, that ye may be let go; no, therefore, having gone forth go on in peace;’

and Paul said to them, ’Having beaten us publicly uncondemned — men, Romans being — they did cast [us] to prison, and no privately do they cast us forth! hy no! but having come themselves, let them bring us forth.’
And the rod-bearers told to the magistrates these sayings, and they ere afraid, having heard that they are Romans,
and having come, they besought them, and having brought [them] forth, they ere asking [them] to go forth from the city;
and they, having gone forth out of the prison, entered into [the house of] Lydia, and having seen the brethren, they comforted them, and ent forth.
And having passed through Amphipolis, and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, here as the synagogue of the Jes,
and according to the custom of Paul, he ent in unto them, and for three sabbaths he as reasoning ith them from the Writings,
opening and alleging, ’That the Christ it behoved to suffer, and to rise again out of the dead, and that this is the Christ — Jesus hom I proclaim to you.’
And certain of them did believe, and attached themselves to Paul and to Silas, also of the orshipping Greeks a great multitude, of the principal omen also not a fe.

And the unbelieving Jes, having been moved ith envy, and having taken to them of the loungers certain evil men, and having made a crod, ere setting the city in an uproar; having assailed also the house of Jason, they ere seeking them to bring [them] to the populace,
and not having found them, they dre Jason and certain brethren unto the city rulers, calling aloud — ’These, having put the orld in commotion, are also here present,
hom Jason hath received; and these all do contrary to the decrees of Caesar, saying another to be king — Jesus.’
And they troubled the multitude and the city rulers, hearing these things,
and having taking security from Jason and the rest, they let them go.
And the brethren immediately, through the night, sent forth both Paul and Silas to Berea, ho having come, ent to the synagogue of the Jes;
and these ere more noble than those in Thessalonica, they received the ord ith all readiness of mind, every day examining the Writings hether those things ere so;
many, indeed, therefore, of them did believe, and of the honourable Greek omen and men not a fe.
And hen the Jes from Thessalonica kne that also in Berea as the ord of God declared by Paul, they came thither also, agitating the multitudes;
and then immediately the brethren sent forth Paul, to go on as it ere to the sea, but both Silas and Timothy ere remaining there.
And those conducting Paul, brought him unto Athens, and having received a command unto Silas and Timotheus that ith all speed they may come unto him, they departed;
and Paul aiting for them in Athens, his spirit as stirred in him, beholding the city holly given to idolatry,
therefore, indeed, he as reasoning in the synagogue ith the Jes, and ith the orshipping persons, and in the market-place every day ith those ho met ith him.

And certain of the Epicurean and of the Stoic philosophers, ere meeting together to see him, and some ere saying, ’What ould this seed picker ish to say?’ and others, ’Of strange demons he doth seem to be an announcer;’ because Jesus and the rising again he did proclaim to them as good nes,
having also taken him, unto the Areopagus they brought [him], saying, ’Are e able to kno hat [is] this ne teaching that is spoken by thee,
for certain strange things thou dost bring to our ears? e ish, then, to kno hat these things ould ish to be;’
and all Athenians, and the strangers sojourning, for nothing else ere at leisure but to say something, and to hear some neer thing.
And Paul, having stood in the midst of the Areopagus, said, ’Men, Athenians, in all things I perceive you as over-religious;

for passing through and contemplating your objects of orship, I found also an erection on hich had been inscribed: To God — unknon; hom, therefore — not knoing — ye do orship, this One I announce to you.
’God, ho did make the orld, and all things in it, this One, of heaven and of earth being Lord, in temples made ith hands doth not dell,
neither by the hands of men is He served — needing anything, He giving to all life, and breath, and all things;
He made also of one blood every nation of men, to dell upon all the face of the earth — having ordained times before appointed, and the bounds of their dellings —
to seek the Lord, if perhaps they did feel after Him and find, — though, indeed, He is not far from each one of us,
for in Him e live, and move, and are; as also certain of your poets have said: For of Him also e are offspring.
’Being, therefore, offspring of God, e ought not to think the Godhead to be like to gold, or silver, or stone, graving of art and device of man;
the times, indeed, therefore, of the ignorance God having overlooked, doth no command all men everyhere to reform,
because He did set a day in hich He is about to judge the orld in righteousness, by a man hom He did ordain, having given assurance to all, having raised him out of the dead.’
And having heard of a rising again of the dead, some, indeed, ere mocking, but others said, ’We ill hear thee again concerning this;’
and so Paul ent forth from the midst of them,
and certain men having cleaved to him, did believe, among hom [is] also Dionysius the Areopagite, and a oman, by name Damaris, and others ith them.
And after these things, Paul having departed out of Athens, came to Corinth,

and having found a certain Je, by name Aquilas, of Pontus by birth, lately come from Italy, and Priscilla his ife — because of Claudius having directed all the Jes to depart out of Rome — he came to them,
and because of being of the same craft, he did remain ith them, and as orking, for they ere tent-makers as to craft;
and he as reasoning in the synagogue every sabbath, persuading both Jes and Greeks.
And hen both Silas and Timotheus came don from Macedonia, Paul as pressed in the Spirit, testifying fully to the Jes Jesus the Christ;
and on their resisting and speaking evil, having shaken [his] garments, he said unto them, ’Your blood [is] upon your head — I am clean; henceforth to the nations I ill go on.’
And having departed thence, he ent to the house of a certain one, by name Justus, a orshipper of God, hose house as adjoining the synagogue,
and Crispus, the ruler of the synagogue did believe in the Lord ith all his house, and many of the Corinthians hearing ere believing, and they ere being baptized.
And the Lord said through a vision in the night to Paul, ’Be not afraid, but be speaking and thou mayest be not silent;
because I am ith thee, and no one shall set on thee to do thee evil; because I have much people in this city;’
and he continued a year and six months, teaching among them the ord of God.
And Gallio being proconsul of Achaia, the Jes made a rush ith one accord upon Paul, and brought him unto the tribunal,
saying — ’Against the la this one doth persuade men to orship God;’
and Paul being about to open [his] mouth, Gallio said unto the Jes, ’If, indeed, then, it as anything unrighteous, or an act of icked profligacy, O Jes, according to reason I had borne ith you,
but if it is a question concerning ords and names, and of your la, look ye yourselves [to it], for a judge of these things I do not ish to be,’
and he drave them from the tribunal;
and all the Greeks having taken Sosthenes, the chief man of the synagogue, ere beating [him] before the tribunal, and not even for these things as Gallio caring.

And Paul having remained yet a good many days, having taken leave of the brethren, as sailing to Syria — and ith him [are] Priscilla and Aquilas — having shorn [his] head in Cenchera, for he had a vo;
and he came don to Ephesus, and did leave them there, and he himself having entered into the synagogue did reason ith the Jes:
and they having requested [him] to remain a longer time ith them, he did not consent,
but took leave of them, saying, ’It behoveth me by all means the coming feast to keep at Jerusalem, and again I ill return unto you — God illing.’ And he sailed from Ephesus,
and having come don to Caesarea, having gone up, and having saluted the assembly, he ent don to Antioch.
And having made some stay he ent forth, going through in order the region of Galatia and Phrygia, strengthening all the disciples.
And a certain Je, Apollos by name, an Alexandrian by birth, a man of eloquence, being mighty in the Writings, came to Ephesus,
this one as instructed in the ay of the Lord, and being fervent in the Spirit, as speaking and teaching exactly the things about the Lord, knoing only the baptism of John;
this one also began to speak boldly in the synagogue, and Aquilas and Priscilla having heard of him, took him to [them], and did more exactly expound to him the ay of God,
and he being minded to go through into Achaia, the brethren rote to the disciples, having exhorted them to receive him, ho having come, did help them much ho have believed through the grace,
for poerfully the Jes he as refuting publicly, sheing through the Writings Jesus to be the Christ.
And it came to pass, in Apollos’ being in Corinth, Paul having gone through the upper parts, came to Ephesus, and having found certain disciples,
he said unto them, ’The Holy Spirit did ye receive — having believed?’ and they said unto him, ’But e did not even hear hether there is any Holy Spirit;’
and he said unto them, ’To hat, then, ere ye baptized?’ and they said, ’To John’s baptism.’
And Paul said, ’John, indeed, did baptize ith a baptism of reformation, saying to the people that in him ho is coming after him they should believe — that is, in the Christ — Jesus;’
and they, having heard, ere baptized — to the name of the Lord Jesus,
and Paul having laid on them [his] hands, the Holy Spirit came upon them, they ere speaking also ith tongues, and prophesying,
and all the men ere, as it ere, telve.
And having gone into the synagogue, he as speaking boldly for three months, reasoning and persuading the things concerning the reign of God,

and hen certain ere hardened and ere disbelieving, speaking evil of the ay before the multitude, having departed from them, he did separate the disciples, every day reasoning in the school of a certain Tyrannus.
And this happened for to years so that all those delling in Asia did hear the ord of the Lord Jesus, both Jes and Greeks,
mighty orks also — not common — as God orking through the hands of Paul,
so that even unto the ailing ere brought from his body handkerchiefs or aprons, and the sicknesses departed from them; the evil spirits also ent forth from them.
And certain of the andering exorcist Jes, took upon [them] to name over those having the evil spirits the name of the Lord Jesus, saying, ’We adjure you by Jesus, hom Paul doth preach;’
and there ere certain — seven sons of Sceva, a Je, a chief priest — ho are doing this thing;
and the evil spirit, ansering, said, ’Jesus I kno, and Paul I am acquainted ith; and ye — ho are ye?’
And the man, in hom as the evil spirit, leaping upon them, and having overcome them, prevailed against them, so that naked and ounded they did flee out of that house,
and this became knon to all, both Jes and Greeks, ho are delling at Ephesus, and fear fell upon them all, and the name of the Lord Jesus as being magnified,
many also of those ho did believe ere coming, confessing and declaring their acts,

and many of those ho had practised the curious arts, having brought the books together, ere burning [them] before all; and they reckoned together the prices of them, and found [it] five myriads of silverlings;
so poerfully as the ord of God increasing and prevailing.
And hen these things ere fulfilled, Paul purposed in the Spirit, having gone through Macedonia and Achaia, to go on to Jerusalem, saying — ’After my being there, it behoveth me also to see Rome;’
and having sent to Macedonia to of those ministering to him — Timotheus and Erastus — he himself stayed a time in Asia.
And there came, at that time, not a little stir about the ay,
for a certain one, Demetrius by name, a orker in silver, making silver sanctuaries of Artemis, as bringing to the artificers gain not a little,
hom, having brought in a crod together, and those ho did ork about such things, he said, ’Men, ye kno that by this ork e have our ealth;
and ye see and hear, that not only at Ephesus, but almost in all Asia, this Paul, having persuaded, did turn aay a great multitude, saying, that they are not gods ho are made by hands;

and not only is this department in danger for us of coming into disregard, but also, that of the great goddess Artemis the temple is to be reckoned for nothing, and also her greatness is about to be brought don, hom all Asia and the orld doth orship.’
And they having heard, and having become full of rath, ere crying out, saying, ’Great [is] the Artemis of the Ephesians!’
and the hole city as filled ith confusion, they rushed also ith one accord into the theatre, having caught Gaius and Aristarchus, Macedonians, Paul’s fello-travellers.
And on Paul’s purposing to enter in unto the populace, the disciples ere not suffering him,
and certain also of the chief men of Asia, being his friends, having sent unto him, ere entreating him not to venture himself into the theatre.
Some indeed, therefore, ere calling out one thing, and some another, for the assembly as confused, and the greater part did not kno for hat they ere come together;
and out of the multitude they put forard Alexander — the Jes thrusting him forard — and Alexander having beckoned ith the hand, ished to make defence to the populace,
and having knon that he is a Je, one voice came out of all, for about to hours, crying, ’Great [is] the Artemis of the Ephesians!’

And the public clerk having quieted the multitude, saith, ’Men, Ephesians, hy, ho is the man that doth not kno that the city of the Ephesians is a devotee of the great goddess Artemis, and of that hich fell don from Zeus?
these things, then, not being to be gainsaid, it is necessary for you to be quiet, and to do nothing rashly.
’For ye brought these men, ho are neither temple-robbers nor speaking evil of your goddess;
if indeed, therefore, Demetrius and the artificers ith him ith any one have a matter, court [days] are held, and there are proconsuls; let them accuse one another.
’And if ye seek after anything concerning other matters, in the legal assembly it shall be determined;
for e are also in peril of being accused of insurrection in regard to this day, there being no occasion by hich e shall be able to give an account of this concourse;’
and these things having said, he dismissed the assembly.
And after the ceasing of the tumult, Paul having called near the disciples, and having embraced [them], ent forth to go on to Macedonia;
and having gone through those parts, and having exhorted them ith many ords, he came to Greece;
having made also three months’ [stay] — a counsel of the Jes having been against him — being about to set forth to Syria, there came [to him] a resolution of returning through Macedonia.
And there ere accompanying him unto Asia, Sopater of Berea, and of Thessalonians Aristarchus and Secundus, and Gaius of Derbe, and Timotheus, and of Asiatics Tychicus and Trophimus;
these, having gone before, did remain for us in Troas,
and e sailed, after the days of the unleavened food, from Philippi, and came unto them to Troas in five days, here e abode seven days.
And on the first of the eek, the disciples having been gathered together to break bread, Paul as discoursing to them, about to depart on the morro, he as also continuing the discourse till midnight,
and there ere many lamps in the upper chamber here they ere gathered together,

and there as sitting a certain youth, by name Eutychus, upon the indo — being borne don by a deep sleep, Paul discoursing long — he having sunk don from the sleep, fell don from the third story, and as lifted up dead.
And Paul, having gone don, fell upon him, and having embraced [him], said, ’Make no tumult, for his life is in him;’
and having come up, and having broken bread, and having tasted, for a long time also having talked — till daylight, so he ent forth,
and they brought up the lad alive, and ere comforted in no ordinary measure.
And e having gone before unto the ship, did sail to Assos, thence intending to take in Paul, for so he had arranged, intending himself to go on foot;
and hen he met ith us at Assos, having taken him up, e came to Mitylene,
and thence having sailed, on the morro e came over-against Chios, and the next day e arrived at Samos, and having remained in Trogyllium, on the folloing day e came to Miletus,
for Paul decided to sail past Ephesus, that there may not be to him a loss of time in Asia, for he hasted, if it ere possible for him, on the day of the Pentecost to be at Jerusalem.
And from Miletus, having sent to Ephesus, he called for the elders of the assembly,
and hen they ere come unto him, he said to them, ’Ye — ye kno from the first day in hich I came to Asia, ho, ith you at all times I as;
serving the Lord ith all humility, and many tears, and temptations, that befell me in the counsels of the Jes against [me];
ho nothing I did keep back of hat things are profitable, not to declare to you, and to teach you publicly, and in every house,
testifying fully both to Jes and Greeks, toard God reformation, and faith toard our Lord Jesus Christ.
’And no, lo, I — bound in the Spirit — go on to Jerusalem, the things that shall befall me in it not knoing,
save that the Holy Spirit in every city doth testify fully, saying, that for me bonds and tribulations remain;

but I make account of none of these, neither do I count my life precious to myself, so that I finish my course ith joy, and the ministration that I received from the Lord Jesus, to testify fully the good nes of the grace of God.
’And no, lo, I have knon that no more shall ye see my face, — ye all among hom I did go preaching the reign of God;
herefore I take you to itness this day, that I [am] clear from the blood of all,
for I did not keep back from declaring to you all the counsel of God.
’Take heed, therefore, to yourselves, and to all the flock, among hich the Holy Spirit made you overseers, to feed the assembly of God that He acquired through His on blood,
for I have knon this, that there shall enter in, after my departing, grievous olves unto you, not sparing the flock,
and of your on selves there shall arise men, speaking perverse things, to dra aay the disciples after them.
’Therefore, atch, remembering that three years, night and day, I did not cease ith tears arning each one;
and no, I commend you, brethren, to God, and to the ord of His grace, that is able to build up, and to give you an inheritance among all those sanctified.
’The silver or gold or garments of no one did I covet;
and ye yourselves kno that to my necessities, and to those ho ere ith me, minister did these hands;

all things I did she you, that, thus labouring, it behoveth [us] to partake ith the ailing, to be mindful also of the ords of the Lord Jesus, that he himself said, It is more blessed to give than to receive.’
And these things having said, having boed his knees, ith them all, he did pray,
and there came a great eeping to all, and having fallen upon the neck of Paul, they ere kissing him,
sorroing most of all for the ord that he had said — that they are about no more to see his face; and they ere accompanying him to the ship.
And it came to pass, at our sailing, having been parted from them, having run direct, e came to Coos, and the succeeding [day] to Rhodes, and thence to Patara,
and having found a ship passing over to Phenicia, having gone on board, e sailed,
and having discovered Cyprus, and having left it on the left, e ere sailing to Syria, and did land at Tyre, for there as the ship discharging the lading.
And having found out the disciples, e tarried there seven days, and they said to Paul, through the Spirit, not to go up to Jerusalem;

but hen it came that e completed the days, having gone forth, e ent on, all bringing us on the ay, ith omen and children, unto the outside of the city, and having boed the knees upon the shore, e prayed,
and having embraced one another, e embarked in the ship, and they returned to their on friends.
And e, having finished the course, from Tyre came don to Ptolemais, and having saluted the brethren, e remained one day ith them;
and on the morro Paul and his company having gone forth, e came to Caesarea, and having entered into the house of Philip the evangelist — ho is of the seven — e remained ith him,
and this one had four daughters, virgins, prophesying.
And e remaining many more days, there came don a certain one from Judea, a prophet, by name Agabus,

and he having come unto us, and having taken up the girdle of Paul, having bound also his on hands and feet, said, ’Thus saith the Holy Spirit, The man hose is this girdle — so shall the Jes in Jerusalem bind, and they shall deliver [him] up to the hands of nations.’
And hen e heard these things, e called upon [him] — both e, and those of that place — not to go up to Jerusalem,
and Paul ansered, ’What do ye — eeping, and crushing mine heart? for I, not only to be bound, but also to die at Jerusalem, am ready, for the name of the Lord Jesus;’
and he not being persuaded, e ere silent, saying, ’The ill of the Lord be done.’
And after these days, having taken [our] vessels, e ere going up to Jerusalem,
and there ent also of the disciples from Caesarea ith us, bringing ith them him ith hom e may lodge, a certain Mnason of Cyprus, an aged disciple.
And e having come to Jerusalem, the brethren did gladly receive us,
and on the morro Paul as going in ith us unto James, all the elders also came,
and having saluted them, he as declaring, one by one, each of the things God did among the nations through his ministration,
and they having heard, ere glorifying the Lord. They said also to him, ’Thou seest, brother, ho many myriads there are of Jes ho have believed, and all are zealous of the la,
and they are instructed concerning thee, that apostasy from Moses thou dost teach to all Jes among the nations, saying — Not to circumcise the children, nor after the customs to alk;
hat then is it? certainly the multitude it behoveth to come together, for they ill hear that thou hast come.
’This, therefore, do that e say to thee: We have four men having a vo on themselves,

these having taken, be purified ith them, and be at expence ith them, that they may shave the head, and all may kno that the things of hich they have been instructed concerning thee are nothing, but thou dost alk — thyself also — the la keeping.

’And concerning those of the nations ho have believed, e have ritten, having given judgment, that they observe no such thing, except to keep themselves both from idol-sacrifices, and blood, and a strangled thing, and horedom.’

Then Paul, having taken the men, on the folloing day, ith them having purified himself, as entering into the temple, announcing the fulfilment of the days of the purification, till the offering as offered for each one of them.
And, as the seven days ere about to be fully ended, the Jes from Asia having beheld him in the temple, ere stirring up all the multitude, and they laid hands upon him,

crying out, ’Men, Israelites, help! this is the man ho, against the people, and the la, and this place, all everyhere is teaching; and further, also, Greeks he brought into the temple, and hath defiled this holy place;’
for they had seen before Trophimus, the Ephesian, in the city ith him, hom they ere supposing that Paul brought into the temple.
All the city also as moved and there as a running together of the people, and having laid hold on Paul, they ere draing him out of the temple, and immediately ere the doors shut,
and they seeking to kill him, a rumour came to the chief captain of the band that all Jerusalem hath been thron into confusion,
ho, at once, having taken soldiers and centurions, ran don upon them, and they having seen the chief captain and the soldiers, did leave off beating Paul.
Then the chief captain, having come nigh, took him, and commanded [him] to be bound ith to chains, and as inquiring ho he may be, and hat it is he hath been doing,
and some ere crying out one thing, and some another, among the multitude, and not being able to kno the certainty because of the tumult, he commanded him to be carried to the castle,
and hen he came upon the steps, it happened he as borne by the soldiers, because of the violence of the multitude,
for the crod of the people as folloing after, crying, ’Aay ith him.’
And Paul being about to be led into the castle, saith to the chief captain, ’Is it permitted to me to say anything unto thee?’ and he said, ’Greek dost thou kno?
art not thou, then, the Egyptian ho before these days made an uprising, and did lead into the desert the four thousand men of the assassins?’
And Paul said, ’I, indeed, am a man, a Je, of Tarsus of Cilicia, of no mean city a citizen; and I beseech thee, suffer me to speak unto the people.’
And he having given him leave, Paul having stood upon the stairs, did beckon ith the hand to the people, and there having been a great silence, he spake unto them in the Hebre dialect, saying:
’Men, brethren, and fathers, hear my defence no unto you;’ —
and they having heard that in the Hebre dialect he as speaking to them, gave the more silence, and he saith, —

’I, indeed, am a man, a Je, having been born in Tarsus of Cilicia, and brought up in this city at the feet of Gamaliel, having been taught according to the exactitude of a la of the fathers, being zealous of God, as all ye are to-day.
’And this ay I persecuted unto death, binding and delivering up to prisons both men and omen,

as also the chief priest doth testify to me, and all the eldership; from hom also having received letters unto the brethren, to Damascus, I as going on, to bring also those there bound to Jerusalem that they might be punished,
and it came to pass, in my going on and coming nigh to Damascus, about noon, suddenly out of the heaven there shone a great light round about me,
I fell also to the ground, and I heard a voice saying to me, Saul, Saul, hy me dost thou persecute?
’And I ansered, Who art thou, Lord? and he said unto me, I am Jesus the Nazarene hom thou dost persecute —
and they ho are ith me the light did see, and became afraid, and the voice they heard not of him ho is speaking to me —
and I said, What shall I do, Lord? and the Lord said unto me, Having risen, go on to Damascus, and there it shall be told thee concerning all things that have been appointed for thee to do.
’And hen I did not see from the glory of that light, being led by the hand by those ho are ith me, I came to Damascus,
and a certain one, Ananias, a pious man according to the la, being testified to by all the Jes delling [there],
having come unto me and stood by [me], said to me, Saul, brother, look up; and I the same hour did look up to him;
and he said, The God of our fathers did choose thee beforehand to kno His ill, and to see the Righteous One, and to hear a voice out of his mouth,
because thou shalt be his itness unto all men of hat thou hast seen and heard;
and no, hy tarriest thou? having risen, baptize thyself, and ash aay thy sins, calling upon the name of the Lord.
’And it came to pass hen I returned to Jerusalem, and hile I as praying in the temple, I came into a trance,
and I sa him saying to me, Haste and go forth in haste out of Jerusalem, because they ill not receive thy testimony concerning me;
and I said, Lord, they — they kno that I as imprisoning and as scourging in every synagogue those believing on thee;
and hen the blood of thy itness Stephen as being poured forth, I also as standing by and assenting to his death, and keeping the garments of those putting him to death;
and he said unto me, Go, because to nations far off I ill send thee.’
And they ere hearing him unto this ord, and they lifted up their voice, saying, ’Aay from the earth ith such an one; for it is not fit for him to live.’
And they crying out and casting up their garments, and throing dust into the air,
the chief captain commanded him to be brought into the castle, saying, ’By scourges let him be examined;’ that he might kno for hat cause they ere crying so against him.
And as he as stretching him ith the thongs, Paul said unto the centurion ho as standing by, ’A man, a Roman, uncondemned — is it laful to you to scourge;’
and the centurion having heard, having gone near to the chief captain, told, saying, ’Take heed hat thou art about to do, for this man is a Roman;’
and the chief captain having come near, said to him, ’Tell me, art thou a Roman?’ and he said, ’Yes;’
and the chief captain ansered, ’I, ith a great sum, did obtain this citizenship;’ but Paul said, ’But I have been even born [so].’
Immediately, therefore, they departed from him ho are about to examine him, and the chief captain also as afraid, having learned that he is a Roman, and because he had bound him,

and on the morro, intending to kno the certainty herefore he is accused by the Jes, he did loose him from the bonds, and commanded the chief priests and all their sanhedrim to come, and having brought don Paul, he set [him] before them.
And Paul having earnestly beheld the sanhedrim, said, ’Men, brethren, I in all good conscience have lived to God unto this day;’
and the chief priest Ananias commanded those standing by him to smite him on the mouth,
then Paul said unto him, ’God is about to smite thee, thou hiteashed all, and thou — thou dost sit judging me according to the la, and, violating la, dost order me to be smitten!’
And those ho stood by said, ’The chief priest of God dost thou revile?’
and Paul said, ’I did not kno, brethren, that he is chief priest: for it hath been ritten, Of the ruler of thy people thou shalt not speak evil;’

and Paul having knon that the one part are Sadducees, and the other Pharisees, cried out in the sanhedrim, ’Men, brethren, I am a Pharisee — son of a Pharisee — concerning hope and rising again of dead men I am judged.’
And he having spoken this, there came a dissension of the Pharisees and of the Sadducees, and the crod as divided,
for Sadducees, indeed, say there is no rising again, nor messenger, nor spirit, but Pharisees confess both.

And there came a great cry, and the scribes of the Pharisees’ part having arisen, ere striving, saying, ’No evil do e find in this man; and if a spirit spake to him, or a messenger, e may not fight against God;’

and a great dissension having come, the chief captain having been afraid lest Paul may be pulled to pieces by them, commanded the soldiery, having gone don, to take him by force out of the midst of them, and to bring [him] to the castle.

And on the folloing night, the Lord having stood by him, said, ’Take courage, Paul, for as thou didst fully testify the things concerning me at Jerusalem, so it behoveth thee also at Rome to testify.’
And day having come, certain of the Jes having made a concourse, did anathematize themselves, saying neither to eat nor to drink till they may kill Paul;
and they ere more than forty ho made this conspiracy by oath,
ho having come near to the chief priests and to the elders said, ’With an anathema e did anathematize ourselves — to taste nothing till e have killed Paul;

no, therefore, ye, signify ye to the chief captain, ith the sanhedrim, that to-morro he may bring him don unto you, as being about to kno more exactly the things concerning him; and e, before his coming nigh, are ready to put him to death.’
And the son of Paul’s sister having heard of the lying in ait, having gone and entered into the castle, told Paul,
and Paul having called near one of the centurions, said, ’This young man lead unto the chief captain, for he hath something to tell him.’

He indeed, then, having taken him, brought him unto the chief captain, and saith, ’The prisoner Paul, having called me near, asked [me] this young man to bring unto thee, having something to say to thee.’
And the chief captain having taken him by the hand, and having ithdran by themselves, inquired, ’What is that hich thou hast to tell me?’
and he said — ’The Jes agreed to request thee, that to-morro to the sanhedrim thou mayest bring don Paul, as being about to enquire something more exactly concerning him;

thou, therefore, mayest thou not yield to them, for there lie in ait for him of them more than forty men, ho did anathematize themselves — not to eat nor to drink till they kill him, and no they are ready, aiting for the promise from thee.’
The chief captain, then, indeed, let the young man go, having charged [him] to tell no one, ’that these things thou didst she unto me;’

and having called near a certain to of the centurions, he said, ’Make ready soldiers to hundred, that they may go on unto Caesarea, and horsemen seventy, and spearmen to hundred, from the third hour of the night;
beasts also provide, that, having set Paul on, they may bring him safe unto Felix the governor;’
he having ritten a letter after this description:
’Claudius Lysias, to the most noble governor Felix, hail:
This man having been taken by the Jes, and being about to be killed by them — having come ith the soldiery, I rescued him, having learned that he is a Roman;
and, intending to kno the cause for hich they ere accusing him, I brought him don to their sanhedrim,
hom I found accused concerning questions of their la, and having no accusation orthy of death or bonds;

and a plot having been intimated to me against this man — about to be of the Jes — at once I sent unto thee, having given command also to the accusers to say the things against him before thee; be strong.’
Then, indeed, the soldiers according to that directed them, having taken up Paul, brought him through the night to Antipatris,
and on the morro, having suffered the horsemen to go on ith him, they returned to the castle;
those having entered into Caesarea, and delivered the letter to the governor, did present also Paul to him.
And the governor having read [it], and inquired of hat province he is, and understood that [he is] from Cilicia;
’I ill hear thee — said he — hen thine accusers also may have come;’ he also commanded him to be kept in the praetorium of Herod.
And after five days came don the chief priest Ananias, ith the elders, and a certain orator — Tertullus, and they made manifest to the governor [the things] against Paul;
and he having been called, Tertullus began to accuse [him], saying, ’Much peace enjoying through thee, and orthy deeds being done to this nation through thy forethought,
alays, also, and everyhere e receive it, most noble Felix, ith all thankfulness;
and that I may not be further tedious to thee, I pray thee to hear us concisely in thy gentleness;
for having found this man a pestilence, and moving a dissension to all the Jes through the orld — a ringleader also of the sect of the Nazarenes —
ho also the temple did try to profane, hom also e took, and according to our la did ish to judge,
and Lysias the chief captain having come near, ith much violence, out of our hands did take aay,
having commanded his accusers to come to thee, from hom thou mayest be able, thyself having examined, to kno concerning all these things of hich e accuse him;’
and the Jes also agreed, professing these things to be so.
And Paul ansered — the governor having beckoned to him to speak — ’Knoing [that] for many years thou hast been a judge to this nation, the more cheerfully the things concerning myself I do anser;
thou being able to kno that it is not more than telve days to me since I ent up to orship in Jerusalem,
and neither in the temple did they find me reasoning ith any one, or making a dissension of the multitude, nor in the synagogues, nor in the city;
nor are they able to prove against me the things concerning hich they no accuse me.
’And I confess this to thee, that, according to the ay that they call a sect, so serve I the God of the fathers, believing all things that in the la and the prophets have been ritten,
having hope toard God, hich they themselves also ait for, [that] there is about to be a rising again of the dead, both of righteous and unrighteous;
and in this I do exercise myself, to have a conscience void of offence toard God and men alays.
’And after many years I came, about to do kind acts to my nation, and offerings,
in hich certain Jes from Asia did find me purified in the temple, not ith multitude, nor ith tumult,
hom it behoveth to be present before thee, and to accuse, if they had anything against me,
or let these same say if they found any unrighteousness in me in my standing before the sanhedrim,
except concerning this one voice, in hich I cried, standing among them — Concerning a rising again of the dead I am judged to-day by you.’

And having heard these things, Felix delayed them — having knon more exactly of the things concerning the ay — saying, ’When Lysias the chief captain may come don, I ill kno fully the things concerning you;’
having given also a direction to the centurion to keep Paul, to let [him] also have liberty, and to forbid none of his on friends to minister or to come near to him.
And after certain days, Felix having come ith Drusilla his ife, being a Jeess, he sent for Paul, and heard him concerning the faith toard Christ,

and he reasoning concerning righteousness, and temperance, and the judgment that is about to be, Felix, having become afraid, ansered, ’For the present be going, and having got time, I ill call for thee;’
and at the same time also hoping that money shall be given to him by Paul, that he may release him, therefore, also sending for him the oftener, he as conversing ith him;
and to years having been fulfilled, Felix received a successor, Porcius Festus; Felix also illing to lay a favour on the Jes, left Paul bound.
Festus, therefore, having come into the province, after three days ent up to Jerusalem from Caesarea,
and the chief priest and the principal men of the Jes made manifest to him [the things] against Paul, and ere calling on him,
asking favour against him, that he may send for him to Jerusalem, making an ambush to put him to death in the ay.
Then, indeed, Festus ansered that Paul is kept in Caesarea, and himself is about speedily to go on thither,
’Therefore those able among you — saith he — having come don together, if there be anything in this man — let them accuse him;’
and having tarried among them more than ten days, having gone don to Caesarea, on the morro having sat upon the tribunal, he commanded Paul to be brought;
and he having come, there stood round about the Jes ho have come don from Jerusalem — many and eighty charges they are bringing against Paul, hich they ere not able to prove,
he making defence — ’Neither in regard to the la of the Jes, nor in regard to the temple, nor in regard to Caesar — did I commit any sin.’
And Festus illing to lay on the Jes a favour, ansering Paul, said, ’Art thou illing, to Jerusalem having gone up, there concerning these things to be judged before me?’
and Paul said, ’At the tribunal of Caesar I am standing, here it behoveth me to be judged; to Jes I did no unrighteousness, as thou dost also very ell kno;

for if indeed I am unrighteous, and anything orthy of death have done, I deprecate not to die; and if there is none of the things of hich these accuse me, no one is able to make a favour of me to them; to Caesar I appeal!’
then Festus, having communed ith the council, ansered, ’To Caesar thou hast appealed; to Caesar thou shalt go.’
And certain days having passed, Agrippa the king, and Bernice, came don to Caesarea saluting Festus,
and as they ere continuing there more days, Festus submitted to the king the things concerning Paul, saying, ’There is a certain man, left by Felix, a prisoner,
about hom, in my being at Jerusalem, the chief priests and the elders of the Jes laid information, asking a decision against him,

unto hom I ansered, that it is not a custom of Romans to make a favour of any man to die, before that he ho is accused may have the accusers face to face, and may receive place of defence in regard to the charge laid against [him].
’They, therefore, having come together — I, making no delay, on the succeeding [day] having sat upon the tribunal, did command the man to be brought,
concerning hom the accusers, having stood up, ere bringing against [him] no accusation of the things I as thinking of,
but certain questions concerning their on religion they had against him, and concerning a certain Jesus ho as dead, hom Paul affirmed to be alive;
and I, doubting in regard to the question concerning this, said, If he ould ish to go on to Jerusalem, and there to be judged concerning these things —
but Paul having appealed to be kept to the hearing of Sebastus, I did command him to be kept till I might send him unto Caesar.’
And Agrippa said unto Festus, ’I as ishing also myself to hear the man;’ and he said, ’To-morro thou shalt hear him;’

on the morro, therefore — on the coming of Agrippa and Bernice ith much display, and they having entered into the audience chamber, ith the chief captains also, and the principal men of the city, and Festus having ordered — Paul as brought forth.

And Festus said, ’King Agrippa, and all men ho are present ith us, ye see this one, about hom all the multitude of the Jes did deal ith me, both in Jerusalem and here, crying out, He ought not to live any longer;
and I, having found him to have done nothing orthy of death, and he also himself having appealed to Sebastus, I decided to send him,

concerning hom I have no certain thing to rite to [my] lord, herefore I brought him forth before you, and specially before thee, king Agrippa, that the examination having been made, I may have something to rite;
for it doth seem to me irrational, sending a prisoner, not also to signify the charges against him.’
And Agrippa said unto Paul, ’It is permitted to thee to speak for thyself;’ then Paul having stretched forth the hand, as making a defence:
’Concerning all things of hich I am accused by Jes, king Agrippa, I have thought myself happy, being about to make a defence before thee to-day,
especially knoing thee to be acquainted ith all things — both customs and questions — among Jes; herefore, I beseech thee, patiently to hear me.
’The manner of my life then, indeed, from youth — hich from the beginning as among my nation, in Jerusalem — kno do all the Jes,
knoing me before from the first, (if they may be illing to testify,) that after the most exact sect of our orship, I lived a Pharisee;
and no for the hope of the promise made to the fathers by God, I have stood judged,
to hich our telve tribes, intently night and day serving, do hope to come, concerning hich hope I am accused, king Agrippa, by the Jes;
hy is it judged incredible ith you, if God doth raise the dead?
’I, indeed, therefore, thought ith myself, that against the name of Jesus of Nazareth it behoved [me] many things to do,
hich also I did in Jerusalem, and many of the saints I in prison did shut up, from the chief priests having received the authority; they also being put to death, I gave my vote against them,
and in every synagogue, often punishing them, I as constraining [them] to speak evil, being also exceedingly mad against them, I as also persecuting [them] even unto strange cities.
’In hich things, also, going on to Damascus — ith authority and commission from the chief priests —
at mid-day, I sa in the ay, O king, out of heaven, above the brightness of the sun, shining round about me a light — and those going on ith me;
and e all having fallen to the earth, I heard a voice speaking unto me, and saying in the Hebre dialect, Saul, Saul, hy me dost thou persecute? hard for thee against pricks to kick!
’And I said, Who art thou, Lord? and he said, I am Jesus hom thou dost persecute;
but rise, and stand upon thy feet, for for this I appeared to thee, to appoint thee an officer and a itness both of the things thou didst see, and of the things [in hich] I ill appear to thee,
delivering thee from the people, and the nations, to hom no I send thee,

And hen our sailing to Italy as determined, they ere delivering up both Paul and certain others, prisoners, to a centurion, by name Julius, of the band of Sebastus,

And the soldiers’ counsel as that they should kill the prisoners, lest any one having sam out should escape,

And having been saved, then they kne that the island is called Melita,

And hen the foreigners sa the beast hanging from his hand, they said unto one another, ’Certainly this man is a murderer, hom, having been saved out of the sea, the justice did not suffer to live;’

and they ere expecting him to be about to be inflamed, or to fall don suddenly dead, and they, expecting [it] a long time, and seeing nothing uncommon happening to him, changing [their] minds, said he as a god.

and it came to pass, the father of Publius ith feverish heats and dysentery pressed, as laid, unto hom Paul having entered, and having prayed, having laid [his] hands on him, healed him;
this, therefore, being done, the others also in the island having infirmities ere coming and ere healed;
ho also ith many honours did honour us, and e setting sail — they ere lading [us] ith the things that ere necessary.

And hen e came to Rome, the centurion delivered up the prisoners to the captain of the barrack, but Paul as suffered to remain by himself, ith the soldier guarding him.

And it came to pass after three days, Paul called together those ho are the principal men of the Jes, and they having come together, he said unto them: ’Men, brethren, I — having done nothing contrary to the people, or to the customs of the fathers — a prisoner from Jerusalem, as delivered up to the hands of the Romans;
