And they said unto him, ’We did neither receive letters concerning thee from Judea, nor did any one ho came of the brethren declare or speak any evil concerning thee,
and e think it good from thee to hear hat thou dost think, for, indeed, concerning this sect it is knon to us that everyhere it is spoken against;’

and having appointed him a day, they came, more of them unto him, to the lodging, to hom he as expounding, testifying fully the reign of God, persuading them also of the things concerning Jesus, both from the la of Moses, and the prophets, from morning till evening,

And not being agreed ith one another, they ere going aay, Paul having spoken one ord — ’Well did the Holy Spirit speak through Isaiah the prophet unto our fathers,

for made gross as the heart of this people, and ith the ears they heard heavily, and their eyes they did close, lest they may see ith the eyes, and ith the heart may understand, and be turned back, and I may heal them.
’Be it knon, therefore, to you, that to the nations as sent the salvation of God, these also ill hear it;’
and he having said these things, the Jes ent aay, having much disputation among themselves;
and Paul remained an entire to years in his on hired [house], and as receiving all those coming in unto him,

Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ, a called apostle, having been separated to the good nes of God —
hich He announced before through His prophets in holy ritings —
concerning His Son, (ho is come of the seed of David according to the flesh,
ho is marked out Son of God in poer, according to the Spirit of sanctification, by the rising again from the dead,) Jesus Christ our Lord;

to all ho are in Rome, beloved of God, called saints; Grace to you, and peace, from God our Father, and [from] the Lord Jesus Christ!
first, indeed, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for you all, that your faith is proclaimed in the hole orld;
for God is my itness, hom I serve in my spirit in the good nes of His Son, ho unceasingly I make mention of you,

And I do not ish you to be ignorant, brethren, that many times I did purpose to come unto you — and as hindered till the present time — that some fruit I might have also among you, even as also among the other nations.
Both to Greeks and to foreigners, both to ise and to thoughtless, I am a debtor,
so, as much as in me is, I am ready also to you ho [are] in Rome to proclaim good nes,

For the righteousness of God in it is revealed from faith to faith, according as it hath been ritten, ’And the righteous one by faith shall live,’

Because that hich is knon of God is manifest among them, for God did manifest [it] to them,

Wherefore also God did give them up, in the desires of their hearts, to uncleanness, to dishonour their bodies among themselves;

Because of this did God give them up to dishonourable affections, for even their females did change the natural use into that against nature;

and in like manner also the males having left the natural use of the female, did burn in their longing toard one another; males ith males orking shame, and the recompense of their error that as fit, in themselves receiving.

having been filled ith all unrighteousness, horedom, ickedness, covetousness, malice; full of envy, murder, strife, deceit, evil dispositions; hisperers,

unintelligent, faithless, ithout natural affection, implacable, unmerciful;

ho shall render to each according to his orks;

and the uncircumcision, by nature, fulfilling the la, shall judge thee ho, through letter and circumcision, [art] a transgressor of la.

much in every ay; for first, indeed, that they ere intrusted ith the oracles of God;

And it as not ritten on his account alone, that it as reckoned to him,

For in our being still ailing, Christ in due time did die for the impious;

And not only [so], but e are also boasting in God, through our Lord Jesus Christ, through hom no e did receive the reconciliation;
because of this, even as through one man the sin did enter into the orld, and through the sin the death; and thus to all men the death did pass through, for that all did sin;

But, not as the offence so also [is] the free gift; for if by the offence of the one the many did die, much more did the grace of God, and the free gift in grace of the one man Jesus Christ, abound to the many;

are ye ignorant that e, as many as ere baptized to Christ Jesus, to his death ere baptized?
e ere buried together, then, ith him through the baptism to the death, that even as Christ as raised up out of the dead through the glory of the Father, so also e in neness of life might alk.
For, if e have become planted together to the likeness of his death, [so] also e shall be of the rising again;
this knoing, that our old man as crucified ith [him], that the body of the sin may be made useless, for our no longer serving the sin;
for he ho hath died hath been set free from the sin.
And if e died ith Christ, e believe that e also shall live ith him,
knoing that Christ, having been raised up out of the dead, doth no more die, death over him hath no more lordship;

so also ye, reckon yourselves to be dead indeed to the sin, and living to God in Jesus Christ our Lord.
Let not then the sin reign in your mortal body, to obey it in its desires;

What then? shall e sin because e are not under la but under grace? let it not be!
have ye not knon that to hom ye present yourselves servants for obedience, servants ye are to him to hom ye obey, hether of sin to death, or of obedience to righteousness?
and thanks to God, that ye ere servants of the sin, and — ere obedient from the heart to the form of teaching to hich ye ere delivered up;
and having been freed from the sin, ye became servants to the righteousness.

In the manner of men I speak, because of the eakness of your flesh, for even as ye did present your members servants to the uncleanness and to the lalessness — to the lalessness, so no present your members servants to the righteousness — to sanctification,
for hen ye ere servants of the sin, ye ere free from the righteousness,
hat fruit, therefore, ere ye having then, in the things of hich ye are no ashamed? for the end of those [is] death.
And no, having been freed from the sin, and having become servants to God, ye have your fruit — to sanctification, and the end life age-during;
for the ages of the sin [is] death, and the gift of God [is] life age-during in Christ Jesus our Lord.
Are ye ignorant, brethren — for to those knoing la I speak — that the la hath lordship over the man as long as he liveth?
for the married oman to the living husband hath been bound by la, and if the husband may die, she hath been free from the la of the husband;

so, then, the husband being alive, an adulteress she shall be called if she may become another man’s; and if the husband may die, she is free from the la, so as not to be an adulteress, having become another man’s.
So that, my brethren, ye also ere made dead to the la through the body of the Christ, for your becoming another’s, ho out of the dead as raised up, that e might bear fruit to God;
for hen e ere in the flesh, the passions of the sins, that [are] through the la, ere orking in our members, to bear fruit to the death;
and no e have ceased from the la, that being dead in hich e ere held, so that e may serve in neness of spirit, and not in oldness of letter.
What, then, shall e say? the la [is] sin? let it not be! but the sin I did not kno except through la, for also the covetousness I had not knon if the la had not said:
’Thou shalt not covet;’ and the sin having received an opportunity, through the command, did ork in me all covetousness — for apart from la sin is dead.

and the command that [is] for life, this as found by me for death;

so that the la, indeed, [is] holy, and the command holy, and righteous, and good.

That hich is good then, to me hath it become death? let it not be! but the sin, that it might appear sin, through the good, orking death to me, that the sin might become exceeding sinful through the command,
for e have knon that the la is spiritual, and I am fleshly, sold by the sin;
for that hich I ork, I do not acknoledge; for not hat I ill, this I practise, but hat I hate, this I do.
And if hat I do not ill, this I do, I consent to the la that [it is] good,
and no it is no longer I that ork it, but the sin delling in me,
for I have knon that there doth not dell in me, that is, in my flesh, good: for to ill is present ith me, and to ork that hich is right I do not find,
for the good that I ill, I do not; but the evil that I do not ill, this I practise.
And if hat I do not ill, this I do, it is no longer I that ork it, but the sin that is delling in me.
I find, then, the la, that hen I desire to do hat is right, ith me the evil is present,

and I behold another la in my members, arring against the la of my mind, and bringing me into captivity to the la of the sin that [is] in my members.
A retched man I [am]! ho shall deliver me out of the body of this death?
I thank God — through Jesus Christ our Lord; so then, I myself indeed ith the mind do serve the la of God, and ith the flesh, the la of sin.
There is, then, no no condemnation to those in Christ Jesus, ho alk not according to the flesh, but according to the Spirit;
for the la of the Spirit of the life in Christ Jesus did set me free from the la of the sin and of the death;
for hat the la as not able to do, in that it as eak through the flesh, God, His on Son having sent in the likeness of sinful flesh, and for sin, did condemn the sin in the flesh,
that the righteousness of the la may be fulfilled in us, ho do not alk according to the flesh, but according to the Spirit.
For those ho are according to the flesh, the things of the flesh do mind; and those according to the Spirit, the things of the Spirit;

because the mind of the flesh [is] enmity to God, for to the la of God it doth not subject itself,
for neither is it able; and those ho are in the flesh are not able to please God.
And ye are not in the flesh, but in the Spirit, if indeed the Spirit of God doth dell in you; and if any one hath not the Spirit of Christ — this one is not His;
and if Christ [is] in you, the body, indeed, [is] dead because of sin, and the Spirit [is] life because of righteousness,
and if the Spirit of Him ho did raise up Jesus out of the dead doth dell in you, He ho did raise up the Christ out of the dead shall quicken also your dying bodies, through His Spirit delling in you.
So, then, brethren, e are debtors, not to the flesh, to live according to the flesh;
for if according to the flesh ye do live, ye are about to die; and if, by the Spirit, the deeds of the body ye put to death, ye shall live;
for as many as are led by the Spirit of God, these are the sons of God;
for ye did not receive a spirit of bondage again for fear, but ye did receive a spirit of adoption in hich e cry, ’Abba — Father.’
The Spirit himself doth testify ith our spirit, that e are children of God;
and if children, also heirs, heirs, indeed, of God, and heirs together of Christ — if, indeed, e suffer together, that e may also be glorified together.
For I reckon that the sufferings of the present time [are] not orthy [to be compared] ith the glory about to be revealed in us;
for the earnest looking out of the creation doth expect the revelation of the sons of God;
for to vanity as the creation made subject — not of its ill, but because of Him ho did subject [it] — in hope,
that also the creation itself shall be set free from the servitude of the corruption to the liberty of the glory of the children of God;
for e have knon that all the creation doth groan together, and doth travail in pain together till no.
And not only [so], but also e ourselves, having the first-fruit of the Spirit, e also ourselves in ourselves do groan, adoption expecting — the redemption of our body;
for in hope e ere saved, and hope beheld is not hope; for hat any one doth behold, hy also doth he hope for [it]?
and if hat e do not behold e hope for, through continuance e expect [it].

And, in like manner also, the Spirit doth help our eaknesses; for, hat e may pray for, as it behoveth [us], e have not knon, but the Spirit himself doth make intercession for us ith groanings unutterable,
and He ho is searching the hearts hath knon hat [is] the mind of the Spirit, because according to God he doth intercede for saints.
And e have knon that to those loving God all things do ork together for good, to those ho are called according to purpose;
because hom He did forekno, He also did fore-appoint, conformed to the image of His Son, that he might be first-born among many brethren;

What, then, shall e say unto these things? if God [is] for us, ho [is] against us?
He ho indeed His on Son did not spare, but for us all did deliver him up, ho shall He not also ith him the all things grant to us?
Who shall lay a charge against the choice ones of God? God [is] He that is declaring righteous,
ho [is] he that is condemning? Christ [is] He that died, yea, rather also, as raised up; ho is also on the right hand of God — ho also doth intercede for us.
Who shall separate us from the love of the Christ? tribulation, or distress, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or peril, or sord?
(according as it hath been ritten — ’For Thy sake e are put to death all the day long, e ere reckoned as sheep of slaughter,’)
but in all these e more than conquer, through him ho loved us;
for I am persuaded that neither death, nor life, nor messengers, nor principalities, nor poers, nor things present,
nor things about to be, nor height, nor depth, nor any other created thing, shall be able to separate us from the love of god, that [is] in Christ Jesus our Lord.
Truth I say in Christ, I lie not, my conscience bearing testimony ith me in the Holy Spirit,
that I have great grief and unceasing pain in my heart —
for I as ishing, I myself, to be anathema from the Christ — for my brethren, my kindred, according to the flesh,
ho are Israelites, hose [is] the adoption, and the glory, and the covenants, and the lagiving, and the service, and the promises,
hose [are] the fathers, and of hom [is] the Christ, according to the flesh, ho is over all, God blessed to the ages. Amen.
And it is not possible that the ord of God hath failed; for not all ho [are] of Israel are these Israel;
nor because they are seed of Abraham [are] all children, but — ’in Isaac shall a seed be called to thee;’
that is, the children of the flesh — these [are] not children of God; but the children of the promise are reckoned for seed;
for the ord of promise [is] this; ’According to this time I ill come, and there shall be to Sarah a son.’
And not only [so], but also Rebecca, having conceived by one — Isaac our father —
(for they being not yet born, neither having done anything good or evil, that the purpose of God, according to choice, might remain; not of orks, but of Him ho is calling,) it as said to her —
’The greater shall serve the less;’
according as it hath been ritten, ’Jacob I did love, and Esau I did hate.’
What, then, shall e say? unrighteousness [is] ith God? let it not be!
for to Moses He saith, ’I ill do kindness to hom I do kindness, and I ill have compassion on hom I have compassion;’
so, then — not of him ho is illing, nor of him ho is running, but of God ho is doing kindness:
for the Writing saith to Pharaoh — ’For this very thing I did raise thee up, that I might she in thee My poer, and that My name might be declared in all the land;’
so, then, to hom He illeth, He doth kindness, and to hom He illeth, He doth harden.
Thou ilt say, then, to me, ’Why yet doth He find fault? for His counsel ho hath resisted?’
nay, but, O man, ho art thou that art ansering again to God? shall the thing formed say to Him ho did form [it], Why me didst thou make thus?
hath not the potter authority over the clay, out of the same lump to make the one vessel to honour, and the one to dishonour?
And if God, illing to she the rath and to make knon His poer, did endure, in much long suffering, vessels of rath fitted for destruction,
and that He might make knon the riches of His glory on vessels of kindness, that He before prepared for glory, hom also He did call — us —
not only out of Jes, but also out of nations,
as also in Hosea He saith, ’I ill call hat [is] not My people — My people; and her not beloved — Beloved,
and it shall be — in the place here it as said to them, Ye [are] not My people; there they shall be called sons of the living God.’
And Isaiah doth cry concerning Israel, ’If the number of the sons of Israel may be as the sand of the sea, the remnant shall be saved;
for a matter He is finishing, and is cutting short in righteousness, because a matter cut short ill the Lord do upon the land.
and according as Isaiah saith before, ’Except the Lord of Sabaoth did leave to us a seed, as Sodom e had become, and as Gomorrah e had been made like.’
What, then, shall e say? that nations ho are not pursuing righteousness did attain to righteousness, and righteousness that [is] of faith,
and Israel, pursuing a la of righteousness, at a la of righteousness did not arrive;
herefore? because — not by faith, but as by orks of la; for they did stumble at the stone of stumbling,

Brethren, the pleasure indeed of my heart, and my supplication that [is] to God for Israel, is — for salvation;
for I bear them testimony that they have a zeal of God, but not according to knoledge,

For Christ is an end of la for righteousness to every one ho is believing,
for Moses doth describe the righteousness that [is] of the la, that, ’The man ho did them shall live in them,’
and the righteousness of faith doth thus speak: ’Thou mayest not say in thine heart, Who shall go up to the heaven,’ that is, Christ to bring don?

Ho then shall they call upon [him] in hom they did not believe? and ho shall they believe [on him] of hom they did not hear? and ho shall they hear apart from one preaching?

But they ere not all obedient to the good tidings, for Isaiah saith, ’Lord, ho did give credence to our report?’

I say, then, Did God cast aay His people? let it not be! for I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin:

’Lord, Thy prophets they did kill, and Thy altars they dug don, and I as left alone, and they seek my life;’

I say, then, Did they stumble that they might fall? let it not be! but by their fall the salvation [is] to the nations, to arouse them to jealousy;

For to you I speak — to the nations — inasmuch as I am indeed an apostle of nations, my ministration I do glorify;

And if certain of the branches ere broken off, and thou, being a ild olive tree, ast graffed in among them, and a fello-partaker of the root and of the fatness of the olive tree didst become —
do not boast against the branches; and if thou dost boast, thou dost not bear the root, but the root thee!
Thou ilt say, then, ’The branches ere broken off, that I might be graffed in;’ right!

Lo, then, goodness and severity of God — upon those indeed ho fell, severity; and upon thee, goodness, if thou mayest remain in the goodness, otherise, thou also shalt be cut off.

For I do not ish you to be ignorant, brethren, of this secret — that ye may not be ise in your on conceits — that hardness in part to Israel hath happened till the fulness of the nations may come in;

and this to them [is] the covenant from Me, hen I may take aay their sins.’
As regards, indeed, the good tidings, [they are] enemies on your account; and as regards the choice — beloved on account of the fathers;

O depth of riches, and isdom and knoledge of God! ho unsearchable His judgments, and untraceable His ays!
for ho did kno the mind of the Lord? or ho did become His counsellor?
or ho did first give to Him, and it shall be given back to him again?
because of Him, and through Him, and to Him [are] the all things; to Him [is] the glory — to the ages. Amen.
I call upon you, therefore, brethren, through the compassions of God, to present your bodies a sacrifice — living, sanctified, acceptable to God — your intelligent service;
and be not conformed to this age, but be transformed by the reneing of your mind, for your proving hat [is] the ill of God — the good, and acceptable, and perfect.

For I say, through the grace that as given to me, to every one ho is among you, not to think above hat it behoveth to think; but to think so as to think isely, as to each God did deal a measure of faith,

so e, the many, one body are in Christ, and members each one of one another.
And having gifts, different according to the grace that as given to us; hether prophecy — ’According to the proportion of faith!’
or ministration — ’In the ministration!’ or he ho is teaching — ’In the teaching!’

The love unfeigned: abhorring the evil; cleaving to the good;
in the love of brethren, to one another kindly affectioned: in the honour going before one another;
in the diligence not slothful; in the spirit fervent; the Lord serving;
in the hope rejoicing; in the tribulation enduring; in the prayer persevering;
to the necessities of the saints communicating; the hospitality pursuing.
Bless those persecuting you; bless, and curse not;
to rejoice ith the rejoicing, and to eep ith the eeping,
of the same mind one toard another, not minding the high things, but ith the loly going along; become not ise in your on conceit;
giving back to no one evil for evil; providing right things before all men.
If possible — so far as in you — ith all men being in peace;
not avenging yourselves, beloved, but give place to the rath, for it hath been ritten, ’Vengeance [is] Mine,
I ill recompense again, saith the Lord;’ if, then, thine enemy doth hunger, feed him; if he doth thirst, give him drink; for this doing, coals of fire thou shalt heap upon his head;
Be not overcome by the evil, but overcome, in the good, the evil.
Let every soul to the higher authorities be subject, for there is no authority except from God, and the authorities existing are appointed by God,
so that he ho is setting himself against the authority, against God’s ordinance hath resisted; and those resisting, to themselves shall receive judgment.
For those ruling are not a terror to the good orks, but to the evil; and dost thou ish not to be afraid of the authority? that hich is good be doing, and thou shalt have praise from it,

for of God it is a ministrant to thee for good; and if that hich is evil thou mayest do, be fearing, for not in vain doth it bear the sord; for of God it is a ministrant, an avenger for rath to him ho is doing that hich is evil.

To no one oe anything, except to love one another; for he ho is loving the other — la he hath fulfilled,

for, ’Thou shalt not commit adultery, Thou shalt do no murder, Thou shalt not steal, Thou shalt not bear false testimony, Thou shalt not covet;’ and if there is any other command, in this ord it is summed up, in this: ’Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself;’
the love to the neighbour doth ork no ill; the love, therefore, [is] the fulness of la.
And this, knoing the time, that for us, the hour already [is] to be aroused out of sleep, for no nearer [is] our salvation than hen e did believe;

as in day-time, let us alk becomingly; not in revellings and drunkennesses, not in chamberings and lasciviousnesses, not in strife and emulation;

And him ho is eak in the faith receive ye — not to determinations of reasonings;

Thou — ho art thou that art judging another’s domestic? to his on master he doth stand or fall; and he shall be made to stand, for God is able to make him stand.

He ho is regarding the day, to the Lord he doth regard [it], and he ho is not regarding the day, to the Lord he doth not regard [it]. He ho is eating, to the Lord he doth eat, for he doth give thanks to God; and he ho is not eating, to the Lord he doth not eat, and doth give thanks to God.
For none of us to himself doth live, and none to himself doth die;
for both, if e may live, to the Lord e live; if also e may die, to the Lord e die; both then if e may live, also if e may die, e are the Lord’s;
for because of this Christ both died and rose again, and lived again, that both of dead and of living he may be Lord.
And thou, hy dost thou judge thy brother? or again, thou, hy dost thou set at nought thy brother? for e shall all stand at the tribunal of the Christ;
for it hath been ritten, ’I live! saith the Lord — to Me bo shall every knee, and every tongue shall confess to God;’
so, then, each of us concerning himself shall give reckoning to God;
no longer, therefore, may e judge one another, but this judge ye rather, not to put a stumbling-stone before the brother, or an offence.
I have knon, and am persuaded, in the Lord Jesus, that nothing [is] unclean of itself, except to him ho is reckoning anything to be unclean — to that one [it is] unclean;
and if through victuals thy brother is grieved, no more dost thou alk according to love; do not ith thy victuals destroy that one for hom Christ died.
Let not, then, your good be evil spoken of,
for the reign of God is not eating and drinking, but righteousness, and peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit;
for he ho in these things is serving the Christ, [is] acceptable to God and approved of men.
So, then, the things of peace may e pursue, and the things of building up one another;
for the sake of victuals cast not don the ork of God; all things, indeed, [are] pure, but evil [is] to the man ho is eating through stumbling.
Right [it is] not to eat flesh, nor to drink ine, nor to [do anything] in hich thy brother doth stumble, or is made to fall, or is eak.
Thou hast faith! to thyself have [it] before God; happy is he ho is not judging himself in hat he doth approve,
and he ho is making a difference, if he may eat, hath been condemned, because [it is] not of faith; and all that [is] not of faith is sin.
And e ought — e ho are strong — to bear the infirmities of the eak, and not to please ourselves;
for let each one of us please the neighbour for good, unto edification,
for even the Christ did not please himself, but, according as it hath been ritten, ’The reproaches of those reproaching Thee fell upon me;’
for, as many things as ere ritten before, for our instruction ere ritten before, that through the endurance, and the exhortation of the Writings, e might have the hope.
And may the God of the endurance, and of the exhortation, give to you to have the same mind toard one another, according to Christ Jesus;
that ith one accord — ith one mouth — ye may glorify the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ;
herefore receive ye one another, according as also the Christ did receive us, to the glory of God.
And I say Jesus Christ to have become a ministrant of circumcision for the truth of God, to confirm the promises to the fathers,
and the nations for kindness to glorify God, according as it hath been ritten, ’Because of this I ill confess to Thee among nations, and to Thy name I ill sing praise,’
and again it saith, ’Rejoice ye nations, ith His people;’
and again, ’Praise the Lord, all ye nations; and laud Him, all ye peoples;’
and again, Isaiah saith, ’There shall be the root of Jesse, and he ho is rising to rule nations — upon him shall nations hope;’
and the God of the hope shall fill you ith all joy and peace in the believing, for your abounding in the hope in poer of the Holy Spirit.
And I am persuaded, my brethren — I myself also — concerning you, that ye yourselves also are full of goodness, having been filled ith all knoledge, able also one another to admonish;
and the more boldly I did rite to you, brethren, in part, as putting you in mind, because of the grace that is given to me by God,
for my being a servant of Jesus Christ to the nations, acting as priest in the good nes of God, that the offering up of the nations may become acceptable, sanctified by the Holy Spirit.
I have, then, a boasting in Christ Jesus, in the things pertaining to God,
for I ill not dare to speak anything of the things that Christ did not ork through me, to obedience of nations, by ord and deed,
in poer of signs and onders, in poer of the Spirit of God; so that I, from Jerusalem, and in a circle as far as Illyricum, have fully preached the good nes of the Christ;
and so counting it honour to proclaim good nes, not here Christ as named — that upon another’s foundation I might not build —
but according as it hath been ritten, ’To hom it as not told concerning him, they shall see; and they ho have not heard, shall understand.’
Wherefore, also, I as hindered many times from coming unto you,
and no, no longer having place in these parts, and having a longing to come unto you for many years,
hen I may go on to Spain I ill come unto you, for I hope in going through, to see you, and by you to be set forard thither, if of you first, in part, I shall be filled.
And, no, I go on to Jerusalem, ministering to the saints;
for it pleased Macedonia and Achaia ell to make a certain contribution for the poor of the saints ho [are] in Jerusalem;
for it pleased ell, and their debtors they are, for if in their spiritual things the nations did participate, they ought also, in the fleshly things, to minister to them.
This, then, having finished, and having sealed to them this fruit, I ill return through you, to Spain;
and I have knon that coming unto you — in the fulness of the blessing of the good nes of Christ I shall come.
And I call upon you, brethren, through our Lord Jesus Christ, and through the love of the Spirit, to strive together ith me in the prayers for me unto God,
that I may be delivered from those not believing in Judea, and that my ministration, that [is] for Jerusalem, may become acceptable to the saints;
that in joy I may come unto you, through the ill of God, and may be refreshed ith you,
and the God of the peace [be] ith you all. Amen.
And I commend you to Phebe our sister — being a ministrant of the assembly that [is] in Cenchrea —
that ye may receive her in the Lord, as doth become saints, and may assist her in hatever matter she may have need of you — for she also became a leader of many, and of myself.
Salute Priscilla and Aquilas, my fello-orkmen in Christ Jesus —
ho for my life their on neck did lay don, to hom not only I give thanks, but also all the assemblies of the nations —
and the assembly at their house; salute Epaenetus, my beloved, ho is first-fruit of Achaia to Christ.
Salute Mary, ho did labour much for us;
salute Andronicus and Junias, my kindred, and my fello-captives, ho are of note among the apostles, ho also have been in Christ before me.
Salute Amplias, my beloved in the Lord;
salute Arbanus, our fello-orkman in Christ, and Stachys, my beloved;
salute Apelles, the approved in Christ; salute those of the [household] of Aristobulus;
salute Herodion, my kinsman; salute those of the [household] of Narcissus, ho are in the Lord;
salute Tryphaena, and Tryphosa, ho are labouring in the Lord; salute Persis, the beloved, ho did labour much in the Lord.
Salute Rufus, the choice one in the Lord, and his mother and mine,
salute Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermas, Patrobas, Hermes, and the brethren ith them;
salute Philologus, and Julias, Nereus, and his sister, and Olympas, and all the saints ith them;
salute one another in a holy kiss; the assemblies of Christ do salute you.
And I call upon you, brethren, to mark those ho the divisions and the stumbling-blocks, contrary to the teaching that ye did learn, are causing, and turn ye aay from them;
for such our Lord Jesus Christ do not serve, but their on belly; and through the good ord and fair speech they deceive the hearts of the harmless,
for your obedience did reach to all; I rejoice, therefore, as regards you, and I ish you to be ise, indeed, as to the good, and harmless as to the evil;
and the God of the peace shall bruise the Adversary under your feet quickly; the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ [be] ith you. Amen!
Salute you do Timotheus, my fello-orkman, and Lucius, and Jason, and Sosipater, my kindred;
I Tertius salute you (ho rote the letter) in the Lord;
salute you doth Gaius, my host, and of the hole assembly; salute you doth Erastus, the steard of the city, and Quartus the brother,
the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ [be] ith you all. Amen.
And to Him ho is able to establish you, according to my good nes, and the preaching of Jesus Christ, according to the revelation of the secret, in the times of the ages having been kept silent,
and no having been made manifest, also, through prophetic ritings, according to a command of the age-during God, having been made knon to all the nations for obedience of faith —
to the only ise God, through Jesus Christ, to him [be] glory to the ages. Amen.
Paul, a called apostle of Jesus Christ, through the ill of God, and Sosthenes the brother,
to the assembly of God that is in Corinth, to those sanctified in Christ Jesus, called saints, ith all those calling upon the name of our Lord Jesus Christ in every place — both theirs and ours:
Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ!
I give thanks to my God alays concerning you for the grace of God that as given to you in Christ Jesus,
that in every thing ye ere enriched in him, in all discourse and all knoledge,
according as the testimony of the Christ as confirmed in you,
so that ye are not behind in any gift, aiting for the revelation of our Lord Jesus Christ,
ho also shall confirm you unto the end — unblamable in the day of our Lord Jesus Christ;
faithful [is] God, through hom ye ere called to the felloship of His Son Jesus Christ our Lord.

And I call upon you, brethren, through the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that the same thing ye may all say, and there may not be divisions among you, and ye may be perfected in the same mind, and in the same judgment,
for it as signified to me concerning you, my brethren, by those of Chloe, that contentions are among you;
and I say this, that each one of you saith, ’I, indeed, am of Paul’ — ’and I of Apollos,’ — ’and I of Cephas,’ — ’and I of Christ.’
Hath the Christ been divided? as Paul crucified for you? or to the name of Paul ere ye baptized;
I give thanks to God that no one of you did I baptize, except Crispus and Gaius —
that no one may say that to my on name I did baptize;
and I did baptize also Stephanas’ household — further, I have not knon if I did baptize any other.
For Christ did not send me to baptize, but — to proclaim good nes; not in isdom of discourse, that the cross of the Christ may not be made of none effect;
for the ord of the cross to those indeed perishing is foolishness, and to us — those being saved — it is the poer of God,
for it hath been ritten, ’I ill destroy the isdom of the ise, and the intelligence of the intelligent I ill bring to nought;’
here [is] the ise? here the scribe? here a disputer of this age? did not God make foolish the isdom of this orld?
for, seeing in the isdom of God the orld through the isdom kne not God, it did please God through the foolishness of the preaching to save those believing.
Since also Jes ask a sign, and Greeks seek isdom,
also e — e preach Christ crucified, to Jes, indeed, a stumbling-block, and to Greeks foolishness,
and to those called — both Jes and Greeks — Christ the poer of God, and the isdom of God,
because the foolishness of God is iser than men, and the eakness of God is stronger than men;
for see your calling, brethren, that not many [are] ise according to the flesh, not many mighty, not many noble;
but the foolish things of the orld did God choose, that the ise He may put to shame; and the eak things of the orld did God choose that He may put to shame the strong;
and the base things of the orld, and the things despised did God choose, and the things that are not, that the things that are He may make useless —
that no flesh may glory before Him;
and of Him ye — ye are in Christ Jesus, ho became to us from God isdom, righteousness also, and sanctification, and redemption,
that, according as it hath been ritten, ’He ho is glorying — in the Lord let him glory.’
And I, having come unto you, brethren, came — not in superiority of discourse or isdom — declaring to you the testimony of God,
for I decided not to kno any thing among you, except Jesus Christ, and him crucified;
and I, in eakness, and in fear, and in much trembling, as ith you;
and my ord and my preaching as not in persuasive ords of human isdom, but in demonstration of the Spirit and of poer —
that your faith may not be in the isdom of men, but in the poer of God.
And isdom e speak among the perfect, and isdom not of this age, nor of the rulers of this age — of those becoming useless,
but e speak the hidden isdom of God in a secret, that God foreordained before the ages to our glory,
hich no one of the rulers of this age did kno, for if they had knon, the Lord of the glory they ould not have crucified;
but, according as it hath been ritten, ’What eye did not see, and ear did not hear, and upon the heart of man came not up, hat God did prepare for those loving Him — ’
but to us did God reveal [them] through His Spirit, for the Spirit all things doth search, even the depths of God,
for ho of men hath knon the things of the man, except the spirit of the man that [is] in him? so also the things of God no one hath knon, except the Spirit of God.
And e the spirit of the orld did not receive, but the Spirit that [is] of God, that e may kno the things conferred by God on us,
hich things also e speak, not in ords taught by human isdom, but in those taught by the Holy Spirit, ith spiritual things spiritual things comparing,
and the natural man doth not receive the things of the Spirit of God, for to him they are foolishness, and he is not able to kno [them], because spiritually they are discerned;
and he ho is spiritual, doth discern indeed all things, and he himself is by no one discerned;
for ho did kno the mind of the Lord that he shall instruct Him? and e — e have the mind of Christ.
And I, brethren, as not able to speak to you as to spiritual, but as to fleshly — as to babes in Christ;
ith milk I fed you, and not ith meat, for ye ere not yet able, but not even yet are ye no able,
for yet ye are fleshly, for here [there is] among you envying, and strife, and divisions, are ye not fleshly, and in the manner of men do alk?
for hen one may say, ’I, indeed, am of Paul;’ and another, ’I — of Apollos;’ are ye not fleshly?
Who, then, is Paul, and ho Apollos, but ministrants through hom ye did believe, and to each as the Lord gave?
I planted, Apollos atered, but God as giving groth;
so that neither is he ho is planting anything, nor he ho is atering, but He ho is giving groth — God;
and he ho is planting and he ho is atering are one, and each his on reard shall receive, according to his on labour,
for of God e are fello-orkmen; God’s tillage, God’s building ye are.
According to the grace of God that as given to me, as a ise master-builder, a foundation I have laid, and another doth build on [it],
for other foundation no one is able to lay except that hich is laid, hich is Jesus the Christ;
and if any one doth build upon this foundation gold, silver, precious stones, ood, hay, stra —
of each the ork shall become manifest, for the day shall declare [it], because in fire it is revealed, and the ork of each, hat kind it is, the fire shall prove;
if of any one the ork doth remain that he built on [it], a age he shall receive;
if of any the ork is burned up, he shall suffer loss; and himself shall be saved, but so as through fire.
have ye not knon that ye are a sanctuary of God, and the Spirit of God doth dell in you?
if any one the sanctuary of God doth aste, him shall God aste; for the sanctuary of God is holy, the hich ye are.
Let no one deceive himself; if any one doth seem to be ise among you in this age — let him become a fool, that he may become ise,
for the isdom of this orld is foolishness ith God, for it hath been ritten, ’Who is taking the ise in their craftiness;’
and again, ’The Lord doth kno the reasonings of the ise, that they are vain.’
So then, let no one glory in men, for all things are yours,
hether Paul, or Apollos, or Cephas, or the orld, or life, or death, or things present, or things about to be — all are yours,
and ye [are] Christ’s, and Christ [is] God’s.
Let a man so reckon us as officers of Christ, and steards of the secrets of God,
and as to the rest, it is required in the steards that one may be found faithful,
and to me it is for a very little thing that by you I may be judged, or by man’s day, but not even myself do I judge,
for of nothing to myself have I been conscious, but not in this have I been declared right — and he ho is discerning me is the Lord:

so, then, nothing before the time judge ye, till the Lord may come, ho ill both bring to light the hidden things of the darkness, and ill manifest the counsels of the hearts, and then the praise shall come to each from God.

And these things, brethren, I did transfer to myself and to Apollos because of you, that in us ye may learn not to think above that hich hath been ritten, that ye may not be puffed up one for one against the other,
for ho doth make thee to differ? and hat hast thou, that thou didst not receive? and if thou didst also receive, hy dost thou glory as not having received?
Already ye are having been filled, already ye ere rich, apart from us ye did reign, and I ould also ye did reign, that e also ith you may reign together,
for I think that God did set forth us the apostles last — as appointed to death, because a spectacle e became to the orld, and messengers, and men;
e [are] fools because of Christ, and ye ise in Christ; e [are] ailing, and ye strong; ye glorious, and e dishonoured;
unto the present hour e both hunger, and thirst, and are naked, and are buffeted, and ander about,
and labour, orking ith [our] on hands; being reviled, e bless; being persecuted, e suffer;
being spoken evil of, e entreat; as filth of the orld e did become — of all things an offscouring — till no.
Not [as] putting you to shame do I rite these things, but as my beloved children I do admonish,
for if a myriad of child-conductors ye may have in Christ, yet not many fathers; for in Christ Jesus, through the good nes, I — I did beget you;
I call upon you, therefore, become ye folloers of me;
because of this I sent to you Timotheus, ho is my child, beloved and faithful in the Lord, ho shall remind you of my ays in Christ, according as everyhere in every assembly I teach.
And as if I ere not coming unto you certain ere puffed up;
but I ill come quickly unto you, if the Lord may ill, and I ill kno not the ord of those puffed up, but the poer;
for not in ord is the reign of God, but in poer?
hat do ye ish? ith a rod shall I come unto you, or in love, ith a spirit also of meekness?
Whoredom is actually heard of among you, and such horedom as is not even named among the nations — as that one hath the ife of the father! —
and ye are having been puffed up, and did not rather mourn, that he may be removed out of the midst of you ho did this ork,
for I indeed, as being absent as to the body, and present as to the spirit, have already judged, as being present, him ho so rought this thing:
in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ — ye being gathered together, also my spirit — ith the poer of our Lord Jesus Christ,
to deliver up such a one to the Adversary for the destruction of the flesh, that the spirit may be saved in the day of the Lord Jesus.
Not good [is] your glorying; have ye not knon that a little leaven the hole lump doth leaven?
cleanse out, therefore, the old leaven, that ye may be a ne lump, according as ye are unleavened, for also our passover for us as sacrificed — Christ,
so that e may keep the feast, not ith old leaven, nor ith the leaven of evil and ickedness, but ith unleavened food of sincerity and truth.
I did rite to you in the epistle, not to keep company ith horemongers —
and not certainly ith the horemongers of this orld, or ith the covetous, or extortioners, or idolaters, seeing ye ought then to go forth out of the orld —

and no, I did rite to you not to keep company ith [him], if any one, being named a brother, may be a horemonger, or covetous, or an idolater, or a railer, or a drunkard, or an extortioner — ith such a one not even to eat together;
for hat have I also those ithout to judge? those ithin do ye not judge?
and those ithout God doth judge; and put ye aay the evil from among yourselves.
Dare any one of you, having a matter ith the other, go to be judged before the unrighteous, and not before the saints?
have ye not knon that the saints shall judge the orld? and if by you the orld is judged, are ye unorthy of the smaller judgments?
have ye not knon that e shall judge messengers? hy not then the things of life?
of the things of life, indeed, then, if ye may have judgment, those despised in the assembly — these cause ye to sit;
unto your shame I speak: so there is not among you one ise man, not even one, ho shall be able to discern in the midst of his brethren!
but brother ith brother doth go to be judged, and this before unbelievers!
Already, indeed, then, there is altogether a fault among you, that ye have judgments ith one another; herefore do ye not rather suffer injustice? herefore be ye not rather defrauded?
but ye — ye do injustice, and ye defraud, and these — brethren!
have ye not knon that the unrighteous the reign of God shall not inherit? be not led astray; neither horemongers, nor idolaters, nor adulterers, nor effeminate, nor sodomites,
nor thieves, nor covetous, nor drunkards, nor revilers, nor extortioners, the reign of God shall inherit.
And certain of you ere these! but ye ere ashed, but ye ere sanctified, but ye ere declared righteous, in the name of the Lord Jesus, and in the Spirit of our God.
All things are laful to me, but all things are not profitable; all things are laful to me, but I — I ill not be under authority by any;
the meats [are] for the belly, and the belly for the meats. And God both this and these shall make useless; and the body [is] not for horedom, but for the Lord, and the Lord for the body;
and God both the Lord did raise, and us ill raise up through His poer.
Have ye not knon that your bodies are members of Christ? having taken, then, the members of the Christ, shall I make [them] members of an harlot? let it be not!
have ye not knon that he ho is joined to the harlot is one body? ’for they shall be — saith He — the to for one flesh.’
And he ho is joined to the Lord is one spirit;
flee the horedom; every sin — hatever a man may commit — is ithout the body, and he ho is committing horedom, against his on body doth sin.
Have ye not knon that your body is a sanctuary of the Holy Spirit in you, hich ye have from God? and ye are not your on,
for ye ere bought ith a price; glorify, then, God in your body and in your spirit, hich are God’s.
And concerning the things of hich ye rote to me: good [it is] for a man not to touch a oman,
and because of the horedom let each man have his on ife, and let each oman have her proper husband;
to the ife let the husband the due benevolence render, and in like manner also the ife to the husband;
the ife over her on body hath not authority, but the husband; and, in like manner also, the husband over his on body hath not authority, but the ife.
Defraud not one another, except by consent for a time, that ye may be free for fasting and prayer, and again may come together, that the Adversary may not tempt you because of your incontinence;
and this I say by ay of concurrence — not of command,
for I ish all men to be even as I myself [am]; but each his on gift hath of God, one indeed thus, and one thus.
And I say to the unmarried and to the idos: it is good for them if they may remain even as I [am];
and if they have not continence — let them marry, for it is better to marry than to burn;
and to the married I announce — not I, but the Lord — let not a ife separate from a husband:
but and if she may separate, let her remain unmarried, or to the husband let her be reconciled, and let not a husband send aay a ife.
And to the rest I speak — not the Lord — if any brother hath a ife unbelieving, and she is pleased to dell ith him, let him not send her aay;
and a oman ho hath a husband unbelieving, and he is pleased to dell ith her, let her not send him aay;
for the unbelieving husband hath been sanctified in the ife, and the unbelieving ife hath been sanctified in the husband; otherise your children are unclean, but no they are holy.
And, if the unbelieving doth separate himself — let him separate himself: the brother or the sister is not under servitude in such [cases], and in peace hath God called us;
for hat, hast thou knon, O ife, hether the husband thou shalt save? or hat, hast thou knon, O husband, hether the ife thou shalt save?
if not, as God did distribute to each, as the Lord hath called each — so let him alk; and thus in all the assemblies do I direct:
being circumcised — as any one called? let him not become uncircumcised; in uncircumcision as any one called? let him not be circumcised;
the circumcision is nothing, and the uncircumcision is nothing — but a keeping of the commands of God.
Each in the calling in hich he as called — in this let him remain;
a servant — ast thou called? be not anxious; but if also thou art able to become free — use [it] rather;
for he ho [is] in the Lord — having been called a servant — is the Lord’s freedman: in like manner also he the freeman, having been called, is servant of Christ:
ith a price ye ere bought, become not servants of men;
each, in that in hich he as called, brethren, in this let him remain ith God.
And concerning the virgins, a command of the Lord I have not; and I give judgment as having obtained kindness from the Lord to be faithful:
I suppose, therefore, this to be good because of the present necessity, that [it is] good for a man that the matter be thus: —
Hast thou been bound to a ife? seek not to be loosed; hast thou been loosed from a ife? seek not a ife.
But and if thou mayest marry, thou didst not sin; and if the virgin may marry, she did not sin; and such shall have tribulation in the flesh: and I spare you.
And this I say, brethren, the time henceforth is having been shortened — that both those having ives may be as not having;
and those eeping, as not eeping; and those rejoicing, as not rejoicing; and those buying, as not possessing;
and those using this orld, as not using [it] up; for passing aay is the fashion of this orld.
And I ish you to be ithout anxiety; the unmarried is anxious for the things of the Lord, ho he shall please the Lord;
and the married is anxious for the things of the orld, ho he shall please the ife.

The ife and the virgin have been distinguished: the unmarried is anxious for the things of the Lord, that she may be holy both in body and in spirit, and the married is anxious for the things of the orld, ho she shall please the husband.
And this for your on profit I say: not that I may cast a noose upon you, but for the seemliness and devotedness to the Lord, undistractedly,
and if any one doth think [it] to be unseemly to his virgin, if she may be beyond the bloom of age, and it ought so to be, hat he illeth let him do; he doth not sin — let him marry.
And he ho hath stood stedfast in the heart — not having necessity — and hath authority over his on ill, and this he hath determined in his heart — to keep his on virgin — doth ell;
so that both he ho is giving in marriage doth ell, and he ho is not giving in marriage doth better.
A ife hath been bound by la as long time as her husband may live, and if her husband may sleep, she is free to be married to hom she ill — only in the Lord;
and she is happier if she may so remain — according to my judgment; and I think I also have the Spirit of God.
And concerning the things sacrificed to idols, e have knon that e all have knoledge: knoledge puffeth up, but love buildeth up;
and if any one doth think to kno anything, he hath not yet knon anything according as it behoveth [him] to kno;
and if any one doth love God, this one hath been knon by Him.
Concerning the eating then of the things sacrificed to idols, e have knon that an idol [is] nothing in the orld, and that there is no other God except one;
for even if there are those called gods, hether in heaven, hether upon earth — as there are gods many and lords many —
yet to us [is] one God, the Father, of hom [are] the all things, and e to Him; and one Lord, Jesus Christ, through hom [are] the all things, and e through Him;
but not in all men [is] the knoledge, and certain ith conscience of the idol, till no, as a thing sacrificed to an idol do eat [it], and their conscience, being eak, is defiled.
But victuals do not commend us to God, for neither if e may eat are e in advance; nor if e may not eat, are e behind;
but see, lest this privilege of yours may become a stumbling-block to the infirm,
for if any one may see thee that hast knoledge in an idol’s temple reclining at meat — shall not his conscience — he being infirm — be emboldened to eat the things sacrificed to idols,
and the brother ho is infirm shall perish by thy knoledge, because of hom Christ died?
and thus sinning in regard to the brethren, and smiting their eak conscience — in regard to Christ ye sin;
herefore, if victuals cause my brother to stumble, I may eat no flesh — to the age — that my brother I may not cause to stumble.
Am not I an apostle? am not I free? Jesus Christ our Lord have I not seen? my ork are not ye in the Lord?
if to others I am not an apostle — yet doubtless to you I am; for the seal of my apostleship are ye in the Lord.
My defence to those ho examine me in this;
have e not authority to eat and to drink?
have e not authority a sister — a ife — to lead about, as also the other apostles, and the brethren of the Lord, and Cephas?
or only I and Barnabas, have e not authority — not to ork?
ho doth serve as a soldier at his on charges at any time? ho doth plant a vineyard, and of its fruit doth not eat? or ho doth feed a flock, and of the milk of the flock doth not eat?
According to man do I speak these things? or doth not also the la say these things?
for in the la of Moses it hath been ritten, ’thou shalt not muzzle an ox treading out corn;’ for the oxen doth God care?
or because of us by all means doth He say [it]? yes, because of us it as ritten, because in hope ought the ploer to plo, and he ho is treading [ought] of his hope to partake in hope.
If e to you the spiritual things did so — great [is it] if e your fleshly things do reap?
if others do partake of the authority over you — not e more? but e did not use this authority, but all things e bear, that e may give no hindrance to the good nes of the Christ.
Have ye not knon that those orking about the things of the temple — of the temple do eat, and those aiting at the altar — ith the altar are partakers?
so also did the Lord direct to those proclaiming the good nes: of the good nes to live.
And I have used none of these things; neither did I rite these things that it may be so done in my case, for [it is] good for me rather to die, than that any one may make my glorying void;
for if I may proclaim good nes, it is no glorying for me, for necessity is laid upon me, and oe is to me if I may not proclaim good nes;
for if illing I do this, I have a reard; and if unillingly — ith a steardship I have been entrusted!
What, then, is my reard? — that proclaiming good nes, ithout charge I shall make the good nes of the Christ, not to abuse my authority in the good nes;
for being free from all men, to all men I made myself servant, that the more I might gain;
and I became to the Jes as a Je, that Jes I might gain; to those under la as under la, that those under la I might gain;
to those ithout la, as ithout la — (not being ithout la to God, but ithin la to Christ) — that I might gain those ithout la;
I became to the infirm as infirm, that the infirm I might gain; to all men I have become all things, that by all means I may save some.
And this I do because of the good nes, that a fello-partaker of it I may become;
have ye not knon that those running in a race — all indeed run, but one doth receive the prize? so run ye, that ye may obtain;
and every one ho is striving, is in all things temperate; these, indeed, then, that a corruptible cron they may receive, but e an incorruptible;
I, therefore, thus run, not as uncertainly, thus I fight, as not beating air;
but I chastise my body, and bring [it] into servitude, lest by any means, having preached to others — I myself may become disapproved.
And I do not ish you to be ignorant, brethren, that all our fathers ere under the cloud, and all passed through the sea,
and all to Moses ere baptized in the cloud, and in the sea;
and all the same spiritual food did eat,
and all the same spiritual drink did drink, for they ere drinking of a spiritual rock folloing them, and the rock as the Christ;
but in the most of them God as not ell pleased, for they ere stren in the ilderness,
and those things became types of us, for our not passionately desiring evil things, as also these did desire.
Neither become ye idolaters, as certain of them, as it hath been ritten, ’The people sat don to eat and to drink, and stood up to play;’
neither may e commit horedom, as certain of them did commit horedom, and there fell in one day tenty-three thousand;
neither may e tempt the Christ, as also certain of them did tempt, and by the serpents did perish;
neither murmur ye, as also some of them did murmur, and did perish by the destroyer.
And all these things as types did happen to those persons, and they ere ritten for our admonition, to hom the end of the ages did come,
so that he ho is thinking to stand — let him observe, lest he fall.

No temptation hath taken you — except human; and God is faithful, ho ill not suffer you to be tempted above hat ye are able, but He ill make, ith the temptation, also the outlet, for your being able to bear [it].
Wherefore, my beloved, flee from the idolatry;
as to ise men I speak — judge ye hat I say:
The cup of the blessing that e bless — is it not the felloship of the blood of the Christ? the bread that e break — is it not the felloship of the body of the Christ?
because one bread, one body, are e the many — for e all of the one bread do partake.

hat then do I say? that an idol is anything? or that a sacrifice offered to an idol is anything? —
[no,] but that the things that the nations sacrifice — they sacrifice to demons and not to God; and I do not ish you to come into the felloship of the demons.
Ye are not able the cup of the Lord to drink, and the cup of demons; ye are not able of the table of the Lord to partake, and of the table of demons;
do e arouse the Lord to jealousy? are e stronger than He?
All things to me are laful, but all things are not profitable; all things to me are laful, but all things do not build up;
let no one seek his on — but each another’s.
Whatever in the meat-market is sold eat ye, not inquiring, because of the conscience,
for the Lord’s [is] the earth, and its fulness;
and if any one of the unbelieving do call you, and ye ish to go, all that is set before you eat, nothing inquiring, because of the conscience;
and if any one may say to you, ’This is a thing sacrificed to an idol,’ — do not eat, because of that one ho sheed [it], and of the conscience, for the Lord’s [is] the earth and its fulness:
and conscience, I say, not of thyself, but of the other, for hy [is it] that my liberty is judged by another’s conscience?
and if I thankfully do partake, hy am I evil spoken of, for that for hich I give thanks?
Whether, then, ye eat, or drink, or do anything, do all to the glory of God;

as I also in all things do please all, not seeking my on profit, but that of many — that they may be saved.
Folloers of me become ye, as I also [am] of Christ.
And I praise you, brethren, that in all things ye remember me, and according as I did deliver to you, the deliverances ye keep,
and I ish you to kno that of every man the head is the Christ, and the head of a oman is the husband, and the head of Christ is God.
Every man praying or prophesying, having the head covered, doth dishonour his head,
and every oman praying or prophesying ith the head uncovered, doth dishonour her on head, for it is one and the same thing ith her being shaven,

for a man, indeed, ought not to cover the head, being the image and glory of God, and a oman is the glory of a man,

but neither [is] a man apart from a oman, nor a oman apart from a man, in the Lord,
for as the oman [is] of the man, so also the man [is] through the oman, and the all things [are] of God.
In your on selves judge ye; is it seemly for a oman uncovered to pray to God?
doth not even nature itself teach you, that if a man indeed have long hair, a dishonour it is to him?
and a oman, if she have long hair, a glory it is to her, because the hair instead of a covering hath been given to her;
and if any one doth think to be contentious, e have no such custom, neither the assemblies of God.
And this declaring, I give no praise, because not for the better, but for the orse ye come together;
for first, indeed, ye coming together in an assembly, I hear of divisions being among you, and partly I believe [it],
for it behoveth sects also to be among you, that those approved may become manifest among you;
ye, then, coming together at the same place — it is not to eat the Lord’s supper;
for each his on supper doth take before in the eating, and one is hungry, and another is drunk;
hy, have ye not houses to eat and to drink in? or the assembly of God do ye despise, and shame those not having? hat may I say to you? shall I praise you in this? I do not praise!
For I — I received from the Lord that hich also I did deliver to you, that the Lord Jesus in the night in hich he as delivered up, took bread,
and having given thanks, he brake, and said, ’Take ye, eat ye, this is my body, that for you is being broken; this do ye — to the remembrance of me.’
In like manner also the cup after the supping, saying, ’This cup is the ne covenant in my blood; this do ye, as often as ye may drink [it] — to the remembrance of me;’
for as often as ye may eat this bread, and this cup may drink, the death of the Lord ye do she forth — till he may come;
so that hoever may eat this bread or may drink the cup of the Lord unorthily, guilty he shall be of the body and blood of the Lord:
and let a man be proving himself, and so of the bread let him eat, and of the cup let him drink;
for he ho is eating and drinking unorthily, judgment to himself he doth eat and drink — not discerning the body of the Lord.
Because of this, among you many [are] eak and sickly, and sleep do many;
for if ourselves e ere discerning, e ould not be being judged,
and being judged by the Lord, e are chastened, that ith the orld e may not be condemned;
so then, my brethren, coming together to eat, for one another ait ye;
and if any one is hungry, at home let him eat, that to judgment ye may not come together; and the rest, henever I may come, I shall arrange.
And concerning the spiritual things, brethren, I do not ish you to be ignorant;
ye have knon that ye ere nations, unto the dumb idols — as ye ere led — being carried aay;
herefore, I give you to understand that no one, in the Spirit of God speaking, saith Jesus [is] anathema, and no one is able to say Jesus [is] Lord, except in the Holy Spirit.
And there are diversities of gifts, and the same Spirit;
and there are diversities of ministrations, and the same Lord;
and there are diversities of orkings, and it is the same God — ho is orking the all in all.
And to each hath been given the manifestation of the Spirit for profit;
for to one through the Spirit hath been given a ord of isdom, and to another a ord of knoledge, according to the same Spirit;
and to another faith in the same Spirit, and to another gifts of healings in the same Spirit;
and to another in-orkings of mighty deeds; and to another prophecy; and to another discernings of spirits; and to another [divers] kinds of tongues; and to another interpretation of tongues:
and all these doth ork the one and the same Spirit, dividing to each severally as he intendeth.
For, even as the body is one, and hath many members, and all the members of the one body, being many, are one body, so also [is] the Christ,
for also in one Spirit e all to one body ere baptized, hether Jes or Greeks, hether servants or freemen, and all into one Spirit ere made to drink,
for also the body is not one member, but many;
if the foot may say, ’Because I am not a hand, I am not of the body;’ it is not, because of this, not of the body;
and if the ear may say, ’Because I am not an eye, I am not of the body;’ it is not, because of this, not of the body?
If the hole body [ere] an eye, here the hearing? if the hole hearing, here the smelling?
and no, God did set the members each one of them in the body, according as He illed,
and if all ere one member, here the body?
and no, indeed, [are] many members, and one body;
and an eye is not able to say to the hand, ’I have no need of thee;’ nor again the head to the feet, ’I have no need of you.’
But much more the members of the body hich seem to be more infirm are necessary,
and those that e think to be less honourable of the body, around these e put more abundant honour, and our unseemly things have seemliness more abundant,
and our seemly things have no need; but God did temper the body together, to the lacking part having given more abundant honour,
that there may be no division in the body, but that the members may have the same anxiety for one another,
and hether one member doth suffer, suffer ith [it] do all the members, or one member is glorified, rejoice ith [it] do all the members;
and ye are the body of Christ, and members in particular.
And some, indeed, did God set in the assembly, first apostles, secondly prophets, thirdly teachers, afterards poers, afterards gifts of healings, helpings, governings, divers kinds of tongues;
[are] all apostles? [are] all prophets? [are] all teachers? [are] all poers?
have all gifts of healings? do all speak ith tongues? do all interpret?
and desire earnestly the better gifts; and yet a far excelling ay do I she to you:
If ith the tongues of men and of messengers I speak, and have not love, I have become brass sounding, or a cymbal tinkling;
and if I have prophecy, and kno all the secrets, and all the knoledge, and if I have all the faith, so as to remove mountains, and have not love, I am nothing;
and if I give aay to feed others all my goods, and if I give up my body that I may be burned, and have not love, I am profited nothing.
The love is long-suffering, it is kind, the love doth not envy, the love doth not vaunt itself, is not puffed up,
doth not act unseemly, doth not seek its on things, is not provoked, doth not impute evil,
rejoiceth not over the unrighteousness, and rejoiceth ith the truth;
all things it beareth, all it believeth, all it hopeth, all it endureth.
The love doth never fail; and hether [there be] prophecies, they shall become useless; hether tongues, they shall cease; hether knoledge, it shall become useless;
for in part e kno, and in part e prophecy;
and hen that hich is perfect may come, then that hich [is] in part shall become useless.
When I as a babe, as a babe I as speaking, as a babe I as thinking, as a babe I as reasoning, and hen I have become a man, I have made useless the things of the babe;
for e see no through a mirror obscurely, and then face to face; no I kno in part, and then I shall fully kno, as also I as knon;
and no there doth remain faith, hope, love — these three; and the greatest of these [is] love.
Pursue the love, and seek earnestly the spiritual things, and rather that ye may prophecy,
for he ho is speaking in an [unknon] tongue — to men he doth not speak, but to God, for no one doth hearken, and in spirit he doth speak secrets;
and he ho is prophesying to men doth speak edification, and exhortation, and comfort;
he ho is speaking in an [unknon] tongue, himself doth edify, and he ho is prophesying, an assembly doth edify;

and I ish you all to speak ith tongues, and more that ye may prophecy, for greater is he ho is prophesying than he ho is speaking ith tongues, except one may interpret, that the assembly may receive edification.
And no, brethren, if I may come unto you speaking tongues, hat shall I profit you, except I shall speak to you either in revelation, or in knoledge, or in prophesying, or in teaching?
yet the things ithout life giving sound — hether pipe or harp — if a difference in the sounds they may not give, ho shall be knon that hich is piped or that hich is harped?
for if also an uncertain sound a trumpet may give, ho shall prepare himself for battle?
so also ye, if through the tongue, speech easily understood ye may not give — ho shall that hich is spoken be knon? for ye shall be speaking to air.
There are, it may be, so many kinds of voices in the orld, and none of them is unmeaning,
if, then, I do not kno the poer of the voice, I shall be to him ho is speaking a foreigner, and he ho is speaking, is to me a foreigner;
so also ye, since ye are earnestly desirous of spiritual gifts, for the building up of the assembly seek that ye may abound;
herefore he ho is speaking in an [unknon] tongue — let him pray that he may interpret;
for if I pray in an [unknon] tongue, my spirit doth pray, and my understanding is unfruitful.
What then is it? I ill pray ith the spirit, and I ill pray also ith the understanding; I ill sing psalms ith the spirit, and I ill sing psalms also ith the understanding;
since, if thou mayest bless ith the spirit, he ho is filling the place of the unlearned, ho shall he say the Amen at thy giving of thanks, since hat thou dost say he hath not knon?
for thou, indeed, dost give thanks ell, but the other is not built up!
I give thanks to my God — more than you all ith tongues speaking —
but in an assembly I ish to speak five ords through my understanding, that others also I may instruct, rather than myriads of ords in an [unknon] tongue.
Brethren, become not children in the understanding, but in the evil be ye babes, and in the understanding become ye perfect;
in the la it hath been ritten, that, ’With other tongues and ith other lips I ill speak to this people, and not even so ill they hear Me, saith the Lord;’
so that the tongues are for a sign, not to the believing, but to the unbelieving; and the prophesy [is] not for the unbelieving, but for the believing,
If, therefore, the hole assembly may come together, to the same place, and all may speak ith tongues, and there may come in unlearned or unbelievers, ill they not say that ye are mad?
and if all may prophecy, and any one may come in, an unbeliever or unlearned, he is convicted by all, he is discerned by all,
and so the secrets of his heart become manifest, and so having fallen upon [his] face, he ill bo before God, declaring that God really is among you.
What then is it, brethren? henever ye may come together, each of you hath a psalm, hath a teaching, hath a tongue, hath a revelation, hath an interpretation? let all things be for building up;
if an [unknon] tongue any one do speak, by to, or at the most, by three, and in turn, and let one interpret;
and if there may be no interpreter, let him be silent in an assembly, and to himself let him speak, and to God.
And prophets — let to or three speak, and let the others discern,
and if to another sitting [anything] may be revealed, let the first be silent;
for ye are able, one by one, all to prophesy, that all may learn, and all may be exhorted,
and the spiritual gift of prophets to prophets are subject,
for God is not [a God] of tumult, but of peace, as in all the assemblies of the saints.
Your omen in the assemblies let them be silent, for it hath not been permitted to them to speak, but to be subject, as also the la saith;

And I make knon to you, brethren, the good nes that I proclaimed to you, hich also ye did receive, in hich also ye have stood,

then, also, those having fallen asleep in Christ did perish;
if in this life e have hope in Christ only, of all men e are most to be pitied.

and each in his proper order, a first-fruit Christ, afterards those ho are the Christ’s, in his presence,

Seeing hat shall they do ho are baptized for the dead, if the dead do not rise at all? hy also are they baptized for the dead?

unise! thou — hat thou dost so is not quickened except it may die;
and that hich thou dost so, not the body that shall be dost thou so, but bare grain, it may be of heat, or of some one of the others,
and God doth give to it a body according as He illed, and to each of the seeds its proper body.

and [there are] heavenly bodies, and earthly bodies; but one [is] the glory of the heavenly, and another that of the earthly;

as [is] the earthy, such [are] also the earthy; and as [is] the heavenly, such [are] also the heavenly;
and, according as e did bear the image of the earthy, e shall bear also the image of the heavenly.

and the sting of the death [is] the sin, and the poer of the sin the la;

let all your things be done in love.

if any one doth not love the Lord Jesus Christ — let him be anathema! The Lord hath come!
The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ [is] ith you;
my love [is] ith you all in Christ Jesus. Amen.
Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ, through the ill of God, and Timotheus the brother, to the assembly of God that is in Corinth, ith all the saints ho are in all Achaia:

ye orking together also for us by your supplication, that the gift through many persons to us, through many may be thankfully acknoledged for us.

For our glorying is this: the testimony of our conscience, that in simplicity and sincerity of God, not in fleshly isdom, but in the grace of God, e did conduct ourselves in the orld, and more abundantly toard you;

and God [is] faithful, that our ord unto you became not Yes and No,
for the Son of God, Jesus Christ, among you through us having been preached — through me and Silvanus and Timotheus — did not become Yes and No, but in him it hath become Yes;
for as many as [are] promises of God, in him [are] the Yes, and in him the Amen, for glory to God through us;
and He ho is confirming you ith us into Christ, and did anoint us, [is] God,
ho also sealed us, and gave the earnest of the Spirit in our hearts.

not that e are lords over your faith, but e are orkers together ith your joy, for by the faith ye stand.

for if I make you sorry, then ho is he ho is making me glad, except he ho is made sorry by me?
and I rote to you this same thing, that having come, I may not have sorro from them of hom it behoved me to have joy, having confidence in you all, that my joy is of you all,
for out of much tribulation and pressure of heart I rote to you through many tears, not that ye might be made sorry, but that ye might kno the love that I have more abundantly toard you.

sufficient to such a one is this punishment, that [is] by the more part,
so that, on the contrary, [it is] rather for you to forgive and to comfort, lest by over abundant sorro such a one may be salloed up;
herefore, I call upon you to confirm love to him,
for, for this also did I rite, that I might kno the proof of you, hether in regard to all things ye are obedient.

that e may not be over-reached by the Adversary, for of his devices e are not ignorant.
And having come to Troas for the good nes of the Christ, and a door to me having been opened in the Lord,
I have not had rest to my spirit, on my not finding Titus my brother, but having taken leave of them, I ent forth to Macedonia;
and to God [are] thanks, ho at all times is leading us in triumph in the Christ, and the fragrance of His knoledge He is manifesting through us in every place,
because of Christ a seet fragrance e are to God, in those being saved, and in those being lost;

for e are not as the many, adulterating the ord of God, but as of sincerity — but as of God; in the presence of God, in Christ e do speak.
Do e begin again to recommend ourselves, except e need, as some, letters of recommendation unto you, or from you?
our letter ye are, having been ritten in our hearts, knon and read by all men,
manifested that ye are a letter of Christ ministered by us, ritten not ith ink, but ith the Spirit of the living God, not in the tablets of stone, but in fleshy tablets of the heart,
and such trust e have through the Christ toard God,
not that e are sufficient of ourselves to think anything, as of ourselves, but our sufficiency [is] of God,
ho also made us sufficient [to be] ministrants of a ne covenant, not of letter, but of spirit; for the letter doth kill, and the spirit doth make alive.

and if the ministration of the death, in letters, engraved in stones, came in glory, so that the sons of Israel ere not able to look stedfastly to the face of Moses, because of the glory of his face — hich as being made useless,

The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ [is] ith your spirit! Amen.

For to hich of the messengers said He ever, ’My Son thou art — I to-day have begotten thee?’ and again, ’I ill be to him for a father, and he shall be to Me for a son?’

And unto hich of the messengers said He ever, ’Sit at My right hand, till I may make thine enemies thy footstool?’
are they not all spirits of service — for ministration being sent forth because of those about to inherit salvation?
Because of this it behoveth [us] more abundantly to take heed to the things heard, lest e may glide aside,
for if the ord being spoken through messengers did become stedfast, and every transgression and disobedience did receive a just recompense,

For not to messengers did He subject the coming orld, concerning hich e speak,
and one in a certain place did testify fully, saying, ’What is man, that Thou art mindful of him, or a son of man, that Thou dost look after him?
Thou didst make him some little less than messengers, ith glory and honour Thou didst cron him, and didst set him over the orks of Thy hands,

and him ho as made some little less than messengers e see — Jesus — because of the suffering of the death, ith glory and honour having been croned, that by the grace of God for every one he might taste of death.
For it as becoming to Him, because of hom [are] the all things, and through hom [are] the all things, many sons to glory bringing, the author of their salvation through sufferings to make perfect,
for both he ho is sanctifying and those sanctified [are] all of one, for hich cause he is not ashamed to call them brethren,

and again, ’Behold I and the children that God did give to me.’

Seeing, then, the children have partaken of flesh and blood, he himself also in like manner did take part of the same, that through death he might destroy him having the poer of death — that is, the devil —
and might deliver those, hoever, ith fear of death, throughout all their life, ere subjects of bondage,

being stedfast to Him ho did appoint him, as also Moses in all his house,
for of more glory than Moses hath this one been counted orthy, inasmuch as more honour than the house hath he ho doth build it,
for every house is builded by some one, and He ho the all things did build [is] God,
and Moses indeed [as] stedfast in all his house, as an attendant, for a testimony of those things that ere to be spoken,
and Christ, as a Son over his house, hose house are e, if the boldness and the rejoicing of the hope unto the end e hold fast.
Wherefore, (as the Holy Spirit saith, ’To-day, if His voice ye may hear —
ye may not harden your hearts, as in the provocation, in the day of the temptation in the ilderness,

then I said, Lo, I come, (in a volume of the book it hath been ritten concerning me,) to do, O God, Thy ill;’
