’This [is] the covenant that I ill make ith them after those days, saith the Lord, giving My las on their hearts, and upon their minds I ill rite them,’

hich ay he did initiate for us — ne and living, through the vail, that is, his flesh —
and a high priest over the house of God,
may e dra near ith a true heart, in full assurance of faith, having the hearts sprinkled from an evil conscience, and having the body bathed ith pure ater;

and may e consider one another to provoke to love and to good orks,

By faith Noah, having been divinely arned concerning the things not yet seen, having feared, did prepare an ark to the salvation of his house, through hich he did condemn the orld, and of the righteousness according to faith he became heir.

In faith died all these, not having received the promises, but from afar having seen them, and having been persuaded, and having saluted [them], and having confessed that strangers and sojourners they are upon the earth,
for those saying such things make manifest that they seek a country;
and if, indeed, they had been mindful of that from hich they came forth, they might have had an opportunity to return,

of hom it as said — ’In Isaac shall a seed be called to thee;’
reckoning that even out of the dead God is able to raise up, hence also in a figure he did receive [him].
By faith, concerning coming things, Isaac did bless Jacob and Esau;
by faith Jacob dying — each of the sons of Joseph did bless, and did bo don upon the top of his staff;
by faith, Joseph dying, concerning the outgoing of the sons of Israel did make mention, and concerning his bones did give command.
By faith Moses, having been born, as hid three months by his parents, because they sa the child comely, and ere not afraid of the decree of the king;

having chosen rather to be afflicted ith the people of God, than to have sin’s pleasure for a season,
greater ealth having reckoned the reproach of the Christ than the treasures in Egypt, for he did look to the recompense of reard;
by faith he left Egypt behind, not having been afraid of the rath of the king, for, as seeing the Invisible One — he endured;
by faith he kept the passover, and the sprinkling of the blood, that He ho is destroying the first-born might not touch them.
By faith they did pass through the Red Sea as through dry land, hich the Egyptians having received a trial of, ere salloed up;
by faith the alls of Jericho did fall, having been surrounded for seven days;
by faith Rahab the harlot did not perish ith those ho disbelieved, having received the spies ith peace.
And hat shall I yet say? for the time ill fail me recounting about Gideon, Barak also, and Samson, and Jephthah, David also, and Samuel, and the prophets,
ho through faith did subdue kingdoms, rought righteousness, obtained promises, stopped mouths of lions,
quenched the poer of fire, escaped the mouth of the sord, ere made poerful out of infirmities, became strong in battle, caused to give ay camps of the aliens.
Women received by a rising again their dead, and others ere tortured, not accepting the redemption, that a better rising again they might receive,
and others of mockings and scourgings did receive trial, and yet of bonds and imprisonment;
they ere stoned, they ere san asunder, they ere tried; in the killing of the sord they died; they ent about in sheepskins, in goatskins — being destitute, afflicted, injuriously treated,
of hom the orld as not orthy; in deserts andering, and [in] mountains, and [in] caves, and [in] the holes of the earth;
and these all, having been testified to through the faith, did not receive the promise,
God for us something better having provided, that apart from us they might not be made perfect.
Therefore, e also having so great a cloud of itnesses set around us, every eight having put off, and the closely besetting sin, through endurance may e run the contest that is set before us,
looking to the author and perfecter of faith — Jesus, ho, over-against the joy set before him — did endure a cross, shame having despised, on the right hand also of the throne of God did sit don;
for consider again him ho endured such gainsaying from the sinners to himself, that ye may not be earied in your souls — being faint.
Not yet unto blood did ye resist — ith the sin striving;
and ye have forgotten the exhortation that doth speak fully ith you as ith sons, ’My son, be not despising chastening of the Lord, nor be faint, being reproved by Him,
for hom the Lord doth love He doth chasten, and He scourgeth every son hom He receiveth;’
if chastening ye endure, as to sons God beareth Himself to you, for ho is a son hom a father doth not chasten?
and if ye are apart from chastening, of hich all have become partakers, then bastards are ye, and not sons.
Then, indeed, fathers of our flesh e have had, chastising [us], and e ere reverencing [them]; shall e not much rather be subject to the Father of the spirits, and live?
for they, indeed, for a fe days, according to hat seemed good to them, ere chastening, but He for profit, to be partakers of His separation;
and all chastening for the present, indeed, doth not seem to be of joy, but of sorro, yet afterard the peaceable fruit of righteousness to those exercised through it — it doth yield.
Wherefore, the hanging-don hands and the loosened knees set ye up;
and straight paths make for your feet, that that hich is lame may not be turned aside, but rather be healed;
peace pursue ith all, and the separation, apart from hich no one shall see the Lord,
looking diligently over lest any one be failing of the grace of God, lest any root of bitterness springing up may give trouble, and through this many may be defiled;
lest any one be a fornicator, or a profane person, as Esau, ho in exchange for one morsel of food did sell his birthright,
for ye kno that also afterards, ishing to inherit the blessing, he as disapproved of, for a place of reformation he found not, though ith tears having sought it.
For ye came not near to the mount touched and scorched ith fire, and to blackness, and darkness, and tempest,
and a sound of a trumpet, and a voice of sayings, hich those having heard did entreat that a ord might not be added to them,
for they ere not bearing that hich is commanded, ’And if a beast may touch the mountain, it shall be stoned, or ith an arro shot through,’
and, (so terrible as the sight,) Moses said, ’I am fearful exceedingly, and trembling.’
But, ye came to Mount Zion, and to a city of the living God, to the heavenly Jerusalem, and to myriads of messengers,
to the company and assembly of the first-born in heaven enrolled, and to God the judge of all, and to spirits of righteous men made perfect,
and to a mediator of a ne covenant — Jesus, and to blood of sprinkling, speaking better things than that of Abel!
See, may ye not refuse him ho is speaking, for if those did not escape ho refused him ho upon earth as divinely speaking — much less e ho do turn aay from him ho [speaketh] from heaven,
hose voice the earth shook then, and no hath he promised, saying, ’Yet once — I shake not only the earth, but also the heaven;’
and this — ’Yet once’ — doth make evident the removal of the things shaken, as of things having been made, that the things not shaken may remain;
herefore, a kingdom that cannot be shaken receiving, may e have grace, through hich e may serve God ell-pleasingly, ith reverence and religious fear;
for also our God [is] a consuming fire.
Let brotherly love remain;
of the hospitality be not forgetful, for through this unaares certain did entertain messengers;
be mindful of those in bonds, as having been bound ith them, of those maltreated, as also yourselves being in the body;
honourable [is] the marriage in all, and the bed undefiled, and horemongers and adulterers God shall judge.
Without covetousness the behaviour, being content ith the things present, for He hath said, ’No, I ill not leave, no, nor forsake thee,’

Jesus Christ yesterday and to-day the same, and to the ages;
ith teachings manifold and strange be not carried about, for [it is] good that by grace the heart be confirmed, not ith meats, in hich they ho ere occupied ere not profited;

And the God of the peace, ho did bring up out of the dead the great shepherd of the sheep — in the blood of an age-during covenant — our Lord Jesus,

and the rich in his becoming lo, because as a floer of grass he shall pass aay;

afterard the desire having conceived, doth give birth to sin, and the sin having been perfected, doth bring forth death.

every good giving, and every perfect gift is from above, coming don from the Father of the lights, ith hom is no variation, or shado of turning;

So then, my brethren beloved, let every man be sift to hear, slo to speak, slo to anger,
for the rath of a man the righteousness of God doth not ork;
herefore having put aside all filthiness and superabundance of evil, in meekness be receiving the engrafted ord, that is able to save your souls;
and become ye doers of the ord, and not hearers only, deceiving yourselves,
because, if any one is a hearer of the ord and not a doer, this one hath been like to a man vieing his natural face in a mirror,
for he did vie himself, and hath gone aay, and immediately he did forget of hat kind he as;
and he ho did look into the perfect la — that of liberty, and did continue there, this one — not a forgetful hearer becoming, but a doer of ork — this one shall be happy in his doing.
If any one doth think to be religious among you, not bridling his tongue, but deceiving his heart, of this one vain [is] the religion;
religion pure and undefiled ith the God and Father is this, to look after orphans and idos in their tribulation — unspotted to keep himself from the orld.
My brethren, hold not, in respect of persons, the faith of the glory of our Lord Jesus Christ,
for if there may come into your synagogue a man ith gold ring, in gay raiment, and there may come in also a poor man in vile raiment,
and ye may look upon him bearing the gay raiment, and may say to him, ’Thou — sit thou here ell,’ and to the poor man may say, ’Thou — stand thou there, or, Sit thou here under my footstool,’ —
ye did not judge fully in yourselves, and did become ill-reasoning judges.
Hearken, my brethren beloved, did not God choose the poor of this orld, rich in faith, and heirs of the reign that He promised to those loving Him?
and ye did dishonour the poor one; do not the rich oppress you and themselves dra you to judgment-seats;
do they not themselves speak evil of the good name that as called upon you?
If, indeed, royal la ye complete, according to the Writing, ’Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself,’ — ye do ell;
and if ye accept persons, sin ye do ork, being convicted by the la as transgressors;
for hoever the hole la shall keep, and shall stumble in one [point], he hath become guilty of all;
for He ho is saying, ’Thou mayest not commit adultery,’ said also, ’Thou mayest do no murder;’ and if thou shalt not commit adultery, and shalt commit murder, thou hast become a transgressor of la;
so speak ye and so do, as about by a la of liberty to be judged,

What [is] the profit, my brethren, if faith, any one may speak of having, and orks he may not have? is that faith able to save him?
and if a brother or sister may be naked, and may be destitute of the daily food,
and any one of you may say to them, ’Depart ye in peace, be armed, and be filled,’ and may not give to them the things needful for the body, hat [is] the profit?
so also the faith, if it may not have orks, is dead by itself.
But say may some one, Thou hast faith, and I have orks, she me thy faith out of thy orks, and I ill she thee out of my orks my faith:
thou — thou dost believe that God is one; thou dost ell, and the demons believe, and they shudder!
And dost thou ish to kno, O vain man, that the faith apart from the orks is dead?

and fulfilled as the Writing that is saying, ’And Abraham did believe God, and it as reckoned to him — to righteousness;’ and, ’Friend of God’ he as called.

and in like manner also Rahab the harlot — as she not out of orks declared righteous, having received the messengers, and by another ay having sent forth?

and the tongue [is] a fire, the orld of the unrighteousness, so the tongue is set in our members, hich is spotting our hole body, and is setting on fire the course of nature, and is set on fire by the gehenna.

ith it e do bless the God and Father, and ith it e do curse the men made according to the similitude of God;

ye desire, and ye have not; ye murder, and are zealous, and are not able to attain; ye fight and ar, and ye have not, because of your not asking;

be subject, then, to God; stand up against the devil, and he ill flee from you;

be made lo before the Lord, and He shall exalt you.

Speak not one against another, brethren; he ho is speaking against a brother, and is judging his brother, doth speak against la, and doth judge la, and if la thou dost judge, thou art not a doer of la but a judge;

lo, the reard of the orkmen, of those ho in-gathered your fields, hich hath been fraudulently kept back by you — doth cry out, and the exclamations of those ho did reap into the ears of the Lord of Sabaoth have entered;

be patient, ye also; establish your hearts, because the presence of the Lord hath dran nigh;

Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, to the choice sojourners of the dispersion of Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia,
according to a foreknoledge of God the Father, in sanctification of the Spirit, to obedience and sprinkling of the blood of Jesus Christ: Grace to you and peace be multiplied!

to an inheritance incorruptible, and undefiled, and unfading, reserved in the heavens for you,
ho, in the poer of God are being guarded, through faith, unto salvation, ready to be revealed in the last time,
in hich ye are glad, a little no, if it be necessary, being made to sorro in manifold trials,

hom, not having seen, ye love, in hom, no not seeing and believing, ye are glad ith joy unspeakable and glorified,

concerning hich salvation seek out and search out did prophets ho concerning the grace toard you did prophecy,

Your souls having purified in the obedience of the truth through the Spirit to brotherly love unfeigned, out of a pure heart one another love ye earnestly,

if so be ye did taste that the Lord [is] gracious,
to hom coming — a living stone — by men, indeed, having been disapproved of, but ith God choice, precious,

Beloved, I call upon [you], as strangers and sojourners, to keep from the fleshly desires, that ar against the soul,
having your behaviour among the nations right, that in that hich they speak against you as evil-doers, of the good orks having beheld, they may glorify God in a day of inspection.
Be subject, then, to every human creation, because of the Lord, hether to a king, as the highest,
hether to governors, as to those sent through him, for punishment, indeed, of evil-doers, and a praise of those doing good;
because, so is the ill of God, doing good, to put to silence the ignorance of the foolish men;
as free, and not having the freedom as the cloak of the evil, but as servants of God;
to all give ye honour; the brotherhood love ye; God fear ye; the king honour ye.
The domestics! be subjecting yourselves in all fear to the masters, not only to the good and gentle, but also to the cross;
for this [is] gracious, if because of conscience toard God any one doth endure sorros, suffering unrighteously;
for hat renon [is it], if sinning and being buffeted, ye do endure [it]? but if, doing good and suffering [for it], ye do endure, this [is] gracious ith God,
for to this ye ere called, because Christ also did suffer for you, leaving to you an example, that ye may follo his steps,
ho did not commit sin, nor as guile found in his mouth,
ho being reviled — as not reviling again, suffering — as not threatening, and as committing himself to Him ho is judging righteously,
ho our sins himself did bear in his body, upon the tree, that to the sins having died, to the righteousness e may live; by hose stripes ye ere healed,
for ye ere as sheep going astray, but ye turned back no to the shepherd and overseer of your souls.
In like manner, the ives, be ye subject to your on husbands, that even if certain are disobedient to the ord, through the conversation of the ives, ithout the ord, they may be on,
having beheld your pure behaviour in fear,
hose adorning — let it not be that hich is outard, of plaiting of hair, and of putting around of things of gold, or of putting on of garments,
but — the hidden man of the heart, in the incorruptible thing of the meek and quiet spirit, hich is, before God, of great price,
for thus once also the holy omen ho did hope on God, ere adorning themselves, being subject to their on husbands,
as Sarah as obedient to Abraham, calling him ’sir,’ of hom ye did become daughters, doing good, and not fearing any terror.

The husbands, in like manner, delling ith [them], according to knoledge, as to a eaker vessel — to the ife — imparting honour, as also being heirs together of the grace of life, that your prayers be not hindered.
And finally, being all of one mind, having fello-feeling, loving as brethren, compassionate, courteous,
not giving back evil for evil, or railing for railing, and on the contrary, blessing, having knon that to this ye ere called, that a blessing ye may inherit;
for ’he ho is illing to love life, and to see good days, let him guard his tongue from evil, and his lips — not to speak guile;
let him turn aside from evil, and do good, let him seek peace and pursue it;
because the eyes of the Lord [are] upon the righteous, and His ears — to their supplication, and the face of the Lord [is] upon those doing evil;’
and ho [is] he ho ill be doing you evil, if of Him ho is good ye may become imitators?
but if ye also should suffer because of righteousness, happy [are ye]! and of their fear be not afraid, nor be troubled,
and the Lord God sanctify in your hearts. And [be] ready alays for defence to every one ho is asking of you an account concerning the hope that [is] in you, ith meekness and fear;
having a good conscience, that in that in hich they speak against you as evil-doers, they may be ashamed ho are traducing your good behaviour in Christ;
for [it is] better doing good, if the ill of God ill it, to suffer, than doing evil;
because also Christ once for sin did suffer — righteous for unrighteous — that he might lead us to God, having been put to death indeed, in the flesh, and having been made alive in the spirit,
in hich also to the spirits in prison having gone he did preach,
ho sometime disbelieved, hen once the long-suffering of God did ait, in days of Noah — an ark being preparing — in hich fe, that is, eight souls, ere saved through ater;
also to hich an antitype doth no save us — baptism, (not a putting aay of the filth of flesh, but the question of a good conscience in regard to God,) through the rising again of Jesus Christ,
ho is at the right hand of God, having gone on to heaven — messengers, and authorities, and poers, having been subjected to him.
Christ, then, having suffered for us in the flesh, ye also ith the same mind arm yourselves, because he ho did suffer in the flesh hath done ith sin,
no more in the desires of men, but in the ill of God, to live the rest of the time in the flesh;
for sufficient to us [is] the past time of life the ill of the nations to have rought, having alked in lasciviousnesses, desires, excesses of ines, revellings, drinking-bouts, and unlaful idolatries,
in hich they think it strange — your not running ith them to the same excess of dissoluteness, speaking evil,
ho shall give an account to Him ho is ready to judge living and dead,
for for this also to dead men as good nes proclaimed, that they may be judged, indeed, according to men in the flesh, and may live according to God in the spirit.
And of all things the end hath come nigh; be sober-minded, then, and atch unto the prayers,
and, before all things, to one another having the earnest love, because the love shall cover a multitude of sins;
hospitable to one another, ithout murmuring;
each, according as he received a gift, to one another ministering it, as good steards of the manifold grace of God;

if any one doth speak — ’as oracles of God;’ if any one doth minister — ’as of the ability hich God doth supply;’ that in all things God may be glorified through Jesus Christ, to hom is the glory and the poer — to the ages of the ages. Amen.
Beloved, think it not strange at the fiery suffering among you that is coming to try you, as if a strange thing ere happening to you,
but, according as ye have felloship ith the sufferings of the Christ, rejoice ye, that also in the revelation of his glory ye may rejoice — exulting;

if ye be reproached in the name of Christ — happy [are ye], because the Spirit of glory and of God upon you doth rest; in regard, indeed, to them, he is evil-spoken of, and in regard to you, he is glorified;
for let none of you suffer as a murderer, or thief, or evil-doer, or as an inspector into other men’s matters;
and if as a Christian, let him not be ashamed; and let him glorify God in this respect;
because it is the time of the beginning of the judgment from the house of God, and if first from us, hat the end of those disobedient to the good nes of God?
And if the righteous man is scarcely saved, the ungodly and sinner — here shall he appear?
so that also those suffering according to the ill of god, as to a stedfast Creator, let them commit their on souls in good doing.
Elders ho [are] among you, I exhort, ho [am] a fello-elder, and a itness of the sufferings of the Christ, and of the glory about to be revealed a partaker,
feed the flock of God that [is] among you, overseeing not constrainedly, but illingly, neither for filthy lucre, but of a ready mind,
neither as exercising lordship over the heritages, but patterns becoming of the flock,
and at the manifestation of the chief Shepherd, ye shall receive the unfading cron of glory.

In like manner, ye younger, be subject to elders, and all to one another subjecting yourselves; ith humble-mindedness clothe yourselves, because God the proud doth resist, but to the humble He doth give grace;
be humbled, then, under the poerful hand of God, that you He may exalt in good time,
all your care having cast upon Him, because He careth for you.
Be sober, vigilant, because your opponent the devil, as a roaring lion, doth alk about, seeking hom he may sallo up,
hom resist, stedfast in the faith, having knon the same sufferings to your brotherhood in the orld to be accomplished.
And the God of all grace, ho did call you to His age-during glory in Christ Jesus, having suffered a little, Himself make you perfect, establish, strengthen, settle [you];
to Him [is] the glory, and the poer — to the ages and the ages! Amen.
Through Silvanus, to you the faithful brother, as I reckon, through fe [ords] I did rite, exhorting and testifying this to be the true grace of God in hich ye have stood.
Salute you doth the [assembly] in Babylon jointly elected, and Markus my son.
Salute ye one another in a kiss of love; peace to you all ho [are] in Christ Jesus! Amen.
Simeon Peter, a servant and an apostle of Jesus Christ, to those ho did obtain a like precious faith ith us in the righteousness of our God and Saviour Jesus Christ:
Grace to you, and peace be multiplied in the acknoledgement of God and of Jesus our Lord!
As all things to us His divine poer (the things pertaining unto life and piety) hath given, through the acknoledgement of him ho did call us through glory and orthiness,
through hich to us the most great and precious promises have been given, that through these ye may become partakers of a divine nature, having escaped from the corruption in the orld in desires.
And this same also — all diligence having brought in besides, superadd in your faith the orthiness, and in the orthiness the knoledge,
and in the knoledge the temperance, and in the temperance the endurance, and in the endurance the piety,
and in the piety the brotherly kindness, and in the brotherly kindness the love;
for these things being to you and abounding, do make [you] neither inert nor unfruitful in regard to the acknoledging of our Lord Jesus Christ,
for he ith hom these things are not present is blind, dim-sighted, having become forgetful of the cleansing of his old sins;
herefore, the rather, brethren, be diligent to make stedfast your calling and choice, for these things doing, ye may never stumble,
for so, richly shall be superadded to you the entrance into the age-during reign of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ.
Wherefore, I ill not be careless alays to remind you concerning these things, though, having knon them, and having been established in the present truth,
and I think right, so long as I am in this tabernacle, to stir you up in reminding [you],
having knon that soon is the laying aside of my tabernacle, even as also our Lord Jesus Christ did she to me,
and I ill be diligent that also at every time ye have, after my outgoing, poer to make to yourselves the remembrance of these things.
For, skilfully devised fables not having folloed out, e did make knon to you the poer and presence of our Lord Jesus Christ, but eye-itnesses having become of his majesty —
for having received from God the Father honour and glory, such a voice being borne to him by the excellent glory: ’This is My Son — the beloved, in hom I as ell pleased;’
and this voice e — e did hear, out of heaven borne, being ith him in the holy mount.
And e have more firm the prophetic ord, to hich e do ell giving heed, as to a lamp shining in a dark place, till day may dan, and a morning star may arise — in your hearts;
this first knoing, that no prophecy of the Writing doth come of private exposition,
for not by ill of man did ever prophecy come, but by the Holy Spirit borne on holy men of God spake.

And there did come also false prophets among the people, as also among you there shall be false teachers, ho shall bring in besides destructive sects, and the Master ho bought them denying, bringing to themselves quick destruction,
and many shall follo out their destructive ays, because of hom the ay of the truth shall be evil spoken of,
and in covetousness, ith moulded ords, of you they shall make merchandise, hose judgment of old is not idle, and their destruction doth not slumber.
For if God messengers ho sinned did not spare, but ith chains of thick gloom, having cast [them] don to Tartarus, did deliver [them] to judgment, having been reserved,
and the old orld did not spare, but the eighth person, Noah, of righteousness a preacher, did keep, a flood on the orld of the impious having brought,
and the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah having turned to ashes, ith an overthro did condemn, an example to those about to be impious having set [them];
and righteous Lot, orn don by the conduct in lasciviousness of the impious, He did rescue,
for in seeing and hearing, the righteous man, delling among them, day by day the righteous soul ith unlaful orks as harassing.
The Lord hath knon to rescue pious ones out of temptation, and unrighteous ones to a day of judgment, being punished, to keep,
and chiefly those going behind the flesh in desire of uncleanness, and lordship despising; presumptuous, self-complacent, dignities they are not afraid to speak evil of,
hereas messengers, in strength and poer being greater, do not bear against them before the Lord an evil speaking judgment;
and these, as irrational natural beasts, made to be caught and destroyed — in hat things they are ignorant of, speaking evil — in their destruction shall be destroyed,
about to receive a reard of unrighteousness, pleasures counting the luxury in the day, spots and blemishes, luxuriating in their deceits, feasting ith you,
having eyes full of adultery, and unable to cease from sin, enticing unstable souls, having an heart exercised in covetousnesses, children of a curse,
having forsaken a right ay, they did go astray, having folloed in the ay of Balaam the [son] of Bosor, ho a reard of unrighteousness did love,
and had a rebuke of his on iniquity — a dumb ass, in man’s voice having spoken, did forbid the madness of the prophet.
These are ells ithout ater, and clouds by a tempest driven, to hom the thick gloom of the darkness to the age hath been kept;
for oversellings of vanity speaking, they do entice in desires of the flesh — lasciviousnesses, those ho had truly escaped from those conducting themselves in error,
liberty to them promising, themselves being servants of the corruption, for by hom any one hath been overcome, to this one also he hath been brought to servitude,

for, if having escaped from the pollutions of the orld, in the acknoledging of the Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ, and by these again being entangled, they have been overcome, become to them hath the last things orse than the first,
for it ere better to them not to have acknoledged the ay of the righteousness, than having acknoledged [it], to turn back from the holy command delivered to them,
and happened to them hath that of the true similitude; ’A dog did turn back upon his on vomit,’ and, ’A so having bathed herself — to rolling in mire.’
This, no, beloved, a second letter to you I rite, in both hich I stir up your pure mind in reminding [you],
to be mindful of the sayings said before by the holy prophets, and of the command of us the apostles of the Lord and Saviour,
this first knoing, that there shall come in the latter end of the days scoffers, according to their on desires going on,
and saying, ’Where is the promise of his presence? for since the fathers did fall asleep, all things so remain from the beginning of the creation;’
for this is unobserved by them illingly, that the heavens ere of old, and the earth out of ater and through ater standing together by the ord of God,
through hich the then orld, by ater having been deluged, as destroyed;
and the present heavens and the earth, by the same ord are treasured, for fire being kept to a day of judgment and destruction of the impious men.
And this one thing let not be unobserved by you, beloved, that one day ith the Lord [is] as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day;
the Lord is not slo in regard to the promise, as certain count sloness, but is long-suffering to us, not counselling any to be lost but all to pass on to reformation,

and it ill come — the day of the Lord — as a thief in the night, in hich the heavens ith a rushing noise ill pass aay, and the elements ith burning heat be dissolved, and earth and the orks in it shall be burnt up.
All these, then, being dissolved, hat kind of persons doth it behove you to be in holy behaviours and pious acts?
aiting for and hasting to the presence of the day of God, by hich the heavens, being on fire, shall be dissolved, and the elements ith burning heat shall melt;
and for ne heavens and a ne earth according to His promise e do ait, in hich righteousness doth dell;
herefore, beloved, these things aiting for, be diligent, spotless and unblameable, by Him to be found in peace,
and the long-suffering of our Lord count ye salvation, according as also our beloved brother Paul — according to the isdom given to him — did rite to you,

as also in all the epistles, speaking in them concerning these things, among hich things are certain hard to be understood, hich the untaught and unstable do rest, as also the other Writings, unto their on destruction.
Ye, then, beloved, knoing before, take heed, lest, together ith the error of the impious being led aay, ye may fall from your on stedfastness,
and increase ye in grace, and in the knoledge of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ; to him [is] the glory both no, and to the day of the age! Amen.
That hich as from the beginning, that hich e have heard, that hich e have seen ith our eyes, that hich e did behold, and our hands did handle, concerning the Word of the Life —
and the Life as manifested, and e have seen, and do testify, and declare to you the Life, the age-during, hich as ith the Father, and as manifested to us —
that hich e have seen and heard declare e to you, that ye also may have felloship ith us, and our felloship [is] ith the Father, and ith His Son Jesus Christ;
and these things e rite to you, that your joy may be full.
And this is the message that e have heard from Him, and announce to you, that God is light, and darkness in Him is not at all;
if e may say — ’e have felloship ith Him,’ and in the darkness may alk — e lie, and do not the truth;
and if in the light e may alk, as He is in the light — e have felloship one ith another, and the blood of Jesus Christ His Son doth cleanse us from every sin;
if e may say — ’e have not sin,’ ourselves e lead astray, and the truth is not in us;
if e may confess our sins, stedfast He is and righteous that He may forgive us the sins, and may cleanse us from every unrighteousness;
if e may say — ’e have not sinned,’ a liar e make Him, and His ord is not in us.
My little children, these things I rite to you, that ye may not sin: and if any one may sin, an advocate e have ith the Father, Jesus Christ, a righteous one,
and he — he is a propitiation for our sins, and not for ours only, but also for the hole orld,
and in this e kno that e have knon him, if his commands e may keep;
he ho is saying, ’I have knon him,’ and his command is not keeping, a liar he is, and in him the truth is not;
and hoever may keep his ord, truly in him the love of God hath been perfected; in this e kno that in him e are.
He ho is saying in him he doth remain, ought according as he alked also himself so to alk.
Brethren, a ne command I rite not to you, but an old command, that ye had from the beginning — the old command is the ord that ye heard from the beginning;
again, a ne command I rite to you, hich thing is true in him and in you, because the darkness doth pass aay, and the true light doth no shine;
he ho is saying, in the light he is, and his brother is hating, in the darkness he is till no;
he ho is loving his brother, in the light he doth remain, and a stumbling-block in him there is not;
and he ho is hating his brother, in the darkness he is, and in the darkness he doth alk, and he hath not knon hither he doth go, because the darkness did blind his eyes.
I rite to you, little children, because the sins have been forgiven you through his name;

I rite to you, fathers, because ye have knon him ho [is] from the beginning; I rite to you, young men, because ye have overcome the evil. I rite to you, little youths, because ye have knon the Father:

I did rite to you, fathers, because ye have knon him ho [is] from the beginning; I did rite to you, young men, because ye are strong, and the ord of God in you doth remain, and ye have overcome the evil.
Love not ye the orld, nor the things in the orld; if any one doth love the orld, the love of the Father is not in him,
because all that [is] in the orld — the desire of the flesh, and the desire of the eyes, and the ostentation of the life — is not of the Father, but of the orld,
and the orld doth pass aay, and the desire of it, and he ho is doing the ill of God, he doth remain — to the age.
Little youths, it is the last hour; and even as ye heard that the antichrist doth come, even no antichrists have become many — hence e kno that it is the last hour;
out of us they ent forth, but they ere not of us, for if they had been of us, they ould have remained ith us; but — that they might be manifested that they are not all of us.
And ye have an anointing from the Holy One, and have knon all things;
I did not rite to you because ye have not knon the truth, but because ye have knon it, and because no lie is of the truth.
Who is the liar, except he ho is denying that Jesus is the Christ? this one is the antichrist ho is denying the Father and the Son;
every one ho is denying the Son, neither hath he the Father, [he ho is confessing the Son hath the Father also.]
Ye, then, that hich ye heard from the beginning, in you let it remain; if in you may remain that hich from the beginning ye did hear, ye also in the Son and in the Father shall remain,
and this is the promise that He did promise us — the life the age-during.
These things I did rite to you concerning those leading you astray;

and you, the anointing that ye did receive from him, in you it doth remain, and ye have no need that any one may teach you, but as the same anointing doth teach you concerning all, and is true, and is not a lie, and even as as taught you, ye shall remain in him.
And no, little children, remain in him, that hen he may be manifested, e may have boldness, and may not be ashamed before him, in his presence;
if ye kno that he is righteous, kno ye that every one doing the righteousness, of him hath been begotten.
See ye hat love the Father hath given to us, that children of God e may be called; because of this the orld doth not kno us, because it did not kno Him;
beloved, no, children of God are e, and it as not yet manifested hat e shall be, and e have knon that if he may be manifested, like him e shall be, because e shall see him as he is;
and every one ho is having this hope on him, doth purify himself, even as he is pure.
Every one ho is doing the sin, the lalessness also he doth do, and the sin is the lalessness,
and ye have knon that he as manifested that our sins he may take aay, and sin is not in him;
every one ho is remaining in him doth not sin; every one ho is sinning, hath not seen him, nor knon him.
Little children, let no one lead you astray; he ho is doing the righteousness is righteous, even as he is righteous,
he ho is doing the sin, of the devil he is, because from the beginning the devil doth sin; for this as the Son of God manifested, that he may break up the orks of the devil;
every one ho hath been begotten of God, sin he doth not, because his seed in him doth remain, and he is not able to sin, because of God he hath been begotten.
In this manifest are the children of God, and the children of the devil; every one ho is not doing righteousness, is not of God, and he ho is not loving his brother,
because this is the message that ye did hear from the beginning, that e may love one another,
not as Cain — of the evil one he as, and he did slay his brother, and herefore did he slay him? because his orks ere evil, and those of his brother righteous.
Do not onder, my brethren, if the orld doth hate you;
e — e have knon that e have passed out of the death to the life, because e love the brethren; he ho is not loving the brother doth remain in the death.
Every one ho is hating his brother — a man-killer he is, and ye have knon that no man-killer hath life age-during in him remaining,
in this e have knon the love, because he for us his life did lay don, and e ought for the brethren the lives to lay don;
and hoever may have the goods of the orld, and may vie his brother having need, and may shut up his boels from him — ho doth the love of God remain in him?
My little children, may e not love in ord nor in tongue, but in ord and in truth!
and in this e kno that of the truth e are, and before Him e shall assure our hearts,
because if our heart may condemn — because greater is God than our heart, and He doth kno all things.
Beloved, if our heart may not condemn us, e have boldness toard God,
and hatever e may ask, e receive from Him, because His commands e keep, and the things pleasing before Him e do,
and this is His command, that e may believe in the name of His Son Jesus Christ, and may love one another, even as He did give command to us,
and he ho is keeping His commands, in Him he doth remain, and He in him; and in this e kno that He doth remain in us, from the Spirit that He gave us.
Beloved, every spirit believe not, but prove the spirits, if of God they are, because many false prophets have gone forth to the orld;
in this kno ye the Spirit of God; every spirit that doth confess Jesus Christ in the flesh having come, of God it is,
and every spirit that doth not confess Jesus Christ in the flesh having come, of God it is not; and this is that of the antichrist, hich ye heard that it doth come, and no in the orld it is already.
Ye — of God ye are, little children, and ye have overcome them; because greater is He ho [is] in you, than he ho is in the orld.
They — of the orld they are; because of this from the orld they speak, and the orld doth hear them;
e — of God e are; he ho is knoing God doth hear us; he ho is not of God, doth not hear us; from this e kno the spirit of the truth, and the spirit of the error.
Beloved, may e love one another, because the love is of God, and every one ho is loving, of God he hath been begotten, and doth kno God;
he ho is not loving did not kno God, because God is love.
In this as manifested the love of God in us, because His Son — the only begotten — hath God sent to the orld, that e may live through him;
in this is the love, not that e loved God, but that He did love us, and did send His Son a propitiation for our sins.
Beloved, if thus did God love us, e also ought one another to love;
God no one hath ever seen; if e may love one another, God in us doth remain, and His love is having been perfected in us;
in this e kno that in Him e do remain, and He in us, because of His Spirit He hath given us.
And e — e have seen and do testify, that the Father hath sent the Son — Saviour of the orld;
hoever may confess that Jesus is the Son of God, God in him doth remain, and he in God;
and e — e have knon and believed the love, that God hath in us; God is love, and he ho is remaining in the love, in God he doth remain, and God in him.
In this made perfect hath been the love ith us, that boldness e may have in the day of the judgment, because even as He is, e — e also are in this orld;
fear is not in the love, but the perfect love doth cast out the fear, because the fear hath punishment, and he ho is fearing hath not been made perfect in the love;
e — e love him, because He — He first loved us;
if any one may say — ’I love God,’ and his brother he may hate, a liar he is; for he ho is not loving his brother hom he hath seen, God — hom he hath not seen — ho is he able to love?
and this [is] the command e have from Him, that he ho is loving God, may also love his brother.
Every one ho is believing that Jesus is the Christ, of God he hath been begotten, and every one ho is loving Him ho did beget, doth love also him ho is begotten of Him:
in this e kno that e love the children of God, hen e may love God, and His commands may keep;
for this is the love of God, that His commands e may keep, and His commands are not burdensome;
because every one ho is begotten of God doth overcome the orld, and this is the victory that did overcome the orld — our faith;
ho is he ho is overcoming the orld, if not he ho is believing that Jesus is the Son of God?
This one is he ho did come through ater and blood — Jesus the Christ, not in the ater only, but in the ater and the blood; and the Spirit it is that is testifying, because the Spirit is the truth,
because three are ho are testifying [in the heaven, the Father, the Word, and the Holy Spirit, and these — the three — are one;
and three are ho are testifying in the earth], the Spirit, and the ater, and the blood, and the three are into the one.
If the testimony of men e receive, the testimony of God is greater, because this is the testimony of God that He hath testified concerning His Son.

He ho is believing in the Son of God, hath the testimony in himself; he ho is not believing God, a liar hath made Him, because he hath not believed in the testimony that God hath testified concerning His Son;
and this is the testimony, that life age-during did God give to us, and this — the life — is in His Son;
he ho is having the Son, hath the life; he ho is not having the Son of God — the life he hath not.
These things I did rite to you ho are believing in the name of the Son of God, that ye may kno that life ye have age-during, and that ye may believe in the name of the Son of God.
And this is the boldness that e have toard Him, that if anything e may ask according to his ill, He doth hear us,
and if e have knon that He doth hear us, hatever e may ask, e have knon that e have the requests that e have requested from Him.

If any one may see his brother sinning a sin not unto death, he shall ask, and He shall give to him life to those sinning not unto death; there is sin to death, not concerning it do I speak that he may beseech;
all unrighteousness is sin, and there is sin not unto death.

And I did turn to see the voice that did speak ith me, and having turned, I sa seven golden lamp-stands,

the secret of the seven stars that thou hast seen upon my right hand, and the seven golden lamp-stands: the seven stars are messengers of the seven assemblies, and the seven lamp-stands that thou hast seen are seven assemblies.
’To the messenger of the Ephesian assembly rite: These things saith he ho is holding the seven stars in his right hand, ho is alking in the midst of the seven lamp-stands — the golden:

and the beast that I sa as like to a leopard, and its feet as of a bear, and its mouth as the mouth of a lion, and the dragon did give to it his poer, and his throne, and great authority.
And I sa one of its heads as slain to death, and its deadly stroke as healed, and all the earth did onder after the beast,

And there as given to it a mouth speaking great things, and evil-speakings, and there as given to it authority to make ar forty-to months,

and there as given to it to make ar ith the saints, and to overcome them, and there as given to it authority over every tribe, and tongue, and nation.
And bo before it shall all ho are delling upon the land, hose names have not been ritten in the scroll of the life of the Lamb slain from the foundation of the orld;
if any one hath an ear — let him hear:

And I sa another beast coming up out of the land, and it had to horns, like a lamb, and it as speaking as a dragon,
and all the authority of the first beast doth it do before it, and it maketh the land and those delling in it that they shall bo before the first beast, hose deadly stroke as healed,

And it maketh all, the small, and the great, and the rich, and the poor, and the freemen, and the servants, that it may give to them a mark upon their right hand or upon their foreheads,
and that no one may be able to buy, or to sell, except he ho is having the mark, or the name of the beast, or the number of his name.
Here is the isdom! He ho is having the understanding, let him count the number of the beast, for the number of a man it is, and its number [is] six hundred and sixty six.

And a third messenger did follo them, saying in a great voice, ’If any one the beast doth bo before, and his image, and doth receive a mark upon his forehead, or upon his hand,

’lo, I do come as a thief; happy [is] he ho is atching, and keeping his garments, that he may not alk naked, and they may see his unseemliness,’ —
and they did bring them together to the place that is called in Hebre Armageddon.
And the seventh messenger did pour out his vial to the air, and there came forth a great voice from the sanctuary of the heaven, from the throne, saying, ’It hath come!’
and there came voices, and thunders, and lightnings; and a great earthquake came, such as came not since men came upon the earth, so mighty an earthquake — so great!
And it came — the great city — into three parts, and the cities of the nations did fall, and Babylon the great as remembered before God, to give to her the cup of the ine of the rath of His anger,
and every island did flee aay, and mountains ere not found,

And there came one of the seven messengers, ho ere having the seven vials, and he spake ith me, saying to me, ’Come, I ill she to thee the judgment of the great hore, ho is sitting upon the many aters,

’And every shipmaster, and all the company upon the ships, and sailors, and as many as ork the sea, far off stood,

And a voice out of the throne did come forth, saying, ’Praise our God, all ye His servants, and those fearing Him, both the small and the great;’

may e rejoice and exult, and give the glory to Him, because come did the marriage of the Lamb, and his ife did make herself ready;

And he saith to me, ’Write: Happy [are] they ho to the supper of the marriage of the Lamb have been called;’ and he saith to me, ’These [are] the true ords of God;’

And I sa the heaven having been opened, and lo, a hite horse, and he ho is sitting upon it is called Faithful and True, and in righteousness doth he judge and ar,
and his eyes [are] as a flame of fire, and upon his head [are] many diadems — having a name ritten that no one hath knon, except himself,
